letters.summary: Welcomes CD; has tried to find him. May see him in Cambridge. Reminisces about CD’s musical taste and memory. Describes Charles Whitley’s wedding and wife. Mentions friends.

letters.title: To Caroline Darwin   [7 December 1836]
letters.summary:
Dinner at the Hensleigh Wedgwoods’. They have agreed to go over his journal. Henry Holland thinks it not worth publishing alone because it goes over FitzRoy’s ground.

His impressions of Harriet Martineau: "She is overwhelmed with her own projects, her own thoughts and own abilities."

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   15 December [1836]
letters.summary: Informs WDF of his activities since theBeaglelanded.

letters.title: To The Master & Fellows, Caius College   [19 December 1836 – 6 March 1837]
letters.deprecated: Master and Fellows, Caius College Cambridge
letters.recipient: Master and Fellows, Caius College Cambridge
letters.summary: "Mr Darwin presents his compliments to the Master & Fellows of Caius Coll. and is extremely sorry he is prevented by a previous engagement the honor of dining with them on Thursday."

letters.title: To Anthony Carlisle   [19 December 1836]
letters.summary: "Read a letter [to AC] of the 19th Instant from Mr Charles Darwin of Christs College, Cambridge stating that understanding from the Conservators that a Series of fossil Bones collected during the voyage of H: M: Surveying Vessel Beagle possesses a peculiar Interest as connected with Specimens already in the Museum of this College that it had always been his intention to present such Bones to some public collection on the condition that Casts thereof should be given to the leading Public Bodies for the sake of making them more generally useful, specifying the British Museum the Geological Society and the Universities of Cambridge and Oxford, and one set for himself: and that under such Conditions he should be most happy to present the entire series to the Museum of this College."

letters.title: To Richard Owen   19 December [1836]
letters.summary: Has written to Royal College of Surgeons, exactly as RO recommended, concerning disposition of his South American fossil bones. He fixed on the British Museum, rather than Paris, to receive plaster casts, because he was on board a King’s ship. Suggests RO propose another set for Paris, where they would be more useful than at BM. Has scarcely begun unpacking his cases.

letters.title: From William Owen Sr   19 December 1836
letters.summary: Asks CD’s help in finding a tutor for his son Charles.

letters.title: From Hensleigh Wedgwood   [20 December 1836]
letters.summary: Has returned CD’sBeaglejournal MS. Thinks it would be an interesting account even if they did not know CD, and that it will be successful if published; the less it is mixed up with FitzRoy’s journal, the better.

letters.title: From Anthony Carlisle   23 December 1836
letters.summary: The Royal College of Surgeons’ Board of Curators approve the terms and conditions under which CD has offered his S. American fossil bones to the College, and have sent their recommendation to the Council.

letters.title: From Sarah Elizabeth (Sarah) Wedgwood   23 December [1836]
letters.summary:
Has been presenting wedding gifts to her nieces and nephews during CD’s absence, without asking whether they are ready for them, so she sends him £40.

Caroline says CD has taken a lecture room for his work at Cambridge.

letters.title: From Charles Lyell   26 December 1836
letters.summary:
Comments on [MS of] CD’s paper ["Elevation on the coast of Chili" (4 Jan 1837),Collected papers1: 41–3].

Invites CD to dinner. "Don’t accept any official scientific place, if you can avoid it".

letters.title: From Catherine Darwin   27 [December 1836]
letters.summary: News of family and friends, Harriet Martineau’s soirée; funds deposited for him.

letters.title: From Robert FitzRoy   30 December 1836
letters.summary: RF has consulted W. J. Broderip, who recommended a joint three-volume publication of Captain King’s journal, FitzRoy’s, and CD’s, with profits divided by three. What does CD think of such a plan? RF promised Colburn an answer in January.

letters.title: To John Maurice Herbert   [1 January 1837]
letters.summary: Enjoyed the merry evening with JMH.

letters.title: From Fanny Myddelton Biddulph   14 January 1837
letters.summary: Apologises for delay in thanking him for the flowers. Has been too unwell to write.

letters.title: From Emily Catherine Darwin   15 [January 1837]
letters.summary:
Morning Heraldhad an account of CD’s 80 specimens of Mammalia and 450 birds at the Zoological Society.

John Gould has described new species in CD’s Galapagos birds.

Much interest in CD’s "Laurels".

Family news.

letters.title: To a member of Downing College, Cambridge   [19 January 1837]
letters.summary: Declines invitation to dine at Downing College because of influenza.

letters.title: From Charles Lyell   13 February 1837
letters.summary: "I could think of nothing for days after your lesson on coral reefs, but of the top of submerged continents. It is all true, but do not flatter youself that you will be believed, till you are growing bald, like me, with hard work & vexation at the incredulity in the world."

letters.title: From Catherine and Caroline Sarah Darwin   [16 February 1837]
letters.summary:
News of family and friends.

Caroline repeats story told to R. W. Darwin of FitzRoy’s feeling of obligation to Captain John White, from whom he gained release to marry Miss O’Brien.

Fanny Biddulph has had a son.

letters.title: From Caroline Darwin   [21 February 1837]
letters.summary:
Interested in Lyell’s address [Proc. Geol. Soc. Lond.2 (1833–8): 479–523]. Asks what the points are on which CD and Lyell are fully agreed.

Inquires about the paper FitzRoy and CD wrote on missionaries ["Moral state of Tahiti" (1836),Collected papers1: 19–38].

News of family.

letters.title: To Caroline Darwin  27 February 1837
letters.summary:
Has just given a paper [on "Sand tubes"] at Cambridge Philosophical Society and exhibited some specimens. It went well, with Whewell and Sedgwick taking an active part.

Herschel thinks 6000–odd years since the creation not nearly long enough to explain the separations from a single stock.

letters.title: To William Whewell   [10 March 1837]
letters.summary: CD seeks to decline the Secretaryship [of the Geological Society] by citing his obligation to FitzRoy to write his volume of the narrative of their expedition. His youth, inexperience, and ignorance of English geology.

letters.title: To William Darwin Fox   [12 March 1837]
letters.summary:
Finished going over his geological specimens at Cambridge, and is now in London.

Describes his plans for writing the journal, and later the geology and zoology of theBeaglevoyage.

letters.title: To Charles Babbage  [14 March 1837 – 31 December 1838]
letters.summary: Would have had great pleasure in accepting CB’s invitation, "whether for beauty or for shells", but has another engagement.

letters.title: From the Misses Horner  [17 March 1837 – 28 December 1838]
letters.summary: "The Botanists" and "The learned Linguists" give thanks for book and assistance.

letters.title: To the Geological Society of London   27 March 1837
letters.summary: Recommends David Williams’ paper on raised beaches of Devon [David Williams, "Letter … on the raised beaches of Barnstaple",Trans. Geol. Soc. Lond.2d ser. 5 (1840): 287–8] be shortened and published immediately after Sedgwick’s and Murchison’s paper ["Description of a raised beach in Barnstaple",ibid., pp. 279–86] as chief point of paper is to support their conclusions.

letters.title: To John Stevens Henslow   28 March [1837]
letters.summary:
Publication plans for the account of theBeagleexpedition – CD to have the third volume for his journal.

News of naturalists and their interest in his specimens. Queries about plant specimens, including one on whether seeds from Keeling Island would endure salt water.

letters.title: To Leonard Jenyns  10 April [1837]
letters.summary: Discusses possibility of publishing the zoology of the voyage of theBeagle. Will need help from more able naturalists. Would LJ object to describing the fishes for such a work rather than for scientific journals? Is working on hisBeaglejournal.

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   18 [May 1837]
letters.summary:
Plans to apply to Government for assistance with publishingZoology.

Robert Brown has taken an interest in the fossil woods.

CD is at work on his journal. Has not begun his geologyyet. Has seen much of Lyell.

letters.title: To Caroline Darwin  [19 May – 16 June 1837]
letters.summary:
Sends a number of questions (to put to his father), mainly concerned with transmission of diseases, between Europeans and natives, "people packed together", etc.

Is investigating how to get Government support [forZoology].

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow  [28 May 1837]
letters.summary:
CD to read paper on formation of coral islands at Geological Society. Lyell seems prepared to give up [his view].

Publication of theNarrativeis now definite. Feels he should have published journal after the geology and zoology of the voyage.

Robert Brown, as well as JSH, is interested in edible fungi from Tierra del Fuego.

letters.title: To John Lort Stokes   [after 31 May 1837]
letters.summary: Asks JLS: "Are there masses of coral or beds of shells some yards above high water mark, on the coast fronting the barrier reef?" [In reference to JLS’s proposed exploration of Australian coasts and rivers.]

letters.title: To Charles Babbage  [June–September 1837]
letters.summary: At Lyell’s request sends his copy of Whewell’sHistory of inductive sciences[1837] to CB.

letters.title: To William Buckland  [15 June 1837]
letters.summary: Describes the two species of lizard [Amblyrhynchus] found in the Galapagos Archipelago.

letters.title: To Francis Beaufort  16 June 1837
letters.summary: CD wants to request the assistance of Government to support the expense of the numerous engravings necessary for the publication of the results of the extensive collections in various departments of Natural History during theBeaglevoyage. To what quarter should he apply?

letters.title: To William Whewell   18 June [1837]
letters.summary:
Asks Whewell questions on earthquake wave action.

Thanks him for signature [to CD’s request to Chancellor of the Exchequer for funds forZoology].

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   [20 June 1837]
letters.summary: Upon the advice of Captain Beaufort and with embarrassment to himself CD asks JSH whether he would be perfectly willing personally to take the letter requesting government assistance directly to Thomas Spring Rice [Chancellor of the Exchequer].

letters.title: To Frederick William Hope   [21 June 1837]
letters.summary: Discusses insect specimens he left with FWH. Asks if he may state on FWH’s authority that a third or a half of the specimens from Sydney and Hobart Town are undescribed – a striking fact, showing imperfect knowledge of the insects in the close neighbourhood of the two Australian capitals.

letters.title: From Charles Cardale Babington   1 July 1837
letters.summary: Reports on the insect specimens [collected by CD] from Australia, New Zealand, and Tierra del Fuego. Has not completed descriptions.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   7 July [1837]
letters.summary:
Has finished theJournal; is readying it for the press.

Adds family news including Caroline’s forthcoming marriage to Josiah Wedgwood III.

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow  [12 or 13 July 1837]
letters.summary:
Has been "cramming up learning to ornament my journal with".

Sends a list of questions on his botanical specimens. Needs answers forJournal of researches, which he expects to go to press in August.

letters.title: To John Richardson   [24 July 1837]
letters.summary:
Questions about woods in cold, northern climates; about JR’s reference to frozen sandstone; about how far out from the shore the sea may become frozen.

His petition for assistance from the government isin statu quo; he is working at hisJournal[of researches].

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   30 July 1837
letters.summary:
Galapagos land birds and reptiles.

No two naturalists agree on any fundamental idea [of species]. "Everything is arbitrary."

Has been with Richard Owen going over the S. American fossils.

Has worked out thenon-relation between animals’ bulk and luxuriance of vegetation.

The horse once common on the Pampas. The mystery of the extinction of these animals.

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   [1 August 1837]
letters.summary: Botanical queries forJournal of researches, which is about to go to press.

letters.title: To William Shoberl  2 August [1837]
letters.summary:
Asks WS to write to his friend to make his corrections [in CD’s MS ofJournal of researches] in ink.

Capt. FitzRoy agrees with the propriety of beginning to print [CD’s volume separately] at once.

letters.title: To William Lonsdale   3 August [1837]
letters.summary: Asks to withdraw abstract of his paper on coral formations ["Elevation and subsidence in the Pacific" (1838),Collected papers1: 46–9].

letters.title: To the Chancellor of the Exchequer, Thomas Spring Rice  3 August 1837
letters.summary: With the encouragement of several scientific gentlemen and supported by the opinions of the Presidents of the three Learned Societies, CD ventures to request a grant of £1000 from Government to cover the cost of 150 engravings to illustrate results of hisBeaglecollections.

letters.title: From Richard Owen   [7 August 1837]
letters.summary: Dissected beak ofRhynchopsshows no extensive innervation. But beak may nevertheless be a sensitive organ of touch as CD suggests.

letters.title: To Anne Susan Horner  [9 August 1837]
letters.summary: Suggests coming to visit on Monday. Sends the Misses Horner a segment of wedding cake from Shrewsbury [marriage of Caroline Darwin to Josiah Wedgwood III].

letters.title: To John Richardson   [11 August 1837]
letters.summary:
Chancellor of the Exchequer has ordered £1000 for the publication of theZoology. Would like to meet JR to ask his advice on one or two points.

Thanks for his long account of the climate of North America.

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   16 August [1837]
letters.summary: Reports his successful interview with the Chancellor of the Exchequer [Thomas Spring Rice] about a grant for publishing [Zoology]. Thanks JSH for help with this; "you have been the making of me from the first".

letters.title: Minutes of the Board of the Treasury  25 August 1837
letters.summary: The Chancellor of the Exchequer and their Lordships after receiving numerous representations in support of Mr Darwin’s proposal concur in the opinion that Public Funds in aid of the Expenses should be granted as soon as he is ready to proceed in conformity with the enumerated conditions.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   28 August [1837]
letters.summary: Proof-sheets [ofJournal of researches] are tumbling in. Mentions future plans forZoologyand geological works. Has £1000 from Government for illustrations.

letters.title: To Sarah Elizabeth (Elizabeth) Wedgwood  [28 August 1837]
letters.summary: Regrets he cannot come to music meeting in Birmingham because he is very busy with the proofs of his book [Journal of researches]. A waste of life to spend a summer in ugly Marlborough Street.

letters.title: From Charles Lyell  29 August and 5 September 1837
letters.summary:
Syenitic granite from Norway carried as far as Osnabruck.

Has met warm reception in Germany.

Leopold von Buch mistaken in believing that granite overlies transition rock in Norway. Granite sends veins into transition and gneiss.

Has been examining fossil shells of Crag with Heinrich Beck. Beck admits some shells are of species still living.

CL still believes Eocene, Miocene, and Pliocene are satisfactory divisions of Tertiary epoch.

letters.title: From the Lords Commissioners of Her Majesty’s Treasury   31 August 1837
letters.summary: The Lords Commissioners of Her Majesty’s Treasury approve CD’s request for £1000 in aid of publication [ofZoology].

letters.title: From Smith, Elder & Co.  12 September 1837
letters.summary: Suggestions are presented respecting CD’s proposed publication of his zoological work in accordance with the Government requirement.

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   [20 September 1837]
letters.summary: Doctors have urged him to knock off all work and go to the country. Arranges proof-reading with JSH, while he is at Shrewsbury.

letters.title: To Alexander Young Spearman   20 September 1837
letters.summary: Encloses a statement [see377a] from Smith, Elder & Co., which appears to provide the best plan for the expenditure of the grant. Asks that it be presented for their Lordships’ consideration. Also encloses a prospectus.

letters.title: To William Shoberl  [22 or 23 September 1837]
letters.summary: Thanks WS for a document [see379]. Promises to send MS and woodcuts before night. Discusses details of printing and correction. Thanks WS and Henry Colburn for assistance.

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   [23 September 1837]
letters.summary: Proof-reading arrangements forJournal of researches. CD’s difficulty in writing correctly.

letters.title: From The Lords Commissioners of the Treasury  [Francis Thornhill Baring] 11 October 1837
letters.deprecated: TreasuryLords CommissionersFrancis Thornhill Baring, Lord Northbrook
letters.sender: TreasuryLords CommissionersFrancis Thornhill Baring, Lord Northbrook
letters.summary: Their Lordships communicate their entire approval of the proposal in CD’s letter of 20 September 1837. [See378a.]

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   14 October [1837]
letters.summary: CD’s reasons for his reluctance to take the Secretaryship of the Geological Society.

letters.title: To the Geological Society of London   20 October 1837
letters.summary: Report on J. G. Forchhammer’s communications on changes of levels of land in Denmark [Proc. Geol. Soc. Lond.2 (1838): 554–6].

letters.title: To William Lonsdale  [November 1837]
letters.summary: Sends an abstract made by J. F. Royle of CD’s paper ["On certain areas of elevation and subsidence in the Pacific and Indian Oceans"]. G. B. Greenough will have problems with the altered references in the coral island section.

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   [4 November 1837]
letters.summary: CD’s work [onZoology] is going smoothly. Marvels at finding himself an author [ofJournal of researches]. Part so far printed has a good many errata.

letters.title: From J. S. Henslow  [5 November 1837 – March 1838]
letters.summary: Fragment glued to CD’s notes on rock specimens. The recto refers to one of CD’s specimens, the verso mentions his Keeling Island plants.

letters.title: From Elizabeth Wedgwood   10 November [1837]
letters.summary:
Sends information about, and dates of treatment of peaty fields. Marl seems to have sunk to the natural stratum of hard white sand which lies below the peat.

Thanks for "Maer Hypothesis" ["Formation of mould" (1840),Collected papers1: 49–53].

letters.title: From Robert FitzRoy   15 November 1837
letters.summary: RF declines to give an opinion on the wording of the preface to CD’s volume [Journal and remarks, vol. 3 ofNarrative, published separately asJournal of researches] and refers him to a disinterested third party.

letters.title: From Robert FitzRoy   16 November 1837
letters.summary: CD’s response [missing] comes from the heart. RF explains that CD’s preface [toJournal and remarks, vol. 3 ofNarrative] offended him in not acknowledging the part RF and the other officers had in helping CD.Beaglevoyage was the first on which officers could have kept any specimens they collected, but they gave preference to CD.

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   [19 November 1837]
letters.summary: Asks JSH to look over the prospectus [forZoology]. Has one more chapter ofJournal of researchesto finish.

letters.title: From Susan Elizabeth Darwin  [early December 1837?]
letters.summary:
Father says he sowed broom plants soon after house was built in 1798; these never came up. In 1835 the terrace was made; thereafter the broom sprang up.

Advice on a medicine CD is taking.

letters.title: To Richard Owen   [c.December 1837]
letters.summary: Sends remaining proofs of RO’s description ofToxodon[Fossil Mammalia] and a revise of first part. Will Owen want a second revise? CD has made "plenty of remarks".

letters.title: To Leonard Jenyns   3 December [1837]
letters.summary:
CD is glad LJ is describing the fishes [forZoology]; would not have permitted J. E. Gray to describe them. New species will be lithographed.

Suggests books; offers coloured drawings made by artist onBeaglevoyage.

letters.title: To Leonard Jenyns   [4 December 1837]
letters.summary: Is sorry the fish [forZoology] give LJ so much trouble. Urges him not to give up. Describes publication plan ofZoology.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   [11 December 1837]
letters.summary:
Writes following his visit to WDF.

Mentions fossils Fox has collected.

News of Albert Way.

Hensleigh Wedgwood has resigned his post because of scruples about taking oaths.

letters.title: To Richard Owen   [15 December 1837 – 9 June 1838]
letters.summary: Sends RO a box of fossils from William Darwin Fox, from the Isle of Wight.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [19 December 1837]
letters.summary: Responds to Lyell’s query [missing] about northern and southern limits of coral islands of the Pacific. Warns that coral islands are much more thinly distributed than people realise and cites examples. Comments on views of Matthew Flinders. Reading work of É[lie] de B[eaumont]. Notes difficulty of setting an east-west boundary to coral islands.

letters.title: To Richard Owen   28 [December 1837]
letters.summary: Sends perfect revise of "Toxodon" [Fossil Mammalia] which he has read and marked.

letters.title: To Richard Owen   [28 December 1837]
letters.summary: CD sorry RO is not well and fears work onMacraucheniamay have contributed. Thinks new name very good. Other details concerning publication [ofZoology, pt 1, no. 1].

letters.title: To Charles Babbage  [1838]
letters.summary: CD is much obliged for invitations to CB’s parties, but is afraid to accept because he would meet people to whom he has sworn he never goes out.

letters.title: To Thomas Livingstone Mitchell  [1838]
letters.summary: Sends suggestions for points that would interest geologists in a description of valleys in the Blue Mountains [New South Wales].

letters.title: To Richard Owen    [January 1838]
letters.summary: Would like to call upon RO to discuss the last engravings sent by George Scharf. CD assumes that the revise ofToxodon[see395] was received.

letters.title: To Charles Babbage  [21 January 1838]
letters.summary: Asks Babbage to take small parcel to Henslow.

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   [21 January 1838]
letters.summary:
Sends rock specimen for W. H. Miller. Asks JSH to see whether there is any geology in P. B. Webb and Sabin Berthelot,Histoire naturelle des Îles Canaries[1835–50]. Finds his work on geology growing so large that it will take more than one volume and asks whether this will make publication aid more difficult.

Has accepted Secretaryship of the Geological Society.

Will not come to Cambridge because "as long as I continue well I cannot bear to leave my work for half a day".

letters.title: To John Gould  [February 1838]
letters.summary: The publishers [ofZoology] have agreed to 50 plates [forBirds]. Asks JG to decide which are most worthy of being done. Also asks him to see whether Bayfield will undertake [to colour] the birds (and quadrupeds) at something under 5d each.

letters.title: Questions for Mr Wynne  [February–July 1838]
letters.summary: Questions on breeding and habits.

letters.title: To A. Y. Spearman   16 February 1838
letters.summary: Encloses the account of Smith, Elder & Co. for the first part of "The Zoology of the Voyage of H.M.S. Beagle" [Fossil Mammalia].

letters.title: From John George Children    21 February 1838
letters.summary: In view of the charges directed by Edward Blyth against George R. Gray for gross incivility and discourtesy in discharging his duties as assistant in the zoological department at the British Museum, CD is asked by the Trustees to comment upon his own experience with Gray and to offer his judgment of these charges.

letters.title: To John George Children   22 February [1838]
letters.summary: Testifies to the courtesy and helpfulness of George Gray [assistant at the British Museum]. [See402b.]

letters.title: From A. Y. Spearman   23 February 1838
letters.summary: Payment of the Smith, Elder & Co. account has been ordered, amounting to the sum of £68.10.10 for the first part of theZoology.

letters.title: From Robert FitzRoy   26 February 1838
letters.summary:
His work [on vol. 2 ofNarrative] is going slowly.

Has no objection to anything in CD’s excellent volume. CD should "entertain no further scruple on that subject".

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow  [26 March 1838]
letters.summary:
Declines Ray Club dinner; too busy withZoology.

Thanks JSH for presenting his work to Cambridge Philosophical Society.

Asks him to get an answer from W. H. Miller on specimen of crystallised mineral.

letters.title: To Susan Darwin  [1 April 1838]
letters.summary:
FitzRoy is hard at work on his book [Narrative, vol. 2].

CD’s health is improved.

Describes his visit to zoo.

Gives news of E. A. Darwin and Harriet Martineau.

letters.title: From Leonard Horner  7 April [1838]
letters.summary: Postpones meeting with CD because he must attend House of Commons for Factory Amendment Act.

letters.title: Notes on marriage [after 7 Apr 1838]
letters.summary: Published as an appendix to vol. 2 of theCorrespondence; seehttp://www.darwinproject.ac.uk/darwins-notes-on-marriage. Considers his options for the future. Debates marriage and the best place to live. Feels the need for experiment and direct observation which would be difficult living in London; he "could not go on as Lyell does correcting & adding up new information to old train".

letters.title: To John Gould   [13 April 1838]
letters.summary:
Gives best wishes for Gould’s trip to Australia.

Notes on Synallaxis behaviour.

letters.title: From John Gould  [13 April] 1838
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his present of a dram bottle [actually a silver-cased compass]. JG will be reminded daily of their friendship when he is in the wilds [of Australia].

letters.title: To Susan Darwin  [26 April 1838]
letters.summary: Thanks for ham and corrections in spelling. Gives account of his social activities in past week.

letters.title: To Caroline Wedgwood  [May 1838]
letters.summary: His books grow in size. Hopes to bring out work on volcanic islands and coral formations in the autumn or winter. TheJournal of researcheswill not be published until autumn [actually not until 1839]. Whewell and Lyell flatter him about it. Has given up all society.

letters.title: To C. T. Whitley    [8 May 1838]
letters.summary:
Treasures recollections of old friends but seldom sees any. Has turned "a complete scribbler".

His scientific activities.

No wife in sight so far.

letters.title: To Susan Darwin  [15 May 1838]
letters.summary: Recounts dinner at Erasmus’ house with Harriet Martineau and others, and a visit to Cambridge to stay with Henslow and meet old friends again.

letters.title: To William Lonsdale  [15 May 1838]
letters.summary: Returns his paper for publication ["Volcanic phenomena in South America" (1840),Collected papers1: 53–86].

letters.title: To John Forbes Royle  [24 May 1838]
letters.summary:
Would like to attend a lecture by JFR on "geography of plants with relation to the Himalayas".

"A grand battle" at the Geological Society between Sedgwick and G. B. Greenough.

letters.title: To Charles Wood  24 May 1838
letters.deprecated: Charles Wood, Lord Halifax, 1st Viscount Halifax
letters.recipient: Charles Wood, Lord Halifax, 1st Viscount Halifax
letters.summary: Asks for permission to have a copy of the published Admiralty chart of the Island of Ascension. The engraved chart will add value to the geological observations to be published in the natural history of the voyage of H.M.S.Beagle.

letters.title: From Francis Beaufort  26 May [1838]
letters.summary: Has been commanded to supply CD with a copy of the plan of Ascension Island to be engraved for the natural history of theBeagle’s voyage. Suggests that a lithographer be sent to the [Hydrographic] office to take a transfer proof.

letters.title: To William Lonsdale  [c.June 1838]
letters.summary: Responds to report of the referee [on his paper "The formation of mould"]. Strikes out a paragraph and wants to add a note. Asks WL’s advice about a sentence.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox  [15 June 1838]
letters.summary:
Has not been well.

Plans a geological trip to Glen Roy in Scotland.

Thanks WDF for remembering the crossing of animals, CD’s "prime hobby". "I really think some day I shall be able to do something on that most intricate subject species and varieties."

letters.title: Notes on marriage [July 1838]
letters.summary: Debates with himself the pros and cons of marriage. Considers plans for future.

letters.title: From Francis Walker  6 July [1838]
letters.summary: Thanks CD for suggestions for improving his descriptions of species by indicating localities. With few exceptions theChalciditesof South America and Australia are remarkably like European species.

letters.title: To Thomas Spring Rice   [before 7 July 1838]
letters.sender: Charles Robert DarwinWilliam BucklandAdam SedgwickJohn PhillipsWilliam WhewellRoderick Impey Murchison, 1st baronetCharles Lyell, 1st baronetCharles StokesWilliam John HamiltonEdward StanleyRichard OwenWilliam CliftCharles BabbageJohn BostockPeter Mark RogetJohn TaylorSpencer Joshua Alwyne Compton, 2d Marquess of NorthamptonWilliam John Broderip
letters.summary: Express their concern that the offer for sale to the British Museum, by G. A. Mantell and Thomas Hawkins, of two valuable collections, has been declined.

letters.title: From Jean Pierre Sylvestre de Grateloup  18 July 1838
letters.summary: Sends to CD, as Secretary of the Geological Society, his work on fossil shells ["Mémoire sur les coquilles fossiles",Actes de la Société Linnéenne de Bordeaux10 (1838): 92–152].

letters.title: To William John Broderip  [August–December 1838]
letters.summary: Would like to arrange a meeting about CD’s collection of shells [from theBeaglevoyage].

letters.title: To George Robert Waterhouse  [August 1838–40]
letters.summary: Determined to make GRW a geologist. Sends copy of C. Lyell [?Elements of geology(1838)].

letters.title: To Emma Wedgwood  [7 August 1838]
letters.summary: His [first] railway journey was disappointing.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell  9 August [1838]
letters.summary:
Comments on receiving copy of Lyell’sElements[of geology]. Much is new to CD, and he is copying out notes and references.

Criticises geological work of John Phillips.

Describes expedition to Glen Roy, about which he is writing a paper ["Parallel roads of Glen Roy" (1839),Collected papers1: 87–137].

Enjoys the Athenaeum Club.

Criticises entomological work of F. W. Hope.

Asks Lyell to obtain for him a copy of barometric readings made at Leith.

Asks him to ascertain altitude of several Scottish lochs.

Comments on FitzRoy’s character.

letters.title: To A. Y. Spearman  18 August 1838
letters.summary: Notification of submission of Smith, Elder & Co. accounts (enclosed) for first numbers of part II and part III of theZoology, which are now published.

letters.title: From Charles Lyell  6 and 8 September 1838
letters.summary:
Would like to talk over Salisbury Craigs with CD.

CL’s father enthusiastic overJournal of researches.

Comments on Élie de Beaumont’s theory of mountain elevation.

Asks about parallel lines of upheaval and depression in the Pacific.

Glad CD likes Athenaeum Club.

Comments on methods of work.

Invites CD to visit Kinnordy.

Defends BAAS: "in this country no importance is attached to any body of men who do not make occasional demonstrations of their strength in public meetings".

With respect to Glen Roy, notes existence of deposits destitute of shells.

letters.title: To the Geological Society of London  7 September 1838
letters.summary: Report on R. A. C. Austen’s paper on the origin of limestone in Devonshire [Proc. Geol. Soc. Lond.2 (1838): 669–70]. CD deems it not worthy of publication inTransactions.

letters.title: To [unidentified]  12 September [1838]
letters.summary: Seeks permission to make another visit to Addiscombe [Military College] to see again the model of St Helena. He needs to correct proportion of some geological sections in hisGeology[seeVolcanic islands, ch. 4].

letters.title: To Charles Lyell  [14] September [1838]
letters.summary:
Comments on an article inEdinburgh Review[by David Brewster, 67 (1838): 271–308] on Comte’sPhilosophie positive.

Discusses falsity of Élie de Beaumont’s views of contemporaneous parallel lines of elevation and subsidence.

Owen’s views of relationship of reptiles to birds.

On "question of species" CD has filled notebook after notebook with facts, "which begin to group themselvesclearlyunder sub-laws".

letters.title: To A. Y. Spearman  22 September 1838
letters.summary: Submits the account of Smith, Elder & Co. for the second number of the second part of theZoology.

letters.title: From Bartholomew James Sulivan  20 October 1838
letters.summary: Reports arrival at Falklands; weather conditions, and unsuccessful search he made for a geological formation CD had seen. Describes cliffs, streams, rocks, and lines of elevation; includes two drawings.

letters.title: From W. D. Fox  [c. November 1838]
letters.summary: Reports on the effects of inbreeding in dogs and the results of crossing Canada and common geese.

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan  [November 1838 – April 1839]
letters.summary: Observations on the geology of the Falkland Islands.

letters.title: To John Frederick William Herschel  2 [November 1838]
letters.summary: Requests information for W. S. Macleay on JFWH’s method of catching pelagic animals while ship is under way.

letters.title: To John Stevens Henslow   3 November 1838
letters.summary: Relates plan for an appendix to hisJournal of researcheswhich will include facts of species of birds’ being different in different islands of the Galápagos and also of the lizards and tortoises on the islands. Asks JSH whether he can supply parallels in the plant life.

letters.title: From Caroline Wedgwood  [11 November 1838]
letters.summary: Expresses her pleasure at CD’s engagement.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell  [12 November 1838]
letters.summary: Announces his engagement to Emma Wedgwood.

letters.title: From Erasmus Alvey Darwin  [14 November 1838]
letters.summary: Sends congratulations on CD’s engagement. "It is a marriage which will give almost as much pleasure to the rest of the world as it does to yourselves."

letters.title: From Charlotte Langton  14 November [1838]
letters.summary: Expresses her pleasure and satisfaction in CD’s forthcoming marriage.

letters.title: To Emma Wedgwood  [14 November 1838]
letters.summary: In his first letter after their engagement, CD reports on the happy reception of the news by his family. He hopes she will not find life with him solitary and dull after the lively social life of Maer.

letters.title: From Emma Wedgwood   [21–2 November 1838]
letters.summary: Writes lovingly of small events since he left Maer. Fears their opinions may differ on "the most important subject", religion, but is grateful for his openness about his "honest & conscientious doubts".

letters.title: From William Owen Sr   21 November 1838
letters.summary: Expresses his pride and pleasure in CD’s friendship and wishes him well on hearing of his forthcoming marriage.

letters.title: To Emma Wedgwood  [21 November 1838]
letters.summary: Recounts his misadventures on the train journey back to London. Tells of a visit to the FitzRoys and a friendly letter from Lyell. Whether CD and Emma should live in central London or in the suburbs is a perplexing problem, much discussed by relatives and friends.

letters.title: From Harriet Henslow   22 November [1838]
letters.summary: Sends congratulations and expresses her pleasure on hearing of CD’s forthcoming marriage.

letters.title: To Charles Thomas Whitley   23 November [1838]
letters.summary:
Announces his engagement.

Glad CW wondered at Glen Roy. "I saw nothing in my peregrinations to the Antipodes nearly so curious in physical geography."

letters.title: From Emma Wedgwood   [25–6 November 1838]
letters.summary: Responds to items in CD’s letter, just received. Suggests parts of London where he might look for a house. Gives news of friends and relatives.

letters.title: To Emma Wedgwood   [27 November 1838]
letters.summary: CD and Erasmus continue to search for a house in central London. They have tea with the Carlyles.

letters.title: From Sarah Harriet Hosier Williams   [27 November 1838]
letters.summary: Invites CD to dine with them on Wednesday, since she will have few more opportunities of seeing "the original old Charles Darwin".

letters.title: From Emma Wedgwood   [30 November 1838]
letters.summary: Has accepted the Hensleigh Wedgwoods’ invitation to go to London with them; can look at houses with CD. She wishes to avoid extravagance; asks him to choose three or four for her to see.

letters.title: To Emma Wedgwood  [30 November – 1 December 1838]
letters.summary: His search for a London house. He visits the Lyells, who give solemn advice to choose their London acquaintances carefully.

letters.title: From William Yarrell  [December 1838]
letters.summary: A "Zoological memorandum" for CD with an extract from L. Hindmarsh, "On the wild cattle of Chillingham Park" [Ann. & Mag. Nat. Hist.2 (1838): 274–84].

letters.title: From Emma Wedgwood   [3 December 1838]
letters.summary: She agrees that London is the place to settle. She is eager to see him and full of plans.

letters.title: To George Robert Gray   [4 December 1838]
letters.summary: Sends GRG a few pages of proofs [ofBirds]. Asks him to make any observations that might occur to him and to check passages in French and Latin.

letters.title: From Charlotte Langton   4 December [1838]
letters.summary: Expresses her pleasure in his forthcoming marriage. "I don’t think anybody ever had so delightful a reception into a family as Emma."

letters.title: From Thomas Bell   [5 December 1838]
letters.summary:
Sends congratulations on CD’s forthcoming marriage.

Has received some of the reptiles back from G. Bibron, who has named them. TB will get "some subjects in readiness for figuring" by CD’s date.

letters.title: To G. R. Gray   [6 December 1838]
letters.summary: Sends proofs [ofBirds, no. 2]. Asks GRG to check Latin accents.

letters.title: To Joseph Beete Jukes   6 December 1838
letters.summary: The Geological Society cannot recommend anyone to the Government of Newfoundland, but CD advises JBJ to get a recommendation from Sedgwick.

letters.title: From Albert Way   9 December 1838
letters.summary:
Congratulations on CD’s engagement.

In answer to CD’s request, tells him how to locate an artist who made excellent sketches of Scotland, and probably of Glen Roy. AW himself made a sketch of the Glen which he offers to CD [Collected papers1: 88].

letters.title: From J. S. Henslow   16 December 1838
letters.summary: On his 15th wedding anniversary JSH writes to CD wishing him happiness as great as JSH has had in his marriage, and adds some advice.

letters.title: From William Yarrell  [c.17 December 1838]
letters.summary: Extract of a letter from Sir Robert Heron to WY, copied for CD, about the crossing of solid- and divided-hoofed pigs, and Angora rabbits of different colours.

letters.title: To the Secretary of the American Philosophical Society  20 December 1838
letters.summary: As Secretary of the Geological Society of London, formally expresses his thanks for initial numbers ofProceedings of the American Philosophical Society.

letters.title: To Adam Sedgwick   21 [December 1838]
letters.summary: CD informs AS of the position of the Council of the Geological Society on recommending J. B. Jukes for a geological survey of Newfoundland. Feels Jukes’s application would have best chance of success if Sedgwick, his Professor at Cambridge, wrote a letter.

letters.title: From Emma Wedgwood   [23 December 1838]
letters.summary: Describes the journey home and the long talks on their return. No maid has been found, so he should engage the one she saw, "for ten guineas & tea & sugar a year". She thought CD looked unwell and overtired.

letters.title: To J. B. Jukes   25 December [1838]
letters.summary: Advises JBJ on preparing himself for geological work in Newfoundland.

letters.title: From Emma Wedgwood   [26 December 1838]
letters.summary: Responds to his "business letter" about the maids, then chides herself for feeling dull and disagreeable when she has had everything all her life.

letters.title: To Emma Wedgwood   [29 December 1838]
letters.summary: The house at 12 Upper Gower Street is theirs.

letters.title: From Emma Wedgwood   [29 December 1838]
letters.summary: Is delighted to learn they have "Macaw Cottage" [12 Upper Gower Street] – their second choice; hopes they have disposed of the dead dog in the garden. Much family news.

letters.title: From Emma Wedgwood   [30 December 1838]
letters.summary: Seeks to persuade CD to leave town at once, go to Shrewsbury for doctoring and some rest, then come to Maer for more rest, for he has looked "so unwell". She knows it must be hard for him to be unable to do his work.

letters.title: To Emma Wedgwood  [31 December 1838 –] 1 January 1839
letters.summary:
Has moved into the Gower Street house. Is pleased with it and its location.

Hopes to be able to finish his Glen Roy paper soon.

letters.title: To Charles Babbage  [1839 – August 1842]
letters.summary: Is so unwell today that he is unable to come [to CB’s party].

letters.title: To John Maurice Herbert   [January 1839 – September 1842]
letters.summary:
Suggests the names of two bird-preservers for JMH’s friend.

In reference to an earlier letter, replies: "As for Birds of Paradise from the West Indies, tell that to the marines, as we used to say on board the Beagle".

letters.title: To Richard Owen  [1839 – April 1840]
letters.summary: Delighted by RO’s discussion in this sheet. RO should return revises to printer and get remaining ones.

letters.title: To Woodbine Parish  [January 1839?]
letters.summary: Likes WP’s book [Buenos Ayres and the province of La Plata(1838)]. Thinks it will interest all "who care for graver things than what the traveller eats and says to the Señoritas".

letters.title: To J. Shillinglaw  (Secretary, Royal Geographical Society) [1839 – May 1842]
letters.summary: Asks for volumes of F. W. Beechey’s work [Narrative of a voyage to the Pacific and Bering Strait (1831)] andNautical magazineand an order on [John] Arrowsmith for atlas of Dumont d’Urville’sVoyage in the "Astrolabe".

letters.title: To Charles Stokes  [1839 – September 1842]
letters.summary: Sends observations he made onFungiaduringBeaglevoyage. Asks CS to make corrections in style or names of parts as he sees fit.

letters.title: From G. R. Waterhouse  [1839 – 10 February 1840]
letters.summary: Sends John Blackwall’s book [Researches in zoology(1834)]. Discusses his reasons for doubting that there are any marsupials in Java or Sumatra.

letters.title: To ? [1839–82]
letters.summary: Is glad addressee’s lectures are going well.

letters.title: To Emma Wedgwood  2 [–3 January 1839]
letters.summary: His dinner with the Carlyles. "He is the best worth listening to of any man" – but CD cannot get up much admiration for Mrs C, partly because of her Scots accent, which makes her difficult to understand.

letters.title: From Emma Wedgwood   [3 January 1839]
letters.summary:
Emma is surprised how quickly CD has moved into the new house and understands his feeling of triumph. Wants him and Fanny [Mrs Hensleigh] Wedgwood to settle on hiring a cook.

Is readingMansfield Park[Jane Austen (1814)], which she finds "very suitable".

letters.title: To William Whewell   4 [January 1839]
letters.summary: Informs him of J. B. Jukes’s plans concerning the Newfoundland survey post.

letters.title: To Emma Wedgwood   [6–7 January 1839]
letters.summary:
Has been with the Lyells doing geology.

Is reading a biography of Sir W. Scott [J. G. Lockhart,Memoirs of the life of Sir Walter Scott(1837–8)]; also Mungo Park’s book [Travels(1799)].

Has hired a cook at fourteen guineas a year with tea and sugar.

letters.title: From Emma Wedgwood   [7 January 1839]
letters.summary:
Still rejoices in having found the house they like.

Thinks he might enjoy Jenny [Jane Welsh] Carlyle’s company more away from Carlyle "as she must have her full swing in talking".

Says the wedding must be fixed for the 29th instead of the 24th.

Hopes he will look better than on his last visit.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell  [c.9 January 1839]
letters.summary:
Discusses his Glen Roy paper [(1839),Collected papers1: 87–137], which he is sending to CL.

Remarks on Charles MacLaren’s treatment of alluvium. Comments on alluvial action in Lochaber.

letters.title: From Emma Wedgwood   [9 January 1839]
letters.summary:
Glad to have his letter; supposes she will receive only two or three more from him in her life.

Thinks he should leave the curtains for her.

Discusses Mungo Park and Sir Walter Scott’sLife.

letters.title: From J. M. Herbert   13 January [1839]
letters.summary: Sends congratulations on CD’s engagement, with a gift.

letters.title: To W. J. Broderip   19 January [1839]
letters.summary:
Hopes Richard Owen will have time to do CD’s shells in spirits.

Doubts WJB’s suggestion that moles may play a part in formation of mould.

letters.title: From Emma Wedgwood   [20–1 January 1839]
letters.summary: Preparations for the wedding, various callers, and other bits of news.

letters.title: To Emma Wedgwood   [20 January 1839]
letters.summary:
Comments on recent visit to Maer. Explains that his notion of happiness as quietness and solitude derives fromBeagleexperience. Hopes Emma will humanise him. Comments on marriage planned for Tuesday.

Describes recent visit by Lyell and his wife. Talked geology for half an hour "with poor Mrs Lyell sitting by". "I wantpracticein ill-treating the female sex."

letters.title: To Edwin C. Prince  21 January [1839]
letters.summary: Asks what generic and subgeneric name John Gould has given to the goatsuckers of the U. S. [forBirds].

letters.title: From Emma Wedgwood   [23 January 1839]
letters.summary:
Responds warmly to his very nice letter. CD need have no fear that she will not be as happy as he.

Again expresses uneasiness that their opinions on religion do not agree on all points. Hopes they will sympathise in theirfeelingson the subject.

letters.title: From Thomas Evans Blackwell   26 January 1839
letters.summary: A newly-elected Fellow returns the obligation to be signed upon entering the Geological Society.

letters.title: To Emma Wedgwood   [26 January 1839]
letters.summary: He has the wedding ring. Agrees to coming straight home after the wedding, if that is what she prefers.

letters.title: To Charles Babbage  [February 1839 – August 1842]
letters.summary: Asks permission to bring Fanny Allen to CB’s party.

letters.title: From Emma Darwin  [c.February 1839]
letters.summary: Discusses CD’s religious doubts. Fears his work may lead him to discount what cannot be proved, and advises that there are some things which, "if true are likely to be above our comprehension" and "that there is a danger in giving up revelation".

letters.title: To A. Y. Spearman   4 February 1839
letters.summary: Submits the account of Smith, Elder & Co. for the third number of part two and second number of part three of theZoology.

letters.title: From J. S. Henslow   7 February 1839
letters.summary: Writes to CD as "Brother Benedick" and sends hearty good wishes for health and happiness in marriage. They are sending a little silver candlestick for a wax taper.

letters.title: To William Whewell   16 February [1839]
letters.summary: Asks WW to alter, before printing, the passages in WW’s Presidential Address to the Geological Society [Proc. Geol. Soc. Lond.3 (1839): 93] which pointedly allude to the delay in publication of CD’sBeaglejournal; they might annoy FitzRoy, who, as Captain, has a right to first use of the papers of all officers on board.

letters.title: To Charles Babbage  19 [February 1839 – August 1842]
letters.summary: Asks to be allowed to bring his sister to CB’s party "that she may see theWorld".

letters.title: From Andrew Irvine   7 March 1839
letters.summary: Supports John Lawrance’s application to become a fellow of the Geological Society.

letters.title: To William Lonsdale   [8 March 1839]
letters.summary: Has finished earthquake paper ["Volcanic phenomena in South America" (1840),Collected papers1: 53–86]. Gives instructions about a woodcut. There should be an outline map.

letters.title: From Andrew Smith  16 March 1839
letters.summary: Sends his congratulations and best wishes on CD’s marriage.

letters.title: To John Phillips  [18 March 1839]
letters.summary: Will send JP a map as requested. Asks for a ticket to one of JP’s lectures.

letters.title: To the Librarian of the Royal Geographical Society   [19 March 1839]
letters.summary: Formal request for F. Lutké’s charts of the Caroline Islands and any charts by Beechey of the Lagoon Islands [Ellice Islands] that the Society might possess.

letters.title: From Robert FitzRoy   [20 March 1839]
letters.summary: Has objected to loadingNarrativewith advertisements, but thinks CD’sZoologyandGeologymight be advertised. Mentions other details of the final stages of publication.

letters.title: To William Shoberl  [21 March 1839]
letters.summary: Captain FitzRoy has no objection to appending advertisement of other works connected withBeaglevoyage to CD’s volume [Journal of researches].

letters.title: Questions for William Herbert  [c.1 April 1839]
letters.summary:
Questions on breeding of plants: variation in established versus new varieties; predominance of wild species and old varieties when crossed with newer forms; predominance of males versus females; correlations between ease of hybridisation and tendency to vary and undergo cultivation; reversion; correlations between hybridisation and geographic distribution.

In WH’sAmaryllidaceae[1837], does he intend to say crossing is inimical to fertility?

[Sent via J. S. Henslow; note to amanuensis Syms Covington.]

letters.title: From William Whewell   11 April 1839
letters.summary: Sends a book [his translation of Goethe’sHermann u. Dorothea] as a wedding gift.

letters.title: From J. S. Henslow  [c.14 April 1839]
letters.summary:
[Note forwarding503.]

Lord Fitzwilliam’s gardener does not believe in hybrid ferns.

letters.title: To William Whewell   16 April [1839]
letters.summary:
Thanks WW for wedding gift.

Expresses admiration for hisHistory of the inductive sciences[1837].

letters.title: To the Secretary of the Geological Society of France   25 April 1839
letters.summary: Acknowledges, on behalf of the Geological Society, receipt of theBulletin de la Société Géologique de France, vol. 9, feuilles 29, 34.

letters.title: From Caleb Burrell Rose   30 April 1839
letters.summary: Sends fee for admission to the Geological Society and a signed obligation.

letters.title: From Richard Sutton Ford   6 May 1839
letters.summary: Answers to [Questions about breeding].

letters.title: From George Tollet  [10 May 1839]
letters.summary: Replies to [Questions about breeding].

letters.title: To Gideon Algernon Mantell   23 May 1839
letters.summary: Writes, as Secretary of the Geological Society, to thank GAM for his presents, a slab of anthracite with plant impressions (from Philadelphia) and some fossils from Cornwall.

letters.title: To the Secretary of the American Philosophical Society  23 May 1839
letters.summary: As Secretary of the Geological Society of London, CD formally expresses thanks for the American Philosophical Society’sProceedings, vol. 1, no. 6.

letters.title: To Alphonse de Candolle   25 May [1839]
letters.summary: Invitation to dine at the Darwins’ with J. S. Henslow.

letters.title: To A. Y. Spearman   27 May 1839
letters.summary: Presents the account of Smith, Elder & Co. for the now published second and third numbers of the first part of theZoology.

letters.title: To William Sharp MacLeay   29 May 1839
letters.summary: Introduces Syms Covington and recommends him for employment in Australia.

letters.title: Letter of recommendation for Syms Covington  29 May 1839
letters.summary: A letter of reference for Syms Covington.

letters.title: To T. L. Mitchell   31 May [1839]
letters.summary:
CD’s servant [Syms Covington] will work his passage to Australia.

Returns a curious stone, of which he hopes to publish an account. [SeeVolcanic islands, p. 38.]

letters.title: To G. R. Gray  [June–October 1839]
letters.summary: Asks for someAnthusskins to examine [forBirds]. Fears they may turn out to be all one species. Sends details from his notes on Falkland Island specimens.

letters.title: From Robert FitzRoy  [2 or 16 June 1839]
letters.summary: Has not yet had time to read CD’sJournal of researchesattentively. He is sure there is no expression referring to himself personally that he could wish were not in it.

letters.title: To Mr Folthorp of Smith, Elder & Co.   6 June [1839]
letters.summary: CD has heard from the Treasury; they will pay the account [for theZoology] as soon as Smith, Elder & Co. like.

letters.title: From William Buckland   7 June 1839
letters.summary: Acknowledges receipt ofJournal of researches.

letters.title: From Richard Owen   11 June 1839
letters.summary: Thanks CD effusively [forJournal of researches] – "the most delightful book in my collection".

letters.title: From William Henry Fitton   13 June 1839
letters.summary: Thanks CD forJournal of researches. Praises its "want of pretension"; "the Geology seems … to be excellent – and a good part of it new".

letters.title: From William Lonsdale   15 June 1839
letters.summary: AcknowledgesJournal of researches.

letters.title: From Robert FitzRoy   20 June [1839]
letters.summary: Robert Brown has mistreated Capt. P. P. King by holding back for nine years the plants collected on King’s voyage of theAdventureandBeagle.

letters.title: To William Herbert  26 June 1839
letters.summary:
CD is led to believe there are no true permanently inbreeding, sexually reproducing beings. Thanks for replies to breeding questions.

Asks for clarification ofHippeastrumcrosses: is selfing or crossing with individual of same species intended and was increased fertility due to constitution of foreign parent or due to the pollen coming from another plant? Has WH known any hybrid or mongrel to revert or to vary in a manner unlikely to be effect of soil?

SendsJournal of researches.

letters.title: From William Herbert  [c.27 June 1839]
letters.summary:
Rejects necessity of outbreeding and any general law of reversion.

Describes further experiments withHippeastrumshowing greater fertility with foreign pollen than with individual’s own pollen or with pollen from another individual of same species.

Does not believe CD’s questions about reversion can be answered in present state of knowledge.

letters.title: To Thomas Green   [after 30 June 1839]
letters.summary: Returns proof sheets and requests revises. Gives his opinion of Mr Walkers’s work.

letters.title: From William Andrew Fane De Salis   8 July 1839
letters.summary: A newly-elected Fellow sends a signed obligation and subscription to CD as Secretary of the Geological Society of London.

letters.title: To A. Y. Spearman   13 July 1839
letters.summary: Transmits, as on former occasions, the Smith, Elder & Co. account for the now published third number of the third part of theZoology.

letters.title: From William Yarrell   14 July 1839
letters.summary: AcknowledgesJournal of researchesand in return sends the first volume of hisHistory of British birds[1839–43].

letters.title: To Leonard Jenyns   15 July [1839]
letters.summary:
Discusses details of LJ’s part ofZoology[Fish].

CD is working hard onCoral reefs.

letters.title: From John Grant Malcolmson   24 July 1839
letters.summary:
Detailed evidence for and against geological elevation along coast of the Indian subcontinent, South Asia, and Arabia. Extensive references to geological literature about these areas.

Describes coral sand-dune and salt-marsh formation.

letters.title: From Jean Baptiste Armand Louis Léonce Élie de Beaumont   31 July 1839
letters.summary: Acknowledges receipt of CD’s gift of theJournal of researches. Praises CD’s "ingenious" views.

letters.title: To William Henry Smyth   7 August [1839]
letters.summary: Asks for details of Smyth’s Island discovered by WHS – particularly whether the islets form a ring surrounding a lagoon. [SeeCoral reefs, p. 158].

letters.title: To William Shoberl  16 August [1839]
letters.summary: Gives his opinion of a MS on geology. It is not really a scientific work. It might sell well, but CD’s opinion on success of sale is worthless.

letters.title: From Carl Friedrich Alexander Hartmann  23 August 1839
letters.summary: Thanks CD for hisJournal of researches, "one of the best scientific travelworks of this time", which CFAH intends to translate into German.

letters.title: From J. G. Malcolmson   31 August 1839
letters.summary: Observations on the geology of Arabia.

letters.title: From Alexander von Humboldt   18 September 1839
letters.deprecated: Friedrich Wilhelm Heinrich Alexander (Alexander) von Humboldt
letters.sender: Friedrich Wilhelm Heinrich Alexander (Alexander) von Humboldt
letters.summary: Praises CD’sJournal of researchesand comments on some of CD’s observations and conclusions. Considers volcanic activity and its effect on past climate and changes in climate over time. Discusses glacial phenomena. Believes the climate of the coast of Peru is modified by cold sea-currents.

letters.title: To Charles Babbage  [October 1839 – August 1842]
letters.summary: Regrets he cannot accept invitation. "My health will not at present stand going out in the evenings."

letters.title: From J. G. Malcolmson   7 October 1839
letters.summary:
Sends notes on soundings made on coral banks in the China Sea.

His recent geological observations.

Finds a difficulty with CD’s erratic block theory.

letters.title: From J. G. Malcolmson   [after 7 October 1839]
letters.summary: Comments on the discussion of erratic blocks inJournal of researches[pp. 619, 621–2].

letters.title: To Leonard Jenyns   14 October [1839]
letters.summary: Informs LJ that Yarrell has recommended B. W. Hawkins to do the plates [forFish]. Discusses arrangements to be made, number of plates, etc. Answers LJ’s questions about several specimens.

letters.title: To A. Y. Spearman   14 October 1839
letters.summary: Presents the Smith, Elder & Co. account for the fourth number now published of the second part of theZoology.

letters.title: To John Washington   14 October [1839]
letters.summary: Returns proof-sheets of an article he has reviewed for theJournal of the Royal Geographical Society. He will find it useful when he comes to describe the Cordilleras of Chile.

letters.title: To John Washington   [14 October 1839]
letters.summary:
Returns proofs of J. O. French’s article ["Account of the province of La Rioja: S. America",J. R. Geogr. Soc.9 (1839): 381–406].

Gratified by Humboldt’s praise ofJournal of researches[J. R. Geogr. Soc.9 (1839): 502].

letters.title: To Leonard Jenyns   17 October [1839]
letters.summary: Discusses details of arrangements for descriptions and engravings [forFish].

letters.title: To Leonard Jenyns  [20 or 27 October 1839]
letters.summary: Details regardingFish. CD is astonished how many new things LJ has found: "four new genera is something".

letters.title: From Susan Darwin   [c.24 October 1839]
letters.summary: Gives some information on Darwin family history.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   24 October [1839]
letters.summary:
Hopes to publish volume on coral formations in a few months.

He and Emma live quietly, having given up parties.

Asks WDF if he remembers the Darwin family motto. He means to have a "seal solemnly engraved".

letters.title: To Caroline Wedgwood  [27 October 1839]
letters.summary:
Describes his routine for a typical day – writingCoral reefs, studying German.

FitzRoy’s "Deluge Chapter" [Narrative2, ch. 28] will amuse her.

His opinion of Carlyle’sCritical and miscellaneous essays[1839].

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow  [November 1839]
letters.summary:
Urges JSH to describe Galapagos species in a paper on the flora of the islands.

Has been interested in geographical distribution and would be interested to have a paper by JSH on the general character of flora of Tierra del Fuego and Patagonia.

"I keep on steadily collecting every sort of fact which may throw light on the origin & variation of species."

letters.title: To Alexander von Humboldt   1 November 1839
letters.deprecated: Friedrich Wilhelm Heinrich Alexander (Alexander) von Humboldt
letters.recipient: Friedrich Wilhelm Heinrich Alexander (Alexander) von Humboldt
letters.summary:
Gratified by AvH’s letter.

Sends data on temperature of the sea in the Galapagos, South Pacific, and the Abrolhos Islands.

letters.title: To John Washington   1 November [1839]
letters.summary: CD thinks report of a rock imbedded in an iceberg is remarkable; wants to write a note for the [Journal] about it. Asks for location of the sighting and a chart of the Antarctic Sea. [See "Rock seen on an iceberg",Collected papers1: 137–9.]

letters.title: To William Hallowes Miller   22 [November 1839]
letters.summary: Asks if WHM would be interested in the meteorological observations of the Falkland Islands made by B. J. Sulivan on a recent survey. Such observations are rare and appear to CD to have many points of interest.

letters.title: To A. Y. Spearman   27 November 1839
letters.summary: Encloses the Smith, Elder & Co. account for the fourth number now published of the third part of theZoology.

letters.title: To Thomas Campbell Eyton   [30 November 1839]
letters.summary: Sends bird specimens for examination by TCE [forBirds].

letters.title: From J. G. Malcolmson   30 November 1839
letters.summary:
Sends specimens of coralline with vermiform holes.

J. Allan’s observations of Aldabra and the Cormoros [seeCoral reefs, p. 186] and news of his experiments on the growth of coral.

letters.title: From [Mr Edwards?]   [before end of 1839?]
letters.summary: Reports on a setter puppy born of apparently pure pointer parents. Any cross must have been far back.

letters.title: To [W. A. Leighton] [1840–77?]
letters.summary: Valediction only of a letter stuck into a writing case.

letters.title: To William Walton  [1840–2]
letters.summary: Comments on the quality of the meat of the guanaco.

letters.title: To William Walton  [1840–2]
letters.summary: Describes the range of conditions under which the guanaco thrives and the ease with which it can be tamed.

letters.title: To John Edward Gray    1 January [1840]
letters.summary: Testimonial in behalf of JEG’s application for the position of keeper of the zoological department of the British Museum from which John George Children was about to resign.

letters.title: From J. G. Malcolmson   2 January 1840
letters.summary: Discusses CD’s Glen Roy paper; would like to see the theory put beyond dispute. Tells of Mr Stables’ observations on the parallel roads. Discusses geological features of Scotland which he is sure are marine in origin.

letters.title: To T. C. Eyton   [6 January 1840]
letters.summary:
Has been unwell.

Thanks TCE for his descriptions [of specimens forBirds]. Has already expended a high proportion of Government grant on birds, but if TCE thinks engravings are needed, he shall have them. He may keep the bones.

CD has become a father.

letters.title: To Basil Hall  [7 January 1840]
letters.summary: CD regrets inconvenience caused by his having Royal Geographical Society’s copy of Krusenstern’sAtlas[de l’océan Pacifique(1824–7)]. Locates Sulphur Island from it.

letters.title: To A. Y. Spearman   16 January 1840
letters.summary: Presents the Smith, Elder & Co. account for the first number of the fourth part (now published) of theZoology.

letters.title: To the Geological Society of London   22 January 1840
letters.summary: W. B. Clarke’s paper on ashes falling at sea off Cape Verde Islands [Proc. Geol. Soc. Lond.3 (1839): 145–6] need not be published inTransactions.

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   [24 January 1840]
letters.summary: Sends specimens from Indian Ocean atolls.

letters.title: To Mr Folthorp of Smith, Elder & Co.  [6 February 1840]
letters.summary: Sends MS [ofCoral reefs?] to be copied.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [19 February 1840]
letters.summary:
Remarks on his illness and treatment.

Discusses MS [ofCoral reefs] and changes in his view of coral reefs sinceJournal of researches. Mentions C. G. Ehrenberg’s observations on coral reefs.

letters.title: To Robert FitzRoy   [20 February 1840]
letters.summary:
Poor health has made him give up all geological work.

Profits on their volumes [ofNarrative] seem absurdly small.

Looks back onBeaglevoyage as the most fortunate circumstance in his life.

Finds marriage a great happiness.

letters.title: To Richard Owen   24 [February 1840]
letters.summary: Asks RO whether he has any MS [ofFossil Mammalia, no. 4] ready and to see that the plates are finished.

letters.title: To William C. Redfield   24 February [1840]
letters.summary:
Much interested in WCR’s paper on "Whirlwinds excited by fire" [Am. J. Sci.36 (1839): 50–9;Edinburgh New Philos. J.27 (1839): 369–79].

Sends a summary account of circular clouds and waterspouts formed during volcanic eruption in the Azores [S. Tillard, "Eruption of a volcano in sea off St Michael",Philos. Trans. R. Soc. Lond.(1812): 152–8].

letters.title: To Benjamin Silliman 26 February 1840
letters.summary: Asks that a letter on tornados be forwarded to W. C. Redfield. Hopes Silliman received a copy ofJournal of Researches.

letters.title: To Leonard Jenyns   [27 February 1840]
letters.summary: Has been unwell. Publication of two numbers [ofZoology] has been delayed. Thought firstFishnumber good.

letters.title: To Richard Owen   [March? 1840]
letters.summary: Sends a proof title page and asks RO to send a list of plates and contents [ofFossil mammalia] to the printer, Mr Stewart.

letters.title: To Basil Hall   15 March 1840
letters.summary: Discussion of the geology of Coquimbo, Chile.

letters.title: To David Milne   [19 March 1840]
letters.summary: About earthquakes: the shock of February 1835 in Chile; possible connection between shocks occurring coincidentally in different parts of the world, and between earthquakes and the weather; DM’s collection of accounts of earthquakes in Scotland.

letters.title: To the President and Council of the Geological Society of London  24 March 1840
letters.summary: Regrets that state of his health forces him to resign as one of the Secretaries of the Society.

letters.title: To the Geological Society of London  28 March [1840]
letters.summary: Feels he has no choice but to comply with the request of Council that he remain in office. Is reluctant to do so as his health has caused him to miss meetings and he has never once attended without suffering the next day. Cannot hold office beyond next anniversary meeting.

letters.title: From David Milne   28 March 1840
letters.summary: Comments on CD’s paper on South American volcanoes [Trans. of the Geol. Soc. of London, 2d ser., pt 3, 5 (1840): 601–31]. Jets of steam or flame issuing from the side of a hill in Glen Almond.

letters.title: To Leonard Jenyns   5 April [1840]
letters.summary:
Health is improved, but would do anything to get strong again. Is consulting his father; will return to London soon to see B. W. Hawkins.

Will send MS [ofFish, no. 2] to the printer, and be there when LJ comes.

letters.title: To Emma Darwin   [5 April 1840]
letters.summary: An amusing description of his railway journey to Shrewsbury.

letters.title: From Benjamin Silliman   7 April 1840
letters.summary: Thanks CD for a copy of hisJournal of researcheswhich is "not second in interest and instruction to any work of the kind I have ever read".

letters.title: To Thomas Walker   5 May [1840]
letters.summary: Acknowledges TW’s letter supplying him with William Kemp’s address.

letters.title: From W. C. Redfield   6 May 1840
letters.summary: Thanks CD for information about Captain Tillard’s account of the volcanic eruption in the Azores in 1811.

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   12 May 1840
letters.summary: Gives CD the results of some calculations for "dip" over different distances, as requested.

letters.title: To Society for the Encouragement of Arts, Manufactures, and Commerce  13 May [1840–2]
letters.summary:
Informs correspondent that he wrote to William Walton all that he knew about the guanaco.

Present state of his health prevents his acceptance of invitation to attend the meeting of the Society.

letters.title: To John Washington, Secretary, Royal Geographical Society   16 May 1840
letters.summary: Has much pleasure "in accepting the honour of being proposed as a member of the Council of the Geographical Society".

letters.title: To William Kemp   1[8] May [1840]
letters.summary: CD has read WK’s abstract in theScotsman, 15 February 1840, p. 3, and asks for further details.

letters.title: To A. Y. Spearman   20 May 1840
letters.summary: The fourth number of part one of theZoologyhas now been published. The Smith, Elder & Co. account is submitted.

letters.title: To Charles Babbage   26 May [1840]
letters.summary: Asks if he can bring his guests, J. C. L. and Mme [Simonde de] Sismondi and [Fanny] Allen, to CB’s parties.

letters.title: To J. M. Herbert  [after 5 June 1840]
letters.summary:
Writes to find whether the date of the event [JMH’s marriage?] has been fixed.

Has been unwell and does not yet feel up to work.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   [7 June 1840]
letters.summary:
Family news.

CD’s health is improving, but he has scarcely put pen to paper in the last half-year, and everything in the publishing line is going backwards.

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   3 July [1840]
letters.summary: Describes an orange tree with curious "horned" fruit; sends specimen. Asks if the horns represent "metamorphoses of some organ into the fruit orange".

letters.title: From Susan and Catherine Darwin  [22 July 1840]
letters.summary: Reference to W. Smellie’sNatural history[1791] requested by CD.

letters.title: To Gilbert Nicholas Smith  [c.15 August 1840]
letters.summary: Questions GNS on remains found in caves on Caldy Island. [CD’s pencilled queries sent via Frances Allen].

letters.title: To William Buckland   [November 1840 – 17 February 1841]
letters.summary:
He encloses an unidentified paper received from R. I. Murchison the previous day.

Is unable to provide information about Dr Du Gard.

Appreciates the maps of Glen Roy sent by WB. Would welcome the opinions of WB and Louis Agassiz concerning the parallel roads but cannot give up the idea of their marine origin.

letters.title: To John Phillips  [November 1840]
letters.summary: Sends his paper on earthquakes [(1840),Collected papers1: 53–86]. Now sets less value on theoretical reasoning in geology than when he wrote it.

letters.title: From J. S. Henslow   2 November 1840
letters.summary: Would like further experimentation to confirm report about germination of wheat from Egyptian tombs. Sir G. Wilkinson may have been deceived by the Arabs.

letters.title: To the Geological Society of London  18 November [1840]
letters.summary: Recommends that Consul Chatfield’s communication on an earthquake in San Salvador [read 5 Feb 1840;Proc. Geol. Soc. Lond.3 (1840): 179] not be published inTransactions.

letters.title: To G. R. Gray  [20 November – 11 December 1840]
letters.summary: Thanks GRG for his gift [A list of the genera of birds(1840)] and trusts that now GRG will be able to finish John Gould’s MS forZoology.

letters.title: To G. N. Smith   20 November [1840]
letters.summary: Sorry that ill health prevented sooner reply. Letter about caves at Caldy was already read by Buckland. Will examine birds’ beaks when better and present to Geological Society of London in Smith’s name.

letters.title: From J. S. Henslow   21 November 1840
letters.summary: Reports on abortive anthers in flowers of thyme sent by CD.

letters.title: To A. Y. Spearman   22 November 1840
letters.summary: The second number of part four of theZoologyhas now been published. The account of Smith, Elder & Co. is presented.

letters.title: To Miles Joseph Berkeley   [26 November 1840]
letters.summary: Remarks that each of two species ofFagusseparated by 1000 miles has a fungus that grows on it; the fungus species are probably closely allied.

letters.title: To W. A. Leighton   1 December 1840
letters.summary: Acknowledges election as Honorary Member of Shropshire and North Wales Natural History and Antiquarian Society.

letters.title: To John Gould   [after 1 December 1840]
letters.summary: Feels he cannot keep the gift of Gould’s "magnificent work" or take out a subscription now that he is a married man.

letters.title: To W. C. Redfield   [22 December 1840]
letters.summary: Illness has long delayed CD’s thanks for WCR’s meteorological pamphlets and geological reports. Mentions a reference to whirlwinds leaving rotary patterns in desert sand.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   [25 January 1841]
letters.summary:
Birdshas gone to the printer.

Continues "to collect all kinds of facts about ""varieties and species"" " for his "some-day work".

Would be grateful for descriptions of offspring of crossbred domestic animals.

letters.title: To G. R. Gray  [February 1841]
letters.summary: In a revise [ofBirds] CD has altered "Colaptes ChilensisVigors" to "Chrysoptilus ChilensisG. R. Gray". Is that right?

letters.title: To G. R. Gray  [February–March 1841]
letters.summary: Sends proof of index of final number ofBirdsfor checking.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell  [21 February – 4 April 1841]
letters.summary:
Answers a number of queries from Lyell concerning geography and geology of Chiloé Island and its relationship to the Cordilleras.

Asks about "perched rocks" on Jura and notes their relevance to Louis Agassiz’s theory. Discusses Agassiz’s view on Jura.

Mentions seeing Robert Brown.

Notes R. I. Murchison’s discovery of shells in central England.

Weakness of negative evidence.

letters.title: To M. J. Berkeley  [March 1841]
letters.summary:
Looks forward to the paper on CD’s edible fungus specimen from Tierra del Fuego [read 16 Mar 1841;Trans. Linn. Soc. Lond.19 (1845): 37–43].

Sends a correction:Fagus betuloides, notF. antarctica, is the common tree of Tierra del Fuego.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell  [March 1841]
letters.summary: Discusses the role of ice in determining the geological features of the Jura. Mentions view of Agassiz. Objects to idea of "a [sea of ice] carrying rocks". Notes Agassiz’s earlier view of "ice expanded in thelineof the Great Swiss Valley". Comments on Pentlands.

letters.title: To Louis Agassiz   1 March [1841]
letters.summary:
Has enjoyed reading LA’s book [Études sur les glaciers(1840)].

Hopes LA will pardon manner in which CD has alluded to his work on glaciers in hisJournal of researches, of which he sends a copy.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [9 March 1841]
letters.summary: Defends his theory [in "Parallel roads of Glen Roy" (1839),Collected papers1: 87–137] against the view that the "roads" were formed by glacial action.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [12 March 1841]
letters.summary:
Discusses at length Louis Agassiz’s book [Études sur les glaciers(1840)] and Agassiz’s explanation of moraines. Defends his own theory of the importance of floating ice. Relates glacier theory to his own interpretation of Glen Roy.

Mentions a paper he is writing on South American boulders and till [Collected papers1: 145–63].

letters.title: To A. Y. Spearman   27 March 1841
letters.summary: The Smith, Elder & Co. account for the now published fifth number of the third part of theZoologyis presented.

letters.title: From Leonard Jenyns   [c.30 March 1841]
letters.summary: LJ has had a letter from R. T. Lowe in Madeira who thinksScorpaena histrio, a species from Galapagos described in no. 1 [ofFish], is the same as the one in the Atlantic and Mediterranean. LJ does not think it is possible.

letters.title: To William Lonsdale   14 April [1841]
letters.summary: Sends paper on erratic boulders [Collected papers1: 145–63] to the Society. Has taken two months to complete it because of illness.

letters.title: From J. S. Henslow   19 April 1841
letters.summary: Reports observations on the behaviour of captive harvest mouse and dormouse. When descending sticks mouse uses its tail like a prehensile-tailed monkey.

letters.title: From William C. Redfield    May 1841
letters.summary: Is sending through John Blunt a copy of the last geological report of the state of New York along with a short paper on the tornado that passed through the state of New Jersey in June 1835.

letters.title: To [E. W. Brayley?]   8 May [1841]
letters.summary: Thanks recipient for finding reference on carbonate of lime. Doubtful when he will publish his geological memoranda.

letters.title: To A. Y. Spearman   17 May 1841
letters.summary: The third number of part four of theZoologyhas been published. CD transmits the Smith, Elder & Co. account.

letters.title: To Leonard Jenyns   24 June [1841]
letters.summary: Doctors predict it will take years for CD’s constitution to recover.

letters.title: To W. A. Leighton   [1–23 July 1841]
letters.summary: Tells WAL where specimen ofCynoglossum sylvaticummay be seen growing.

letters.title: To Emma Darwin   [1 July 1841]
letters.summary: Family news. Mainly concerned about Doddy’s [W. E. Darwin’s] health.

letters.title: To Emma Darwin   [3 July 1841]
letters.summary: The happy family life at Shrewsbury. CD is looking so well his father would not have known there was anything the matter with him. The year’s accounts come to £1380.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   6 [July 1841]
letters.summary:
Discusses various types of coral reefs on which he has been collecting notes. Views of C. G. Ehrenberg. His conception of the formation of Bermuda.

Pessimistic about the effect of his poor health on his scientific work.

letters.title: From Catherine Darwin  8 July 1841
letters.summary: Describes the appearance and occurrence of imperfect flowers of "Hex.[?] Trigynia".

letters.title: From Charles Lyell  [c.16 July 1841]
letters.summary:
Regrets not seeing CD before leaving on trip [to the U. S.]. CD’s move from London will be a privation for CL.

Returns charts on coral reefs.

letters.title: ToGardeners’ Chronicle  [16 August 1841]
letters.summary: Reports detailed observations on humble-bees boring holes in flowers to extract nectar instead of brushing over the stamens and pistils. Some hive-bees seem to use the holes made by the humble-bees; speculates that this would be a case of acquired knowledge in insects.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   [23 August 1841]
letters.summary:
Consents to be godfather to WDF’s child.

Sends family news.

letters.title: To Richard Owen   25 August [1841–2]
