letters.summary: Sends elephant tooth from Africa. Suggests it may be interesting in light of his [mistaken] memory of Cuvier’s opinion about tusk brought from Peru by Humboldt.

letters.title: From Richard Owen   [17 September 1841?]
letters.summary: CD and [Emma Darwin] are invited to "a holiday musical evening".

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   [28 September 1841]
letters.summary:
Sends news of his house-hunting.

Envies WDF his discovery ofCheirotheriumfootprints.

letters.title: To J. P. Gaimard   14 October 1841
letters.summary: Asks if JPG can supply him with the source of M. Cordier’s assertion that the reef of Vanikoro is of recent formation.

letters.title: From Abberley (Darwin gardener)and R. W. Darwin  18 October 1841
letters.summary: The family gardener reports on seeds he has gathered. RWD transmits the letter.

letters.title: To Leonard Jenyns  [November 1841]
letters.summary:
Details regarding volume onFish.

Sends notes onDiodon.

Must give up attending Geological Society evening meetings; knocks him up.

letters.title: To the Council of the Geological Society of London  [before 6 December 1841]
letters.sender: Charles Robert DarwinCharles James Fox Bunbury, 8th baronetArthur AikinGeorge Bellas Greenough
letters.summary: Committee suggests Council resolve to have William Lonsdale pack away non-fossil specimens from S. America and volcanic islands of the Atlantic [signed G. B. Greenough, A. Aiken, C. Darwin, C. J. F. Bunbury].

letters.title: To William Baxter or W. W. Baxter   [1842–82]
letters.summary: Orders pot of soft spermaceti ointment.

letters.title: From Hugh Falconer    [1842–3]
letters.summary: Has seen lately a true ruminant with the two central metacarpals distinct. It was the foot of anAnoplotheriumin a recent ruminant.

letters.title: To Charles Stokes    [January–March 1842]
letters.summary:
Returns snuff box.

Sends a microscope for repair.

Makes appointment to discuss some corals that he is sending.

letters.title: To ?   [1842–82]
letters.summary: Will be glad to see recipient and Mr Morris at Down the following day.

letters.title: To W. W. Baxter or William Baxter  10 [October 1842 – March 1882]
letters.summary: Orders distilled water, 2 oz of camphorated spirits, and perfume.

letters.title: To Leonard Jenyns   [13? January 1842]
letters.summary: CD is pleased with LJ’s introduction [toFish]. He rejoices that he persuaded LJ to undertake this work.

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   [26 January 1842]
letters.summary: CD relates that Robert Brown is anxious to have [C. M.] Leman[n] elected librarian of the Linnean Society and urges JSH to come to vote for him. CD joins in the request.

letters.title: To the Geological Society of London  31 January [1842]
letters.summary: Hopes to meet with museum committee after 11 o’clock next day.

letters.title: To J. F. Royle   [2 February 1842]
letters.summary: Asks JFR to support E. A. Darwin’s election to the Athenaeum.

letters.title: To Francis Boott   [3 February 1842]
letters.summary: "My Dear Sir, I have called on you, to solicit your vote & interest at the Athenaeum Club […] in favour of my brother, Erasmus Darwin".

letters.title: To Richard Owen   [4 February 1842]
letters.summary: Informs Owen of the fossil finds of F. J. Muñiz in south America.

letters.title: To Henry Thomas De la Beche   7 February 1842
letters.summary: Asks De la Beche about variation among domesticated animals in Jamaica.

letters.title: To Hugh Edwin Strickland   17 February [1842]
letters.summary: CD approves of HES’s "laws" [of nomenclature]. Regrets that [J. E.?] Gray does not approve of the scheme. CD has sent the paper to William Ogilby and suggests that HES send it to G. R. Waterhouse, of whom he has a high opinion.

letters.title: To H. E. Strickland   [19 February 1842]
letters.summary: CD saw Andrew Smith, who is interested in the subject [of zoological nomenclature], but CD thinks he differs from HES on some points. Sends Smith’s address.

letters.title: To Susan Darwin   [22 February 1842]
letters.summary:
Comments on birth [of Catherine Elizabeth Sophia Wedgwood].

Plans to visit Shrewsbury.

Describes behaviour of William Darwin.

Discusses speculation losses of acquaintances, including T. Carlyle’s. Mentions his own loss onJournal of researches.

letters.title: To Emma Darwin   [8 March 1842]
letters.summary: Family news from Shrewsbury.

letters.title: To Emma Darwin   [13 March 1842]
letters.summary:
News of family and of his stay at Shrewsbury.

Calculates the newly instituted income tax will mean £30 per annum.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   23 March [1842]
letters.summary: Letter of condolence on the death of WDF’s wife [Harriet Fletcher Fox].

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   [31 March 1842]
letters.summary: Second letter of condolence, following burial of Mrs Fox.

letters.title: To A. Y. Spearman   29 April 1842
letters.summary: The fourth number of part four is now published; the Smith, Elder & Co. account is presented.

letters.title: To Leonard Jenyns  [May–September 1842]
letters.summary:
Glad to hear that LJ will repeat his notes to Gilbert White’s [Natural history of]Selborne[1843] in a separate work.

Critical of G. R. Gray’s attaching his own name toFurnarius cunicularius[inBirds, pp. 65–6]. Strickland’s nomenclature laws are needed to check egoism.

letters.title: To Mary-Anne Herbert   [5 May 1842]
letters.summary: Acknowledges Mrs H’s disappointing answer to his quest for a house in the country. Five miles from a railway station is "the length of my tether".

letters.title: To Leonard Jenyns   [9 May 1842]
letters.summary:
Is sending fish skins and bottles off to Cambridge Philosophical Society.

Fish numbers [ofZoology], now finished, give CD satisfaction when he doubts whether he ought to have applied for Government money.

Wishes Thomas Bell would finish his part [Reptiles].

CD has just corrected last page of index ofCoral reefs.

letters.title: To Emma Darwin   [9 May 1842]
letters.summary: Is "stomachy and be-blue-devilled" because of costs of publishing [ZoologyandCoral reefs]. Wonders how the remainder [of theZoologyandGeology of "Beagle"] can be published without taking £200 or £300 out of their personal funds.

letters.title: To Smith, Elder & Co.   [17 May 1842]
letters.summary: Gives instructions for sending out copies ofCoral reefsto various journals. Discusses the complimentary copies which have already been sent out.

letters.title: To H. E. Strickland   31 May [1842]
letters.summary: Comments on HES’s Report ["Report of a committee … (on) nomenclature of zoology",Rep. BAAS12 (1842): 105–21]. Suggests limit be put to changing names that are only partially erroneous to prevent those who detect the error from coining new names and attaching their own. HES’s rule for "authority for a species" is difficult, though on the whole best. Suggests stating it boldly to prevent appropriation of species names by "tacker[s] of two old names together".

letters.title: To W. H. Fitton  [c.28 June 1842]
letters.summary:
[Excerpt copied from a letter CD wrote to WHF.]

CD’s gratefulness to William Buckland for his guidance on the glaciated terrain of N. Wales. "I am also convinced that the valleys of Glen Roy … have been occupied by arms of the Sea, & very likely, (for on that point I cannotof coursedoubt Agassiz & Buckland) by glaciers also."

letters.title: To Susan Darwin   [late July–August 1842]
letters.summary: Has made an offer for house at Down, renting having been refused. Discusses price, risks involved, and Edward Cresy’s advice.

letters.title: From John Provis   14 July 1842
letters.summary: Discusses elevations along Holyhead Road [Anglesey].

letters.title: From John Provis   20 July 1842
letters.summary: Location of village of Bethesda [NW Wales].

letters.title: To Catherine Darwin   [24 July 1842]
letters.summary: Describes the village of Down and the house they are thinking of buying.

letters.title: To A. Y. Spearman   5 August 1842
letters.summary: The Smith, Elder & Co. account for the first number of part five of theZoology, now published, is presented.

letters.title: From Thomas Blunt   11 August 1842
letters.summary: Gives the height of Shrewsbury above sea-level.

letters.title: To H. E. Strickland   [11 August 1842]
letters.summary:
Congratulates HES on producing an authoritative document [BAAS committee report on zoological nomenclature].

Has been to N. Wales looking at glacier traces described by W. Buckland, which are most interesting and clear. Has written an article on what he saw ["Ancient glaciers of Caernarvonshire" (1842),Collected papers1: 163–71].

letters.title: To W. J. Broderip   [31 August 1842]
letters.summary:
Discusses toad [mentioned inJournal of researches, p. 115].

Describes house at Down.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell  [September–December 1842]
letters.summary: Discusses relationship of subsidence to the formation of coral reefs.

letters.title: From Alexander Bridport Becher   1 September 1842
letters.summary: Francis Beaufort has instructed ABB to order three copies ofCoral Reefs.

letters.title: To G. R. Waterhouse  [4 or 11 September 1842]
letters.summary:
Thanks GRW for collection [of insects] he has made up for CD’s nephew.

Leaves decision to GRW as to which institutions should receive CD’sBeagleinsects.

letters.title: To William Yarrell  [5 or 12 September 1842]
letters.summary:
CD is too dull and languid to see Mr Bicheno but will be glad to answer his questions if he writes.

Asks WY to ask J. Sebright "whether the cross with white bantam brought back any of the ""secondary male characters"" to the hen–cock breed".

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   16 September [1842]
letters.summary: CD gives JSH Fuegian paints and spears and a Pacific dolphin hook for his museum.

letters.title: To Catherine Darwin   [16 September 1842]
letters.summary: Emma and Doddy [W. E. Darwin] like Down. CD has met, and plans to employ, the local surgeon. "I feel sure I shall become deeply attached to Down, with a few improvements".

letters.title: From Elizabeth Wedgwood  [25 September 1842]
letters.summary: Reports on Josiah Wedgwood [II], who is seriously ill.

letters.title: From Hensleigh Wedgwood   25 September [1842]
letters.summary: Gives an account of his father’s illness.

letters.title: To the Geological Society of London  4 October 1842
letters.summary: Papers by T. J. Newbold [Proc. Geol. Soc. Lond.3 (1842): 702–5], T. C. Hunt [3 (1842): 565–6] and J. Phillips [3 (1842): 705–6] need not be printed inTransactions of the Geological Society.

letters.title: To Anne Susan Horner   [4 October 1842]
letters.summary:
Emma recovering well from birth of third child, Mary Eleanor.

Sorry to hear Leonard Horner has been ill.

Has received high praise ofCoral reefsfrom Lyell.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell  [5 and 7 October 1842]
letters.summary:
Discusses growth of various species of coral. Explains significance of dead reefs.

Describes meeting of the Council of the Geological Society; the controversy involving Edward Charlesworth.

Mentions conversations with William Lonsdale about Lonsdale’s work on corals and the financial support for his work.

Murchison’s views on glaciation in Wales.

Agassiz’s observations at Glen Roy.

letters.title: To Julian Jackson   13 October [1842]
letters.summary: Discusses JJ’s proposed review of his volume [Coral reefs].

letters.title: To W. H. Miller  [16 October – 27 November 1842]
letters.summary:
Mentions preparing geological notes for press. Asks whether WHM still has some geological specimens he had examined for CD.

Urges WHM to attend important meeting of Geological Society on 3 December.

letters.title: To William Baxter or W. W. Baxter   24 October [1842–5 or 1853 or 1855–68?]
letters.summary: Sends enclosed order for two bottles [of unspecified chemical].

letters.title: To Charles Lyell  [November–December 1842]
letters.summary: Believes "absurd letter" hastily read at last Geological Society Council meeting was from Charlesworth’s solicitor. Suggests that it may have been sent to entrap the Council and that it should be read over carefully.

letters.title: To Samuel Pickworth Woodward  [12 November 1842]
letters.deprecated: Samuel Pickworth WoodwardGeological Society of London
letters.recipient: Samuel Pickworth WoodwardGeological Society of London
letters.summary: Asks SPW to have obsidian specimens and book [Dieudonné de Gratet de Dolomieu,Voyage aux îles de Lipari(1783)] ready when he comes.

letters.title: To Charles Maclaren  [15 November – December 1842]
letters.summary: Responds to CM’s review ofCoral reefs[Edinburgh New Philos. J.34 (1843): 33–47].

letters.title: To John Price    29 November [1842–55]
letters.summary:
Not able to assist JP as he knows no schoolmaster in the area.

Cannot answer zoological question but thinks the twoSerpulaeare distinct.

letters.title: To William Baxter or W. W. Baxter   8 December [1842–81]
letters.summary: Orders large pot of spermaceti ointment.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   [9 December 1842]
letters.summary:
CD likes Down House, describes countryside.

Tells of Edward Charlesworth fracas at Geological Society.

Is at work onVolcanic islands.

letters.title: To Charles Edward and Mary Kingford Mudie   10 December [1842–5 or 1855–68]
letters.summary: Declines invitation.

letters.title: To [Susan? Darwin]  [1843 – 8 March 1846]
letters.summary:
Reports events at Down.

The "atrocious doings" of "Old Price". Price’s dispute with Sir John Lubbock over a boundary fence.

letters.title: To William Baxter or W. W. Baxter?   2 [October 1842 – March 1882]
letters.summary: Requests some carbonate of ammonia.

letters.title: To Smith, Elder & Co.   [14 January 1843]
letters.summary:
Asks for account.

Discusses delay ofReptilesby Thomas Bell. Asks them to inform R. B. Hinds of delay.

letters.title: To Smith, Elder & Co.   21 January [1843]
letters.summary:
Discusses his account.

Sends addresses [for subscribers toZoology].

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   [22 January 1843]
letters.summary:
Comments on JSH’s botanical work with his parishioners. Lyell will be pleased that he has done some fossil botanical work.

Describes a Geological Society meeting about Edward Charlesworth’s complaints.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   22 [1843–82]
letters.summary:
Discusses books returned

and invites him to Down for a few days.

letters.title: To ?   23 January [1843–6 or 1856–69]
letters.summary: Obliged for memoir with illustrations on most interesting point [unspecified] to occur in many years.

letters.title: To Charles Maclaren  [c.February 1843]
letters.summary: [Written on CD’s annotated copy of a pamphlet reprint of CM’s review ofCoral reefs.] CD asks CM to return the pamphlet to him.

letters.title: To the Royal Geographical Society    February 1843
letters.summary: George Suttor’s paper not worthy of publication in theJournalof the society. It contains no new facts worth insertion.

letters.title: To London Library   1 February [1843 or later]
letters.summary: Orders John Pye Smith’s book [Relations between the Holy Scriptures and some parts of geological science(1839)].

letters.title: To Richard Owen  [March 1843 – 15 May 1846]
letters.summary: Invites the Owens to stay at Down, joining Falconer and a few others.

letters.title: To the Geological Society of London  12 March [1843]
letters.summary: Asks how many copies ofProceedingsare commonly sold.

letters.title: To William Jackson Hooker   12 March [1843]
letters.summary: Asks WJH to thank his son [J. D. Hooker, away on Antarctic survey] for his note. Has also read a letter JDH wrote to Lyell. Hopes JDH will publish a journal. If he publishes an Antarctic flora, CD will place his collection of South American alpine plants at his disposal.

letters.title: To William Baxter or W. W. Baxter   21 March [1843–82]
letters.summary: Requests a mixture of verdigris, sal ammoniac, and lamp-black.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   [25 March 1843]
letters.summary:
Sympathises with WDF’s persisting grief.

Describes Down House and additions being built, which interfere withGeology[of "Beagle"].

Bodily health is improved, but cannot stand mental excitement.

letters.title: From William Mostyn Owen Sr   26 March 1843
letters.summary: Discusses the death of his son. Thanks CD for his letter of condolence and invites him to visit.

letters.title: To Robert FitzRoy   31 March [1843]
letters.summary: Congratulates FitzRoy on his appointment as Governor of New Zealand. Wants to see him and his wife before their departure. Proposes to call on them in London next Thursday.

letters.title: To William Kemp   7 April [1843]
letters.summary: CD will sent seeds to specialists for identification.

letters.title: To John Lindley   8 [April 1843]
letters.summary: CD sends seeds found by W. Kemp of Galashiels with explanation and request that they be planted and a report sent to him, so that Kemp may publish his discovery if results are interesting.

letters.title: From John Lindley  [after 8 April 1843]
letters.summary: Will be happy to report on seeds sent by CD. Suggests names.

letters.title: From Charles Lyell   [9 April 1843]
letters.summary:
Spoke to Henry Warburton, W. H. Fitton, and E. B. Greenough on CD’s idea of a Government grant for publication [not identified].

Will read at next meeting his paper on erect Nova Scotia fossil trees [Proc. Geol. Soc. Lond.4 (1843–5): 176–8].

E. P. Halstead reports on shores rising off Burma and Bay of Bengal.

Unpacking his U. S. fossils.

Phillips looked at beds below coal in Pennsylvania. Result is the usual different species found but with complete representation of forms.

letters.title: From Richard Brinsley Hinds   21 April 1843
letters.summary: Replies to queries by CD. Describes Clipperton Rock [SW. of Mexico] and Cocos Island. Mentions possible species ofCactornis. Discusses depth of water at Bow Island [Hao, Tuamotu Archipelago], and occurrence of coral formations at various islands.

letters.title: To G. A. Mantell   21 [April 1843]
letters.summary: Regrets that he can offer little aid. If he sees Captain FitzRoy, he will give him GAM’s letter to read at leisure.

letters.title: To Royal Geographical Society  23 April [1843]
letters.deprecated: Julian Jacksonsecretary of R. Geographical Soc.
letters.recipient: Julian Jacksonsecretary of R. Geographical Soc.
letters.summary: Thanks Jackson for putting him on list for Council of Geographical Society, but he is unable to serve.

letters.title: To William Kemp   24 [April 1843]
letters.summary: Has not yet heard from R. Brown, but John Lindley thinks species will probably turn out to be common ones.

letters.title: To Susan Darwin   27[–8] April [1843]
letters.summary: Describes alterations being made at Down House. Accepts father’s offer to lend him money.

letters.title: To Dr Bakewell   30 April [1843–5 or 1856–68]
letters.summary: Thanks for case of inherited malconformation.

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   [10 May 1843]
letters.summary:
Describes siege [of Montevideo].

Reports on appearance and habits of horses and cattle of Falkland Islands; wild rabbits and pigs. Geology of the Falklands, especially of West Island. Discusses supposed discovery of coal. Has sent fossil specimens to CD.

letters.title: To G. A. Mantell   13 May [1843]
letters.summary: Capt. FitzRoy has read GAM’s letter to CD regarding an appointment for GAM’s son and is disposed to help, but has resolved to make no appointments until he arrives in New Zealand [as Governor].

letters.title: To [Leonard Horner?]   25 June 1843
letters.summary:
Sends notes on volcanic islands for LH to read and return.

[Letter could be an inaccurate contemporary copy to which the copyist interpolated details, or a forgery. The address "Down House Orpington Kent" occurs nowhere else.]

letters.title: To Smith, Elder, and Company 29 June [1843]
letters.summary: Requests information as to means of sending two pamphlets to a professor in the United States.

letters.title: To Henry Colburn   4 July [1843]
letters.summary: Offers to pay for use of plate of map of S. America and for three woodcuts, for German edition ofJournal of researches[1844].

letters.title: To Ernst Dieffenbach    4 July [1843]
letters.summary:
CD gratified that ED wants to translate hisJournal. Will send a copy ofCoral reefs, which contains a fuller treatment of topic. Perhaps ED would insert a note to this effect. Can lend woodcuts fromCoral reefsif ED wants. CD will send a few corrections; he wants to amend way he criticised Agassiz’s glacier theory.

He is also enclosing a questionnaire concerning differences between races or varieties and species, about which he intends to publish sometime.

letters.title: To G. R. Waterhouse   8 July 1843
letters.summary: Testimonial letter for GRW for position at British Museum.

letters.title: To Edward Holland  [after 12 July 1843]
letters.summary: Discusses fossil bones found in Australia by Mr Isaac. Suggests they be sent to Richard Owen.

letters.title: To Ernst Dieffenbach   19 July [1843]
letters.summary: Says Colburn will allow German publisher to use copperplate and woodcuts [forJournal of researches]. Has been delayed in corrections owing to death of a relative [Josiah Wedgwood II].

letters.title: From R. B. Hinds   19 July [1843]
letters.summary: CD will be gratified to learn that RBH has recognised a species ofCactornisas a native of Bow Island [Hao, Tuamotu Archipelago].

letters.title: To G. R. Waterhouse   [26 July 1843]
letters.summary: Classification consists of grouping beings according to descent from common stocks. Analogies are resemblances between forms not inherited from common stocks. Neither number of species nor grade of organisation should be considered in classification. Admits that caution is necessary in admitting a few species to form a group of rank equal to one containing many species.

letters.title: To G. R. Waterhouse   [31 July 1843]
letters.summary: Has no objection to uniting Monotremata and other marsupials but would object to doing so solely on ground that Monotremata consists of only two species. Members of a natural group need not share common character so long as they are linked with those which do. Believes that if every organism that ever lived were collected, a perfect series would be presented. What are reasons that unite Aptera and Diptera?

letters.title: ToGardeners’ Chronicle  [late August 1843]
letters.summary: Sends some examples ofGentianathat he thinks may shed light on the origin of double flowers. Since specimens grew in sterile soil their double flowering cannot be attributed to excess food. CD advances the hypothesis that some change in natural conditions causes sterility, which then causes compensatory development of petals, the organs closest in morphology to those whose functions have been checked.

letters.title: From G. R. Waterhouse  [c.2 August 1843]
letters.summary:
Discusses classification of animals. Degree of affinity different for different taxonomic groups. Discusses affinity ofOrnithorhynchusorEchidnato reptiles.

Brain of whale is highly developed; on differences among brains of Quadrumana.

letters.title: From J. S. Henslow  [5 August 1843]
letters.summary: Calls CD’s attention to an article about William Herbert’s hybridNarcissus.

letters.title: From G. R. Waterhouse   9 August 1843
letters.summary:
Explains what he means when he attempts a "natural classification", defining his words and using man as a standard; gives examples. Classification of Aptera and Diptera.

Discusses his discharge from the Zoological Society. Is to see Robert Brown about the British Museum position.

letters.title: To Ernst Dieffenbach   15 August [1843]
letters.summary: CD sends off his notes [corrections and additions to hisJournal of researches] which he hopes ED will introduce [in German translation].

letters.title: From John Lindley   [before 2 September 1843]
letters.summary:
Much interested in CD’s communication [about W. Kemp] and seeds sent; does not know the species; has sent seeds to Henslow.

Describes a monstrous plant found near Ely.

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow  [2 September 1843]
letters.summary:
Tells how W. Kemp found the seeds ofAtriplex, which Lindley sent to JSH for identification.

Asks about monstrous plant mentioned by Lindley [see690].

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   [4 September 1843]
letters.summary:
Comments on his visit to N. Wales and the evidence of glaciation, of which he feels certain.

His marine theory [of the parallel roads of Glen Roy] has revived after Louis Agassiz’s "ice work" knocked it on the head.

letters.title: To William Kemp   [8 September 1843]
letters.summary: Seeds sent by Kemp have germinated and been identified by Lindley asRumex acetosellaand an Atriplex which has been sent on to J. S. Henslow.

letters.title: To John Edward Davis   15 September [1843]
letters.summary:
Thanks him for specimens collected.

Comments on JED’s voyage [on H.M.S.Terror, 1839–43].

Mentions activities of oldBeaglecrew.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell  [15 or 22 September 1843]
letters.summary:
Mentions expected birth of child [Henrietta Emma].

BAAS meeting.

Comments on letters from G. R. Waterhouse and William Lonsdale.

Describes survival of apparently "fossil" seeds sent by W. Kemp.

Is at work on MS [ofVolcanic islands].

letters.title: To S. P. Woodward   29 [September 1843]
letters.summary: Says he will call tomorrow to examine indicated specimens and books at Geological Society.

letters.title: To Benjamin Waterhouse Hawkins  [c.1 October 1843]
letters.summary: Discusses poor impression of plates [forReptilesby Thomas Bell].

letters.title: To Ernst Dieffenbach   2 October 1843
letters.summary:
On ED’s planned edition [German] of CD’sJournal of researches.

Informs him of his forthcoming volume,Volcanic islands.

"I am well acquainted with your paper on Chatham Island ["An account of the Chatham Islands",J. R. Geogr. Soc.11: 195–215], & … those passages on the very curious fact of the apparent specific differences of the birds there & at New Zealand".

Thanks ED for recognition of his "small labours in Natural History… . praise from men, like yourself, is the only, though quite sufficient, reward I ever expect or wish to obtain for my works. – I have lately had the extreme satisfaction of hearing that Hooker speaks highly of the accuracy … of my statements". Refers to Humboldt and Owen.

letters.title: From William Kemp   2 October 1843
letters.summary:
Describes germination of seeds found in sand-pit and the geological setting of the sand-pit.

Postulates existence of ancient lake along the course of the River Tweed. Notes evidence of glaciation.

letters.title: To Syms Covington   7 October 1843
letters.summary:
A new ear trumpet has been sent to SC as a present.

Sends news of his publications, health, and other developments since SC left for Australia.

letters.title: From J. S. Henslow   9 October 1843
letters.summary: Thinks W. Kemp’s specimens are all common varieties of living species ofAtriplex.

letters.title: To William Kemp   9 October [1843]
letters.summary: WK’s paper has reached him safely.

letters.title: To Smith, Elder & Co.   [9 October 1843]
letters.summary: Says he is forwarding the Smith, Elder & Co. account to the Treasury. Discusses advertisements ofZoologyandCoral reefs.Volcanic islands"is almost ready for press".

letters.title: To A. Y. Spearman   9 October 1843
letters.summary: The work of theZoologyis now completed. The Smith, Elder & Co. account for the second number of part five is presented. CD expresses his "grateful thanks" to the Lords Commissioners.

letters.title: To Emma Darwin   [12–24 October 1843]
letters.summary: News of the Shrewsbury family. He cannot get his father to sympathise with the numbness in his finger ends or his fears of "ruin and extravagance".

letters.title: To Josiah Wedgwood III   [12–24] October 1843
letters.summary: Note of hand, signed by CD, for £260 13s 6d.

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   [14 October 1843]
letters.summary: CD has written to W. Kemp to ascertain what precautions he took in sowing his seeds. "It will be ratherflatif you … pronounce theAtriplexto be merely a variety". Suggests sending plants to C. C. Babington.

letters.title: To William Kemp   [14 October 1843]
letters.summary: J. S. Henslow expresses his doubts about WK’s seeds.

letters.title: From J. S. Henslow  17 October 1843
letters.summary:
Regards [W. Kemp’s] plant as clearly onlyAtriplex patula, though with "an unusual habit".

Adds report on success of his Roman tomb exhibit.

letters.title: From William Kemp   17 October 1843
letters.summary:
Describes germination of seeds he discovered. Cites similar story of seeds found in coal-mine.

Gives further description of gravel bank [of River Tweed] and other geological details.

letters.title: From C. C. Babington   26 October 1843
letters.summary: IdentifiesAtriplexraised from seeds found by W. Kemp asA. angustifolia.

letters.title: To Smith, Elder & Co.  27 October [1843]
letters.summary: Treasury ready to make payment [forZoologyplates].

letters.title: To G. R. Waterhouse  [November 1843]
letters.summary: Congratulates GRW on appointment to position at British Museum.

letters.title: To William Kemp   1 November [1843]
letters.summary: J. S. Henslow’s and C. C. Babington’s opinions on WK’s seeds.

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   [4 November 1843]
letters.summary: Babington has reared a facsimile [of W. Kemp’sAtriplex] by sowing seeds ofA. angustifolia. CD has advised Kemp not to publish since anyone would say it was more probable that the seeds of his specimens were in the soil, than that the ones he found had retained vitality. CD regrets this, as he has no doubt of the antiquity of the seeds.

letters.title: From William Kemp   4 November 1843
letters.summary: Thanks CD for kind letter concerning seeds. Believes soil in which they were planted was contaminated.

letters.title: To William Kemp   [9 November 1843]
letters.summary: CD has been reflecting on John Lindley’s and C. C. Babington’s comments.

letters.title: From William Kemp   10 November 1843
letters.summary: Describes growth of plants raised from seeds he found in sand-pit.

letters.title: To Joseph Dalton Hooker  [13 or 20 November 1843]
letters.summary:
Congratulations on JDH’s safe return.

Henslow has sent CD’s S. American plants to JDH for examination.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   [20 November 1843]
letters.summary: Family news and their quiet life at Down.

letters.title: To William Kemp   22 November [1843]
letters.summary: CD is pleased with how good a case WK’s facts have made.

letters.title: From William Kemp  24 November 1843
letters.summary:
Approves of the paper CD has drawn up concerning WK’s seed discovery.

Mentions article inGardeners’ Chronicle.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   28 November 1843
letters.summary:
Thanks for use of CD’s collection.

Comments and queries on the botany of the Southern Hemisphere.

Looks forward to seeing CD’s Galapagos plants.

letters.title: To William Kemp   1 December [1843]
letters.summary: Robert Brown has cast much doubt on the integrity of the seed-planting experiment.

letters.title: To Susan Darwin   2 December 1843
letters.summary: Thanks SD for some furniture. Describes arrangement of furnishing at Down and work carried out on the grounds. Children are "very full of their approaching lessons".

letters.title: To G. R. Waterhouse  [3 or 17 December 1843]
letters.summary: Comments on GRW’s paper [Rep. BAAS(1843): 65–7;Ann. & Mag. Nat. Hist.12 (1843): 399–412]. CD says by "link" between any two groups he never understood a half-way link, merely one in a long series. Observes that one cannot have a simple species intermediate between two great families. Criticises GRW’s use of circles to represent groups, which leads to thinking that groups are of equal value.

letters.title: From William Kemp   4 December 1843
letters.summary: Describes circumstances surrounding discovery of seed in sand-pit. Encloses certificates testifying to the good character of the men involved.

letters.title: To William Kemp   7 December [1843]
letters.summary: Has sent WK’s paper to theAnnals and Magazine of Natural History(Kemp 1844).

letters.title: To Susan Darwin   [8 December 1843]
letters.summary: Thanks father for loan. Explains difficulty of acquiring the land through which the approach to Down House now runs.

letters.title: From Francis Walker  10 December 1843
letters.summary: Chalciditescollected by CD are all similar to those of Europe. Mentions other specimens quite different from European forms.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker  [12 December 1843 – 11 January 1844]
letters.summary: Henslow has sent him CD’s Galapagos plants along with Macrae’s. JDH impressed by the island endemism, which "overturns all our preconceived notions" on centres of radiation. Describes the extent, and the sharp demarcation at longitude 60° W, of the American and European Northern Hemisphere floras. CD’s plants among those he is using to do Antarctic flora.Drimys winterishows a graded series of states down the length of the South American continent.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [12 December 1843]
letters.summary: Thanks JDH for short sketch of botanical geography of Southern Hemisphere. Comments on his own S. American collections and observations; notes other Galapagos collections.

letters.title: To Ernst Dieffenbach   16 December 1843
letters.summary: "You will have been sorry to have seen in the newspapers, the disturbances & fightings with the New Zealanders. – I have lately been much interested in reading your chapters on the slow decrease in numbers … of these poor people. The case appears to me very curious, especially as the decrease has commenced or continued since the introduction of the potato – the relation between the amount of population & of food is hence inverted. It would have been a case for the great Malthus to have reflected on".

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [16 December 1843]
letters.summary: Description and defence of his view of the tosca in Banda Oriental, along the Rio Uruguay and at the Rio Negro, taking issue with A. D. d’Orbigny. Refers to the pumice in the Patagonian Territory. Two tables show the layered tosca formation along the Uruguay.

letters.title: To Edward Cresy   26 [December 1843 – April 1846 or September 1855 – October 1860?]
letters.summary: Says Hooker does not want plant.

letters.title: To Geological Society of London  [3 January 1844]
letters.summary: Asks that A. d’Orbigny’s geological map of S. America be sent to him with a card of the Society’s evening meetings.

letters.title: To Joseph Dalton Hooker   [11 January 1844]
letters.summary: Queries on ratios of species to genera on southern islands. CD’s observations on distribution of Galapagos organisms, and on S. American fossils, and facts he has gathered since, lead him to conclusion that species are not immutable; "it is like confessing a murder".

letters.title: To Henry Denny   20 January [1844]
letters.summary: Discusses sending HD lice specimens. Asks him to check with G. R. Waterhouse.

letters.title: To Ernst Dieffenbach   25 January 1844
letters.summary: Delighted to be able to contribute Infusoria to ED’s "great countryman Ehrenberg". Includes a list of eight substances from his collection described in detail, which Ehrenberg might find useful in his researches.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [27 January 1844]
letters.summary: C. G. Ehrenberg would like some earth from Galapagos, Tierra del Fuego, and the Falklands; wishes to hunt for Infusoria.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   29 January 1844
letters.summary:
Remarks on geographical divisions of the flora of the Southern Hemisphere.

JDH beginning Galapagos plants. Value of studying insular floras with respect to inquiries about adaptation of species.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [3–17 February 1844]
letters.summary: Thanks for information for Ehrenberg.

letters.title: To Henry Denny   5 February [1844]
letters.summary: Dicussion of some specimens from theBeaglevoyage.

letters.title: To Charles Wicksted  13 February [1844?]
letters.summary: Inquires about the habits of a litter of foxhounds whose sire was particularly good at recovering the scent in paths or roads.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker [23 February –  6 March 1844]
letters.summary:
Island floras; relationships with mainland. Ranges of species in mundane genera.

Galapagos plants one-third done.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   23 February [1844]
letters.summary:
Has just completedVolcanic islands.

Sends queries on Galapagos flora in particular and island floras in general; also on relationship of wide-ranging species to wide-ranging genera.

letters.title: To William Kemp   23 February [1844]
letters.summary: Regrets the delay in sending copies of his paper.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [6 March 1844]
letters.summary: Affinity of Galapagos with nearest Pacific islands. Relationship between ranges of species in time and space. Comparison of Malden Island and Galapagos plants. Affinities of Oceania plants with continental floras.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   9 March 1844
letters.summary:
Thanks for information on Malden Island. Comments on its plants and their relationship to the Galapagos flora. Discusses the flora of Oceania. Gives his opinion on the extent of the uniformity in species and forms amongst South Sea Islands. Large genera are more widely diffused and have a larger proportion of species with wide ranges.

Seeks advice on expense of preparing plates [forFlora Antarctica].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   11 March [1844]
letters.summary:
Advice to JDH on problems of printing and publishing.

Remarks on differences of species between islets of Galapagos group.

letters.title: To Ernst Dieffenbach   14 March 1844
letters.summary: [With the notation "If not there to be forwarded by favour of Prof. Liebig" on the address.] "I am very glad to hear that you are going to edit a German Geological Journal".

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   16 March [1844]
letters.summary:
Asks JDH to forward publishing information to J. E. Gray.

Has received JDH’s infusorial specimens for Ehrenberg.

letters.title: ToGardeners’ Chronicle and Agricultural Gazette  [27 March 1844]
letters.summary: Writes to correct a statement made in his 1837 paper "On the formation of mould" [Collected papers1: 49–53]. He should have said that marl was put on the field 30 years ago, not 80. Observations made on a visit to the field showed that worms had undermined the marl spread on the field at a faster rate than previously reported.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   31 March [1844]
letters.summary:
Thanks for JDH’s interesting details about the Galapagos.

Clarification of CD’s query about the relationship between the range of a genus and the ranges of its constituent species.

letters.title: From George Robert Waterhouse    [April 1844]
letters.summary:
Regularly attends Owen’s lectures. Owen at pains to show groups are not linked. Thus makesLepidosirenappear fish-like.

GRW thinks embryology will become chief guide to insect classification. But contradictions between classification based on embryological and adult characters do occur.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   5 April 1844
letters.summary:
Answer to CD’s query on genera and species ranges.

Comments on typical forms.

Preparing first part of Galapagos plants for printing.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [17 April 1844]
letters.summary:
Thanks for information on printing charges

and for clarifying "typical forms".

In a few days CD will go away for six weeks.

letters.title: To Christian Gottfried Ehrenberg   20 April [1844]
letters.summary: Sends samples likely to contain Infusoria and some that Hooker collected in Antarctic regions.

letters.title: From George Robert Waterhouse   26 April 1844
letters.summary: Defines the term "typical species" and discusses its use among zoologists. Cites example of type of Carnivora. Comments on general law of development of parts in animals. Cites teeth of Carnivora.

letters.title: From G. R. Waterhouse   [after 26 April 1844]
letters.summary: Is puzzled by CD’s question about the Viverridae; thinks if there were only one species he might regard it as an aberrant of some other group and not select it as a type of the Carnivora.

letters.title: From Erasmus Alvey Darwin   [May 1844 – 1 October 1846]
letters.summary:
Sends calculations of angles of elevation [of sea-bottom, forSouth America?].

Swale has sentLady Willoughby’s diary, which EAD will forward to CD.

letters.title: To Josiah Wedgwood III  [May 1844]
letters.summary: Family financial matters.

letters.title: From Philip de Malpas Grey-Egerton   5 May [1844]
letters.deprecated: Philip de Malpas Grey- Egerton, 10th baronet Egerton
letters.sender: Philip de Malpas Grey- Egerton, 10th baronet Egerton
letters.summary: Sends Lord Enniskillen’s account of origin of the Irish yew: transplanted from the wild; propagated by cuttings thereafter. Offspring recently raised from seed are intermediate between common and Irish [weeping] yew.

letters.title: To Julian Jackson   23 May [1844]
letters.summary: Discusses a paper on the Rio Negro.

letters.title: From George Brettingham Sowerby and Edward Forbes   28 May 1844
letters.summary: [Recto is a list of Galapagos shells, by island, signed GBS. Verso is another list of shells in EF’s hand.]

letters.title: To Henry Denny   1 June [1844]
letters.summary: Sends HD a reference to human lice from Charles White 1799.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   1 June [1844]
letters.summary:
Asks if J. E. Gray has returned [printing] estimates forZoology.

Henslow has some Galapagos plants which he forgot to forward to JDH.

letters.title: To Henry Denny   3 June [1844]
letters.summary:
Discusses intestinal worms among humans.

Comments on origin of human races.

letters.title: To Emma Darwin   [3 June 1844]
letters.summary:
Arrangements for Emma’s return to Down.

CD has been "wonderfully strong".

letters.title: ToGardeners’ Chronicle and Agricultural Gazette  [before 8 June 1844]
letters.summary: Sends a quotation from de Vallemont’sCuriosities of nature and art in husbandry and gardening(1707) showing that the value of saltpetre in manure and the advantage of steeping seeds in specially prepared liquid manure were well known at the time.

letters.title: To G. R. Waterhouse   10 [June 1844 – March 1845]
letters.summary: Invites GRW and his family to visit.

letters.title: To Ernst Dieffenbach   11 June [1844]
letters.summary: About the researches of Ehrenberg. "I have … sent him several packets of objects from my voyage & that of Dr. Hooker".

letters.title: From C. G. Ehrenberg    15 June 1844
letters.summary: Thanks for earth samples. Discusses Infusoria in samples from Galapagos and Cape Verde Islands. Would like samples from other sites. Will send further results of investigations.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   29 [June 1844]
letters.summary:
Encloses letter from Ehrenberg [758] about Infusoria.

Intends to visit Kew.

letters.title: To Josiah Wedgwood III   31 July 1844
letters.summary: Acknowledges receipt of the order for £48 4s. 8d., and offers full indemnity for the £5,000 deposited without security.

letters.title: To C. G. Ehrenberg   4 July [1844]
letters.summary: Astonished that dust sample contains Infusoria. Thinks dust is volcanic. Will write account of falling dust [see775]. Offers further samples.

letters.title: To Emma Darwin   5 July 1844
letters.summary: Asks that in the event of his death, Emma should have the sketch of his species theory edited and published. Suggests possible editors, among them Lyell, Edward Forbes, and J. D. Hooker. [CD annotation on cover: "Hooker by far best man to edit my species volume Aug 1854".]

letters.title: From C. G. Ehrenberg   11 July 1844
letters.summary: Thanks for shipments of earth samples. Sends copy of article describing Infusoria in samples ["Einige vorläufige Resultate … über das Verhalten des kleinsten Lebens in den Oceanen",Ber. k. Preuss. Akad. Wiss. Berlin(1844): 182–207]. Asks for more information and samples, especially from the soundings of Ross’s expedition.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [14 July 1844]
letters.summary: Health and weather permitting, CD proposes to visit Kew.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   22 July [1844]
letters.summary: Encloses letter from Ehrenberg [762], who wants information on deep-sea soundings from JDH’s voyage, and on isolated islands.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [25 July – 29 August 1844]
letters.summary:
Encloses Ehrenberg letter, Galapagos seaweed, and specimens ofConferva.

H. Denny would like specimens of AntarcticPediculi.

letters.title: To John Stevens Henslow   [25 July 1844]
letters.summary:
Sends a specimen of rusty wheat from the banks of the Plata.

Asks for bits of peat he collected

and a bit of the paint used by Fuegians to colour themselves.

He will send these to C. G. Ehrenberg for analysis.

letters.title: To Josiah Wedgwood III and E. A. Darwin  25 July 1844
letters.summary: Requests to JW III and EAD as trustees of the marriage-settlement, to make some funds available.

letters.title: To Henry Denny   [27 July – 10 August 1844]
letters.summary: Sends four packets of lice and suggests writing to Dr A. Smith, "the S. African traveller", for assistance.

letters.title: To The Royal Geographical Society   [30 July 1844 – 1 October 1846]
letters.summary: Urgently needs a Spanish map of the Cordilleras of central Chile near St Jago [Santiago].

letters.title: To Adolf von Morlot   9 August [1844]
letters.summary:
Declines to undertake to have AM’s journal published but recommends possible publishers in England.

Expresses scepticism about AM’s glacier theory. Emphasises role of floating ice instead. Mentions article by William Hopkins on movement of glaciers.

letters.title: To Henry Denny   12 August [1844]
letters.summary: Can hardly believe he made a mistake in specimens sent to HD. Recopies numbers in case he transposed them. [Has to do with lice taken from a specimen ofapereaand put into spirits duringBeaglevoyage.]

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   29 [August 1844]
letters.summary: Encloses pamphlet from Ehrenberg who asks about deep-sea soundings from JDH’s voyage.

letters.title: To Leonard Horner   29 August [1844]
letters.summary:
Thanks Horner for his letter [aboutVolcanic islands].

Discusses craters of elevation with respect to the views of Leopold von Buch and Élie de Beaumont. Compares Lyell’s views to those of continental geologists. Mentions reading A. D. d’Orbigny [Voyage dans l’Amérique méridionale(1835–47)].

Encloses note from Emma to Mrs Horner, inviting the Horners to visit Down.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [1 September 1844]
letters.summary:
Asks about CL’s new book [Travels in North America(1845)].

Discusses views of A. D. d’Orbigny on elevation.

Mentions reading W. H. Prescott [History of the conquest of Mexico(1843)].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [c. 3 September 1844]
letters.summary: Suggests there is a direct relation between temperature and abundance of plant species.

letters.title: To C. G. Ehrenberg   5 September [1844]
letters.summary:
Has at last received first letter CGE wrote.

More specimens being sent.

Sends his sketch of paper ["Fine dust in the Atlantic Ocean" (1846),Collected papers1: 199–203].

D’Orbigny considers Pampas clay deposit result of debacle. CD cannot doubt it is slow, estuary deposit. Would be grateful for information on this point.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker  [8 September 1844]
letters.summary:
Acknowledges note and parcel for Ehrenberg.

Considers why different areas have different numbers of species. Gives an example opposing JDH’s view that paucity of species results from vicissitudes of climate. CD has concluded that species are most numerous in areas that have most often been divided, isolated from, and then reunited with, other areas. Cannot give detailed reasons but believes that "isolation is the chief concomitant or cause of the appearance ofnewforms".

letters.title: ToGardeners’ Chronicle and Agricultural Gazette  [before 14 September 1844]
letters.summary: Referring to a correspondent who had written aboutPelargoniumplants whose leaves had become regularly edged with white, CD reports that nearly all the young leaves of box-trees he had planted have become symmetrically tipped with white. Though these facts seem trivial, CD believes the first appearance of any peculiarity which tends to become hereditary deserves being recorded.

letters.title: ToGardeners’ Chronicle and Agricultural Gazette  [before 14 September 1844]
letters.summary: Asks whether salt and carbonate of lime (in the form of seashells) would act upon each other if slightly moistened and left in great quantities together. The question occurs from CD’s having found in Peru a great bed of recent shells that were mixed with salt, decayed and corroded "in a singular manner". Mentions, as relevant to the value of seashells as manure, that they are dissolved more rapidly by water than any other form of carbonate of lime.

letters.title: To E. A. Darwin   [before 1 October 1844]
letters.summary: Writes about canal shares EAD holds as trustee.

letters.title: To Solicitor?   1 October 1844
letters.summary: CD and Emma request transfer of some shares to E. A. Darwin.

letters.title: To Adolf von Morlot   10 October [1844]
letters.summary: Says AM’s letters on glacial action not publishable since they do not give facts. Suggests readings on the subject of glaciers. Expresses doubts about AM’s theory that Scandinavian glaciers brought the boulders he was studying.

letters.title: To James David Forbes   11 October [1844]
letters.summary: Discusses a specimen of Mexican obsidian with an unusual laminated structure.

letters.title: To Leonard Jenyns   12 October [1844]
letters.summary: Asks whether LJ can throw light on this subject: "What are the checks and what the periods of life by which the increase of any given species is limited?" CD has been driven to conclude that species are mutable; allied species are co-descendants from common stocks.

letters.title: To Emma Darwin   [20 or 27 October 1844]
letters.summary: Has been discussing wills and other legal matters with his father.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   28 October 1844
letters.summary: Discusses the connection between climate and vegetation. Believes that an equable climate is unfavourable to increase of species either by importation or modification of existing forms; illustrates his view with reference to particular floras. Hopes to acquire facts to support CD’s idea that isolation is important in producing new forms. Considers the floras of islands some of which do have distinctive species but others of which do not. Agrees that the wide ranges of cryptogams are a consequence of their means of dispersal. Asks for references to works on original creation and species mutability in order to get the best notions of "the (mad) theories of some men from Lamarck’s twaddle upwards".

letters.title: From Henry Denny   30 October 1844
letters.summary: Has never heard of species of same genus [of parasites] being found on both birds and mammals, or different genera and species being found on animals in the domestic and wild states. Implications of this for relationship ofapereaand guinea-pig.

letters.title: To J. D. Forbes  [November? 1844]
letters.summary: Believes JDF’s discoveries in the structure of glacier ice will explain the structure of many volcanic masses. Will JDF’s views throw any light on the primary laminated rocks?

letters.title: To Henry Denny   7 November [1844]
letters.summary:
Discusses HD’s information that same species of birds at remote stations have identical parasites. Urges him to investigate N. American land-bird parasites.

Is deeply interested in everything connected with geographical distribution, and the differences between species and varieties.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   8 November 1844
letters.summary:
Sends notes on Infusoria for Ehrenberg.

Comments on distribution of species in natural orders that have local distributions. Intermediate forms between species ofLycopodium.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [10–11 November 1844]
letters.summary:
Origin of Antarctic brash ice.

Further on case ofLycopodium: does JDH know any genera of plants whose species are variable in one continent but not in another? Discussion on variations between floras as regards species richness, and factors affecting geographical distribution. On species, CD expects "that I shall be able to show even to sound naturalists that there are two sides to the question of the immutability of species; – that facts can be viewed and grouped under the notion of allied species having descended from common stocks". Mentions books and papers for and against species mutability. CD believes past absurd ideas arose from no one’s having approached subject on side of variation under domestication.

Would like to see Clarke’s paper

and would welcome visit from JDH.

letters.title: To J. D. Forbes  13 [November 1844]
letters.summary:
Mexican specimen of laminated obsidian.

Comments on Forbes’s publication comparing lava streams and glaciers. Mentions ice-action theories of a young German.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   14 November 1844
letters.summary:
Differences in variability of species within a single genus. Further observations onLycopodium.

Interested in Humboldt’s river with different floras on opposite banks, and other unexplained cases of very local distributions.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [18 November 1844]
letters.summary: Would like JDH to visit. Regrets he will not be fit to visit JDH.

letters.title: To Leonard Jenyns   25 [November 1844]
letters.summary: On checks to increase of species and the observations which led him to regard species as mutable in form. Would welcome "at some future time" LJ’s criticism of the "sketch" of his conclusions.

letters.title: To W. A. Leighton   25 November [1844?–6]
letters.summary: Thanks for procuring cuttings of weeping yew.

letters.title: To Susan Darwin   [27 November 1844?]
letters.summary:
Sends thanks for money.

Comments on treatment prescribed by his father.

Encloses notes by John Higgins with investment advice. Discusses advisability of investing in farmland in Lincolnshire. Cites advice of Sir John Lubbock concerning purchase of land.

letters.title: To Adolf von Morlot   28 November [1844]
letters.summary:
Mentions his Plutonic view of earth history.

Cites Lyell’s opinions on loess.

CD doubts contemporaneousness of extinct great animals with ice period.

Cites applicability of Forbes’s theory of glacier structure to structure of volcanic obsidian.

CD is falling astern in the geological race for knowledge.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   29 November 1844
letters.summary:
Would like to visit on the weekend of 7–8 December.

Differences in floras of St Helena and Ascension.

letters.title: To Hugh Falconer    [December? 1844]
letters.summary:
Returns notes on mule yaks [seeNatural selection, p. 438]

and sends queries on silkworms.

A bed is ready any time HF will come.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [2 December 1844]
letters.summary: Instructions for JDH’s trip to Down.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [4 December 1844]
letters.summary: Change in train times.

letters.title: To William Benjamin Carpenter   6 December [1844]
letters.summary: Asks WBC if he will examine a specimen of calcareous rock.

letters.title: CD’s notes arising from conversations with J. D. Hooker 8 December 1844
letters.summary: [Notes on conversations with J. D. Hooker.] Geographical distribution; diffusion and distribution of species. Island and mountain floras; means of migration (high-roads, icebergs).

letters.title: To William Benjamin Carpenter   [11 or 18 December 1844]
letters.summary: Thanks WBC for offer to examine specimen and for offer of slices of shells, but has no achromatic microscope.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   12 December 1844
letters.summary:
Thanks for pleasant stay at Down.

Remarks on boulders found on southern islands.

Describes the alpine character of the Andes flora and relays information on other mountain floras.

Quotes instances of seeds that retained their vitality after being carried by ocean currents.

Sends notes on the comparative floras of New Zealand, Australia, and west coast of South America.

Encloses a copy of part of a letter from George Gardner in Ceylon concerning the European character of the mountain flora.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   16 [December 1844]
letters.summary: Thanks for botanico-geographical remarks. CD greatly appreciates JDH’s valuable generalisations.

letters.title: To William Darwin Fox   20 December [1844]
letters.summary:
Tells of his father’s ill health.

Discusses mesmerism and Harriet Martineau’s recovery. If animals could be put into a stupor, he would be convinced. Suggests WDF have some mesmeriser attempt it with cats.

letters.title: From W. B. Carpenter   21 December 1844
letters.summary: Discusses microscopic examination of rock specimens taken from Pampas deposit and from Chilean tuff. Says he finds organic remains only in the tuff.

letters.title: To William Benjamin Carpenter 25 December [1844]
letters.summary: Is obliged for the account of the structure of the Pampas specimen and its difference from specimens of the modern calcareous bed of Coquimbo in Chile. If he thinks that J. S. Bowerbank can make out the nature of the specimens, they should be shown to him.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   25 December [1844]
letters.summary: Questions on JDH’s sketch comparing floras of Australia, New Zealand, and western S. America; wishes to know botanical relations between other southern islands. Botanico-geographical discussions and comments on books sent by JDH.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   30 December 1844
letters.summary:
Thanks for CD’s comments on "sketch".

Lengthy discussion of geographical distribution and island floras.

Has been "delighted with" [Robert Chambers’]Vestiges[of creation(1844)].

Galapagos flora work goes on well.

letters.title: To David Thomas Ansted, assistant secretary, Geological Society of London [c.January 1845]
letters.summary: Asks about Fuegian specimens stored at the Geological Society. CD needs them soon.

letters.title: To Hugh Falconer   [1845?–7 or 1857–64]
letters.summary: Arranges a time for visiting HF.

letters.title: From J. E. Gray   [1845–75]
letters.summary: Lateral teeth in Arcadae.

letters.title: From Woodbine Parish   [1845?]
letters.summary: Sends names of species found in banks of marine shells near Buenos Aires. Shells identified by G. B. Sowerby (elder). [SeeSouth America, pp. 2–3.]

letters.title: To G. B. Sowerby   [1845?]
letters.summary: Arranges to call on correspondent and bring some shells.

letters.title: From W. B. Carpenter   2 January [1845]
letters.summary: Says tuff collected by CD in Pampas and Chile contains organic remains. Wants to examine specimens further and hopes for Government support in doing so.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [7 January 1845]
letters.summary:
Sends specimens of a Tertiary sandstone from Tierra del Fuego in which there are leaves; CD thought they were beech. What is JDH’s opinion?

Asks whether JDH can make sense of a note on silicified wood.

Has readVestiges[of creation(1844)]; "his geology strikes me as bad, & his zoology far worse".

Would like to see lists [of plants] from Society and Sandwich Islands.

Doubts JDH’s information regarding imagination of mother affecting offspring.

letters.title: From Bartholomew James Sulivan   13 January – 12 February 1845
letters.summary:
Describes stratification of cliffs on south shore of Rio Gallegos; fossils found at base of cliffs. Speculates about geological past of the area. Discusses climate of southern Patagonia; navigation problems at the mouth of Rio Gallegos.

Gives results of soundings taken between Falkland Islands and South American mainland. Describes geology of Falklands, especially the dikes found on many islands. Comments on climate of Falklands. Discusses horses and cattle, health of his children in the Falklands. Mentions volutes found in the Falklands.

Passes on report of FitzRoy’s policies as governor of New Zealand.

letters.title: To Charles Hamilton Smith   14 January [1845]
letters.summary: Has read CHS’s paper, "Original population of America" [Edinburgh New Philos. J.38 (1844–5): 1–20], and is eager to know reference for the account of a "ruined city in the Caroline Group", indicating that the land has subsided. Refers to his own subsidence hypothesis in his work [Coral reefs].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker  [22–30 January 1845]
letters.summary: Sends comparison of the floras of Society and Sandwich Islands.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   22 [January 1845]
letters.summary:
Would like copy of "Galapagos flora" when published ["Plants of the Galapagos Archipelago",Trans. Linn. Soc. Lond.20 (1851): 163–233].

Will keep JDH’s Pacific island notes till his return.

letters.title: From C. H. Smith   22 January 1845
letters.summary: Reports on an ancient town on Ascension, which is now at sea-level and approachable only by boat.

letters.title: To C. G. Ehrenberg   23 January [1845]
letters.summary:
Would like sketch returned [see775].

Would be particularly thankful for result of CGE’s observations on earth of Pampas.

Asks that Ernst Dieffenbach return copperplate and woodcuts.

letters.title: To C. H. Smith   26 January [1845]
letters.summary:
Discusses extract sent by CHS dealing with island of Pouynipéte. Agrees account of island by Lloghtsky [Johann Lhotsky] is suspect.

Comments on view that former migration of animals, plants, and man was by continental extensions now submerged.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [late February 1845]
letters.summary:
Previous letter [missing] on Edinburgh position was ill-tempered. Friends assure him that he ought to be thankful for opportunity to try for professorship.

Reports meeting with Humboldt in Paris.

letters.title: To Emma Darwin   [3–4 February 1845]
letters.summary: News of the children and books he is reading.

letters.title: To Emma Darwin  [7–8 February 1845]
letters.summary: Mainly news of the three children.

letters.title: To Edward William Brayley  7 February 1845
letters.summary: Discusses EWB’s application for a position and his qualifications.

letters.title: To Trenham Reeks   [before 8 February 1845]
letters.summary: CD sends queries on chemical composition of variousBeaglemineral specimens.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [8 February 1845]
letters.summary:
Remarks on fossils described in A. D. d’Orbigny’sVoyage dans l’Amérique méridionale.

Asks CL whether he has talked with John Murray concerning 2d ed. [ofJournal of researches].

Mentions conversation with Hugh Cuming about South American shells. Has had G. B. Sowerby (elder) look at some specimens.

letters.title: From Trenham Reeks   8 February 1845
letters.summary:
Sends results of chemical tests on specimens [of salt, seeSouth America, pp. 73–5].

Encloses abstract from Justus Liebig on composition of bones and their ability to withstand decay.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [10 February 1845]
letters.summary:
Congratulates JDH and condoles with him on possible position at Edinburgh. Although CD will miss him bitterly, he encourages JDH to view it as a good opportunity.

Sorry to hear that Humboldt is failing.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   [13 February 1845]
letters.summary:
News of his family and his own health. He is able to work three hours a day on the geology of South America.

Harriet Martineau is greatly excited by mesmerism.

Tells of Sydney Smith’s dream.

Asks for some [S. American] potatoes to test "sporting".

letters.title: To Leonard Jenyns   14 February [1845]
letters.summary: Discusses checks on growth of species population; use of term "mutation" in his species theory. His belief in species mutability.

letters.title: From Alcide Charles Victor Dessalines d’Orbigny   14 February 1845
letters.summary: Agrees that CD’s fossil shells do not differ from those ADd’O saw in South America. Apparent differences due to errors by G. B. Sowerby. Collection magnificent; recommends special publication. Enabled ADd’O to correct error in dating of sandstone of Concepción. Lists geological periods represented in collection from Jurassic to Diluvian. Collection includes unusual group ofcrepidules.

letters.title: From A. C. V. D. d’Orbigny  [14 February 1845?]
letters.summary: Identifications of CD’s fossil shells. New species marked; many described previously by ADd’O.

letters.title: From Edward Forbes   [after 14 February 1845]
letters.summary: Sends information onGryphaea orientalis. [SeeSouth America, p. 212.]

letters.title: From Trenham Reeks   25 February 1845
letters.summary: Encloses analysis of salt from Patagonia. Cannot account for its inferiority.

letters.title: From Edward Forbes  [March? 1845]
letters.summary: Comments on G. B. Sowerby’s identifications of South American fossil shells [812]. [Notes from more than one original memorandum].

letters.title: From William Hopkins   3 March 1845
letters.summary: Comments on a compass diagram designed to show the dip, strike, and anticlinal lines of a geological formation.

letters.title: To Hugh Falconer   8 March [1845?]
letters.summary: Has written down what he gathered from HF on Tibetan dogs. Would welcome a few more details at any time, as he knows of nothing parallel to it.

letters.title: From William Hallowes Miller   8 March [1845]
letters.summary: Discusses cleavage planes of mineralogical specimens.

letters.title: From C. G. Ehrenberg   13 March 1845
letters.summary:
Regrets J. D. Hooker did not visit Berlin.

Describes legal difficulties of Ernst Dieffenbach.

Lists species of Infusoria found in dust samples. Discusses origin of Atlantic dust. Discusses Infusoria in cosmetic paint from Tierra del Fuego and Patagonian earth. Thanks CD for samples. Would like samples from sea-bed.

letters.title: From Trenham Reeks   14 March 1845
letters.summary: Discusses chemical reaction involving common salt and carbonate of lime.

letters.title: From John Higgins  15 March 1845
letters.summary: Reports that he has an offer of an estate of about 325 acres that CD may find suitable.

letters.title: To John Murray   17 March [1845]
letters.summary: CD has heard from Lyell that JM is inclined to publish a second edition ofJournal of researches. His agreement with Henry Colburn leaves CD free to publish with anyone. Will have no further relations with Colburn. Discusses details of proposed revisions.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   19 March [1845]
letters.summary:
Would like to borrow the pamphlet on variation [Frédéric Gérard, "De l’espèce dans les corps organisés" (1844), extract fromDictionnaire universel d’histoire naturelle, ed. C. D. d’Orbigny].

Glad to hear Humboldt’s views on migration. CD believes we cannot "put any limit to the possible and even probable migration of plants".

Wants good book on plant morphology.

letters.title: To John Murray   20 March [1845]
letters.summary: Thanks for note; encloses copy of FitzRoy’s agreement with Henry Colburn [see379], to the effect that after sale of first edition ofNarrative, CD is at liberty to publish hisJournal of researchesin any manner he chooses.

letters.title: To C. G. Ehrenberg  23 March [1845]
letters.summary:
Cannot doubt that Atlantic dust comes from Africa. Could Gulf Stream have brought South American organisms to African coast?

Has come to same conclusion as CGE on volcanic origin of Patagonian stone. Formation extends 550 miles.

Could CGE examine Pampas mud to see if Infusoria are freshwater or salt-water? Results would be important.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [23] March 1845
letters.summary: JDH recommends Augustin de Saint-Hilaire’sLeçons de botanique[1841]. Relates opinions of European botanists on migration and plant distribution.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [26 March 1845]
letters.summary: Has received pamphlet from JDH [John Murray,Strictures on morphology(1845)].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   31 March [1845]
letters.summary:
Hopes JDH will enjoy Edinburgh.

Has just finished Isidore Geoffroy Saint-Hilaire on animal monsters [Anomalies de l’organisation chez l’homme et les animaux(1832–7)], "and a nasty curious subject it is".

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [2–6 April 1845]
letters.summary:
A TasmanianCyttariais same species as CD’s Fuegian fungus. Did the species originate on the beeches of Fuegia or of Tasmania?

JDH gives interpretation ofVestiges.

John McCulloch, J. F. Schouw, and Lamarck on the species question.

letters.title: To John Murray   [5 April 1845]
letters.summary: Thanks for note. Believes agreement with Henry Colburn does not cover 2d ed. ofJournal of researches. Regrets Murray’s Colonial Library series will require one-fifth reduction of text; will consult Lyell on how to reduce scientific part. Prefers that JM consult with Colburn, but in case he declines, encloses draft of letter he would send to Colburn. Anticipates co-operation of Colburn, as he has paid CD nothing for 1st ed. ofJournal.

letters.title: To Ernst Dieffenbach   6 April 1845
letters.summary: With thanks for ED’s publication. "I consider your having made my work known in Germany a full & ample recompense to such exertions as I made during our Voyage".

letters.title: To Ernst Dieffenbach   8 April [1845]
letters.summary: Thanks ED for copy of German edition ofJournal of researches. Asks him to write and ask German publisher to return plates and MS.

letters.title: From C. G. Ehrenberg    8 April 1845
letters.summary:
Discusses table of Atlantic dust samples. Thinks dust came from South America.

Discusses Patagonian tuff samples.

Answers CD’s query about material from Pampas. Believes deposit made in brackish water.

Criticises account of Atlantic dust in F. J. F. Meyen [Reise um die Erde(1834–5)].

letters.title: To John Murray   [10 April 1845]
letters.summary: Is certain he never signed any paper with Henry Colburn or he would have kept a copy as he did of FitzRoy’s agreement. Wishes JM success in his negotiations with Colburn; asks him to remind Colburn that the copperplate has been left with editor of German edition.

letters.title: To John Murray   12 April [1845]
letters.summary: CD clarifies his relationship with Henry Colburn with regard to a 2d ed. of theJournal of researches. "I never signed any agreement of any kind; but the separate sale of my Journal in the first edition was with myverbal consent&approval."

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker  [16 April 1845]
letters.summary:
Thanks for information about books.

Murray is publishing CD’sJournal of researches. Would be grateful for a sentence on Galapagos plants.

letters.title: To John Murray   17 [April 1845]
letters.summary: Pleased to hear that Colburn has behaved more liberally than CD anticipated. Three numbers of the Colonial Library, each of 171 pages, will hold hisJournal of researches. Accepts financial arrangements for its publication offered by JM.

letters.title: To John Murray   [23 April 1845]
letters.summary: Has lost a week’s work onJournal of researchesowing to poor health. Has copperplate of map, and favours inclusion. Thinks book should be called a "Journal".

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   [24 April 1845]
letters.summary:
Murray will publish a second edition of theJournal[of researches].

CD has finished first version ofSouth America.

A strange book,The vestiges[of creation(1844)] has appeared and some have attributed it to CD. He is "flattered and unflattered".

letters.title: To Thomas Bell   [26 April – August 1845]
letters.summary: Asks for Gabriel Bibron’s address. He has two questions about snakes in S. America for which he wants answers, as he is preparing a new edition of hisJournal of researches.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [28 April 1845]
letters.summary: Returns specimens and drawings ofConfervaewith many thanks. Would appreciate any corrections for second edition ofJournal of researches.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [28 April 1845]
letters.summary:
First part of "Galapagos flora" ["Plants of the Galapagos Archipelago",Trans. Linn. Soc. Lond.20 (1851): 163–233] finished but not printed.

Details of distribution of Galapagos flora. Peculiarity of island floras.

Leaves for Edinburgh on Wednesday.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker  [May 1845]
letters.summary:
Returns notes onConfervae.

Has had information from Ehrenberg on organic forms in Atlantic dust.

Thanks for sketch of Galapagos flora.

letters.title: To G. B. Sowerby  [May 1845]
letters.summary: Asks for list of the Bahia Blanca fossil shells.

letters.title: From W. B. Carpenter   5 May 1845
letters.summary: Discusses the microscopic structure of rock samples from Chile and the Pampas. Describes organic remains found in the samples.

letters.title: From Edward Forbes   [9 May 1845]
letters.summary: Has marked probable depths of the specimens on CD’s list of S. American shells. Asks for details which would provide more precise conclusions. [SeeSouth America, p. 226.]

letters.title: To Edward Forbes   13 May [1845]
letters.summary:
Fears he cannot supply additional data [on shells].

Makes suggestions for Thomas Edmondston, naturalist on board theHerald, of places to visit and geological data to collect on proposed California expedition.

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   16 May [1845]
letters.summary:
Is at work on second edition ofJournal of researches.

Hopes to finish geology of theBeagleby autumn.

Hooker gives "a wonderful account" of Galapagos plants.

letters.title: To C. G. Ehrenberg   21 May [1845]
letters.summary:
CGE’s account of Pampas mud confirms CD’s view of its origin. Will send Patagonian specimens. Discusses dust-carrying winds in the Atlantic.

Was not referring to F. J. F. Meyen’s voyage.

Corrects error concerning samples.

letters.title: From G. R. Waterhouse   21[–22] May 1845
letters.summary: Discusses insects collected by CD on St Paul’s Island and the Galapagos.

letters.title: To George Robert Waterhouse   [after 22 May 1845]
letters.summary:
Thanks him for describing the niata ox.

He is delighted that GRW is grappling with Galápagos insects. Needs to know immediately whether any entomologists beside GRW, Walker and A. White have described his insects.

letters.title: To Paul Edmund de Strzelecki   [25 May 1845]
letters.summary:
Thanks PEdeS for gift of his book [Physical description of New South Wales and Van Diemen’s Land(1845)].

Asks how much engravings of shells cost.

letters.title: To John Murray   [31 May 1845]
letters.summary: Will send MS of first part [ofJournal of researches] on Thursday morning, enclosing suggested title and dedication. Urges inclusion of map. Requests another £50 for copyright, as offer of £100 was made when only two parts were planned.

letters.title: From G. R. Waterhouse   [c. June 1845]
letters.summary: Notes on Galapagos Coleoptera.

letters.title: From G. R. Waterhouse   [c.June 1845]
letters.summary: Is about to send his paper on Galapagos beetles to press. Has written some introductory material on which he invites CD’s comments.

letters.title: From G. R. Waterhouse   [c. June 1845]
letters.summary: Discusses his paper on CD’s Galapagos beetles ["Coleopterous insects … in the Galapagos Islands",Ann. & Mag. Nat. Hist.16 (1845): 19–41] which he will forward when printed. Has drawn up descriptions of several other insects from CD’s collections.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [4 June 1845]
letters.summary:
JDH’s books have arrived safely.

Is sending him corrected MS of first part ofJournal of researches[2d ed.].

Lyells have just visited.

letters.title: To John Murray   [4 June 1845]
letters.summary: Obliged to JM for acceding to request for an additional £50 [forJournal of researches, 2d ed.]. Will reconsider title when type is set up. Gives up the map. Writes about other details of publication.

letters.title: To John Murray   [6 June 1845]
letters.summary: Has sent off MS of first part [ofJournal of researches, 2d ed.]. Has so much to add about Fuegians [at beginning of second part] and so much to condense and rewrite in scientific part that he may not have second part ready at end of month; it depends on his health, which is good lately.

letters.title: To John Murray   20 [June 1845]
letters.summary: Writes to report progress on MS of second part [ofJournal of researches].

letters.title: To John Murray   [23 June 1845]
letters.summary: Asks JM to look at William Clowes’s arrangement of the title. CD had intendedJournalto stand alone, so scientific part would be less prominent. His health is poor.

letters.title: To John Murray   [26 June 1845]
letters.summary: Agrees with JM’s criticism of preface [ofJournal of researches, 2d ed.].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [27 June 1845]
letters.summary:
Busy correcting proofs. Thanks for JDH’s remarks; asks him to send any other corrections soon; goes to press with second part ofJournal of researchesin less than a week.

Urges collections of all kinds on any isolated islands.

letters.title: To John Murray   [28 June 1845]
letters.summary:
If copies [of part one ofJournal of researches] are to be sent to periodicals for review, suggestsGardeners’ Chronicle.

MS for second part will be ready in four to five days.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker  [mid-July 1845]
letters.summary:
The translation of Humboldt’sKosmos[Cosmos(1846–58)] is delayed.

Gives instances of peculiar genera with several good species in very small islands. Scarcity of insects on islands.

JDH cannot prove that there is much hybridising, but does not see why there should not be. "Bother variation, development & all such subjects, it is reasoning in a circle I believe after all."

letters.title: To John Murray   [3 July 1845]
letters.summary: Thanks JM for present of 12 copies [of first part ofJournal of researches, 2d ed.]. MS [of second part] will be sent to printer Monday or Tuesday.

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   4 July 1845
letters.summary:
On marking and shipment of fossils.

Has met the artist, J. M. Rugendas.

Discusses British and French relations with Rosas government [of Argentina].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   5 July 1845
letters.summary:
Raises some points for revision of CD’sJournal of researches.

Southern island floras. "The more I ponder upon Insular Floras the less inclined I am to admit the mutation of species to any very great amount."

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [5 July 1845]
letters.summary:
Sends the first part ofJournal of researches[2d ed.]. Explains his dedication of book to CL. Describes revisions.

Has received CL’s book [Travels in North America, 2 vols. (1845)].

letters.title: To Ernst Dieffenbach   [before 9 July 1845]
letters.summary:
"It is evident that you have not time now to pay me a visit, & indeed as Mrs Darwin is in daily expectation of her confinement I could hardly have asked you … When I saw your name & that of many other naturalists at Cambridge, I wished much to have been there; but my strength so often fails me, that I expected more mortification than pleasure …

I should have liked to have heard the Crater-of-Elevation discussion; after having read both sides, I cannot subscribe to that view; but I think there remains something unexplained about those many vast circular volcanic ruins …
