I presume it is very unprobable [sic] that there will ever be a second German Edition of my Journal … I have largely condensed, corrected & added to the Second English Edition, & I am sure have considerably improved & popularised it".

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [11–12 July 1845]
letters.summary:
A son [George Howard Darwin] was born on Wednesday.

Sends queries on Galapagos flora.

Discusses JDH’s comments on [Journal of researches].

CD feels that with his views on descent "really Nat. Hist. becomes a sublimely grand result-giving subject".

"How differently people view the same subject, for I look at insular Floras … as leading to an opposite view to yours."

letters.title: From G. R. Waterhouse   [11 July 1845]
letters.summary: Notes the islands, where known, on which CD’s Galapagos beetles were found. Remarks that in none of the species whose place of origin is known, does he have specimens from more than one island.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [after 12 July 1845]
letters.summary: Answers CD’s questions relating to the flora of the Galapagos. [See889.]

letters.title: To John Murray   16 [July 1845]
letters.summary: Sent MS [of second part ofJournal of researches] to William Clowes [printer] on the 7th and has had only three sheets for correction. Asks JM to see to it that Messrs Clowes send a sheet a day, as CD’s health is uncertain, and he cannot do more at last moment if sheets accumulate.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [22 July – 19 August 1845]
letters.summary:
Thanks for facts on solitary islands having several species of peculiar genera; "it knocks on the head some analogies of mine".

Has long been trying to discover in how many flowers crossing is probable, but finds it difficult to show "even a vague probability of this".

Will JDH proof-read Galapagos chapter ofJournal of researches?

Gives information on his Galapagos collection; explains why it differs from others.

letters.title: From Louis Fraser   23 July 1845
letters.summary: Informs CD about characteristics of certain species of Galapagos birds.

letters.title: From Louis Fraser   [24? July 1845]
letters.summary: Discusses colour ofZenaidafrom the Galapagos.

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   25 July 1845
letters.summary:
CD has bought a farm in Lincolnshire. Criticises primogeniture and stamp laws on land purchase.

Announces birth of G. H. Darwin.

letters.title: To John Murray   [27 July 1845]
letters.summary: Sent last sheet [of second part ofJournal of researches] to printer yesterday. Will send half of MS for next part in four or five days.

letters.title: From Hugh Cuming   28 July 1845
letters.summary: Discusses names and distributions of Pacific shells. [Lists by CD and Edward Forbes record names and ranges of shells collected by HC in the Galapagos.]

letters.title: From William Yarrell   29 July 1845
letters.summary: Answers CD’s queries about the number and distribution of species in certain fish genera.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell [30 July –  2 August 1845]
letters.summary: Comments extensively on CL’s book [Travels in North America(1845)]. Lyell’s views on slavery, the clergy, education, and coalfields. Has difficulty in tracing Lyell’s course. Comments on geological portions, especially CL’s comparisons of living and fossil organisms to those of South America and Tasmania; animal formation of carbonic acid and effects of vegetable decay; Indians’ use of lumber. Discusses water-borne transportation of wood, fruit, and seeds. Notes distribution of Arctic flora.

letters.title: From Charles Lyell  [after 2 August 1845]
letters.summary:
CD’s criticism of his book [Travels in North America(1845)].

Compares invertebrate animals of Tasmania and England.

Mentions views of C. J. F. Bunbury on climate of the Carboniferous period.

Robert Brown says Australian flora has the widest range.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [15 or 22 August 1845]
letters.summary:
Sorry to hear about condition of JDH’s grandfather.

Sends proofs of Galapagos chapter ofJournal of researches.

Grieves to hear labels are displaced on his plants.

May he annotate [F. Gérard’s]L’espèce[(1844), extracted fromDictionnaire universel d’histoire naturelle, ed. C. D. d’Orbigny (1839–49)]?

letters.title: To William Jackson Hooker  [23 August 1845]
letters.summary: Will be pleased to provide a testimonial for J. D. Hooker, who is seeking the Chair in Botany at Edinburgh, but fears he himself is so little known that it could only be of the smallest service. Has asked Lyell to write to J. F. W. Herschel giving an opinion of J. D. Hooker.

letters.title: To John Murray   [23 August 1845]
letters.summary:
Has again overrun his limits [in MS of third part ofJournal of researches]. Sends JM a proof sheet of his account of Cape of Good Hope for decision whether to strike it out and save four pages.

Favourable notice ofJournalhas appeared inGardeners’ Chronicle.

letters.title: To W. J. Hooker   [25 August 1845]
letters.summary: Encloses a testimonial letter for J. D. Hooker [see907]. If WJH thinks the letter could be improved CD will alter it. Feels it a disgrace that a professor should be appointed by men "who never heard of Humboldt & Brown".

letters.title: To W. J. Hooker   25 August 1845
letters.summary: A letter in support of J. D. Hooker as a candidate for Edinburgh Chair in Botany. No one better qualified. Wishes him success.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   25 August [1845]
letters.summary:
Discusses the power of land covered with snow to radiate heat.

Criticises CL’s discussion of slavery [inTravels in North America(1845)]. A review of CL’s book is inGardeners’ Chronicle.

Mentions John Lindley’s views on carbonic acid gas and extinction;

refers to the discussion of multiple and single creations in Humboldt’sKosmos.

The origin of volcanic craters of elevation.

There is a popular demand for a new edition ofPrinciples.

Praises palaeobotanical work of C. J. F. Bunbury.

letters.title: To John Murray   27 August [1845]
letters.summary: Has finished MS for second edition ofJournal of researches. Instructs JM regarding author’s copies, and woodcuts; asks to be informed if volume sells well.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [29 August 1845]
letters.summary:
Anxious to hear of JDH’s prospects [at Edinburgh].

Has completed hisJournal of researches.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   1 September [1845]
letters.summary:
JDH’s grandfather’s death.

Collecting testimonials for the Edinburgh chair.

letters.title: To John Murray   2 September [1845]
letters.summary: Encloses signed receipt for promissory note for £150 from John Murray. Hopes to have pleasure of meeting him soon. Is particularly obliged for promise of information on success of volume.

letters.title: To Susan Darwin   3[–4] September 1845
letters.summary: "All about household and money matters." The family is now living on about £1000 per annum. Plans a new walk and additions to the house.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker  [3 September 1845]
letters.summary:
Condolences on JDH’s grandfather’s death.

When his wife can move, they will go to Staffordshire.

Returns some books; would like to see copy ofKosmos[by Alexander von Humboldt]. Would be proud owner of JDH’s work [Flora Antarctica(1844–7)].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker  [4–9 September 1845]
letters.summary:
The most experienced botanists argue for the "validity of species in nature". Against taxonomic "splitters".

CD’s Cape Tres Montes plants.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [10 September 1845]
letters.summary:
Going to Shrewsbury on Monday.

Means to attempt the question of species: "though I shall get more kicks than half-pennies, I will, life serving, attempt my work".

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   14 September 1845
letters.summary:
Thanks forJournal of researches.

Puzzled over pea flower from Cape Tres Montes.

Thinks species a fair and most profitable subject for discussion, but has no formed opinion of his own.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [18 September 1845]
letters.summary:
Kosmos[by Alexander von Humboldt] has arrived safely.

CD acknowledges his presumption in speculating on variation without having worked out his due share of species, but "for nine years it has been anyhow the greatest amusement to me".

letters.title: From John Higgins   2 October 1845
letters.summary: Sends a list of the work he feels should be done at Beesby [Lincolnshire] to put the farm in order. Hopes to get purchase deeds completed by 10 October.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [8 October 1845]
letters.summary: Sorry to hear JDH did not get Edinburgh chair. Invites him to Down.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   8 October [1845]
letters.summary:
Discusses American Negroes and their parasitic lice. Henry Denny’s need for lice specimens.

Discusses effects of racial crosses in man.

Describes his trip to Yorkshire.

Comments on Sedgwick’s review [ofVestiges of creation].

Mentions Humboldt’sKosmos. Criticises Humboldt’s geology.

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   28 October [1845]
letters.summary:
Comments on potato disease and its effects on the poor.

Describes visit to his Lincolnshire farm,

to York where he discussed hybrids with the Dean of Manchester [William Herbert],

his meeting with Charles Waterton, and his delight with Chatsworth.

Disappointed at Hooker’s failure to receive the Edinburgh chair; believes JDH will make a great botanist.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   28 October [1845]
letters.summary:
Would like to see JDH’s testimonials.

Disappointed withKosmos.

Has visited Dean of Manchester, who is very heterodox on species.

letters.title: To C. G. Ehrenberg   29 October [1845]
letters.summary:
Sends specimens. Asks for information about specimens from Rio Gallegos.

What does CGE mean by the term "Fluthgebiete"?

French translation gives impression that Ehrenberg attributes Pampas deposit to debacle.

letters.title: To John Lort Stokes  [November–December 1845]
letters.summary: Comments on book by George Grey [Journals of two expeditions of discovery in north-west and Western Australia(1841)]. "The whole expedition was that of a set of School Boys".

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [5 or 12 November 1845]
letters.summary:
Thanks for Antarctic flora [Flora Antarctica(1844–7)].

Agrees geographical distribution will be "the key which will unlock the mystery of species".

Could JDH look over a rough sketch on species?

letters.title: To Edward Hitchcock   6 November [1845]
letters.summary: Thanks EH for hisFinal report on the geology of Massachusetts[1841]. Comments on EH’s discovery of fossil footprints.

letters.title: To G. B. Sowerby  12 [November 1845]
letters.summary: Asks for a meeting in order to go over the shells [which GBS was to describe in the appendix on Tertiary fossil shells inSouth America].

letters.title: To Smith, Elder & Co.   13 November [1845]
letters.summary: Sends corrections and suggestions for an advertisement forZoologyandGeology of "Beagle".

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [17 November 1845]
letters.summary:
Comments on JDH’sFlora Antarctica. CD is delighted with it.

"I can never cease marvelling at the similarity of the Antarctic floras: it is wonderful."

Questions JDH on points raised by the work: absence of alpine flora on southern islands; comparison of climate and floras of Tasmania and New Zealand.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker  [19 November 1845]
letters.summary:
Answers CD’s queries arising fromFlora Antarctica.

Would like CD to come to town and go over Galapagos plants with him.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker  [21 November 1845]
letters.summary: Is busy with shell work and cannot make it to Kew. Invites JDH to Down. Intends asking Edward Forbes and Hugh Falconer.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [25 November 1845]
letters.summary: Can JDH come to Down on 6 December? If this is convenient, CD will ask Forbes, Falconer, and perhaps Waterhouse.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker  [29 November 1845]
letters.summary: Delighted that JDH will come to visit him.

letters.title: To G. B. Sowerby   [1 December 1845]
letters.summary: Cannot find two specimens of S. American fossil shells.

letters.title: To G. B. Sowerby   [3 December 1845]
letters.summary: Suggests location of lost shell specimens.

letters.title: To G. B. Sowerby   [9? December 1845]
letters.summary: Discusses GBS’s completion of his descriptions of fossil shells for the appendix toSouth America.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker  [10 December 1845]
letters.summary:
CD’s enjoyment of JDH’s visit and "all our raging discussions".

Would like to compare insects from Kerguelen Islands with those from Tierra del Fuego.

letters.title: From Roderick Impey Murchison   [1846?]
letters.summary: Gives CD page references [inThe new statistical account of Scotland, vol. 14, pp 446, 507] for information regarding parallel roads.

letters.title: From G. B. Sowerby   [1846]
letters.summary: Note on editorial details concerning names of fossil shells [forSouth America, appendix]. The Latin for "Darwin" is "Darvinius".

letters.title: To John William Lubbock   [16 January 1846]
letters.summary: Thanks JWL for having acceded to CD’s wish to acquire a piece of land to provide a sheltered walk at Down.

letters.title: From G. B. Sowerby   17 January 1846
letters.summary: Describes his reasoning in classifying CD’sTurritella ambulacrumspecimens into two sorts. GBS holds that distinguishing characters, whether of species or varieties, should always be noticed. [SeeSouth America, appendix, pl. III, fig. 49.]

letters.title: To Royal Geographical Society   [28 January or 4 February 1846]
letters.deprecated: Julian Jacksonsecretary of R. Geographical Soc.
letters.recipient: Julian Jacksonsecretary of R. Geographical Soc.
letters.summary: Enclosed MS by Lieut. W. Christopher misrepresents CD’s views. Contains errors in zoology.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [31 January 1846]
letters.summary:
Disappointed with Webb and Berthelot.

Delighted to hear of more species from the Galapagos, surprised to hear W. Indian character of flora.

letters.title: From A. C. V. D. d’Orbigny   31 January 1846
letters.summary: Sends identifications of CD’s Bahia Blanca fossil shells [see830].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   1 February 1846
letters.summary:
Goes on the assumption that each species has one origin, is immutable, and migrates.

Disagrees with Gaudichaud[-Beaupré] that volcanic island species are polymorphous.

Some mundane genera vary, others do not (SeneciovsGnaphalium).

John Lindley’s doctrine of longevity of trees is amazing.

Edward Forbes’s health is better.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [5 February 1846]
letters.summary: Will come to visit Kew if Claude Gay speaks English. Otherwise would prefer to wait until spring.

letters.title: From G. B. Sowerby   7 February 1846
letters.summary: Gives his opinion on the tropical character of fossil shells listed by CD. The shells of Navidad [Chile] are not particularly tropical.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [8? February 1846]
letters.summary:
Will visit JDH in spring.

Will JDH ask Gay what birds, reptiles, or mammifers inhabit Juan Fernández [Island]?

Has JDH seen William Herbert’s paper ["Local habitation and wants of plants",J. Hortic. Soc. Lond.1 (1846): 44–9]?

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker  [10 February 1846]
letters.summary:
Thinks JDH’s explanation of polymorphism on volcanic islands is probably correct.

Proposes experimental test to see whether alpine form of a plant is inherited like a true variety.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker  [15 February 1846]
letters.summary:
Has had to make a Post Office order to JDH payable at Charing Cross instead of Kew.

Does Sir William [Hooker] know the Dean of Manchester’s London address?

letters.title: To William Thompson   18 February [1846?]
letters.summary:
Thanks for note on Atlantic dust.

Suggested in private to Edward Forbes that bird migration might follow lines of now sunken land.

Has admired WT’s work for years.

Will some day publish on variation.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker [25 February –  2 March 1846]
letters.summary: Sends enclosure for JDH to read [letter from E. Forbes,956]. "I cannot see my way about his post-miocene land."

letters.title: From Edward Forbes   [25 February 1846]
letters.summary: Answers CD’s objections with botanical and geological arguments supporting the existence of an ancient post-Miocene land extending over what is now the Mediterranean and past the Azores in the Atlantic [EF’s "Atlantis" theory in "On the connexion between the distribution of the existing fauna and flora of the British Isles and the geological changes which have affected their area",Mem. Geol. Surv. G. B.1 (1846): 336–432].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker  [25 February 1846]
letters.summary:
Glad to hear of JDH’s botanical appointment [with Geological Survey].

Edward Forbes has written about his subsidence doctrine; CD objects to its hypothetical base.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   2 [March] 1846
letters.summary:
Thanks for Edward Forbes’s letter. Botanical evidence conflicts with parts of his theory but supports others. Is becoming more of a migrationist.

Bentham agrees with JDH on polymorphism.

letters.title: From C. G. Ehrenberg   11 March 1846
letters.summary:
Describes Infusoria in Rio Gallegos samples.

"Fluthgebiete" means estuary deposit.

Discusses dust samples from Malta. Asks for further samples.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [13 March 1846]
letters.summary:
Agrees with JDH about Forbes’s views.

Discusses A. Saint-Hilaire’s lectures and asks on what grounds botanists judge the relative "highness" of plants.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [24 March 1846]
letters.summary: C. G. Ehrenberg wants specimen grasses from Ascension Island.

letters.title: To C. G. Ehrenberg   25 March [1846]
letters.summary: Sends copy [of "Fine dust in the Atlantic Ocean",Collected papers1: 199–202]. Attempting to obtain further samples for CGE.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [25 March 1846]
letters.summary:
JDH recognises the existence of "altered states" of continental species in island floras. The botanists’ difficulty in determining a new species is no grounds for dismissing the important question of altered forms.

Will look for Ascension plants for Ehrenberg.

French Galapagos collections confirm JDH’s view that plants arrived from north.

Cannot agree with Forbes on North Atlantic flora.

Botanical definition of "highness" and "lowness" usually means complexity and simplicity.

Some plants, such as aquatic ones, are cleistogamous. Cannot see why they should not be.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [29 March or 5 April 1846]
letters.summary: If JDH can send grasses CD will write to Ehrenberg enclosing them.

letters.title: To Smith, Elder & Co.   30 March [1846]
letters.summary: Discusses publication of his book [South America].

letters.title: From G. R. Waterhouse   [30 March 1846]
letters.summary: Sends a list of mammalian remains found in the Buenos Aires district and purchased by the British Museum.

letters.title: To Thomas Gold Appleton   31 March [1846]
letters.summary: Thanks for the gift of Frémont 1845. Has had a visit from R. J. Mackintosh and his wife Mary, Appleton’s sister.

letters.title: To George Brettingham Sowerby Jr  31 [March 1846]
letters.summary: Thanks for his note; as soon as CD knows how many Cordillera Tertiary fossil shells require illustration he will make arrangements for GBS jr to begin.

letters.title: To Robert Hutton  [April 1846]
letters.summary: Returns copy [ofJ. Hortic. Soc. Lond.]. Mentions article by William Herbert ["Local habitation and wants of plants",J. Hortic. Soc. Lond.1 (1846): 44–9].

letters.title: To Ernst Dieffenbach   6 April [1846]
letters.summary:
On geological works of Tschudi and Buch.

"My health keeps indifferent & I do not suppose I shall ever be a strong man again: everything fatigues me, & I can work but little at my writing: this summer, however, I shall get out my geology of S. America".

"I found Bronn’s Geschichte, which you recommended me, very useful, for references to facts on variation".

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   10 April [1846]
letters.summary:
Is pleased JDH will attend to polymorphism and also with the botanical relation, as stated by JDH, between Africa and Java.

Would welcome any information on impregnation in the bud.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker  [11–15 April 1846]
letters.summary:
Hugh Falconer gives no specific objections to Forbes’s views.

Botanical contrast between Cape of Good Hope and the rest of Africa is as strong as that between Australia and India.

Wishes CD would leave off snuff.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [16 April 1846]
letters.summary:
CD’s suggestions for improving a paragraph by JDH.

On distribution of certain species and their variation relative to a central, typical form.

letters.title: To Richard Owen   [21 April 1846]
letters.summary: Asks to visit RO to talk about mammifers of the [Rio] Plata.

letters.title: From William Hopkins   27 April 1846
letters.summary: Writes concerning CD’s "geometrico-geological problem". Attempts to square some of CD’s observations with certain geometrical theories concerning geological elevation.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker  [May 1846]
letters.summary:
Interested in sterility of alpine plants in lowland and sterility of some plants in cultivation.

Curious to see Galapagos paper.

letters.title: From William Hopkins   5 May 1846
letters.summary: Discussion of CD’s geological problem, relating to elevation of laminated beds around a rising granitic ridge.

letters.title: To the Admiralty   9 [May 1846]
letters.summary: Encloses letter and paper to be forwarded to B. J. Sulivan.

letters.title: From George Grey  10 May 1846
letters.summary: Returns letter from CD to J. L. Stokes [see940and1030].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [19 May 1846]
letters.summary:
CD brought some plants in spirits from Tierra del Fuego. Did JDH see them?

Problems of explaining formation of coalfields. Comments on recent work on coal formation.

letters.title: To John Higgins   27 May [1846]
letters.summary: Acknowledges receipt of draft. When does JH want the money for the new farmhouse? Bankers are Robarts, Curtis & Co. JH to pay them the rent directly.

letters.title: From A. C. V. D. d’Orbigny  [June–July 1846]
letters.summary: ACVDdO asks CD to assist him in finding correspondents willing to provide British fossil shells for his proposed work,Paléontologie universelle, in exchange for parts of ACVDdO’s palaeontological works.

letters.title: From William Darwin Fox [1 June 1846]
letters.summary: Hybrid geese.

letters.title: From Searles Valentine Wood   5 June 1846
letters.summary: Variation in Mollusca.

letters.title: To Smith, Elder & Co.   6 June [1846]
letters.summary: Arrangements for publishing [South America].

letters.title: To Richard Owen   21 [June 1846]
letters.summary: B. J. Sulivan has just arrived with fossil bones from Patagonia. Wants to arrange meeting.

letters.title: To William Crawford Williamson  23 June [1846]
letters.summary: Does not remember where specimens came from. CD picked fossils most likely to contain Infusoria. Discusses composition of Tertiary strata of South America from which they came. Questions WCW’s statement that they contained siliceous matter.

letters.title: To Emma Darwin   [24 June 1846]
letters.summary:
News of progress in remodelling. He and Etty [Henrietta] miss the rest of the family.

Was sick, but "two pills of opium righted me".

letters.title: To Emma Darwin   [25 June 1846]
letters.summary:
CD has been stomachy and sick, but not very uncomfortable.

Working on proofs [ofSouth America] and cannot keep printer supplied with manuscript.

His thoughts of her, and news of the children who are at Down with him.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [8 or 15 July 1846]
letters.summary:
Regrets he cannot visit JDH.

Has been talking with Lyell about coal, which he finds utterly perplexing.

Is delighted with the generalisations in latest numbers ofFlora Antarctica.

letters.title: To Reeve Brothers  [August 1846]
letters.summary: Discusses printing of a plate [forSouth America(1846)].

letters.title: From Edward Forbes   [7 August 1846]
letters.summary: Has completed descriptions of S. American fossil shells [forSouth America]. Proposes to name aNautilusafter A. D. d’Orbigny.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [8 August 1846]
letters.summary:
Comments on forthcoming edition [7th (1847)] of CL’sPrinciples. Mentions other books relevant to CL’s needs by Hooker, H. G. Bronn, Edward Forbes, and J. G. Kölreuter. Discusses his own books on volcanoes and the geology of S. America.

Mentions expected visit to Down by the Lyells.

letters.title: To Leonard Jenyns   [14 or 21 August 1846]
letters.summary:
Looks forward to LJ’s volume [Observations in natural history(1846)].

Observations on what the world would call trifling points in natural history are always very interesting to him. Deplores their absence in foreign periodicals.

Is slaving away to finish S. American geology.

letters.title: To Leonard Horner  [17 August – 7 September 1846]
letters.summary: Discusses proposed survey of Glen Roy. Mentions Glen Roy theories of Agassiz and William Buckland. Includes a memorandum calling for a careful survey of the parallel roads of Glen Roy. Mentions M. A. Bravais ["On the lines of ancient level of the sea in Finmark",Q. J. Geol. Soc. Lond.1 (1845): 534].

letters.title: To Robert Mallet   26 August [1846]
letters.summary: Thanks RM for "Dynamics of earthquakes" [Trans. R. Irish Acad.21 (1848): 50–106]. It has cleared up his ideas on undulations. Now wishes he had said nothing about them inJournal of researches. Sends his paper ["Certain volcanic phenomena in S. America",Collected papers1: 53–86]. Wishes RM would investigate Chile. Speculates whether earthquakes coincide with moon or tides.

letters.title: From Edward Forbes  [September 1846]
letters.summary: Returns corrected proof of his descriptions of S. American fossil shells [South America, appendix].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [before 3 September 1846]
letters.summary:
Has done Edmondston’s Galapagos plants.

Dispute between Edward Forbes and H. C. Watson.

letters.title: To John Maurice Herbert  [3 September? 1846]
letters.summary:
Is slaving atSouth America– ¾ finished.

Has discovered geologists never read each other’s works – "the only object in writing a book is a proof of earnestness … Geology is at present very oral".

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [3 September 1846]
letters.summary:
Has nearly finishedSouth America.

Pleased to hear JDH has worked out identical and representative species of N. Temperate and Antarctic regions.

Geoffroy Saint Hilaire’s "loi du balancement" as applied to plants.

CD jaded by, but has nearly completed,South America.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   28 September 1846
letters.summary:
Cannot come to Down to meet B. J. Sulivan as W. H. Harvey is calling.

Plant distribution and soil nature.

Forbes’s modification of Watson’s types of vegetation.

JDH will write comparison of representative plant species of the N. and S. Hemispheres.

letters.title: To W. B. Carpenter  [October–December 1846]
letters.summary: Asks for address of the artist who drew the sections exhibited by WBC at BAAS meeting in September. CD needs drawings of minute corallines, Articulata, and Mollusca.

letters.title: To John Gould   [c. October 1846]
letters.summary: Recommends Ernst Dieffenbach for expedition to Guatemala.

letters.title: To Robert FitzRoy   1 October 1846
letters.summary:
Has just heard of RF’s return [from New Zealand]. Hopes to see him.

CD and family are well, but he is a different man in strength and energy from when he was "Flycatcher" in theBeagle.

Has just finished his book [South America].

letters.title: To Georgina Tollet   1 October [1846?–71]
letters.summary: Describes results of experiments on cobwebs, "neither spider or anything else had caused a line to disappear". Apologises for having to draw this conclusion as she had cheered him so in his work on species.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [2 October 1846]
letters.summary:
Hopes to start looking over his species notes in about a year.

Very much enjoyed Southampton [meeting of BAAS, 9–12 Sept].

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   [before 3 October 1846]
letters.summary: The potato seeds were collected in 1835 from tubers in a remote area of the Cordilleras of Chile and were certainly wild. Refers him toJournal[of researches, p. 347].

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [3 October 1846]
letters.summary: Discusses A. C. Ramsay’s article ["On the denudation of South Wales",Mem. Geol. Surv. G. B.1 (1846)]. Mentions his own paper ["Volcanic phenomena in South America",Collected papers1: 53–86]. Emphasises that sedimentary deposits are not ordinarily preserved.

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   [5 October 1846]
letters.summary:
The third and last part of theGeology[South America] will be published in a few days. Apologises for not sending JSH the other volumes.

Has attended Southampton [BAAS] meeting.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [6 October 1846]
letters.summary: Sulivans are coming on Friday. Can JDH come?

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [8 October 1846]
letters.summary:
Can JDH bring a good book onCorallinaorNulliporaof Lamarck?

CD intends writing paper on their propagation.

letters.title: To John Lindley   [c. 10 October 1846]
letters.summary: CD sends a copy [ofSouth America] toGardeners’ Chronicleand refers to a passage on Patagonian salt; asks for backing and specific information supplementing his suggestion that an added chloride would increase the salt’s preserving power.

letters.title: To A. C. Ramsay   10 October [1846]
letters.summary:
Thanks ACR for paper and comments on it ["On the denudation of South Wales",Mem. Geol. Surv. G. B.1 (1846): 297–335].

Sends copy ofSouth America.

Discusses action of the sea.

Criticises ACR’s views on sudden elevation of mountain chains.

letters.title: To Leonard Jenyns   17 October [1846]
letters.summary:
Comments on LJ’sObservations[in natural history(1846)].

Discusses variation among British birds, and the conflicting treatment of bird species by C. W. L. Gloger and C. L. Brehm.

Describes collecting incident of his student days involvingCarabus.

Mentions squirrels eating insects.

Astonished to hear of terrestrialPlanaria.

Comments on BAAS meeting in Southampton.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [18 October 1846]
letters.summary: Will be in London tomorrow and will try to pop over to Kew.

letters.title: To Joseph Beete Jukes  [18 October 1846]
letters.summary: Knows nothing about missing fossils collected by J. L. Stokes.

letters.title: To Smith, Elder & Co.   [19 October 1846]
letters.summary: Objects to the stupid way a plate is bound intoSouth America.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [26 October 1846]
letters.summary: Many thanks for JDH’s beautiful cirripede drawing. Questions on JDH’s observations.

letters.title: To Librarian   27 October [1846 or 1848?]
letters.summary: Orders Andrew Knight’s paper ["An account of some experiments on the fecundation of vegetables",Philos. Trans. R. Soc. Lond.(1799): 195–204] and J. E. Gray’s book [Gleanings from the menagerie and aviary at Knowsley Hall(1846)].

letters.title: To Robert FitzRoy   28 October [1846]
letters.summary: Has read RF’s pamphlet on New Zealand [Remarks on New Zealand(1846)]. Sympathises with his difficulties as Governor.

letters.title: To Daniel Sharpe   [1 November 1846]
letters.summary: Discusses foliation and cleavage. Comments on dip of cleavage laminae in mountains. Mentions views of Sedgwick and Studer. Suggests reading C. L. von Buch [Travels through Norway and Lapland(1813)] "as an amusement". Praises views of William Hopkins. Suggests reading paper by H. D. Rogers ["On cleavage of slate-strata",Edinburgh New Philos. J.41 (1846): 422–3)]. Comments on the paper.

letters.title: To J. L. Stokes   3 November 1846
letters.summary: CD’s note to Stokes [see940] has been forwarded to George Grey; CD fears he may be offended. Asks how it could have happened.

letters.title: To Daniel Sharpe   [4 November 1846]
letters.summary: Supposes Sharpe does not want Von Buch’s tract, so sent Hopkins. Asks it be returned to CD at the Athenaeum Club.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [6 November 1846]
letters.summary:
Observations on barnacles.

Would like to meet JDH in London.

letters.title: From J. L. Stokes   6 November 1846
letters.summary: Is upset by what has happened [see1017], but does not know how CD’s note reached Grey.

letters.title: To George Grey   10 November 1846
letters.summary:
CD apologises for his note to J. L. Stokes [see940], which somehow found its way into GG’s hands.

Praises GG’s work on Australia.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker  [12 November 1846]
letters.summary:
Will JDH be in London?

Cirripede observations.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [14 November 1846]
letters.summary: Proposes to visit Kew.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [15 November 1846]
letters.summary: Will come to Kew on Friday.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [17 November 1846]
letters.summary: CD’s visit to Kew.

letters.title: To Catherine Darwin   [22 November 1846]
letters.summary:
Concerned about Father’s health.

Forwards a letter from FitzRoy.

Dr Erasmus Darwin’s scientific prophecies are the talk of London.

letters.title: To Robert FitzRoy   23 November [1846]
letters.summary:
J. D. Hooker has described Capt. King’s Tierra del Fuego plants and CD’s Galapagos plants [inFlora Antarctica, pt 2 (1847)] which have extraordinary interest and novelty.

A malicious person has sent George Grey, Governor of New Zealand, a letter CD had written to J. L. Stokes, containing a derogatory statement likening Grey’s expedition to "a set of school boys".

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker  [23 November 1846]
letters.summary: Has read JDH’s paper ["Plants of the Galapagos Archipelago",Trans. Linn. Soc. Lond.20 (1851): 116–233] and thinks it the best essay on geographical distribution he has ever met with. Comments on the paper.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker  [24 November 1846]
letters.summary: Thanks for reading paper. Accepts CD’s criticisms; discussion of some points.

letters.title: To David Thomas Ansted   25 November [1846]
letters.summary:
Encloses a set of proof sheets of the fossil shells inSouth America.

Also encloses some specimen sheets by G. B. Sowerby to disseminate as an advertisement.

Asks that E. A. Darwin’s name be added to the lists of subscribers to John Price’s work on the Invertebrata.

letters.title: To Richard Owen   25 November [1846]
letters.summary: Asks to borrow specimens of sessile cirripedes from Museum of Royal College of Surgeons.

letters.title: To J. L. Stokes   [c.26 November 1846]
letters.summary:
Discusses CD’s unintended insult to George Grey.

Compliments JLS on his book [Discoveries in Australia(1846)].

letters.title: To Francis Wedgwood   27 November [1846]
letters.summary: Instructs FW to send off a bundle of deeds which he holds for their trust.

letters.title: ToAnnals and Magazine of Natural History  [December 1846]
letters.summary: Discusses enclosed MS of CD’s review [of G. R. Waterhouse,A natural history of the Mammalia, vol. 1 (1846);Collected papers1: 214–17].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker  [December 1846]
letters.summary:
Hopes JDH can come to stay in January.

Thanks for the corallines.

Mention of JDH’s capital speech.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [December 1846 – January 1847]
letters.summary: Can JDH come on 16 Jan? CD will ask the "old set" to come and also the Lyells.

letters.title: To John Higgins   12 December [1846]
letters.summary: Thanks JH for draft. Glad to hear account of farmhouse.

letters.title: To A. C. Ramsay   21 December [1846]
letters.summary:
Discusses the geological origin of terraces.

Mentions R. I. Murchison’s paper ["On the superficial detritus of Sweden",Q. J. Geol. Soc. Lond.2 (1846) pt 1: 349–81].

Comments on Tertiary beds of South America. Doubts that durable formations are now accumulating. Discusses formation of trap-rock. Notes effect of decomposition of lava; discusses action of submerged gravel on underlying rock.

letters.title: To Leonard Horner  [23 December 1846 – January 1847]
letters.summary:
Responds to LH’s comments onSouth America.

Thinks it unsound to designate a geological epoch after man. Doubts people’s confidence in date of man’s introduction.

Criticises A. D. d’Orbigny’s theory of elevation of the Cordillera.

Lists sections ofSouth Americaof special interest.

letters.title: To John Murray   30 December [1846]
letters.summary: Asks JM for information on sales of hisJournal of researchesand to procure for him a copy of the American edition. He is curious to see if the part on slavery has been altered.

letters.title: To William Benjamin Carpenter   [January? 1847]
letters.summary: Arranges to meet with WBC to get his advice about buying a microscope.

letters.title: To Leonard Horner   [January 1847]
letters.summary:
Responds to LH’s comments onSouth America.

Discusses inclination of lava stream.

Sketches in second edition ofJournal of researchesmore accurate than in first.

letters.title: To Robert Hutton   [1847 – 12 November 1848]
letters.summary: Tells RH that he has secured an introduction to Lady Emily Finc[-Hatton] through a friend of his father’s. Thanks RH for his efforts.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [1847 or 1848]
letters.summary: Replies to note from CL asking about views of glaciers.

letters.title: To Richard Owen   [1847?]
letters.summary: Asks to meet RO to get his opinion on zoological points.

letters.title: To J. L. Stokes   2 January [1847]
letters.summary:
Thanks for sending his "magnificent book" [Discoveries in Australia(1846)].

Asks JLS to visit Down on "Saturday the 16th" and Sunday. He has also invited Forbes, Falconer, Hooker and Waterhouse. [See1036.]

letters.title: To Daniel Sharpe   [19 January 1847]
letters.summary: Comments on letter by Bernhard Studer ["Remarks on the geological relations of the gneiss of the Alps",Edinburgh New Philos. J.42 (1846–7): 186] and on article by DS ["On slaty cleavage",J. Geol. Soc. Lond.3 (1847): 74–105]. Discusses geological cleavage and foliation.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [on or before 20 January 1847]
letters.summary: Quotes fromSouth America[p. 167] on the foliation of metamorphic rocks.

letters.title: To Bernhard Studer   20 January [1847]
letters.summary:
Much interested in BS’s letter on gneiss ["Remarks on the geological relations of the gneiss of the Alps",Edinburgh New Philos. J.42 (1847): 186–7].

Sends copy ofSouth America.

Has shown that lamination of metamorphic schists closely allied with cleavage.

letters.title: To Leonard Jenyns   21 [January 1847]
letters.summary: Acknowledges receipt of [The naturalist’s pocket]almanackedited by LJ. Suggests some improvements.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [23 January 1847]
letters.summary:
Asks CL to address a letter to Charles Maclaren.

Discusses recent publication by David Milne on erratic boulders [Edinburgh New Philos. J.42 (1847): 154–172].

Views of Bernhard Studer on foliation of gneiss in the Alps. Asks CL to tell Leonard Horner of Studer’s views.

letters.title: To Daniel Sharpe   [23 January 1847]
letters.summary: Comments on manuscript [? "On slaty cleavage",J. Geol. Soc. Lond.5 (1849): 111–29]. Discusses phenomenon of cleavage. Will write to J. D. Forbes about DS’s paper.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [24 January 1847]
letters.summary:
Comments on investigation of coral reefs by A. A. Gould, particularly the reefs around Tahiti. Mentions description of reefs of Tahiti by W. Forbes.

Hooker’s view of work by C. J. F. Bunbury.

letters.title: To Joseph Dalton Hooker   8 [February 1847]
letters.summary:
Cirripede observations.

Would like to hear what JDH has to say about his species sketch.

letters.title: To Ernst Dieffenbach  9 February [1847]
letters.summary:
On the results of Robert Bunsen’s journey to Iceland, which he compares in detail with his own research.

"I have for the present given up Geology, & am hard at work at pure Zoology & am dissecting various genera of cirripedes, & am extremely interested in the subject." "I always, however, keep on reading & observing on my favourite work on Variation or on Species, & shall in a year’s time or so, commence & get my notes in order."

letters.title: To Charles Nichols, Geological Society  10 February [1847]
letters.summary:
Encloses 12s for the year.

Anxious for February number of theJournal.

letters.title: To Richard Owen   12 February [1847]
letters.summary: F. J. Muñiz has offered fossil bones collected around Buenos Aires to the Royal College of Surgeons. He believes he can complete theirMegatheriumskeleton and provide other specimens. CD feels he should be encouraged in his work.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [17 February 1847]
letters.summary: Asks JDH not to think of looking at his species sketch until he has leisure.

letters.title: From Henry Allen Wedgwood  21 February 1847
letters.summary: Concerning the purchase of shares.

letters.title: To Francisco Javier Muñiz   26 February 1847
letters.summary:
If FJM wishes to sell the fossils he has discovered, CD suggests he appoint some agent to dispose of them.

Is surprised at the account of the earthquake in the pampas.

Offers to send hisSouth America.

Greatly admires FJM’s zeal

and would welcome any information on the domestic animals of La Plata.

letters.title: To Robert Chambers   [28 February 1847]
letters.summary: Asks to call on RC.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [28 February 1847]
letters.summary: Can JDH come to 7 Park St. on Wednesday?

letters.title: To Thomas Salt   [March 1847]
letters.summary: Maer purchase-money; London and Birmingham Railway Company shares.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [1 March 1847]
letters.summary: Will come to 7 Park St. on Wednesday for a palaver on distribution, species mutability, migration, etc.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [1 March 1847]
letters.summary: Illness has delayed his departure. Will try to call on JDH on Thursday.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [c. 4 March 1847]
letters.summary: Notes on part of CD’s species sketch.

letters.title: ToGardeners’ Chronicle and Agricultural Gazette  [before 6 March 1847]
letters.summary: Corrects a misunderstanding of his description of salt deposits [inSouth America, pp. 74–5]. The salt referred to was from Rio Negro, and was coarsely crystallised and free of other saline substances found in sea-salt. CD believes its lesser value in curing meat is owing to the absence of muriates of lime and magnesia and suggests that it might be worth while to add them to the Rio Negro salt.

letters.title: To Richard Owen   [6 March 1847]
letters.summary:
A specimen ofMachairodusoffered for sale by F. J. Muñiz.

Discusses possible publication in England of paper by Muñiz describing the skeleton.

Sends pamphlet on scarlatina in the Pampas.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [7 March 1847]
letters.summary:
Has received copy of CL’sPrinciples[7th ed.].

Comments on readingAnnales des sciences naturelles.

David Milne’s and Robert Chambers’ views on Glen Roy.

Mentions sales ofSouth America.

Describes visit to his father at Shrewsbury.

letters.title: To John Russell   [10 March 1847]
letters.summary: Memorial presented by members of the British Association for the Advancement of Science and other scientific societies, submitting that natural history is inadequately provided for by the present constitution of the Board of Trustees of the British Museum.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [14 March 1847]
letters.summary: Thanks for JDH’s notes on species sketch. Proposes to drive to Kew to discuss them with him.

letters.title: To Gustav von Leonhard  20 March [1847]
letters.summary:
Honoured by GL’s review ofVolcanic islands.

Sends copy [ofSouth America].

letters.title: To Bernhard Studer  21 March [1847]
letters.summary:
Sends copy ofSouth America.

Will consult BS’s article in theBulletin.

Recommends article by Daniel Sharpe ["On slaty cleavage",J. Geol. Soc. Lond.3 (1847): 74–105].

Cites his description of thin laminae in volcanic rocks inVolcanic islands. Suggests similar process may have affected metamorphic schists.

Thanks him for offer of his book [Lehrbuch der physikalischen Geographie und Geologie(1844–7)]. Since he reads German poorly, BS should send book only if short and inexpensive.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [23 March 1847]
letters.summary: Health permitting, proposes to visit Kew on Friday.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [25 March 1847]
letters.summary:
Health bad, cannot get to Kew.

Will sendNulliporaeto [L. A.?] Reeve.

letters.title: To William Henry Harvey   [7 April 1847]
letters.summary: Descriptions of the algae specimens found on theBeaglevoyage.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   7 April [1847]
letters.summary:
JDH’s proposed India trip.

Will sorely miss discussions with JDH on species theory.

CD is getting on wretchedly with cirripedes.

letters.title: To John Forbes Royle   [12 April – 17 May 1847]
letters.summary: Will send village carrier for volumes [of theTrans. Agric. & Hortic. Soc. India].

letters.title: To J. F. Royle   [16 April – 21 May 1847]
letters.summary:
CD understands that JFR cannot lend him the volumes [ofTrans. Agric. & Hortic. Soc. India] at present. Thanks for offer to inform him of other works on the breeds of animals in India.

CD fears his belonging to the new club [Philosophical Club of the Royal Society] would be useless, since he is seldom able to dine out.

letters.title: To Robert Patterson   17 April [1847]
letters.summary: Admires RP’s volume [Introduction to zoology, pt 1 (1846)]; he has condensed a great deal of accurate information. CD hopes some good naturalists will spring up as a result.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [18 April 1847]
letters.summary:
Thanks for H. C. Watson’s interesting letter. Disagrees with him on intermediate varieties.

CD has read latest numbers of JDH’sThe botany of the Antarctic voyage[pt I,Flora Antarctica(1844–7)]; notes several sentences against "us Transmutationists".

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [1 May 1847]
letters.summary:
Delighted that Brongniart thinksSigillariaaquatic, and that E. W. Binney thinks coal is a sort of submarine peat. Thinks coal-plants will prove to be aquatic, though JDH will sneer at this.

Has acquired a new microscope.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [after 1 May 1847]
letters.summary: [Extract of letter to WJH from T. E. Cantor] on zoological distribution in the Malay Peninsula.

letters.title: To Adolf Wilhelm Hermann Kolbe   5 May [1847]
letters.summary: Sends parcel of specimens for R. W. Bunsen.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [6 May 1847]
letters.summary: CD defends his position on submarine coal formation and coal-plants against JDH’s strong objections.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [12 May 1847]
letters.summary: Thinks JDH should arrange his facts against the aquatic formation of coal.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [22 May 1847]
letters.summary: CD would like to call on JDH.

letters.title: To John Higgins   25 May [1847]
letters.summary:
Discusses accounts.

Cannot visit Alford [farm] this summer.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [25 May 1847]
letters.summary: Will call on JDH on Thursday, if convenient.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [28 May 1847]
letters.summary:
Has heard JDH does not return until tomorrow, so will not be able to see him at Kew but hopes to do so at Oxford meeting of BAAS.

Bunbury and Falconer strongly against idea of coal being submarine.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [2 June 1847]
letters.summary:
Encloses quasi-hybridLaburnum.

Suggests a new view of symmetry of flowers.

Will discuss coal and species sketch at Oxford [BAAS meeting (1847)].

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [2 June 1847]
letters.summary:
Comments on correspondence between CL and Whewell [concerning university reform].

Criticises S. G. Morton’s "Hybridity in animals" [Am. J. Sci.2d ser. 3 (1847): 39–50, 203–12].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [10 June 1847]
letters.summary:
Gives further details on peculiarLaburnum.

Can JDH lend him a full treatise on grafting?

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [12 June 1847]
letters.summary: Encloses another specimen of the "bilateral"Laburnumflower.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   16 June 1847
letters.summary:
JDH’s aunt cannot find lodgings for CD.

Similarities between floras of Tierra del Fuego, Van Diemen’s Land, and New Zealand; does not feel migration sufficient explanation.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [17 June 1847]
letters.summary: CD will take a room in Magdalen Hall at Oxford; thanks JDH’s aunt for trouble.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [19 June 1847]
letters.summary:
JDH’s books have arrived.

Glad to hear of new plants from Van Diemen’s Land and New Zealand.

letters.title: To Josiah Wedgwood III   [22 June – 13 August 1847]
letters.summary: Wants JW’s permission to carry out certain investments.

letters.title: To James Clark Ross  [27 June 1847]
letters.summary: Must decline invitation for dinner; he is unwell.

letters.title: To Bernhard Studer   4 July [1847]
letters.summary: Glad BS intends to visit England. Fears there will be few geologists in London in August. Would be truly glad to see BS at Down, but cannot offer much geological information respecting England.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   15 [July 1847]
letters.summary: Must look after his wife, so is unable to come to visit.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [19 July 1847]
letters.summary:
Congratulations on JDH’s engagement.

Sorry JDH is so determined on an expedition.

letters.title: To Henry Denny   21 July [1847]
letters.summary:
Regrets not seeing HD at Oxford meeting [of BAAS].

He may keep duplicates of parasitic insects from CD’s collection. Lyell has collectedPediculifor HD from Negroes in North America.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   28 July [1847]
letters.summary: Cannot come to Hitcham as he is anticipating a visit from Bernhard Studer of Bern.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [4 August 1847]
letters.summary:
Wants to go over remainder of species sketch when he sees JDH.

Urges JDH to go to Scotland.

Pleased JDH works on geographical distribution of Van Diemen’s Land flora.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [12 August 1847]
letters.summary: Planning a visit to Kew. Wishes to meet H. C. Watson.

letters.title: To Bernhard Studer   13 August [1847]
letters.summary:
Invites BS to visit Down. Advises him to call on Daniel Sharpe. Suggests he see the work of the Ordnance Survey in Wales.

Offers to lend him Murchison’sThe Silurian system[3 vols. (1839)].

letters.title: To J. F. Royle   14 August [1847]
letters.summary:
CD thanks JFR for remembering about the work he wanted to borrow [Trans. Agric. & Hortic. Soc. India].

Does JFR have Ambrose Blacklock,Treatise on sheep[1838]?

letters.title: To Josiah Wedgwood III   14 August [1847]
letters.summary: Sends a letter for JW to forward to Charles Stokes concerning the purchase of Leeds and Bradford railway shares for Emma Darwin’s trust fund.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [18 August 1847]
letters.summary: Will visit JDH on Friday. Coming by phaeton to save five changes of conveyance.

letters.title: To Henry Thomas De la Beche   19 August [1847]
letters.summary:
Bernhard Studer has been at Down. Studer will not be able to join HDelaB’s Ordnance Survey working party.

CD is glad to hear about very old rocks under Silurians. "There is something grand and mysterious at these depths."

letters.title: To Josiah Wedgwood III   [20? August 1847]
letters.summary: Discusses the buying and selling of certain railway shares.

letters.title: To Josiah Wedgwood III   [22 August? 1847]
letters.summary:
Writes concerning Charles Stokes’s purchase of stock in the Leeds and Bradford Guaranteed Railway.

Is glad that JW III is settled for life at Leith Hill Place.

letters.title: To J. F. Royle   1 September [1847]
letters.summary: Returns JFR’s copies ofTransactions[Agric. & Hortic. Soc. India]. Has not found quite as much as he thought he might on varieties of Indian domestic animals and plants; "the attempts at introduction have been too recent for the effects, if any, of climate to have been developed". Is impressed by the work of the English in India.

letters.title: To Mary Anne Theresa Whitby  2 September [1847]
letters.summary: Questions Mrs W on difference in flight capacity of male and female silkworm moths and asks her for results of experiments he suggested she do with silkworms to determine hereditariness of dark "eyebrows". [SeeVariation1: 302.]

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   8 [September 1847]
letters.summary: Discusses David Milne’s Glen Roy paper ["On the parallel roads of Lochaber",Trans. R. Soc. Edinburgh16 (1849): 395–418]. Rejects Milne’s theory that outlet of Glen Roy is blocked by detritus. Impressed by Milne’s discovery of an outlet at the level of the second shelf. Believes this strengthens theory that lakes were formed by glacier blocking Glen Roy. Offers arguments against glacier theory.

letters.title: To John Higgins   10 September [1847]
letters.summary: Agrees to lease land to Mr Mason. Discusses arrangements for bank draft.

letters.title: To Robert Chambers  11 September 1847
letters.summary:
Comments on David Milne’s paper ["On the parallel roads of Lochaber" (1847),Trans. R. Soc. Edinburgh16 (1849): 395–418]. CD still believes in marine origin. Rejects barrier of detritus at mouth of Glen Roy. If roads were formed by lake, it must have been ice-lake.

Comments on evidence of glaciers and icebergs in North Wales. Thinks pass caused by tidal channel, not river. Suggests that RC make altitude measurements at various points.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [12 September 1847]
letters.summary:
David Milne’s attack on his Glen Roy paper ["On the parallel roads of Lochaber", (1847)Trans. R. Soc. Edinburgh16 (1849): 395–418] made CD horribly sick.

Wants Thomas Thomson to establish geographical range of erratic boulders in India.

letters.title: To David Milne   20 [September 1847]
letters.summary:
Comments on paper by DM ["On the parallel roads of Lochaber", (1847)Trans. R. Soc. Edinburgh16 (1849): 395–418]. "I am not in the least convinced about the Barriers … [but] I am very much staggered in favour of the ice-lake theory of Agassiz & [William] Buckland." Will "send a letter to the Scotsman, in which I give briefly my present impression".

Cites facts mentioned inSouth Americapossibly of use to DM.

letters.title: To theScotsman  [after 20 September 1847]
letters.summary: Comments on article by David Milne ["On the parallel roads of Lochaber" (1847),Trans. R. Soc. Edinburgh16 (1849): 395–418]. Refers to his paper on Glen Roy [Collected papers1: 87–137]. Comments on Louis Agassiz’s article ["The glacial theory and its recent progress",Edinburgh New Philos. J.33 (1842): 217–83]. Cites his own observations on glaciers in N. Wales. Discusses possibility of ice barrier creating lake. Notes objections to theory of an ice barrier. Defends his own theory that the roads are sea-beaches. Suggests questions for further investigation.

letters.title: To William Baxter   2 October [1847?]
letters.summary: Reorders six 2–oz bottles with corks.

letters.title: To Mary Elizabeth Lyell   [4 October 1847]
letters.summary:
Thanks Mrs Lyell for barnacle specimens.

Mentions Agassiz’s classification of saurians.

Discusses letter from Chambers on "roads" in Scottish glens; views of Agassiz and Buckland on the glens.

Is reading Hugh Miller [First impressions of England and its people(1847)].

letters.title: From Robert Chambers   5 October 1847
letters.summary: Supposition that glaciers made Glen Roy is a dream. Has received three letters from CD on river terraces. Reports on trip to terraces at Belleville. Comparison with Glen Roy.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [5 October 1847]
letters.summary:
Mystified by the origin of coal-plants.

Milne’s Glen Roy theory is absurd but, oddly, it has staggered CD in favour of Agassiz’s ice-lake theory.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [6 or 13 October 1847]
letters.summary: Difficulty of scheduling visit before JDH departs on Himalayan expedition.

letters.title: To Joseph Beete Jukes   8 October [1847]
letters.summary: Flattered by JBJ’s discussion of coral reefs [inVoyage of H.M.S. "Fly"1 (1847): 347–8]. CD has always thought hisCoral reefs"too bold and speculative", so he is gratified "when anyone who has had opportunities of observation does not give his verdict against it".

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [11 October 1847]
letters.summary: Discusses enclosed figures on elevation of terraces in several Scottish glens as surveyed by William Kemp and David Stevenson. Comments on Robert Chambers’ view of the terraces. Mentions a letter on the terraces, originally written for publication, which he has asked Robert Jameson [editor of theEdinburgh New Philos. J.] to destroy.

letters.title: To M. A. T. Whitby   14 October [1847]
letters.summary: Thanks for a suite of male and female specimens of Lepidoptera. Lack of difference in size of wings surprises CD; the female’s being smaller than male’s in early growth is new to him. Will ask a friend in India for comparable facts.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [21 October 1847]
letters.summary: On scheduling farewell meeting.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [25 October 1847]
letters.summary: Continued problems in scheduling farewell meeting.

letters.title: To Abraham Clapham  [29 October 1847?]
letters.summary:
Accepts AC’s offer to conduct hybridisation experiments, and offers suggestions.

Sends book [Journal of researches, 2d ed. (1845)].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [31 October 1847]
letters.summary:
CD very ill; tries to arrange departure meeting with JDH.

CD’s guess at composition of Maldive flora.

letters.title: To Emma Darwin  [31 October 1847]
letters.summary:
Has had two bad days with boils.

Is readingLast days of Pompeii[Edward Bulwer Lytton (1834)].

letters.title: To Richard Owen  [November 1847 – 51]
letters.summary:
"I had not heard before of Whench [Whewell?] having scolded you; I am rather glad of it …

What a grand number of novelties Hooker no doubt will bring home".

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [6 November 1847]
letters.summary:
Now plans to come to Kew for an hour’s farewell if his stomach permits.

Congratulations on JDH’sFlora Antarctica[1847].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [8 November 1847]
letters.summary: CD too unwell to see JDH. Encloses Emma’s farewell note.

letters.title: To Editor?   9 November [1847–80]
letters.summary: Returns proofs of a notice which he finds "highly honourable" to himself.

letters.title: To George Grey   13 November 1847
letters.summary: Responding to GG’s offer to aid CD’s natural history researches on New Zealand, CD suggests that limestone caverns should be examined for fossils and that observations on the presence and range of erratic boulders in New Zealand would be very valuable.

letters.title: To Henri Milne-Edwards   18 November [1847]
letters.summary:
Offers HM-E some specimens ofLernaea, a crustacean parasite onBalanus elongatus.

Mentions opinion of Harry Goodsir about a form CD believes to be the larva ofLernaea.

letters.title: To John Higgins   11 December [1847]
letters.summary: Discusses account. Glad that all is prosperous.

letters.title: To J. E. Gray   18 December 1847
letters.summary: Seeks permission from the Trustees of the British Museum to borrow the cirripede specimens in the public collection. Explains his intention to produce a monograph of the Cirripedia.

letters.title: To John Edward Gray   [18 December 1847]
letters.summary: Discusses loan of cirripede specimens from the British Museum.

letters.title: To Richard Owen    23 December [1847–54]
letters.summary: Is searching for a tooth ofCarchariaswhich he might have left with RO.

letters.title: To J. C. Ross   31 December 1847
letters.summary: Asks JCR to collect cirripedes for him on forthcoming expedition [to the Arctic in search of Sir John Franklin].

letters.title: To James Scott Bowerbank   [January–August 1848]
letters.summary: Thanks him forBalanusspecimens. Comments on his findings. A largeAcastain the wet state would be valuable. Asks JSB to mention his work to J. T. Quekett at the College of Surgeons.

letters.title: From Susan Elizabeth  Darwin [1848?]
letters.summary: [Valediction only.] CD note on verso: Athenaeum/48/p. 839 "E. Forbes on genera being continuous in time––good––fact".

letters.title: To Benjamin Waterhouse Hawkins   [1848–51]
letters.summary: Testimonial recommending B. Waterhouse Hawkins [for a teaching post].

letters.title: To John Innes  [1848?]
letters.summary: Suggests various remedies for toothache.

letters.title: To George Warde Norman  [1848]
letters.summary: Seeks excuse from jury duty on grounds of ill health.

letters.title: To James Smith  28 January [1848]
letters.summary:
CD asks if he may have the use of the cirripedes JS collected in Portugal. He will need to break up or make a section of at least one of each species.

Expresses admiration for JS’s paper on Malta ["On recent depressions in the land",Q. J. Geol. Soc. Lond.3 (1847): 234–40], with its striking demonstration of the change of level between land and water there discovered.

letters.title: To William Crawford Williamson   31 January [1848]
letters.summary: Thanks WCW for his article ["Microscopical objects found in mud of Levant",Mem. Lit. & Philos. Soc. Manchester2d ser. 8 (1848):1–128]. Comments on it; offers to send Ascension Island specimens. Urges WCW to re-examine coal-beds for Infusoria to determine whether intervening beds were deposited by sea-, brackish, or fresh water.

letters.title: To John Frederick William Herschel   4 February 1848
letters.summary: Undertakes to write geological part of Admiralty Instructions [A manual of scientific enquiry(1849),Collected papers1: 227–50]. Has doubts as to his success.

letters.title: To Richard Owen   [4 February 1848]
letters.summary:
Has been invited to contribute geological instructions [to J. F. W. Herschel, ed.,Manual of scientific enquiry(1849);Collected papers1: 227–50]. Asks RO whether remarks on coral reefs appertain to geology rather than zoology.

Looks forward to visit by Owens.

letters.title: To Andrew Crombie Ramsay   4 February [1848]
letters.summary:
Invites him to dinner on Saturday the 12th. Charles and Mrs Lyell, Edward Forbes, Richard Owen, and Thomas Bell coming also.

"Will you bring your map of S. America … and we will have a talk over it."

letters.title: To J. E. Gray   5 [or 6] February 1848
letters.summary: Thanks the Trustees of the British Museum for entrusting to him the collection of Cirripedia and allowing him to disarticulate one specimen of each species.

letters.title: To J. E. Gray [5 or 6 February 1848]
letters.summary: Discusses loan of cirripede specimens from the British Museum and problems of classification. Encloses a note of thanks to be laid before the Trustees [see1153].

letters.title: To James Smith   6 February [1848]
letters.summary:
Thanks for present of fossil Balani.

Thanks also for JS’s request to [David?] Landsborough to send barnacle specimens.

letters.title: To George Robert Waterhouse   [6 February 1848]
letters.summary: Invites GRW to a dinner party with other scientists.

letters.title: To W. C. Williamson   12 February [1848]
letters.summary: CD cannot find the lagoon-island mud that WCW asked about, but he sends other geological specimens he hopes will be interesting.

letters.title: To Robert Chambers   [14 February – 20 March 1848]
letters.summary: Thanks RC for information on hand-level; he has recommended it in his "Instructions" ["Geology",Collected papers1: 227–50].

letters.title: To John Phillips   14 February [1848]
letters.summary: Asks for the reference in which JP states that some erratic boulders came from a lower to a higher level. CD is writing a paper ["Transportal of erratic boulders",Collected papers1: 218–26] in which he believes he has the true explanation. Would like as many instances, with details, as possible.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   20 February – 16 [March] 1848
letters.summary:
Though correspondence has never ebbed so low, CD is constantly in his thoughts.

Observations on cheetahs used as domesticated hunting animals.

Finds geographical barriers sometimes separate species, but also finds species that remain separate where there are no barriers to migration.

Colour "individuates" isolated animal species.

Plains and alpine animal distribution show altitude not strictly analogous to latitude.

Impact of timber cutting on climate has led to extinction of crocodiles.

Will discuss coal formation in letter to Edward Forbes.

CD often asked whether isolated mountains in southern latitudes had closely allied representatives of Arctic and north temperate plants; JDH has found a representative barberry.

Making for Darjeeling via Calcutta.

letters.title: To James Clark Ross    25 February [1848]
letters.summary: Thanks for sending cirripedes. Cannot make out the label, so can JCR tell him the bank and the depth. Hopes to keep the specimens for 6 or 8 weeks before returning them.

letters.title: To John Higgins   28 February [1848]
letters.summary: Arranges to pay subscription on 15 Feb and 16 Aug as requested by Mr Mason.

letters.title: From John Higgins   1 March 1848
letters.summary: Agrees to pay Mr Mason as requested.

letters.title: To John Phillips   7 March [1848]
letters.summary: JP’s reference was clear, but seems to be different from the case cited by W. Hopkins about erratic conglomerate boulders. Asks for more details on the latter. CD does not think much of Hopkins’ paper ["Elevation and denudation of the district of the lakes of Cumberland and Westmorland",Q. J. Geol. Soc. Lond.4 (1848): 70–98].

letters.title: To John Phillips   [12? March 1848]
letters.summary: Thanks JP for his note and reference. CD’s paper will not deal with the general question of erratics but only their transportal from a lower to a higher level ["The transportal of erratic boulders",Collected papers1: 218–27]. His notion is that the boulders were transported by coast-ice, not drifting icebergs, and that during the period of transportal the land was subsiding. Can JP tell him whether the raised conglomerate boulders he observed were rounded or angular?

letters.title: To J. F. W. Herschel   [21 March 1848]
letters.summary: Sends MS of his chapter on geology forManual[Collected papers1: 227–50]. Fears it may be too long. Does not much like it but can do no better. After hesitation, has recommended books. Defends his point that mere collection of rock specimens is "of hardly any use to Geology".

letters.title: To Robert Ball   25 March [1848]
letters.summary:
Cannot give information about hook. Fuegian women fish without hooks.

Robert Mallet’s suggestion about space for specimens on board men-of-war forwarded to Sir J. Herschel.

letters.title: To Richard Owen   [26 March 1848]
letters.summary: Describes his new microscope and its advantages for dissecting. Suggests RO might discuss topic [in his contribution to J. F. W. Herschel, ed.,Manual of scientific enquiry(1849)].

letters.title: To William Alexander Baillie Hamilton   28 March [1848]
letters.summary: Sir John Herschel has not received the parcel of "Scientific Instructions", which was posted on the 15th. He requests anaccurate searchat the Admiralty.

letters.title: To Richard Owen   [April? 1848]
letters.summary:
Pleased at RO’s praise ofCoral reefs.

Has read with very great interest RO’s "Report on the archetype" [Rep. BAAS16 (1846): 169–340]. RO should give name to every letter or number in his woodcuts.

letters.title: To John Stevens Henslow   [1 April 1848]
letters.summary: Thanks JSH for his address [Address delivered in the Ipswich Museum on 9th March 1848]. Questions a sentence which implies that only the practical use of a scientific discovery makes it worth while. The instinct for truth justifies science without any practical results. Cites his work on cirripedes.

letters.title: To Richard Owen   [2 April 1848]
letters.summary: Apologises for length of notes of advice for microscopic work.

letters.title: To H. T. De la Beche   7 April [1848]
letters.summary: CD discusses questions about his coral reef theory that were raised by HTDlaB [in his Geol. Soc. Anniversary Address (1848)].

letters.title: To John Phillips   [7 or 14 April 1848]
letters.summary: Some geologists (especially H. T. De la Beche) doubt boulders have really been carried above their parent rock, but rather thought they were left behind as a result of denudation. Asks JP’s view of this, which he can quote. Supposes he will be well abused for his paper, but is resolved "not to show a white feather".

letters.title: To A. C. Ramsay   7 April [1848]
letters.summary: Asks ACR to establish height of Moel Tryfan in Caernarvonshire; "in my notice on this hill [""Ancient glaciers of Caernarvonshire"" (1842),Collected papers1: 163–71] I give a very much less height than others". [See also another mention of the elevation of Moel Tryfan in "On the transportal of erratic boulders" (1848),Collected papers1: 218–27.]

letters.title: To Edward Cresy  [before May 1848?]
letters.summary:
Obliged for account of change in quality of wool. "Some authors will not admit that climate has any perceptible action."

Hopes his health is re-established.

letters.title: To Edward Cresy   [before May 1848?]
letters.summary: Agrees that naval expeditions to the Arctic are a waste of money. Believes Sir J. Barrow responsible. "Dr [Richard?] King is quite right in the advantage of Land Expeditions".

letters.title: To Edward Cresy   [May 1848]
letters.summary:
May go to Paris next summer about barnacles.

Unable to appreciate second volume of Alexander von Humboldt’sCosmos[1848].

Recommends review by Sir John Herschel [Edinburgh Rev.87 (1848): 170–229].

Recommends book by Mary Somerville [Physical geography(1848)].

Mentions article [on species] by M. E. Chevreul [Ann. Sci. Nat. (Bot.)3d ser. 6 (1846): 142–214].

letters.title: To J. F. W. Herschel   7 May [1848]
letters.summary: Sends MS of "Geology" forManual[Collected papers1: 227–50]. First parcel lost. Asks JFWH to give advice on an unclear note, translated from Élie de Beaumont, on measuring incline of lava-flows.

letters.title: To John Innes   [8 May 1848]
letters.summary:
Encloses his £3 subscription to JBI’s Sunday School. Asks to reduce it in the future to £2 per annum.

Has been unwell.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   10 May 1848
letters.summary:
Confident of species theory as result of applying it to cirripede sexual systems.

CD’s opinion of E. Blyth. JDH should meet Blyth, inquire about domesticated varieties, study insular flora, solve coal-plant problem.

letters.title: To J. F. W. Herschel   11 May [1848]
letters.summary: Describes colour changes from blue to red in valves of operculum of the cirripede genusIbla.

letters.title: To Emma Darwin   [20–1 May 1848]
letters.summary:
Reports on his father’s health, and Catherine’s. CD, himself, has been a little sick.

Hensleigh [Wedgwood] thinks he has settled the free-will question – "we have none whatsoever".

letters.title: To Emma Darwin   [22 May 1848]
letters.summary:
His health not good.

Has been reading John Evelyn’sLife of Mrs Godolphin, and Mme Sévigné.

letters.title: To Emma Darwin   [23 May 1848]
letters.summary: Family news. Finds Shrewsbury too noisy.

letters.title: To Emma Darwin   [25 May 1848]
letters.summary: Anxiety about R. W. Darwin’s health.

letters.title: To Emma Darwin   [27–8 May 1848]
letters.summary: Has been unwell but is improving. His father also very ill.

letters.title: To Robert Chambers  [June 1848]
letters.summary:
Congratulates RC on his work on Scottish sea-margins [Ancient sea-margins(1848)].

Discusses Glen Roy; Milne staggered him in favour of the glacier view, but now his opinion has reverted.

letters.title: To J. F. W. Herschel   6 June [1848]
letters.summary:
Sends two valves ofIbla.

In his chapter [forManual,Collected papers1: 227–50], he will strike out any part that JFWH wants struck out, but if much shortening is required it will need rewriting.

letters.title: To John Higgins   6 June [1848]
letters.summary: Mentions his account; visit to Lincolnshire by his sister [Susan Darwin].

letters.title: To John Higgins   14 June [1848]
letters.summary: Discusses possible land transactions.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [16 June 1848]
letters.summary:
Comments on Ann Susan Horner’s escape in a dangerous incident at sea.

Compares addresses by William Buckland and CL, delivered at recent meeting of the Geological Society.

Discusses the views on Glen Roy in Chambers’Ancient sea-margins[1848].

Speculates that Chambers wroteVestiges[of creation(1844)].

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [21? June 1848]
letters.summary: Comments on apology by Chambers for using some of CD’s material without acknowledgment in discussing Glen Roy. His opinion of Chambers’ book [Ancient sea-margins(1848)].

letters.title: To J. E. Gray   28 [June 1848]
letters.summary:
Mentions returning borrowed book by Camillo Ranzani.

Discusses loan of cirripede specimens from British Museum. "In truth never will a mountain in labour have brought forth such a mouse as my book on the Cirripedia. It is ridiculous the time each species takes me."

letters.title: To Josiah Wedgwood III  [July 1848]
letters.summary: Writes about Emma’s trust account investments and calls due upon them. Sends his record and asks JW to bring it up to date.

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   2 July [1848]
letters.summary:
Criticises lecturing system in education and emphasis on classics. Has forgotten all his classical knowledge.

Asks JSH’s help in naming cirripedes, on which he is working. Believes he has made "some very curious points".

Expects a sixth child [Francis] in August.

letters.title: To Edward Cresy   [5 or 12 July 1848]
letters.summary: Has written to William Buckland, recommending EC for position.

letters.title: To John Russell   [10 July 1848]
letters.sender: Charles Robert DarwinNassau William SeniorJohn Stevens HenslowBaden PowellBonamy PriceThomas Jodrell Phillips-JodrellJames HeywoodEdmund Walker Head, eighth baronetThomas James Agar RobartesPhilip le BretonGeorge Nugent Grenville, 2d Baron Nugent of CarlanstownCharles Lyell, 1st baronetHarry Verney, second baronetPeter John Locke KingHenry Galgacus Redhead YorkeJoseph KayEdward France PercivalEdward HorsmanErasmus Alvey DarwinHensleigh WedgwoodThomas Henry Farrer, 1st Baron Farrer
letters.summary: Ask JR to advise the Queen to issue Her Royal Commission of Inquiry into the best methods of securing the improvement of the Universities of Oxford and Cambridge.

letters.title: To Samuel Pickworth Woodward   10 July 1848
letters.summary: Is pleased to support SPW’s application for a position in the fossil department at the British Museum.

letters.title: From William Buckland   15 July [1848]
letters.summary: Will forward recommendation of Edward Cresy to Edwin Chadwick, but thinks there will be no further need of engineers.

letters.title: To Edward Cresy   [15 July 1848]
letters.summary: Encloses note from William Buckland [1190], stating that no appointment of surveyor is to be made. Thinks further recommendation would be unwise, but will write to Sir Henry De la Beche and [Robert?] Hutton if EC wishes.

letters.title: To Edward Cresy   [20 July 1848]
letters.summary:
Will speak to Richard Owen, Henry De la Beche, and Robert Hutton concerning appointment for EC.

Leaving for sea-side on Saturday.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   24 July [1848]
letters.summary:
Brian Hodgson reading CD’sJournal of researcheswith delight.

Forwarding breeding pamphlets.

JDH recommends P. S. Pallas on degeneration.

CD’s facts on sex in barnacles startling.

Hugh Falconer’s health.

letters.title: To Francis Boott    20 August 1848
letters.summary: CD will write to A. A. Gould for aid. Thanks for sympathy and assistance about chloroform.

letters.title: To Daniel Sharpe   23 August [1848?]
letters.summary:
Thanks for note.

Glad DS sticks to cleavage and foliation question. Bernhard Studer one of few to take correct view on subject.

letters.title: From J. E. Gray   26 August 1848
letters.summary: Is sorry that any person has misunderstood his intentions. JEG read his papers on cirripedes at the Zoological Society without intending to interfere with CD’s work; he merely wished to record his old observations, made before CD commenced his study, and thought that by so doing he was helping CD. [See "Description of a new species ofAnatifa" and "OnThaliella",Proc. Zool. Soc. Lond.(1848): 44.]

letters.title: To J. E. Gray   29 August [1848]
letters.summary: It had been suggested to CD that JEG intended to anticipate some of his work on the Cirripedia. CD doubted this because JEG had suggested that CD commence the work and has assisted throughout; however, CD sought assurances regarding JEG’s intentions as he wished that "what little novelty there yet remained in the subject, should be the reward of my work". CD apologises for having spoken to JEG on the subject and will communicate JEG’s assurances to those who had expressed their opinions regarding JEG’s intentions.

letters.title: From Edmund Saul Dixon    [September–October 1848]
letters.summary:
He can distinguish varieties of guinea-fowl as soon as birds are hatched.

Behaviour of Malay hens.

letters.title: To Henri Milne-Edwards   1 September [1848]
letters.summary:
Describes his cirripede work. Asks whether HM-E can arrange for him to borrowspecimens, especially of species described in Dumont d’Urville,Voyage of"Astrolabe"[1830–2]. Lists species that interesthim.

Compliments HM-E on hisCrustacés[1834–40].

letters.title: To Augustus Addison Gould   3 September [1848]
letters.summary: Describes his research on cirripedes. Asks to borrow specimens. Comments on previous work on the subject.

letters.title: To John Thomas Quekett  7 September [1848]
letters.deprecated: John Thomas QuekettRoyal College of Surgeons
letters.recipient: John Thomas QuekettRoyal College of Surgeons
letters.summary:
Asks about collection of mollusc specimens he had lent to Richard Owen.

Asks about seeing cirripede collection of the College.

Comments on larva ofScalpellum.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [24 September 1848]
letters.summary: Congratulations on CL’s knighthood.

letters.title: From William Thompson   29 September 1848
letters.summary: Concerning the measurements ofBalanusspecimens with respect to growth.

letters.title: To William Hellier Baily  5 October 1848
letters.summary: Send thanks for informing him of barnacles and asks that they be sent, directed to him, to the Geological Society.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   6 October [1848]
letters.summary:
CD makes progress with barnacles. Describes "supplemental" males in detail. In working out metamorphosis, their crustacean homologies followed automatically.

CD opposes appending first describer’s name to specific name.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   13 October 1848
letters.summary:
Hugh Falconer’s misbehaviour.

Waiting out rains at Brian Hodgson’s.

Will make botanical transverse section of Himalayas from plains to snow.

Arrangements to pass Sikkim Rajah’s territory.

No evidence of glacial or diluvial action in sub-Himalayan mountains. No evidence of detrital coal formation.
