Hodgson’s replies to CD on introduced species and hybrids.

letters.title: To ?   [15 or 22 October 1848]
letters.summary:
Thanks for note and enclosure. Has written to [David?] Landsborough to say dried specimen was just what he wanted. Would like some more in spirits.

Very unwell.

letters.title: To Jean Louis Rodolphe Agassiz   22 October 1848
letters.summary: Thanks LA and sends thanks to A. A. Gould for specimens. Describes principal findings of his research on cirripedes. Is obliged for information Joseph Leidy gave about cirripede eyes. Describes anatomical features and chief aspects of growth. Describes discovery of parasitic males and a species parasitic upon other cirripedes.

letters.title: From Emily Catherine Darwin   [12 November 1848]
letters.summary: Gives details of the illness of R. W. Darwin.

letters.title: From Catherine Darwin   [13 November 1848]
letters.summary: Informs CD of the death of their father and the funeral arrangements.

letters.title: To Emma Darwin   [17 November 1848]
letters.summary: CD fears he must wear Emma with his unwellness and complaints.

letters.title: To Harriet Lubbock   [December 1848 – 1849]
letters.summary:
Belittles the loss of a book borrowed from CD.

Acknowledges cheque in payment for purchase of microscope for John Lubbock.

letters.title: To J. W. Lubbock   [December 1848–9]
letters.summary: Obliged for drawings and coins. Cannot tell what the stone is.

letters.title: To John William Lubbock [December 1848–9]
letters.summary:
Thanks JWL for the use of a schoolroom.

Arranges to meet JWL’s son [John] to discuss use of microscope.

Mentions illness.

Thanks JWL for his paper ["Shooting stars",London Edinburgh & Dublin Philos. Mag.32 (1848): 81–8, 170–2; 35 (1849): 356–7].

letters.title: To John Higgins   6 December [1848]
letters.summary: Discusses his account. Mentions death of his father and his own inheritance.

letters.title: To Maria Hooker   [17 December 1848]
letters.summary:
Returns letters [from her son, J. D. Hooker, in India].

Asks that B. H. Hodgson’s zoological pamphlets be sent to him at Athenaeum.

letters.title: To Richard Owen   [1849?]
letters.summary: CD proposes to call for tea if he is well enough on Thursday.

letters.title: To C. R. Weld   [1849]
letters.summary: Will return books, and asks for more.

letters.title: To Hugh Edwin Strickland   29 January [1849]
letters.summary:
Has altered and added to HES’s list [compiled forBibliographia zoologiæ et geologiæ, edited by Louis Agassiz and enlarged by HES, (1848–54)].

On zoological nomenclature CD cites a case in which he believes more harm than good would be done by following the rule of priority. Thinks the rule of the first describer’s name being attached in perpetuity to a species has been the greatest curse to natural history. Every genus of cirripedes has a half-dozen names and not one careful description.

Sends a paper he once wrote [missing] on the subject [of zoological nomenclature].

letters.title: From H. E. Strickland  31 January 1849
letters.summary: Responds to CD’s two objections to the principles involved in the "Rules of zoological nomenclature": (1) that strict enforcement of the rule of priority would cause much inconvenience, and (2) attaching name of the first describer in perpetuity puts a premium on careless description by "species mongers".

letters.title: To W. J. Hooker   [c. February 1849]
letters.summary:
Thanks WJH for information on J. D. Hooker’s progress.

J. D. Hooker promised a copy of his Galapagos paper. Can WJH forward one to the Athenaeum?

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   3 February 1849
letters.summary:
Physical description of Sikkim mountains.

Travelling through Kinchin snows.

Transported boulders.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   3 February 1849
letters.summary:
Continues prior letter of this date. Has received CD’s [1202]. Thanks CD for saving his correspondence.

Sent "a yarn about species" in October mail.

Some "puerile" JDH letters printed inAthenæum.

Requests CD extract anything valuable from his letters to CD and Lyell forAthenæum.

CD’s complemental males in barnacles wonderful.

Warns CD to drop his battle about perpetuity of names in species descriptions.

letters.title: To H. E. Strickland   [4 February 1849]
letters.summary: HES’s arguments are of great weight, but CD cannot yet bring himself to reject well-known names for obscure ones. Sends four cases that he thinks will stagger HES. Cites his problems in classifying cirripedes. CD cannot bear to give new names, yet may do wrong to attach old ones. Not one species is correctly defined. The harm done by "species mongers".

letters.title: To William Darwin Fox   6 February [1849]
letters.summary:
His memory of his recently deceased father is a treasure to him.

Thanks WDF for information on the water-cure. Dislikes the thought of it.

Reports results of his experiments with tied-up fruit-trees.

letters.title: From H. E. Strickland   8 February 1849
letters.summary: The priority rule has only diverted vanity to a rush to be first. Has no objection to CD’s suggestion that good books be quoted in preference to first descriptions if there is a chance by this means of developing this silly vanity into ambition to advance knowledge. Still, this must not affect the rule of priority. Responds to CD’s four cases.

letters.title: To Johannes Peter Müller   10 February [1849]
letters.summary: Requests JPM’s assistance by lending or giving him cirripede specimens. The anatomy of cirripedes has been most imperfectly done, and their classification is a perfect chaos.

letters.title: To H. E. Strickland   10 February [1849]
letters.summary:
HES’s letter will fructify to some extent: CD will try to be more faithful to rigid virtue and priority. Would not adopt his own notion in cirripede book without prior approval by others. Will not append "Darwin" to any of his species. Feels sure many others share his aversion.

Asks HES’s opinion on retention of generic nameConchoderma.

letters.title: From H. E. Strickland   15 February 1849
letters.summary: Clarifies the notion and use of type-species and applies it to CD’s problem withConchoderma.

letters.title: To Smith, Elder & Company  [16 February 1849]
letters.summary: Asks for account onSouth Americaand sales ofCoral reefsandVolcanic islands.

letters.title: To H. E. Strickland   [19 February 1849]
letters.summary: Thanks HES for solving his problem. Has some difficulty with HES’s type-species. In arranging genera in a natural order it is often impossible to say which species should be considered the type.

letters.title: To J. S. Bowerbank   24 February [1849]
letters.summary: Thanks him for cirripede specimens.

letters.title: To Richard Owen   [24 February 1849]
letters.summary:
Thanks RO for his note onConchoderma hunteri[seeLiving Cirripedia1: 153].

Has been very unwell; has lost four-fifths of his time. Will go to Malvern to try the water-cure for his vomiting, which regular doctors cannot cure.

Has done some pretty homological work with cirripedes.

letters.title: To Peter Lund Simmonds  25 February [1849]
letters.summary: Sends detailed report on the prospects for a settlement on the coast of Patagonia, pointing out many problems, and recommending instead the Falkland Islands.

letters.title: To ?   [28 February 1849]
letters.summary: Thanks correspondent for lecture tickets, but regrets he will be unable to attend.

letters.title: To William Thompson   [1 March 1849]
letters.summary:
Encloses diagram illustrating difference betweenChthamalusandBalanus. Specimens sent. Finds noChthamalusin WT’s collection.

Has read with much interest WT’s book [The natural history of Ireland, vol. 1 (1849)].

Recommends E. S. Dixon’s book [Ornamental and domestic poultry; their history and management(1848)].

letters.title: To Henri Milne-Edwards   2 March [1849]
letters.summary:
CD is obliged to put off his journey to Paris because of ill-health, but this will give CD more time to study the specimens.

Values HM-E’s opinion on CD’s barnacle work more than any man’s in Europe.

letters.title: To Lovell Augustus Reeve   [before 14 March 1849]
letters.summary: Happy to support LAR’s application to the Royal Society.

letters.title: To Susan Darwin   [19 March 1849]
letters.summary: Writes a detailed account of his treatment at J. M. Gully’s hydropathy establishment at Malvern.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   24 [March 1849]
letters.summary: Reports progress with water-cure. Describes the treatment.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   28 March 1849
letters.summary:
CD’s health and his father’s death have delayed his answer. Describes J. M. Gully’s water-cure.

JDH’s Galapagos papers [Trans. Linn. Soc. Lond.20 (1851): 163–233] have excellent discussion of geographical distribution, but why no general treatment of affinities?

CD’s views on clay-slate laminae.

Turmoil in Royal Society between naturalists and physicists.

letters.title: To Syms Covington  30 March 1849
letters.summary:
Reports on developments in recent years, his father’s death, his own poor health, publications, and work on barnacles. Asks SC to collect some specimens, if he lives near the sea.

News of FitzRoy and B. J. Sulivan.

letters.title: From Edmund Saul Dixon  [April–June 1849]
letters.summary: On domestication of pigeons and hybrid geese.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   9 April 1849
letters.summary:
Does not recommend that JDH publish extracts of his letters from India in theAthenæum.

CD criticises JDH’s observations on glacial deposits in Himalayas as insufficiently clear and detailed.

CD will live to finish barnacles and make a fool of himself over species.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   18 April [1849]
letters.summary: Continues to improve, but water-cure has produced "indolence and stagnation of mind".

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   6 May 1849
letters.summary:
Describes cold water cure he has been taking for two months at J. M. Gully’s establishment.

Plans to go to BAAS meeting at Birmingham if health improves.

letters.title: To Roderick Impey Murchison   [before 30 May 1849]
letters.summary: CD believes that floating ice and glaciers produce indistinguishable effects in actions such as scoring or polishing rocks.

letters.title: To John Higgins   5 June [1849]
letters.summary: Comments on his account.

letters.title: To John Murray   7 June [1849]
letters.summary: CD’s vexation at the serious printer’s error in his "Geology" [Collected papers1: 227–50].

letters.title: To John Murray   12 June [1849]
letters.summary: Appreciates what Murray and the printer are doing to rectify the error [transposition of pages of text in "Geology"]. But if the responsible person will be fined heavily, CD would want to "make some present".

letters.title: To J. F. W. Herschel  13 June [1849]
letters.summary:
Thanks JFWH for the trouble he has taken to correct printing error in "Geology".

Discusses Dr Gully’s water-cure.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [14–28 June 1849]
letters.summary:
Mentions illness of Emma Darwin.

Comments on CL’sSecond visit to the United States[1849].

His water treatment by J. M. Gully.

CD’s contribution ["Geology"] to J. W. Herschel’sManual of scientific enquiry[(1849),Collected papers1: 227–50].

letters.title: To Edward Cresy   [24 June 1849]
letters.summary:
Declines to canvass for Richard King.

Water-cure has benefited health.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   24 June 1849
letters.summary:
Pleasure at receiving CD’s scientific letters to JDH and Hodgson.

The H. Wedgwoods’ pecuniary loss.

Condolences at CD’s father’s death.

Rajah harasses JDH’s work. Lack of supplies, rain, malarial valleys, and landslips make going difficult. Cannot get into Tibet.

"Twenty species [of plants] here [Camp Sikkim] to one there [Tierra del Fuego?] always are asking me the vexed question, ""where do we come from?""."

From observation of terraces descending to steppes and plains of India, he thinks that the Himalayas were once a grand fiord coast.

Has information CD requested on Yangsma valley. JDH’s detailed hypothesis of origin of dam there. Does not agree with CD’s interpretation.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   3 July [1849]
letters.summary: Discusses CL’sSecond visit to the United States[1849]. Corrects CL’s error regarding location ofMegatheriumfinds.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   7 [July 1849]
letters.summary: Continues water-cure treatment at home and must do so for a year. Considers himself absolutely cured.

letters.title: To Thomas Salt 27 July [1849]
letters.summary: Returns the enclosed from his brother [Erasmus Alvey Darwin]

letters.title: To Emily Harriet Stanhope   9 August [1849]
letters.summary: Accepts EHS’s invitation for Thursday.

letters.title: To James Dwight Dana   12 August [1849]
letters.summary: Describes his research on cirripedes: an "anatomical and systematic catalogue". Asks to borrow specimens.

letters.title: To M. A. T. Whitby  12 August [1849]
letters.summary: Thanks MATW for the results of her experiments on the inheritance of caterpillar peculiarities and would be grateful for any further observations on differences in structure or habits between silkworm breeds, or peculiarities in inheritance.

letters.title: To A. A. Gould   20 August [1849]
letters.summary: Thanks J. D. Dana for cirripede specimens. Describes his work. Comments onIbla. Would like to see AAG’s notes and figures onAnatifa. Asks for references to cirripede descriptions by T. A. Conrad.

letters.title: To George Ransome  27 [August 1849]
letters.summary: Regrets that state of his health prevents acceptance of invitation [to be present at inauguration of J. S. Henslow as President of Ipswich Museum in Dec 1850].

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [2 September 1849]
letters.summary:
Discusses effect of subsidence and elevation on deposits. Cites examples along coasts of South America and Wales. Proposes theory to explain thickness of deposits in south Wales.

Asks CL’s opinion of his theory of "craters of elevation" described inVolcanic islands.

Mentions CL’s comparison of Mississippi beds to the Pampas.

Comments on Poulett Scrope’s views on the separation of basalt and trachyte.

Describes his cirripede work.

letters.title: To Albany Hancock  [21 September 1849]
letters.summary:
Describes his research on cirripedes.

Comments on paper by AH ["Notice of a burrowing barnacle",Ann. & Mag. Nat. Hist.2d ser. 4 (1849): 305–14]. Asks to borrow specimens.

letters.title: To Johan Georg Forchhammer   25 September [1849]
letters.summary: Asks to borrow cirripede specimens. Describes his research.

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   [26 September 1849]
letters.summary:
Describes the Birmingham meeting [1849] of BAAS.

His health is poor. Continues with water-cure with considerable benefit.

letters.title: To Albany Hancock   29 September [1849]
letters.summary:
Thanks AH for specimens ofAlcippe.

Discusses capacity ofLithotryato bore its own hole. BelievesArthrobalanusalso makes cavities this way.

Asks to see paper on cirripedes by Sven Lovén.

Comments on paper by AH [see1253].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   30 September 1849
letters.summary:
CD partly right. JDH was calling "stratification" what CD calls "foliation". Answers CD’s question on cleavage foliation in Himalayas. Glacial action.

Charmed by CD’s Admiralty instructions on geology [inManual of scientific enquiry(1849),Collected papers1: 227–50], but complains he does not give prices of books and instruments he recommends.

letters.title: To Hugh Cuming  [October? 1849]
letters.summary: Discusses cirripede specimens borrowed from HC.

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   [7 October 1849]
letters.summary:
Thanks JSH for information and suggestions on benefit clubs,

and for a shipment of fossil cirripedes.

letters.title: To J. D. Dana   8 October 1849
letters.summary:
Discusses cirripedes collected by JDD.

Gratified that he agrees "to some extent" with CD’s views on coral reefs.

Mentions his health.

Asks for JDD’s publication on cirripedes.

Sends message from William Baird concerning Crustacea research of J. O. Westwood.

Mentions Joseph Leidy’s discovery of cirripede eyes.

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   [before 12 October 1849]
letters.summary: J. B. Innes is greatly obliged for JSH’s letter. JSH’s observation of chalk flints strikes CD as "very curious".

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   12 October 1849
letters.summary:
CD thinks great dam across Yangma valley is a lateral glacial moraine.

Reports on Birmingham BAAS meeting.

Details of water-cure.

Barnacles becoming tedious; careful description shows slight differences constitute varieties, not species.

Lamination of gneiss.

letters.title: To Swale and Wilson  [on or before 24 October 1849]
letters.summary:
Orders books [Hugh Miller,Foot-prints of the Creator(1849)

and Carl Wilhelm von Humboldt,Thoughts and opinions of a statesman, Sir Arthur Helps, ed. (1849)].

letters.title: To M. E. Lyell  [24 October 1849]
letters.summary:
Asks MEL to translate page of paper by Sven Lovén ["Ny art af Cirripedia",Ofvers. K. Vetensk. Acad. Forh. Stockholm1 (1844): 192–4]. CD is "dreadfully interested" in the barnacles [Alepas squalicola] described.

Hopes Charles Lyell’s "craters of Denudation" prosper.

letters.title: To George Ransome   25 October [1849]
letters.summary: Agrees to subscribe £1 toward the portrait of a bishop of Norwich.

letters.title: To Albany Hancock   [29 or 30 October 1849]
letters.summary:
Thanks him for specimens ofAlcippe.

Comments on sketches by AH and on cirripede paper by Lovén.

DiscussesLithotryaand its burrowing habits.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [1 November 1849]
letters.summary: Discusses CL’s refutation of CD’s concept of "craters of elevation" and CL’s new concept of "craters of denudation". Mentions examples of such craters. Admits that his own concept of these craters was unsatisfactory. Urges CL to publish article ["On craters of denudation",Q. J. Geol. Soc. Lond.6 (1850): 207–34].

letters.title: To Hugh Cuming  [4 November
letters.summary: Arranges to call on Wednesday but declines a breakfast invitation, as his stomach is so particular that he is afraid to go about before eating.

letters.title: To J. G. Forchhammer   12 November [1849]
letters.summary: Encloses a letter to be forwarded to Sven Lovén, asking for a specimen of a remarkable cirripede. Still anxious to receive JGF’s specimens.

letters.title: To Sven Lovén   12 November 1849
letters.summary: To make his monograph on cirripedes complete, would appreciate a specimen ofAlepas squalicola, which CD is sure is a new genus.

letters.title: To Thomas Salt   12 November [1849]
letters.summary: Asks if Mr Salt could arrange to invest up to £30,000 on his behalf.

letters.title: From J. G. Forchhammer  [15 November 1849]
letters.summary: Has sent all the fossil pedunculated cirripedes in the Copenhagen collection, together with a letter from Johannes Steenstrup concerning changes he believes are needed in the descriptions.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [18 November 1849]
letters.summary:
Criticises Élie de Beaumont’s view of a right angle junction of a stream of lava and a dike.

Mentions his misgivings in voting to recommend J. D. Forbes for Royal Medal.

Notes Daniel Sharpe’s work on mica schist.

letters.title: To Thomas Salt 19 November [1849]
letters.summary: He is willing to wait until the end of February 1850 for Mr Salt to find him an opportunity to invest up to £30,000.

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   20 November [1849]
letters.summary:
Has had his portrait taken;

is anxious about scarlet fever among his children.

letters.title: To J. G. Forchhammer   1 December [1849]
letters.summary: Inquires about parcel of cirripede specimens lost in transit. Asks him to tell Steenstrup about the loss.

letters.title: To Robert Fitch   3 December [1849]
letters.summary: Asks to borrow specimen ofPollicipesfrom the Chalk.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   4 December [1849]
letters.summary: Discusses J. D. Dana’sGeology[1849]. Pleased that the part on corals confirms his views [Coral reefs(1842)]. Discusses Dana’s observation that in Sandwich Islands lava streams often join dikes at right angles with no cone. Retracts earlier denial of this possibility. Criticises Dana’s view of Australian valleys.

letters.title: To J. D. Dana   5 December [1849]
letters.summary:
Comments on JDD’s book [Geology(1849)]. Is sending copies of various geological papers. Their agreements and differences on coral reefs, volcanic geology, denudation, and subsidence.

Comments on Robert Chambers’ book [Ancient sea-margins(1848)].

Asks to borrow cirripede specimens.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell  [7? December 1849]
letters.summary: Continues discussion of Dana’sGeology[1849]. Comments on dikes of Hawaiian volcanoes and Dana’s view of craters of denudation. Compares role of sea and rivers in forming valleys. Criticises Dana’s treatment of CD’s account of coral reefs.

letters.title: To Abraham Clapham   10 December [1849]
letters.summary: Comments on AC’s experiments onPhloxandMimulus.

letters.title: To John Higgins   10 December [1849]
letters.summary: Discusses his accounts.

letters.title: To Albany Hancock   25 December [1849]
letters.summary: Discusses the new genus,Alcippe, described by AH ["Notice of the occurrence on the British coast of a burrowing barnacle",Ann. & Mag. Nat. Hist.2d ser. 4 (1849): 305–14]. Comments onLithotrya,Clitia, andAnatifa. Discusses cirripede larvae. Asks which Mollusca specimens AH wishes to borrow.

letters.title: To Johannes Japetus Smith Steenstrup   30 December [1849]
letters.summary: CD is distressed that JS’s shipment of fossils has been lost: "of all the Cirripedes in the world, I most wish to dissect the Alepas squalicola". Welcomes JS’s offer to send some northern recent species. CD finds great confusion in the current classification of cirripedes in British museums; different genera are made into one species, mere varieties are made into distinct species. If JS would give him some named common northern species, it would be of great assistance.

letters.title: To W. J. Hooker  [January 1850]
letters.summary: Thanks WJH for information about J. D. Hooker; CD was very anxious to hear something about his safety.

letters.title: To Richard Owen   [January – 23 March 1850]
letters.summary:
CD regrets the trouble RO has had about C. G. Ehrenberg’s parcel.

He is readingOn the nature of limbs[1849] with uncommon interest and admires the way Owen worked out the toes.

Also has readOn parthenogenesis[1849] with great interest.

letters.title: To G. R. Waterhouse  [January–June 1850]
letters.summary:
Wishes to propose John Lubbock as a member of the Entomological Society.

Asks for B. H. Hodgson’s pamphlet on sheep ["Tame sheep and goats",J. Asiat. Soc. Bengal16 (1847): 1003–26]. Asks for odd numbers of GRW’s work [A natural history of the Mammalia(1846–8)]. Regrets that this work has stopped.

letters.title: To Adam White   [January–March 1850]
letters.summary:
Requests AW to ask Arthur Adams, who is going on a polar expedition to Lancaster Sound, to collect cirripedes.

Asks location of "Cape Rivers".

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [3 January 1850]
letters.summary: Discusses CL’s paper, "On craters of denudation" [Q. J. Geol. Soc. Lond.6 (1850): 207–34], which "will be a thorn in the side of É[lie] de B[eaumont]". Notes evidence from Galapagos overlooked by CL. Mentions other examples of craters.

letters.title: To Robert Fitch   6 January [1850]
letters.summary: Asks to borrow some more cirripede specimens.

letters.title: From Charles Pickering  9 January 1850
letters.summary: Lists plants of Metia or Aurora Island collected during visit in Sept 1839. Flora same as that of neighbouring Tahiti.

letters.title: To George Brettingham Sowerby Jr  9 January [1850]
letters.summary:
Sends thanks for a note and returned drawing.

He is sending more text.

letters.title: To Robert Fitch   10 January [1850]
letters.summary: Thanks him for sending fossil cirripede specimens. Unfortunately one was broken in transit. Asks if James de Carle Sowerby may draw specimens.

letters.title: To Robert Fitch   15 January [1850]
letters.summary: Discusses fossil cirripede specimens from RF’s collection. Comments on problems of describing their valves.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   [17 January 1850]
letters.summary:
Account of the birth of Leonard Darwin, during which he administered the chloroform to Emma.

Continues the water-cure.

Has begun work on fossil cirripedes.

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   17 January [1850]
letters.summary: Announces birth of his fourth son, Leonard.

letters.title: To J. S. Bowerbank   19 January [1850]
letters.summary: Describes result of his dissection of one of JSB’s cirripede specimens, "now a hundred fold more instructive". Awaits fossils from Copenhagen Chalk for comparison with British specimens. Asks permission for J. de C. Sowerby to draw specimens.

letters.title: To Robert Fitch   [23 January 1850]
letters.summary: Thanks for fossil cirripede specimens. "Yours is incomparably the finest collection in the world of fossil Secondary cirripedes."

letters.title: To J. S. Bowerbank  [24 January–7 March 1850]
letters.summary: Thanks JSB for specimens of fossil Balanidae.

letters.title: To J. J. S. Steenstrup   25 January [1850]
letters.summary: Thanks JS for fossil cirripedes. Discusses the specimens. Sends thanks to J. G. Forchhammer for specimens.

letters.title: To Albany Hancock   [26 January – March 1850]
letters.summary: Discusses mollusc specimens and related notes sent to AH. Thanks him for cirripede specimens. Discusses various cirripede species.

letters.title: To Robert Fitch   [28 January 1850]
letters.summary: Thanks him for cirripede specimens. Discusses RF’s collection.

letters.title: To Robert Fitch   1 February [1850]
letters.summary:
Mentions illness.

Describes work on fossil cirripedes. Asks to keep specimens somewhat longer.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   3 February [1850]
letters.summary:
Hooker’s imprisonment.

Birth of Leonard Darwin.

Barnacles will never end; on to fossils.

letters.title: To Robert Fitch   [5 February 1850]
letters.summary: Asks permission to clean specimen. Describes research on cirripedes.

letters.title: To Robert Fitch   [6 February 1850]
letters.summary: RF’s specimens have arrived.

letters.title: To James de Carle Sowerby   12 February [1850]
letters.summary:
Because of health, CD will postpone coming to London until all drawings are finished.

Asks JdeCS, if he is able "with any honesty", to "purloin" for him a proof-sheet of Frederick Dixon’s plate with cirripedes [inGeology and fossils … of Sussex(1850)].

Requests statement of total owed to JdeCS as a guide to the future.

letters.title: To the Palaeontographical Society  [before 22 February 1850]
letters.summary: Read letter from CD offering a monograph of British fossil cirripedes.

letters.title: To J. D. Dana   24 February [1850]
letters.summary:
Regrets delay in sending pamphlets for JDD.

Thanks him for information concerning cirripedes.

Sends thanks to Charles Pickering for information about plant distribution.

Discusses boring species of cirripedes.

Believes Harry D. S. Goodsir mistaken about parasites onBalanus["Observations on organs of generation in Crustacea",Edinburgh New Philos. J.36 (1843–4): 183–6]. In fact parasites are the males of the species.

letters.title: To James Scott Bowerbank   25 February [1850]
letters.summary:
Is sending JSB sponges.

He returns thePlumulariaon which the beautifulScalpellum ornatumwas attached. [See1229.]

letters.title: To W. B. R. H. Dunker 3 March [1850]
letters.summary: Explains that he is working on recent and fossil Cirripedia, and asks if WBRHD can aid him with specimens of Roemer’sPollicipesspecies.

letters.title: To J. de C. Sowerby   3 March [1850]
letters.summary: Has lost a good many days and will need another fortnight to finish the pedunculate fossil cirripedes. The Palaeontographical Society will publish the fossil species. "If I was but better in health, I shd work quicker."

letters.title: To Charles Henry Lardner Woodd   4 March 1850
letters.summary:
Comments on paper by CHLW.

Considers effect of heat on bending of strata, and producing volcanoes and elevation.

"I can have no doubt that speculative men, with a curb on, make far the best observers."

letters.title: To J. S. Bowerbank   [8 March 1850]
letters.summary:
Thanks JSB for cirripede specimens. Discusses publication [ofFossil Cirripedia].

Discusses his membership in Palaeontographical Society.

letters.title: From Abraham Clapham   8 March 1850
letters.summary: Results of crosses inPhlox.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [8 March 1850]
letters.summary:
Comments on CL’s Anniversary address [Q. J. Geol. Soc. Lond.6 (1850): xxvii–lxvi]. Notes CL’s criticism of R. I. Murchison’s catastrophism.

Asks whether there are Lower Cretaceous beds in Scandinavia. Thinks Leopold von Buch must have neglected them.

letters.title: To J. S. Bowerbank   17 March [1850]
letters.summary:
Thanks JSB for information regarding Sylvanus Hanley’s residence.

Sends stamps for specimen.

letters.title: To Robert Fitch   17 March [1850]
letters.summary: Describes progress of cirripede research. Palaeontographical Society will publish monograph [Fossil Cirripedia].

letters.title: To Samuel Pickworth Woodward   21 March [1850]
letters.summary:
Thanks SPW for his history ofAptychus, which makes A. D. d’Orbigny’s view [that it is a cirripede] improbable. [SeeFossil Cirripedia1: 3.]

Specimens SPW sent are very useful and interesting.

letters.title: To Albany Hancock   [31 March or 7 April 1850]
letters.summary:
AH may keep CD’s MS as long as he likes.

Comments on various cirripede species. "I mean now to continue at Systematic Part till I have finished."

letters.title: To S. P. Woodward  [April 1850 – January 1851]
letters.summary: Thanks JWF and G. R. Waterhouse for cirripede specimens.

letters.title: From William Masters   3 April 1850
letters.summary: Replies to CD’s questions regarding impregnation of peas, beans, cabbages, and other plants by insects, wind, etc.

letters.title: To J. J. S. Steenstrup   3 April [1850]
letters.summary: Describes progress of research on fossil cirripedes. Comments on specimens sent by JS. Asks about age of several European formations, and for information about specimens.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   6 and 7 April 1850
letters.summary:
Spoke too harshly about CD’s involvement in nomenclatural reform.

JDH used to think CD "too prone to theoretical considerations about species", hence was pleased CD took up a difficult group like barnacles. CD’s theories have progressed but JDH not converted. Sikkim has not cleared up his doubts about CD’s doctrines.

Argument with Falconer.

letters.title: To Thomas Salt   7 April [1850]
letters.summary: Thanks for the information about a possible investment.

letters.title: To A. A. Gould   8 April [1850]
letters.summary: Parcel from AAG containing cirripede specimens has been received by CD from Hugh Cuming.

letters.title: To Robert Fitch   [13? April 1850]
letters.summary: Illustration of RF’s fossil cirripede specimens by J. de C. Sowerby.

letters.title: To J. de C. Sowerby   [13 April 1850]
letters.summary: CD wants Lepadidae drawings [forFossil Cirripedia] harder, with lines of growth more distinct; he wants no shading or similarity to lithography, which he thinks has harmed natural history. He realises that mutilated specimens may make accuracy difficult.

letters.title: To Albany Hancock   15 [April 1850]
letters.summary: Thanks AH for specimens of cirripedes. Believes all species ofLithotryabore.

letters.title: To J. S. Bowerbank   [24 April 1850]
letters.summary: Requests permission to include foreign species inFossil Cirrpedia(1851). Asks whether sponges arrived. Has not yet heard from Pearce about Pollicipes concinus.

letters.title: To Richard Owen   [before 28 April 1850]
letters.summary: Asks to borrow a cirripede specimen from collection of Frederick Dixon.

letters.title: To Richard Owen   28 April [1850]
letters.summary:
Discusses possibility of providing B. J. Sulivan with a vessel for fossil hunting in Patagonia.

Asks RO to ask Mrs Dixon about borrowing cirripede specimen.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   [May 1850]
letters.summary: Details of his continuing water-cure regimen.

letters.title: To J. de C. Sowerby   4 May [1850]
letters.summary: The Palaeontographical Society will give him only one plate for foreign species. Work should stop until he knows how many will fit in. He must know what progress has been made.

letters.title: To Robert Fitch   5 May [1850]
letters.summary: Thanks him for additional fossil cirripede specimens.

letters.title: To John Higgins   9 May [1850]
letters.summary: Agrees to reduce rent on farm because of bad times.

letters.title: To Albany Hancock   12 May [1850]
letters.summary: Mentions AH’s ["On the boring of the Mollusca into rocks",Ann. & Mag. Nat. Hist.2d ser. 2 (1848): 225–48]. Discusses anatomy and habits ofLithotrya.

letters.title: To J. G. Forchhammer   20 May [1850]
letters.summary:
Thanks JGF for geological information.

Steenstrup’scirripedespecimens have been of great use and interest. CD has now described 33 fossil pedunculated cirripedes.

letters.title: To the Secretary, Royal Geographical Society   20 May [1850]
letters.summary: Asks for whatever numbers, since 1845, of theJournal[of the Royal Geographical Society] he, as a Fellow, is entitled to receive gratis.

letters.title: To J. J. S. Steenstrup   20 May [1850]
letters.summary: Describes progress in illustration of fossil cirripede specimens. Thanks for answers to questions. Comments on hermaphroditism. Describes his discovery of parasitic male cirripedes.

letters.title: To W. J. Hooker   22 May [1850]
letters.summary: Encloses a letter from J. D. Hooker [see1257], thinking that WJH would like to see it.

letters.title: To J. de C. Sowerby   [26 May 1850]
letters.summary: Urges dispatch on illustrations [forFossil Cirripedia]; CD’s MS has been ready for some time and all depends on JdeCS. Suggests a way to hasten progress.

letters.title: To John Higgins   27 May [1850]
letters.summary: Discusses his account.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [8 June 1850]
letters.summary:
Discusses depths at which ripple-marks appear on sea-floor.

Personal and social comment.

Mentions receiving Agassiz’sLake Superior[1850].

letters.title: To J. de C. Sowerby   [8] June [1850]
letters.summary: CD is pleased with the drawings forFossil Cirripediabut wants a few corrections which he would like very soon.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   13 June [1850]
letters.summary:
On Himalayan stratigraphy. Believes JDH’s observations of glacial action are the first ever done east of Urals.

Barnacles and the species theory; impressed with variation.

Effect of CD’s species sketch on JDH’s view of willow systematics.

letters.title: To Louis Agassiz   15 June [1850]
letters.summary:
Thanks LA for presentation copy of his book,Lake Superior[1850].

Comments on species of cirripedes sent by LA and A. A. Gould.

letters.title: To J. J. S. Steenstrup   15 June [1850]
letters.summary: Asks him to send additional cirripede specimens.

letters.title: To J. de C. Sowerby   8 July [1850]
letters.summary: Has received plates. Gives instructions for scale and arrangement of engravings.

letters.title: To Mr Downie?   14 July [1850]
letters.summary: An enquiry about the availability, size, and cost of cork-lined boxes for entomological collections.

letters.title: To William Harris   6 August [1850]
letters.summary: Reports on the fossil cirripedes sent him; several are new, some are "elegant".

letters.title: To Nathaniel Thomas Wetherell   8 [August 1850]
letters.summary: Has not completed description of NTW’sLoricula. Wants permission to have it figured by James de Carle Sowerby. Does NTW have other fossil cirripedes?

letters.title: To J. de C. Sowerby   [12 or 19 August 1850]
letters.summary:
CD asks for the return of a specimen [to be used for illustration inFossil Cirripedia(Lepadidae)], so he can do some identifying.

J. S. Bowerbank has again asked on behalf of the Palaeontographical Society what progress has been made.

letters.title: To J. de C. Sowerby   27 August [1850]
letters.summary: Returns one figure and sends two minute new species to be figured [forFossil Cirripedia(Lepadidae)]. "Pray observe how time slips by."

letters.title: To J. de C. Sowerby   [28 August or 4 September 1850]
letters.summary: CD insistently requests JdeCS to have all rough illustrations [forFossil Cirripedia(Lepadidae)] done in time for next Council meeting of the Palaeontographical Society.

letters.title: To Maria Hooker   31 August [1850]
letters.summary:
Expresses sympathy to MSH on W. J. Hooker’s illness.

Will send his comments on Hodgson’s physico-geographical memoir ["On the physical geography of the Himalayas",J. Asiat. Soc. Bengal18 (1849): 761–88] directly to him.

letters.title: To J. de C. Sowerby   1 September [1850]
letters.summary: CD has received an enormous lot of Scanian and Copenhagen cirripede fossils, some of which he thinks may be better than those sent to JdeCS earlier; asks him to delay engraving foreign specimens until CD has time to go through the new lot.

letters.title: To J. J. S. Steenstrup   1 September [1850]
letters.summary:
Fossil cirripede specimens have arrived.

Describes progress on his monograph [Fossil Cirripedia].

Would be grateful for the paper onLithotrya. Asks for information.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   4 September [1850]
letters.summary:
Has heard that Louis Agassiz maintains the doctrine of several species of man "much I daresay to the comfort of the slave-holding southerners".

Homeopathy excites his wrath even more than clairvoyance.

letters.title: To J. S. Bowerbank   10 September [1850]
letters.summary: Discusses woodcut illustrations [forFossil Cirripedia, vol. 1]. Wants species descriptions to be in both Latin and English.

letters.title: To Richard Owen   10 September [1850]
letters.summary:
About to go to press with "wearyful"Fossil Cirripedia[vol. 1 (1851)];

would like to borrow proof-sheets of Frederick Dixon’s work [The geology and fossils of the Tertiary and Cretaceous formations of Sussex(1850)]. Would also like to borrow a specimen ofBalanus glacialisfrom Royal College of Surgeons. Encloses formal request [see1356].

letters.title: To Richard Owen   10 September [1850]
letters.summary: Asks to borrow specimen ofBalanus glacialisfrom the Museum of the Royal College of Surgeons. It will be necessary to disarticulate it, but CD will return the valves to the Museum.

letters.title: To J. de C. Sowerby   10 September [1850]
letters.summary: New specimens have shown CD he has two distinct species under one name [inFossil Cirripedia(Lepadidae)]. He adds new figures and suggests deletions. Will come to London when he has proofs.

letters.title: To J. de C. Sowerby   12 September [1850]
letters.summary: CD has two corrections in spelling on woodcut [forFossil Cirripedia(Lepadidae)]. Has asked J. S. Bowerbank who should cut the blocks and suggested JdeCS get it done. Repeats arrangements to compare specimens and proofs in London.

letters.title: To Wilhelm Bernhard Rudolph Hadrian Dunker20 September 1850
letters.summary:
Thanks for fossil cirripede specimens.

Describes progress on his book [Fossil Cirripedia] and his work on living cirripedes. Asks to borrow specimens.

Comments on book [F. C. L. Koch and Wilhelm Dunker,Norddeutschen Oolithgebildes(1837)].

Sends thanks to Friedrich Adolph Roemer and R. A. Philippi for specimens.

letters.title: To J. de C. Sowerby   23 September [1850]
letters.summary: Plans to come to London to examine the proofs of JdeCS’s plates [forFossil Cirripedia(Lepadidae)]. Has new German specimens; one is unknown and must be introduced but a woodblock will do.

letters.title: From the Ray Society   [after 7 October 1850]
letters.summary: "Resolved that the Secretary be requested to ask Mr. Darwin if he would agree to the publication of his work [Living Cirripedia] in parts."

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   10 October [1850]
letters.summary:
Is concerned about the education of his boys and is undecided between Rugby and Bruce Castle schools; is inclined toward the latter, but afraid to experiment on so important a subject.

Reports on his pear-trees.

letters.title: To Adam Sedgwick   11 October [1850]
letters.summary:
Thanks AS for a copy of his book,Discourse[on the studies of the University, 5th ed.].

Thinking of not sending his eldest son [William] to a classical school.

letters.title: To Edwin Lankester, Ray Society   [18–22 October 1850]
letters.summary: CD will write again when he returns to Down and has looked over his MS.

letters.title: To Edwin Lankester, Ray Society   27 October [1850]
letters.summary: MS [ofLiving Cirripedia, vol. 1] can be ready in two weeks, but CD would like a decision from the Council of the Ray Society on number of plates. Thinks specimen should be sent to G. B. Sowerby Jr for an estimate on price of engraving. Regrets he is not familiar with routine of the Society. Systematic section will be in two parts; the third part will be on anatomy, habits, etc.

letters.title: To Robert Fitch   3 November [1850]
letters.summary: Explains that fossil cirripede specimens have not been returned because J. de C. Sowerby has been monstrously delayed with the engravings. Members of Palaeontographical Society have urged Sowerby to complete task.

letters.title: From the Ray Society   [4–6 November 1850]
letters.summary: In response to CD’s letter [see1364] the Secretary is instructed to request that he send a specimen plate to James de Carle Sowerby for estimate of cost.

letters.title: To Edwin Lankester, Ray Society   7 November [1850]
letters.summary: Has sent G. B. Sowerby Jr some skeleton plates [for vol. 1 ofLiving Cirripedia] which the Council [of the Ray Society] may also wish to see, along with GBS’s finished drawings. He reminds EL that he has not heard about colour for the plates and adds he has not been told what type should be used; gives estimated lengths of part 1 in different sizes of type (part 2 will be fully twice the size of this). Hopes if the Council does not publish part 1 in 1851 it will publish all in 1852.

letters.title: To Robert Fitch   11 November [1850]
letters.summary: Describes progress in illustrating fossil cirripede specimens by J. de C. Sowerby.

letters.title: To J. de C. Sowerby   11 November [1850]
letters.summary: CD likes the engravings [forFossil Cirripedia(Lepadidae)] but is distressed by JdeCS’s slow progress and is being pressed by owners to return their specimens.

letters.title: To Syms Covington   23 November 1850
letters.summary:
Thanks SC for box of specimens [of cirripedes].

Often wishes he had settled in one of the colonies because of opportunities for his children.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   26 November 1850
letters.summary:
Falconer’s misbehaviour.

Geology of Khashia [Khasi] mountains. Speculations on mountain building and origin of Himalayas.

letters.title: To Salt & Son   26 November [1850]
letters.summary: Inquires about financial matters.

letters.title: To Robert Fitch   [December? 1850]
letters.summary: Describes progress of J. de C. Sowerby in engraving fossil cirripede specimens.

letters.title: To Josiah Wedgwood III   1 December [1850]
letters.summary: Discusses share dealings and investment matters.

letters.title: To Edwin Lankester, Ray Society   5 December [1850]
letters.summary: Discusses illustrations [forLiving Cirripedia1 (1851)]. Mentions drawings by G. B. Sowerby [Jr].

letters.title: To John Higgins   13 December [1850]
letters.summary: Discusses his account. Mentions reduction in rent due to agricultural conditions.

letters.title: To John Higgins   21 December [1850]
letters.summary: Asks his opinion concerning possible investment. Asks about possible land sale to Mr Mason.

letters.title: To Albany Hancock   25 December [1850]
letters.summary: Discusses capacity of some cirripedes to bore into rock. Describes progress of his research.

letters.title: From J. D. Dana   [before 29 December 1850]
letters.summary: Gives his opinion that the larval antennae inLepascorrespond with the inferior antennae, the superior not present, as in most Daphnidae. [See1381.]

letters.title: To J. D. Dana   29 December [1850]
letters.summary:
Discusses attachment of antennae in larvae of cirripedes.

Asks for information about how parasitic cirripedes are attached to host.

letters.title: To John Edward Gray   [January 1851]
letters.summary: Is coming tomorrow to see Lorenz Spengler on cirripedes [Auserlesne Schnecken, Muscheln und andre Schaalthiere(1758)] and the remaining sessile cirripedes in the collection. Has finishedBalanus.

letters.title: To John Mumford  1 January 1851
letters.summary: Receipt for £3 5s, proceeds of a lecture, for the Down Coal and Clothing Club.

letters.title: To Rowland Hill   6 January 1851
letters.summary: Drawings of the apteryx in three positions.

letters.title: To James de Carle Sowerby   21 January [1851]
letters.summary: CD is pleased with plates [forFossil Cirripedia(Lepadidae)]; most corrections need only a touch. Requests revises soon and asks how much he owes.

letters.title: To Robert Fitch   24 January [1851]
letters.summary: Collection of fossil cirripedes to be returned. Would RF be willing to donate duplicates to the British Museum?

letters.title: To the Palaeontographical Society  [before 31 January 1851]
letters.summary: Read a letter from CD. Resolved that labels be printed for the backs of each number of monograph printed and forthcoming.

letters.title: To J. de C. Sowerby   10 February [1851]
letters.summary: CD likes the plates [forFossil Cirripedia(Lepadidae)] except pl. I [Scalpellum], which calls for several revisions; he sees that not all corrections were made, but assumes they called for too extensive changes.

letters.title: To J. de C. Sowerby   13 February [1851]
letters.summary: CD appreciates JdeCS’s care. Sends specimens, noting points to be observed. He adds that the figures which have been most troublesome are those of which drawings were made [forFossil Cirripedia(Lepadidae)].

letters.title: To William Jackson Hooker   17 February [1851]
letters.summary:
Encloses letter from J. D. Hooker. Glad he will soon be home.

Everyone will be astonished at oaks and birches of tropics.

letters.title: To J. de C. Sowerby   19 February [1851]
letters.summary: Comments on JdeCS’s plates [forFossil Cirripedia(Lepadidae)]. Asks if JdeCS can lend him specimens of fossil Balanidae.

letters.title: To Samuel Pickworth Woodward  3 March [1851]
letters.summary: Cirripede fossil specimens returned.

letters.title: To William Harris  4 March [1851]
letters.summary: Has finished the last proof of his monograph [Fossil Lepadidae] and returns WH’s specimens. Has named two new species from the collection.

letters.title: To Edwin Lankester, Ray Society  4 March [1851]
letters.summary: Asks EL to request the Council [of the Ray Society] to permit him to have nine plates [for vol. 1 ofLiving Cirripedia] instead of eight (of which two were to be in colour) and a tenth plate if he pays for it himself.

letters.title: To J. W. Flower   [11 March 1851?]
letters.summary: Thanks for specimens. Will return books on Monday.

letters.title: To John Wickham Flower   23 March [1851]
letters.summary:
Thanks JWF for [cirripede] fossils; one species seems from a new formation.

Regrets that his health makes it necessary to decline an invitation.

letters.title: To William Darwin Fox   [27 March 1851]
letters.summary: Sends condolences to WDF on the death of his father. Has brought his daughter [Anne] to J. M. Gully for the water-cure.

letters.title: From Joseph Dalton Hooker   [c.April 1851]
letters.summary: Wants catalogue of small islands that contain peculiar plants. Thinks complete floras of islands in various stages of depression [subsidence] would provide good data.

letters.title: To Johannes Japetus Smith Steenstrup   3 April 1851
letters.summary: Fossil cirripedes specimens being returned. Will send a copy of monograph [Fossil Cirripedia]. Discusses work on recent cirripedes.

letters.title: To Wilhelm Bernhard Rudolph Hadrian Dunker   5 April [1851]
letters.summary: Returns fossil cirripede specimens to WD, Friedrich Adolph Roemer, R. A. Philippi, and F. C. L. Koch.

letters.title: To Emma Darwin   [17 April 1851]
letters.summary: Reports the state of Anne Darwin’s health.

letters.title: To Emma Darwin   [18 April 1851]
letters.summary: Reports on Anne’s illness.

letters.title: To Emma Darwin   [18 April 1851]
letters.summary: Reports on Anne’s condition.

letters.title: To Erasmus Alvey Darwin   19 April 1851
letters.summary: Asks EAD to forward a message of Anne’s improved state to Down.

letters.title: To Emma Darwin   [19 April 1851]
letters.summary: Detailed account of progress of Anne’s illness.

letters.title: From Emma Darwin   [19 April 1851]
letters.summary: Is hopeful about Anne after receiving an encouraging message.

letters.title: From Emma Darwin   [19 April 1851]
letters.summary: Gives her reactions to CD’s reports on Anne’s health.

letters.title: To Emma Darwin   [20 April 1851]
letters.summary: Reports on Anne’s health throughout the night and from 8 a.m. through to 4.30 p.m.

letters.title: To Emma Darwin   [21 April 1851]
letters.summary: Further reports on Anne’s illness.

letters.title: To Emma Darwin   [21 April 1851]
letters.summary: An evening report on Annie Darwin’s somewhat improved condition.

letters.title: From Emma Darwin   [21 April 1851]
letters.summary: Discusses Anne’s sickness and her hope.

letters.title: To Frances Mackintosh Wedgwood   [21 April 1851]
letters.summary: Asks FW to come over to feel his daughter’s pulse.

letters.title: From Emma Darwin   [22–3 April 1851]
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his Monday notes about Anne, which are much better than previous ones.

letters.title: From Emma Darwin   [23 April 1851]
letters.summary: Tells of the hopes raised by CD’s letter of Monday regarding Anne’s health.

letters.title: To Emma Darwin   [23 April 1851]
letters.summary: Tells of Anne’s death.

letters.title: From Sarah Elizabeth (Elizabeth) Wedgwood   [24 April 1851]
letters.summary: Tells CD how Anne’s death is affecting Emma. Hopes he may soon return.

letters.title: From Emma Darwin   [24 April 1851]
letters.summary: Her reactions to Anne’s death; hopes CD may soon return.

letters.title: To Fanny Mackintosh Wedgwood   [24 April 1851]
letters.summary: Arrangements for leaving Malvern after death of Anne.

letters.title: To E. A. Darwin   [25 April 1851]
letters.summary: Writes about the death of Anne. Wishes EAD to insert an announcement of the death in the newspapers.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   [25 April 1851]
letters.summary: Feels deeply for them at their "impossible loss" [of Anne].

letters.title: From Susan Elizabeth Darwin   [25 April 1851]
letters.summary: Commiseration on the death of Anne.

letters.title: From Emily Catherine Darwin   [25? April 1851]
letters.summary: Commiseration on the death of Anne.

letters.title: To Fanny Mackintosh Wedgwood   [25 April 1851]
letters.summary: Is glad he returned home to be with Emma, and is grateful to Fanny for following Anne to the grave.

letters.title: From Fanny Mackintosh Wedgwood   25 April [1851]
letters.summary: Tells of the burial of Anne.

letters.title: To Elizabeth Mary Thorley   26 April [1851]
letters.summary: Expresses gratitude to Mrs T’s daughter for devotion to his daughter in final illness.

letters.title: From Emily Catherine Darwin   [27 April 1851]
letters.summary: Thoughts on the death of Anne.

letters.title: From Fanny Mackintosh Wedgwood   28 [April 1851]
letters.summary: Thoughts after the death of Anne.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   29 April [1851]
letters.summary: His favourite child, Anne, has unexpectedly died.

letters.title: To Edward Forbes   [1 May – 5 June 1851]
letters.summary: Comments on MS by C. S. Bate. Bate not aware of other work onCirripedia; cites Bate’s errors. Would Bate allow CD to use his drawings inLiving Cirripedia? [SeeLiving Cirripedia1: 9–16.]

letters.title: To Edward Adolphus Seymour Seymour   May 1851
letters.deprecated: Edward Adolphus Seymour Seymour, 12th duke of Somerset
letters.recipient: Edward Adolphus Seymour Seymour, 12th duke of Somerset
letters.summary: Testimonial on behalf of J. D. Hooker, addressed to Lord Seymour as Chief Commissioner of Her Majesty’s Woods and Forests, signed by CD and many other scientists.

letters.title: To Hensleigh and Fanny Mackintosh Wedgwood   1 May [1851]
letters.summary: Thanks HW for the trouble he has taken; sends a cheque [to cover expenses of Anne’s funeral?]. Emma Darwin adds a note to FMW.

letters.title: To J. S. Dismorr  6 May [1851]
letters.summary: Congratulates JD on discovery of fossil footsteps near Port Philip, Australia. Richard Owen would be glad to examine them. J. B. Jukes most likely to know geology of Port Philip.

letters.title: To J. S. Dismorr   15 May [1851]
letters.summary: Comments on concretionary bodies found by JD. Encourages him to continue geological study.

letters.title: To A. S. Horner   25 May [1851]
letters.summary: Thanks for her sympathy on the death of Annie Darwin, and sends news of Emma Darwin and the baby Horace.

letters.title: To Robert Ball   26 May [1851]
letters.summary:
Obliged for letter about cirripedes attached to turtles’ backs. Genus isChelonobia, Leach. Cirripedes do not penetrate skin, but surrounding tissue grows up around them.

Asks RB to send S. AmericanBalanus. Already has specimens from Irish coast.

letters.title: To W. B. R. H. Dunker   2 June [1851]
letters.summary: Collection of recent cirripedes received. The fossil cirripedes have been returned.

letters.title: To Augustus Addison Gould   2 June [1851]
letters.summary: Thanks for cirripede specimens. Describes progress [onLiving Cirripedia].

letters.title: To John Higgins   7 June 1851
letters.summary: Mentions his account. Reduction in rent paid by Mr Hardy.

letters.title: To Robert Ball   8 June [1851]
letters.summary: Thanks for cast and account of cirripede [Chelonobia caretta] burrowing in turtle shell. Believes base of cirripede absorbed by bone below.

letters.title: To Albany Hancock   8 June [1851]
letters.summary: Asks whether he can borrow from Joshua Alder an article [Sven Ludvig Lovén, "Ny art af CirripediaAlepas squalicola",Ofers. Kongl. Vetensk. Acad. Förh.1 (1844): 192–4] in order to have the plate copied. Asks to borrow additional specimen ofIbla.

letters.title: To S. P. Woodward   9 June [1851]
letters.summary: Asks for reference to article by Kölliker, ["Some observations on the structure of two new species of Hectocotyle",Trans. Linn. Soc. Lond.22 (1851): 9–22]. Asks for information.

letters.title: To Charles Spence Bate   13 June [1851]
letters.summary: Thanks CSB for drawings of [cirripede] larva and for permission to cite unpublished paper ["On the development of the cirripedes",Ann. & Mag. Nat. Hist.2d ser. 8 (1851): 324–32]. Describes method of preserving specimens. MentionsBalanuscommon on tidal rocks at Tenby.

letters.title: To J. S. Dismorr   13 June [1851]
letters.summary:
Suggests that JD consult with Edward Forbes about dredging.

Delighted he will look for fossil bones.

Asks him to look for Australian cirripedes.

letters.title: To James Dwight Dana    15 June [1851]
letters.summary:
Thanks for note of 13 May and tracings of the "curiousBopyrid".

Is astonished at amount of work JDD does and frightened it will cause ill-health, such as CD has experienced.

letters.title: To Albany Hancock   22 June [1851]
letters.summary: Thanks AH for assistance and Joshua Alder for his kindness.Iblaspecimens offered would not aid him.

letters.title: To James Scott Bowerbank   25 June [1851]
letters.summary: Asks to re-examine specimen ofScalpellum. Discusses publication [ofFossil Cirripedia] by Palaeontographical Society.

letters.title: To James Smith   4 July [1848]
letters.summary:
Discusses the Jura blocks.

...

letters.title: To J. S. Bowerbank   7 July [1851]
letters.summary: Asks to borrow woodcut from Palaeontographical Society for use inLiving Cirripedia, vol. 1.

letters.title: To Josiah Wedgwood III   [after 12 July 1851]
letters.summary: Inquires about the nature of some money recently paid to him.

letters.title: To Thomas Henry Huxley   17 July [1851]
letters.summary: Thanks for report [on echinoderms,Ann. & Mag. Nat. Hist.2d ser. 8 (1851): 1–19]. Wanted to learn about metamorphosis of the class. Agrees with THH’s distinction between individuals and zooids, but thinks zooids will never cease to be called individuals.

letters.title: To Edwin Lankester, Ray Society   19 July [1851]
letters.summary: Finds he needs four woodcuts for the introduction [to vol. 1 ofLiving Cirripedia], which calls for quick action. Will send entire MS by the end of the month.

letters.title: To Edwin Lankester, Ray Society   22 July [1851]
letters.summary: Will bring MS [of vol. 1 ofLiving Cirripedia] on the last day of July, and proofs of the eight plates now engraved will be sent soon. CD has failed to get materials for the one coloured plate he wanted, so none will be in colour. There will be ten altogether. He will ask later whether he must pay for the extra one. G. B. Sowerby Jr comes next day to complete drawings for two not yet engraved.

letters.title: To George Newport   24 July [1851]
letters.summary:
Asks to borrow an old pair of GN’s dissecting scissors so that Weiss & Co. can use it as a model.

Health has been poor.

Has finished MS on pedunculated cirripedes for Ray Society [Living Cirripedia, vol. 1 (1851)].

letters.title: To Edwin Lankester, Ray Society   26 July [1851]
letters.summary: Asks EL whether he should use both Latin and English descriptions of specific characters [in vol. 1 ofLiving Cirripedia].

letters.title: To Edwin Lankester, Ray Society   30 July [1851]
letters.summary: Sends completed MS [vol. 1 ofLiving Cirripedia] with instructions for the printers; reviews number of plates and woodcuts, and offers to pay for extras and for excess corrections, if they occur. Hopes the Council [of the Ray Society] will print his second volume at the end of the ensuing year.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [late August – early September 1851]
letters.summary:
James Wilson reports case of salmon hybrids.

Herrings inhabit freshwater lake in Scotland during winter.

JDH will edit juror reports for the Great Exhibition.

letters.title: To Edwin Lankester, Ray Society   [7 August 1851]
letters.summary: CD returns home Saturday and would like his servant to take his MS [ofLiving Cirripedia] to Adlard that morning; he does not have a copy and would on no account re-undergo the labour he has spent on it.

letters.title: To Edwin Lankester, Ray Society   [9 August 1851]
letters.summary: Wants his MS [ofLiving Cirripedia] taken to Adlard by a trustworthy person and wants to be told when and how it was done; leaves a note for Adlard that he wants proof on the 17th or 18th.

letters.title: To George Newport   12 August [1851]
letters.summary:
Returns scissors with thanks.

Young John Lubbock who has a strong taste for dissecting insects would benefit greatly from conversation with GN.

letters.title: To C. S. Bate   18 August [1851]
letters.summary:
Thanks CSB for cirripede larvae.

Has been unwell.

Cannot see transverse articulation referred to and does not believe in it.

Sends species synonyms.

Discussion ofChthamalinae.

Suggests using asphalt to seal specimen containers.

Comments on mouth of larva.

letters.title: From John Gwyn Jeffreys   7 September 1851
letters.summary: Has sent CD some cirripedes and notes which he hopes will be of use. Gives details of occurrence and source of some of the specimens.

letters.title: To James Dwight Dana   9 September [1851]
letters.summary:
Thanks him for letter andBalanusspecimen.

Acastais curious; may be a new genus.

Is sending copy [ofFossil Cirripedia1]. Correcting proofs [ofLiving Cirripedia1].

Mentions comment by Hermann Abich on JDD’s chapters on the Sandwich Islands [inGeology(1849)].

letters.title: To J. J. S. Steenstrup   9 September [1851]
letters.summary:
Returns fossil cirripede specimens to JS and Forchhammer.

Sends copies [ofFossil Cirripedia] to them and to Sven Lovén.

Reading proofs [ofLiving Cirripedia].

letters.title: To J. S. Bowerbank, Ray Society  28 September [1851]
letters.summary: G. B. Sowerby’s plates [forLiving Cirripedia] are ready for the printer.

letters.title: To William Erasmus Darwin  3 October [1851]
letters.summary: Discusses domestic affairs and gives some advice on manners.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   9 October 1851
letters.summary: Testimonial for THH’s application for Chair in Natural History at Toronto.

letters.title: To Daniel Sharpe   16 October [1851]
letters.summary:
Thanks DS for writing about his research on foliation and cleavage. Discusses nature of slate and metamorphic schists.

Makes suggestions for the paper DS is preparing for the Royal Society and raises questions for his consideration; CD hopes he can attend the Society meeting when the paper is read ["On foliation and cleavage of Scotland",Philos. Trans. R. Soc. Lond.142 (1852): 445–62].

letters.title: To J. J. S. Steenstrup   16 October [1851]
letters.summary:
Thanks him for specimens ofXenobalanus. Discusses systematic relations of the genus.

Comments on paper by J. T. Reinhardt ["Om slaegtenLithotryas",Vidensk. Medd. Naturhist. Foren. Kjobenhavn2 (1850): 1–8].

letters.title: To James Hilton?   25 October [1851?]
letters.summary: Thanks for offer of Cirripedia specimens from the Northern Atlantic, but has seen so many that he does not need more.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker  [November 1851]
letters.summary:
Flora of New Zealand.

Reconsidering variability of insular species.

Becoming convinced of the probability that the southern flora is a fragmentary one – all that remains of a great southern continent.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [November–December 1851]
letters.summary: Detailed critique of CL’sA manual of elementary geology[3d ed. (1851), used in editing 4th ed. (1852)].

letters.title: To Thomas Salt 4 November 1851
letters.summary: Returns the enclosed parchment.

letters.title: To J. J. S. Steenstrup   4 November [1851]
letters.summary: Asks for reference to publication aboutXenobalanus.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   22 November [1851]
letters.summary: Proposes to send THH vol. 1 ofLiving Cirripedia.

letters.title: To John Stevens Henslow   11 December [1851]
letters.summary:
Sends cirripede specimens for Ipswich Museum.

Asks how much a village fireworks display would cost.

Comments on the need in education for good habits of expression and accurate observation instead of making "wretched Latin verses".

letters.title: To Christian Ferdinand Friedrich von Krauss   21 December [1851]
letters.summary: Asks to borrow FK’s specimen ofConia rosea. Would like to know if FK collected it himself [in S. Africa] or was given it, because CD has a closely allied species from Australia, which surprises him. [SeeLiving Cirripedia2: 335.]

letters.title: To Thomas Salt   24 December 1851
letters.summary: Asking Thomas Salt to inform the Executors of Captain Muckleston that he wishes to foreclose the mortgage.

letters.title: To Thomas Salt   26 December [1851]
letters.summary: Asks Thomas Salt to accept the repayment of a mortgage from Captain Muckleston’s executors, if Josiah Wedgwood agrees.

letters.title: To Adam White   26 December 1851
letters.summary: Testimonial letter expressing CD’s high opinion of AW’s zoological attainments.

letters.title: To John Richardson   30 December [1851]
letters.summary: Will send JR’s box of cirripedes on Thursday.

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   [1852–60]
letters.summary: Sends an enclosure forwarded from Down.

letters.title: To J. J. S. Steenstrup   3 January [1852]
letters.summary:
Asks JS to compare cirripede specimens with those of Lorenz Spengler to establish comparative nomenclature.

Requests reference to article describingXenobalanus.

letters.title: ToGardeners’ Chronicle  [before 10 January 1852]
letters.summary: Asks readers ofGardeners’ Chroniclewhether they have experience with light wire rope instead of chain in drawing water buckets from deep wells. Describes the problem of his own well with its 325 foot chain.

letters.title: To Edward Forbes   23 January [1852?]
letters.summary: DiscussesBalanus unguiformis. Promises to return specimen.

letters.title: To Edwin Lankester, Ray Society   30 January [1852]
letters.summary: The Binder "by some wonderful Blunder" has bound the enclosed in all of CD’s copies [ofLiving Cirripedia, vol. 1]. He requests that it be pulled out. It may belong to W. A. Leighton’s volume [Lichens(1851)].

letters.title: To J. D. Dana   15 February [1852]
letters.summary:
Sending first volumes onLivingandFossil Cirripedia. Solicits JDD’s opinion, especially on sexual relations ofScalpellumandIbla, on which he "hardly expect[s] to be believed".

Sends unusual crustacean specimen collected by B. J. Sulivan.

TheSporillussent by JDD is averycurious species ofAcasta[seeLiving Cirripedia2: 319].

Asks JDD to identify and give geographical distribution of pieces of coral in which some cirripedes are imbedded.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   24 [February 1852]
letters.summary: Is glad WED has made a good beginning [at Rugby?].

letters.title: To A. A. Gould   29 February [1852]
letters.summary: Sends presentation copy ofFossil Cirripedia.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   7 March [1852]
letters.summary:
Congratulates and "condoles" with WDF on a tenth child.

On education, he has not had courage to break away from "the old stereotyped stupid classical education"; has sent William to Rugby.

The first Ray Society volume [Living Cirripedia] is finished.

Has joined in a society to prosecute violators of the act against use of children in climbing chimneys.

letters.title: To Syms Covington  14 March 1852
letters.summary:
Asks for details about the discoveries of gold in Australia.

Has published one book on barnacles [1851].

Sulivan has just returned from his cattle farm in the Falklands.

letters.title: To the Chairman of the Committee of Papers, Royal Society   16 March [1852]
letters.deprecated: Chairman, Committee of Papers, Royal Society of London
letters.recipient: Chairman, Committee of Papers, Royal Society of London
letters.summary: Referee’s report on paper by Daniel Sharpe ["On foliation and cleavage",Philos. Trans. R. Soc. Lond.142 (1852): 445–62].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [April 1852]
letters.summary:
Questions on variation in nature: taxa varying in one region but not another. Variation between vs within species. Rarity of variation in important organs within a species. G. R. Waterhouse’s views on variation in highly developed organs, which CD relates to variation in rudimentary organs.

Asks for cases of obligate self-fertilising plants.

[CD annotation proposes using the SteudelNomenclator botanicus(1821–4) to determine if variable species occur in genera with many species.]

letters.title: From Johannes Japetus Smith Steenstrup    8 April 1852
letters.summary:
His difficulties in answering CD’s letter of 3 Jan [1852] [see1469]. There is noLepas mitrain the Lorenz Spengler collection. He undertakes to compare the specimens ofBalanussent by CD with those of Spengler.

He thanks CD for his book [Fossil Cirripedia(1851)].

His work with Professor Forchhammer and Mr Worsaae.

letters.title: To George Crawford Hyndman   16 April [1852]
letters.summary: Thanks GCH forBalanusspecimens.

letters.title: To John William Parker  5 May [1852]
letters.summary: As an author of some scientific works CD is of the opinion that each bookseller should settle, each for himself, the retail price.

letters.title: To J. D. Dana   8 May [1852]
letters.summary:
Gratified by JDD’s opinion of his work.

Discusses problem of homologies of cirripede larva in first stage and reasons for his view.

JDD’s information on corals was just what CD needed.

Would like specimen of blind cave rat described by B. Silliman [Jr] ["On the Mammoth Cave of Kentucky",Am. J. Sci.2d ser. 11 (1851): 336] for Waterhouse to examine.

Discusses origin of Australian valleys; he disagrees with JDD’s river-erosion hypothesis.

letters.title: To Henry Norton Shaw, Secretary, Royal Geographical Society   17 May [1852]
letters.deprecated: Henry Norton ShawSecretary, R. Geographical Soc.
letters.recipient: Henry Norton ShawSecretary, R. Geographical Soc.
letters.summary: Asks for catalogue and latest number of theJournal[of the Royal Geographical Society].

letters.title: To John Higgins   19 June [1852]
letters.summary: Discusses his account and rent reduction. Comments on agricultural prices.

letters.title: To Richard Owen   17 July [1852]
letters.summary: Gratified by what RO says about his book [Living Cirripedia, vol. 1 (1851)]. The anatomical work is the only part he is really interested in; finds the "mere systematic part infinitely tedious"; but will be surprised if he is ever proved wrong on the males ofIblaandScalpellum.

letters.title: To Philip Henry Stanhope   30 July [1852]
letters.summary: Declines invitation to Chevening [Lord Stanhope’s residence].

letters.title: To John Higgins   2 August [1852]
letters.summary: Discusses rent reduction and possibility of a lease.

letters.title: To George Ransome   5 August [1852]
letters.summary: Forwards an order for £1 1sin response to a circular from Ipswich Museum.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   27 August [1852]
letters.summary: Thanks for his letter; hopes he is managing all right [at Rugby?].

letters.title: To George Robert Waterhouse   8 September [1852]
letters.summary:
Knows no one in Buenos Aires. Suggests sites in South America where Auguste Bravard can find fossils.

Ray Society has delayed distribution [ofLiving Cirripedia(1851)].

letters.title: To Josiah Wedgwood III   21 October [1852]
letters.summary: Informs JW of his intention to sell his N. W. Railway shares.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   24 [October 1852]
letters.summary:
News of his health; has been well of late, but cannot stand excitement. Hereditary weakness is another of his bugbears.

At work on cirripedes – "I hate a Barnacle as no man ever did before."

letters.title: To Josiah Wedgwood III  20 November 1852
letters.summary: A statement of payments made by trustees to CD and by CD to trustees for the years 1851 and 1852.

letters.title: To George Johnston   23 November 1852
letters.summary: Recommends GJ for Government pension.

letters.title: To J. D. Dana   25 November [1852]
letters.summary:
Thanks JDD for information.

DiscussesAcasta sporillus.

Comments on review of first volume ofLiving Cirripedia[Am. J. Sci.2d ser. 14 (1852): 125–7].

Asks JDD to examine Lerneidae.

Will read with interest the geographical discussion of Crustacea when JDD’s volume [Crustacea(1852–5)] appears. John Lubbock will purchase a copy.

Discusses error inLiving Cirripedia.

letters.title: To Joseph Augustin Hubert de Bosquet   17 December [1852]
letters.summary:
At request of Edward Forbes sends vol. 1 ofLiving Cirripediaand vol. 1 ofFossil Cirripedia.

Calls attention to sexual relations ofIblaandScalpellum.

letters.title: To John Higgins   18 December [1852]
letters.summary: Discusses his account. Mentions the rent.

letters.title: To ? 19 December  [1852 or 1854]
letters.summary: Ray Society has given CD 22 copies [ofLiving Cirripedia, vol. 1].

letters.title: To Albany Hancock   25 December [1852]
letters.summary:
Discusses capacity of some cirripedes to bore into rock.

MentionsAlcippespecimens borrowed from AH.

Relation of sexes inIblaandScalpellum.

letters.title: To ?   31 December [1852–3]
letters.summary: Responds to correspondent’s request for information about shells from the Coquimbo beds in Chile. Difficulty in deciding on age of deposits and species. Notes views of Alcide d’Orbigny.

letters.title: To William Sharpey?   [1853 – 72?]
letters.summary: If Hooker [presumably Joseph Dalton Hooker] knows he is proposed [for something at the Royal Society?] he will enquire if he can attend.

letters.title: To C. S. Bate   10 January [1853]
letters.summary: Asks if CSB can help him obtain specimen ofVerruca.

letters.title: To Albany Hancock   10 January [1853]
letters.summary:
Grateful for AH’s long letter and suggestions. Delighted at what he says about "complemental males". CD feared no one would believe in them but now that Owen, Dana, and AH accept them, he is content.

Agrees with AH on cross-impregnation; has collected facts on this head but has done nothing with them.

AH’s paper onAlcippe[Ann. & Mag. Nat. Hist.2d ser. 4 (1849): 305–14] caused him to lose sleep over its anomalous structure.

letters.title: To G. R. Waterhouse   18 January [1853]
letters.summary:
Thanks GRW for his sympathy on his ill health. Feels better lately.

Sends thanks to G. P. Deshayes for his advice.

Asks what "original work" GRW has begun so his name will become better known.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   29 January [1853]
letters.summary:
Discusses education of his sons. Would like to see more diversity.

He is pleased that Richard Owen and others had a good opinion of his first volume [onLiving Cirripedia].

letters.title: To Albany Hancock   29 January [1853]
letters.summary: DiscussesAlcippe. Asks to borrow specimens. Would like to hire fishermen to collect specimens.

letters.title: To Thomas Salt   31 January [1853]
letters.summary: Asks if Thomas Salt can dispose of the £600 Shrewsbury Street mortgage.

letters.title: To Albany Hancock   10 February [1853]
letters.summary: Has found plenty of maleAlcippeon specimens. Would eventually like more specimens. Did not recognise males at first. Has foundAlcippedifficult to make out.

letters.title: To Albany Hancock   12 February [1853]
letters.summary: Describes anatomy and growth stages ofAlcippein close detail.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   15 February [1853]
letters.summary:
ReturnsLake Superior[1850], which he already has received from Agassiz. Thanks for pamphlets by C. B. Adams [on Mollusca,Contrib. Conchol.10 (1851): 189–206; 11 (1852): 207–15].

Describes his dissection of an unusual cirripede [Alcippe lampas] with 12 males attached [seeLiving Cirripedia2: 556, 558].

letters.title: To Josiah Wedgwood III   18 February 1853
letters.summary: Sends his written consent regarding custody of the deeds of the Owen mortgage. Other financial matters.

letters.title: To Albany Hancock   25 February [1853]
letters.summary: Asks at what depthAlcippeis found and on what date the shell withAlcippespecimens that AH sent was taken.

letters.title: From Albany Hancock   25 February 1853
letters.summary: Discusses taxonomic relations ofAlcippe.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   1 March [1853]
letters.summary:
Discusses WED’s affairs and events at Down.

Writes of the benefits of reading.

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   8 March [1853]
letters.summary: CD has been reassured about his "speculation" in Mr Warren’s company. Thanks JSH for his advice and trouble.

letters.title: To Thomas Salt   15 March [1853]
letters.summary: Thanks for finding a purchaser for the Shrewsbury Street Act securities and encloses the Transfers.

letters.title: To Edwin Lankester, Ray Society   19 March [1853]
letters.summary: Objects to early deadline for submitting manuscript [ofLiving Cirripedia2 (1854)]. Discusses illustrations by G. B. Sowerby [Jr].

letters.title: To Charles Wigley 21 March 1853
letters.summary: Encloses the transfer, signed and witnessed.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   24 March [1853]
letters.summary: Volcanic activity of Mt Kilauea as described by Dana [Am. J. Sci.2d ser. 9 (1850): 347–64]. Discusses the mechanics of volcanic eruption. Disputes view of William Hopkins that simultaneous action by volcanoes of different heights must come from separate lava sources. Notes relationship of continental elevation to volcanic action.

letters.title: To Albany Hancock   30 March [1853]
letters.summary: Thanks AH for assistance. ComparesAlcippeto South American boring cirripedes.

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   31 March [1853]
letters.summary: Would like to meet JSH in London.

letters.title: To C. S. Bate   1 April [1853]
letters.summary:
Thanks for specimens of cirripedes attached to rocks, which show no boring. CD hopes to see some on limestone.

Encourages CSB to do research on the complemental males ofScalpellum vulgare.

letters.title: To Andrew Crombie Ramsay   9 April [1853]
letters.summary: Discusses geological foliation and cleavage. Urges ACR to read CD’s remarks on subject in hisSouth Americabefore ACR publishes his paper ["On the lower Palaeozoic rocks",Q. J. Geol. Soc. Lond.9 (1853): 161–79].

letters.title: To John Higgins   11 April [1853]
letters.summary: Has changed his bank to Union Bank, Charing Cross Branch.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   11 April [1853]
letters.summary:
Offers to send Ascidia specimens ofBeaglevoyage. Describes some of them.

Hopes THH will review his book [Living Cirripedia, vol. 1] which has been published for a year with no notice taken of it except briefly by Dana.

DiscussesLimulus-like larva. "I have become a man of one idea.– cirripedes morning & night."

letters.title: To J. A. H. de Bosquet   15 April [1853]
letters.summary:
Discusses the development and morphology ofVerruca.

Would be proud to receive memoir ["Les crustacés fossiles du Limbourg" (1854)].

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   23 April [1853]
letters.summary:
On THH’s paper on cephalous Mollusca [Philos. Trans. R. Soc. Lond.143 (1853) pt 1: 29–66]. Discovery of the type or "idea" (in THH’s sense, not Owen’s or Agassiz’s) is one of the highest ends of natural history.

Discusses anamorphism;

position of heart inCleodora.

Variability within species;

cementing process in cirripedes.

letters.title: To Josiah Wedgwood III   25 [April 1853]
letters.summary: Discusses the [CD/Emma] marriage trust.

letters.title: To E. A. Darwin   26 [April 1853]
letters.summary: Writes concerning marriage trust.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   26 April 1853
letters.summary: Acknowledges the receipt of some securities.

letters.title: ToGardeners’ Chronicle  [c.27 April 1853]
letters.summary: Solicits information about the kind of syphon required to convey water from a proposed large water tank to existing smaller ones.

letters.title: To Edward Cresy   29 April [1853]
letters.summary: Discusses installation of watering system. Sent question toGardeners’ Chroniclebut, through EC’s kindness, superfluously.

letters.title: To Edward Cresy   15 May [1853]
letters.summary: Apologises for the trouble he has given EC. CD has given up the siphon plan and intends to make only an ordinary tank with a pump.

letters.title: To J. A. H. de Bosquet   7 June [1853]
letters.summary: Discusses JAHdeB’s drawing of aVerruca.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   7 June [1853]
letters.summary:
Describes meeting of Geological Society [1 June 1853].

Mentions his criticism of Murchison’s lecture on flints.

Describes Robert Chambers’ "On the glacial phenomena in Scotland" [Edinburgh New Philos. J.54 (1853): 229–82].

Mentions controversial election of members to the Royal Society.

letters.title: To John Higgins   14 June [1853]
letters.summary: Discusses account.

letters.title: To J. A. H. de Bosquet   18 June 1853
