Thanks JDH for response on variation. Studying variations that seem correlated with environment, e.g., north vs south, ascending mountains.

CD’s weed garden: observations on slugs killing seedlings.

Seed-salting. One-seventh of the plants of any country could be transported 924 miles by sea and would germinate.

letters.title: From T. V. Wollaston   [12 April 1857]
letters.summary: Lists groups of insects absent from the Madeiran fauna.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   13 April [1857]
letters.summary:
CD returns a letter from Wollaston.

Although opposed to the Forbesian doctrine [of continental extension] as a general rule, CD would have no objection to its being proved in some cases. Does not think Wollaston has proved it; nor can anyone until more is known about the means of distribution of insects – but the identity of the two faunas is certainly interesting.

His health is very poor and his "everlasting species-Book" quite overwhelms him with work. It is beyond his powers, but he hopes to live to finish it.

letters.title: From George Robert Waterhouse   14 April 1857
letters.summary: Has found no reference to construction of bees’ cells in works referred to by CD. Describes cell ofOsmia atricapilla. Hive-bees’ cell was described at Entomological Society.

letters.title: To Laurence Edmondston   19 April [1857]
letters.summary:
Thanks for pigeon.

Are there Shetland birds chequered with black marks, as Carl Julian Graba states are in Faeroes [Reise nach Färö(1830)] and Col. King in the Hebrides?

letters.title: From James Tenant   23 April 1857
letters.summary: Fish will take both sorts of seeds sent by CD, but will not take oats.

letters.title: From J. D. Dana   27 April 1857
letters.summary:
In reply to CD’s query [see2072], JDD describes what little is known about the crustacea of the Antarctic and southern lands.

Knows of no species of the cold temperate south identical with those of the cold temperate north.

letters.title: To P. H. Gosse   27 April [1857]
letters.summary: Asks PHG to conduct an experiment to see if young littoral molluscs will cling to a duck’s foot – CD seeks to explain distribution of molluscs without adopting E. Forbes’s [continental extension] theory.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [29 April 1857]
letters.summary:
Curative power of hydropathy.

General hairiness of alpine plants questioned: direct environmental effect.

CD has long felt JDH is too hard on bad observers.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   [30 April 1857]
letters.summary:
His impressions of the hydropathic establishment and E. W. Lane. Is convinced the only thing for "chronic cases" is the water-cure.

Asks if WDF knows of any breed of pig that originated or was modified by a cross with a Chinese or Neapolitan pig, and whether the crossbreed bred true.

letters.title: To Alfred Russel Wallace   1 May 1857
letters.summary:
Reports long preparation of work on how species and varieties differ. Agreement with Wallace’s conclusions as reported inAnnals and Magazine of Natural Historyand in his letter to CD of 10 0ct [1856]. On distinction between domestic varieties and those in "a state of nature".

On mating of jaguars and leopards, the breeding of poultry, pigeons, etc.

Requests help for his experimenting on means of distribution of organic beings on oceanic islands.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [2 May 1857]
letters.summary:
JDH has shaved the hair off the alpine plant.

CD apologises for his criticism.

Apparent but false relations of plant structure to climate: heath-like foliage of all Cape of Good Hope plants.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [3 May 1857]
letters.summary:
JDH’s last letter demolishes woolly alpine plant theory.

Correlation of apetalous flowers and cold climate.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   9 May [1857]
letters.summary:
Thanks for new part of "Statistics".

Interested in disjoined species; do they tend to belong to large or small genera, and are they generally members of small families?

Is glad AG will tackle introduced plants; has noticed that the proportion of a particular family to the whole flora tends to be similar in introduced and indigenous plants.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   12 [May 1857]
letters.summary:
Accepts a dozen eggs of rumpless Polands. Having so many enables him to see whether the breed "comestrue".

Asks what colour turbits have dark tails – "it is just the class of facts which interest me".

Do fowls when crossed throw odd and unexpected colours like pigeons?

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   13 May [1857]
letters.summary: Discusses family health and affairs.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   16 [May 1857]
letters.summary:
Asks JDH’s opinion, and botanical evidence, on important law: parts that are highly developed in comparison to other allied species are very variable.

Interest in hairiness of alpine plants revived by reading A. Moquin-Tandon [Éléments de tératologie végétale(1841)]; correlation with dryness. CD seeks interpretation independent of direct environmental effect.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   18 May [1857]
letters.summary:
Lists pigeons and poultry he is forwarding to WBT.

Wants details of WBT’sPoultry book[1856–7]

and is anxious to purchase his long-winged runt.

Thanks him for help and information on fowl crosses.

letters.title: To William Sharpey   22 May [1857]
letters.summary: Agrees with Thomas Henry Huxley that Albany Hancock has a good claim on a Royal Society medal. Thinks that geology has not been sufficiently honoured by the Royal Society, and suggests Joseph Prestwich. Expresses his strong opinion that Charles Lyell would be a worthy recipient of the Copley Medal.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   [c.24 May 1857]
letters.summary: Discusses difficulties involved in deciding which genera are protean in the light of some comments by H. C. Watson.

letters.title: To J. D. Dana   25 May [1857]
letters.summary:
Thanks him for information concerning Crustacea.

Comments on natural history study in the U. S.

Mentions work done by Huxley on Crustacea ["Description of a new crustacean",J. Geol. Soc. Lond.13 (1857): 363–9];

John Lubbock on larvae of Diptera.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker  [June 1857]
letters.summary:
Request forFlorasof Pacific Islands and Greenland.

Individual variation.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   1 June 1857
letters.summary:
Comments on species with disjoined ranges; does not feel, despite CD’s expectations, that they tend to belong to small families.

Gives the proportion of U. S. trees in which the sexes are separate [seeNatural selection, p. 62].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   2 June [1857]
letters.summary: Qualifications of John Lindley, Huxley, Albany Hancock, Joseph Prestwich, J. C. Ross, and Francis Beaufort for Royal Medal.

letters.title: To William Sharpey   2 June [1857]
letters.summary: Supports nomination of John Lindley for award of Royal Medal of the Royal Society.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   3 June [1857]
letters.summary:
"Law" [see2092] correlating variability and abnormal development not confirmed by JDH for plants.

CD studies struggle for existence in his weed garden.

Scotch fir observed at Moor Park.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   5 June [1857]
letters.summary:
Royal Society medals.

Correlation of variability and abnormal development is G. R. Waterhouse’s law. Relation of this law to polymorphism.

Colouring and marks of ancestral horse deduced from facts observed in pigeons.

letters.title: To T. C. Eyton   9 June [1857]
letters.summary:
Comments on TCE’s work [Catalogue of the species of birds in his collection(1856)].

Mentions African dog’s skin.

Asks about colours of horses

and about variation in tracheae of male birds.

letters.title: ToGardeners’ Chronicle  [before 13 June 1857]
letters.summary: Requests information from readers on breeding of dun or mouse-coloured ponies with a dark stripe down their backs. Must one or both parents be dun?

letters.title: From H. C. Watson   14 June [1857]
letters.summary: Sends a reference toSubulariawhich bears on a query CD made some time ago [see2002].Subulariawas seen to flower in the air in a remarkably dry season.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   18 June [1857]
letters.summary:
Thanks for AG’s remarks on disjoined species. CD’s notions are based on belief that disjoined species have suffered much extinction, which is the common cause of small genera and disjoined ranges.

Discusses out-crossing in plants.

Has failed to meet with a detailed account of regular and normal impregnation in the bud.Podostemon,Subularia, and underwater Leguminosae are the strongest cases against him.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   [18 June 1857]
letters.summary: Is glad WBT is investigating "the tail question"; hopes he will work out "down & colour point". Is much interested in runts, which seem to vary more than other breeds.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   23 June [1857]
letters.summary: CD anxious to examine rumpless chick 24 hours before hatching.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   25 June [1857]
letters.summary: Seedling leaves of gorse look like clover leaves. This is like young lions being striped. Thus, laws of animal embryology apply to plants.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   25 [June 1857]
letters.summary:
Needs only one nearly-hatched chick.

Has all published numbers ofPoultry book[1856–7].

letters.title: To T. C. Eyton   26 [June 1857]
letters.summary:
Ill.

Comments on TCE’s study of birds’ bones.

His work on variation progresses.

Asks about horses with bars like zebra or ass.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [27] June 1857
letters.summary:
Embryology of plants of low systematic order. Comparative development begins only with first post-cotyledonary leaves.

Curt letter to JDH from George Henslow.

letters.title: CD memorandum   July 1857
letters.summary: Memorandum about £250 investment in Patent Siliceous Stone Company, owned by David Thomas Ansted and Frederick Ransome.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   1 July [1857]
letters.summary:
George Henslow’s curtness to JDH: "an attack of religion".

Embryonic leaves. Adaptive functions and taxonomic significance of cotyledons.

Asa Gray. Separation of sexes in U. S. trees.

letters.title: To [W. W. Baxter?]   [after June 1857]
letters.summary: Requests a quart of distilled water for photography to be sent in a clean bottle via the postman on the following day.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   5 July [1857]
letters.summary:
Does JDH’sWahlenbergiaconfirm CD’s law? Variations of one species assume the character of a distinct but allied species or genus.

Seed-salting: old ones float and germinate.

Owen’s "grand paper" [?J. Proc. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Zool.)2 (1858): 1–37].

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   5 July [1857]
letters.summary:
Asks THH’s opinion on embryological views of G. A. Brullé [Ann. & Mag. Nat. Hist.13 (1844): 484–6] and F. M. Barnéoud [Ann. des Sci. Nat.ser. 3,Bot.6 (1846): 268–96] and on Milne-Edwards’ classification.

Has been reading John Goodsir ["On the morphological constitution of the skeleton of the vertebrate head",Edinburgh New Philos. J.2d ser. 5 (1857): 123–78].

Has embryology of bats ever been worked out?

letters.title: To Francis Galton   7 July [1857]
letters.summary:
Encloses signed document.

"Much interested about all domestic animals of all savage nations."

letters.title: From Asa Gray   7 July 1857
letters.summary:
Believes, with CD, that extinction may be an important factor in explaining plant distributions, but sees no reason why the several species of a genus must ever have had a common or continuous area. "Convince me of that, or show me any good grounds for it … and I think you would carry me a good way with you". It is just such people as AG that CD has to satisfy and convince.

Feels that the crossing of individuals is important in repressing variation and perhaps in perpetuating the species, but instances some plants in which it cannot, apparently, take place.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   7 July 1857
letters.summary: THH comments on G. A. Brullé’s paper ["Researches upon the transformations of the appendages of the Articulata",Ann. & Mag. Nat. Hist.13 (1844): 484–6].

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   9 July [1857]
letters.summary: Thanks THH for his cautionary response on Brullé, but departs from THH in thinking that Barnéoud, if true, would shed light on Milne-Edwards’ proposition that the wider apart classes of animals are the earlier they depart from common embryonic plan.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   14 July [1857]
letters.summary: Asks to borrow severalFloras. Must redo calculations as John Lubbock has shown him an important error.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   14 [July 1857]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Thanks JL for saving him from "a disgraceful blunder". Following their conversation he has divided the New Zealand flora as JL suggested and finds genera with four or more species are more variable than those with three or less. It will take several weeks to go back over all his material.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   [19 July 1857]
letters.summary: Has acquired some runts. Thanks WBT for information. Lists pigeons he is sending.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   20 July [1857]
letters.summary:
Believes species have arisen, like domestic varieties, with much extinction, and that there are no such things as independently created species. Explains why he believes species of the same genusgenerallyhave a common or continuous area; they are actual lineal descendants.

Discusses fertilisation in the bud and the insect pollination of papilionaceous flowers. His theory explains why, despite the risk of injury, cross-fertilisation is usual in the animal and vegetable kingdoms, even in hermaphrodites.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   21 [July 1857]
letters.summary: Writes of WED’s recent excursion to Manchester and his future educational plans.

letters.title: To T. C. Eyton   22 [July 1857]
letters.summary: Sends TCE West African dog’s skin.

letters.title: ToGardeners’ Chronicle  [before 25 July 1857]
letters.summary: CD has saved an enormous amount of labour since he replaced the chain on his deep well with wire rope. He now asks readers whether they have had experience of saving on the weight of the bucket by using some material other than oak.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   27 July [1857]
letters.summary: Arrangements for delivery of pigeons and poultry to Down.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   [August 1857]
letters.summary: States he has "misgivings about the definiteness of species". Believes there is some inherent tendency for plants to originate varieties. Cross-fertilisation is likely in most cases but sees difficulties with plants likeAdlumia.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   1 August [1857]
letters.summary: Important issue at stake with new flora calculations: evidence that species are only strongly marked varieties. Planning large-scale survey.

letters.title: From Henrietta Emma Darwin   [2 August 1857]
letters.summary: Is looking forward to returning home [from Moor Park hydropathic establishment]. News of other patients and the books she is reading. Although feeling well, cannot walk much.

letters.title: To Laurence Edmondston   2 August [1857]
letters.summary:
Thanks for rabbit.

Are there dun-coloured ponies in Shetlands? Are they striped?

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   10 August [1857]
letters.summary: Delighted that JSH is coming to Down. Sends correct train time.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   11 August [1857]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary:
Asks JL not to call as he has a "very old friend" [J. S. Henslow] coming to visit him.

Yesterday visited poultry show at Crystal Palace.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   12 [August 1857]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Invites JL to dine and meet J. S. Henslow.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   22 August [1857]
letters.summary: Tabulation of varieties goes on; very important as it shows the branching of forms. Mentions his principle of divergence.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   5 September [1857]
letters.summary:
Encloses an abstract of his ideas on natural selection and the principle of divergence; the "means by which nature makes her species".

Discusses varieties and close species in large and small genera, finding some data from AG in conflict with his expectations.

Has been observing the action of bees in fertilising kidney beans andLobelia.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   6 September [1857]
letters.summary:
Some negative results in variety tabulation survey.

Galls on wild carrot.

letters.title: To Secretary, Academia Caesarea Leopoldino-Carolina Naturae Curiosorum   8  September [1857]
letters.summary: CD acknowledges honour of his election to the Academy.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [before 11 September 1857]
letters.summary: Writes of the extension to Down House.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   11 September [1857]
letters.summary:
Representative species may complicate tabulation of varieties.

Questions for Mr Anderson about horse colouring in Norway.

Has been writing an "audacious little discussion" to show that "organic beings are not perfect, only perfect enough to struggle with their competitors".

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   15 September [1857]
letters.summary:
Thanks for three last lectures and the account of cirripedes.

Difficulty of classifying the higher groups.

letters.title: To William Walmisley Baxter   23 September [1857–9?]
letters.summary: The returned gloves are similar to some he has already, and he would prefer a pair with stiffer bristles.

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   25 September [1857]
letters.summary:
Thanks JSH for his magnificent present. Hopes Hooker will bring the specimens.

Have water-fowl ever been seen at Ipswich on Mr Ransome’s great tank?

letters.title: From Robert Schlagintweit   25 September 1857
letters.summary: Gives CD further details of the fertility of the offspring from cross of a yak and Indian cow, the so-calledchooboos, whose fertility he has traced to the seventh generation [seeNatural selection, pp. 437–8].

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   26 September [1857]
letters.summary:
Agassiz’s superficiality and wretched reasoning powers. But he stirred up Europe on glaciers. Lyell has been working on their effects – testing work of others.

CD believes "Natural Systems" ought to be simply genealogical. "Time will come when we shall have true genealogical trees of each great kingdom of nature."

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   [27 September 1857]
letters.summary:
Refers to CD’s letter of "May last". ARW’s views on order of succession of species are in accordance with CD’s.

Disappointed that his paper ["On the law which has regulated the introduction of new species",Ann. & Mag. Nat. Hist.2d ser. 16 (1855): 184–96] elicited no discussion; now ARW is trying to prove it. Paper merely states the theory.

On black jaguars breedinginter se: ARW has never heard of a parti-coloured one.

letters.title: From Hensleigh Wedgwood   [before 29 September 1857]
letters.summary: Suggests CD use the common origin of the French "chef" and the English "head" or "évêque" and "bishop" to illustrate the parallels between extinction and transitional forms in language and palaeontology [seeNatural selection, p. 384].

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier  29 September [1857]
letters.summary: Will collect no more pigeons. Is awaiting Burmese fowls’ skins coming via Berlin.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   30 September [1857]
letters.summary:
C. F. Ledebour [Flora rossica(1842–53)] particularly useful for variety tabulation. Results generally favourable.

Additions to Down House.

Last two chapters of MS took six months to write.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   [before 3 October 1857]
letters.summary: On classification and possibilities of a scientific morphology and zoology. CD’s "pedigree business" is important for physiology but has nothing to do with pure zoology any more than human pedigree has to do with the census. Zoological classification is a census of the animal world.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   3 October [1857]
letters.summary: Thinks naturalists look for something further than Cuvier’s view of classification. Poses a theoretical problem on the classification of the races of man to prove that a genealogical system is best.

letters.title: To James Buckman   4 October [1857]
letters.summary:
Asks JB to obtain information about pigeons.

Inquires where his article has been published ["On the discovery ofCnicus tuberosusat Avebury, Wilts.",Ann. & Mag. Nat. Hist.2d ser. 20 (1857): 337–9].

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   14 October [1857]
letters.summary: JSH’sMyosotisis beginning to sport. Asks whether some features are not odd.

letters.title: ToGardeners’ Chronicle  18 October [1857]
letters.summary:
Describes his experiments with kidney beans to test the agency of bees in their fertilisation. His results suggest they are essential.

Asks what George Swayne could mean by the advantage of artificial fertilisation of early beans [Trans. Hortic. Soc. Lond.5 (1824): 208–13].

Has observed that hive-bees, which normally suck nectar from the flower of the kidney bean, will use holes cut through the calyx by humble-bees, though the holes cannot be seen from the mouth of the flower. Suggests hive-bees see humble-bees at work and understand what they are doing and "rationally" take advantage of the shorter path to the nectar. [See also2359.]

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   18 October [1857]
letters.summary: Sends details onMyosotissports. Feels sure he could make any flower in some degree monstrous in four or five generations.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   20 October [1857]
letters.summary:
Returns some of the systematics books borrowed from JDH. Will now take on A. P. and Alphonse de Candolle [Prodromus].

Arrangements for a visit.

letters.title: From Bernard Peirce Brent   23 October 1857
letters.summary: Discusses the difficulties of breeding mules by crossing canaries and finches.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [23 October 1857]
letters.summary:
Return of books.

JDH coming to Down.

letters.title: From Thomas Glover   26 October 1857
letters.summary: Describes his work, which demonstrates that hybrids ofCactusare fertile.

letters.title: From Walter White   26 October 1857
letters.summary: Writes concerning library books requested by CD.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [before 29 October 1857]
letters.summary: Reports progress of work on the new rooms [at Down].

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   29 [October 1857]
letters.summary: Discusses WED’s future education, the work on the extension, and other domestic affairs.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   30 October [1857]
letters.summary:
Has come to think his brains were not made for thinking – he immediately feels better when at Moor Park.

News of his family.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin  [November 1857]
letters.summary: Is trying to find a tutor for WED.

letters.title: From T. V. Wollaston   [November–December 1857]
letters.summary:
He was unaware that varieties occurred proportionately more in large genera.

Recommends a work [Leonard Gyllenhaal,Insecta Suecica, 4 vols. (1808–27)] for tabulating varieties.

Lists "close geographical representatives of Europaean species" based on the species numbers [in T. V. Wollaston,Catalogue of the coleopterous insects of Madeira(1857)].

letters.title: To T. C. Eyton   2 November [1857]
letters.summary: Has TCE observed whether hybrids of Chinese and common forms [of geese] were wilder, or less tame, than both parents?

letters.title: From Henry Coe   4 November 1857
letters.summary: Responds to CD’s article on kidney beans [Collected papers1: 275–7]. Sends beans as evidence of crossing.

letters.title: From Frederick Smith   10 November 1857
letters.summary: Sends drawings of two forms of workers ofCryptocerus discocephalusin response to CD’s request for examples of insects whose workers show disparity of form.

letters.title: ToGardeners’ Chronicle  [before 12 November 1857]
letters.summary: Asks writer of an article on weeds why he supposes "there is too much reason to believe that foreign seed of an indigenous species is often more prolific than that grown at home?" The point is of interest to CD "in regard to the great battle of life which is perpetually going on all around us". Cites analogous observations by Asa Gray and J. D. Hooker. Does writer know "of any other analogous cases of a weed introduced from another land beating out … a weed previously common in any particular field or farm?"

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   [before 12 November 1857]
letters.summary:
Glad THH has taken up aphid question versus Owen ["On the agamic reproduction and morphology ofAphis",Trans. Linn. Soc. Lond.22 (1858): 193–236].

Fertilisation and inheritance discussed. Speculates that fertilisation may be a mixture rather than a fusion. Can understand in no other way why crossed forms tend to go back to ancestral forms.

letters.title: To Robert Patterson   12 November [1857]
letters.summary: The [Irish] rabbits arrived safely. "They shall be skeletonized." CD now has rabbits from Shetland, Madeira and Ireland; hopes to receive one from Jamaica.

letters.title: From Henry Coe   14 November 1857
letters.summary: More on kidney bean crosses.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker  14 [November 1857]
letters.summary:
Rule that species vary most in larger genera seems universal.

Response toGardeners’ Chroniclenote on "Bees and kidney beans" [Collected papers1: 275–7].

letters.title: From Williams & Norgate   17 November 1857
letters.summary: CD is informed that a certain work [unspecified] is not available separately.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker  21 November [1857]
letters.summary: Mrs J. S. Henslow’s illness.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier  21 November [1857]
letters.summary: When he has reviewed his work, he will give up pigeons and will probably give them away next summer. Wants a few Malay eggs in the spring.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   [22 November 1857]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Huxley and William Sharpey praise JL’s paper [? onDaphnia,Philos. Trans. R. Soc. Lond.147 (1857): 79–100] at Philosophical Club.

letters.title: To Hugh Falconer   23 November 1857
letters.summary: Can HF ask Col. E. Dickie [probably Col. Edward John Dickey] enclosed questions about Indian horses? [Questions relate to striped markings on the Kutch breed of horses.]

letters.title: To C. S. Bate   29 November [1857]
letters.summary: Asking for specific information about reproduction in barnacles.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   29 November [1857]
letters.summary:
Thanks AG for his criticisms of CD’s views; finds it difficult to avoid using the term "natural selection" as an agent.

Discusses crossing inFumariaand barnacles.

Has received a naturally crossed kidney bean in which the seed-coat has been affected by the pollen of the fertilising plant.

Finds the rule of large genera having most varieties holds good and regards it as most important for his "principle of divergence".

letters.title: To George Bentham   1 December [1857]
letters.summary:
Thanks GB for his help on naturalised plants; comments on spreading of plants.

Wants to quote GB on the names of species and varieties ofSileneon which C. F. von Gärtner experimented.

Thinks GB will be disappointed in his book [Natural selection]. "It will be grievously too hypothetical."

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker  [2 December 1857]
letters.summary:
News of Mrs Henslow’s death.

StudyingImpatiens, which bears on CD’s problems. Though genus is endemic to India, with over 100 species, CD will be glad to know they do not run into one another.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker  4 December [1857]
letters.summary: Inquiries on effect of dry heat on temperate plants for glacial chapter.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker  [6 December 1857]
letters.summary: Finds CD’s results [of his survey of well-marked varieties from A. P. and Alphonse de Candolle’sProdromus systematis naturalis regni vegetabilis(1824–73)] "very curious and suggestive". Thinks the Labiatae will present an obstacle to him as it is a very large and distinct order with well-defined species and genera. Would like to see him tackle more volumes of Candolle’sProdromus, as his case can only be established by evidence from mundane plants. CD should beware of generalising from local species variability. A comparison of C. C. Babington’s and G. Bentham’s [British]Floras[BabingtonManual of British botany(1843, 4th ed., 1856); BenthamHandbook of British flora(1858)] would be invaluable. Suggests CD write to Ferdinand Müller and Charles Moore in Australia. Moisture favouring extension of species is important for CD’s view.

letters.title: To Ferdinand Jakob Heinrich von Mueller  8 December [1857]
letters.summary: Asks whether British or north European perennial plants can, under cultivation, withstand the climate of S. Australia.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   9 December [1857]
letters.summary: Survey of species with well-marked varieties: JDH’s Labiatae case a "great blow", but result is very generally consistent.

letters.title: To E. W. V. Harcourt   13 December [1857]
letters.summary:
Thanks for offer of pigeons, if breeding is successful; hopes to go to poultry show to see them.

Several questions about the Boz or Booz pigeon of Tunis.

If any of EWVH’s birds die and he does not want the skin, perhaps he would send it to CD.

letters.title: From H. C. Watson  14 December [1857]
letters.summary: Will shortly return CD’s list of varieties of British plants. Discusses the situations in which different varieties of species are often found and the ranges of varieties relative to those of the species.

letters.title: To George Bentham   15 December [1857]
letters.summary: For his studies on fertility of crosses, asks GB to mark a list of pairs ofCucubalusas to whether they are varieties of the same species, or distinct species.

letters.title: To E. W. V. Harcourt   15 December [1857]
letters.summary:
Will not accept invitation to Hastings, or offer to send pigeons to Down.

Is looking forward to seeing pigeons at Crystal Palace poultry show.

letters.title: From George Bentham   [16 or 17 December 1857]
letters.summary: Returns CD’s lists [sent with2184]. Confusion in genera ofSileneis great in continental botanic gardens. One would have to know whether C. F. v. Gärtner had the right names for species in his experiments.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley  16 December [1857]
letters.summary: THH’s catalogue [THH and R. Etheridge,A catalogue of the collection of fossils in the Museum of Practical Geology(1865), part published in 1857] bestrésuméhe has seen of science of natural history. On classification he is not quite sure that he wholly goes along with THH. Encloses a few criticisms of THH’s preface.[enclosure survives as copy only].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker  [17–23 December 1857]
letters.summary:
Sending more Candolle volumes for survey of species with well-marked varieties.

Has begun his introduction [toFlora Tasmaniae]; will not make generalisations.

J. D. Dana’s pamphlet too metaphysical for JDH.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   17 December [1857]
letters.summary: Thanks WDF for his letter about a rabbit breed that he thinks is the Himalaya. He is particularly glad to hear of it because it breeds so true.

letters.title: To George Bentham   18 December [1857]
letters.summary: Thanks GB for his answers [to2184], which were as explicit as he expected.Cucubalus viscosusanditalicusare extremely sterile together; all other forms extremely fertile. Other instances of infertility found by Gärtner.

letters.title: From Edward Hewitt   18 December 1857
letters.summary: Hybrid varieties of pheasant and common fowl. Reply to CD queries.

letters.title: From H. C. Watson  20 December [1857]
letters.summary: Finds he cannot annotate CD’s list of subspecies and varieties as wanted. Mentions again his difficulties with "species"; he "cannot find the proof of species being definite and immutable whatever they may seem to be at any one time and spot".

letters.title: From Edward Hewitt   22 December 1857
letters.summary: Replies to more queries about fowl hybrids.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   22 December 1857
letters.summary:
Comments on agreement of their respective views on distribution.

Reference to differences on subsidence.

Reports on progress of his work and praises ARW’s investigations.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker  25 December [1857]
letters.summary:
Species with marked varieties.

Dana’s pamphlet also too metaphysical for CD.

Natural selectionchapter on hybridism completed.

Doubts JDH will resist theory in his introduction toFlora Tasmaniae.

letters.title: From James Hunt   [before 29 December 1857]
letters.summary: Birds that have been hybridised.

letters.title: To a librarian [1858 or later]
letters.summary: Will return Benjamin Jowett’sEpistles of St Paul(Jowett 1855) and requests several books, of which the latest is Hugh Miller’sCruise of the Betsey(Miller 1858).

letters.title: From Hewett Cottrell Watson   3 January 1858
letters.summary: Discusses the ranges and distribution of varieties relative to the type species.

letters.title: To Jean Louis Armand de Quatrefages de Bréau4 January [1858?]
letters.deprecated: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.recipient: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.summary:
The information correspondent hopes to get from M.-J.-P. Flourens will be valuable.

CD is keeping all varieties of pigeons, poultry, ducks, etc. for his work on variation.

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   [8 January 1858]
letters.summary:
Zebra-striped asses.

Markings of a Bengal jungle cock.

Refers to some of his own articles on birds in India.

Reports the arrival of the "glorious garrison of Lucknow". The "wonderful superiority of the European to the Asiatic" made the success of the insurrection inconceivable.

letters.title: From John Innes   9 January [1858–9]
letters.summary: Sends record of pigeon flight from London to Antwerp. [Lord W. Lennox,Merrie England(1857), p. 185.]

letters.title: To Joseph Dalton Hooker   12 January [1858]
letters.summary: On papilionaceous flowers and CD’s theory that there are no eternal hermaphrodites. Connects this theory to absence of small-flowered legumes in New Zealand and the absence of small bees as pollinators.

letters.title: To E. W. V. Harcourt   13 January [1858]
To William Darwin Fox   14 January [1858]
letters.summary:
Asks to borrow W. C. Hewitson’s book [British oology, 2 vols. (1831–44)].

CD is searching for reliable information on slight variations in the degree of perfection of nests of the same species of birds.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   15 January [1858]
letters.summary:
CD has never doubted probability of Bering Strait land connection.

Family illness.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   15 January 1858
letters.summary: Has gone over to CD’s side on the fertilisation of clover in New Zealand by bees.

letters.title: To William Bernhard Tegetmeier   17 January [1858]
letters.summary: Has received Burmese fowls’ skins from Walter Elliot.

letters.title: To John Stevens Henslow   25 January [1858]
letters.summary: Mrs Henslow’s death stirs reminiscences of happier days.

letters.title: To William Benjamin Carpenter   26 January [1858]
letters.summary: Asks WBC to plant some kidney beans [on Holy Island near Arran] and to see whether they are ever visited by bees. If no bees visit the island, it would be "curious" to observe what plants grow there.

letters.title: To George Bentham   27 January [1858]
letters.summary: Asks GB to vote for "a distant connexion of mine" at Athenaeum, and to mention this to Hooker.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   31 January [1858]
letters.summary:
Thanks WDF for information on blackbirds’ nests [seeNatural selection, p. 505].

Problem of choosing from among the load of curious facts for chapter on "Instinct" [Natural selection, ch. 10;Origin, ch. 7] perplexes him.

Asks about behaviour of chicks in danger and whether crossed animals are wilder than either parent.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   4 [February 1858]
letters.summary: Returns books by Candolle and Robert Brown.

letters.title: To George Henry Kendrick Thwaites   7 February [1858]
letters.summary: Thanks GHKT for letter on plant acclimatisation and variation among alpine and lowland forms in Ceylon.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   9 February [1858]
letters.summary: Six volumes of Candolle’sProdromusconfirm rule that small genera vary less than large. Labiatae an exception to rule.

letters.title: From George Robert Waterhouse   10 February 1858
letters.summary: Bees’ cells. Observations onOsmia atricapilla.

letters.title: From William Balfour Baikie   11 February 1858
letters.summary: Describes some species of fauna peculiar to Fernando Po. The ocean currents make it unlikely that animals have been floated to the little islands [off the west coast of Africa].

letters.title: To William Erasmus Darwin   11 [February 1858]
letters.summary:
Writes of domestic matters

and asks WED to observe cart-horses for traces of dark stripes on spine and cross-stripes on shoulder.

letters.title: From G. R. Waterhouse   13 February 1858
letters.summary: GRW’s observations of and ideas on bees’ and wasps’ cells.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [17 February 1858]
letters.summary: General success of survey makes CD very concerned about sources of error. Wants to meet JDH for an important talk about big genera. Arranges meeting.

letters.title: To Louis Agassiz 21 February [1858]
letters.summary: Thanks LA for presentation copy ofContributions[to the natural history of the United States of America, vol. 1, pt 1:Essay on classification, and vol. 1, pt 2:North American Testudinata(1857)]. Flattered; CD sees there is much of highest interest to him.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   21 February [1858]
letters.summary:
Asks whether botanists tend to record varieties more carefully in large genera or small genera.

Wants information on the ranges of varieties of a species compared to the range of the species.

letters.title: To Charles Cardale Babington   22 February [1858]
letters.summary: CD and J. D. Hooker have differed on the following question and agreed to ask several botanists: would a good botanist describing a local flora record varieties as readily in large as in small genera?

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   22 February 1858
letters.summary: Gives some observations on birds; has forwarded a box of specimens.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   22 February [1858]
letters.summary:
Thanks for Hewitson [British oology].

Has found more variability in birds’ nests than he expected.

Interested in WDF’s note about turkey terrified by a frog [seeNatural selection, p. 488 n.].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   23 February [1858]
letters.summary:
Fertilisation of clover by bees in New Zealand.

Uneasy about biggest genera and their varieties.

H. T. Buckle’s sophistry [History of civilisation in England(1857)].

Working on bees’ cells.

letters.title: From H. C. Watson   23 February [1858]
letters.summary: Believes that botanists tend to mark more varieties in large than in small genera, but notes that where many varieties of a species exist these varieties may well be passed over, whereas similar varieties of another species which are fewer in number may well be recorded.

letters.title: To Thomas Henry Huxley   24 February [1858]
letters.summary:
Congratulations on birth of THH’s daughter [Jessie].

On aboriginal dun colour of horses.

Examples of inaccuracies and perpetuation of errors [on hybrids] by "compilers, of which I am one".

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [25] February 1858
letters.summary:
Botanical practice can confuse CD’s compilations. Many small genera would have been species had the whole natural order [family] been known.

JDH’s low opinion of Buckle;

high opinion of Mrs Farrer.

letters.title: From Frederick Smith   26 February 1858
letters.summary:
Identifies an ant described by CD and discusses the predatory habits ofFormica sanguinea.

Describes some wasps’ nests.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   27 [February 1858]
letters.summary:
CD intends to enter WED at Christ’s College.

Thanks him for inquiries made about horses.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   28 February [1858]
letters.summary:
WDF’s nephew has forgotten to mention the most important element, whether the lizards’ eggs floated and stayed alive on sea-water.

Thanks for facts about turkeys and terrier [seeNatural selection, p. 481 n.].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   28 February [1858]
letters.summary:
JDH has confirmed CD’s opinion on the affinities of species in great genera. Is looking at large genera in several localFlorasto find the "range & commonness of varying species".

Has been "beyond measure interested" in the construction instincts of the hive-bee.

letters.title: From C. C. Babington   3 March 1858
letters.summary: States his belief that there is a tendency to note varieties in the larger genera rather than in the very small ones.

letters.title: To C. C. Babington   4 March [1858]
letters.summary:
Notes views of Hooker and George Bentham on monotypic forms.

Has tabulated several floras and finds that large genera show preponderance in numbers of varieties. Now sees his results are quite worthless.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   5 [March 1858]
letters.summary: C. C. Babington agrees with JDH that botanists tend to note varieties more in large genera than in very small ones.

letters.title: To the Secretary, Royal Society  5 March 1858
letters.summary: C. P. Smyth’s observations on geology and natural history of Tenerife are not precise enough to warrant publication inPhilosophical Transactions. Suggests CPS draw up an abstract, for theProceedings, of specific points actually observed, rather than conclusions arrived at on insufficient grounds.

letters.title: To Frederick Smith   [before 9 March 1858]
letters.summary: Four queries regarding the habits of bees and ants with answers by FS interlined between each query.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   10 [March 1858]
letters.summary: Heartened that tabulations of small and large genera done in different ways yield good results. JDH has done some tabulations but has not followed CD’s method of getting equal numbers of small and large genera.

letters.title: To Richard Kippist   10 March [1858]
letters.summary: In great want of two books, which he had borrowed previously: BoreauFlora du Centre de la Franceand A. E. Fürnrohr,Naturhistorische Topographie von Regensburg, Bd 2Flora Ratisbonensis.

letters.title: To Trenham Reeks?  10 March [1858]
letters.summary: Asks whether correspondent can assist in determining value of slate slabs with relief figures executed for Josiah Wedgwood [I].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   11 March [1858]
letters.summary: JDH’s "objection" that small local genera do not vary and mundane ones do, is exactly CD’s point. Local floras useful to test idea that varieties are incipient species. Same genus in different countries cannot be lumped.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [14 March 1858]
letters.summary: Summary of JDH’s objections to CD’s survey of floras and conclusion that large genera vary more than small.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   16 [March 1858]
letters.summary: Thanks JDH for his objections; will respond by sending fair copy of MS when written.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   18 March 1858
letters.summary: Continued objections to methods and conclusions of CD’s survey.

letters.title: To the Secretary, Royal Society  22 March 1858
letters.summary: Recommends Leonard Horner’s "Account of some recent researches near Cairo" for publication inPhilosophical Transactions[R. Soc. Lond.148 (1858): 53–9]. Believes all the details and sections should be published in full because of importance of investigations leading to the conclusion that man has existed in Egypt for over 13000 years.

letters.title: From H. C. Watson   23 March 1858
letters.summary: Discusses the ranges of species in large and small genera; difficulties involved in limiting the discussion to Britain.

letters.title: From H. C. Watson   [after 23 March 1858]
letters.summary: Extracts from MS of vol. 4 of HCW’sCybele Britannica[1847–59] showing the diversity of views on species among botanists.

letters.title: To ?   26 March [1858?]
letters.summary: Returns the Greenland catalogue, which he has kept too long.

letters.title: To George Busk, Linnean Society  30 March [1858]
letters.summary: Expresses his strong opinion that Huxley’s paper ["Agamic reproduction and morphology ofAphis",Trans. Linn. Soc. Lond.22 (1858): 193–220, 221–36] should be published.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   30 [March? 1858]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Comments and criticisms on JL’s paper [possibly: "On the development ofChloëon dimidiatum",Trans. Linn. Soc. Lond.24 (1863): 61–78].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   31 March [1858]
letters.summary:
Writing section on large and small genera [forNatural selection, ch. 4].

Huxley supersedes Owen on parthenogenesis.

Buckle’sHistory of civilisation in Englandextremely interesting.

letters.title: To Leonard Jenyns   1 April [1858]
letters.summary:
Thanks LJ for his book [Observations in meteorology(1858)].

CD has been working on his species book [Natural selection].

Has become dreadfully heterodox on immutability of species.

His work on pigeons: variation under domestication throws the greatest light on variation in a state of nature.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   [before 3 April 1858]
letters.summary: List of close species taken from AG’sManual of botany[1848].

letters.title: To Asa Gray   4 April [1858]
letters.summary:
Discusses the variation of species in large and small genera.

Thanks AG for his list of close species.

Laments the slow progress he makes with his book [Natural selection].

letters.title: To A. A. Gould   6 April [1858]
letters.summary:
Thanks AAG for procuring an authoritative answer from T. M. Brewer on the habits of the [American] cuckoo. Surprised William Yarrell erred so much.

Wishes AAG had time to give an account of Japanese shells, which would be interesting from the geographical point of view.

letters.title: To Leonard Jenyns   9 April [1858]
letters.summary:
Asks LJ to lend him a copy of his paper ["Variation of species",Rep. BAAS26 (1856): 101–5] and any notes or references he has. Although CD has a large accumulation of facts, it is impossible to see and consider too many.

His health is poor.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   10 April [1858]
letters.summary:
Asa Gray’s criticism of Buckle and his comments on large and small genera.

CD suspects glacial epoch immensely long. Rates of organic change too variable to make them a good measure of geological time.

Bees’ cells are a difficulty for theory.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   14 April [1858]
letters.summary: CD will go over his pigeon MS and then dispose of all his birds. Has Burmese fowls’ skins if WBT is interested.

letters.title: To William Hallowes Miller  [15 April 1858]
letters.summary: A set of questions CD prepared for his meeting with WHM to discuss the geometry of bees’ cells.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   16 April [1858]
letters.summary:
Asks WDF for facts about stripes in horses and ponies.

Health has been very bad.

letters.title: To Henry Norton Shaw, Royal Geographical Society  16 April [1858]
letters.deprecated: Henry Norton ShawSecretary, R. Geographical Soc.
letters.recipient: Henry Norton ShawSecretary, R. Geographical Soc.
letters.summary: Is much obliged and honoured by the Diploma of the Geographical Society of Vienna.

letters.title: From G. R. Waterhouse   17 April 1858
letters.summary: Bees’ cells; GRW thinks hexagonal shape is accidental. Encloses notes on cells ofIcaria.

letters.title: From Leonard Jenyns   [before 18 April 1858]
letters.summary: [Copy of some rough notes.] References about species. Variations within species.

letters.title: To Leonard Jenyns   18 April [1858]
letters.summary:
Thanks LJ for his MS [of "Variation of species",Rep. BAAS26 (1856): 101–5].

Will read it at his hydropathic establishment [Moor Park], where he is going for a rest.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   [21 April 1858]
letters.summary:
"Excessively" interested in theory of bees’ cell formation.

Fears few of his pigeons will be of any use to WBT.

Hopes WBT will describe foreign poultry breeds.

letters.title: To Emma Darwin   [25 April 1858]
letters.summary:
Concerned about ED’s headaches, CD writes an affectionate letter.

Believes he has found a rare slave-making species of ant.

Is reading novels:Beneath the surfaceandThree chances.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [26 April 1858]
letters.summary: Has been at Moor Park since Tuesday. Is passing his time watching ants.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   26 [April 1858]
letters.summary:
Confidential revelation concerning W. F. Daniell.

Georg Hartung confirms CD’s supposition from flora of Azores that icebergs had been stranded there.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   26 April [1858]
letters.summary:
Comments on letter from Georg Hartung to CL dealing with erratic boulders.

Discusses migration of plants and animals.

A letter from Thomas Thomson on heat endured by temperate plants.

letters.title: To Leonard Jenyns   [28 April 1858]
letters.summary:
Returns MS [of "Variation of species"]; several facts were new to him, especially interested in wagtails.

Wishes he could swallow Florent Prévost on sparrows ["Du régime alimentaire des oiseaux",C. R. Hebd. Acad. Sci.46 (1858): 136–8].

LJ’s facts seem to bear out CD’s conclusion that secondary sexual characters were most variable of all.

Explains how he intends to deal with variation, and general facts in natural history in the light of species theory. Can only afford one chapter on variation in nature. It seems more important to make out variation in domestic animals.

Asks for facts on birds’ nests for his chapter on instincts.

letters.title: To Emma Darwin   [28 April 1858]
letters.summary: CD recounts an idyllic stroll and nap – "as pleasant a rural scene as ever I saw, and I did not care one penny how any of the beasts or birds had been formed".

letters.title: From Erasmus Alvey Darwin   [May–June 1858]
letters.summary: Calculations relating to bees’ cells.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [3 May 1858]
letters.summary:
Discusses bees’ cells

and WED’s botanical interests.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [before 6 May 1858]
letters.summary:
Reports that N. J. Andersson finds every European willow bar one is also American.

Has heard from David Livingstone and reports on his progress.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   6 May [1858]
letters.summary:
Sends MS on large and small genera.

Observed slave-making ants at Moor Park.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   8 May [1858]
letters.summary:
Will be most curious to hear results of WDF’s experiment with a kite and turkey chicks "by themselves".

If WDF ever sees a striped dun horse, he should ascertain colour of dam and sire.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   9 May [1858]
letters.summary: Inquires about the structure and formation of bees’ comb; is interested in seeing its form at the commencement of building.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   14 [May 1858]
letters.summary:
Relates events at home;

hopes WED gets the scholarship.

letters.title: From W. H. Miller   [14 May 1858]
letters.summary: [Six fragments, mainly diagrams.] The geometry of bees’ cells.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   16 May [1858]
letters.summary:
Arranges meeting with JDH at Thatched House Tavern.

Eager for JDH’s reaction to MS on large and small genera.

letters.title: To Syms Covington   18 May [1858]
letters.summary: CD’s health has been poor owing to hard work [onNatural selection]. He has to treat of every branch of natural history, which is beyond his strength.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   18 [May 1858]
letters.summary: Arrangements for JDH to visit Down for weekend.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [26 May 1858]
letters.summary:
Has come to heavy grief about bees’ cells, unless Huber is wrong [François Huber,New observations on the natural history of bees, new ed. (1841)].

Discusses cart-horses and stripes on a Belgiman [Belgian?].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   3 June [1858]
letters.summary: CD’s receipt of diploma from Caesarea Leopoldino-Carolina Academy [Dresden].

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier 5 June [1858]
letters.summary:
Hopes to begin pigeon MS in a week.

Has lately been working on bees’ cells and wishes very much to examine a cylindrical one.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   [before 8 June 1858]
letters.summary: Gives calculations on the structure of bees’ cells.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   [8 June 1858]
letters.summary: Encloses projections and models relating to geometry of bees’ cells.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   8 [June 1858]
letters.summary:
Pleased with JDH’s reaction to MS on large and small genera.

Confident of soundness of principle of divergence.

CD experimenting on pollination mechanism of Leguminosae. Asks JDH to investigate Fumariaceae.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   8 [June 1858]
letters.summary: Discusses bees’ cells. Wants hive and swarm; would be glad to have WBT’s box with commenced cells. "I am partly a disciple of Waterhouse, but not wholly."

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   [after 8 June 1858]
letters.summary: Sends a model of bee cells "as bad as a Chinese puzzle". [A series of paper cut-out figures.]

letters.title: From John Lubbock   10 June 1858
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary:
Thanks for queen-bee larva and pupa.

Nervous system ofCoccus.

letters.title: From W. D. Fox   11 June [1858]
letters.summary:
Discusses instinct in ducks and turkeys.

Reports a case of the inheritance of an acquired characteristic in a pig.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   18 [June 1858]
letters.summary: Encloses MS by A. R. Wallace. CD has been forestalled. " . . . if Wallace had my MS sketch written out in 1842 he could not have made a better short abstract!" Wallace does not say if he wishes CD to publish MS, but CD will offer to send it to journal.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   [19 June 1858]
letters.summary: Discusses geometry related to the structure of bees’ cells. Encloses notes and diagrams dealing with intersections of spheres.

letters.title: To Roderick Impey Murchison  19 June [1858]
letters.summary: There is much weight in what RIM says about not breaking up the natural history collection of the British Museum. The botanical collection might be moved to Kew, but CD thinks "it would be the greatest evil which could possibly happen to natural science in this country if the other collections were ever to be removed from the British Museum and Library".

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [20 June 1858]
letters.summary:
Relates domestic affairs.

Thinks his bees’ cell theory will hold good.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   21 June 1858
letters.summary:
Self-fertilisation in Fumariaceae.

[CD note on bees’ visiting some members of Fumariaceae.]

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   22 June [1858]
letters.summary:
Thanks for hive.

Has started [writing up] pigeons and hopes to have finished with them in a week or two.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   23 [June 1858]
letters.summary: Etty [Henrietta Darwin] very ill with diphtheria.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   24 June [1858]
letters.summary: Gives his opinion of the charges against E. W. Lane.

letters.title: To R. I. Murchison   24 [June 1858]
letters.summary:
Extremely sorry for trouble he has given about his signature.

One child dangerously ill with diphtheria, another with much fever.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [25 June 1858]
letters.summary: Everything in Wallace’s sketch also appears in CD’s sketch of 1844. A year ago CD sent a short sketch of his views to Asa Gray. Can CD honourably publish his sketch now that Wallace has sent outline of his views? "I would far rather burn my whole book than that he or any man shd. think that I had behaved in a paltry spirit." Does not believe Wallace originated his views from anything CD wrote to him.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   26 [June 1858]
letters.summary:
Is it fair to take advantage of knowing that Wallace is in the field? Seems hard on CD to lose priority of many years, but does not feel this alters justice of case.

Baby [Charles Waring Darwin] has much fever. Frightened because three children in village have died from scarlet fever.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   27 [June 1858]
letters.summary:
Profoundly sorry for Lane.

Thanks WDF for facts about call ducks, pigs, and Leicester sheep.

Has been observing and experimenting on the construction of bees’ cells. Thinks he has a theory which simplifies the problem.

Scarlet fever in family; nurse ill.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker [29 June 1858]
letters.summary:
Death of Charles Waring Darwin [1856–8] from scarlet fever.

JDH’s and Lyell’s kindness [presumably about A. R. Wallace’s letter]. CD can provide a copy of his letter to Asa Gray [about CD’s species theory].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [29 June 1858]
letters.summary: JDH wants papers at once. CD sends Wallace’s paper and CD’s abstract of his letter to Asa Gray. Sends [species] sketch of 1844 with JDH’s notes to assure JDH he had read it.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   2 July [1858]
letters.summary: Baby [Charles Waring Darwin] died of scarlet fever on 28 June. "Fear has almost driven away grief."

letters.title: To Asa Gray   4 July 1858
letters.summary:
Believes that, inDicentra,FumariaandCorydalis, flower structures are related directly to visits from bees. Flower stigmas generally are placed in the path of bees.

Has received paper from Wallace on natural selection; has sent abstract of his notions, with Wallace’s paper, to Linnean Society.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   4 [July 1858]
letters.summary: Death in family [Charles Waring Darwin]. Illness of children forces him to leave home and interrupt work on pigeons.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   5 July [1858]
letters.summary: Thanks JDH for his report on the reading of the Wallace and Darwin papers at the Linnean Society [read 1 July 1858;Collected papers2: 3–19]. Considers how to publish his work. Offers to forward a note from JDH to Wallace.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   6 July [1858]
letters.summary: The crisis is abating – no further scarlet fever in the family.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   13 [July 1858]
letters.summary:
JDH’s letter to Wallace perfect. CD’s feelings about priority. Without Lyell’s and JDH’s intervention CD would have given up all claims to Wallace. Now planning 30-page abstract for a journal.

Observations on floral structure

and slave-making ants.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   13–15 July 1858
letters.summary:
Sends proofs [of "On the tendency of species to form varieties … ", read 1 July 1858,Collected papers2: 3–19]. CD could publish his abstract [later theOrigin] as a separate supplemental number of [Journal of the Linnean Society].

JDH has studied in detail CD’s manuscript on variable species in large and small genera and concurs with its consequences. Discusses methodological idiosyncrasies of systematists, e.g., Bentham, Robert Brown, and C. C. Babington, which complicate CD’s tabulations.

letters.title: From William Swale  13 July 1858
letters.summary: Discusses the absence of a native bee in New Zealand and the insects which probably performed its fertilising function [see "Agency of bees in fertilization",Collected papers2: 21]. Describes the success of the naturalised hive-bee and also the rapid spread of introduced members of the Fabaceae.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [18 July 1858]
letters.summary: Regards from Isle of Wight.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   18 July [1858]
letters.summary:
Thanks for abstract of Etna paper [Philos. Trans. R. Soc. Lond.148 (1858): 703–86]. Never expected to see Élie de Beaumont’s theory ["craters of elevation"] so completely upset. "He must have picked out favourable cases for measurement."

More than satisfied by what was done at Linnean Society [joint reading of CD’s and Wallace’s papers: "Tendency of species to form varieties",Collected papers2: 3–19]. Intends to prepare longer abstract.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   21 [July 1858]
letters.summary:
After all, CD is now beginning to prepare an abstract of his species theory. Recounts the events leading to joint paper with A. R. Wallace at Linnean Society. Lyell and Hooker urge strongly that he publish a fuller abstract. It is impossible to do justice to subject in an abstract.

His sister, Marianne Parker, has died.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   21 July [1858]
letters.summary:
Correcting proof for CD–Wallace paper. Has begun abstract.

Large and small genera.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   30 [July 1858]
letters.summary:
Six children have died of scarlet fever in Down village.

Writing abstract is amusing and improving work. Thanks JDH and Lyell for setting him to it.

letters.title: To William Jackson Hooker   [30 July 1858]
letters.summary: Thanks WJH for an extract on seed transport by sea. [Letter sent with2314.]

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   31 July 1858
letters.summary:
The CD–Wallace paper has gone to press.

JDH’s tabulation of variable species from Bentham was done in haste.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   [August–September 1858]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Variations in the structure ofPelargoniumflowers.

letters.title: From G. R. Waterhouse   2 August 1858
letters.summary: Bees’ cells; is the hexagonal shape deliberate or merely the result of lateral pressure on cylinders?

letters.title: To Thomas Campbell Eyton   4 August [1858]
letters.summary:
Has finished arranging his pigeons’ skeletons. May consult TCE on them.

CD is at work on an abstract of his conclusions on species and varieties [Origin]. His "bigger book" [Natural selection] will take two or three more years.

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   4 August [1858]
letters.summary:
CD and his family have come to the seashore, driven from home by scarlet fever at Down, death [of Charles Waring Darwin], and other family illness. Sorry to miss seeing JSH.

Would be grateful to hear his objections to CD’s species speculations.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [5 August 1858]
letters.summary: Working on abstract, which now is to consist of a number of sections each to be read at Linnean Society and to be published as a unit. Has finished section on variation under domestication.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [10 August 1858]
letters.summary:
Thanks JDH for stylistic corrections on MS of large and small genera.

Observations, while walking along headlands, on thistle-down blown out to sea and then blown inland.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   11 August [1858]
letters.summary:
Species migration since the Pliocene. Effect of the glacial epoch. Present geographical distribution, especially similarities of mountain floras, explained by such migration; mountain summits as remnants of a once continuous flora and fauna.

Cross-fertilisation in Fumariaceae.

letters.title: From Charles Moore   11 August 1858
letters.summary: Encloses a list of British perennials which seed in New South Wales and explains the source of his information. Lists plants which have become weeds in the country.

letters.title: To Trenham Reeks?  13 August [1858]
letters.summary: Has been asked to set a price on slate relief slabs [see2236]. Would appreciate advice from correspondent as he would like to buy pictures with the money.

letters.title: To John Phillips   1 September [1858]
letters.summary: Explains that he cannot serve as President of the Zoological Section at the BAAS meeting [1858].

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   8 September [1858]
letters.summary:
Has finished with and is disposing of his pigeons.

Invites WBT to Down; would like to see his bees’ cells.

letters.title: From J. Burningham[10 September 1858?]
letters.summary: Reports his observations on an ants’ nest.

letters.title: From Henry Coe   18 September 1858
letters.summary: Cannot explain impurity of his alleged pure lines.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   22 [September 1858]
letters.summary:
Discusses domestic affairs.

Is working at the abstract of his book [Origin].

Asks WED to examine birds’ feet for dirt sticking to them, as this may represent a means of seed dispersal across seas.

letters.title: To the Secretary, Royal Society  28 September 1858
letters.summary: Recommends W. B. Carpenter’s latest part of memoir on Foraminifera be published inPhilosophical Transactions[R. Soc. Lond.149 (1859): 1–41].

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   2 October [1858]
letters.summary:
Ask some questions on pigeons.

Remarks on the discussion of bees’ cells at the Leeds BAAS meeting. CD fancies he has the true theory with regard to their construction.

letters.title: To T. C. Eyton   4 October [1858]
letters.summary:
Comments on TCE’s skeletons.

Must get advice from Hugh Falconer on names of some bones.

Preparing his abstract [Origin].

Asks about colours of horses and stripes on asses.

letters.title: To [J. D. Hooker]   [before 6 October 1858]
letters.summary: Asks whether there are dogs in Spain like English pointers.

letters.title: From Henry Coe   6 October 1858
letters.summary: Sends more bean seeds.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   6 October [1858]
letters.summary:
Sends £20. Family news.

Answers WED’s questions about CD’sJournal of researches: Galapagos "productions" all came from America, but "they have since been modified by my principle of Natural Selection".

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   6 October [1858]
letters.summary:
Abstract growing to inordinate length.

Writing in support of S. Passell as assistant at Linnean Society.

letters.title: To T. C. Eyton   11 October [1858]
letters.summary: Asks about dirt clinging to feet of birds as means of seed distribution.

letters.title: From Henry Coe   12 October 1858
letters.summary: Answers CD’s queries about seed lot he has just sent.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   12 [October 1858]
letters.summary:
Abstract will run into a small volume.

Urges JDH not to reject natural selection until he has read abstract.

[Enclosed are CD’s comments on a ?JDH manuscript that perhaps belong elsewhere.]

letters.title: To Skeffington Poole  13 October [1858]
letters.summary: Asks about Indian horses. Encloses questions.

letters.title: To George Bentham   15 October [1858]
letters.summary: At Hooker’s request, sends his copy of Gärtner [Bastarderzeugung(1849)], "shamefully scribbled over".

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   15 [October 1858]
letters.summary: Writes to WED about his living arrangements at Christ’s College; reminisces about his own Cambridge days.

letters.title: To Hugh Falconer   15 October [1858]
letters.summary: Cannot come to London until Tuesday. Arriving about 11: 15.

letters.title: From T. C. Eyton   16 October 1858
letters.summary: Has examined feet of many partridges, but has not been able to obtain any quantity of mud from them.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   17 [October 1858]
letters.summary: Has read WBT’s interesting communication on bees’ cells [Athenæum16 Oct 1858]. Would like to see his excavated cells.

letters.title: From Henry Coe   20 October 1858
letters.summary: Further answers on his seed lot.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   20 [October 1858]
letters.summary:
Fertilisation of papilionaceous flowers [Collected papers2: 19–25].

JDH’s reactions to CD’s theory.

Discussed human fossil evidence with Hugh Falconer.

letters.title: To Skeffington Poole   20 October [1858]
letters.summary: Asks about Kattywar (Kathiawari) horses in India.

letters.title: From Skeffington Poole   [21 October 1858]
letters.summary: Information about about Kattywar (Kathiawari) horses in India.

letters.title: To Skeffington Poole   22 October [1858]
letters.summary: Asks supplementary questions about Kattywar (Kathiawari) horses in India.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   23 October [1858]
letters.summary: CD’s reasons for not signing the memorial requesting removal of natural history exhibits from British Museum. Less sure about moving botanical specimens to Kew. His notion of museum organisation.

letters.title: From Skeffington Poole   23 October 1858
letters.summary: Further information about about Kattywar (Kathiawari) horses in India.

letters.title: To Skeffington Poole   [27 October 1858]
letters.summary: Thanks for the information about about Kattywar (Kathiawari) horses in India.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   29 [October 1858]
letters.summary: Memorial concerning British Museum collection. CD opposes removing the natural history collection of the British Museum to Kensington.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [30 October 1858]
letters.summary:
Glad WED has begun under George Henslow in the way that he has. CD wishes he had had such practice under J. S. Henslow.

Has had luck in his search for striped horses.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   [November 1858]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Praise for abstract of JL’s paper on insects ["On the ova and pseudova of insects",Proc. R. Soc. Lond.9 (1857–9): 574–83].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   2 November [1858]
letters.summary:
On moving the natural history collection of the British Museum to Kensington.

Subscription for John Ralfs.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [3 November 1858]
letters.summary: Sends WED a bank draft.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   3 November [1858]
letters.summary: Hooker has convinced him that move of British Museum by Government is anticipated. He is now willing to sign the memorial. Still fears for library needs, and objects to distant Kensington site. Lyell should be asked to sign.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   5 [November 1858]
letters.summary: Discusses matters relating to WED’s first term [at Cambridge].

letters.title: To James Egan  8 November [1858]
letters.summary: Asks about dark stripes on shoulders and legs of Hungarian horses. Are stripes plainer in foal or adult?

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   9[–10] November [1858]
letters.summary: Lyell receives Copley Medal; CD to write notes for JDH’sélogeof Lyell.

letters.title: To J. S. Henslow   9 November [1858]
letters.summary: Arrangements to meet JSH at station for his visit to Down.

letters.title: To Robert Monsey Rolfe   10 November [1858]
letters.deprecated: Robert Monsey Rolfe, 1st Baron Cranworth of Cranworth
letters.recipient: Robert Monsey Rolfe, 1st Baron Cranworth of Cranworth
letters.summary: Thanks RMR for contribution to Down charities. Declines invitation.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   12 November 1858
letters.summary:
Busy with introductory essay to [The botany of the Antarctic voyage, pt III]Flora Tasmaniae[printed separately asOn the flora of Australia(1859)].

Now explains greater abundance of European species in Tasmania than in Fuegia by CD’s "refrigeration" hypothesis.

letters.title: ToGardeners’ Chronicle  [before 13 November 1858]
letters.summary:
Reports the decreased yield of pods resulting from excluding bees from the flowers of the kidney bean. Gives other observations suggesting the importance of bees in the fertilisation of papilionaceous flowers.

Cites cases of crosses between varieties of bean grown close together and requests observations from readers on the subject. States his belief "that is a law of nature that every organic being should occasionally be crossed with a different individual of the same species".

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   13 November [1858]
letters.summary:
Has suggested WDF’s name to Hooker and Henslow, who are sending a circular for aid to John Ralfs.

Is working steadily at his abstract, hopes to publish in spring.

Asks if WDF has seen a donkey with double shoulder stripe; also, has he seen a black greyhound with tan feet and a tan spot over each eye? "Such must existbecausetheory tells me it ought!"

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   14 November [1858]
letters.summary:
Hermaphrodite trees are enough to "knock" CD down. Can JDH observeEucalyptusto see whether pollen and stigma mature at same time?

JDH’s facts showing European plants are more common in southern Australia than in South America are disturbing because they are improbable on CD’s views of migration.

JDH said he would give examples of Australian forms that have migrated north along the mountains of the Malay Archipelago.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [14 November 1858]
letters.summary: An enclosure sent with the letter to JDH, 14 November [1858] (Correspondencevol. 7) - questions and comments on lists of European species found in south-west Australia and Tasmania, and European genera found in Australia.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   16 November [1858]
letters.summary: Wants WBT’s advice on poultry breeding experiments. Are certain birds true to their kind, and what should he pay for them?

letters.title: From Samuel Wells   17 November 1858
letters.summary: Reports on difference between first and second plantings of beans.

letters.title: To the Chancellor of the Exchequer 18 November 1858
letters.summary: CD and eight zoologists and botanists publish a memorial on "the arrangements by which National Collections in Natural History can be best adapted to the advancement of science and its general diffusion among the Public".

letters.title: To Asa Gray   18 November [1858]
letters.summary: Wishes to know whether differences in constitution (such as disease susceptibility) are related to differences in complexion. "Liability to such a disease as yellow fever would answer my question in the best possible way."

letters.title: From William Allport Leighton  19 November 1858
letters.summary: Sends an account of different colours and shapes of seeds raised from ordinary seeds of scarlet runner. [SeeCross and self-fertilisation, p. 151.]

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [20 November 1858]
letters.summary:
At work on the introductory essay toFlora Tasmaniae.

Discusses the effects of climate and geography on "vegetable strife".

letters.title: To W. A. Leighton   21 November [1858]
letters.summary: Thanks WAL for specimens and observations [on scarlet runner beans]. CD is perplexed whether to account for the changes as due to simple variation or to crossing. The information will be used when he finally comes to a conclusion on the subject [seeCross and self-fertilisation, p. 151].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [23 November 1858]
letters.summary: CD declines to write Lyelléloge[for Copley Medal] because of his ill health.

letters.title: From John Pearson   23 November 1858
letters.summary: Refers to CD’s article "Fertilisation of papilionaceous flowers" inGardeners’ Chronicle[Collected papers2: 19–25] and asks how forced beans flower in winter when no insect is on the wing.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker  24–5 November [1858]
letters.summary:
Praises JDH’s Australian introduction.

Disputes JDH’s emphasis on SE. and SW. Australian flora.

letters.title: To James Egan   25 November [1858]
letters.summary:
Thanks JE for information about striped horses.

Says John Lindley wants to know about Hungarian horticulture.

letters.title: To Herbert Spencer   25 November [1858]
letters.summary:
Thanks for HS’sEssays:[scientific, political, and speculative, vol. 1 (1858)]. Admires his general argument for the development theory.

CD is preparing an abstract on change of species. He treats subject as a naturalist, not from a general point of view. Otherwise he might have quoted HS’s argument to great advantage.

CD particularly liked articles on music and style. Expression is a favourite topic with CD. Agrees all expression is biological.

letters.title: From Samuel Wells   25 November 1858
letters.summary: Replies to CD’s question on whether beans in first or second year were planted near any other varieties.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   27 [November 1858]
letters.summary:
Memorial concerning British Museum collection.

Relation of Cape of Good Hope and Australian flora a great trouble. CD’s high estimation of importance of glacial period for distribution.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   27 [November 1858]
letters.summary: "I thank you much for your note. The object, of course, is what you say. I did not guess that I shd have to pay so much per hen to Baker & the experiment would not be at all worth such a sum. I have not a single hen worth sending to Steven’s. If it really will not cost you much trouble, & you could get me some Hens & ayoungSpanish cock of pure breed . . . I will try to experiment and shall be very heartily obliged to you". CD mentions satisfactory local hens of a particular breed and an experiment being conducted on "Silver Barbs [with] black wing bars & white rump or bar at end of tail".

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   1 December [1858]
letters.summary: Has had some misgivings about the memorial but now thinks his fears were vain and cowardly. Regrets R. I. Murchison was not told in advance. His low opinion of the Government and B. Disraeli.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   3 December [1858]
letters.summary: Examining JDH’s list. CD struck by how many plants are common to Europe, S. America, and Australia.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [9 December 1858]
letters.summary:
Approves of WED’s moving into CD’s old rooms [at Christ’s College]. Gives fatherly advice on Cambridge’s temptation to idleness. Christmas plans.

Health poor of late.

letters.title: To Walter Elliot   12 December [1858]
letters.summary:
Thanks WE for an oriental treatise on pigeons, a paper on poultry, and specimens.

Asks about stripes on shoulders and legs of horses and donkeys.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   17 December 1858
letters.summary: K. E. von Baer’s view of the air bladder of fishes.

letters.title: To James Paget   19 December [1858]
letters.summary:
Asks JP to remember him if anything occurs to him "in regard to inheritance atcorresponding or rather earlier ages". Sends JP a few examples for his "Chronometry of life". CD is sure he often met with striking facts but he disregarded them. "Deviations alone would have struck me."

Effects of different climates on breeding periods.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   22 December 1858
letters.summary:
Would appreciate loan of CD’s chapter on transmigration across tropics, which may help with the difficulties of Australian distribution.

Still regards plant types as older than animal types.

The Cape of Good Hope and Australian temperate floras cannot be connected by the highlands of Abyssinia.
