letters.summary: [Queries in CD’s hand answered on same pages by WBT.] Sexual selection of fowls; role of beauty in cocks.

letters.title: From Bernard Peirce Brent   29 May 1861
letters.summary: Sexual behaviour of fowls.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   30 May [1861]
letters.summary: Has written recollections of Henslow [Collected papers2: 72–4].

letters.title: From Emma Darwin   [June 1861]
letters.summary: Describes her compassion for all his sufferings and writes of her wish that his gratitude could be offered to heaven as well as to herself. To her, the only relief is to try to believe that suffering and illness are from God’s hand "to help us to exalt our minds & to look forward with hope to a future state".

letters.title: To C. W. Crocker   1 June [1861]
letters.summary: Suggests procedures for breeding experiments with hollyhocks. Recommends C. F. v. Gärtner [Bastarderzeugung(1849)]. [See also3151]

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   1 [June 1861]
letters.summary: Writes about dealings through John Lubbock regarding [a banking partnership for] WED.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   1 June [1861]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: William Darwin can go to Southampton any time should the banking proposition come to anything. CD is sure he would work hard.

letters.title: To A. G. More   2 June 1861
letters.summary:
Asks for specimens ofAceras.

Mentions orchid species he has seen. Asks AGM to make observations.

letters.title: To P. L. Sclater   2 June [1861]
letters.summary: Discusses feral rabbits of Porto Santo. Arranges for care of rabbits while the Darwins visit Torquay.

letters.title: To A. G. More   4 June 1861
letters.summary: Sends queries concerning insect fertilisation ofEpipactis palustris.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   5 June [1861]
letters.summary:
AG’s review of John Phillips’ book [Life on earth(1860), inAm. J. Sci.2d ser. 31 (1861): 444–9].

Thinks his experiments will explainPrimuladimorphism.

Insect fertilisation of orchids.

Wishes that the "greatest curse on Earth", slavery, were abolished.

letters.title: To Samuel Pickworth Woodward   5 June [1861]
letters.summary:
Gives directions to Down. Would be happy to see SPW but regrets they "have no attractions".

Agrees about colonisation of Arctic region.

CD thought that his St Helena land shells had quite recently become embedded; his specimens are at the Geological Society.

Can SPW ask A. Günther for any references toSilurusescaping from the Danube?

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   6 [June 1861]
letters.summary: Writes regarding the possibility of banking partnership for WED; second note arranges a meeting between the involved parties in London.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   6 June [1861]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Arrangements for a meeting.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   [8 June 1861]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Asks to meet JL for a final talk about the banking partnership for William Darwin.

letters.title: To ?   11 June [1861–8]
letters.summary: CD regrets he has to turn down an invitation because of his ill health.

letters.title: From Thomas Francis Jamieson   13 June 1861
letters.summary:
Will look for botanical specimens CD requested.

Tells of a kestrel with a broken leg which apparently was forced to change its diet to worms and snails because of the injury.

letters.title: To Edward Walford   13 June [1861]
letters.summary: Sends "the dates of the principal events of my Life" requested by EW [for use in hisMen of the time(1862)].

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   14 June [1861]
letters.summary: Sends MS on fowls for WBT’s inspection.

letters.title: ToGardeners’ Chronicle   [before 15 June 1861]
letters.summary: Reports his experiment with fertilising the large periwinkle (Vinca major), which he had never known to produce seed. He found that the pollen could not reach the stigma without the aid of insects, which in England never visit the flower. CD produced seeds by inserting a fine bristle, like the proboscis of a moth. Asks readers to repeat this experiment with other species that do not habitually seed and to report the result.

letters.title: To theField   [before 15 June 1861]
letters.summary: His thanks to "Eques" of Argyllshire for his remarkable information on the inheritance of colour in horses. Acknowledges the difficulty of defining dun. Requests further information.

letters.title: To Bingham Sibthorpe Malden   15–16 June [1861]
letters.summary: Thanks BSM for orchid specimens. Discusses various species ofOrchisandOphrys.

letters.title: From B. P. Brent   15 June 1861
letters.summary:
On his father’s crossing experiments with cacti, in which hybrids were found quite fertile.

On his breeding of guinea-pigs.

Sends Miss E. Watts’s message about crested fowls and Brahmas.

letters.title: To George Bentham   17 June [1861]
letters.summary: Asks for specimen ofOrchis pyramidalisfor his work on insect fertilisation of orchids.

letters.title: To George Gordon   17 June [1861]
letters.summary: Asks whether GG can help CD get specimens ofCorallorhiza.

letters.title: To A. G. More   17 June 1861
letters.summary:
Would be grateful for observations on orchids.

BelievesSpiranthesvisited by moths. Asks AGM to repeat experiment onSpiranthes.

letters.title: ToJournal of Horticulture   [before 18 June 1861]
letters.summary: CD, commenting on a case of peloric flowering inAuricula, urges readers to send in their observations on whether flowers nearest the axis tend to differ from others on the plant. Such a law of variation would be worth discovering.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   19 June [1861]
letters.summary:
CD’s changing taste in periodical literature.

William Darwin’s partnership in bank.

Work: variation and orchids.

letters.title: To Frederick Smith   19 June [1861]
letters.summary: Discusses pollen-masses found on various insects.

letters.title: To ?   20 June [1861–8]
letters.summary: Sends a copy of the paper [with A. R. Wallace, "On the tendency of species to form varieties" (1858),Collected papers2: 3–19] about which his correspondent asked; CD’s parts were written years ago and not intended for publication; he gave permission for publication of the extracts. Wallace’s paper seems to him excellent.

letters.title: To George Bentham   22 June [1861]
letters.summary:
Thanks GB for specimen [ofOrchis pyramidalis].

Discusses a great difficulty with orchids: "Insects visit several species which never secrete an atom of honey." [SeeOrchids, p. 44ff.] Does GB know whether nectar is ever secreted and reabsorbed promptly?

letters.title: To George Gordon   22 June [1861]
letters.summary:
Thanks GG for his efforts.Corallorhizawould be most valuable.

Leaves for Torquay on 1 July.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   22 June [1861]
letters.summary: Many mutual acquaintances are ill.

letters.title: To Henry Bence Jones   23 June [1861]
letters.summary: Noting that he is not an M.D., he would be much gratified should the University of Breslau think fit to honour him.

letters.title: From Hugh Falconer   23 June 1861
letters.summary:
Offers CD a liveProteus anguinusfrom Adelsberg cave. In his hands it will have a fair chance of developing into "some type of Columbidae (say a pouter or tumbler)".

TheOriginis universally praised in Italy and Germany, even by those who disagree with it.

letters.title: To Hugh Falconer   [24 June 1861]
letters.summary:
Thanks HF for offer of valuable specimen, but CD has no aquarium. Suggests the Zoological Society would be the best place for it.

Will keep HF’s note among a very few precious letters.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   24 June [1861]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary:
There have been delays, but William Darwin’s banking position is nearly settled.

Is going to Torquay, where he will write up his work on orchids.

letters.title: From Robert Colgate   25 June 1861
letters.summary: Notes observations on the spread of bees in New Zealand and their importance as pollinators of clover and other introduced plants.

letters.title: To George Gordon   4 July [1861]
letters.summary: Thanks GG for his great kindness aboutCorallorhiza. CD will try to get plants from J. H. Balfour.

letters.title: To George Dickie   [5 July 1861]
letters.summary: Thanks forListeraspecimen, which arrived withered from being sent in a wooden box.

letters.title: To George Gordon   6 July [1861]
letters.summary: Apologises for trespassing on GG’s kindness again. Believes there is a new point of structure inListera cordataand asks GG to send specimens if it is still in flower.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [6 July 1861]
letters.summary:
Trip to Torquay.

Superiority ofJournal of HorticulturetoGardeners’ Chroniclefor CD’s purposes.

letters.title: To A. G. More   7 July 1861
letters.summary: Asks for more flowers ofEpipactis palustris. Asks AGM to experiment onEpipactis.

letters.title: From Tiberius Cornelis Winkler   7 July 1861
letters.summary:
Sends his article ["Quelques nouvelles espèces de poissons fossiles",Hollandsche Maatschappij der Wetenschappen, Haarlem2d ser. 14 (1861)]

and Dutch translation of theOrigin.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   8 July [1861]
letters.summary:
Family news.

Henslow’s death a sad loss. Leonard Jenyns will write a biography.

letters.title: ToJournal of Horticulture   [before 9 July 1861]
letters.summary: CD thanks correspondents for information relating to the fertilisation ofPelargoniumand of wheat. Suggests further observations and experiments.

letters.title: To Charles Lovegrove   9 July [1861?]
letters.summary: Regrets he does not have pedigree of CL’s "pretty pony", but assures him information was very useful, "more especially as it confirms what I heard from Norway & did not know whether fully to believe".

letters.title: To John Lubbock   10 July [1861]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Seeks JL’s advice on the articles of partnership in the Southampton bank. CD and his solicitor fear they will be unfavourable to William.

letters.title: To Frances Julia Wedgwood   11 July [1861]
letters.summary:
Admires FJW’s article ["The boundaries of science",Macmillan’s Mag.4 (1861): 237–47]. Thinks she understands his book [Origin] perfectly.

On design in nature: the more CD thinks on the subject the less he can see proof of it.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   13 July [1861]
letters.summary:
Has worked out homologies of orchids’ pollinia and rostellum.

On W. H. Harvey’s review ["The natural evolution of organic species considered",Dublin Hosp. Gaz.8 (1861): 146–52].

letters.title: To George Maw   13 July [1861]
letters.summary:
Thanks GM for his fair review [ofOrigin,Zoologist19 (1861): 7577–611].

Feels it is a pity to mingle science and religion;

explains why he did not deal with the case of man.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   14 July [1861]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Thanks JL and his father for advice regarding Southampton bank. Has written to Atherley for fair terms.

letters.title: From Henry Fawcett   16 July [1861]
letters.summary: Elaborates on his article ["A popular exposition of Mr Darwin on the origin of species",Macmillan’s Mag.3 (1860): 81–92]. Was anxious to point out that CD’s method of investigation is philosophically correct. Asks permission to call.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   17 [July 1861]
letters.summary:
Orchids from Kew.

JDH’s income problems.

letters.title: To A. G. More   17 July 1861
letters.summary:
Asks for specimen ofOrchis latifoliaandO. maculata. " … as some Botanists doubt whether they are distinct species it would be rather curious to show them insects distinguish them".

Found a lot of bee orchids. "All facts point clearly to self-fertilisation in this species; yet I cannot swallow the bitter pill."

letters.title: To Hewett Cottrell Watson   [17 July 1861]
letters.summary:
Difficulty of distinguishing varieties and species. Did HCW suggest a printed list that might help?

Polymorphic genera.

letters.title: To Peter Martin Duncan?   18 July [1861]
letters.summary:
He is no longer able to answer any of the correspondent’s questions concerning corals.

Places "much trust" in J. D. Dana.

letters.title: To George Maw   19 July [1861]
letters.summary: Has read GM’s review and thanks him for its fair and liberal spirit. Discusses briefly several specific difficulties raised by it.

letters.title: To A. G. More   19 July 1861
letters.summary: Thanks forEpipactis palustris. Doubts moths are the visitants. Thanks for experiment.

letters.title: To Henry Fawcett   20 July 1861
letters.summary: "You could not possibly have told me anything which would have given me more satisfaction than what you say about Mr. Mill’s opinion." [See2868.]

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   20 July [1861]
letters.summary:
Mentions George Maw’s "good review" ofOrigin[Zoologist19 (1861): 7577–611].

Relates remark by J. S. Mill concerning soundness of logic and method ofOrigin.

Is at work [onOrchidsandVariation].

letters.title: To Asa Gray   21 July [1861]
letters.summary:
Is writing his paper on orchids.

Is surprised that AG gets little or no response withDrosera.

Describes the two forms ofPrimulaand asks whether AG knows any analogous cases of dimorphism.

Reports that John Stuart Mill approves of CD’s scientific method.

Discusses American politics.

letters.title: To John Tyndall   24 July [1861]
letters.summary:
Has been idling and enjoying the scenery.

"At dinner we were all sticking bits of ice together by their points, marvelling at the phenomenon and talking of you."

letters.title: From H. C. Watson   24 July 1861
letters.summary:
Distribution of varieties and subspecies.

George Maw’s review of theOrigin[Zoologist19 (1861): 7577–611].

letters.title: From H. C. Watson   [after 24 July 1861]
letters.summary: Gives CD an instance of facts that can be read either way as to whether a plant (Veronica humifusa) is a species or a variety.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   26 July [1861]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary:
Thanks JL for assistance with William Darwin’s banking partnership; considers everything is now settled.

Is enjoying himself and doing a little work on orchids.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   27 July [1861]
letters.summary: On orchids supplied by Kew; homologies of pollen and rostellum.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [28 July – 10 August 1861]
letters.summary:
Puzzled by function of orchids’ rostellum.

Orchids’ pollen concentrated in two pollinia; hence one flower can fertilise only two others. This may explain precision of orchid pollination mechanisms.

letters.title: From William Branwhite Clarke   [August 1861]
letters.summary: Evidence of glacial action in Australia. [SeeOrigin, 4th ed., p. 443.]

letters.title: To John Lubbock   1 [and 2] August [1861]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary:
Has visited T. V. Wollaston, who is working hard but lives too solitary a life.

There are further legal complications with William Darwin’s partnership and CD’s solicitor wants to call on JL.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [1 August 1861]
letters.summary:
Mentions Dutch translation [ofOrigin].

Discusses evolutionary origin of sexuality.

Asa Gray’s suggestion that variation was directed by a higher power and Herschel’s view of providential arrangement in nature.

Compares variation in domestic and wild species.

Asks CL for introductions for his son William in Southampton, where he has joined a bank.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   [2 August 1861]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Asks JL’s advice about details of William’s proposed banking partnership. CD’s solicitor is suspicious of Atherley’s long-term intentions.

letters.title: From the University of Breslau   4 August 1861
letters.summary: CD awarded honorary doctorate of medicine and surgery by the University of Breslau. [See3194a.]

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   6 August [1861]
letters.summary: Bentham has sent a damaged spurlessOrchis pyramidalis; asks CL to send another. Fears they are irregular monsters. [SeeOrchids, pp. 47–8.]

letters.title: To John Lubbock   9 August [1861]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: JL’s kindness has laid William and himself "under an enduring obligation". One clause in the partnership agreement seems harsh but will probably never signify.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   10 August [1861]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: With some hesitation CD’s solicitor advises acceptance of partnership offered to William.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [11 August 1861]
letters.summary: Has found function of rostellum: modified stigma guarantees attachment of pollinia.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   13 [August 1861]
letters.summary:
Personal regards.

William Darwin will make a botanist.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   13 [August 1861]
letters.summary:
Thanks CL for orchids acquired from a collector.

Discusses role of Providence in variation. Does CL honestly think it applies to variations in domestication? If not ordained there, sees no reason for it in nature either.

letters.title: To A. G. More   13 August 1861
letters.summary: Has found hundreds ofSpiranthes.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   14 August [1861]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: JL is thinking of moving to Brighton.

letters.title: To John Obadiah Westwood   15 August [1861]
letters.summary:
As a general rule CD thinks it best to deposit specimens in the British Museum, and "bitterly regrets" he did not send all his specimens there. Nevertheless he agrees to sending his crustaceans to the Oxford Museum.

CD is at work onOrchids. He would be greatly obliged if JOW could send him specimens of pollen-masses attached to head or base of proboscis of moths.

Asks for reference to Morren’s paper that JOW mentioned before [see2862].

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   21 August [1861]
letters.summary:
Suggests change in a passage [in MS] of CL’s [Antiquity of man(1863)] dealing with adaptations for travel.

Comments on review ofOriginby F. W. Hutton [Geologist(1861): 132–6, 183–8].

Emphasises importance of variability for natural selection.

Discusses possiblity of intelligent causes in variation.

letters.title: To ?   24 August [1861–8]
letters.summary: Thanks correspondent for a remarkable instance of inheritance [not specified].

letters.title: To Williams & Norgate   25 August [1861]
letters.summary: Instructions to a book seller.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   [27 and 29 August] and 2 September [1861]
letters.summary: Gives some observations on the sensitivity ofDroseraspecies and comments on cases of "dioecio-dimorphism".

letters.title: From George Maw   27 August [1861]
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for his letter about GM’s review of theOrigin.

Sends instances of correlative organisation and functions which he finds difficult to believe could have accumulated by gradual modifications.

[Letter erroneously dated 1862 by GM.]

letters.title: To Neil Arnott   29 August [1861]
letters.summary: Found NA’sA survey of human progress[1861] on his return home after two months’ absence. Is glad to see NA kept his intention of publishing on this subject.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   29 August [1861]
letters.summary: Asks for return of his MS [unspecified].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   30 August [1861]
letters.summary: Orchid anatomy. Requests Lindley’s work on orchids [The genera and species of orchidaceous plants(1830–40)].

letters.title: To George Maw   31 August [1861]
letters.summary: Would welcome any facts on correlation, or GM’s criticisms. Explains how natural selection could produce apparent correlation of characters, but feels GM’sPelargoniumexample must arise from the leaves and petals being similarly affected at an early stage by an unknown cause.

letters.title: From George Rolleston   1 September 1861
letters.summary: The embryology of the vertebrate nervous system may be an exception to the law of inheritance at corresponding ages.

letters.title: From T. F. Jamieson 3 September 1861
letters.summary: Observations from a fortnight in Lochaber. Found the entrance to Loch Treig to present the clearest evidence of intense glacial action. States, in contradiction of David Milne-Home, that there is glacial scoring in Glen Spean, as Louis Agassiz described, and moraine around the mouth of Loch Treig. There is little sign of water erosion on the rocks crossed by the lines in Glen Roy. Believes the smoothed rocks at the eastern end of Loch Laggan are due to flow from the lake and not tidal action. The lines in Glen Roy are too neat for a lake shore subject to tides. Given the glacial scoring sweeping round from Glen Spean into Glen Treig, and all the boulders, TFJ is astonished that anyone could deny that there had been glaciers there. [See3247.]

letters.title: To Charles Hardy?   4 September [1861]
letters.summary: Has modified the statements about bees visiting clover for honey in 3d ed. ofOrigin. Can correspondent find out if clover in Lowestoft district was a second crop?

letters.title: To J. O. Westwood   4 September [1861]
letters.summary:
Is certain he never had Morren’s paper from JOW or heard of it before JOW’s note; will write toGardeners’ Chronicleabout it [see3252].

Thanks for the twoSphinxmoths; unfortunately the pollen-masses do not belong to orchids but toAsclepias.

Asks whether R. B. Todd’sCyclopedia of Anatomy and Physiology[1835–59] has an article on fertilisation of orchids.

letters.title: To George Rolleston   5 September [1861]
letters.summary:
GR’s letter is a gold-mine.

Pleased to have Pierre Gratiolet’s comment on the embryology of greatly modified organs

and GR’s valuable cases of analogous variation.

Doubts craniologists, but recounts his father’s opinion that the shape of CD’s head was altered when he returned from theBeagle.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   6 September [1861]
letters.summary: After much crossing, has worked out meaning of dimorphism inPrimula.

letters.title: To T. F. Jamieson   6 September [1861]
letters.summary: Has read TFJ’s letter on Glen Roy. His arguments seem conclusive. CD gives up the ghost. "My paper is one long gigantic blunder." How rash it is "to argue that because a case is not one thing it must be some second thing which happens to be known to the writer".

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   6 September [1861]
letters.summary:
Sends an enclosure [a letter from T. F. Jamieson, see3247].

"I am smashed to atoms about Glen Roy. My paper was one long gigantic blunder."

letters.title: ToJournal of Horticulture   [before 10 September 1861]
letters.summary: Requests the names of the parents ofGladiolus gandavensisand six varieties for the purpose of determining their probable origin.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   10 September [1861]
letters.summary:
Absence of organic remains in many deposits.

Discusses presence of marine animals near icebergs.

Comments on former geological state of England.

letters.title: To John Murray   10 September [1861]
letters.summary:
Asks that a copy ofOrigin[3d ed.] be sent to Mlle Clémence-Auguste Royer; she has arranged with a publisher for a French translation.

Originis exciting much attention in Germany.

Surprised to receive a Dutch translation.

Has never seen an advertisement [of 3d ed.], which is a pity. Hopes "Bishop of Oxford & Co." have not made JM sorry he published it.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   11 September [1861]
letters.summary:
Has putDroseraoff while amusing himself withPrimulaand orchids.

Dionaeais prettily adapted to weight detection.

letters.title: ToGardeners’ Chronicle   [before 14 September 1861]
letters.summary:
Requests orchid specimens from Arethuseae division for his investigation of the many contrivances by which orchids are fertilised by insect agency.

Asks whether Charles Morren has published on the fertilisation of orchids by insect agency.

letters.title: ToGardeners’ Chronicle   [before 14 September 1861]
letters.summary: Two correspondents report fertilisingVinca roseaby imitating the action of an insect inserting its proboscis. Another says hisVinca roseaseed profusely without artificial fertilisation. CD asks what might explain the difference in results. In the latter instance, are the plants kept in a greenhouse with windows left open, so that moths could get access at night?

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [15 September 1861]
letters.summary: Discusses CL’s correspondence with T. F. Jamieson. Comments on Jamieson’s theory that the roads of Glen Roy were formed by a glacial lake. Discusses elevation of Scotland during the glacial period.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   16 September [1861]
letters.summary: Is interested in cases of dimorphism likePrimula. DiscussesPrimulaandLinum.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   17 September [1861]
letters.summary:
U. S. politics and relations with England.

Wants examples of dimorphism similar toPrimula.

Structure and function ofSpiranthesflower.

Observations and experiments onDrosera.

CD’s views on design.

letters.title: To Henry Fawcett   18 September [1861]
letters.summary:
Comments on MS of HF’s address ["On the method of Mr Darwin in his treatise on the origin of species",Rep. BAAS(1861) pt 2: 141–3]. "How odd it is that anyone should not see that all observation must be for or against some view if it is to be of any service."

Describes his health.

The response to his views in Germany, Holland, and Russia.

letters.title: From H. C. Watson   20 September 1861
letters.summary: ThePrimulaexperiments of J. Sidebotham; HCW’s distrust of the results [see J. Sidebotham, "Specific identity of the cowslip and the primrose",Phytologist3 (1849): 703–5].

letters.title: To John Murray   21 September [1861]
letters.summary: Asks JM’s opinion on publishing his MS on orchids. It has new facts, and resembles a Bridgewater Treatise, but only those who care for natural history would be interested. Would share the risk.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   22 September [1861]
letters.summary: Additional discussion of Jamieson’s theory that the roads of Glen Roy were formed by a glacial lake. Suggests the possible marine origin of the Glen Spean terraces. Comments on the power of lakes to produce pebbles. Discusses elevation of Wales and Scotland during the glacial period.

letters.title: To A. G. More   23 September 1861
letters.summary: Would like capsule ofEpipactis palustris. Asks for information.

letters.title: From John Murray   23 September 1861
letters.summary: Offers to publishOrchids, giving CD one-half of the profits of each edition.

letters.title: To Joseph Reay Greene?   24 September [1861]
letters.summary: Thanks for gift of treatise on Coelenterata [?Manual of the sub-kingdom Coelenterata(1861)]. "… I was but lately wishing to read some treatise up to the present mark, on these animals. I have cut the pages & can clearly see that your work will much interest & instruct me".

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   24 September [1861]
letters.summary:
CD’s orchid paper is to become orchid book [Orchids].

Primulapaper is done [Collected papers2: 45–63].

letters.title: To John Murray   24 September [1861]
letters.summary: Thanks JM for his liberal offer [to publishOrchids]. CD fears the public will not be interested, but thinks it will "do good to theOriginas it will show that I worked hard on details and it willperhapsserve [to] illustrate how Natural History may be worked under the belief of the modification of Species".

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   [before 25 September 1861]
letters.summary: Mention ofVolucella.

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   25 September [1861]
letters.summary:
Recommends publisher for HWB; admires J. van Voorst but suggests Murray.

In reply to HWB’s letter [missing], comments on neuters and mimicry.

letters.title: From J. O. Westwood   26 September 1861
letters.summary:
Has found the reference to Charles Morren’s paper, "On the agency of insects in causing sterility in flowers" [Proc. R. Entomol. Soc. Lond.1 (1836): xliv–xlv].

Common white butterflies remove pollen-masses with their tarsi from plants of the Asclepiadaceae.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   28 September [1861]
letters.summary:
Bates agrees with CD on neuter ants.

Orchids.

Repeating experiment of C. F. v. Gärtner to study Huxley’s idea of physiological species.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [28 September 1861]
letters.summary: List of Australian plants that have become naturalised in the Nilgiris [India] and are turning out the native trees.

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   30 September 1861
letters.summary:
Discusses the mimicry of theVolucellaflies, and the bees and wasps they mimic. Compares it with the different object of mimicry in butterflies.

Refers to incompleteness of Cuthbert Collingwood’s paper [? "On homophormism, or organic representative forms",Proc. Liverpool Lit. & Philos. Soc.14 (1860): 181–216].

Thanks CD for help in selecting a publisher for his book [The naturalist on the river Amazons(1863)].

letters.title: From Charles Lyell   30 September 1861
letters.summary:
Asks for copy of CD’s paper ["Ancient glaciers of Caernarvonshire",Collected papers1: 163–71]. Gathers that drift of Moel Tryfan is glacial.

Believes Glen Roy roads formed later than submergence of Scotland.

Asks CD’s opinion concerning relative chronology of various glacial deposits, particularly a flint tool find in the Ouse River near Bedford.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   1 October [1861]
letters.summary:
The flint tools found at Bedford.

Further discussion of Jamieson’s theory of the formation of the roads of Glen Roy by a glacial lake. Comments on formation of Glen Spean terraces. Mentions glaciers in North Wales.

Agreement with John Murray to publish [Orchids].

letters.title: To A. G. More   1 October 1861
letters.summary:
Discusses seed capsules [ofEpipactis palustris?].

Sorry AGM is in bad health.

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   2 October 1861
letters.summary:
Thanks HWB for information onVolucella, although he does not know when he will use it.

Is glad HWB is beginning his book.

CD is beginning work on his orchid book.

letters.title: To John Murray   3 October [1861]
letters.summary: Would JM object to size ofOrchidsbeing same as W. N. Hutchinson,Dog breeding[1850]? Prefers little book, not to look pretentious.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   4 October [1861]
letters.summary:
Query on orchid homology.

Critical of F. A. Bauer on orchids [Illustrations of orchidaceous plants(1830–8)].

letters.title: To John Murray   5 October [1861]
letters.summary: Likes the idea of matchingOrchidswithOrigin. Begs for large print and spacing so that the book will not look "ridiculously small".

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   6–7 October [1861]
letters.summary: Orchid anatomy.

letters.title: To John Gould   6 October [1861]
letters.summary:
Thanks for JG’s book [An introduction to the Trochilidae, or family of humming-birds(1861)], which he has read carefully. Hopes someday to use the information on the close alliance of species in large genera.

CD repudiates hybridity of birds in nature.

Intends to extract the cases of "races" or doubtful species. They show that "determination of species is not a simple affair".

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   8 October [1861]
letters.summary: Asks DO to look for nectar inStanhopea saccatalabellum. CD’s theory predicts nectar should be present, but afraid there is none.

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   [after 8 October 1861]
letters.summary: Finds no trace of nectar inStanhopea saccata.

letters.title: From Thomas White Woodbury   [9–22 October 1861]
letters.summary: Fancies articles on "The queen bee" and "Drone influence" [J. Hortic.8 October 1861, p. 39] may be of interest. Since writing the latter, one of his drones hybridised a queen at a distance of a mile and a half.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   11 October 1861
letters.summary: Notes several cases of "dioecio-dimorphism" in different genera; feels the discovery of pollen that will act only on the pistil of another flower is most important. Believes CD should next turn his attention to investigating cases of "precocious fertilisation".

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   11 October [1861]
letters.summary: Orchid anatomy: movement inMormodescolumn.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   [after 11 October 1861]
letters.summary:
Thanks AG for notes on hollies.

Replies to an argument for design. Feels it monstrous to consider orchids created as they are now seen, since every part reveals modification on modification.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   12 October [1861]
letters.summary:
Asks whether WED has signed the articles of partnership in the bank.

Has been working at orchid drawings with G. B. Sowerby, Jr.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   13 October [1861]
letters.summary: Orchid anatomy.Catasetumexemplifies slight modification of structure leading to new structure.

letters.title: To John Rogers   14 October [1861]
letters.summary: Would like to quote JR on the trigger mechanism of Catasetum inOrchids

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   15 [October 1861]
letters.summary: Orchid anatomy. Wind as agent of self-fertilisation in orchids.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   17 [October 1861]
letters.summary: Discusses business matters relating to WED and the bank.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   18 October [1861]
letters.summary:
Orchid anatomy. Movements of labellum.

Repeating Gärtner’s experiment withVerbascumvarieties.

letters.title: To John Lindley   18 October [1861]
letters.summary:
Thanks JL for identifyingCatasetum saccatum.

Writes of his interest ("more than almost anything in my life") in orchids, but fears he is rash to publish.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   20 October [1861]
letters.summary:
Continued discussion of Jamieson’s Glen Roy theory. Mentions river erosion of glaciers. Quotes from old letter to CL [1116].

Is working hard on orchids; fears subject is too complex for the public.

letters.title: To John Murray   21 October [1861]
letters.summary: G. B. Sowerby, Jr has done the drawings forOrchidswoodcuts. Calls JM’s attention to the fact that a first-rate cutter must be employed.

letters.title: To theJournal of Horticulture   [before 22 October 1861]
letters.summary: Asks H. W. Newman whether the queen humble-bee is fertilised on the ground or in the air, and whether the fertilisation often takes place as late as September. [Newman’s reply follows CD’s letter.]

letters.title: From Henry Wenman Newman   [before 22 October 1861]
letters.summary: Replies to CD’s query (see3778): the queens or females of the humble bees are not fertilised in the air. Offers a number of observations relating to the fertilisation of bees and wasps, which he has made in the course of sixty years.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   22 October [1861]
letters.summary:
Tells of a shooting competition at Down.

Has been working hard at orchid drawings with G. B. Sowerby, Jr.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   22 October [1861]
letters.summary:
Mr Campbell (recommended by H. Spencer) would be a treasure but doubts any man has patience to experiment at another’s suggestion.

Jocular comments about THH’s audacity in doubtingCatasetum.

letters.title: From Charles Lyell   22 October 1861
letters.summary: Ice could not have formed the blockages in Lochaber unless in every case the water escaped over some col into a contiguous valley on the same watershed, or into the eastern watershed. Supposes that the cols were not land-straits, but the places where the lakes were drained when forced to flow the wrong way.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   23 October [1861]
letters.summary:
JDH’s work onGnetum: a living fossil.

Orchid anatomy.

Encloses lists of orchids and other specimens he would be interested in seeing.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   23 [October 1861]
letters.summary: Comments especially on the "intermediate shelf" problem of Glen Roy; views of Jamieson and Milne. CD "cannot help a sneaking hope that the sea might have formed the horizontal shelves".

letters.title: From T. F. Jamieson   24 October 1861
letters.summary: Discusses his observations at Glen Roy. Mentions glaciers seen by Hooker in the Himalayas. Discusses problems of glacier–lake theory.

letters.title: To W. B. Clarke   25 October [1861]
letters.summary:
Thanks WBC for his account of glacial action in Australia. A mundane cooler period would throw a flood of light on geographical distribution. Has sketched a large MS on subject but does not know whether he will live to publish it.

Questions WBC on striated granite boulders.

Asks him to make a botanical experiment on insect fertilisation.

letters.title: To John Lindley   25 October [1861]
letters.summary:
Sends thanks for an informative letter;

would be grateful for any orchids; names some he would particularly like.

letters.title: To Lionel Smith Beale   26 October [1861]
letters.summary: Subscribes to present for Mrs J. T. Quekett only on condition that no public testimonial is planned for JTQ.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [27 October 1861]
letters.summary: Discusses affairs at Down and Southampton.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   27 October [1861]
letters.summary: Acroperaanatomy puzzling.Malaxisanatomy deciphered.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   31 October [1861]
letters.summary: Owen’s new résumé of his brain doctrine ["On the cerebral character of man and ape",Ann. & Mag. Nat. Hist.3d ser. 7 (1861): 456–8]; an attack on CD’s views. Quotes Owen on cavillers and controversialists.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   1 November [1861]
letters.summary: Orchid anatomy.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   1 November [1861]
letters.summary:
Orchid homologies.

Sensitive responses inCatasetum.

Acroperabecoming clear.

T. F. Jamieson impressed by JDH’s work on Himalayan glaciers.

letters.title: To John Lindley   1 November [1861]
letters.summary:
CD is sending an orchid flower; asks JL to identify it.

Also asks if JL can spare a dried flower of another orchid (name forgotten) [which CD describes] so that he can try to trace its ducts or spiral vessels.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   3 November [1861]
letters.summary:
Thanks for "multitudinous" references.

Thanks Hooker for orchids.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   4 November [1861]
letters.summary:
Reports events at Down;

has been doing good work on the homologies of orchids.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   5 [November 1861]
letters.summary: Asks JDH to look at movement of labellum in an orchid.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   6 [November 1861]
letters.summary: Rostellum ofMasdevallia.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   7 November [1861]
letters.summary:
JDH’s Fernando Po case.

Madeiran fauna pre-glacial according to Oswald Heer.

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   [before 8 November 1861]
letters.summary: List of references on orchid structure and fertilisation.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   8 November [1861]
letters.summary:
Orchid anatomy: homologies of column vascularisation.

Primulapaper sent to Linnean Society.

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   8 November 1861
letters.summary: Refers CD to a paper which he ought to know: Ch. Fermond, "Faits pour servir à l’histoire générale de la fécondation chez les végétaux",Recueil des travaux de la Société d’émulation pour les sciences pharmaceutiques3 (1859).

letters.title: To George Bentham   9 November [1861]
letters.summary: Thanks GB for arranging for his paper ["Two forms ofPrimula",Collected papers2: 45–63] and for his photograph.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   9 November 1861
letters.summary:
Discusses observations of his own and of John Torrey on dimorphism, especially inAmsinckia.

Is trying to find specimens ofHoustoniafor CD.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   10 November [1861]
letters.summary: CD fears he has misinterpreted vascularisation of butterfly orchid flowers.

letters.title: To Dorothy Fanny Nevill   12 November [1861]
letters.summary: Writes at Lindley’s suggestion to ask whether DN can send several orchid specimens. Describes his work in preparation forOrchids.

letters.title: To George Robert Waterhouse   12 November [1861]
letters.summary: Returns a letter from a Mr Walsh – "a clear-headed man on my side". What he says about sea trout in lochs would make a good case for CD if borne out by professional ichthyologists.

letters.title: To J.-B. P. Guépin   14 November 1861
letters.summary: Has read about JPG’s article on the fertilisation of orchids inAnnales de la Societé Linnéenne d’Angers[1853], but has been unable to secure a copy. Seeks information about the role of bees in distributing pollen masses and about the varieties of orchids in Angers.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   14 November [1861]
letters.summary: Homologies of orchid flower vascularisation.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   15 November [1861]
letters.summary: Discusses stock-brokers; hopes to be able to see WED at Christmas.

letters.title: To John Lindley   16 November [1861]
letters.summary: CD sends thanks for many valuable dried specimens [of orchids]. Has been promisedCatasetumand someDendrobiumby Mr Rucker; has written also to Lady Dorothy [Nevill].

letters.title: To Robert Scot Skirving   16 November [1861–8]
letters.summary: Knows nothing of the habits of earwigs. Thinks Edward Newman may be trusted on the point [as to whether or not earwigs can fly].

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [17 November 1861]
letters.summary: Describes in detail his day at home and at the bank in Southampton.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   17 November [1861]
letters.summary:
JDH’s letter on grounds of generalisation in plant morphology.

Faunal distribution and the glacial period.

Orchid homologies.

letters.title: To John Lindley   17 November [1861]
letters.summary: Lady Dorothy [Nevill] has written very obligingly and sent a lot of orchids.

letters.title: To D. F. Nevill   19 November [1861]
letters.summary: Declines invitation to visit DN’s orchid collection. Thanks for orchids and list [of available plants]. Requests a few more spikes ofBolbophyllum, particularly of species with irritable labellum.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   20 [November 1861]
letters.summary: JDH asked to check Lindley onAcropera.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [22 November 1861]
letters.summary: Transport of an orchid to Down.

letters.title: From William Hugh Gower   23 November 1861
letters.summary: Sends notes on fertilisation ofVictoria regiatending to show that impregnation with foreign pollen increases productivity of seeds.

letters.title: To George Bentham   24 November [1861]
letters.summary: Requests more precise details aboutOxalis, to which GB referred in his remarks onPrimula.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   25 November [1861]
letters.summary:
Acroperaspecies may be males of other orchids.

Homologies of ducts in orchids.

Went to British Museum to see Bates’s mimetic butterflies.

letters.title: To ?   25 November [1861–8]
letters.summary: Has read correspondent’s notice on bent cleavage. Refers him to observations on the same fact inSouth America, p. 160. CD has also suggested a conjectural explanation.

letters.title: To George Bentham   26 November [1861]
letters.summary: Would prefer to havePrimulapaper published in the Linnean Society’sJournalrather thanTransactions.

letters.title: From George Bentham   26 November 1861
letters.summary: Remarks about Labiatae,Linum,OxalisandViolaoccasioned by hearing CD’s paper ["Two forms ofPrimula", read 21 Nov 1861,Collected papers2: 45–63].

letters.title: To Dorothy Fanny Nevill   27 November [1861]
letters.summary: Thanks Dorothy Nevill for her assistance in supplying him with plants, but he will not require any more. Asks her to remember him to A. E. Knox.

letters.title: From George Bentham   29 November 1861
letters.summary: Lists pairs ofOxalisspecies with differing proportions of stamens and styles.

letters.title: To George Bentham   30 November [1861]
letters.summary:
Thanks GB for valuable letter [3331].

Will follow his suggestion about violets.

Discusses differences betweenThymusandPrimula.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   30 November [1861]
letters.summary: Reports on state of family’s health.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   30 November [1861]
letters.summary:
Requests that DO examine enclosed microscope slides ofAcroperaovules, to confirm CD’s opinion that females are non-functional.

Can DO comment on disagreement between Robert Brown and John Lindley over the number ofAcroperacarpels?

O. Heer’s Atlantis theory vs CD’s hypothesis of a migration north during warm periods.

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   [1 December] 1861
letters.summary: Furnishes CD with more information onVolucellaand gives him references relating to this and butterfly colourings. States that colours are not necessarily related to resting-places but rather an endowment to enable them to withstand adverse conditions.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   1 December [1861]
letters.summary:
Rudimentary ovules ofAcropera.

High opinion of Bates.

Orchid anatomy.

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   3 December [1861]
letters.summary:
Thanks HWB for references.

Praises his paper ["Contributions to an insect fauna of the Amazon valley", read before Linnean Society, 21 Nov 1861,Trans. Linn. Soc. Lond.23 (1862) : 495–566] which solves "one of the most perplexing problems which could be given to solve".

Discusses the difficulties of writing and expresses disappointment at Wallace’s book [Travels on the Amazon(1861)].

letters.title: To Ludwig Rütimeyer   5 December [1861]
letters.summary:
Admires LR’s book [Die Fauna der Pfahlbauten(1861)].

Will attempt to arrange for skull of wild white Chillingham cattle to be sent by Earl of Tankerville.

CD has come to same conclusion as LR on zebus.

CD’s MS ofVariationis half-prepared.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   7 December [1861]
letters.summary: Trusts DO’s opinion onAcroperaovules.

letters.title: To ?   8 December [1861–8]
letters.summary: Thanks for information on inheritance of mental peculiarities in cats.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [9 December 1861]
letters.summary:
Henri Lecoq’s miserable book on plant geography [Étude sur la géographie botanique de l’Europe(1854–8)].

H. W. Bates’s pleasure at meeting JDH.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   11 December [1861]
letters.summary:
Discusses the worsening relations between their two countries and the possibility of war.

ExpectsOrchidsand hisPrimulapaper [Collected papers2: 45–63] to be out soon.

Thanks AG for some facts on dimorphism.

George Bentham has given him a list ofOxalisandMenthaspecies that are dimorphic likePrimula.

Is in a "thick mud" regarding design in nature.

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   15 December [1861]
letters.summary: Praises MS of first chapter of HWB’s book [The naturalist on the river Amazons(1863)]. Suggests he give common names and make comparisons to familiar English species to help readers. Suggests a few changes. Will speak strongly to Murray about publishing whenever HWB is ready.

letters.title: To John Innes   15 December [1861]
letters.summary: Delighted to have Quiz [Johnny Innes’ dog].

letters.title: To John Lindley   15 December [1861]
letters.summary:
Thanks JL for a flower ofBolbophyllum, a genus that puzzles him.

Recent work has convinced him a number of orchids are male. Points out that JL [inThe vegetable kingdom(1846), pp. 177–8] "accidentally misquoted" R. H. Schomburgk on this point.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   18 [December 1861]
letters.summary:
Lindley suggestsGongoramay be femaleAcropera.

CD’s orchid book nearly ready for press.

Discovers trimorphism inLythrumis in H. Lecoq [Études sur la géographie botanique de l’Europe(1854–8)].

letters.title: To John Innes   19 December [1861]
letters.summary: Arrangements for receiving Quiz.

letters.title: From B. O’Neile Wilson   22 December 1861
letters.summary: Variation in instincts among domestic animals.

letters.title: From John Innes   [24 December 1861]
letters.summary: Arrangements for sending Quiz.

letters.title: To John Lindley   24 December [1861]
letters.summary:
Delayed thanking JL for two notes until he heard from Hooker aboutAcropera luteola; had no ideaA. luteolawas not a well-known name.

Cites his reasons for identifyingA. loddigesiias male; hopes for aGongoraflower from Hooker which, JL suggested, may be the female.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   27 [December 1861]
letters.summary: Seeks information on heating hothouses night and day.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   28 [December 1861]
letters.summary:
Gongoracannot be female ofAcropera; it may itself be a male.

Hopes Daniel Oliver will "sink Atlantis" in his Royal Institution lecture.

letters.title: To John Lindley   28 December [1861]
letters.summary:
Thanks JL for information aboutAcropera luteola.

Also thanks for theGongora; cannot avoid the impression it is male.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [29 December 1861]
letters.summary:
Asks CD whether he hears from Asa Gray. JDH’s opinion of the crisis [Trentcase, Nov 1861] and the American Civil War.

Julius von Haast alludes to glacial drift in Middle Island of New Zealand.

Backwardness of JDH’s son, Willy.

Encloses a reference from Daniel Oliver which may be useful.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [30 and 31 December 1861]
letters.summary: Asks JDH to arrange for some melastomads to be sent to him.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [30 December 1861 or 6 January 1862]
letters.summary:
Glad CD has given up onAcroperaovules.

Doubts phanerogams less different in extreme forms [than Crustacea].

No systematic parallelism between plants and animals.

Offers list of Arctic plants with their colours. Asks CD whether it is useful to add colour to [descriptions of] plants.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   31 December 1861
letters.summary:
Discusses dimorphism and suggests CD investigateValeriana.

Praises CD’s views with respect to the U. S. Civil War and relations with England. Worsening relations between Britain and U. S.

letters.title: From Leonard Jenyns   31 December 1861
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his contribution to the memoir of Henslow [L. Jenyns,Memoir of the Rev. John Stevens Henslow(1862)].

letters.title: To ?   31 December [1861–8]
letters.summary: "As I have never especially attended to Conchology I am sorry to say I cannot tell you the name of the enclosed shell which I now return–"

letters.title: From Joseph Dalton Hooker   [1 January 1862]
letters.summary: Sends plant specimens. William Borrer will be glad to send seeds.

letters.title: To Charles Edouard Brown-Séquard   2 January [1862]
letters.summary: Pleased to hear through Miss Pennington that CEB-S intends to reviewOriginin a French journal. Suggests 3d ed. as this will soon appear in French translation. Does not expect perfect agreement on so complex a subject as descent.

letters.title: From John Brodie Innes   2 January [1862]
letters.summary:
Quiz has been sent off to Down.

JBI will leave for Scotland on Monday.

letters.title: From Henry Holland   [3–14] January [1862]
letters.summary:
Condolences on death of Charlotte Langton [néeWedgwood].

Is waiting to hear from Lord Tankerville [see3339].

letters.title: To J. B. Innes   [3] January [1862]
letters.summary:
Quiz arrived safely.

CD’s three sons are in bed with bad colds.

letters.title: From Henry Walter Bates   6 January 1862
letters.summary:
Sends CD ch. 2 of his book [The naturalist on the river Amazons] for suggestions, having accepted CD’s recommendations concerning ch. 1.

Effects of climate on dress in ch. 1 similar to, but independent of, notions expressed by CD in hisJournal of researches[p. 381].

On geology, book deals with distribution and theory of deltas of the Amazon.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   6 January 1862
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Sends paper [on ancient Swiss lake-habitations,Nat. Hist. Rev.n.s. 2 (1862): 26–51] for CD’s opinion.

letters.title: To Edward Cresy   8 January [1862 or 8]
letters.summary: Obliged for the Theophrastus. Will return it.

letters.title: From Imperial Zoological Society of Acclimatisation   10 January 1862
letters.summary: Announces a meeting of the Society to elect its officers.

letters.title: To Société Impériale Zoologique d’Acclimatation   [after 10 January 1862]
letters.summary: Asks how much he owes for his annual subscription to the Society.

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   11 January 1862
letters.summary:
Grieved to hear of CD’s illness; begs him not to give moment’s thought to his MS until health has returned.

Plans to exhibit mimetic butterflies at Linnean Society.

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   13 January [1862]
letters.summary: Has been in bad health and has just read HWB’s MS in the last two days. Praises the book; assured it will be successful. Offers to write to Murray. Hooker interested in conclusions on colour.

letters.title: From Charles Carter Blake   13 January 1862
letters.summary:
Thanks for note on hisMacraucheniapaper [Ann. & Mag. Nat. Hist.3d ser. 7 (1861): 441–3].

Asks for references to descriptions of certain bones found in South America.

Lists four fossil New World monkeys; is CD aware of any others?

letters.title: From C. E. Brown-Séquard   13 January 1862
letters.summary: Apologises for not answering CD sooner about where he will publish review [ofOrigin]. Review is to appear in his own journal, but will postpone publishing it until the French translation of 3d ed. appears. Expresses substantial agreement with CD’s views.

letters.title: From Thomas Henry Huxley   13 January 1862
letters.summary:
Against all predictions his Edinburgh lecture was well received [Evidence as to man’s place in nature(1863)].

Took his old line about problem of infertility of hybrids as a test of CD’s views.

Report [from a newspaper] not quite right about what he said, but they have not refuted his statement that some form of progressive development theory is certainly true, nor that man and the apes come from same stock. Owen has gone in for progressive development in second edition of thePalaeontology[1861].

letters.title: From John Hutton Balfour   14 January 1862
letters.summary:
Thanks forPrimulapaper [Collected papers2: 45–63]; will examine some [Edinburgh] Botanic Garden samples in its light.

Huxley visiting Edinburgh and spoke on man’s zoological relations with monkeys [seeMan’s place in nature(1863)]. JHB disagrees with his views.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   14 [January 1862]
letters.summary:
On success of THH’s Edinburgh lectures.

Agrees that THH is right that the hybrid question is a "hiatus" [in the argument for natural selection] but he overrates it. Crossedvarietiesfrequently produce sterile offspring. On this question asks THH to read hisPrimulapaper [Collected papers2: 45–63]. CD suspects sterility will come to be viewed as aselectedcharacter.

letters.title: From Henry Holland   15 January [1862]
letters.summary:
Has read CD’sPrimulapaper.

Regrets to hear that CD and family are victims to the influenza epidemic.

letters.title: To Ludwig Rütimeyer   15 [and 16] January [1862]
letters.summary: Lord Tankerville has not responded to the request for the skulls which LR requires for his research. CD addressed Lord T through his friend Sir Henry Holland, who is prepared to try again, despite Lord T’s rudeness.

letters.title: From William Branwhite Clarke   16 January 1862
letters.summary: Answers CD’s questions on Australian flora, bees, geology.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   16 January [1862]
letters.summary:
Entire family down with influenza. Has done nothing for three weeks.

Asks for Haast reference on New Zealand glacial deposits.

CD’s view of the North sinceTrentcase. Can no longer write with sympathy to Asa Gray.

Encourages JDH about his son, Willy.

Problem of relation of colour to external conditions. Hopes JDH will undertake the investigation.

letters.title: From Charles Cardale Babington   17 January 1862
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for hisPrimulapaper [Collected papers2: 45–63].

Asks if CD has observed the true oxlip (Primula elatior).

Comments onHottoniaandStellaria graminea. [SeeForms of flowers, pp. 72, 313.]

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [19 January 1862]
letters.summary:
JDH castigates the Americans after theTrentaffair. The value of an aristocracy. How will CD answer Asa Gray’s letter?

His "remarkable plant" [Welwitschia mirabilis] exhibited at Linnean Society.

Genera plantarumis in press.

letters.title: To C. C. Babington   20 January [1862]
letters.summary:
DiscussesStellariaand other plants said to be dimorphic.

Asks for plants he wants for experiments.

Preparing a little book onOrchids.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   20 January 1862
letters.summary:
TheWitnessattacks THH’s lecture.

Assures CD he spoke more favourably of his doctrines than the reports show.

Agrees with CD’s arguments on sterility of hybrids and predicts physiological experiments will produce physiological species sterileinter se. Has come even closer to CD’s view especially sincePrimulapaper. Will soon be more Darwinian than CD.

letters.title: From Conrad Martens   20 January 1862
letters.summary:
He will send CD one of his sketches to add to the two CD has kept sinceBeagledays.

Asks for FitzRoy’s address.

letters.title: From W. B. Clarke 21 January 1862
letters.summary: Seeks to define oldest fossil cirripede.

letters.title: From Henry Holland [21 January 1862?]
letters.summary: Has received a satisfactory answer from Lord Tankerville.

letters.title: From Dorothy Frances Nevill   [before 22 January 1862]
letters.summary:
Will enclose list of orchids in bloom for CD’s use.

Asks for photograph; her pleasure in knowing CD.

Most interested in the account of pigeons in CD’s book [Origin].

letters.title: From D. F. Nevill   [before 22 January 1862]
letters.summary:
Thanks for promise of photograph.

Has no melastomads in bloom.

Describes sensitive anthers ofCynorchis.

Thanks CD for "your little pamphlet".

letters.title: To Asa Gray   22 January [1862]
letters.summary:
Dimorphism: "new cases are tumbling in almost daily".

U. S. politics.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   22 January [1862]
letters.summary:
Much amused at theWitness.

Pleased at what THH says on hybridity.

Odd that objectors never allude to the arguments that alone have weight in their favour – affinities, rudimentary organs, etc.

Has 16 ill in the house!

Natural History Reviewa capital number.

letters.title: From Leonard Jenyns   22 January [1862]
letters.summary: Sends proof-sheets of CD’s contribution to LJ’sMemoirof Henslow.

letters.title: To D. F. Nevill   22 January [1862]
letters.summary:
Thanks for orchids and other flowers.

Will send photograph.

letters.title: From John Rogers   22 January 1862
letters.summary: Reports that the orchidsMyanthusandCatasetumare identical.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   23 January [1862]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary:
Has had 16 in the household ill.

Wants to meet JL.

Praises JL’s paper ["Ancient lake-habitations of Switzerland",Nat. Hist. Rev.n.s. 2 (1862): 26–51].

letters.title: To Leonard Jenyns   24 January [1862]
letters.summary: CD has sent to printer proofs of his contribution toMemoirof Henslow.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   25 [and 26] January [1862]
letters.summary:
His answer to Asa Gray.

On JDH’s view of aristocracy. Primogeniture is dreadfully opposed to selection.

Orchid book proofs ready soon – has no idea whether it is worth publishing.

Huxley on Owen.

Feeble letter from J. H. Balfour against Huxley’s lectures ["Relation of man to lower animals", pt 2 ofMan’s place in nature(1863)].

Has received the "astounding"Angraecum sesquipedalewith nectary 1ft long: "what insect could suck it?"

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   25 January 1862
letters.summary: Thanks CD for returned MS and letter with its good opinion. Asks CD to write to Murray.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker [25 January 1862]
letters.summary:
Will send anArethusa; offers other specimens.

Dimorphism.

Falconer contradicts Sumatra and Ceylon elephant story.

Lyell as rabid as ever about America.

letters.title: To William Walmisley Baxter   26 January [1862]
letters.summary: Discusses deduction from bill for medicine.

letters.title: From Francis Boott   27 January 1862
letters.summary: Has sent CD the published part of his work onCarex[Illustrations of the genus Carex(1858–67)]. Hopes to add 200 more figures. Comments on great variability among the 600–odd species, and on their geographical distribution.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   27 January 1862
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Grateful for CD’s approval of "Lake-habitations".

letters.title: From Robert Bateman [28 January 1862]
letters.summary: For his father [James Bateman], he sends three more species of orchids and names of others described by CD.

letters.title: From John Edward Gray   28 January 1862
letters.summary: The Japan pig, an unusual domestic species with no wild prototype.

letters.title: To John Murray   28 January [1862]
letters.summary: H. W. Bates is, at CD’s urging, writing a book of travel and natural history. CD suggests JM might be interested in publishing it. Recommends HWB and his MS highly.

letters.title: From J. E. Gray   29 January 1862
letters.summary:
Owen’s paper on the aye-aye [Rep. BAAS32 (1862) pt 2: 114–16];

his attacks on CD and his theories.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   29 January 1862
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Will visit CD on Saturday.

letters.title: From C. C. Babington   30 January 1862
letters.summary:
Encloses seeds.

Lecoq’s work mentions instances of apparent dimorphism. [H. Lecoq,Études sur la géographie botanique de l’Europe, 9 vols. (1854–8).]

letters.title: From Henry Holland   30 January [1862]
letters.summary: Is preparing a volume of his articles [Essays on scientific and other subjects(1862)], to one of which he would like to add a postscript referring to CD’sOrigin[pp. 100–1]. Sends proposed postscript for CD’s approval.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   30 January [1862]
letters.summary:
Is JDH sure it is aBletia, just received? Its pollen very different from any Epidendreæ he has seen. If it isBletia, Lindley’s grand divisions are fanciful.

Accepts JDH’s offer to collect cases of dimorphism.

James Bateman has sent a lot of orchids withAngraecum sesquipedale. What a proboscis the moth that sucks its 11½ inch nectary must have!

letters.title: From John Murray   30 January [1862]
letters.summary:
Discusses manuscript by H. W. Bates [Naturalist on the river Amazons(1863)].

Mentions CD’s forthcoming book [Orchids].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [31 January – 8 February 1862]
letters.summary:
Wrote a "frightful screed" about aristocracy’s being a necessary consequence of natural selection, and then burnt it.

H. W. Bates is the only man "thinking out" natural selection to any purpose. "I think I have driven Bates back to Nat. Sel. as the only way of solving his difficulties."

HWB’s mimetic butterflies.

JDH wishes he had time to do the same thing with plants.

Owen and Huxley involved in a "contemptible" squabble in the Edinburgh newspapers.

Maximovitch reportsStellaria bulbiferais a Siberian form which never ripens its seeds.

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   31 January [1862]
letters.summary: Encloses note from Murray, hoping it will be satisfactory. Murray is ready to see as much of MS as possible. Murray is considered honest but may be cautious, since HWB’s name is unknown to the public.

letters.title: From Charles Kingsley   31 January 1862
letters.summary:
CK defended CD’s theory at a shooting party with the Bishop of Oxford, the Duke of Argyll, and Lord Ashburton. The discussion started as a result of shooting some blue rock-pigeons which were different from blue rocks of other localities. CK held that all pigeons were descended from one species.

CK proposed that mythological races, e.g., elves and dwarfs, were intermediate species between man and apes, and have become extinct by natural selection; i.e., by competition with a superior white race of man.

letters.title: To C. C. Babington   1 February [1862]
letters.summary: Thanks for seeds.

letters.title: From James Bateman [1 February 1862]
letters.summary:
Glad CD approves of the orchids he sent.

Believes the pollinia ofMormodesare projected; thinks CD should look at the pollinia ofChysisand investigate the hybrid betweenLimatodesandCalanthe.

letters.title: From J. E. Gray   1 February 1862
letters.summary: Agrees with CD’s estimate of the man [unidentified]. Hopes CD will use his influence with Lubbock to try to prevent the Council’s placing him at the head of the Zoological Society.

letters.title: From Henry Holland   [1 or 8 February 1862]
letters.summary: Suggests a change in the postscript [referred to in3423].

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   2 February [1862]
letters.summary: Returns a letter, which, when it is published, he believes will make readers take up THH’s lectures in a more impartial spirit.

letters.title: To George Bentham   3 February [1862]
letters.summary: Asks GB’s help to clear up discrepancies between his and John Lindley’s observations on pollination of Melastomataceae.

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   [4–8 February 1862]
letters.summary: Cites descriptions of melastomads in C. V. Naudin,Annales des Sciences Naturelles3d ser., vols. 12–18.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   6 February [1862]
letters.summary:
Returns "The Week" [unidentified].

Agrees with THH’s published letter that writer is a man of excellent spirit, but doubts he is a good logician.

letters.title: To Charles Kingsley   6 February [1862]
letters.summary:
Comments on CK’s letter [3426].

Identifies species of pigeon shot by party.

On CK’s "grand and awful" notion of genealogy of man, CD recalls how revolting was the thought that his ancestors must have been like the Fuegians. His present belief that they were hairy beasts is less revolting.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   7 [February] 1862
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Sir George Clerk to be new President of the Zoological Society.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [8 February 1862]
letters.summary: Sends dried specimens of Melastomataceae.

letters.title: From Charles Augustus Bennet, Lord Tankerville   [9 February 1862]
letters.deprecated: Charles Augustus Bennet, 6th earl of Tankerville
letters.sender: Charles Augustus Bennet, 6th earl of Tankerville
letters.summary: Describes battles among bulls for leadership of the [Chillingham] herd.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   9 February [1862]
letters.summary:
Thanks JDH for box of melastomes

and a very valuable reference from Daniel Oliver.

Is crossingMonochaetumwhich he thinks is dimorphic.

Is "sometimes half tempted to give up species & stick to experiments".

Pollen ofBletia hyacinthinais quite unlike otherBletiaspecies but exactly the same asEpipactis.

letters.title: To John Murray   9 [February 1862]
letters.summary: Sends MS ofOrchidsexcept last chapter. It contains many new and curious facts and conclusions, but he has no idea whether it will sell. If it does not, will hold himself largely responsible.

letters.title: From Maurice Alberts   10 February 1862
letters.summary: Has received diploma from the University of Breslau [honorary doctorate in medicine and surgery]. Should he forward it or will CD pick it up in London? [See3226aand3446.]

letters.title: To Ludwig Rütimeyer   11 February [1862]
letters.summary:
Chillingham cattle leg bones will be sent to LR.

J. E. Gray has read a paper on unusual Japanese domesticated pig at the Zoological Garden ["On the skull of the Japanese pig",Proc. Zool. Soc. Lond.(1862): 13–17].

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   12 February [1862]
letters.summary: Discusses his new microscope.

letters.title: From Maurice Alberts   13 February 1862
letters.summary: Has forwarded a diploma from the University of Breslau [Honorary Doctorate in Medicine and Surgery].

letters.title: From John Lubbock   13 February 1862
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Hopes CD will come to lunch on Saturday. The Busks and J. D. Hooker are with JL.

letters.title: To Maurice Alberts   [after 13 February 1862]
letters.summary: Acknowledges receipt of a diploma for Doctor’s degree from the University of Breslau and expresses his thanks.

letters.title: To William Erasmus Darwin   14 February [1862]
letters.summary:
Discusses WED’s growing interest in botany; would be grateful for certain observations.

Is much concerned about Horace’s illness.

Has sentOrchidsMS to printers

and will work a little at dimorphism.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [before 15 February 1862]
letters.summary: Asks for the address of C. W. Crocker.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [before 15 February 1862]
letters.summary:
Sends C. W. Crocker’s address.

Doubts CWC can help withMormodes.

Will see CD at Lubbock’s.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   16 February [1862]
letters.summary: Floral structure ofMelastoma. Asks AG to observe position of pistils in lately-opened flowers of different plants.

letters.title: From Charles William Crocker   17 February 1862
letters.summary:
Thanks forPrimulapaper [Collected papers2: 45–63].

Separation of sexes inBillbergia.

Offers to experiment under CD’s direction, now that he has retired from Kew.

letters.title: From Andrew Crombie Ramsay   17 February 1862
letters.summary: In his paper for Geological Society ["Glacial origin of certain lakes",Q. J. Geol. Soc. Lond.18 (1862): 185–204] he will prove that all the lake-basins of the Alps were scooped out by glaciers.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   18 February 1862
letters.summary: Discusses politics in the U. S. and relations between Britain and America.

letters.title: To A. C. Ramsay   18 February [1862]
letters.summary: Would like to hear ACR’s new views on origin of mountain lakes, but cannot stand the hot, late meetings [at Geological Society].

letters.title: From Searles Valentine Wood   18 February 1862
letters.summary: Variation in Mollusca. The most abundant forms vary most.

letters.title: From J. B. Innes   19 February [1862]
letters.summary:
Reports on a bird, offspring of a male mule between a canary and greenfinch, and a hen canary.

Family news.

letters.title: From J. E. Gray   21 February 1862
letters.summary: Cites case of Owen’s getting compiler’s name removed from title of a British Museum catalogue.

letters.title: To Camilla Ludwig   21 February [1862 or later]
letters.deprecated: Camilla Frederike Antonie (Camilla) LudwigCamilla Frederike Antonie (Camilla) Pattrick
letters.recipient: Camilla Frederike Antonie (Camilla) LudwigCamilla Frederike Antonie (Camilla) Pattrick
letters.summary: Asks her to translate passage of letter about treatment.

letters.title: To J. B. Innes   24 February [1862]
letters.summary:
Has heard of mules of canary and other finches breeding occasionally, but it is rare, and there is hardly one authenticated case of two such mules breeding together.

Sixteen of the household at Down are sick with influenza.

letters.title: To Ladies   24 February [1862–9]
letters.summary: Thanks for their kind feelings towards him.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   25 February [1862]
letters.summary:
Admires JDH’s paper on Arctic plants ["Distribution of Arctic plants",Trans. Linn. Soc. Lond.23 (1862): 251–348]. Such papers compel people to reflect on modification of species;

JDH will be driven to a cooled globe.

Serious erratum in paper.

New and original evidence in case of Greenland. Its flora requires accidental means of transport by ice and currents.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker [26 February 1862?]
letters.summary:
Box of Melastomataceae has arrived.

Talked with [Duke of] Argyll aboutOrigin. He is between stools: Owen and Lyell.

letters.title: To Maxwell Tylden Masters   26 February [1862]
letters.summary: Obliged for MTM’s ["Vegetable morphology",Br. & Foreign Med.-Chir. Rev.29 (1862): 202–18].

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   27 [February 1862]
letters.summary: Writes that [Murray’s] terms areveryfavourable; has never heard of such terms offered for a first work. HWB can depend on fact that Murray is pleased with it [The naturalist on the river Amazons].

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   27 February [1862]
letters.summary:
Thanks for information on domestic animals of Indians.

Glad Murray thinks well of MS ofThe naturalist on the river Amazons.

CD working on proofs ofOrchids.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   27 February 1862
letters.summary:
Pleased at CD’s opinion of his Arctic plants paper. CD has caught great blunder.

Lack of Arctic–Asiatic species in mountains of tropical Asia does not trouble him. Species seem to indicate some "current of migration" from Europe and W. Asia southeastward to Ceylon – an awful staggerer to bridge migrations.

letters.title: To John William Salter   28 February [1862]
letters.summary: CD returns a paper he has received through [G. B.?] Sowerby. He wishes he could persuade his correspondent to publish papers on such subjects. The series on brachiopods was very striking.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [1 March – 15 May 1862]
letters.summary: [List of plants in CD’s hand, with notes by JDH identifying them.]

letters.title: From George E. Harris   3 March 1862
letters.summary: GEH, a tailor, wishes to trade some work for a presentation copy of theOrigin.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   3 March 1862
letters.summary:
Had it not been for CD, JDH would never have written such papers as his one on Arctic flora. The "evulgation" of CD’s views is the purest pleasure he derives from them.

He too is staggered that Greenland ought to have been depopulated during the glacial period. Absence ofCalthais fatal to its re-population by chance migration.

letters.title: To G. E. Harris   5 March [1862]
letters.summary: Has directed Murray to send Harris a copy ofOrigin.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   6 March [1862]
letters.summary: Will observeRhexiafor CD to see whether it is dimorphic.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   7 March [1862]
letters.summary:
CD wishes he could sympathise with Asa Gray’s politics.

Orchidsto appear soon.

Pre-glacial Arctic distribution.

Work on floral dimorphism.

High opinion of Buckle as a writer.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [10 March 1862]
letters.summary: Returns Asa Gray’s letter. Disappointed with Gray. Comments on America. British–American relations.

letters.title: From H. G. Bronn   [before 11 March 1862]
letters.summary:
Asks if CD will have corrections for 2d German ed. ofOrigin.

CD’s theory only natural way to explain creation but contradicts current knowledge about origin of life from inorganic matter.

Has readPrimulapaper [Collected papers2: 45–63] with interest.

letters.title: To H. G. Bronn   11 March [1862]
letters.summary:
Pleased that new German edition ofOriginis wanted. Wishes to make corrections.

Suggests German translation ofOrchids.

Comments on HGB’s book [Untersuchungen(1858)].

letters.title: To ?   11 March [1862–9]
letters.summary: Gives permission to insert in his magazine anything from CD’s works.

letters.title: From C. W. Crocker   [before 13 March 1862]
letters.summary:
Will experiment on hollyhocks as CD suggests.

On desirability of a place for experiments to be set up by Government or a scientific society. Kew is too busy for experiments.

letters.title: From C. W. Crocker   13 March 1862
letters.summary:
Informs CD where, at Kew, to findEpipactis palustris.

Has never trusted Donald Beaton.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   14 March [1862]
letters.summary:
Thinks JDH is a bit hard on Asa Gray.

Bates’s letter is that of a true thinker. Asks to see JDH’s to Bates. Point raised in it is most difficult. "There is one clear line of distinction; – when many parts of structure as in woodpecker show distinct adaptation to external bodies, it is preposterous to attribute them to effect of climate etc. – but when a single point, alone, as a hooked seed, it is conceivable that it may thus have arisen." His study of orchids shows nearly all parts of the flower co-adapted for fertilisation by insects and therefore the result of natural selection.Mormodes ignea"is a prodigy of adaptation".

letters.title: From D. F. Nevill   [c.14 March 1862]
letters.summary:
Belated thanks for CD’s photograph.

When in London at Rucker’s wonderful gardens she learned he had sent CD aMormodes.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   15 March [1862]
letters.summary:
Gives some observations on changes in pistil position with age inMonochaetum. Asks whether AG can observeRhexiafor similar movements.

"One of the best men, though at present unknown", H. W. Bates, has taken up natural selection.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   17 March 1862
letters.summary:
JDH has probably influenced Bates by pointing out applicability of CD’s views to his cases.

Is greatly puzzled by difference in effect of external conditions on individual animals and plants. Cannot conceive that climate could affect even such a single character as a hooked seed.

Does not think Huxley is right about "saltus".

letters.title: From M. T. Masters   17 March 1862
letters.summary: He has only an uncertain memory of the placement of stamens in the [monstrous?] primrose CD asked about.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   18 March [1862]
letters.summary:
On effect of external conditions: CD thinks all variability due to changes in conditions of life because there is more variability under unnatural domestic conditions than under nature, and changed conditions affect the reproductive organs. But why one seedling out of thousands presents some new character transcends the wildest powers of conjecture.
