Not shaken by "saltus" – he had examined all cases of normal structure resembling monstrosities which appearper saltum. Has fought his tendency to attribute too much to natural selection; perhaps he has too much conquered it.

letters.title: To Richard Kippist   18 March [1862]
letters.summary: Asks that referee of his [Catasetum] paper be informed that if it is ordered to be printed he will borrow woodcuts. But if referee thinks fit, he will withdraw it, for almost all will be published inOrchids. He is not willing to spare time to condense it.

letters.title: To Richard Kippist   18 March [1862]
letters.summary: Sends paper to be read ["Sexual forms ofCatasetum",Collected papers2: 63–70].

letters.title: To William Bernhard Tegetmeier   18 March [1862]
letters.summary:
Orchidstaking up all his time.

He longs to be at work again on poultry and rabbits.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   22 [March 1862]
letters.summary:
Asks JDH to correct names of two species ofCalanthe.

Note from Asa Gray ends "Yours cordially", so CD hopes he is forgiven.

HisCatasetumpaper will be read 3 Apr [Collected papers2: 63–70].

Plants and seeds sent will be of great use, especiallyLythrum, which according to J. P. E. Vaucher seems grand case of trimorphism. Asks what sort of man Vaucher is.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker [23–5 March 1862]
letters.summary:
IdentifiesCalanthe masuca.

Asa Gray would not quarrel with them – "snubbing from us may have done him more good than our sympathy".

If CD means the old Vaucher, he was considered a very accurate, acute, able observer.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [23 March 1862]
letters.summary:
Lighthearted thoughts on "the development of an Aristocracy" after a visit to Walcot Hall, Shropshire.

On CD’s point about the effect of changed conditions on the reproductive organs, JDH does not see why this is not "itself a variation, not necessarily induced by domestication, but accompanying some variety artificially selected".

letters.title: From Thomas Francis Jamieson   24 March 1862
letters.summary: Writes with an important fact about the parallel roads of Glen Roy. The watershed at Makoul corresponds with the lowermost of the Glen Roy lines. Over a stretch of 20 miles from east to west the lowermost of the Glen Roy lines is near parallel with the present sea level.

letters.title: From Charles Lyell   [26–31 March 1862]
letters.summary: Suggests that the height of the water which formed the shelves in Glen Roy was determined not by the height of the blocking glacier but by the height of a col. Notes problems in the idea.

letters.title: From Henry Holland   26 March [1862]
letters.summary: Gives CD advice on the illness of one of his sons [presumably Horace].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   26 [March 1862]
letters.summary:
Both JDH’s and Bates’s letters are excellent. JDH has said all that can be said against direct effect of conditions, but CD still sticks to his own and Bates’s side. CD should have done what JDH suggests (since naturally he is pleased to attribute little to conditions) – viz., started on the fundamental principle that variation is innate and stated that afterwards, perhaps, this principle would be made explicable.Variationwill show that "use and disuse" have some effect. Does not believe in perfect reversion. Demurs at JDH’s "centrifugal variation"; the doctrine of the good of diversification amply accounts for variation being centrifugal.

The wonderful mechanism ofMormodes ignea.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [after 26 March 1862?]
letters.summary:
Variations are centrifugal because the chances are a million to one that identity of form once lost will return.

In the human race, we find no reversion "that would lead us to confound a man with his ancestors".

letters.title: From H. G. Bronn   27 March 1862
letters.summary:
CD can add revisions since he cannot begin work on 2d German ed. ofOriginuntil May.

Schweizerbart wants to publish translation ofOrchids. Asks for woodcuts for illustrations.

letters.title: To ?   29 March [1862–9]
letters.summary: Declines, regretfully, to contribute to or to have his name appear on a new magazine.

letters.title: To George Bentham   30 March [1862]
letters.summary: Will try to come to Linnean Society to read his paper, but has been "extra headachy". Fears his paper ["Sexual forms ofCatasetum",Collected papers2: 63–70] will not be worth Lindley’s attendance.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   31 March [1862]
letters.summary:
Has been reading J. D. Morell’s new book on psychology [An introduction to mental philosophy, on the inductive method(1862)].

Progress of the Civil War.

letters.title: From Erasmus Alvey Darwin   [April – May? 1862]
letters.summary: Asks for an order to buy a CD photograph for Mr Tait.

letters.title: From Henry Holland   [c.April 1862]
letters.summary: Louis Pasteur’s memoir "is a very able and convincing one" ["Mémoire sur les corpuscles organisés qui existent dans l’atmosphère",Ann. Sci. Nat. (Zool.)3d ser. 16 (1861): 5–98].

letters.title: From George Busk   1 April 1862
letters.summary: E. A. Parkes informs him there will be difficulty about the Army returns [on CD’sQuery to Army surgeons, see Freeman,Works of Charles Darwin, p. 111] owing to official obstructions by Director General. [Enclosed letter from Parkes to GB says that the Director General does not think that Army surgeons could be asked to collect information systematically for CD, but perhaps some informal, voluntary arrangement could be made.]

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   1 April [1862]
letters.summary:
Explains how melting of ice in Glen Spean could have successively freed two lower cols, thus establishing the water-levels that determined the two lower shelves in Glen Roy.

Plans to read a paper to the Linnean Society ["Sexual forms ofCatasetum",Collected papers2: 63–70].

letters.title: To Octavian Blewitt 2 April [1862]
letters.summary: Declines the honour of acting as Steward at the Annual Dinner of the Royal Literary Fund.

letters.title: From Edward Newman   6 April 1862
letters.summary:
Has several specimens illustrating dimorphism in insects that he would be happy to leave where CD could examine them.

Discusses the ant generaFormicaandAtta, and the origin of the two forms of workers commonly found in the species of these genera.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [7 April 1862]
letters.summary:
Will hope to be able to sendVanillaflowers in a day or two.

How is CD after his tremendous effect on the placid Linneans? ["Sexual forms ofCatasetum",Collected papers2: 63–70; read 3 Apr 1862.]

letters.title: From Alfred Russel Wallace   7 April 1862
letters.summary:
Cannot accept invitation at present.

Is sending a wild honeycomb from Timor.

letters.title: From Edmund Alexander Parkes   8 April 1862
letters.summary: Suggests CD use a tabular form for Army doctors to write their observations on, and suggests it be limited to malaria, yellow fever, and dysentery.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   9 [April 1862]
letters.summary:
OnVanilla.

Asks JDH to observe whether he has both long- and short-styled form ofMenyanthes

and whether he has "Saxifrages with long hairs glandular at the tip".

The Linnean Society session made him vomit all night. Fears he must give up trying to read papers or speak. "It is a horrid bore. I can do nothing like other people."

letters.title: To John Murray   9 April [1862]
letters.summary: JM is a bold man to print 1500 copies [ofOrchids].

letters.title: To Andrew Murray   10 April [1862]
letters.summary: Did CD lend AM a pamphlet on cave insects by S. Scudder ["On the genusRaphidophora",Proc. Boston Soc. Nat. Hist.8 (1861–2): 6–14]? CD much wants it and remembers lending it to someone.

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   10 April 1862
letters.summary:
Now believes flowers of Fumariaceae must be self-fertilised.

Planning a piece on dimorphism in theNatural History Review["On the two forms, or dimorphic condition, in the species ofPrimula… by Charles Darwin", n.s. 2 (1862): 235–43].

Observations onCampanuladimorphism.

letters.title: From Andrew Murray   12 April 1862
letters.summary: AM did not borrow a Samuel Scudder pamphlet from CD; in fact he was not aware of its existence.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   12 [April 1862]
letters.summary:
DO’s observations on polymorphism inPrimulaandCampanula. CD recognises three classes of dimorphism, as inPrimula,Thymus, andCampanulaand violets.

DO’sCampanulapaper and Royal Institution lecture [Not. Proc. R. Inst. G. B.3 (1858–62): 431–3].

CD’s interest in Fumariaceae from A. Gray’s comments on "selfing".

Bees bite holes in flowers when same species grows in high density.

Organisation of CD’s notes.

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   14 April 1862
letters.summary:
Discusses primrose ovules,

Atlantis paper [Nat. Hist. Rev.(1862): 149–70],

plant migrations;

Corydalis.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [15 April 1862]
letters.summary: Is it convenient for him and Willy to come to Down from Thursday to Sunday?

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   15 April [1862]
letters.summary: Encourages DO to publish his paper and put his name to it. [Paper apparently not published.] Concurs with his views on primordial nature of hermaphroditism.

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   16 April [1862]
letters.summary: Invitation to visit; Hooker will be present. Gives directions to Down. Also plans to invite John Lubbock over for an evening.

letters.title: To C. E. Brown-Séquard   16 April [1862]
letters.summary:
French translation of 3d edition ofOriginhas been greatly delayed.

Very pleased with CEB-S’s intent to write a review and with his near agreement. CD believes that so many really good judges concur with him in the main that his views will ultimately prevail. Continental reviews have been more positive than British ones. Édouard Claparède’s ["M. Darwin et sa théorie de la formation des espèces",Rev. Ger.16 (1861): 523–59; 17 (1861): 232–63] is too favourable.

letters.title: To Edouard Claparède   [c. 16 April 1862]
letters.deprecated: Jean Louis René Antoine Edouard (Edouard) Claparède
letters.recipient: Jean Louis René Antoine Edouard (Edouard) Claparède
letters.summary: Thanks correspondent for his excellent review [of French edition ofOrigin(1862)], which he feels will help the spread of his views in France.

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   [17 April 1862]
letters.summary: Accepts CD’s invitation.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   17 April 1862
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: JL is going on a geological excursion with Joseph Prestwich and John Evans.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   20 [April 1862]
letters.summary: RequestsOxalis acetosella, which he suspects is dimorphic.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   21 April [1862]
letters.summary:
Is sending first half of orchid book.

Feels he is wrong aboutMelastoma.

letters.title: From C. W. Crocker   22 April 1862
letters.summary: Certain there are three forms ofPrimula sinensis.

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   23 April 1862
letters.summary: Distinguishes two kinds of floral dimorphism: that affecting sexual organs and that affecting outer envelopes.

letters.title: From Thomas Gold Appleton   24 April [1862]
letters.summary:
Sends letter via his brother visiting England. Awaits continuation of CD’s "wonderful book", which excites much interest.

Comments on Civil War which he expects will end slavery.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   24 April [1862]
letters.summary:
Thanks forOxalis. Only experimentation will show whether disproportion of long- to short-styled flowers is a functional dimorphism.

Case of aestival flowers is very curious.

letters.title: From Berthold Carl Seemann   24 April 1862
letters.summary:
Encloses a passage from his book,The botany of the voyage of H.M.S. "Herald"[1852–7].

Discusses possibility of publishing work on flora of Hawaiian Islands.

letters.title: To H. G. Bronn   25 April [1862]
letters.summary:
Sends additions and corrections for 2d German ed. ofOrigin[1862–3].

Before a German translation ofOrchidsis done, CD thinks HGB should read part of it and decide if it is worth while; CD has doubts.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   26 April [1862]
letters.summary:
Thanks WED for eyeglass.

Reports on health of Horace and family matters.

Has finishedOrchids.

letters.title: From E. A. Parkes   28 April 1862
letters.summary: The Director-General of the Army Medical Department [J. B. Gibson] agrees to have CD’s circular distributed to Army surgeons in India and the West Indies, with reply being voluntary. [SeeDescent1: 244–5 n.]

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   30 April 1862
letters.summary:
Discusses insects of south temperate S. America and New Zealand, especially with respect to the distribution and origin of ChileanCarabi, and has sent for a German monograph to learn about the eleven species he has found.

He refers to Chilean poverty in butterflies; scanty New Zealand insect fauna.

An analysis of south temperate insects is desirable, but the small English collections make him afraid to undertake it.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   30 April [1862]
letters.summary: Thinks THH’s [Anniversary] Address [to Geological Society, Feb 1862,Q. J. Geol. Soc. Lond.18 (1862): xl–liv] a wonderful condensed and original summary of palaeontology.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   1 May [1862]
letters.summary:
Asks JDH to look at stigma ofLeschenaultia biloba; it seems certain there is no stigma within the bud. Case would be important.

Singular case of peculiar structure now remodified into the functional condition of aCampanula.

letters.title: To J. B. Innes   1 May [1862]
letters.summary:
Quiz has had to be killed because he became vicious.

Horace Darwin strangely ill.

letters.title: To John Murray   2 May [1862]
letters.summary: Has returned last page of index [ofOrchids]. Hopes JM will reconsider price – 10s seems high. Suggests two reviewers likely to be favourable. Sends list for presentation copies.

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   4 May [1862]
letters.summary:
Thanks for letter and "valuable" extracts.

If S. AmericanCarabidiffer more from other species than do those from other distant locations (e.g., Siberia, Europe, etc.), CD agrees that difference would be too great to have occurred in the recent glacial age; CD also rejects independent origin. Plants seem to migrate more readily than animals. HWB should not underrate length of glacial period; CD also believes they will be driven to an older glacial period.

Sorry about news of British Museum – hopeless to contend against anyone supported by Owen.

CD dearly wishes HWB could find a situation in which he could give time to science.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [5 May 1862]
letters.summary:
Household problems – stolen silver, maids. His house for some months has had reputation for being not a little disreputable.

On Cameroon plants.

letters.title: From J. B. Innes   5 May [1862]
letters.summary:
About Quiz and [Horace Darwin’s] health.

Asks whether CD has tried W. B. Tegetmeier’s beehives.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   6 May 1862
letters.summary:
Glad to receive CD’s pat on back for address.

Wants to know what CD thinks of the argument on geological contemporaneity.

On his poor health.

letters.title: From Hugh Falconer   7 May [1862]
letters.summary: Wanted to talk with CD about the astonishing new Pliocene fossil discoveries in North America reported by Leidy. One horse fossil’s dentition, if it could be believed, would be of great interest to CD’s views.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [8 May 1862]
letters.summary: Hooker has written about WED’s going to Kew.

letters.title: To Hugh Falconer   [8 May 1862]
letters.summary: Will try to call tomorrow. What HF tells him about horses makes him eager to come.

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   9 May [1862]
letters.summary:
Referring to conversation with Lyell, CD is certain that there was a Miocene glacial period.

Compliments HWB on the mimetic display at the British Museum. Those at the Museum readily accepted HWB’s "doctrine".

Was shown genital organs of closely allied Chrysomelidae.

Albert Günther is candidate for position at Museum.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   9 May [1862]
letters.summary:
Sorry to hear of JDH’s household troubles.

Will try to get a couple of flowers ofLeschenaultiato send him.

"What a good case that of the Cameroons"; the 4000ft [elevation] is much to CD’s "private satisfaction".

Sends JDH a copy ofOrchids.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   10 May [1862]
letters.summary: Nearly agrees on contemporaneity, but THH pushes his ideas too far. Would require strong evidence before believing that the so-called Silurian, Devonian, and Carboniferous strata could be contemporaneous. Thinks THH’s case on advancement of organisation is strong. But he should read Bronn, before publishing again, and say more on other side. Cannot help hoping he is not as right as he seems to be.

letters.title: To William Darwin Fox   12 May [1862]
letters.summary:
Asks if WDF has ever crossed wild and common turkeys. Would like to quote his authority [seeVariation1: 292].

Also curious whether WDF has known the so-called japanned peacock to appear from common peacock [Variation1: 290].

letters.title: To Philip Lutley Sclater   12 May [1862]
letters.summary: Asks for information about japanned peacocks from Hudson [John Henry?] Gurney’s flock.

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   14 May 1862
letters.summary: Thanks forOrchids.

letters.title: To P. L. Sclater   14 May [1862]
letters.summary: Asks for information about peacocks, especiallyPavo nigripennis. Suggests a crossing experiment.

letters.title: From John Obadiah Westwood   14 May 1862
letters.summary:
Thanks forOrchids.

Has captured a bee with pollinia adhering to its head. Will send it to CD if he likes.

letters.title: From George Bentham   15 May 1862
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his book [Orchids]. CD has opened a new field for observation and a new unexpected track to explore phenomena that had before appeared "irreconcilable with ordinary opinion and method shown in the organic world".

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   15 [May 1862]
letters.summary:
Yellow anthers ofHeterocentronproduce on the same plant thrice as many seeds as the crimson anthers. Crimson anther seeds produce dwarf plants, others rise high up.Monochaetum ensiferumfacts are still more strange. Wants to investigate the case, and asks for a plant of the Melastomataceae just before flowering.

Has JDH aRhododendron boothiifrom Bhutan with pistil bent the wrong way?

letters.title: From John Lubbock   15 May 1862
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary:
Thanks forOrchids.

"The big book [Variation] will no doubt go on again now."

JL is writing on Somme implements ["Evidence of antiquity of man",Nat. Hist. Rev.n.s. 2 (1862): 244–69].

letters.title: From M. T. Masters   [c.15 May 1862]
letters.summary: Thanks forOrchids.

letters.title: From George Chichester Oxenden   15 May 1862
letters.summary:
Thanks for the book [Orchids].

Found thousands ofOphrys araniferaplants.

letters.title: From George Henry Kendrick Thwaites   15 May 1862
letters.summary:
Sends CD a quotation from Plato which anticipates theOrigin.

Has been enjoying CD’s paper on dimorphism in theJournal of the Linnean Society["Two forms ofPrimula",Collected papers2: 45–63]. He has found similar structures [seeForms of flowers, pp. 116, 122].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker  [16 May 1862]
letters.summary: Has dissectedLeschenaultia bilobaflowers. Finds no stigmatic surface in the indusium. Describes what is the apparent stigma but has found no pollen-tubes to confirm it as the real one.

letters.title: From D. F. Nevill   [16? May 1862]
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his book [Orchids].

letters.title: FromC. W. Crocker   17 May 1862
letters.summary:
Comments on presentation copy ofOrchids. Has CD studied the orchidSobralia?

Cannot get material for hollyhock experiment.

Sends his notes onPrimula sinensis.

He is experimenting onRanunculus.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   [17 May 1862]
letters.summary: Thanks WDF for interesting letter about turkeys. Would be grateful for information on fertility of the hybrids.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [17 May 1862]
letters.summary:
DiscussesLeschenaultia, finds no stigmatic surface in the indusium.

Gives information on where to obtain paper for drying plants and where to obtain a microscope.

letters.title: From Georgina Tollet   17 May [1862]
letters.summary: Thanks forOrchids.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   18 May 1862
letters.summary:
Has received first sheets ofOrchidsand is very impressed. "What a skill & genius you have for these researches."

Details of U. S. orchids.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [18 May 1862]
letters.summary:
Leschenaultiaseems very odd. Will try with pollen left on for 48 hours. Illustrates diversity of structures for same purpose.

Bentham’s and Oliver’s good opinion ofOrchidsis reassuring.

Anxious to experiment on Melastomataceae; thinks it will give important results.

WantsLeschenaultia formosato try whether viscid outside surface can be fertilised.

letters.title: To Alexander Goodman More   18 May 1862
letters.summary: Asks AGM to experiment onEpipactis palustris.

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   19 May 1862
letters.summary:
Miocene glacial period a remarkable discovery; if it is true, enlargement of Tertiary period necessary.

Received German monograph on ChileanCarabithat does not answer where isolated species came from.

HWB finds genital modifications ofChrysomelastrong support for the theory.

Thanks for copy ofOrchids.

letters.title: From H. G. Bronn   19 May 1862
letters.summary:
Thanks for revisions in 2d ed. ofOrigin. Suggests correction regarding species numbers in the Tertiary.

Comments on pages ofOrchidsand problems of German translation.

Believes CD’s theory not yet proven, but that it will finally lead to truth.

letters.title: From Edward Cresy   19 May 1862
letters.summary: Comments on presentation copy ofOrchids: beeOphrysself-fertilisation; origin of nectar; odour of orchids. Book gives strong cases for special creationists.

letters.title: From Henry Holland   19 May [1862]
letters.summary: Thanks forOrchids.

letters.title: From Thomas Campbell Eyton   [after 19 May 1862?]
letters.summary: Sends photograph. Asks CD for his.

letters.title: From C. C. Babington   22 May 1862
letters.summary: Thanks for copy ofOrchids.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   23 May 1862
letters.summary: Does not knowRhododendron boothii; is sendingRhododendron keysii, a remarkable form. Will send Melastomataceae anon.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   23 May 1862
letters.summary:
AcknowledgesOrchidswith its disclosures of "wonderful adaptations".

Warns that CD aids critics by overstating the difficulties.

Did Owen write the article in theQuarterly Review? [Review ofOriginby Samuel Wilberforce,Q. Rev.108 (1860): 225–64].

letters.title: To Leonard Jenyns   24 May [1862]
letters.summary: Thanks LJ forMemoirof Henslow; thinks it will be invaluable as an example to other clergymen.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   24 [May 1862]
letters.summary:
Quarterly Reviewpiece written by Bishop Wilberforce with aid of Owen.

Other reviews mentioned.

Health.

letters.title: From Joseph Beete Jukes   25 May 1862
letters.summary:
JBJ explains his theory of atmospheric denudation of Irish river valleys, to be published [as "On the river valleys in the south of Ireland",Q. J. Geol. Soc. Lond.18 (1862): 378–403], and suggests its application to the Weald. This slow process would make the Weald far older than CD’s 300 million years.

Thanks forOrchids.

letters.title: From G. C. Oxenden   26 May 1862
letters.summary:
Reminisces about Andrew Knight, whom he knew as a young man.

PraisesOrchidsfor its "analogies of Creation".

Will send lizard orchid.

letters.title: From Leonard Jenyns   28 May 1862
letters.summary: Pleased with CD’s opinion of the HenslowMemoir[L. Jenyns,Memoir of the Rev. John Stevens Henslow(1862)]

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [29 May 1862]
letters.summary:
Sends two flowers ofVanillaand two Melastomataceae.

Has worked on Cameroon list ["Mountain flowering plants and ferns of the Cameroons", in Burton,Abeokuta and the Cameroons Mountains(1863) 2: 270–7]

andGenera plantarum.

letters.title: From G. C. Oxenden   [before 30 May 1862]
letters.summary: Has looked for [Ophrys]arachnitesfor CD, but it is too early in the season.

letters.title: From George Dickie   30 May 1862
letters.summary:
Reports observations onListera cordatain accordance with CD’s wishes.

Agrees with what CD says about adaptations [inOrchids, p. 28–31], but cannot comprehend how they can be explained by natural selection.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   30 May [1862]
letters.summary:
Has receivedMelastomaandVanilla.

Has seen again the two sets of plants ofHeterocentronraised from two lots of pollen from same flower – a marvellous difference in stature.

"But oh Lord what will become of my book on variation: I am involved in a multiplicity of experiments."

Observations onViola.

CD’s fancied dimorphism ofOxalisis all a confounded mistake; only great variability in length of pistils.

Found Henslow’s life [L. Jenyns,Memoir of the Rev. J. S. Henslow(1862)] interesting but fears the public will think it dull.

letters.title: From J. B. Jukes   30 May 1862
letters.summary:
Elaborates his denudation theory: marine denudation works horizontally, atmospheric works vertically.

Answers point in CD’s letter on Sydney Harbour, N. S. W.

Who is the "goose" who reviews CD’s books in theAthenæum[review ofOrchids, 24 May 1862]?

letters.title: From G. C. Oxenden   30 May [1862]
letters.summary:
Awaits instructions for sending lizard orchid.

Asks for a coloured plate ofMalaxis paludosaso that he can find specimens for CD.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [31 May 1862]
letters.summary:
Wants WED to forward driedMalaxisto G. C. Oxenden.

Has been dissectingViolaflowers.

[Letter from Emma Darwin to WED, verso p. 3.]

letters.title: From G. C. Oxenden   31 May [1862]
letters.summary:
Sends plants.

The disappearance of rare plants from localities where they have been abundant can be explained.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   June 1862
letters.summary: Found 27 flowers ofOrchis latifoliaand in 16 of them were dead flies of one particular kind.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   [late June 1862]
letters.summary:
Has not had time to look atRhexia.

Progress of Civil War.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   [2 June 1862]
letters.summary: Discusses heterostyly inHoustonia.

letters.title: From G. C. Oxenden   4 June [1862]
letters.summary: Sends orchids.

letters.title: From George Chichester Oxenden   5 June [1862 or 1864?]
letters.summary: Sends musk orchid.

letters.title: From E. Schweizerbart’sche Verlagsbuchhandlung   7 June 1862
letters.summary: Discusses publication of second German edition ofOrigin[1863] and German edition ofOrchids[1862].

letters.title: To A. G. More   7 June 1862
letters.summary: Suspects that bee orchid is self-fertilising form ofOphrys arachnites, which requires insect aid.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   8 June [1862]
letters.summary:
Describes floral anatomy of aCatasetumsent by DO.

Has gone on from orchids to studying insect agency inPelargonium.

His doubts on the worth of publishingOrchids.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   9 June 1862
letters.summary:
Oliver has written able paper on dimorphism forNatural History Review[n.s. 2 (1862): 235–43].

CD’s account ofViolais novel and interesting.

Has finished Cameroon mountain plants.

Jury work at exhibition.

Domestic problems – wife is ill, no cook, etc.

letters.title: ToJournal of Horticulture   [before 10 June 1862]
letters.summary: Asks whether any correspondents have observed any sensible differences between the bees kept in different parts of Great Britain. CD has heard from several sources that breeds of bee in different areas vary.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   10–20 June [1862]
letters.summary:
Thanks AG for praise ofOrchidsand his notes on several American species of orchid. Comments on AG’s observations.

Is experimenting [on dimorphism] withRhexiaandMelastoma.

Asks AG’s opinion of a paper by Thomas Meehan ["On the uniformity of relative characters between allied species of European and American trees",Proc. Philadelphia Acad. Nat. Sci.(1862): 10–13] which is the best case of the apparently direct action of the conditions of life CD has seen.

Requests postage stamp for his ill son [Leonard].

Thanks AG for observations onCypripediumand gives recent observations of his own.

Arethusais very pretty; structure seems like that ofVanilla.

Finds the little (so-called imperfect) flowers ofViolaandOxaliscurious: the pollen-grains emit their tubes whilst within the anthers, and they travel in straight lines right to the stigmas.

Sympathises with events in the U. S.

Reports on French translation ofOriginby Mlle C. Royer, "one of the cleverest & oddest women in Europe".

Alphonse de Candolle says he wants direct proof of natural selection; "he will have to wait a long time for that".

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   [before 11 June 1862]
letters.summary: Asa Gray approves ofOrchids; his work on American species confirms CD’s findings.

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   11 June [1862]
letters.summary: Encloses a question [missing] concerning language [from Hensleigh Wedgwood].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   11 June [1862]
letters.summary:
Sorry to hear of Mrs Hooker’s health and domestic problems. Wishes natural selection had produced neuters who would not flirt or marry.

Will be eager to hear Cameroon results.

Wishes JDH would discuss the "mundane glacial period". Still believes it will be "the turning point of all recent geographical distribution".

Pollen placed for 65 hours on apparent (CD still thinks real) stigma ofLeschenaultiahas not protruded a vestige of a tube.

"Oliver the omniscient" has produced an article inBotanische Zeitungwith accurate account of all CD saw inViola.

Asa Gray’s "red-hot" praise ofOrchids[Am. J. Sci.2d ser. 34 (1862): 138–51].

letters.title: From Frederick Currey   12 June 1862
letters.summary: Offers rare Irish orchid (Spiranthes).

letters.title: From George Howard Darwin [12 June 1862]
letters.summary: Leonard Darwin has scarlet fever so GHD has said he should be sent home and has asked E. A. Williams to call at Down.

letters.title: From Alphonse de Candolle   13 June 1862
letters.summary:
Has read theOriginseveral times. His position is like Asa Gray’s: he wishes to believe in descent, but proofs of natural selection are lacking.

Looks forward to CD’s promised large book.

Thanks forPrimulapaper [Collected papers2: 45–63]. Did CD sow the seeds of his crosses? One would like to know whether the two forms reappear at random.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   13 [June 1862]
letters.summary: Leonard has scarlet fever; CD is sorry WED is unwell.

letters.title: To Leonard Horner   13 June [1862]
letters.summary: Sends condolences on death of LH’s wife. Recalls many pleasant hours in Bedford Place. He and Emma thank LH for sending the memorial paper.

letters.title: To Patrick Matthew   13 June [1862]
letters.summary: It would be a pleasure to see "the first enunciator of the theory of Natural Selection" but his health makes it impossible. Hopes to come to London soon and would like to arrange an interview with PM if he is staying more than a week.

letters.title: To John Murray   13 June [1862]
letters.summary:
CD orders electrotypes for German edition ofOrchids.

Asa Gray doubts an American publication is possible but will review it inSillimans Journal.

[British] botanists have praised it. Other reviews.

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   14 June 1862
letters.summary:
Sends answer to Wedgwood’s query

and is sorry to hear CD is again unwell.

His book is progressing very slowly.

Asks that CD not make use of any of the facts about generative organs in beetles for he finds "such a chaos of statements" that facts are not to be depended upon.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   14 June [1862]
letters.summary: WED’s travel plans; an insect he has observed onOrchis maculata.

letters.title: To J. H. Balfour   15 June [1862?]
letters.summary:
Thanks JHB for specimen ofCorallorrhiza;

would like some seeds ofCorydalis claviculata.

letters.title: To G. H. K. Thwaites   15 June [1862]
letters.summary: Refers to hisPrimulapaper [Collected papers2: 45–63]. Asks GHKT to investigate a similar case inCinchona.

letters.title: To Alphonse de Candolle   17 June [1862]
letters.summary:
Is pleased that AdeC is interested in thePrimulacase ["Dimorphic condition ofPrimula",Collected papers2: 45–63]. Is pursuing analogous experiments on other plants and on seedlings raised from the unions.

CD’s "large work" progresses slowly owing to ill health and his work onOrchids.

CD is not surprised that AdeC is unwilling to admit natural selection – "the subject hardly admits of direct proof or evidence. It will be believed in only by those who think that it connects & partly explains several large classes of facts".

Hopes AdeC will publish onQuercus

and rejoices that he intends to return to the study of geographical distribution. No one can claim to have read AdeC’s truly great work on that subject [Géographie botanique(1855)] with more care than CD.

letters.title: From Charles Pritchard   17 June [1862]
letters.summary: Has broken up school a few days early to avoid danger. Hopes CD’s son is nearly recovered.

letters.title: ToBienen Zeitung   18 June 1862
letters.summary: Asks experienced observers whether there are any marked differences between bees kept in different parts of Germany.

letters.title: To John Murray   18 [June 1862]
letters.summary: Superb, but exaggerated, review [ofOrchids, by M. J. Berkeley] inLondon Review[& wkly J. Polit.4 (1862): 553–4]. Asa Gray thinks almost as highly. "I have not been a fool, as I thought I was, to publish." TheAthenæumreview will hinder sales greatly.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   19 [June 1862]
letters.summary:
Household problems: wife’s health, visitors to Kew.

Will go to sale of J. C. Ross’s effects looking for glacial and Kerguelen Land works not at British Museum.

letters.title: From W. B. Clarke   20 June 1862
letters.summary: Has received Australian government grant to collect and publish on fossils. Has collected thousands of fossils.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   20 June [1862]
letters.summary: Asks CD to help Thomas Carlyle find and borrow a book.

letters.title: To John Murray   20 [June 1862]
letters.summary:
It is not certain cuts are wanted by an American publisher [ofOrchids].

Has fixed price of £10 for Schweizerbart [Stuttgart publisher].

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   20 June 1862
letters.summary: Testimonial in support of WBT’s application for curatorship of the Hartley Institution.

letters.title: To G. H. K. Thwaites   20 June [1862]
letters.summary: Asks for information concerning heterostyled and dioecious plants.

letters.title: From G. C. Oxenden   [before 21 June 1862]
letters.summary: Sad that CD is quitting his studies of orchids.

letters.title: From H. G. Bronn   21 June 1862
letters.summary:
L. C. Treviranus inclined to translateOrchids, but "unfortunately" HGB has already done it. Book’s discussion of plant sexuality important for zoology as well as botany.

Originis in press. Attaches a list of "quelques petites difficultées" encountered in his translation.

letters.title: To E. A. Darwin   21 June [1862]
letters.summary: His friend Trenham Reeks [Secretary of Museum of Practical Geology] would give Carlyle information and help. This note will serve as introduction.

letters.title: From G. C. Oxenden   21 June 1862
letters.summary: Yesterday found hundreds of [Ophrys]apiferaand [Ophrys]arachnitesin bloom in the same area. The two species grow in clumps and do not mix with each other.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   23 June [1862]
letters.summary:
Has been ill (violent skin inflammation).

Has done hardly anything except tend to his experiments. RepeatingPrimulawork has verified former results and very curious facts on sterility of homomorphic seedlings.

Wonders who reviewedOrchidsforLondon Review & Wkly J. Polit..

Asa Gray also infatuated withOrchids.

letters.title: To Nicholas Trübner   23 June [1862]
letters.summary: "I have received a letter from Dr. Asa Gray this morning who says ""pray ask Mr. Trubner to send at once 1/2 dozen copies of the Orchid book"". Will you be so good as to attend to it."

letters.title: From Francis Walker   24 June [1862]
letters.summary: Identified two flies as species ofEmpisthat suck flowers, but the females also feed on small Diptera.

letters.title: From C. V. Naudin   26 June 1862
letters.summary:
Thanks forOrchids.

Plans to publish soon on hybrids.

letters.title: To Joseph Bullar   27 June [1862]
letters.summary: Thanks JB for "orchid flowers with Diptera".

letters.title: From August Wilhelm von Hofmann   27 June 1862
letters.summary: Forwards carbonate of ammonia and gelatine free of chlorine.

letters.title: From Frederick Smith   27 June [1862]
letters.summary: Roughly identifies some insects sent by CD; is waiting to see Francis Walker, who, he believes, has written a monograph on the family to which they belong.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   28 June 1862
letters.summary:
M. J. Berkeley wroteLondon Review & Wkly J. Polit.article.

CD is "out of sight the best physiological observer and experimenter that Botany ever saw".

Laments how much he [JDH] missed when doing theListera["Functions and structure of the rostellum ofListera ovata",Philos. Trans. R. Soc. Lond.144 (1854): 259–64].

Illness of wife and father.

"More plants from Fernando Po and more European".

letters.title: From Frederick Smith   28 June 1862
letters.summary: Has seen Francis Walker, who has identified CD’s two Hymenoptera species ["caught in Musk Orchis" – CD note].

letters.title: From E. A. Parkes   29 June 1862
letters.summary: Circulars are being sent to Army surgeons.

letters.title: To James Brown Gibson   [after 29 June 1862]
letters.summary: Thanks JBG for acceding to his wishes in the endeavour to discover whether hair colour in Europeans is correlated with susceptibility to tropical diseases [seeDescent1: 244–5].

letters.title: To H. G. Bronn   30 June [1862]
letters.summary: Encloses answers and corrections [concerningOrchids]. Thanks HGB for translating it.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   30 [June 1862]
letters.summary:
Remembers JDH’s encouragement when he was "utterly weary of life".

Marvellous about European forms in Fernando Po.

C. V. Naudin will publish a book on hybridity ["Nouvelles recherches sur l’hybridité dans les végétaux",Nouv. Arch. Mus. Hist. Nat. Paris1 (1865): 25–176; part also inAnn. Sci. Nat. (Bot.)(1863)].

CD fears Naudin has underestimated distribution of pollen by insects.

Melastomatous plants are ready for his work on meaning of two sets of anthers.

Very curious aboutMasdevallia.

George [Darwin] observing orchids.

Adaptation ofHerminiumbeats almost every other orchid.

letters.title: From George Maw   30 June 1862
letters.summary: Discusses cases of assumed correlation, e.g., facial hair and generative organs, sexual characters in castrated oxen. Finds it difficult to see how correlation of functions which would be useless separately can be accumulated gradually through natural selection.

letters.title: From John Murray   [1 July – 23 August 1862]
letters.summary: Account ofOrchids.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   1 July [1862]
letters.summary: Asks for a note to the Geological Society, since the museum did not have the book Carlyle wanted.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   1 July [1862]
letters.summary:
Thanks for notes onCypripediumandPlatanthera hookeri, which is really beautiful and quite a new case.

His son, George, has been observing the insect fertilisation of orchids.

CD has been crossing peloric flowers ofPelargonium, but doubts he will get good results with respect to sterility of hybrids.

Rhexia glandulosadoes not appear to be dimorphic.Lythrumis trimorphic.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   2–3 July 1862
letters.summary:
Discusses dimorphic plants and the occurrence of "precocious fertilisation" in the bud.

Gives some comments on design in nature in the light of the translator’s commentary in the French edition of theOrigin.

Reports the recent events of the Civil War.

[Note on verso of envelope:]Utricularia vulgarisis "about as neatly contrived for cross-fertilisation by insects as almost anyorchid".

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   2 July [1862]
letters.summary: Never mind the letter to the Geological Society; the museum got the book for Carlyle.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   2 July 1862
letters.summary:
Will see toMasdevalliaandBonatea.

Domestic matters.

Lyell’s health.

CD’s eczema.

Hopes CD will solve the mystery ofMelastoma.

letters.title: To John St Barbe   [before 3 July 1862]
letters.summary: Wishes to invest some money in railway shares; asks for the advice of the bank’s brokers.

letters.title: From Frederick Currey   3 July 1862
letters.summary: G. B. Wollaston [in "British Orchideae",Phytologistn.s. 1 (1855–6): 225–7] saysOphrys arachnitesis a hybrid, which contradicts CD, who says it is a new species.

letters.title: To George Maw   3 July [1862]
letters.summary:
Thinks GM’sPelargoniumis a case of true correlated characters. Feels secondary sexual characters are only accidental correlations; does not see the same necessity for close simultaneous development of certain characters as GM does.

Will forward a copy of hisOrchids.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   4 [July 1862]
letters.summary: Reports some observations on the fertilisation of wheat which WED might follow up.

letters.title: To William Pamplin   4 [July 1862]
letters.summary: Requests priced samples of paper for mounting dried plants.

letters.title: From Charles Giles Bridle Daubeny   5 July 1862
letters.summary:
Sends concluding part of his recent lecture on orchids so CD may see how his inquiries were represented in one of the great centres of clerical influence.

Asks whether insects are attracted to one species of orchids more than another.

letters.title: From George Chichester Oxenden   5 July [1862]
letters.summary: His gardener kept an all-night watch onEpipactis palustrisbut saw no insects visit.

letters.title: From William Alexander Wooler   5 July 1862
letters.summary:
Believes, contrary to CD, that when anthers arise from petals the development of the pollen is affected by the amputation of the petal.

Believes interbreeding can be used to combine desirable characters, but that, carried beyond narrow limits, it leads to deterioration of the breed.

Has been experimenting on crossing polyanthus.

letters.title: From George Maw   7 July 1862
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for sendingOrchids.

Reports observations by his uncle relating to the successful breeding of a male mule with a horse.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   8 July [1862]
letters.summary: WED reports on studying the pollen of grass and Valerian through his microscope.

letters.title: To M. T. Masters   8 July [1862]
letters.summary: CD has been experimenting on the fertility of peloric flowers, with the forlorn hope of illustrating sterility of hybrids; seeks further plants or seeds.

letters.title: From G. C. Oxenden   8 July 1862
letters.summary:
Has not found insects visitingEpipactis palustriseither at night or in the day.

Reality of hybrid plants and birds in nature is controversial.

letters.title: From G. C. Oxenden   8 July [1862]
letters.summary: Has misplaced CD’s forwarding address.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   9 July [1862]
letters.summary:
Lenny [Leonard Darwin]’s illness.

Polymorphism in valerian andLythrum salicaria.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   10 July 1862
letters.summary:
JDH’s trip to Switzerland with his wife.

Has seen Oswald Heer’s fossils, including a leaf, apparently dicotyledonous, from the Lower Lias in Jura.

Value of insect and crustacean fossils for systematic determination.

JDH "impressed with identity of physical features and what wonderful analogy ofbiological[features] between Alps and Himalayas".

letters.title: To H. G. Bronn   11 July 1862
letters.summary: Sends additional notes.

letters.title: From E. Schweizerbart’sche Verlagsbuchhandlung   11 July 1862
letters.summary:
Relates death of H. G. Bronn.

Discusses publication of German edition ofOrchids[1862].

letters.title: To Armand de Quatrefages   11 July [1862]
letters.deprecated: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.recipient: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.summary:
Thanks for answers to CD’s questions; would appreciate any new information on similarity of moths of distinct races.

CD has been "atrociously abused by religious countrymen, but it does not hurt except when it comes from an old friend like Prof. Owen".

Wishes French translator ofOriginhad known more natural history.

letters.title: From Armand de Quatrefages   [after 11 July 1862]
letters.deprecated: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.sender: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.summary: Their views on transformism differ a great deal, as CD says, but perhaps not as much as CD thinks. Sending his [Physiologie comparée: métamorphoses de l’homme et des animaux(1862)].

letters.title: From M. T. Masters   12 July 1862
letters.summary: Will be sending information on peloric plants from his father [William Masters] soon.

letters.title: From G. C. Oxenden   13 July [1862]
letters.summary: Offers moreEpipactis.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   14 July 1862
letters.summary: Sends observations onValeriana officinalis.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   14 July [1862]
letters.summary:
Adaptations of orchid flowers. Believes the structure of all irregular flowers is adaptation to insect fertilisation.

Linum grandiflorumdistinguishes its own pollen so that when placed on stigma of same flower the pollen-tube is not even exserted.

letters.title: From Friedrich Hermann Gustav Hildebrand   14 July 1862
letters.summary: Offers to translateOrchids, since H. G. Bronn has died.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [after 14 July 1862]
letters.summary:
Leonard’s illness.

Polymorphism in valerian andErythraea.

letters.title: ToJournal of Horticulture   [before 15 July 1862]
letters.summary: Is obliged for information concerning differences in the bees of Britain. Relates case of the Jamaican bees which were introduced long ago and have remained the same in size and character except that the diameter of the cells is larger, the wax tougher, and the walls of the hive thicker.

letters.title: From Bernard Peirce Brent   15 July 1862
letters.summary:
Continues breeding guinea-pigs to test effects of warmth on gestation period. Concludes period is ten weeks and warmth has no influence. Offers CD the specimens.

AwaitsVariation.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   15 July [1862]
letters.summary:
Observations onPlatanthera.

Possibility of trimorphism inMertensia.

letters.title: To John St Barbe   [16 July 1862]
letters.summary: Wants to invest some money, as Treasurer of the Down Friendly Society.

letters.title: To Friedrich Hildebrand   17 July [1862]
letters.summary: Thanks for Hildebrand’s offer to translateOrchidsinto German, but H. G. Bronn had finished his translation before his death (Bronn trans. 1862). Has not yet received Hildebrand’s work on the distribution of coniferous trees (Hildebrand 1861). Asks that his compliments be presented to L. C. Treviranus.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   21 July 1862
letters.summary: Encloses stamps for Leonard Darwin.

letters.title: ToJournal of Horticulture   [before 22 July 1862]
letters.summary: Confesses to having made a gross blunder with reference to the size of bee cells in West Indian combs [see3658a].

letters.title: To Asa Gray   23[–4] July [1862]
letters.summary:
AG’s orchid observations are admirable.

Owen has lectured on birds’ descending from one form.

French criticism of CD’sPrimulapaper.

Only AG has seen thatOrchidswas "a ""flank movement"" on the enemy".

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [24 July 1862]
letters.summary: Discusses dimorphic plants, valerian andErythraea. Would like to look at them; suggests WED draw up a paper on them.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [24 July 1862]
letters.summary:
Wife’s health improved by trip.

Heer’s collections convince JDH that Miocene vegetation was Himalayan, not American, as Heer supposed.

Zurich promises to be a good natural history school.

Review ofNatural History ReviewinParthenon[1 (1862): 373–5].

letters.title: To M. T. Masters   24 July [1862]
letters.summary:
CD grateful to have had the distinction of the two sorts of peloria pointed out to him.

His very sick son rallied; is out of danger, thanks to port wine.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   24 July [1862]
letters.summary:
Asa Gray has a self-fertilisingPlatanthera, like the bee orchid. CD believes problem of the latter will some day be explained. Speculates [Ophrys]arachnitesmay be crossing form and bee orchid self-fertilising form of the same species.

Cytisus adamiis a puzzle.

Pleased if DO will reviewOrchids[Nat. Hist. Rev.n.s. 2 (1862): 371–6] .

His review ofPrimulapaper was capital. [Nat. Hist. Rev.n.s. 2 (1862): 235–43].

Requests peloric plants.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   26 July [1862]
letters.summary:
Illness of his son [Leonard]. Has done no work for weeks.

JDH’s hybrid orchids are interesting; CD is surprised many hybrids are not produced.

George [Darwin] caught a moth suckingGymnadenia conopseawith a pollen-mass ofHabenaria bifoliasticking to it.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   28 July [1862]
letters.summary:
AG’s "capital" review ofOrchids[Am. J. Sci.2d ser. 34 (1862): 138–44].

Thinks there are three forms ofLythrum salicaria.

Discusses transport of seeds by sea.

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   28 July 1862
letters.summary: Sends orchids from W. H. Gower.

letters.title: From Philip Henry Stanhope   28 July 1862
letters.summary: Invites CD and Emma to dine.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   29 July 1862
letters.summary:
Is observingGymnadenia tridentata.

Has received six copies ofOrchids.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   29 [July 1862]
letters.summary: Cares more for dimorphism now than for orchids. Today saw the three forms ofLythrum, which means there should be 18 different practicable crosses.

letters.title: To J. O. Westwood   30 July 1862
letters.summary: Asks JOW if he can see bee with pollen masses, and gives details for sending it by post or rail.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [1 August 1862]
letters.summary: Suggests sending plant specimens. Asks about visit of Emma and the boys.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   1 August 1862
letters.summary: WED has been collectingLythrumplants. Numerical proportions of the three forms.

letters.title: From J. O. Westwood   1 August 1862
letters.summary: Bee with adhering orchid pollinia lent to Charles Daubeny. Pollen-masses shaken off but if CD still interested he is welcome to specimen.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin [2–3 August 1862]
letters.summary:
DiscussesLythrum, "a really wonderful case"; asks WED to make observations and collect specimens; sends a diagram which shows what crosses he believes are fertile.

Would like George to watch bees visiting the flowers; wants some pods from different forms to compare shapes and count seeds.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   2 August [1862]
letters.summary: Sends specimens of the three forms ofLythrum. Remarks on the numerical proportions of different forms.

letters.title: From Margaret Susan Wedgwood   [before 4 August 1862]
letters.summary: Proportions of different forms ofLythrum.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   4 August 1862
letters.summary: Gives J. T. Rothrock’s observations on the structure and fertility of the two forms ofHoustonia. Mentions his own observations onRhexia virginicaandGymnadenia tridentata.

letters.title: From G. C. Oxenden   4 August [1862?]
letters.summary: Finds many beautifulEpipactisspecimens.

letters.title: To K. E. S., L. C., and M. S. Wedgwood   4 [August 1862]
letters.deprecated: Katherine Elizabeth Sophy (Sophy) WedgwoodMargaret Susan WedgwoodLucy Caroline WedgwoodLucy Caroline Harrison
letters.recipient: Katherine Elizabeth Sophy (Sophy) WedgwoodMargaret Susan WedgwoodLucy Caroline WedgwoodLucy Caroline Harrison
letters.summary:
Their enumeration [of forms ofLythrum?] is invaluable. He will write later to explain what he is trying to prove aboutLythrumthrough laborious crosses.

Asks for flowers of both forms ofHottoniato measure pollen and compare stigmas.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   5 August 1862
letters.summary: Has read CD’s long letter onLythrumand agrees with it. Is examining the pollen of the different types.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [after 5 August 1862]
letters.summary: Describes insects caught while visitingLythrum.

letters.title: From M. S. Wedgwood   [6 August 1862]
letters.summary: Looked forHottoniabut with little success.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   8 August 1862
letters.summary:
Muscular fibres of whale no larger than those of bee – evidence of a community of origin.

Problem of the abortive wings of ostrich in relation to conditions of their survival.

letters.title: To Hewett Cottrell Watson   8 [August 1862]
letters.summary: Asks HCW’s help with his experiments onLythrum salicaria, for which he needs flowers of the rareLythrum hyssopifolia.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   9 August [1862]
letters.summary: BelievesLythrumis trimorphic. Asks AG for seeds of plants he suspects are polymorphic.

letters.title: From Thomas White Woodbury   9 August 1862
letters.summary: Breeding cells of Ligurian bee are larger than those of common bee. Thanks CD for comb.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   12 August [1862]
letters.summary: WBT’s "too kind and flattering" article onOrchids.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   18–19 August 1862
letters.summary: Notes and observations on orchids.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   20 August 1862
letters.summary: Observations onWelwitschia.

letters.title: From Charles Lyell   20 August 1862
letters.summary:
Jamieson has revisited Glen Roy and confirmed his theory of glacier lakes.

A. G. More considers CD the most profound of reasoners.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   20 August [1862]
letters.summary:
Family illnesses.

On disposition of wild honeycomb gift.

Discounts the difficulty presented by ostrich wings.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   [after 20 August 1862]
letters.summary:
Would be pleased to have third edition ofOrigin.

Is unwell and dreads the winter.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   21 August [1862]
letters.summary:
Emma and Leonard have scarlet fever.

Houstoniaseems "a grand case"; J. T. Rothrock should publish his observations on the two pollens and the reciprocal action of two hermaphrodites.

Rhexia glandulosaoffers nothing odd, butHeterocentronwill turn out something marvellous likeLythrum.

Would like to know what AG thinks of last chapter ofOrchids.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   21 August [1862]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary:
Leonard Darwin’s illness.

William Darwin and the bank.

Beginning to make out a marvellous case of trimorphism.

letters.title: To ?   21 August [1862]
letters.summary: Thanks for monstrous floral specimen, but it is a common one.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   22 [August 1862]
letters.summary:
Lythrum. Wants to examine fresh flowers of Lythraceae.Lythrum salicariahas interested him very much.

Microscopes.

Asks whether JDH can think of plants that have different coloured anthers or pollen in same flowers (as inMelastoma) or on same and in different plants as inLythrum. Would be a safe guide to dimorphism.

Observation of action of pollen inLinum grandiflorum.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   22 August [1862]
letters.summary:
Relates personal news about family members.

CD is "glad Glen Roy is settled".

Mentions evolutionary remarks on birds by Owen.

Compares variability among lower and higher organisms. Comments on Hooker’s view of the subject.

Forthcoming publication of Huxley’s book [Evidence as to man’s place in nature(1863)] and Lyell’s [Antiquity of man(1863)].

letters.title: From John Lubbock   23 August 1862
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary:
JL’s Swiss tour with Tyndall and Huxley.

Lake-habitations.

letters.title: To John Murray   24 August [1862]
letters.summary: CD is well content with sale of 768 copies [ofOrchids]. Hopes and expects remainder will ultimately be sold.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [26–31 August 1862]
letters.summary:
On microscopes.

Cannot remember any plants butMelastomawith different coloured polliniferous anthers.

letters.title: To Camilla Ludwig   26 August [1862]
letters.deprecated: Camilla Frederike Antonie (Camilla) LudwigCamilla Frederike Antonie (Camilla) Pattrick
letters.recipient: Camilla Frederike Antonie (Camilla) LudwigCamilla Frederike Antonie (Camilla) Pattrick
letters.summary: Family news; mostly an account of ill health.

letters.title: From A. C. Ramsay   26 August 1862
letters.summary: Sends his paper [on glacial lakes, see3450]. Falconer attacked it. Falconer thinks Himalayas confound the theory, but Hooker writes that it explains the absence of lakes there.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin [2–3 September 1862]
letters.summary:
Asks WED to send some specimens [ofLythrum?].

[Letter from Emma Darwin to WED on verso.]

letters.title: To C. C. Babington   2 September [1862]
letters.summary:
Can CCB getLythrum hyssopifoliumseeds?

Hottoniasplendidly dimorphic.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   2 September [1862]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Hive-bees and clover.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   2 September [1862]
letters.summary:
Exciting work on trimorphism inLythrum salicaria. Requests Lythraceae from Kew.

Wants to know of plants other thanMelastomaandLythrumwith coloured pollen.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   [3–]4 September [1862]
letters.summary:
Glad AG will publish some separate notes on orchids ["Fertilization of orchids through the agency of insects",Am. J. Sci.2d ser. 34 (1862): 420–9].

Trimorphism inLythrum.

Bee behaviour.

letters.title: To John Lubbock [3 September 1862]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: CD was in error about bees’ behaviour at clover.

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   4 September 1862
letters.summary: Sends flowers with anthers of two colours.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   5 September 1862
letters.summary:
Suggests CD try to getLythrum hyssopifoliafrom France.

Dimorphic flowers.

Differences between newly opened and older orchids.

Flowers ofSpiranthesandGoodyera.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   5 September [1862]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Finds JL’s facts on the diving insect that remains four hours under water new and interesting [see "On two aquatic Hymenoptera",Trans. Linn. Soc. Lond.24 (1864): 135–42].

letters.title: To A. C. Ramsay   5 September [1862]
letters.summary:
On ACR’s paper on glacial origin of lakes. CD thinks it is correct. Suggests further investigation to corroborate it. His only doubt has to do with areas of great activity.

On ACR’s view of cause of glacial period: CD did battle with Hooker on same point.

T. F. Jamieson has smashed CD’s Glen Roy marine theory in splendid style.

letters.title: From Edouard Claparède   6 September 1862
letters.deprecated: Jean Louis René Antoine Edouard (Edouard) Claparède
letters.sender: Jean Louis René Antoine Edouard (Edouard) Claparède
letters.summary:
Acknowledges CD’s approval of his review ofOrigininRevue Germanique[16 (1861): 523–59; 17 (1861): 232–63]. Praises natural selection;

criticises C.-A. Royer’s [French] translation.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [9? September 1862]
letters.summary: Asks for advice on where a local chemist can send his brother’s meteorological observations from Missouri.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [10? September 1862]
letters.summary: Gives advice as to whether certain meteorological observations would be worth making.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   11 September [1862]
letters.summary: Has passed the time by dissecting flowers of Cruciferae. Sends results, with diagrams, to JDH.

letters.title: From G. C. Oxenden   11 September 1862
letters.summary: He collectedSplachnum luteumnorth of Spitzbergen 40 years ago. Now an acquaintance has brought the plant back from the identical spot.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   12 September [1862]
letters.summary:
WDF’s information on turkeys will be useful when CD resumes his half-finished volume [seeVariation1: 292].

Illness in the family.

letters.title: From Edward Cresy   13 September 1862
letters.summary: Walter White [Asst.-Sec. and Librarian, Royal Society] has introduced EC to Richard Kippist of the Linnean Society, who has made little progress toward acceptingOrigin.

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   13 September 1862
letters.summary:
Has given directions to save seeds ofLythrum hyssopifolium.

CD’s diagram ofLythrum salicariais very remarkable. [SeeCollected papers2: 107.]

letters.title: To John Lindley   14 September [1862]
letters.summary: Thanks JL for review [ofOrchids,Gard. Chron.(1862): 789–90, 863]; CD published almost by accident, having been led on in part by encouragement from JL.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   14 September [1862]
letters.summary: Asks DO to name enclosedLythrumreceived from CD’s sister-in-law [Sarah Elizabeth Wedgwood]

letters.title: To Edward Cresy   15 September [1862]
letters.summary:
Son [Leonard] ill with scarlet fever. Also Mrs Darwin.

Intends to give up work onDroserauntilVariationis done.

letters.title: From C. C. Babington   16 September 1862
letters.summary:
Hopes to haveLythrum hyssopifoliumseeds to send soon.

BAAS is meeting in Cambridge and all eminent Cambridge men are wanted present. If his health were reliable, CD would be in chair of Botany and Zoology Section.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   16 September 1862
letters.summary:
Wife’s health better.

Visited Duke of Argyll.

Thanks CD for Cruciferae diagram; will ponder it.

Staggered by complexity ofWelwitschia.

letters.title: From Philip Gidley King   16 September 1862
letters.summary:
PGK’s brother is coming to England and will call on CD.

He is impressed but not absolutely convinced by theOrigin.

Raises a question about which CD wrote years ago: why do sheep degenerate in Australia, necessitating periodic importation?

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver 16 September 1862
letters.summary: Envelope containing specimens (apparently mentioned in the letter from Daniel Oliver 27 February 1863 (S 4015)).

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver [17 September 1862]
letters.summary:
Performed a large number ofLythrumcrosses before leaving home.

Working onDroserafor amusement. Has tried effect on plants of vegetable substances active on animal nervous systems, e.g., opium; makesDroserainactive for hours.

letters.title: From G. C. Oxenden   17 September [1862]
letters.summary: Strongly recommends Condy’s "Ozonised Disinfectant" as a cure for scarlet fever.

letters.title: From Alphonse de Candolle   18 September 1862
letters.summary:
PraisesOrchids.

He has finished his work onQuercus.

H. Lecoq has worked on hybridism,

and P. Duchartre on orchid polymorphism.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [18 September 1862]
letters.summary:
Thanks for JDH’s letter [3725].

Has become interested in experimenting onDrosera.

Observations on the ovaria of Cruciferae.

letters.title: From W. B. Clarke   20 September 1862
letters.summary:
Acknowledges presentation copy ofOrchids.

Asks advice on what to do with all his fossils. Sending various specimens.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   20 [September 1862]
letters.summary:
Would like to go to Cambridge [for BAAS meeting]. Reminisces about his student days.

Pleased that WDF likes his book [Orchids]. At one time CD agreed with Lyell that he was an ass to publish it.

Working on dimorphism and sensibility of other plants.

letters.title: From Emile M. J. M. P. Goubert   20 September 1862
letters.deprecated: Emile M. J. M. P. Goubert
letters.sender: Emile M. J. M. P. Goubert
letters.summary: Offers to exchange fossils with CD. He has very good series of French and German fossils.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   20 September 1862
letters.summary: Asks his opinion of A. C. Ramsay’s glacial lake theory. [Encloses Haast communications on glacial phenomena (missing).]

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   21 [September 1862]
letters.summary:
Thanks for Haast’s observations. Particularly glad to get geological evidence of glacial action (in Southern Hemisphere).

Thinks Ramsay’s theory to large extent true, but thinks that in a much disturbed country some lakes would have been formed in depressions.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   22 September 1862
letters.summary:
Last chapter ofOrchidsopens up a "knotty sort of question aboutaccident or design".

Changes in orchid flowers as they age.

Thinks CD may find trimorphism inNesaea verticillata.

letters.title: From Hugh Falconer   24–7 September [1862]
letters.summary:
Encloses MS ["On the American fossil elephant",Nat. Hist. Rev.(1863): 43–114]. Shows persistence of specific characters through glacial period.

Eocene monkeys mistakenly described as pigs.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   26 September [1862]
letters.summary: Encloses MS on observations and experiments onDrosera. JDH’s opinion will help him decide whether to pursue subject in some future year.

letters.title: To A. G. More   26 September 1862
letters.summary: Describes experiment on role of labellum in fertilisation of orchids. Asks for information.

letters.title: From G. C. Oxenden   27 September [1862]
letters.summary: Thinks "ozonised fluid" is a pure solution of permanganate of soda. Sends dosage.

letters.title: From Bartholomew James Sulivan   27 September [1862]
letters.summary: J. C. Wickham and Arthur Mellersh are in town and BJS wonders whether there is any chance CD might join them.

letters.title: From Henry Johnson   30 September 1862
letters.summary:
HHJ’s paper ["On the distorted skulls found at Wroxeter (Salop)",Proc. R. Soc. Lond.12 (1862–3): 149–50].

He has been approached about becoming F.R.S., but would like to know how expensive it would be.

Requests a photograph.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   30 September 1862
letters.summary:
Acknowledges 3d edition ofOrigin.

Praise of Herbert Spencer’sFirst Principles[1862].

letters.title: To Hugh Falconer   1 October [1862]
letters.summary:
Extreme interest in MS of HF’s paper on the American fossil elephant [Nat. Hist. Rev.n.s. 3 (1863): 43–114].

Pleased HF does not believe in immutable species. Significance of proboscidean group verging towards extinction. Comments on natural selection preserving type despite variability. Natural selection solves problem of how every part of each creature has become adapted.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   1 October [1862]
letters.summary:
Mentions a discussion of man by Isidore Geoffroy Saint-Hilaire in hisHistoire naturelle générale[1854–62].

Mentions a book by Friedrich Rolle [Ch. Darwin’s Lehre von der Entstehung der Arten(1863)].

Cites evolutionary statements on elephants by Hugh Falconer and notes Falconer’s objection to natural selection.

letters.title: To A. G. More   1 October 1862
letters.summary: Thanks for information. Asks for more information about labellum of orchids.

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   2 October [1862]
letters.summary: Hopes to visit CD with Mellersh and Wickham the week after next.

letters.title: From Hugh Falconer   3 October 1862
letters.summary: Inquires whether previous letter was received by CD.

letters.title: From Hugh Falconer   4 October 1862
letters.summary: Although their views differ, HF is glad they can discuss those differences without offending.

letters.title: To Hugh Falconer   4 October [1862]
letters.summary: Explains that he returned the MS - part of a paper on fossil and living species of elephant (Falconer 1863) - to Falconer’s house in Park Crescent the previous Thursday.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   4 and 13 October 1862
letters.summary: Thinks Max Müller’sLectures on the science of language[1861–4] will do a real service to CD and natural selection.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [5 October 1862]
letters.summary: Has found Lythrum, and sends some. Wants to know what CD thinks of frog discussion between Sandars and James. Asks CD to send objects for microscope demonstration. Means to go see the London Exhibition again. Has finished reading Orley Farm and returns it.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   6 October [1862]
letters.summary:
Thanks for opinion onDrosera. After working for a time on a subject he is absolutely incapable of judging its value.

Has found a case inLythrumof a necessary triple alliance between three hermaphrodites; the strangest case of propagation recorded among plants or animals.

Asks forL. thymifoliato see how a trimorphic form passes or graduates into dimorphic.

Questions JDH onLinum perenne.

Has found 33 hybrids in one field betweenVerbascum thapsusandV. lychnitis. The perfect series of varieties would have justified running the species together, but every one of the intermediate forms is sterile.

letters.title: To John Murray   7 October [1862?]
letters.summary: Reports misprint in announcement of his book [Orchids].

letters.title: From Henry Johnson   8 October 1862
letters.summary:
Doubts he has a chance of being elected F.R.S. because he is 58.

Will send a skull.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   9 October 1862
letters.summary: Discusses length of pistils, and measuring seeds and pods for botanical work.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   9 October 1862
letters.summary:
The BAAS meeting at Cambridge was exhausting.

Owen came to attack him but was beaten; his paper fell flat.

A "society for propagation of common honesty in all parts of the world" was established at Cambridge [THH’s "Thorough Club"?].

letters.title: ToNatural History Review   [before 10 October 1862]
letters.summary: In his work on cirripedes [Cirripedia, vol. 1Lepadidae(1851), pp. 53–5] CD described a particular organ as an "auditory-sac" although he was unable to trace the supposed nerve from it to any ganglion. August Krohn [in "Observations on the development of the Cirripedia",Ann. & Mag. Nat. Hist.3d ser. 6 (1859): 423–8] concluded that the organ was ovarian. CD supposes that Krohn is correct, but gives further observations that suggest an auditory function. If someone could find ova within the curious organ it would confirm Krohn’s view.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   10 October [1862]
letters.summary:
Thanks for a contribution ["On the so-called ""auditory-sac"" of cirripedes",Nat. Hist. Rev.(1863): 115–16;Collected papers2: 85–7]. Is sending a proof.

This year’s lecture to working men to be devoted to CD’s book.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   11 October [1862]
letters.summary: Sends comments on Lythrum.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [12 October 1862]
letters.summary:
Has sent twoImpatiensflowers; curious to know what CD makes of the floral whorls and their vascular bundles.

Cassiais another genus that has different [coloured] anthers in same flower.

Continues to work onWelwitschia.

Feels as CD does about his work, which after a time seems flat and stale. He could never have done what CD did in hisOrchids.

CD’s facts aboutVerbascumhave horrible bearing on JDH’s practice of lumping species together.

letters.title: To George Bentham   13 October [1862]
letters.summary: Asks for reference to GB’s summary of Targioni-Tozzetti’s book ["Historical notes on the introduction of various plants into the agriculture and horticulture of Tuscany: a summary of a work entitledCenni storici sulla introduzione di varie piante nell agricultura ed orticultura Toscanaby Dr Antonio Targioni-Tozzetti, Florence, 1850",J. Hortic. Soc. Lond.9 (1855): 133–81]. [SeeVariation, 1st ed., 1: 306 n.]

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   13 October [1862]
letters.summary:
RequestsLinum, for dimorphism study.

Reviewer ofOrchids[Nat. Hist. Rev.n.s. 2 (1862): 371–6]is correct about the organisation of the book; he wonders who the reviewer is.

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   13 October [1862]
letters.summary: If Wickham remains in town and CD is well enough, BJS thinks they might come about the 22d.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   14 [October 1862]
letters.summary:
Thanks forAldrovandareference andCassia.

Has wasted labour on Melastomataceae without getting a glimpse of the meaning of the parts.

Wants seeds, from their native land, ofHeterocentronorMonochaetum.

Is beginning to change his view about rarity of natural hybrids.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   14 October [1862]
letters.summary:
Further comments on Jamieson’s theory of the formation of the roads of Glen Roy; paper by Jamieson dealing with glaciation in Scotland ["On the ice-worn rocks of Scotland",Q. J. Geol. Soc. Lond.18 (1862): 164–84].

Comments on paper by A. C. Ramsay on the glacial formation of lakes ["On the glacial origin of certain lakes",Q. J. Geol. Soc. Lond.18 (1862): 185–204].

Criticises remarks by John Tyndall on glacial formation of Swiss valleys.

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   14 October [1862]
letters.summary: Arranges to come to Down on the 21st if CD is well enough.

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   15 October [1862]
letters.summary:
Asks for news of HWB and his book.

There has been sickness in CD’s family; one of the boys [and Emma] had scarlet fever.

Has had a letter from Edwin Brown of Burton who is working on classification ofCarabi.

letters.title: From George Bentham   15 October 1862
letters.summary:
Sends CD the reference for GB’s summary of Targioni-Tozzetti’s work [see3760].

Hopes for a communication to the Linnean Society from CD "this winter".

letters.title: From C. C. Babington   16 October 1862
letters.summary: Believes the [Lythrum] seeds have been sent to CD by Stratton [Curator, Cambridge Botanic Garden]. They have none of the others requested.

letters.title: From E. Schweizerbart’sche Verlagsbuchhandlung   16 October 1862
letters.summary:
Discusses German editions ofOriginandOrchids.

Sends publication dealing with leaves.

Relates amusing case of paternity confirmed.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   16 October [1862]
letters.summary:
Lythrum salicariais coming out clear.

Would be glad ofNesaeaseed.

Is disappointed withMelastoma, but is sure there is something curious to be made out.

His experiments with poisons onDroseralead him to conclude that it possesses something analogous to nervous matter.

Comments on natural hybrids ofVerbascum.

Deplores the Civil War and the feelings it has fostered in Britain.

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   17 October 1862
letters.summary:
Still working on book and has completed 620 out of 700 pages.

Rewrote memoir [on mimicry in Amazon Lepidoptera] forTrans. Linn. Soc. Lond.[23 (1862): 495–566].

Edwin Brown, HWB’s earliest naturalist friend, will have a hard time classifyingCarabias he is unable to travel.

letters.title: To Walter White   17 [October – November 1862?]
letters.summary: CD needs first volume of the second series [ofTrans. R. Hortic. Soc. Lond.].

letters.title: To Friedrich Rolle   17 October [1862]
letters.summary: Rolle has done great service by publishing his book [Ch. Darwin’s Lehre von der Entstehung der Arten(1863)].

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   18 October [1862]
letters.summary:
Thanks for last note. Assures HWB that all writers have problems similar to his.

Plans to inquire at Linnean Society for HWB’s paper.

His family, including Mrs Darwin and Leonard, are now well.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [18 October 1862]
letters.summary:
Does CD wantMasdevallia?

Sends addresses of persons in S. America who would send Melastomataceae seeds.

Has ordered Matthieu Bonafous on maize [Histoire naturelle du maïs(1836)].

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   18 October [1862]
letters.summary: Confirms arrangements for his trip to Down.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   21 October [1862]
letters.summary: Effect on seed production of differences in distance betweenLythrumplants.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   23 October [1862]
letters.summary: Sends observations on Lythrum. Reports bad health of Maud Atherley.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   23 October [1862]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Would like JL to call.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [25 October 1862]
letters.summary: Asks WED to make some observations on differences in pods ofLythrum.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   25 October 1862
letters.summary:
Has sentMasdevalliaand other plants.

J. J. F. W. v. Parrot’sArarat[(1834), trans. W. D. Cooley, inThe world surveyed in the XIXth century, vol. 1 (1845)] refreshing in its simple faith in the ark.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   25 October 1862
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary:
CD’s health is bad.

Would like to visit CD on Friday.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   27 October 1862
letters.summary:
SendsNesaeaseeds for CD

and stamps for Leonard Darwin.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   27 [October 1862]
letters.summary:
Masdevalliaturns out to be nothing wonderful, "I was merely stupid about it."

Asks for plants for experiments.

HedysarumandOxalis sensitivaseeds.

Asks whether Oliver knows of experiments on absorption of poisons by roots.

CD finds he cannot publish this year onLythrum salicaria; he must make 126 additional crosses!

Asks for odd variations of common potato; he wants to grow a few plants of every variety.

Variationis crawling.

Has had some bad attacks lately.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   27 [October 1862]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary:
Hopes to be well enough on Friday to see JL.

Several of the family have had influenza.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   28 October 1862
letters.summary: Distances betweenLythrumplants.

letters.title: From Henrietta Emma Darwin   [29 October 1862]
letters.summary: Instinct in cats.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   30 [October 1862]
letters.summary:
Thanks WED for observations onLythrum.

Discusses family affairs.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   30 October 1862
