letters.summary: RT has sent his observations on orchids to CD. Has found only one case of an insect with a pollinium adhering to it.

letters.title: ToJournal of Horticulture and Cottage Gardener   [17–24 March 1863]
letters.summary: Reports the observations of Hermann Crüger and John Scott that fruit is set by orchids whose flowers never open and that pollen-tubes are emitted from pollen-masses still in their proper position. These cases convince CD that inOrchidshe underestimated the power of tropical orchids to produce seed without insect aid but he is not shaken in his belief that the structure of the flowers is mainly related to insect agency.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   17 March [1863]
letters.summary:
Lyell’sAntiquity of manlacks originality.

Statements in Lyell provoke CD to determine exact publication date ofOriginand JDH’s introductory essay [toFlora Tasmaniae].

CD now believes in repeated periods of global cooling and migration.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   17 March [1863]
letters.summary:
His better opinion [of work of Boucher de Perthes].

Explains his position on CL’s treatment of species.

Mentions positive response to his ideas on the part of a German professor [Ernst Haeckel], Alphonse de Candolle, and a botanical palaeontologist [Gaston de Saporta].

Notes negative reaction of entomologists.

Mentions Falconer’s objections [toAntiquity].

Mentions work of Hooker.

Comments on paper by Owen ["On the aye-aye",Rep. BAAS32 (1862) pt 2: 114–16]

and CD’s review of Bates’s paper [Collected papers2: 87–92].

ThinksNatural History Reviewis excellent.

letters.title: From T. W. Woodbury   17 March 1863
letters.summary: Bee species of different sizes build cells the same size.

letters.title: To T. W. Woodbury   [after 17 March 1863]
letters.summary: Thanks for the artificial comb.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   20 March [1863]
letters.summary:
Discusses the meaning of C. K. Sprengel’s term "dichogamy". Dichogamous plants are functionally monoecious;Primulais functionally dioecious.

Reports Hermann Crüger’s observations ofCattleyaand of bees pollinatingCatasetum. Crüger will observe Melastomataceae.

Has built a hothouse.

FearsAmsinckiacannot be dimorphic.

Ill health slows his work onVariation.

letters.title: From Alfred Newton   21 March 1863
letters.summary:
Sends tuber of Chilean wild potato, requested through Hooker and P. L. Sclater.

Plans to exhibit a bird’s foot with a large ball of clay attached. This phenomenon supports CD on seed dispersal.

letters.title: From John Scott   21 March [1863]
letters.summary:
Thanks for CD’s answers onPassiflora

and Asa Gray review.

Has observed gradation of sterility inOncidiumspecies.

Has observed rostellar germination and fertilisation inLaelia. The latter was prevented inBletiaby covering the stigma with plaster of Paris.

Gongora atropurpureacapsules are swelling.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   22–30 March 1863
letters.summary:
Discusses the Duke of Argyll’s article on the supernatural [Edinburgh Rev.116 (1862): 378–97].

Has heard that the Incas married their sisters; this may be worth investigating as a case of inbreeding.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   23 March [1863]
letters.summary:
Thanks WDF for authentic details of number and colour of lambs [Variation2: 30].

Complains of his eczema.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   24–5 March [1863]
letters.summary: Observation on morphology ofPrimulaovarium sent for DO’s use.

letters.title: To an editor   24 March [1863?]
letters.summary: Encloses a dialogue on species from a New Zealand newspaper [S. Butler’s First dialogue on evolution, from theChristchurch Press].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [24 March 1863]
letters.summary:
Has been looking at separation of sexes in poplars.

Interested in reversion.

Does not understand all CD said on inheritance.

JDH now remembers thatOriginwas "published" some time before it was "distributed" and therefore appeared prior to his own essay [see also2478].

Impossible to say whether some Dipterocarpaceae survived a cold period or have developed since.

letters.title: To Alfred Newton   24 March [1863]
letters.summary:
Thanks for potatoes, which may be useful in crossing.

Germination of seeds in earth on partridge’s foot.

letters.title: To John Scott   24 March [1863]
letters.summary:
Enthusiastic about JS’s work onPassifloraself-incompatibility.

CD quotes JS on rostellar pollen germination [in "Fertilisation of orchids",Collected papers2: 77–8]. H. Crüger attributes it to ants’ carrying stigmatic secretion to pollen.

Homomorphic cowslip seedlings are, sadly, showing variation.

letters.title: From Armand de Quatrefages   25 March 1863
letters.deprecated: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.sender: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.summary:
Charles Martins of Montpellier will collect the varieties of silkworm for CD.

QdeB is battling with the polygenists in the Société d’Anthropologie.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   26 [March 1863]
letters.summary:
CD’s opinion of Lyell’sAntiquity of man.

Geographical distribution during and between glacial periods.

Latent characters and reversion.

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   [26 March 1863]
letters.summary: Discusses the female parts of thePrimulaflower; the true character of the free placenta is not completely understood.

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   27 March 1863
letters.summary: Wants to know when he may visit CD.

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   [27 March 1863]
letters.summary:
Sends some specimens for CD.

Is busy with W. AfricanAmomum, whose floral structure he discusses.

letters.title: To Armand de Quatrefages   27 March [1863]
letters.deprecated: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.recipient: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.summary:
Specimens obtained from Charles Martins will be most interesting.

Comments on QdeB’s book [Physiologie comparée(1862)].

letters.title: From Armand de Quatrefages   [28 March] – 11 April 1863
letters.deprecated: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.sender: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.summary: Continues to support, in debates at the Société d’Anthropologie, the view that variability of animals and anatomical modifications are produced by environment. Wishes to use CD’s niata cattle example fromJournal of researches[2d ed., pp. 145–6].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [28 March 1863]
letters.summary:
Evidence of tropical floras continuous since Tertiary cannot fit CD’s position on intermittent cold periods.

Agrees with CD on reversion and latency.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   28 March [1863]
letters.summary:
Nectar secretion inEdwardsia. Could the stamen protect stigma?

Sends monstrousPrimulawith three pistils.

Had never heard of Robert Caspary, but what DO thinks is the placenta could be a whorl of pistils without stigmas.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   29 [March–June 1863 or 1864?]
letters.summary: Would like WED to send a specimen of the unusual plant organ of which he sent a drawing.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [29 March 1863]
letters.summary:
CD regrets he used "creation" inOriginwhen he meant "appeared".

An Oken-like article in "Owenian style" inAthenæum.

Tropical plants continue to be troublesome.

letters.title: To G. H. K. Thwaites   30 March [1863]
letters.summary:
Thanks GHKT for specimens ofSethia. Discusses functions of their dimorphism for insect fertilisation.

Discusses polymorphism and fertilisation in Lythraceae.

Asks for seed ofLimnanthemum.

Describes his interest in galls.

Discusses curious specimens ofGomphiaandLesemia.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [31 March 1863]
letters.summary: Owen is the author of theAthenæumarticle [28 Mar 1863, pp. 417–19]. JDH dismisses it as vulgar rubbish. W. B. Carpenter intends to write a reply.

letters.title: From Richard Trevor Clarke   [April? 1863]
letters.summary: Encloses strawberry blossoms used in his crossing experiments.

letters.title: From John Scott   [1–11] April [1863]
letters.summary:
Studying self-sterility, particularly inOncidium, where abortion occurs consistently but stigma functions normally. His hybrid orchid crosses show sterility occurs capriciously. Thus it is not a "special endowment".

Disputes Asa Gray’s and Hermann Crüger’s view of rostellar germination.

Doubts absolute sterility ofCatasetum.

Disappointed by results with homomorphic cowslips.

letters.title: To Charles Turner   [1 April – 16 June 1863?]
letters.summary: Asks correspondent whether, when growing hollyhocks, he finds it necessary to space out the different varieties to prevent crossing and thus to obtain true seed [seeVariation2: 108].

letters.title: From James Anderson   1 April 1863
letters.summary:
Sends CD seeds ofCattleya crispaas requested [seeCollected papers2: 77–8].

Anticipates success for his attempts to cross orchids artificially. Has not had a single seed germinate from a pod that was not produced by artificial crossing.

letters.title: From Arthur Rawson   1 April [1863]
letters.summary: Conducted crosses onGladiolusvarieties exactly according to CD’s letter. Flowers of same variety are self-sterile, whether from the same plant or not.

letters.title: To Arthur Rawson   2 April [1863]
letters.summary: Discusses unusual primula flowers and asks for details of Rawson’s experiments with gladioli. Asks for loan ofCypripediumbut admits he will probably mutilate it.

letters.title: To the chairman of Bromley District Highway Board from the parishioners of Down, Kent   3 April 1863
letters.summary: Testimony by the parishioners of Down, Kent, to the moral character and integrity of George Snow, District Surveyor. Signed by nearly fifty local residents, including CD.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   5 April [1863]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary:
JL’s review of Lyell’sAntiquity of man(1863) [Nat. Hist. Rev.n.s. 3 (1863): 211–19].

Owen’s review of W. B. Carpenter inAthenæum[28 Mar 1863, pp. 417–19].

letters.title: To Maxwell Tylden Masters   6 April [1863]
letters.summary: Comments on MTM’s article ["On the existence of two forms of peloria",Nat. Hist. Rev.n.s. 3 (1863): 258–62]. Cites interesting case of peloric flower.

letters.title: From Arthur Rawson   [6 April 1863]
letters.summary:
Provides evidence of self-sterility inGladiolus.

Has observed three seed-leaves in someDianthusseedlings.

Cannot cross, or grow from seed,Dielytra spectabilis.

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   7 April 1863
letters.summary: Has seen some curious hybrid ducks and geese of Bartlett’s. Bartlett will do experiments suggested by CD when he has time.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   7 April 1863
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary:
JL is off to visit Scotch "kjökken möddings".

Hopes Lyell is not really vexed by his article.

letters.title: To M. T. Masters   [8–13 April 1863]
letters.summary:
Sends two spikes ofCorydalis.

Admits he may have drawn false inference from MTM’s division of peloria into two classes.

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   8 April 1863
letters.summary:
Preparations under way to move to London account for delay in thanking CD for his review [Collected papers2: 87–92].

His book is finished, and he is sending a copy to CD; owing to the great expense few copies will be sent to reviewers.

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   9 April [1863]
letters.summary:
Thanks HWB for his book [Naturalist on the river Amazons]. Feels sure it will often be alluded to in other works.

Asa Gray is fascinated by the "Butterfly paper" ["Contributions to an insect fauna of the Amazon valley",Trans. Linn. Soc. Lond.23 (1862): 495–566].

letters.title: From Asa Gray   11 April 1863
letters.summary: The war is nearly finished, "rebeldom is ""gone up"" ".

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   [12 April 1863]
letters.summary: Working on monstrousPrimula. Is ovule anatropous as Asa Gray says, or amphitropous? Does he know natural path of pollen tubes inPrimula. Can the tube enter the ovule by the chalaza?

letters.title: To John Scott   12 April [1863]
letters.summary:
Encourages JS to publish on sterility of orchids and to experiment onPassiflora.

Doubted Hooker’s poppy case.

Describes case of primrose with three pistils: when pulled apart allowed pollen to be placed directly on ovules. This supports JS’s explanation of H. Crüger’s case.

letters.title: From John Scott   [after 12] April [1863]
letters.summary:
Thanks for CD’sLinumpaper [Collected papers2: 93–105].

Has not published much because he would be ignored as a gardener; hence he is looking for a foreign appointment.

Has prepared orchid sterility paper at CD’s suggestion [Trans. Bot. Soc. Edinburgh7 (1863): 543–50].

letters.title: From David Thomas Ansted   13 April 1863
letters.summary: Is ready to make some arrangement to repay CD’s bond. Has written to F. Ransome to help arrange repayment and wants CD to write his opinion of a fair scheme.

letters.title: To William Henry Flower   13 April [1863]
letters.summary: Asks WHF to obtain photographs of skull of ox for J. L. A. Quatrefages de Bréau.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   13 April 1863
letters.summary:
Hopes CD will finish and bring out his book on variation.

AG will publish extracts of H. W. Bates’s paper on mimetic analogy [Am. J. Sci.2d ser. 36 (1863): 279–94].

letters.title: From George Bentham   [c.14 April 1863]
letters.summary: Asks CD whether he knows of "anything worth looking at" that has appeared abroad on his theory of the origin of species.

letters.title: From M. T. Masters   14 April 1863
letters.summary: Thanks CD for specimens which show that an abnormality in one genus is normal in another, which bears on CD’s views on descent.

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   14 April 1863
letters.summary: The ovule ofPrimulais amphitropous or what J. Georg Agardh calls apotropo-amphitropous [seeTheoria systematis plantarum(1858), tab. 24, fig. 5–6].

letters.title: To Armand de Quatrefages   [14 April 1863]
letters.deprecated: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.recipient: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.summary:
The niata is a very good case because the race is well established and must originate in South America. There is a description of the head by [Richard] Owen in theDescriptive catalogue of the osteological collection of the College of Surgeons.

Has observed modifications in the skeletons of rabbits, ducks, poultry, and pigeons. There is an extract about modifications in pigeons in the first chapter ofOrigin. Encloses a woodcut of crested or polish fowls; there is a change in the brain as well as in the exterior bones.

letters.title: From Robert Swinhoe   14 April 1863
letters.summary: Difference in plumage ofArdeola, a species of heron, in summer and winter. [SeeDescent2: 190.]

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   [after 14 April 1863]
letters.summary: Thanks for information onPrimulaovules. From what DO says the pollen-tubes ought to find their way to the micropyle.

letters.title: To D. T. Ansted   15 April 1863
letters.summary: Discusses the repayment of a loan made by CD to DTA and F. Ransome.

letters.title: To George Bentham   15 April [1863]
letters.summary: Sends GB a selection of reviews of theOriginfrom his collection of about 90, with his opinion of some of them.

letters.title: From W. H. Flower   15 April 1863
letters.summary: Discusses having skull photographed and a cast made.

letters.title: From William Hepworth Dixon   16 April 1863
letters.summary: Thinks CD’s letter ["The doctrine of heterogeny",Collected papers2: 78–80] will appear "with a clearer field and to better effect" if delayed a week, since next issue [ofAthenæum] has Lyell’s reply to Hugh Falconer, and W. B. Carpenter’s report on the Abbéville jaw.

letters.title: From Isaac Anderson-Henry   17 April 1863
letters.summary: Has donePrimula polyanthusexperiment CD suggested.

letters.title: From D. T. Ansted   17 April 1863
letters.summary: Was unable to see Ransome [to find out whether DTA’s shares in the patent had earned any income so he could repay CD] but believes Ransome’s work will be profitable. Bemoans his own constant financial misfortune and asks CD to give up the deed of his loan to him, on the promise that if the shares ever yield any income, CD will be paid.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [17 April 1863]
letters.summary:
Likes JDH’s review of Alphonse de Candolle [Mémoires et souvenirs de A. P. de Candolle(1862)].

Falconer’s article on Lyell ["Primitive man. What led to the question?",Athenæum4 Apr 1863, pp. 459–60] too severe.

CD has written a letter to theAthenæum"to say, under the cloak of attacking Heterogeny, a word in my own defence" [Collected papers2: 78–80].

Bates’sTravels[Naturalist on the river Amazons(1863)] are excellent.

letters.title: ToAthenæum   18 April [1863]
letters.summary:
Attacks the doctrine of "heterogeny" (spontaneous generation during each geological period) as completely lacking in evidence.

Defends natural selection as connecting large classes of facts in natural history. That certain forms have not changed since remote epochs is not an objection of any force.

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   18 April [1863]
letters.summary:
Has finished vol. 1 [ofNaturalist on the river Amazons]. CD praises book as "best ever published in England".

The review in theAthenæumwas cold, as always, and insolent.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   18 April [1863]
letters.summary:
Describes a letter he has written to theAthenæumin which he mentions CL’s views on species modification ["Doctrine of heterogeny",Collected papers2: 78–80].

Comments on criticism of Lyell’s book [Antiquity] by Falconer and others.

Mentions his eczema.

Invites the Lyells to visit.

letters.title: From Philip Gidley King   19 April 1863
letters.summary: CD’s photograph evokes PGK’s reminiscence of CD in theBeagle.

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   20 April 1863
letters.summary:
Expresses hope that CD is ready to pronounce sentence on his book;

he relates his financial position and mentions that he hopes to get a position at the British Museum.

letters.title: From H. B. Dobell   20 April 1863
letters.summary: Sends CD a form he has devised of a proper genealogical table of three or four generations of the families of medical cases, so that hereditary transmission may be more accurately and fully recorded.

letters.title: From Hugh Falconer   20 April [1863]
letters.summary:
Has been in France, conveys good wishes from Quatrefages.

Describes the fossil of an unusual mammal head from Brazil.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   20 April [1863]
letters.summary:
Fears England and U. S. will drift into war; he and AG must "keep to Science".

Thanks for facts on Incas; regrets he has always avoided the case of man.

Has sent hisLinumpaper [Collected papers2: 93–105].

Is it true that Ohio has legislated against marriage of cousins?

Can AG explain the invariable angles in phyllotaxy; are they the consequence of packing in the early bud?

Owen’s comments on heterogeny in theAthenæum[28 Mar 1863] have vexed W. B. Carpenter; CD has replied [Collected papers2: 78–80].

Hopes AG will observeGymnadenia; John Scott has been experimenting on its fertilisation.

Gives his observation on pollination ofCypripedium.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   20 April 1863
letters.summary: AG’s opinion of Lyell’sAntiquity of man.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   20 April 1863
letters.summary:
Attacks by Falconer [Athenæum4 Apr 1863, pp. 459–60] and Joseph Prestwich on Lyell.

W. B. Carpenter fails to attack Owen.

Welwitschiamale cones with useless ovules marvellous example of lost function and retained structure.

JDH evaluates his sons.

letters.title: From George Bentham   21 April 1863
letters.summary: Has not yet read the pamphlets [selection of reviews ofOrigin, sent by CD at GB’s request]. Though GB does not go so far as Hooker in accepting all of CD’s hypotheses and does not feel up to a thorough discussion of his views, he hopes in his Linnean Anniversary Address [Proc. Linn. Soc. Lond.(1863): xi–xxix] to speak on the present state of the [species] question.

letters.title: To H. B. Dobell   21 April [1863]
letters.summary:
CD thinks HBD’s tables would be a considerable gain because "the importance of hereditary transmission can hardly be exaggerated from every point of view". Makes suggestions.

Asks him to send any remarkable cases of inheritance to him and, as well, any case of regrowth of amputated additional digit.

letters.title: From John Hutton Balfour   22 April 1863
letters.summary:
Thanks for paper onLinum[Collected papers2: 93–105].

One of his gardeners [John Scott] is also studying such fertilisation and appreciates CD’s encouragement; Scott has paper to read for Edinburgh Botanical Society.

letters.title: To George Bentham   22 April [1863]
letters.summary: Disagrees with GB when he says he is not up to treating the whole subject [the present state of the species question]. He is especially equipped to handle the "great subject of affinities in relation to descent and independent creation".

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   22 April [1863]
letters.summary: Sent off Corydalis. Observations on Corydalis pistils.

letters.title: To Hugh Falconer   22 April [1863]
letters.summary: Good of HF to tell him about Brazilian beast. So intermediate a form is "very glorious". Must assume it is very old.

letters.title: From D. T. Ansted   23 April 1863
letters.summary:
Is very grateful for CD’s note and return of the bond for £250; promises to repay CD any profits made from those shares, even in the event of DTA’s death.

Is sorry to hear CD is ill.

letters.title: From Hermann Crüger   23 April 1863
letters.summary:
Observations onCatasetum.

Figs require insects in order to set seed.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   23 April [1863]
letters.summary:
Grieved by Falconer’s and Prestwich’s treatment of Lyell.

Reproductive anatomy of the common ash reminds CD of JDH’sWelwitschiabecause of its transitional forms.

Pleased JDH encourages Oliver to do orchids.

letters.title: From Isaac Anderson-Henry   24 April 1863
letters.summary: Bryanthus erectus, said by [D. D.?] Cunningham to be a hybrid, has been found wild in North America.

letters.title: From Hugh Falconer   24 April [1863]
letters.summary: Further description of theToxodon-like mammal,Typotherium.

letters.title: From George Maw   25 April 1863
letters.summary: Has obtained fossils from Gibraltar that he believes are human. Requests Lyell’s address so that he can send the bones.

letters.title: To Lovell Augustus Reeve   25 April [1863]
letters.summary: Thanks for LAR’s book [The land and freshwater mollusks indigenous to, or naturalised in, the British Isles(1863)].

letters.title: From John James Aubertin   27 April 1863
letters.summary:
Reminds CD of their acquaintance at Ilkley Wells; encloses portrait of self;

describes the topography, trade, commerce, produce, and population of São Paulo province.

Sends pieces of rock blasted for railway for CD to analyse.

letters.title: From Edward Cresy   27 April 1863
letters.summary:
CD’sLinumpaper [Collected papers2: 93–105].

Sending up-to-date railway map of southern region.

letters.title: To ?   28 April [1863?]
letters.summary: Discusses exchange of photographs with Édouard Claparède, "for whom I feel the highest respect".

letters.title: To Andrew Crombie Ramsay   29 April [1863]
letters.summary:
Interested in ACR’s Presidential Address [Q. J. Geol. Soc. Lond.19 (1863): xxix–lii] on the breaks in succession (of formations). Hopes ACR will provide a diagram of breaks, with the percentage of fossils that "pass upwards", i.e., continue to appear.

Horrified at Huxley’s geology.

Wishes ACR would discuss "creeps".

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   30 April [1863]
letters.summary: After finishing vol. 2 [ofNaturalist on the river Amazons], CD still has only praise. Remarks that his family is also enjoying the book. He regrets having finished, since he so enjoyed the descriptions.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [30 April 1863]
letters.summary: JDH has lost a letter from Julius von Haast intended for CD.

letters.title: From Charles William Crocker   1[–4] May 1863
letters.summary:
ObservesPlantago’s out-crossing mechanism.

Observations of style lengths of primroses and cowslips.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   1 May [1863]
letters.summary: Discusses dimorphism in linum and primula. Describes death of Mrs. Ashworth.

letters.title: To Isaac Anderson-Henry   2 May [1863]
letters.summary:
Convinced length of stamens has no relation to powers of fertilisation in many plants.

Suggests experiments onPelargoniumandPhlox.

Advises about use of microscope.

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   2 May [1863]
letters.summary:
His satisfaction at CD’s acceptance of book as well as total public acceptance. Murray has given him a £250 advance. His pleasure at Asa Gray’s words.

Next task will be to write on origin [of species] by segregation of local races.

letters.title: To John Scott   2 May [1863]
letters.summary:
Impressed by JS’s attempts to fertiliseGongora.

CD has large collection of notes on orchids, but does not know when he will publish on them again.

Asks for JS’s papers on sterility of individual orchids and onDrosera.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   4 May [1863]
letters.summary: Sends observations on [Anchusa] plants from Isle of Wight.

letters.title: From Charles and Emma Darwin to William Erasmus Darwin   [4 May 1863]
letters.summary: Glad to hear of the plant; CD instructs WED to make further observations. If it is a good case he will insist on WED’s sending a communication to the Linnean Society.

letters.title: ToAthenæum   5 May [1863]
letters.summary: Replies to a reviewer’s statement, that any theory of descent will connect large classes of facts, by pointing out that no other explanation has been as satisfactory as natural selection. But whatever view is adopted "signifies extremely little in comparison with the admission that species have descended from other species and have not been created immutable".

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [5 May 1863]
letters.summary: Discusses dimorphic plants.

letters.title: From William Alexander Wooler   5 May 1863
letters.summary: Encloses plants derived from a cowslip–polyanthus cross.

letters.title: From A. C. Ramsay   6 May 1863
letters.summary:
Glad CD likes his Presidential Address to Geological Society [1863].

Will continue the practice [of discussing the break in succession of strata].

Has devised a diagram showing number of genera and species in each geological formation and the number that pass from formation to formation.

Describes the glaciated terrain of S. Wales.

letters.title: From Isaac Anderson-Henry   7 May 1863
letters.summary: CD is right on heterostyly inPrimula. High praise. Has confirmed it withPrimula polyanthus.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [7 May 1863]
letters.summary:
Falconer going to France in defence of his views.

On scientific squabbling.

Herschel’s theory of the earth.

Bates’s book.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [7 May 1863]
letters.summary:
Falconer’s letter [attacking CL,Athenæum4 Apr 1863, pp. 459–60] is most unjust.

Regrets his letter [toAthenæum, on heterogeny] now criticised by Owen.

Comments on article by Samuel Haughton [On the form of cells made by wasps – with an appendix on the origin of species(1863)].

Mentions forthcoming reviews by Asa Gray [inAm. J. Sci.].

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   8 May [1863]
letters.summary: Describes the structure ofCorydalisand its arrangement for making pollen accessible to bees.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [8 May 1863]
letters.summary: JDH encourages a Mr Salwyn [Osbert Salvin] to collect in Galapagos; would like CD to add his encouragement.

letters.title: From W. H. Flower   9 May 1863
letters.summary: Sends photos of the niata ox skull presented by CD.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [9 May 1863]
letters.summary:
Lists the six honest believers in his species theory in England.

Asa Gray complains that Lyell acts like a judge on species, whereas CD complains of Lyell’s indecision.

CD working on divergence of leaves.

Distribution of Cameroon plants and the glacial theory.

Survival of island relics.

letters.title: From Charles Lyell   9 May 1863
letters.summary: Has been to Osborne on the Isle of Wight to visit Queen Victoria, who had lots of questions about CD.

letters.title: To Thomas Rivers   [9 May 1863]
letters.summary:
Doubts the fruit will stick on his Chinese double peach and asks TR to send him a couple when ripe.

Would like to grow seeds of the "curious monstrosity" of a wall-flower, to see whether the monstrosity is hereditary.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [10 May 1863]
letters.summary:
Thanks WED for his botanical specimens and observations.

DiscussesCorydalisand the fertilisation of Fumariaceae.

letters.title: From Henry Fletcher Hance   10 May 1863
letters.summary:
Sends sketch ofCatasetum tridentatumfruit at request of Edward Bradford.

CD incorrectly asserted thatCatasetumis male [Orchids, pp. 236–8].

letters.title: From George Howard Darwin   [before 11 May 1863]
letters.summary: Notes, calculations, and diagrams on phyllotaxy.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   11 May [1863]
letters.summary:
CD despairs when men like AG and Lyell consider themselves incapable of judging on change of species by descent.

Is confused over phyllotaxy.

Has been looking atPlantago lanceolata.

letters.title: To Osbert Salvin   11 [May 1863]
letters.summary: At the suggestion of J. D. Hooker CD offers his opinion on the value of a proposed collection to be made at the Galápagos. The display would not be attractive or appealing to amateurs in natural history, but the scientific value of good collections of every species would be very great if those of each island are rigorously kept separate.

letters.title: From H. B. Dobell   12 May 1863
letters.summary:
Sends copy of the table, which now embodies CD’s suggestions [see4117].

Gives instances of persons born with two thumbs and comments on hereditary factor.

letters.title: To W. H. Flower   12 May [1863]
letters.summary: Thanks WHF for photographs [of niata ox skull]. Will tell Quatrefages de Bréau about the cast. May have the photographs copied for woodcuts to illustrate his book on variation under domestication.

letters.title: From John Edward Gray   12 May 1863
letters.summary: Cites instance in which different varieties of same species of plant flourished side by side under same conditions.

letters.title: To George Maw   12 May [1863]
letters.summary:
Believes GM’s human bones from Gibraltar must be of very doubtful age. Lyell agrees, but feels any skull found should be forwarded to George Busk or Hugh Falconer.

Suggests GM look carefully for shells in the drift.

letters.title: From Osbert Salvin   12 May 1863
letters.summary: Has just returned from collecting in Central America and is planning to go to the Galapagos to gather specimens in all branches of natural history.

letters.title: To Edward Cresy   13 May [1863]
letters.summary:
Thanks for maps.

George [Darwin] failed at St John’s [College, Cambridge] and will stay another year at school.

letters.title: To H. B. Dobell   13 May [1863]
letters.summary: The [genealogical] table seems excellent. Would be obliged for any further information about the children of the cousins – the case surprises CD.

letters.title: From Julius von Haast   13 May 1863
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for letter [3935].

Encloses report [missing] of his latest expedition [to west coast], which had a grand result.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [13 May 1863]
letters.summary:
Lyell is "half-hearted but whole-headed" for CD’s theory. George Bentham wholly converted.

Bates’s book delightful but has a Darwinistic bias.

Cameroon plants.

JDH defends Bates against J. E. Gray’s slanders.

letters.title: To Richard Kippist   13 May [1863 or 1868]
letters.summary: Asks to borrow J. J. Audubon [Ornithological biography(1831–9)].

letters.title: From George Chichester Oxenden   13 May 1863
letters.summary: Going abroad; will miss the English orchid season.

letters.title: From Hugh Algernon Weddell   13 May 1863
letters.summary:
Has searched in vain for theOphrys apiferaCD asked for.

Thanks CD for paper onLinum[Collected papers2: 93–105].

Calls CD’s attention to his observations on Rubiaceae.

letters.title: To James Digues La Touche   14 May [1863?]
letters.summary: Thanks for drawing and note about peach–nectarine.

letters.title: To Armand de Quatrefages   14 May [1863]
letters.deprecated: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.recipient: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.summary: Is sending photographs of the niata skull [requested in4082]. W. H. Flower reports that he could have a cast made for £3.3s.0d.

letters.title: From La Société des Sciences Naturelles de Neuchâtel
letters.deprecated: Société des sciences naturelles de Neuchâtel
letters.sender: Société des sciences naturelles de Neuchâtel
letters.summary: CD named corresponding member of the Society.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   15 and 22 May [1863]
letters.summary:
The Lyell–Falconer squabble.

Discusses island vs continental floras and their degree of modification.

Critical of Wallace.

CD’s observations on phyllotaxy.

letters.title: From W. D. Fox   [16–22 May 1863]
letters.summary: A "quiz" on CD has appeared in theIllustrated Times[2 May 1863, p. 317].

letters.title: From Isaac Anderson-Henry   16 May 1863
letters.summary:
Sends sprig ofLinum luteum corymbiflorum[?]. CD is right about its being dimorphic.

Will try some odd strawberry crosses this summer.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   17 and 20 May [1863]
letters.summary: Alarmed that CD did not see what WED saw inCorydalis lutea. Has found buckbean in the New Forest. Will get seeds ofCorydalis claviculata.

letters.title: From Lydia Ernestine Becker   18 May 1863
letters.summary: Sends flowers of a variety ofLychnis dioicawhich has bisexual flowers.

letters.title: From Armand de Quatrefages   19 May [1863]
letters.deprecated: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.sender: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.summary:
Spoke on Moulin-Quignon Jaw before Académie des Sciences.

Thanks CD for photograph [of Niata skull].

Controversy on species fixity [at Société d’Anthropologie].

Sends photographs of Mouin-Quignon Jaw.

letters.title: From L. E. Becker   21 May [1863]
letters.summary: Has forwarded a box ofLychnisplants to CD; gives her observations on the variations in stamen length.

letters.title: From George Bentham   21 May 1863
letters.summary:
Returns CD’s pamphlets.

Wishes CD would work out further what keeps certain species immutable for great periods.

Feels himself a convert, but cannot go all lengths with CD.

Feels some reviewers distort CD’s argument.

letters.title: From John Scott   21 May [1863]
letters.summary:
Supports, in his orchid paper, CD’s view that sterility occurs at random [Trans. Bot. Soc. Edinburgh7 (1863): 543–50].

Cannot get hisDroserapaper published [abstract inEdinburgh New Philos. J.2d ser. 17 (1863): 317–18].

letters.title: To George Bentham   22 May [1863]
letters.summary: Natural selection implies that a form remains unaltered unless an alteration is to its benefit. This is not inconsistent with some forms remaining stable for long periods. Natural selection must at present be grounded entirely on general considerations. Of details we are still greatly ignorant.

letters.title: From John Scott   22 May 1863
letters.summary:
J. H. Balfour has arranged a position for him at aCinchonanursery. Reluctant to take this position in part because of his experiments for CD.

Asks CD’s advice and solicits his aid in finding a better colonial position. James McNab mistreats him.

letters.title: From L. E. Becker   23–4 May [1863]
letters.summary: Gives the results of her observations onLychnis; lists four different types of flower present and their occurrence.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [23–7 May 1863]
letters.summary: Encloses his notions [missing] on John Scott’s offer; some points in explanation.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   23 May [1863]
letters.summary:
Health has been poor but eczema is improved.

A "squib" about Owen and Huxley on the brain has appeared inPublic Opinion[3 (1863): 497–8].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   23 May [1863]
letters.summary: Seeks advice for John Scott on job offer in India.

letters.title: To John Scott   23 May [1863]
letters.summary: Has written to Hooker for his advice about the Darjeeling position. JS should not refuse the position on account of his experiments.

letters.title: To Roland Trimen   23 May [1863]
letters.summary:
CD has drawn up a paper from RT’s orchid notes on the fertilisation ofDisa grandiflorafor the Linnean Society [J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)7 (1863): 144–7].

CD would welcome seeds of any CapeOxalisfor his investigation of dimorphism.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [24 May 1863]
letters.summary:
Flora of Cameroons shakes JDH’s faith in ability to explain past or present migrations. Sees need for a major novel explanation such as natural selection, glacial cold, or continental connections.

Lyell in a bad way about feud with Falconer.

JDH’s opinion of Wallace, Bates, J. E. Gray, Owen, Asa Gray, Lubbock, and Bentham.

Bentham’s Linnean Society address [see4118].

letters.title: To Hermann Crüger   25 May [1863]
letters.summary:
Thanks for news about fertilisation of Melastomataceae.

Discusses fertilisation of orchids.

Mentions observations by John Scott.

Asks about "bud-variations".

letters.title: To W. H. Flower   25 May [1863]
letters.summary: Sends cheque to pay for photographs.

letters.title: To John Scott   25 and 28 May [1863]
letters.summary:
CD does not think he could be wrong about the stigma ofBolbophyllum.

Will not write upDroserafor years.

Praises JS’s experiments. Invites him to send a paper to Linnean Society.

L. C. Treviranus says all species ofPrimulapresent two forms exceptP. longiflora.

letters.title: To Lydia Ernestine Becker   [26 or 27 May 1863]
letters.summary: Thinks the dark purple anthers are a mass of a Cryptogamic plant, allied to the smut of Wheat. There remains a case of a reversion from a diœcious to a hermaphrodite condition.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   26 May 1863
letters.summary:
Discusses recent correspondence in theAthenæum: the disagreement between Lyell and Hugh Falconer and Owen’s remarks on heterogeny [see4110].

Briefly discusses orchids and some problems in phyllotaxy.

Mentions the political situation and the quarrelsome behaviour of the English.

letters.title: From John Scott   26 May [1863]
letters.summary:
Discusses Darjeeling position. Thanks CD for advice.

Will send orchid paper [see4087].

letters.title: From John Thomas Austen   27 May 1863
letters.summary: Has written to G. Dennen to ask him for an explanation regarding his behaviour in a financial transaction involving the savings bank of which JTA and CD are trustees.

letters.title: From L. E. Becker   28 May [1863]
letters.summary:
Thanks for CD’s paper [not named].

Inquires whetherLychnis, as an hermaphrodite, is more susceptible to fungus, disease, other weaknesses.

letters.title: From John Scott   28 May [1863]
letters.summary:
Sends abstract fromEdinburgh Courantof his orchid sterility paper [see4087]. Balfour altered title to obscure its theoretical nature.

Sends specimens showing curious variation.

letters.title: From J. T. Austen   29 May 1863
letters.summary: Has not yet received any reply from Dennen.

letters.title: From W. D. Fox   29 May [1863]
letters.summary: Recommends that CD visit Dr MacLeod’s [hydropathic] establishment near Ilkley.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   29 May [1863]
letters.summary:
CD’s encouragement of John Scott, who has found a case of self-incompatibility in orchids, like William Herbert’s inCrinum.

Nägeli on phyllotaxy.

CD’s observations on broom fertilisation.

letters.title: From J. T. Austen   30 May 1863
letters.summary: Sends letter from G. Dennen. GD improperly proposed to a depositor, Percival, to lend his savings at 10% to Dennen’s brother; asks CD whether matter should be brought before bank trustees.

letters.title: From Philip Henry Gosse   30 May 1863
letters.summary: Asks CD’s help with problem that arose when he tried to impregnate an orchid following CD’s text inOrchids.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   31 May [1863]
letters.summary:
AG’s review of Alphonse de Candolle’s paper [Am. J. Sci.2d ser. 35 (1863): 430–44] is excellent.

Does not AG consider that orchids oppose Oswald Heer’s view that species arise suddenly by monstrosities?

Infers that AG cannot explain the angles of phyllotaxy; has been looking at Carl Nägeli on the subject.

Reports Gaston de Saporta’s belief that natural selection will ultimately triumph in France.

Is working slowly atVariation.

Reports his observations on the imperfect flowers ofViolaandOxalis.

letters.title: To John Scott   31 May [1863]
letters.summary: Thanks JS for abstract of orchid sterility paper fromEdinburgh Courant. His case of individual sterility will be of highest use to CD. Criticises JS’s writing. Points out weaknesses in the organisation of his argument and the use of inflated, imprecise language.

letters.title: To P. H. Gosse   2 June [1863]
letters.summary:
Can only conjecture that the problem occurs because the plant is not living in its natural conditions. Refers to what he said onAcropera[inOrchids]. Many plants under culture have sexual functions altered.

Asks PHG to look at beeOphrysat Torquay to see if pollinia are ever removed. "It is my greatest puzzle."

letters.title: From J. T. Austen   3 June 1863
letters.summary: Does not think Dennen’s transaction was dishonest, but can see no satisfactory explanation for it; feels they must inform their fellow trustees.

letters.title: From John Scott   [3 June 1863]
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for influence used with Hooker to obtain a colonial position. Has offended J. H. Balfour by refusing the Darjeeling post and James McNab has become unfriendly, although his experiments do not detract from his garden work.

Will writePrimulapaper for Linnean Society as CD suggests.

His Darwinism is unpalatable at Edinburgh Botanic Garden.

Describes results with non-dimorphicPrimulaspecies. Such cases do not accord with CD’s view that characters are slowly acquired.

Thanks for criticism of his writing style.

letters.title: From P. H. Gosse   4 June 1863
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his full reply. Sends additional facts derived from further observation, and a possible solution.

letters.title: To P. H. Gosse   5 June [1863]
letters.summary: PHG’s hypothesis [regarding the self-fertilising mechanism ofStanhopea] may prove quite true, but CD suggests that PHG should observe another spike to make sure. CD will observe hisStanhopeaif it flowers.

letters.title: From S. P. Woodward   5 June 1863
letters.summary:
Has been writing a notice of H. W. Bates’s "capital book" [Naturalist on the river Amazons(1863)].

P. M. Duncan’s coral paper [J. Geol. Soc. Lond.29 (1863): 406–58] strengthens SPW’s belief in the general diffusion of marine forms westward in the course of time.

letters.title: To Arthur Rawson   6 June [1863]
letters.summary: CD thanks the sender of aCypripedium. He finds its pollination contrivances interesting.

letters.title: To John Scott   6 June [1863]
letters.summary:
CD has spoken to Hooker of JS’s scientific merit, but has not suggested him for a colonial appointment.

Advice on style of writing.

Making extensive extract of JS’s orchid paper to communicate to Linnean Society [J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)8 (1865): 162–7].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   8 [June 1863]
letters.summary:
Sends Asa Gray letter to JDH. Gray’s "Coolness about England and U. S. beats anything".

John Scott’s difficulties at Edinburgh Botanic Garden.

JS’s paper onPrimulacrossing experiments.

Sends MS note about closing of stigma in orchids being dependent on affinity of pollen and independent of protusion of pollen-tubes.

letters.title: From G. H. K. Thwaites   8 June 1863
letters.summary:
Dimorphism inLinum.

Situation in some of the lower Algae is analogous to that in phaenogams. In some, conjugation occurs between separate filaments, in others between cells of same filament.

Forwards a letter from S. O. Glenie enclosing specimens ofCassia fistulawhich show the two forms of the anthers.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [9–15 June 1863]
letters.summary:
Discusses some angles [relating to phyllotaxy].

The forthcoming school holidays.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   [10–16] June [1863]
letters.summary:
Possible dimorphism inPhlox.

Knows of no U. S. law prohibiting marriage of cousins.

Gives references to papers on phyllotaxy.

letters.title: From Booth Bacon   10 June 1863
letters.summary: On CD’s application to pay up at once his shares in the Penarth Harbour Dock and Railway; directors’ policy is to receive payment on only 50% of shares allotted.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   10 June 1863
letters.summary: JDH lays hard treatment of John Scott to J. H. Balfour’s anti-Darwinism.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [after 10 June 1863]
letters.summary: Notes on drops of nectar on sepals of cypripedium.

letters.title: To John Scott   11 June [1863]
letters.summary:
Hooker is impressed by JS’s MS on closing of stigma.

He will help find him a position. Hooker says if it is known that JS agrees with CD’s views, he will be unpopular in Edinburgh.

letters.title: From John Scott   16 June [1863]
letters.summary:
Orchid paper in press.

Asks CD to correct MS of hisPrimulapaper [J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)8 (1865): 78–126].

letters.title: From J. T. Austen   17 June 1863
letters.summary: Gives G. Dennen’s explanation of why he attempted to lend Percival’s savings at 10%: to assist his brother then repaying a loan made at 10%. Meeting [of trustees] to be called soon.

letters.title: From James Anderson   18 June 1863
letters.summary: Sends a capsule ofDendrobium cretaceum. [SeeOrchids, 2d ed.]

letters.title: To George Bentham   19 June [1863]
letters.summary: GB’s address [Proc. Linn. Soc. Lond.(1863): xi–xxix] pleased him as much as Lyell’s book [Antiquity of man] disappointed him on species question. GB has done a "real good turn to theright side".

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   19 June 1863
letters.summary:
Has heard from Julius von Haast that some of his letters were lost before leaving New Zealand. Haast’s enclosure for CD has been forwarded.

Haast and James Hector have both sent accounts of their travels in New Zealand.

letters.title: To John Scott   20 [June 1863]
letters.summary:
Glad to hear of JS’s orchid paper [Trans. Bot. Soc. Edinburgh7 (1863): 543–50].

Suggests experiments on peloria.

Wants to count seed of the self-fertile red cowslip with equal stamens and styles.

Can send account ofHottonia.

letters.title: To Charles Thomas Whitley   20 June [1863]
letters.summary: Recalls the long walks in Cambridge with the "expectant senior wrangler". Cannot accept invitation (related to meetings of the BAAS) because of continuing bad health, his own and that of his children.

letters.title: From William Allport Leighton   [before 21 June 1863]
letters.summary:
His observations of varieties of Verbascum.

Reference to Abbé Correa in theLife of Sir J. E. Smith.

letters.title: From Jacques Boucher de Perthes   23 June 1863
letters.deprecated: Jacques Boucher de Crèvecoeur de Perthes (Jacques Boucher de Perthes)
letters.sender: Jacques Boucher de Crèvecoeur de Perthes (Jacques Boucher de Perthes)
letters.summary: Sends his tranformist book [De la création: essai sur l’origine et la progression des êtres, 5 vols. (1838–41)]; his admiration for CD’s work.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   23 [June 1863]
letters.summary: Herbert Spencer’s work disappointing – "all words & generalities".

letters.title: To Charles Loring Brace   24 June [1863]
letters.summary: Discussion of, and thanks for, CLB’s new work,Races of the Old World[1863]. Special interest in p. 388 on colour and constitution; CD mentions questions sent previous year to surgeons serving in tropical countries regarding diseases and colour of hair and skin.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   25 [June 1863]
letters.summary: CD describes first observation of gyratory motion of tendrils: explains its adaptive function is to find objects to hold on to.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   26 June [1863]
letters.summary:
Thanks AG for references about phyllotaxy

and information on marriage laws.

Has been looking for dimorphism inPhloxandEuonymus.

Has observed the irritability of tendrils ofEchinocystiswith great interest. Was also struck by the rotating movements of the leading shoots, which he proposes to investigate.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   27 June [1863?]
letters.summary: Spoke to Rosas, and gave him CD’s paper.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   27 June [1863]
letters.summary:
Has caught a frog and examined its possibly rudimentary toe. Asks THH if he will dissect it.

Has heard THH is abused inEdinburgh Reviewand inAnthropological Review[reviews ofMan’s place in nature,Edinburgh Rev.117 (1863): 541–69 andAnthrop. Rev.1 (1863): 107–17].

Owen on heterogeny and the aye-aye.

Has been very ill.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [28 June 1863?]
letters.summary: Sends description of Chrysosplene, asks about glands.

letters.title: From W. B. Tegetmeier   29 June – 7 July 1863
letters.summary:
Progress of pigeon and poultry breeding experiments. No loss of fertility observed yet.

Blue-eyed cats and deafness.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker [2]9 June 1863
letters.summary:
JDH and Oliver impressed with CD’s observations on gyratory motion of plants.

CD pleased with Bentham’s Linnean Society address on the reception of Darwinism [J. Proc. Linn. Soc. Lond.7 (1863): xi–xxix].

JDH’s social "dogma": "Brains x Beauty = Breeding + wealth".

[Dated 9 June by JDH.]

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   1 July [1863]
letters.summary: Describes experiments on rotation of tendrils and shoots.

letters.title: ToGardeners’ Chronicle   2 July [1863]
letters.summary: Asks M. J. Berkeley to identify the microscopical spherical bodies CD found in drops of yellowish rain-water that fell on his garden in a brief shower.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   2 July 1863
letters.summary:
Too busy to examine specimen. Will ask W. H. Flower to do it. Long catalogue of what keeps him busy and concerned.

C. Carter Blake, "a jackal of Owen’s", is the reviewer inEdinburgh ReviewandAnthropological Review[see4223]. Has sent back his diploma of Hon. Fellowship to Anthropological Society.

letters.title: To John Scott   2 July [1863]
letters.summary:
CD’s great interest in JS’s work on fertility ofPrimulacrosses.

Thanks forPassifloratrials.

"By no means modify even in slightest degree any result."

CD wishes he had counted rather than weighedPrimulaseeds.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   3 July [1863]
letters.summary: Will be obliged if Flower examines specimens. States questions he wants answered.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   7 July 1863
letters.summary:
Has extracted CD’sLinumpaper [Am. J. Sci.2d ser. 36 (1863): 279–84].

Elaborate co-adaptations of orchids and insects demonstrate against "chance blows", whether few, as Oswald Heer would have, or many and slight as CD proposes.

letters.title: From L. E. Becker   8 July [1863]
letters.summary:
Sends seeds of femaleLychnis diurna; has found none in hermaphrodites.

On variation, hybridity, and inheritance of parasites in this plant.

letters.title: From George Sigerson   8 July 1863
letters.summary: Discusses leaf form and phyllotaxy; clarifies a part of his paper ["On a protomorphic phyllotype",Atlantis(1863)].

letters.title: To William Forsell Kirby   9 July [1863]
letters.summary: CD is particularly struck by WFK’s observations on Corsican and N. American subspecies in his paper ["On the geographical distribution of European Rhopalocera",Trans. R. Entomol. Soc. Lond.3d ser. 1 (1862–3): [!?bib has 1862–4] 481–92]. Thinks it would be interesting for WFK to examine specimens from the Shetland Islands, for even faint trace of differentiation.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   9 July [1863]
letters.summary:
WBT progressing with breeding experiments for CD.

CD making quicker progress withVariation.

letters.title: To W. H. Flower   11 July [1863]
letters.summary: Discusses rudimentary sixth toe of frogs.

letters.title: From P. H. Gosse   13 July 1863
letters.summary: On CD’s request to observe beeOphrys: PHG’s son collected 16 plants – of the 32 flowers, two had lost both pollinia, two had lost one each. He himself found two plants with pollinia adhering to the stigma.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   14 July [1863]
letters.summary: Requests tendril-bearing plants.

letters.title: From Friedrich Hildebrand   16 July 1863
letters.summary: He and L. C. Treviranus have repeated many of CD’s orchid observations with the same results. Sends his paper ["Fruchtbildung der Orchideen",Bot. Ztg.21 (1863): 329–33, 337–45].

letters.title: From Roland Trimen   16, 17, and 19 July 1863
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for two letters and his portrait.

CD’s book [Orchids] opened upterra incognitafor him.

His work on S. African butterflies continues.

Reports on a moth that punctures peach skins.

Interesting that thoughtful naturalists are forced to admit mutability of species.

Some notes onOxalis.

letters.title: To Julius von Haast   18 July [1863]
letters.summary:
Acknowledges receipt of JvH’s letters and report of his expedition. Congratulates him on its success.

Has sentOrigin.

There is hardly a place in the world as interesting as New Zealand with respect to geographical distribution.

Will quote the case of the ducks that nest in trees.

Is working hard onVariation.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   18 July [1863]
letters.summary: Sends F. Hildebrand’s paper for publication by the Linnean Society or inNatural History Review.

letters.title: To J. J. Aubertin   19 July 1863
letters.summary:
Discusses geology of Brazil.

Asks for Brazilian stamps for his son.

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   20 July 1863
letters.summary: Hildebrand’s paper is unsuitable for theNatural History Review.

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   [after 20 July 1863]
letters.summary: Gives a reference to a paper.

letters.title: From Henry Farncombe Billinghurst   [21 July 1863 – August 1870?]
letters.summary: Acknowledges the receipt of some signed transfers.

letters.title: From Julius von Haast   21 July [– 7? August] 1863
letters.summary:
In a forthcoming paper JvH will show geological age of the world to be "incalculable" and will confirm CD’s theory that "the old system of chronological sequence of formationsall over the worldmust be abandoned in a great degree".

Predicts the links between species, genera, and classes will be found.

CD elected an Honorary Member [of Philosophical Institute of Canterbury].

letters.title: From Asa Gray   21 July 1863
letters.summary:
Gives some observations onDrosera.

Comments on Richard Owen’s "transmutation theory" in his aye-aye paper [Trans. Zool. Soc. Lond.5 (1866): 33–101].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [21 July 1863]
letters.summary: Encourages CD to continue observations on tendrils.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   22 July [1863]
letters.summary:
Differences between tendrils derived from leaves and those derived from branches.

CD on Asa Gray’s attitude on the Civil War.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   23 July [1863]
letters.summary: Could not find Anchusa but will go out and find some.

letters.title: From John Scott   23 July [1863]
letters.summary:
Discusses heterostyly inHottonia.

Criticises L. C. Treviranus’ statements onPrimula longiflora’s having short-styled form.

Describes his results with crossing different coloured primroses. Will let CD, when he reads his paper, decide whether his finding white and red varieties perfectly sterile when crossed, yet fertileinter se, ought to be published.

Difficulty in getting his orchid paper published inEdinburgh New Philosophical Journal.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [25 July 1863]
letters.summary:
Relates events at Down;

asks WED to make some observations onLythrum.

His present hobby-horse is tendrils.

letters.title: To John Scott   25 [July 1863]
letters.summary:
Encourages JS to continue work on coloured primrose. No one has noticed this since Gärtner. CD will send his own data for JS’s use and will read MS when ready. Advises JS to repeat experiments if evidence is weak – for his reputation’s sake and for satisfaction at fully establishing a fact.

Treviranus made a slip of pen in writing ofPrimula longifloraas short-styled.

letters.title: From John Scott   [26 July – 2 August 1863]
letters.summary:
His orchid paper limited because he does not give illustrations from distinct genera.

Discusses the self- and cross-fertility of coloured primrose varieties. Thanks CD for tables of unpublishedPrimulawork.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   26 [July 1863]
letters.summary:
Asa Gray writes as if Civil War were a holy war.

J. E. Renan on Jesus [Vie de Jésus(1863)].

Literature on tendrils ofCucurbitais contradictory.

letters.title: To Friedrich Hildebrand   28 July [1863]
letters.summary: Comments on FH’s paper ["Fruchtbildung der Orchideen",Bot. Ztg.21 (1863): 329–33, 337–45].Annals and Magazine of Natural Historywill publish it in September [3d ser. 12 (1863): 169–74].

letters.title: From Robert Swinhoe   29 July 1863
letters.summary: Describes the similarity in plumage changes between Japanese and Chinese birds on the one hand and British and continental birds on the other. Suggests the changes are due to the warm gulf streams around both islands.

letters.title: To G. H. K. Thwaites   29 July [1863]
letters.summary:
Thanks GHKT forLimnanthemumseed.

Comments on his view of algal reproduction.

Discusses flower ofCassia.

Sends photograph of himself.

letters.title: From L. E. Becker   31 July [1863]
letters.summary: Has found seeds produced by an hermaphroditicLychnisand will send them. On structural obstacles to fertilisation of hermaphroditeLychnis.

letters.title: From Edward Bradford   31 July 1863
letters.summary: Doubts CD’s view inOrchids[pp. 236–46] thatCatasetum tridentatumis exclusively male and has as its female form the genusMonachanthus. EB has grown many of this type in Trinidad; has never seen that female form.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [31 July 1863]
letters.summary:
Sends "tendrilliferous" plants.

Plans visit to Down.

Naudin’s paper on tendrils [Ann. Sci. Nat. (Bot.)4th ser. 9 (1863): 180–203].

T. V. Wollaston snubs Bates’s work.

letters.title: From Henrietta Emma Darwin    [1 August 1863]
letters.summary: A memorandum describing the expressive behaviour of a cat with added notes by CD.

letters.title: To John Scott   1 and 3 August [1863]
letters.summary:
Thanks JS for orchid paper [Trans. Bot. Soc. Edinburgh7 (1863): 543–50]. JS presents excellent new facts on sterility of orchids.

His argument that coloured primroses are not hybrids is good, as is idea of discovering primrose parentage by breeding for colours.

letters.title: To L. E. Becker   2 August [1863]
letters.summary:
Thanks LEB for theLychnisseed [see4258], which he will plant in the hope of fertilising the little ovaria.

Comments on the two forms ofLinum.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   3 August [1863]
letters.summary:
Tendril plants received.

Has just completed large crossing experiment withLythrum.

letters.title: To Alphonse de Candolle   4 August [1863]
letters.summary: Asks AdeC to observe two species ofLythrumto see whether they are dimorphic as stated by Vaucher. CD can find no trace of this in dried specimens he has examined; "if either species present any difference in length of pistil and stamens, it is most likely that three forms should be presented".

letters.title: To Asa Gray   4 August [1863]
letters.summary:
Anticipated AG’s attitude on design in orchids. Does he not think that the variations that gave rise to fancy pigeon varieties were accidental?

Has been working hard atLythrum

and spontaneous movements of tendrils.

DefendsDroseraas a "sagacious animal" but does not know whether he will ever publish on it.

Comments on political situation in U. S.

letters.title: From Julius von Haast   6 August 1863
letters.summary: Sends a map of the province of Canterbury, marking his own and other explorations.

letters.title: From Hermann Crüger   8 August 1863
letters.summary:
Thanks for presentation copy ofLinumpaper [Collected papers2: 93–105].

Ficusexperiments confirm CD’s supposition that insects visitMelastomafor nectar, but HC thinks pollen-seekers fertilise the flowers.

Marantafertilisation.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   12–13 August [1863]
letters.summary:
Doubts Decaisne’s report of larkspur self-fertilisation.

Enthusiastically observes climbing plants. Needs to know how novel his observations are. Finds R. J. H. Dutrochet has made similar observations, so he has wasted some time. [SeeClimbing plants, p. 1 n.]

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   14 August [1863]
letters.summary:
Congratulates CL on finding Arctic shells.

Comments on paper by E. B. Hunt ["On the origin, growth, substructure and chronology of the Florida reef",Am. J. Sci.2d ser. 35 (1863): 197–210].

Mentions J. D. Dana’s health.

George Bentham’s statement on species [Proc. Linn. Soc. Lond.(1863): xi–xxix].

Praises Bates’s book [Naturalist on the river Amazons(1863)].

letters.title: From Robert Swinhoe   14 August 1863
letters.summary:
Sends two interesting cases: a flamingo with barnacles covering its legs

and castrated wild asses of Kutch.

letters.title: ToGardeners’ Chronicle   [before 15 August 1863]
letters.summary: Reports on the appearance, in a gravel walk near his house, of an orchid,Epipactis latifolia, never seen in his neighbourhood before. Asks whether a seed could have been blown from a distance and germinated during a season when the walk was neglected.

letters.title: To Thomas Rivers   17 August [1863]
letters.summary:
The almond-tree TR gave him produced no fruit, but the Chinese double peach has three. Asks for ripe almond fruits and anyoddpeaches, to compare the stones.

Asks about modification in fruit or foliage in any fruit-trees from being grafted,

and about seedlings of pears and wheat said to have been found in hedges and woods.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   21 August [1863]
letters.summary: Has signed and forwarded some orders.

letters.title: From John Goodsir   21 August [1863]
letters.summary: Agrees to examine a slide preparation of fluid [from CD’s vomit] to determine presence ofSarcinaas a possible cause of his stomach ailment. Sends some authoritative references on it. Warns CD thatSarcinahas been found in healthy stomachs.

letters.title: From Hugh Falconer   24 August [1863]
letters.summary:
Sends information about Pliocene fauna of the "Forest Bed" of the Norfolk coast.

A genus described as extinct by Owen is found by E. A. I. H. Lartet to exist in Russia.

Edouard Suess attributes to Oswald Heer and HF the generalisation "That the time during which a new species is formed, is (as a rule) very short in comparison with the time during which it persistently presents the same peculiar specific characters". [Edouard Suess, "Über die Verschiedenheit und die Aufeinanderfolge der tertiären Landfaunen in der Niederung von Wien",Sitzungsberichte der Kaiserlichen Akademie der Wissenschaften in Wien(Math-naturw. Klasse) 47 (1863): 306–31.] [See4277.]

letters.title: To Hugh Falconer   [25–6 August 1863]
letters.summary:
Thanks for information about Pliocene mammal. Interested in relating process of formation to duration of the species. Oswald Heer’s view that species suddenly formed surely false.

Bad summer with much sickness. Going to Malvern [for water-cure] for a month.

Muddled over phyllotaxy and made out nothing.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   25 [August 1863]
letters.summary:
CD’s illness: he is vomiting "vegetable" cells.

Dutrochet has published the best of CD’s observations on tendrils [seeClimbing plants, p. 1 n.].

Lyell has found Joshua Trimmer’s Arctic shells on Moel Tryfan.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   26 August 1863
letters.summary:
JDH working on the New Zealand flora.

Jules Planchon excited about CD’sLinumexperiments.

T. F. Jamieson’s paper on glaciers gives great pleasure.

letters.title: From George Busk   [c.27 August 1863]
letters.summary: Discusses and suggests treatments for CD’s stomach complaint. Recommends he consult William Brinton.

letters.title: From John Goodsir   27 August [1863]
letters.summary: Has found noSarcinaon the slides of fluid [see4272] and nothing referable to the food. Will repeat examination if vomiting recurs.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [27 August 1863]
letters.summary: Suggests CD consult George Busk about his stomach.

letters.title: To Roland Trimen   27 August [1863]
letters.summary:
Discusses methods of pollination in orchids.

Thinks RT should investigatePhysianthusto see if it requires insect aid for fertilisation as the Asclepiadaceae do.

letters.title: To [Gardeners’ Chronicle]   [after 27 August 1863]
letters.summary: [Roland] Trimen of the Cape of Good Hope sends evidence that a moth [Achaea chamaeleon] is capable of perforating the skin of a peach with its delicate proboscis. Have any readers observed moths or butterflies sucking any fruit of which the skin was not previously broken?

letters.title: From John Goodsir   28 August [1863]
letters.summary: The phial of fluid sent by CD is acid. Sends his microscopical examination.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [28 August 1863]
letters.summary:
Admits, at last, that New Zealand must have been connected to some continent, but not Australia.

Climbing plants: asks for more plants.

letters.title: ToGardeners’ Chronicle[before 29 Aug 1863]
letters.summary: On the cruelty of setting steel traps to catch vermin. Requests suggestions for putting an end to the practice. [This item is mentioned inCorrespondence11: 781 n.6. (Appendix IX)]

letters.title: From Hugh Falconer   29 August 1863
letters.summary: HF will send E. Suess’s paper [Edouard Suess, "Über die Verschiedenheit und die Aufeinanderfolge der tertiären Landfaunen in der Niederung von Wien",Sitzungsberichte der Kaiserlichen Akademie der Wissenschaften in Wien(Math–nat. Klasse) 47 (1863): 306–31] which deals directly with natural selection.

letters.title: From John Brodie Innes   29 August [1863]
letters.summary:
Duke of Argyll has been dubbed "Duke Darwinii" by papers.

Large number of toads have been found in railway cuttings; wishes a scientific observer had taken pains to explain where they came from.

Comments on Scottish schools and on the morals of the adult poor.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   1 September 1863
letters.summary:
Sees difficulties in adhering to the concept of design in nature.

Is surprised at Hooker’s and Daniel Oliver’s ignorance regarding spontaneous movements of tendrils.

CD should continue his work on climbing plants, "it will be fruitful in your hands".

letters.title: To J. B. Innes   1 September [1863]
letters.summary:
Family and local news, and memories of old times.

CD’s youngest son, Horace, is too delicate to go to school.

CD has had a bad summer, is still ill, can do very little work – "Botany … is all that I am good for".

letters.title: From J. J. Aubertin   3 September 1863
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for his letter and geological report on the stones JJA sent.

Encloses postage stamps for CD’s son.

letters.title: To Hugh Falconer   4 [September 1863]
letters.summary:
Sends address.

Comments on BAAS meeting at Newcastle.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   4 [September 1863]
letters.summary:
His bad health has caused him to return to Malvern.

Emma cannot find the gravestone of their child, Anne. Asks WDF whether he can remember its location.

letters.title: From J. B. Innes   4 September [1863]
letters.summary:
Explains "Duke Darwinii" reference [in4283].

Family news.

Writes of Scottish immorality and pious talk.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   4 September 1863
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary:
Has returned from trip to Norway, Sweden, and Denmark.

Has been made President of the Ethnological Society.

letters.title: From Edward Levett Darwin   7 September 1863
letters.summary:
Glad to find they are cousins.

Sends his book [High Elms (pseud.),The game-preserver’s manual(1858)].

letters.title: From W. D. Fox   7 September [1863]
letters.summary: Gives directions to CD’s daughter’s [Anne’s] grave.

letters.title: To John Price   [8 September – 13 October 1863]
letters.summary:
Comments on JP’s work [Old Price’s remains(1863–4)].

Anglo-American relations. Progress of the Civil War.

letters.title: From W. F. Kirby   8 September [1863]
letters.summary: Describes some cases of geographical distribution of butterflies. Raises the perplexing question of the distribution ofPyrameis atalantain Europe andP. calliroein the Canaries.

letters.title: From Hugh Falconer   10 September 1863
letters.summary: Is having E. Suess’s essay [see4284] translated; will forward it as soon as it is done.

letters.title: From the secretary of the Philosophical Institute of Canterbury, New Zealand   14 September 1863
letters.summary: CD elected an honorary member of the Society.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   15 September 1863
letters.summary:
Pleased CD accepts continental extension for New Zealand, whose flora has many genera likeRubuswith great diversity and connecting intermediates. Suggests geological uplifting creates more space, hence opportunities for preservation of intermediates. Sees clash with CD on causes of extreme diversity of form in a group.

JDH’s attitude toward democratisation of science.

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   21 September 1863
letters.summary:
Sends some original observations on British ferns [not found].

Has secured a small pension and hopes to acquire a house near Kew.

letters.title: From John Scott   21 September [1863]
letters.summary:
SendsPrimulaMS, which CD has promised to communicate to Linnean Society [see4213].

Will soon send results on peloricAntirrhinum.

letters.title: From Joanna B. Horner   24 September 1863
letters.summary: News of C. J. F. Bunbury and the Lyells.

letters.title: From G. H. K. Thwaites   24 September 1863
letters.summary: Sends information on the flowers ofCassia roxburghii; will send flowers of all the species ofCassiafor CD to study with a view to discovering the law which operates to bring about the differences.

letters.title: From W. B. Tegetmeier   [c.26 September 1863]
letters.summary: Encloses a cutting from theField: C. R. Bree on zebra-striped asses.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   26 September 1863
letters.summary:
Encloses flowers ofMelastomafrom Singapore.

Acclimatisation of plants.

Striped horses in London.

Bees’ cells; has been promised information from the East.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [28 September 1863]
letters.summary: Grieves over the death of his second daughter [Maria Elizabeth].

letters.title: From Louis Agassiz   29 September 1863
letters.summary: Introduces J. P. Lesley, "the most accomplished geologist of the United States".

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   29 September 1863
letters.summary:
HWB’s concern over CD’s poor health.

Gives accounts of reviews of his book in theTimesand in theRevue des Deux-Mondesby E.-D. Forgues ["Un naturaliste sous l’équateur",Rev. Deux-Mondes46 (1863): 703–37].

Thanks CD for the A. Gray review of his paper [see4022].

Reports his current work is a monograph on Mantidae.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   [29? September 1863]
letters.summary:
Baffling problems withMelastoma. Appreciates ARW’s help with it and the "gorze case".

Has read report of ARW’s paper [to Newcastle BAAS meeting, "On the geographical distribution of animal life"] in theReader[2 (1863): 352–3].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   1 October 1863
letters.summary: Sorrow at loss of his daughter.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [4 October 1863]
letters.summary: Condolences on death of JDH’s daughter.

letters.title: From Roland Trimen   10, 13, and 18 October 1863
letters.summary:
Comments on CD’s paper onLinum[Collected papers2: 93–105].

Sends specimens of dimorphic and trimorphicOxalis.

Comments on H. W. Bates’s work [Naturalist on the river Amazons].

letters.title: From John Lubbock   14 October 1863
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Is working on a notice for theNatural History Review[n.s. 4 (1864): 37–43] of Huxley’s lectures to working men on the origin of species.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   23 October 1863
letters.summary: With scientific party to Amiens to look at gravel-pits, the geology of which JDH describes at length.

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   24 October 1863
letters.summary:
Returns Gray’s review [of paper on mimetic analogy,Am. J. Sci.2d ser. 36 (1863): 285–90]

and expresses his sorrow over CD’s health.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [30 October 1863]
letters.summary: Has a letter from Haast on the spreading of European plants.

letters.title: From Alfred Newton   31 October 1863
letters.summary: Tells CD where to pick up the partridge’s foot with the ball of earth attached; sends a copy of his remarks on the same. [SeeAnn. & Mag. Nat. Hist.3d ser. 13 (1864): 99–101.]

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [1 or 3 November 1863]
letters.summary:
Anxious to see Haast’s letter.

JDH’s views on Poles and Franco-Prussian conflict.

letters.title: To John Scott   7 November [1863]
letters.summary:
Has read JS’s paper [MS of "Observations on the functions and structure of the reproductive organs in the Primulaceae",J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)8 (1865): 78–126] which has interested him greatly. Will communicate it to the Linnean Society if JS carries out a few corrections.

Would like to hear about hisVerbascumandPassifloraexperiments.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   9 November [1863]
letters.summary:
Moncure Conway wants to call on CD.

EAD has seen the extract from Mill’s [System of]Logicwhich Carpenter read when arguing CD should have the Copley. Has CD seen it?

letters.title: From George Clendon Jr   10 November 1863
letters.summary: Suggests a possible explanation of the supposed paucity of intermediate forms in fossil formations.

letters.title: From Friedrich Hildebrand   10 November 1863
letters.summary:
Pleased CD has had his [FH’s] orchid paper published [Ann. & Mag. Nat. Hist.3d ser. 12 (1863): 169–74].

Extension of CD’sPrimulaheterostyly work.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   10 [November 1863]
letters.summary:
Pleased with JDH’s account of his French tour.

Doctor Brinton, recommended by Busk, does not believe CD’s brain or heart affected. Feels he is going steadily downhill. If so, hopes his life will be short.

Sends Haast’s letter.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [13 November 1863]
letters.summary:
Sends Haast’s report; JDH may use any and all of the details in the letter.

Asks identity of a reviewer of Lyell’sAntiquity of man[Edinburgh Rev.118 (1863): 254–302].

letters.title: To Hurst & Blackett   15 November [1863]
letters.summary: Offers letters to Eliza Meteyard for her book [The life of Josiah Wedgwood(1865–6)].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   16 [November 1863]
letters.summary: CD has a Wedgwood vase of his father’s for JDH.

letters.title: From Robert Monsey Rolfe   [20 November 1863]
letters.deprecated: Robert Monsey Rolfe, 1st Baron Cranworth of Cranworth
letters.sender: Robert Monsey Rolfe, 1st Baron Cranworth of Cranworth
letters.summary: Sends annual cheque for Down parish charities.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [22–3 November 1863]
letters.summary:
Tendril-bearing plants seem to CD "higher" organised with respect to adaptive sensibility than lower animals.

Wishes to encourage John Scott.

Death of JDH’s daughter makes CD cry over his own dead daughter Annie.

Sedgwick’s scientific merit.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   23 November 1863
letters.summary:
CD’s poor health.

Agassiz’s attempt to do away with Darwinism.

letters.title: To Roland Trimen   25 November [1863]
letters.summary:
CD’s doctor [J. M. Gully] has ordered him to do nothing for six months.

Thanks RT for orchid specimen.

Dares not look atOxalisflowers.

Regrets RT cannot get seed, especially from his trimorphic flowers.

Asks for bulbs of two or three forms.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   [before 27 November 1863]
letters.summary: Recommends Wyman’s short notice ["Report on Dr Jeffries Wyman’s experiment on the cause of contractility in vegetable tissues"] in theProceedings of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences3 (1852–7): 167.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   27 [November 1863]
letters.summary:
On Wedgwood vases for JDH.

Willy Hooker’s scarlet fever.

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   27 November 1863
letters.summary:
Discusses the contraction of hygroscopic bundles in seed-pods,

and a paper by Hugo von Mohl ["Über dimorphe Blüthen",Bot. Ztg.(1863): 309–15, 321–8] in which he discussesOxalisand determines thatFumariais a necessarily self-fertilising plant.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   28 [November 1863]
letters.summary: Fertile flowers of violets, exceptViola tricolor, require insect visits.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   5 [December 1863]
letters.summary:
His bad health continues.

Thirty-two plants have come up from the earth attached to partridge’s foot.

Originto be published in Italian.

Owen was wrong:Originwill not be forgotten in ten years.

letters.title: From J. B. Innes   17 December [1863]
letters.summary: Suggests a new school for CD’s son [Horace].

letters.title: To the Geological Society of London[c.28 December 1863]
letters.summary: Recommendation of the admission of George Maw to the fellowship of the Geological Society of London.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   30 December [1863] – 3 January [1864]
letters.summary:
Will be proud to receive EH’sDie Radiolarien[1862].

Health continues very weak.

[P.S. 3 Jan] Has sent EH another letter by mistake.

letters.title: From Hugh Falconer   31 December [1863]
letters.summary: Returns a letter wrongly addressed by CD [4361].

letters.title: From Erasmus Alvey Darwin   [1864?]
letters.summary: Asks CD to sign some "Sunday tickets" [for the Zoological Garden?].

letters.title: To John Lubbock   [1 January 1864]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: JL’s review of Huxley ["Lectures to working men",Nat. Hist. Rev.n.s. 4 (1864)].

letters.title: To Alfred Russel Wallace   1 January 1864
