letters.summary: Asa Gray’s high opinion of ARW as a reviewer [reference to S. Haughton’s paper on bees’ cells,Ann. & Mag. Nat. Hist.3d ser. 11 (1863): 415–29, reviewed by ARW in "Remarks on the Rev. S. Haughton’s paper",Ann. & Mag. Nat. Hist.3d ser. 12 (1863): 303–9].

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   2 January 1864
letters.summary:
Returns letter mailed by mistake [see4361].

Hopes CD will accept gift of hisRadiolarien[Die Radiolarien, 2 vols. (1862)].

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   2 January 1864
letters.summary:
Remarks on ARW’s review of Samuel Haughton’s paper on bees’ cells

andOrigin.

Agassiz’s strength as geologist and weakness in natural history theory.

Work problems.

His butterfly collection.

Problems with book on Malay journey.

Recommends Herbert Spencer and hisSocial statics.

Spencer’s "masterly" nebular hypothesis.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   5 January [1864]
letters.summary: Calls CD’s attention to an article by Paul Janet.

letters.title: From Charles Spence Bate   6 January 1864
letters.summary: Asks CD’s opinion on the accuracy of stating that barley and wheat are different varieties of the same species.

letters.title: From John Scott   7 January [1864]
letters.summary:
Has finished correctingPrimulapaper [see4332].

Has presented paper on monoecious spikes of maize [Edinburgh New Philos. J.2d ser. 19 (1864): 213–20].

letters.title: To John Scott   8 January [1864]
letters.summary:
Glad correspondent’s paper went well.

Poor health and much work forces CD to be brief.

letters.title: To Joseph Dalton Hooker   [10 and 12 January 1864]
letters.summary:
CD very ill.

Suspects F. Boott’s widow is illegitimate granddaughter of Erasmus Darwin.

CD, like JDH, has speculated that agrarian weeds have become adapted to cultivated ground. Suggests comparison with country of origin.

Wallace’s praise of Herbert Spencer’sSocial staticsbaffles CD.

[Letter completed by E. A. Darwin.]

letters.title: From John Lubbock   10 January 1864
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary:
JL’s article on Huxley’s "Lectures [to working men]".

Planning a volume of essays [Prehistoric times(1865)].

letters.title: From John Scott   [13 January 1864]
letters.summary:
Glad CD is sending hisPrimulapaper to Linnean Society.

Sends promisedLinumseeds.

letters.title: From Thomas Henry Huxley   16 January 1864
letters.summary: Asks CD to sign certificate nominating Flower for Royal Society.

letters.title: From Mary Boott   18 January 1864
letters.summary: On his deathbed her husband [Francis] expressed admiration for CD.

letters.title: From Robert Goodwin Mumbray   18 January 1864
letters.summary:
Has verified J. M. Bechstein’s contention that species of finches hybridise.

Quotes Thomas Bewick’s observations on hybrids between pheasants and common fowl. RGM had often noticed so-called "pheasant fowl", but thought it was a foreign bird.

letters.title: From Charles Parker   18 January 1864
letters.summary: Collecting subscriptions for a school at Ford.

letters.title: From Hermann Crüger   21 January 1864
letters.summary:
Sends his MS of orchid paper ["A few notes on the fecundation of orchids and their morphology",J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)8 (1865): 127–35] for CD to send to an editor.

CD was right aboutCatasetumsexes.

Ficusexperiments fail.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   24 January 1864
letters.summary:
JDH’s opinion of Herbert Spencer.

Rejects CD’s view of inheritance of induced modifications.

Huxley grows fat.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [25 January 1864]
letters.summary:
CD’s illness.

The difficulty of getting John Scott to publish his work. Has sent Scott’s paper [on Primulaceae] to Linnean Society. CD is sure it is valuable.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [27 January 1864]
letters.summary:
CD continues very ill.

His only work is a little on tendrils and climbers. Asks whether all tendrils are modified leaves or whether some are modified stems.

Last number [Jan 1864?] ofNatural History Reviewis best that has appeared.

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   [28 January – 8 February 1864]
letters.summary: Botanists are obliged to regard tendrils as either leaf- or stem-formations.Vitis,Passiflora, andClematisare discussed. [See4398.]

letters.title: To Charles William Crocker   31 January [1864]
letters.summary: Reminds CWC that he offered to give information with respect to his observations on hollyhocks. Wishes he could persuade CWC to undertake experiments on the fertility of some crosses between the most distinct varieties.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   1 February [1864]
letters.summary: Tells of a declaration and a subscription list to defend the rights of Bishop Colenso.

letters.title: From William Bernhard Tegetmeier   1 February 1864
letters.summary:
Would like his fowl skulls back.

Breeding experiments seem to show mongrels are just as fertile as pure breeds.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   2 February [1864]
letters.summary: Returns WBT’s box of skulls. One or two skulls may be elsewhere, but CD does not have the strength to search for them.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   5 February 1864
letters.summary:
John Scott’s paper [see4332] read at Linnean Society; praised by George Bentham.

Himalayan pine in Macedonia.

JDH is in a quarrel with H. C. Watson.

letters.title: To John Scott   6 February [1864]
letters.summary: JS’sPrimulapaper was read at the Linnean Society and praised warmly by G. Bentham. Hooker was not present.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [8 February 1864]
letters.summary:
ComparesClematisandTropaeolumwith respect to touch response.Tropaeolumshows a momentary response and quick recovery.Clematistakes hours to respond, and shows no recovery.

CD can show the gradations between leaves and tendrils, but how a branch passes into a tendril utterly puzzles him.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [before 9 February 1864]
letters.summary: Bentham proposes John Scott be made an associate of the Linnean Society.

letters.title: To John Scott   9 February [1864]
letters.summary: Bentham so impressed with JS’s paper that he is invited to become Associate Member of Linnean Society.

letters.title: From John Scott   12 [February 1864]
letters.summary:
Regrets sending his MS missing two pages.

Has proofs of his paper on the monoecious spikes of maize [Edinburgh New Philos. J.2d ser. 19 (1864): 213–20].

J. H. Balfour objected to notion of maize descent from a hermaphrodite.

Reading of JS’s paper onSelaginellahybrid [Edinburgh New Philos. J.2d ser. 19 (1864): 192–9] deferred until March. Believes it is first example of experimentally produced hybridity in higher cryptogams.

letters.title: From Andrew Murray   15 February 1864
letters.summary: A regular column is to appear in theProceedings of the Royal Horticultural Societyon successful and failed interspecific crosses.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   16 February 1864
letters.summary:
Is sending his monograph ["A revision and arrangement of the North American species ofAstragalusandOxytropis",Proc. Am. Acad. Arts & Sci.6 (1863): 188–236].

Death of Francis Boott.

U. S. is now determined to do away with slavery.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   16 February 1864
letters.summary:
CD’s climbing plant experiments make it impossible to deny nerve force in plants.

Has discussed Frankland’s new glacial theory with Lyell.

Bishop Colenso’s trial.

Possibility of Scott’s coming to Kew as a curator.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   17 February [1864]
letters.summary:
Sends Hermann Crüger’s paper ["A few notes on the fecundation of orchids and their morphology",J. Proc. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)8 (1865): 127–35] for publication.

"Boasts" of confirmation that sexes are separate inCatasetum.

letters.title: To Frederick Smith   [c.17 February 1864?]
letters.summary: Sends, for identification, specimens of bees and wasps which fertilise orchids. [Notes in FS’s hand on the same sheet identify the specimens.]

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   18 February 1864
letters.summary: Thinks the paper by H. Crüger should appear in theJournal of the Linnean Society.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [20–]22 February [1864]
letters.summary:
Does not know Scott’s qualifications to be curator at Kew.

Frankland’s theory of glaciers is absurd.

Has JDH heard claim that plants in Northern and Southern Hemispheres turn in opposite directions?

Are there plant families with no twining and climbing plants?

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [20 February 1864]
letters.summary:
Sends aCorydalis.

Hermann Crüger’s paper [see4394] splendid, but he has made a mess of propagatingCinchonain Trinidad.

JDH’s opinion of Germans.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   24 [February 1864]
letters.summary: Asks for aSmilaxto study movement.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   25 February [1864]
letters.summary:
Has not worked for six months due to illness.

Has been looking at climbing plants.

Hermann Crüger’s paper shows that CD was right aboutCatasetumpollination. Crüger’s account of pollination ofCoryanthes"beats everything".

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   3 March [1864]
letters.summary: Has received EH’sDie Radiolarien. Drawings admirably executed. Had no idea such low animals could develop such beautiful structures.

letters.title: From Frederick Ransome   7 March 1864
letters.summary: Acknowledges cancelled bond and thanks CD for declining to accept interest. Suggests 4 Mar 1865 as date for payment of the bill CD holds.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   9 March 1864
letters.summary: Thanks for paper ["Über die Entwicklungstheorie Darwins",Amtl. Ber. Versamml. Dtsch. Naturforsch. Aerzte38 (1863): 17–30]. Delighted EH confirms his views. Many in England afraid to express views openly.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   9 [March] 1864
letters.summary:
Reception of Scott’s paper.

Difficulty of writing Boott’s obituary.

Critical of Edward Frankland’s glacial theory.

Falconer’s and Ramsay’s views on Himalayan lakes lack support of basic evidence.

Taxonomic distribution of climbing plants.

Huxley picks quarrels with minor figures and thus magnifies them.

letters.title: From John Scott   10 March 1864
letters.summary: Has left his position at Edinburgh Botanic Garden.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   11 March [1864]
letters.summary:
Struck with corresponding positions of tendrils and flower-stalks inPassiflora. Sends [W. E. Darwin’s] dissection drawings of earliest stages. Infers that tendril is a modified flower peduncle.

Requests DO look at mode of climbing inTecoma.

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   12 March 1864
letters.summary:
Discusses homologies of plant organs.

The passion-flower tendril should be considered a modified branch rather than a modified flower. Considers the distinction between the peduncle and the leaf midrib.

letters.title: From William Erasmus Darwin   [15 March 1864]
letters.summary: Has drawn all three forms of primroses CD sent "with same result". Has found no pink variety with middle style.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   16 March 1864
letters.summary: List of four plants sent.

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   [17 March 1864]
letters.summary: Observations on climbing species ofTacoma. [Tecoma!?]

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   [after 2 January 1864]
letters.summary:
Has seen that ARW has read a paper to the Linnean Society.

Thinks that Herbert Spencer’sSocial Statics(Spencer 1851) would be too deep for him.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   18 March [1864]
letters.summary:
Thanks for information onTecoma.

Cannot believe DO’s statement aboutCatasetum; is sureC. tridentatumsets seeds in its native country.

CD erred onAcropera, but how is it naturally fertilised?

letters.title: From Bartholomew James Sulivan   18 March [1864]
letters.summary: Has six months’ leave from the Admiralty because of his health; intends going to Europe for four months.

letters.title: From John Scott   19 March 1864
letters.summary:
On fertilisation ofGongora.

His work on peloricAntirrhinum,Passiflora, andVerbascum, done at CD’s suggestion, is at CD’s disposal.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   22 March [1864]
letters.summary: Sends drawings of the pollen from ChinesePrimulaplants with styles and pistils of different lengths; observations on sizes and condition of their pollen.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   26[–7] March [1864]
letters.summary:
John Scott has left Edinburgh Botanic Garden.

Asks JDH to ask Tyndall whether Frankland exaggerates the effect of snowfall on advance of European glaciers.

Huxley and Falconer squabble too much in public.

letters.title: From John Scott   28 March 1864
letters.summary:
Surprised at CD’s account ofBryanthus.

H. Crüger’s approach toGongorafertilisation is beset with difficulties.

Reports his work on self-sterility ofOncidium.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   29 March 1864
letters.summary:
John Scott’s career.

Huxley’s vicious attack on anthropologists.

Critique of Joseph Prestwich’s theory of rivers.

Bitter feelings between the Hookers and the Veitch family of nurserymen.

letters.title: To Alfred Newton   29 March [1864]
letters.summary: Eighty-two plants have germinated from earth on wounded partridge’s foot.

letters.title: From Lydia Ernestine Becker   30 March 1864
letters.summary: Sends CD a copy of her book [Botany for novices(1864?)], intended to encourage the young, especially ladies, to study nature.

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   [before 31 March 1864]
letters.summary: Encloses memorandum on tendrils. Nature of tendrils inModecca.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   31 March [1864]
letters.summary:
Asks DO to give enclosed [letter?] from John Scott to Hooker.

JS’s work on orchid self-sterility;Acroperahas 371250 seeds in one capsule.

Wishes something could be done for Scott.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   [after 31 March 1864?]
letters.summary: Sends "2 pods ¼ gr each" to tide CD over.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [1 April 1864]
letters.summary: Proposes to support John Scott in research on relative fertility and self-incompatibility of plants. CD would pay him for a year or two but wants JDH to give him research facilities at Kew.

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   [1 April 1864]
letters.summary: References to and résumés of articles on climbing plants.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [2 April 1864]
letters.summary:
JDH explains why he cannot take Scott on at Kew.

John Tyndall cannot answer CD’s questions on glaciers. Edward Frankland’s ignorance. In JDH’s opinion, heaviness of winter snowfall is the greatest element in size of glaciers and this is a function of low mean temperature. Discusses descent of glaciers.

letters.title: From Alfred Newton   2 April 1864
letters.summary: Marvels that seeds from the lump of clay on the partridge’s foot have germinated. At Zoological Society [J. E.?] Gray ridiculed him. Now Frank Buckland would like to see the specimen.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [4 April 1864]
letters.summary: JDH has written to J. H. Balfour for a character reference for John Scott.

letters.title: From Robert Swinhoe   4 April 1864
letters.summary:
Reports on a strange breed of sheep at Aden,

a Brazilian plant naturalised in Ceylon,

the AustralianCasuarina equisetumspreading in Taiwan,

and an excrescence on wing of several thrushes of Taiwan similar to a growth on wing of a Syrian species.

letters.title: From Philip Henry Gosse   5 April 1864
letters.summary:
Asks how he can identify pollen-tubes.

Has succeeded in impregnating orchids of widely different genera with each other’s pollinia. "Is not this something new?"

Offers to exchangeCatasetumfor other varieties.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   5 April [1864]
letters.summary:
Sees difficulty of placing Scott at Kew. Suspects Balfour is prejudiced because Scott is a Darwinian.

CD’s former letter onClematis[4403] blundered; work now being revised.

letters.title: To George Howard Darwin   [after 5 April 1864?]
letters.summary: Enquires about the relationship of English grains to French milligrammes.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   6 April 1864
letters.summary:
J. H. Balfour gives Scott excellent character reference, but says he is unfit either to superintend or be subordinate.

Herbert Spencer’s review of J. M. Schleiden is interesting [see4457].

letters.title: To Alfred Newton   6 April [1864]
letters.summary: CD has thrown away injured partridge’s foot.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [after 6 April 1864?]
letters.summary: Calculates the relationship between grains and milligrams; asks his mother for a fruit tart and twelve napkins.

letters.title: To P. H. Gosse   7 April [1864]
letters.summary:
Discusses microscopic observation of pollen tubes.

Unable to exchange orchids because of his illness.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   7 April [1864]
letters.summary: CD apologises for having asked JDH to help him with Scott and now seeks advice on how to break the news.

letters.title: From Alfred Newton   7 April 1864
letters.summary: CD need not worry about having discarded the partridge’s foot.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   8 April 1864
letters.summary:
Men of Scott’s Celtic temperament are very troublesome. Tries to dissuade CD from hiring him as a scientific gardener.

George Rolleston, not Spencer, wrote review of Schleiden [Nat. Hist. Rev.(1864): 187–99].

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   9 April [1864]
letters.summary: Lyell thinks an expedition should be sent to the caves in Borneo, supported by the sale of surplus specimens; thinks "our progenitors" may well be there.

letters.title: To John Scott   9 April 1864
letters.summary:
Regrets that JS has left the [Edinburgh] Botanic Garden and that [J. D.] Hooker is not in a position to secure a foreign appointment for him. Offers financial assistance on the grounds of science.

Has sent JS a copy of theReader.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   11 April [1864]
letters.summary:
Thanks forLectures on the elements of comparative anatomy[1864].

If Owen wrote article on "Oken" [Encyclopaedia Britannica, 8th ed.] and French work on archetype he never did a baser act [seeML1: 246 n.].

Bad health lately.

letters.title: To Council of the Royal Horticultural Society   11 April 1864
letters.summary: The signatories warn the RHS that in offering prizes for collections of specimens of wild English plants, the Society will cause serious injury to varieties already threatened without any real promotion of scientific botany.

letters.title: To Louis Agassiz   12 April 1864
letters.summary:
Thanks LA forMethods of study[1863].

Is gratified that he has not taken a personal dislike to CD, though he is strongly opposed to nearly everything CD has written.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin, Charles Darwin, and W. E. Darwin to Thomas Salt 12 April 1864
letters.sender: William Erasmus DarwinErasmus Alvey DarwinCharles Robert Darwin
letters.summary: Instructions concerning the payment of the principal and interest of the mortgage to Mr Childe.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   13 April [1864]
letters.summary:
CD has told Scott not to hope for help from JDH.

Health improving.

Hopes to writeLythrumpaper soon.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   14 April [1864]
letters.summary: Observations on [length of style and length of filament and stigmas of]Pulmonaria.

letters.title: From John Scott   14 April [1864]
letters.summary: Thanks for CD’s consoling letter. His mind cannot concentrate after losing his position, and he feels "an inward dread of life’s future". Would have been glad to work for CD. Understands why Hooker cannot recommend him.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [after 14 April – 5 May 1864]
letters.summary: Describes difference betweenPulmonariaflowers; wishes to know whether it is general.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   [15? April 1864]
letters.summary:
Sir Henry Holland wants to see [Erasmus Darwin]Zoonomia.

Snow [F. J. Wedgwood] has gone, hoping to meet Fanny who is in a state of anxiety.

letters.title: To David J. Brown   18 April 1864
letters.summary: Discusses DJB’s MS concerning the origin of species.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   18 April 1864
letters.summary: CD is right about variability [ofPulmonaria]. Encloses observations and diagrams of additional plants.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   18 April 1864
letters.summary:
No doubt that Owen wrote "Oken" and the archetype book, which appeared in its second edition in French.

Pressures of work and family.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   19 [April 1864]
letters.summary:
Another plea to take Scott on at Kew. Emma begs CD not to employ him at Down.

Has just received a long article on theOriginfrom D. J. Brown, an Edinburgh baker [see4464].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   20 April 1864
letters.summary: Again refuses to help Scott as "unfitted" to make his way in the world. Scott is unwilling to take his part in the "struggle for life", unlike Tyndall, Faraday, Huxley, and Lindley, who established themselves. Scott’s work is not science, but "scientific horticulture".

letters.title: To [William Mackmurdo Hacon]   21 April [1864]
letters.summary: Writes about a land transaction.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   25 April [1864]
letters.summary:
CD thinks JDH takes a hard view of Scott’s character, but will not argue further.

Leersia.

Working on homomorphic and heteromorphic crosses inPrimula.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [26 or 27 April 1864]
letters.summary:
JDH on John Scott.

Curious about the rationale of pollen prepotence.

Working on variation in New Zealand flora.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [after 28 April 1864]
letters.summary: Forwards a letter from H. W. Bates to JDH announcing HWB’s appointment as Assistant Secretary of the Royal Geographical Society.

letters.title: From Benjamin Dann Walsh   29 April – 19 May 1864
letters.summary:
Recalls being introduced to CD when [undergraduate] at Cambridge.

Sends CD some of his pamphlets

and expresses support ofOrigin.

Has discovered there are "3 sexes" in the solitaryCynipsas well as social insects.

letters.title: From William Bennett   29 April 1864
letters.summary:
Will send grasses CD asked about.

Reports observations on brood of Australian chicks he is hatching.

letters.title: From[C. P.]   29 April 1864
letters.summary: On rereading theOrigin, he offers a criticism on two grounds: 1. Blending inheritance; 2. The tendency of species to elude competing species. Also competition within species eliminates the weak and thus preserves the species.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [30 April 1864]
letters.summary: [Outline sketches of pollen from long- and short-styled yellow cowslips and from red cowslip, magnified 350x.]

letters.title: To William Erasmus Darwin   [1 May 1864]
letters.summary: Writes of dimorphic plants.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   3 May [1864]
letters.summary: Thanks WED for measuring cowslip pollen. Sends dimorphic flowers.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   4 May [1864]
letters.summary:
Thanks for DO’sLessons in elementary botany[1864].

Asks him to inquire whether there are any twining species ofPassiflora.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   5 May [1864]
letters.summary: Experiment instructions.

letters.title: From William Darwin Fox   5 [May 1864]
letters.summary: Would like to come to Down to visit.

letters.title: From John Scott   5 May [1864]
letters.summary:
Encloses MS of his paper ["On individual sterility ofOncidium",J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)8 (1865): 162–7].

His next will be onPassiflora,Disemma, andTacsonia[J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)8 (1865): 197–206].

When he receives proofs of hisPrimulapaper he will add CD’s case about equal-styled cowslip.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   6 May 1864
letters.summary: Diagrams of short- and long-styledPulmonariaunder magnification.

letters.title: To Richard Kippist   6 May [1864]
letters.summary: Recommends paper by John Scott to be read at Linnean Society.

letters.title: To William Lonsdale   6 May [1864]
letters.summary:
Thanks WL for his MS on coral and suggests that it be sent to the Geological Society for printing or preserving in the archives.

Comments on his and WL’s bad health and recalls WL’s past kindness to him.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   7 May [1864]
letters.summary:
Henry Holland sends thanks forZoonomia.

Sir Henry would not expect podophyllin to be good for CD.

letters.title: From Henry Trimen   10 May 1864
letters.summary: Cannot give information about the box ofOxalisbulbs that his brother [Roland Trimen] has forwarded to CD.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   10 May 1864
letters.summary:
On the Borneo cave exploration.

ARW will send his contribution to theory of origin of man. The vast mental and cranial differences between man and apes, whereas structural differences in other parts of body are small. The problem of explaining diversity of human races along with the stability of man’s form during all historical epochs. Discussion with "Anthropologicals" [following reading of ARW’s paper, "The origin of human races", before the Anthropological Society, 1 Mar 1864].

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   12 May [1864]
letters.summary: Observations on style length of 150 flowers ofPulmonaria[angustifolia]. [SeeForms of flowers, p. 105.]

letters.title: To Roland Trimen   13 May 1864
letters.summary:
Oxalisplants have arrived safely [see4347].

CD regrets his mistake aboutDisa; will correct it.

Thanks RT for his additional facts aboutDisa.

Is recovering slowly from ten months’ illness.

Asks whetherStrelitzia reginaegrows in gardens at the Cape. Suspects it must be fertilised by a bird.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [14–17 May 1864]
letters.summary: Instructions on measuring pollen of dimorphic plants.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   14 May [1864]
letters.summary: Discusses WED’s observations on polymorphic flowers.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   14 May 1864
letters.summary:
Is burning to hear CD’s reaction to Wallace’s excellent paper on man ["Origin of human races and the antiquity of man",J. Anthropol. Soc. Lond.2 (1864): clviii–clxxxvi].

Wallace’s disclaimer of credit for natural selection is high-minded.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [15 May 1864]
letters.summary:
CD finishingLythrumpaper [Collected papers2: 106–31].

Pleased at Bates’s appointment

and Wallace’s paper.

letters.title: From John Scott   16 May [1864]
letters.summary:
Thanks for communicatingOncidiumsterility paper [see4485] to Linnean Society.

Surprised that CD’s seedlings of non-dimorphic cowslip breed true.

Surprised also that the red primrose he sent reverts to wild form. He had reasoned from red’s infertility with yellow that it was an established variety. Tries to correlate inheritance of colour and sterility between varieties.

letters.title: From H. C. Watson [16 May 1864]
letters.summary: Cover containing some seeds mentioned in the letter to H. C. Watson, 28 May [1864], f.2 (S 4512).

letters.title: From Charles Cardale Babington   18 May 1864
letters.summary:
Glad to hear CD well again.

Will sendLythrum hyssopifoliumflowers from Botanic Garden if they are in bloom; does not know where to find wild specimen, but thinks they are same as garden type.

Is finishing his course of lectures, which was attended by 35–45 people.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   18 May [1864]
letters.summary: SendsPulmonariaanthers, with measurements of styles and pollen counts.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [19 May 1864]
letters.summary: Sends specimens ofMenyantheswith observations and drawings [seeForms of flowers, p. 115].

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [19 May 1864]
letters.summary: Mentions WED’s extraordinary discovery of some pollen-grains of different sizes. The observations must be followed up.

letters.title: From William Henry Harvey   19 May 1864
letters.summary: Sends dandelion [enclosed] with peculiar form of achene; suggests this solitary "sport" must have arisen by sudden jump from normal type.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   19 May 1864
letters.summary:
JDH suggests Scott go to India; he will write letters of introduction.

Conversation with Herbert Spencer.

George Bentham would like to know how CD’s view of hybridism diverges from Charles Naudin’s.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [after 19 May 1864]
letters.summary: [Outline sketches of pollen from long- and short-styled yellow cowslips and from a red cowslip.]

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [20 May 1864]
letters.summary: Clarifies his letter of 18 May [4500].

letters.title: To John Scott   20 May [1864]
letters.summary:
Corrects his former account of cowslips.

The delay in the publication of JS’s Primula paper.

Delights in JS’s experimentation on Verbascum which confirms [C. F.] Gärtner’s statements.

Should be pleased if JS would accept offer of help.

letters.title: From H. C. Watson [20 May 1864]
letters.summary: Taeas [?] allied to L. hyssopifolia. [Cover containing packets of seed specimens.] Mentioned in the letter to H. C. Watson, 28 May [1864], f.2 (fS 4512).

letters.title: From Emma and Charles Darwin to W. E. Darwin   [20 May 1864]
letters.summary: CD much obliged for specimen and drawings.

letters.title: From C. C. Babington   21 May 1864
letters.summary: CCB thought CD wanted live specimens, but now will send some dried ones from his herbarium.

letters.title: To John Scott   21 May [1864]
letters.summary: Encloses an extract from a letter received from [J. D.] Hooker which suggests a job opportunity in India. Advises careful reflection about the risks and the need for a character recommendation. Would like to support the costs of the voyage and initial living expenses.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   22 [May 1864]
letters.summary:
CD’s pleasure at JDH’s willingness to help Scott find a position in India.

Naudin underrates contamination of his experiments by insects. Thus CD doubts Naudin’s results on rapidity and universality of reversion in hybrids.

Wallace’s paper on man [see4494] reflects his genius, although CD does not fully agree with it.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   24 May 1864
letters.summary: Encloses drawings ofMenyanthesandPulmonariaanthers.

letters.title: From William Bennett   25 May 1864
letters.summary: Sends plant and directions to his home so that CD’s gardener may call for another plant.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   28 May [1864]
letters.summary:
Is slowly writingLythrumpaper [Collected papers2: 106–31].

Thanks for [Charles?] Wright’s observations on orchids

– could he note what attracts insects toBegoniaandMelastoma? H. Crüger, who was going to observe Melastomataceae, has died.

Describes the climbing habits ofBignonia capreolataandEccremocarpus scaber.

How does AG know the perfect flowers ofVoandzeiaare quite sterile?

He has a case of dimorphism in holly; asks AG to report on American hollies.

letters.title: From John Scott   28 May [1864]
letters.summary:
Discusses the negative testimonial provided him by James McNab.

Sends testimonial from J. H. Balfour.

Would be glad if offered the sort of colonial opportunity Hooker suggests.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   28 [May 1864]
letters.summary:
Response to ARW’s papers on Papilionidae ["On the phenomena of variation and geographical distribution",Trans. Linn. Soc. Lond.25 (1866): 1–71; abstract inReader3 (1864): 491–3],

and man ["The origin of human races",J. Anthropol. Soc. Lond.2 (1864): clviii–clxxxvi].

The former is "really admirable" and will be influential.

The idea of the man paper is striking and new. Minor points of difference. Conjectures regarding racial differences; the possible correlation between complexion and constitution. HisQuery to Army surgeonsto determine this point. Offers ARW his notes on man, which CD doubts he will be able to use.

On sexual selection in "our aristocracy"; primogeniture is a scheme for destroying natural selection.

[Letter incorrectly dated March by CD.]

letters.title: To Hewett Cottrell Watson   28 May [1864]
letters.summary:
Thanks HCW forLythrumspecimens.

CD has at last finished hisLythrumpaper. ["Three forms ofLythrum",Collected papers2: 106–31.]

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   29 May [1864]
letters.summary:
Argues the antiquity of the human species because natural selection acts differently with respect to men. Changes in man are largely confined to head and brain. Warfare and sex are very uncertain as means of selection.

Gives CD complete credit for theory of natural selection.

Is beginning his narrative of his travels.

Lyell argues against tracing man as far back as Miocene times. R. I. Murchison’s argument that Africa is the oldest existing land implies that Africa is the place to look for early man.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   30 May [1864]
letters.summary: Forwards two character references for John Scott, for position JDH is arranging in India.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   31 [May 1864]
letters.summary: Request for climbing plants.

letters.title: From Julius von Haast   2 June 1864
letters.summary: Inquires about CD’s health.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   2 June [1864]
letters.summary:
Requests climbing plants.

Asks that Oliver be told that he now does not care "how many tendrils he makes axial".

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [4 June 1864]
letters.summary:
JDH is writing letters for Scott, whose temper will be "no obstacle for Hindoos and Musselmen working under him".

New curator at Kew finds considerable neglect, with hundreds of plants dying.

letters.title: From C. C. Babington   6 June 1864
letters.summary: Cannot get anyStellaria gramineafor CD. It is rare. Some, producing different kinds of flowers, once grew in Sandgate, Kent. Variations in flowers need to be re-examined.

letters.title: From Patrick Matthew   6 June 1864
letters.summary:
Would like to meet CD.

He is writing a piece on the Schleswig-Holstein affair which will expose the British press.

letters.title: From Lucy Caroline Wedgwood   [6 June 1864]
letters.summary: Sends observations on seeds ofPulmonaria officinalisrequested by CD.

letters.title: From John Scott   8 June 1864
letters.summary: Discusses cost of trip to India and CD’s offer to advance sum. Thanks Hooker for assistance. Would prize a scientific testimonial from CD.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   10 June [1864]
letters.summary:
CD has proved common oxlip to be a hybrid of cowslip and primrose.

Reviewing literature on climbing plants, CD finds he has much new material.

W. H. Harvey claims evidence of saltation in a dandelion.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   [c.10 June 1864]
letters.summary: Asks DO to draw diagram ofLythrumon board at Linnean Society for reference during the reading of CD’s paper.

letters.title: From John Scott   10 June [1864]
letters.summary:
SendsPassiflorapaper [see4485].

Sends seeds of peloricAntirrhinumcrossed by normal form and sends results of his experiments [table of crosses].

letters.title: From John Scott   10 June [1864]
letters.summary: Thanks CD for £25. Discusses preparations for trip to India.

letters.title: To John Scott   10 June 1864
letters.summary: Letter of recommendation stating his high opinion of John Scott.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [11 June 1864]
letters.summary:
CD’s photograph looks like J. R. Herbert’s Moses in the fresco in the House of Lords.

JDH is delighted about oxlip, but hybridity does not explain some large patches that are uniform and do not vary towards either cowslip or primrose.

Encloses letter from W. H. Harvey discussingMyosotis sylvaticaand the common dandelion.

letters.title: From William Marshall   12 June 1864
letters.summary: Informs CD of two distinct forms ofPlantago lanceolata.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   13 June [1864]
letters.summary:
W. H. Harvey’s dandelion case worth publishing.

Suspects the uniformPrimula elatiorJDH referred to is a distinct species.

Scott’s paper onPassiflorashows variability of reproductive systems.

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   14 June 1864
letters.summary:
Will be glad to do diagram for CD;

asks whether he has read a Hugo von Mohl paper [see4349].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   15 June 1864
letters.summary:
JDH busy reforming Kew’s operations.

Falconer may "fall foul" of Huxley’s anger over his attacks on Lyell.

Has heard of a coffee plantation post for Scott.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   15 June [1864]
letters.summary: L. H. Palm [Über das Winden der Pflanzen(1827)] is better on climbing plants than H. von Mohl [Über den Bau und das Winden der Ranken und Schlingpflanzen(1827)].

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   15 June [1864]
letters.summary:
Short reply to ARW’s long letter. Reaffirms belief in sexual selection.

Postscript on M.-J.-P. Flourens’ "little dull book against me" [Examen du livre de M. Darwin(1864)].

letters.title: From Bernard Peirce Brent   18 June 1864
letters.summary:
Has been informed Miss E. Watts retiring from poultry department of theFieldand would like to take the post if made available. Asks CD if he would provide a reference for him if necessary.

Has bred and reared a young turtle-dove.

On progress of his lawsuit.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   18 June [1864]
letters.summary: Doesn't think will be able to find Buckthorn. Sends reference from Revue de Deux Mondes. Is settled at the Bank.

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   18 June 1864
letters.summary: Thanks for photograph.

letters.title: To John Traherne Moggridge   19 June [1864]
letters.summary: Discusses fertilisation of flowers by bees. Thanks JTM for drawings.

letters.title: From John Scott   20 June [1864]
letters.summary:
Preparations for trip to India. Thanks for testimonial.

Surprised by the self-fertility of CD’s peloricAntirrhinum.

letters.title: From Friedrich Hildebrand   21 June 1864
letters.summary:
Studying insect pollination inSalvia

and heterostyly inPulmonaria officinaliswhich is similar toLinumcase.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   23 June 1864
letters.summary:
JDH going to visit W. H. Harvey in Ireland.

New curator at Kew.

letters.title: To Friedrich Hildebrand   25 June [1864]
letters.summary:
Thanks for orchids.

Recovering from nine months’ illness.

Discusses fertilisation ofPulmonaria.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   25 [June 1864]
letters.summary: John Scott preparing to leave soon.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   27 June [1864]
letters.summary: CD will be proposed for the Copley Medal. Hugh Falconer wants information: list of all CD’s papers, dates of the voyage, things not judicious to mention, when his sickness came on, etc.

letters.title: To Frances Emma Elizabeth Wedgwood   28 June [1864]
letters.summary: Family matters; CD’s feelings on death of FW’s son [James Mackintosh Wedgwood, 1834–64].

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   30 June [1864]
letters.summary: Henry Holland thought CD would be interested to know that Buxton’s brewery cannot go on with their own yeast, but are obliged to interchange with other breweries.

letters.title: To E. A. Darwin   30 June 1864
letters.summary:
Has heard nothing about the Copley Medal. Is grateful for Hugh Falconer’s interest [see4546].

Supplies details about circumstances of his voyage on theBeagle.

Does not believe that his sea-sickness was the cause of his subsequent ill-health.

Encloses the requested list of publications [see4550].

letters.title: From Charles Parker   1 July 1864
letters.summary: Returns CD’s £5 as the school subscription has failed.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   5 July 1864
letters.summary:
JDH pursues the coffee plantation job for Scott.

Wrote 14 letters today. JDH’s work load.

letters.title: To George Bentham   7 July [1864]
letters.summary:
Asks for names of plants mentioned in an article inNatural History Review["South European Floras", n.s. 4 (1864): 369–84] so he can get seeds.

Also would like specimens of the two forms ofAegiphila.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   9 [July 1864]
letters.summary:
No book has made such a powerful impression on EH as theOrigin. Most older German scholars opposed to it, but number of supporters growing among the young. Fortunately strength of religious dogmas now small among educated Germans. Situation in Jena especially favourable. Defended CD’s theory last year at Congress of German Scientists in Stettin.

Intends special study of jellyfish.

Plans general work on natural history.

Hard fate [death of Anna Sethe Haeckel] has made EH indifferent to criticism.

Colleagues August Schleicher and Carl Gegenbaur also convinced by CD’s theory.

letters.title: From George Bentham   10 July 1864
letters.summary: Sends specimens of two species ofAegiphila[seeForms of flowers, p. 123]. Discusses similar forms in other plants.

letters.title: From Andrew Crombie Ramsay   10 July 1864
letters.summary:
Sends 2d ed. of hisPhysical geology[1864]; hopes that he will burn the 1st because of its errors.

ACR is convinced he is right about denudation of the Weald.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   11 July 1864
letters.summary:
Discusses CD’s and Mrs Gray’s health.

Comments on some climbing plants.

Praises Wallace’s article applying natural selection to man ["The origin of human races",J. Anthropol. Soc. Lond.2 (1864): clviii–clxxxvi].

Discusses the reported sterility of the flowers ofVoandzeiaandAmphicarpaea.

Feels the ending of slavery is worth the cost of the Civil War.

letters.title: To George Bentham   12 July [1864]
letters.summary: Thanks GB for specimens [ofAegiphila] and his information.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   12 July [1864]
letters.summary:
Ernst Haeckel writes that young German scientists are enthusiastic for natural selection.

Did JDH write the article inNatural History Reviewon trees not producing flowers ["Botanical lesson books", (1864): 355–69]?

Encourages Harvey to publish on his "disagreeable" monster plants.

letters.title: To A. C. Ramsay   12 July [1864]
letters.summary:
Thanks for his book [Physical geology and geography of Great Britain, 2d. ed. (1864)].

Pleased that ACR’s glacial lake theory is progressing. New Zealand lakes support the view. Suggests he write to Charles Gould in Tasmania, calling his attention to glacial action.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   13 July [1864]
letters.summary: If CD understoodNepenthes, he would understand every class of climbers.

letters.title: From Horace Benge Dobell   15 July 1864
letters.summary:
Suggests man’s original mode of walking and running is similar to that of quadrupeds.

He also suggests CD answer critics who say no new species has ever been unequivocally traced to its origins, by pointing out that there is no unequivocal account of the origin of surnames.

letters.title: From J. T. Moggridge   15 July [1864]
letters.summary: Sends seeds ofTrichonemaand bulb and leaves ofRomulea rollii, plus specimens showing two forms ofPrimula marginata.

letters.title: To H. B. Dobell   17 July [1864]
letters.summary: Thanks HBD for his note. The analogy of surnames had not occurred to CD – only that of language generally, as shown so well by Lyell. Fears HBD’s argument about progression would not have much weight.

letters.title: To J. T. Moggridge   1[7] July [1864]
letters.summary: Discusses dimorphism in flowers. Describes his experiments.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   19 July [1864]
letters.summary:
Thanks for praise [ofOrigin].

Comments on EH’sDie Radiolarien.

Grieved EH has suffered calamity [death of Anna Sethe Haeckel].

CD recovering from long illness.

Doing easy botanical work.

Mentions variability.

Discusses reception of CD’s views in Germany.

letters.title: From J. T. Moggridge   19 July [1864]
letters.summary: Offers notes onRomulea rolliiwith sketch of a dissection.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [21 July 1864]
letters.summary: Returned from Ireland, JDH wishes to visit Down.

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   21 July 1864
letters.summary: Reports his limited observations on climbing ofNepenthes.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   [22 July 1864]
letters.summary: Will DO observe whether leaf [ofNepenthes] with pitcher ever wound round a stick? CD’s plant is improving.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [24 July 1864?]
letters.summary: Notes and queries on climbing plants for JDH [? given to him by CD at their meeting of 24 July 1864].

letters.title: From Robert Thomson   24 July 1864
letters.summary: Observations on insects visiting Melastomataceae.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   28 July 1864
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Has obtained microscopes for CD.

letters.title: From Edward Cresy   29 July 1864
letters.summary:
Requests letter of introduction to Asa Gray.

Went to Linnean Society to hear CD’sLythrumpaper read [Collected papers2: 106–31].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [29 July 1864]
letters.summary: The Kew agent has looked into ships to Calcutta for Scott, who should come to Kew.

letters.title: From John Scott   29 July [1864]
letters.summary: Asks for additional financial aid for trip to India.

letters.title: From James Scott Bowerbank   1 August 1864
letters.summary: Cannot find his Chalk or Gault formationPollicipes. Inquires how CD sent these back.

letters.title: From G. C. Oxenden   1 August 1864
letters.summary:
Spent two days watchingEpipactis palustrisin a bog. Never saw a moth.

Thinks "Suddenism" and not "Graduality" is the great Law of Nature.

letters.title: To ?   1 August [1864 or 1865]
letters.summary: Sends a photograph of himself.

letters.title: From John Scott   2 August 1864
letters.summary: Thanks CD for loan of £10.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [4–]6 August 1864
letters.summary: Replies to CD’s queries on climbing plants.

letters.title: From G. C. Oxenden   4 August [1864?]
letters.summary: A minute black beetle visits the flowers ofEpipactis grandiflora.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [5 August 1864]
letters.summary: JDH’s visit stimulates CD’s interest in his own work. Encloses list of queries on climbing plants. [Missing]

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   10 August 1864
letters.summary:
Sends photographs of himself and his late wife [Anna Sethe]. Describes death of his wife.

Plans trip to the Alps.

Thanks CD for biographical information about himself.

Mentions Goethe as early evolutionist.

Cites Kant as early supporter of epigenesis.

Mentions criticism of CD’s theory by R. A. von Kölliker ["Über die Darwin’sche Schöpfungstheorie",Z. Wiss. Zool.14 (1864): 174–86].

letters.title: From Joseph Beete Jukes   10 August 1864
letters.summary: CD’s support in JBJ’s controversy with Hugh Falconer is welcome. R. I. Murchison supports Falconer, and Lyell does not support their side strongly enough. Falconer and Jukes remain friends in private.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   [after 10] August – 8 October [1864]
letters.summary:
Can understand EH’s feelings on death of his wife.

CD was impressed by manner in which species in South America are replaced by closely allied ones, by affinity of species inhabiting islands near S. America, and by relation of living Edentata and Rodentia to extinct species. When he read MalthusOn population, the idea of natural selection flashed on him.

Agrees with EH’s remarks on Kölliker ["Darwin’sche Schöpfungstheorie",Z. Wiss. Zool.14 (1864): 174–86].

Asks EH to thank Carl Gegenbaur [forVergleichende Anatomie der Wirbelthiere(1864)].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   11 August [1864]
letters.summary: Clarifies queries on climbing plants.

letters.title: From William Jenner   14 August 1864
letters.summary: CD’s urine sample was probably alkaline when passed. The deposit was phosphate of lime. Prescribes a new antacid and continuation of podophyllin. He can judge CD’s state as described by his letter.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [15 August 1864]
letters.summary:
Replies to queries on climbing plants.

JDH meets Scott and finds him an intelligent and superior-looking man. Scott wishes to come to Down before leaving England.

letters.title: From George Varenne Reed   15 August 1864
letters.summary: Horace Darwin making progress, but tires easily and does not like drudgery.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [16 August 1864]
letters.summary: Scott would be very welcome at Down for a short visit.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   17 August [1864]
letters.summary:
Asks JDH to name aBignonia.

Coming to end of climbing plants paper.

letters.title: From A. C. Ramsay   18 August 1864
letters.summary:
R. I. Murchison has criticised ACR’s glacial lake theory in his Presidential Address to Royal Geographical Society [J. R. Geogr. Soc.34 (1864): cix–cxcii].

ACR has finished his Geology of N. Wales.

letters.title: From Roderick Impey Murchison   19 August 1864
letters.summary: Is sending CD an article which he hopes will make him see that there are more causes than ice to account for the structure and wearing away of rocks. [Possibly "On the relative powers of glaciers and floating ice-bergs in modifying the surface of the earth",Can. Nat.2 (1865): 21–33.] [J. of R. Geog. Soc. London34 (1864)]

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [23 August 1864]
letters.summary:
First draft of climbing plants paper is completed.

Nepenthesis a true climber.

Scott has visited Down.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [25 August 1864]
letters.summary: Believes he gave JDH wrong address.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   26 August 1864
letters.summary:
Hookers and Lyells will visit Lubbocks so he cannot see CD in London.

Will CD sit for Woolner?

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   28 August [1864]
letters.summary:
CD is not well enough to sit for Woolner.

TwoBignoniaplants, which JDH does not distinguish as species, can be separated by differences in climbing and sensitivity behaviour.

Wants to write a non-quarrelsome reply to R. A. Kölliker ["Darwin’sche Schöpfungstheorie",Z. Wiss. Zool.14 (1864): 174–86] in theReader. Lyell opposes, but E. A. Darwin and Hensleigh Wedgwood support the idea.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   30 August 1864
letters.summary:
John Scott has sailed.

Concurs with Lyell that CD need not reply to Kölliker.

CD’sBignoniaplants cannot be told apart without flowers.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [1 September 1864]
letters.summary:
CD continues to have trouble reconciling the Veitch’s names forBignoniaplants and Kew names.

Lyell and Falconer called on CD in London.

letters.title: From B. P. Brent   2 September 1864
letters.summary:
Did not get appointment to poultry department of theField; W. B. Tegetmeier has the position.

His lawsuit concluded well but expensive. Thanks CD for aid during his distress; encloses cheque.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   2 September 1864
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Wishes to borrow volumes 1 and 3 ofNarrative[vol. 1 by Capt. P. P. King, vol. 3 by CD].

letters.title: To Auguste Laugel   4 September [1864]
letters.summary: Thanks for a copy of AAL’sProblèmes de la nature1864 (Problems of Nature; Laugel 1864).

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   5 September 1864
letters.summary:
R. I. Murchison’s address [see4595] smashes Ramsay’s glacial theory.

JDH defends his view that CD should not answer Kölliker.

letters.title: From Hermann Kindt   5 September 1864
letters.summary: Requests permission, for a friend, to publish extracts ofOrchidsin German translation.

letters.title: To Hermann Kindt   7 September [1864]
letters.summary: Explains thatOrchidshas been translated into German (Bronn trans. 1862); and thatLiving Cirripediacan now be purchased at Hardwicke’s, 192 Piccadilly, London.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   13 September [1864]
letters.summary:
Has finishedClimbing plants;

resuming work onVariation.

Sends abstract of John Scott’s paper [see4332].

Has received review of Herbert Spencer but cannot believe AG wrote it unless he has muddled his brains with metaphysics.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   13 September [1864]
letters.summary:
Pleased that Bentham is cautious about Naudin’s view of reversion. CD can show experimentally that crossing of races and species tends to bring back ancient characters.

Suggests Gärtner’sBastarderzeugung[1849] be translated

and that Oliver review Scott’sPrimulapaper [J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)8 (1865): 78–126] for a future issue ofNatural History Review.

Is working onVariation.

letters.title: To John Hutton Balfour   15 September [1864]
letters.summary: Inquires which nurserymen near Edinburgh cultivate coloured primroses and cowslips. Wants to repeat John Scott’s remarkable experiments.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   16 September 1864
letters.summary:
Rejoices that CD is beginning "the book of books",Variation.

Suggests that changes in colour of pollen, stigma, and corolla, as Scott reports in hisPrimulapaper, may be related to changes in the insects required for pollination.

Supports Gärtner translation by Ray Society.

Comments on recent addresses by Lyell [Rep. BAAS34 (1864): lx–lxxv], Bentham [Proc. Linn. Soc. Lond.8 (1864): ix–xxiii], and Murchison [Rep. BAAS34 (1864): 130–6].

letters.title: From Hermann Kindt   16 September 1864
letters.summary:
CD’s views go hand-in-hand with those of Ludwig Büchner.

He requests an autograph for a friend.

letters.title: To Hermann Kindt   17 September 1864
letters.summary: Sends his thanks for a kind letter; he has copied out the last sentence of theOrigin.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   17 September [1864]
letters.summary: Glad that Oliver is to review John Scott’s paper in theNatural History Review(Scott 1864a). Apologises that his enclosed references (now missing) are so paltry.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [19 September 1864]
letters.summary: Reports on personalities at the Bath meeting of BAAS [Sept 1864].

letters.title: From Maxwell Tylden Masters   19 September 1864
letters.summary: Explains several monstrous flowers sent by CD.

letters.title: From Hermann Kindt   20 September 1864
letters.summary: Thanks for autograph.

letters.title: To M. T. Masters   20 September [1864]
letters.summary: CD sends thanks for MTM’s note on monsters. Adds comment on MTM’s point that some species become monstrous more frequently than others.

letters.title: From J. H. Balfour   22 September 1864
letters.summary:
Does not know an Edinburgh nurseryman who can supply the cowslips and primroses CD wants; will try to get them from the Botanic Garden.

Hears from Hooker that CD is also examiningLythrum.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   23 September [1864]
letters.summary:
Pleased with news of BAAS meeting

and Scott’s possible position as Thomas Anderson’s curator.

Suggests Wallace is due for a Royal Medal.

Agrees with JDH’s criticism of Lyell’s address [see4614].

Bentham’s Linnean Society address treats continuity of life in a vague non-natural sense.

Rereading his old MS [Natural selection] CD is impressed with work he had already done.

WritingVariationmuch harder thanClimbing plants.

Encloses request to JDH to propose, or suggest on his behalf, that the Ray Society publish a translation of C. F. von Gärtner’sVersuche und Beobachtungen über die Bastarderzeugung im Pflanzenreich(1849).

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   23 September [1864]
letters.summary: BJS’s health much improved by his continental tour.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [28 September 1864]
letters.summary:
SendsNepenthes laevis.

Wallace for the Royal Medal is a good thought.

W. H. Harvey is at Kew and JDH has asked him about desert climbers.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   3 October 1864
letters.summary:
Review of Spencer was by Chauncey Wright.

Will get a note on John Scott’s paper off toSillimans Journal[Am. J. Sci.2d ser. 39 (1865): 101–10].

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   3 October [1864]
letters.summary: Admires THH’s article on Kölliker’s and Flourens’ criticisms ofOrigin[inNatural History Review(1864): 566–80].

letters.title: From Robert Monsey Rolfe   4 October 1864
letters.deprecated: Robert Monsey Rolfe, 1st Baron Cranworth of Cranworth
letters.sender: Robert Monsey Rolfe, 1st Baron Cranworth of Cranworth
letters.summary: Sends £10 for Down charities.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   5 October 1864
letters.summary:
Surprised at Kölliker’s misunderstanding; of Flourens he could have believed anything.

Family news.

letters.title: From John Beck   6 October 1864
letters.summary: Has heard about but not readOrigin; is concerned that it may contribute to unbelief. Gives many pages of scriptural quotations and exegesis on the creation of earth, species, etc.

letters.title: ToGardeners’ Chronicle   [before 8 October 1864]
letters.summary: Asks anyone who possesses a treatise on gardening, or an almanac, one or two centuries old, to look up what date is given as the proper period for sowing scarlet runners or dwarf French beans. CD wants to ascertain whether these plants can now be sown earlier than was formerly the case.

letters.title: From George Edward Frere   8 October 1864
letters.summary: Responds to the letter toGardeners’ Chronicle, [before 8 October 1864].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   8 October [1864]
letters.summary:
Huxley has answered Kölliker inNatural History Review[(1864): 566–80].

CD is correcting two of Scott’s papers; is convinced primrose and cowslip are two good species.

letters.title: From James Buckman   10 October 1864
letters.summary: Sends a poem about sowing kidney beans.

letters.title: From John Cook Gould   10 October 1864
letters.summary: Encloses an extract concerning beans from theSystema Horticultureæof 1688 by J. Worlidge. Will be pleased to lend the volume if needed.

letters.title: From Hermann Kindt   11 October 1864
letters.summary: Requests photograph.

letters.title: To Charles Buxton   12 October [1864]
letters.summary: Has heard that the yeast in CB’s brewery has failed. Asks for confirmation and answers to some questions.

letters.title: From Charles Wentworth Dilke   12 October 1864
letters.summary: In response to CD’s notice inGardeners’ Chronicle[Collected papers2: 93], sends planting times of peas from an 1861 almanac.

letters.title: From William Jenner   15 October 1864
letters.summary: Prescribes continuing the phosphate of iron.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [16? October 1864]
letters.summary:
Morphological differences only partly define species; physiological differences, e.g., incompatibility results inPrimula, are far more interesting.

T. Thomson’s review of Agardh’s muddled book ["Agardh’s classification of plants",Nat. Hist. Rev.(1864): 536–51].

letters.title: To J. H. Balfour   21 October [1864]
letters.summary:
Thanks Balfour forCorydalisseed

and sends a photo of himself.

letters.title: From Charles Buxton   21 October 1864
letters.summary: Forwards a letter from his head brewer, Laurence Burleigh, on yeast. They seldom exchange yeast with other brewers, and he doubts whether weak yeast from one brewery will ferment strongly in another.

letters.title: To B. D. Walsh   21 October [1864]
letters.summary:
Thanks for letter and memoirs.

Suggests a "rather hopeless experiment" of introducing poisons into tissues of plants on the chance that monstrous growths may be produced.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   22 October [1864]
letters.summary:
To Lyell’s chagrin, CD has come round again to A. C. Ramsay’s glacial theory.

On primrose and cowslip, CD maintains they are good species, notwithstanding Scott’s work.

CD defines species by power of remaining constant for a good long time and showing appreciable amount of difference from close species.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   26[–8] October 1864
letters.summary:
Comments at length on Ramsay’s glacial paper ["On the erosion of valleys and lakes",Philos. Mag.4th ser. 28 (1864): 293–311]. Prefers it to Tyndall, but unconvinced about sea action and unwilling to grant that ice power sculptures the totality of landscape.

Unwilling to support Wallace for Royal Medal.

Herbert Spencer’s noisy vacuity.

Garden varieties that are constant and infertile with parent deserve to be called species.

Scott ineligible to be Linnean Society associate because he is not in England.

George Busk’s incoherent talk on Gibraltar cave fossils.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   26 October 1864
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for notes concerning the development of his ideas about the origin of species. Says August Schleicher and Carl Gegenbaur also interested.

Names new supporters of CD’s theory, including Max Schultze, Rudolf Leuckart, and Alexander Braun. Zoologists have been more interested than botanists.

He is writing a general work on the relationships among animals [Generelle Morphologie der Organismen(1866)].

Comments on Fritz Müller’sFür Darwin[1864].

Gegenbaur is revising hisGrundzüge der vergleichenden Anatomie[2d ed. (1870)] to accord with evolution.

Thanks CD for copy of book on balanids [Living Cirripedia, vol. 2].

letters.title: To Asa Gray   29 October [1864]
letters.summary:
Sends question [missing] for an ornithologist.

Is plodding on atVariation.

Has added toClimbing plants.

letters.title: From Andrew Murray   31 October 1864
letters.summary: Proposes to work on geographical distribution before leaving the Society.

letters.title: To Andrew Murray   2 November [1864]
letters.summary:
Wishes AM success in undertaking his work on geographical distribution [The geographical distribution of mammals(1866)]. CD has no suggestions to make as he has not recently attended to the subject.

He is still weak after his long illness and supposes he will ever remain so.

letters.title: From Hugh Falconer 3 November 186[4]
letters.summary: Council of the Royal Society have awarded CD the Copley Medal.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   3 November [1864]
letters.summary:
Asks JDH to verify an observation onDicentra– what CD thought was a branch in the young plant now looks like a gigantic leaf in the old.

Concurs on Spencer’s clever emptiness.

Ramsay exaggerates role of ice. Sorry to hear that Tyndall grows dogmatic.

Admits difficulty of making case for Wallace’s Royal Medal at this time.

Will soon finish the first draft ofVariation.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   3 November 1864
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Congratulates CD on receiving the Copley Medal.

letters.title: From Edward Sabine   3 November 1864
letters.summary: Announces that the Council of the Royal Society has awarded CD the Copley Medal.

letters.title: To Ray Society   [before 4 November 1864]
letters.summary: "Read a letter from Mr Darwin suggesting the Translation of Gaertner’s work [Bastarderzeugung im Pflanzenreich(1849)]."

letters.title: To Hugh Falconer   4 November [1864]
letters.summary:
[Copley] Medal very great honour. Cordial thanks.

Chuckled over [Gaspard-Auguste] Brullé and pupils.

Splendid converts in Rudolf Leuckart and Carl Gegenbaur.

letters.title: From Henry Holland   4 November [1864]
letters.summary: Congratulations on the Copley Medal.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   4 November 1864
letters.summary: His pleasure at Royal Society Copley Medal for CD. Recounts meeting of Royal Society Council.

letters.title: From Charles Lyell   4 November 1864
letters.summary: Delighted to hear that CD was awarded Copley Medal. Important because award by chartered institution acts on outsiders and helps increase stock of moral courage.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   5 November [1864]
letters.summary:
Appreciates THH’s note more than Medal.

Encourages THH to write a popular treatise on zoology.

Sends Mrs Huxley a quotation from Tennyson, with sarcastic comment.

letters.title: To Edward Sabine   5 November [1864]
letters.summary: Thanks ES in connection with award [of Copley Medal].

letters.title: From Hugh Falconer   7 November [1864]
letters.summary: Hopes CD will be able to receive the Copley Medal in person. HF sees it as doubly significant in recognising CD’s work and as a protest against the profession of religious as opposed to scientific faith.

letters.title: From B. D. Walsh   7 November 1864
letters.summary:
Notes Louis Agassiz’s opinions on CD’s views.

Mating and sexual organs of insects.

letters.title: To Hugh Falconer   8 November [1864]
letters.summary: Gratified to receive Copley Medal. Cannot attend anniversary [of Royal Society]. Would HF receive medal for him?

letters.title: From W. H. Harvey   8 November [1864]
letters.summary: The plants from the Cape did not show climbing habit in native country; WHH believes it a consequence of their being grown under disadvantages of climate.

letters.title: From William Jenner   9 November 1864
letters.summary: Prescribes "syrup of phosphate of iron". Requests a urine sample.

letters.title: From Hugh Falconer   10 November [1864]
letters.summary: Is sure that any of CD’s friends would be proud to accept the medal on his behalf.

letters.title: From W. H. Harvey   10 November 1864
letters.summary: Identifies South African species of plants that are normally non-climbers in the wild but climb freely when grown from seed at Glasnevin. Thinks there is probably a gradation in the wild between climbing and non-climbing varieties related to the degree of exposure each particular plant faces.

letters.title: From W. H. Harvey   11 November 1864
letters.summary: Has examined his specimens discussed in his previous note and adds further observations.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   19 November [1864]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: About buying shares.

letters.title: From William Robinson   19 November 1864
letters.summary: Identifies a climbing plant that CD saw at the Society’s gardens.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   21 November [1864]
letters.summary:
SendsLiving Cirripedia[vol. 2].

Has employed translator for Fritz Müller’s book [Für Darwin(1864)].

Thanks for paper and speech.

letters.title: From William Jenner   21 November 1864
letters.summary: Has analysed CD’s urine and suggests he omit the alkaline powders. Continues to prescribe iron phosphate.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [23 November 1864]
letters.summary:
JDH’s "shock" that CD was awarded the Copley Medal.

Oliver, Thomson and JDH independently concur mature tendrils ofDicentraare foliar, though JDH remembers they were axial in the spring. Expects he and CD were fooled, but will have to look again next spring.

Praises CD’sLythrumpaper [Collected papers2: 106–31].

JDH completing F. Boott’s work onCarex[Illustrations of the genus Carex].

JDH now does suspect Mrs Boott is illegitimate daughter of Dr Erasmus Darwin [see4389].

letters.title: From William Jenner   24 November 1864
letters.summary: Prescribes carbonate of ammonia with horseradish. CD is to avoid any magnesia. Recommends CD go without medicine for a time and avoid the "evil habit" of taking too much water.

letters.title: To Richard Kippist   24 November [1864]
letters.summary: CD sends [to the Linnean Society] a paper "On one of the most curious orchids in the world" [readJ. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)9 (1865): 156–62]. [See4680].

letters.title: From William Jenner   [after 24 November] 1864
letters.summary: CD’s urine is normal. He may take antacids for his stomach.

letters.title: From Richard Trevor Clarke   25 November [1864]
letters.summary: Observations onGossypiumvarieties.

letters.title: To Roland Trimen   25 November 1864
letters.summary:
Has forwarded RT’s paper onBonateato the Linnean Society [J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)9 (1865): 156–60].

TheOxalissent by RT flowered but CD has made out only two forms; he thinks there ought to be three, so would welcome more seed.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   26 November [1864]
letters.summary:
CD’sLythrumpaper has given him as much satisfaction as working out complemental males in cirripedes.

Response to award of Copley Medal.

Letters from Germany and France support natural selection.

Now that climbing plants are done, CD asks forDrosera.

letters.title: From W. D. Fox   28 November [1864]
letters.summary: Congratulates CD on the Copley Medal.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   29 November 1864
letters.summary:
JDH is making inquiries for CD on temperate climbing plants.

Discusses politics of Royal Society Council in awarding CD the Copley Medal.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   [before 30 November 1864]
letters.summary: Gives Lyell’s report of conversation with Sabine about the grounds for the award of CD’s [Copley] Medal.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   30 November [1864]
letters.summary:
The Copley Medal is considered a great honour, but such things make little difference to CD, except for the several kind letters he received. It shows that natural selection is making some progress.

His health is poor.

Work is crawling onVariation;

occasional botany recreative.

letters.title: To Editor of theNatural History Review   [December? 1864]
letters.summary: Forwards a communication from A. Fonblanque for possible publication inNatural History Review. [See "Notice of mule breeding",Nat. Hist. Rev.n.s. 5 (1865): 147–8.]

letters.title: From George Busk   1 December 1864
letters.summary: Has received CD’s Copley Medal for him. Conveys regrets of Royal Society at his absence.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   1 December 1864
letters.summary:
Discusses the affairs of the late Edward Evans for whom CD and EAD are trustees.

Has got CD’s [Copley] Medal, "it is rather ugly to look at, & too light to turn into candlesticks".

letters.title: From Hugh Falconer   2 December 1864
letters.summary: The [Royal Society] President’s address is in theReader[4 (1864): 708–9], but one or two sentences have been omitted.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   2 December 1864
letters.summary:
Recounts row at the Royal Society over exclusion of mention ofOriginfrom Sabine’s address awarding Copley Medal to CD.

Encloses two letters to JDH from James Hector in New Zealand.

letters.title: From John Obadiah Westwood   2 December 1864
letters.summary: Sends photo for B. D. Walsh; requests those of New World entomologists, and CD’s.

letters.title: To George Busk   4 December [1864]
letters.summary: Thanks GB for proposing him for Copley Medal; suspects he is responsible for the praise in Sabine’s "splendid eulogy" on his work. Has, however, written to Sabine to say he would have liked a little more said about theOrigin.

letters.title: To Hugh Falconer   4 December [1864]
letters.summary:
Much pleased by Edward Sabine’s address.

Grateful to HF for his interest [in the award of Copley Medal to CD].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   4 December [1864]
letters.summary:
CD pleased with Huxley for defending him against Sabine. Also pleased with much of Sabine’s address. Is sure JDH wrote the botanical part.

Suggests James Hector observe which insects visit endemic New Zealand plants

and JDH examine distribution of white vs coloured corollas in New Zealand.

letters.title: To Edward Sabine   4 December [1864]
letters.summary:
Thanks ES for his "splendid eulogium" [in Presidential Address to Royal Society on award of Copley Medal]. CD would have liked him to have said "a little more" aboutOrigin.

CD feels no doubt about natural selection. Has heard from Germany of "a string of excellent men" who accept it.

letters.title: To B. D. Walsh   4 December [1864]
letters.summary:
Discusses Agassiz’s misrepresentations of his views and J. D. Dana’s "wild notions".

The reception is friendlier from younger scientists in France, and many of the best men in Germany.

letters.title: To B. D. Walsh [4 December 1864?]
letters.summary: Sends J. O. Westwood’s direction.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   5 December 1864
letters.summary:
Congratulates CD on the Copley Medal.

Is making inquiries on the habits of American cuckoos and sends a letter from Henry Bryant on that subject.

Discusses the Civil War.

Encloses letter from W. H. Leggett containing observations onAmphicarpaea.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [6 December 1864]
letters.summary:
Sabine’s address, printed in theReader[4 (1864): 708–9], is good on the whole. Sends Huxley’s account of the row.

Praises John Ruskin’s eloquent reply to Jukes.

letters.title: From C. V. Naudin   6 December 1864
letters.summary:
Congratulates CD on the Copley Medal.

Directs CD to his short memoir on crossing ["De l’hybridité",C. R. Hebd. Acad. Sci.59 (1864): 837–45].

letters.title: From Elizabeth Juliana Sabine   7 December [1864]
letters.summary: Acknowledges the receipt of CD’s letter on behalf of her husband, who is unwell.

letters.title: To [Frederick Wollaston Hutton]   8 December [1864]
letters.summary: Regrets he has no notes on periods when albatrosses were abundant off Cape Horn.

letters.title: To C. V. Naudin   8 December [1864]
letters.summary:
Thanks CVN for reference to theComptes Rendus[Académie Française].

Mentions CVN’s work on Cucurbitaceae and notes that he (CD) has quoted extensively from it inVariation.

Hopes to send paper onLythrum[Collected papers2: 106–31] soon.

Mentions exchange of photographs.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   10 December [1864]
letters.summary:
Has found incipient stages of adhesive discs inHanburiatendrils.

Huxley was probably right to have challenged Sabine, but the poor old man is sick.

CD remembers the old Disraeli novel [Tancred(1847)] that sneers at transmutation.

letters.title: From Francis Trevelyan Buckland   [before 11 December 1864]
letters.summary:
Salmon and trout increase in size with river.

Wishes to show CD fish hatchery near Hampton Court.

Quoted CD’s book on self-destruction within species in a salmon arbitration case.

letters.title: To F. T. Buckland   11 December [1864]
letters.summary:
Asks for comparison of otter-hounds’ feet with those of other dogs.

Changes in oysters.

letters.title: From F. T. Buckland   13 December 1864
letters.summary:
Sorry to hear CD ill.

On his return from Galway, will arrange with CD about visiting and showing him his specimens.

letters.title: From Leo Lesquereux   14 December 1864
letters.summary: Fossil flora of the Carboniferous. Variation of forms found in coal analogous to succession of forms in peat-bogs.

letters.title: To F. T. Buckland   15 December [1864]
letters.summary:
Would be delighted to see FB for a few minutes but his health is so poor he doubts it would be worth the trouble for FB to visit.

Thanks about the otter-hound.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   15 December [1864]
letters.summary: Sends a power of attorney to be executed and sent to the Old Bank; asks acknowledgment.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   15 December [1864]
letters.summary: Requests addresses of J. E. Planchon, W. F. Hofmeister and M. J. Schleiden so he can send them copies ofLythrumpaper [Collected papers2: 106–31].

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   16 December 1864
letters.summary:
Sends addresses of Planchon, Hofmeister, and Schleiden.

Hermann Crüger left no widow.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   20 December 1864
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Vexed at the address of the President of the Royal Society [on award of Copley medal to CD].

letters.title: From W. B. Tegetmeier   [before 21 December 1864]
letters.summary:
Sends paper on mimetic analogy [Intellect. Obs.6 (1864): 307–13].

Mongrel experiments are progressing, but he has observed no signs of sterility.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   21 December [1864]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: The Copley medal. Sabine’s Presidential Address and Huxley’s response.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   21 December [1864]
letters.summary:
CD working onVariation; he will soon want corrected fowl MS [Variation, ch. 7].

WBT’s breeding experiments produced no sterility.

letters.title: To Thomas Campbell Eyton   29 December [1864?]
letters.summary: Asks TCE to verify whether otter-hounds have more skin between their toes than other hounds. Also interested in cases of infertile matings between normally fertile individuals.

letters.title: From John Struthers   31 December 1864
letters.summary: Sends CD part two of his anatomical papers [Anatomical and physiological observations(1863) [part 1 (1854)]]; thinks CD may be interested in the paper dealing with variation in numbers of digits in man. Draws CD’s attention to another variation: the occurrence of a supra-condyloid process in the human arm.

letters.title: From Francis Trevelyan Buckland   [1865–6]
letters.summary:
Was glad to see CD at museum.

Asks CD to sign and return enclosed item.

CD did not cover oysters in his book; FB can point out curious facts about them.

letters.title: From Richard Spruce   [1865–77]
letters.summary: Notes on various instances of dimorphism.

letters.title: From Joseph Dalton Hooker   1 January 1865
letters.summary:
Forwards H. T. Stainton letter for reply.

Finds manyCucurbitahave tendrils with sticking ends.

The "potentiality of so many organs in plants to play so many parts is one of the most wonderful of your discoveries . . . one day it will itself play a prodigious part in the interpretation of both morphological and physiological facts".

Is disgusted with Sabine’s address [see4708] because of its mutilation of what JDH wrote.

THH’s slashing leader inReader["Science and ""Church policy"" ", 4 (1864): 821] – as usual he destroys all in his path.

Encloses letter from G. H. K. Thwaites with a message for CD [see encl].

letters.title: From Henrietta Anne Huxley   1 January 1865
letters.summary: Has just been shown CD’s remarks on Tennyson. Upbraids CD for "Owen-like quotation" out of context, and getting source wrong. "If ""facts"" in Origin are of this sort I agree with Bishop of Oxford."

letters.title: From Thomas Henry Huxley   1 January 1865
letters.summary:
Sends photograph.

THH wishes he could write the popular zoology but writing is a boring and slow process when he is not interested, and he is overburdened with lectures.

letters.title: From Henry Holland   2 January 1865
letters.summary:
Thanks forLythrumpaper [Collected papers2: 106–31].

T. S. Cobbold’s book on the Entozoa [1864].

Remarks on development of the tapeworm.

letters.title: From Ludwig Rütimeyer   3 January 1865
letters.summary:
Regrets he has not yet finished his monograph onBos. Has examined and discusses theBosskull from Lord Tankerville.

Would like CD’s opinion on the conclusions in LR’s paper on fossil horses.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   4 January [1865]
letters.summary:
Thanks for photograph, charmed by Mrs Huxley’s letter.

Regrets THH cannot do the popular work on zoology.

Has heard THH wrote leading article in lastReader["Science and ""church policy"" ", 4 (1864): 821].

letters.title: To Hugh Falconer   6 January [1865]
letters.summary: "I return your letter to [William] Sharpey." Grandest eulogium CD has received.

letters.title: From William Darwin Fox   6 January [1865]
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for hisLythrumpaper [Collected papers2: 106–31].

Tells of the birth of his 16th child. Has five grandchildren.

letters.title: From Thomas Rivers   6 January [1865]
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for his paper onLythrum[Collected papers2: 106–31].

Astonished by CD’s powers of observation and perseverance.
