His elms raised from three varieties of weeping elms are doing well.

letters.title: To Ray Society   [before 7 January 1865]
letters.summary: Concerning the proposed translation of K. F. von Gärtner’sBastarderzeugung(1849).

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   7 January [1865]
letters.summary:
Has finished long paper on "Climbing plants". Prefers sending it to Linnean Society if Bentham does not think it too long.

ForNew Zealand flora[1864–7] CD suggests JDH count plants with irregular corollas and compare with England.

Does not quite agree aboutReader.

Is Tyndall author of piece on spiritualism?

CD’s illness diagnosed as "suppressed gout".

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [8–18 January 1865]
letters.summary:
Bentham wants "Climbing plants" forJournal of the Linnean Society, however long [J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)9 (1865): 1–118]. Publication inProceedings of the Royal Societyrestricts correspondence.

Readermuch improved.

Tyndall did write piece on spiritualism ["Science and the spirits",Reader4 (1864): 725–6].

"Suppressed gout" annoys him as a term cloaking ignorance.

letters.title: To Thomas Campbell Eyton   9 January [1865?]
letters.summary:
Thanks TCE for information about breeding

and for his promise to measure feet of otter-hounds [seeVariation1: 39–40].

letters.title: To Ray Society   [14–18 January 1865]
letters.summary: "Read a letter from Mr Darwin expressing his regret that the state of his health would not permit of his writing an Introductory Chapter to the Translation of Gaertner’s work [Bastarderzeugung im Pflanzenreich(1849)]."

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   15 January 1865
letters.summary:
Thanks for [E. Eudes?] Deslongchamps’ paper.

Henry Huxley born.

Leader inReader[4 (1864): 821] is by THH. It has got him into trouble with some of his friends.

letters.title: From Charles Lyell   16 January 1865
letters.summary:
His view ofOrigin.

Belief of Duke of Argyll that substituting "variation" and "selection" for creation deifies them.

Thinks Argyll would accept evolution except for man.

A’s view of humming-birds.

Describes discussion with [Victoria,] Princess Royal of Prussia, about evolution.

New edition ofElementsconsistent withOrigin.

letters.title: To Henry Denny   17 January [1865]
letters.summary:
Pleased to learn that HD has resumed research on Anoplura.

Are Chiloe pediculi a distinct species?

Do lice differ on different races of humans?

Is there evidence supporting Mr Marshall’s statement about Polynesian lice?

letters.title: From Asa Gray   17 January 1865
letters.summary:
New herbarium is finished.

Congratulations on Copley Medal.

letters.title: To Richard Kippist   18 January [1865]
letters.summary: Asks that the long paper that he is sending for the Society be acknowledged when received.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   19 January [1865]
letters.summary:
"Climbing plants" sent off.

Encourages JDH to include notes on gradation of important characters inGenera plantarumor to write a paper on the subject. Has given prominence to gradation of unimportant characters in climbing plants. Believes that it is common for the same part in an individual plant to be in different states. Same may be true of important parts – for example position of ovule may differ.

Two articles in lastNatural History Reviewinterested him; "Colonial floras" [n.s. 5 (1865): 46–63]

and "Sexuality of cryptogams" [n.s. 5 (1865): 64–79].

Fact of similarity of orders in tropics is extremely curious. Thinks it may be connected with glacial destruction.

Leo Lesquereux says he is a convert for the curious reason that CD’s books make birth of Christ and redemption by grace so clear to him!

"Not one question [for JDH] in this letter!"

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [20 January 1865]
letters.summary:
Cannot come until week from Saturday.

Worked to death byGenera plantarum.

letters.title: From John Scott   20 January 1865
letters.summary:
Comments on hisPrimulapaper [see4213].

Describes his situation in Calcutta.

letters.title: From Alfred Russel Wallace   20 January 1865
letters.summary:
His distress that his engagement has been broken off.

Sends copies of two papers ["On the parrots of the Malayan region",Proc. Zool. Soc. Lond.(1864): 279–97;

"On the physical geography of the Malay Archipelago",J. R. Geogr. Soc.33 (1863): 217–34].

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   22 January [1865]
letters.summary:
Criticises Duke of Argyll’s address [to the Royal Society of Edinburgh (1864)] and demurs on Argyll’s "new birth" theory.

Agrees with CL on beauty.

Enjoyed hearing of Princess Royal’s discussion [on Darwinism].

CD’s illness.

CL’s advice on chapter [ofVariation] on dogs was excellent.

letters.title: To Edward Walford   22 [January–April 1865?]
letters.summary: CD would be proud to be one of EW’s series [Portraits of men of eminence(1863–7)]. If he goes to London in the summer he will call on Mr Edwards [the photographer].

letters.title: From Henry Denny   23 January 1865
letters.summary: Species of lice and the animals they infest. Different kinds of dogs, fowls, and pigeons are infested by the same species ofPediculi[seeDescent1: 219].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [26 January 1865]
letters.summary: John Scott has arrived in Calcutta and has been given an appointment by Thomas Anderson.

letters.title: To John Edward Gray   27 January [1865]
letters.summary:
Thanks JEG for congratulations [on Copley Medal?].

Mentions JEG’s illness.

letters.title: From Frances Harriet Hooker   [27 January 1865]
letters.summary: J. D. Hooker will not be able to visit CD because of ill health.

letters.title: From Henry Walter Bates   28 January 1865
letters.summary:
Pleased at receiving CD’s letter.

HWB informs him of favourable notice of the mimetic paper [in Wiegmann’sArch. Naturgesch.29 (1863) pt 2: 315–19].

He is pleased with his post [Asst. Sec. of Royal Geographical Society].

letters.title: To Henry Denny   28 January [1865]
letters.summary:
Returns [Andrew] Murray’s paper;

especially values HD’s note that the same species of lice infect the different varieties of fowl, pigeon, and dog. Further queries about the relationship of the same species of pediculi to different domestic varieties.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   29 January [1865]
letters.summary:
Commends ARW’s papers on parrots

and on the theory of geographical distribution [see4750].

Wild pigs in Aru Islands must have been introduced and later ran wild. Does ARW have an opinion on the subject?

letters.title: To Abraham Dee Bartlett   30 January [1865]
letters.summary:
Orders that one of CD’s Porto Santo rabbits be killed and sent to him.

Asks whether ADB has got young from mating these with females of other breeds.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   31 January [1865]
letters.summary:
Sends papers with comments. Convinced that the Aru pig is a species peculiar to New Guinea fauna, not a domestic animal that ran wild.

Admires CD’s paper ["Three forms ofLythrum",Collected papers2: 106–31].

letters.title: From William Erasmus Darwin [late February–May 1865]
letters.summary: [Outline sketches of pollen from short-styled yellow primrose and from long-styled yellow and red primroses.]

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   1 February [1865]
letters.summary:
Exchange of photographs.

Aru pigs present perplexing case, whether wild or domesticated.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   2 February [1865]
letters.summary:
Hugh Falconer’s death great loss to science.

His own health has been especially bad this last week.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   3 February 1865
letters.summary:
Falconer’s illness and suffering. His great ability and knowledge.

CD’s paper ["Climbing plants"] went extremely well [at Linnean Society]. M. T. Masters and Bentham commented.

letters.title: To [Robertson Munro?]   3 February [1865 or 1866?]
letters.summary:
Is glad MTM is going to experiment onPassiflora.

Is grieved to hear that John Scott has been inaccurate but cannot think he recorded, in his paper, experiments that he never made [see4485].

letters.title: To Max Ernst Wichura   3 February [1865]
letters.summary:
He has finished MEW’s work on hybrid willows [Die Bastardbefruchtung im Planzenreich(1865)] and sends his thanks. The extreme frequency of hybrid willows is new to CD, and he finds the explanation of their numbers in certain locations ingenious.

Comments on the criticism of Gärtner’s view of reversion

and the differences between MEW and Naudin.

CD now has doubts regarding his own view that hybrids are sterile from not being perfectly accommodated to their conditions of life.

letters.title: From Maxwell Tylden Masters   7 February 1865
letters.summary: MTM heard part of the abstract of CD’s paper on climbing plants, read at the Linnean Society on 2 Feb. Offers CD his opinion and information on the subject, which he has studied for many years.

letters.title: To Richard Kippist   8 February 1865
letters.summary: Requests all parts ofTransactionsdue him.

letters.title: To A. D. Bartlett   9 February [1865]
letters.summary: Inquires about body of Porto Santo rabbit which has not arrived.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   9 February [1865]
letters.summary:
Falconer’s death haunts him. Personal annihilation not so horrifying to him as sun cooling some day and human race ending.

His health has been wretched.

Masters has written his agreement with CD’s "Climbing plants".

letters.title: From August Schleicher   9 February 1865
letters.summary:
Sends a pamphlet and photograph to CD [missing];

announces a botanical congress at Erfurt at which CD’s theory will be discussed.

letters.title: To A. D. Bartlett   14 February [1865]
letters.summary:
CD sends thanks for feather of theGallus.

The rabbit arrived safely, but unfortunately the entrails had been removed; if ADB catches the other one, CD would like it sent unmutilated.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   15 [February 1865]
letters.summary:
Hildebrand has sent copy of his paper onPulmonariainBotanische Zeitung.

How much should CD contribute to Falconer’s bust?

Oswald Heer on alpine and Arctic floras.

A. R. Wallace on geographical distribution in Malay Archipelago.

Lyell’s new edition ofElements. Wishes someone would do a book like it on botany.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [17 February 1865]
letters.summary:
Why botanists will not subscribe to Falconer’s bust with enthusiasm.

Scott has been offered curatorship at Calcutta Botanic Garden.

letters.title: From George Busk   20 February 1865
letters.summary: On a proposed meeting of friends of the deceased Hugh Falconer to decide on a memorial to him. Invites CD’s support.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   21 February [1865]
letters.summary:
Belated thanks to CL for copy ofElements. Praises CL’s work. Notes especially Atlantic continents, the Weald, the Purbeck beds, glacial action, and the formation of lake-basins.

Also mentions account of Heer’s work

and CD’s disagreement with J. D. Forbes.

Suggests that CL have Murray print a two-volume edition [of theElements].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [27 February 1865?]
letters.summary: Will arrive Saturday [4 Mar] on afternoon train.

letters.title: To William Bernhard Tegetmeier   27 February [1865]
letters.summary:
Wants his fowl MS.

Will shortly return WBT’s skulls.

letters.title: From W. B. Tegetmeier   [28 February – 5 March 1865]
letters.summary:
Encloses some poultry feathers.

Will read over and return CD’s MS on fowls. Has been delayed by an eye injury.

letters.title: From Benjamin Dann Walsh   1 March 1865
letters.summary:
Sends his paper on "Willow-galls" [Proc. Entomol. Soc. Philadelphia3 (1864): 543–644].

Lengthy criticism of Agassiz’s views on species as stated in hisEssay on classification[1857].

Interested by CD’s trimorphism inLythrum. Thinks some great mystery may lie in the fact that in some genera, some species are tri-, some di-, and some monomorphic, and in other genera,Apis,Vespa,Bombus, all the known species are dimorphic.

letters.title: From Frederick Ransome   6 March 1865
letters.summary: Requests a postponement of payment on a note for £100.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   6 [March 1865]
letters.summary: Asks for return of page about pigeon crossing.

letters.title: From Frederick Ransome   9 March 1865
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his consideration in meeting his convenience respecting the payment of the £100.

letters.title: From Rudolph Heine   10 March 1865
letters.summary: AdmiresOrigin, but CD does not consider hereditary law of use and disuse.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [10 March 1865]
letters.summary: Thomas Thomson has gone over Scott’s paper; encloses his conclusions. Not fit for publication in present form. His experiments should have been repeated to resolve his disagreement with Gärtner.

letters.title: From W. B. Tegetmeier   13 March 1865
letters.summary:
Will return page on pigeons.

Has concluded his crossing experiments and found no trace of hybrid sterility or loss of fertility.

TheFieldis publishing a series of papers on different pigeon varieties [24 (1864): 366, 395, 459; 25 (1865): 115, 139, 155, 228, 258].

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   14 March [1865]
letters.summary: Asks for WBT’s help in arranging for woodcuts to illustrate pigeon chapters ofVariation.

letters.title: To Rudolph Heine   16 March [1865]
letters.summary: Is pleased to hear of Dr Heine’s interest inOrigin. Questions whether Dr Heine’s law of inheritance can be demonstrated.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   16 [March 1865]
letters.summary: Thanks for Thomson’s and JDH’s views on Scott’s paper. Will send it back with advice and explanations.

letters.title: From Francis Trevelyan Buckland   18 March 1865
letters.summary: Introduces Cholmondely Pennell of the Admiralty, who wants to speak to CD about a literary matter.

letters.title: From George Stewardson Brady   19 March 1865
letters.summary: CD’s statement inOriginthat clover is utterly dependent on humble-bee for fertilisation has been questioned by his friend’s evidence of visits by other insects. Asks CD’s opinion.

letters.title: To Frank Buckland   21 March [1865]
letters.summary: Has heard from Mr Pennell, and written to say too ill to see him. Would like to hear about skin between toes of otter hounds in comparison with other hounds.

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   22 March 1865
letters.summary:
Expresses pleasure at signs of CD’s recovery.

HWB’s work on the identification of species of the genusColobthea; relates the large number of modifications that occur in the sexual organs of closely allied species. Does not doubt that this contributes greatly to multiplication of species in nature.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   22 and 26 March 1865
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary:
JL’s MS at printer’s [Prehistoric times(1865)].

Apologises for failure to post letter.

letters.title: To Henry Denny   23 March [1865]
letters.summary:
Interested by HD’s information onaperea; CD had concluded that it was not the progenitor of domestic guinea-pigs.

Is unsure what HD means by "stock-dove"; properly this isColumba oenasand the domestic pigeon isC. livia.

Suggests that the Zoological Society might arrange for some specimens [unspecified] to be supplied from the Gardens.

letters.title: From Edward Perceval Wright   24 March 1865
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for subscribing to theCybele Hibernica.

Reports some observations made on the common buffaloes of India seen swimming and diving in 12ft of floodwater in order to crop the herbage beneath.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   25 March [1865]
letters.summary:
Mentions Miss Buckley’s information on roosting in trees [seeVariation1: 181 n.].

Refers to Duke [of Argyll] and his Lamarckian view of change.

Roosting habits and behaviour of pigeons in Egypt.

Criticises Herbert Spencer’s works.

Has finishedElements; comments on Laurentian stages.

Remarks on his health

and forthcoming work [Variation].

letters.title: To E. P. Wright   26 March [1865]
letters.summary:
Thanks for fact about the buffalo diving.

Asks whether the animal was a Bos or a Bubalus.

letters.title: To E. P. Wright   3 April [1865]
letters.summary:
Did not know that the Arnee had been called a Bubalus.

Thanks for information about shrimps.

letters.title: From W. B. Tegetmeier   27 March 1865
letters.summary:
Sends copies of theFieldcontaining all the pigeon articles [see4785].

Luke Wells will undertake engravings forVariation.

letters.title: To B. D. Walsh   27 March [1865]
letters.summary:
Comments on BDW’s papers ["On certain entomological speculations of the New England school of naturalists",Proc. Entomol. Soc. Philadelphia3 (1864): 207–49; "On insects inhabiting the galls of certain species of willow",ibid.3 (1864): 543–644]; much is new to CD.

Asks about wide-ranging insect genera,

Rocky Mt. wingless insects,

willow hybrids,

galls,

and other subjects.

letters.title: From Charles Cardale Babington   28 March 1865
letters.summary: University has at last provided room for a small zoological museum. The Philosophical Society might donate its collections to it, including CD’s fishes.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   28 March [1865]
letters.summary:
Arrangements for woodcuts forVariation.

WBT’s excellent article on crossing.

letters.title: From W. B. Tegetmeier   [29 March – 7 April 1865]
letters.summary:
WBT’s eye is getting on very well.

Enclosure comments on a note to folio 1 [of CD’s MS on variation], WBT thinks his works not worth citing: his edition of thePoultry bookwas never completed andProfitable poultryis out of print.

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   29 March 1865
letters.summary:
He encloses a portrait and asks for one of CD.

He has sent mimetic paper to B. D. Walsh.

Mentions work at Royal Geographical Society on N. Pole business [plans for an Arctic expedition, eventually postponed until 1875–6].

letters.title: To John Murray   31 March [1865]
letters.summary:
Has made progress [onVariation]. Hopes it will go to press in the autumn. Lists his needs for cuts to be made – altogether 50.

SupposesOriginhas ceased selling. Would be sorry to have labour of another edition. A new French edition is wanted.

letters.title: From E. P. Wright   31 March 1865
letters.summary: It isBos arniwhich dives for herbage and in so doing it also swallows many freshwater shrimps.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [April–May 1865]
letters.summary: Sends camera outlines of pollen. Thinks the red longstyled ones are more sterile than the yellow.

letters.title: From Clémence Auguste Royer[April–June 1865]
letters.summary: Notes on the caste system of India; its influences on form and habit.

letters.title: From Lucy Caroline Wedgwood   [April–May 1865?]
letters.summary: Observations for CD on oxlips, which she finds never grow near cowslips or primroses.

letters.title: From John Murray   1 April 1865
letters.summary: Will be proud to publish CD’s new work on domestic animals [Variation]. Will announce it as the complement of theOrigin. Advises on woodcuts; does not wish to limit number; agrees to CD’s suggestions for artists.

letters.title: To John Murray   4 April [1865]
letters.summary: Discusses proposed publication ofVariation.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   6 April [1865]
letters.summary:
Asks to borrowBotanische Zeitung(1860) with Friedrich Alefeld onPisum[pp. 204–5].

JDH should ask George Busk whether he knows a better doctor than William Jenner "for giving life to a worn out poor devil".

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   6 April [1865]
letters.summary: Instructions for Luke Wells about woodcuts forVariation.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [7–8 April 1865]
letters.summary:
Reforms at Kew.

X Club Dinner. H. B. Wilson and J. W. Colenso as guests.

Troubled by Lubbock’s going into Parliament – loss to science.

Has written to Busk.

SendingBotanische Zeitung.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   [7 April 1865]
letters.summary:
Fowl MS has arrived safely.

Sends pigeon MS for WBT’s perusal.

Further instructions for Luke Wells.

letters.title: From William Duppa Crotch   10 April 1865
letters.summary: Supports Atlantis hypothesis.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   10 [April 1865]
letters.summary:
Roguery at Kew.

Who wrote reviews of Linnean Society’sTransactions, of Planchon, and of subspecies inNatural History Review[Apr 1865]?

Is rereadingOriginfor second French edition.

letters.title: From John Scott   10 April 1865
letters.summary:
Comments on CD’sLythrumpaper [Collected papers2: 106–31]

and on H. Crüger’s orchid paper [J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)8 (1865): 127–35].

May take position at Calcutta Botanic Garden.

Regrets he cannot be elected to Linnean Society.

Pleased Asa Gray has commented on JS’s paper.

letters.title: From W. B. Tegetmeier   10 April 1865
letters.summary:
MS [of CD’s pigeon chapter] arrived safely.

Pigeon and poultry engravings [forVariation].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   12 April [1865]
letters.summary:
W. J. Hooker is unwell.

Bentham wrote on Planchon ["The ancient and modern floras of Montpellier",Nat. Hist. Rev.(1865): 202–25],

T. Thomson on subspecies ["Species and subspecies",Nat. Hist. Rev.(1865): 226–42]

and Greene of York on ["The Linnean Society’s transactions",Nat. Hist. Rev.(1865): 189–202].

JDH did the leader inGardeners’ Chronicle[(1865): 267–8, 291–2].

Delighted with CD’s calm opinion ofOrigin. Has same view of some of his own papers.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   13 April [1865]
letters.summary:
Strelitziahas arrived

but no books or bottles from G. H. K. Thwaites.

Hopes his own judgment aboutOriginis as good as Hooker’s about his own papers.

Strelitzia’s neat mechanism for exposing pollen.

letters.title: To John Murray   14 April [1865]
letters.summary: Thanks for advertisement, and pleased Murray likes title (ofVariation).

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   17 April [1865]
letters.summary:
On Lubbock’s plans.

Visited by Antoine Auguste Laugel.

Guessed right on Bentham’s "Planchon".

Much struck by Thomson’s article on nomenclature [see4812]; importance of this subject.

Sorry best scientists read so little; few read any long papers.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   19 April [1865]
letters.summary:
Congratulates AG on the "grand news of Richmond".

Still interested in dimorphism and would welcome new cases.

Working onVariation

and correcting proofs ofClimbing plants.

Would like seed of AG’s dimorphicPlantago.

Cannot understand how the wind could fertilise reciprocally dimorphic flowers.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [19 April 1865]
letters.summary:
Pleased at CD’s opinion of Thomson’s article.

Non-reading is great fault of the best school of English scientific men.

Opposed to Lubbock’s going into Parliament.

W. J. Burchell’s collections are coming to Kew.

letters.title: From Herbert Spencer   22 April 1865
letters.summary: Wonders whether CD might contribute, if possible, an occasional letter to theReaderto help in their effort to establish the journal.

letters.title: From Eliza Meteyard   25 April 1865
letters.summary: Sends CD the first volume of herLife of Josiah Wedgwood[2 vols. (1865–6)].

letters.title: From George Busk   28 April 1865
letters.summary: Has heard from Hooker that CD is very ill and asking for suggestion of a doctor to consult. Recommends A. B. Garrod as specialist in gouty complaints.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [1 May 1865]
letters.summary:
Feels a little better, but sickness continues.

Wants to borrow Robert Caspary’s paper on the union of buds inCytisus[see5012].

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   1 May 1865
letters.summary:
SendsCatalogue[of the collection of fossils in the Museum of Practical Geology(1865)], most of which was written in pre-Darwinian epoch [i.e., 1857].

Hears magnum opus [Variation] completely developed, though not yet born.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   2 May 1865
letters.summary:
On FitzRoy’s suicide.

The Lyell–Ramsay disagreement [on formation of lakes?].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   4 May [1865]
letters.summary:
On FitzRoy’s life and character.

Carl von Siebold’s cases of males and females of gall insects [True parthenogenesis in moths and bees(1857)]. Each sex produced on different plants.

Haeckel’s astonishing case of propagation in a Medusa.

letters.title: To Friedrich Rolle    6 May [1865]
letters.summary: Thanks FR for copy [of first number] ofDer Mensch[1866].

letters.title: To James Philip Mansel Weale   6 May [1865]
letters.summary:
Sends advice on naturalist matters.

W. H. Harvey’s work [with Wilhelm Sonder,Flora capensis(1859–65)],

and Robert Brown’s publication ["On the organs and mode of fecundation in Orchideae and Asclepiadeae",Trans. Linn. Soc. Lond.16 (1833): 685–745].

Writes of having seen in S. America a Hymenopteran with tarsi covered with pollen-masses ofAsclepias.

Interested in JPMW’s researches in South American caverns.

Mentions poor health.

Thanks for tracings.

letters.title: From Bartholomew James Sulivan   8 May [1865]
letters.summary:
Reports on the funeral of Robert FitzRoy.

His own health has deteriorated and he must give up his work.

letters.title: To B. J. Sulivan [9 May 1865]
letters.summary: Would rejoice to see BJS at Down, but explains that he can only spend short spells of time in his company if he comes.

letters.title: From Emma and Charles Darwin   13 May 1865
letters.summary: CD and ED bequeath an annuity of £50 to J. Parslow [the Darwins’ butler].

letters.title: From Asa Gray   15 and 17 May 1865
letters.summary:
Reports Lincoln’s murder.

The end of Civil War is in sight.

Must look at dimorphism inPlantago.

letters.title: To John Chapman   16 May [1865]
letters.summary: Asks JC to pay him a professional visit at Down to consider whether the ice treatment would apply to his case. Describes his sickness.

letters.title: From John Traherne Moggridge   17 May [1865]
letters.summary:
Sends fresh plants from France:Lythrum graefferi,Romulea.

Does CD knowPulmonariais dimorphic?

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [26 May 1865]
letters.summary:
All overworked at Kew.

Burchell collections enormous.

Lyell has sent MS ofPrinciplesp. 111 on changes of temperature. JDH thinks Lyell blunders and is out of his depth.

Charmed with E. B. Tylor’s book on man [Early history of mankind(1865)],

disappointed in Lubbock’s [Prehistoric times(1865)].

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   27 May [1865]
letters.summary:
Thanks forCatalogue.

Has had a bad month. Somewhat improved as a result of John Chapman’s ice-bag cures.

Asks THH to read MS on his hypothesisPangenesis. THH only man whose judgment on it would be final with him.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   29 May 1865
letters.summary:
Glad to read what CD sends. Any glimmer of light on those subjects is of utmost importance.

Quotes a letter from Haeckel on progress of Darwinism in Germany.

letters.title: From William Allport Leighton    29 May 1865
letters.summary: Describes the floral structure of the lupin and gives his observations on its pollination by bees.

letters.title: From B. D. Walsh   29 May 1865
letters.summary:
Discusses several subjects, including examples of "Unity of coloration",

the origin of gall-producing poison,

Wagner’s theory of viviparous larvae,

and stridulation in insects.

Sends a reference supporting CD’s statement inOriginthat flies check propagation of horses and cattle.

letters.title: From Edward Cresy   30 May 1865
letters.summary:
Impressed by Fritz Müller’s argument for natural selection in air-breathing apparatus of crustaceans ["The Darwinian hypothesis supported by observations on Crustacea",Ann. & Mag. Nat. Hist.3d ser. 15 (1865): 410–16].

Plans to visit CD.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   30 May [1865]
letters.summary: Thanks for THH’s willingness to readPangenesisMS. Thinks some such view will have to be adopted but it overthrows, in an uncomfortable manner, ordinary development.

letters.title: From Charles Kingsley   30 May 1865
letters.summary: Requests CD’s photograph.

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   31 May [1865]
letters.summary: Would like to call on CD for an hour or so before leaving London to settle in Bournemouth.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   1 June [1865]
letters.summary:
Bad month of sickness. John Chapman’s ice bag on spine.

Does not quite agree with JDH about Lubbock’s plagiarism charges. Lyell’s memory must have failed him.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   1 June 1865
letters.summary: MS arrived. Has glanced at it and sees he must put on his sharpest spectacles and best considering cap.

letters.title: From George Maw   1 June 1865
letters.summary: Reports a monstrous pig that looks like an elephant. It was born of a pregnant sow which had been frightened by a circus elephant. He offers the monster, which died at birth, to any London museum.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [2 June 1865]
letters.summary: JDH on the Lyell–Lubbock plagiarism controversy. His view of the true cause of Lubbock’s behaviour.

letters.title: To John Murray   2 June [1865]
letters.summary: There is no chance of publication [ofVariation] by autumn, because of CD’s illness.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   2 June [1865]
letters.summary:
Has lost time through illness.

Suggests an experiment to see whether the progeny of a pigeon cross are affected by a previous impregnation.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [4 June 1865]
letters.summary: Agrees with JDH on Lyell–Lubbock controversy except that Lubbock’s printed note does not seem to him insulting. Hopes JDH can heal the breach.

letters.title: To [Richard Kippist]   4 June [1865]
letters.summary:
Thanks for note; mentions borrowing and returning volumes. Orders a volume containing a paper by R. J. H. Dutrochet ["Recherches sur la volubilité des tiges de certains végétaux et sur la cause de ce phénomène",C. R. Hebd. Acad. Sci.19 (1844): 295–303].

Notes that his health is better.

letters.title: To George Maw   4 June [1865]
letters.summary: Believes GM’s reported monstrosity is not rare. Does not believe it resulted from the effect of the imagination of the mother on her offspring.

letters.title: To John Chapman   7 June 1865
letters.summary: Reports on progress of ice treatment.

letters.title: From Edward Cresy   9 June 1865
letters.summary:
Sends Fritz Müller citation as CD requested.

Huxley is boldly proclaiming his Darwinism at Royal Institution ["Methods and results of ethnology",Not. Proc. R. Inst. G. B.4: 460–3; alsoCollected essays7 (1894)].

letters.title: From Charles Kingsley   10 June 1865
letters.summary: Thanks for CD’s photograph.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   11 June [1865]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary:
JL’s book [Prehistoric times(1865)] is "most original".

Wishes him success in politics.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   12 June [1865]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Delighted at CD’s praise of his book [Prehistoric times(1865)].

letters.title: From Charles Kingsley   14 June 1865
letters.summary: CD’s paper on "Climbing plants" [J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)9 (1867): 1–118] has made nature come alive for CK.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [15 June 1865]
letters.summary:
Impressed by Tylor’s book [see4836].

Encloses admirable note from Huxley on Lyell–Lubbock affair.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [17 June 1865]
letters.summary:
Huxley’s capital, witty letter.

Charles Kingsley has written of his interest in "Climbing plants".

Health has been very bad.

letters.title: To Charles Kingsley   [17 June 1865]
letters.summary:
Did not think anyone would notice case ofLathyrus.

Recalls reading correspondent’s paper on great fir woods of Hampshire.

Thanks for photograph.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [after 17 June 1865]
letters.summary:
Recommends J. W. Kayes’ book [History of the Sepoy War, vol. 1 (1864)].

Wife improving.

Glad CD liked Huxley’s letter.

Not an admirer of Kingsley.

letters.title: From C. V. Naudin   18 June 1865
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for his paper "Climbing plants" [see4861] and for a photograph.

Hopes soon to send a copy of his memoir on hybridisation

and with it will forward a short note on the tendrils of the Cucurbitaceae.

letters.title: From W. B. Tegetmeier   20 June 1865
letters.summary: WBT will try experiment for CD if Mr Zurhorst cannot do it.

letters.title: From Henry Holland   25 June [1865]
letters.summary: Thanks for "Climbing plants" [see4861].

letters.title: From Thomas Rivers   6 July 1865
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for "Climbing plants" [see4861].

Encloses sketch of a climbing French bean.

Tells of a row of non-climbing haricot beans that in good season put out slender climbing shoots.

He has the peach almond in fruit this season.

letters.title: To B. D. Walsh   9 July [1865]
letters.summary: Thanks BDW for his interesting letter [4839] and for the case ofPanagaeus, a genus almost sacred to him since Cambridge days.

letters.title: From Charles and Emma Darwin to J. D. Hooker   [10 July 1865]
letters.summary:
Health very bad. All scientific work stopped for 2½ months.

E. B. Tylor’sEarly history of mankind[1865] impresses him.

Would like JDH’s opinion of last number of Spencer’s [Principles of]Biology[vol. 1 (1864)], especially on umbellifers. CD not satisfied with Spencer’s views on irregular flowers.

ED reports on CD’s health.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   12 July [1865]
letters.summary: Thanks THH for reading Pangenesis MS. Will read Buffon and Bonnet (as he does not want to republish their views) and will try to persuade himself not to publish.

letters.title: From M. T. Masters   12 July 1865
letters.summary:
Will forward Robert Caspary’s paper to CD when it is published ["Sur les hybrides obtenus par la greffe",Bull. Congr. Int. Bot. & Hortic. Amsterdam(1865): 65–80].

MTM is to become editor ofGardeners’ Chronicle.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   13 July 1865
letters.summary:
Studying moraines.

On Lubbock’s book [see4860], and Lyell’s apology. Recapitulates whole affair.

W. E. H. Lecky [Rise of rationalism in Europe(1865)] and other reading.

Spencer’s observations are wrong on umbellifers, his reasoning partially right.

Natural History Reviewis all but defunct.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [14 July 1865]
letters.summary: Wants to borrow money to buy stock in the bridge over the Itchen.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   16 July 1865
letters.summary: Did not intend to persuade CD against publishing Pangenesis. Will not take the responsibility, nor risk being made a horrible example 50 years hence.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   [17 July 1865]
letters.summary: Has read Buffon; whole pages are like his own. But CD is not converted to non-belief. There is a fundamental distinction between Pangenesis and Buffon. Fears he may not resist publishing it, but will be cautious.

letters.title: From John Scott   21 July 1865
letters.summary:
JS has now taken post of Curator of the Royal Botanic Garden, Calcutta.

Wishes to vindicate himself of the charge that he pursued his experiments at Edinburgh to the detriment of his work.

Apologises for poor quality of hisVerbascumpaper, which was written from his notes during the passage to India [J. Asiat. Soc. Bengal36 (1865) pt 2: 145–74].

letters.title: From Asa Gray   24 July 1865
letters.summary:
Is reading CD’s "Climbing plants".

The Civil War is ended; slavery is dead.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [29 July 1865]
letters.summary:
Was glad to read JDH’s article on glaciers of Yorkshire ["Moraines of the Tees Valley",Reader6 (1865): 70].

Readerarticle [6 (1865): 61–2] about English and foreign men of science is unjust.

Lubbock is now lost to science.

B. Verlot’s pamphlet on variations of flowers [Sur la production et la fixation des variétés dans les plantes d’ornement(1865)] is very good.

letters.title: To William Bowman   30 July [1865?]
letters.summary:
Thanks WB for his note, states that it will be taken care of on the publication of CD’s book [Variation].

Mentions loss of many months owing to illness.

Thanks WB for favour to CD’s son.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   10 August [1865]
letters.summary:
Has read and admires FM’s work on species.

Observations on Crustacea are good and original; asks FM to dissect and check some of CD’s observations on cirripedes.

Has sent "Climbing plants" paper [J. Proc. Linn. Soc. Lond.9 (1865): 1–118] and would like to sendOrchids.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   12 August 1865
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his paper on climbing plants. Lists the many genera that he has found in his area in a short period since reading CD’s paper. [See4881.]

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   [12 and 31 August, and 10 October 1865]
letters.summary: FM’s comments onClimbing Plants.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   15 August [1865]
letters.summary:
Gratified by AG’s praise of "Climbing plants".

Thanks forSpeculariaseed.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   16 August [1865]
letters.summary:
Condolences on W. J. Hooker’s death [12 Aug 1865].

His own health is bad.

letters.title: From F. H. Hooker   [17 August 1865]
letters.summary:
J. D. Hooker is ill with rheumatic fever.

W. J. Hooker is dead and was buried yesterday.

letters.title: From F. H. Hooker   [21 or 28 August 1865]
letters.summary: Reports on J. D. Hooker’s health.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   24 August [1865]
letters.summary: Sends an allotment of shares which he presumes are Emma’s.

letters.title: From Ellen Frances Lubbock   [27 August – 1 September 1865]
letters.summary: JL is in France with J. Steenstrup.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   31 August 1865
letters.summary:
Hopes CD has received his letter of 12 August.

Sends some new observations on climbing plants. [The observations are part of "Notes on some of the climbing-plants, near Desterro, in South Brazil",J. Linn. Soc. (Bot.)9 (1867): 344–9.]

letters.title: From M. T. Masters   September 1865
letters.summary: He will soon take over editorship ofGardeners’ Chronicleand hopes for CD’s continued support.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   1 September [1865]
letters.summary: Sends a "Lanc & York" [railway share?].

letters.title: From F. H. Hooker   6 September [1865]
letters.summary: They have left Kew to improve J. D. Hooker’s health.

letters.title: To Edward Cresy   7 September [1865]
letters.summary:
May his son George call for advice on his career?

CD has been ill for past four months.

letters.title: From Edward Cresy   10 September 1865
letters.summary:
Reading Carl Vogt [Lectures on man(1864)].

Vogt, though anti-Lamarck, is converted to Darwinism.

letters.title: From F. H. Hooker   13 September [1865]
letters.summary:
J. D. Hooker’s health is improving;

he has been offered the Directorship at Kew.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   18 September 1865
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for paper ["Climbing plants"].

Reports case of variation becoming at once hereditary – a crested blackbird with crested young.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   20 September [1865]
letters.summary:
Thanks for interesting letter on climbing plants.

FM’s view onAnelasmaseems probable.

Difficulty quoted by FM from A. Agassiz on embryology of Echinodermata is quite beyond CD.

letters.title: From F. H. Hooker   22 September [1865]
letters.summary: J. D. Hooker is recovering from his ill health.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   22 September [1865]
letters.summary:
Crests as inherited variations; domesticated birds.

Belief in value of travel journals.

Current reading.

letters.title: From Jeffries Wyman   22 September 1865
letters.summary: Discusses the climbing movements of plants and describes experiment to establish a mechanical explanation for double spiralling movements of tendrils.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [26 September 1865]
letters.summary:
On his reading: George Eliot,

T. F. Jamieson on Scottish glaciation.

Glad Lyell–Lubbock affair is over.

His grief over loss of father and child.

letters.title: From Julius von Haast   27 September 1865
letters.summary:
Expects to publish an account of his journeys soon.

Asks CD’s support for his Royal Society candidacy.

Goldfields he discovered are now being worked.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   27 [or 28 September 1865]
letters.summary:
Agrees with JDH on difference in grief over loss of father and of child. His love of his father.

TheReader.

Politics and science.

Health improved by Bence Jones’s diet.

[Dated "Thursday 27th" by CD.]

letters.title: To Samuel Butler   30 September [1865]
letters.summary:
Thanks SB for hisEvidence[for the resurrection of Jesus Christ(1865)], the main argument of which is new to CD. He particularly agrees with the preface.

Has been confined to his bedroom for the last five months.

letters.title: From Robert Swinhoe   [before 1 October 1865?]
letters.summary:
Reports that dogs caught in the act of sodomy have been attacked by their fellows, who mutilate the offender’s genitals.

Gives a description of the nature and occurrence of the wildBosof Formosa.

letters.title: From Samuel Butler   1 October 1865
letters.summary:
Autobiographical letter describing how, when he could not conscientiously take orders, he went to New Zealand and has now returned to England to study art.

Fascinated and delighted byOrigin

and is pleased that his pamphlet [Evidence for the resurrection of Jesus Christ] pleases CD.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   2 October 1865
letters.summary:
Has returned from holiday. Family news.

Concern over Hooker’s health.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   2 October 1865
letters.summary:
Information concerning improvements in theReaderunder new sponsorship.

Current reading and work [on pigeons forIbis1 (1865): 365–400, and catalogue of his collection of birds].

Book of travels postponed indefinitely.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   3 October [1865]
letters.summary:
Encloses letter [from A. R. Wallace?] about theReader.

Wants his opinion of a letter from Fritz Müller on climbing plants.

letters.title: From Charles Shaw   3 October 1865
letters.summary: Admiral FitzRoy’s daughters by his first marriage have been left without means. The largest subscription to the fund has been £100.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   4 October [1865]
letters.summary:
Has done nothing since 1 May. Slowly getting better under Bence Jones’s diet.

TheReaderhas been sold – would regret its failure as a newspaper for general science.

Pangenesis is recovering from shock it received from THH’s criticism.

letters.title: To Samuel Butler   6 October [1865]
letters.summary:
Thanks SB for letter of 1 October.

Returns the printed letter in which SB replied to the Bishop [of Wellington, N. Z.]; it amused him.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   6 October 1865
letters.summary:
On novels he has been reading: Eliot, Richardson, etc.

On Wallace, theReader, and anthropology.

letters.title: To Jeffries Wyman   8 October [1865]
letters.summary:
Experiments with string and elastic paper answered well.

Does JW know Ferdinand Cohn’s paper on contraction of stamens of certain Compositae [Edinburgh New Philos. J.n.s. 18 (1863): 190–4]?

Formerly made observations on movement in plants, but weak health has made it impossible to publish.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   10 October 1865
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for his photograph.

Sends a paper ["Über das Holz einiger um Desterro wachsender Kletterpflanzen",Botanische Zeitung24 (1866): 57–60, 65–9].

Believes species of sponge with different mineral spiculae are descended from a form with organic spiculae.

Reports observations on motions ofLinumstalks following the sun.

RegardsAnelasmaas a connecting form between cirripedes andRhizocephala.

letters.title: To Frederic William Farrar   11 October [1865]
letters.summary: Thanks for book on language [Chapters on language(1865)], which he hopes to read soon if his weak health permits.

letters.title: To J. T. Moggridge   13 October [1865]
letters.summary:
Discusses self-fertilisation in bee and spider orchids. Asks JTM to conduct experiment.

Comments on plates [see J. T. Moggridge’s contribution toFlora of Mentone and winter flora of the Riviera, including the coast from Marseilles to GenoaLondon 1866, 1871. Part II dated 1865; Part I, 1866].

letters.title: From J. T. Moggridge   14 October [1865]
letters.summary: Thanks for "Climbing plants".

letters.title: To Hermann Kindt   [17–23 Oct 1865]
letters.summary: Handwritten extract fromOrigin3d ed., p. 514.

letters.title: From Hermann Kindt   17 October 1865
letters.summary: Requests CD copy out a passage ofOriginand autograph it for publication.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   17 October [1865]
letters.summary:
Is sending FM’s two letters on climbing plants as a paper to the Linnean Society ["Notes on some of the climbing plants near Desterro, in south Brazil",J. Proc. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)9 (1867): 344–9].

Adaptations for pollination inCatasetum.

letters.title: From Edward Cresy   18 October 1865
letters.summary: How did CD handle his sons’ expenses at Cambridge?

letters.title: To Edward Cresy   19 October [1865]
letters.summary: Discusses income provided for sons at Cambridge.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   19 October [1865]
letters.summary:
AG’s article on climbing plants [Am. J. Sci.2d ser. 40 (1865): 273–82] is admirable and complimentary.

Reports Fritz Müller’s observations on climbers.

Experiments on dimorphism withMitchellaandPulmonaria.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   20 October [1865]
letters.summary: Sends Fritz Müller’s paper ["Notes on some of the climbing plants near Desterro, in S. Brazil",J. Proc. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)9 (1867): 344–9] to be refereed.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   22 and 28 [October 1865]
letters.summary:
Thinks Royal Society’s failure to honour W. J. Hooker may be due to small number of botanists on Council.

Interest in H. J. Carter’s papers inAnnals and Magazine of Natural Historyon lower organisms.

On Wallace; anthropology.

H. H. Travers’ paper on Chatham Islands [J. Proc. Linn. Soc. Lond.9 (1865): 135–44].

W. C. Wells’s paper of 1813 ["Essay on dew",Two Essays(1818)] anticipates discovery of natural selection.

letters.title: From Hermann Kindt   23 October 1865
letters.summary: Thanks for autograph [Autographic Mirror3 (1865) no. 262] and corrections of HK’s biographical sketch of CD [Autographic Mirror3 (1865): 82–3].

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   23 October 1865
letters.summary:
Returns a paper which he has looked over.

Cannot name the scrap ofStrychnoswith any certainty.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   24 October [1865]
letters.summary: Thanks for correcting Fritz Miller’s paper on climbing plants. CD will send it to Linnean Society.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   25–6 October [1865]
letters.summary:
Bad health during last six months has prevented scientific work.

News of family.

letters.title: From W. D. Fox   [before 26 October 1865]
letters.summary:
His second son [C. W. Fox] has a studentship at Christ Church, Oxford.

[Isolated fragments only.]

letters.title: From Alfred Newton   27 October 1865
letters.summary: Asks CD to support his candidacy for Professorship of Zoology at Cambridge. Since he has spent many years travelling, he is not well enough known at the University.

letters.title: To Alfred Newton   29 October [1865]
letters.summary: Declines writing testimonial for AN for the Cambridge Professorship in Zoology. The post requires expertise in comparative anatomy and histology, whereas AN’s work is on habits and colours of birds.

letters.title: From Alfred Newton   30 October 1865
letters.summary: CD need not apologise for not writing a testimonial for him. He knows comparative anatomy, although he has confined his publication to ornithology. Agrees that with a few members of the University a recommendation from CD would be harmful.

letters.title: From George Henslow   1 November 1865
letters.summary:
Has made observations on pollination mechanism inMedicago sativa[J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)9 (1867): 327–9], which his brother-in-law [J. D. Hooker] would accept. Wants to check that CD has not already made them.

Also sends interpretation ofSalvia.

His observations come from following CD’s generalisation inOrigin[p. 79] on necessity of out-crossing.

letters.title: To George Henslow   [2–5 November 1865]
letters.summary: Reports the results of an experiment to compare the weight of seeds produced in plants of [Medicago sativa] by self-pollination and by insect pollination.

letters.title: To F. W. Farrar   2 November [1865]
letters.summary:
Has enjoyed FWF’s volume [Chapters on language]. Had found Max Müller’s theory obscure and weak.

Believes FWF would come to agree with him on species if he studied general questions in natural history. To argue for immutability of species on the basis of geology resembles a wise savage in a nation with no books saying his language has never changed.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [3 November 1865]
letters.summary:
Kew affairs.

H. J. Carter’s observations are wonderful but want verification.

Skeptical of H. H. Travers’ observations.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   5 November 1865
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for the copy ofOrchidsand papers onLinumandLythrum[Collected papers2: 93–105; 106–31].

Intends to travel to the River Itajahy and will make observations on climbing plants. Is not sure whetherDalbergiais a winding plant.

CD has changed FM’s whole perception of nature.

CD has helped him to understand distribution of coastal flora.

The vegetation on Desterro is changing.

Louis Agassiz is seeking evidence against transmutation in the distribution of the fish in the Amazon.

letters.title: From F. W. Farrar   6 November 1865
letters.summary:
Grateful for CD’s approval ofChapters on language.

Is inclined to believe that the races of man were primordially distinct.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   6 November 1865
letters.summary:
Discusses "Climbing plants" and his own abstract of it.

CD should publish results of self-fertilising dimorphic plants.

letters.title: From George Henslow   6 November 1865
letters.summary:
Pleased CD confirms his observations onSalvia.

Spring action ofMedicagostamens described.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   11 November 1865
letters.summary:
Has heard from Huxley that CD has been ill.

Progress on his book [Generelle Morphologie(1866)] has been slow.

Has been named "ordentlicher Professor". Has 150 listeners in his lectures on CD’s theory.

Thanks CD for copy [of "Climbing plants"].

Sends his book [Beiträge zur Naturgeschichte der Hydromedusen, 1. Heft:Die Familie der Rüsselquallen (Geryonidae)(1865)] and two articles.

Calls attention to a new rhizopod from Nice.

letters.title: From B. D. Walsh   12 November 1865
letters.summary:
Acknowledges CD’s paper on "Climbing plants".

Mentions Asa Gray’s complimentary notice in Silliman’s Journal [Am. J. Sci. and Arts2d ser. 40 (1865): 273–82].

His difficulty in understanding how males ofDaphniaor any other genus can produce eggs. If there is no impregnation, how can there be sexual organs? Why call one form male and another female?

He has sent CD his paper on "the new Potato Bug".

Will soon send "On Phytophagi Species & Unity of Coloration". [phytophagic!?]

Complaints about practices of the English Post Office.

His current research and description of therationaleof his experiments.

letters.title: From Hermann Kindt   13 November 1865
letters.summary: Sends facsimile reproduction of CD’s handwriting [Autographic Mirror3 (1865) no. 262]. Requests a sample of Dr Erasmus Darwin’s hand and autograph for publication.

letters.title: To Eliza Meteyard   16 November [1865]
letters.summary: Asks her to send some specimens of Dr Erasmus Darwin’s handwriting for theAutographic Mirror.

letters.title: From Eliza Meteyard   17 November 1865
letters.summary: Returns 19 of the letters CD lent her, so that he can choose one for theAutographic Mirror.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   [20 November 1865?]
letters.summary:
John Brent [book?] has come, and he will send it.

Hopes CD will visit again.

letters.title: From James Shaw   20 November 1865
letters.summary:
Praises CD’s theory.

Comments on criticism of CD’s work by Duke of Argyll.

Beauty in nature as caused by sexual selection.

letters.title: To Hermann Kindt   22 November 1865
letters.summary:
Comments on the facsimile of his handwriting made by HK, and points out two errors in the letter press.

Encloses three letters written by Erasmus Darwin, and asks HK to return them to Eliza Meteyard.

letters.title: From Hermann Kindt   24 November 1865
letters.summary: Thanks for the three Erasmus Darwin letters. Two have been returned to Eliza Meteyard. HK has kept the one about the French gentleman for publication [Autographic Mirror4 (1866) no. 70].

letters.title: To James Shaw   30 November 1865
letters.summary:
Gratified that JS defends views ofOrigin.

Thinks beauty of flowers is solely to attract insects.

letters.title: To Robert Burn   2 December [1865]
letters.summary: Enters Francis Darwin at Trinity College, Cambridge. Encloses certificate from Alfred Wrigley and £20 entrance and caution money. Wants Francis to have rooms in College.

letters.title: From George Henslow   2 December 1865
letters.summary: Has been writing a review of CD’s "Climbing plants" forPopular Science Review[5 (1866): 55–65].

letters.title: From William Pollard Pattison   4 December 1865
letters.summary: An actuary wants to know whether the probability that a woman of English–Indian parentage will have a child after age 35 is the same as for a European woman.

letters.title: From Thomas Gold Appleton   5 December [1865]
letters.summary: Sends specimen of Californian fish that inhabits mountain lakes. The lakes often dry up and the fish have developed legs to enable them to wander in search of water.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   6 December [1865]
letters.summary:
Not surprised at delay of his book [Generelle Morphologie(1866)].

P. M. Duncan taking side of evolution.

Has received paper on Geryonidae ["Über eine neue Form des Generationswechsels bei den Medusen",Monatsber. K. Akad. Wiss. Berlin(1865): 85–94]. Had often speculated on whether such a case ever occurred in nature.

letters.title: To Henry Wentworth Acland   8 December [1865]
letters.summary:
Acknowledges HWA’s oration.

Discusses design in nature, Asa Gray’s views, and his own confusion.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   9 December [1865]
letters.summary:
Has forwarded FM’s MS to Max Schultze, but did not read it.

Movement of stem apex inLinum.

Haeckel’s paper on reproduction in certain Medusae.

letters.title: From Roland Trimen   13 December 1865
letters.summary:
Butterflies of Mauritius.

RT’sBonateapaper published by Linnean Society [J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)9 (1867): 156–60].

letters.title: To B. D. Walsh   19 December [1865]
letters.summary:
Discusses a variety of subjects:Cynips, galls, potato bugs,

maleDaphnialaying eggs.

HisPrimulaexperiment results differ from John Scott’s.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   22 December [1865]
letters.summary:
Is working one hour a day now, on illegitimate seedlings ofLythrumandPrimula.

Begins to doubt John Scott’s accuracy about primrose and cowslip.

Does JDH believe in Karsten’s denial of parthenogenesis ofCoelebogyne?

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [23] December 1865
letters.summary:
No one believes in Karsten.

Surprised by CD’s observations that illegitimate crosses within a species produce hybrid-like offspring.

JDH’s scepticism of Scott’s observations.

On proposing James Hector vs Julius von Haast for Royal Society; on learned society honours.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   24 December 1865
letters.summary:
Oliver says H. E. Baillon found stamens on female flowers ofCoelebogyne, but JDH and many botanists have never found any stamens.

Lyell wants to propose JDH for Copley Medal.

letters.title: To Julius von Haast   26 December [1865]
letters.summary:
Has been ill since April, so has not read all of JvH’s papers.

Encloses his photograph.

Has written to support JvH for Royal Society.

Samuel Butler [returned from New Zealand] is now established in London as an artist.

letters.title: From J. T. Moggridge   27 December [1865]
letters.summary: Sends a tin full ofOphrysby his brother, who should take about 60 hours to reach Down.

letters.title: From Robert Monsey Rolfe   28 December 1865
letters.deprecated: Robert Monsey Rolfe, 1st Baron Cranworth of Cranworth
letters.sender: Robert Monsey Rolfe, 1st Baron Cranworth of Cranworth
letters.summary: Sending cheque for Down parish charities.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [31 December 1865]
letters.summary:
Will explain about the so-called hybrids ofLythrumwhen they meet.

JDH should not be proposed for Copley Medal this year because Royal Society Council has so few naturalists on it.

letters.title: To George Howard Darwin   [1866]
letters.summary: Asks GHD what the chances are against squinting and non-squinting children coming alternately in a family of ten.

letters.title: To a local landowner   [1866?]
letters.summary: Requests that correspondent take some action regarding the state of horses on his farm. Robert Ainslie of Tromer Lodge, Down, was fined in 1852 following CD’s complaints.

letters.title: From Charles John Robinson   [1866?]
letters.summary:
Has a small living at Norton Canon.

Will visit Charles Whitley next week.

letters.title: To Henry Bence Jones   3 January [1866]
letters.summary: A report on his somewhat improved health.

letters.title: From Emily Catherine Langton to Emma and Charles Darwin [6 and 7? January 1866]
letters.summary: CL is aware that she is dying and so says her farewells.

letters.title: To Philip Lutley Sclater   6 January [1866]
letters.summary:
Discussion of ducks. CD asks for information on a domestic Chinese race about which Robert Swinhoe wrote to CD. Compares Chinese duck withAnas poecilorhynchaandBoschas.

Notes improvement in health.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   11 January 1866
letters.summary:
Comments on CD’s health.

Discusses origin of life and differentiation of principal classes of plants and animals.

DiscussesGenerelle Morphologieand its chapter on embryological development.

His lectures on CD’s theory.

Asks CD for larger portrait of himself and for several copies of the small photograph. Will send photographs of German scientists in exchange.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   11 January 1866
letters.summary:
Has read FM’s paper on sponges ["Über Darwinella aurea",Arch. Miskrosk. Anat.1 (1865): 344–53] with interest.

Has also read FM’s work on the metamorphoses ofPeneus[Ann. & Mag. Nat. Hist.3d ser. 14 (1864): 104–15], an interesting and important embryological discovery.

CD regards Louis Agassiz’s opinions as valueless.

letters.title: From Jeffries Wyman   11 January 1866
letters.summary: Has made observations on bees’ cells. Their dimensions are not constant, nor do single bees make single cells; each one is a result of co-operation.

letters.title: To Joseph Dalton Hooker   15 [January 1866]
letters.summary: In despair: has lost his copy of Verlot’s memoir on variations of flowers [Sur la production et la fixation des variétés(1866)]. Has JDH borrowed it?

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   16 January 1866
letters.summary:
Is in a mess with his correspondence and will get no assistance before 1 April.

Has agreed to give an address on the Darwinian theory at Nottingham [meeting of BAAS].

letters.title: To William Bernhard Tegetmeier   16 January [1866]
letters.summary:
What progress has been made with pigeon drawings forVariation?

Can WBT persuade Mr Zurhorst to repeat a pigeon experiment?

letters.title: To [James Samuelson?] 19 January [1866?]
letters.summary: CD is happy to sign photograph. He will only require one copy of the journal.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   20 January [1866]
letters.summary:
Sends copies of photographs of himself. Asks for photographs of German naturalists.

Comments on EH’s account ofProtogenes primordialis.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   21 [January 1866]
letters.summary:
Has found Verlot.

His sister [Emily Catherine Langton] is dying [d. 2 Feb 1866].

His stomach still very bad. Writes one or two hours and reads a little.

JDH is a wretch to remind CD of his coal-plant prophecy.

Glad JDH will give Nottingham lecture.

letters.title: From W. B. Tegetmeier   22 January [1866]
letters.summary:
Discusses pigeon and poultry woodcuts [forVariation].

WBT’s poultry book is at last in the hands of a solvent publisher [The poultry book(1867)].

letters.title: To Alfred Russel Wallace   22 January 1866
letters.summary:
Welcomes ARW’s paper on pigeons ["On the pigeons of the Malay Archipelago",Ibis1 (1865): 365–400].

Influence of monkeys on distribution of pigeons and parrots.

Asks ARW to explain a passage in his paper on Malayan Papilionidae [Trans. Linn. Soc. Lond.25 (1866): 1–71] on how dimorphic forms are produced. CD knows of varieties "that will not blend or intermix", but which produce offspring quite like either parent.

ARW’s remarks on geographical distribution in Celebes "will give a cold shudder to the immutable naturalists".

Presses ARW to work on his travel journal.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   23 January 1866
letters.summary: Sorrow about Mrs Langton. Has been haunted by death these six or eight years. Now cannot bear to look at children asleep in bed – a sight he once thought the loveliest thing in creation.

letters.title: From W. B. Tegetmeier   [after 24 January 1866]
letters.summary:
Thanks for the remittance.

Both WBT and Mr Zurhorst will repeat Zurhorst’s experiment to eliminate any chance of error.

Edward Blyth is writing on Indian cattle for theField[27 (1866): 55–6, 77].

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   28 January 1866
letters.summary:
Discusses exchange of photographs with German scientists.

Comments on attitudes of German scientists toward CD’s theory.

Names several scientists who exchanged photographs: Braun, Virchow, Leydig, and Dohrn.

letters.title: From Friedrich Rolle   28 January 1866
letters.summary:
Last fascicles of FR’s bookDer Mensch[1866] being sent.

Finds roots of human race in Negroes of Africa, Bushmen of South Africa and New Guinea, and short-headed peoples of south Asia.

Has translated natural selection asnatürliche Auslese.

Ludwig Rütimeyer active in developing the descent of mammals.

letters.title: From Frederic Ward Putnam   29 January 1866
letters.summary: Sends a paper onBombus["On the habits of some species of humble-bees",Commun. Essex Inst.4 (1866): 98–104].

letters.title: From Frederic William Farrar   1 February [1866]
letters.summary: Is seeking election to the Royal Society.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   1 February 1866
letters.summary: Thanks for photographs [of German scientists].

letters.title: To Friedrich Rolle   1 February [1866]
letters.summary:
Thanks for all five numbers ofDer Mensch[1866].

Had not known that Rütimeyer had written on modification of species.

letters.title: To Jeffries Wyman   2 February 1866
letters.summary: Obliged for JW’s information on variability of size of bees’ cells. Hexagonal cells not always work of several insects. W. H. Miller found great variability in thickness of cell walls.

letters.title: To F. W. Farrar   3 February [1866]
letters.summary: Will be pleased to sign FWF’s certificate for the Royal Society if he can send it to CD, who does not have the strength to go to London.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   4 February 1866
letters.summary:
Asks CD whether he knows of a medicine to check vomiting – for a friend dying from starvation as a result.

Duke of Somerset is looking for two naturalists for survey ship to Korea and Strait of Magellan.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   4 February 1866
letters.summary:
Looks forward to readingVariation.

Explains how two or more female forms occur in one species through selection. The physiological problem remains of how each produces offspring like the other without intermediates. Is not CD’s case of varieties that will not blend the physiological test of a species needed for "complete proofof the origin of species"?

"Travels" postponed.

letters.title: From F. W. Farrar   5 February 1866
letters.summary: Thanks CD for supporting his application to the Royal Society.

letters.title: From James Shaw [6–10 February 1866]
letters.summary: Memorandum of a meeting of the Natural History & Antiquarian Society held in Dumfries on Tuesday 6 February 1866.

letters.title: To Frederick Ransome   [6 February 1866]
letters.summary: Requests repayment of loan as FR promised last spring.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   [6 February 1866]
letters.summary:
ARW’s simple explanation of dimorphic forms is satisfactory.

On "non-blending" of certain varieties, CD thinks ARW has not understood him. He does not refer to fertility. He crossed two differently coloured varieties of peas and "got both varieties perfect, but none intermediate". Something like this must occur in ARW’s butterflies.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   7 February [1866]
letters.summary:
Discussion of Mrs Agassiz’s letter [to Mary Lyell, forwarded to CD] regarding S. American glacial action,

with comments on Bunbury’s letter on temperate plants.

Refers to opinions of Agassiz, David Forbes, Hooker, and CD on glacial period and glaciers.

Wishes he had published a long chapter on glacial period [Natural selection, pp. 535–66] written ten years ago.

Tells of death of his sister, Catherine, and other family matters.

letters.title: From Frederick Ransome   7 February 1866
letters.summary: Is compelled to ask for postponement of payment of principal. His invention is gaining ground. Will pay interest until payment is made.

letters.title: From Lionel Smith Beale   9 February 1866
letters.summary: Sends the numbers [of periodicals?] CD wished to see, and a list of other journals in which his papers have appeared.

letters.title: ToGardeners’ Chronicle   [before 10 February 1866]
letters.summary: Asks botanical readers to inform him "whether in those monoecious or dioecious plants, in which the flowers are widely different, it has ever been observed that half the flower, or only a segment of it, has been of one sex and the other half or segment of the opposite sex, in the same manner as so frequently occurs with insects?"

letters.title: From H. B. Jones   10 February [1866]
letters.summary: Sends a diet for CD’s flatulence.

letters.title: From Frederick Ransome   10 February 1866
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his kind expressions [of sympathy] and for his consideration. Encloses cheque for £5 interest.

letters.title: To Williams & Norgate   10 February [1866]
letters.summary:
Orders Richard Owen’sAnatomy of vertebrates[1866–8],

subscribes toAnnals and Magazine of Natural History,

and orders three back numbers ofMedical Times and Gazette.

letters.title: To James Shaw   11 February [1866]
letters.summary: Discusses beauty of birds and butterflies.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   13 February 1866
letters.summary:
Thanks CD forJournal of researches.

Insect genusElateris an exception to the rule that all luminous organs give out a green light.

Gives some observations on climbing plants at Itajahy.

His study of orchids has convinced him of the value of CD’s book.

letters.title: From James Shaw   14 February 1866
letters.summary: Reports instances of birds admiring their images in mirrors or on pictures.

letters.title: From Cuthbert Collingwood   15 February 1866
letters.summary: Going to Orient as naturalist aboard theRifleman. Offers CD his services.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   15 February [1866]
letters.summary:
Thanks CL for Hooker’s letter.

Discussion of Hooker’s views on glacial action and temperature with specific reference to S. America.

His squabbles with Hooker on transport of seeds via water currents,

temperate plants, and preservation of tropical plants during cooler period.

Expresses interest in seeing Agassiz’s letter.

letters.title: From John Traherne Moggridge   15 February [1866]
letters.summary: Is sendingOphrysplants marked as CD requested as wild or under cultivation. Discusses arrangements for a scheme planned for 1867 and his method for marking hisOphrysspecimens.

letters.title: To Cuthbert Collingwood   16 February [1866]
letters.summary: Regrets that his health prevents their meeting, but offers some suggestions for the expedition to the Malay Archipelago and coast of China: the search of caverns in the Malay Archipelago for fossil bones, deep sea dredging in the tropics, glacial action in any moderately steep mountains, means of geographical distribution, the history of domestic animals in these regions, and gestures and expressions of real savages as compared with our civilised expressions. [See5008and5011.]

letters.title: From Erasmus Alvey Darwin   17 February [1866]
letters.summary: Suggests two ways of financing what Susan will owe Catherine’s estate.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   19 February [1866]
letters.summary:
Division of Catherine’s estate.

Arrangements for EAD’s will.

Wishes CD would pay him another visit.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   [before 20 February 1866?]
letters.summary: Lyell calculates enviously that CD can do more work than any of the philosophers.

letters.title: From Cuthbert Collingwood   20 February 1866
letters.summary: Thanks for CD’s suggestions. [From CD’s notes on CC’s previous letter, these were (1) means of distribution; (2) domestic animals; (3) gestures of savages.]

letters.title: From Kent Church Penitentiary Society   [before 21 February 1866]
letters.summary: Appeal for funds for paying of the Society’s debt, and for an annual subscription.

letters.title: To Robert Caspary   21 February [1866]
letters.summary: Requests copy of paper read at Amsterdam Horticultural Congress, on graft-hybrids like that ofCytisus adami[see5018].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   21 February 1866
letters.summary:
Had Busks and Lyells to dinner.

Examines and criticises evidence for CD’s hypothesis that the glacial period was not one of universal cold. Physicists deny its possibility.

letters.title: From John Murray   21 February [1866]
letters.summary: Informs CD third edition ofOriginis exhausted. Proposes a new edition. Has CD any changes? Since demand is slowing up, proposes printing only 1250 copies and deferring payment of CD’s share until sales have repaid manufacturing costs.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   22 February [1866]
letters.summary:
Comments on errors [inOrigin] pointed out in C. J. F. Bunbury’s letters.

Mentions CD’s notes onDrimys,Fuchsia, and fossil mammals of Brazilian caves.

Sorrowful that his work must be put aside because Murray wants a new [4th] edition ofOrigin. Remarks on changes to be made regarding Organ Mountains and Agassiz’s glacial markings.

letters.title: To John Murray   22 February [1866]
letters.summary: CD is pleased [about need for a new edition ofOrigin] but even more grieved – for it will delay his next book [Variation]. Progress of natural history will make many changes necessary inOrigin. Nevertheless, proceeds with 32 more woodcuts forVariation.

letters.title: From John Murray   24 February [1866]
letters.summary:
Sends sheets ofOrigin[4th edition] for CD to correct [for 3d German edition?].

Still has 600 copies ofOrchids, but deficit reduced to £30.

Undertakes to pay two-thirds of profits of the [fourth] edition ofOriginas soon as one-half of the copies are sold.

letters.title: From Robert Caspary   25 February 1866
letters.summary: Sends papers on graft-hybrids ["Sur les hybrides obtenus par la greffe",Bull. Congr. Int. Bot. & Hortic. Amsterdam(1865): 65–80, and "Über Mischlinge, durch Pfropfen entstanden",Sitzungsber. K. Phys.-oekon. Ges. Königsberg6 (1865): 11–21].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [26 or 27 February 1866]
letters.summary:
Lyell wants to see JDH’s last letter [the part on glacial periods]. Lyell full of concern about astronomical causes of heat and cold on the globe.

Encloses letter from John Scott.

letters.title: From John Edward Gray   28 February 1866
letters.summary: Has received the larva of the batrachian. Outlines its affinities. Problems of batrachian systematics.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [28 February 1866]
letters.summary:
Refers to part of JDH letter on glacial period sent on to Lyell. CD will not yield. Cannot think how JDH attaches so much attention to physicists. Has "come not to care at all for general beliefs without the special facts".

His health is improved but not so good as JDH supposes.

letters.title: From W. D. Fox   [before 1 March 1866]
letters.summary: Would much like to see Dr Birchfield appointed superintendent of the new asylum at Woking.

letters.title: From Maxwell Tylden Masters   March 1866
letters.summary: As Honorary Secretary of the Botanical Congress he asks that CD’s name be listed as a member of its committee.

letters.title: From Frederick Smith   March 1866
letters.summary: Discusses the stinging habits of wasps and bees and whether or not they leave their sting in the wound.

letters.title: From Charles Lyell   1 March 1866
letters.summary: Feels sure that at times the globe must have been superficially cooler. Believes CD will turn out right with regard to migration across the equator via mountain chains, while the tropical heat of certain lowlands was retained.

letters.title: To Thomas Gold Appleton   2 March [1866]
letters.summary: The specimen is not a fish but the larva of some batrachian or frog-like animal. Has sent it to British Museum, which says it resembles the axolotl of Mexico.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [3 March 1866]
letters.summary:
Has returned memorial to Chancellor of Exchequer; thanks CL for his note.

Lengthy remarks on cool period. Did not know of CL’s interest. New facts in new German and English [4th] editions ofOriginwill be too late for CL’s use. CD’s ten-year-old MS on cool period is available.

letters.title: To Robert Caspary   4 March 1866
letters.summary: Thanks RC for photograph and for papers, which are of highest interest to CD. He is not fully convinced about the rose by RC’s graft-hybrid paper [Bull. Congr. Int. Bot. & Hortic. Amsterdam(1865): 65–80]. Still retains faith in his own view that no plant is perpetually self-fertilised.

letters.title: From Charles Lyell   5 March 1866
letters.summary: Surprised at Hooker’s introducing "so organic a change as a deviation in the axis of the planet" to explain the cold of the Glacial Period.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   6 March 1866
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for German translation ofOrigin.

Droughts over the summers have brought about changes in the numbers of plants and animals in the area. The small quantity ofOrchestia darwiniithat has survived the changes no longer includes two previously common male forms. Great changes also take place without such unusual physical conditions. The disappearance of a briefly abundant bryozoan in local caves has made way not for the return of original bryozoan inhabitants but for a completely new fauna.

letters.title: From George Henslow   8 March 1866
letters.summary:
Reviewing C. V. Naudin’s article ["Nouvelles recherches sur l’hybridité dans les végétaux",Ann. Sci. Nat. (Bot.)4th ser. 19 (1863): 180–203] forPopular Science Review[5 (1866): 304–13]. Requests references.

Proposes to visit Down on Easter weekend.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   8 March [1866]
letters.summary: Gives details of enclosed MS on cool period. Mentions Hooker’s opposed "axis of the earth" view. Causes of glacial period are beyond CD; "cannot believe change in land and water being more than a subsidiary agent".

letters.title: From Charles Lyell   10 March 1866
letters.summary: Comments on cool-period MS. Still believes geographical changes principal cause of former changes of climate.

letters.title: From George Henslow   12 March 1866
letters.summary: Thanks for references for his Naudin–hybridism paper [see5029].

letters.title: From Benjamin Dann Walsh   13 March 1866
letters.summary: On the "bullae" as constant, regular generic characters in Hymenoptera. Disagrees with Louis Jurine ["Observations sur les ailes des hyménoptères",Mem. Accad. Sci. Torino24 (1820): 177–214].

letters.title: From Rudolf Suchsland   16 March 1866
letters.summary: Asks, on behalf of his father, whether he might publish a new German translation of theOrigin, believing Bronn’s to be inadequate.

letters.title: From George Henslow   17 March [1866]
letters.summary: Forgot to thank CD for his praise of tendril paper [see4944].

letters.title: From George Henslow   [18–30 March 1866]
letters.summary: Cannot come to Down on weekend because of teaching duties.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [19 March 1866]
letters.summary: Asks to visit Down on Saturday.

letters.title: From E. Schweizerbart’sche Verlagsbuchhandlung   23 March 1866
letters.summary: Describes plans for new German edition ofOrigin[1867].

letters.title: To Robert McLachlan   23 March [1866]
letters.summary: Thanks for the paper on Sterrha (McLachlan 1865).

letters.title: From Albert Müller   28 March 1866
letters.summary: Oswald Heer [inDie Urwelt der Schweiz(1866)] agrees with CD that Swiss ants (Formica sanguinea) capture more slaves than do British ants. Does this contradict selection, since the British ants are exposed to harder conditions and a poorer fauna?

letters.title: To Albert Müller   28 March [1866]
letters.summary: Writes on slave-making ants; cannot explain why fewer slaves are caught in England than in Switzerland.

letters.title: From Robert Swinhoe   28 March 1866
letters.summary: Sends CD comb of the Chinese honey-bee, as requested.

letters.title: To Richard Kippist   31 March [1866]
letters.summary: Asks [Secretary] to list the proper titles of foreign societies of which he is an honorary member; he has mislaid diplomas.

letters.title: From Albert Müller   31 March 1866
letters.summary: Calls for more study of behaviour and less of classification to determine whether descent theory can bear the weight not [only] of reasoning but of fact. Hopes CD’s intended book [Variation] will help.

letters.title: From Harriet Lubbock   [April? 1866]
letters.summary: Local matters.

letters.title: From Rudolf Suchsland   2 April 1866
letters.summary: In response to a letter from RS’s father [translation enclosed] Schweizerbart has suggested H. B. Geinitz revise Bronn’s edition of theOrigin, but RS doubts he is suitable.

letters.title: To Rudolf Suchsland   4 April 1866
letters.summary: Cannot support another edition ofOrigin, so unable to send English pages. Suggests some of his other works that might be worth translating into German.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   4 April [1866]
letters.summary: Extensive discussion of Pangenesis in reply to JDH’s comments.

letters.title: From John Walton   [after 4 April 1866]
letters.summary:
Reports of a tooth found in the testicle of a horse.

Hares are very fleet in countries in which greyhound coursing is developed, slow in those in which no greyhounds are kept.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [5 April 1866]
letters.summary: Queries for John Smith [Kew curator] on crossing a cucumber variety.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker [6 April 1866]
letters.summary:
Reference to description ofBegonia phyllomaniaca.
