Thanks for the explicit account of Pangenesis. Thinks he now follows CD’s ideas but Pangenesis is very difficult and speculative.

Oliver has lost his little girl.

letters.title: From George Henslow   7 April 1866
letters.summary:
Sends copies ofScience gossipandThe leisure hour.

Enjoyed visit.

His criticism ofPrimulafertility referred to table 2 [Collected papers2: 56] where weight of seeds produced from good pods by long-styled homostylous cross and short-styled heterostylous cross are virtually identical.

letters.title: From James Samuelson   8 April 1866
letters.summary:
Pleased CD does not consider review of his works prejudiced [Anon., "Darwin and his teachings",Q. J. Sci.3 (1866): 151–76].

Supports gradual development of species over time.

Confused by the metaphysical view implied in the analogy between a creative power that has made new species and artificial selection governed by human reason (Origin, 3d ed., p. 492).

Doubts natural selection.

Cites his discussion of the origin of Infusoria [Proc. R. Soc. Lond.14 (1865): 546–7].

letters.title: From J. E. Gray   9 April 1866
letters.summary: Invites CD to dine and meet Alphonse de Candolle.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [9 April 1866]
letters.summary:
Sad about Oliver’s loss.

JDH’s reference to oddBegoniaat same time as an article about it came out inGardeners’ Chronicle[(1866): 313–14].

Is astonished that Pangenesis seems perplexing to JDH. Pleads guilty to its being "wildly abominably speculative (worthy even of Herbert Spencer)".

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   [9 and] 15 April [1866]
letters.summary:
Structure ofScaevolaand its fertilisation with insect aid.

Fertilisation ofAristolochia.

FM’s paper on climbing plants [see5146].

Is preparing new edition ofOrigin.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   10 April [1866]
letters.summary:
Has been offered proof impressions of Maguire’s portrait of CD.

Sorry to hear of CD’s "heap of maladies".

Georgina [Tollet?] wants to see the review in theQuarterly Journal of Science[3 (1866): 151–76].

letters.title: From William Reeves   10 April 1866
letters.summary: CD elected honorary member of the Royal Irish Academy.

letters.title: From Friedrich Rolle   12 April 1866
letters.summary:
Gustav von Leonhard and Hans Bruno Geinitz’sNeues Jahrbuch für Mineralogie, Geologie und Paläontologie[1862–79] unfriendly to CD’s theory.

Lists various German publications dealing with CD’s theory.

letters.title: To [H. B. Jones?]   13 April [1866]
letters.summary: CD’s plans have changed. He will be in London the following week and therefore able to call on correspondent.

letters.title: From J. E. Gray   13 April 1866
letters.summary: Tameness of whales and porpoises.

letters.title: To Henrietta Emma Darwin   [14–21 April 1866]
letters.summary: Discusses some observations on, and the fertilisation of,Ophrys.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   16 April [1866]
letters.summary:
AG’s second article onClimbing plants[Am. J. Sci.2d ser. 41 (1866): 125–30].

Fritz Müller’s observations on Rubiaceae.

New edition [4th] ofOrigin.

letters.title: To George Henslow   16 April [1866]
letters.summary: F. Hildebrand, in his recent article [Bot. Ztg.10 (1866): 73–8], describes what GH showed CD aboutIndigofera’s irritability.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [16 April 1866]
letters.summary: Asks how many plants are proper to New Zealand for new edition [4th] ofOrigin.

letters.title: From Rudolf Suchsland   16 April 1866
letters.summary: Reports that his father has given up the idea of publishing a new edition of theOriginbut points out that H. B. Geinitz of Dresden has, to date, only written against CD’s theory.

letters.title: To George Henslow   [before 19 April 1866]
letters.summary: Describes the pollination of broom by bees.

letters.title: From James Shaw   19 April 1866
letters.summary: Anecdotes about appreciation of beauty by animals.

letters.title: To B. D. Walsh   [19] April [1866]
letters.summary: CD has followed Lyell’s advice and avoided controversy overOriginbut encourages BDW to attack S. H. Scudder and others who argue foolishly or misquote him.

letters.title: From George Henslow   [after 19 April 1866]
letters.summary:
Thanks for explanation on relative fertility of homostyled and heterostyled crosses inPrimula. Sends an intermediate form with small stamens, but stigma only slightly above stamens.

Election as Botanical Lecturer at St Bartholomew’s Hospital.

letters.title: To Friedrich Hildebrand   20 April [1866]
letters.summary:
Is obliged to receive FH’s papers. The cases ofLopeziaandSchizanthusare new to him.

In 1860 CD watchedBombus lapidariussucking the flowers ofPedicularis sylvestrisand saw what FH has described.

Has not yet read the paper onSalvia.

letters.title: From M. T. Masters   20 April 1866
letters.summary:
Expects R. Caspary’s paper to be published soon.

Reports the conclusions of another of RC’s papers on the movement of tree branches due to cold [Bull. Congr. Int. Bot. & Hortic. Lond.(1866): 98–117]

and discusses a paper by H. Lecoq on the mountain flora of the Auvergne [Proc. Bot. Congr.(1866): 158–65]. He disagrees with CD on glaciation and its effect on geographical distribution.

letters.title: To Friedrich Rolle   21 April 1866
letters.summary:
Thanks for information about publications.

Hopes Hans Geinitz will take care in correcting Bronn’s translation [ofOrigin].

letters.title: To Rudolf Suchsland   21 April [1866]
letters.summary: Asks for additional details ofConfessions of a Metaphysician.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [22 April 1866]
letters.summary: Thanks for facts about New Zealand flora.

letters.title: To H. B. Jones   [23 April 1866?]
letters.summary: Had hoped to call, but cannot do so comfortably, so will HBJ call on CD instead, for a consultation?

letters.title: To James Shaw   [23 April 1866]
letters.summary: Thanks for sending facts on birds admiring themselves; mentions use in new edition [4th] ofOrigin.

letters.title: From Charles Wentworth Dilke   24 April 1866
letters.summary: Invites CD and wife to dine with Alphonse and Mme de Candolle.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [26 April 1866 – 14 December 1871]
letters.summary: CD asks if he can call tomorrow (Friday) at 9: 30, and offers to come on Saturday if that would suit CL better.

letters.title: From Robert Caspary   26 April 1866
letters.summary:
Coming to London for Botanical Congress. Requests interview.

Thanks for photograph.

letters.title: From William Robert Grove   26 April 1866
letters.summary: Sorry he missed CD when he called. Suggests a time he can call.

letters.title: To W. R. Grove   [26 April 1866]
letters.summary: Makes arrangements to call.

letters.title: To Thomas Rivers   27 April [1866]
letters.summary: Asks for racemes ofCytisus purpureus-elongatusandC. adamifor comparison, because Robert Caspary argues thatC. adamiis not a common hybrid.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [28 April 1866]
letters.summary:
NeedsAnnales de la Société d’horticulture de Paris7 (1830).

Asks that Oliver provide a reference for microscopical appearance and structure of a bud.

Was very well on first part of London visit.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [after 28 April 1866]
letters.summary:
Orchids.

Lyell has written to JDH about coal-plants of Melville Island.

Has glanced at first edition ofPrinciplesand has no doubt that Lyell meant the whole globe was cooler when land was massed at poles. JDH doubts this.

letters.title: From William Turner   [after 28 April 1866?]
letters.summary: Observations on a bird that used a stone to break open a snail.

letters.title: To William Robinson   [29 April 1866]
letters.summary:
Is sorry to have missed seeing WR.

Mentions some crossing experiments withNymphaeaandEuryalein which he would be interested, if WR ever had the chance to make them [seeCross and self-fertilisation, p. 365].

letters.title: To Robert Hunt   3 May [1866]
letters.summary: Encloses a sketch of the principal events in his life [for RH’s memoir on CD in Walford, ed.,Portraits of men of eminence(1863–7)].

letters.title: To Julius von Haast   5 May [1866]
letters.summary: Regrets that JvH is not on list of candidates for Royal Society. This year the Council of Royal Society is extraordinarily deficient in natural historians and geologists. Thinks JvH is sure to be elected another year.

letters.title: To William Robinson   5 May [1866]
letters.summary: Writes a line of thanks; includes instructions on procedure for crossing experiments.

letters.title: From Robert Caspary   7 May 1866
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for invitation. Solicitous of CD’s health. Will let Hooker decide whether CD’s health will allow his visit.

[Alexander] Braun in poor health.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   7 May 1866
letters.summary:
Thinks a new U. S. edition ofOriginis needed.

Gives observations on the climbing habits ofBignonia capreolata.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   8 May [1866]
letters.summary: Describes the floral structure of broom, particularly the form of the varying anthers. Encloses drawings of anthers and pollen.

letters.title: To John Gould?   [before 10 May 1866]
letters.summary: Asks for the name of a humming bird.

letters.title: From H. E. Darwin   [c.10 May 1866]
letters.summary:
Mogg [John Traherne Moggridge] wants to visit CD.

Self-fertilising orchids.

letters.title: From E. Schweizerbart’sche Verlagsbuchhandlung   10 May 1866
letters.summary:
Encloses letter from H. B. Geinitz, who declines to handle translation of new edition ofOrigin. Recommends Julius Victor Carus. Also suggests Gustav von Leonhard as translator forOrigin.

Discusses translation ofVariation.

letters.title: From John Gould   10 May 1866
letters.summary: Gives CD genus and species names of the singular humming-bird; distressed by specific name made necessary by revised laws of nomenclature.

letters.title: From J. T. Moggridge   10 May [1866]
letters.summary: Sends a box of orchids.

letters.title: To ?   10 May [1866?]
letters.summary: The apparent difference in arm lengths of compositors is due to a drooping shoulder. File-makers stand in a peculiar position and call one of their legs the hind leg.

letters.title: From William Erasmus Darwin   [7 May – 11 June 1866]
letters.summary: Sends flowers of buckthorn [Rhamnus catharticus] collected on Isle of Wight.

letters.title: From Friedrich Hildebrand   11 May 1866
letters.summary:
Sending his paper on tristyly inOxalis.

Cannot attend botanical congress, where CD will be vice-president.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [12 May 1866]
letters.summary:
Caspary wants to visit Down. CD would like to see him but dreads the exertion.

Pleased that JDH will get D.C.L. at Oxford.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   13 May 1866
letters.summary:
Refers to enclosure from Asa Gray

with whom he can talk calmly now that war is over. North had no right to resort to bloodshed.

Startled by CD’s attendance at Royal Society soirée.

Has asked E. B. Tylor to make up questions for consuls and missionaries, through whose wives a lot of most curious information [forDescent?] could be obtained.

Tying umbilical cord has always been a mystery to JDH.

John Crawfurd’s paper on cultivated plants is shocking twaddle ["On the migration of cultivated plants in reference to ethnology",J. Bot. Br. & Foreign4 (1866): 317–32].

R. T. Lowe back from Madeira.

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver    [after 13 May 1866]
letters.summary:
Gives CD some references to papers.

Reports improvement in his wife’s health.

letters.title: To William Ewart Gladstone   14 May 1866
letters.summary: Memorial to the Chancellor of the Exchequer from the fellows of the Royal, Linnean, Geological, and Zoological Societies of London, stating the importance of separating the administration of the national natural history collections of the British Museum from that of the library and art collections, and placing it in the hands of one officer, immediately responsible to one of the Queen’s ministers.

letters.title: To Friedrich Hildebrand   16 May [1866]
letters.summary:
Has forwarded FH’s paper on Fumariaceae to horticultural congress. Comments on its findings.

Discusses forms ofOxalis.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   16 May [1866]
letters.summary:
Glad to see Asa Gray’s letter.

Asks whether he may insert a sentence about Cape Verde alpine plants in new edition [4th] ofOrigin.

Fears "twaddle" may also be the word for his two chapters on cultivated plants. Asks for Crawfurd’s paper.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [17 May 1866]
letters.summary:
W. H. Harvey is dead. His loss to science.

Will get a copy of Crawfurd’s paper. It was such trash he tore his up.

His letter to Asa Gray was about his [JDH’s] proof that America will have an aristocracy from interbreeding of wealth, intellect, and beauty; and the lower classes, not having time for politics, will leave them to the aforementioned.

letters.title: From Thomas Rivers   17 May 1866
letters.summary: Will be sure to send theCytisusandLaburnumblooms when they flower.

letters.title: From George Henslow   18 May 1866
letters.summary:
Has written his Naudin–hybridism article [Pop. Sci. Rev.5 (1866): 304–13]. Would like CD to criticise proofs.

Will return books borrowed from CD.

letters.title: From Thomas Rivers   20 May 1866
letters.summary:
Sends a sketch of the haricot climbing the shoot of the plum-tree [see4866].

Hopes to see CD at the [Horticultural] Congress on Wednesday [30 May].

Sends data on movement direction ofWisteriashoots.

letters.title: From J. T. Moggridge   21 May [1866]
letters.summary:
Sends plants from France.

J. B. E. Bornet of Antibes, working in G. A. Thuret’s garden, findsCistushybrids do not follow the old dictum of having the mother’s foliage and the father’s habit. Bornet is engaged in long-term study.

JTM seeks invitation to Down.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   23 May 1866
letters.summary:
Thanks for information on orchids

and facts on coastal flora and fauna.

Asks FM to look out for dimorphic aquatic and marsh plants.

Has read pamphlets "in our favour" by Carl v. Nägeli and Oscar Schmidt.

letters.title: From Robert Caspary   25 May 1866
letters.summary: Plans to come to Down on 27 May.

letters.title: From J. T. Moggridge   25 May [1866]
letters.summary: Accepts invitation for 23 June.

letters.title: From John Murray   25 May [1866]
letters.summary: Printing [of 4th edition ofOrigin] nearly complete. Will print 1000 copies which, at present rate of sale, may last three to five years.

letters.title: To John Murray   28 May [1866]
letters.summary:
Has corrected and improvedOrigin.

Now hopes to make real progress [onVariation].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   29 May 1866
letters.summary: JDH sends a list of the principal confirmatory evidences of CD’s theory which he has prepared at W. R. Grove’s request for Nottingham speech ["Presidential address",Rep. BAAS26 (1866): liii–lxxxi].

letters.title: From John Murray   30 May [1866]
letters.summary: On reflection, in view of the extensive additions CD has made toOrigin, has decided to print 1500 copies [of 4th ed.].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   31 May [1866]
letters.summary:
Comments on JDH’s list – very good, butOrchidsandPrimulapaper have too indirect a bearing to be worth mentioning. TheEozoonis a very important fact and to a much lesser degree theArchaeopteryx. Müller’sFür Darwin[1864] perhaps the most important contribution.

CD has forgotten to mention Bates on variation and JDH’s Arctic paper ["Distribution of Arctic plants",Trans. Linn. Soc. Lond.23 (1862): 251–348] in new edition ofOrigin.

Now finds that Owen claims to be originator of natural selection.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [31 May 1866]
letters.summary:
No enclosure in JDH’s last letter.

Would like to be amused "for my stomach & the whole Universe is this day demoniacal in my eyes".

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [2 June 1866]
letters.summary: He is not grieved at CD’s omissions of his [JDH’s] work [fromOrigin, 4th ed.]. It proves nothing – claims only to be illustration of using CD’s methods.

letters.title: From Alphonse de Candolle   3 June 1866
letters.summary:
In London for the Botanical Congress; regrets missing CD.

Lyell and CD have mistaken H. Lecoq’s position on glaciers. He has not denied the possibility of a glacial period, only that decreased temperature is needed for their extension.

Recommends F. J. Ruprecht on vegetable detritus in the black earthchernozemof Russia.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [4 June 1866]
letters.summary:
Thanks for Asa Gray’s letter, enclosed.

Knew JDH would not care about omissions but was vexed at his own forgetfulness.

letters.title: To William Turner   5 June [1866]
letters.summary: Thanks for WT’s papers, especially ["The present aspect of the doctrine of cellular pathology",Edinburgh Med. J.8 (1863): 873–97].

letters.title: From Thomas Rivers   6 June 1866
letters.summary: Sends blooms ofCytisus purpureus-elongatus.

letters.title: To Thomas Rivers   8 June [1866]
letters.summary: Examined theCytisusand forwarded to Caspary. TheC. adamicase "gets more and more perplexing", asks for report ifCytisus purpureus-elongatusproduces any pods.

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   9 June 1866
letters.summary:
Identifies a plant.

CD will not find Hermann Schacht’sLehrbuch[der Anatomie und Physiologie der Gewächse(1856–9)] at the Linnean Society Library.

letters.title: From Robert Caspary   [after 9 June 1866]
letters.summary: Data on good and bad pollen-grain yields of different species. Sends sketches of two maleRhamnus catharticusflowers [seeForms of flowers, p. 294].

letters.title: From George Henslow   11 June [1866]
letters.summary:
Sends proofs [of "On hybridization among plants",Pop. Sci. Rev.5 (1866): 304–13].

Regrets delay in returning CD’s books.

Encourages CD to make "disparaging remarks".

letters.title: To George Henslow   12 June [1866]
letters.summary:
Returns proofs of GH’s paper ["On hybridization among plants",Pop. Sci. Rev.5 (1866): 304–13] with his criticisms. Prefers that GH not state that CD has read the proofs.

Does C. V. Naudin really say that ovules (not seed) of hybridLuffaandCucumisare imperfect?

letters.title: To Carl Wilhelm von Nägeli   12 June [1866]
letters.summary:
Comments on CWvN’sDie Entstehung und Begriff[der Naturhistorischen Art(1864)].

Discussion of beauty of flowers in new edition ofOriginnot based on CWvN’s article.

Comments on CWvN’s argument that flower structures are not due to natural selection.

letters.title: From George Henslow   [13 or 14 June 1866]
letters.summary:
Thanks for criticism of proofs of his paper [see5117].

Not sure whether CD believes in reversion and would like a positive statement as this is the one point C. V. Naudin especially observed. Naudin offers his remarks on ovules as a matter to be proved ["Nouvelles recherches sur l’hybridité",Nouv. Arch. Mus. Hist. Nat.1 (1865): 25–176].

letters.title: From J. T. Moggridge   14 June [1866]
letters.summary: Will take earlier train to Down.

letters.title: To George Henslow   15 [June 1866]
letters.summary:
CD believes most strongly in reversion. J. G. Kölreuter’s, K. F. v Gärtner’s, and some of Charles Naudin’s cases leave no doubt in his mind. Forgets whether Herbert gave cases but in conversation he certainly believed in it. Thinks Gärtner is right to say reversion occurs only rarely in plant hybrids which have not been cultivated. [See5120.]

Variation

letters.title: To Andrew Crombie Ramsay   15 June [1866]
letters.summary: Thanks forGeological survey of North Wales[1866]. Longs to return to the mountains with which he was once familiar, but did not understand.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [18 June 1866]
letters.summary: Sends some specimens of three kinds of buckthorn.

letters.title: From George Maw   18 June 1866
letters.summary: In response to CD’s request for bud-sports, he sends a piece of a fern-leaved beech.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   19 [June 1866]
letters.summary: Different forms of flowers ofRhamnus.

letters.title: From George Henslow   19 June 1866
letters.summary:
Has altered paper according to CD’s comments.

Returns books.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   20 June [1866]
letters.summary: ThinksRhamnusis a case of a dimorphic plant that has become dioecious.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   21 June [1866]
letters.summary: "It [Rhamnus catharticus?] is certainly a case of dimorphic become dioecious."

letters.title: To George Maw   21 June [1866]
letters.summary: Thanks GM for a specimen; it is a sport with which he is already familiar.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   22 June [1866]
letters.summary: Polymorphism inRhamnus.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [23 June 1866]
letters.summary: Ovules of males of two forms [ofRhamnus catharticus?] are abortive and both females have incomplete stamens.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [24 June 1866]
letters.summary: Polymorphic flowers ofRhamnus[seeForms of flowers, p. 294].

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin [26–8 June 1866]
letters.summary: He has had a great struggle with Buckthorn, and would like CD to see the measurements some time.

letters.title: From Bartholomew James Sulivan   27 June 1866
letters.summary:
Reports on his health.

Discusses a surveying expedition under Richard Charles Mayne on which his son will be Second Lieutenant; hopes to arrange for them to excavate some bones in the Falklands.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   29 June [1866]
letters.summary: Sends flowers of the differing kinds [ofRhamnus?] with observations.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   30 [June 1866]
letters.summary: Cuttings have arrived. Different flower forms [inRhamnus?].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   30 June [1866]
letters.summary:
Has heard from B. J. Sulivan about the fossils at Gallegos, Patagonia. Would be a great haul for palaeontology if Duke of Somerset would encourage Capt. Mayne to collect them [on survey of Magellan Strait].

Tells JDH of a new map of world that he might use in his lecture [on "Insular floras", BAAS, 1866,J. Bot. Br. & Foreign5 (1867): 23–31;Gard. Chron.(1867): 6, 27, 50, 75].

Impressed by H. Spencer’s last number, but each suggestion would require years of work to be of use to science.

letters.title: To George Bentham   [July–September 1866]
letters.summary: Asks GB to consider whether it is necessary for the Linnean Society to be so strict about the number of books members may borrow.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   1 July [1866]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Returns [Fritz?] Müller’s work [probablyFür Darwin(1864)]. It is a remarkable memoir.

letters.title: To the Lords of the Admiralty   [2–4 July 1866]
letters.summary: Petition earnestly requesting that a ship surveying the Strait of Magellan collect fossil bones in the south of Patagonia.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   2 July 1866
letters.summary: Suggests a memorial from Huxley, Murchison, and other geologists on the Gallegos fossils. He will speak privately to Duke of Somerset.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   2 July 1866
letters.summary: Lengthy analysis of sources of misunderstanding of natural selection. Advocacy of Spencer’s term "survival of the fittest" instead of "Natural Selection". ARW urges CD to stressfrequencyof variations.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   3 July 1866
letters.summary:
Is trying to arrange a new American edition ofOrigin.

Gives notes onPassiflora acerifolia[on cover].

letters.title: To Thomas Henry Huxley   4 July [1866]
letters.summary: Sends a draft of memorial to Admiralty [to be signed by geologists and palaeontologists] requesting that an expedition to survey Strait of Magellan collect fossils discovered by Admiral B. J. Sulivan [see5142].

letters.title: From W. B. Tegetmeier   4 July 1866
letters.summary: All the blocks [forVariation] are now engraved except the rock-dove.

letters.title: From Frederick Currey   5 July 1866
letters.summary: Fritz Müller’s paper ["Notes on climbing plants"] is about to appear [inJ. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)9 (1867): 344–9]. Would CD approve of figures being reduced in size?

letters.title: From J. T. Moggridge   5 and 6 July [1866]
letters.summary: Sends onion and mint seeds.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   5 July [1866]
letters.summary:
CD considers "the survival of the fittest" as alternative term to "Natural Selection". Reflections upon misunderstanding and his own ambiguity.

Health improved; can now work "some hours daily".

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   6 July 1866
letters.summary: Has taken memorial to G. H. Richards, the Hydrographer. He favours the proposal and will instruct Capt. Mayne. THH will communicate with Dr Cunningham, the naturalist for the expedition.

letters.title: From George Stacey Gibson   7 July 1866
letters.summary: Asks CD if he can explain the results of an experiment that produced barley from oats that had been cut down to prevent their flowering.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   9 July [1866]
letters.summary: WBT’s fowls’ skulls are being engraved; will see pigeon illustration proofs when he can.

letters.title: From Charles Kingsley   12 July 1866
letters.summary: Asks for CD’s opinion of the manner of migration of the eye of flatfish.

letters.title: To John Murray   15 July [1866]
letters.summary: 4th edition ofOriginwill soon be bound. Suggests sending copies to scientific periodicals that might notice it. Hopes JM will specify in advertisements that the work is corrected and enlarged. Hopes pages will be cut. Only insanity accounts for this not being done in England.

letters.title: From Searles Valentine Wood   16 July 1866
letters.summary: Barley growing from old oat stalks.

letters.title: From Julius von Haast   17 July 1866
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for photograph.

JvH will send his notes on origin of species;

he is now writing a paper on glacier period of the New Zealand west coast, and his account of the highly glaciated headwater region of the Rakaia River is being printed.

letters.title: From Alfred Hanson   17 July 1866
letters.summary: About duties in consequence of the death of Catherine Langton,néeDarwin.

letters.title: From B. D. Walsh   17 July 1866
letters.summary:
On H. A. Dubois’ attack on "Darwin, Huxley and Lyell"

and H. J. Clark’sMind in nature[1865].

BDW’s work [on Cynipidae].

letters.title: From Asa Gray   18 July 1866
letters.summary: Appleton’s cannot alter their plates so as to reproduce revised work [Origin, 4th ed.]. Has made it clear that CD could not do otherwise than object strenuously to course they intend to pursue, and has asked them to return the sheets. Wishes CD’s publisher would supply U. S. market with large numbers of copies, as the English edition could well compete with any American one. Encloses [statement of sales of U. S. edition ofOriginto 1 February 1866].

letters.title: From John Murray   18 July [1866]
letters.summary:
Proposes to delay issue [of 4th ed. ofOrigin] until November to obtain better market conditions. Now printing 1250 copies.

Explains practice of not cutting pages is due to propensity of English public to read books without buying them.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   21 [July 1866]
letters.summary: Asks help in naming a lupin, enclosed. Nurseryman said parties who make experiments should find the names. He might have added "and not trouble their friends".

letters.title: To Christian Gottfried Ehrenberg   22 July [1866?]
letters.summary: Thanks CGE for two papers and for his assistance of many years ago.

letters.title: To Friedrich Hildebrand   22 July [1866]
letters.summary: Points out an error in proof-sheets of Hildebrand’s paper onCorydalis cava(Hildebrand 1866d) and suggests some improvements to the English.

letters.title: From John Murray   23 July [1866]
letters.summary: Will attend to CD’s wishes regarding six presentation copies [ofOrigin, 4th ed.] for England and America.

letters.title: From Friedrich Hildebrand   24 July 1866
letters.summary:
Assures CD of his belief in descent from his first reading ofOrigin.

Describes a case of dichogamy.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [24 July 1866]
letters.summary:
Working on "Insular floras" lecture for BAAS Nottingham meeting [see5135].

Puzzled at distribution of Madeiran and Canaries plants and insects.

Supports Forbes’s Atlantis hypothesis [see956], which he has reread and to which he will allude.

Wollaston disappointing on Madeiran insects.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   30 July [1866]
letters.summary: His reasons for rejecting Atlantis hypothesis connecting Madeira and Canary Islands.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   31 July 1866
letters.summary:
Questions for his lecture on "Insular floras".

Comments on CD’s criticism of Atlantis. Has no fixed opinion on continental extensions. Great objections to hypotheses of CD and Forbes: botanical to CD’s; geological to Forbes’s. Will point out that natural selection is necessary to both hypotheses.

letters.title: To Casimir de Candolle   1 August [1866]
letters.summary:
Thanks CdeC for hisMémoire sur la famille de Piperacées[1866]. Regrets he has not sufficient knowledge of botany to understand all the points discussed.

Sorry his health prevented his attending [Botanical] Congress and meeting CdeC’s father.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   2 August [1866]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Has read abstract of JL’s paper ["On the present state of archaeological science",Athenæum21 July 1866, pp. 79–82] and praises it.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   2 August 1866
letters.summary: Gives some observations on orchids and on some plants which seem to be dichogamous.

letters.title: From W. B. Tegetmeier   2 August 1866
letters.summary:
Encloses feathers from a diseased hen which has assumed cock plumage.

Forwards proofs of the engravings forVariation.

letters.title: To ?   2 August [1866]
letters.summary:
Has not seen K. E. von Baer’s paper ["Über Papuas und Alfuren",Mem. Acad. Imp. Sci. St.-Pétersbourg (Sci. Nat.)8 (1859): 269–346], but has read extract.

Knew of case of hairy and toothless family through John Crawfurd,Journal of an embassy from the Governor-General of India[2d ed. (1834)].

Working on causes of variability.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   3 and 4 August [1866]
letters.summary:
Answers JDH’s questions on connection of SE. England and continent,

on the effect of breaking the Isthmus of Panama,

and on Madeira flora as remnant of Tertiary flora.

Cautionary remarks for JDH on his "Insular floras" speech, designed to strengthen case of "occasional migration" theory.

letters.title: From J. T. Moggridge   3 August [1866]
letters.summary: Sends packet ofOnonis columnaeseed and references to the species.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   4 August [1866]
letters.summary:
Thanks for AG’s trouble about new edition ofOrigin.

Will be printing his new book [Variation] at the end of the year.

[Forwarded by AG, with covering note, to Mr Fields of Ticknor & Fields.]

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   4 August 1866
letters.summary:
Alexander Beatson mentions a bird in considerable numbers on St Helena which appears to contradict CD’s statement inJournal of researchesthat only introduced land birds exist there.

The Azores flora and fauna tell heavily against Atlantis joining them with America and against transoceanic migration from America.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   4 August 1866
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: ReturnsPrimulapaper [Collected papers2: 45–63].

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   4 August [1866]
letters.summary:
Comments on pigeon and poultry woodcuts.

Observations and queries on poultry.

letters.title: From W. B. Tegetmeier   [after 4 August 1866]
letters.summary: Alterations to the woodcuts of poultry forVariation.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   5 August [1866]
letters.summary:
CD defends his view of land birds on St Helena.

Explains why he would not expect American plants on the Azores.

It makes him miserable that he and JDH look at everything so differently.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [6 August 1866]
letters.summary:
Will do justice to CD’s objections to continental extension theory.

CD misunderstood his question about Isthmus.

Responds to CD’s other points about Madeira and the Azores.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   7 August 1866
letters.summary:
Appleton’s will not print a new edition ofOrigin.

AG has read sheets of new English edition [4th] and is much pleased by the passage on Richard Owen in the historical sketch.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   7 August 1866
letters.summary: Is attempting to sum up the two theories impartially and must raise all the difficulties with each. More on his differences with CD.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   8 and 9 August [1866]
letters.summary: Notes on examining Rhamnus Frangula

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   8 August [1866]
letters.summary: Admits that occasional transport is not a well-established hypothesis but believes it more probable than continental extension as an explanation for the stocking of islands.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   9 August 1866
letters.summary:
More on continental extension vs transport [or migration] hypothesis. New questions raised. On Madeira, why were insects and plants changed so much, birds hardly at all?

Erratic boulders of the Azores.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   10 August [1866]
letters.summary:
Thanks WBT for help with woodcuts [forVariation].

Has returned WBT’s curious feathers.

letters.title: ToGardeners’ Chronicle   [before 11 August 1866]
letters.summary: Asks readers to examine the flowers ofOxalis boweito observe where the summits of the branching stigmas stand with respect to the two sets of anthers. In CD’s plants the stigmas stand beneath the lower anthers, but he believes two other forms exist: long-styled and mid-styled. Would be grateful for flowers of these types so he can fertilise them and obtain seed.

letters.title: ToGardeners’ Chronicle   [before 11 August 1866]
letters.summary: Describes the difficulties of crossing papilionaceous flowers. Believes the lack of success is a consequence of the need for early castration and successive applications of pollen on the stigma. Gives details of a method he has used to cross such flowers successfully.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   12 August [1866]
letters.summary: Will be glad to see JDH at Down.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [17 August 1866]
letters.summary: Hopes to arrive with MS of "Insular floras" on Saturday.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   18 August [1866]
letters.summary:
Comments on sheet of EH’sGenerelle Morphologie[1866]. In emphasising divergence of character EH shows his clear understanding of CD’s views. It was years before CD saw necessity of divergence.

Interested in Carl Claus [Copepodenfauna von Nizza(1866)].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   18 August 1866
letters.summary:
Returns two volumes ofFelix Holt[George Eliot (1866)]

and the Coddington [lens].

John Smith will sendDrosera.

Nationreports that Louis Agassiz holds that the Amazon Valley was formed since the glacial epoch.

letters.title: From William Darwin Fox   20 August [1866]
letters.summary: Is looking for CD’s book [Variation]; does not know whether it is yet published.

letters.title: To B. D. Walsh   20 August [1866]
letters.summary:
On various subjects: Dana’s misquotations,

H. J. Clark’s bookMind in nature[1865],

BDW’sCynipsexperiments, galls,

Balbiani’s paper on aphids ["Sur la reproduction et l’embryogénie des pucerons",C. R. Hebd. Acad. Sci.62 (1866): 1231–4, 1285–9, 1390–4].

Claus and other Germans testing CD’s views of variability in common lower animals.

letters.title: To W. A. Knight   22 August [1867]
letters.summary: Will not attend the British Association meeting at Dundee.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   23 August [1866]
letters.summary:
Thanks for observations on orchids.

FM’s paper on climbing plants [see5146]; CD has received proofs.

Carl Claus’s pamphlet on copepods [Die Copepodenfauna von Nizza(1866)].

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   24 August [1866]
letters.summary:
Family news. Describes [final] illness of Susan Darwin [d. 3 Oct 1866]. CD’s health better.

Making rapid progress onVariation.

Has heard of hybrids between moths mentioned by WDF.

Work on [4th] edition ofOriginhas delayedVariation.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   27 August 1866
letters.summary:
Hopes to make good arrangement for publication of CD’sVariation.

Agassiz claims to have proved all of America was covered with unbroken ice during the glacial period.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [28 August]1866
letters.summary: BAAS lecture on "Insular floras" [see5135] went well.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   30 August [1866]
letters.summary:
Pleased by JDH’s success. JDH gives argument for occasional transport with perfect fairness.

W. R. Grove’s address [see5201] good, but is disappointed that species part was so general.

letters.title: From W. R. Grove   31 August 1866
letters.summary: Responds to CD’s criticism of his handling of adaptation theory [inRep. BAAS26 (1866): liii–lxxxi].

letters.title: To Robert Swinhoe   [September 1866]
letters.summary:
Hooker’s lecture to BAAS ["Insular floras"] was capital,

but hears Wallace’s paper [Address to Anthropology Section,Rep. BAAS36 (1866): 93–4] was best.

Pleased RS continues zealous work for natural history.

CD considers the report that N. American antelopes’ horns are intermediate between hollow and solid horns of ruminants to be one of the more curious facts he has lately heard of with respect to higher animals [C. A. Canfield, "On the habits of the prongbuck",Proc. Zool. Soc. Lond.(1866): 105–11].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [4 September 1866]
letters.summary:
On his "Insular floras" lecture.

Huxley’s success as President of Section.

D. W. R. Grove’s address. Grove left Darwinism to JDH after "sounding the charge".

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   8[–9] September [1866]
letters.summary:
Disappointed to put off CL’s visit because of illness of CD’s sister [Susan], but hopes to see him in October.

Thanks for lending pamphlet [L. Agassiz,Geology of the Amazons]. Agassiz has written "wild nonsense".

Refers to a translation of Pictet and Humbert’s "capital" paper on fossil fish ["Recent researches on the fossil fishes of Mount Lebanon",Ann. & Mag. Nat. Hist.3d ser. 18 (1866): 237].

Hooker’s lecture at BAAS Nottingham meeting.

letters.title: From Julius von Haast   8 September 1866
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for his efforts on behalf of JvH’s Royal Society candidacy.

Is at work on a large-scale map of the Southern Alps [of New Zealand].

The ever-growing goldfields and their effect on the country.

letters.title: From W. R. Grove   9 September 1866
letters.summary: Sends a "remarkable" enclosure [missing], evidently by a working man, which will interest CD as "shewing that ideas are spread".

letters.title: To Asa Gray   10 September [1866]
letters.summary:
L. Agassiz’s evidence [for glaciation of America] is very weak.

Thanks AG for arranging for American edition ofVariation, but doubts that the book will be successful.

Has found no differences in pollen ofRhamnusso cannot conjecture whether it is dimorphic.

The common oxlip of England is certainly a hybrid between the primrose and the cowslip whereasPrimula elatioris a good species.

Reports experiments on the relative vigour of seedlings from cross- and self-fertilised plants.

letters.title: From W. B. Tegetmeier   12 September 1866
letters.summary:
Has had the blocks cut as requested and forwards the proofs.

Encloses article on habits of jungle fowl.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   14 September [1866]
letters.summary: Blocks forVariationare much improved. WBT deserves membership in Zoological Society.

letters.title: To Albert Gaudry   17 September [1866]
letters.summary:
Thanks AG forConsidérations générales[sur les animaux fossiles]de Pikermi[1866]. The observations on the various intermediate fossil forms seem most valuable.

AG does not fully understand what CD means by "the struggle for existence, or concurrence vitale".

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   19 September 1866
letters.summary:
[N. C.?] Seringe’s article [unspecified] has come safely.

Feels deeply at CD’s distress [Susan Darwin is dying].

Droserawill go in a day or two.

letters.title: From George Warde Norman   20 September 1866
letters.summary: Sends a paper, by the wife of the local curate, on the habits of animals.

letters.title: From L. C. Wedgwood   [22 September 1866]
letters.summary: QuotesBotanical MagazineonErica massoni. Its branches terminate in large umbels of flowers that are extremely viscous and entrap insects.

letters.title: To Lucy Caroline Wedgwood   [before 25 September 1866]
letters.summary:
Asks her to see whether the flowers or leaves ofErica massoniare noted as glutinous in theBotanical Magazine.

Inquires about the pods of peony: are they brilliantly coloured and do birds eat them?

letters.title: From George Bentham   25 September 1866
letters.summary:
Replies to CD’s two memoranda, GB explains: 1. That he never said thistles do not produce seeds, but rather that the infinite majority of new plants are propagated from buds

2. That book-borrowing rules of the Linnean Library are not so stringent as the Librarian makes out.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   25 September [1866]
letters.summary:
Susan Darwin still lives, but is dying.

Requests anErica massonito compare withDrosera.

On L. Agassiz’s "astonishing" view that Amazon Valley was filled with gigantic glacier. Asa Gray says LA is determined to cover the globe with glaciers in order to destroy "Darwinian views".

Excellent review of A. Murray [The geographical distribution of mammals] inGardeners’ Chronicle[(1866): 902].

Frankland’s Royal Institution lecture ["On the source of muscular power"Not. Proc. R. Inst. G. B.4 (1862–6): 661–85].

Wallace’s paper.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   25 September [1866]
letters.summary:
Fertilisation in orchids: Friedrich Hildebrand’s paper.

Self-sterility.

Climbing plants.

Agassiz’s attempts to eliminate all Darwinian views.

letters.title: To William Bowman   26 September [1866]
letters.summary: Thanks WB for his paper ["Address in surgery",Br. Med. J.(1866): 186–97, read at British Medical Association annual meeting, 9 Aug 1866].

letters.title: To George Bentham   27 September [1866]
letters.summary: His memory deceived him about GB’s statement [on propagation of thistles].

letters.title: From Thomas Francis Jamieson   27 September 1866
letters.summary: Sends his paper ["On the glacial phenomena of Caithness",Q. J. Geol. Soc. Lond.22 (1866): 261–81], which shows glaciation under marine conditions in Scotland.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   28 September 1866
letters.summary:
DroseraandErica massonihave been sent.

Had heard of Agassiz’s theory but not that CD’s theory had raised it.

JDH wrote the article on A. Murray.

Frankland’s lecture too much for him.

letters.title: From Francis Trevelyan Buckland   29 September 1866
letters.summary: Sends copy ofLand and Water, a journal he now edits. Has quit theField. Asks CD to patronise his columns with queries, as other zoologists do.

letters.title: To George Bentham   1 October 1866
letters.summary: Invites GB and wife to luncheon.

letters.title: To E. F. Lubbock [1 October 1866]
letters.summary: "… Mr Herbert Spencer. I will call tomorrow about half past 12".

letters.title: From E. F. Lubbock [1 October 1866]
letters.summary: Herbert Spencer is staying with the Lubbocks and would much like to see CD.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   1 and 3 October 1866
letters.summary: Discusses dimorphism ofOxalis; one form has 99% sterile anthers. Has found three kinds of fertile anthers.

letters.title: To F. T. Buckland 2 October 1866
letters.summary: Declines contributing toLand and Water. Asks if F. T. Buckland can insert a question about the feet of otter hounds.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   2 October [1866]
letters.summary:
Did not think JDH had written Murray review [see5217].

Does not thinkGardeners’ Chroniclebest for publication of "Insular floras" [Gard. Chron.(1867): 6–7, 27, 50–1, 75–6].

T. Laxton’s article, on direct action of pollen of peas on seed and pod, a grand physiological fact and "delightful" for Pangenesis.

Interview with Herbert Spencer.

letters.title: ToLand and Water   [2 October 1866]
letters.summary: Requests information about the feet of otter-hounds. Is the membrane between the toes more largely developed than in other hounds? To which part or joint of the toes does the skin extend? Is it hollowed out?

letters.title: From George Bentham   4 October [1866]
letters.summary: Is unable to fix a day for luncheon until later.

letters.title: From F. T. Buckland   4 October [1866]
letters.summary:
Thanks for CD’s patronage;

will pursue CD’s query about otter-hounds.

Remarks on continuing debate over CD’s views in BAAS.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   4 October [1866]
letters.summary:
Would CD like to have Susan’s Indian chessmen?

EAD should settle something about the house but has no power without consent of all parties.

Caroline looks worn – it has been a most painful time.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [4 October 1866]
letters.summary: Susan Darwin is dead.

letters.title: From William Bowman   5 October 1866
letters.summary: Is pleased CD approved of his effort ["Address in surgery", see5219] in which he alluded to CD’s views.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   7 October [1866]
letters.summary:
Disposal of Susan’s effects.

Frank and Henry [Parker] are executors.

EAD is bringing away a large packet of CD’s letters from abroad.

letters.title: From Charles Pritchard   8 October 1866
letters.summary: Sends sermon he preached at the BAAS Nottingham meeting ["The continuity of the schemes of nature and revelation" (1866)], in which he disagrees with CD on the gradual genesis of the human eye by natural selection.

letters.title: From Thomas Rivers   8 October 1866
letters.summary: Has searched scores of purple-fruited nut-trees, but not a nut is to be found. Has heard there are some nearby and will send them as soon as he receives them.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   9 October [1866]
letters.summary:
Comments on proofs [ofPrinciples of geology, 10th ed. (1867–8)]: CL does not allude to the specialisation of classes.

Discusses CL’s argument from the absence of Cetacea in Secondary rocks;

finds his discussion of man "superfluous and too orthodox".

letters.title: From Asa Gray   10 October 1866
letters.summary: Does not think he can persuade American publishers to reprint [4th English ed. of]Originin U. S. Suggests Murray supply copies of it and the new book [Variation] to the American market.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   11 October [1866]
letters.summary:
Disposal of Susan’s effects. Legacies to CD’s children. EAD has taken the letters and papers and asked Henry [Parker] to forward the George Richmond pictures of CD and Emma.

Caroline looks "miserably ill".

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   12 October [1866]
letters.summary:
More comments on proofs [of CL’sPrinciples of geology, 10th ed.]. Discusses permanence of continents and other points.

Refers to passage describing evaporation of snow inJournal[of researches, pp. 277–8].

Cites astronomers’ views on increasing length of day.

letters.title: To Charles Pritchard   12 October [1866]
letters.summary:
Responds to CP’s sermon. Corrects CP’s confusion of what CD said about eyes of the Articulata with human eye,

and questions applicability of CP’s mathematical arguments about length of geological time needed for evolution.

Agrees he was foolish about the Wealden, now struck from later editions [Origin, pp. 285–7].

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [after 12 October 1866]
letters.summary: Instructions on paying a bill.

letters.title: To Thomas Rivers   13 October [1866]
letters.summary: Greatly interested in case of purple nuts but, after seeing TR’s specimens, dares not trust his case. Wishes he lived near TR or were strong enough to visit.

letters.title: From Thomas Rivers   14 October 1866
letters.summary: Sends CD a letter from Mr Claydon responding to TR’s doubts and confirming the truth of a report that a farmer had "transmuted" oats into barley.

letters.title: From W. B. Tegetmeier   15 October 1866
letters.summary:
The blocks [forVariation] have been forwarded to Murray.

WBT has been corresponding with Prof. Newton.

letters.title: To John Murray   16 October [1866]
letters.summary:
Arrangements for woodcuts [inVariation]. Hopes to be ready to print early in 1867.

Encloses letter from Asa Gray [5160] about Appleton’s refusal to alter their plates for a new edition ofOrigin.

CD asks JM to consider Gray’s plan to have the English edition compete with the American.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   16 October [1866]
letters.summary: Hopes to begin printingVariationat the beginning of next year.

letters.title: From John Murray   18 October [1866]
letters.summary:
JM states he will publish [Variation] on same basis asOrigin, i.e., paying CD two-thirds of the profits.

In response to Asa Gray’s suggestion, he could supply Ticknor & Fields with 250 copies [ofOrigin, 4th ed.] at half-price.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   19 October 1866
letters.summary:
Will visit CD on Sunday, 21 October.

Will spend winter in research on Madeira and Tenerife.

CD will soon receive copy ofGenerelle Morphologie.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   19 October 1866
letters.summary:
Lyell has sent chapters [of 10th ed. ofPrinciples] to JDH, who objects to CL’s ignoring the part vapour plays in affecting temperature of the globe.

Parliament will be asked to buy W. J. Hooker’s collection.

letters.title: To Mary Elizabeth Lyell   [19? October 1866]
letters.summary: Mary Somerville may use diagrams fromOrchids[in herMolecular and microscopic science(1869)], but permission should be obtained from John Murray.

letters.title: To George Brettingham Sowerby Jr   19 October [1866]
letters.summary: Lists some alterations which must be made to the drawings [forVariation].

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   [20 October 1866]
letters.summary: Explains how to get to Down for visit.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [21 October 1866]
letters.summary:
Introduces Ernst Haeckel.

Lyell sent same chapters to CD, who thinks them very good but is not convinced that changes of land and water will do all he thinks.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   [21 October 1866]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Anxious to make acquaintance of Ernst Haeckel [who was staying with CD].

letters.title: From Friedrich Hildebrand   23 October 1866
letters.summary: Explains dichogamy inAristolochia. C. K. Sprengel was wrong.

letters.title: To John Murray   23 October [1866]
letters.summary: A letter from Asa Gray informs CD that Ticknor & Fields will not publish a new edition ofOriginto compete with Appleton’s unrevised edition. They recommend sending copies of the English edition for the American market.

letters.title: From John Murray   25 October [1866]
letters.summary: Under circumstances [reluctance of Ticknor & Fields to compete with Appleton], best course is to offer Appleton the 250 copies [of 4th English edition ofOrigin].

letters.title: From E. Schweizerbart’sche Verlagsbuchhandlung   26 October 1866
letters.summary: Plans to have J. V. Carus handle translation of new edition ofOrigin. Describes Carus’ views on the edition.

letters.title: From Rudolf Oldenbourg   28 October 1866
letters.summary: Proposes O. F. Peschel as a German translator ofVariation, which his firm would like to publish.

letters.title: From Mary Somerville   30 October 1866
letters.summary: Thanks CD for permission to use illustrations fromOrchidsin her work [On molecular and microscopic science(1869)].

letters.title: To Thomas Laxton   31 October [1866]
letters.summary: Thanks for box of crossed peas.

letters.title: From Frances Harriet Hooker   1 November [1866]
letters.summary: Mentions a note inNotes and Queries[3d ser. 10 (1866): 343–4] which refers toA sketch of the life and works of Erasmus Darwin.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   1 November [1866]
letters.summary:
Requests water-lily pods to count, weigh, and to germinate some of the seeds of the crossed and uncrossed pods.

Hopes Haeckel did not bore him.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   [2 November 1866]
letters.summary:
Sends his observations on sterility ofEschscholzia,

onOxalis,

and on recently found dimorphic plants.

Sends specimen ofHedyotis[seeForms of flowers, p. 133].

letters.title: From Herbert Spencer   2 November 1866
letters.summary: Asks whether CD will add his name to a list supporting them in the "[Edward John] Eyre prosecution matter".

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   3 November 1866
letters.summary:
Left strict orders aboutEuryaleseeds but "labour, difficulty and expense of getting anything done scientifically by practical men is untold".

The E. J. Eyre controversy [Jamaica uprising]. Odd that Huxley joins the "persecution fund". The principles involved are fiddlesticks.

letters.title: To Thomas Laxton   3 November [1866]
letters.summary:
Has examined TL’s crossed peas. Observes that in several lots crossed peas are smooth, like paternal stock, not wrinkled like maternal stock. Is this a result of mere variation, peculiar culture, or pollen of the father?

Encloses queries [missing].

Intends planting peas at once if TL approves.

letters.title: From Richard Trevor Clarke   6 November [1866]
letters.summary:
Wants to publish his observation on colour changes inMatthiolaseeds.

Has been crossing cotton.

Approves of C. V. Naudin and Max Wichura.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   6 November [1866]
letters.summary: Arranges for distribution of new [4th] English edition ofOriginin the U. S.

letters.title: From Julius Victor Carus   7 November 1866
letters.summary:
JVC has been asked by Schweizerbart [CD’s German publisher] to revise H. G. Bronn’s translation ofOrigin, and he will be pleased to try to do it.

Asks CD’s advice on what to do about Bronn’s notes and concluding chapter, with which JVC disagrees. Would CD agree to omission?

letters.title: From James Shaw   7 November 1866
letters.summary: Thanks CD for copy of theOrigin[4th ed.]; makes some observations on beauty and ugliness in nature.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   8 November [1866]
letters.summary: Tells WED of a change in his will.

letters.title: From J. T. Moggridge   9 November [1866]
letters.summary: At CD’s request he is looking into the gardeners’ custom of separating all sweetpea varieties in order to obtain pure seed.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   10 November 1866
letters.summary:
Expresses gratification that JVC is to undertake new translation and revision of German edition of theOrigin.

Has heard many complaints about Bronn’s translation. JVC would be justified in omitting Bronn’s appendix.

Suggests additions and changes, including reference to C. W. v. Nägeli’sEntstehung und Begriff[1865], though he disagrees with it.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   10 November [1866]
letters.summary: Has made will. Discusses financial arrangements and asks whether CD would like a mortgage.

letters.title: From Armand de Quatrefages   10 November 1866
letters.deprecated: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.sender: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.summary: Sends his book [Histoire naturelle des annelés marins et d’eau douce, 2 vols. (1865)].

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   11 November 1866
letters.summary:
Thanks for 4th ed. ofOrigin.

What a basting CD gives "our mutual friend" [Owen].

Glad he argrees with THH on Jamaica affair [Gov. Eyre and the "rebellion"].

letters.title: From Clair James Grece   12 November 1866
letters.summary:
Sends clipping about a pig that has cast its outer skin.

Identifies himself as having a year or two ago pointed out a passage from Aristotle showing that natural selection was known to the ancients.

letters.title: To J. T. Moggridge   13 November [1866]
letters.summary: Discusses fertilisation of peas by bees. Asks for seeds.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   15 November 1866
letters.summary:
JVC proposes to correct Bronn’s mistakes [in his translation ofOrigin], but will not add his own notes.

Asks CD to write a note on Nägeli’s pamphlet [Entstehung und Begriff] for the revised edition.

Also requests biographical information for an encyclopedia article he has been asked to write.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   15 November 1866
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Asks JL to look up a paper by Thomas Hincks on Polyzoa or Bryozoa [Q. J. Microsc. Sci.2d ser. 1 (1861): 278–81].

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   19 November 1866
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for 4th ed. ofOrigin.

Discusses abnormal sexual characters produced by mimicry. ARW’s papers on the subject.

Agassiz’s "marvellous" Amazonian glacier theory.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   20 November [1866]
letters.summary:
Requests roots of two species ofMirabilisfor "a curious experiment in crossing".

Has subscribed £10 to Jamaica committee to prosecute Governor Eyre.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   21 November 1866
letters.summary:
Answers some question about species.

Sends biographical sketch.

Now considers that a note on Nägeli would have to be too long to include. Discusses his differences with Nägeli. Cannot believe in spontaneous generation. At present the principle of life seems to him beyond the confines of science.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [22 November 1866]
letters.summary:
His views on the Eyre controversy.

Went to Shrewsbury (for sale of Susan’s effects), hoping to buy some Wedgwood medallions, but they had been bought.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [23 November 1866]
letters.summary: Will visit Kew on Tuesday [27 Nov].

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   [23 November 1866?]
letters.summary: Will call on Wallace tomorrow (Saturday) at 10.

letters.title: To James Shaw   24 November [1866]
letters.summary: Has seen theAthenæumand admires his article on beauty ["Feeling of beauty among animals",Athenæum(24 Nov. 1866): 681].

letters.title: To H. A. Huxley   [before 25 November 1866?]
letters.summary: Asks if he may call on Sunday at 10 o’clock.

letters.title: From Anne Marsh-Caldwell   27 November [1866]
letters.summary: Writing for Mr Corbet, she asks what diet has helped in the treatment of CD’s illness.

letters.title: From Alfred Newton   27 November 1866
letters.summary:
Thanks for new edition ofOrigin[4th ed.].

Has met CD’s son [George] at Trinity College.

letters.title: From B. D. Walsh   [28 November 1866]
letters.summary:
Says Jacob W. Velie wants to exchange birds’ skins with European naturalist.

Comments on meaning of "Darwinism".

Encloses papers fromPractical Entomologist.

DiscussesOrnithorhynchus paradoxus

and his paper on willow galls.

Mentions human skull found in California.

letters.title: From Herbert George Henry Norman   30 November 1866
letters.summary: Encloses foot of a woodcock with earth attached. CD asked about this many years ago with reference to seed dispersal.

letters.title: To H. G. H. Norman   [after 30 November 1866]
letters.summary: Thanks his correspondent for remembering to send him a woodcock’s leg and informing him that "from a ball of earth attached to the leg of a Red Partridge no less than 82 plants germinated". [See5287.]

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker [December 1866?]
letters.summary: Asks CD to send W. R. Grove titles and place of publication of the Müller [Für Darwin(1864)] and Wallace [J. Proc. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Zool.)3 (1859): 54–62] papers he referred to in his address [BAAS lecture at Nottingham, see5135].

letters.title: To Edouard Bornet   1 December 1866
letters.summary: Thanks JBEB forPapaverseeds. Has long wished to see some of the closely allied subspecies and hopes to make some crossing experiments with them.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [1 December 1866]
letters.summary: William asks what to do about a complication in settling Aunt Catherine’s estate.

letters.title: From Daniel Hanbury 1 December 1866
letters.summary: Wishes to consult Fritz Müller on pharmacological matters.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   1 December [1866]
letters.summary: Thanks CL for copy of his "grand book" [Principles of geology, 10th ed., vol. 1 (1867)]. Congratulates him on additions.

letters.title: To Anne Marsh-Caldwell   1 December [1866]
letters.summary:
Mentions visit to E. A. Darwin.

Encloses note for Mr Corbet.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   1 December 1866
letters.summary:
Gives observations on orchid ovules ripening long after blooming.

Infertility with own pollen sometimes does and sometimes does not indicate dimorphism; gives observations onXimenia,EschscholtziaandOncidium flexuosum.

Describes some striking seeds eaten by birds,

and some new dimorphic species.

Variation inThillia.

Confirms CD’s suspicion that the lancet-fish [Amphioxus] lives in competition with invertebrates: it shares its habitat with a similar-lookingOphelia, which is quite unlike other annelids, just as the lancet-fish is unlike other fishes.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   4 December 1866
letters.summary:
Lyell’s volume [Principles, 10th ed.] received.

"We must now keep him straight anent origin and development."

Some of Spencer’s new part is interesting but much is dull and ponderous.

Huxley’sElementary physiology[1866].

Has finished his New Zealand manual [Handbook of New Zealand flora(1864–7)]. New Zealand flora [and past geological conditions] suggest islands were once connected.

Speculates on the total amount of living organised matter on the globe, and whether it varies.

Balfour Stewart on sunspots.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   4 December [1866]
letters.summary:
Is tempted to cite Mr Zurhorst’s case.

Hopes to send pigeon and fowl MS [ofVariation] to press in a fortnight.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   5 December [1866]
letters.summary:
Is sending some plants and seeds to JDH.

Thanks Mrs Hooker for telling him of a life of his grandfather [Erasmus Darwin] of which he had not heard.

letters.title: To Miss Behrens   7 December 1866
letters.summary: Sends his autograph.

letters.title: To Linnean Society   7 December [1866]
letters.summary: Asks to have author’s spare copies of F. Müller’s article on climbing plants [J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)9 (1867): 344] sent to him for forwarding to FM.

letters.title: From Robert Monsey Rolfe   8 December 1866
letters.deprecated: Robert Monsey Rolfe, 1st Baron Cranworth of Cranworth
letters.sender: Robert Monsey Rolfe, 1st Baron Cranworth of Cranworth
letters.summary: Sending annual Down charities cheque.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   [before 10 December 1866]
letters.summary:
Hildebrand’s paper on trimorphism inOxalis["Über den Trimorphismus in der GattungOxalis",Monatsber. K. Preuss. Akad. Wiss. Berlin(1866): 352–74].

Problems of explaining brightly coloured, attractive seeds.

Haeckel has visited Down.

FM’s climbing plants paper is printed [J. Proc. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)9 (1867): 344–9].

letters.title: To Edward Blyth   10 December [1866]
letters.summary: Asks for reference to EB’s article about tame deer on island in Aral Sea.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   10 December [1866]
letters.summary:
A confounded cock ground the crimson seeds up so CD could not find them in its excrement. CD is puzzled by how seeds can be disseminated if merely ground up by birds. Perhaps like acorns from seeds accidentally dropped by birds?

A woodcock’s leg with dry clay clinging to it, from which CD has grown a microscopical rush.

Spencer would have been wonderful if he had trained himself to observe more.

On New Zealand flora and connection with Australia.

Difficulty of speculating about the amount of organic chemical change at different periods.

letters.title: From W. B. Tegetmeier   10 December [1866]
letters.summary:
WBT interested in ancestors of domestic guinea-fowl, ducks, and geese.

Egg colours in fowls.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [12 December 1866]
letters.summary:
Plants arrived.

Delightful dinner at Lyell’s.

Will be interested in seeds passed through a fowl.

Wedgwood medallions were bought by a Miss W. [Sophy Wedgwood] of Leith Hill.

Lubbock’s account of a new centipede at Linnean Society gave rise to lively discussion by Busk and Huxley.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   12 December [1866]
letters.summary: Gives his opinion on the ancestry of domestic ducks, geese, and guinea-fowl.

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   13 [December] 1866
letters.summary:
Gives CD reference to case of the saiga, an antelope, fearless of man.

Reports observations by New Zealander who has seen heaps of pebbles presumably voided byDinornis.

letters.title: From Mary Everest Boole   13 December 1866
letters.summary: Asks whether CD believes natural selection obviates man’s ability to be guided by spiritual motives. Is anxious that his theory be compatible with her faith.

letters.title: From Eleanor Corbet   13 December 1866
letters.summary: Mr Corbet too ill to write. Thanks for CD’s letter [see5290].

letters.title: To M. E. Boole   14 December 1866
letters.summary: Is unable to answer her questions about religious implications of natural selection, but would prefer to believe that suffering in world is due to natural events.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   14 December 1866
letters.summary:
Scarlet seed isAdenanthera pavonina. JDH’s suggestion on how disseminated.

On Herbert Spencer, "all oil no bone – a thinking pump", but his paper on sap and wood [Trans. Linn. Soc. Lond.25 (1866): 405–30] is good science. His refusal to bring a specimen for analysis when confronted by JDH.

Bentham and Martin disagreement.

Speculations on New Zealand flora.

Albert Günther’s paper on fishes on each side of Isthmus of Panama [Proc. Zool. Soc. Lond.(1866): 600–4].

On the quantity (bulk and weight) of organic life [matter].

letters.title: To William Turner   14 December [1866]
letters.summary:
Thinks of adding chapter on man toVariation. Asks about muscles connected to os coccyx in man and existence of other rudimentary organs in man.

Sends copy ofOrigin.

letters.title: From W. B. Tegetmeier   15 December [1866]
letters.summary: Thanks for information. Sclater was source of statement aboutNumida ptiloryncha[as origin of guinea-fowl] inThe poultry book[pt 12 (Dec 1866): 288].

letters.title: To Charles Lovegrove?   16 December [1866?]
letters.summary: Acknowledges a subscription to the Down [Coal and Clothing] Club.

letters.title: From M. E. Boole   17 December [1866]
letters.summary: Thanks CD for reassurance that moral and religious faith are valid independently of his theory.

letters.title: To ?   17 December [1866]
letters.summary:
Gives information about obtaining the most recent (4th) edition ofOrigin.

Is glad to hear that his correspondent is interested in the subject.

letters.title: To Henry Walter Bates   18 December [1866]
letters.summary: Asks for a letter on the tameness of deer, written by Commander A. Boutakoff to R. I. Murchison and printed in theJournal[J. R. Geogr. Soc.23 (1853): 93–101].

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   18 [December 1866]
letters.summary: Thanks for calling his attention to ancestry of guinea-fowl.

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   19 December 1866
letters.summary: HWB sends a copy [missing] of Boutakoff’s letter, explaining that the deer were saiga antelopes and the islands were new discoveries.

letters.title: To John Murray   21 and 22 December [1866]
letters.summary: Submits the MS ofVariation, all excepting the section on Man.

letters.title: From Lydia Ernestine Becker   22 December 1866
letters.summary: Thanks CD for previous communications. Asks him to send a paper relating to flowers to be read at first meeting of her ladies’ literary and scientific society.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   22 December [1866]
letters.summary:
First impressions of Haeckel’sGenerelle morphologie.

Has received THH’s [Lessons in elementary]Physiology[1866]

and rereadMan’s place.

Asks THH to read revised "Hybridism" chapter in new edition ofOrigin. Hopes it will change THH’s view.

Convinced of P. S. Pallas’ view of loss of sterility under domestication.

letters.title: From John Murray   22 December [1866]
letters.summary: The presentation copy [ofOrigin, 4th ed.] was sent to B. D. Walsh in August. Will send another.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   24 December [1866]
letters.summary:
Has finishedVariation. May insert a chapter on man.

Still puzzled by seeds ofAdenanthera.

New Zealand and Borneo flora problems continued.

Fritz Müller found six genera of dimorphic plants in one day.

letters.title: From John Murray   24 December [1866]
letters.summary: Two parcels of MS [ofVariation] have arrived. Will proceed with printing immediately after Christmas.

letters.title: To P. L. Sclater   24 December [1866]
letters.summary: Encloses a portion of a letter from B. D. Walsh [5319] concerning an American interested in exchanging birds’ skins.

letters.title: To William Turner   24 [December 1866]
letters.summary: Thanks WT for information about rudimentary parts in man.

letters.title: To B. D. Walsh   24 December [1866]
letters.summary: Balbiani’s puzzling observations onAphis.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   25 December 1866
letters.summary:
Analysis of New Zealand flora; proportion of indigenous annuals.

Uniform climates are poor in species.

Evergreen and deciduous vegetation: relationship to flora and fauna.

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   25 December 1866
letters.summary:
Discusses the South American mission.

Has been busy digging out fossil leaves from local Eocene deposits.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   26 December [1866]
letters.summary: Requests a change in text [of ch. 12 ofOrigin: "Geographical distribution"] owing to recent observations of Albert Günther on the marine faunas of the eastern and western shores of South and Central America.

letters.title: From L. E. Becker   28 December [1866]
letters.summary:
Thanks for "Climbing plants" and other papers [as requested in5316].

Sends specimens of a variety ofPrimulanot mentioned by CD [inPrimulapaper,Collected papers2: 45–63?].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   28 [December 1866]
letters.summary:
B. J. Sulivan offers fossil leaves from Eocene beds at Bournemouth to CD or JDH. Does JDH want them, or should they go to Oswald Heer?

Has written toAthenæum[see5308] about publishers cutting pages of their books.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [29 December 1866]
letters.summary:
Suggests fossil leaves go to Heer.

Agrees with CD on cut pages in books.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   [late December 1866 and] 1 January 1867
letters.summary:
Thanks for observations on dimorphic plants. Dimorphism prevalent in certain groups throughout the world.

Retarded fertilisation in certain orchids.

letters.title: From John William Salter   31 December 1866
letters.summary: JWS is seeking financial help. He is in debt and struggling and wonders if there is any paid service he might perform for CD.

letters.title: To B. J. Sulivan   31 December [1866]
letters.summary:
Thanks BJS for his account of S. America and the Fuegians.

Can BJS ask W. H. Stirling to make observations on expression?

Has asked Hooker about the fossil leaves, and he suggests they be sent to Oswald Heer.

Has just sent MS on domestic animals [Variation] to the printer.

letters.title: From F. J. Wedgwood to H. E. Darwin? [1867–72]
letters.summary: An extract from Macrobius’Saturnaliadealing with blushing.

letters.title: From Ellen Frances Lubbock   [1867–8?]
letters.summary: Has marked a page fromAdam Bedewhich may be relevant to CD’s work on expression.

letters.title: To ? [1867?]
letters.summary: [Excised fragment only.] "I am greedy for facts. – "

letters.title: From S. E. Wedgwood [1867–72?]
letters.summary: Jessie [Wedgwood] says driving in sun made one of her eyes water.

letters.title: From F. J. Wedgwood [1867–72]
letters.summary: Sends extract from Charma [Essai sur le langage(1846)] on the origin of nodding and shaking the head [SeeExpression, p. 273 n. 17].

letters.title: From F. J. Wedgwood [1867–72]
letters.summary: Extract from Seneca’s letters establishes that hiding the face in shame was not a classical gesture.

letters.title: From Hensleigh Wedgwood [1867–72]
letters.summary: On origin of hand-shaking.

letters.title: From Hensleigh Wedgwood [1867–72]
letters.summary: Expression: derivation of the term "brown study".

letters.title: From Hensleigh Wedgwood [1867–72?]
letters.summary: A fragment that may contain information forExpression.

letters.title: ToAthenæum   1 January 1867
letters.summary: Expresses his support for new books being sold with the pages cut.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   1 January 1867
letters.summary:
Describes his experiments in fertilisingOncidium flexuosumand comparison withNotylia.

Has been examiningCatasetum.

Encloses seeds of two species ofGesneriaand describes hairs in the seed capsule. Hairs in other plants seem to have a different function.

Starting tomorrow for a botanical excursion on the Continent.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [after 1866?]
letters.summary: Sends abstract, and will bring book on Saturday.

letters.title: From John Murray   2 January [1867]
letters.summary: William Clowes [printer for J. Murray] estimates thatVariationwill come to a first volume of 648 pages and a second volume of 624 pages – which is too much for volumes the same size asOrigin. Murray proposes a larger size.

letters.title: To John Murray   3 January [1867]
letters.summary: Sorry about enormous size ofVariationMS, but cannot shorten it now. If JM is afraid to publish, CD will consider agreement cancelled. Suggests he ask someone with judgment to read the MS. Has written concluding chapter on man. Whether it will be included depends on size of volume.

letters.title: From John William Salter   4 January [1867]
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for his kindness and hopes one day to return it.

Finds more and more observations fall in with CD’s theory but still finds it difficult to account for the sudden leaps in the fossil record and to explain why some organisms first appear as such high forms.

letters.title: To William Bernhard Tegetmeier   6 January [1867]
letters.summary:
Returns some of WBT’s skulls.

His MS is with printer, but book [Variation] will probably not be out until November.

letters.title: From Thomas Henry Huxley   [before 7 January 1867]
letters.summary: On Haeckel’sGenerelle Morphologie; the logical argument for natural selection is still incomplete. THH jumps over the hole by an act of faith.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   7 January [1867]
letters.summary:
Gives up plan to have Haeckel’sGenerelle morphologietranslated.

His big book [Variation] has gone to printer. Thinks of adding a chapter on man.

Will order Duke of Argyll’s book [Reign of law(1867)].

"Nature never made species mutually sterile [by selection]; nor will man.–"

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   8 January 1867
letters.summary:
Comments on EH’s "great work" [Generelle Morphologie].

An English translation "hopeless".

Asks about EH’s expedition.

MS ofVariationsent to printers.

Fritz Müller working on plants.

letters.title: To John Murray   8 January [1867]
letters.summary: CD annoyed at large size ofVariation. Suggests printing detailed parts in small type. JM can, of course, decline to publish altogether.

letters.title: To Joseph Dalton Hooker   9 January [1867]
letters.summary: Criticisms and comments on JDH’s "Insular floras" inGardeners’ Chronicle[(1867): 6].

letters.title: From John Murray   9 January [1867]
letters.summary:
CD should not be discouraged by the bulk ofVariation. CD’s suggestion to print technical details in small type is good.

Murray has sent MS to a "man of letters and good information" as an experiment to test its effect. Has no intention of throwing up publication.

letters.title: From James Philip Mansel Weale   9 January 1867
letters.summary:
Sends paper on new species ofBonatea, to which he has given the nameDarwinii.

Has now an extensive collection of insects.

Has discovered moths whose larva cases resemble perfectly the thorns of theAcacia horrida.

Has asked for the head of a Bushman murderer. Difficult to convince authorities of interest of science.

letters.title: To John Murray   10 January [1867]
letters.summary: Relieved by JM’s note and by his agreement on type size. Is alarmed by what the verdict [onVariation] of JM’s friend will be. He is not a man of science. An unscientific reader would have condemned theOrigin. An eminent semi-scientific man thought theJournal of researchesnot worth publishing.

letters.title: From Bartholomew James Sulivan   11 January 1867
letters.summary:
Has given CD’s queries about expression to W. H. Stirling. Thomas Bridges, the catechist, had previously answered some questions incompletely [see2643]; BJS forwards them [seeExpression].

BJS answers CD’s query about when some calves show their adult colour.

letters.title: From Thomas Belt   12 January 1867
letters.summary: MS essay "On esculent fruits" [apparently enclosed in a missing letter].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [12 January 1867]
letters.summary: Responds to CD’s criticisms. JDH is sometimes confused as to what he has borrowed from CD.

letters.title: From Robert Monsey Rolfe   14 January 1867
letters.deprecated: Robert Monsey Rolfe, 1st Baron Cranworth of Cranworth
letters.sender: Robert Monsey Rolfe, 1st Baron Cranworth of Cranworth
letters.summary: Will introduce Charles Kingsley to CD.

letters.title: To Thomas Belt   15 January [1867]
letters.summary: Comments on MS on seed distribution sent by TB.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   15 January [1867]
letters.summary: More comments on "Insular floras": community of peculiar genera in the Atlantic islands descended from European plants now extinct.

letters.title: To John Murray   15 January [1867]
letters.summary: Approves of type [forVariation]. Pleased to hear from Hooker that he is not surprised that MS is big.

letters.title: To B. J. Sulivan   15 January [1867]
letters.summary:
Thanks BJS for W. H. Stirling’s answers [to queries about expression]

and for information on cattle and breeding of dogs.

letters.title: To William Turner   15 January [1867]
letters.summary: Requests information about rudimentary muscles and organs in man. Asks about marrow of os coccyx, and about testes and ovaria in early embryos of both sexes.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   16 January 1867
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: JL’s brother-in-law [Robert Birkbeck] would like a note of introduction to John Murray.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   17 January [1867]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
