letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Encloses note of introduction to Murray.

letters.title: From Julius Victor Carus   18 January 1867
letters.summary: Asks CD questions relating to the revised translation ofOrigin.

letters.title: To Alfred Newton   19 January [1867]
letters.summary:
Seeks explanation of the case of theRhynchaea, of which the female is more beautiful than the male, with the young resembling the latter. Wallace has told CD that at Nottingham AN explained this by the male being the incubator.

Does the male black Australian swan, or the black and white S. American swan, differ from the female in colour of plumage?

letters.title: To Charles Henry Middleton   20 [1867?]
letters.summary:
Sorry he cannot remember where S. Filippe [San Felipe?] is.

Doubts that bones of ox, sheep, and horse could have been deposited inguano[on coast of Chile], but they would be worth examination.

[Tipped in copy ofOrigin(1866) with CHM’s bookplate.]

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   20 January 1867
letters.summary: His view of CD’s hypothesis that Atlantic island genera are descended from extinct European plants.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   21 January [1867]
letters.summary: On recent instalment of "Insular floras" inGardeners’ Chronicle[(1867): 50]. Approves of JDH’s abstract of argument for transport of species [i.e., migration, as opposed to continental extension hypothesis].

letters.title: From Alfred Newton   21 January 1867
letters.summary: Suggests that, in some birds, plumage of males is less colourful than that of females; the reason is that the males perform the duties of incubation [seeDescent2: 204 n.].

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   22 January [1867]
letters.summary: Answers JVC’s questions about the rock-thrush, the tortoise-shell cat, and the logger-headed duck.

letters.title: From John Scott   22 January 1867
letters.summary:
Position as Curator allows no time for experiment.

Describes plans for vast new layout of Calcutta Botanic Garden according to natural orders.

Himalayan and Scottish plants are doing well.

Hopes to experiment on temperate plants in tropics, to test CD’s views of migration during glacial periods.

Sends observations on acclimatisation of English cultivated plants.

LeersiaCD sent are growing and fertile.

letters.title: To Alfred Newton   23 January [1867]
letters.summary: Thanks for the information about the male plumage. [See5374.] Will look to the papers inIbisto which AN has referred him. He finds AN’s theory captivating.

letters.title: From E. Schweizerbart’sche Verlagsbuchhandlung   24 January 1867
letters.summary: Describes progress in preparation of third German edition of theOrigin. Asks about use of photograph for edition.

letters.title: To [A. J. Woodhouse?]   25 January [1867?]
letters.summary:
Two queries on teeth: 1. Is there evidence of inherited peculiarities in milk teeth?

2. Are male incisors longer than female?

letters.title: From Alexander F. Boardman   26 January 1867
letters.summary:
Encloses letter written a week ago. Letter and enclosure speculate on origins of human races in relation to geological and political changes, according to a theory of progressive development.

Was sorry CD wrote so little on man inOrigin.

letters.title: To John Murray   27 January [1867]
letters.summary: Hopes JM’s friend will give his judgment [onVariation] soon; and urges JM to come to a decision about publishing. CD believes it will have "a fair sale".

letters.title: From John Murray   28 January [1867]
letters.summary:
JM will publish [Variation] "coute qui coute", paying CD half the profits.

Thinks he can count on 500 purchases of what he calls the "Pièces Justificatives" of theOriginand will print 750 copies.

His literary friend found it "difficult of digestion".

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   29 January [1867]
letters.summary:
On final instalment of "Insular floras" [Gard. Chron.(1867): 75]; rejoices at extent of their agreement.

Some criticisms of JDH’s position on geographical affinities, and volcanic islands.

letters.title: To John Murray   29 January [1867]
letters.summary: CD agrees to JM’s proposal of half-profits. Thinks it a mistake to print only 750 copies. The agreement on half-profit is for first edition only. CD estimates his book at a higher value than JM does.

letters.title: From John Murray   30 January [1867]
letters.summary: First portion ofVariationMS has been set up. Murray will not decide on number to be printed until he has read a good portion. The agreement applies only to the first edition.

letters.title: To John Murray   31 January [1867]
letters.summary: Is convinced his chapter on man [forVariation] will excite plenty of attention and abuse, which he supposes is as good as praise for selling a book.

letters.title: From William Darwin Fox   1 February [1867]
letters.summary: Wants to know whetherVariationis published and how the other book [CD’s proposed volume on variation in nature] is going.

letters.title: To William Turner   1 February [1867]
letters.summary: Thanks for information about rudimentary organs. Asks about rudimentary character of human hair and panniculus carnosus.

letters.title: From Mary Elizabeth Barber [after February 1867]
letters.summary: Replies toQueries on expressionbased on observations of the Kaffir and Fingoe tribes in South Africa.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   2 February 1867
letters.summary:
Thanks for CD’s letter inquiring about capsules produced by theMaxillariawith larger pods [see5331]. Gives descriptions ofMaxillariaand of the other Vandeae.

DescribesOncidium flexuosum.

Tells of botanical results of recent excursion to the German colony Theresopolis. Brought home fine collection of living orchids.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   4 February 1867
letters.summary:
Has declined Presidency of BAAS.

Relation of insular and continental genera will always be difficult problem.

On Providence and the "continuity theory".

letters.title: From Lydia Ernestine Becker   6 February 1867
letters.summary: Thanks CD forLythrumpaper [Collected papers2: 106–31] and "Climbing plants" sent to Manchester Ladies’ Literary Society. Comments onLythrum.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   6 February [1867]
letters.summary:
Has just sent MS ofVariationoff to printer. Is in darkness about its merits.

News of family and their health. Riding seems to help him.

letters.title: From William Henry Kinnaird Gibbons   7 February 1867
letters.summary: Asks CD whether he has given any thought to the phenomena of spiritualism.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   7 February [1867]
letters.summary:
CD’sVariationis in printer’s hands.

Orchid self-sterility.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   8 February [1867]
letters.summary:
On the Duke of Argyll and a review of hisReign of law.

Asa Gray’s theological view of variation. God’s role in formation of organisms; JDH’s view of Providence.

Insular and continental genera.

Owen on continuity and ideal types

and on bones of Mauritius deer.

On man.

letters.title: From William Turner   8 February 1867
letters.summary: On muscles in man for moving skin, hair, ears, etc.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   11 February 1867
letters.summary:
Sends CD an English translation of his preface to the revised German edition ofOriginand asks his opinion of it.

Asks CD where he might get a specimen ofEozoon.

letters.title: To William Turner   11 February [1867]
letters.summary:
Thanks WT for information.

Will not include chapter on man inVariationbut plans separate essay in future.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   12 February 1867
letters.summary: Relieved that CD approves his declining the Presidency of BAAS. The BAAS and the role of scientific men in it.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   12 February 1867
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: H. T. Stainton should be elected F.R.S.

letters.title: To William Benjamin Carpenter   [13–16 February 1867]
letters.summary: Asks for specimen [of Eozoon] for J. V. Carus of Leipzig.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   17 February [1867]
letters.summary:
CD thinks JVC’s preface is fair to Bronn. Regrets JVC has not added notes of his own, but, having dropped Bronn’s appendix, it is perhaps best to leave the text without comment. Rejoices that the German public can now judge theOriginfairly.

Has written to W. B. Carpenter for a specimen ofEozoonto send to JVC.

letters.title: To Edward Blyth   [18 February 1867]
letters.summary: Asks to meet EB for a walk in the Zoological Gardens.

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   19 February 1867
letters.summary:
Encloses memorandum onOrigin[1866]

discussing mimicry in mammals and birds,

abnormal habits shown by birds,

behaviour of cuckoos,

and analogies existing between mammals of the same geographical region.

Speculates on possible lines of development linking groups of mammals.

[CD’s notes on the verso of the letter are for his reply.]

letters.title: To Edward Blyth   [19 February 1867]
letters.summary: Is so unwell he must cancel appointment to meet at Zoological Gardens.

letters.title: To King’s College, London   22 February [1867]
letters.summary: Asks for information concerning study at King’s College.

letters.title: To the Linnean Society   22 February [1867]
letters.summary: Sends J. P. M. Weale’s paper onBonateafor consideration by Linnean Society [J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)10 (1869): 470–6].

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   22 February [1867]
letters.summary:
Observations on orchid self-sterility.

Wants information on characters that may have originated through sexual selection in lower animals.

Encloses queries on expression.

letters.title: To J. P. M. Weale   22 February [1867]
letters.summary:
Discusses JPMW’s paper onBonatea[see5411].

Mentions Robert Brown’s views on pollen.

letters.title: To Edward Blyth   23 February [1867]
letters.summary:
Many of EB’s remarks aboutOrigin[4th ed. (1866)] are new to CD.

Thinks of writing a short essay on man.

Struck by EB’s remarks about orang. They are similar to Carl Vogt’s remarks on origin of man from distinct ape families.

Thinks similarity of orang to Malay must be accidental.

Will sendVariationwhen it is published.

letters.title: To Paul Rohrbach   23 February [1867]
letters.summary:
Thanks PR for his memoir onEpipogium["Über den Blüthenbau vonEpipogium" (1866)]. The structure and manner of fertilisation are new to CD;

he has long suspected that the classification of orchids requires considerable modification.

letters.title: To Alfred Russel Wallace   23 February 1867
letters.summary:
Asks why caterpillars are sometimes beautifully coloured. It poses a problem for view that sexual selection is the explanation of colours of male butterflies.

More on mimetic butterflies.

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   24 February 1867
letters.summary:
Discusses sexual and seasonal differences in the plumage of birds and coats of mammals.

Remarks upon variations in the form of the canine tooth between the sexes in mammalian groups.

Plumage of allied species of plover.

Asks CD’s help with work on unimproved domestic animals.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   24 February [1867]
letters.summary: Protective role of colours in caterpillars and butterflies. Sexual differences in colours of butterflies.

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   [after 24 February 1867]
letters.summary: Sexual differences in bird species and seasonal variation in plumage.

letters.title: From Benjamin Dann Walsh   [25 February 1867]
letters.summary:
Sends a copy [missing] of a lecture by L. Agassiz on glaciers.

Claims worker wasps can generate additional workers in the absence of the fertile female.

letters.title: From Trübner & Co   26 February 1867
letters.summary: Vladimir Kovalevsky wishes to translateVariationinto Russian. He offers £1 per advance sheet.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   26 February [1867]
letters.summary:
ARW’s explanation of protective value of conspicuous coloration is ingenious.

CD still holds to sexual selection with respect to beauty in male butterflies.

Sexual selection and the races of man.

Expression of emotions is another subject he plans to include in his essay [Descent].

Asks ARW to suggest an observer in Malay Archipelago to whom he might send queries [on expression].

letters.title: To Julius von Haast   27 February [1867]
letters.summary: Asks JvH’s assistance in making observations on the expression of emotions. Encloses 17 queries that are being sent to various parts of the world.

letters.title: To Robert Swinhoe   [27 February 1867]
letters.summary: CD’s queries on expression as reprinted inNotes and Queries on China and Japan1 (1867): 105.

letters.title: To J. P. M. Weale   27 February [1867]
letters.summary: Encloses his queries about expression which he asks JPMW to forward to trustworthy observers who associate with Hottentots and Kaffirs.

letters.title: To Ferdinand von Mueller   28 February [1867]
letters.summary: Sends his [MS] questionnaire on expression and asks FvM’s help in obtaining answers based on observations of aborigines living in the interior of Australia.

letters.title: From Alfred Newton   1 March 1867
letters.summary: Male dotterels take care of young and are less brilliantly coloured than females.

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   [2–30 March 1867]
letters.summary: Discussion of origin of domestic sheep races. Some comments on the yak and the wild ancestors of the llama and alpaca.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   2 March [1867]
letters.summary:
Pleased that CD approves his idea about caterpillars.

Thinks CD is right about selection in butterflies, but still believes protective adaptation has kept down colours of females.

Cannot yet see action of natural selection in forming the races of man.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   3 March 1867
letters.summary: He has promised Mark [coachman to R. W. Darwin and Susan] that CD will continue the payment of £20 a year after EAD’s death; the house is rent free.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller 4 March 1867
letters.summary: Reports observations on fertility of orchids he has self-pollinated and crossed with pollen of other species.

letters.title: To Alfred Newton   4 March [1867]
letters.summary:
Thanks for information about the dotterel.

CD had ascertained by dissection that the female of the carrion-hawk of the Falkland Islands is very much brighter coloured than the male. Has inquired about its nidification. Mentions other instances of female birds that are brighter and more beautiful than the males and suggests causes for this anomaly.

letters.title: To Frederic William Farrar   5 March 1867
letters.summary: Much obliged for lecture [On some defects in public school education(1867)]. Would leave classics to those with zeal and taste for appreciation. Learned nothing at school except by reading and experimenting in chemistry.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   5 March [1867]
letters.summary: Asks whether WBT can carry out poultry mating experiments for him.

letters.title: To George Robert Waterhouse   5 March [1867?]
letters.summary: Wishes to know the correct name for the British Museum’s specimen of an Abyssinian wolf described by Wilhelm Rueppell,Neue Wirbelthiere zu der Fauna von Abyssinien[1835–40] .

letters.title: From John Traherne Moggridge   6 March [1867]
letters.summary: Observations onOphrysplants andThymus vulgaris. Encloses sketch of different forms ofT. vulgaris[seeForms of flowers, p. 302].

letters.title: From F. W. Farrar   7 March [1867]
letters.summary: On improving the educational system.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   7 March [1867]
letters.summary:
Grateful for addresses of informants, especially that of Rajah James Brooke.

Dispatch of queries on expression. Answers will make interesting appendix to his "Essay on man" [Descent].

Protective adaptation of female butterflies believed probable.

Believes in sexual selection as applied to man.

letters.title: From Francis Trevelyan Buckland   9 March 1867
letters.summary:
Has been hunting for an otter-hound for CD.

Hopes CD will visit his museum at the Horticultural [Society].

letters.title: From Henry Walter Bates   11 March 1867
letters.summary:
Sexual ornamentation of insects: coloration ofEpicaliagenus [of tropical S. American butterflies];

horned genera of lamellicorn beetles [seeDescent1: 370, 388].

Wallace brought CD’s question about gay-coloured caterpillars before the Entomological Society. Members now seeking explanations.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   11 March [1867]
letters.summary:
ARW responds to CD’s list of queries about expression. Suggests acquiring informants through publishing the queries in newspapers. His doubts about their importance.

Has submitted caterpillar question to Entomological Society.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace [12–17] March [1867]
letters.summary:
Asks to be kept informed on gaudy caterpillars.

Problems of his work on man; scope and role of sexual selection.

Indulgence of interest in expression is simply a "hobby-horse". Will see whether he can get queries inserted in an Indian newspaper.

letters.title: From Benjamin Clarke   12 March 1867
letters.summary: Requests CD’s subscription to hisOn systematic botany and zoology[1870]. "Progressive development" is a leading principle of his work.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   14 March 1867
letters.summary:
Has been persuaded to accept BAAS Presidency.

On Charles Naudin’s discovery of seeds ofChamaeropsfertilised by the date-palm.

letters.title: From Vladimir Onufrievich Kovalevsky   15 March 1867
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for permission to translateVariationinto Russian. The translation will be guided by his brother Alexander, a follower of Darwin,

whose articles on the affinity of ascidians and vertebrates he forwards.

letters.title: From J. T. Moggridge   15 March [1867]
letters.summary: Sends several plants with abortive anthers or bad pollen.

letters.title: To George Moultrie Salt   16 March [1867]
letters.summary: Thanks for note and returns signed paper. Asks that the payment be made to his bank account.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   17 March [1867]
letters.summary:
The date-palm seed case is important for Pangenesis.

Reports experiments on pollination ofIpomoea.

"Insular floras": A. Murray’s paper inGardeners’ Chronicleis poor.

John Scott’s work on acclimatisation of plants.

The anomaly of the Azores flora on the migration theory.

letters.title: From Friedrich Hildebrand   18 March 1867
letters.summary:
Intends to begin a journal reviewing the botanical literature.

Sends his book [Die Geschlechter-Vertheilung bei den Pflanzen(1867)].

letters.title: To John Murray   18 March [1867]
letters.summary: The compositors have invented a title [forVariation] which CD thinks is better than the advertised one. CD can form no opinion on number of copies. Asks that clean sheets be sent to German and Russian publishers for translation.

letters.title: To E. Schweizerbart’sche Verlagsbuchhandlung   [19 March 1867]
letters.summary: Offers the German rights ofVariationif J. V. Carus is prepared to translate it.

letters.title: From John Murray   19 March [1867]
letters.summary: Agrees that new title ofVariationis an improvement. Now thinks 1500 copies a safe number to print.

letters.title: To Friedrich Hildebrand   20 March [1867]
letters.summary: Thanks for two copies of Hildebrand’s monograph on plant sexuality (Hildebrand 1867a).

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   20 March 1867
letters.summary:
Sends Naudin’s letter.

Pangenesis.

Benjamin Clarke is mad.

Interested in CD’sIpomoeaexperiment.

Scott’s experiments are all in CD’s favour.

Clarifies a sentence in "Insular floras".

letters.title: To John Murray   20 March [1867]
letters.summary: The new title is fixed. Thanks for clean sheets. As to number of copies, now that JM proposes 1500, CD is frightened.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   21 March [1867]
letters.summary:
Suggests change in sentence of JDH’s "Insular floras" to make meaning clear.

Naudin’s letter about hybrids.

Pangenesis.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   22 [March 1867]
letters.summary: Is sending a copy of [John] Shaw’s book, which Lady Bell says is based on Charles Bell’s papers [possibly C. Bell,A treatise on diseases of the urethra, 3d ed. with notes by John Shaw (1822)].

letters.title: From E. Schweizerbart’sche Verlagsbuchhandlung   22 March 1867
letters.summary:
Agrees to publish German edition ofVariation.

Discusses publication of third German ed. ofOrigin.

Thanks CD for portrait.

letters.title: To [?] 22 [March? 1867]
letters.summary: CD must decline his correspondent’s kind offer [unspecified], but he is out of health and has passed the part about dogs in a work now at the printer’s [Variation].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   23 March 1867
letters.summary:
More on Naudin’s hybrid; the wonder lessened slightly.

JDH’s view that insular plants [distantly] related to those of continents are common came to him only after the lecture was in print; has not yet thought it out fully.

Moroccan flora may throw some light on Madeira flora.

letters.title: From Hermann Müller 23 March 1867
letters.summary:
TheOriginconverted him from a Linnean interpretation of flowers and mosses.

Glad that CD appreciates his continuing work on mosses, in support of natural selection.

Plans to repeat CD’s orchid experiments.

Sends interpretation of the floral anatomy ofLopezia miniata.

letters.title: To B. D. Walsh   23 March [1867]
letters.summary: Thanks for Agassiz’sLectures. Lyell does not believe a word about glacial action of any kind in lowlands of Brazil. Agassiz’s view of glacial movement has been given up by physicists.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   24 [March 1867]
letters.summary:
Returns Charles Naudin’s letter with its case in support of CD’s view of impregnation.

Twits JDH for trying to wriggle out of error made in his lecture and admires his "candour in letting the rat out of the bag". [See5449and5451.]

letters.title: From Benjamin Clarke   25 March 1867
letters.summary:
Thanks for subscription.

Reports experiments with wheat.

Sends notes on producing varieties by pruning.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   25 March 1867
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Discusses the practice of exogamy; asks if any animals have an instinctive repugnance to inbreeding.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   25 March [1867]
letters.summary:
Thanks for facts on orchids.

Friedrich Hildebrand’s new book on fertilisation of plants [Die Geschlechten-Vertheilung bei den Pflanzen(1867)].

CD correcting proofs ofVariation.

FM likes Ernst Haeckel’s book [Generelle Morphologie(1866)].

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   26 March [1867]
letters.summary:
Sends CD a Cardigan Jacket, ‘one of the most delightful inventions of the age’.

Discusses the Duke of Argyll.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   26 March 1867
letters.summary: Has printed copies of CD’s queries [on expression] and will distribute them.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   26 [and 27] March 1867
letters.summary:
Will be glad to have seeds of plants and CD’s climbing plant, which he has no doubt isSiphocampylus.

Anxious about his baby [Reginald Hooker].

letters.title: To V. O. Kovalevsky   26 March [1867]
letters.summary:
Answers VOK’s questions regarding the size of forthcomingVariationand gives his consent to a translation.

But ifOriginhas not yet been translated into Russian, CD thinks it would be a better book to undertake.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   26 March [1867]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Close inbreeding and factors acting against it.

letters.title: From Andrew Smith   26 March 1867
letters.summary: On Hottentot ideas of beauty in women; their preference for women with large posteriors. [SeeDescent2: 345–6.]

letters.title: To William Erasmus Darwin   27 [March 1867]
letters.summary:
Thanks WED for a present.

Discusses the Duke of Argyll’sReign of law[1867].

Is busy revising proofs [ofVariation].

letters.title: To M. T. Masters   [28 March – 5 April 1867]
letters.summary: Discusses the orchid specimens received from MTM. Remarks on the self-sterility ofCypripediumand other orchids.

letters.title: From Maxwell Tylden Masters   28 March 1867
letters.summary: Forwards some plant specimens to CD for his comments.

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   29 March 1867
letters.summary:
Working on sexual differences in collection of horned beetles and will send CD results.

Answers CD’s questions [sent on behalf of Miss Tollet of Betley Hall, Staffs.] on mimicry – how it helps prevent extinction, the modifications occurring with a change of habitat until mimicry occurred.

Also gives some cases of sexual differences.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   29 [March 1867]
letters.summary:
Anxious for news about baby.

Will remember to save all foreign plants for JDH when he has finished experimenting with them.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   29 March 1867
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Thanks CD for information.

letters.title: To Hermann Müller 29 March [1867]
letters.summary: Has learned that Fritz Müller is HM’s brother.

letters.title: To William Ogle   29 March [1867]
letters.summary: Thanks WO for information on inheritance of deficient phalanges [Variation2:73] and for interesting case of the occurrence of anomalous fingers and teeth in twins[Variation2: 253].

letters.title: From W. B. Tegetmeier   29 March 1867
letters.summary: Answers CD’s queries about polygamous birds. Does not think appearance of cock makes any difference to female. Dyeing the male has no effect on female.

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   30 March [1867]
letters.summary:
Would like tabulation of horned beetles if not too troublesome, but would easily settle for general remarks.

On the subject of other species mocking Heliconidae, asks whether full-coloured ones were mocked. Expresses full belief in HWB’s theory.

Encloses a copy of A. R. Wallace’s letter to theFieldrequesting observations on which caterpillars birds devour.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   30 March [1867]
letters.summary: Believes beauty of male bird important for attracting mate in wild. Will be interested to hear how a dyed male pigeon is received by the hens.

letters.title: From George Gibbs   31 March 1867
letters.summary: Finds that after 12 years among north-western Indians he can answer positively only one of CD’s queries about expression. They do blush from shame or anger.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   31 March 1867
letters.summary:
Baby’s situation hopeless.

E. Perceval Wright on way to Seychelles for collecting.

letters.title: From C. W. Nägeli   31 March 1867
letters.summary: Summarises his 12-page letter in which he responds to CD’s criticisms of his theory of ‘perfectibility’.

letters.title: To Stephen Paul Engleheart?   [April 1867?]
letters.summary: Asks for a note about sling for Leonard’s arm, as he is about to leave for school.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   1 April 1867
letters.summary:
Cites cases of difference in coloration between the sexes of some species of Crustacea, annelids, and spiders.

Discusses dimorphic plants and self-sterility.

Outlines some experiments involving the crossing of different species of orchids.

Encloses extract from Carl Claus,Die freilebenden Copepoden[1863].

letters.title: From Hermann Müller 1 April [1867]
letters.summary:
Thanks for "Climbing plants" offprint and for references on fertilisation of flowers.

Considering the bounty of work already done, he is looking for something original to do.

Subulariadoes not grow in Westphalia.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   2 April 1867
letters.summary:
On whether to make woodcuts forVariationin Russia or use Murray’s stereotypes. He has similar advance publication agreements with Carl Vogt, E. A. Rossmässler and Theodor Billroth.

The Russian version ofOriginis translated from Bronn’s German edition.

letters.title: From John Murray   2 April [1867]
letters.summary: Asks if he should give the clichés ofVariationto E. Schweizerbart.

letters.title: From Isaac Anderson-Henry   3 April 1867
letters.summary: Will find out identity of Robert Trail.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   3 April 1867
letters.summary: Begins to hope baby may survive; description of symptoms.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   4 April [1867]
letters.summary:
Rejoices over baby’s improvement.

Horace Darwin has intermittent fever.

Thanks JDH for page of theFarmer, a great service.

R. Trail’s potato grafting case would be of extreme value for demonstrating Pangenesis. [SeeVariation1: 395.]

letters.title: To John Murray   4 April [1867]
letters.summary: Asks JM not to send stereotypes [ofVariation] to Schweizerbart until he has heard that Carus will translate it.

letters.title: To Thomas Blunt   5 April [1867]
letters.summary:
Congratulates TB on his son’s success in scientific studies.

Susan Darwin’s death [Oct 1866] has severed last ties of family with Shrewsbury.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   5 April 1867
letters.summary:
JVC is willing to translate [Variation], especially because of his conviction that progress of biology depends on proving CD’s theory.

Ernst Haeckel’s book [Generelle Morphologie(1866)] will do mischief because EH is so immoderate. Suggests CD tell EH that he has done him a bad service. CD is the only one to whom EH would listen.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   5 April [1867]
letters.summary:
C. Nägeli’s long letter on his four years of work onHieraciumappears to be valuable. Nägeli wants a set of British forms in exchange for German ones.

Sends note on a new genus of Umbelliferae (Drusa) in Canaries; speculates on origin.

letters.title: From Robert Trail   5 April 1867
letters.summary: Reports on an experiment in crossing potato varieties.

letters.title: From Frances Harriet Hooker   [6 April 1867]
letters.summary:
JDH has left for Paris with Thomas Thomson.

Baby is better.

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   8 April 1867
letters.summary: Arrangements for obtaining Carl Nägeli a set of BritishHieraciumspecimens.

letters.title: From Carl Vogt   8 April 1867
letters.summary: Asks whether he may have right to translateVariationinto German.

letters.title: To Carl Wilhelm von Nägeli   [after 8 April 1867]
letters.summary: Thanks for his long letter on morphological laws.

letters.title: To John Murray   10 April [1867]
letters.summary: CD writes about stereotypes for German and Russian editions ofVariation.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   11 April [1867]
letters.summary:
CD is delighted that JVC will undertake translation ofVariation.

Agrees with JVC’s opinion of Haeckel’s book [Generelle Morphologie(1866)]. CD believes it is bad policy for Haeckel to speak so positively about a disputed theory [i.e., CD’s] and particularly regrets the severity of EH’s criticisms of other authors.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel 12 April [1867]
letters.summary:
Struck by singular clarity of EH’sGenerelle Morphologie. Remarks on various authors seem too severe. Severity leads the reader to take the side of the attacked person.

Making slow progress in correctingVariation.

letters.title: To Carl Vogt   12 April [1867]
letters.summary:
Would be great honour to have CV translateVariation, but Schweizerbart has arranged for J. V. Carus to do it.

Has read CV’sLectures on man[1864] with extreme interest.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   13 April 1867
letters.summary:
Trail’s case is interesting, hopes it is true.

Has little faith in I. Anderson-Henry’s exactness.

Pleased with Paris exposition.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   15 April 1867
letters.summary:
Asks CD to decide which translator he would prefer forVariation. JVC frankly thinks Carl Vogt not the best man to introduce CD to the German public, though he has a greater name than JVC.

Vogt now preaches materialism in its most absurd form.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   15 April [1867]
letters.summary:
Thanks AG for his trouble about expression queries; wishes he had thought earlier of having them printed.

Is "plodding on" correctingVariation

and getting "a little amusement" from plant experiments.Oxalisis trimorphic likeLythrum.

Is continuing his experiments on seedling vigour.

Has heard hybrid potatoes can be produced by joining halves of different tubers.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   15 [April 1867]
letters.summary: Agrees with JDH about Anderson-Henry. He has however described in detail a curious case of the ovaria ofRhododendrondirectly affected by foreign pollen, like theChamaeropsand date-palm case.

letters.title: From John Murray   17 April [1867]
letters.summary: On cost of electrotypes from woodcuts forVariationand price to charge Schweizerbart.

letters.title: From Carl Vogt   17 April 1867
letters.summary:
Will send CD a memoir onLes microcéphales[1867]; CV believes microcephalism is an atavistic abnormality.

Recommends H. von Nathusius’ work on domestic pig [Die Racen des Schweines(1860)].

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   18 April [1867]
letters.summary:
Reassures JVC [who had received the impression that CD would prefer Carl Vogt as translator ofVariation].

CD surprised at receipt of an application for a Russian translation.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   20 April [1867]
letters.summary: Sends the revisions in the latest edition ofOrigin.

letters.title: From J. T. Moggridge   22 April [1867]
letters.summary:
SendsOrchis.

Is coming to London.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   22 April [1867]
letters.summary:
Self-sterility in orchids.

Growth differences in plants raised from self- and cross-fertilised seed.

letters.title: From Francis Parker   22 April 1867
letters.summary: Sends £600 bequeathed by Susan Darwin to CD’s younger children.

letters.title: From Carl Vogt   23 April 1867
letters.summary: Asks whether his former pupil, J. J. Moulinié, might translateVariationinto French for Reinwald. CV would provide a preface. Encloses letter from Moulinié to Reinwald.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   24 April [1867]
letters.summary:
Agrees to use Murray’s stereotypes.

Offers to send rug made from a black Russian bear he shot.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   25 [April 1867]
letters.summary: Has sent JDH’sGenera plantarumto Fritz Müller who finds it useful and offers to supply JDH with Brazilian plants.

letters.title: From Thomas Rivers   26 April 1867
letters.summary: Sends a root of a wild oat-grass from California and the root of a variety of barley that came from it. Several varieties of barley, all differing from English varieties, came up in the same bed of oat-grass. "The transmutation of a genus seems almost incredible" but TR has seen so many changes he has ceased to doubt strongly.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   26 April [1867]
letters.summary: Describes his view on colour [of plumage] of males and females – i.e., that absence of brilliant colour in either sex is due to need for protection in incubation, rather than to sexual selection.

letters.title: From Charles Loring Brace   29 April 1867
letters.summary: Letter of introduction to CD for CLB’s friend Robert S. Rowley.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   29 April [1867]
letters.summary: Comments on ARW’s view of colouring in relation to sexual selection and protection. It is not new to CD. Hopes to discuss subject fully in his "Essay on Man" [Descent]. As to the problem of brightly coloured females, CD is not satisfied that it is due to males taking over incubation. Admires "value and beauty" of ARW’s generalisations.

letters.title: To Charles Kingsley   30 April [1867]
letters.summary: Regrets that he is too busy getting his book [Variation] ready for publication to contribute an article toFraser’s Magazine.

letters.title: From Peter S. Robertson    30 April 1867
letters.summary: Describes his attempts to cross different varieties of borecole, and the results of the crosses.

letters.title: From Charles-Ferdinand Reinwald   [May 1867]
letters.summary: Writes about the Carl Vogt and J. J. Moulinié translation [ofVariation].

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   1 May 1867
letters.summary: Never imagined that the facts about sexual selection could be new to CD. Thought fact that brightly coloured females build concealed nests and almost all those in which sexes differ remarkably build exposed nests might be new to him. Some problems remain. Sends his notes for CD to use if he wants.

letters.title: To V. O. Kovalevsky   2 May [1867]
letters.summary: CD has sent some revised proof-sheets and ordered the stereotypes [for Russian translation ofVariation]. First volume is dull, but he hopes second is more interesting.

letters.title: From John Maurice Herbert   3 May 1867
letters.summary: Asks whether CD will subscribe to a memorial for Richard Dawes [1793–1867].

letters.title: From Jean Jacques Moulinié   3 May 1867
letters.summary: Through Carl Vogt, he has received the right to translateVariationinto French [(1868), preface by Carl Vogt].

letters.title: To Ludwig Rütimeyer   4 May [1867]
letters.summary:
Thanks LR for sending his works.

Correcting proofs ofVariation.

Chapter on pigs and cattle derived mostly from LR’s work.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   5 May [1867]
letters.summary:
Returns ARW’s notes. He will work up subject much better than CD.

Apologises for the note of illiberality in his letter regarding ARW’s work on the colouring and other sexual differences in mammals.

Discusses laws of inheritance based on sexual selection.

He questions the extent of applicability of principles of protection and sexual selection to lower animal forms, though Ernst Haeckel has shown how protection may account for transparency and absence of colour in lower oceanic animals.

letters.title: To J. M. Herbert   7 May [1867]
letters.summary:
Contributes to a memorial for Richard Dawes.

Describes his health.

letters.title: From Nicholas Trübner   7 May 1867
letters.summary: Weisse of Stuttgart is keen to publish a translation of the book on which CD is working [Variation].

letters.title: From Julius von Haast   12 May – 2 June 1867
letters.summary: JvH will help with expression queries. Considers CD’s investigation highly important and original. Sends list of men to whom he is sending copies of the questions.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   12 May 1867
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for new edition ofOrigin[4th ed. (1866)].

Comments on CD’s criticism of the harsh tone ofGenerelle Morphologie. Thinks he may have harmed himself but not the cause. Believes a radical reform of the science necessary, and since most scientists take a prejudiced view of the matter, a vigorous attack is essential.

Describes his travels in Canaries, Spain, and France.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [12] May [1867]
letters.summary: Sends Fritz Müller’s address; has sent himInsular floras[pamphlet].

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   14 May 1867
letters.summary: The proofs CD sent seem to have been lost in the post. Asks him to send another set by ordinary letter post.

letters.title: From J. W. Salter   14 May 1867
letters.summary: Having tried all other sources for aid, JWS is forced to turn to CD’s generosity. His financial position is bad; frequent and serious illness prevents him from working properly.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   15 May 1867
letters.summary:
Lost proofs have arrived.

Proposes to append the woodcuts of dog and cat varieties from Brehm [Illustrirtes Thierleben(1864–7)], which he has also translated, to the Russian edition ofVariation.

letters.title: To V. O. Kovalevsky   16 May [1867]
letters.summary: Sends proof-sheets [ofVariation]. Will not charge VOK for right of translation.

letters.title: To J. J. Moulinié   16 May [1867]
letters.summary: Sheets dispatched. Book [French edition ofVariation] not so large as expected.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   17 May 1867
letters.summary:
Cannot come to Down; John Smith is unwell.

Will go to Paris again at end of month.

Wallace and F. J. H. von Mueller of Victoria are most likely candidates for Royal Society Gold Medal for biology.

Encloses letter from Henry Barkly.

letters.title: From Camille Dareste   19 May 1867
letters.summary: CD’s letter [3992] gave him encouragement in his work [on monstrosities], which, he regrets, is little understood or appreciated in France. Hopes to be able to produce anomalies at will as a result of his experiments. Sends a recent paper ["Rapport sur un veau monstrueux",Arch. Com. Agric. Arrondissement Lille(1867)].

letters.title: From Isaac Anderson-Henry   20 May 1867
letters.summary:
Offers to send Benoît de Maillet’sTelliamed[1750].

Encloses a letter [16 May 1867] from John Anderson, a nurseryman, giving information on budding of blotched ash at the nursery.

letters.title: To V. O. Kovalevsky   20 May [1867]
letters.summary: CD is sorry proof-sheets were lost; hopes clean sheets will have arrived.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel 21 May [1867]
letters.summary:
Discusses his previous criticisms of EH’sGenerelle Morphologie. Fears it will make enemies.

Discusses reception of descent theory in England.

Mentions EH’s trip to Canary Islands.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [21 May 1867]
letters.summary:
Glad to hear Wallace is contender for Gold Medal. Has highest esteem for his extraordinary talents.

Thanks for H. Barkly’s letter from Mauritius.

Glad to see HB takes same view as CD about bones of deer [see5395].

Objections to continental extension theory.

Progress [onVariation] very slow.

letters.title: To Isaac Anderson-Henry   22 May [1867]
letters.summary:
Obliged for case of grafted ash.

Asks about pods ofArabis.

Would like to borrow Maillet [Telliamed(1750)].

letters.title: From Albert Gaudry   22 May 1867
letters.summary:
Sends a notice on a reptile intermediate between true Triassic reptiles and Devonian fishes ["Sur le reptile (Actinodon)",C. R. Hebd. Acad. Sci.63 (1866): 341–4].

Expresses his admiration for CD, and his growing sense that transformation of species is probable, though he does not share CD’s explanation of the cause. He avoids the question, since he lacks requisite knowledge and is convinced that there are causes of which God alone knows the secret.

letters.title: To Camille Dareste   23 May 1867
letters.summary:
Praises Dareste’s work on teratology; is convinced that it will be highly valued.

Is working onVariation; will send a copy when published.

letters.title: From Isaac Anderson-Henry   24 May 1867
letters.summary:
Has crossed pods ofArabis blepharophyllalarger than normal ones.

SendsTelliamedas gift.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   24 May 1867
letters.summary:
Does not share CD’s objection to continental extension, i.e., that it must be extended to every island in every ocean.

Sends paper on domesticated animals by Brian Hodgson [J. Asiat. Soc. Bengal16 (1847): 1003–26].

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   [after 24? May 1867]
letters.summary: Repeats details of his previous letter [5537] as he was unsure whether CD received it.

letters.title: From Isaac Anderson-Henry   25 May 1867
letters.summary: Details ofArabiscrosses. Seed-pods ofA. blepharophyllaandA. soyericrosses are longer and wider than those of either species.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   26 [May 1867]
letters.summary: It was foolish of him to say a word about continental extensions so briefly that he thinks JDH misunderstood him.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller 26 May [1867]
letters.summary:
Thanks for information on sexual differences.

Orchids; self-sterility and difficulty of getting seeds to germinate.

Dimorphism.

letters.title: To George Howard Darwin   27 May [1867]
letters.summary: CD has come to think a name better than "Pangenesis" is needed. Asks GHD to get a suggestion from a classics scholar. "Cell-genesis wd be perfect if it cd be put into Greek."

letters.title: To Albert Gaudry   27 May [1867]
letters.summary:
Is much obliged for AG’s two memoirs ["Mémoire sur le reptile découvert par M. Frossard",Nouv. Arch. Mus. Hist. Nat.3 (1867): 21–40;Bull. Soc. Géol. France2d ser. 24 (1867): 397–400].

All "inosculating forms" are very interesting to CD.

Agrees with AG on the importance of attempts to affiliate extinct and existing species.

Will send French edition ofVariationwhen published.

letters.title: From J. T. Moggridge   29 May [1867]
letters.summary:
Wrote to J. B. E. Bornet on CD’s behalf, declining the offer of seeds ofDraba. But now Bornet writes that he is sending seeds to CD anyway [see5592].

Corrects his previous description of the fertilisation ofIndigofera.

letters.title: From Frederick F. Geach   June 1867
letters.summary: Encloses observations on Malays who have not had communication with Europeans [in answer to CD’s queries about expression].

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   1 June [1867]
letters.summary:
Comments on a discussion of humming-birds by the Duke of Argyll [inThe reign of law(1867)].

Encloses article by Henry Parker on the Duke’s book [Saturday Rev.23 (1867): 82–4].

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   1 June [1867]
letters.summary: Asks DO to identify a plant grown from earth adhering to the foot of a woodcock.

letters.title: From J. J. Moulinié   2 June 1867
letters.summary: Has received the first four sheets ofVariation. Reinwald has received the stereotypes and is ready for printing.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   2 June 1867
letters.summary:
Discusses dimorphism in plants, especially the Rubiaceae.

Gives observations on orchids; notes varying degrees of self-sterility and a varying success at crossing distinct species.

Mentions local ferns he is collecting

and considers the phenomenon of apparently mimetic plants.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [3 June 1867]
letters.summary:
Has asked a classics scholar about a word for Pangenesis. He suggests "atomogenesis".

Is getting in rather a fright about the coming exams.

letters.title: To V. O. Kovalevsky   3 June [1867]
letters.summary: Sends a sheet of proofs. Will hold four others until he hears from VOK, because of expensive postage. Thinks illustrating Russian translation [ofVariation] with woodcuts from A. E. Brehm’s work [Illustrirtes Thierleben, 4 vols. (1864–7)] is an excellent idea.

letters.title: From Edward Cresy   6 June 1867
letters.summary: Returns Hooker’s paper [unidentified].

letters.title: From Charles Kingsley   6 June 1867
letters.summary:
Criticises the Duke of Argyll’s book [Reign of law(1867)], particularly on sexual selection.

But CD overlooks God’s intention to instruct man by nature’s beauty.

Criticism of anonymous article inNorth British Review[by Fleeming Jenkin, 46 (1867): 277–318].

CK supports large sports in response to large environmental changes.

letters.title: To L. C. Wedgwood   8 June [1867–72]
letters.summary: Asks her to observe whether her dog exposes his teeth when barking and to think of any facts about expression in her birds.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   9 June [1867]
letters.summary:
Discusses hybridisation in cowslip and primrose.

Mentions proposed visit.

letters.title: To Charles Kingsley   10 June [1867]
letters.summary:
Discusses the Duke of Argyll’s book [Reign of law(1867)].

Cites his own views on diversity of structure and beauty.

Encloses letter from Wallace. Sexual selection: evidence advanced by Wallace.

Discusses correlation of growth.

Comments on article in theNorth British Review[by Fleeming Jenkin].

Discusses the evidence from physics on the age of the earth.

[Four pages of the final letter are missing, but the draft is complete.]

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   12 June [1867]
letters.summary: Asks THH to think about a better name for "Pangenesis"; suggests "Cytarrogenesis" or "Atomogenesis", but still prefers vaguer "Pangenesis".

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   12 June 1867
letters.summary: CD probably advised omitting mention of experiments suggesting that oxlips, cowslips, and primroses could be produced from the seed of a single plant

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [16 June 1867]
letters.summary: Leaves for London tomorrow. Hopes to see JDH there or perhaps at Kew, but doubts the latter. He is not strong and has a good deal to do.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   18 June 1867
letters.summary:
Has been reading [H. C. Fleeming Jenkin’s] review inNorth British Review. Would answer it if not so lazy.

Has readMount Sorel[A. Marsh-Caldwell (1845)] and Disraeli’s life of Lord G. Bentinck [1852]. Bad science, bad literature, bad politics.

letters.title: From J. W. Salter   18 June 1867
letters.summary:
Offers to send parts of J. Syme,English botany[1863–86] in appreciation of CD’s aid.

Comments on CD’s species theory.

Will exhibit Cambrian fossil at next meeting of Geological Society.

letters.title: To J. W. Salter   19 [June 1867]
letters.summary: CD is relieved that JWS’s circumstances have improved. He is pleased to accept Supplement to English Botany. He will try to attend Geological Society meeting.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   [19 June 1867]
letters.summary:
CD is invited to see ARW’s collections at Bayswater.

ARW has written an answer to the Duke of Argyll andNorth British Reviewcriticisms.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [23 June 1867]
letters.summary: Disappointed at not seeing JDH in London.

letters.title: To V. O. Kovalevsky   24 June [1867]
letters.summary:
Thanks VOK for the present of A. E. Brehm’sIllustrirtes Thierleben[1864–7].

The woodcuts will do admirably [forVariation].

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   [24 June 1867]
letters.summary: CD now acknowledges that the sometimes very great sexual, i.e.,ornamental, differences in fishes offer a difficulty to the view that females are not brightly coloured on account of the danger to propagation of the species.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   28 June 1867
letters.summary:
Is engaged to marry Agnes Huschke. Will make wedding trip to Switzerland and Italy in autumn; therefore cannot visit CD as hoped.

Discusses present research. Comments onProtoamoebawith respect to origin of life. Says it makes question of common or separate origin of phyla unimportant.

CD to receive honorary diploma from Imperial Zoological Botanical Society in Vienna.

Sends photograph of Viennese botanist, August Kanitz.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   4 July [1867]
letters.summary:
Congratulates EH on approaching marriage.

Sorry he will not visit in autumn.

Glad EH is re-examiningProtoamoebabut puzzled to think what he can find.

Describes newspaper account of criticism by Agassiz ofGenerelle Morphologie.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   4 July 1867
letters.summary:
Has been too busy to write. Is leaving for Switzerland that evening.

A friend, who ran away from home as a boy, has two sons who have done the same several times. Is the case worth investigating for CD?

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   6 July [1867]
letters.summary: Acknowledgment of article on mimicry [Westminster Rev.88 (1867): 1–43].

letters.title: From J. P. M. Weale   7 July 1867
letters.summary:
Has distributed CD’s questions on expression. Observations on the natives.

Floral structure encouraging cross-pollination inPolygala.

letters.title: From James Paget   9 July 1867
letters.summary: Will seek answers to CD’s questions on expression. Observing patients’ blushing. Is CD interested in the platysma during screaming under chloroform?

letters.title: From Charles Lyell   16 July 1867
letters.summary:
Curious to read what CD will say on man and his races.

Has CD seen Ludwig Rütimeyer’sUeber die Herkunft unserer Thierwelt(Rütimeyer 1867c)?

Discusses J. F. W. Herschel’s theory of active volcanoes existing at the junction of continents and the sea.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   17 [July 1867]
letters.summary: Wynne [gardener] suggests he should be paid from the money from the sale of the Mount, but EAD suggests an annual subscription instead.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   17 July 1867
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for sending F. H. G. Hildebrand’s book on fertilisation [Die Geschlechter-Vertheilung bei den Pflanzen(1867)]

and J. D. Hooker’s "Lecture on insular floras".

Describes work on Rubiaceae,Oxalis,

and on crossing orchids. Lists crosses made.

As for CD’s query concerning sexual differences among invertebrates, he gives the case of the local amphipod,Brachyscellus diversilor. Male differs in shape of antennae and coloration.

Also mentions local fish in sea near Sta Catharina which emits melodic tone to attract females.

letters.title: From Salt & Sons   17 July 1867
letters.summary: Discusses proposed sale of house and provision for Wynne, the gardener, and his wife.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   18 July [1867]
letters.summary:
Chapter 12 [ofVariation] finished;

too late to include information on six-fingered men. Plans for book on man [Descent].

Mentions coral reefs of Tahiti.

Discusses volcanic islands; volcanoes of the Cordillera.

letters.title: To Henrietta Emma Darwin 26 July [1867]
letters.summary: Prefers not to send her proof-slips of the present chapter [ofVariation], which has been enormously altered, but will be glad to have her see slips and revises in future.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [27 July 1867]
letters.summary: Back from Switzerland. Mrs Hooker much improved.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   29 July [1867]
letters.summary:
Pleased JDH will come next Saturday.

Asks him to returnAdam Bede.

letters.title: To William Bowman   30 July [1867]
letters.summary: Plans to write a book on expression. Questions WB on orbicular muscle in screaming infant and function of muscle contractions in looking at a distant object.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   30 July [1867]
letters.summary:
Plans to come to Down on Saturday.

ReturnedAdam Bedetwo years ago.

Wishes CD would return Tylor’sEarly history of mankind

and his ownHimalayan journalwith his notes, "both of which I have lent, i.e., lost".

Lyell well and full of "Insular" difficulties which he will propound.

letters.title: From Hermann Julius Meyer   30 July 1867
letters.summary: Sends fourth volume of A. E. Brehm’sThierleben. First three sent at V. O. Kovalevsky’s request. Asks CD’s support for an English edition, since this is the first extensive popular work based on CD’s theory.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   31 July [1867]
letters.summary:
Has abstracted for insertion in his sterility chapter [Variation2, ch. 18], FM’s observations of plant’s pollen being poisonous to itself.

Occurrence of mimetic plants.

Colouring ofPlanariae.

letters.title: From George Henslow   [c.August 1867?]
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his interesting papers.

letters.title: From Charles Lyell   4 August 1867
letters.summary:
Comments on proof-sheets ofVariation.

His revisions ofPrinciples of geology, 10th ed.

letters.title: To John Murray   4 August [1867]
letters.summary:
Asks whether JM is interested in publishing A. E. Brehm,Illustrirtes Thierleben[4 vols. (1864–7)], which has had immense sale on the continent.

Is making good progress with proofs [ofVariation].

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   4 August [1867]
letters.summary:
Thanks WBT for proofs of his new book [Pigeons(1868)].

Hopes he still intends to try the experiment with dyed pigeons.

Was surprised to hear of B. P. Brent’s death.

letters.title: From William Bowman   5 August 1867
letters.summary:
Supposes that infants’ eyes bulge and become engorged with blood during fits of sneezing or screaming, but doubts Charles Bell’s experiment of opening and observing eyes turn from pale to red [Anatomy and philosophy of expression(1844)].

Discusses the action of the eye when looking at distant objects.

letters.title: From John Murray   5 August [1867]
letters.summary: He is unacquainted with Brehm’s work [Thierleben]. Asks that a volume be sent so he can form an opinion on publishing it.

letters.title: From Robert Swinhoe   5 August 1867
letters.summary:
Will do his best to get observations on expression among the Chinese.

Reports observations on hedgehogs collecting fruit with their spines.

Discusses the domestic pig of Formosa, its wild ancestors, and its capacity to breed with other races.

letters.title: To John Murray   6 August [1867]
letters.summary: Sends the four volumes [of Brehm’sThierleben] for Murray’s consideration.

letters.title: To William Bowman   7 August [1867]
letters.summary: Thanks for reply to queries. Spectroscope an instance of unimagined glorious prospects of science.

letters.title: To Carl Vogt   7 August [1867]
letters.summary: Thanks for CV’sMémoire sur les microcéphales[1867]. Curious how CD and CV have come to similar conclusions about atavism.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   8 August [1867]
letters.summary: Thanks AG for sending W. M. Canby’s letter onDionaea. Although already familiar with the facts concerning the secretions, the letter "fires me up to complete and publish on Drosera, Dionæa, etc."

letters.title: From Seth Sutton    8 August 1867
letters.summary: Reports observations, as requested by CD, on expression in chimpanzees and orangs at Zoological Garden, London [seeExpression, p. 95].

letters.title: To B. D. Walsh   9 August [1867]
letters.summary: Is not sure he thinks so much of BDW’s argument in his last paper as of some others he advanced. Is BDW sure Lucanidae use jaws for holding female in copulation rather than for fighting other males?

letters.title: From Andrew Murray   12 August 1867
letters.summary: He is planning a new journal to replaceNatural History Review. Unlike the old one, it would be confined to reviews and would include an index of works on travel.

letters.title: From George Henslow   15 August 1867
letters.summary: Proposes writing a note for Linnean Society ["Note on the structure ofGenista tinctoria",J. Proc. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)10 (1869): 468], in part using information CD gave him at Down.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   15 August [1867]
letters.summary:
Queries about expressions in crying monkeys.

Has received letter from Hermann Müller on orchid fertilisation.

letters.title: To Hermann Müller   16 August [1867]
letters.summary: Made aware by Asa Gray of error with respect toCypripedium. Does not doubt it is self-fertilised.

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   16 August [1867]
letters.summary: Discusses a rare shell found by BJS on theBeaglevoyage, an account of which has just been written by Davidson [possibly inAnn. & Mag. Nat. Hist.3d ser. 20 (1867): 81–3].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   17 August 1867
letters.summary:
His opinion of two novels:Mary BartonandNorth and south[both by Mrs Gaskell].

Sends R. O. Cunningham’s letters.

letters.title: From Edouard Bornet   [before 20 August 1867]
letters.summary:
Sends ten different forms ofDrabaand Jordan’s instructions on when to sow seeds.

Reports sterility of a cross of two varieties ofPapaver.

Thanks CD for a memoir.

letters.title: To Edouard Bornet   20 August [1867]
letters.summary:
Thanks JBEB for seeds ofDrabawhich he will sow next year.

Describes the results of some crossing experiments withPapaver.

letters.title: From William Angus Knight   20 August 1867
letters.summary: Offers CD a room for his forthcoming visit to the BAAS meeting at Dundee.

letters.title: From William Boyd Dawkins   22 August 1867
letters.summary:
On the breeding out of horns in Galloway cattle.

Has a finely graded series linking the dentition of the rhinoceros with that of thePalaeotheriumof the Eocene.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   22 August [1867]
letters.summary:
Thanks CL for comments [onVariation].

Thinks Pangenesis would be important step in biology if admitted as probable.

Introduction to French edition [ofOrigin] has injured the book.

letters.title: To Cassell, Petter, & Galpin   24 August [1867]
letters.summary: Letter recommending V. O. Kovalevsky to a publisher.

letters.title: From Thomas Wright   24 August 1867
letters.summary: Discusses coral reefs and sends CD his paper on "Coral reefs present and past" [Cotteswold Club Proc.4 (1868): 60–74].

letters.title: To W. B. Dawkins   26 August [1867]
letters.summary:
Thanks for information on Galloway cattle. [See5614.]

Interested in WBD’s work on descent of the rhinoceros; is pleased to learn that he does not consider species to be immutable.

letters.title: From W. B. Dawkins   27 August 1867
letters.summary: Thanks for CD’s letter; hopes by his work to add one grain of proof to CD’s theories.

letters.title: To J. P. M. Weale   27 August [1867]
letters.summary:
CD finds the case ofMuraltiawith irritable stamens curious.

Thanks JPMW for his help with expression queries and would be grateful for any more information. Believes the action of the so-called "grief muscles" is a result of combined action of two muscles.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   30 August [1867–70]
letters.summary: Asks FD to check whether a Latin sentence is correct.

letters.title: To W. B. Dawkins   30 [August 1867]
letters.summary: Suggests Dawkins publish a paper on new facts on changes in the skeletal structure of animals kept but not bred in captivity.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   31 August 1867
letters.summary:
Has given up Scotland trip due to his mother’s illness.

Asks for Fritz Müller’s full name – "he can help us much".

Reports on self-impregnatedVictoriaand impregnation of Chatsworth plants. Difficult to get foreman [of gardens] to keep accurate register.

letters.title: To Alfred Wrigley   [September 1867]
letters.summary: CD wishes his son Leonard to try for University this winter and intends sending Horace to a private tutor.

letters.title: From John Brodie Innes   1 September [1867]
letters.summary: Recommends a tutor for CD’s son.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   2 September [1867]
letters.summary:
Sends Fritz Müller’s address;

disagrees onMary Barton.

Seeks name of theMimuluson which he has experimented [seeVariation2: 128].

Requests flowers of yellow variety ofMirabilis jalapa.

letters.title: From Federico Delpino   5 September 1867
letters.summary:
Support CD’s views on variability of species, but believes they must be interpreted "spiritualisticamente".

Cross-fertilisation in the Asclepiadaceae.

letters.title: From W. B. Dawkins   7 September 1867
letters.summary: Variation between individuals of a species.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   9 September [1867]
letters.summary:
Suggests investments for CD;

discusses the opening of the Blackmore Museum, Salisbury;

mentions Edward Lumb of Buenos Aires, with whom CD stayed in Argentina.

letters.title: From Thomas Rivers   9 September 1867
letters.summary: Reports on a curious cross in peach varieties, in which the male made a firm large peach into a fruit more almond-like than itself.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   11 September 1867
letters.summary: JVC is having difficulty in translating the names of dogs [inVariation]. Also asks CD for help with names of pigeons.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [14 September 1867]
letters.summary: Is going to Norwich again on account of his mother’s health.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   16 September 1867
letters.summary:
Thanks JVC for his biography [of CD].

Has almost finished first proofs ofVariation.

Has difficulty in answering JVC’s queries about dogs because of differences in German names and breeds. Refers him to A. E. Brehm’sIllustrirtes Thierleben[1868] and, on pigeons, to Gottlob Neumeister’s book [Das Ganze der Taubenzucht(1837)].

Hopes JVC is not discouraged by first volume. Thinks second will be more interesting.

letters.title: From Andrew Murray   16 September 1867
letters.summary: AM discusses his new journal [J. Travel & Nat. Hist.] of which general opinion seems to be favourable. Has room for the occasional contributor, if CD knows of any.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   [after 17 September 1867]
letters.summary: AG has promised to review CD’s new book [Variation] for theNation[forwards a letter from E. L. Godkin of theNationto this effect] and wonders if he might have sheets a little in advance.

letters.title: From John Murray   19 September [1867]
letters.summary:
Sends CD cheque for £250, two-thirds of the profits on the sale of 700 copies ofOrigin, 4th ed.

Hopes he has found a suitable indexer forVariation.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [20 September 1867]
letters.summary: Would be delighted to see CD at Kew.

letters.title: To John Murray   20 September 1867
letters.summary:
Thanks for "pleasant remittance" of £250 for 4th edition ofOrigin.

Glad to see thatOrchidssells a little.

HopesVariationwill be more successful.

letters.title: From John Murray   23 September [1867]
letters.summary: Schweizerbart anxious to getVariationsheets for German translation. Hopes he has found a good indexer in W. S. Dallas.

letters.title: To John Murray   [24 September – 31 October 1867]
letters.summary: Instructions for the index toVariation

letters.title: From John Scott   24 September 1867
letters.summary:
Sends seeds ofViola roxburgianawhich produces perfect flowers in the cold season and imperfect ones in the rains, all perfectly fertile.

Leersiahas not produced a single perfect flower though it grows freely.

Discusses cockatoos eating various seeds. Finds it difficult to make exact and satisfactory observations.

Appends list ofVandelliaspecies which have perfect flowers.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   28 September [1867]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary:
Returns R. G. Haliburton’s paper ["The unity of the human race proved by the universality of certain superstitions connected with sneezing", reprinted inNew materials for the history of man(1863)] and sends one of his own partly in answer to it ["The early condition of man",Anthropol. Rev.6 (1868): 1–14].

Capital BAAS meeting at Dundee.

letters.title: To J. T. Moggridge   1 October [1867]
letters.summary:
Hopes JTM’s health will improve.

Asks for information about crosses of peas.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   1 October [1867]
letters.summary:
Informs CD of his reply to Argyll and theNorth British Reviewcriticisms [in "Creation by law",Q. J. Sci.4 (1867): 471–88]. Cites "thepredictedMadagascar moth" andAngraecum sesquipedale.

Birth of Herbert Spencer Wallace.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   4 October [1867]
letters.summary:
Replies to CL’s further comments [onVariation].

Discusses direct action of the environment as a cause of variation.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   5 October 1867
letters.summary: Asks CD’s help in translating names and descriptions of fowls [inVariation].

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   7 October 1867
letters.summary: Some sheets ofVariationhave gone astray.

letters.title: To George Warington   7 October [1867]
letters.summary:
Admires his paper ["On the credibility of Darwinism",J. Trans. Victoria Inst.2 (1867): 39–62, and discussion 63–125].

Ridicules William H. Ince and Admiral FitzRoy on their naive ideas about Noah’s ark.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   8 October [1867]
letters.summary: CD provides explanations and advice on translating names and descriptions of breeds of fowls.

letters.title: From Ferdinand von Mueller   8 October 1867
letters.summary: Forwards answers from Charles Walter to some of CD’s queries about expression.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   [8 October 1867]
letters.summary:
Has CD ever considered that the colour of seeds of Amarantaceae would attract the attention of birds?

Describes case of a climbingChamissoaof the local flora.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   10 October [1867]
letters.summary: Sends a corrected revise to replace a sheet which has been lost in the mail.

letters.title: From J. J. Moulinié   11 October 1867
letters.summary: Has received moreVariationsheets; some are missing. In a few days the first six chapters of the French translation will be printed.

letters.title: To George Warington   11 October [1867]
letters.summary:
Thanks recipient for the pamphlet, but he had already procured theTransactions.

Does not think that his views onOriginbear in any way on the question whether some one organic being was originally created by God, or appeared spontaneously through the action of natural laws.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   12 and 13 October [1867]
letters.summary:
Response to ARW’s "Creation by law", especially theAngraecum sesquipedaleand the predicted Madagascar moth.

ARW’s argument on beauty strikes CD as good.

Wishes ARW had made more clear the assumption of the reviewer [inNorth Br. Rev.] that each variation is a strongly marked one.

The Duke of Argyll’s argument on beauty is not candid.

letters.title: To James Samuelson   12 October [1867]
letters.summary: Thanks forQuarterly Journal of Science4 (1867). Has just read Wallace’s admirable article in last number ["Creation by law",Q. J. Sci.4 (1867): 471–88]. He is a master of clear argument.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   16 October 1867
letters.summary:
Anxious to read the second volume [ofVariation].

Appreciates "the way in which you [CD] teach us all how to look on, and how to study, nature".

letters.title: To Asa Gray   16 October [1867]
letters.summary:
Sends sheets of first volume ofVariation.

Transport of seeds in locust dung.

Pangenesis will be called "a mad dream".

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   18 October 1867
letters.summary: Must cut short visit to Down because of domestic problems.

letters.title: From William Houghton   18 October 1867
letters.summary:
Studying freshwaterPlanariae. Did CD find they had nervous systems?

News of T. C. Eyton and [William?] Owen.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   19 October [1867]
letters.summary: Concerning German translation ofVariation. Fears chapter 27Pangenesisis very wild, but believes physiologists will some day be compelled to admit some such doctrine.

letters.title: To John Murray   19 October [1867]
letters.summary: An absurd error ("Election" for "Selection") in the advertisement ofVariation. Dallas is the best man for index.

letters.title: From Joseph Plimsoll   21 October 1867
letters.summary: Seeks to save CD’s soul.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   22 October [1867]
letters.summary:
Response to CD’s comments on "Creation by law" [see5637].

The limits of variation discussed.

letters.title: From Hermann Müller 23 October 1867
letters.summary:
Thanks for German version ofOrigin[1867].

Dipterous insects are adapted to eating pollen rather than only to sucking nectar. He describes such adaptations in two dipteran species.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   27 October [1867]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Wants information on Fuegian harpoons. Must prepare second edition ofPrehistoric times.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   30 October 1867
letters.summary: Asks CD for exact title ofVariationfor German advertisement.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   31 October [1867]
letters.summary: Describes seeds transported in locust dung. Discusses other cases of transport and migration.

letters.title: From Charles Kingsley   1 November 1867
letters.summary: Sends a letter he wrote in 1862 [see3482].

letters.title: From John Murray   1 November [1867]
letters.summary:
Sends Dallas’ specimen of indexing [forVariation].

Asks CD’s opinion of likelihood of a hybrid of ass and bull, reported in a MS of a journey to Asia Minor he is reading.

letters.title: From Isaac Anderson-Henry   2 November 1867
letters.summary: Will send proto-Lamarckian pamphlet [1799] by Charles White, if CD wishes. It has a graduated scale of types from snipe to man.

letters.title: To John Murray   2 November [1867]
letters.summary:
Dallas’ index [forVariation] well done but rather too full.

A hybrid from an ass and a bull is utterly incredible.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   2 November 1867
letters.summary:
Variationto be published at end of month.

Dimorphism and self-sterility.

Seed dissemination inAdenanthera.

letters.title: From James Scott Bowerbank [4 November 1866?]
letters.summary: Reports two observations on crossing in dogs: the preservation of both pure types in the offspring of a pointer and a setter, and the influence of a first mating with a mongrel on the progeny of a Barbary bitch and a subsequent Barbary male.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   4 November [1867]
letters.summary: Sends corrected title ofVariationand report of progress in printing.

letters.title: From William Sweetland Dallas   4 November 1867
letters.summary: WSD is pleased that CD approves his index draft [forVariation]; notes his objection to long list of references under "Dogs" and will try to find a principle for shortening it. He has not indexed all authors’ names; is this practice satisfactory?

letters.title: To Charles Kingsley   6 November [1867]
letters.summary: He had no idea that the double function of an excretory passage had played a part in the history of religion.

letters.title: To W. S. Dallas   8 November [1867]
letters.summary: Suggestions on listing authors in the index [forVariation].

letters.title: From Charles Kingsley   8 November 1867
letters.summary:
Remarks on Darwinism’s reception. The radical press shies away, out of ignorance, because CD may be made out to be a Tory. He has met a Darwinian Marchioness.

The mystery of sex is the origin of all religion.

letters.title: From Edward Wilson   8 November 1867
letters.summary: Has sent CD’s queries on expression to some friends; encloses one set of replies [missing].

letters.title: From Francis Elliott Kitchener   9 November 1867
letters.summary:
Sends SwissAquilegiaflowers in which insects have eaten away the spurs.

Suggests fetid smell ofStapeliaattracts carrion flies.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   10 November 1867
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his two notes [on indexing references to authors]; will increase the scope of his citations by including those quoted in footnotes in support of statements in the text.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   11 November 1867
letters.summary:
Is not writing prospectus [ofVariation] – merely sketch of contents and tenor of first volume for advertisement to booksellers.

Questions on details for the translation.

Publisher anxious to get volume out.

letters.title: From C. L. Brace   14 November 1867
letters.summary:
Distribution of plants.

Removal of posterior molars a common dental practice in America [seeDescent1: 27].

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   14 November [1867]
letters.summary: Sends revision of vol. 1 [ofVariation]. Advance sale at auction sold 1200 copies, to CD’s great surprise. Publication delayed by index.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   17 November [1867]
letters.summary:
Has finished last revise of his book [Variation].

Is curious to know what JDH thinks of Pangenesis. It is fearfully imperfect, yet satisfying, for it connects large groups of facts by an intelligible thread.

Thomas Woolner is coming [to do a bust of CD].

letters.title: From Isabella Elinor Aylmer   18 November 1867
letters.summary: Writing article on Chillingham Park and its wild cattle; requests information on CD’s observations on their character and original breed. Was referred to CD by Lord and Lady Tankerville.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   18 November 1867
letters.summary: Is reading sheets ofVariation.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   19 November 1867
letters.summary: Suggests his father lend him the money to pay WED’s succession duty and thereby secure a discount.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   19 November 1867
letters.summary:
Will not be inclined to challenge Pangenesis.

Admits CD’s victory over JDH’s continental hypothesis (but will not give up Greenland).

Relation of variation to circumstances is shown by discovery of endemic St Helena umbellifer having same palm-like habit as an endemic Madeiran species.

Has completed Boott’sCarices[Illustrations of the genus Carex, pt 4 (1867)],

is printing W. H. Harvey’s work [Genera of South African plants, 2d ed. (1868)],

and is revising English edition of Alphonse de Candolle’sLaws of botanical nomenclature[trans. H. A. Weddell (1868)].

Arrangements at Kew. Gardener [John Smith] is very ill; Oliver reigns supreme in the Herbarium.

letters.title: From Edward Cresy   20 November 1867
letters.summary: Sends references to books by Charles Lebrun.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   20 November 1867
letters.summary: Has adopted CD’s plan of giving every author’s name in index [ofVariation], but it causes delay.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   20 November [1867]
letters.summary: Sends WED £200.

letters.title: From R. M. Rolfe   20 November 1867
letters.deprecated: Robert Monsey Rolfe, 1st Baron Cranworth of Cranworth
letters.sender: Robert Monsey Rolfe, 1st Baron Cranworth of Cranworth
letters.summary: Sends cheque for Down charities.

letters.title: From Samuel James Augustus Salter   20 November 1867
letters.summary: Has read CD’s queries in theFieldregarding the markings of dun-coloured horses. JS has for some years been working on and observing the occurrence of ass-like striped markings in horses and wonders whether CD received any response to his queries.

letters.title: From John Edward Gray   21 November 1867
letters.summary:
Thanks for skins and skeletons.

Has been arranging sponges [Proc. Zool. Soc. Lond.(1867): 495–558].

letters.title: From Joseph Plimsoll   21 November 1867
letters.summary: Extract from a sermon.

letters.title: From Karl von Scherzer   21 November 1867
letters.summary:
Sends copy of book containing measurements taken of individuals of different races during voyage ofNovara[Karl Heinrich von Scherzer, ed.,Reise der Fregatte "Novara", Anthropologischer Theil(1867)].

Asks for scientific advice concerning newly planned expedition.

Says Carl Vogt plans to use data from book in lectures.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin 22 November [1867]
letters.summary: Thanks CD for £200 and discusses meeting in London at the beginning of December.

letters.title: To E. Schweizerbart’sche Verlagsbuchhandlung   22 November [1867]
letters.summary: Encloses list of people to whom he would like presentation copies of the German edition ofVariationsent.

letters.title: To J. J. Moulinié   22 November [1867]
letters.summary: Will volumes [ofVariation] be published separately? What is name and address of publisher in Paris?

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   25 November [1867]
letters.summary:
Woolner’s bust.

Smith’s health.

St Helena Umbelliferae.

Brambles.

letters.title: From J. J. Moulinié   25 November 1867
letters.summary: First volume ofVariationhas been translated. He does not support CD’s suggestion that the two volumes might be published separately.

letters.title: To Anton Dohrn   26 November [1867]
letters.summary:
Thanks AD for his paper on "Morphology of the Arthropoda" [Rep. BAAS37 (1867) pt 2: 82], a deeply interesting subject.

Suggests he examine specimens ofScalpellum.

Fritz Müller thinks CD is mistaken, but CD cannot persuade himself he was wrong in his observations on Balanidae [Living Cirripedia2: 105].

letters.title: From Anton Dohrn   30 November 1867
