letters.summary: Pleased by CD’s letter; his object was to apply CD’s principles to the reform of zoology. When this is done, it is wonderful to see how improved one’s understanding of the Crustacea (Arthropoda) becomes. Cites examples.

letters.title: To J. J. Moulinié   30 November [1867]
letters.summary: Glad that Reinwald does not intend separate publication of [Variation] volumes. Book had large sale at [Murray’s] auction.

letters.title: From Henry James Slack   30 November 1867
letters.summary: Writes, as editor of theIntellectual Observer, saying how much he would like to be able to publish papers by CD.

letters.title: ToHardwicke’s Science-Gossip   [before 1 December 1867]
letters.summary: Sends, as corroboration of earlier articles on hedgehogs carrying fruit on their spines, a passage from a letter from R. Swinhoe [5598] describing hedgehogs carrying strawberries to their holes.

letters.title: From Daniel MacKintosh   1 December 1867
letters.summary: Seeks CD’s opinion and references on the causes of terraces in the south of England. He supports sea action as cause, either by currents or on coasts, and has been engaged in a controversy in theGeological Magazine[4 (1867): 571–5] with the subaerial school. Poulett Scrope thinks they are agricultural.

letters.title: To H. J. Slack   2 December [1867]
letters.summary: Explains that he has made it a rule not to write for periodicals, however eminent.

letters.title: From Joseph Plimsoll   3 December 1867
letters.summary: A sermon.

letters.title: From Julius von Haast   4 December 1867
letters.summary:
JvH forwards J. Stack’s replies to CD’s queries about expression [seeExpression, p. 20].

Sends photos of skeletons of six species ofDinornishe is assembling for the Museum.

letters.title: From I. E. Aylmer   5 December 1867
letters.summary: Thanks CD for showing him proofs [ofVariation] relating to cattle at Chillingham Park [seeVariation1: 81, 83–4]; has made abstracts of them for his own article.

letters.title: From Thomas Woolner   6 December 1867
letters.summary: Will have to delay starting on the bust of CD.

letters.title: To Albert Charles Lewis Gotthilf Günther   7 December [1867]
letters.summary:
Sends his photograph.

Asks for any information of well-marked sexual differences in snakes, batrachians, or lizards. The rattlesnakes at the Zoological Garden differ considerably in colour.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   7 December [1867]
letters.summary: Discusses transport of frog spawn and young molluscs by birds.

letters.title: From Edward Wilson   7 December 1867
letters.summary: Wants to catch some queen bees to ship to Australia; wonders whether CD’s sons can help.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   8 December 1867
letters.summary: Some corrections and queries aboutVariationtext. Is pushing hard to finish, but CD is right that the names in the notes make the work interminable. Fears he is causing delay in publication. Is astonished at "the wonderful array of facts brought together and at the manner in which you bring them to bear".

letters.title: From Daniel MacKintosh   8 December [1867]
letters.summary: Thanks CD for information on inclined terraces in S. America, which DM thinks applies to the chalk downs of S. England. CD’s definition that the sea widens and fresh water deepens is key to the subject.

letters.title: To Abraham Dee Bartlett   9 December [1867]
letters.summary:
Asks for name of the birds that have only once obtained summer plumage.

Wishes he could persuade ADB to experiment to see whether bower-birds prefer gay colours.

letters.title: From A. D. Bartlett   9 December 1867
letters.summary: On the summer, or breeding, plumage of birds.

letters.title: To the Linnean Society   9 December [1867]
letters.summary: Gives his comments on the merits of a paper on South African botany [by J. P. M. Weale, "Notes onBonatea",J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)10 (1869): 470–6].

letters.title: From John Lubbock   9 December [1867]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Introduction of humble-bees into Australia.

letters.title: To St George Jackson Mivart   9 December [1867]
letters.summary: Thanks for his memoir ["On the appendicular skeleton of thePrimates"].

letters.title: To Philip Lutley Sclater   9 December [1867]
letters.summary:
Asks for index to Zoological Society’sProceedings.

Mentions article on "Barbets" by PLS inIntellectual Observer[12 (1867–8): 241–6].

letters.title: To Herbert Spencer   9 December [1867]
letters.summary:
Thanks for copy of HS’sFirst principles[? 2d ed. (1867)].

Comments on HS’sPrinciples of biology[1864, 1867].

letters.title: From Francis Walker   9 December 1867
letters.summary: The horns and spines of homopterous insects do not vary between sexes. Sexual differences in Blattidae.

letters.title: To J. P. M. Weale   9 December [1867]
letters.summary:
Has had no less than seven grasses germinate from locust dung sent by JPMW.

JPMW’s paper onBonateais being printed by Linnean Society. [See J. P. M. Weale, "Structure and fertilisation of the genusBonatea",J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)10 (1869): 470–6.]

Refers to Lyell’s new edition ofPrinciples[10th ed., 2 vols. (1867–8)].

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   10 December [1867]
letters.summary: Sends errata for German edition ofVariation.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   10 December 1867
letters.summary: WSD is pushing forward as fast as he can with [index to] second volume [ofVariation]. The work is fearfully heavy.

letters.title: From J. P. M. Weale   [10 December 1867]
letters.summary: On expression among Kaffirs.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   11 December 1867
letters.summary: Regrets that the remarks in his letter [5712] seemed to CD to be criticisms. Nothing was further from his intention. He is working hard. "The subjects often seem to elude the Index-maker."

letters.title: From Charles Kingsley   11 December 1867
letters.summary: CK is drawn into discussions of Darwinism everywhere in Cambridge. The climate has changed in the past three years: the younger M.A.s are greedy to know more and the criticism of the older Fellows has a new tone.

letters.title: From Eduard Koch   11 December 1867
letters.summary: He is sending two copies of vol. 1 of German edition ofVariation. Thanks CD for rights to translate future works. Carus has begun translation of second volume. Asks when English edition will appear.

letters.title: To Charles Kingsley   13 December [1867]
letters.summary:
Discusses the reception of CD’s views at Cambridge and elsewhere.

Variationdelayed by the index, but will appear at the end of the year.

letters.title: To Eduard Koch   13 December [1867]
letters.summary: English edition ofVariationdelayed by the index, ES may publish German edition at the end of December. Asks that Carl Gegenbaur be substituted for Haeckel on list of presentation copies of German edition, Haeckel will receive copy of English edition.

letters.title: From Andrew Murray   13 December 1867
letters.summary: Will return Federico Delpino’s two pamphlets soon.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   17 December 1867
letters.summary:
Hopes to get afternoon train from Victoria.

Woolner comes on Sunday morning.

letters.title: From Joseph Plimsoll   17 December 1867
letters.summary: A sermon.

letters.title: From A. C. L. G. Günther   19 December 1867
letters.summary: Sexual differences in reptiles, especially Indian [see A. Günther,The reptiles of British India(1864)].

letters.title: From Frederick Du Cane Godman   21 December [1867]
letters.summary:
Sends a copy of his paper inIbis[2d ser. 2 (1866): 88–109] on the birds of the Azores,

and one by G. R. Crotch on the Coleoptera [Proc. Zool. Soc. Lond.(1867): 359–91].

letters.title: To A. C. L. G. Günther 21 December [1867]
letters.summary: Thanks AG for information.

letters.title: From Henry Holland   21 December [1867]
letters.summary: Has received a copy of an attack on CD ["Darwinian theory examined"] from the author, but does not know who it is.

letters.title: To F. Du C. Godman   23 December [1867]
letters.summary: Will be pleased to receive FCG’s paper. Already has that of [G. R.] Crotch. Encourages further independent work.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [23 December 1867?]
letters.summary: Left his box of plants in dog-cart [on his visit to Down].

letters.title: To Roland Trimen   24 December [1867]
letters.summary: Invites RT to come to Down for a week-end.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   26 December 1867
letters.summary: He is vexed that CD has had to write again about the index. He has no excuse except "the nature of the work itself".

letters.title: To John Smith   26 December [1867]
letters.summary: CD is obliged for a note by JS on crossing theVictoria regia, just received from Hooker; encourages JS to further experiments, saying there is much to be learned on self-fertilisation of plants.

letters.title: From Clair James Grece   29 December 1867
letters.summary: Asks CD to write a letter on his behalf to John Murray. CJG plans to translate Eduard Maetzner’sEnglische Grammatik[1860–5] if publication can be arranged.

letters.title: From A. C. L. G. Günther   [late December 1867 or early January 1868]
letters.summary: The Cyprinodontidae family of fishes exhibits sexual differences as remarkable as any in reptiles or birds [Descent2: 7, 9–10].

letters.title: To John Murray   31 December [1867]
letters.summary: Introduces Clair Grece who wishes to translate a work on English grammar from the German.

letters.title: From Roland Trimen   31 December 1867
letters.summary:
On ocelli.

Sexual differences and proportion of sexes in butterflies.

Coleoptera.

[SeeDescent1: 310; 2: 132.]

letters.title: From Richard Barwell [1868?]
letters.summary: Crying and the action of the orbicularis.

letters.title: To G. R. Gray   [1868–72]
letters.summary: Testimonial for a position as a librarian. Recipient is the author of a great monograph on the Picidae [woodpeckers].

letters.title: From Hermann Müller January [1868]
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for his photograph.

Intends to start experimenting with mosses to determine which differences in structure are effected by altered conditions of life.

letters.title: From Osbert Salvin   [1868?]
letters.summary: Notes on sexual differences within certain species of birds.

letters.title: From Hensleigh Wedgwood   [1868–70?]
letters.summary: Development of complex language does not require an early civilisation. [SeeDescent1: 56ff.]

letters.title: From Friedrich Hildebrand   2 January 1868
letters.summary:
Reports making graft-hybrid potatoes.

Has found direct action of pollen inMays[Zea] crosses and apple-trees.

F. Delpino has asked for CD’s address.

letters.title: To Roland Trimen   2 January [1868]
letters.summary: CD seeks information on the variation of ocelli within species of butterflies.

letters.title: From Alfred Wrigley   2 January 1868
letters.summary: Expresses his gratification on reading of Leonard Darwin’s high placing on the Sandhurst list.

letters.title: From C. S. Vesselofski   3 January 1868
letters.summary: CD has been elected a Corresponding Member of the Biology Section of the Académie Impériale des Sciences, St Petersburg.

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   4 January 1868
letters.summary: Discusses mule canaries which show a tendency to revert to wild plumage colours.

letters.title: From F. A. von Hartsen   5 January 1868
letters.summary: Sends portion of his book,Grundlegung von Aesthetik[1869]. Argues that CD’s theory can be reconciled with religion.

letters.title: To Friedrich Hildebrand   5 January [1868]
letters.summary: Congratulates FH on graft-hybrid of potato. Importance of FH’s discovery to be discussed inVariation[2d ed., 1: 420].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [before 6 January 1868?]
letters.summary: DiscussesBalanophorawith conspicuous male flowers and absent female perianth.

letters.title: To Thomas Belt   6 January [1868]
letters.summary: Asks about expression of emotion among Negroes and American Indians in Nicaragua. Queries enclosed.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   6 January [1868]
letters.summary:
Thanks for plant names.

H. C. Watson a renegade about natural selection. Discusses HCW’s views.

F. Müller’s letter enclosed.

Friedrich Hildebrand’s experiments are splendid for Pangenesis [Die Geschlechter-Vertheilung bei den Pflanzen(1867)].

letters.title: From William Sweetland Dallas   8 January 1868
letters.summary: Has sent off last portion of index [toVariation]. Hopes CD will be pleased with it. Will never undertake such labour again. He fears it has been an unfavourable way to make CD’s acquaintance. Trusts to CD’s goodness not to hate his name for the rest of his life.

letters.title: From John Scott   8 January [1868]
letters.summary: Asks CD for memorandum giving his opinion on a proposal to move the site of the Calcutta Botanic Garden. Gives details of the position, the physical character and the climate of the present site to show how desirable a move would be.

letters.title: From William Bernhard Tegetmeier   8 January [1868?]
letters.summary: Has seen CD’s "carte" offered for sale.

letters.title: To John Scott   [after 8 January 1868]
letters.summary: Supports relocating the Calcutta Botanic Garden to a site near the Himalayas.

letters.title: To John Murray   9 January [1868]
letters.summary:
CD exasperated by Dallas’ delay in finishing index [forVariation]. "I am prepared to throw the Index overboard."

Thinks JM should reconsider publishing a translation of Brehm’sThierleben. It is excellent and would "sell largely".

letters.title: To Henry Hennessy   10 January [1868]
letters.summary:
Thanks for papers.

Discusses case of the Asturian plants and HH’s view of their introduction through the agency of man. Although botanists question whether plants are thus introduced, those working closely on insular floras are admitting this view more and more.

letters.title: From John Murray   10 January [1868]
letters.summary: CD’s anxiety about the index [ofVariation] will be relieved somewhat when he learns it has at last been set up.

letters.title: From Albert Gaudry   11 January 1868
letters.summary:
Sends an article ["Des lumières que la géologie peut jeter sur … l’histoire ancienne des Athéniens"] extracted from his work [Animaux fossiles et géologie de l’Attique(1862–7)]. CD’s letters have been an encouragement.

Hopes the belief in transformation will gradually be accepted. For himself the idea in no way undermines his idea of spirituality and his respect for human dignity.

Hopes to continue his work on the genealogical relationship (enchaînement) of fossils.

letters.title: From Roland Trimen   13 January 1868
letters.summary:
Variations in the ocelli of Lepidoptera.

Encloses six pages from his catalogue of S. African butterflies [Rhopalocera Africae australis, 2 pts (1862, 1866)].

letters.title: To W. S. Dallas   [14 January 1868]
letters.summary: CD was frustrated by the delay [in producing index forVariation], but was quite mollified by WSD’s note; is sorry the work turned out so badly for him.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   14 January [1868]
letters.summary: Has read sheets ofVariationup to Pangenesis.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   15 January 1868
letters.summary: Thanks CD for cheque for £5.5.0 supplementing fee from J. Murray’s. Will return it if Murray provides an additional amount. Is glad CD is so well pleased. Sends notes for errata.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   15 January 1868
letters.summary:
Sends a pamphlet by W. R. Greg [Malthus: re-examined by the light of physiology(1868)].

Many Cucurbitaceae have smaller male than female flowers.

Has written to H. C. Watson on the counterbalance [to variation] of crossing and uniform conditions. Watson has forgotten the argument.

Has written to F. Müller on abnormalSolanum.

Does not understand Hildebrand on potatoes.

letters.title: From John Brodie Innes   16 January 1868
letters.summary: Sends school subscription to CD as treasurer. Hopes Henrietta will assist in teaching there.

letters.title: To Roland Trimen   16 January [1868]
letters.summary: Thanks RT for drawings of ocelli, especially for the description of ocelli of S. African Saturniidae. Would like to know of any cases in which the ocelli are confined to the male, to illustrate better the case of the peacock.

letters.title: To J. B. Innes   20 January [1868]
letters.summary:
CD thanks JBI for contribution to Down school.

George [Darwin] has passed his examination at Cambridge;

Henrietta has been poorly.

letters.title: To Albert Gaudry   21 January [1868]
letters.summary:
Thanks AG for his essay on geology and Athenian history [see5784].

Comments on French rejection of evolution. "How strange that the country of Buffon, Geoffroy and especially Lamarck should now cling to species as immutable creations."

Variationwill soon appear in French.

letters.title: From Henry Lee   21 January 1868
letters.summary: Table of numbers of trout taken for ova; includes males counted. [SeeDescent1: 308].

letters.title: To J. P. M. Weale   23 January [1868]
letters.summary:
Thanks for information on expression.

Poor progress of civilisation in South Africa. CD’s doubts and fears about democracy.

JPMW’s views on glaciation in S. Africa will discredit him unless supported by clearest evidence.

letters.title: From the Commission générale des Ordres Royaux   24 January 1868
letters.summary: CD made a knight of the Royal Orders.

letters.title: To George Howard Darwin   24 January [1868]
letters.summary: Congratulations on GHD’s brilliant tripos success.

letters.title: From Charles Pritchard   24 January 1868
letters.summary: Congratulations on success of CD’s son [George].

letters.title: From Charlotte Maria Cooper Darwin   25 January [1868]
letters.summary: Expresses her pleasure at seeing George Darwin’s name as Second Wrangler.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   25 January [1868?]
letters.summary:
FG’s congratulations [on publication ofVariation] have given CD pleasure.

Trusts that FG is well again.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [25 January 1868]
letters.summary:
T. V. Wollaston’s financial misfortunes.

CD’s son George’s success [at Cambridge].

letters.title: From Henry Bonham-Carter   26 January 1868
letters.summary: Congratulates CD on George’s success at Cambridge.

letters.title: From John Maurice Herbert   26 January 1868
letters.summary: Congratulates CD on George’s success.

letters.title: From Frances Harriet Hooker   [26 January 1868]
letters.summary: Congratulates CD on George’s success at Cambridge.

letters.title: From Edward Cresy   27 January 1868
letters.summary: Congratulations on George’s being Second Wrangler at Cambridge.

letters.title: From Henry Holland   27 January [1868]
letters.summary:
Congratulations on George Darwin’s success at Cambridge.

Has still not discovered the author of "Darwinian theory examined".

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   27 [January 1868]
letters.summary:
Grieved by Wollaston’s troubles. Offers contribution of £100. "How foolish men are in their investments."

Delight about George’s success.

letters.title: To Benjamin Dann Walsh   27 January [1868]
letters.summary:
Is sending a copy ofVariation[to be published in a few days]. It cost more labour than it is worth.

George Darwin is Second Wrangler.

letters.title: From Julius Victor Carus   28 January 1868
letters.summary: Queries concerned with translating vol. 2 ofVariation.

letters.title: To Julius von Haast   28 January [1868]
letters.summary:
Thanks JvH for J. Stack’s answers [to queries about expression]. Though few, they are the best and clearest he has received. Sends a corrected printed version of queries.

Belatedly thanks JvH for his splendid report on glaciers [missing].

CD lives "in constant state of overwork and fatigue".

Everyone astonished byDinornisphotos.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   28 January 1868
letters.summary:
Wollaston’s situation hopeless; he must go to Boulogne or Jersey to live. A friend will keep his collection and books together.

JDH’s opinion of Wollaston’sColeoptera Hesperidum[1867].

Cannot read Duke of Argyll.

CD’s view of Asa Gray as foreign member of Royal Society; compares him to Candolle.

letters.title: From Alexander F. Boardman   29 January 1868
letters.summary: Gives his speculative thoughts on geographical, political, and biological factors in the origin and development of human races.

letters.title: To Edward Cresy   29 January [1868]
letters.summary: Thanks for note about George Darwin’s gaining Second Wrangler.

letters.title: From Alfred Newton   29 January 1868
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for present [ofVariation].

Congratulates CD on success of his son George in mathematical tripos.

letters.title: From James Paget   29 January 1868
letters.summary: Thanks forVariation. Expects to be made more ashamed by his ignorance of the "influence of inheritance on the variations and mixtures of disease".

letters.title: From Thomas Henry Huxley   [before 30 January 1868]
letters.summary:
Congratulations on George’s attaining Second Wrangler.

Variationhas just arrived. Wishes he had two heads or a body that needed no rest.

letters.title: To J. M. Herbert   30 January [1868]
letters.summary:
Thanks JMH for his congratulations.

Recalls gift of microscope [from JMH in 1831]. [See99].

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   30 January [1868]
letters.summary:
Thanks for congratulations.

Doubts THH’s response to Pangenesis will give him pleasure. "Oh Lord what a blowing up I may receive."

Still thinks THH has been too "sharp sighted" on hybridism.

Sends Mrs HuxleyQueries about expression.

letters.title: From J. B. Innes   30 January 1868
letters.summary: Congratulates CD on son’s [George’s] distinction [Second Wrangler] at Cambridge.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   30 January 1868
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Many thanks for the book [Variation].

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   30 January [1868]
letters.summary:
SendsVariationand would like to hear what FM thinks of Pangenesis.

Thanks for information on expression.

Dimorphic plants;

differences in seed production in cross- and self-fertilised plants.

letters.title: From William Boyd Dawkins   31 January 1868
letters.summary:
Thanks for copy of CD’s latest book [Variation].

European converts to CD’s theory.

letters.title: To F. H. Hooker   31 January [1868]
letters.summary:
Thanks for congratulations on George’s attaining Second Wrangler.

George will try for a fellowship at Trinity.

CD believes real education begins after school days.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [31 January 1868]
letters.summary:
Royal Society Council would feel bound to vote for Candolle, but privately would twenty times rather see Asa Gray elected.

Asks for title of Wollaston’s Cape Verde book [Coleoptera Hesperidum(1867)].

Supposes JDH has received his letter in answer to Gray.

Has been writing two long papers for Linnean Society [reprinted inForms of flowers].

letters.title: From Henry Johnson   31 January 1868
letters.summary:
Congratulations on George Darwin’s success at Cambridge

and CD’s world-wide reputation.

letters.title: From Thomas Rivers   31 January 1868
letters.summary: Thanks CD for sending himVariationand for honouring his name by its frequent mention in the work.

letters.title: From Bartholomew James Sulivan   31 January 1868
letters.summary: Congratulations on George Darwin’s performance at Cambridge.

letters.title: To George Henry Kendrick Thwaites   31 January [1868]
letters.summary: Asks GHKT about eyes of screaming elephants.

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   [before February 1868]
letters.summary: Notes on the taxonomy ofPrimula.

letters.title: From William Blenkiron Jr   [c.February 1868?]
letters.summary: Answers for father, who is ill, on difference between manes of stallions and mares.

letters.title: To Reviewer   [February–April 1868?]
letters.summary: Suggests, if further notice is to be taken ofVariation, that the reviewer grapple with the subject of Pangenesis. Thanks him for his fair and friendly spirit.

letters.title: From William Bowman   1 February 1868
letters.summary: Thanks CD for the gift of his new work [Variation].

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   1 February [1868]
letters.summary: Questions arising in German translation ofVariation; its sales prospects. CD from the first has said it was very doubtful that the book was worth translating.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   1 February 1868
letters.summary:
Amazed that Hugo von Mohl and E. M. Fries are not foreign members of Royal Society; Thomson going over the whole matter.

Candolle’s contribution to botany.

Lubbock shocked about Wollaston.

CD’s answer to Greg was capital.

Comments onVariation.

Charles Murchison’s work on Falconer’sMemoirs[Palaeontological memoirs and notes of the late Hugh Falconer(1868)] and JDH on Falconer.

letters.title: To William Lonsdale   1 February [1868]
letters.summary:
Thanks WL for sending congratulations [on George Darwin’s attaining Second Wrangler].

Relays news about Sedgwick’s condition.

Has finished a large book on variation.

letters.title: From Albrecht Graf von Bernstorff   3 February 1868
letters.summary: His Majesty the King of Prussia has conferred upon CD the Order,Pour le Mérite, for Sciences and Arts.

letters.title: From William Darwin Fox   3 February [1868]
letters.summary:
Congratulates [G. H. Darwin] on being Second Wrangler.

Thanks CD forVariation.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   3 February [1868]
letters.summary:
Comments on Wollaston’s troubles

and his book [Coleoptera Hesperidum(1867)].

Mohl’s claim to foreign membership in Royal Society very strong.

Has been in despair aboutVariation– not worth a fifth part of the labour it cost him.

Is reading F. A. W. Miquel’sFlora du Japon[Prolusio florae Japonicae(1866–7)]; wonders whether A. Murray could be correct in his view that an area of the sea prevented Asiatico-Japan flora colonising western N. America.

Comments on A. Murray’s book [Geographical distribution of mammals(1866)].

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   [after 3 February 1868]
letters.summary: Recommends J. Scott’s paper on crossing varieties ofVerbascum.

letters.title: From John Edward Gray   4 February 1868
letters.summary:
Discussion of the pig in light of CD’sVariation.

Work of Hermann von Nathusius [Die Racen des Schweines(1860)].

letters.title: From Edward Wilson   4 February 1868
letters.summary:
Sends some Australian boiled beef for CD to sample.

Congratulations on George Darwin’s success at Cambridge.

letters.title: To George Moultrie Salt   5 February [1868]
letters.summary: Forwards a letter from John Horner of Market Drayton, Shropshire, concerning £2000 he considers due to him from CD under the terms of the will of Sarah Bayley.

letters.title: To G. G. Stokes   5 February [1868]
letters.summary:
Thanks for congratulations on Francis Darwin’s success in the tripos examinations at the university of Cambridge.

The king of Prussia has awarded him the order Pour le Mérite für Wissenschaften und Künste.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   [before 6 February 1868]
letters.summary:
Describes his lectures on CD’s theory.

Thanks CD for copy ofVariation. Comments on book.

Describes work of two protégés in Jena: Nicolas von Miklucho[-Maclay] and Anton Dohrn.

His cousin, Wilhelm Bleek, is sending an article about the origin of language.

Asks to keep book a few months longer but will return it if CD needs it [Webb and Berthelot,Histoire naturelle des Îles Canaries, vol. 3, pt 1:Géographie botanique(1840)].

Describes research on Siphonophora.

Describes life in Jena. Mentions alpine accident during wedding trip.

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   6 February 1868
letters.summary:
Discusses the origin and characters of sheep breeds, particularly the merino.

Reports observations on reversion to wild type in canary mules

and lists some animals that show a unique development restricted to one side of their bodies.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   6 February 1868
letters.summary:
Forwards a letter from Secretary of Yorkshire Philosophical Society. Hopes CD will honour them by accepting.

Has heard nothing ofVariation.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   6 February [1868]
letters.summary: There is so much detail inVariationthat WDF will never be able to finish it. Some chapters, like that on reversion, are "curious".

letters.title: From J. E. Gray   6 February 1868
letters.summary:
Would like a look at Nathusius.

Edward Blyth’s inability to recognise cats’ skulls.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   6 February [1868]
letters.summary:
Delighted to hear of success of EH’s lectures.

Ernest Faivre [La variabilité des espèces(1868)] sees no reason to favour common descent of allied species.

Asks EH to pass German edition ofVariationon to Gegenbaur.

Comments on work of Miklucho[-Maclay], Dohrn, and Bleek.

Has begun work onDescent.

letters.title: From John Murray   6 February [1868]
letters.summary: Advance sale ofVariationhas exhausted the 1500 copies printed. Murray sends note for £300 author’s payment. Wants to print 1250 more immediately.

letters.title: From William Baird   7 February 1868
letters.summary: Colour differences in annelids and entozoa.

letters.title: From Edward Cresy   7 February 1868
letters.summary: Thanks for loan ofVariation. "The Saturday Sadducees" do not believe there are a hundred people who understand the argument. EC fancies he does.

letters.title: From Alfred Russel Wallace   7 February 1868
letters.summary:
Thanks forVariation.

Reports work on his travel book [The Malay Archipelago(1869)].

letters.title: From Albany Hancock   8 February 1868
letters.summary: On the colours of the nudibranch Mollusca. [SeeDescent1: 326.]

letters.title: To Yorkshire Philosophical Society   8 February [1868]
letters.summary: CD appreciates the honour of being elected an Honorary Member of the Yorkshire Philosophical Society.

letters.title: From Herbert Spencer   8 February 1868
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for copy ofVariation.

Discusses Pangenesis and considers CD’s "gemmules" comparable to his own hypothetical "physiological units" ["On alleged ""spontaneous generation"", and on the hypothesis of physiological units", appendix inThe principles of biology, vol. 1 (1864)].

letters.title: From J. Daly   [before 9 February 1868]
letters.summary: Corrections [incorporated in 2d issue ofVariation].

letters.title: To Asa Gray   9 February [1868]
letters.summary: Asks that Gray forward a parcel to J. T. Rothrock.Variationis selling well. Nearly all chapters written beforeOriginwas published.

letters.title: To John Murray   9 February [1868]
letters.summary: Heartily glad for JM’s sake at sale [ofVariation]. Thinks JM right to publish a smaller second edition, for "the public will soon find out that it is dull" – though scientifically valuable. The index is excellent. CD is "always greedy" for presentation copies.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   10 February [1868]
letters.summary: Has heard thatVariationsold the whole edition of 1500 copies in a week [see5844]. Has done him a world of good.Pall Mall Gazettehas review which pleased him exceedingly [see5874].

letters.title: From Roland Trimen   10 February 1868
letters.summary: Sends prospectus of forthcoming work by his brother [Henry Trimen] and W. T. Thiselton-Dyer [Flora of Middlesex(1869)]. Hopes CD will subscribe.

letters.title: From Charles Spence Bate   11 February 1868
letters.summary: On the colours of sexes in Crustacea; the structure of male crabs.

letters.title: To Henry Walter Bates   11 February [1868]
letters.summary: Asks about proportions of male to female insects.

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   11 February 1868
letters.summary:
Corrects some facts and gives further information on some points for the 2d ed. ofVariation.

Specific distinctions among animals.

Cercopithecusof Africa contrasted with theCebusof South America.

Notes on domestic fowls and their ancestors.

Slow growth of wild animals compared with domestic varieties.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   11 February 1868
letters.summary:
WSD is delighted to hear that first edition [ofVariation] has sold so well.

Has received a cheque from J. Murray for 30 guineas, double what was agreed upon. Sends a postal order for the five guineas CD sent him [see5788].

letters.title: ToGardeners’ Chronicle   11 February [1868]
letters.summary: Requests information on published observations on the proportional number of males and females born to various domestic animals.

letters.title: From Henry Holland   11 February [1868]
letters.summary: Thanks for copy ofVariation. Comments on it, especially on Pangenesis.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   11 February 1868
letters.summary: Is working on sexual selection and is interested in any anomalous sex ratios in lower animals and any sex-related characters.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   11 February [1868]
letters.summary: Wants information on sex ratios in domestic animals. Can WBT help?

letters.title: From John Blackwall   12 February 1868
letters.summary: Variability of sizes and colours in spiders; on proportion of sexes; courtship of spiders.

letters.title: To Francis Trevelyan Buckland   12 February [1868]
letters.summary: CD is much interested in FB’s remarks inLand and Wateron the apparent excess of male trout over females and asks for further information on other fish, birds, and domestic quadrupeds.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   12 February [1868]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary:
Discusses [Fritz?] Müller’s confusion about ova and pseudova; JL’sDaphniapaper [Philos. Trans. R. Soc. Lond.147 (1857): 79–100; see1979] first demonstrated their structural identity.

Points out a misleading statement inVariation.

letters.title: From John Murray   12 February [1868]
letters.summary:
CD’s letter encourages Murray to proceed with a new edition ofVariation; corrections will cost £176.

First notice has appeared inPall Mall Gazette[7 (1868): 555].

letters.title: To Roland Trimen   12 February [1868]
letters.summary: Is interested in the relative numbers of males and females of all animals; wants any instances of males, or females, being in excess.

letters.title: From Charles Owen Waterhouse   12 February 1868
letters.summary:
On blind beetles [seeDescent1: 367].

Development of mandibles inBrentus.

letters.title: From J. E. Gray   13 February 1868
letters.summary:
JEG and Nathusius on pigs.

Reference to JEG’s paper on African and Indian cats [Proc. Zool. Soc. Lond.(1867): 258–77, 874–6].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   13 February 1868
letters.summary:
Rejoices over news ofVariationsales.

Pall Mall Gazettereview [7 (1868): 555, 636, 652] is undoubtedly by G. H. Lewes [see5951].

Dinner at Lyells’.

Dean Stanley favours a monument to Faraday in Westminster Abbey.

Perceval Wright is back from Seychelles and reports on plants he collected.

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   13 February [1868]
letters.summary:
Sends photo of four Fuegians, including Jemmy Button’s son.

Reports incident of two wild stallions on the Falklands acting together in an attempt to take a troop of mares from an introduced English horse [seeDescent2: 241].

letters.title: To G. H. K. Thwaites   13 February [1868]
letters.summary: Asks whether mane in male ofMacacus silenusprotects it from bites or is merely ornamental.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   14 February 1868
letters.summary: WSD expresses his willingness to do further translating for CD. Sends terms of remuneration.

letters.title: To B. D. Walsh   14 February 1868
letters.summary:
Requests entomological data on sexual selection, especially proportions of sexes.

SendsQueries about expressionwith note: "a great hobby of mine".

letters.title: From W. B. Tegetmeier   [before 15 February 1868]
letters.summary: Agrees to help determine the sex ratios in domestic animals.

letters.title: From J. E. Gray   15 February 1868
letters.summary:
Slashing article onVariationinAthenæum.

Discussion of relationships of various pigs.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   15 February [1868]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary:
ReturnsAnthropological Review.

Asks to borrow Desmarest on Crustacea [Considérations générales sur la classe des crustacés(1825)].

Has been reading JL’s address to the Entomological Society [Trans. R. Entomol. Soc. Lond.3d. ser. 5 (1865–7): cxiii–cxxxi].

Would like to hear JL’s conclusion for or against Pangenesis.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   15 February [1868]
letters.summary: Is much obliged that WBT will undertake tabulation of sex ratios in racehorses, greyhounds, and cattle.

letters.title: From W. B. Tegetmeier   [16–20 February 1868]
letters.summary: Encloses information on sex ratios in thoroughbred horses.

letters.title: To A. D. Bartlett   16 February [1868]
letters.summary:
Asks ADB to perform experiment on colour perception in bower-bird.

Asks for rabbit specimens.

letters.title: From C. S. Bate   [17 February 1868]
letters.summary: On the proportion of sexes in crabs; coloration and structural differences.

letters.title: From William Farr   17 February 1868
letters.summary: Will gladly supply any information he can. Sends Registrar General’s reports; will inquire about the animals.

letters.title: To J. E. Gray   17 February [1868]
letters.summary:
Thanks for Nathusius [Die Racen des Schweines(1860)].

CD will call on JEG to hear his views on specific differences of pigs.

Does not know who has "cut me up so severely" in theAthenæumbut suspects "your great man in the Museum" [Richard Owen].

letters.title: From J. E. Gray   17 February 1868
letters.summary:
JEG’s paper on pigs is being printed [Proc. Zool. Soc. Lond.(1868): 17–49].

Colouring in horses.

letters.title: From James Shaw   17 February 1868
letters.summary:
Mentions review [ofVariation] in theAthenæum[15 Feb 1868, pp. 243–4].

Comments on adaptive utility of the right hand, an organ still undergoing specialisation.

letters.title: From George Brettingham Sowerby   17 February 1868
letters.summary: Sends data from J. G. Jeffreys on the form of shells of the sexes of Mollusca. [SeeDescent1: 324, 326.]

letters.title: To B. D. Walsh   17 February [1868]
letters.summary: Has looked through BDW’s papers and finds heaps of facts on sexual differences. Asks questions on sexual differences in particular species.

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   18 February 1868
letters.summary:
Has put question of proportion of sexes in insects to the Entomological Society. Quotes H. T. Stainton and F. Smith. Cites some cases mentioned by other members.

Is readingVariation; does not quite understand Pangenesis.

letters.title: From John Blackwall   18 February 1868
letters.summary: Proportion of sexes in spiders; coloration.

letters.title: From Robert Caspary   18 February 1868
letters.summary: Discusses the flowers of, and cross- and self-fertilisation in, certain aquatic plants. Gives cases of dichogamy and perfect self-fertility.

letters.title: To Henry Tibbats Stainton   18 February [1868]
letters.summary: Asks for information on coloration and proportions of sexes in butterflies and moths for his work on sexual selection.

letters.title: To George Gabriel Stokes   18 February [1868]
letters.summary: Wants to know how the colour of the eye of the peacock’s tail is produced, whether it depends upon colouring matter in the feathers or reflection, and whether any varying structural change will account for the series of colours surrounding it.

letters.title: To B. J. Sulivan   18 February [1868]
letters.summary:
CD thanks BJS for photographs of Jemmy [Button]’s son

and for the curious case about stallions, which leads him to ask whether BJS has observed that horses when fighting try especially to bite each other’s necks.

Does he know anything about male seals fighting?

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   19 February [1868]
letters.summary:
CD in utter confusion about differences between J. O. Westwood and HWB on division of certain insects. Asks if HWB will homologise certain families for him, telling him which terms would be most generally understood.

Asks also about differences on sound-producing organs of AchetidaeGryllidae.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   19 February 1868
letters.summary:
TheAthenæumarticle [review ofVariation, 15 Feb 1868, pp. 243–4] is a disgrace.

WSD will keep CD’s queries about Hemiptera in mind. Secondary sexual characters are certainly more marked in exotic than in British species.

letters.title: From C. O. Waterhouse    19 February 1868
letters.summary:
Coloration of blind beetles.

Sizes of sexes inTaphroderes.

letters.title: From Edward Wilson   19 February 1868
letters.summary: Encloses letter (not found) from Australian friend responding to CD’s queries on expression.

letters.title: From John William Douglas   20 February 1868
letters.summary: Notes on sexual differences in British Hemiptera.

letters.title: From William Henty   20 February 1868
letters.summary: Has read CD’s inquiry about proportional numbers of males and females born to domestic animals [see5863] and outlines his theory regarding the factors determining the sex of offspring.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   20 February 1868
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Found [Variation] full of interest. Has not yet made up his mind about Pangenesis; wants to hear what can be said against it.

letters.title: To James Shaw   20 February 1868
letters.summary: Is obliged for note on right-handedness. The subject is a very curious one, but CD has never attended to it and can give no additional facts.

letters.title: From H. T. Stainton   20 February 1868
letters.summary: Sends a preliminary reply to CD’s query [5890]. Ten males to one female among captured micro-Lepidoptera. Six females to four or five males in those he has bred. HTS is aware this is diametrically opposed to information from [Alexander] Wallace and Bates, but the true proportion of sexes can only be ascertained by breeding.

letters.title: From Roland Trimen   20 February 1868
letters.summary:
Proportion of sexes in butterflies; discussion of subject at meeting of Entomological Society, London.

Attraction of males by femaleLasiocampa quercus. [seeDescent1: 311–12.]

letters.title: To Edward Wilson   20 February [1868]
letters.summary: Thanks EW for information [on expression] about Australians.

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   21 February 1868
letters.summary:
Comments on J. O. Westwood’s entomological nomenclature.

Discusses the organs for stridulation in Orthoptera [seeDescent1: 352ff].

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   21 February [1868]
letters.summary:
THH’s offer to read proof of essay on man encourages CD to write with satisfaction instead of a vague dread.

Begs Mrs Huxley not to forget corrugator supercilii in a crying child.

letters.title: From Robert McLachlan   21 February 1868
letters.summary:
On numerical proportions of sexes in insects; coloration. Dimorphism in dragonflies (Agrion) in which usual coloration is reversed in sexes [seeDescent1: 362–4].

Wallace seems to ride his hobby too hard.

letters.title: To H. T. Stainton   21 February [1868]
letters.summary: Discusses factors possibly influencing the sex of caterpillars. Is gathering information on sex ratios in insects and would welcome any cases in which males seem to outnumber females.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   21 February [1868]
letters.summary: Thanks WBT for tabulation of sex ratios in racehorses.

letters.title: To Roland Trimen   21 February [1868]
letters.summary: RT’s argument about theLasiocampastrikes him as very good; asks for any similar cases. Wonders whether male butterflies may serve more than one female.

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   22 February [1868]
letters.summary:
Thanks HWB for bringing "the question of sexes" before the Entomological Society. Feels he will come to some conclusion by comparison of numerous observations.

It appears Pangenesis "will expire unblessed and uncursed by the world".

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   22 February [1868]
letters.summary:
Sends sheets of second issue [ofVariation] with errata and changes to be made.

Refers to a favourable review,

and a contemptuous one inAthenæumwritten, he thinks, by Richard Owen [see5931].

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   22 February 1868
letters.summary:
Has sent his translations [of parts of Theodor Piderit,System der Mimik und Physiognomik(1867)].

Fritz Müller’sFür Darwin[1864] would sell if well translated. WSD would be glad to undertake it.

letters.title: To Leonard Jenyns   22 February [1868]
letters.summary:
Asks LJ which British birds are polygamous. His query relates to the possession by the male of secondary sexual characters.

CD is also interested in the numerical proportion of the sexes in birds.

Asks about the use of the horns in male lamellicorn or coprophagous beetles.

letters.title: To Jean Jacques Moulinié   22 February [1868]
letters.summary: Sends corrections [for French edition ofVariation].

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   22 February [1868]
letters.summary: Reports work on sexual selection. Problems with the relative numbers of the two sexes and polygamy. Asks ARW’s help with several questions on polygamous birds.

letters.title: From Edward Wilson   22 February 1868
letters.summary:
CD’s queries on expression.

Sends photo of a native Australian.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   23 February [1868]
letters.summary:
Review inAthenæumfull of contempt. Is sure Owen wrote it [see5931].

Gardeners’ Chroniclereview [(1868): 184] favourable.

Fears Pangenesis is still-born. Cites Bates, Spencer, Lubbock, and Sir Henry Holland. Is sure Pangenesis will sometime reappear. Questions that are connected and answered by Pangenesis.

letters.title: To Hermann Müller   23 February [1868]
letters.summary: Offers to undertake publication of English translation of Fritz Müller’sFür Darwin. W. S. Dallas will translate it.

letters.title: From Hermann Müller   [after 23 February 1868]
letters.summary:
HM is certain his brother Fritz would like to seeFür Darwintranslated into English by Dallas. He will make arrangements with the German publisher.

Two friends are writing Darwinian works: Adolf Speyer on phylogeny of Lepidoptera

and August Röse on genealogy of mosses.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   24 February 1868
letters.summary:
Has difficulty translating Piderit’s use ofverbissen.

Will hold F. Müller’s book until CD decides about translating it.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   24 February 1868
letters.summary:
AG is writing notice of American edition ofVariation[Nation6 (1868): 234–6].

Pangenesis is "as good an hypothesis as one can now make".

letters.title: From Robert McLachlan   24 February 1868
letters.summary: Reports that when August Meyer confined several distinct species of Phryganeidae they coupled and produced fertile ova, indicating that some specific characters are not so important so far as reproduction is concerned [seeDescent1: 342 n. 2].

letters.title: From John Murray   24 February [1868]
letters.summary:
Second issue [ofVariation] is ready.

Murray thinks that theAthenæumreview was written by J. E. Gray [see5931].

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   24 February 1868
letters.summary:
Responds to CD’s queries on polygamy in birds and orang.

Discusses sexual selection and secondary characters; colours and sexual preference.

Expresses his admiration for Pangenesis; it is superior to Herbert Spencer’s theory.

ARW differs somewhat with CD’s chapter on causes of variability [ch. 22 inVariation]. Thinks several of CD’s arguments are unsound.

Briefly discusses how natural selection might aid in producing sterility between allied species.

letters.title: To Robert Caspary   25 February [1868]
letters.summary:
Will send English edition [ofVariation] when available.

Mentions revisions in second issue concerning graft-hybrids.

Asks forEuryaleseed for experiment.

Discusses fertility of crossed and self-fertilised plants.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   25 February [1868]
letters.summary: Is working on "Sexual selection"; asks WDF to send observations on birds’ finding new mates during breeding season [seeDescent2: 103–7].

letters.title: From Asa Gray   25 February [1868]
letters.summary: AG is not surprised at popularity of CD’sVariation. Gives some corrections for next edition.

letters.title: To Henry Lee   25 February [1868]
letters.summary: Thanks for results on sexes of trout. [See5793.] CD is collecting information about the proportional numbers of sexes in animals.

letters.title: To Robert McLachlan   25 February [1868]
letters.summary:
Is obliged for the facts about the hybrids [see5910], which permit him to reject the view of B. D. Walsh (and H. W. Bates?) that organs play an important part in keeping incipient species distinct.

He has asked John Murray to send RM a copy ofVariation.

letters.title: To John Murray   25 February [1868]
letters.summary:
Thanks JM for presentation copies [ofVariation]. Sends directions and list.

Has been told positively that hostile review inAthenæumwas by Berthold Seemann, to whom he once refused a testimonial.

On the whole, reviews have been very good.

letters.title: To Ludwig Rütimeyer   25 February [1868]
letters.summary: Will forward LR’s memoir to Earl of Tankerville. Has sent LR’s pamphlet on "Darwin Lehre" [Die Grenzen der Thierwelt(1868)] to a German lady he employs as a translator. Cannot agree that there is an innate principle of perfection.

letters.title: From Alexander Wallace   25 February 1868
letters.summary: Asks CD to make his queries about proportion of sexes more precise so he can keep them in mind in his experiments with silkworms. [seeDescent1: 313.]

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   26[–7] February 1868
letters.summary:
Could not believe Owen to be so demoniacal as to write theAthenæumreview [ofVariation].

Gardeners’ Chroniclereview [see5918] is weak. CD’s ideas on causes of variation may be as hazy as the reviewer’s.

Huxley’s clever remark on Pangenesis. JDH’s view of Pangenesis as fundamental to development doctrines, but nothing is gained by formulation in terms of germs or gemmules.

Tries to answer question on last page of CD’s letter anent sexuality.

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   26 February 1868
letters.summary:
Finds no absolute differences in size of sexes ofCopridae. Gives several other genera in which males are larger than females.

Confirms his view of stridulation organ of house cricket. [seeDescent1: 354–5.]

Tells CD of a powerful convert to Darwinism: H. von Kiesenwetter of Berlin.

letters.title: From Robert Buist   26 February 1868
letters.summary: On the pugnacity of male salmon during the spawning season.

letters.title: From Vladimir Onufrievich Kovalevsky   26 February 1868
letters.summary:
His translation and printing ofVariationwill be completed in two months.

His work on a relief committee for Russia’s agricultural distress has forced him to travel 1000 miles in the last week.

Plans to visit CD in July.

letters.title: From F. T. Buckland   27 February 1868
letters.summary: On the proportion of sexes in salmon, trout, and rats. [seeDescent1: 305, 308.]

letters.title: From William Farr   27 February 1868
letters.summary: Encloses table showing proportion of sexes in Rutland.

letters.title: From Leonard Jenyns   27 February 1868
letters.summary: On polygamous birds and the pairing of birds. Late singing of males. [seeDescent2: 107.]

letters.title: To Alfred Newton   27 February [1868]
letters.summary: Thanks for corrections of errors [inVariation].

letters.title: From Robert Russell   27 February 1868
letters.summary:
A reply to CD’s inquiry inGardeners’ Chronicle[Collected papers2: 135]. The proportion of females to males in lambs of highland black-faced sheep.

Sends paper on conditions that favour predominance of plants.

letters.title: From G. G. Stokes   27 February 1868
letters.summary: On the play of colours in the peacock’s tail.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   27 February [1868]
letters.summary:
Pleased by ARW’s response to Pangenesis.

On negative reception by his friends.

Further argument concerning sterility and natural selection.

Polygamy and sexual selection.

Protection.

letters.title: To John Jenner Weir   27 February [1868]
letters.summary:
Thanks JJW for his paper on apterous insects [see5939], which contained much new information.

Asks JJW for any information he may have on sexual selection.

Describes an experiment, still untried, of staining tail-feathers of male pigeons in bright colours to find the effect on courtship.

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   [after 27 February] 1868
letters.summary:
Trusts his paper ["Apterous Lepidoptera" (1867), printed for the West Kent Natural History, Microscopical, and Photographic Society] showed that he is thoroughly a disciple of CD.

Cites evidence that birds undoubtedly distinguish colours. [seeDescent2: 110.]

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   28 February 1868
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for second issue ofVariation.

Is glad CD is satisfied with his translation of Piderit.

Will not start on Müller [Für Darwin] until CD has communicated with the author.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   28 February [1868]
letters.summary:
Does not understand JDH on Pangenesis: on last page he appears to admit all that he regards as mere words on previous pages.

Wallace admires chapter on Pangenesis.

Pangenesis is a comfort. CD gains no idea from words like "potentiality" or "diffusing an influence"; atoms and cells give a distinct idea.

A. Newton told George that Berthold Seemann wrote theAthenæumreview

and that Lewis [Lewes] did not write thePall Mall Gazettereview [see5874].

letters.title: To Philip Lutley Sclater   28 February [1868]
letters.summary: Bird specimens collected by Capt. P. P. King eventually went to British Museum, but many specimens were incorrectly marked.

letters.title: To H. T. Stainton   28 February [1868]
letters.summary: Asks whether the colouring of particular butterflies has any protective function, to ascertain whether the function is other than sexual.

letters.title: To G. G. Stokes   28 February [1868]
letters.summary: Thanks GGS for information on the peacock’s feathers. Asks whether the colour zones around the "eye" could result from varying the thickness of the film of colouring matter or whether it would require different kinds of colouring matter.

letters.title: From Alexander Wallace   28 February 1868
letters.summary: Proportion of sexes in insects, captured and bred. [seeDescent1: 313.]

letters.title: To F. T. Buckland   29 February [1868]
letters.summary:
CD sends thanks for information; he will write to Mr Bush.

In relation to the fecundation of ova CD adds that he has compared the use of very little pollen against an immense supply; found no difference in number or weight of seeds or in their germination.

letters.title: To John Bush   29 February [1868]
letters.summary:
Writes at Frank Buckland’s suggestion. Can JB provide any information on the proportion of sexes in rats?

Do male rats fight for the possession of the female? Are they polygamous?

letters.title: To J. B. Baillière et ses fils 29 February [1868]
letters.deprecated: J. B. Baillière et ses fils
letters.recipient: J. B. Baillière et ses fils
letters.summary: Sends stamps to the value of 1s. 1d. and asks for parcel to be sent to 6 Queen Anne Street, Cavendish Square, London.

letters.title: To Leonard Jenyns   29 February [1868]
letters.summary: Thanks LJ for his useful facts. Will "look to" the reference about the nightingale.

letters.title: From William Sedgwick   29 February 1868
letters.summary:
Sends extracts giving details of the case of age-limited, hereditary blindness [seeVariation2: 78].

Recounts some cases of reversion that he has encountered.

letters.title: From H. T. Stainton   29 February 1868
letters.summary: Replies to CD on proportion of sexes in butterflies, coloration of moths, and courtship. Encloses copies of letters on these subjects between HTS, Henry Doubleday, and John Hellins.

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   29 February [1868]
letters.summary:
JJW’s note on birds was one of the most interesting CD has ever received. Asks several questions. CD is puzzled by cases of magpies whose mates were killed but who always immediately found others.

Alexander Wallace denies any effect of colour in sexual selection among Lepidoptera.

letters.title: To Henry Doubleday   1 March [1868]
letters.summary:
Has been interested in copy of HD’s letter to H. T. Stainton on numerical proportions of the sexes of insects. Do they vary during different years?

Does he have opinions about the courtships of butterflies?

Will send a copy of his paper onPrimulawhen it is published. [See5997.]

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   1 March 1868
letters.summary:
Offers enclosure demonstrating that natural selection could produce sterility of hybrids.

More on Pangenesis and the inadequacy of H. Spencer’s approach.

letters.title: From J. E. Gray   2 March 1868
letters.summary: Canine teeth in males are always larger than in females and certainly so inCervulus moschus.

letters.title: From George Henry Lewes   2 March 1868
letters.summary:
Is engaged on an article forFortnightly ReviewonVariation["Mr Darwin’s hypotheses", n.s. 9: 353–73, 611–28; n.s. 10: 61–80, 492–509]. Asks CD some questions.

While he agrees with natural selection, he believes many "organic details" develop irrespective of advantage.

letters.title: To H. T. Stainton   2 March [1868]
letters.summary:
Thanks HTS for his valuable information. Hopes to arrive at probable answer to question of proportion of males to females in the progeny of butterflies bred in domestication.

On courtship of butterflies, CD believes something more than chance is involved in determining which male is successful.

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   [before 3] March 1868
letters.summary:
Aggressive behaviour of a bullfinch toward new arrival in JJW’s aviary.

Sexual differences in goldfinches: size of beaks.

Sexual selection in Lepidoptera.

Thinks Dr Alex Wallace’s observations onBombyxnot conclusive in proving that no preference is shown by females.

letters.title: From C. S. Bate   3 March 1868
letters.summary: Quotes information from Dr Power on colour of sexes of Crustacea in Mauritius [seeDescent1: 335].

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   3 March [1868]
letters.summary: Asks CD to collect from the Jermyn Street Museum a box containing a skull and bones which belong to Mr Cumberbatch.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [3 March 1868]
letters.summary:
Now quite understands Pangenesis. Satisfaction given by it, as CD says, may depend on one’s mental constitution. In all cases of descent JDH has always thought "all the properties of the parents are transmitted in the one cell and were diffused to every part of the future offspring".

Tyndall believes he feels atoms as firmly as St Paul believed he saw Christ.

letters.title: From John Murray   3 March [1868]
letters.summary: JM offers a note for 400 guineas as author’s payment on sale of 1250 copies of 2d issue ofVariation.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [4 March 1868]
letters.summary: Arrangements to dine at JDH’s club.

letters.title: To V. O. Kovalevsky   4 March [1868]
letters.summary: Sends sheets with alterations to be made [in Russian translation ofVariation]. VOK should consider adding to the title-page that CD is a Corresponding Member of the Imperial Academy of Sciences (St Petersburg).

letters.title: To John Murray   4 March [1868]
letters.summary: Payment of 400 guineas [Variationroyalties] delights CD.

letters.title: From Jonathan Peel   4 March 1868
letters.summary:
Sends copy of a paper on his flock of sheep, which confirms much of what CD says inVariation,

together with a note he made of an instance of cattle "determining the existence" of a tree [cf.Origin, ch. 3].

letters.title: From Armand de Quatrefages   4 March 1868
letters.deprecated: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.sender: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.summary:
Proportions of sexes of the silkworm are about equal, but knows of no statistics.

Cannot share his view of origin of species.

letters.title: To William Sedgwick   4 March [1868]
letters.summary:
Thanks WS for information about moss roses and the Le Compte family.

Mentions WS’s recent papers on inheritance [Brit. & Foreign Med.-Chirurg. Rev.(1867)].

letters.title: To C. S. Vesselofski   4 March 1868
letters.summary: Acknowledges his election as a Corresponding Member of the Imperial Academy of Sciences, St Petersburg.

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   [before 5] March 1868
letters.summary: Does not think females give preference to any males. Coloration, pugnacity; cases of use of colour in struggle for existence. [seeDescent1: 395.]

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   [5–9 March 1868]
letters.summary: Would like to meet with WBT while in London.

letters.title: From Robert Buist   5 March 1868
letters.summary: Replies to CD on salmon: the pugnacity of males and the proportions of sexes. [seeDescent1: 308, 2: 3.]

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   5 March [1868]
letters.summary: Crying in babies.

letters.title: From John Price   5 March 1868
letters.summary:
Visiting W. D. Fox.

Sends specimen ofCardamine pratensis,

and an account of a striped horse.

Discusses Pangenesis.

Has returned to religion and has been reflecting on God’s mercies, one of which CD should remember from about 1828 at Bodnant.

letters.title: From J. J. Moulinié   6 March [1868]
letters.summary: First volume ofVariationin French has been printed. Second volume has been translated. CD’s additions to chapter 11 arrived in time.

letters.title: From John Murray   6 March [1868]
letters.summary:
JM sends note for £420.

Asks CD to use his good offices on behalf of William Clowes’s son who is up for election to Athenaeum.

letters.title: To John Murray   6 March 1868
letters.summary:
Acknowledges receipt of bill for £420.

Will try to attend Athenaeum meeting to help elect Clowes’s son.

letters.title: To William Ogle   6 March [1868]
letters.summary: Wishes he had known of the views of Hippocrates, which are almost identical to his Pangenesis hypothesis. CD advances it as provisional, but secretly expects some such view will have to be admitted.

letters.title: To Jonathan Peel   6 March [1868]
letters.summary:
Obliged for JP’s account of sheep. Such articles would make naturalists think more of natural selection.

E. A. Darwin’s health bad.

Asks about sex ratio in sheep births.

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   [6 March 1868]
letters.summary:
Discusses beaks and relative numbers of the sexes of goldfinches.

Comments on sexual selection among butterflies.

Mentions Kerguelen moth collected by Hooker.

Comments on JJW’s observations on coloured birds.

letters.title: From H. T. Stainton   7 March 1868
letters.summary:
Protective coloration in butterflies.

[Alexander] Wallace’s suggestion that collecting larger larvae of females accounts for error in counting proportion of sexes.

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   7 March 1868
letters.summary: Various facts about birds: pairing, finding new mates, protective coloration, polygamy, sexual differences.

letters.title: To Alfred Wrigley   7 March [1868]
letters.summary: States his intentions regarding Horace’s future education. CD thought he had made those intentions clear in an earlier letter.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   8 March 1868
letters.summary: Expresses his pleasure at the opportunity of meeting CD.

letters.title: From Henry Doubleday   8 March 1868
letters.summary:
Proportion of sexes in Lepidoptera.

Sexual preference.

Role of coloration [seeDescent1: 311–12].

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   8 March [1868]
letters.summary:
On critical exchanges at the Linnean Society on natural selection and mimicry.

Roland Trimen’s paper on South African mimetic butterflies ["On some remarkable mimetic resemblances among African butterflies",Trans. Linn. Soc. Lond.26 (1870): 497–523; read 5 Mar 1868].

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [9 March 1868]
letters.summary: Asks to borrowPhilosophical Transactions, vol. 157, pt 2 (1868).

letters.title: From W. B. Tegetmeier   9 March 1868
letters.summary: On proportion of sexes in birds.

letters.title: From Alfred Wrigley   9 March 1868
letters.summary: Wants to know why Horace has been removed from school without any notification.

letters.title: From Hermann Müller   10 March 1868
letters.summary: Has heard from W. Engelmann of Leipzig; he is willing to let CD have the woodcuts to Fritz Müller’s work [Für Darwin(1864)] for 22 thalers.

letters.title: From Frederick Smith   [c.10 March 1868?]
letters.summary: On the relative size of sexes in aculeate Hymenoptera. [SeeDescent1: 347–8.]

letters.title: To Edward A. Smith   [11–31 March 1868]
letters.summary: Instructions for woodcuts showing sexual differences in beetles, forDescent.

letters.title: To G. G. Stokes   11 March [1868]
letters.summary: Sends GGS examples of feathers from an albino peacock and repeats his query about the zones of colour [see5950].

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   11 March 1868
letters.summary: Courtship of goldfinches. Male display. [SeeDescent2: 95.]

letters.title: To Alfred Wrigley   11 March [1868]
letters.summary: Regrets and apologises for a misunderstanding regarding Horace’s leaving Clapham School. Is sure he wrote an earlier letter which AW evidently did not receive.

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   12 March 1868
letters.summary: Results of his examination of divergence in sexual coloration of tropical American butterflies. [SeeDescent1: 389 onJunoniaandPapilio.]

letters.title: From Alfred Wrigley   12 March 1868
letters.summary: Had hoped that the intention of removing Horace from school had been abandoned and regrets that it has not.

letters.title: To Rolla Charles Meadows Rouse   [after 12 March 1868]
letters.summary: Discusses tuition arrangements for Horace Darwin.

letters.title: To Alfred Wrigley   [after 12 March 1868]
letters.summary: Assures AW he has not hurt Horace’s feelings. CD has always been doubtful about a private tutor for Horace. Fears a letter [giving notice of removal] was lost in the post.

letters.title: From Giovanni Canestrini   13 March 1868
letters.summary: On the proportions of the sexes in silk moths, fish, and eels.

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   13 March [1868]
letters.summary:
Thanks for facts about birds displaying plumage during courtship; "for Butterflies I must trust to analogy altogether in regard to sexual selection".

Invites JJW to visit in summer.

letters.title: From Alexander Wallace   14 March 1868
letters.summary:
On proportion of sexes [of moths?] raised from larvae: AW does not select largest exclusively.

Account of lambing in 1864 after unusual drought.

letters.title: From Alphonse de Candolle   15 March 1868
letters.summary: Thanks forVariation.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [15 March 1868]
letters.summary:
Asks WED to observe blushing in the blind, and yawning.

Mentions elephants’ crying while trumpeting.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   15 March [1868]
letters.summary:
Coloration of butterflies; brilliantly coloured females.

Commends CD on his paper on specific differences inPrimula[J. Proc. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)10 (1869): 437–54; reprinted and revised inForms of flowers] as a test-case proving origin of real species.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   16 March [1868]
letters.summary: CD arranging for a translation of FM’sFür Darwinby W. S. Dallas.

letters.title: To Roland Trimen   [16 March 1868]
letters.summary: Asks whether RT will call.

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   16 March 1868
letters.summary:
Sexual selection of pigeons, ducks;

polygamous birds.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   17 March 1868
letters.summary:
Some questions on errata in second English issue ofVariation.

Sends a paper by Robert Hartmann on domestic animals of the countries bordering the Nile ["Geographische Verbreitung der im nordöstlichen Afrika wild lebenden Säugethiere"Z. Ges. Erdkd. Berlin3 (1868): 28–69, 232–70, 345–68, 404–20].

Has thought much about CD’s theory of Pangenesis. It "seems rather a little too complicated … as a molecular theory".

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   17 March 1868
letters.summary: Will start translatingFür Darwin. Suggests it be called "A Lift for Darwin".

letters.title: From Jonathan Peel   17 March 1868
letters.summary: Proportions of male and female lambs.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   17 [March 1868]
letters.summary: For experiment on effect of male beauty, pigeons should be coloured on the breast.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   17 [March 1868]
letters.summary:
On hisPrimulapaper for the Linnean Society ["On the specific difference betweenPrimula veris, Brit. Fl. (var.officialis, Linn.),P. vulgaris, Brit. Fl. var.acaulis, Linn.), andP. elatior, Jacq.; and on the hybrid nature of the common oxlip; with supplementary remarks on naturally produced hybrids of the genusVerbascum", [officinalis!?]J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)10 (1869): 437–54].

Peacocks and sexual selection.

ARW’s sterility argument has driven CD’s sons half-mad.

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   18 March [1868]
letters.summary: Requests information on the standard of beauty of savages and on whether the female has any influence in selecting a male.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [19 March 1868]
letters.summary:
The second volume of Lyell’s [Principles, 10th ed.] gives a "fair history of the progress of opinion on Species".

Pleased by allusion to Pangenesis: "an untried hypothesis is always dangerous ground".

Looks forward to chapter on domestication and on man.

letters.title: From Paolo Mantegazza  19 March 1868
letters.summary: Sends papers.

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   19 March 1868
letters.summary:
Writes of his son’s affairs.

Is readingVariationand discusses a point relating to feeding habits of horses.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   19 March 1868
letters.summary:
On sterility of natural species and natural selection. Closely allied forms from adjacent islands offer best chance of finding good species fertileinter se.

Problem ofminutevariations and sexual selection.

letters.title: From Elinor Mary Bonham-Carter   20 March [1868]
letters.summary: Reports her sister-in-law’s observations of her child, up to three months old, while crying and screaming.

letters.title: To Henry Doubleday   20 March [1868]
letters.summary:
CD asks about HD’s observation of sexual call of Coleoptera.

Also comments on statements by collectors that they breed more females than males from caterpillars. CD had thought this might be accounted for by the collection of largest and finest caterpillars, but Alexander Wallace says the collectors take large and small equally. Does HD agree with Wallace?

letters.title: To David Forbes   [20 March 1868]
letters.summary:
Any notes on idea of human beauty by natives who have little association with Europeans would interest CD.

Also influence of females on males’ choice.

Sends copy ofQueries about expression.

letters.title: From William Robert Grove   20 March 1868
letters.summary: Asks CD to breakfast in London on Tuesday [24 Mar].

letters.title: From George Henslow   20 March 1868
letters.summary: Asks for CD’s "candid criticisms" of his paper [onVariation].

letters.title: From Roland Trimen   20 March [1868]
letters.summary: On attraction of males by females in moths. H. T. Stainton mentions a case.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   21 March [1868]
letters.summary:
Corrections for German translation ofVariation.

Discusses Pangenesis. CD not surprised at JVC’s unfavourable opinion. Huxley’s joke that it is more difficult to believe than Genesis. Lyell’s and Sir H. Holland’s opinions. For CD, it provides a bond for connecting many phenomena.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   21 March [1868]
letters.summary: Suggests possible arbitrators to act in a business transaction involving WED.

letters.title: To Maxwell Tylden Masters   21 March [1868]
letters.summary:
Sends his niece’s [Lucy Wedgwood] observations on worms, vouches for her accuracy, and suggests the piece be inserted inGardeners’ Chronicle[see "Worms",Gard. Chron.(1868): 324].

Adds his thanks for a "very kind review" of his book [Variation,Gard. Chron.(1868): 124].

letters.title: To J. J. Moulinié   21 March [1868]
letters.summary: Corrects error in spelling of name [inVariation].

letters.title: To Roland Trimen   [21 March 1868]
letters.summary: Arranges for RT to call.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   [21 March 1868]
letters.summary:
On problem of sterility, CD cannot persuade himself that it has been gained by natural selection.

On sexual selection and minute variations, he tends to agree with ARW. Sends George Darwin’s notes on ARW’s argument.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   22 [March 1868]
letters.summary:
Asks WED to observe a suppressed yawn.

Asks whether scratching a tickling point makes tears come to his eyes.

letters.title: To Edward Hewitt   [c.22 March 1868]
letters.summary: Asks for facts relating to courtship of birds and especially cases of females preferring particular males.

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   22 March [1868]
letters.summary:
Glad to hear about pigeons. Did not know some birds could win affections of females more than others, except among peacocks.

Comments on polygamy in birds.

Discusses sex ratios among birds.

letters.title: To W. R. Grove   23 March [1868]
letters.summary: Arranges to call on WRG.

letters.title: To Albert Günther   23 March [1868]
letters.summary: Asks AG for details of variation in patterning of the banded snake.

letters.title: From Albert Günther   [c.23 March 1868?]
letters.summary: Note on sexual differences inMonacanthus.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   23 March 1868
letters.summary:
Has received English edition ofVariation. First volume of German edition came three months ago. Comments on book.

Will send copy of recent lectures on human evolution [Entstehung des Menschengeschlechts(1868)]. Gegenbaur much interested in the subject.

ConsidersSelachiusthe ancestral form of the fish and hence of all higher vertebrates. Believes their swim-bladder became lung of amphibians.

Mentions cases of hybrid crosses between rabbits and hares producing fertile offspring.

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   23 March 1868
letters.summary: Relates a variety of facts about sexual selection in birds. [SeeDescent2: 104–5.]

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   [24 March 1868]
letters.summary: CD relays the advice of Sir W. R. Grove on the dismal prospects of a law career.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   24 March [1868]
letters.summary: Returns George Darwin’s criticisms of his notes on sterility and sends further notes in reply. Since there are degrees of sterility between varieties, "is it not probable that natural selection can accumulate these variations?" Varieties that are adapted to new conditions could then survive and form new species without being isolated.

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   24 March 1868
letters.summary: Experiments to test Wallace’s theory that brightly coloured caterpillars are rejected by birds. [SeeDescent1: 417.]

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   [before 25 March 1868]
letters.summary: Detailed notes on secondary sexual differences in various species of birds and mammals.

letters.title: To Edward Blyth   25 March [1868]
letters.summary: Has found EB’s MS most interesting and valuable. Fully half the facts were new to him; will probably use some.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   25 March [1868]
letters.summary: Gives his opinion on a business transaction involving WED and the Southampton bank.

letters.title: To John Murray   [25? March 1868]
letters.summary: American publishers will not wait for woodcuts, so asks Murray to have a copy of the reprint sent to Asa Gray. Will call soon to talk aboutFür Darwinand to hear about sale of latest edition ofOrigin

letters.title: From B. D. Walsh   25 March 1868
letters.summary:
Sexual preference in insects;

structures for seizing females;

coloration.

Doubts whether CD can make much of a case from insects in support of sexual selection.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [after 25 March 1868]
letters.summary: Blushing in boys blind from birth. Has got information from R. H. Blair, the principal of a college for the blind.

letters.title: From David Forbes   26 March 1868
letters.summary:
Blushing in South American Indians.

Hairlessness of Aymaras and Quechuas. [SeeDescent2: 322–3.]

letters.title: From Ferdinand von Hochstetter  26 March 1868
letters.summary: Thanks CD for advice received before hisNovaravoyage. Sends volumes [Reise der österreichischen Fregatte Novara um die Erde … Geologischer Theil, ed. FCvH, 2 vols. in 3 (1864–6)].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [26 March 1868]
letters.summary: He and Lizzie [Elizabeth Darwin] will come to Kew on Saturday.

letters.title: From C.-F. Reinwald   26 March 1868
letters.summary: French translation ofVariationhas just appeared. Copies sent to Quatrefages de Bréau, C. V. Naudin, A. J. Gaudry, Camille Dareste, and Ernest Faivre.

letters.title: From Roland Trimen   26 March 1868
letters.summary:
Coloration in moths.

Quotes Achille Guénée on relative proportion of sexes inPhalaenites.

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   [26] March 1868
letters.summary: Proportions of sexes in birds as reported by bird-catchers.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [27] March [1868]
letters.summary:
Discusses law versus engineering and business as a career.

Supposes ARW will have "squashed" GHD’s criticisms of his notes on sterility.

letters.title: To Roland Trimen   27 March [1868]
letters.summary: Thanks RT for letter which saves him from a "terrible mistake": that no moths were more brilliantly coloured beneath than above. Suggests revised version for comment. [SeeDescent1: 397.]

letters.title: From Roland Trimen   27 March 1868
letters.summary:
Approves CD’s revision on coloration of moths.

Impressed with apparent adverse tendencies: one toward sexual selection, the other toward protection.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   27 March [1868]
letters.summary: There are so many doubtful points on the problems relating to sterility that they will never agree.

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   27 March [1868]
letters.summary:
Thanks for information [about sex ratios] received from bird-catchers.

"Can you form any theory about all the many cases which you have given me and others which have been published, of when one pair is killed, another soon appearing?"

Facts about gay-coloured caterpillars very satisfactory.

Comments on Pangenesis.

letters.title: From Henry Doubleday   28 March 1868
letters.summary:
On the proportion of sexes in moths; Lepidoptera females command higher prices; quotes Staudinger’s catalogue [seeDescent1: 311–12].

Ticking ofAnobium tessellatum[seeDescent1: 385].

letters.title: From George Henslow   28 March 1868
letters.summary:
