Thanks for criticism of his paper [onVariation].

If external conditions induce variability, what is the internal cause?

Does not agree with Duke of Argyll that "Origin of Species" is an incorrect term.

Sees playfulness of animals as a mark of the Deity’s creative playfulness.

Will visit soon.

letters.title: From Edward Hewitt   28 March 1868
letters.summary: On various subjects related to sexual selection: preferences, proportion of sexes. [SeeDescent2: 117–18, 122.]

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [28 March 1868]
letters.summary: Defers visit [to Kew] because of ill health.

letters.title: From Harrison Weir   28 March 1868
letters.summary: Recognition of colour by animals.

letters.title: From C. V. Naudin   29 March 1868
letters.summary:
Thanks forVariation.

Complains of a severe facial neuralgia.

He is planning to build an experimental laboratory in the south.

letters.title: To William Bowman   30 March [1868]
letters.summary: Clarifies his earlier query on Bell’s observations. Seeks confirmation of Bell’s statement that the conjunctiva of a child whose eyes are opened forcibly during a screaming fit become engorged with blood. CD has noted a relationship between contraction of the orbicular muscle and secretion of tears; can WB explain why they appear related?

letters.title: From John Bush   30 March 1868
letters.summary: His impression is that male rats outnumber females. Males are pugnacious and polygamous. Gives details of the inheritance of colour in a colony he kept.

letters.title: From Cuthbert Collingwood   30 March 1868
letters.summary: Sends CD his book [Naturalist on the China Sea(1868)].

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   30 March [1868]
letters.summary:
Now understands importance of swim-bladder in selachians. Always imagined animal likeLepidosirenwas parent form of vertebrates.

Has been nearly a month in London, collecting facts on sexual selection from breeders and at Zoological Gardens.

Astonished at hybrid of rabbit and hare. Is it certain that work was done with hare?

letters.title: To Ferdinand von Hochstetter   31 March [1868]
letters.summary: Thanks for gift of work on the geology of the Novara expedition

letters.title: To William Thierry Preyer   31 March 1868
letters.summary: Glad to hear that WP defends species transmutation. German support is the chief reason to hope that their views will prevail.

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   31 March 1868
letters.summary:
Sexual behaviour of chaffinches.

Numbers of female linnets in September.

His experiments on brightly coloured larvae [as food], testing A. R. Wallace’s theory.

His observations of a rookery make him wonder whether it may not be more difficult than we think for birds to pair.

letters.title: From Frederick F. Geach   April 1868
letters.summary: Sends expanded answers [toQueries about expression], in view of CD’s statement that his first list had not been sufficiently explanatory. Is pleased that some answers confirmed CD’s views [seeExpression,passim].

letters.title: To Moritz Wagner   [April–June 1868]
letters.summary:
Thanks MW for his essay [Die Darwin’sche Theorie und das Migrationsgesetz der Organismen(1868)]. Is highly gratified that MW agrees with him to a considerable extent.

Almost wishes that he could believe in the importance of isolation to the same extent as MW.

letters.title: From William Bowman   1 April [1868]
letters.summary: Asks for precise reference in Charles Bell to subject of CD’s question. Agrees to assist CD’s investigation. Asks about Bell’s observations on eyes engorged with blood. Has noticed that eyes of children with excessive photophobia tend to be pale when forced open.

letters.title: From G. H. K. Thwaites   1 April 1868
letters.summary: Has circulated CD’sQueries about expressionand gives some of his observations of the natives.

letters.title: To William Bowman   2 April [1868]
letters.summary: Gives Charles Bell’s explanation of the contraction of the orbicularis during screaming and seeks confirmation of his view because the action is "the key-stone of a whole class of expressions". Curious to learn WB’s conclusion in regard to the relation between contraction of the orbicularis and secretion of tears. Notes that voluntary contraction of the orbicularis causes no tears.

letters.title: To John Bush   2 April [1868]
letters.summary: Thanks JB for his information. Has heard of analogous cases to JB’s observations on [colours of] crossed rats; the offspring of white and grey mice are stated to be either white or grey and never piebald.

letters.title: From Robert Caspary   2 April 1868
letters.summary:
Finds important differences between English and German versions ofVariationon graft-hybrids.

Experiments and observations on submerged flowers.

letters.title: From George Robert Gray   2 April 1868
letters.summary: On the changes in plumage of scarlet ibis at the zoo in breeding season.

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   [3 April 1868]
letters.summary: Discusses apes and their relationships to each other. Writes particularly of the gibbon, its structure and well-developed legs giving it the ability to walk without using its hands.

letters.title: From Camille Dareste   3 April 1868
letters.summary:
Thanks forVariation.

CD must be happy about the tendency toward acceptance of his views, though it is regrettable that France is backward in this regard.

His own work goes slowly, but he still hopes his work on artificially produced monstrosities will help to answer the question of the origin of species.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin 3 April 1868
letters.summary: Discusses how they might enquire about any provisions in the laws of partnership concerning lunacy.

letters.title: From Henry Doubleday   3 April 1868
letters.summary: Otto Staudinger’s catalogue shows prices of female Lepidoptera to be higher than those of males.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   3 April [1868]
letters.summary:
Asks for [John?] Smith’s exact count of seeds of the crossed and self-fertilisedVictoriawater-lily. Similar question onEuryaleseed and seedlings.

JDH’s coming [BAAS] Presidential Address.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   3 April [1868]
letters.summary:
Movement in plants.

Dimorphism.

Would welcome FM’s opinion of Pangenesis.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   3 April 1868
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for sending him copy ofVariation.

Describes results of his brother’s [August Müller] experiments on effect of climate on maize.

Like ancestors of horses, young tapir is also striped.

letters.title: To Edward Blyth   4 April [1868]
letters.summary:
Glad to hear about colours ofHylobates.

Cannot find any statement about which digits in man are most subject to syndactylism in Isidore Geoffroy [Saint-Hilaire]’sHistoire des anomalies[1832–7].

Asks questions concerned with seasonal and sexual changes in plumage of various bird species.

Does male woodpecker share in incubation?

letters.title: From M. T. Masters   4 April 1868
letters.summary:
MTM did not writeGardeners’ Chroniclereview ofVariation[(1868): 184].

Encloses letters supporting a project [Botanical Congress?] to promote horticulture, and hopes CD will reconsider giving his support.

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   4 April [1868]
letters.summary:
CD thanks JJW for the mine of information his last "ten!" letters contain. Comments on sexual display of pheasants and colour preferences of pigeons.

Asks about hens that pair earliest in spring and about possible existence of unpaired birds.

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   5 April 1868
letters.summary:
Discusses the human foot and its abnormalities; notes an example of syndactylism.

Gives his observations on sexual differences in coloration of terns and ostriches.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [5 and 8? April 1868]
letters.summary: Langstaff has seen no trace of blushing on the body.

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   5 April 1868
letters.summary: George Rolleston’s son was born with a scar on his knee exactly where GR cut himself with a knife years before his marriage. Gives several other examples of inherited mutilation.

letters.title: From F. T. Buckland   6 April [1868]
letters.summary: SendsSalmon Fisheries Report. Asks for CD’s opinion on his "close season" chapter.

letters.title: From St George Jackson Mivart   6 April 1868
letters.summary: Has asked gentlemen who administer chloroform to make observations [on expression?] for CD.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   6 April [1868]
letters.summary: More on the "terrible problem" of natural selection and sterility. CD’s reasons for disagreeing with ARW. CD analyses and answers ARW in detail in defence of his conclusion that sterility cannot be increased through natural selection.

letters.title: From ?   6 April 1868
letters.summary: Gives details of some points that occurred to him while readingVariation, including observations on horses, cattle, silkworms, and hereditary baldness and disease.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [7–15 April 1868]
letters.summary: Langstaff has never seen the platysma act, and he believes it to be rudimentary in humans.

letters.title: From C. S. Bate   7 April 1868
letters.summary:
On dentition of moles. On double teeth [seeVariation2: 391].

Difference in size of male and female Crustacea.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [7 April 1868]
letters.summary: Describes the action of facial muscles at the onset of crying as observed by Langstaff.

letters.title: From Ernest Faivre   7 April 1868
letters.summary: Thanks for sendingVariation.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   7 April 1868
letters.summary:
Goes to N. Wales with Huxley.

Wishes to borrow Duke of Argyll’sReign of law.

The BAAS Presidential Address [Rep. BAAS38 (1868): lviii–lxxv] – his unhappiness about it; history of botany requires too much reading.

Smith will supply notes onEuryale.

letters.title: From Giovanni Canestrini   8 April 1868
letters.summary: Reports on Prof. Cornalia’s observations on the proportion of sexes in bees, and in healthy and sick silk moths, in nature and under domestication.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   8 April 1868
letters.summary: He never intended "A Lift for Darwin" as a serious title but as a way of arranging it. Lyell’s suggestion seems best to him: "Facts and Arguments For Darwin".

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   8 April [1868]
letters.summary: Thanks C. L. Langstaff for his observations relating to expression. Has requested observations on the platysma. Discusses the actions of other facial muscles, especially during crying. [Encloses5828.]

letters.title: From G. R. Gray   8 April 1868
letters.summary: Difference between sexes ofIbis rubra; change in plumage.

letters.title: From John Smith   8 April 1868
letters.summary: Notes the differences in seed production between cross- and self-fertilized flowers ofVictoria regia.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   8 [April] 1868
letters.summary:
If CD is not convinced by his notes on sterility, ARW has little doubt that he is wrong. In fact he was onlyhalf-convinced by his own arguments.

Modifies his first proposition [a species varies occasionally in two directions, but owing to free inter-crossing the variations never increase] and further discusses the subject.

Encloses Berthold Seemann’s notes on flora of the Hawaiian Islands. Presence of European alpine species in Hawaiian volcanoes is a "hard nut" for geographical distribution [but see ARW’sIsland life(1880), p. 323].

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   9 April [1868]
letters.summary: Warns ARW of dubious character of list of European alpine genera and species in volcanoes of Hawaii. Problems of geographical distribution in oceanic islands.

letters.title: From James Samuelson   10 April 1868
letters.summary: Corrects errors of detail inVariation.

letters.title: From Albert Gaudry   11 April 1868
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for copy ofVariation.

CD’s work on pigeons demonstrates the close relationship between modifications in soft tissues and the hard parts, which are the only ones we possess in the fossil state.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [13 April 1868]
letters.summary: Action of facial muscles at onset of crying.

letters.title: To Peter Martin Duncan   13 April [1868?]
letters.summary: Promises to send coral specimens.

letters.title: From George Henslow   13 April 1868
letters.summary: Thanks for Casimir de Candolle’s paper ["Théorie de l’angle unique en phyllotaxie",Arch. Sci. Phys. & Nat.23 (1865): 199–212].

letters.title: To John Murray   13 April [1868]
letters.summary:
Asks JM to sendVariationto G. Boccardo in Italy.

Sends title (suggested by Lyell) for translation of Fritz Müller’sFür Darwin(which Dallas is translating). CD does not wish to go to great expense in advertising it.

letters.title: From Roland Trimen   13 April 1868
letters.summary: Extract from Émile Blanchard’sMetamorphoses, moeurs et instincts des insectes[1868], on attraction of males by female Lepidoptera, and possible explanation.

letters.title: To B. D. Walsh   13 April [1868]
letters.summary:
BDW’s letter [6051?] and his notes are a "mine of wealth". The negative evidence is of much value. Sexual selection is a perplexing subject – finds he "must make the best of a rather bad job".

Sends copy [ofVariation].

letters.title: From Richard Trevor Clarke   14 [April 1868]
letters.summary:
Solicits CD’s support for the newly set up Royal Horticultural Society’s Scientific Committee.

Very pleased that he was put into CD’s book [Variation1: 352].

Sends "hybridising pincers" of his own making.

letters.title: From W. G. Howell   14 April [1868 or 1874]
letters.summary: Has some "vegetable caterpillars" from New Zealand and will be pleased to show them to CD if he is interested.

letters.title: To John Murray   14 April [1868]
letters.summary: About the advertising and title of a book [the translation of Fritz Müller’sFür Darwin, see6114].

letters.title: To Roland Trimen   14 April [1868]
letters.summary:
Has tried using dealers’ price-lists as a guide to sex ratios in Lepidoptera; finds numerous cases in which the sexes bring different prices and in virtually all of them the males are cheaper. This seems to confirm the impression of the field collectors.

Wishes RT good luck with natural history in S. Africa.

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   [14 April 1868]
letters.summary:
Starlings find new mates readily. Nesting in threes common.

Recognition of song by birds.

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   15 April [1868]
letters.summary:
CD has questions related to colour differences in the sexes of butterflies, especially in relation to HWB’s paper ["On variation in sexes ofArgynnis diana",Proc. Entomol. Soc. Philadelphia4 (1865): 204–7].

Mentions that his MS on Lepidoptera [forDescent] is longer than he intended and the information is four-fifths owed to HWB.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [15 April 1868]
letters.summary: Gives details of the subjects on whom Langstaff made his observations on crying. Langstaff has not seen the platysma contract under chloroform.

letters.title: To Henry Doubleday   15 April [1868]
letters.summary: Submits lists of insects [missing] for correspondent to check whether brightly coloured. Wants to determine whether there is any relation between bright colouring, whether in both sexes or one alone, and an unequal number of males and females.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   15 April [1868]
letters.summary:
Admires ARW’s "Theory of birds’ nests" [J. Travel & Nat. Hist.1 (1868): 73].

Discusses their respective views on birds’ nests, sexual selection, and protection.

Asks why, if brilliant colours of female butterflies are result of protective mimicry, do not males become equally brilliant? CD believes variation in females alone accounts for it, rather than protection.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   16 April [1868]
letters.summary: Asks WED whether Langstaff could make some observations on certain facial muscles in expression.

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   16 April 1868
letters.summary:
Describes a curious litter of rabbits.

Pairing of rooks, courtship of golden pheasant.

Behaviour of finch hybrids.

Seasonal coloration of birds; bright plumage results from sexual selection.

letters.title: From Charles Henry Binstead   17 April 1868
letters.summary: In readingVariation, notices CD has not observed that after mallards have been domesticated their claws turn from black to white.

letters.title: From W. R. Grove   17 April 1868
letters.summary: He and another Bencher of Lincoln’s Inn have signed the necessary certificates for admission of CD’s son [George].

letters.title: From George Thurber   18–20 April 1868
letters.summary: About an American edition ofVariation.

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   18 April [1868]
letters.summary:
Discusses rapid replacement of mates among birds. "I begin to think that the pairing of birds must be as delicate and tedious an operation as the pairing of young gentlemen and ladies. If I can convince myself that there are habitually many unpaired birds it will be a great aid to me in sexual selection". Notes rivalry of singing birds.

Heard from George Rolleston of the inherited effects of an eye injury.

Disagrees with A. R. Wallace’s idea "that birds learn to make their nests from having seen them whilst young" ["The philosophy of birds’ nests",Intellect. Obs.11 (1867): 413–20].

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   20 April 1868
letters.summary:
In addition to the drawing of a caterpillar which CD intends to use,

HWB sends information on differences of colour and pattern between the sexes of species ofPapilio.

Argynnis dianaandA. saganahave females that are brightly coloured, but these may be cases of protective mimicry.

letters.title: From John Hellins   20 April 1868
letters.summary: Gives the evidence on which he relied for his view, which CD thinks is erroneous, of proportion of sexes in Lepidoptera.

letters.title: From Henry Holland   20 April [1868]
letters.summary: Sends CD a copy of a book he has had printed mainly for the interest of his children and grandchildren [later published asRecollections of past life(1872)].

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   20 April 1868
letters.summary:
Instinct in birds; nest-building.

Inheritance of acquired characters.

letters.title: From George Bentham   [before 22 April 1868]
letters.summary:
Has studiedVariationwith interest.

Cannot quite follow CD on reversion and Pangenesis,

but is amazed at CD’s observations and method.

Comments on varieties of asses, kidney beans, and artichokes.

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   22 April [1868]
letters.summary:
Thanks HWB for answering questions.

The MS on Lepidoptera is almost finished and he is glad HWB will read it; he is fearful of mistakes, not being familiar with the subject.

letters.title: To George Bentham   22 April 1868
letters.summary:
Is not surprised that GB cannot digest Pangenesis, but it has been an immense relief to CD in tying together large classes of facts.

Sends names of men writing on crossing of plants. Criticises some French observations. Praises Hildebrand and Federico Delpino.

Sends pamphlets.

CD is experimenting on a large scale on difference in plants raised from self-fertilised and crossed seeds.

F. Hildebrand has produced a graft-hybrid which seems to lend important support to Pangenesis.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [22? April 1868]
letters.summary:
C. L. Langstaff on action of muscles in crying. He believes the primary object of the contraction of the orbicularis is to protect the eye from blood.

Blushing on the body.

letters.title: From Henry Doubleday   22 April 1868
letters.summary:
On proportion of sexes;

coloration of sexes in Lepidoptera.

Sexual attraction of femaleSaturnia carpini.

letters.title: To Richard Kippist   22 April [1868]
letters.summary: "Please give Bearer Books for me.–"

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   22 April 1868
letters.summary:
His opinion of Pangenesis.

On relative proportion of sexes in marine animals [sthg missing!?]Crustacea.

Sexual differences.

Music of Cicadae.

letters.title: From Charles L. Langstaff   [after 22? April 1868]
letters.summary: Describes the appearance of the nose in crying.

letters.title: From Gerolamo Boccardo   23 April 1868
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for gift ofVariation.

GB sent copies of hisFisica del globo[1868] to Lyell and the presidents of British scientific societies but has received no acknowledgment; asks CD to check that they received the work. Could CD arrange for a notice of the book to appear in England?

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   23 April [1868]
letters.summary:
Likes WBT’s review [ofVariation] in theField[31 (1868): 309, 350].

Awaits remarks on coloured pigeons and proportion of sexes.

letters.title: From Theodor Engelmann   25 April 1868
letters.summary: In response to CD’s letter of 21 April, TE has forwarded the 67 clichés of the woodcuts from Fritz Müller’s work [Für Darwin(1864)]; acknowledges CD’s bank draft for £3 in payment.

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   [before 28 April] 1868
letters.summary:
Proportion of sexes in chaffinches.

Pugnacity of blackbirds and robins.

Harrison Weir reports up to nine eggs in starling nests.

Newspaper report of a sheep born with its owner’s brand.

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   28 April – 4 May 1868
letters.summary:
Observations on root-climbers. Variegated and arborescent varieties ofHedera.

[CD’s notes are for his reply,6165.]

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   28 April [1868]
letters.summary: Various topics related to sexual selection: sexual differences, sexual preferences, coloration.

letters.title: From George Bentham   30 April 1868
letters.summary:
Discusses Hildebrand

and criticises Delpino.

Asks to borrow C. K. Sprengel’sEntdeckte Geheimniss der Natur[1793].

Botanists have no explanation of the case ofViola odorataand other showy flowers being sterile while inconspicuous ones bear seed.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   30 April [1868]
letters.summary:
More on CD’s objections to ARW’s views on protection and natural selection.

Sexual selection.

letters.title: To George Bentham   1 May [1868]
letters.summary:
Sends Ernst Haeckel’s [Generelle]Morphologie[1866] and C. K. Sprengel’s book [Entdeckte Geheimniss der Natur(1793)].

A. Gaudry and L. Rütimeyer have declared in favour of CD’s views.

letters.title: From George Cupples   1 May 1868
letters.summary:
Has readVariation;

is preparing a monograph on Scotch deerhounds. Offers CD information on size of male and female deerhounds.

Might not the effect of human mother’s imagination on "character of offspring" support Pangenesis?

letters.title: From James Murie   1 May 1868
letters.summary: Measurements of the Bornean ape (Macacus inornatus, Gray). [SeeDescent1: 151.]

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   1 May [1868]
letters.summary: Answers CD’s objection [see6121and6146] about sexual differences and protective colouring. Summarises his theory of colour in nature.

letters.title: From B. D. Walsh   1 May 1868
letters.summary:
BDW believes the coloration of species [ofAnthocaris] provides a case of sexual selection.

The state of entomology in the U. S.; Darwinism now a common creed, especially among entomologists.

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   3 May 1868
letters.summary: Reports another case of syndactylism.

letters.title: From Gilbert William Child   3 May [1868]
letters.summary: Requests CD testimonial for Sherardian Professorship of Botany.

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   [4–7] May 1868
letters.summary:
Proportion of sexes in ruffs [seeDescent1: 306].

Colour display in linnets, songbirds. Courtship display of Australian pigeon at zoo.

letters.title: From John Scott   4 May 1868
letters.summary: Replies to CD’s query on expression of emotions.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   5 May [1868]
letters.summary:
Criticism of ARW for too little esteem of the role of sexual selection as agent in giving colour.

Response to other topics.

letters.title: To G. W. Child   6 May [1868]
letters.summary: Cannot judge GWC’s fitness for the Botanical Chair at Oxford. But CD appreciates his work, particularly that on spontaneous generation [Proc. R. Soc. Lond.13 (1863–4): 313; 14 (1865): 178].

letters.title: To G. W. Child   [6 May 1868]
letters.summary: Encloses a testimonial for GWC [see6162]. Feels himself poorly qualified to give a testimonial for a botanist and apologises for his brevity.

letters.title: To Otto Staudinger   6 May [1868]
letters.summary: Asks about the ratio of male to female Lepidoptera.

letters.title: From G. W. Child   7 May [1868]
letters.summary: Thanks CD for testimonial.

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   7 May [1868]
letters.summary:
Thanks JJW for his great assistance.

Discusses sexual selection in birds.

Sends queries on secondary sexual characteristics of birds.

Has often marvelled at the different growth of the flowering and creeping branches of ivy.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   8 May [1868]
letters.summary:
AG’s review ofVariation[Nation6 (1868): 234–6] very good.

CD’s fondness for Pangenesis; although an "infant cherished by few", CD expects it to have a long life.

letters.title: From Leonard Jenyns   9 May 1868
letters.summary: Sends his notes on Florent Prévost’s reference to the habits of the cuckoo.

letters.title: From George Cupples   11–13 May 1868
letters.summary: Answers CD’s queries on difference in size of male and female Scottish deerhounds; female preference for larger males; details about ratio of sexes born. Quotes from letter of Archibald McNeill on difference in size of male and female Scotch deerhounds.

letters.title: To Albert Günther   12 May [1868]
letters.summary:
Sends some questions on secondary sexual differences of fishes [missing], which he hopes AG will look over.

Invites AG to come to Down.

Encloses queries on sexual differences and nest-building habits of fish.

letters.title: To Richard Kippist   12 May [1868?]
letters.summary:
Returns volumes of theIbis.

Requests T. C. Jerdon’sBirds of India

and Thomas Bell’sBritish reptiles

as well as vols. 5 & 6 ofIbis.

letters.title: From Albert Günther   13 May 1868
letters.summary:
Sends proofs of his fish paper.

Will observe modification of colour in fish.

Is studying the development of the axolotl.

Encloses notes in reply to CD’s queries on fishes.

letters.title: From W. D. Fox   [before 14 May 1868]
letters.summary:
Pairing habits of birds: polygamy among ducks and canaries.

Information on the proportion of sexes in fowls and other birds.

letters.title: From Giovanni Canestrini   14 May 1868
letters.summary: Asks CD’s permission to translateVariationinto Italian [translation not published until 1876].

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   14 May [1868]
letters.summary:
WDF’s letter gives CD the kind of facts he wants. His story about peacocks is so good that CD will quote it [Descent2: 46].

Pleased WDF approves of his book [Variation]

– "beloved Pangenesis disagrees badly with many".

letters.title: To Albert Günther   15 May [1868]
letters.summary:
Thanks for answer to questions.

Has analogous questions on reptiles that he will send to AG. The subject interests him, but CD must try not to fall into his common error of "being too speculative".

letters.title: From John Harward   15 May 1868
letters.summary: On false claims that female cattle can be produced at will.

letters.title: From Otto Staudinger   15 May 1868
letters.summary: Has often thought CD would find vast material for his ideas in study of entomology and Lepidoptera. His price-list of specimens proves only that collectors of Lepidoptera catch more males than females, not that there are more. He accounts for this by the less active habits of the females. [SeeDescent1: 312.]

letters.title: From Henry Nicholson Ellacombe   16 May 1868
letters.summary: Asks function of several twisted parts (stem, petals, germen) in hardy orchids. His reading ofOrchidsmakes him suspect that the parts are connected with fertilisation.

letters.title: From Thomas Henry Farrer   17 May 1868
letters.summary: Raises a question about a statement inOrchids; his observations differ.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   [before 18 May 1868]
letters.summary: Questions on marmosets and the vocal organs ofHylobates.

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   [before 18 May 1868]
letters.summary: CD cannot remember whether correspondent believed the wing thatGallus bankivaopens and scrapes before the female, is ornamented. He fears it is not.

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   18 May 1868
letters.summary: Replies to CD’s queries regarding sexual differences in gibbons’ voices, chameleon behaviour, and the occurrence of spurs in pheasants and peahens. Discusses sexual differences in structure and habit within certain bird species.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   18 May 1868
letters.summary: Is confirmed about the bending of the fly orchid pollinia. [See "Fertilisation of orchids",Collected papers2: 141.]

letters.title: From Asa Gray   18 May 1868
letters.summary: Has passed on copy ofVariationto American Academy [of Arts and Sciences]. The U. S. reprint is not very nicely printed.

letters.title: From Friedrich Hildebrand   18 May 1868
letters.summary: Sends graft-hybrid notice.

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   18 May 1868
letters.summary: Answers CD’s question on whether any female birds regularly sing.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   19 May [1868]
letters.summary:
Thanks THF for correcting the error inOrchids.

Asks him to find out what insects visit the fly orchid and for what purpose.

letters.title: From W. D. Fox   19 May [1868]
letters.summary: Regrets he cannot get to Down.

letters.title: From William Winwood Reade   19 May 1868
letters.summary:
Going to the Gold Coast. Will collect plants for Kew.

Offers his services. Particularly interested in making inquiries for CD about the human race.

letters.title: To G. H. K. Thwaites   19 May [1868]
letters.summary:
GHKT should not take more trouble about human expression. Discusses contraction of orbicular muscles in elephants.

Asks about colour of first plumage of breeds of Ceylon fowls in which hens alone are coloured.

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   20 May 1868
letters.summary: HWB thinks he can buy specimens of male and female insects at Mr Janson’s.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   20 May 1868
letters.summary:
Trip with Huxley was perfect.

At Torquay later he had a lecture on "Kent’s hole" from Joseph Pengelly.

George Bentham acknowledges himself unreservedly a convert to Darwinism. Many will still cling to a "rag of protection, but will eventually haul it down".

A. Murray’s later parts better than first [?Geographical distribution of mammals(1866)].

Wallace’s paper shows great ability.

Disgusted with [Duke of Argyll’s]Reign of law.

His depression and exhaustion.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [20 May 1868]
letters.summary: Encloses grass from locust dung sent from Natal. Asks for name of grass.

letters.title: From St G. J. Mivart   20 May 1868
letters.summary:
Answers CD’s queries on sexual characters and differences among the Urodela.

Is interested in the relationship of pectoral and pelvic limbs in man and apes and has looked at reptiles and amphibians to find traces of the earlier conditions of the limbs.

Asks whether CD knows any instances of deformities or pathological conditions occurring simultaneously in both sets of limbs.

letters.title: From Albert Müller   20 May 1868
letters.summary:
Wilson Armistead’s death cut short his work on galls, but Müller is continuing it.

In China only uni-coloured animals are sold for meat, the rest are killed in the litter.

letters.title: To Otto Staudinger   20 May 1868
letters.summary:
Thanks for information on sex ratios of Lepidoptera.

Agrees that entomologists have best means of proving derivation of species.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   20 May [1868]
letters.summary: Inquires about the colour of first plumage of poultry breeds and development of distinguishing features.

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   21 May [1868]
letters.summary:
Lists specimens he wants from Mr Janson, emphasising that he always wants male and female.

He extends an invitation for a Sunday in early June.

letters.title: From William Farr   21 May 1868
letters.summary:
Has sent the Registrar General’s Report which shows proportion of male to female births in every county.

Consanguineous marriages.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   21 May [1868]
letters.summary:
JDH too severe on Duke of Argyll.

Pities JDH on [BAAS] address [see6099]; Huxley feels JDH will do well and will not pity him.

Thinks Huxley will give an excellent and original lecture on geographical distribution of birds.

Has been working hard on sexual selection and correspondence about it.

Mignonette is sterile with its own pollen but any two distinct plants are fertile together. It is utterly mysterious and not even Pangenesis will explain it.

On Lyell’s book [Principles, 10th ed.].

Wallace’s wonderful cleverness, but he is not cautious enough. CD differs from Wallace on birds’ nests and protection.

A. Murray’s miserable criticism of Wallace [J. Travel & Nat. Hist.1 (1868): 137–45].

letters.title: To W. W. Reade   21 May [1868]
letters.summary:
Thanks WWR for information in answer to his queries concerning expression.

Asks when horns first appear among a breed of sheep on the Guinea coast,

and for information about the gorilla and chimpanzee.

Asks about African ideas of beauty.

letters.title: From John Harward   22 May 1868
letters.summary: Will obtain information on sheep.

letters.title: To Deane Parker Pennethorne   22 May [1868]
letters.summary: Comments on DP’s paper on man ["Transmutation of man according to the Darwinian theory" (n.d.)].

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   22 May [1868]
letters.summary: Inquires about plumage of poultry breeds.

letters.title: From Joseph Bullar   23 May 1868
letters.summary: Is interested in CD’s remarks on role of pollen in modifying ovarium. Sends his own observations on numerical relations of stamens and pistils to divisions in the ovarium.

letters.title: From William Henty   23 May 1868
letters.summary: Sex ratios in cattle and sheep.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   23 May 1868
letters.summary:
Will answer CD’s queries from Africa.

Reports extreme amazement of some natives in Gabon upon seeing a white man for the first time.

letters.title: From C. S. Bate   24 May 1868
letters.summary: On structure of Crustacea; size of claws [seeDescent1: 330–1].

letters.title: To C. S. Bate   25 May [1868]
letters.summary: Thanks for note about enlarged left arm ofGelasimus.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   25 May 1868
letters.summary: CD’s book taking on famously. AG’s review inNation[see5921] and preface to American edition.

letters.title: From Edward Westey Janson   25 May 1868
letters.summary:
Sends specimens selected by H. W. Bates.

Among the Lamellicornes the family Dynastidae have most instances of presence of stridulating organs; Frederick Smith says that in Hymenoptera femaleMutillahas stridulating faculty in high degree.

[Itemised bill for Coleoptera specimens enclosed.]

letters.title: To John Murray   25 May 1868
letters.summary:
Asks JM to consider publishing a MS on John Wesley by CD’s niece, Frances Julia Wedgwood [John Wesley and the evangelical reaction of the eighteenth century(1870)].

Has received clean sheets for Italian translation [ofVariation?].

letters.title: From W. B. Tegetmeier   25 May 1868
letters.summary: Describes change of plumage in chickens in order to be sure he is clear about the age of chickens on which CD wants information. Encloses feathers to illustrate changes.

letters.title: From George Cupples   26 May 1868
letters.summary:
Refers to letter from John Wright offering to help CD on his queries about deerhounds and sexual preferences.

More details about a terrier bitch previously referred to [letter missing].

letters.title: To William Henty   26 May 1868
letters.summary: Thanks WH for sending a table about sheep. Wishes to know if the sheep belonged to one or several breeds. Mr Harward, a breeder of shorthorns, has tried M. Thury’s plan, and it failed.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   26 May 1868
letters.summary: Did not know of complex change of plumage. From WBT’s letter, CD thinks six weeks to two months old is the best period. Sends details of breeds and other particulars.

letters.title: From John Murray   27 May [1868]
letters.summary:
Will be glad to see Miss Wedgwood’s MS on Wesley.

The clichés of Fritz Müller’s work [Für Darwin] have arrived.

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   28 May 1868
letters.summary:
He has been occupied with Royal Geographical Society anniversary meeting, but did go to Janson and selected various specimens for CD, some of which have remarkable stridulating organs.

The habits ofLethrusare found in Kirby and Spence’sIntroduction[to entomology, 7th ed. (1856)].

letters.title: From Friedrich Rolle   28 May 1868
letters.summary:
Questions CD’s view inVariationthatTorfschweinformerly ranged from Europe to China.

Cites numerous German publications relating to CD’s theory.

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   [before 30 May 1868]
letters.summary: Reversion of tamed animals to wild behaviour.

letters.title: From Hugh Browne   30 May 1868
letters.summary: Is reading CD’s instances of inherited peculiarities of eye [Variation2: 8–10]. Gives cases of colour-blindness of males in his family.

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   30 May [1868]
letters.summary:
Glad to have JJW’s opinion on nest-building. Wallace’s view [that skill is learned] is opposed to many facts.

Asks JJW about birds and their behaviour.

Wants information on the first plumage of different breeds of canaries.

letters.title: To Friedrich Rolle   31 May 1868
letters.summary:
Thanks for references.

CD in error aboutTorfschwein.

Comments on German publications.

Asks about breed of fowl in which females have spurs.

letters.title: To Linnean Society   1 June 1868
letters.summary: Requests 50 copies of his paper ["Offspring of illegitimate unions of di- and trimorphic plants",J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)10 (1869): 393–437].

letters.title: To Osbert Salvin   1 June 1868
letters.summary:
Encloses some queries.

Would also like information about proportion of male to female humming-birds.

Reference to OS’s paper inIbis, vol. 2.

letters.title: To Bryceson Brothers & Co.   [after June 1868?]
letters.summary: Reports the whereabouts of S. J. O’H. Horsman, who has failed to pay for an organ he ordered.

letters.title: To ?   [after June 1868]
letters.summary: Testimonial for James Archer, who leaves CD’s service after six months.

letters.title: From Samuel James O’Hara Horsman 2 June [1868]
letters.summary: Resigns curacy of Down.

letters.title: From Williams & Norgate   2 June 1868
letters.summary: Progress of CD’s order for certain books.

letters.title: To S. J. O’H. Horsman   3 June 1868
letters.summary: Thinks SJOH is right not to return to Down. Asks him to forward certain documents. Hopes final arrangements will soon be made for a resident clergyman in Down.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   3 June 1868
letters.summary:
Is glad FM approves of a translation ofFür Darwin.

Hopes FM will think well of Pangenesis.

Sexual differences in insect auditory and stridulating organs.

Read FM’s paper onBalanuswith great interest ["OnBalanus armatus",Ann. & Mag. Nat. Hist.4th ser. 1 (1868): 393–412].

letters.title: To John Scott   3 June 1868
letters.summary:
As JS’s powers of observation seem to exist in all lines, CD begs further information from him and [H. N. B.] Erskine about the natives’ expressions of indignation, affirmation, and negation. The movements of the eyebrows and forehead of a girl in violent grief are of particular interest.

Do sub-breeds of pigeons exist in India as in Europe, but not in England? If so, what is the colour of the plumage in males and females at different stages of development?

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   3 June 1868
letters.summary: Plumage of canaries; changes in plumage with successive moults.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   4 June 1868
letters.summary: Describes work with pollinia of anotherOrchisspecies.

letters.title: From E. W. Janson   4 June 1868
letters.summary:
Sends specimens of Coleoptera.

Quotes from W. F. Erichson [Naturgeschichte der Insecten Deutschlands3: 927] on stridulating organs inTrox.

letters.title: From George Rogers   4 June 1868
letters.summary: Suggests variation in seed-covering membranes as a cause of variation in plants.

letters.title: To H. B. Tristram   4 June 1868
letters.summary: Asks about camouflage of birds in the Sahara desert.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   5 June 1868
letters.summary: "I have seen the action onOphrysexactly as you describe and am thoroughly ashamed of my inaccuracy."

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   5 June 1868
letters.summary: Horrified to find he has forgotten to announce birth of daughter.

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   5 June 1868
letters.summary:
Sorry JJW cannot visit.

Will go to sea-side for five weeks at end of July.

DoesViduahave double annual moult? [SeeDescent2: 181.]

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   6 June [1868]
letters.summary:
Congratulations on birth of daughter. CD used to dread birth-time.

Sexual selection has turned out to be a large subject.

letters.title: From Henry Baker Tristram   6 June 1868
letters.summary: Will answer CD’s queries when he returns home in a month.

letters.title: To Bibliographisches Institut, Hildburghausen   8 June 1868
letters.summary:
Discusses possible English translation of A. E. Brehm’s [Illustrirtes]Thierleben[1864–9].

Asks for permission to use 15 of Brehm’s illustrations [inDescent].

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   8 [June? 1868]
letters.summary: A cheque written out for FD has never been presented to CD’s bankers.

letters.title: From Rosa Bullar   9 June 1868
letters.summary: Reports case of black retriever that always burrows in earth before giving birth and keeps pups in hole thereafter. CD’s book says this habit rare.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   9 June 1868
letters.summary:
F. Müller’s corrections warrant stating that the English translation has "additions and corrections by the author".

Is gratified to hear his index [toVariation] is considered a good one.

Ernst Haeckel’s book [Generelle Morphologie(1868)], though speculative, strikes him as "one of the most remarkable books of our time".

letters.title: To B. D. Walsh   9 June 1868
letters.summary:
Thanks BDW for new facts aboutAnthocaris[see6156].

Asks BDW to observe stridulation apparatus in male and female lamellicorns.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   10 June 1868
letters.summary:
W. S. Dallas asks whether Ray Society would publish translation of Haeckel’sGenerelle morphologie. If THH thinks suggestion good, he might make inquiries.

Family news.

letters.title: From John Wright   11 June 1868
letters.summary:
Preference of females for particular males certainly exists occasionally.

On the proportion of males to females in horses and in dogs.

letters.title: From J. B. Innes   13 June 1868
letters.summary: Writes about difficulties in which S. J. O. Horsman, curate at Down, has involved himself and others. Horsman has said he would resign. JBI offers to give up his interests in the living at Down.

letters.title: From W. B. Dawkins   15 June 1868
letters.summary:
Variation in recent leonine skeletons.

Miocene fauna of Europe.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   15 [June 1868]
letters.summary: Sends second lot of grass grown from locust dung pellets from Natal.

letters.title: To J. B. Innes   15 June [1868]
letters.summary: CD writes in detail about difficulties with Horsman’s financial accounts and the affairs of the parish.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   15 June [1868]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Has been looking at the school accounts. Has any interest been paid to S. J. O’H. Horsman this year? CD will keep accounts temporarily; he has not yet received from Horsman the balance in hand from last year.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   16 June 1868
letters.summary:
Will get name of grass [see6243] from Gen. William Munro.

Has heard from Charles Wheatstone that CD has Prussian Order of Merit. Rejoices because it is the only distinction worth a fig.

Went to Handel festival; heardMessiah.

Went to poor old N. B. Ward’s funeral.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   17 [June 1868]
letters.summary:
OnPour le Mérite; JDH has made him think more highly of it.

Messiahis the one thing he would like to hear again, but thinks his soul might be too dried up now to appreciate it. Sometimes hates science for making him "a withered leaf" for everything else.

Frank [Darwin] now doing botany seriously.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   17 June 1868
letters.summary:
Again thanks CD for trouble in arranging for translation ofFür Darwin.

Sends addition answering critics of his idea of insect metamorphosis [see Möller ed. 1915–21, 1: 259].

Agrees with Charles Lyell’s suggested English title "Facts and arguments in favor of Darwin", although perhaps more accurate to call it "Darwinism tested by Carcinology" or "Carcinology as bearing on the origin of species".

Says any profit should go to CD for his trouble and expense with the translation.

Thanks for seeds ofEschscholtzia.

Gives observations on number of climbing plants, includingDilleniacea,Marantacea,Catasetum.

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   [before 18 June 1868]
letters.summary:
Coloration of linnets.

Sexual behaviour of black hen bullfinch.

letters.title: From J. B. Innes   18 June [1868]
letters.summary: Further discussion of the difficulties with S. J. O’H. Horsman [curate at Down].

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   18 June [1868]
letters.summary:
CD thanks JJW for letter about the crimson breast of linnets

and the fate of a pugnacious female bullfinch.

Refers to JJW’s pointing out the number of Jenners and Weirs who have been naturalists, and cites some writings by men of those families about striking cases of birds.

letters.title: To Frederick Bates   19 June [1868?]
letters.summary: "Though next Spring will be rather late, I do not think it will be too late, & if in your power to send me some living specimens ofTrox sabulosus, I shd. be greatly indebted to you.––-"

letters.title: From John Lubbock   19 June [1868]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: JL’s Royal Institution lectures.

letters.title: From Osbert Salvin   20 June 1868
letters.summary:
Shot a sandpiper in Norway, the hind toe of which was clasped by a freshwater bivalve.

Sends replies to CD’s queries about sex ratios in humming-birds.

letters.title: From George Cupples   22 June 1868
letters.summary: Weighing ten deerhound puppies for CD each week.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   22 June 1868
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for article by G. H. Lewes ["Mr Darwin’s hypotheses, pt 1",Fortn. Rev.n.s. 3 (1868): 353–73]. Comments on article.

Describes hybridisation experiment carried out on rabbits and hares by Dr Conrad.

Encloses description ofMonera

and a phylogenetic table of vertebrates.

Mentions work on Medusae.

The controversy over CD in Germany.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   22 June 1868
letters.summary:
The grass [see6243] isSporobolus elongatus, common in the tropics.

Visit to Oxford with X Club.

On his forthcoming address.

letters.title: From Oskar Schmidt   22 June 1868
letters.summary:
Has received copy ofVariation.

Sends copy of his book [Die Spongien der Küste von Algier(1868)]. Comments on it.

letters.title: To George Bentham   23 June 1868
letters.summary:
Expresses thanks and pleasure at what GB has said about his book [Variation] in GB’s [Presidential] Address [to the Linnean Society, 1868,Proc. Linn. Soc. Lond.(1868): lvii–c]. "What you say about Pangenesis quite satisfies me".

CD discussed "bud-variation" to show that it was an error to believe all variability is due to sexual generation.

letters.title: To Osbert Salvin   23 June [1868]
letters.summary: CD thanks OS for answering his questions and especially for giving the case of the sandpiper; "such little facts are my delight". [See6253.]

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   24 June [1868]
letters.summary:
Thanks for name of grass.

Plans to go to Isle of Wight on 17 July.

Frank cannot come to Kew, as he will be reading this long vacation at Cambridge.

Delighted with Bentham’s Presidential Address [Linnean Society, 1868].

letters.title: To ? [before 1 July 1868]
letters.summary: Sends a copy of George Bentham’sAnniversary address to the Linnean Society of London(Bentham 1868).

letters.title: From H. B. Tristram   1 July 1868
letters.summary: On the coloration of 26 species of Saharan birds.

letters.title: To Edward Blyth   [after July 1868]
letters.summary: Questions from CD related to bird plumage and sexual differences, with answers by EB.

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   2 July 1868
letters.summary: Has examined three races of the mouflon sheep and remarks on the extent of variation in them.

letters.title: From Alphonse de Candolle   2 July 1868
letters.summary:
Offers notes and reflections onVariation.

Not convinced by Pangenesis, particularly its dependence on theCytisus[graft hybrid] examples [ch. 27 and ch. 11].

What a book could be written on the application of natural history to man! Gives examples of inheritance in man.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   3 July 1868
letters.summary:
Thanks for two small works.

Will read essay on man [Entstehung des Menschengeschlechts] with much interest.

Generelle Morphologiereviewed by G. Bentham ["Anniversary Address",Proc. Linn. Soc. Lond.(1867–8): lviii–c].

Extremely sceptical of hare–rabbit hybrid.

letters.title: From Friedrich Hildebrand   3 July 1868
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for mentioning hisCorydalisandPrimulaexperiments inVariation.

Has become Professor of Botany at Freiburg.

Encloses specimen ofCorydalis cava.

letters.title: From William Pole   3 July 1868
letters.summary: InVariationCD mentions colour-blindness in women. WP does not believe there are any proven cases.

letters.title: From F. F. Geach   4 July 1868
letters.summary: Answers toExpressionquestionnaire.

letters.title: To H. D. Tristram   4 July 1868
letters.summary: Thanks for interesting letter. ‘How very curious the case of the bright-colour birds which conceal themselves in holes!’

letters.title: From John Addison   6 July 1868
letters.summary: Sends newspaper clipping about a nest of young birds, apparently hybrid offspring of a cock goldfinch and a hen green linnet.

letters.title: To Alphonse de Candolle   6 July 1868
letters.summary:
Thanks AdeC for his long letter full of interesting facts, which will be of great use if a new edition [ofVariation] is demanded.

As for when CD will publish on variation in a state of nature: he has had the MS almost ready for several years butVariationfatigued him so much

that "I determined to amuse myself by publishing a short essay on the Descent of Man".

AdeC will have plenty of time to publish his views. Asks permission to quote AdeC on a case of inheritance of scalp-muscles [seeDescent1: 20].

Hooker has expressed a view, similar to AdeC’s, "that morals & politics would be very interesting if discussed like any branch of Natural History".

Agrees with AdeC on acclimatisation

and on graft-hybrids.

CD is repeating Hildebrand’s method in producing graft-hybrid potatoes.

As for Pangenesis, very few people approve of it though it has some enthusiastic friends and CD has much faith in its vitality.

letters.title: From Julia Margaret Cameron   [before 10 July 1868]
letters.summary: On the rental by the Darwins of a house at Freshwater Bay, Isle of Wight.

letters.title: From J. M. Cameron   10 July 1868
letters.summary: More on the rental by the Darwins of a house at Freshwater Bay.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   12 July [1868]
letters.summary:
Sketches out subjects he intends to speak on at Norwich [BAAS meeting]: museums, CD’s work in botany, Pangenesis, early history of mankind.

Asks about CD’s "book on man" [Descent].

letters.title: From George Cupples   13 July 1868
letters.summary:
Offers deerhound puppy.

Asks for photograph.

Encloses letter from George Cupples of notes, with excerpts from letters from Peter Robertson and John Wright, relating to difference in size between male and female deerhounds. Reports on weight statistics of ten [deerhound] puppies being observed.

letters.title: From William Thomas Bridges?   14 July [1868–70?]
letters.summary: Asks CD what prompts dogs of all kinds to roll themselves in decayed animal matter; inherited habit or immediate gratification?

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   14 July 1868
letters.summary: Thinks JDH would be wise not to touch on Pangenesis; it has very few friends. Bentham is doubtful, Carus against, and Alphonse de Candolle likes it least in the book. CD still convinced it will be hereafter looked on as "best hypothesis of generation inheritance & development". If JDH means to cut up Pangenesis he has no word to say in opposition.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   14 July 1868
letters.summary:
Comments favourably, though often differing, on articles by G. H. Lewes.

Discusses claim of Agassiz [inA journey in Brazil(1868)] that he found evidence of glaciers in Brazil. Suggests sponsoring an expedition to test these claims.

letters.title: From Alphonse de Candolle   15 July 1868
letters.summary:
Corrects himself onRobinia pseud-acacia: its spines are stipules, which explains hereditary fixity.

AdeC’s observations on movement of scalp muscles.

letters.title: To Inland Revenue   [17–21 July 1868?]
letters.summary: Cannot fill out a return [for foreign revenue?] until his return home.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   17 July 1868
letters.summary:
Comments on CD’s health.

Has received gold medal from Dutch Academy of Science forZur Entwicklungsgeschichte der Siphonophoren[1869].

HisEntstehung des Menschengeschlechts[1868] has been sharply attacked by the clergy.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [18 July 1868]
letters.summary:
Looks forward to seeing JDH and hearing about address.

Feels better already.

Disappointed in house [they have taken at Freshwater].

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   20 July 1868
letters.summary: Reports on newly discovered Sclater’s pea-fowl from Cochin China.

letters.title: To Alphonse de Candolle   20 July [1868]
letters.summary:
Thanks AdeC for correcting an error about thorns, which CD might have quoted.

CD will be cautious in regard to the muscles of the scalp. [Descent1: 20].

His health has failed again "in the usual manner" and he has been ordered to do no work.

Repeats how interested and pleased he was by AdeC’s last long, remarkable letter.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   20 July 1868
letters.summary: Prof. Kühne would like to visit CD.

letters.title: From Eduard Koch   21 July 1868
letters.summary: Sends completed translation of vol. 2 ofVariation. Thanks CD for co-operation and asks to be informed when CD is finished with additions. Comments on sale of first volume and distribution of presentation copies of the second.

letters.title: From Louis Agassiz   22 July 1868
letters.summary:
LA clarifies his opposition to CD’s views, which does not blind him to the great value of CD’s original researches.

Answers CD’s questions regarding sexual coloration of Amazonian fishes and the protuberances on the head of maleGeophagusandCichladuring the spawning season [seeDescent, pp. 520, 529].

letters.title: From G. H. K. Thwaites   22 July 1868
letters.summary:
GHKT is going to procure some local smoke-coloured fowls and investigate them for CD.

Encloses letter on expression queries from S. O. Glenie.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   23 July [1868]
letters.summary: Has come to Freshwater for five weeks for his health. Sends regrets to Prof. Kühne at not being able to see him.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   25 July 1868
letters.summary:
Asks for information on how many languagesOriginhas appeared in, how many English and American editions it has gone through, and its reception abroad. Wants to disprove statement that the theory is "fast passing away".

Baby ill, scarcely any hope of recovery.

Some botanical books have come for CD.

letters.title: To Horace Darwin   26 [July 1868]
letters.summary: Writes to express his pleasure at Leonard’s success [second in the Woolwich Academy entrance examination].

letters.title: From G. H. Lewes   26 July 1868
letters.summary:
Replies to CD’s letter [missing]. He does intend to treat of Pangenesis "as the most remarkable hypothesis yet put forth".

His articles inFortnightly Reviewhave grown in number so that he plans to make a book of them. Asks CD to send him notes of his objections.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   28 July [1868]
letters.summary:
Sorry to hear of baby’s illness.

Comments on statement that belief in natural selection is passing away. Common descent of species is almost universally accepted now, and this is more important. In large part acceptance is due toOrigin. Discusses reception of and interest inOriginin various countries.

letters.title: To G. H. Lewes   28 July [1868]
letters.summary: Thanks GHL for his support of Pangenesis.

letters.title: From Alfred Wrigley   28 July 1868
letters.summary: Leonard Darwin is to enter Woolwich Military Academy.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   29 July 1868
letters.summary:
Thanks for information in CD’s letter.

Baby has been ill.

Has finished rough sketch of [BAAS] address.

Has got G. H. Richard to take Geographical Section at Norwich meeting.

letters.title: From G. H. Lewes   30 July 1868
letters.summary:
In consideration of CD’s health, withdraws his request for notes on GHL’s articles.

While in Freiburg, heard that August Weismann’s inaugural address on CD’s views [Über die Berechtigung der Darwin’schen Theorie(1868)] created a sensation.

letters.title: To Cassell, Petter & Galpin   [August–December 1868]
letters.summary: CD arranges for copies of some blocks [for use inDescent] from Brehm’s [Illustrirtes Thierleben(1864–7)].

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   3 August 1868
letters.summary: Discusses peacocks and the rediscovery of the long-lost crested turkey.

letters.title: From M. J. S. Schultze   4 August 1868
letters.summary: CD has been awarded an honorary doctorate by the University of Bonn.

letters.title: From Robert Swinhoe   4 August 1868
letters.summary:
Discusses a domestic oriental fowl.

Is having problems getting answers to CD’s queries on expression as Chinese facial expressions are limited and controlled. Answers as well as he can. [SeeExpressionindex.]

letters.title: To M. J. S. Schultze   [after 4 August 1868]
letters.summary: Expresses gratitude for the distinguished honour conferred upon him by the University of Bonn.

letters.title: From Ludwig Molendo and Alexander Walther   5 August 1868
letters.deprecated: Ludwig MolendoAlexander Wilhelm Hannibal Franz (Alexander) Walther
letters.sender: Ludwig MolendoAlexander Wilhelm Hannibal Franz (Alexander) Walther
letters.summary: Send their work [Die Laubmoose Oberfrankens(1868)].

letters.title: From Richard Bowdler Sharpe   5 August 1868
letters.summary: Is writing to Australia to answer CD’s questions about resemblance of tail-feathers of young and mature female kingfishers. [SeeDescent2: 188.]

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   6 August 1868
letters.summary:
Coming on Saturday.

Baby and wife pretty well.

letters.title: To G. H. Lewes   7 August [1868]
letters.summary:
Thinks GHL’s articles are quite excellent; hopes they will be republished.

Discusses adaptation. Doubts whether similar conditions without selection can produce similar organs independent of blood relationship: "resemblances due to descent and adaptation can commonly be distinguished".

Discusses luminous insects, electrical organs of fish,

thorns and spines.

letters.title: From G. H. Lewes   8 August 1868
letters.summary:
Gratified by CD’s approval of his articles, which the public has not much liked.

Clarifies the obscure sentence CD criticised – forms having a different genesis can be similar.

Calls CD’s attention to Kovalevsky’s memoir onAmphioxus[Mem. Acad. Imp. Sci. St.-Pétersbourg7th ser. 11 (1868) no.4]. K’s views are all in favour of CD’s and against GHL’s.

letters.title: From George Cupples   10 August 1868
letters.summary: Thanks for photograph.

letters.title: From Gustavus Detlef Hinrichs   [before 13 August 1868]
letters.summary: Sends work proving all elements formed of one substance: "Pantogen". Feels affinity with CD. His work will cause as great a stir. Has already been preached against. Asks CD for a note as a token of his sympathy.

letters.title: From Dyson Lacy   [before 13 August 1868]
letters.summary:
Answers to CD’s queries on expression in natives of Queensland, Australia.

[Forwarded by Edward Wilson to CD.]

letters.title: To G. D. Hinrichs   13 August 1868
letters.summary:
Acknowledges GH’s letter and the lecture on "Faith and science".

Cannot form a judgment on his chemical theory, but if GH establishes his case it will be a magnificent discovery.

"Faith and science" contained many ideas new to CD. Hooker, too, has read it with interest.

letters.title: To Charles Alexander Johns   13 August [1868?]
letters.summary: CD not a good enough botanist to form a judgment of specimen. Does not understand whether CAJ supposes the variety to be a result of hybridism or of the present very hot summer, which CD cannot doubt will have an effect on some British plants in their struggle for life.

letters.title: From Robert Brough Smyth   13 August 1868
letters.summary: Relates some observations on expression among Australian aboriginals and encloses answers to CD’s queries from other observers. [These include letters and observations from: J. A. Hagenauer, 28 May 1868; Archibald Grahame Lang, 17 June 1868; H. B. Lane, 24 June 1868; Templeton Bunnett, 25 June 1868; J. Bulmer (1868). (See introduction toExpression.)]

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   14 August 1868
letters.summary: Asks whether it would be convenient if he came to Down. JVC would be sorry to leave England without seeing and thanking CD.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   15 August [1868]
letters.summary:
AG’s coming visit to England.

Hooker’s Presidency of BAAS.

A month at the Isle of Wight has done almost nothing for CD.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   16 August [1868]
letters.summary:
Regrets having missed JVC’s visit. CD’s health is poor. He hopes JVC will come to Down after BAAS meeting.

Has heard second part [ofVariation] is out in German. Thanks JVC for his great care in making translation accurate.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   16 August [1868]
letters.summary:
The problem of sterility, and its relation to natural selection.

George Bentham’s support of Darwinism.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   17 [August 1868]
letters.summary:
Enjoyed JDH’s visit.

Mrs Cameron’s photograph of JDH is grand.

Has heard J. V. Carus will be at Norwich. Suggests JDH mention thatOriginwas translated by two distinguished naturalists, H. G. Bronn and Carus.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   17 August 1868
letters.summary:
FM’s additions for English edition [1869] ofFür Darwin.

Dimorphic plants.

letters.title: To Ernesto Susanni   18 August [1868]
letters.summary: Hopes to find the article by Terenzio Mamiani della Rovere (Mamiani della Rovere 1868) on his return home.

letters.title: To Louis Agassiz   19 August 1868
letters.summary: Thanks LA for information on sexual differences in the coloration of Amazonian fish. CD was anxious to know how the sexes differed because they are unusual in that the male has the largest share in looking after ova and young.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   19 August 1868
letters.summary:
The material [from F. Müller] makes the translation more like a new edition.

German entomologists are becoming Darwinists.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   19 August 1868
letters.summary: Asks JDH to obtain from Sven Nilsson information on whether, in reindeer species in which both sexes are horned, the horns are first developed earlier or later than in species in which males alone have horns.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   19 August [1868]
letters.summary: The problem of dimorphic plants and their fertility.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [20 August 1868]
letters.summary:
Reports on Norwich address [Rep. BAAS38 (1868): lviii–lxxv]. Left out some things, i.e., Asa Gray’s being superseded.

Tyndall says CD and JDH are types of "unconscious merit".

letters.title: From Thomas Campbell Eyton   23 August [1868]
letters.summary:
Sends a copy of hisOsteologia avium.

Variation in pigs’ heads

and inConvolvulus.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   23 August [1868]
letters.summary:
Pleased at success of JDH’s address. Has read several press reports.

Spectatorpitches into JDH about theology ["Dr Hooker on the evidences", 22 Aug 1868, pp. 986–7].

Feels JDH has "immensely advanced the belief in evolution of species".

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   24 August 1868
letters.summary: Discusses the development of horns in antelopes. Remarks on the variation within and between the species ofCervusand on their relationship to each other.

letters.title: To Henry Austin Bruce   24 August [1868?]
letters.summary:
Thanks correspondent for information. CD does not care much for more cases of striped asses,

but is pleased at the interesting case of the affectionate jackal that licks like a domestic dog.

letters.title: To T. C. Eyton   25 August [1868]
letters.summary:
Thanks TCE for copy of his book [Osteologia avium(1867)].

Recalls visits to Eyton.

letters.title: To Eduard Koch   27 August 1868
letters.summary:
Would like to see reviews of book [Variation].

Health has lately been indifferent.

Cannot at present pledge to give [EK?] translation rights to next book.

letters.title: From B. D. Walsh   29 August 1868
letters.summary:
On the delay in receiving CD’s new book [Variation] and his delight in a borrowed copy.

Encloses a Prospectus on his new periodical "American Entomologist" devoted to economic entomology.

Comments on the talents of his young partner, C. V. Riley.

Requests photographs for Riley of CD and Westwood.

Dr J. L. Le Conte has not yet received the request that he furnish CD with information about the stridulatory organs of Coleoptera.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   30 August 1868
letters.summary:
The newspapers’ pother about his mild theology.

Tyndall’s reference to JDH and CD as the two "modestest" men in science.

Huxley offended the clergy twice without cause or warrant.

William Hooker ill.

Astronomers do not like JDH’s reference to them.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   30 August [1868]
letters.summary:
On triumph of "Darwinianism".

Discussion of their differences on subject of protection.

letters.title: From Ellen Frances Lubbock   [before 31 August 1868]
letters.summary:
Sven Nilsson may visit John Lubbock.

Norwich [BAAS] meeting was most successful.

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   31 August 1868
letters.summary:
EB is moving to Wiltshire for a week.

Tells CD of animals acquired, or about to be acquired, by the Zoological Garden.

letters.title: From G. D. Hinrichs   31 August 1868
letters.summary:
Explains "Pantogen".

Summarises his papers.

Asks for help in finding a publisher.

Criticises d’Archiac’s review ofOrigin[inPaléontologie stratigraphique2 (1864)].

letters.title: From J. B. Innes   31 August 1868
letters.summary: JBI has been charmed withVariation. Does not think there is really any theological difficulty in the "predestination of variation".

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   [September 1868 – August 1870]
letters.summary:
Sends a bill he thinks is Caroline’s.

Tells CD of officers’ praise of Leonard.

letters.title: To the Traffic Manager, South Eastern Railway   [c.September 1868]
letters.summary: Wishes correspondent to investigate immediately the loss of two boxes in transit.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   1 September [1868]
letters.summary:
Athenæum[Owen’s?] attack on JDH [BAAS address] and CD. False statement that CD’s sole groundwork is from pigeons.

Agrees with JDH on foolishness of Red Lion Club.

Huxley’s want of judgment.

JDH’s argument about astronomy and astronomers.

Pall Mall Gazette[8 (1868): 593, 595–6] andMorning Advertiseron JDH’s address.

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   1 September 1868
letters.summary: Invites JJW to visit Down. Will try to get A. R. Wallace and H. W. Bates also.

letters.title: To J. B. Innes   2 September 1868
letters.summary:
Surprised and pleased JBI liked his "big book" [Variation].

Luckily, naturalists do not seem to think he has committed suicide with the work.

CD wants to turn over the school accounts to John Robinson [curate of Down]. Writes of other parish news.

Will vote in person for Sir John Lubbock.

letters.title: From William Ogle   2 September 1868
letters.summary: Returns a pamphlet onSalvia[F. Hildebrand, "Über die Befruchtung der Salviaarten" (1865)Jahrb. Wiss. Bot.4 (1866): 451–78].

letters.title: To G. H. K. Thwaites   2 September 1868
letters.summary: Thanks GHKT and S. O. Glenie for information about fowls.

letters.title: From Henry Fletcher Hance   3 September 1868
letters.summary: Sends CD an article [missing] on the early domestication and culture of the goldfish.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   3 September [1868]
letters.summary: Would like information on the first plumage of poultry.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   5 September 1868
letters.summary:
Has met A. J. Gower, Consul at Nagasaki, Japan, who knows all about the Ainus. JDH has given away all the copies of CD’sQueries about expression.

Nettled byPall Mall Gazettereview of BAAS address [see6342].

Owen is indeed an ass. Carlyle’s comment on Owen’s smile.

The Asa Grays at Kew.

letters.title: From H. B. Tristram   5 September 1868
letters.summary: Sexual differences in plumage of birds; various species compared.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   5 September [1868]
letters.summary: Accepts invitation.

letters.title: From Gaston de Saporta   6 September 1868
letters.deprecated: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.sender: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.summary:
Strong support for theory of descent.

Observations on palaeobotany of S. France. Most woody angiosperm genera date far back.Magnoliatype unchanged. Intermediate fossil species. Ancient species ofQuercuspersists as variety of modern species. Fossil evidence of ice age.

CD’s works have been an inspiration in France.

letters.title: From Emanuel Bonavia   [before 7 September 1868]
letters.summary: Peloric forms of flowers:Clitoria Ternatea.

letters.title: To Miles Joseph Berkeley   7 September 1868
letters.summary:
Appreciates MJB’s address [Rep. BAAS38 (1868): 83–7]. Has had great respect for MJB’s knowledge since his undergraduate days at Cambridge.

Agrees that Pangenesis gemmules probably do not develop into free cells, but penetrate other cells in a manner analogous to fertilisation, and modify their development.

letters.title: From M. T. Masters   7 September 1868
letters.summary: Thanks for Emanuel Bonavia’s letter on aLaburnummonster.

letters.title: From J. J. Moulinié   7 September 1868
letters.summary:
Pleased to have met the Darwins.

Sends his photograph.

Printers are past the index in vol. 2 ofVariation.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [8–10 September 1868]
letters.summary:
Has written to A. J. Gower.

Sends more copies ofQueries about expression.

Pall Mall Gazettearticle [see6342] is monstrous to say religion did not attack science. Should scientific men ignore whole subject of religion?

Sends French journal with article on JDH and one (weak) by Agassiz on geographical distribution.

M. J. Berkeley has sent his address [Rep. BAAS38 (1868): 83–7].

CD differs with JDH on Owen; could hardly bear to shake hands with him.

Wallaces, Blyth, Jenner Weirs are coming to stay on Sunday.

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   8 September 1868
letters.summary: Thanks CD for invitation to Down.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   8 September [1868]
letters.summary:
Asks about the differences in colour of plumage of adult male, female, and young birds. Suggests pile game as subject.

Asks about relative proportion of sexes in ducks and fowls.

letters.title: To H. D. Tristram   8 September 1868
letters.summary: Thanks for answers to questions, but declines loan of specimens.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   9 September 1868
letters.summary:
Will repeat CD’s experiments on dimorphic and trimorphic plants.

Auditory organs of Orthoptera; stridulation in lamellicorn beetles.

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   10 September 1868
letters.summary: Because of work on the first number of the new Royal Geographical Society magazine, a manual of geography, and other things, HWB finds he must decline CD’s invitation.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   10 September 1868
letters.summary: Sends a paper he has written [on scarlet runner].

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   [11 September 1868]
letters.summary: ARW’s wife will accompany him to Down.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   12 September 1868
letters.summary: BAAS Norwich meeting. Hooker [President] came out in great force. "Darwinismus" spread over the sections and crept into everything. CD will have rare happiness of seeing his ideas triumph during his life.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   [13–21 September 1868]
letters.summary:
Sends a page to be sent on to Charles William Nunn.

Offers sympathy for the illness of THH’s son, Henry (Harry) Huxley.

Wishes he could have attended the British Association for the Advancement of Science meeting at Norwich.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   [14 September 1868]
letters.summary: On sounds produced byEuchirus longimanusbeetle. Sends a pair by post.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   15 September [1868]
letters.summary: Comments on THF’s MS [on fertilisation of scarlet runners]. Suggests publication, though CD anticipated main features ten years before. Is amused at the caution with which THF put his case that the final end [of the contrivances] was crossing distinct individuals.

letters.title: From A. B. Meyer   15 September 1868
letters.summary:
Sends essay by Karl Bettelheim.

Describes preparations for scientific journey.

letters.title: To G. D. Hinrichs   16 September 1868
letters.summary: Acknowledges letter of 31 August and various works. Regrets he is unable to help GH with his works but will seek to interest Tyndall. Discourages GH on prospect of publication of his new book in England.

letters.title: To John Murray   16 September [1868]
letters.summary: B. D. Walsh has not received his copy ofVariation. Several other foreign correspondents have similar complaints.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   16 September [1868]
letters.summary: CD’s oscillating views relating to protection and sexual selection.

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   17 September 1868
letters.summary: Wonders if George Darwin can explain why a thin stream of water poured from a jug always spirals right to left.

letters.title: From John Syer Bristowe   17 September 1868
letters.summary: Reports a case of peculiar colouring in grapes, each with well-defined segments of purple.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   17 September 1868
letters.summary:
Encouraged by CD’s reply. Sends another paper, on blueLobelia.

Asks advice on books.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   17 September 1868
letters.summary:
Reached Kew last evening.

Hooker is in Scotland for two or three days.

letters.title: To J. S. Bristowe 18 September 1868
letters.summary: Thanks JSB for his information about coloured grapes, but asks that he take no further trouble.

letters.title: To John Dean Caton   18 September 1868
letters.summary: Thanks JDC for paper ["AmericanCervus",Trans. Ottawa Acad. Nat. Sci.(1868); read 21 May 1868].

letters.title: To Frederic Higgins?   18 September 1868
letters.summary: Thanks correspondent for gift of game and sends remembrances to his father [John Higgins]. Would like to visit Alford and Beesby, but fears he will have neither time nor strength.

letters.title: From John Murray    18 September [1868]
letters.summary: JM will send another copy ofVariationto B. D. Walsh.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   18 September [1868]
letters.summary: Submits a 15–point argument against CD’s views on the coloration of female birds and insects.

letters.title: To James Croll   19 September 1868
letters.summary: Discusses papers by JC dealing with erosion. Comments on papers on the subject by J. B. Jukes, A. C. Ramsay, and William Whitaker. Formerly believed in power of the sea. Never fully realised the truth until reading JC’s papers.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   19 September [1868]
letters.summary:
Will send THF’s paper [on scarlet runners] toAnnals and Magazine of Natural Historywith a note recommending publication [see6384].

Suggests books onLobelia.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   20 September 1868
letters.summary: Sends an addition toLobeliapaper; admires adaptations for fertilisation.

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   21 September 1868
letters.summary: Discusses the top-knot turkey and the occasional appearance of the top-knot in a breed of cream-coloured turkeys.

letters.title: To B. D. Walsh   21 September 1868
letters.summary:
Thanks BDW for pamphlets [by S. H. Scudder and J. D. Caton].

His information aboutCicadais of extraordinary interest. Discusses stridulation organs which certainly sometimes differ in the sexes. CD would be curious to know if "dumb"Cicadacan breed.

letters.title: To the editor ofAnnals and Magazine of Natural History   22 September [1868]
letters.deprecated: editor of Ann. & Mag. Nat. Hist.
letters.recipient: editor of Ann. & Mag. Nat. Hist.
letters.summary: Sends addition to T. H. Farrer’s [Lobelia] paper [Ann. & Mag. Nat. Hist.4th ser. 2 (1868): 255–63].

letters.title: From John Murray   22 September [1868]
letters.summary: Lost copy ofVariationsent to B. D. Walsh has been traced as far as New York.

letters.title: From James Croll   23 September 1868
letters.summary: Sends two papers; glad CD appreciates two he has already sent. Cannot send two others on glaciers (Philosophical Magazine, 1866 and 1867).

letters.title: From Charles William Nunn   23 September 1868
letters.summary: Sends an ear of wheat that has an oat kernel growing on it.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   23 September [1868]
letters.summary: On their differences concerning sexual selection and protection.

letters.title: From Erasmus Alvey Darwin   [24 September – 10 October 1868]
letters.summary: Has talked with J. J. Sylvester [Professor of Mathematics at the Royal Military Academy, Woolwich] and thinks Leonard [Darwin] should call on him.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   24 September [1868]
letters.summary: Informs THF thatAnnals and Magazine of Natural Historywill publish his paper [see6384].

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   24 September 1868
letters.summary: Wonderful how every flower one looks at is explained by, and throws light on, the fertilising process.

letters.title: To Gaston de Saporta   24 September 1868
letters.deprecated: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
