letters.recipient: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.summary:
Discusses GdeS’s studies on fossil plants;

response toOriginin France.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   25 September 1868
letters.summary:
Sends an ear of wheat with two florets of oats growing out of it. Expects it will all turn out a humbug.

Berkeley’s address inGardeners’ Chronicle[(1868): 920, alsoRep. BAAS38 (1868): 83–7] praises CD tremendously.

letters.title: To C. W. Nunn   25 September [1868]
letters.summary: Thanks CWN for specimen. CD has sent it to Hooker for examination.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [28 September 1868]
letters.summary: The wheat and oat specimen has been examined "in congress" by Oliver, Bentham, Asa Gray, and JDH. No organic connection of any kind.

letters.title: From J. B. Innes   28 September 1868
letters.summary:
The election of 1868.

Remarkable deflection of the plummet observed east of Forres.

letters.title: To G. H. K. Thwaites   28 September [1868]
letters.summary:
Asks him to thank E. L. Layard for trouble taken.

Says Zoological Society "very foolishly" wants no specimens of domestic varieties [from Ceylon].

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   29 September 1868
letters.summary: Informs CD of K. G. Semper’s desire to meet him and to discuss new information on volcanic phenomena, geographical distribution, etc.

letters.title: From Tristram Charles Sawyer Speedy   29 September 1868
letters.summary: Sends some answers to CD’s queries on expression, based on his observations of Abyssinians.

letters.title: From George Bentham   [after 29 September 1868]
letters.summary: Asks CD to sign enclosed certificate first, as he does not know T. H. Farrer personally. [On top part of first two pages of a letter to Hooker from H. C. Rothery about Farrer’s nomination for Linnean Society]

letters.title: From George Rolleston   30 September 1868
letters.summary: CD’s doctrines apply to man’s mental organisation, but the soul is a different matter. Cites Dean Henry Alford, M. J. Berkeley, and Prof. [J. F.?] Ferrier.

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   1 October 1868
letters.summary:
Gives CD a reference to one of his papers ["Remarks on the modes of variation of nearly affined species or races of birds",J. Asiat. Soc. Bengal19 (1850): 221–9]

and discusses moulting in birds.

Quotes instance of an action by an elephant that apparently displays considerable intelligence.

letters.title: To Henry Michael Jenkins   [after 1 October 1868]
letters.summary: Feels there is little he could say as a testimonial for HMJ.

letters.title: From J. D. Caton   2 [October] 1868
letters.summary: Observations on lateral spots on coats of two specimens of deer. PS on habits of wild and domestic turkeys.

letters.title: From George Robert Crotch   2 October [1868]
letters.summary: Bibliographical references on [stridulation in] Coleoptera. Finds no idea of sex has occurred to authors [i.e., they do not find the stridulating organs differing according to sex;cf.Descent1: 378–85].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   3 October 1868
letters.summary: Encloses copy of H. Barkly’s answer to JDH’s inquiry on the Seychelles Island crocodile.

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   4 October 1868
letters.summary: Replies to CD’s questions on sexual differences in birds.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   4 October 1868
letters.summary: Sexual differences in coloration. Sexual selection versus natural selection as explanations. ARW continues to argue against sexual selection, saying that natural selection, in keeping the female dull for protection, would account for differences in sexual colouring more effectively than inheritance and partial transmission of sexually selected male colours. Colours of female birds of paradise. Protective coloration. Disagrees with CD on coincidence of hidden nests and bright colours of females.

letters.title: From Joseph Plimsoll   5 October 1868
letters.summary: A sermon.

letters.title: From G. R. Crotch   [after 5 October 1868]
letters.summary: Note identifying insects and remarking on stridulation.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   6 October [1868]
letters.summary: Sexual selection, protection.

letters.title: To John Tyndall   7 October 1868
letters.summary:
Asks JT to distribute some circulars about the work of Gustavus Hinrichs of Iowa, whom CD wishes to help.

Admires JT’s Norwich address [to Mathematics and Physics Section, BAAS meeting,Rep. BAAS38: 1–6] and hisFortnightly Reviewpaper on scientific discovery [7 (1867): 645–60].

letters.title: To Hermann Müller   9 October 1868
letters.summary: Pleased HM says good words for Pangenesis.

letters.title: From John Tyndall   9 October 1868
letters.summary:
Gustavus Hinrichs is also a [not highly regarded] correspondent of JT’s; he will put GH’s papers on the table at Royal Institution to ease CD’s conscience.

Dined with the Asa Grays at Hooker’s. Told Mrs Gray that CD’s ill health was a benefit because it caused him topondera great deal.

letters.title: From Ludwig Büchner   9 October [1868 or later]
letters.summary: Thanks CD for letter of 3 Oct [missing] about LB’s publication.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   [before 11 October 1868]
letters.summary: C[harles?] P[arker?] says he has made a "fearful mistake", and the marriage cannot be; EAD hopes to come to CD next week.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   [11 October 1868]
letters.summary:
J. J. Sylvester reports George’s fellowship "the most enviable position on earth".

Charles [Parker?] "appears to be ruined".

letters.title: From Asa Gray   11 October [1868]
letters.summary: Wants seeds ofPassiflora gracilis.

letters.title: From Adam Sedgwick   11 October 1868
letters.summary:
Congratulates CD on election of his son [George] as a Fellow of Trinity College.

Describes his ill health.

Invites CD to visit Cambridge.

[Letter dated November in error.]

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   12 October 1868
letters.summary:
Will finish translation ofFür Darwinin a week.

Asks CD to use his influence to get him appointed Assistant Secretary of the Geological Society [London].

letters.title: To Adam Sedgwick   13 October 1868
letters.summary:
Thanks AS for congratulations on George Darwin’s Trinity fellowship.

Reminiscence of his geological tour of North Wales with AS and the encouraging messages received during theBeaglevoyage.

letters.title: From Edward Wilson   14 October 1868
letters.summary: Encloses further replies from Australia to CD’s queries on expression. Wilson’s letter to CD enclosed the letter from Smyth with its enclosures (see S6314).

letters.title: From G. H. K. Thwaites   16 October 1868
letters.summary:
On local black-boned fowls,

CD’s new book [Variation], and Pangenesis.

letters.title: From G. R. Crotch   [after 16 October 1868]
letters.summary: Lists stridulating organs of various Coleoptera.

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   [before 17] October 1868
letters.summary:
Both sexes ofCrossoptilon auritum(eared pheasant) obtained the red cheeks the first year.

Coloration of the linnet.

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   17 October 1868
letters.summary:
Enjoyed JJW’s visit.

Interested in changes in plumage of pheasants.

Still at work on sexual selection in birds.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   19 October 1868
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his promise of support and his flattering opinion of his qualifications for the position of Assistant Secretary of the Geological Society.

letters.title: From Karl von Scherzer   20 October 1868
letters.summary:
Describes departure of expedition to China, Japan, and South America.

Copy of CD’s queries provided to expedition.

Invites CD to make suggestions for scientific work to be carried out.

letters.title: To John Tyndall   20 October 1868
letters.summary: Invites JT to come to Down with the Asa Grays and Hookers.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   21 October [1868]
letters.summary:
Reminds WDF to write about the "great magpie marriage". Sexual selection an "everlasting subject".

News of his children.

Asks for information on instances of sexual preference in animals and data on numbers of males and females born in various domesticated species.

letters.title: To August Weismann   22 October 1868
letters.summary:
Fears copy of AW’s publication [Über die Berechtigung der Darwin’schen Theorie(1868)] lost in mail. Asks for another.

Glad AW approves of his work

and objects to Nägeli’s law of perfection.

Thinks Moritz Wagner overrates necessity for emigration and isolation.

letters.title: From J. P. M. Weale   23 October 1868
letters.summary:
DescribesLappago aleina, a species of South African grass,

and reports his observations on locusts and their feeding habits.

letters.title: To Karl von Scherzer   25 October 1868
letters.summary: Thanks KvS for information about expression.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   26 October 1868
letters.summary: Delighted with mechanisms ofSalviaandViola. How can anyone who compares structure ofViola cornutaand common violet still suppose them to be separate creations?

letters.title: To G. H. K. Thwaites   26 October [1868]
letters.summary: EnclosesQueries about expression.

letters.title: From John Price   28 October 1868
letters.summary:
Congratulates CD on success at Cambridge [of George Darwin].

Would like CD to study the anomalousCardamine pratensis.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   29 October [1868]
letters.summary:
Suggests THF write a paper on violets. Asa Gray, once a sceptic, now declares he is convinced whole structure of a flower is adapted for a cross with another individual.

Urges THF not to give up Pangenesis lightly. "It has thrown light on my mind in regard [to] a great series of complex phenomena."

letters.title: From W. D. Fox   29 October [1868]
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for a recent letter.

Reports on his health, which has been bad for 12 months.

Sends extracts of works on domestication.

Discusses the pairing of various birds; comments on the pugnacity of partridges, pheasants, male guinea-fowl, and peacocks.

Gives proportions of sexes in pheasants.

letters.title: From B. D. Walsh   [before 31 October 1868]
letters.summary: Beginning of extract from William Dell Hartman’s "Journal of the doings ofCic[ada?] septemdecim" [unidentified] in Pennsylvania in 1851.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   31 October 1868
letters.summary: Writes on various observations and discoveries on dimorphic and trimorphic plants.

letters.title: To Sven Nilsson   31 October [1868]
letters.summary:
Thanks SN for the reference about the reindeer, received via Hooker.

CD wishes to ascertain whether there is any relation between the period of development of a character and its transmission to one sex alone.

letters.title: To B. D. Walsh   31 October 1868
letters.summary:
Thanks BDW for extracts about "drumming" [of maleCicadato attract females].

Asa Gray and Hooker doubt that 13–year and 17–yearCicadaforms should be considered distinct species. CD is inclined to agree with them.

Suggests observations be made of ratio of females to males in the rarer form.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   2 November 1868
letters.summary:
The conversion of Asa Gray must be a pleasure.

CD’s doctrine accounts for and gives avera causaof structures.

Discusses F. Hildebrand’s book.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   2 November [1868]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Would like to borrow CD’s carriage on polling day.

letters.title: From M. T. Masters   2 November 1868
letters.summary: After examining a basket of piebald potatoes he does believe them to be a graft-hybrid as Friedrich Hildebrand might suggest.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   4 November 1868
letters.summary:
Much interested in WDF’s letter on inheritance and courtship of birds. CD "in a great muddle" on many points.

Asks for further information on proportion of sexes in sheep.

letters.title: From Friedrich Hildebrand   4 November 1868
letters.summary:
Potato graft-hybrid fails to give potatoes.

August Weismann requests Wallace’s address to find out about experiments on butterflies hinted at inVariation.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   6 November [1868]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Arrangements for polling.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   7 November 1868
letters.summary:
The position at Geological Society is now vacant, and he is working for it in earnest. Asks CD for a testimonial.

Continues his work onFür Darwin.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   7 November 1868
letters.summary:
Thanks for [Natürliche]Schöpfungsgeschichte[1868]. "What an indomitable worker you are."

Agrees with EH’sEntstehung des Menschengeschlechts[1868].

letters.title: From Albert Gaudry9 November 1868
letters.summary: Asks permission to dedicate to CD his book on the fossil animals and geology of Attica [Animaux fossiles et géologie de l’Attique(1862–7)]. CD will find much in it relating to the "filiation" of species, genera, and families.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   9 November 1868
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for comments [onEntstehung des Menschengeschlechts].

Comments on Goethe and Kant as early evolutionists.

Describes birth of his son. Mentions child’s "atavisms".

letters.title: To W. S. Dallas   11 November [1868]
letters.summary: A letter strongly recommending him for the post of Assistant Secretary of the Geological Society.

letters.title: From John Lubbock and E. F. Lubbock   11 November [1868]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron AveburyEllen Frances HordernEllen Frances Lubbock
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron AveburyEllen Frances HordernEllen Frances Lubbock
letters.summary: Further arrangements for polling. Everything looks well. [Ellen Lubbock notes, "he is too sanguine – ".]

letters.title: From G. H. Lewes   12 November 1868
letters.summary:
Disappointed that he missed CD. Hopes still to see him in the flesh.

Has CD seen August Weismann’s inaugural address [see6297]?

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   13 November 1868
letters.summary: CD is welcome to come for breakfast on Sunday.

letters.title: To G. H. Lewes   [13 November 1868]
letters.summary: Arranges to call on GHL.

letters.title: To Friedrich Hildebrand   14 November [1868]
letters.summary:
Suggests FH’s graft-hybrid potatoes should remain with FH.

Sends addresses of Alfred Russel Wallace and Alexander Wallace for August Weismann.

letters.title: To Friedrich Hildebrand   16 November 1868
letters.summary:
Thanks forBotanische Zeitungnotice of CD’s paper ["On the character and hybrid-like nature of the offspring from the illegitimate unions of dimorphic and trimorphic plants",J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)10 (1869): 393–437]. FH writes clearest style of all German authors.

Asks that August Weismann be told about papers by Wallace and Bates.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   17 November 1868
letters.summary: Thanks CD for kind and flattering testimonial.

letters.title: ToGardeners’ Chronicle   17 November 1868
letters.summary: Is interested to know whether there are differences in the period of development of horns in sheep in those breeds in which horns are common to both sexes, and in those in which horns are confined to males.

letters.title: To Albert Gaudry   17 November 1868
letters.summary: Thanks AG forAnimaux fossiles et géologie de l’Attique[1862–7]. Refers to Lyell’s quotation from AG as "one of the most striking I have ever read on the affiliation of Species".

letters.title: From G. H. Lewes   [17 November 1868]
letters.summary:
Asks CD to propose him for Linnean Society.

Would like to have Lyell put his objections to GHL’s papers [Fortn. Rev.9 (1868): 353–73, 611–28; 10 (1868): 61–80, 492–509] in the form of notes, so he can have them before him when he recasts his papers into a book.

letters.title: To G. H. Lewes   18 November 1868
letters.summary:
Will propose GHL for the Linnean Society.

Writes of his objections to GHL’s views.

Considers Weismann’s remarks on the importance of the nature of the organism as well as conditions of life in determining variability have much truth.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   19 November 1868
letters.summary:
Congratulates EH on birth of child.

Mentions projected translation ofGenerelle Morphologie.

Comments on EH’s last book [Natürliche Schöpfungsgeschichte]. Criticises EH’s statements on palaeontology.

letters.title: From Alfred Tylor   19 November 1868
letters.summary: On corals and coral-formation.

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   20 November 1868
letters.summary:
Describes his tour of the Netherlands. Reports on some of the specimens he saw on his trip.

Discusses the coloration of hair in aged monkey

and sexual differences in bird species.

letters.title: From Friedrich Rolle   20 November 1868
letters.summary: Has little information about hens with spurs. Encloses information from Robert Oettel and C. F. Friderich, and from J. F. Blumenbach’sVergleichende Anatomie[1805]. Recommends various German publications.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   21 November 1868
letters.summary: Thinks CD’s views of insect agency and crossing might explain structure and variations of papilionaceous flowers. Lists five points. Asks CD’s opinion.

letters.title: To James Croll   24 November 1868
letters.summary:
Comments on glaciers in North America.

Asks if glacial periods have occurred alternately in the Northern and Southern Hemispheres. Relevant to his glacial discoveries in South America: "it would have been an immense relief to my mind if I could have assumed … this". CD wishes to discuss subject in new edition ofOrigin[5th].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   24 November 1868
letters.summary:
On H. C. Watson’s false and contemptuous criticism of [J. D. Hooker and T. Thomson]Flora Indica[1855].

W. B. Carpenter’s deep-sea dredgings.

James Croll’s last paper ["On geological time",Philos. Mag.35 (1868): 363; 36 (1868): 141, 362].

letters.title: To Friedrich Rolle   24 November 1868
letters.summary:
Thanks for information on fowls.

Glad to see extracts from Blumenbach about sexual differences in fowls.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   25 November [1868]
letters.summary:
Comments on experience of being a father.

Discusses possible English edition ofGenerelle Morphologie. Mentions necessary revisions.

Thanks CD for comment onNatürliche Schöpfungsgeschichte.

Discusses problem of assigning specific times to origin of classes.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   26 November 1868
letters.summary: Advises THF that best plan is to investigate the part certain structures play with all plants or orders, instead of describing means of fertilisation in particular plants. Naturalists value observations far more than reasoning.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   26 November [1868]
letters.summary:
CD thought Watson’s article beastly in its criticisms of JDH. Watson’s criticism of CD was not new or important, but fair, so CD could honestly thank him, adding his regret at what was said about JDH.

Is sitting for Woolner bust.

Has read James Croll on alternation of glacial and warmer periods in north and south, which would remove JDH’s objections to cool period extending to equator.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   26 November 1868
letters.summary: Anxious to hear how the Lubbocks take the disastrous termination to their hopes. [Sir John Lubbock was defeated in the Parliamentary election on 25 Nov 1868.]

letters.title: From John Lubbock   26 November [1868]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: JL’s failure to be elected to Parliament.

letters.title: To John Price   26 November 1868
letters.summary:
Thanks JP for congratulations on success of George Darwin at Cambridge.

Does not have time to investigate propagation ofCardamine.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   27 November 1868
letters.summary:
WSD has been elected Assistant Secretary of the Geological Society after a sharp struggle. CD’s support was greatly in his favour.

Has finishedFür Darwin. It has been a difficult job.

letters.title: From S. O. Glenie   27 November 1868
letters.summary:
He and Mrs G pleased to receive CD’s letter indicating that he found their observations worthy of attention.

Hopes soon to be able to answer CD’s queries on first plumage of chickens of black-boned variety of fowl.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [28 November 1868]
letters.summary:
Is doing a BritishFlora[The student’s flora of the British Islands(1870)], for students, more scientific and more complete than former editions.

His opinion of Bentham’s [British]Flora[1858].

On Croll’s extension of glaciers – a huge relief to get rid of simultaneous cooling of the whole globe.

Watson’s garbling of passage in JDH’sFlora Indicais unprincipled.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   28 November 1868
letters.summary:
Delay in translatingFür Darwin.

Comments on plan to repeat CD’s experiments on illegitimate offspring.

FM’s observations on stridulation.

letters.title: To Natura Artis Magistra   28 November 1868
letters.summary: Asks whether the spurs in the young ofPavo muticusare developed earlier or later in life than in the young males ofPavo cristatus.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   30 November 1868
letters.summary: Thanks CD for advice to watch the action and not only the structure [of plants].

letters.title: To J. B. Innes   1 December 1868
letters.summary: Problems with Mr Robinson, who has suddenly departed for Ireland for a month. The parish urgently needs some respectable man to hold the living permanently.

letters.title: From James Croll   2 December 1868
letters.summary: Sends abstract of his views on change of climate and a copy of a paper.

letters.title: From James Croll   [2 December 1868]
letters.summary: Glacial climates.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   2 December 1868
letters.summary:
Enthusiastic about JDH’s plan for a BritishFlora– "a grand idea to make a Flora a guide for knowledge already acquired & to be acquired". Gives examples of subjects.

No work exists on various biological points in plants.

letters.title: From Frederick Behrens   3 December 1868
letters.summary: Requests autograph.

letters.title: To James Croll   4 December [1868]
letters.summary: Acknowledges receipt of book and manuscript.

letters.title: From J. B. Innes   4 December 1868
letters.summary: Full background on the difficulties of the vicarage of Down.

letters.title: To Frederick Behrens   6 December 1868
letters.summary: Sends his autograph.

letters.title: From J. B. Innes   7 December 1868
letters.summary: Describes a supposed cross between a cow and a red deer or doe.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   8 December 1868
letters.summary: Sends news of his and Frank’s doings at Cambridge.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   8 December 1868
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Thanks for the pamphlets; JL’s paper, "Primitive condition of man" [Nat. Hist. Rev.n.s. 6 (1868): 328].

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   [9 December 1868]
letters.summary: Asks GHD to look in William Thomson’s book [W. Thomson and P. G. Tait,Treatise on natural philosophy, vol. 1 (1867)] to see how many million years ago Thomson says earth’s crust solidified. CD is troubled by "brevity of the world", because pre-Silurian creaturesmusthave lived during endless ages "else my views wd be wrong, which is impossible – Q.E.D.".

letters.title: From W. D. Fox   9 December [1868]
letters.summary:
Hybrid geese.

Proportions of sexes in sheep and cattle.

Pairing habits of crows.

letters.title: To J. B. Innes   10 December [1868]
letters.summary:
Does not think the supposed cow–deer hybrid worth investigating.

John Robinson [the curate at Down] reported to be walking with girls at night.

letters.title: From J. Noordhoek Hegt   11 December 1868
letters.summary: On spurs in peacocks. [SeeDescent1: 290 n.]

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   12 December [1868]
letters.summary:
Thanks WDF for information about sheep and cattle.

Mentions corrections for new edition ofOrigin[5th ed. (1869)].

letters.title: From J. B. Innes   12 December 1868
letters.summary:
Will try to get more information about the supposed hybrid [of cow and deer].

The rumours about John Robinson [curate of Down] cause JBI concern. He will seek to get the facts – will try to protect Robinson against malicious rumours, but if he is immoral he must go forthwith.

letters.title: From John Evans   14 December 1868
letters.summary: Apologises; CD is correct: the object his foreman found is not organic.

letters.title: From J. B. Innes   14 December 1868
letters.summary:
Hopes Miss [Sarah Elizabeth] Wedgwood will sell part of her land for a parsonage at Down. Recounts his futile efforts to obtain land in the past.

Encloses news item about the supposed hybrid [of cow and deer].

letters.title: From John Hellins   16 December 1868
letters.summary: Results of his breeding have not borne out his opinion that females are more numerous in Lepidoptera [seeDescent1: 313]. Still convinced he is right, suggests only way to settle question is by controlled breeding of large numbers of each species.

letters.title: To J. B. Innes   16 December 1868
letters.summary: Has received JBI’s two letters; agrees with him, but does not know what to do about [the alleged misconduct of] John Robinson. Reports in a long postscript on vain efforts to confirm rumours. Suggests JBI come to Down to see how affairs stand.

letters.title: From Thomas Barbot Beale   17 December [1868 or later]
letters.summary: On why it is said Indian elephants do not breed in captivity; mating habits of male so violent as to require restraint.

letters.title: To J. N. Hegt   18 December 1868
letters.summary: Thanks for information about the spurs in the young ofPavo muticusandPavo cristatus.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   18 December 1868
letters.summary:
Sends letter [from Haeckel?] opened by mistake.

August Schleicher a great loss.

letters.title: From J. B. Innes   18 December 1868
letters.summary:
Has forwarded a veterinary surgeon’s description of the supposed hybrid [of cow and deer, see6504]. A neighbour who has seen it is convinced it is genuine.

JBI can do no more about John Robinson.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   20 December 1868
letters.summary: Concerning death of August Schleicher.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   22 December 1868
letters.summary:
The first half of vol. 2 ofVariationis printed.

News of his marriage.

Sends portraits of Russian scientists.

Hopes CD will write his book on man and asks permission to translate it.

Moving to Germany for two or three years.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [23 December 1868]
letters.summary: T. H. Farrer’s paper is capital.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   25 December [1868]
letters.summary:
Is working on new edition ofOrigin[5th (1869)].

Asks JDH’s assistance on a problem posed by Nägeli on morphological differences that are of no utility to plants and hence could not be selected. CD wants to show that these differences do not support the idea of progressive development as Nägeli suggests.

Owen pitches into CD and Lyell in third volume ofAnatomy of vertebrates[1866–8].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   29 December 1868
letters.summary:
JDH’s letter invaluable for an answer to Nägeli’s essay [Entstehung und Begriff der Naturhistorischen Art(1865)].

Has gone through his index toGardeners’ Chroniclebut finds little of use to JDH for hisFlora.

letters.title: To G. H. K. Thwaites   29 December 1868
letters.summary:
Discusses experiments in breeding fowls.

Comments on letter from S. O. Glenie [see6440] concerning the eyes of trumpeting elephants.

letters.title: From William Alexander Wooler   29 December 1868
letters.summary: Observations that confirm CD’s deduction that half-bred Persian cats are fruitful one with another. Relates case of Persian characters reappearing in the offspring of a common cat which was the descendant of a half-bred Persian.

letters.title: From Cassell, Petter & Galpin   31 December 1868
letters.summary: Bill for electrotypes from Brehm’sThierleben[for use inVariation].

letters.title: From Sven Nilsson   31 December 1868
letters.summary: On the development of horns in Lapland reindeer. [SeeDescent1: 288.]

letters.title: From William Erasmus Darwin   [January 1869]
letters.summary: A list of investments presumably belonging to CD.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [1869–75]
letters.summary: Sends a letter from Capt Forrest, recommending a Mr Knight.

letters.title: From Vladimir Onofrievich Kovalevsky   [January–March 1869]
letters.summary:
Has written to Moscow about translations ofOrigin. Wishes to translate additions to the fifth English edition and print them as a supplement.

Pleased by CD’s high opinion of Alexander Kovalevsky.

letters.title: From James Paget   [1869]
letters.summary: "I enclose a note from Lord Fitzwilliam about his horse with zebra-marks. The case seems as striking as I believed."

letters.title: From George Cupples   4 January 1869
letters.summary:
Receiving notes on inbreeding from T. T. Wright, who has long experience with the subject.

Reports six-toed pup.

letters.title: From James Orton   4 January 1869
letters.summary:
Describes the novelties found on his recent expedition to South America sponsored by the Smithsonian Institution.

Wants to dedicate to CD book [The Andes and the Amazon(1870)] which is modelled onJournal of researches.

letters.title: To Julius Victor Carus   5 January 1869
letters.summary:
Asks JVC to ascertain the age at which merino rams develop horns, and whether they grow faster or more slowly than in other breeds of sheep in which both sexes have horns.

Asks how JVC’s translation [ofVariation] has sold.

letters.title: To Sven Nilsson   5 January 1869
letters.summary: Thanks SN for the trouble he has taken for him [on Lapland reindeer horns].

letters.title: To George Cupples   [6–9? January 1869]
letters.summary: Discusses the development of horns in reindeer and other deer.

letters.title: From George Maw   9 January 1869
letters.summary: Planning to visit Gibraltar and Morocco. Is there anything he can do for CD?

letters.title: From George Cupples   11 January 1869
letters.summary: Writing to friends on CD’s behalf about deer: T. T. Wright, Archibald McNeill.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   12 January 1869
letters.summary:
Gives details of some crossing experiments withEschscholzia.

Describes the grassStreptochaeta, which FM believes to be a primitive grass.

Relates some observations on maize that are well explained by Pangenesis.

letters.title: From Lydia Ernestine Becker   13 January 1869
letters.summary:
PraisesVariationand Pangenesis.

Reports observations on parrots and cockatoos.

letters.title: To Joseph Dalton Hooker   13 January 1869
letters.summary: Sends MS of 13 pages in answer to Nägeli, for new edition ofOrigin[5th ed., p. 151].

letters.title: To George Maw   13 January 1869
letters.summary:
Thanks GM for offer of observations. Would be interested to know when the horns of merino rams first appear,

and has long wished for living specimens ofDrosophyllum.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   14 [January] 1869
letters.summary: Oliver overlooked CD’s request about rutaceous flowers. Of precisely which points about the ovules does CD want illustrations?

letters.title: From George Maw   14 January 1869
letters.summary: In Gibraltar he will make notes on merino lambs andDrosophyllumas CD requests.

letters.title: From George Cupples   15 January 1869
letters.summary: Forwards A. McNeill’s letter on deer horns. McNeill wrote portion on deerhounds in William Scrope’s book [The art of deer-stalking(1838)].

letters.title: From Thomas Henry Farrer   15 January 1869
letters.summary:
Red tape leaves no time for botany.

New ministry laudably attempting economies.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   15 January 1869
letters.summary: Criticisms of and suggestions for CD’s draft MS on Nägeli [forOrigin, 5th ed.].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   16 January [1869]
letters.summary: Finds JDH’s comments of utmost value. Answers some questions, and asks new ones. Transmission of variations. Relation of uniformity of structure to natural selection.

letters.title: To George Maw   17 January [1869]
letters.summary: DescribesDrosophyllumand its habitat.

letters.title: From William Winwood Reade   17 January 1869
letters.summary:
Expressions of emotions in Gold Coast tribes.

Differences between males and females in sexual characteristics.

Castrated rams lose horns and manes.

Female members of tribes have no difficulty getting the husbands they want.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   18 January 1869
letters.summary: Replies to CD’s questions. Advice on use of term "morphology". Is much struck by CD’s idea that uniformity of an organ throughout a group implies functional inutility; the paradox of this position for classification.

letters.title: From Alfred Russel Wallace   20 January 1869
letters.summary:
Dedication ofMalay Archipelagoto CD.

Comments on scientific papers.

letters.title: To W. K. Bridgman   21 January [1869]
letters.summary: Discusses fertilisation ofAucubaandPolygala.

letters.title: From George Cupples   21 January 1869
letters.summary: Forwards reply from [Peter Robertson] head forester for Marquis of Breadalbane on development of horns in Scottish deer.

letters.title: From Maxwell Tylden Masters   21 January 1869
letters.summary: Sends CD another piebald potato and a spray of holly, from Mr Fish, discussed inGardeners’ Chronicleof 22 Jan [1869, p. 83].

letters.title: To Mary Somerville   21 January [1869]
letters.summary: Thanks for copy of MS’s book [On molecular and microscopic science, (1869)]. Part on orchids is an excellent summary.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   22 January 1869
letters.summary: On development of horns in merino sheep. Encloses reports from herdsmen he has approached.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [22 January 1869]
letters.summary: No paradox that unimportant characters are important systematically. This view removes heavy burden from CD’s shoulders. Relief that JDH does not object.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   22 January [1869]
letters.summary:
Response to letter about dedication ofMalay Archipelagoand several scientific papers.

Changes in 5th ed. ofOrigin.

Now feels individual differences of paramount importance. Fleeming Jenkin has convinced him about "single variations".

letters.title: From Thomas Campbell Eyton   [before 23 January 1869]
letters.summary: Is trying to determine conditions governing whether or not a salmon will rise for a fly.

letters.title: From W. K. Bridgman   23 January 1869
letters.summary:
Is assembling apparatus of lenses and reflector to observe flower from opening to first shedding of pollen, and to determine whether fertilisation is by night- or day-feeders.

Will also examine reasons for absence of nectar inPolygala linaria.

letters.title: To James Orton   23 January [1869]
letters.summary:
Thanks JO for intending to dedicate hisThe Andes and the Amazonto him.

The discovery of marine shells high up the Amazons CD finds extremely interesting.

letters.title: From C. F. Claus   24 January 1869
letters.summary:
Sends a paper on reproductive modes ofLeptodera["Organisation und Fortpflanzen vonLeptodera",Schr. Ges. Beförd. Naturw. Marburg(1869)].

Criticises Ernst Haeckel’s work as too unripe and enthusiastic.

Asks CD for some specimens of cirripedes in pupal stage for a work in progress.

letters.title: To T. C. Eyton   24 January 1869
letters.summary:
Has heard that book by Alphonse M[ilne]-Edwards [?Recherches anatomiques et paléontologiques, 4 vols. (1867–71)] is excellent.

Asks when horns appear on young male fallow deer.

letters.title: From Archibald McNeill   24 January 1869
letters.summary: Answer to CD’s query as to whether horns on deer are for use or ornament. [SeeDescent2: 252–3.]

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [25 January 1869]
letters.summary:
Does not fact that characters important in systematics are often of no use, corroborate CD’s view that such characters, if not detrimental, may persistad infinitum?

Social news.

letters.title: From T. C. Eyton   26 January [1869]
letters.summary: On development of horns in fawns of fallow deer.

letters.title: From William Chester Tait   26 January 1869
letters.summary: Believes Portuguese habit of removing tails of pointers is responsible for birth of some tailless dogs.

letters.title: To John Phillips   27 January 1869
letters.summary: Thanks JP for his bookVesuvius[1869].

letters.title: To C. F. Claus   28 January 1869
letters.summary:
Thanks CC for two memoirs [see6575. The other was possibly "Die Cypris-ähnliche Larve der Cirripedien",Schr. Ges. Beförd Naturw. Marburg(1869)].

Haeckel is too enthusiastic and too bold in drawing conclusions.

CD sees no reason to add to what he says on isolation, in new edition ofOrigin.

Lists specimens he has available for CC’s intended study of metamorphoses ofLepas.

letters.title: From David Forbes   30 January 1869
letters.summary: DF’s opinion of Gustav Jenzsch’s book [Mikroskopische Flora und Fauna(1868)]. Encloses extract of a letter from Ferdinand Zirkel also mentioning Jenzsch’s work.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   30 January 1869
letters.summary: Argues that [general variability] of species, not single variations or sports, is basis for modification and adaptation to new conditions.

letters.title: To James Croll   31 January [1869]
letters.summary:
Returns book with thanks. "Joyfully accepts" idea of the warming of Southern Hemisphere during glacial period in the Northern. Lyell is unwilling.

Mentions H. N. Moseley’s study of descent of glaciers [Proc. R. Soc. Lond.17 (1869): 202–8].

CD greatly troubled by problem of age of the earth and calculations of Sir William Thomson. Asks about changes in the form of the globe.

letters.title: From Charles Phipps Haussoullier   31 January 1869
letters.summary: Requests authorisation to translateJournal of researchesinto French.

letters.title: To Richard Kippist   31 January [1869?]
letters.summary: "You are most perfectly welcome to Fragmenta [F. J. H. von MuellerFragmenta phytographiae Australiae(1858–64)], & I shall be delighted if they are of the slightest use to you."

letters.title: To John Murray   [1–3 February 1869]
letters.summary: Asks JM to grant permission for a French translation of his "Naturalist’s voyage" [Journal of researches].

letters.title: From Charles Spence Bate   1 February 1869
letters.summary: A case of fighting in crabs (Portunus puberagainstCarcinus maenas) [seeDescent1: 332].

letters.title: From S. A. Merrell   1 February 1869
letters.summary: Corrects T. M. Brewer’s statement, cited in theOrigin, that the American cuckoo never uses other birds’ nests. [SeeOrigin, 5th ed., p. 266.]

letters.title: To John Warburton Robinson   1 February 1869
letters.summary: Statement of sum due from Rev. Robinson "On account of School".

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   2 February 1869
letters.summary: Sends translation of Mr Steiger’s letter responding to question CD had asked about growth of horns of merino rams.

letters.title: From Andrew Crombie Ramsay   2 February 1869
letters.summary: Lyell says CD is revising what he says about the Weald in theOrigin. Asks CD to look at his subaerial denudation views in his book [Physical geology and geography of Great Britain, 2d ed. (1864)].

letters.title: To W. C. Tait   2 February [1869]
letters.summary:
Discusses case of tailless dogs.

Does not intend to follow up work on variation under domestication.

Asks for specimen ofDrosophyllumfrom Portugal.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   2 February [1869]
letters.summary: CD expressed himself badly. F. Jenkin’s argument was against single variations ever being perpetuated.

letters.title: From John Murray   3 February [1869]
letters.summary:
Gives consent, which is unnecessary because term of protection has expired, for French translation ofJournal of researches.

Is at a loss to know how many copies of F. Müller’sFacts and arguments for Darwinto print.

The printer is ready for copy for a new "edition" ofVariation. [Presumably another issue. 2d edition did not appear until 1875.]

letters.title: To A. C. Ramsay   3 February [1869]
letters.summary: Received and read ACR’sPhysical geology. Places him at head of the subaeria denudationists. Unfortunately CD confounded William Whitaker’s article with ACR’s views and gave Whitaker credit for first producing the evidence. Will rectify it now. Has eliminated the rubbish he wrote on the Weald and will add a paragraph on importance of subaerial denudation.

letters.title: From James Croll   4 February 1869
letters.summary:
Argues for great age of earth before the Cambrian period. Opposes measuring age from secular cooling. Opposes Sir William Thomson. Lyell’s error on secular cooling.

Thanks for Moseley citation ["On the mechanical possibility of the descent of glaciers",Proc. R. Soc. Lond.17 (1869): 202–8].

In Edinburgh he feels out of touch with latest developments.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   5 February 1869
letters.summary:
Thanks JVC for his information (from two correspondents) on the rate of growth of merino rams’ horns.

CD has been revisingOrigin[5th ed.]. Has found a good deal to alter.

letters.title: From Frederik Anthony von Hartsen   5 February 1869
letters.summary:
Believes that species or genus may have originated more than once from separate ancestors, i.e., polyphyletically.

Discusses relation of CD’s theory to religion. Has written popular account of CD’s theory in Dutch [Darwin en de Godsdienst(1869)].

letters.title: To William Bernhard Tegetmeier   5 February [1869]
letters.summary: Repeats request for information on colours of plumage of poultry breeds and asks for WBT’s facts on proportions of sexes.

letters.title: From C. F. Claus   6 February 1869
letters.summary:
Pleased by CD’s good opinion and offer to provide material. Discusses work he would do on cirripedes.

Moritz Wagner’s views on migration of species;

his doubts about Fritz Müller’s views on developmental stages of Crustacea.

letters.title: To James Croll   6 February [1869]
letters.summary:
Consoling to CD that JC gives "a little more age to the world".

Cites article by Henry Moseley ["On the mechanical possibility of the descent of glaciers",Proc. R. Soc. Lond.17 (1869): 202–8].

Mentions article by A. R. Clarke on shape of the globe.

letters.title: To George Howard Darwin   6 February [1869]
letters.summary: John Lubbock regrets GHD did not take the Eton post. JL thinks scientific masters will soon occupy places as high and as profitable as classical masters.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   6 February 1869
letters.summary:
Has inquired about magnetic storms. Any effect that could be produced by the sun’s energy in retarding the cooling of the earth would be utterly insignificant.

Tells of his visit to Eton.

Is uncertain about next steps to take for a legal career.

letters.title: To David Forbes   7 February [1869]
letters.summary: Asks for DF’s observations on the Aymara Indians for use in writing manuscript [seeDescent, 2d ed., pp. 34–5].

letters.title: From John Lubbock   8 February 1869
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Down School funds.

letters.title: From Georg Recht   9 February 1869
letters.summary: Sends MS. Asks CD to recommend it to a scientific society.

letters.title: From Ferdinand Maria Malven   12 February [1869]
letters.summary: Librarian to the Board of Trade proposes a celebration of CD’s 60th birthday by the ViennaFree Press.

letters.title: From Edward Wilson   12 February 1869
letters.summary: Returns a book on beavers borrowed from CD.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   [before 13 February 1869]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Asks whether JL would be prepared to sign a petition on behalf of Miss Eliza Meteyard who is seeking a civil list pension.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   13 February [1869]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Down School funds.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   14 February 1869
letters.summary:
Explains the point about gravitation and heat that CD does not understand in J. Croll’s letter [6218?].

Cambridge news.

letters.title: From James Croll   15 February 1869
letters.summary: Thanks for abstract of Moseley’s paper on motion of glaciers [see6599]. Reading it convinced him that Tyndall’s received view is wrong. Has formed a new view, which he has sent toPhilosophical Magazine[4th ser. 37 (1869): 201–6].

letters.title: From Jean Jacques Moulinié   15 February 1869
letters.summary: Sends abstract of an article by Carrière [J. Agric. Pratique1 (1869): 159–67] on the improvement of wild radish by selection.

letters.title: From Philip de Malpas Grey-Egerton   18 February 1869
letters.deprecated: Philip de Malpas Grey- Egerton, 10th baronet Egerton
letters.sender: Philip de Malpas Grey- Egerton, 10th baronet Egerton
letters.summary: Habits of the fallow deer during the breeding season. [SeeDescent, 2d ed., p. 803.]

letters.title: From Ernest Faivre   18 February 1869
letters.summary: One of his students is interested in translatingOrchidsinto French.

letters.title: To Eliza Meteyard   [18 February 1869]
letters.summary: CD signed the petition, had Sir Charles Lyell do so also, and then forwarded the memorial to Sir John Lubbock.

letters.title: From Hugo Thiel   18 February 1869
letters.summary:
Sends CD his pamphlet [Über Landwirtschaftlichen Genossenschaften(1868)];

expresses his admiration for CD’s work.

letters.title: From Eliza Meteyard   19 February 1869
letters.summary: Her memorial [for civil list pension] with the signatures of CD, John Lubbock, and Charles Lyell has arrived. It is now going to W. E. Gladstone.

letters.title: From W. C. Tait   19 February 1869
letters.summary:
Has been trying to getDrosophyllum lusitanicumfor CD.

Intends to breed from two pointers born tailless.

letters.title: From Archibald McNeill   20 February 1869
letters.summary: Answers CD’s letter of 15 Feb about voice of female and odour of stag red deer.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   22 February 1869
letters.summary:
There will be no objection to the French translation or difficulty about woodcuts ofOrchids.

Has not yet received the information about Müller’sFacts and arguments for Darwin.

letters.title: To Robert Francis Cooke   [22 February 1869]
letters.summary: Assumes Murray will give permission for French translation ofOrchids; asks that stereotypes of woodcuts be supplied at cost, since if expensive the work will not appear.

letters.title: From George Henslow   22 February 1869
letters.summary:
Asks CD for references to animal breeders in order to test the hypothesis that mimicry arises through direct action of mental impressions received through the sense of sight.

Supports natural selection and Pangenesis.

letters.title: To J. J. Moulinié   22 February [1869]
letters.summary: Thanks JJM for translating long paper [by Carrière,J. Agric. Pratique48 (1869): 159–67]. Paper interesting especially for showing variation has been different under different conditions.

letters.title: From George Henslow   [after 22 February 1869]
letters.summary: Sends information from a Kent sheep-breeder.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   23 [February 1869]
letters.summary: Agrees to printing 1000 copies of Fritz Müller’sFacts and arguments for Darwinthough he fears it is foolish. Lists seven publications for review copies.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   23 February 1869
letters.summary: Estimates cost of F. Müller’sFacts and arguments for Darwinat £86 for 750 copies, less than £10 extra for 1000.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [23 February 1869]
letters.summary:
Encloses a letter [from J. Croll?].

Has been unable to find a paper CD wanted.

Is leaving shortly for Paris.

letters.title: To James Croll   24 February [1869]
letters.summary: Thanks JC for his proofs of article on the movement of glaciers.

letters.title: To W. C. Tait   24 February 1869
letters.summary:
Discusses method for shippingDrosophyllumspecimens.

Asks about inheritance in tailless dogs;

the growth of horns in merino sheep.

letters.title: From Philip Gidley King   25 February 1869
letters.summary: CD’s queries on expression of aborigines were difficult to answer because he encounters mainly those touched by civilisation. Hopes CD did get answers.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   25 February [1869]
letters.summary: Inquires about colour and development of plumage of poultry breeds. Is endeavouring to trace sexual differences throughout the animal kingdom.

letters.title: To Hugo Thiel   25 February 1869
letters.summary: Thanks for publication applying CD’s theory to moral and social questions.

letters.title: From C. S. Bate   1 March 1869
letters.summary:
On hybridism between the fox and dog; asks whether CD knows of a reliable case of offspring from this cross.

Does CD want details on a white cat with blue eyes, but not deaf?

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   1 March 1869
letters.summary: Sexual differences in antelopes (Indian and African).

letters.title: From Georg Recht   1 March 1869
letters.summary: Thanks for money, which will enable him to complete publication. Explains principles of his physiological theory.

letters.title: From W. C. Tait   2 March 1869
letters.summary:
Sends a single specimen ofDrosophyllum lusitanicumwith description from F. de Avellar Brotero’sFlora Lusitanica[1804].

Discusses Portuguese ferns,

inherited mutilation,

and the earth’s geological history.

Evolution of behaviour and beauty by natural selection.

letters.title: To Thomas Roscoe Rede Stebbing   3 March 1869
letters.summary: Thanks TRRS for copy of his lecture [Darwinism(1869)]. Praises his "admirable example of liberality".

letters.title: From T. C. Eyton   4 March 1869
letters.summary: Further observations on horns of fallow deer. Sends fawn’s head.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   5 March [1869]
letters.summary: Discusses wear and tear due to glaciation and significance of this evidence for dating the glacial period. Mentions views of James Croll and Archibald Geikie on the issue.

letters.title: From T. R. R. Stebbing   5 March 1869
letters.summary: Explains how he, as "an orthodox clergyman" reading CD’s works, was totally convinced by his arguments. Expresses pleasure "that Science might make gigantic strides without offering such collateral opinions as, if true, would certainly dispense with clergymen altogether".

letters.title: From W. C. Tait   5 March 1869
letters.summary:
Is forwarding potted specimens ofDrosophyllum.

Will make inquiries about sheep.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   5 March [1869]
letters.summary: Reception of ARW’s book,Malay Archipelago.

letters.title: To T. C. Eyton   6 March [1869]
letters.summary: Thanks TCE for fawn’s head.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   8 March [1869]
letters.summary:
Transmits letter [from Fritz Müller].

Has been asked to permit a French translation ofOrchidsandJournal of researches.

At work on sexual selection.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   9 March [1869]
letters.summary: Suggests best form of lettering for spine of Müller’sFacts and arguments for Darwin.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   10 March 1869
letters.summary: Sends statement [missing] of cost and proceeds of publishingFacts and arguments for Darwinat 6s. Asks whether CD agrees to this price.

letters.title: To Thomas Henry Huxley   10 March 1869
letters.summary: At writer’s request, forwards long letter on Comte by Vernon Lushington.

letters.title: From Henry Landor   10 March 1869
letters.summary: Suggests that ground ice, in Canada and similar countries, is a mode of distribution of boulders and animal and vegetable life.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   10 March 1869
letters.summary: Weir’s paper on relation of protection to colour of caterpillars [Trans. R. Entomol. Soc. Lond.(1869): 21–6; (1870): 337–9] confirms ARW’s hypothesis.

letters.title: From George Cupples   11 March 1869
letters.summary: Differences in size and weight in deerhounds, with tables of comparative weights according to sex. Promises information on weights of deerhound puppies. Effects of cross- and inbreeding.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   11 March 1869
letters.summary:
Orchidstranslation should goad [French] Academy into electing CD.

JDH will be sent to St Petersburg congress by Government.

Huxley on protoplasm; his address to Geological Society.

Fertilised anAucubawith pollen of various species. Reports on results.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   11 March 1869
letters.summary: Nothing new in Lushington’s letter. Two paragraphs are offensive – that THH sought to stir up Scotch Presbyterian prejudices against Comte at Edinburgh and that he had not read Comte.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   12 March 1869
letters.summary: Book [Facts and arguments for Darwin] is being bound; it is probably too late to alter lettering.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   12 March [1869]
letters.summary: Apologises for passing on what he agrees were offensive remarks in V. Lushington’s letter. Has told VL he had no right to make them. Asks THH to make allowance for red-hot disciples defending the master.

letters.title: To Vernon Lushington   [12 March 1869]
letters.summary: Huxley has acknowledged receipt of VL’s letter. Both he and CD feel that some of VL’s statements were a little offensive although CD is sure this was not intended. Was glad to read the condensed statement of Comte’s claims in VL’s letter.

letters.title: To W. C. Tait   12 and 16 March 1869
letters.summary:
Thanks for specimen ofDrosophyllum.

Describes capacity of various plants to catch flies.

Cannot name fern specimen.

Laugher pigeon descended fromColumba livia.

Discusses tailless dogs.

Believes astronomical phenomenon responsible for oscillation of level of earth’s crust.

Would WCT like copy ofOrchids?

Expected plants [Drosophyllum] have arrived.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   14 March 1869
letters.summary:
Translation ofFür Darwinhas been published [Facts and arguments for Darwin(1869)].

Discusses dimorphic plants, commenting on FM’s observations onOxalis.

Is greatly interested inEschscholzia, which seems somewhat more self-sterile in Brazil than in England.

Thinks FM’s grass is "most wonderful".

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   14 March 1869
letters.summary:
Describes experiments with sterility inAbutilon.

Describes hermaphroditism in a wildBegoniain Brazil.

Has been observing humble bees onSalvia.

letters.title: From Ernest Faivre   15 March 1869
letters.summary: EF is seeking a French editor forOrchids[1870]. Introduces L. Rérolle, his student. [See6667.]

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   17 March [1869]
letters.summary:
Envies JDH’s Russian trip.

Thanks for information onAucuba. Urges him to experiment – case "has highest physiological importance, not to mention Pangenesis".

Has heard that Huxley has been attacking views of Sir W. Thomson.

Has received 12 plants ofDrosophyllum lusitanicumfrom Oporto.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   17 March 1869
letters.summary: Last letter was written to be passed on for Lushington’s edification. "(Standing on the points of my toes and my tail very stiff)." Is tiring of controversy as a waste of time. Begins to understand CD’s sufferings overOrigin.

letters.title: From Louis Rérolle   17 March 1869
letters.summary: LR undertakes translation ofOrchids[1870]. Awaits CD’s new footnotes and intends to look at every flower CD mentions.

letters.title: To George Cupples   18 March [1869]
letters.summary: Suggests that Cupples weigh puppies from one week old, rather than two weeks old.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   18 March 1869
letters.summary: On English edition ofFür Darwin; CD’s gratitude and admiration.

letters.title: From C. F. Claus   19 March 1869
letters.summary: The cirripede material mentioned in CD’s letter of 10 Feb has not arrived. [Asks CD to inquire of Williams and Norgate, who forwarded it.]

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   19 March [1869]
letters.summary: Thanks for THH’s address [to Geological Society,Q. J. Geol. Soc. Lond.25 (1869): 28–53]. Admires it and enjoyed attack on William Thomson hugely, but would tremble if he were in THH’s boots. Distinction made by THH between evolutionists and uniformitarians is too great. CD’s sentences on age of world inOriginwill do, but he might have been less timid had he read THH.

letters.title: To John Dean Caton   20 March 1869
letters.summary:
Asks about coat colour of elk,

the mane of American bison,

and about sexual preferences of female deer.

letters.title: To Julius Dub   20 March 1869
letters.summary: CD will supply the sheets of the new edition of theOrigin[5th ed. (1869)] if JD goes ahead with his work [?Kurze Darstellung der Lehre Darwin’s über die Entstehung der Arten der Organismen(1870)]. Has no objection to JD’s quoting him, but wonders whether the German publisher ofOriginmight not feel injured.

letters.title: From Samuel Owen Glenie   20 March 1869
letters.summary:
His observations of the chickens hatched from eggs of an isolated pair of pure-bred black-boned fowl. Nine were black-boned, two were like ordinary fowl.

Quotes a Mr Holdsworth on unusual expressions of Singhalese and Tamils in pointing and beckoning.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   20 March [1869]
letters.summary:
Discusses views of Wallace, H. N. Moseley, and Croll on the mechanics of glacier movement.

Comments on Wallace’s new book [The Malay Archipelago(1869)].

letters.title: To William Thierry Preyer   [before 21 March 1869]
letters.summary: Replies to inquiries about his life and career.

letters.title: From W. T. Preyer   21 March 1869
letters.summary:
Has given a lecture series on Darwinism which was attended by 200–500 students.

Would like to compile a list of CD’s works.

letters.title: From George Cupples   22 March 1869
letters.summary:
Will look for sex ratio statistics.

Will weigh pups.

Deerhound breeding;

wolves.

letters.title: From Karl von Seidlitz   22 March 1869
letters.summary:
Mentions his publication [Die Bildungsgesetze der Vogeleier(1869)].

Comments on importance of heredity for evolution.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   22 March [1869]
letters.summary: Comments on Wallace’sMalay Archipelago.

letters.title: From Harrison William Weir   23 March 1869
letters.summary:
Proportion of sexes in pigeons, pigs, and pheasants.

Sexual preferences of females.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   24 March 1869
letters.summary:
Comments on Fritz Müller’s book [Facts and arguments for Darwin].

Responds to CD’s corrections of his work [Malay Archipelago].

Plumage of birds of paradise.

letters.title: From Martin Wilckens   25 March 1869
letters.summary: Sends two of his publications ["Bericht über die wissenschaftlichen Fortschritte der Thierzucht",Jahrb. Landwirtsch.(1869) and "Die Aufgaben der landwirtschaftlicher Biotechnik",Landwirtsch. Wochenbl.(1869)].

letters.title: To Martin Wilckens   [after 25 March 1869]
letters.summary: Thanks MW for two publications [see6682].

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   27 March [1869]
letters.summary:
Hopes ARW has not "murdered too completely your own and my child" [natural selection] in hisQuarterly Reviewarticle ["Sir Charles Lyell on geological climates and theOrigin", 126 (1869): 359–94] on Lyell’sPrinciples[10th ed.].

CD is attributing more significance to useless variability in new [5th] edition ofOrigin.

letters.title: To W. T. Preyer   29 March 1869
letters.summary:
Congratulates WP on the success of his lectures.

Discusses the phrase "struggle for existence".

Sends a list of his papers.

letters.title: From Armand de Quatrefages   29 March 1869
letters.deprecated: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.sender: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.summary: Comments on their differences regarding evolution. Acknowledges that CD alone has produced an evolutionary theory that is scientific and all-embracing. Appreciates grandeur of CD’s work.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker 30 March [1869]
letters.summary:
Interested in Barkly’s letter about Mauritius. Doubts non-volcanic origin. Urges collection of all forms of terrestrial life to determine whether they are of a former continent or "waifs and strays". He leans to latter view, as snakes and reptiles are different.

Huxley’s address wonderfully "brilliant", but it is a mistake to separate evolutionists from uniformitarians.

Bentham has come out "splendidly" on descent of species.

letters.title: To C. F. Claus   31 March 1869
letters.summary: Williams and Norgate inform CD that they dispatched the small parcel to Leipzig on 23 February. CD fears it may not be worth the trouble to CC.

letters.title: From Richard Spruce   [before 1 April 1869]
letters.summary:
Sends CD a paper ["Ant-agency in plant structure", published in SpruceNotes of a botanist on the Amazon and Andes, ed. A. R. Wallace (1908)] on plant structures he believes are the work of insects; asks him to forward it to the Linnean Society [read 15 Apr 1869].

Writes of his support for theOrigin, before which he had been much concerned by the delimitation of so-called species.

letters.title: To Richard Spruce   1 April 1869
letters.summary: RS’s facts are remarkable. A year or two ago CD would not have believed ants could produce an inherited effect, but he has "lately come to believe rather more in inherited mutations". However, CD is not satisfied that the sacs are inherited and urges RS to produce any other evidence he might have.

letters.title: To Benjamin Dann Walsh   3 April [1869]
letters.summary:
Glad BDW has proved his case on dimorphism ofCynips.

Interested in galls

and BDW’sCicadaarticles [Proc. Entomol. Soc. Philadelphia(1864)].

letters.title: From George M’Ilvaine Ramsey   5 April 1869
letters.summary: Describes the work he is writing,Cosmology(Ramsay 1870).

letters.title: To ?   6 April [1869–71]
letters.summary:
"My experiment was intended solely to show that colour reappeared, and I choose kinds which breed [true] to colour, as is certainly the case with [sports] and those which I tried . . .

I have recorded an undoubted case of wild rock Pigeons caught in Scotland having bred in confinement …"

letters.title: To W. C. Tait   7 April [1869]
letters.summary: Drosophyllumplants recovering [from trip]. Describes experiments on them.

letters.title: From Alfred Newton   9 April 1869
letters.summary:
Regrets Frank [Darwin] did not pass the Trinity scholarship examination, but he hears Frank did well on theviva vocepart.

Pleased CD is willing to help the University’s Museum of Zoology; he encloses the printed appeal.

letters.title: From W. C. Tait   13 April 1869
letters.summary:
Insectivorous plants;Drosophyllum lusitanicum.

Descriptions of the local sheep.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   14 April 1869
letters.summary:
ARW’s review of 10th ed. of Lyell’sPrinciples[see6684] is admirable.

But he differs "grievously" with ARW on man. CD sees no necessity for an additional and proximate cause.

letters.title: From Richard Spruce   15 April 1869
letters.summary:
Describes the floral structure and fertilisation of some melastomes;

discusses the direct agency of insects in modifying the structure of flowers.

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   17 April 1869
letters.summary:
Will attempt to provide CD with the information requested as soon as he can.

Gives references to some recent papers and articles which might interest CD.

Is currently reviewing Wallace’s new book [Malay Archipelago].

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   17 April 1869
letters.summary:
Wants information on plumage of chickens

and table of sex ratios in greyhounds.

letters.title: From W. B. Tegetmeier   [before 18 April 1869]
letters.summary: Numerical proportion of males to females in greyhound puppies.

letters.title: From George Maw   18 April 1869
letters.summary: He has found abundantDrosophyllumin Andalusia.

letters.title: To W. C. Tait   18 April [1869]
letters.summary:
Not well owing to fall from horse.

[Drosophyllum] plants going on very well.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   18 April [1869]
letters.summary: Thanks for greyhound table; interested in transmission of colour in greyhounds and relationship to sex.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   18 April [1869]
letters.summary: Expands upon their differences in regard to man and the question of the existence of forces not yet recognised by science.

letters.title: To George Charles Wallich   18 April [1869]
letters.summary: Regrets he cannot come to London to be photographed [for GCW’sEminent men of the day(1870)]. Invites GCW to Down.

letters.title: To J. Noordhoek Hegt   19 April 1869
letters.summary:
Enquires about spurs in the last year’s birds ofPavo Spiciferandcristatus.

Enquires about sexual differences in mandrills.

Asks the correct spelling of JNH’s surname and offers to send a copy ofJournal of Researches.

letters.title: From Orange Judd & Co   21 April 1869
letters.summary: Reports on the sales ofVariation; discusses the difficulties of inserting additions and corrections.

letters.title: From Georg Recht   21 April 1869
letters.summary:
GR regarded as a dreamer in Bavaria. Laments local social and political conditions.

Describes his ideas of mechanics in nature.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   [after 21 April 1869]
letters.summary: Discusses CD’s health and James Paget’s "verdict".

letters.title: From Alfred William Bennett   22 April 1869
letters.summary:
Sends paper on mechanisms of cross-fertilisation in flowers ["Note onParnassia palustris",J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)11 (1871): 24–31].

Studying how fertilisation takes place without the aid of insects in winter varieties.

letters.title: From J. N. Hegt   [23 April 1869]
letters.summary: The peacocks mentioned in his last letter as yet show no differences in development of spurs. [SeeDescent1: 290 n.]

letters.title: To P. G. King   24 April 1869
letters.summary:
Thanks PGK for his aid in reporting the curious case of the parrot.

Will consult John Gould about rosella [Australian parakeet].

Recalls with pleasure their friendship on board theBeagle.

letters.title: From John Price   24 April 1869
letters.summary:
Has experimented with some success in growing twigs with buds

and a grass plant from which a ptarmigan had extracted the core.

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   26 April 1869
letters.summary: Has found no difference between male and female rhesus monkeys at the Zoological Gardens in amount of facial hairiness. Observations on other monkeys.

letters.title: To J. N. Hegt   27 April [1869]
letters.summary: Arranges to send a copy ofJournal of researches.

letters.title: To George Maw   27 April [1869]
letters.summary: Thanks GM for specimens ofDrosophyllum; by a strange coincidence CD has also received plants from a correspondent in Oporto [W. C. Tait].

letters.title: From John Murray   28 April [1869]
letters.summary:
Has sold 400 copies ofFacts and arguments for Darwin. It is a poor time for bookselling.

LastQuarterly Reviewhas best exposition of Darwinism he has met with [A. R. Wallace, "Geological climates, and origin of species",Q. Rev.126 (1869): 359–94].

Proposes to print 2000 copies of a new [5th] edition ofOrigin.

letters.title: From Spiridion Brusina   29 April 1869
letters.summary:
SB is founding a natural history society to study the flora and fauna of the southern Slavic countries.

Plans to print portraits of the four most distinguished naturalists and asks for a photograph of CD.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   29 April 1869
letters.summary:
A new edition [4th German] ofOriginto be published by Schweizerbart. JVC asks CD to send any changes or additions.

Variationhas sold two-thirds of the first printing [1868].

Hopes he may do translation of CD’s new work [Descent].

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   29 April 1869
letters.summary: Confirms a request by CD that Murray’s supply electrotypes ofOrchidsat most reasonable possible price.

letters.title: To John Murray   29 April [1869]
letters.summary:
Thanks JM forQuarterly Review. A. R. Wallace’s article inimitably good – and a triumph that it appears where it will make B[ishop] of O[xford] and Owen gnash their teeth.

Delighted at the sale of F. Müller’s book.

Thinks he has broughtOriginup to "present standard of science" [5th ed. (June 1869)].

Slow progress onDescent.

His horse rolled over him, but he is recovering rapidly.

letters.title: To James Paget   29 April [1869]
letters.summary:
Has made a wonderful recovery [from riding accident].

Asks for information on blushing and screaming [forExpression].

letters.title: To Max Schmidt   [29 April 1869]
letters.summary: Asks MS whether he will examine adult mandrills and describe the sexual differences in colouring.

letters.title: From Lawrence Ruck   [after 29 April 1869?]
letters.summary: On the horns of castrated lambs.

letters.title: From M. T. Masters   30 April 1869
letters.summary:
Sends paper on the "Origin of genera".

J. Decaisne, in last week’sGardeners’ Chronicle, on the apple, cannot mean there are no intermediates betweenMalusandPyrus.

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   [1–13] May 1869
letters.summary: South Down sheep: variability in colouring and patterning of lambs compared with constancy of adult coat.

letters.title: From A. W. Bennett   3 May 1869
letters.summary: Sends CD some notes [missing] on the mode of fertilisation of winter-flowering plants, and outlines his conclusions regarding the different types of winter-flowerers and the means by which they are fertilised.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   4 May 1869
letters.summary: Discusses changes in 5th edition ofOriginowing to new evidence. CD now places more value on action of external conditions; thinks lapse of time [required for development of species] not so great as some geologists have thought, and single variations [saltations] of even less importance compared with individual differences.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   4 May [1869]
letters.summary:
Asks for a photograph of CL to be used by a society [in Serbia].

Comments on article by Wallace ["Sir Charles Lyell on geological climates and theOrigin",Q. Rev.126 (1869): 359–94].

Has finished new edition ofOrigin[5th (1869)]

and is back at work on sexual selection [Descent].

letters.title: From J. D. Caton   5 May 1869
letters.summary: Females have no preference for particular males in deer and elk. Observations on sexual behaviour and characteristics of elk, deer, bison, and other animals.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   5 May 1869
letters.summary: Justifies his use of term "degraded" by comparing contrivances for cross-fertilisation in different species ofViola.

letters.title: From Charles Lyell   5 May 1869
letters.summary:
Recalls Cuvier’s reaction toPrinciples of geology.

Comments on Wallace’s article in theQuarterly Review[see6684].

Not opposed to ARW’s idea that Supreme Will might direct variation.

Quotes passage in letter from ARW arguing for causes other than selection in determining human abilities.

Discusses excavation of lakes by glaciers.

J. P. Lesley does not believe ice-sheets involved in eroding Appalachians.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   6 May [1869]
letters.summary: Dislikes the use of the term "degradation" as applied to the closed flowers ofViolaspecies. Species with such self-fertilising flowers also have flowers adapted for crossing. The development of closed flowers adapted to ensure a sufficient stock of seed is progressive.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [before 8 May 1869]
letters.summary: Reports what he must pay for university courses. Forgets what CD wants to know about vermiform appendage.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [before 7 May 1869]
letters.summary: Asks whether in Slavonic races the hair of the beard and head are different colours.

letters.title: From George Bentham   7 May 1869
letters.summary: The Linnean Society Council wants CD to review two papers, with reference to their value for publication.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   7 May 1869
letters.summary: H. M. S.Nassau, surveying Magellan Straits, has found fossils at Gallegos River. They have been sent to THH by R. O. Cunningham [naturalist of H. M. S.Nassau]. Skull of entirely new ungulate mammal.

letters.title: From Harrison William Weir   7 May 1869
letters.summary:
Daisies.

A tame rabbit with a litter of 18.

letters.title: To Spiridion Brusina   8 May [1869]
letters.summary: Sends photograph of Sir C. Lyell and Professor Owen, generally considered our most distinguished [British] naturalists. Includes the requested photograph of himself [see6720].

letters.title: From Asa Gray and Jane Loring Gray   8 and 9 May 1869
letters.summary:
Sorry to hear of CD’s accident.

Recounts his travels.

Jane Gray writes a description of the Arabs.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   8 May [1869]
letters.summary: Thanks for [D. D. Cunningham’s] letter. Had hoped for a better haul but delighted to hear of the curious fossil.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   9 May 1869
letters.summary: Thanks CD for lesson that it is wrong to call any plant which lives and thrives "degraded".

letters.title: ToGardeners’ Chronicle   9 May [1869]
letters.summary: In response to a query from a Mr D. T. Fish, CD reaffirms his view of the efficiency of worms in bringing up in their intestines fine soil from below the surface. Reports on observations, during the past 25 years, which confirm his views.

letters.title: To George Bentham   10 May [1869]
letters.summary: Sends a letter (and seeds) from Fritz Müller about a strange monstrous form ofBegoniafound wild in Brazil. Asks GB whether it is worth communicating to Linnean Society.

letters.title: From George Bentham   10 May 1869
letters.summary:
Will have Fritz Müller’s letter ["On the modification of the stamens in a species ofBegonia",J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)11 (1871): 472–4] read at next Linnean Society meeting [read 3 June 1869].

Has given the seeds to Daniel Oliver.

letters.title: From John Hellins   10 May 1869
letters.summary: Notes sex ratios in Lepidoptera he is breeding.

letters.title: To Linnean Society, President and Council   [10 May 1869]
letters.summary: Referee report on paper by Richard Spruce on sacs inMelastoma[see6690]. CD says RS’s suggestions that sacs are inherited is not supported and should be deleted.

letters.title: To Linnean Society, President and Council   10 May 1869
letters.summary: Recommends publication of Mrs Barber’s paper on a rare case of fertilisation of a plant by one kind of insect alone, with access of others prevented by a mechanical obstacle [Mary Elizabeth Barber, "On the fertilisation and dissemination ofDuvernoia adhatodoides",J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)11 (1869): 469–72].

letters.title: From Louis Rérolle   10 May 1869
letters.summary: French translation ofOrchidswill be published by Reinwald. Asks for CD’s new footnotes to be sent.

letters.title: From W. C. Tait   10 May 1869
letters.summary:
Development of the horns of local sheep.

Results of breeding tailless pointers: of six puppies, three had stumps like parents.

Observations onDrosophyllum.

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   13 May [1869]
letters.summary: Comments on paper by JJW ["On insects and insectivorous birds",Trans. R. Entomol. Soc. Lond.(1869): 21–6]. JJW’s verification of A. R. Wallace’s suggestion regarding inheritance is quite a discovery.

letters.title: From John Beck   15 May 1869
letters.summary: Sends his MS "The real presence" [on transubstantiation] for CD’s comments.

letters.title: To William Bowman   16 May [1869–81]
letters.summary: "I shall not be in London on Monday, but I have written to my Brother to ask him to aid you"

letters.title: From George Maw   17 May 1869
letters.summary: He is managing to salvage a few AndalusianDrosophyllumplants from the voyage and will send some to CD.

letters.title: To the registrar of friendly societies   18 May [1869, 1870, 1875, 1880 or 1881]
letters.summary: CD has misplaced the annual audited balance sheet for the Down Friendly Society and wonders whether he has sent it to his correspondent in error.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   20 May 1869
letters.summary:
Cites article by David Forbes dealing with the geology of the S. American Cordillera ["Geology of Bolivia and South Peru",Q. J. Geol. Soc. Lond.17 (1861): 7–62].

Discusses the flexures of the Cordillera, the age of the mountains, and basaltic dikes in granite areas.

letters.title: From Henry Maudsley   20 May 1869
letters.summary: He forwarded CD’s queries on the insane to James Crichton-Browne who has now answered.

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   20 May [1869]
letters.summary: Asks for information about male birds migrating before females.

letters.title: To John Wheldon   20 May [1869]
letters.summary: Orders two second-hand books from a dealer’s catalogue.

letters.title: To James Crichton-Browne   22 May 1869
letters.summary: Thanks for MS observations on expression. Discusses hair standing on end in terror and rage. Asks JC-B to observe contraction of platysma myoides. "Your description of the grinning and exposure of the canine teeth under furious rage is excellent. I presume that you would not object to my quoting it." Asks about contraction of "grief muscles". Comments on blushing. Offers to send book by G. B. A. Duchenne [Mécanisme de la physionomie humaine(1862)].

letters.title: To George Maw   22 May [1869]
letters.summary: Thanks GM for specimens ofDrosophyllum.

letters.title: To J. D. Caton   24 May 1869
letters.summary:
Discusses secondary hoofs in antelope and deer.

Mentions tuft of hair on turkey hen.

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   26 May 1869
letters.summary:
Migratory male nightingales and blackcaps arrive before females [seeDescent1: 259].

Discusses chaffinch "Peggers".

Disagrees with CD’s opinion that canary mules are fertile.

Display of colour of greenfinches in courtship.

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   27 May [1869]
letters.summary:
Thanks for information about bird migration.

Comments on canary hybridisation.

letters.title: From Adolf Reuter   30 May 1869
letters.summary: AR, gardener to the King of Prussia, has readVariationand wishes to send CD observations.

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   June 1869
letters.summary: Loss of juvenile colouring in South Down sheep.

letters.title: From James Crichton-Browne   1 June 1869
letters.summary: Discusses the bristling of hair in melancholics and the action of the platysma myoides muscle and the grief muscles in the insane.

letters.title: From George Cupples   [1 June 1869]
letters.summary: Note on proportion of sexes born in sheep.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   1 June [1869]
letters.summary:
Thanks for answers about expression.

Is going to N. Wales to recover after his riding accident.

New edition ofOrigin.

French edition ofOrchids.
