letters.title: To W. C. Tait   1 June [1869]
letters.summary:
WCT should send specimens to Orpington Station.

Invites him to visit, but afraid conversation "would quite knock me up".

letters.title: To George Cupples   [June 1869 or later]
letters.summary: Wishes Cupples had said something about health. Sends regards to Mrs Cupples.

letters.title: To Stephen Paul Engleheart   2 June [1869]
letters.summary:
Asks about orbicular muscles in eyes of women suffering in labour.

Inquires about treatment for dyspeptic weakness involving "Volta-Electric Chain bands".

letters.title: To Adolf Reuter   2 June 1869
letters.summary: Thanks AR for his offer to send his observation notes, but since CD will not pursue the subject of variation under domestication, and his German is poor, he urges him to publish them in some periodical.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   3 June 1869
letters.summary: Will use new English edition [5th, ofOrigin] in preparing for [4th] German edition. Bronn’s translation ofOriginin the title as "Entstehung" is not so precise as "Ursprung" would be. The publisher does not object to changing the title, but JVC is doubtful, because theOriginis so well known in Germany asEntstehung. Asks CD’s opinion.

letters.title: To Joseph Henry Gilbert   3 June [1869]
letters.summary: Declines invitation.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   6 June 1869
letters.summary: Account of his Russian trip.

letters.title: To John Traherne Moggridge   7 June 1869
letters.summary:
Glad JTM intends to write a paper. Discusses JTM’s research onArbutus.

CD’s riding accident.

letters.title: From Henry Walter Bates   8 June 1869
letters.summary: Ashamed that members of the Entomological Society have almost no information on sex ratio of bred insects in response to CD’s query of months ago. One exception, William Buckler, promises results. [SeeDescent1: 313.]

letters.title: To James Crichton-Browne   8 June 1869
letters.summary:
Thanks for information about expression.

Comments on JC-B’s photographs of insane people.

Sends copy of Duchenne [see6755].

Asks for further information about platysma, hisbête noirefor a year or two.

letters.title: From William Buckler   [after 8 June 1869]
letters.summary: List giving the numbers of Lepidoptera of different species reared in 1869 and the proportions of the sexes [seeDescent1: 313].

letters.title: From George Swaysland   12 June 1869
letters.summary: Observations on birds entering the country in spring. Some have clods of earth on their feet.

letters.title: From Max Schmidt   14 June 1869
letters.summary: Frankfurt Zoological Garden has only male mandrill. Does CD want description? Antwerp garden may have a pair.

letters.title: From Gerolamo Boccardo   15 June 1869
letters.summary: Sends CD a copy of his new bookSismopirologia[1869]. Is sending no other copy to England because his previous book was unacknowledged.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   15 June 1869
letters.summary:
FM much gratified by the appearance ofFür Darwintranslation.

Discusses dimorphism in Rubiaceae.

letters.title: From Eduard Koch   17 June 1869
letters.summary:
Carus will soon begin translating 5th ed. ofOrigin.

Sale ofVariationis satisfying.

C. J. Dub will write popular work on CD’s theory.

Gustav Jäger has written on it [Die Darwin’sche Theorie und ihre Stellung zu Moral und Religion(1869)].

letters.title: To theAthenæum   19 June 1869
letters.summary: Thanks correspondent, "Ponderer", for pointing out his erroneous calculation of the rate of increase of elephants inOrigin[p. 64]. [!?or p. 74!? (see 6775f), or 75, (see 6790)]

letters.title: From George Cupples   20 June 1869
letters.summary: On proportion of sexes in litters of dogs.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   21 June [1869]
letters.summary:
Sends new edition of theOrigin. Has made some corrections.

Has been led into dreadful blunder on p. 75 by erroneous calculations of a mathematical friend.

Opposes change ofEntstehungintoUrsprung[in title] even if more correct. It would make readers think it is a new book.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   22 June 1869
letters.summary:
RC has sent a copy of the new [5th] edition ofOrigin.

Electrotypes [ofOrchids] have been sent to Bologna.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   22 June [1869]
letters.summary:
The house at Barmouth.

His poor health.

Bentham’s interesting Linnean Society Address ["On geographical biology",Proc. Linn. Soc. Lond.(1869): lxv–c].

CD particularly wishes to know how botanists agreed with zoologists on distribution.

Still thinks isolation more important in preserving old forms than Bentham is inclined to believe.

letters.title: To Eduard Koch   22 June [1869]
letters.summary:
Pleased that Julius Dub will publish with ES [Kurze Darstellung der Lehre Darwin’s(1870)].

Would like Gustav Jäger’s brochure [Die Darwin’sche Theorie(1869)].

letters.title: From Alexander F. Boardman   23 June 1869
letters.summary: Reports having seen a very human-looking monkey on exhibit. Gives a phrenological analysis of its skull.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   23 June [1869]
letters.summary:
He told Giovanni Canestrini that stereotypes [forVariation] would cost £10.

Reminds RC of his suggestion that a copy [ofOrigin, 5th ed.] be sent toScientific Opinionfor review.

letters.title: From James Croll   23 June 1869
letters.summary:
Thanks for presentation copy ofOrigin[5th ed.].

Clarifies his point on north and south glacial periods. Supports CD’s view that temperate plants will move up mountains during the alternation.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   23 June [1869]
letters.summary: Asks whether sexual selection could produce the changing plumules or "battledore" scales on the wings of certain butterflies.

letters.title: To ?   23 June 1869
letters.summary: [A quotation in CD’s hand, signed and dated, from the introduction toOrchids.] "I have never once expressed a wish for aid or for information, which has not been granted, as far as possible, in the most liberal spirit."

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   24 June 1869
letters.summary:
Recounts the trip back from St Petersburg – visits to botanic gardens and museums throughout Western Europe.

Pleased that CD admired Bentham’s address [see6793]. JDH had read it in MS and modified some very heterodox passages about insularity. CD has hit the flaw in it.

F. A. W. Miquel is a convert.

letters.title: To Alexander Goodman More   24 June 1869
letters.summary:
Asks AGM to observe fertilisation ofEpipactis palustris. Has found thatE. latifoliais fertilised by wasps.

Making revisions for French edition ofOrchids.

letters.title: To Edwin Ray Lankester   25 June 1869
letters.summary: Testimonial letter for ERL, praising his ability, knowledge, and zeal for science.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   25 June [1869]
letters.summary:
On butterfly scales: there are many secondary characters which baffle conjecture.

Was forced to make additions toOriginas short as possible.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   28 June [1869]
letters.summary:
Horned rams of Guinea sheep.

CD’s queries about expression are too difficult for him to answer.

letters.title: To Edward A. Smith   [before 30 June 1869]
letters.summary: Sends engraved plates with instructions about illustrations forDescent.

letters.title: To Edward A. Smith   30 June [1869]
letters.summary: Thanks EAS for excellent proofs of woodcuts [forDescent].

letters.title: From W. B. Tegetmeier   30 June 1869
letters.summary: Forwards a basket of eggs of pile game fowl.

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   1 July [1869]
letters.summary:
"My health got so bad I could do nothing at Down".

Gives information about migration of male and female birds.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   2 July [1869]
letters.summary: Thanks for [July 1869] issue ofQuarterly Review.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   2 July 1869
letters.summary:
Comments on 5th edition of theOrigin[1869];

preparation of second edition ofNatürliche Schöpfungsgeschichte[1870].

The reception of CD’s theory. Mentions support of Pieter Harting and Michael Sars.

EH’s research on calcareous sponges and plans to publish monograph on them.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   2 July [1869]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Asks for reference to Louis Agassiz’s views on embryos indicating ancestral structures.

letters.title: From John Scott   2 July 1869
letters.summary: Observations on expression and colour of beard and hair in natives of India.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   2 July [1869]
letters.summary:
Thanks for procuring eggs.

CD’s health has necessitated his leaving home.

letters.title: From William Erasmus Darwin   5 July [1869]
letters.summary: Observations on flies visitingEpipactis.

letters.title: From Louis Agassiz   6 July 1869
letters.summary: Introduces his son Alexander; believes CD will find him "more tractable" on certain questions than LA himself is.

letters.title: To theAthenæum   7 [July] 1869
letters.summary:
Because readers have arrived at different answers to the problem of the rate of increase of elephants, CD offers a rule, used by his son George, for calculating the product for any number of generations.

[Letter erroneously dated June.]

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   7 [July 1869]
letters.summary: Thanks him for his excellent observations [onEpipactis?]; would like WED to watch for some large insect visiting the plant.

letters.title: To William Ogle   7 July [1869]
letters.summary: Comments on WO’s paper onSalvia[Pop. Sci. Rev.8 (1869): 261–73], which he admires.

letters.title: From William Ogle   [after 7 July 1869]
letters.summary: WO very gratified by CD’s complimentary remarks on hisSalviaarticle.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   8 July [1869]
letters.summary:
Simeon Habel of New York has returned from Galapagos. CD has asked him to send any plants to JDH.

Reading Nägeli convinces him that it is all-important to learn all about polymorphic or protean genera for the "Laws of Variability".

New Zealand genera are interesting and have perplexed him for years.

Has read paper on snakes. Thinks it is not fascination but fear that makes the victim fall into snake’s power.

letters.title: From George Robert Gray   9 July 1869
letters.summary: Asks for a testimonial.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   9 July [1869]
letters.summary:
Haeckel wants British specimens of calcareous sponges. Can THH tell him to whom he can apply?

Health not improving – cannot climb even a hill.

Has heard THH’s article on Comte ["Scientific aspects of Positivism",Lay sermons(1870)] is a splendid success.

letters.title: From W. C. Tait   11 July 1869
letters.summary:
Drosophyllum lusitanicum.

Believes principle of natural selection can be more widely applied.

Flower structure ofGeranium.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   12 July 1869
letters.summary: Bees visitingEpipactis.

letters.title: To G. R. Gray   12 July 1869
letters.summary: Would be glad to send GRG a testimonial of his abilities as a naturalist, but is not qualified to express opinion on his works in ornithology or entomology.

letters.title: To W. B. Dawkins   14 July [1869]
letters.summary: Knows Dawkins interested in cave animals; has just heard from a Lloyd of Rhaggatt that a fissure has opened full of bones and teeth. Will send some.

letters.title: From Alexander Wallace   15 July [1869]
letters.summary: Gives information on the proportions of sexes of certain moths. [SeeDescent1: 313.]

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   16 July 1869
letters.summary:
Has already referred Haeckel’s request to J. S. Bowerbank.

Has lost track of collectors and naturalists "by grace of the dredge" because of other work and ""the great question of "Darwinismus" which is such a worry to us all"".

Family health.

letters.title: From W. B. Dawkins   17 July 1869
letters.summary: On the genealogy of the horse.

letters.title: To Albany Hancock   17 July [1869]
letters.summary: Ernst Haeckel is working on calcareous sponges. Does AH have any British specimens that he can spare? [See6842.]

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   17 July 1869
letters.summary:
On reading F. Müller’sFacts and arguments for Darwin[1869].

Pangenesis.

Agrees with CD on fascination [of snakes].

Huxley is at Comte again.

letters.title: To W. C. Tait   17 July [1869]
letters.summary:
Discusses need for cross-fertilisation inGeranium.

Hooker begins to doubt whetherDrosophyllumso closely allied toDrosera.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   18 July [1869]
letters.summary:
Reports reviews ofFacts and arguments for Darwin[1869].

Is preparing for a French translation ofOrchids.

The case ofAbutilonwhich is sterile with some individuals is remarkable.

Has sent FM’s account of the monstrousBegoniato the Linnean Society.

letters.title: From Adolph Reuter   18 July 1869
letters.summary:
Sends notes on lack of variation in seedlings of trees and shrubs

and on climbers changing their character with age.

letters.title: To W. B. Dawkins   19 July [1869]
letters.summary: Admits that he had disobeyed his instructions and dispatched a box of bones to him by rail. Gives an account of the discovery of the bones at Perth y Chwaril on the Rhagatt estate. He has promised Miss Lloyd to obtain from WBD the English names of the principal bones.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   20 July [1869]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Has been asked by Henry Powell [new vicar of Down] for help to build a house at Down; asks for CD’s advice.

letters.title: From W. B. Tegetmeier   20 July 1869
letters.summary:
Sends C. M. Browne’s notes on transmission of colour in greyhounds [seeVariation, 2d ed., 2: 40]

and a letter from Major Holland.

WBT to visit America.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   21 July [1869]
letters.summary:
Further queries on poultry plumage.

WBT’s visit to America.

letters.title: To the editors of theAnnals and Magazine of Natural History   23 July 1869
letters.deprecated: Annals and Magazine of Natural History
letters.recipient: Annals and Magazine of Natural History
letters.summary: CD passes on notes prepared for the French translation ofOrchidsso that his book may be brought up to date in English as well.

letters.title: From Jules Joseph Fleury   23 July 1869
letters.summary: Wants to know whether CD is related to Edward Darwin, who married a French woman in 1823.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   24 July [1869]
letters.summary:
An article inNorth British Reviewby mathematician against Hooker and Huxley and for William Thomson [P. G. Tait, "Geological time",North Br. Rev.50 (1869): 406–39]. Feels a conviction that world will be found older than reviewer makes it.

Article on "Design" [by J. B. Mozley] inQuarterly Review[127 (1869): 134–76].

Has JDH studiedDrosophyllum?

letters.title: To Mary Charlotte Lloyd   [24 July 1869]
letters.summary: Forwards letter from W. B. Dawkins. The bones, though not themselves interesting, may indicate the work of prehistoric man.

letters.title: To Adolph Reuter   24 July [1869]
letters.summary: Thanks for facts on inheritance. May be used if CD corrects 3d ed. [2d ed.] ofVariation.

letters.title: From Albany Hancock   25 July 1869
letters.summary: Cannot help CD with his request for calcareous sponges.

letters.title: From Charles Voysey   27 July 1869
letters.summary: Acclimatisation of potatoes by selection.

letters.title: To Dudley Campbell   29 July [1869]
letters.summary: Sends cheque for £5 as subscription toWestminster Review.

letters.title: To Alfred Merle Norman   29 July [1869]
letters.summary: Asks whether AMN has any specimens of British calcareous sponges that CD could forward to Haeckel, who is studying them.

letters.title: From Louis Rérolle   30 July 1869
letters.summary: Progressing with translation of new footnotes forOrchids. Asks for help with a few words.

letters.title: From C. S. Bate   31 July 1869
letters.summary:
Mating practice ofCarcinus maenas[seeDescent1: 331].

Difference in size in sexes of Crustacea.

letters.title: From W. B. Dawkins   31 July 1869
letters.summary: Reports on prehistoric finds from caves at Rhagatt.

letters.title: From A. M. Norman   2 August 1869
letters.summary:
Apologises for and explains the delay in supplying Haeckel with sponge specimens.

Mentions some of the interesting crustacean specimens he has received from thePorcupinecruise off the West of Ireland.

letters.title: To Walter Elliot   3 August [1869]
letters.summary: Asks whether the wild boar in India is polygamous.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   3 August [1869]
letters.summary: Suggests Englishmen who might provide sponge specimens.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   3 August 1869
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Sexual differences inLabidocera darwinii, in Entomostraca, and Myriapoda.

letters.title: To M. C. Lloyd   4 August [1869]
letters.summary: Encloses letter from W. B. Dawkins concerning "our old savage progenitors with their ground-down teeth".

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   5 August 1869
letters.summary:
Huxley has shown him the jaws of anAnoplotheriumbrought from the Gallegos by R. O. Cunningham.

Saw Hallett’s wheat crops at Brighton; results of his selection very striking.

Huxley is assembling his Darwiniana papers for republication.

Has written a crushing reply to Richard Congreve ["The scientific aspects of positivism",Fortn. Rev.n.s. 5 (1869): 653–70] and JDH feels "infantine" beside him.

Comments on Sabine’s being offered and accepting K.C.B.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   5 August [1869]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary:
On the antennae ofLabidocera.

Size of sexes in Entomostraca.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   [after 5 August 1869]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Visiting arrangements.

letters.title: From Walter Elliot   7 August 1869
letters.summary: Polygamous breeding habits of the Indian wild boar. [SeeDescent1: 267.]

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   7 August [1869]
letters.summary:
Replies to JDH on Hallett; doubts that already improved varieties do not vary in other respects.

The North British Reviewarticle [see6841] is worth reading "scientifically"; it made CD feel small.

Awaits JDH’s decision on affinities ofDrosophyllumandDrosera.

Is curious to see proportion of males to females in recent census in India.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   8 August 1869
letters.summary: Speculates on the function of the separate stamen of papilionaceous flowers.

letters.title: To Thomas Spencer Cobbold   9 August [1869]
letters.summary: Offers TSC specimens of parasitic worms collected by CD in S. America.

letters.title: To Achille Quadri   9 August 1869
letters.summary: Thanks for two copies ofTeoria Darwiniana, one of which has been sent to the Royal Society.

letters.title: From John Blackwall   10 August 1869
letters.summary: Immature male spiders usually resemble in colour the females of their species of the same age. In some species colours of sexes differ when mature.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   10 August [1869]
letters.summary: THF’s view, if confirmed, pleases CD in that what appears a mere morphological character is found to be of use. Carl Nägeli has been attacking him on this head.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   12 August 1869
letters.summary: Will work on papilionaceous flowers since CD encourages it. Discusses function of hairs in certain plants.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   13 August 1869
letters.summary:
Did not intend to imply that Hallett said variation stopped, but that it arrives at a point where further accumulation in direction sought is so slow as to result practically in fixity of type – but not absolute fixity.

Duke of Argyll has requested JDH to superintend publication of a flora of India. JDH thinks he [Argyll] is paying him off for his kick at natural theology.

Willy [Hooker] returning from New Zealand.

A unique character inDrosophyllum.

Sees no reason for CD to contribute to Ross and Faraday memorials.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   14 August [1869]
letters.summary:
Faraday memorial is an exception.

George [Darwin] has convinced CD thatNorth British Reviewarticle is by P. G. Tait [see6841].

Surprised that leaves ofDrosophyllumare always rolled backwards at their tips, but did not know it was unique character.

letters.title: From George St Clair   14 August 1869
letters.summary: Reports on a family of cats observed locally in which some members are six-toed.

letters.title: From John Beddoe   21 August 1869
letters.summary: Encloses results of several more years of observation on conjugal selection and hair coloration.

letters.title: From John Beddoe   [22 August – 12 September 1869]
letters.summary: Results of CD’s examination of data subvert JB’s former inferences. Will send abstracts from the data for his paper on colour of hair of single and married women 35 to 45 years old ["On the supposed increasing prevalence of dark hair in England",Anthropol. Rev.1 (1863): 310–12].

letters.title: From Federico Delpino   22 August 1869
letters.summary:
Declares himself CD’s defender; but he is a "teleologist".

Sends CD three more papers.

His research confirms his faith and belief in variability of species.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   23 August 1869
letters.summary: Announces his return to England.

letters.title: From W. C. Tait   [23 August 1869]
letters.summary: Will obtain someDrosophyllumseed for CD.

letters.title: To Federico Delpino   24 and 25 August [1869]
letters.summary:
Thanks FD for his three publications.

CD is pleased that FD has discussed Pangenesis, although he does not favour the hypothesis. Will seek English publisher.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   25 August 1869
letters.summary: Inquires about the differences in plumage between chicks and adults of certain poultry breeds. Is anxious to know whether the chick’s plumage closely approaches the adult’s in those breeds in which the sexes resemble each other in plumage.

letters.title: From Frederick Smith   26 August 1869
letters.summary: On the colours of sexes of Australian bees [seeDescent1: 366].

letters.title: To W. C. Tait   27 August [1869]
letters.summary: Will not trouble WCT for more specimens ofDrosophyllum. Hooker says genus is closely allied toDrosera, though having such different habits.

letters.title: From T. S. Cobbold   1 September [1869]
letters.summary: Thanks CD for parasitic worms [see6858] specimens. Supports "fact of succession".

letters.title: From William Bowman   3 September [1869]
letters.summary: Asks whether he may come with F. C. Donders to visit CD.

letters.title: To Frans Cornelis Donders   6 September 1869
letters.summary: Asks about Charles Bell’s statement concerning contraction of eye muscles. Asks whether such contraction is related to secretion of tears.

letters.title: From Walter Elliot   7 September 1869
letters.summary: Sends excerpt on polygamous breeding habits of Asiatic elephants by Lieut. Johnstone [Proc. Asiat. Soc. Bengal(1868): 128]. [SeeDescent1: 268.]

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   7 September 1869
letters.summary:
Reports on events at Exeter [BAAS] meeting. G. G. Stokes made a first-rate President.

Huxley "poured boiling oil" over James McCann in answer to his "conceited dogmatic sermon".

F. A. W. Miquel is coming to stay.

letters.title: From John Blackwall   8 September 1869
letters.summary:
His observations on young ofTheridion lineatumreveal no characteristics distinguishing one from another;

quotes N. Westring on stridulation inTheridion serratipes[seeDescent1: 339].

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   8 September [1869]
letters.summary:
Wants observations on aPapilioto see whether ticking noise is confined to one sex.

Experiments on self-sterility.

Will send copy of his orchid paper ["Fertilisation of orchids",Collected papers2: 138–56].

Eschscholziawhen self-fertilised, produced pods.

letters.title: From James Orton   8 September 1869
letters.summary: Sends a lower molar of fossil horse from Quito. Curious as to its species, especially in view of Owen’s findings in Mexico.

letters.title: From Edward Burnett Tylor   8 September 1869
letters.summary: Wishes to borrow a paper by R. G. Haliburton on superstitions connected with sneezing [see5635].

letters.title: To Gustav Jäger   9 September 1869
letters.summary:
Admires GJ’s book [Die Darwin’sche Theorie(1869)].

Asks about plumage of rejected male pheasant.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   10 September [1869]
letters.summary:
F. C. Donders has been to lunch – a good "Darwinian"!

JDH’s speech of resignation [as BAAS President] at Exeter was charming [Rep. BAAS(1869)]. JDH should have been an ambassador.

Has received Indian census.

Is unusually well.

letters.title: From John Beddoe   13 September 1869
letters.summary: Encloses last instalment of data on colour of women’s hair and conjugal selection. Fears results are inconclusive.

letters.title: From Edward Blyth   13 September 1869
letters.summary: Gives some observations and opinions on the appearance and behaviour of mandrills.

letters.title: From George Cupples   13 September 1869
letters.summary: Proportion of sexes in rats.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   13 September 1869
letters.summary:
Since March has been living in Heidelberg, where his wife is studying mathematics and physics.

The Russian translation ofVariationhas been printed in his absence; he will bring a copy to Down if he receives one from Russia.

letters.title: To Edward Blyth   14 September [1869]
letters.summary:
Thanks EB for his attempts to find out about the mandrills;

sorry to hear that he has been so badly treated by the manager ofLand and Water.

letters.title: From Frederick Smith   14 September 1869
letters.summary: On stridulation of Coleoptera,Trox sabulosus,Mutilla. [SeeDescent1: 380.]

letters.title: To Samuel Hubbard Scudder   15 September [1869]
letters.summary: Thanks SHS for papers he has sent.

letters.title: From J. T. Moggridge   16 September [1869]
letters.summary:
Thanks for CD’s ["Fertilization of orchids",Collected papers2: 138–56].

Although Thomas Meehan’s paper ["Variations inEpigaea repens",Proc. Philadelphia Acad. Nat. Sci.(1868): 153–6] shows great variability in this genus, JTM sees a need to qualify the generalisation that there is as much variation in the wild as under domestication. He knows no evidence for a constant proportion between variability in the wild and under cultivation.

Observations on correlation between leaf size and exposure to sun and shade.

Has evidence for two varieties ofOphrys apiferain England, which live in mutually exclusive colonies.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   17 September 1869
letters.summary:
Will come to Down on 25 Sept.

Thanks CD for supplementaries ["Fertilization of orchids",Collected papers2: 138–56] which he will quote in theBritish flora[The student’s flora of the British Islands(1870)].

F. A. W. Miquel could not come.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   18 September 1869
letters.summary: Asks CD’s opinion of a paper he has written on papilionaceous flowers.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   18 [September 1869]
letters.summary: Asks JDH to consult colleagues learned in physiology for answer to query: when a large piece of bark is removed from a tree, does the bark ever regrow in isolated points [separate] from the growing margin of the surrounding bark? Query bears on Pangenesis and on power of repair in plants.

letters.title: From J. T. Moggridge   18 September 1869
letters.summary: Leaflet variation at the tip ofLathyrusstems.

letters.title: From John Murray   18 September [1869]
letters.summary: JM is about to start a new monthly literary review [theAcademy]. Would like to publish in first number a short notice of the new work upon which CD is engaged [Descent].

letters.title: To John Murray   [after 18 September 1869]
letters.summary:
Wishes JM’s new periodical [theAcademy] could have been a weekly so it might kill theAthenæumby a lingering death.

Has drafted a piece [aboutDescent] but is not pleased with it.

letters.title: To Albert Günther   21 September 1869
letters.summary:
Sends a list of queries for AG.

Asks whether AG can supply specimens for illustrations [forDescent]. Hopes Mr Ford will do the drawings.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   21 September [1869]
letters.summary: James Orton, U. S. naturalist, has sent him a tooth from skull of a horse found in Quito, Ecuador in deposits containingMastodon, etc. JO asked CD to send it to Owen, but, since he does not communicate with Owen, he is sending it to THH.

letters.title: From M. T. Masters   21 September 1869
letters.summary: Robert Fenn exhibited potatoes at the Horticultural Society which showed general failure of graft-hybrids and provided an example of reversion to a wild Peruvian tuber resulting from cross-fertilisation.

letters.title: To [?]   21 September [1869]
letters.summary: Thanks correspondent for sending curious facts about his cats.

letters.title: From Hermann Müller   22 September 1869
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for the English edition of his brother’s book [Fritz Müller,Facts and arguments for Darwin(1869)]

and for CD’s memoir on orchids ["Fertilization of orchids",Collected papers2: 138–56].

letters.title: From Albert Günther   23 September 1869
letters.summary:
Mr Ford is attending to CD’s drawings [forDescent].

Death of AG’s wife.

letters.title: From Adolf Reuter   23 September 1869
letters.summary: Sends notes on variation in plants.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   24 September 1869
letters.summary:
Time of his arrival.

Will bring bark story with him.

letters.title: To Albert Günther   25 September 1869
letters.summary: Is "astonished & deeply grieved" at loss [of AG’s wife].

letters.title: From George Henslow   25 September 1869
letters.summary: Thanks for a paper on phyllotaxy.

letters.title: To Ellen Frances Lubbock   [26 September 1869?]
letters.summary: Would have liked to come to lunch, but has been talking so much to Hooker that he has no strength left.

letters.title: From Albert Günther   [before 27 September 1869]
letters.summary: Replies to CD’s queries on sexual habits and differences in fish and lizards.

letters.title: To Albert Günther   27 September [1869]
letters.summary:
Thanks AG for full answers to queries.

Delighted Mr Ford will undertake drawings [forDescent]; comments on some illustrations he would like.

letters.title: To Adolf Reuter   27 September 1869
letters.summary: Thanks AR for specimens and notes. Will keep them for future edition [ofVariation]. Particularly struck by difference in hardiness of varieties ofSyringa persica.

letters.title: From Alphonse de Candolle   28 September 1869
letters.summary:
Reports on the differences of growth and development of plants of three species grown at Geneva from seed collected at different localities. Forwards seed for CD to plant and observe differences in development.

Carl Linsseer has published a memoir on the times of flowering, foliation, etc. of diverse species in different parts of Europe [Mem. Acad. Imp. Sci. St.-Pétersbourg7th ser. 11 no. 7 (1868)] and concludes that the northern forms are more forward and that this is hereditary. AdeC’s experiments carried out on annuals, show only the effects of heredity; probably the direct action of physical conditions affects development, at least in perennial species.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   28 September 1869
letters.summary:
Will do his best on the tooth [sent by CD] but does not put much weight on conclusions based on a single tooth of a horse.

Darwin attacked by three clergymen at BAAS meeting [Exeter, 1869].

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   28 September [1869]
letters.summary: He will send carrier to theFieldoffice to collect pigeons.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   29 September 1869
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for assistance concerning sponge specimens. Mentions Englishmen who have sent specimens. J. S. Bowerbank has not answered requests.

Sends articles dealing with sponges and Medusae. Cites passages for CD to read. Suggests passages fromEntwicklungsgeschichte der Siphonophoren[1869].

Describes meeting with Sars and his trip to Norway.

letters.title: From W. C. Tait   29 September 1869
letters.summary: On endemic flora and fauna of Portugal.

letters.title: From Victor Masson   29 September 1869
letters.summary: Asks CD to send 5th ed. ofOriginso Mlle Royer can use it in her work. Regret they have upset CD to the extent that he would reproach them so untowardly.

letters.title: To Victor Masson   [after 29 September 1869]
letters.summary: Is annoyed that a new French edition ofOrigin[1870] has been prepared without making use of the corrections CD made in the 5th English edition [1869].

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   1 October [1869]
letters.summary: V. O. Kovalevsky, Russian translator [ofVariation], wishes to hear THH lecture.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   1 October [1869]
letters.summary: Chickens have arrived safely.

letters.title: From S. P. Engleheart [October 1869 or later]
letters.summary: Blushing begins as early as the fifth year.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   2 October [1869]
letters.summary: Sends letter from Candolle [6915] proposing an experiment with seeds that seems excellent. CD has little time and strength but will do his best. If the staff at Kew could do it, it would be wisest to hand the whole lot over to JDH.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   3 October [1869]
letters.summary:
Mentions views of Sars on species.

EH’s work on Siphonophora.

letters.title: To James Orton   7 October [1869]
letters.summary: Has forwarded the horse’s tooth, sent by JO, to Huxley, who may be able to identify it.

letters.title: From Frederick Smith   8 October 1869
letters.summary: Both sexes ofMononychus pseudacoriand other Coleoptera stridulate.

letters.title: From Federico Delpino   9 October 1869
letters.summary:
Acknowledges receipt of CD’sPrimulapaper [J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)10 (1869): 437–54].

Nectar-sucking birds fertilise tropical flowers.

Writing a "Dualistic apologia for Pangenesis" [see translation inSci. Opin.2 (1869): 365–7, 391–3, 407–8].

Homology of the orchid rostellum.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   9 October 1869
letters.summary: Federico Delpino’s book has very nearly all that THF has found and a great deal more.

letters.title: To T. Thompson  9 October 1869
letters.summary: Writes, as county magistrate, in an attempt to get payment from the Club for a Mr Reeves.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   10 October [1869]
letters.summary: Sympathises with THF at being forestalled by Delpino, but urges him to publish confirmation.

letters.title: To Alphonse de Candolle   11 October 1869
letters.summary: Thanks AdeC for his interesting letter [6915]. The experiment strikes CD as a very valuable one. CD has forwarded the letter to Hooker, who is glad to make the trial. CD will have many experiments in progress next spring but he will open the packet of seeds and if they are numerous, will try a few himself.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   11 October 1869
letters.summary: Is glad that JDH is willing to try Candolle’s experiment [see6915]. Encloses all the seeds except a few taken from the Moscow and Palermo packets.

letters.title: From John Fox & Sons   12 October 1869
letters.summary: Acknowledges receipt of CD’s cheque in payment of his account.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   13 October 1869
letters.summary:
On the fertilisation ofTacsoniaandPassiflora.

Encloses a poem, "The Biological Teleologist", written after reading Delpino.

letters.title: From L. E. Becker   14 October 1869
letters.summary: Sends abstract of her BAAS paper on the role of a parasitic fungus in producing bisexual flowers inLychnis.

letters.title: To Federico Delpino   14 October 1869
letters.summary:
Cautions FD about fluid in labellum ofCoryanthes.

T. H. Farrer is enthusiastic about FD’s papers.

Believes humming-birds fertilise many American flowers.

Mentions his reply to FD’s criticisms ["Pangenesis: Mr Darwin’s reply to Professor Delpino",Sci. Opin.2 (1869): 426;Collected papers2: 158–60].

Suggests that FD study fertilisation of Gramineae.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   14 October 1869
letters.summary:
Delighted with THH’s review [inAcademy(1869)] of Haeckel’s [Natürliche]Schöpfungsgeschichte[1868],

but groans about THH’s view of rudimentary organs. CitesOriginandVariation.

letters.title: From John Brodie Innes    15 October 1869
letters.summary:
R. H. Hutton has given a paper about CD at Liverpool Church Congress.

JBI has seen four milk-white partridges among brown ones this year.

letters.title: From Robert Swinhoe   16 October 1869
letters.summary: Has a book of photographs of Japanese that CD might be interested in for his work on expression.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   17 October 1869
letters.summary: Sends notes on observations ofPassifloraandTacsonia; Hooker thinks they would be worth reading at Linnean Society.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [18 October 1869]
letters.summary: Asks for some money for his fees.

letters.title: To J. B. Innes   18 October 1869
letters.summary:
CD gets so many foolish letters from foolish people he has little heart to write to friends.

Gives Down news.

R. H. Hutton, editor of theSpectator, is a clever man.

CD has been much abused, praised, and chaffed by newspapers lately.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   18 October 1869
letters.summary:
Describes experiments to test the fertility ofAbutilon, which appears self-sterile,

and briefly mentions dichogamy inEschscholzia.

letters.title: From W. B. Dawkins   19 October 1869
letters.summary:
Reports on his findings in Denbighshire caves ["The Denbighshire caves",Trans. Manchester Geol. Soc.9 (1869–70): 31–7].

Sends his paper ["On the prae-historic Mammalia in Great Britain",Intellect. Obs.(1868): 403–10].

Has changed his view on the descent of British cattle from the wild aurochs. No evidence that aurochs survived into historic times in Britain.

letters.title: ToScientific Opinion   [before 20 October 1869]
letters.summary: Replies to F. Delpino’s criticisms of Pangenesis [Sci. Opin.2 (1869): 365–7, 391–3, 407–8], especially concerning the difficulty of explaining the regrowth of amputated organs.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   20 October 1869
letters.summary: Koch [of Schweizerbart’s, publisher of German translations of CD’s works] has inquired when CD’s new book on man will be out. JVC assures CD that the book should be translated into German, and offers his services.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   20 October [1869]
letters.summary: Comments on notes made by THF onPassifloraandTacsonia. Suggests he examine more species. Recalls his own observations onP. princepsandTacsonia.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   20 October 1869
letters.summary:
Has sent CD someDroseraspecimens.

Returns to U. S. on 9 November.

letters.title: From J. B. Innes   20 October 1869
letters.summary:
SendsGuardiancontaining Hutton’s paper on CD.

Discusses Henry Powell, the new vicar of Down, and plans for the parsonage.

letters.title: From J. J. Moulinié   20 October 1869
letters.summary: Wishes to translate CD’s forthcoming work on man into French.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   20 October 1869
letters.summary:
Looks forward toDescent, though he expects to find more to differ with than in any other of CD’s books.

Problems of usefulness of incipient organs and of the independent origin of similar complex organs are real difficulties.

Plans a little book on "Distribution of animals".

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   21 October 1869
letters.summary:
Anticipates that all their differences are fated to find expression in projected book on man.

Offers his early MS with useful references related to the distribution of animals. Hopes ARW’s book will not be "little".

letters.title: From Emile Alglave   22 October 1869
letters.summary: Has learned CD will soon publish a new work, in three parts: I. "Descent of man", II. "On sexual selection", and III. "Expression of the emotions"; would like to translate one part for inclusion inRevue des Cours[Littéraires et]Scientifiques, and at the same time translate and publish the complete work for France.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   22 October [1869]
letters.summary: His book [Descent] will not be ready for a year because of his health and the laboriousness of work on sexual selection. Has deferred arrangements for German translation, but would feel secure with JVC. Carl Vogt has offered to translate it.

letters.title: To J. J. Moulinié   23 October [1869]
letters.summary:
Would be delighted to have JJM translate new book [Descent].

Can CD legally bring out new edition ofOriginin France with new publisher? Has been ill-used by V. Masson and C. Royer. Wants edition without Royer’s preface.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   26 and 29 October [1869]
letters.summary: As CD is to be in London, AG will try to get to Queen Anne St to see him.

letters.title: From Carl Vogt   26 October 1869
letters.summary: Would like to translateDescentinto German, if Carus is not doing so.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   27 October 1869
letters.summary:
Observations onPassiflora.

Hildebrand on geraniums.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   [30 October 1869]
letters.summary: Has received a letter from Carl Vogt, expressing his readiness to translateDescentat the request of the publisher Franz Anton Ricker

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   30 October 1869
letters.summary: Carl Vogt has written that JVC is no longer a professor at Leipzig. Since this circumstance would provide more time to JVC for translation, Vogt withdraws his offer to translate [Descent]. CD asks JVC to accept the right to translate and to negotiate for best terms with whatever publisher he chooses.

letters.title: From Eduard Koch   30 October 1869
letters.summary:
Sends copy of C. J. Dub [Kurze Darstellung der Lehre Darwin’s über die Entstehung der Organismen(1870)].

Asks about appearance of CD’s next book.

Comments on the Duke of Argyll’sPrimeval man[1869].

New [4th] German edition ofOriginto appear soon.

letters.title: To Carl Vogt   30 October 1869
letters.summary:
Thanks for proposal about translation [ofDescent]. Will write to J. V. Carus to make agreement with publisher.

Hopes JVC’s holding CD’s views only secondary cause of loss of professorship.

letters.title: To ?   30 October [1869 or 1870]
letters.summary:
Comments on a case of crossing distant plants ofHabenaria

and on hermaphroditism in hybrid plants.

letters.title: To Francis Henry Salvin?   31 October 1869
letters.summary: Thanks correspondent for sending extracts about the jackal.

letters.title: From Federico Delpino   1 November 1869
letters.summary:
Comments on Hermann Crüger’s paper, sent by CD, on fertilisation of orchids [J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)8 (1865): 127–35].

Observations on dichogamy in grasses (wheat, rye, barley).

Has not yet read CD’s reply to his article on Pangenesis [Collected papers2: 158–60].

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   2 November 1869
letters.summary: Thinks it best for Murray’s to engrave the "Monkeys", etc. for themselves.

letters.title: From Charles Lyell   2 November 1869
letters.summary:
Comments on Huxley’s address ["Geological reform",Q. J. Geol. Soc. Lond.25 (1869): xxxviii–liii].

Physicists have ignored variation in sea-level in calculating effects.

Doubts if sun only source of heat.

Notes average depth of sea is 15 times height of land.

Criticises CD’s concept of permanent continents.

Sedimentary strata of Alleghenies must have derived from continent located where Atlantic is. Thinks enormous amount of denudation, submergence, and elevation may have accompanied relatively insignificant organic changes.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [3 November 1869]
letters.summary: Takes "much to heart" solar evidence for short age of the earth. Cites evidence for "long endurance of our existing continents". Comments on process of denudation.

letters.title: From George Cupples   [4–10 November 1869]
letters.summary: Weight statistics on deerhound puppies born 23 Sept 1869.

letters.title: To Eduard Koch   4 November 1869
letters.summary:
Thanks EK for Julius Dub’s work [see6961].

Has sent the new [5th] edition ofOriginto Carus.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   5 November 1869
letters.summary:
Sends a "guess" aboutMimosaleaf structure as an answer to one of CD’s questions.

Has found aPassiflora princeps.

letters.title: From J. J. Moulinié   5 November 1869
letters.summary:
Reinwald will be pleased to publishDescent.

He would also like to publish a Moulinié translation of the latest English edition ofOrigin. Negotiations with the old publisher are needed.

letters.title: From Frederick Smith   5 November 1869
letters.summary: Sends reference to stridulation in an article aboutScolytusby Dr Chapman "Observations on the economy of British species ofScolytus",Entomol. Mon. Mag.6 (1870): 126–31.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   6 November 1869
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for his kind offer [of translation rights forDescent].

Feels it a duty to make CD’s "way of looking to fields [rectefacts] under the guidance of ideas" known to his countrymen, especially since zoologists and physiologists seem to think science is nothing but the accumulation of facts and have almost forgotten to reason about them.

Explains that, contrary to Carl Vogt’s report to CD, he continues as Professor of Comparative Anatomy at Leipzig, but he has failed to get the place of the late Professor of Zoology, as he had hoped.

letters.title: From George Busk   7 November 1869
letters.summary: The Polyzoa CD saw emerging from cells of a particular growth appear to be parasites. The main growth is a species ofSertularia; the minute parasites take possession of vacated cells.

letters.title: To Antoinette Louisa Brown Blackwell   8 November [1869]
letters.summary: Thanks forStudies in general science[by A. B. Blackwell (1869)].

letters.title: To John Murray   8 November [1869]
letters.summary: Masson et Fils have brought out a third French edition [ofOrigin] without informing CD and without the advantage of the corrections of the 4th and 5th English editions. For this and other reasons CD wants to give translation rights for the 5th English edition to C. Reinwald.

letters.title: From John Murray   8 November [1869]
letters.summary: JM advises CD regarding his relations with Masson, the French publisher of theOrigin[1866], and the possibility of Reinwald’s publishing a translation of the 5th edition.

letters.title: To James Paget   8 November [1869]
letters.summary:
Thanks for confirmation about the extent of blushing.

Passed JP’s house but did not call; and now regrets his restraint.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   9 November [1869]
letters.summary: Glad to hear the news about the professorship was partly erroneous, but still wishes JVC to have the rights to translate [Descent]. Has written to Herr Koch [of Schweizerbart], but not in such a way as to commit JVC to publish with him.

letters.title: To Frederick Smith   9 November [1869]
letters.summary: CD thanks FS for his note onScolytus. Asks that his son [E. A. Smith] send proofs when the last woodcuts [for Coleoptera chapter ofDescent] are completed.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   11 November [1869]
letters.summary: A parcel of engravings has come; shall EAD send them on?

letters.title: From F. C. Donders   12 November 1869
letters.summary: CD’s questions [on expression] are more difficult than he thought and have led him further afield than he expected. If CD is not hurried, he promises less imperfect answers in six weeks. Thanks CD for drawing his attention to a really important question from different points of view.

letters.title: From Hermann Müller   12 November 1869
letters.summary: Would like Frederick Smith of the British Museum to determine whether or not some unidentified Westphalian bees are new species.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   13 November [1869]
letters.summary:
Congratulates JDH on his becoming a C.B.

Hard at work on sexual selection – weary of everlasting males and females, cocks and hens.

Has read J. H. Stirling vs Huxley on protoplasm [As regards protoplasm(1869)]

and E. B. Tylor on survival of old thoughts in modern civilisation.

Bentham’s Linnean Society [Presidential] Address [see6793] is worth its weight in gold in making converts. C. J. F. Bunbury is impressed by it.

Likes JDH’s review of K. F. Schimper’s work [Paléontologie végétale, inNature1 (1869): 48].

letters.title: ToNature   13 November [1869]
letters.summary:
Comments on A. W. Bennett’s letter [Nature1 (1869): 58] on fertilisation of winter-flowering plants. CD used net, not a bell-glass to coverLamium.

Refers to F. Delpino’s observations on fertilisation of grasses; CD is glad to say these observations are compatible with "the very general law that distinct individual plants must be occasionally crossed".

letters.title: From Charles-Ferdinard Reinwald   13 November 1869
letters.summary: Pleased to undertake publication of a new French translation ofOriginbased on the 5th English edition. J. J. Moulinié to be translator, with Carl Vogt reviewing his work. Will make arrangements to buy out the Royer edition [V. Masson et Fils; Guillaumin et Cie.].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   14 November 1869
letters.summary:
Describes how the offer of C.B. was made. He declined a knighthood. Murchison and Lyell are trying to get him made Knight Commander of the Star of India, but he does not think there is a chance. The Duke [of Argyll?] might do it, but does not like JDH’s Darwinism.

Next Presidency of Royal Society discussed: all (Brodie, the X Club botanists,et al.) are agreed on Lyell.

Everyone is disappointed withNature.

What did CD think of "Huxley’s rhapsody on Goethe’s ditto" [Nature1 (1869): 9–11]?

letters.title: To J. J. Moulinié   15 November [1869]
letters.summary: Makes suggestions for French translation ofOrigin.

letters.title: From Adolf Bernhard Meyer   16 November 1869
letters.summary:
Sends his translation of Wallace’sMalay Archipelago.

Wishes to translate 1858 essays by CD and Wallace from Linnean SocietyProceedings[Collected papers2: 3–19].

Plans journey to tropics.

Hopes to meet CD.

letters.title: To F. C. Donders   17 November [1869]
letters.summary:
There is no hurry for information. Delighted that FCD is making experiments.

It was a sincere pleasure to make FCD’s acquaintance.

letters.title: From Albert Hugh Jones   17 November 1869
letters.summary: Statistics on sexes of Lepidoptera reared this season. [SeeDescent1: 313.]

letters.title: From John Murray   17 November 1869
letters.summary:
JM reports sales ofFacts and arguments for Darwin,Variation, andOrigin[5th ed.].

Sends best wishes for success in putting down "Parisian blasphemers".

letters.title: From Camille Dareste   18 November [1869]
letters.summary: Asks CD to write a letter sponsoring him for the Chair of Comparative Physiology at Paris. There are some who do not think his work on artificial production of monstrosities belongs in physiology.

letters.title: To Christian Gottfried Ehrenberg   18 November [1869]
letters.summary: Thanks CGE for memoir on the Bacillariae of Mexico [Abh. K. Akad. Wiss. Berlin (Phys.)(1869): 1–66].

letters.title: From Roland Trimen   18 November 1869
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for his orchid paper ["Fertilization of orchids",Collected papers2: 138–56]. Comments briefly on orchids.

Discusses moths in which the wing underside is the most brightly coloured, and relates his observations on sexual selection by a moth,Syntomis.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   19 November [1869]
letters.summary:
Glad to know about C.B.

Thinks better ofNaturethan JDH does.

LikesAcademy.

Is reading Anton Kerner onTubocytisus[inDie Abhängigkeit der Pflanzen von Klima und Boden(1869)].

The genealogical tree reveals the very steps of the formation of the species.

Mlle Royer has brought out a third edition of her translation of theOriginwithout informing CD, so corrections to fourth and fifth English editions are lost. Has arranged for a new translator of the fifth English edition.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   20 November 1869
letters.summary:
Encloses a few additions [missing] for new [4th] German edition ofOrigin

and a new application to publish translation of [Descent].

letters.title: To George Cupples   20 November [1869]
letters.summary:
Thanks GC for his assistance. "The data for all that I have to say about the Scotch deer-hound are, owing to you, almost sufficient; and much better data than I have got in many other cases." [SeeDescent2: 260.]

Believes Dr Stirling would be compelled to admit some change in "the famous protoplasm in our domestic races, both in regard to the structure of the body & qualities of the mind".

letters.title: To Camille Dareste   20 November 1869
letters.summary: Glad Dareste is candidate for Paris Chair. No subject more important than modification of structure by direct action of changed conditions, and Dareste has thrown much light on subject. Believes monstrosities cannot be separated from slighter variations.

letters.title: To J. J. Moulinié   20 November 1869
letters.summary: Sends corrections of JJM’s translation ofOrigin. Sends preface.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   21 November 1869
letters.summary:
Has corresponded with Macmillan aboutNature.

Will get the Kerner book.

Mere guesses must determine which form to fix on as the type.

Raises questions about the genealogical tree.

Serves Mlle Royer right.

Lyell declines Royal Society Presidency; now look to W. R. Grove. Long postscript on JDH’s views about knighthood.

letters.title: From George Henslow   22 November 1869
letters.summary: Observations on fertilisation ofLapageria roseaby E. G. Henderson, florist of St John’s Wood.

letters.title: From Charles Layton   22 November 1869
letters.summary:
Appleton & Co. wish to be supplied with set of stereotype plates of CD’s new book [Descent] for American market; will pay for cost of plates, and 10% of sales to CD.

Also desire plates for new edition of theOrigin.

letters.title: From George Bentham   23 November 1869
letters.summary: Has heard that CD thinks GB is wrong on some points in his [Presidential] Address [to Linnean Society, see6793]. Asks CD to point out where he is wrong.

letters.title: To Charles Layton   24 November [1869]
letters.summary:
CD long anxious for new American edition ofOriginto incorporate corrections since 2d ed. [of 1860]; believes such updating has kept English and continental sales high. If Appleton unable to comply, he will ask Asa Gray to find another publisher.

Mentions possible arrangements for U. S. edition of new book [Descent].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   24 November [1869]
letters.summary: Sends title of Kerner’s book [see6997] and comments that AK does not give theoneparent form of the genus.

letters.title: From A. B. Meyer   24 November 1869
letters.summary: Wants to arrange a joint photograph of CD and Wallace for a publication on their lives and works.

letters.title: To George Bentham   25 November [1869]
letters.summary:
CD finds GB’s address interesting; assures him that he has never said GB was wrong on any point, but that there were differences between them, which he now thinks are not great.

Comments on specific parts of the address [see6793]: colonisation, variability of large and small genera, descent from a single parent or pair of parents, rapid multiplication and change in species, isolation.

letters.title: From Charles Boner   25 November [1869]
letters.summary:
Gives account of inherited blindness in a family,

and observations contravening CD’s view inVariationthat sheep and other domestic animals never run wild.

letters.title: From Charles Layton   25 November 1869
letters.summary:
Asks CD to have stereotype plates made of new edition ofOrigin[5th English], if type still standing, though Appleton will reset type if necessary. Warns there is smaller audience in the U. S. for "good scientific books".

Appleton would also like plates made of new book [Descent] when possible.

letters.title: From George Bentham   26 November 1869
letters.summary: Comments on CD’s observations on his address; clarifies his view of the importance of isolation, the effect of climate, the plants of S. Africa and Australia.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   26 [November 1869 or later]
letters.summary: Has seen J. J. Sylvester again.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   [27 November 1869]
letters.summary:
Encloses extract from a letter from Fritz Müller about humming-birds visitingPassiflora, "as a caution aboutPassiflorain contrast withTacsonia".

[Signed with CD’s name by Emma Darwin.]

letters.title: To A. B. Meyer   27 November [1869]
letters.summary:
Not willing to sit for photographer again.

ABM’s translation of Wallace’sMalay Archipelagohas not yet arrived.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   28 November 1869
letters.summary:
Agrees that it is wise to delay [publishing?] onPassiflora.

Puts queries he wants CD to send [to Fritz Müller] on bees visiting flowers in winter.

letters.title: From C. S. Bate   29 November 1869
letters.summary: Reports a case of a smooth-leaved holly tree with one branch of prickly leaves; is willing to supply more details.

letters.title: From Charles Boner   [December 1869 – early January 1870]
letters.summary: In answer to CD’s queries, relates further details about feral sheep: they are sterile when wild, but can become tame again.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   1 December [1869]
letters.summary:
Role of humming-birds in plant fertilisation.

Alexander Agassiz has visited Down.

Sales ofFacts and arguments for Darwin.

Encloses copy of T. H. Farrer letter [7015] and observations on the self-sterility ofEschscholzia.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [2 December 1869]
letters.summary: Discusses some calculations which he is doing for CD on the ratios of red and brown colouring in some animals.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   4 December [1869]
letters.summary:
Inquires about arrangements for the German translation and publication of their original Linnean Society papers [Collected papers2: 3–19].

ARW thinks he has hit upon a solution to problem of geological time.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   5 December [1869]
letters.summary: Further comments on arrangements for German translation of their joint paper.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   7 December [1869]
letters.summary: Encloses a letter to which he had replied and saw no need for further attention.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   8 December [1869]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary:
Is glad CD likes the new edition [ofPrehistoric times].

Has been lecturing in Scotland.

letters.title: From C. S. Bate   11 December 1869
letters.summary: Provides further detail on his smooth-leaved holly tree with a spiny-leaved branch; his gardener asserts no budding or grafting has taken place.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   11 December 1869
letters.summary: Asks CD’s advice on procuring rabbits for experiments [to test Pangenesis by transfusing alien blood into does and breeding from them].

letters.title: From J. T. Moggridge   12 December 1869
letters.summary:
Sends seeds ofLathyrusand suggests an advantage of climbing plants is to shed their seeds in places secure from animals.

Contrary to F. Delpino, in JTM’s experienceOphrys araniferais not sterile. However, seed germination is poor.

In a densely overgrown plotConvolvulus sabatius, not normally a twiner, becomes one.

Continues his extensive study on variability inArbutus, and speculates on selection in fruit shape.

letters.title: From Camille Dareste   13 December [1869]
letters.summary: CD’s letter on his behalf made a great impression, but his candidacy nevertheless failed, largely owing to the hostility of Claude Bernard. CD’s opinion sustains his belief that his work will be a service to science.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   18 December 1869
letters.summary:
Discusses dimorphic and trimorphic plants; mentions especially Rubiaceae and a dimorphic monocotyledon.

Notes observations on the monstrous male flowers ofBegonia,

and on self-sterile plants.

letters.title: From John Scott   21 December 1869
letters.summary:
Observations on expression and variation in Asian peoples: when colour of beard and hair differ, beard is always lighter. Differences in swimming strokes. Polydactylism.

Has just sent Hooker a paper on Sikkim tree-ferns [Trans. Linn. Soc. Lond.30 (1875): 1–44, read 1870].

Has had fever since the end of the rains.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   23 December [1869]
letters.summary: Praises FG’s book [Hereditary genius(1869)]. CD is converted by its argument. Previously CD believed men did not differ much in intellect, but only in zeal and hard work.

letters.title: From Charles Layton   23 December 1869
letters.summary:
Has received letter from Appleton’s that they agree to reprint from the latest edition of theOrigin[5th English] and will add corrections sent by CD.

They wish also to receive early sheets of new book [Descent] on which they will pay £10.

Will send cheque for sales ofOrigin, based on older agreement between Appleton’s and Asa Gray to pay CD 5%.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   24 December 1869
letters.summary: Greatly pleased by approbation from CD, whom he admires and whoseOrigindid much for him.

letters.title: To Anton Dohrn   25 December 1869
letters.summary: Thanks AD for his work. CD regrets he is not a better German scholar, but he must endeavour to understand AD’s views.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   26 December 1869
letters.summary:
Has seen some natives who express surprise by clapping the hand to mouth.

Reports on a tribe that sells its ugliest slaves in order to maintain its uniformly fine appearance.

In America in 1867 Darwinism was afait accompli. Asa Gray’s religious defence unnecessary after Theodore Parker and Emerson.

letters.title: From L. E. Becker   29 December 1869
letters.summary: Asks CD to which journal she should send herLychnispaper and whether she may quote extracts from his letters to her.

letters.title: From Anton Dohrn   30 December 1869
letters.summary:
He has gone through the whole embryology of the Crustacea and has arrived at a pretty well-established genealogy of the whole class; has even tried to write a history of the whole tribe. Finds he cannot adopt the old separation of Orders in the Class; the limits between them are indistinct.

Would like to study embryology ofLimulus. Asks CD’s help in obtaining a female specimen.

Outlines his proposal to establish a marine zoological station.

letters.title: To ?   [1870–82?]
letters.summary: Suggests the recipient catch the 4.12 train.

letters.title: From J. L. Sinclair   31 December 1869
letters.summary:
Would like CD’s opinion on his "theory of organic disturbance" and his "law of organic combination"; hopes CD might notice them in theAcademy.

Writes of his unfortunate circumstances.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   [1870–81]
letters.summary: Share dealings.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [1870–82]
letters.summary:
Two letters have arrived for WED.

Joseph has had two teeth out.

letters.title: From Federico Delpino   [1870]
letters.summary: Sends CD "L’applicazione della teoria Darwiniana ai fiori ed agli insetti visitatori dei fiori" [Bull. Soc. Entomol. Ital.2 (1870)]. Continues to support vitalism and teleology.

letters.title: To District Health Office   [after 1869]
letters.summary: Gives opinion on the merits of Mr [Stephen P. J.] Eng[leheart (Darwin family doctor)]. Believes he would make an excellent county officer if elected to the district office of health.

letters.title: From Charles Ottley Groom Napier   January 1870
letters.summary: COG-N sends, at the request of the late Lord Brougham, a copy of his work,The book of nature and the book of man[1870].

letters.title: From Rowland H. Wedgwood   [1870–82]
letters.summary: An instance of long memory in a horse.

letters.title: To?   [1870–82]
letters.summary: Printed acknowledgment of the receipt of a letter.

letters.title: To ?   [1870–82]
letters.summary: Query [possibly for publication] on ridges and furrows in pasture-land that had been ploughed long ago. Gives directions for measuring ridges on sloping land.

letters.title: From William Turner   3 January 1870
letters.summary: On the development of the mammae and the glands of the skin. R. A. v. Kölliker and Carl von Langer are the authorities [SeeDescent1: 209].

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [before 4 January 1870]
letters.summary: Humphrey does not think more bones in female os coccyx than in male. Because of maceration it is impossible to compare male and female skeletons. Has another coach while Stuart ill.

letters.title: To Anton Dohrn   4 January 1870
letters.summary:
The Zoological Garden has only one old adult male ofLimulus. When there were females, eggs wereneverobserved.

Encloses a separate letter [7071] about AD’s scheme [for a zoological station].

Suggests AD be cautious [in his work]. "Caution is almost the soul of science."

letters.title: To Abraham Dee Bartlett   5 January [1870]
letters.summary:
Thanks ADB forLimulus.

DoesCallithrix sciureuswrinkle the skin around its eyes when it screams? Do the eyes become suffused with moisture?

letters.title: To Charles Boner   [before 8 January 1870]
letters.summary:
Has received [read?] CB’s two works [Chamois hunting in the mountains of Bavaria(2d ed., 1860) andForest creatures(1871)] and has made use of them in his present book [Descent].

CB’s descriptions of the Tyrol make CD long to be "strong and young again to ramble over the mountains".

letters.title: From Charles Boner   8 January 1870
letters.summary:
Is glad CD likedChamois hunting[in Bavaria(1853, 1860)].

Regrets CD’s poor health.

Sends his book,Transylvania[1865].

letters.title: To Richard Kippist   10 January [1870 or 1871]
letters.summary: Is sending some books for the Linnean Society Library.

letters.title: From Adolf Reuter   11 January 1870
letters.summary:
Sends monstrous oranges,

red grape leaves,

and a bean with blue fruits (a hybrid ofPhaseolus vulgarisand aDolichosspecies).

letters.title: From Anton Dohrn   13 January 1870
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for his support and for his cautionary advice.

Will send his work on embryology of arthropods as soon as it is finished [Bau und Entwicklung der Arthropoden(1870)].

letters.title: To Albert Günther   13 January [1870]
letters.summary: Delighted with proofs of illustrations [forDescent]. Hopes AG is pleased with them, as they illustrate facts given on his authority.

letters.title: From Albert Günther   [after 13 January 1870]
letters.summary: Is glad CD likes the proofs; looks forward to the appearance of his work.

letters.title: To Adolf Reuter   15 January [1870]
letters.summary: Thanks AR for specimens of fruit.

letters.title: To Albert Günther   16 January [1870]
letters.summary: Invites AG to Down for a weekend with A. Newton, R. Swinhoe, and Hooker.

letters.title: To Richard Kippist   16 January [1870 or 1871]
letters.summary: Requests the return of some plates sent in error.

letters.title: From Henry Walter Bates   17 January 1870
letters.summary:
Returns CD’s MS [of entomological section ofDescent] marked with suggested alterations.

Suggests qualifications about rudimentary horn in femaleOnitis furcifer[SeeDescent1: 372].

Sends additional data on colour differences in sexes of longicorn Coleoptera [SeeDescent1: 367–8].

Suggests a modification of CD’s view of female coloration that would bring him "nearly into harmony" with Wallace.

letters.title: To Charles Boner   20 January [1870]
letters.summary:
Thanks CB forTransylvania[1865].

CD’s health has declined steadily. He must now be content to read about nature as described by CB and others.

letters.title: From Thomas Henry Huxley   21 January 1870
letters.summary: Refers to "Devonshire Man"’s attack on him ["Professor Huxley’s last new theory",Pall Mall Gaz.18 Jan 1870, p. 6]. His intention to answer – a waste, except for political bearing of Celt question ["Professor Huxley on Celts and Teutons",Pall Mall Gaz.21 Jan 1870, p. 6].

letters.title: From Alfred Russel Wallace   22 January 1870
letters.summary: Plans for his new book,Contributions to the theory of natural selection(1870), which will contain his papers on the subject.

letters.title: From Gilbert William Child   26 January [1870]
letters.summary: Sends 2d ed. of hisEssays on physiological subjects(1869).

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   26 January [1870]
letters.summary:
Response to ARW’s MS on geological time ["The measurement of geological time",Nature1 (1870): 399–401, 452–5].

Groans over [what is said about] man.

letters.title: From John Brodie Innes   28 January 1870
letters.summary: JBI sends clipping about a hybrid between a deer and a cow, from the same parish as the one reported in 1868.

letters.title: From William Boyd Dawkins   29 January [1870]
letters.summary: Discovery of skull of "River-bed" race of man near Corwen.

letters.title: To James Crichton-Browne   31 January [1870]
letters.summary: Asks JC-B to return copy of Duchenne [Mécanisme de la physionomie humaine(1862)] and sends some notes "as your former notes were of such extreme interest to me".

letters.title: From D. Appleton & Co. to Asa Gray   1 February 1870
letters.summary: Statement of sales of U. S. edition ofOrigin.

letters.title: From George Howard Darwin   [1 February 1870 or earlier]
letters.summary: Discusses buying a horse [for CD].

letters.title: From Mary Susan Owen   2 February [1870]
letters.summary: Asks CD to be godfather to her third child [Maud Mostyn Owen].

letters.title: From Robert Swinhoe   2 February 1870
letters.summary:
Sends a copy ofNotes and Queriesfor Francis Galton, as it contains a reply to Galton’s circular on hereditary genius.

RS much refreshed by his trip to Down.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [3 February 1870 or earlier]
letters.summary: Conveys some information on a quiet horse which CD may be able to purchase from a riding school.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [4 February 1870]
letters.summary: Believes he has found a quiet cob suitable for CD. Encloses a letter for CD to sign and send to the owner if he approves the idea.

letters.title: To the American Philosophical Society   5 February 1870
letters.summary: Sends thanks for election to American Philosophical Society.

letters.title: From M. S. Owen   7 February [1870]
letters.summary: CD’s goddaughter, Maud, has been christened.

letters.title: To Henrietta Emma Darwin   [8 February 1870]
letters.summary: Sends MS [of chs. 3 and 4, "Comparison of the mental powers of man and the lower animals",Descent] to HED for her criticism. CD fears parts are too much like a sermon; "who wd ever have thought I shd turn parson?"

letters.title: From H. E. Darwin   [after 8 February 1870]
letters.summary: Responds to note about the MS [Descent] with great interest and promises to obey his instructions. [See7124.]

letters.title: From Berry Benson   9 February 1870
letters.summary:
ComplimentsOrigin.

Sends extract about a waterplant to illustrate CD’s points about the means of dispersal in geographical distribution.

letters.title: To Alfred Newton   9 February [1870]
letters.summary: Was gratified "beyond measure" by AN’s comments on his pigeon chapter [inVariation] in the [Zoological]Record[5 (1868): 94–6]. AN is the first man capable of forming a judgment who seems to have thought anything of this part.

letters.title: From George P. Bissell   10 February 1870
letters.summary: Sends information on the distribution of various species in the U. S.

letters.title: From Robert Swinhoe   10 February 1870
letters.summary: Asks who the gentleman is who is studying cattle skulls; RS has some that he would like examined.

letters.title: From Alfred Newton   11 February 1870
letters.summary:
Is glad to hear that CD is pleased with AN’s notice of his work on pigeons.

He will not soon forget the pleasure of his visit to Down.

letters.title: To [?] 12 February [1870–82]
letters.summary: Send information about the bust of himself by Thomas Woolner and suggests applying to the sculptor himself about a cast.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   14 February 1870
letters.summary:
Louis Agassiz’s ill health means AG will not get an answer to CD’s query from him. Suggests CD ask Agassiz’s son, Alexander.

Has no details about the origin of the cat-like behaviour of his dog.

letters.title: From Jane Loring Gray   14 February 1870
letters.summary: About a dog she supposes was suckled by a cat, since it washes its face with its paws.

letters.title: From Edward Caldwell Rye   14 February 1870
letters.summary: Draws CD’s attention to a paper by Maurice Girard containing observations on the fertilisation of Orchidaceae by two species of Longicornia [Ann. Soc. Entomol. France9 (1869): xxxi–xxxii].

letters.title: From William Darwin Fox   15 February [1870]
letters.summary: Hopes CD is coping with the very hard winter.

letters.title: From G. W. Child   16 February [1870]
letters.summary: Criticises chapter on good effect of crossing inVariation: (1) does not accept that inbreeding alone results in degeneracy; (2) good effects of crossing exaggerated; (3) denies deleterious effects of close marriage in humans.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   16 February 1870
letters.summary: Sends specimens ofPassifloraand seeds for T. H. Farrer [letter enclosed with7188].

letters.title: From William Swale   16 February [1870?]
letters.summary: Sends CD some notes on the habits of the "American Blight Bird" in New Zealand.

letters.title: From William Thierry Preyer   [before 17 February 1870]
letters.summary:
Notes the differences in haemoglobin between species; this proves, to WP, that natural selection does not act only on morphological development.

Remarks on the differences and similarities in the effects of prussic acid on different groups of animals.

Questions CD on his early education and influences.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [c.17 February 1870]
letters.summary: Ask whether CD would like to subscribe again to National Education League. Describes the League’s goals.

letters.title: To Gustav Jäger   17 February 1870
letters.summary: Encloses his letter to GJ [6885], which was returned.

letters.title: To W. T. Preyer   17 February [1870]
letters.summary:
Comments on effects of prussic acid on different individuals of the same species and other physiological research by WP.

Provides information about his studies in Edinburgh and Cambridge and qualifications he had forBeaglevoyage. Describes influence of R. E. Grant and J. S. Henslow.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   18 February [1870]
letters.summary:
Invites WDF to visit.

Describes activities of his children.

letters.title: From Vladimir Onufrievich Kovalevsky   20 February [1870]
letters.summary:
Moritz Wagner is going to attack selection theory in his new book on his travels in America [Naturwissenschaftliche Reisen im tropischen Amerika(1870)].

K. G. Semper may attack CD’s theory of coral islands.

letters.title: To Joseph Dalton Hooker   21 February [1870]
letters.summary:
Has read the notes on Rond [Round] Island which he owes to JDH. What an enigma its flora and fauna present, especially the problem of monocotyledons! Asks JDH’s opinion.

A new book on St Helena confirms CD’s observations.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   22 February [1870–9?]
letters.summary: Seeks investment advice.

letters.title: To Robert Garner   22 February [1870–1]
letters.summary: Thanks for sending him a hybrid.

letters.title: To V. O. Kovalevsky   22 February [1870]
letters.summary:
"I have received a very large box full of beautiful tea from Russia yesterday … my life is as regular & monotonous as a clock.

I make sure, but wofully slow progress, with my new book."

letters.title: To James Orton   24 February [1870]
letters.summary:
Thanks JO for hisThe Andes and the Amazon.

Is sorry he has failed to get any information on the horse’s tooth.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   26 February [1870]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary:
Congratulations [on election to Parliament]; hopes science will not suffer because of politics.

Previously wrote inquiring about savages and suicide, but JL need not hurry to answer.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   27 February and 1 March 1870
letters.summary:
Forwards part of a note [by Mrs L. Agassiz] asking AG to tell CD that Agassiz has never been able to secure one of the fishes sitting on eggs.

In P.S., AG adds, "Agassiz evidently regrets having abused you in former times."

letters.title: From John Lubbock   27 February [1870]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Suicide is rare among savages [seeDescent1: 94].

letters.title: From Federico Delpino   28 February 1870
letters.summary:
Transformism explains rudimentary organs, and teratology, which are otherwise inexplicable.

Looking forward to publication ofDescent

and CD’s expected book on "Variation in nature" [seeVariation1: 4].

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   28 February [1870]
letters.summary:
Describes his brother Alexander’s discovery of male ofBonellia, a striking example of dimorphism. Encloses a plate with notes on his brother’s work.

The difficulty his wife, Sofya Kovalevsky, has had as a woman in being admitted to Berlin University. Kirchow [Gustav Robert Kirchhoff], at Heidelberg, has taken an interest in her.

letters.title: To H. E. Darwin   [March] 1870
letters.summary: Responds to her suggested corrections [ofDescent].

letters.title: From Hensleigh Wedgwood   [March 1870]
letters.summary: On the expression of disagreeable surprise.

letters.title: From Charles Edward Cutts Birchall Appleton   2 March [1870]
letters.summary: CD was good enough to send notice of his new book [Descent] for the first number of theAcademy; asks for further contributions and suggestions.

letters.title: From George Henslow   3 March 1870
letters.summary: Experiments withLapageria.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [7 March 1870]
letters.summary:
Does not give much for botanical results of Round Island, but the zoology is wonderful.

Lyell’s new book [The student’s elements of geology(1870)]. Urges Lyell to make itElementary principles.

Grove is disgusted with CD for being disquieted by William Thomson: "Take another dose of Huxley’s penultimate address to Geol. Soc." [Q. J. Geol. Soc. Lond.25 (1869): 28–53].

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   7 March [1870?]
letters.summary: Would like to call at 10 o’clock on Wednesday morning.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   8 March [1870]
letters.summary:
Would like to see JDH becomeSirJ. H. Does not think JDH owes his position in science to his father.
