Sends questions on Round Island – if JDH should write [to Henry Barkly?].

Has he read Federico Delpino on Marantaceae [Nuovo G. Bot. Ital.1 (1869): 293–206]?

letters.title: From St George Jackson Mivart   8 March [1870]
letters.summary: Will not be returning to London for a week; writes to save CD’s calling.

letters.title: From Hermann Müller   8 March 1870
letters.summary: HM intends studying bees to find evidence supporting CD’s theories. His work has shown him there are problems in separating species from varieties, and has also revealed many surprising instances of variation in habits.

letters.title: To Thomas Woolner   10 March [1870]
letters.summary: Thanks for drawing. ‘The "Woolnerian tip" is worth anything to me.’

letters.title: To Hermann Müller   14 March 1870
letters.summary: Interested that HM is studying structure of insects in relation to flowers.

letters.title: From James Crichton-Browne   15 March 1870
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for copy ofOrigin.

Encloses extensive, but incomplete, notes on expression among the insane, dealing specifically with blushing and the actions of the platysma and grief muscles.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   15 March 1870
letters.summary: Interim report on the experiments with rabbits [to test Pangenesis].

letters.title: To Asa Gray   15 March [1870]
letters.summary:
The "man-essay" [Descent] is "very interesting but very difficult".

Cat-like behaviour in dogs.

Thanks for information from Louis Agassiz;

wishes he could feel he deserves what Alexander Agassiz says of him.

letters.title: To Edwin Ray Lankester   15 March [1870]
letters.summary: CD much interested by ERL’s book [On comparative longevity(1870)]. Is pleased to find ERL refers to CD’s "despised child" Pangenesis, and is also pleased how thoroughly ERL appreciates Herbert Spencer, a philosopher perhaps equal to any that has lived.

letters.title: From R. F. Albrecht   16 March 1870
letters.summary:
Is currently at work on the development in birds of organs of flight according to CD’s principles; asks permission to quote CD in stating the theory.

Urges CD to republish his works in a collected edition, to make them more readily available to Germans.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   17 March 1870
letters.summary: Experiments are not going well, but the quantity of blood transfused was small.

letters.title: From Georg Recht   17 March 1870
letters.summary: Explains that law of inertia, and most of modern mechanics, is all wrong. Explains his concept of "elasticity" of bodies. Applies it to physiology.

letters.title: From John Jenner Weir   17 March 1870
letters.summary: Describes the unusual appearance of a horse whose mother had previously borne a foal by a quagga. The effect of one mating on the subsequent pregnancy of another mating is explained by JJW using Pangenesis.

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   17 March [1870]
letters.summary: CD thinks JJW’s account [in7137] is significant for a theory of generation and should go to some scientific society; suggests additional data is needed. Quotes cases of subsequent progeny apparently affected by a previous impregnation. Perhaps not prudent to allude to "despised" Pangenesis, which CD fully believes will have its day.

letters.title: To James Crichton-Browne   18 March 1870
letters.summary: JC-B’s essays are the fullest CD has received. His observations on blushing closely agree with James Paget’s. Platysma and horror: Duchenne’s statement doubtful.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   22 March 1870
letters.summary: Variety in rabbits less than he hoped for; will try a new mode of transfusion.

letters.title: To Frances Power Cobbe   23 March [1870?]
letters.summary:
Has read and enjoyed the Kant that FPC sent.

Returns P. C. Despine [?Psychologie naturelle(1868)].

letters.title: To Albert Günther   23 March [1870]
letters.summary: Expresses his "unbounded admiration" for Mr Ford’s woodcuts [forDescent]. Thanks AG for his kindness.

letters.title: To ?   23 March [1870–1]
letters.summary: Declines offer of book on physics.

letters.title: To W. H. Flower   25 March [1870]
letters.summary: Thanks WHF for his very good lecture.

letters.title: From F. P. Cobbe   28 March [1870?]
letters.summary: Pleased to have encouraged CD to look at Kant.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   29 March 1870
letters.summary:
His observations on mimicry in butterflies

and self-sterility in plants.

letters.title: From H. E. Darwin   [30 March 1870]
letters.summary: Describes crying in an infant.

letters.title: From Armand de Quatrefages   30 March 1870
letters.deprecated: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.sender: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.summary:
He and Milne-Edwards are nominating CD for the Académie Française.

Sending book [Charles Darwin et ses précurseurs Français(1870)].

Despite their differences of opinion, expresses his respect and admiration.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   31 March 1870
letters.summary: Better news about the rabbits.

letters.title: From James Orton   31 March 1870
letters.summary:
JO found fossil shells in the Amazon Valley, which discredits Agassiz’s claim of a glacial origin.

Would like Huxley’s opinion of the fossil horse’s tooth from Quito.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   31 March [1870]
letters.summary:
Thanks for a woodcut sent by ARW forDescent.

Congratulations on his removal from London,

and praise of his review of Francis Galton ["Hereditary genius",Nature1 (1870): 501–3]. CD agrees with every word of it.

letters.title: To [Henry Hussey Vivian?]   [April or May 1870?]
letters.summary: Discusses the reasons for inserting questions on consanguineous marriages in the forthcoming Census.

letters.title: From Erasmus Alvey Darwin   1 April [1870?]
letters.summary: "Your financial operations excite my envy beyond words." Reports on stock just received.

letters.title: To James Crichton-Browne   2 April [1870]
letters.summary: Copy of Duchenne [see7089] has not arrived; CD is concerned that it may be lost.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   8 April 1870
letters.summary: The mark he had thought a variation is not, and he thinks his infusion still too small even when the blood is defibrinised.

letters.title: From William Winwood Reade   [c.8 or 9 April 1870]
letters.summary:
Brief observations on expression in Africa.

Alexander Agassiz is a good investigator, who differs with his father on evolution.

The behaviour of women and savages is a little easier to understand than that of civilised men.

letters.title: From Albert Günther   [c.9 April 1870]
letters.summary:
CD should soon receive woodcuts.

R. A. v. Kölliker would much like to visit CD.

letters.title: To John Murray   9 April [1870]
letters.summary:
FindsAcademycontains valuable matter for his work.

Descentprogresses slowly – will not be ready for press for several months.

letters.title: From Charles Warren Stoddard   11 April 1870
letters.summary: Writes of some observations on the Sandwich Islands.

letters.title: From Albert Günther   12 April 1870
letters.summary: Arranges to come to Down with R. A. v. Kölliker.

letters.title: From Julius Victor Carus   16 April [1870]
letters.summary:
Would like to visit CD at Down.

[Fourth] German edition ofOriginwill be out in a few weeks.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   18 April 1870
letters.summary: Regrets he cannot come to Down on day suggested.

letters.title: To Rudolf Albert von Kölliker   18 April [1870]
letters.summary:
Has sent off specimens ofVirgulariabut fears they are in bad state. He could not find his dried specimens. Encloses notes that can be relied upon but may be of little use.

Also encloses a memorandum for Prof. K. G. Semper.

CD thinks Alcide d’Orbigny may have given name ofVirgularia pectagonica.

CD enjoyed RAvK’s recent visit [see7164].

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [20 April 1870]
letters.summary:
Is leaving tonight for Genoa;

sends a French paper [not identified].

letters.title: From George Rolleston   20 April 1870
letters.summary: Asks CD to look at the "special phylogonies" on pp. 138 and 152 of his book [Forms of animal life(1870)]. His comments are based on reading Haeckel, who is highly speculative and quite wrong.

letters.title: To Tord Tamerlan Teodor Thorell   20 April 1870
letters.summary: Thanks TTTT for his study of European spiders [On European spidersPart 1 (1869–70)] which bases its classification system on the theory of evolution.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   20 April [1870]
letters.summary: Appreciation of eulogy in preface of ARW’s book [Theory of natural selection].

letters.title: From Giovanni Canestrini   21 April 1870
letters.summary:
Italian translation [ofVariation] is delayed, but printing should begin soon.

Will send CD one of his writings in which he defends the natural descent of man [Origin dell’uomo, 2d ed. (1870)].

CD’s theory is making great progress in Italy and daily gains supporters.

letters.title: To St G. J. Mivart   21 April [1870]
letters.summary:
On amount of modification and lines of descent in determining the position in man.

Reference to StGJM’s article "On the appendicular skeleton of the primates"Phil. Trans. R. Soc.[157 (1867): 299–430],

and his [and James Murie’s] article on lemurs ["On the anatomy of Lemuroidea"]Trans. Zool. Soc.[7 (1872): 1–114].

letters.title: From St G. J. Mivart   22 April 1870
letters.summary: Is not prepared to express an opinion on man’s origin. On pure anatomical grounds he would form a family of the higher division of the primates, but if man’s intellectual, moral, and religious nature is considered, then "he differs more from an Anthropoid Ape than such an Ape differs from a lump of granite".

letters.title: To St G. J. Mivart   23 April [1870]
letters.summary: Thanks StGJM for prompt answer correcting inaccuracies in CD’s notes on StGJM’s opinions. Expects "universal disapprobation" when he publishesDescent.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   24 April 1870
letters.summary: Sends insect that carries dead ants, dead leaves, etc., on its back, as protective imitation.

letters.title: From St G. J. Mivart   25 April 1870
letters.summary: Apologises for saying more than was necessary in his previous letter. Although he feels gratitude and esteem for CD, he execrates those who use natural selection to oppose man’s higher interests and impede his advance. Has seen Huxley’sMan’s place in naturefor sale among a crowd of obscenities at most Italian railway stations.

letters.title: From Lucy Caroline Wedgwood   [25 April 1870]
letters.summary: Aggressive behaviour of dogs and horses.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   26 April 1870
letters.summary: Rabbits still running true; hopes to increase alien blood to 30%.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   [27 April 1870?]
letters.summary: Is much obliged for information [about rabbits?].

letters.title: From George Cupples   29 April 1870
letters.summary:
Will send deerhound puppy.

Is critical of Herbert Spencer.

letters.title: To Ferdinand Vandeveer Hayden   2 May [1870]
letters.summary: Thanks for copies of FVH’s "Preliminary field report [of the U. S. Geological Survey] of Colorado and New Mexico" [Am. J. Sci.49 (1870): 258–63] andGeological report[of the exploration]of the Yellowstone[and Missouri]River[s under the direction of Captain W. F. Reynolds(1869)].

letters.title: From John Michels   3 May 1870
letters.summary: Sends drawings of atypicalGeraniumand honeysuckle pollen-grains. Would they produce variation in seedlings?

letters.title: To C. W. Stoddard   5 May [1870]
letters.summary: Discusses flora of Sandwich Isles. "There is nothing I shd enjoy so much as to visit California, but I am growing old & my health is weak".

letters.title: From L. C. Wedgwood   [5 May 1870]
letters.summary:
Expression in horses.

Crying in babies.

letters.title: From W. T. Preyer   9 May 1870
letters.summary: Sends his "Charles Darwin, eine biographische Skizze" [Das Ausland2 Apr 1870].

letters.title: From H. H. Vivian   10 May 1870
letters.summary: About the insertion of a column on marriage of cousins in the census form.

letters.title: To H. H. Vivian   11 May [1870]
letters.summary: Thanks for HHV’s interest in the census [CD’s plan to add questions on consanguineous marriage to the census] on which CD hopes to persuade Sir J. Lubbock to speak.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   12 May 1870
letters.summary: Good news: one little rabbit has a white forefoot.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   12 May 1870
letters.summary:
Crossing experiments and self-sterility [inEschscholzia].

Pangenesis.

Hermann Müller on insect adaptations for fertilisation of flowers.

CD working on book on man and sexual selection.

letters.title: To Frans Cornelis Donders   13 May [1870]
letters.summary: In a fortnight will begin to arrange notes on expression. Asks for FCD’s conclusions about the contraction of eye muscles. Is interested in abstract of FCD’s experiments on "rate of travelling of the nervous powers".

letters.title: To Thomas Henry Farrer   13 [May 1870]
letters.summary:
Encloses part of letter from Fritz Müller onPassiflora, with seeds.

Is endeavouring to have included in next census a question as to whether the parents in each household are cousins.

letters.title: From Patrick Nicol   13 May 1870
letters.summary: Answers to CD’s queries on expression; observations on the facial expressions of the insane.

letters.title: To W. T. Preyer   15 May 1870
letters.summary: Comments on WP’s biographical article on CD. Asks him to thank O. F. Peschel for his present of the publication [Das Ausland2 Apr 1870].

letters.title: From F. C. Donders   17 May 1870
letters.summary:
The illness and death of his daughter have delayed his answers to CD’s queries. He has, however, worked on the circulation of the eye and has almost finished a paper on it, which he will send to CD. In general, the views of Charles Bell are confirmed.

As for CD’s second query, he doubts that the relationship exists, but will answer fully in next letter.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   17 May 1870
letters.summary: On death of his wife. Botany a solace.

letters.title: From C. E. C. B. Appleton   18 May [1870]
letters.summary: Asks CD to review Wallace’s recent book of essays [Natural selection(1870)], particularly the new essay, which questions the applicability of natural selection to man.

letters.title: To F. C. Donders   19 May 1870
letters.summary:
Expresses sympathy [on death of FCD’s daughter].

Will be grateful for his paper and letter.

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   20 May 1870
letters.summary:
Concern over Wallace’s book [Contributions to the theory of natural selection(1870)] and its apparent backsliding from Darwinian theory. HWB suggests that only CD is capable of criticising the book.

HWB hopes not too much was made over his few comments on man in M. F. Somerville’s book [Physical geography, revised ed. (1870)].

letters.title: From Federico Delpino   20 May 1870
letters.summary:
Responds to CD’s request forCannaseeds.

Studying dichogamy inLotus. Describes mechanism that pumps pollen on to a visiting bee. Corrects Axell onLotus.

letters.title: From Charles Renard   20 May 1870
letters.deprecated: Charles (Carl Ivanovich) RenardSecretary, Soc. Imp. Nat. Moscou
letters.sender: Charles (Carl Ivanovich) RenardSecretary, Soc. Imp. Nat. Moscou
letters.summary: Announces CD’s election as Honorary Member of the Société Impériale des Naturalistes de Moscou.

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   [22 May 1870]
letters.summary: Explains why he has declined writing a review for Messrs Appleton.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [22 May 1870]
letters.summary:
Willy is back from New Zealand. JDH perturbed by what to do with him.

J. W. Dawson’s Bakerian lecture for Royal Society is full of errors, and JDH is forced to recommend that it not be published. [An abstract of the lecture was published: "On the pre-Carboniferous floras of north-eastern America",Proc. R. Soc. Lond.18 (1869–70): 333–5.]

letters.title: To Alfred Newton   [22 May 1870]
letters.summary:
Intends to see Adam Sedgwick.

Arranges to meet AN.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   25 May [1870]
letters.summary:
Concern about futures of Willy [Hooker] and Horace [Darwin].

Henrietta [Darwin] back from Cannes.

CD has been to Cambridge to visit Frank [Darwin]. Saw Sedgwick, who took him to the [Geological] Museum and utterly exhausted him. Humiliating to be "killed by a man of 86".

Saw Alfred Newton.

CD has been working away on man, to much greater length (as usual) than expected,

and on cross- and self-fertilisation.

Does JDH happen to have seeds ofCanna warszewicziimatured in some hot country?

Sympathises with JDH on Dawson’s paper – amusing that Dawson hashes up E. D. Cope’s and L. Agassiz’s views.

letters.title: From James Philip Mansel Weale   [25 May 1870]
letters.summary: Behaviour of ants.

letters.title: To E. P. Wright   25 May [1870]
letters.summary: Thanks for copy of part one of EPW’sSpicilegia biologica(Wright 1870).

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   26 May 1870
letters.summary:
Not discouraged by F. Müller’sPassiflora.

Observations on insects visiting barberries.

letters.title: From F. C. Donders   27 May 1870
letters.summary: Has finished the article [on the action of the eyelids inNed. Arch. Geneeskd. & Natuurkd.5 (1870), also see7238]; summarises: the occlusion of the eyelids protects the vessels, and the eye itself, against the danger of pressure caused by excessive expiratory action. The weakness of the conclusion is that the extent of the danger caused by the pressure to the normal state of the eye is not precisely known.

letters.title: From F. C. Donders   28 May 1870
letters.summary: A detailed description of the physiological and anatomical processes related to the prolonged involuntary contraction of the orbicular muscles and the secretion of tears (as in retching, violent coughing, or laughing). [SeeExpression, p. 160.].

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   28 May [1870]
letters.summary:
Fertilisation of barberries.

Passiflora.

Is continuing his experiments on the comparative growth of crossed and self-fertilised plants.

letters.title: To Armand de Quatrefages   28 May [1870]
letters.deprecated: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.recipient: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.summary:
Comments on QdeB’s volume [Charles Darwin et ses précurseurs Français(1870)]. Mentions error concerning his views onParusand nuthatch.

DiscussesCanis magellanicus.

Discusses reception of his views in France and Germany.

letters.title: To Charles Renard   28 May 1870
letters.deprecated: secretary of Soc. Imp. Nat. Moscou
letters.recipient: secretary of Soc. Imp. Nat. Moscou
letters.summary: Thanks Society for honour of his election as Honorary Member.

letters.title: From Adam Sedgwick   30 May 1870
letters.summary: Writes of CD’s recent visit to Cambridge and the joy it gave him.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [31 May 1870]
letters.summary:
Sends enclosure [a letter from Lady Lyell?]. He is choking with vanity.

Is going to send Willy to Mr La Touche in Salop; he brought up young Colenso and Frank Lyell. Some of his friends will think he is sending his son into a nest of young adders!

letters.title: To Federico Delpino   1 June [1870]
letters.summary:
Thanks FD for seeds ofCanna.

Still thinks it would be worth FD’s while looking at the fertilisation ofLotus; does not think Frank Darwin has exaggerated the novelty of the contrivance.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   1 June 1870
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his help and encouragement in his series of experiments [to test Pangenesis].

letters.title: To Adam Sedgwick   1 June [1870]
letters.summary: Thanks AS for his kindness towards himself and his family. Looks back with great satisfaction to his last visit ("as it will probably prove") to Cambridge.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   2 [June 1870]
letters.summary:
Returns H. C. Watson’s letter.

CD must study JDH’s manner of arrangement of varieties and subspecies, etc.

letters.title: To F. C. Donders   3 June [1870]
letters.summary:
Thanks FCD for information.

Hopes that translation of his paper will appear inDublin Journal.

Notes experience of his son [Leonard Darwin] on engorgement of eyes with blood. Discusses secretion of tears when eye muscles are involuntarily contracted.

letters.title: To James Paget   4 June [1870]
letters.summary: Asks to have observations made of a person retching violently, but ejecting nothing from stomach, in order to test relation between spasmodic contraction of orbicular muscles and tears. CD believes tears are caused by matter filling nostrils.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   4 June 1870
letters.summary:
The Negro’s idea of beauty is the same as white man’s.

Believes the Jollops select for blackness.

Native immunity from coast fever is not complete.

Has found stone instruments.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   5 June 1870
letters.summary: Has sent F. Müller "a long screed" about thePassiflora.

letters.title: From James Crichton-Browne   6 June 1870
letters.summary:
Returns copy of Duchenne (found in cupboard) with notes [see7221].

Sends photograph of woman patient with hair standing on end.

letters.title: From James Crichton-Browne   [6 June 1870]
letters.summary: Comments on various figures [in Duchenne’sMécanisme].

letters.title: From Robert Cecil   7 June 1870
letters.summary: Informs CD that Oxford proposes to confer an honorary degree upon him.

letters.title: To James Crichton-Browne   8 June [1870]
letters.summary:
Duchenne [Mécanisme] has arrived. Has been testing the photographs with 20 or 30 persons; when all or nearly all agree with Duchenne, CD trusts him. Not one understood the "contracted pyramidal of the nose". CD does not think the so-called muscle of lasciviousness worth exhibiting.

His MS [ofDescent] is so large he may print only what he has, and make a second volume of what he is now writing on expression.

Discusses photographs he would like to have: baby screaming, person in paroxysm of fear.

letters.title: From Benjamin Collins Brodie   9 June 1870
letters.summary: Hears CD may come to Oxford at Commencement to receive an honorary degree. Invites CD, his wife, and daughter to stay at his house. [CD declined Hon. D.C.L. on grounds of ill health.]

letters.title: From John Murray   10 June [1870]
letters.summary: Asks CD whether he is far enough along with his new work [Descent] to allow him to announce it as a forthcoming publication in his next quarterly list.

letters.title: From St G. J. Mivart   11 June 1870
letters.summary:
Asks by what action CD believes bee, spider, and fly orchids came to resemble their namesakes

and how the beauty of bivalves could have been produced by natural or sexual selection.

letters.title: From David Forbes   13 June 1870
letters.summary:
Has completed a memoir on the Aymara Indians of Bolivia [J. Ethnol. Soc.n.s. 2 (1870): 193–305] and is going to lecture on them.

Believes he has data relevant to CD’s work on man.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [13 June 1870?]
letters.summary: Orders seeds, ripened in Algiers; imported seed would be of no use. [Forwarded to Algiers by JDH, see7272.]

letters.title: To St G. J. Mivart   13 June [1870]
letters.summary:
In his reply to [7227] CD questions the significance of the supposed likeness of the bee, spider, and fly orchids to their presumed namesakes.

He thinks that the beauty of shells is altogether incidental and of no use to the animals.

letters.title: From F. V. Hayden   14 June 1870
letters.summary: Sends maps of U. S. Far West for CD to follow explorations.

letters.title: To R. A. von Kölliker   14 June 1870
letters.summary:
Thanks for RAvK’s work [Anatomisch-systematische Beschreibung der Alcyonarien, pt 1,Die Pennatuliden(1870)].

Asks whether muscles to quills of porcupine are striped. Are they homologous to muscles of ordinary hairs? Could unstriped muscles develop into striped?

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   14 June [1870]
letters.summary:
Asks about birds erecting feathers when enraged or frightened. Interested in examples of expression in birds and animals.

Tells of the sheldrake dancing on tidal sands to make worms come out.

letters.title: From Thomas W. Wood   14 June 1870
letters.summary:
Orange-tip butterfly at rest imitates a flower.

The argus pheasant cannot be explained by natural selection.

letters.title: To ?   14 June [1870]
letters.summary: When CD comes to London in ten days, he will "immediately call on you and explain why I cannot at once answer your question".

letters.title: From Louis Rérolle   15 June 1870
letters.summary: French translation ofOrchidsis published.

letters.title: From T. W. Wood   16 June 1870
letters.summary: Argus pheasant.

letters.title: From Joachim Barrande   19 June 1870
letters.summary:
Encloses a copy of a letter he has written to a French geologist. In it he raises objections to evolutionary theory:

why are corals inadequately represented in the fossil record?

How can one explain the widespread appearance and then disappearance of groups like the trilobites?

If Mollusca and Articulata have a common ancestor, why are not ancient forms more akin than present ones?

letters.title: From George Cupples   20 June 1870
letters.summary:
Will send CD a deerhound puppy.

Reaffirms his statement that dogs in breeding form decided preferences toward each other, based on size, colour, or character.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   20 June [1870]
letters.summary: Asks for figures of embryos by A. Ecker and T. L. W. Bischoff to copy [forDescent, ch. 1].

letters.title: To F. C. Donders   21 June 1870
letters.summary:
Comments on translation of FCD’s paper ["On the action of the eyelids",Arch. Med.5 (1870): 20–38].

Speculates that closing eyelids may protect eyes from vibrations.

Discusses publication ofExpression.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   22 June 1870
letters.summary: Reports "shindy" at Oxford over persons proposed for doctorate. Pusey assented to CD’s being "doctored" to keep out seven worse devils.

letters.title: From Louis Rérolle   22 June 1870
letters.summary: Copies of the French translation ofOrchidswere sent to C. V. Naudin, Quatrefages de Bréau, and Charles Martins at CD’s request and to Duchartre, Brongniart, Baillon, Lecoq, Godron, and Alphonse de Candolle on Rérolle’s initiative.

letters.title: From John and Emma Pender   [before 23 June 1870]
To Ernst Haeckel   23 June [1870]
letters.summary:
Comments on new edition of EH’s book [Natürliche Schöpfungsgeschichte, 2d ed. (1870)].

Mentions his own book [Descent].

Visit by Kölliker.

letters.title: From Hermann Hoffmann   23 June 1870
letters.summary: Sends drawings of the foot of chicken showing swimming membrane.

letters.title: From Osbert Salvin   24 June 1870
letters.summary: Publication Committee of Zoological Society has granted CD use of woodblock from the Society’sProceedings.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   25 June 1870
letters.summary: Two, perhaps all three, doe [rabbits] are sterile after the transfusions; will try another method.

letters.title: From St G. J. Mivart   [25 June 1870?]
letters.summary: Sets a time for CD to call.

letters.title: To Edward Burnett Tylor   25 June 1870
letters.summary:
Mentions passage on gestures in EBT’sEarly history of mankind[1865].

Asks Tylor whether the deaf and dumb use opposite signs for objects, qualities, etc., of an opposite nature.

letters.title: To Frederick Bates   26 June [1870?]
letters.summary: Thanks forTroxbeetles which have been forwarded [to London], but unfortunately CD has no microscope here. Is "in despair how to observe them … they sham dead" and are not inclined to stridulate.

letters.title: From T. W. Wood   [after 26 June 1870]
letters.summary: Is surprised to find CD disagrees about the argus [see7229]. TWW finds others he has consulted, including Edward Blyth, agree with him.

letters.title: From Bartholomew James Sulivan   27 June 1870
letters.summary:
Tells of his health and family matters.

Congratulates CD on being honoured by Oxford.

Discusses the state of Tierra del Fuego and the success of missionaries there.

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   27 June 1870
letters.summary:
On behaviour of birds when frightened and when threatening.

PurpleCytisusgrafted onto yellow stock produces some yellow flowers.

Mutations in rabbits.

Cites case of variegated leaf form of one plant apparently spreading to a neighbour.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   28 June 1870
letters.summary:
[William Rathbone] Greg is author [of "Failure of ""natural selection"" in the case of man",Fraser’s Magazine78 (1868): 353–62].

Comments on findings in J. M. Duncan [Fecundity, fertility, sterility and allied topics(1866)].

Saw A. D. Bartlett about monkeys.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   [29 June 1870]
letters.summary: Encloses seeds from Fritz Müller, of a species ofPassiflora, fertilised by a humble-bee.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   29 June 1870
letters.summary: Has procured aPassifloraflower at last. Structure suited for humming-birds rather than bees.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [29 June 1870]
letters.summary: Asks whether JDH can send seeds ofHibiscus africanusand ofNolana prostrataraised at Kew.

letters.title: From E. C. Rye   29 June 1870
letters.summary: Draws CD’s attention to a paper inAmerican Naturalist[3 (1869): 109] describing honey-bees killed by entanglement in pollen-masses ofAsclepias.

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   29 June [1870]
letters.summary:
On birds erecting feathers.

Comments on production of buds inCytisus.

Discusses case of rabbit-breeding which affected subsequent progeny of female.

letters.title: To W. W. Reade   30 June [1870]
letters.summary: Thanks WWR for information on the Nehro idea of beauty and other facts relating to expression.

letters.title: To B. J. Sulivan   30 June [1870]
letters.summary:
Congratulates BJS on his K.C.B.

In autumn he will publish a book partly on man [Descent], which he expects "many will decry as very wicked".

Thinks the success of the Tierra del Fuego mission is wonderful.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   1 July 1870
letters.summary:
HibiscusandNolanaseeds not harvested at Kew. Sends list of the best plants ofLiliumhe can give.

Asks CD for name of work on orchids mentioned in his supplementary paper ["Fertilization of orchids",Collected papers2: 138–56].

letters.title: From John Murray   1 July 1870
letters.summary:
Financial adjustments for last edition ofOrigin

and a tentative title for the new work: "Descent of man and selection according to sex". [Later changed to "in relation to sex".]

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   1 July 1870
letters.summary: Sends copies of a mission magazine [missing] and discusses the missionaries’ work in S. America, especially that of Thomas Bridges and W. H. Stirling.

letters.title: To John Murray   [after 1 July 1870]
letters.summary: Wants to keep "The origin of man" as first part of title of book.

letters.title: From Camille Dareste   2 July 1870
letters.summary: Has found a remarkable anatomical character in the niata skull of which he wrote [see5540]. Asks whether the skull CD brought from South America [at the Royal College of Surgeons] shows the same character. If so, it would provide incontestable evidence of the origin of this race of cattle.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   2 July [1870]
letters.summary:
Thanks JDH for offer of lilies.

The paper on orchids is by Hermann Müller [Verh. Naturhist. Ver. Preuss. Rheinlande & Westphalens25 (1868): 1–62], onPlatantheraandEpipactis.

Cites another work by P. Rohrbach [Über den Blüthenbau(1866)].

MS [ofDescent] ready for printer.

Has read Bentham’s last Linnean Society [Presidential] Address [Proc. Linn. Soc. Lond.(1870): lxxiv–xciv] with great interest.

letters.title: To B. J. Sulivan   2 July [1870]
letters.summary: Thanks BJS for a journal and an interesting letter.

letters.title: To Friedrich Hildebrand   4 July 1870
letters.summary: Requests seeds of Nolana prostrata & Hibiscus Africanus, which have been matured in Germany or in the more Southern parts of Europe.

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   4 July 1870
letters.summary:
On mutations in rabbits.

Cytisuscase is not a double graft.

Aggressive behaviour of birds of prey.

letters.title: To W. H. Flower   5 July 1870
letters.summary: Encloses a query from Camille Dareste [see7262] about the niata ox skull CD gave to the museum [of the Royal College of Surgeons].

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   5 [July 1870]
letters.summary: CD sends a "curious drawing" [missing] relating to imitation and protection.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [6 or 7 July 1870]
letters.summary:
Has CD read E. Claparède ["Remarques à propos de l’ouvrage de M. Alfred Russel Wallace sur la théorie de la sélection naturelle",Arch. Sci. Phys. & Nat.n.s. 38 (1870): 160–89]? Is it worth translating?

CD and J.-F. de Brandt are "en lutte for Ac. of Sc. [France]. What a farce it is".

His work onNepenthessupports Miquel’s and Wallace’s view of the zoology of Borneo and Sumatra.

Brian Hodgson on dogs.

H. C. Bastian’s book [The modes of origin of lowest organisms(1871)] unsatisfactory.

Lyell does not share CD’s view of Bentham’s address.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   6 July 1870
letters.summary:
Discusses applicability of evolutionary theory to the question of human origins.

Describes revisions in 2d edition ofNatürliche Schöpfungsgeschichte.

His research on calcareous sponges.

Mentions evolutionary content in Gegenbaur’sVergleichende Anatomie[2d ed. (1870)].

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   6 July 1870
letters.summary:
Thanks for the drawing.

E. Claparède’s review [ofTheory of natural selection,Rev. Cours Sci.7 (1870): 564–71] is weak.

Looks forward [toDescent] with fear of being "crushed under a mountain of facts!"

letters.title: From George Green Gascoyen   7 July 1870
letters.summary: Sends CD information on two points which St George Mivart has asked him to provide, respecting the platysma myoides muscle. It is always in a state of violent contraction when a person is struggling for breath. In persons to whom chloroform is about to be administered, there is contraction but not so marked. No doubt contraction was strong before use of chloroform in operations.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   8 July [1870]
letters.summary:
Thinks well of Claparède’s criticism; worth publishing as an answer to Wallace. Bates thinks Wallace’s heterodox views have done mischief to the cause of evolution. Wallace thinks Claparède’s article very weak, CD concludes, because Claparède has arrived at an unpleasant judgment very much like Lyell’s about Bentham’s address.

CD would wager Lyell lately has said something about European Proteaceae.

Does not remember anyone before Wallace on Sumatra and Java.

CD does not think he has a chance against Brandt in French Academy election.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   10 July 1870
letters.summary:
Sends seeds from R. L. Playfair in Algiers.

F. Delpino writes asking where M. A. Curtis has published physiological observations onDionaea["Enumeration of plants growing spontaneously around Wilmington, North Carolina",Boston J. Nat. Hist.1 (1834–7): 82–140; seeInsectivorous plants, p. 301 n.].

Talk with Duke of Argyll on CD’s and Wallace’s views on man.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   12 July [1870]
letters.summary:
Has not heard of Curtis onDionaea.

Duke of Argyll is clever, but it is a sin to speak of a real old Duke as a "little beggar".

"My theology is a simple muddle: I cannot look at the Universe as the result of blind chance, yet I can see no evidence of beneficent Design."

On spontaneous generation and Bastian.

letters.title: From William Bernhard Tegetmeier   14 July 1870
letters.summary:
Sends a letter by Mr Teebay on variation in wild ducks.

Offers to lend Dr Cooper’s book on game fowls.

Is preparing a new edition [1873] of hisPoultry book.

letters.title: To Albert Günther   15 July [1870]
letters.summary:
Asks AG to identify the species ofTritonMr Ford has drawn.

AG’s help has turned CD’s chapter on fishes and reptiles from "much the worst" into "one of the best" [inDescent].

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   15 July [1870]
letters.summary: WBT may use any of CD’s material for the new edition of his poultry book. Hopes WBT will keep firmly to his idea of working out pigeon variation.

letters.title: From William Farr   16 July 1870
letters.summary: Discusses the Census Bill and CD’s attempt to get questions on consanguineous marriage added to the census.

letters.title: From Friedrich Hildebrand   16 July 1870
letters.summary:
Sends CD some seeds.

Has been experimenting withOxaliscrosses.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   16 July [1870]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: The Census Bill is down on the paper for tomorrow; will CD restate how he wants to put the question [on cousin marriages]?

letters.title: To William Farr   17 July [1870]
letters.summary: Writes concerning the questions on consanguineous marriages which CD wishes to have inserted into the Census. Discusses the form the questions might take and the value of the information that would be gained from them.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   17 July 1870
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: CD would like questions on consanguineous marriages inserted in the Census to ascertain effects, if any, on fertility.

letters.title: From Armand de Quatrefages   18 July 1870
letters.deprecated: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.sender: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.summary:
CD lost first round of nominations at the Académie Française to Jean-Frédéric de Brandt. QdeB and Milne-Edwards continue the battle, but CD is fiercely attacked.

Asks for complete citation of CD’s geological work on South America because it has to be shown he did more than collect objects.

letters.title: From Arthur Gardiner Butler   19 July 1870
letters.summary:
Supplies names of moths and references.

Describes his breeding experiments with butterflies to test effects of reduced light.

letters.title: To Armand de Quatrefages   20 July [1870]
letters.deprecated: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.recipient: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.summary:
Sends list of his publications.

Is grateful for interest QdeB has taken in his election [to Académie Française].

letters.title: To John Lubbock   21 July [1870]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary:
Thanks JL for his book [Origin of civilization(1870)], which he has read with "extreme interest". Wishes JL had published four or five months earlier as CD would have "so profited & saved so much work". CD will have to modify some of what he has written [inDescent]. Sees they differ a good deal about moral sense "but hardly two men ever do agree on this perplexing subject".

JL’s note of the 16th [see7277] about the Census arrived too late for CD to answer.

letters.title: To Armand de Quatrefages   21 July [1870]
letters.deprecated: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.recipient: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.summary: Thanks Quatrifages for his work on species. Explains that he received the Wollaston Medal for his three geological works.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   23 July [1870]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Brought forward the "cousin question" in the House; read most of CD’s letter to the House.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   26 July [1870]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Some good men spoke for CD’s amendment, but in vain.

letters.title: To Richard Kippist   28 July [1870]
letters.summary: Sends five papers from J. P. M. Weale for consideration by the Linnean Society.

letters.title: From David Forbes   30 July 1870
letters.summary: Would much like CD to contribute a note for insertion after his paper on Aymara Indians.

letters.title: To J. P. M. Weale   30 July 1870
letters.summary:
Has forwarded JPMW’s papers to the Linnean Society [four articles by J. P. M. Weale,J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)13 (1870–2): 42–58].

Comments on JPMW’s findings concerning flowers and their fertilisation.

letters.title: To David Forbes   31 July [1870]
letters.summary: Thanks DF for proofs of his paper on Aymara Indians.

letters.title: From Henry Bence Jones   2 August 1870
letters.summary: CD has complained of pins and needles keeping him from working on his book [Descent]. If he could spend ten days with HBJ, he would be well and fit.

letters.title: To H. B. Jones   3 August [1870]
letters.summary: Despite HBJ’s good aid, CD’s stomach will not permit a visit.

letters.title: From Paul Broca   4 August 1870
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for compliments on the first part of his "discours",

but the later part was critical of natural selection. Nevertheless, CD should see him not as a systematic adversary, but in the camp of Quatrefages de Bréau and Milne-Edwards.

letters.title: To John Murray   5 [August 1870]
letters.summary: MS ofDescent, except last chapter, is ready to send to printer. Hopes the printer will be able to keep him steadily at work correcting proof. "It drives me mad to change from job to job."

letters.title: From William Farr   6 August 1870
letters.summary: Is glad John Lubbock made the fight he did [to amend Census Bill to enable insertion of questions on consanguineous marriages].

letters.title: From John Murray   6 August [1870]
letters.summary:
JM informs CD that he will have Clowes give him written assurance that the printing [ofDescent] will proceed without interruption.

The [Franco-Prussian] War is a sad damper on international science and his publishing plans.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   7 August [1870]
letters.summary: Plans to visit Down in a week.

letters.title: To Mr Dorrell   9 August 1870
letters.summary: Sends instructions to Messrs Clowes concerning typesetting and printing of proof-sheets ofDescent.

letters.title: From Lewis Henry Morgan   9 August 1870
letters.summary:
Sends last chapter of his book in press [Systems of consanguinity and affinity of the human familyvol. 17 inSmithsonian contributions to knowledge(1871)], which supports CD on man.

Ethnology must study the ages of barbarism as the formative portions of man’s physical and mental history.

letters.title: To Mr Dorrell   11 August [1870]
letters.summary: He will not be ready to begin correcting proofs until 28 or 29 August.

letters.title: To L. H. Morgan   11 August [1870]
letters.summary: Thanks LHM for concluding chapter [toSystems of consanguinity and affinity of the human family(1871)]. Agrees that it is important to study the habits and institutions of savages.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   15 August [1870]
letters.summary: Wishes to visit Down.

letters.title: From Charles Lawford Acland   17 August 1870
letters.summary: Is studyingVariation, especially Pangenesis. Reports earlier notion of Dr Robert Lee, that resemblance between husband and wife may be partly owing to her having man’s blood circulating in her during pregnancies; thus spouses most resemble each other in large families.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   18 August 1870
letters.summary:
Has just sent MS ofDescentto printers. Recognises that [because of Franco-Prussian War] the publisher will have given up idea of a German translation.

Though the war is a misfortune for science, CD rejoices at the wonderful success of Germany; has met no one who does not share this feeling.

letters.title: To Jean Jacques Moulinié   18 August 1870
letters.summary: Under present circumstances [Franco-Prussian War] gives up French translation ofDescent.

letters.title: To F. P. Cobbe    20 August [1870]
letters.summary:
CD writes for Emma, who is ill.

Delighted with FPC’s "most just" article [inEcho?]. Sends £1 subscription.

Thanks for telling CD about theFraser’s Magazinearticle [F. W. Farrar, "Hereditary genius (by F. Galton)", n.s. 2 (1870): 251–65].

CD wrote as Justice of Peace for Kent to the Home Secretary about Holder’s case.

Tropaeolumtransmits every shade of colour if self-fertilised for six or seven generations.

letters.title: To Armand de Quatrefages   23 August [1870]
letters.deprecated: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.recipient: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.summary:
Thanks QdeB for his continued support of CD’s election to French Academy.

Discusses views of Milne-Edwards on species.

Comments on views of Élie de Beaumont.

"I fear my next book [Descent] … will greatly displease you."

letters.title: To [?]   23 August [1870–80]
letters.summary: Discusses evolution of species.

letters.title: To George F. Kittredge   24 August [1870]
letters.summary: Thanks GFK for offer of information.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   28 August 1870
letters.summary:
Mimicry in Lepidoptera.

Sexual selection.

The Franco-Prussian war.

letters.title: To Philip Lutley Sclater   30 August [1870]
letters.summary: Encloses, for publication, note about Pampas woodpecker, opposing W. H. Hudson [see7354].

letters.title: From D. Appleton & Co. to Asa Gray   1 September 1870
letters.summary: Statement of sales of U. S. edition ofOrigin.

letters.title: From Sofia Vasilyevna Kovalevskaya and V. O. Kovalevsky   1 September 1870
letters.summary:
Accepts CD’s offer to order books from the Royal Society Library.

VOK asks for information about W. B. Carpenter’s dredging expedition in thePorcupine.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   3 September 1870
letters.summary:
Could not go up the Niger, as trading steamers are trying to keep their trade in the dark.

Has seen several albinos, but no blushing. Thinks blacks do blush.

letters.title: To John Murray   4 September [1870]
letters.summary: Variationis a much better looking volume thanOrigindue to quality of paper and binding. Hopes JM will attend to this point inDescent. Printers have sent "splendid lot" of proofs.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   5 September [1870]
letters.summary:
Will order the first set of casts from Murray.

Thanks CD for a book for his wife from the Royal Society Library.

His brother [Alexander] is delighted at being referred to in CD’s work [Descent1: 205].

letters.title: From John Tyndall   7 September 1870
letters.summary:
Sends CD proofs of a lecture he will give at Liverpool. Asks CD to check the part referring to him.

Élie de Beaumont’s remark, in which he requires CD to recant before being admitted to the [French] Academy, is intolerable. "This spirit has much to do with the present condition of France."

letters.title: To John Tyndall   8 September 1870
letters.summary:
CD finds JT’s discourse "grand and most interesting" [On the scientific use of the imagination(1870)]. Flattered by what JT says about him.

He is "a rash man to say a good word for Pangenesis for it has hardly a friend among naturalists".

CD is much struck with what JT says about "pondering" and delighted by his "as if" argument.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   15 September 1870
letters.summary: Requests a copy of[Living]Cirripediato send to his brother, Alexander, who is working in Naples and wishes to verify CD’s discovery of complementary males.

letters.title: From George Cupples   17 September 1870
letters.summary: CD’s deerhound puppy will be ready soon.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   20 September 1870
letters.summary: Thanks forCirripedia. Sorry CD has had to buy the books.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   24 September 1870
letters.summary:
Reports on the 1870 BAAS meeting at Liverpool. Huxley’s address was over the heads of the laymen.

Tyndall’s was eloquent to listen to, disappointing to read.

George Rolleston’s "Rococo" address [Nature2 (1870): 423–7, 442–6].

Murchison.

Lyell.

Has done an immense lot of work.

Regrets CD has not kept the simple title "Origin of man" [forDescent].

letters.title: From Alexander Onufrievich Kovalevsky   25 September 1870
letters.summary: Outlines the evidence for his view that ascidian larvae are true vertebrates presented in his paper ["Weitere Studien über die Entwicklung der einfachen Ascidien",Arch. Mikrosk. Anat.7 (1871): 101–302]. CD can cite this as confirmation of AOK’s earlier claims.

letters.title: From Edward Livingston Youmans   25 September 1870
letters.summary: Concerning an American edition ofDescentby Appleton’s.

letters.title: From E. L. Youmans   25 September 1870
letters.summary: A note to inform CD that ELY has sent his earlier letter [7324] to the Athenaeum, being unsure of CD’s address.

letters.title: To John Murray   26 September 1870
letters.summary: Wants sheets [ofDescent] for foreign editions. Asks JM to determine price to be charged for the stereotypes of 62 cuts. Dallas would be excellent for the index but must be "civilly warned" not to delay. Encloses memo on the index.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   27 September [1870]
letters.summary:
Comments on JDH’s report of Liverpool meeting.

Huxley’s address.

Sir Roderick [Murchison]’s "apotheosis".

Tyndall’s lecture is "grand" except for egotistical beginning. Some Frenchmen have pitched into CD for using the "as if" reasoning, which Tyndall shows is justified.

Has just read George Rolleston’s address inNature.

Anton Dohrn says German public have high opinion of Lyell.

letters.title: From John Murray   28 September [1870]
letters.summary:
Various arrangements concerning the publication ofDescent. "It will cause men to prick up [their] ears – & to elevate their eyebrows." JM thinks he will venture to print 2500 copies.

Suggests CD tone down as possibly indelicate a passage on proportion of advances made by the two sexes in animals.

letters.title: To John Murray   29 September [1870]
letters.summary:
CD did not promise Appleton stereotypes of text [ofDescent]; only of cuts.

Wishes to know which passage JM thought "coarse". Remembers only a quotation from John Hunter on courtship of female being required "to give her desires" [Descent1: 273]. He fancied a quotation rendered the sentence less coarse.

letters.title: To Hermann Settegast   29 September 1870
letters.summary: Thanks HS for a copy of his book [?Die Thierzucht(1868)].

letters.title: To [Edward William Blore]   [October 1870 or later]
letters.summary: Horace Darwin wishes to have private tuition to help him pass the "Little Go" and so CD wonders if he might be excused College lectures for the present, to prevent undue strain.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   2 October 1870
letters.summary:
The outbreak of war and war work have interfered with JVC’s scientific work.

Publisher does not, however, think the war will hurt success ofDescentin Germany, and JVC asks for corrected sheets for his use in translating it.

Wishes struggle between Romanic and Teutonic races could be fought out in a form more appropriate to their cultures and civilisation.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   5 October [1870]
letters.summary:
Sympathetic to JVC’s views on Franco-Prussian war [see7332].

Astonished at JVC’s readiness to begin work. Will send sheets as soon as possible. Has asked Murray to charge for stereotypes of 64 woodblocks at cost. JVC must make his own agreement with publisher.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   5 October 1870
letters.summary: Forwards Alexander Kovalevsky’s letter [7326] with the information on the vertebrate character of ascidian larvae.

letters.title: To Robert Main   6 October 1870
letters.summary: Regrets he is unable to correct his "little manual" ["Geology" inManual of scientific enquiry(1849)]. Recommends that John Phillips revise it.

letters.title: From Charles Wyville Thomson   7 October 1870
letters.summary: Seeks CD’s support as a candidate for Edinburgh Chair in Natural History.

letters.title: From George Cupples   8 October 1870
letters.summary: Delay in sending deerhound puppy.

letters.title: From Hermann Hoffmann   8 October 1870
letters.summary: Cancelled. Now enclosure to S7695.

letters.title: From John Murray   10 October [1870]
letters.summary:
Cannot find the [indelicate] passage he referred to in last letter.

Various publication arrangements.

letters.title: To C. W. Thomson   10 October 1870
letters.summary: Testimonial letter hoping that CWT will be successful in getting Chair of Natural History at Edinburgh.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   11 October [1870]
letters.summary:
Sends first four sheets [ofDescent]. Murray charges £14 for the 64 stereotypes.

Cannot supply copies of woodcuts from Brehm’sIllustrirtes Thierleben[1864–9]. Hopes JVC’s publisher will be able to arrange to include them.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   11 October [1870]
letters.summary:
Leaving England.

Asks CD to send four sheets [ofDescentproofs].

letters.title: To John Murray   11 October [1870]
letters.summary: Glad to hear Dallas will do index ofDescent, but he needs keeping up to the mark. Agrees to a Dutch edition.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   12 October 1870
letters.summary: Bentham has translated Miquel’s Sumatran supplement to hisFlora van Nederlandsch Indie. It should be published. What does CD think is best vehicle?Natureis wretched and too ephemeral. What aboutPopular Science Review?

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   14 October [1870]
letters.summary:
Does not think so poorly ofNatureas JDH does, by any means; fearsPopular Science Reviewis rather ephemeral but more durable thanNature.

The case of the charlock.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [before 18 October 1870]
letters.summary: Needs more money to pay his tutoring bills.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   18 October [1870]
letters.summary: Sends a cheque to pay off FD’s debts. Warns him of the dangers of overspending his income and advises him strongly to keep accounts.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [after 18 October 1870]
letters.summary: Thanks CD for the cheque. Gives account of money owed for tutoring and tennis.

letters.title: From John Gage   19 October 1870
letters.summary:
Convinced by CD’sOrigin.

As a "student of spirit intercourse", he asks CD for more details about the scene of the dancing spoon inJournal of researches[p. 546].

letters.title: From Alexander Agassiz   22 October 1870
letters.summary: Asks whether he may see CD before leaving England.

letters.title: To John Murray   22 October [1870]
letters.summary:
He agrees with his family that binding ofVariationlooks much better thanOrigin.

Asks JM to report the number of copies he has printed ofNaturalist’s Voyage[Journal of researches].

letters.title: To Alexander Agassiz   [23 October 1870?]
letters.summary: Suggests time for AA to visit.

letters.title: From John Murray   24 October [1870]
letters.summary:
Sends table of sales [ofJournal of researches]. 2000 copies sold since 1860.

Descenthas gone to press for 2500 copies.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   27 October 1870
letters.summary:
Returning CD’s books.

Sympathises with women’s lot in life.

letters.title: From W. D. Fox   28 October [1870]
letters.summary:
Has heard of CD’s forthcoming book [Descent] from J. D. Hooker.

Leaves next week for winter quarters in Sandown.

letters.title: From S. A. Merrell   28 October 1870
letters.summary: Offers to send his short article on the "Unity of generation" which supports the developmental hypothesis.

letters.title: From Benjamin Clarke   1 November [1870]
letters.summary:
Sends CD some Indian corn seeds to demonstrate the extreme effect sometimes producible on progeny by the mutilation of a parent.

Writes of a recent book.

letters.title: To George Cupples   3 November [1870]
letters.summary:
Will collect the "precious animal" [deerhound puppy] from King’s Cross.

Thanks GC for information on the perch.

letters.title: From Henry Holland   4 November [1870]
letters.summary: A month in the West Indies, where he saw the luxuriant struggle of tropical vegetation, has brought HH "still more closely within the circle" of CD’s doctrine.

letters.title: To P. L. Sclater   4 November [1870]
letters.summary: Asks PLS whether he will look over list of names of birds [forDescent] to make sure they are spelled correctly. "I have a most unfortunate weakness … to copy proper names incorrectly".

letters.title: From Worthington George Smith   4 November 1870
letters.summary: Describes his children, who all seem to have inherited both dark hairs from their mother and light hairs from WGS with the latter greatly outnumbering the former.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   6 November 1870
letters.summary: W. C. Wells’s theory relating black skin-colour and immunity to malaria may be true. Has seen Negroes come down with fever, but these were generally light in colour.

letters.title: To W. G. Smith   6 November 1870
letters.summary: Thanks for the information sent by WGS in his letter of 4 November 1870.

letters.title: From Thompson Forster   8 November 1870
letters.summary: Details of an apparently hereditary deformity in a man.

letters.title: From William Ogle   [before 9 November 1870]
letters.summary: Sends CD a paper dealing in part with animal pigmentation [Med.-Chir. Trans.2d ser. 411 [check vol no!?] (1870): 263–90]. Discusses relationship between white colouring and susceptibility to poisonous plants.

letters.title: To William Ogle   9 November 1870
letters.summary:
Has read WO’s paper [see7361] with great interest. If WO’s views are confirmed he will be able to explain many odd little details about the colouring of animals.

Can WO observe if the platysma myoides is brought into strong action in people suffering from severe dyspnoea?

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   9 November 1870
letters.summary: Ideas of female beauty of W. African Negroes are on the whole the same as those of Europeans.

letters.title: To P. L. Sclater   9 November 1870
letters.summary:
Thanks PLS for his generous offer to go over the part on birds [inDescent]. Does not think PLS realises that there are more than 200 pages – most of which will have nothing new for him.

W. H. Hudson’s proofs have arrived ["Letters on the ornithology of Buenos Ayres",Proc. Zool. Soc. Lond.(1870): 87–9, 158–60, 332–4, 545–50, 671–3, 748–50, 798–82; (1871): 4–7, 258–62, 326–9].

letters.title: From William Ogle   [10–17 November 1870]
letters.summary:
Relates instances of rabbits suffering from a condition which affects only the patches of white on their fur.

Will make observations on the platysma for CD.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   11 November 1870
letters.summary: Pleased CD is quoting him inDescent.

letters.title: To P. L. Sclater   11 November [1870]
letters.summary:
Accepts PLS’s offer to read proofs of [Descent].

W. H. Hudson’s paper is interesting.

letters.title: From Jacob Heinrich Schmick   12 November 1870
letters.summary: Sends CD two books outlining a new geological theory. Believes his theory explains the discontinuities in the fossil record.

letters.title: From George Cupples   14 November 1870
letters.summary: Glad "Bran" [deerhound puppy] arrived safely.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   15 November [1870]
letters.summary: Discusses his present book [Descent].

letters.title: To John Murray   15 November [1870]
letters.summary: Would like to hear results of JM’s November booksale.

letters.title: From John Murray   16 November [1870]
letters.summary:
JM reports 1900 [advance] copies ofDescentwere taken at his annual sale,

and 340 copies ofOrigin[5th ed.] were sold.

Sheets for Dutch publisher will be sent to CD immediately. JM cautions against possibility that Dutch edition will anticipate the English.

letters.title: From John Dean Caton   17 November 1870
letters.summary:
Observations on winter colour of coats of male and female elk,

spots on deer,

and tuft of hair on breasts of wild female turkeys.

letters.title: To John Murray   17 November [1870]
letters.summary: Pleased at [advance] sale [ofDescent]. Suggests 3000 copies be printed. Corrections are frightful and, CD fears, will not be done until end of year.

letters.title: To William Ogle   17 November [1870]
letters.summary:
Thanks WO for information on platysma, which he did not know could be brought into voluntary action. Is coming to believe it has nothing to do with expression.

On the relation between white colouring and susceptibility to poisonous plants, CD suggests WO send his paper to J. Wyman and propose he investigate whether white as well as black pigs will eat paint-root.

letters.title: To ?   17 November [1870]
letters.summary: CD has already agreed that Julius Victor Carus will translate his next book.

letters.title: From W. D. Fox   18 [November 1870]
letters.summary: Has heard "sad tales" about CD’s forthcoming book [Descent]; does not think even CD can persuade him his ancestors were apes.

letters.title: From E. F. Lubbock   [18 November 1870]
letters.summary: John Lubbock has nearly finished his Thysanura book [Monograph of the Collembola and Thysanura(1873)].

letters.title: From Asa Gray   21 November 1870
letters.summary: Reports case of apparent incipient dimorphism. Observations on variations in flower structure, especially style length, within species of Polemoniaceae.

letters.title: To P. L. Sclater   21 November [1870]
letters.summary: Sends two sheets [ofDescent] for correction of names of birds. PLS will save him many disgraceful misspellings.Descentnow being prepared in five foreign editions.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   22 November 1870
letters.summary:
Sofya Kovalevsky not admitted to University in Berlin.

Translating the four sheets CD sent. When will book [Descent] be printed?

Alexander [Kovalevsky] has gone to the Red Sea to study corals.

Will work on liveScalpellumat Naples in spring.

Bemoans England’s Prussian sympathies. Paris will fall without bombardment.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   22 November [1870]
letters.summary:
Praise for ARW’s reply [Nature3 (1870): 49–50] to a paper by A. W. Bennett ["Natural selection from a mathematical point of view",Nature3 (1870): 30–3] holding that mind is a leading cause of variation.

Is reading proof of his "confounded book" [Descent].

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   24 November 1870
letters.summary:
On a good criticism of ARW’s views [North Am. Rev.(1870)].

Problems of establishing a permanent residence.

His Presidential Address for Entomological Society will answer A. Murray on geographical distribution of Coleoptera.

letters.title: To George Cupples   27 November [1870]
letters.summary: Bran [deerhound puppy] is thriving; enjoys English life.

letters.title: From Hermanus Hartogh Heijs van Zouteveen   27 November 1870
letters.summary: Concerning the Dutch edition ofDescent.

letters.title: From Anne Jane Cupples   [28 November 1870]
letters.summary: Requests CD write in support of Government pension for her husband, George Cupples.

letters.title: To Alexander Stuart Strahan   29 November 1870
letters.summary: A recommendation for George Cupples who has applied for a government pension: "I have corresponded with him on scientific subjects during several years. On some very intricate points he has been so kind as not only to collect, at the cost of much trouble, information from various sources, but has likewise made for me valuable observations".

letters.title: From Charles Anthoni Johnson Brooke   30 November 1870
letters.summary: Encloses a few answers to CD’s queries on expression. Continues to observe the expressions and habits of the Malays, Dyaks, and Saribus tribes [SeeExpression, pp. 21, 209].

letters.title: To Hermanus Hartogh Heijs van Zouteveen   30 November [1870]
letters.summary: Is pleased to hear that the translator for the Dutch edition [ofDescent] is a person so well qualified [see7384]. He encloses a facsimile of the title page. Reports arrangements with John Murray.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [before 5 December 1870]
letters.summary: Sends list of bills.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [before 5 December 1870]
letters.summary: Has no chance of paying his debts, and asks for money.

letters.title: From Robert Francis Cooke   5 December 1870
letters.summary: Has just heard that 1st volume of Dutch edition [ofDescent] has been announced for 10 December. Was CD aware that the Dutch intended to publish vol. 1 by itself?

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   5 December [1870]
letters.summary: Sends a cheque to clear FD’s debts. Hopes he will be more careful in the future.

letters.title: To P. L. Sclater   5 December 1870
letters.summary: Is sending by this post three sheets and will send another tomorrow thus almost completing the part on birds. His congratulations and thanks for PLS’s labours with them.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   7 December 1870
letters.summary:
Believes AG’s cases of incipient dimorphism are due to mere variability. Has found examples inNolanaandAmsinckia; believes such variation is the basis for the development of dimorphism. Was unaware of variations inPhlox.

Sensitivity ofDroseraandDionaea.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   12 December [1870]
letters.summary:
Progress on his Russian translation ofDescent.

Alexander Kovalevsky is at Tor in Sinai, where C. G. Ehrenberg was in 1827.

Has CD seen Ernst Haeckel’s new book [Biologische Studien(1870–7)]?

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   15 December 1870
letters.summary:
Forgot to send books.

Saw Miss [Henrietta] Darwin; chastised her for being out when book [Descent] has not yet appeared.

letters.title: From Lambert Adolphe Jacques Quetelet   15 December 1870
letters.summary: CD elected Associate Member of the Royal Belgian Academy.

letters.title: To L. A. J. Quetelet   [after 15 December 1870]
letters.deprecated: Lambert Adolphe Jacques (Adolphe) QueteletSecretary, Acad. R. Sci. Belgique
letters.recipient: Lambert Adolphe Jacques (Adolphe) QueteletSecretary, Acad. R. Sci. Belgique
letters.summary: Thanks Academy for his election as Associate Member.

letters.title: From Edouard van Beneden   17 December 1870
letters.deprecated: Édouard Joseph Louis Marie (Édouard) van Beneden
letters.sender: Édouard Joseph Louis Marie (Édouard) van Beneden
letters.summary:
CD has been nominated as aMembre Associéof the Belgian Royal Academy.

Discusses crustacean embryology; EvB is at variance with Dohrn.

letters.title: To William Ogle   17 December [1870]
letters.summary:
Thanks WO for valuable letter. Feels he need not trouble any more about platysma. If WO ever sees someone suffering great fear, CD asks him to observe the neck.

Hopes to visit WO when next in London.

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   17 December 1870
letters.summary:
Congratulations on Leonard Darwin’s success at Woolwich Academy.

Mentions the current activities of his own sons and of some old acquaintances.

letters.title: From William Ogle   [after 17 December 1870]
letters.summary:
Would be pleased to be visited by CD.

J. Wyman will make observations on black pigs and white pigs in Florida.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   19 [December 1870]
letters.summary:
Has received a letter, and two packets of securities.

Comments on George’s escape.

letters.title: From Laurent-Guillaume De Koninck   19 December 1870
letters.summary: Congratulates CD on his election to L’Académie Royale de Belgique.

letters.title: To L.-G. De Koninck   [after 19 December 1870]
letters.summary: Thanks LGK for the part he played in getting CD elected as an Associate [of Royal Belgian Academy of Sciences].

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   20 December 1870
letters.summary: CD is correct; his notes are on the Jollof, not the Tollof, tribe.

letters.title: To B. J. Sulivan   20 December [1870]
letters.summary:
Thanks BJS for his congratulations [on Leonard Darwin’s success].

CD is "as usual, always ailing and grumbling".

Expects his new book [Descent] to "disgust you & many others".

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   21 [December 1870]
letters.summary:
Confirms number of shares.

Reports on conversation with Henry Holland.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   25 December [1870]
letters.summary:
Thanks CL for his book [The student’s elements of geology(1871)].

Is correcting proofs [ofDescent].

letters.title: To P. L. Sclater   26 December [1870]
letters.summary: Sending two sheets [ofDescent]. About one-and-a-half more will complete PLS’s task.

letters.title: To ?   28 December [1870]
letters.summary: Regrets that Hartogh Heijs van Zouteveen has already translated his new book into Dutch.

letters.title: To P. L. Sclater   29 December [1870]
letters.summary: CD is obliged for PLS’s correction [ofDescentproofs]. Will add a caption to the woodcut [of the wart-hog] since it is too late to make a new one.

letters.title: To W. H. Flower   [1871?]
letters.summary: Does not know rules for admission to museum [of the Royal College of Surgeons]. CD’s son [Francis] wishes much to inspect some of the preparations.

letters.title: From O. G. Rejlander   [1871]
letters.summary: Observations on expression.

letters.title: From C. H. Thiebout   [1871]
letters.summary: As a follower of CD, Spencer, and Kant, wishes to announce his work on the origin of "foolish illnesses" and prostitution [?Kort begrip der proefunderlijke zielkunde(1869)].

letters.title: From William Turner   [1871?]
letters.summary: Extract from Robert Knox on hermaphroditism [Lond. Med. Gaz.12 Jan 1844].

letters.title: From L. C. Wedgwood   [January 1871]
letters.summary: Describes a pouting expression in a 3½–year-old child.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   [1871 or later]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: All the inhabitants of Down hope JL will endeavour to induce the Post Office to improve the telegraph service.

letters.title: To P. L. Sclater   4 January [1871]
letters.summary: Is infinitely obliged for a correction. "You men who do only or chiefly original work have an immense advantage over compilers like myself, as you can know what to trust." Wishes he had consulted PLS before using A. E. Brehm’sThierlebenwoodcuts [forDescent]. PLS’s assistance has saved him from "endless blunders"; he now feels safe.

letters.title: From Francis Wedgwood   4 January 1871
letters.summary: Depth of furrows in old field.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   6 January [1871]
letters.summary: On sexual selection and the sense of beauty among the W. African Negroes.

letters.title: From Federico Delpino   7 January 1871
letters.summary:
Sends his new work,Ulteriori osservazioni sulla dicogomiapt 2, fasc. 1.

Has found no nectar inOrchis morioorO. maculatain Italy and has seen no insects visiting the plants.

Gives his observations on cross- and self-fertilisation in cereals.

letters.title: From A. F. Boardman   8 January 1871
letters.summary: More speculations [see5811] on the evolutionary development of man, relating progress to the consumption of better food and the availability of moist air.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   9 January 1871
letters.summary: Definite results have been delayed, but he is optimistic.

letters.title: From Francis Wedgwood   9 January 1871
letters.summary: Appearance and depth of furrows in old field.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   10 January 1871
letters.summary:
Sends quotation about Lycurgus and Spartan exposure of infants who were deemed defective.

Bibliographic references on sense of beauty and morals.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   11 January 1871
letters.summary: Sends title-page ofDescentfor approval. Asks whether CD has any idea of size of index.

letters.title: From L. A. J. Quetelet   11 January 1871
letters.deprecated: Lambert Adolphe Jacques (Adolphe) QueteletSecretary, Acad. R. Sci. Belgique
letters.sender: Lambert Adolphe Jacques (Adolphe) QueteletSecretary, Acad. R. Sci. Belgique
letters.summary: Sends diploma of election to the Royal Belgian Academy.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   12 January [1871]
letters.summary: Has no idea about length of index [forDescent]. W. S. Dallas wrote it would take ten days more. Asks how many presentation copies he may have. Lists journals to receive review copies.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   13 January 1871
letters.summary: Sends list of journals to be sent review copies ofDescent. If CD wants to add others, they will be included. Printing of 2500 copies ordered; retail price 24s.

letters.title: To J. B. Innes   13 January 1871
letters.summary: CD has forgotten about S. J. O. Horsman and the church organ and asks for any information that will help him inform his solicitors in connection with a document he has received and encloses. Will not apologise for what he said, but is ignorant of what it was.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   14 January [1871]
letters.summary:
Suggests periodicals to receive review copies [ofDescent].

Is "ashamed at my corrections".

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   15 January [1871]
letters.summary:
Has received (from CD) the sheets of the second volume [ofDescent].

He fears he has offended CD or someone in England and he begs to know his offence.

His brother is working at the Red Sea and wishes CD to know that he has evidence for the affinity of ascidians and vertebrates in their nervous systems.

Plans to go to Paris upon its imminent capitulation to help his sister-in-law.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   16 January 1871
letters.summary: Meeting with CD postponed.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   17 January [1871]
letters.summary: Discusses mailing of presentation copies [ofDescent]. Sends addresses of A. R. Wallace and St George Mivart.

letters.title: To J. B. Innes   18 January [1871]
letters.summary:
CD’s anxiety about being examined in court if Horsman [former curate at Down] brings suit. He doubts it will happen, but if so will defend himself to utmost.

Has pleasant recollections of his relations with JBI.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   18 January [1871]
letters.summary: Sends ARW advance copy of vol. 1 [ofDescent] for his review inAcademy. Vol. 2 is delayed by index. "Do not swear at me more than you can help."

letters.title: From St G. J. Mivart   19 January 1871
letters.summary: Has sent CD his book [Genesis of species(1871)]. Has not said a word in opposition to CD except where his view of the truth necessitated it.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   20 [January or February 1871?]
letters.summary:
Asks WED’s help in acquiring expression photographs and engravings.

Wishes to send Langstaff a copy of his book [Expression], in gratitude for his valuable notes.

letters.title: To Albert Günther   21 January [1871]
letters.summary: Invites AG to stay at Down. Winwood Reade and, he hopes, Hooker and Robert Swinhoe will be there.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   21 January [1871]
letters.summary:
Finished the last proofs ofDescenta few days ago. "I shall be well abused."

St George Mivart’sGenesis[of species]: very good, unfortunately theological. Will tell heavily against natural selection but not against evolution, and this is "infinitely more important".

letters.title: From J. B. Innes   21 January 1871
letters.summary:
JBI regrets his part in appointments of his successors.

His friendship with CD and its effect on his fellow clerics.

letters.title: To St G. J. Mivart   21 January [1871]
letters.summary:
Is obliged for StGJM’s book [On the genesis of species(1871)].

Would not have sent him vol. 1 [ofDescent] if he had known that StGJM’s book was already published.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [after 21 January 1871]
letters.summary: Responds to Mivart’sGenesis of species. "I complain of his incessently speaking as if I trusted exclusively to natural selection … Mivart speaks in many places as if I entirely ignored the direct action of external conditions". Answers some of Mivart’s particular criticisms. Suggests FD read the letter to Marlborough Robert Pryor, as Pryor will never be able to read it himself.

letters.title: From St G. J. Mivart   22 January 1871
letters.summary: Thanks CD for vol. 1 ofDescent. Feels nothing but sympathy and esteem for a writer labouring for the promotion of what he conscientiously believes to be the truth.

letters.title: To [M. R. Pryor?]   [after 21 January 1871?]
letters.summary: Suggests Mivart should have read account of Niata Cattle.

letters.title: To St G. J. Mivart   [23 January 1871]
letters.summary: Comments on StGJM’s book [Genesis of species(1871)]. Has no personal objection to a word of it, but regrets their views differ so much.

letters.title: To St G. J. Mivart   23 January [1871]
letters.summary:
Acknowledges StGJM’s kind letter. [See7451.]

Offers to alter the "dogmatic assertion" referred to on page 102 [of StGJM’sOn the genesis of species] but in 5th ed. ofOriginand inVariationCD finds only qualified expressions.

letters.title: From St G. J. Mivart   24 January 1871
letters.summary: Is sorry CD foundGenesis of speciesunfairly critical. Assures CD of his just intentions and offers to alter certain words and phrases in a new edition. Emphasises his high regard for CD but fears his views are leading to religious decay.

letters.title: To William Bowman   [before 26] January [1871]
letters.summary: Sends enclosure copied from letter of F. C. Donders [7207?] dealing with orbicular muscle. Asks about secretion of tears resulting from spasmodic action of orbicular muscle.

letters.title: To Erasmus Wilson   [26 January – 3 February 1871]
letters.summary: Seeks information and observations on the contraction of the orbicular muscles as a consequence of skin irritation.

letters.title: From William Bowman   26 January 1871
letters.summary: Reports his observations on the concurrence of orbicular muscle spasms, engorgement of eyes with blood, and formation of tears.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   26 January 1871
letters.summary: A bibliographical query arising in translation ofDescent. Two misprints noted.

letters.title: To J. B. Innes   26 January [1871]
letters.summary:
CD’s health has been poor.

Appreciates JBI’s letter and his expression of friendship.

In the opinion of a Q.C., Horsman has no case.

letters.title: From St G. J. Mivart   26 January 1871
letters.summary: Is glad CD does not believe he is biased by anodium theologicum. Comments on the first volume ofDescent. Is convinced of the truth of evolution, but believes natural selection plays only a secondary role and that man is fundamentally different from the rest of creation.

letters.title: To St G. J. Mivart   26 January [1871]
letters.summary:
CD apologises for having thought that StGJM’s religious feelings had led him to feel personal animosity towards him. [See7454.]

He remembers having thought and written that belief in evolution isinfinitelymore important for science than belief in Natural Selection.
