For his own part he would have felt little interest in evolution apart from the explanation "in a general manner" of how each organism is so adapted to its conditions.

letters.title: To W. S. Dallas   27 January [1871]
letters.summary: Accepts the proposed corrections of his spelling except for "chloèn". [WSD was preparing the index forDescent, vol. 2.]

letters.title: To George King   27 January [1871]
letters.summary:
Obliged for specimens [ofParitium?].

Discusses difference between sport and parent tree.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   27 January 1871
letters.summary:
Response to [vol. 1 of] CD’sDescent.

Not yet convinced on sexual selection and protection, though their differences are not so great as CD thinks.

On man, he does not think CD has accounted foreverystep of his development by "ascertained laws".

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   28 January [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks RM for information on case of hexadactyly [see RM’s paper, "Hexadactylism",Land and Water, 11 March 1871, p. 179.

letters.title: To St G. J. Mivart   28 January [1871]
letters.summary: He has found passage on false belief,Variation2: 414, and does not think the whole with context is dogmatic. [Encloses copy of the passage.]

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   29 January 1871
letters.summary:
Has received all the proof-sheets of first volume and of second volume to p. 168 [Descent].

Leaves for Paris tomorrow.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   30 January 1871
letters.summary: Thanks JVC for his corrections. Will send other errata. Hopes to send remainder of vol. 2 [ofDescent] in a fortnight.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   30 January [1871]
letters.summary:
Asks that review copy [ofDescent] be sent to F. P. Cobbe.

Discusses mailing of presentation copies.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   30 January [1871]
letters.summary: Returns and sends comments on Clarke Hawkshaw’s essay ‘The persistence of forms of life in the depths of the sea’.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   30 January [1871]
letters.summary:
Responds to ARW’s comments on CD’s argument about protection inDescent.

Comments on St G. Mivart’s criticism [Genesis of species(1871)]. "The pendulum will now swing against us."

letters.title: From St G. J. Mivart   31 January 1871
letters.summary: Thanks CD for the second volume ofDescent.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   31 January 1871
letters.summary: Thinks G. H. Lewes will reviewDescentinPall Mall Gazette.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   1 February [1871]
letters.summary:
Returns pamphlets.

B. T. Lowne’s observation [Mon. Microsc. J.4 (1870): 326–30] that boiling does not kill certain moulds is curious, but then how account for absence of all living things in Pasteur’s experiment?

Always delighted to see a word in favour of Pangenesis.

Thiselton-Dyer’s paper ["On spontaneous generation and evolution",Q. J. Microsc. Sci.10 (1870): 333–54] is Spencerian.

The chemical conditions for first production of life are said to exist at present, but in some warm little pond today such matter would be absorbed or devoured, which would not have been the case before living creatures were formed.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   1 February 1871
letters.summary: Sir Andrew Smith says Hottentots and Kaffirs laugh till they cry.

letters.title: From C.-F. Reinwald   1 February 1871
letters.summary:
Has left Paris because of the war.

J. J. Moulinié and Carl Vogt are at work onDescent, which CR plans to publish in Paris.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   3 February 1871
letters.summary:
Encloses a letter [missing] from C. Reinwald, publisher of the French edition ofDescent[1872].

Vincenzi [of Unione, Turin – publisher of Italian translation] has not yet paid the account.

letters.title: From Erasmus Wilson   3 February 1871
letters.summary: On irritation of cutaneous nerves exciting responses in unconnected skin muscles.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   5 February [1871]
letters.summary:
Sends questions on expressions of Laura Bridgman.

Has finishedDescent. Believes that parts, like that on moral sense, will aggravate AG.

Working on an essay on expression.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   6 February 1871
letters.summary: Does shut eyes when scratching himself. Will ask Langstaff about muscles used when playing flute. Is back at work but hobbling around.

letters.title: To James Crichton-Browne   8 February 1871
letters.summary:
Will send copy ofDescent.

Comments on JC-B’s MS on expression among insane. Asks about weeping in insane men. Do idiots laugh when pleased?

Thanks for photographs of insane. Asks for additional photographs.

Comments on Henry Maudsley [Body and mind(1870)].

Pointed ears in the insane.

letters.title: From W. B. Dawkins   8 February 1871
letters.summary: The box of bones sent by CD has led to a series of explorations. Reports on Yorkshire cave-hunting.

letters.title: To Miss Fenwick   8 February [1871–82]
letters.summary: Sends two waste sheets of MS ofDescent; Miss F can cut out any portion she likes.

letters.title: From Felice Finzi   9 February 1871
letters.summary:
Sends a publication to Darwin.

Asks for a portrait.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   10 February [1871]
letters.summary: Asks that a presentation copy [ofDescent?] be sent to Edward Blyth. Comments on publication.

letters.title: From Thomas Meehan   10 February 1871
letters.summary:
Sends CD some remarks he made before the Academy of Natural Sciences [Philadelphia].

TM is indebted to theOriginfor first suggesting to him which observations might be useful to those working out the greater laws of nature.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   11 February [1871]
letters.summary: Would like precise details about pouting of English children to add to his information about children of savages.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   14 February [1871]
letters.summary: Discusses presentation copies [ofDescent]. Dallas returned proofs of index on Friday. Asks for John Stuart Mill’s address.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   15 February [1871]
letters.summary: Hopes German edition [ofDescent] has not yet been printed because he has fallen into a most serious blunder [about sexual selection never acting on the young] on pp. 297–9 of vol. 1.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   15 February 1871
letters.summary: Printing ofDescentwill be done this day. Cannot publish until next week.

letters.title: From James Crichton-Browne   16 February 1871
letters.summary:
Values CD’s approbation more than that of anyone else now living.

CD’s "searching questions". Sends answers separately.

Offers his observation on morbid pigmentation of skin.

Offers photographs of abnormal features in patients – ears with bristles, women with two sets of nipples.

Encloses notes on weeping and laughter in the insane.

letters.title: To Hermanus Hartogh Heijs van Zouteveen   16 February 1871
letters.summary: "I have made a serious blunder in p. 297, vol 1 of my book [Descent of man]. Kindly inform me by return of post whether this is printed in Dutch; for if not I will send you a correction in M.S. There are also two short omissions to be made in Vol. 2 … "

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   17 February 1871
letters.summary:
The pages [ofDescent] CD wishes to correct are not yet printed.

JVC’s work on the translation has been interrupted by illness.

letters.title: From David Forbes   18 February 1871
letters.summary: Thanks for copy ofDescent.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   18 February 1871
letters.summary:
VOK and his wife walked 25 miles through the Prussian lines to Paris.

Natural history collections undamaged by bombardment, but Edmond Hébert and A. J. Gaudry fear Prussians will rob them.

Several sheets ofDescentlost as they passed through the lines.

letters.title: From John Murray   18 February [1871]
letters.summary:
Bound copies [ofDescent] have been dispatched to CD.

Robert Cooke, JM’s cousin and partner, has been nominated for Athenaeum; asks CD’s support.

Begs CD not to permit any notice by F. P. Cobbe to appear until after next week.

letters.title: From J. W. Abernethy   [after 18 February 1871]
letters.summary: A poem, "Burns to Darwin".

letters.title: From James Crichton-Browne   19 February 1871
letters.summary:
Thanks forDescent.

Offers photo of patient with a second small milk-giving nipple on one breast, and of man with bristles on his ears, which come somewhat to a point.

letters.title: From G. R. Crotch   19 [February 1871]
letters.summary:
Thanks for presentation copy ofDescent.

Mivart’sGenesis of species[1871] is poor.

Mathematical illustrations of Pangenesis at Cambridge.

Wallace’s address on Madeira not convincing ["The President’s Address",Trans. R. Entomol. Soc. Lond.(1870): xliv–lxix; A. R. Wallace,Studies scientific and social(1900) 1: 250–66].

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [19 February 1871]
letters.summary: Thanks CD for copy ofDescent.Is considering running for School Board.

letters.title: From Henry Holland   19 February [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks for copy ofDescent.

letters.title: To John Murray   19 February [1871]
letters.summary:
Discusses publication ofDescent. Orders copies of vol. 2 sent to Wallace, Mivart, and F. P. Cobbe.

Will attend Athenaeum and vote for RC.

letters.title: From C. C. Blake   20 February 1871
letters.summary:
Has just received copy of CD’s work [Descent].

Can corroborate artificial compression of skull practised by Indians.

May have to modify his earlier published opinions on CD’s views.

letters.title: To James Crichton-Browne   20 February [1871]
letters.summary:
JC-B’s MS most useful.

P. Gratiolet’s observations on contraction and dilation of pupils of eye of a person in extreme terror. Has JC-B ever observed this? Expression has been his hobby-horse for 30 years.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   20 February 1871
letters.summary: Thanks for new book [Descent].

letters.title: From Robert McLachlan   20 February 1871
letters.summary:
Thanks forDescent; will forward any information he has after he has studied it.

Instance of inequality in left and right anal appendices of caddis-fly.

letters.title: To J. J. Moulinié   20 February [1871]
letters.summary: Sends corrections for French edition ofDescent.

letters.title: From John Murray   20 February [1871]
letters.summary: A second edition [issue] ofDescentmay be needed in short time; preparations should be made, and corrections sent to Clowes. Wallace, Mivart, and F. P. Cobbe have been sent copies of both volumes.

letters.title: From Thomas Woolner   20 February 1871
letters.summary: Thanks CD for sending his book [Descent].

letters.title: From Hermanus Hartogh Heijs van Zouteveen   [before 21 February 1871]
letters.summary: Notes onVariationandDescent.

letters.title: From George Cupples   21 February 1871
letters.summary: Thanks for presentation copy ofDescent.

letters.title: From William Farr   21 February 1871
letters.summary: Thanks for the gift of the book [Descent].

letters.title: From F. W. Farrar   21 February [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks for copy ofDescent.

letters.title: From W. D. Fox   21 February [1871]
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for copy ofDescent.

Notes the death of Frank Parker [CD’s nephew].

letters.title: To Hermanus Hartogh Heijs van Zouteveen   21 February 1871
letters.summary:
Thanks HHHvZ for a memoir

and answers some queries;

mentions some corrections for his Dutch translation ofDescent.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   21 February 1871
letters.summary:
Various comments onDescent;

on suicide on Gold Coast;

on mulattoes’ not being prolific.

letters.title: From George Rolleston   22 February 1871
letters.summary: Applauds CD’s expression of dissent from J. S. Mill’s view of differences of mental powers of men and women [Descent2: 326–9]. Sends some corrections.

letters.title: From George Rolleston   [after 22 February 1871]
letters.summary: Suggests alteration inDescent[1st ed. 7th thousand] in citing pagination of George Busk’s paper "The caves of Gibraltar" [Trans. Int. Congr. Prehist. Archaeol.3 (1868): 106–67].

letters.title: From W. B. Dawkins   23 February 1871
letters.summary: Thanks for the present of CD’s long-expected book [Descent].

letters.title: From John Murray   23 February [1871]
letters.summary: Descentpublication costs, "including a heavy item of £126 for corrections" have been received. JM can now offer CD 600 guineas for the edition of 2500 copies.

letters.title: To John Murray   23 February 1871
letters.summary: Receipt for payment by John Murray of £630 for the first edition, consisting of 2500 copies, ofDescent.

letters.title: From John Tyndall   23 February [1871]
letters.summary: Has devised a respirator for firemen by moistening cotton wool with glycerine and adding charcoal. JT suggests the nose with its hairs and mucus is a respirator that would give protection against diseases caused by floating particles. The presence of hair and mucus is thus explained by CD’s theory.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   24 February 1871
letters.summary:
Received copy ofDescent.

Discusses CD’s comments on EH’s work.

Speculates about reception by press and scientists.

Remarks on sexual selection;

on human relationship to catarrhine apes.

Has rejected offer of chair at Vienna.

Compares Jena to Down.

Describes growth of his salary.

Mentions birth of Emma Haeckel.

A. M. Norman’s collection of calcareous sponges is very valuable.

letters.title: From St George Jackson Mivart   24 February [1871]
letters.summary: Would be pleased if CD called.

letters.title: From Julius Sachs   24 February 1871
letters.summary:
Thanks for copy ofDescent.

Admires natural selection.

Climbing plantshas attracted attention in Germany, but most botanists are interested in cell development and similar questions.

letters.title: To P. L. Sclater   [24 February 1871]
letters.summary: Will send F. Du Cane Godman’s book [Natural history of the Azores(1870)] as soon as he returns home.

letters.title: From James Anderson   [after 24 February 1871?]
letters.summary:
Sends two books detailing a new medical method that will produce "a state of health & vigour on every occasion & in every instance" and is applicable to "the entire circle of animated nature" [William Hibbert,Important discovery. Hibbert’s new theory and practice of medicine(1870) andThe new theory and practice of medicine(1870)]. The volumes apply to animals and man. Subsequent books will detail the method for insects and plants.

[Letter erroneously addressed to E. A. Darwin, and forwarded by EAD to CD.]

letters.title: From E. F. Lubbock   [after 24 February 1871]
letters.summary: Verses on theOriginandDescent.

letters.title: To E. F. Lubbock   [after 24 February 1871]
letters.summary: Thanks for verses onOriginandDescent.

letters.title: From C. L. Bernays   25 February 1871
letters.summary: Older settlers in U. S. are taller and thinner than recent immigrants.

letters.title: From William Ogle   25 February [1871]
letters.summary:
Thanks forDescent.

He believes he has observed a predominance of the right side over the left in monkeys and man. If so, this is another support of their relatedness.

letters.title: To ?   25 February [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks for two reviews ofDescent. Second is "most fair, kind and carefully abstracted".

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   26 February [1871]
letters.summary: Suggests sending his book [Descent?] toPopular Science Review.

letters.title: From Andrew Smith   26 February 1871
letters.summary: Admires CD’s ability to work so hard under adverse circumstances; finds his health makes all work an effort.

letters.title: From John Murray   27 February [1871]
letters.summary: First edition [issue] ofDescentis exhausted. Asks CD to send corrections at once for a new printing of at least 1000 copies.

letters.title: To John Tyndall   [27 February 1871]
letters.summary:
Thinks JT’s discovery of a glycerine respirator is an interesting practical discovery. CD has been wondering about the hairs in our nostrils, but doubts that JT has explained their function, since there are hardly enough.

Will ask W. Ogle to observe hairs in nostrils of different races.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [28 February 1871]
letters.summary:
SaysDescentis "selling like Mad.––" Murray will print another 1500 or 2000 copies. Has received £630 for the 2500.

On Monday he visited Mivart, who is a charming man.

He seemed to be taken aback by CD’s points about the larynx and giraffe.

[See7507and7519.]

He seemed to have forgotten CD’s argument regarding the formation of the greyhound.

Discussed the larynx and the silence of the Cetaceans.

If FD mentions any of this to [Marlborough Robert] Pryor, ask him not to mention it to anyone else "as it is perhaps rather a breach of confidence to repeat even to friends private conversation."

letters.title: From Anton Dohrn   28 February 1871
letters.summary:
Thanks CD forVariation.

From his work on insect embryology he sees a great parallelism between insect and vertebrate embryology.

The zoological station is slowly advancing.

letters.title: From Charles and Emma Darwin to F. J. Wedgwood   [March 1871?]
letters.summary:
A draft letter [but sent in the original state by Emma Darwin]. Approves of FJW’s notice of his views.

CD has slightly revised parts in view of both approving and disapproving critics, but still remains convinced about his fundamental notions.

letters.title: From J. J. Aubertin   1 March 1871
letters.summary:
Was reminded of CD by his new book [Descent] in a shop;

reports having come on train as far as Bromley in previous summer, but found no means of travelling the seven miles to Down. Might try again.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   1 March 1871
letters.summary: Parallel between CD’s account of morality [inDescent], of social instinct preceding selfishness, and Henry Maine’s account of notions of property of a community preceding individual property [inAncient law(1861)].

letters.title: To John Murray   [1 March 1871]
letters.summary: Discusses new edition ofDescent.

letters.title: To John Tyndall   1 March [1871]
letters.summary:
Ogle will keep JT’s suggestion in mind in observing less hairy races of man and the lower animals.

Asks JT whether he can help Ogle on a troublesome point on the colour of tissues with olfactory nerves, and the relation of colour to the absorption of odours. Does JT’s respirator deprive odorous substances of their smell?

letters.title: To John Tyndall   1 March [1871]
letters.summary: Ogle is unacquainted with JT; would be proud and pleased to call on him. CD likes what little he has seen of him.

letters.title: From John Tyndall   1 March [1871]
letters.summary: JT suggests that Ogle call upon him so that they can arrange experiments suitable for his purpose.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   2 [March 1871]
letters.summary: Was aware of Maine’s view but never thought of its extension to morals. Cannot avoid thinking that personal property like flint tools must have "strictly belonged to individuals as much as a bone to a dog".

letters.title: From W. R. Greg   2 March [1871?]
letters.summary: Quotes authority on the decline in height of French army recruits.

letters.title: From Hermanus Hartogh Heijs van Zouteveen   2 March 1871
letters.summary:
Dutch translation [ofDescent].

Notes about reversion.

Hermaphroditism in fishes.

Polydactylism.

letters.title: From James Murie   2 March 1871
letters.summary:
Thanks forDescent.

He is "driven" from his post.

He has homologised the face muscles of cetaceans and man. Although the former do not show expression, the nose and upper lip muscles are highly developed.

letters.title: From Hensleigh Wedgwood   [before 3 March 1871]
letters.summary: On "moral sense" inDescent.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [3–9 March 1871]
letters.summary: Comments on points made in Hensleigh Wedgwood’s letter [7470] on moral sense inDescent.

letters.title: From Hensleigh Wedgwood   [3–9 March 1871]
letters.summary: Agrees that social instinct or love for fellows is the beginning of moral feeling. Responds to CD’s letter [7537].

letters.title: To J. J. Aubertin   3 March [1871]
letters.summary:
Invites him to visit.

Miss Butler is dead.

letters.title: From A. F. Baillie   3 March 1871
letters.summary: RereadingJournal of researches, particularly on Buenos Aires and varieties of cattle observed there [pp. 145–6]. Reports a case of a cow in which the characters of the niata and two other breeds were combined.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   3 March 1871
letters.summary: On private property, with regard to tools and arms; comments on Maine’s book and the history of law regarding property.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   3 March 1871
letters.summary:
Comments onDescent.

EH’s refusal of position at Vienna.

letters.title: From J. J. Moulinié   3 March 1871
letters.summary:
French translation ofDescentall but complete.

Hopes translation ofOriginwill soon be finished.

letters.title: From Herbert Spencer   3 March 1871
letters.summary: Thanks CD for copy ofDescent; wishes it had appeared earlier so that he could have made use of the facts in hisPrinciples of psychology[2d ed. (1870–2)].

letters.title: To Hensleigh Wedgwood   3 March [1871]
letters.summary:
Admits pointer illustration is faulty.

Discusses shame, remorse, social instincts, approbation, and other topics discussed inDescent, ch. 4. "But as yet I nail my colours to the mast."

letters.title: To Joseph Wolf   3 March 1871
letters.summary: Asks for a drawing from life of a "laughing monkey" (Cynopithecus niger) forExpression[p. 136].

letters.title: From J. J. Aubertin   4 March 1871
letters.summary:
Thanks for letter and invitation to come to Down.

Sorry about CD’s bad health; Brazilian climate has improved his own.

Sorry to hear Miss Butler is dead.

letters.title: To F. du C. Godman   4 March [1871]
letters.summary:
Has forwarded FDuCG’s book [Natural history of the Azores(1870)] to Dr Hartlaub.

Asks about eyes of camel when the animal is uttering a loud sound.

letters.title: To the Linnean Society   4 March [1871]
letters.summary: Thinks J. P. M. Weale’s papers all require great condensation.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   4 March 1871
letters.summary: Praise for gentle but resolute tone ofDescent.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [after 4 March 1871]
letters.summary: Very glad about profits of book. Glad CD flummoxed Mivart.

letters.title: From Leonard Darwin   [after 4 March 1871]
letters.summary: Recommends a photographer to CD forExpression.

letters.title: To Hermanus Hartogh Heijs van Zooteveen   5 March [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks for letter [7533] and the interesting notes. Even more interesting is HHHvZ’s case of the De Haas family.

letters.title: From William Johnson   5 March 1871
letters.summary:
Reports case of apparent consciousness of complicity in an elephant.

Believes that Darwinism is applicable to Greek language.

letters.title: From J. F. McLennan   6 March 1871
letters.summary: Thanks for copy ofDescent. Dining with Vernon Lushington, who is jubilant over the book.

letters.title: To J. J. Moulinié   7 March [1871]
letters.summary: Pleased that JJM has finished translation ofDescent.

letters.title: From Arthur Nicols   7 March 1871
letters.summary: Referring to CD’s passage on monkeys’ acquiring taste for tea, coffee, and tobacco, AN tells of three monkeys he kept in Australia that developed strong taste for rum and smoking tobacco without being taught in any way [seeDescent, 2d ed., p. 7 n.].

letters.title: To William Ogle   7 March [1871]
letters.summary:
Will write again to Tyndall about odours.

Asks for the circumstances under which WO saw a man arrested for murder; quotes from notes he made from WO’s conversation [Expression, p. 294].

Also would like to quote WO on the expression of resignation by persons about to undergo serious operations [Expression, p. 271].

letters.title: To John Tyndall   7 March [1871]
letters.summary: Ogle wants very much to meet JT.

letters.title: From Alphonse de Candolle   8 March 1871
letters.summary:
Thanks forDescent.

Reveals that it is his own family that has the movable scalp.

The Franco-Prussian war has held up the publication of the 17th and last volume of theProdromus.

letters.title: To John Murray   8 March [1871]
letters.summary:
Asks what his profits on the reprints ofDescentwill be when half have been sold.

Good reviews inSaturday ReviewandPall Mall Gazette;

contemptuous one as usual inAthenæum.

letters.title: To John Tyndall   8 March [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks JT for his kindness to Ogle.

letters.title: From John Tyndall   8 March [1871]
letters.summary: Has seen Ogle. His subject [olfactory nerve tissue and absorption of odours] has often occupied JT’s attention.

letters.title: From Emile Alglave   9 March 1871
letters.summary: Reminds CD of earlier promise to permit extracts ofDescentto be translated and published in EA’sRevue Scientifiqueonce entire work is printed. Book appeared weeks ago, so EA again requests permission.Revuehas been appearing irregularly owing to war with Germans.

letters.title: From John Murray   9 March [1871]
letters.summary: JM will print 2000 more copies ofDescentas a second edition [issue]. Profits should be large as expenses are small.

letters.title: To Hensleigh Wedgwood   9 March 1871
letters.summary: Seeks to clarify his and HW’s views on the causes of repentance or shame.

letters.title: From Hensleigh Wedgwood   [after 9 March 1871]
letters.summary: Answers CD’s letter [7560], on points of agreement between them, the chief one being the sympathy which man has with his fellows. Disagrees however with CD’s "principle" of the painful feelings of dissatisfied instinct.

letters.title: From George Busk   10 March 1871
letters.summary: Clarification of the supra-condyloid foramen in humans and animals.

letters.title: To G. B. A. Duchenne   about 10 March [1871]
letters.summary: Asks permission to copy plates from GBAD’s work [Mécanisme de la physionomie humaine(1862)] to illustrateExpression.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   10 and 14 March [1871]
letters.summary:
Has received CD’s new book [Descent].

Will try to get answer to CD’s queries on Laura Bridgman.

letters.title: From R. M. Kettle   10 March [1871]
letters.summary: Requests permission to quote from CD’s letters to Charles Boner in her edition [ofMemoirs and letters of Charles Boner(1871)].

letters.title: From G. B. Murdoch   10 March 1871
letters.summary: Relation of surplus vigour of males to sexual selection.

letters.title: From John Jeremiah   11 March 1871
letters.summary: Case of cat transmitting a habit to her offspring.

letters.title: To Frederick Currey   11 March 1871
letters.summary: Gives his opinion on four papers by J. P. M. Weale.

letters.title: From Arthur Nicols   11 March 1871
letters.summary:
His previous account ofPhaseolarctuswas based on notes made at the time of observation.

His report of the successful adoption of a koala infant by a cat comes from a trustworthy observer.

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   11 March 1871
letters.summary:
Recounts case of parrot whose talking seems to show "power of connecting definite sounds with definite ideas" [seeDescent, 2d ed., p. 85 n.].

Has not seen CD’s daughter yet. Hopes the fine weather will continue while she is there [in Bournemouth].

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   11 March 1871
letters.summary:
Admiration for vol. 2 ofDescent, and plans for his review of it for theAcademy[2 (1871): 177–82].

News of his new residence.

letters.title: From D. Thomas   [after 11 March 1871]
letters.summary: CD is "bent upon linking the monkey race to us"; DT finds it striking that CD should so resemble an ape.

letters.title: To George Busk   12 March [1871]
letters.summary:
Discusses his blunder in "confounding the two foramina" [in the skull] of apes [inDescent].

Discusses views of George Rolleston, St George Mivart, and Huxley on the occurrence of the foramina.

letters.title: From Patrick Matthew   12 March 1871
letters.summary:
Encloses an article he wrote for theScotsman[9 Mar 1871, p. 5].

Wishes he had time to write a critique ofDescent. There is evidence of design and benevolence in nature. Beauty cannot be accounted for by natural selection.

letters.title: To William Ogle   12 March [1871]
letters.summary:
Thanks WO for his replies [to7551]. Discusses the open mouth in surprise; asks WO to investigate its function in hearing and breathing.

Asks why deaf persons generally keep mouths open.

letters.title: To G. B. Murdoch   13 March 1871
letters.summary: Believes he has committed an oversight with regard to sexual selection in insects. Cites conclusions of B. T. Lowne, which are similar to GBM’s.

letters.title: To John Murray   13 March 1871
letters.summary: Pleased about sale and new issue [ofDescent]. Discusses presentation copies.

letters.title: To B. J. Sulivan   13 March [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks BJS for his interesting letter about parrots and language.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   13 March [1871]
letters.summary: Asks whether Bugis [Buggess] are Malays. [See7587.]

letters.title: From F. C. Donders   14 March 1871
letters.summary:
Thanks CD forDescent.

Sends a copy of hisoratio inauguralisonDe harmonie van het dierlijke leven[1848] in which he espoused evolution, but did not see the influence of natural selection.

letters.title: From W. R. Greg   14 March [1871]
letters.summary: Comments on various points inDescent: proportion of sexes, moral sentiments in animals, etc. Encloses "packet of data" [missing].

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   14 March 1871
letters.summary:
Russian translation ofDescentin progress, but the Minister of Interior has banned CD’s work and the book will be seized.

His foolish brother-in-law, Mayor of Montmartre, attempted to defend their section against the government.

CD’s queries on man and camels have gone to Alexander [Kovalevsky] in Sinai.

letters.title: From Robert Swinhoe   14 March 1871
letters.summary: Is leaving for Ningpo; asks CD for another copy of his [Queries about expression], which he will try to answer.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   15 March 1871
letters.summary: Sends CD a list of misprints in vol. 1 ofDescent.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   15 March [1871]
letters.summary: Wants WED to thank F. de Chaumont for some valuable observations.

letters.title: To Patrick Matthew   15 March [1871]
letters.summary: PM’s letter and newspaper article [see7576] show him to be still vigorous. CD doubts that he himself will be good for much more.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   [15 March 1871]
letters.summary: Although their language is different, the Bugis are typical Malays both physically and mentally.

letters.title: To R. H. Blair   [before 16 March 1871]
letters.summary:
Thanks RHB for information on expression in the blind.

Sends queries on expression and asks whether he could answer them with respect to those born blind.

letters.title: From R. H. Blair   16 March 1871
letters.summary: Will be pleased to collect information on the blind for CD when time allows. Generally very few (about one quarter) of blind people entering institutions are born blind.

letters.title: From George Busk   16 March 1871
letters.summary: The presence of the inter-condyloid perforation in man no more indicates his simian relations than it does his relations to numerous other animals.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   16 March 1871
letters.summary: Appreciative response to ARW’s "grand review" ofDescentin theAcademy[2 (1871–2): 177–82]. Comments in detail on ARW’s criticisms.

letters.title: From Emile Alglave   17 March 1871
letters.summary: Comments on continued appearance ofRevue[des cours scientifiques] despite German siege. Plans enlarged format to include politics and political economy. Repeats request to publish first part ofDescent, chapter by chapter, to be followed by publication of the whole.

letters.title: From Lewin Hill   17 March 1871
letters.summary: Case of hereditary transmission; in his own family ten of LH’s generation suffer a defect in the right knee-joint.

letters.title: To F. C. Donders   18 March 1871
letters.summary:
Comments on FCD’s 1848 work [see7582] in which he came near to anticipating CD.

Comments on FCD’s paper [on action of the eyelids, see7203]. Asks about contraction or dilation of the iris due to emotional states, illness, or prostration.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   18 March [1871]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Comments onDescent[2: 358–60] especially on CD’s view that behaviour of lower animals is evidence against JL’s interpretation [of aboriginal promiscuity]. View on communal marriage.

letters.title: From George Morrish   18 March 1871
letters.summary: Having read extracts of CD’s work, he argues that the scriptural version of man’s origin is superior, and he is concerned about CD’s salvation.

letters.title: From John Murray   18 March [1871]
letters.summary:
Second "edition" [ofDescent] published this day. Offers CD 800 guineas.

Mentions Wallace’s review inAcademy.

letters.title: To William Ogle   18 March [1871]
letters.summary:
Agrees that in a deaf person the jaw may fall because of concentrated attention.

In surprise, mouth is opened suddenly and chest filled with air. This expression occurs in all parts of the world. Odd that so simple a movement is so perplexing to understand.

letters.title: To T. R. R. Stebbing   18 March [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks TRRS for copy of his book [Essays on Darwinism(1871)].

letters.title: From Edwin Brown   19 March 1871
letters.summary:
Is studyingDescent.

Raises two questions for CD: on the great percentage of female illegitimate births compared with legitimate,

and on clothing as accounting for hairlessness of humans.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   19 March 1871
letters.summary:
Describes plans for travel in Morocco with George Maw and John Ball.

Has not yet readDescent.

letters.title: To H. E. Darwin   20 March 1871
letters.summary:
Reports on sales and reception of his book [Descent]. Thanks HED for her help.

Wallace’s article in theAcademy[2 (1870–1): 177–82] shows CD has had no influence on him; the review has had hardly any influence on CD.

letters.title: To John Murray   20 March 1871
letters.summary:
Pleased with sum the reprint [ofDescent] has produced. Terms of payment accepted.

Thanks JM forNonconformist[review ofDescent, 32 (1871): 240–1].

Would like to see other out-of-way reviews – especially religious.

Other reviews favourable, including Wallace’s [see7569], which is admirable.

letters.title: From John Murray   20 March [1871]
letters.summary: Demand [forDescent] is such that JM thinks he will have to print 1000 more copies. Does not want to trouble CD for corrections.

letters.title: To W. R. Greg   21 March [1871]
letters.summary:
Comments on WRG’s MS on ratio of the sexes at birth.

Offers to send J. M. A. Thury’s paper ["Loi de production des sexes",Arch. Sci. Phys. & Nat.18 (1863): 91–8].

letters.title: To Pieter Harting   21 March 1871
letters.summary: Thanks PH for his memoir onPoterion[Natuurkd. Verh. Utrecht2 (1870)].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   21 March [1871]
letters.summary:
Asks name of anAbutilonfrom Fritz Müller.

Questions aboutDrosophyllumfor experiments;

the meaning of "Sirdar".

Wonderful success ofDescent. Astonished by liberality of public. No abuse yet.

Marvels at JDH’s plans for a trip to Morocco. Asks him to look for alpine insects.

letters.title: To John Murray   21 March 1871
letters.summary: Is astonished at sale [ofDescent]. Will make no additions, but must correct a few misprints and errors [for third issue].

letters.title: From Hensleigh Wedgwood   [21 March 1871]
letters.summary: Copy of and note on a picture of Noah’s daughter averting her eyes in shame.

letters.title: To E. R. Lankester   22 March [1871]
letters.summary: Asks for photograph of pointed ear of ERL’s friend.

letters.title: To John Murray   22 March [1871]
letters.summary: Has this day sent off corrections for new issue [ofDescent]. Asks whether title-page may read "Sixth Thousand".

letters.title: From John Murray   22 March 1871
letters.summary: Completes payment for 2d issue [ofDescent]; has sold 1300 of the 2000 copies printed. Will probably print 2000 more for 3d issue.

letters.title: To Lewin Hill   23 March [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks LH for his account of a family weakness of the knee.

letters.title: To John Murray   23 March 1871
letters.summary: Amount received from 2d issue ofDescentnow stands at £840. Would be glad to have 2000 more copies printed because he wants time to collect information for a corrected edition.

letters.title: From R. H. Tiddeman   23 March 1871
letters.summary: On the case of a male acquaintance with two pairs of mammae.

letters.title: To Annie Dowie   24 March 1871
letters.summary:
Robert Chambers, AD’s father, spoke of CD’s book [Descent?] during his last hours of life.

CD’s respect for Chambers, to whose scientific work he had not done justice.

letters.title: To Frederick Greenwood   24 March [1871]
letters.summary: Encloses a letter [7617] to be forwarded to the author of the review ofDescentinPall Mall Gazette.

letters.title: To P. B. Mason   24 March [1871]
letters.summary: Interested in occurrence of hair on backs of weakly children. Asks PBM if he would report particulars of any case he observes during next 6–12 months.

letters.title: From J. F. McLennan   24 March 1871
letters.summary: Unfortunately he has missed an opportunity to reviewDescentinNature.

letters.title: To E. S. Newall?   24 March 1871
letters.summary: Sends his signature.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   24 March [1871]
letters.summary: On the flourishing sales of their respective books. Mentions reviews ofDescentinPall Mall Gazette[21 Mar 1871] and in theSpectator[11 Mar 1871, pp. 288–9; 18 Mar 1871, pp. 319–20].

letters.title: From M. B. Bathoe   25 March [1871]
letters.summary:
Anecdotal comments on various sections ofDescent:

Red Indians erecting their ears;

reasoning in a pet antelope, stag deer, and mongoose;

use of foot as prehensile organ by carpenters in India.

letters.title: From Mary Charlton   25 March 1871
letters.summary: Thanks for £50 contribution to Edward Cresy’s memorial. £1000 collected so far for an annuity for Mrs Cresy.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   25 March [1871]
letters.summary: If FD gets the chance, will he observe whether the platysma contracts in a shivering fit? Wants much to know whether the platysma of frightened patients contracts before chloroform is given.

letters.title: From G. B. A. Duchenne   25 March 1871
letters.summary: Gives CD permission to use photographs of expressions.

letters.title: To William Ogle   25 March [1871]
letters.summary: Asks WO to act out the sudden discovery of a dreadful object and to observe whether his platysma contracts. CD has found in his notes that it is never contracted in cases of severe dyspnoea [Expression, p. 301].

letters.title: To James Crichton-Browne   26 March [1871]
letters.summary:
Has sent photographs of insane woman to be engraved. Assumes JC-B has no objection.

Is making immense use of JC-B’s MS. The book ought to be described as "by Darwin & Browne".

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   26 March 1871
letters.summary:
Answers CD’s questions.

Reception ofDescent. Evolution accepted everywhere; descent of man accepted calmly.

Morocco plans.

Fears for Huxley, who is overworked.

letters.title: From John Morley   26 March 1871
letters.deprecated: John Morley, Viscount Morley of Blackburn
letters.sender: John Morley, Viscount Morley of Blackburn
letters.summary: Thanks for CD’s letter on his review ofDescentin thePall Mall Gazette[21 Mar 1871].

letters.title: To A. D. Kindermann   [27 March 1871]
letters.summary: Wants permission to have some of AK’s photographs copied forExpression.

letters.title: To James Crichton-Browne   28 March [1871]
letters.summary:
Asks whether capillary circulation is ever influenced by the mind’s being directed intently to any part of the body.

Has JC-B ever seen idiots blush? JC-B’s MS on blushing is capital.

letters.title: From F. C. Donders   28 March 1871
letters.summary: Answers to CD’s queries will take time. CD may not be aware of the influence of accommodation on the diameter of the pupil of the eye. Parrots, for example, contract or dilate the pupil independently of amount of light [seeExpression, p. 304]. Sends his book on the subject [On the anomalies of accommodation and refraction of the eye(1864)].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   28 March [1871]
letters.summary:
SendsHibiscus

and enclosure [Queries about expression?] on chance of "any point being observed" in Morocco.

Murray informs him edition ofDescentwill probably be 6500 copies.

letters.title: To William Ogle   28 [March 1871]
letters.summary: Thanks WO for his reply to letter of 26 March. Has tried several people and platysma seemed to act, but it is difficult to observe when they shudder.

letters.title: To William Turner   28 March [1871]
letters.summary:
Discusses errors inDescent. Not surprised that WT is not committed to full acceptance of evolution of man.

At work onExpression. Asks about muscles that raise spines of hedgehog and tail coverts of peacock. Asks about influence of mind on capillaries with regard to blushing. Mentions views of James Paget on influence of the mind on nutrition of body parts.

letters.title: From Harrison Weir   28 March 1871
letters.summary:
Effects of first impregnation on litters from subsequent pregnancies.

Power of selective breeding to produce different varieties.

letters.title: From William Turner   [after 28 March 1871]
letters.summary: Note on errata in first volume ofDescent.

letters.title: From James Crichton-Browne   [29–31 March 1871]
letters.summary: On the power of concentration to influence body organs.

letters.title: From James Crichton-Browne   29 March 1871
letters.summary: Sends scraps of information. Everything he has sent is unreservedly at CD’s disposal.

letters.title: To G. B. A. Duchenne   29 March [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks GBAD for permission to use his photographs [see7623] and for the information on the expression of astonishment in monkeys.

letters.title: From J. M. Fleming   29 March 1871
letters.summary: Discusses breeding fancy pigeons from the wild blue rock-dove.

letters.title: From P. B. Mason   29 March 1871
letters.summary:
More details on children with hairy backs;

reasons for greater mortality rate of male children.

letters.title: To William Turner   29 March [1871]
letters.summary: Comments on influence of nervous system on nutrition of body parts as discussed in James Paget’sLectures on surgical pathology[delivered at the Royal College of Surgeons of England, 3d ed. (1870)]. Asks about mental influence on capillary circulation.

letters.title: To Erasmus Wilson   29 March [1871]
letters.summary: Wonders whether correspondent might possibly know of any cases in which intense concentration of the mind on one portion of the skin produces dilation of the capillary vessels and hence reddening of the area.

letters.title: From Anne Barnard   30 March 1871
letters.summary: On readingDescentwas reminded of having seen, on a visit to an idiot asylum with her father [J. S. Henslow], a woman with long pointed ears.

letters.title: To Thomas Guthrie?   30 March [1871]
letters.summary: Sends correspondent a £25 subscription for George Cupples.

letters.title: From John Morley   30 March 1871
letters.deprecated: John Morley, Viscount Morley of Blackburn
letters.sender: John Morley, Viscount Morley of Blackburn
letters.summary: Questions CD’s attribution of a sense of beauty to animals and his use of natural selection to explain phenomena JM feels it more appropriate to describe as social selection.

letters.title: To Anne Barnard   31 March [1871]
letters.summary:
Thanks AHB for her letter about girl with pointed ears.

His undying gratitude to her father [J. S. Henslow].

letters.title: From Frederic Bateman   31 March [1871]
letters.summary: Sends his work discussing the anatomical seat of the faculty of language [On aphasia(1870)]. Concludes that it may be impossible to find any cerebral centre for speech and that this fact opposes the idea of the descent of man from some lower form.

letters.title: From Edouard van Beneden   31 March 1871
letters.deprecated: Édouard Joseph Louis Marie (Édouard) van Beneden
letters.sender: Édouard Joseph Louis Marie (Édouard) van Beneden
letters.summary:
Many thanks for copy ofDescent.

Would like to visit CD when he comes to England.

letters.title: To P. B. Mason   31 March [1871]
letters.summary:
Thanks him for information on children with hairy backs.

Discusses paper by J. M. Duncan on the relative weights of male and female infants.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [1–4 April 1871]
letters.summary: Mentions some photos relating to expression.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [April 1871?]
letters.summary: J. S. Mill’s account of the moral sense inUtilitarianism[1863] appears muddled. [SeeDescent1: 71 n.]

letters.title: To Frederic Harrison   1 April [1871]
letters.summary: Discusses his concept of beauty. "I daresay I have made too much of natural selection".

letters.title: To F. J. Wedgwood   [after 1 April 1871?]
letters.summary: Protests against FJW making the struggle for existence still more odious by calling it ‘selfish competition’.

letters.title: From E. B. de Fonblanque   2 April 1871
letters.summary: Encloses notes that illustrate apparent intelligent reasoning by a dog which tricked an adversary, and by an elephant peaceably enduring a painful operation.

letters.title: From J. E. Gray   2 April 1871
letters.summary: Sexual differences in sloths. J. G. Wagler article on sloths [Isis24 (1831): 604–12].

letters.title: From Hubert Airy   3 April 1871
letters.summary:
Comments on discussion of residual organs inDescent[ch. 1].

Describes his ability to contract the platysma myoides at will.

Suggests reason for loss of voluntary movement of ears in men and monkeys.

letters.title: From A. F. Boardman   3 April 1871
letters.summary: Apologises for shortcomings of his argument in earlier letters, explaining he has had little scientific education, but a life-long interest in progressive development. Resumes theorising.

letters.title: From James Crichton-Browne   3 April 1871
letters.summary:
Sends photographs of general paralytics. Expressions of exaltation of [these?] patients do not come out well in the photographs.

Is experimenting with idiots under his care. Has been unable to produce a blush in any one of them.

letters.title: From C. M. C. Darwin   3 April 1871
letters.summary: A friend with similar interests has asked to be introduced to CD, as he has some facts that will amuse him.

letters.title: From J. E. Gray   3 April 1871
letters.summary: Corrects error in his letter [7652] about date of Wagler article inIsis. Wagler said it was females that had the yellow dorsal spot.

letters.title: To Hubert Airy   5 April [1871]
letters.summary: Discusses loss of voluntary movement of ears in man and monkey.

letters.title: To John Le Couteur   6 April [1871]
letters.summary: Is honoured to hear from JLC and would welcome the communication of any facts that he cares to send him.

letters.title: From David Wedderburn   6 April 1871
letters.summary:
Sexual selection in deer.

Assemblies of black cocks.

Nests of spotted flycatcher.

letters.title: From John Wood   6 April 1871
letters.summary: Corrects CD on his assertion that the platysma myoides "cannot voluntarily be brought into action" [Descent1: 19].

letters.title: To James Crichton-Browne   7 April [1871]
letters.summary:
Thanks for information about blushing of idiots.

Case of pregnant woman "truly wonderful".

Thanks for photographs.

Has found London photographer, O. G. Rejlander, with passion for photographing expression.

Received information about iris of eye from F. C. Donders; shows contraction and dilation of pupil is very complex.

letters.title: From J. E. Gray   7 April 1871
letters.summary: Sexual differences in coloration inLemur macaco.

letters.title: From Hermanus Hartogh Heijs van Zouteveen   7 April 1871
letters.summary:
On some errata inDescent.

Sends extracts from a statistical study giving proportion of sexes in [population of] Netherlands.

letters.title: To Thomas Woolner   7 April [1871]
letters.summary: Asks TW to persuade painters to observe how far down body blush extends on models.

letters.title: To ?   7 April [1871]
letters.summary: Asks correspondent to thank Thomas Laycock for his references. CD has been away from home and has not yet consulted his copy of Laycock’sMind and brain[1860].

letters.title: From G. F. Ansell   8 April 1871
letters.summary: Anecdotes about a dog and cat evidencing "a high order of instinct".

letters.title: From Napoleon de la Fleurière   8 April [1871]
letters.summary:
Believes CD should answer the critical article [review ofDescent] in theTimes[of 7 and 8 Apr].

Moral sense and moral conduct.

letters.title: To J. P. Knight   8 April 1871
letters.summary: Formally declines dinner invitation.

letters.title: To Louisa Stevenson   8 April 1871
letters.summary: Agrees to have his or Emma Darwin’s name added to the General Committee for securing medical education to women.

letters.title: To James Crichton-Browne   9 April [1871]
letters.summary: Asks JC-B to read CD’s MS on confusion of mind, which often or generally accompanies blushing.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   9 April [1871]
letters.summary: Arrangements for transfer of rabbits to CD.

letters.title: To J. E. Gray   9 April [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks for information on colour differences in sexes ofLemur.

letters.title: From J. N. Hoare   10 April 1871
letters.summary: Sends quotations from Xenophon and Horace pointing to sexual selection. [SeeDescent, 2d ed., p. 29 n.]

letters.title: From R. M. Kettle   11 April [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks CD for correcting proof slips quoting CD letters to Charles Boner, though she does not agree with CD’s too short comments.

letters.title: From John Wood   11 April 1871
letters.summary: Emotional states leading to contraction of the platysma. Contraction of skin muscles.

letters.title: To James Crichton-Browne   12 April 1871
letters.summary: Discusses blushing. CD believes confusion of mind alone can account for it. Sends MS for JC-B’s comments and corrections.

letters.title: To W. B. Dawkins   12 April [1871]
letters.summary: Sends contribution of £5 to Settle Cave Exploration Fund.

letters.title: From George Fraser   12 April 1871
letters.summary: On sexual selection in butterflies. [See GF’s article inNature3 (1870–1): 489; alsoDescent(1875): 312.]

letters.title: From John Murray   12 April [1871]
letters.summary:
Asks CD’s opinion of a request from Loescher of Turin. Thinks Loescher should have named his translator.

Does CD know the name of theTimesreviewer?

letters.title: From George Fraser   13 April 1871
letters.summary: Corroborates and offers explanation of fact that male ghost-moths (Hepialis humuli) closely resemble females. [SeeDescent1: 402.]

letters.title: To John Murray   13 April [1871]
letters.summary: Has no idea who wrote theTimesreview [ofDescent]. Writer has no knowledge of science and "seems a windbag full of metaphysics & classics".

letters.title: To William Ogle   13 April [1871]
letters.summary: Reports further observations on contraction of platysma. Has been assisted by J. Wood. [SeeExpression, pp. 302, 303.]

letters.title: To George Fraser   14 April [1871]
letters.summary: Cannot provide comment on GF’s paper for publication. Hopes GF will publish inNature. Will consider his remarks when revising book [Descent].

letters.title: To Francis Galton   14 April [1871]
letters.summary: Reports safe arrival of rabbits.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   14 April 1871
letters.summary:
Is readingDescent.

Encloses some answers to CD’s queries about expressions of Laura Bridgman.

letters.title: From Eduard Koch   14 April 1871
letters.summary: Sends German edition ofDescent, vol. 1. Expects good sale. Hopes CD will offer him additional books to publish.

letters.title: To John Morley   14 April [1871]
letters.deprecated: John Morley, Viscount Morley of Blackburn
letters.recipient: John Morley, Viscount Morley of Blackburn
letters.summary:
Comments on JM’s review ofDescent, vol. 2 [Pall Mall Gaz.13 (1871): 1358–9].

Mistake CD made "in speaking of greatest happiness as the foundation of morals" is unintelligible to CD. Discusses J. S. Mill’s view of moral feelings as natural. Discusses basis of conscience.

Glad to read remarks on hive-bees.

letters.title: To C. L. Balch   15 April 1871
letters.summary:
Thanks for the report of CLB’s lecture aboutDescentto the New York Liberal Club on 3 March 1871.

Sends four photographs of himself for the sculptor J. W. A. MacDonald.

letters.title: From Arthur Nicols   15 April 1871
letters.summary:
Objects to the negative reviews ofDescent, notably in theAthenæumand theTimes.

The exceptions are theAcademy,Nature, and his own, in theField[37 (1871): 210].

letters.title: From C. L. Balch   [after 15 April 1871]
letters.summary:
CD’s photographs have been sent to [J. W. A.] McDonald, the sculptor, who will make a marble bust for the Liberal Club of New York and a bronze or plaster one for sale; CD will receive a copy. CD has been elected an Honorary Member of the Club, and

CB asks whether he could give them a few words of advice on a practical method of biological study for beginners.

letters.title: From James Crichton-Browne   16 April 1871
letters.summary:
Is sending notes on blushing. Offers information on physiology and pathology of blushing.

Has sent photograph of seven imbeciles in one family.

letters.title: To Michael Foster   16 April 1871
letters.summary: Encloses two questions he hopes MF can answer: the mechanism of transmission by nerves; and the mechanism by which contemplating part of our body, we become conscious of its existence

letters.title: To J. N. Hoare   16 April [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks for the information about the passages in Xenophon and Horace.

letters.title: From Hugh Browne   17 April [1871]
letters.summary:
Raises two points on CD’s view, inDescent[2: 229], on how aquatic birds acquire white plumage.

Also remarks on effect of will in certain human modifications,

on colour-blindness in his children,

and on ability to move his ears.

letters.title: To Bartholomäus von Carneri   17 April [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks BvC for the present of his book,Sittlichkeit und Darwinismus.

letters.title: From Hermann Hoffmann   17 April 1871
letters.summary:
Comments onDescent.

Reports a case of protective coloration of bugs onTilia

and observations on frogs fighting [seeDescent, 2d ed., pp. 281, 350].

Encloses drawings of chicken feet.

letters.title: From E. R. Lankester   17 April [1871]
letters.summary: Has had Hinrich Nitsche’s pointed ear photographed. Nitsche also has photographed the ear of a foetal orang. [SeeDescent1: 21–3.]

letters.title: From John Morley   17 April 1871
letters.deprecated: John Morley, Viscount Morley of Blackburn
letters.sender: John Morley, Viscount Morley of Blackburn
letters.summary:
Gratified that CD approves his analysis of CD’s views of moral sense. Does not think there is a fundamental difference between J. S. Mill (Utilitarianism[1863], p. 45) and CD.

His view of those who object to CD’s "new doctrine of the moral sense".

letters.title: From Andrew Smith   17 April 1871
letters.summary:
On Hottentots’ blushing.

Gives case of a baboon’s revenge. [SeeDescent, 2d ed. (1874), p. 69.]

letters.title: From Roland Trimen   17 and 18 April 1871
letters.summary:
Man’s spiritual life separates him from other animals.

Why are moths attracted, often fatally, to lights?

Thanks for copy ofDescent.

letters.title: To James Crichton-Browne   18 April 1871
letters.summary:
Comments on notes by JC-B on relation between blushing and mental disturbance. Asks for further information about blushing. "The single pencil line down this MS is my mark that I have used it once."

Thanks for "dreadful photo of the imbeciles".

letters.title: From Hinrich Nitsche   18 April 1871
letters.summary: Sends CD photographs of his atavistic ears and ears of a foetal orang in the collection of the Zoological Museum, Leipzig.

letters.title: From T. G. Cresy   19 April 1871
letters.summary: Thanks for contribution to fund for his brother’s widow.

letters.title: From W. R. Greg   19 April [1871]
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for thinking of his speculation.

Has made a note of the paper mentioned by CD.

letters.title: From John Wood   19 April 1871
letters.summary: Movement of hair; action of occipito-frontalis muscle.

letters.title: To Hermann Hoffmann   20 April [1871]
letters.summary:
Obliged for letter about dog.

Comments on HH’s article ["Zur Geschlechtsbestimmung",Bot. Ztg.29 (1871): 81–9, 97–109].

letters.title: From H. M. Westropp   20 April [1871]
letters.summary:
Anecdote of bear reasoning [seeDescent, 2d ed., p. 76].

Similarity of forms of ornamentation and implements in widely separate races and ages [Descent1: 233].

letters.title: To St G. J. Mivart   21 April [1871]
letters.summary: "If you feel astonished at my bringing man & brutes so near together in their whole nature (though with a wide hiatus) I feel still more astonished, as I believe, at your judgment on this head. I much wish you had enlarged your concluding sentence a little so as to say whether you consider the ordinary mental faculties so distinct, or whether you confine the enormous difference to spiritual powers including the moral sense.––"

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [before 22 April 1871?]
letters.summary: Expressions in attitudes of prayer and adoration.

letters.title: From Louisa Albano   22 April 1871
letters.summary:
Replies to CD’s letter;

inquires about CD’s intended terms for Italian translator ofDescent; hopes to offer best terms herself.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   22 April 1871
letters.summary: On ratios of the sexes in insects, and other facts relating to sexual selection.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   22 April [1871]
letters.summary:
Detailed questions about illustrations for [forthcoming]Expression.

Asks whetherTimesreview has hurt sales ofDescent.

The type on specimen page ofOrigin[6th ed.] seems clear, but lines are close. The cost is the great point for a wide circulation.

letters.title: From George Cupples   22 April 1871
letters.summary:
On reception ofDescentin Edinburgh.

Anecdote about a dog helping another by separating combatants.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   22 April [1871?]
letters.summary: Please thank Mr Jackson for facts about shrugging, but case not distinct enough. Gestures associated with laughter.Platysma.

letters.title: To H. M. Westropp   22 April [1871]
letters.summary: Case of the reasoning bear is analogous to the elephant blowing with trunk to bring object within reach.

letters.title: To Elliott & Fry   23 April [1871]
letters.summary: Gives permission for the photographer to come to Down, but states that O. J. Rejlander has recently taken several photographs of him which would be available to purchasers.

letters.title: From St G. J. Mivart   23 April 1871
letters.summary: Feels their conflict lies in the field of philosophy rather than in that of physical science. Regrets that they differ so widely.

letters.title: To John Murray   23 April [1871]
letters.summary:
Asks JM to lend him his copy of 1st edition (1806) of Charles Bell’sAnatomy of expression.

JM should tell him when he wants new cheap edition ofOrigin, so he can arrange his plans and time.

letters.title: From T. W. Wood   24 April 1871
letters.summary: John Murray has commissioned him to redraw two birds. Hopes to re-do all of the birds taken from Brehm’sThierleben.

letters.title: From Frank Chance   [before 25 April 1871]
letters.summary: His beard is darker than his hair, an exception to CD’s rule inDescent[2: 319]. Encloses sample of his hair, beard, and whiskers.

letters.title: From W. B. Tegetmeier   [before 25 April 1871]
letters.summary: WBT’s beard exceptional in that it is darker than his hair [seeDescent2: 319].

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   25 April [1871]
letters.summary:
Corrections forDescent. Has sold 6500 copies in England.

Has finished rough draft ofExpression, but will put it aside for the summer.

Will refresh himself with some curious observations on the response of plants to certain stimuli.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   25 April 1871
letters.summary: Upset to learn he has misrepresented CD’s doctrine on Pangenesis [inProc. R. Soc. Lond.19 (1871): 393–410]. Hopes that CD’s letter toNature[3 (1871): 502–3;Collected papers2: 165–7] will clarify the doctrine and attract attention to it.

letters.title: To Henry Johnson   25 April [1871?]
letters.summary:
Condolence on death of HJ’s daughter; "I know from old experience how bitter a loss it is".

Thanks for information about intelligence of dog.

letters.title: From F. T. Köppen   25 April 1871
letters.summary:
Sends his paper on locusts ["Die geographische Verbreitung der Wanderheuschrecke",Petermann’s Geogr. Mittheil.(1871)]. The effect of the growth of forest land on their increase; meteorological and climatic effects.

Also observations made on increase in mice as a result of increase of locusts, on whose eggs they fed, and of increase of weasels that fed on mice.

letters.title: To Hinrich Nitsche   25 April [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks HN for photographs of his ears and one showing the form of the ears in a foetal orang. He will show them to a wood-engraver when a new edition ofDescentis called for [seeDescent, 2d ed., p. 17].

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   25 April [1871]
letters.summary: Has read theFieldreview ofDescent["Darwin on the descent of man", 37 (1871): 210]. Thanks WBT for his remarks.

letters.title: From W. B. Tegetmeier   [after 25 April 1871]
letters.summary: Points out errata inDescent.

letters.title: From E. J. Pfeiffer   [before 26 April 1871]
letters.summary: Suggests aesthetic sense in animals is merely secondary to sexual selection.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   26 April 1871
letters.summary:
Believes heliotype process is best for book illustrations. Has sent copies [ofDescent] to Loescher and Carus.

Is working on an estimate for the cheap [6th] edition of theOrigin.

TheTimesreview has not hurt sales ofDescent.

letters.title: To E. J. Pfeiffer   26 April [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks for EJP’s suggestion that it is fascination rather than aesthetic appreciation that drives sexual selection.

letters.title: ToNature   [before 27 April 1871]
letters.summary: Replies to Francis Galton’s paper on tranfusing blood between rabbits to test Pangenesis [Proc. R. Soc. Lond.19 (1871): 393–40]. FG’s conclusion that his experiments prove Pangenesis to be false is "a little hasty", since CD had never maintained that gemmules in the blood formed any part of his hypothesis.

letters.title: From William Preyer   27 April 1871
letters.summary:
Thanks CD forOrigin, 5th ed.

Comments on reviews ofDescentby the Duke of Argyll and A. R. Wallace.

Lists the Darwinian professors at Jena.

WP’s work shows external ear to have no physiological functions.

W. Müller’s book not yet arrived. Will send Müller’s next works.

letters.title: From R. I. Thompson   27 April 1871
letters.summary: About a dog that acquired habits from a cat and her kittens.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   28 April 1871
letters.summary: Concerned with photographic processes for illustrations [forExpression].

letters.title: To F. T. Köppen   28 April [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks for FTK’s locust paper ["Die geographische Verbreitung der Wanderheuschrecke",Petermann’s Geogr. Mittheil.(1871)].

letters.title: From Williams & Norgate   28 April 1871
letters.summary: Information on the publishing history of a book [J. C. Lavater,Physiognomische Fragmente, 4 vols. (1775–8)].

letters.title: To William Ogle   29 April [1871]
letters.summary: Discusses action of the platysma in a state of fear.

letters.title: From C. A. J. Brooke   30 April 1871
letters.summary: Sends a small apparatus from Sarawak for getting fire.

letters.title: To William Preyer   30 April 1871
letters.summary:
Is sending copy ofDescent.

Thanks for copy of WP’s book [Die Blutkrystalle(1871)].

Discusses shape of external ear.

letters.title: From O. G. Rejlander   30 April 1871
letters.summary: Since it is difficult to catch the expressions CD wants, OGR is posing himself.

letters.title: To E. B. Tylor   30 April [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks EBT for present ofPrimitive culture[1871]. Feels certain he will regret not having read it before writingDescent.

letters.title: From C. H. Brett   1 May 1871
letters.summary: CorrectsDescent: snipes do breed in Ireland.

letters.title: From C. W. Peach   1 May 1871
letters.summary:
Sends specimens of gulf-weed and cirripedes for CD to identify.

Various observations onDescent,

inherited deafness,

recognition of musical notes by dog, etc.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   2 May 1871
letters.summary: Is sending his reply toNature, justifying his misunderstanding as well as he can [see7717].

letters.title: From Herbert Spencer   2 May 1871
letters.summary: Intends to answer Sir A. Grant’s article if CD does not. [A. Grant, "Philosophy and Mr Darwin",Contemp. Rev.17 (1871): 274–81; H. Spencer, "Mental evolution",Contemp. Rev.17 (1871): 461–2.]

letters.title: To V. O. Kovalevsky   3 May 1871
letters.summary:
Asks VOK to translate a passage from Franz Körte,Die Streich-, Zug- oder Wander-Heuschrecke[1828], p. 33.

Deplores the "fearful piece of tyranny" that is obstructing publication ofDescentin Russia.

letters.title: From Charles Langstaff   3 May 1871
letters.summary: Contraction of platysma occurs during surgery under chloroform from touch of knife, independently of fear.

letters.title: From Henry Lonsdale   3 May 1871
letters.summary: Credit for observation on supra-condyloid foramen in man is really due to Robert Knox, not John Struthers, as inDescent.

letters.title: To G. R. Jesse   4 May [1871]
letters.summary: Asks for information about habits of a breed of terriers.

letters.title: From M. T. Masters   6 May 1871
letters.summary: After readingDescent, MTM sends report of a dog that woke its master at 7 a.m. on work days and 8 a.m. on Sunday.

letters.title: From Luigi Pomba   6 May 1871
letters.summary: Arrangements for Italian translation ofDescent[1871].

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   8 May 1871
letters.summary: Sends photographs he intends to use inExpressionand asks for estimates of cost per thousand of each process [Woodburytype and Heliotype] suggested by RC and for different numbers of photos on each plate.

letters.title: From William Preyer   8 May 1871
letters.summary:
Delighted that CD does not hesitate to follow his theory to its last consequences. "This is far more difficult in England than in Germany."

Wilhelm Müller in his new book [Beiträge zur pathologischen Anatomie und Physiologie des menschlichen Rückenmarks(1871)], adduces many facts in favour of CD’s theory.

Various observations on the human ear. [SeeDescent, 2d ed., p. 14 n.]

letters.title: To M. T. Masters   9 May [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks correspondent for information about a dog.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   10 May 1871
letters.summary:
Paris is in the hands of "brigands and socialists", but one grows accustomed to sporadic bombardment,

and VOK is peacefully studying invertebrate palaeontology collections.

Reports on Paul Gervais’ successful cross between aTritonand an axolotl.

letters.title: To John Murray   10 May [1871]
letters.summary: CD is perplexed about illustrations forExpression, i.e., whether photographs are better than woodcuts. He thinks photographs, but does not know which process is preferable. Asks JM to inquire.

letters.title: From John Murray   10 May 1871
letters.summary:
Offers CD same payment for the 3d issue ofDescentas for 2d.

Has bespoke four better drawings of birds in case a 4th issue is needed.

Vanity Fairwants CD’s portrait by Carlo Pellegrini ["Ape"].

letters.title: To Luigi Pomba   10 May 1871
letters.summary: Has no objection to LP’s replacing Loescher in publishing an Italian translation ofDescent. Murray will give proper authorisation.

letters.title: From J. W. Spengel   10 May 1871
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his letter referring to JWS’s bibliographical paper ["Darwinian bibliography",Z. Ethnol.3 (1871): 56–67]. Will be glad to inform CD of any additions to the list and would be grateful for information on future publications.

letters.title: To ?   10 May [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks correspondent for item of criticism in a foreign newspaper.

letters.title: From F. E. Abbot   11 May 1871
letters.summary: Wishes to inform CD that, contrary to CD’s impression, natural selection is widely accepted in U. S. by educated men; encloses copies of his lectures, papers, and theIndex.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   [11 or 18 May 1871]
letters.summary: Asks for a ticket for THH’s lecture at the Royal Institution for WED. With ED’s and HED’s forgeries of CD’s signature.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   12 May 1871
letters.summary:
Writes that he does not share at all in Lionel Beale’s letter inNature[4 (1871): 25–6];

his new experiments are not hopeful.

letters.title: To John Murray   12 May [1871]
letters.summary:
Will require at least six weeks’ notice before a new edition ofDescenthas to go to press because of considerable corrections needed.

Thinks cheap edition ofOriginis needed, since he could answer objections in it.

letters.title: To William Preyer   13 May 1871
letters.summary: Obliged for letter about human ear. Comments on ears and on E. R. Lankester’s idea about the ear-lobe.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [14 May 1871]
letters.summary: Has arranged a trip to the U. S. with Cambridge friends; believes it would be much jollier if Frank could go too.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   14 May 1871
letters.summary: Recommends [W. M. Williams]The fuel of the sun[1870] as remarkably illuminating about physical astronomy. Williams solves the problem of duration of sun’s heat in "a most satisfactory manner".

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   16 May [1871]
letters.summary: George [Darwin] plans a trip to America and would like FD to go [see7757]. CD will gladly pay whole cost if the trip will not interfere with FD’s medical work.

letters.title: To Gustav Lindström   16 May [1871]
letters.summary: Is pleased GL is to translate theJournal of researchesinto Swedish.

letters.title: From Andrew Smith   16 May 1871
letters.summary: Disagrees with CD and especially with Lubbock and McLennan about communal marriage. [SeeDescent2: 361–3.]

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [after 16 May 1871]
letters.summary: He is waiting to hear about the requirements for the MB examination before considering the possible trip to north America.

letters.title: To V. O. Kovalevsky   17 May [1871]
letters.summary:
Interested in W. Hepworth Dixon’sFree Russia, but does not know "whether he is to be trusted".

VOK’s hard work in palaeontology will prepare him for future original investigations.

letters.title: To F. W. Farrar   19 May [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks for present of FWF’sThe witness of history[1871].

letters.title: To ?   19 May [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks for references about dogs. Fears work will not allow him to deal with subject again. Heartily subscribes to what correspondent says about qualities of dogs. Loves his "with all my heart".

letters.title: From J. W. Strutt   [after 20 May 1871?]
letters.summary: Criticises a book [W. M. Williams,The fuel of the sun(1870)] whose author does not understand thermodynamics, spectrum analysis, and W. Thomson’s papers.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   21 May [1871]
letters.summary:
CD will pay for the American trip if it takes place.

Asks whether FD can help him understand the eyes of cephalopods; is the structure the same as in the Vertebrata and are the parts developed from homologous layers of skin?

Has been pleased by a recent review.

Postscript: Is thinking of a cheap edition of theOrigin[1872] in which he hopes to answer St George Mivart’s criticisms.

Asks FD whether he can get some references to good papers on cephalapod eyes.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [after 22 May 1871]
letters.summary: Thanks for the cheque, and also for the offer to pay for him to go on a trip to north America with G. H. Darwin.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [after 22 May 1871]
letters.summary: Explains about the attendance at St George’s hospital that is required for the MB examaminations, and how this would affect plans for a trip to north America.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   23 May [1871]
letters.summary:
Will translate passages as CD requests [see7735].

Bitter at Prussian militarism.

letters.title: To Roland Trimen   24 May [1871]
letters.summary:
Cannot explain why moths fly into candle flames and birds against lighthouses. Has felt it was just curiosity which attracted them.

CD does believe dogs have some sense of humour.

letters.title: From Henry Reeks   25 May 1871
letters.summary: Comments on and corrections for chapter 13, "Mammals", ofDescent.

letters.title: From A. G. Butler   26 May 1871
letters.summary: Several observations on protective coloration and sexual selection.

letters.title: From J. B. Innes   26 May 1871
letters.summary:
Has finishedDescent, which charmed but did not convert him.

Sends examples of dogs’ reasoning.

Has given up his farm.

letters.title: From John Murray   26 May [1871]
letters.summary: Sends two bills [JM’s notes for payments due to CD] for £420 each for 3d issue ofDescent.

letters.title: To F. E. Abbot   27 May [1871]
letters.summary:
CD is surprised and gratified by the interest in his views in America.

Has read the extract from theLiberal Christiansent by FEA and alsoTruths for the times, which he admires.

letters.title: To John Murray   27 May [1871]
letters.summary: Asks JM for final decision about a cheap edition ofOrigin. Would like to begin soon to revise and answer recent objections.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   28 May 1871
letters.summary: Sends corrections forDescent.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   28 May [1871]
letters.summary:
More discussion of the illustrations forExpression.

A Swedish naturalist [G. Lindström] has asked to translate theJournal of researches.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   28 May [1871]
letters.summary:
Reports on the wholesale murder in Paris.

His wife, Sofya Kovalevsky, is working for her examinations.

VOK is studying embryology.

Alexander has left Suez and is now in Jaffa.

letters.title: From Karl Scherzer   28 May 1871
letters.summary:
Craniological part ofNovaravoyage report is done.

Expresses his satisfaction at CD’s election as a Foreign Honorary Member of the Academy of Sciences, Vienna.

letters.title: To C. L. Balch   29 May 1871
letters.summary: Thanks for informing him that the New York Liberal Club has elected him a member. Responds to request to give advice to beginners in biology.

letters.title: From Henry Gillman   29 May 1871
letters.summary:
Offers to send some of his botanical field notes.

Convinced that certain families and genera vary in certain directions. CitesLobelia’s "inclination" to produce albinos and other cases.

Reports a plant that is abundant in localities unfitted for its full development.

Wild buffaloes will help a wounded calf.

Response to CD’s views among American naturalists.

letters.title: To J. B. Innes   29 May [1871]
letters.summary:
Not surprised that JBI does not agree with him. Many professed naturalists do not. But there has been a great change since publication ofOrigin, and CD believes agreement on man will come soon, "as far as his corporeal frame is concerned".

Horsman has not been heard from.

letters.title: From Alfred Newton   29 May 1871
letters.summary:
[Reference to Japanese nuthatch (seeDescent, 2d ed., p. 410 n.) excised from letter.]

Sorry they will not have Frank Darwin with them any more.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   30 May 1871
letters.summary: Thanks JVC for corrections forDescent. Index, which is too full, was hurried at the end.

letters.title: From J. B. Holder   30 May 1871
letters.summary: Explains condor’s mode of flight.

letters.title: To Alfred Newton   30 May [1871]
letters.summary:
Thanks AN for facts and corrections [forDescent].

The case of the gull must come out [Descent2: 108 n. 9]. "Oh Lord, how difficult accuracy is!"

letters.title: From Henry Reeks   30 May 1871
letters.summary: Retention of horns by female deer with fawn [seeDescent, 2d ed., p. 503].

letters.title: From John Murray   31 May [1871]
letters.summary:
On photographic illustrations [forExpression].

Estimates 7s 6d price for a cheap edition ofOrigin[6th].

letters.title: From Alexander Agassiz   [before 1 June 1871]
letters.summary:
Instances of sexual differences in viviparous fishes, suggested by reading chapters on sexual selection [inDescent] and by Mivart’sGenesis of species.

Notes on echinoderms.

letters.title: From Hugh Browne   June 1871
letters.summary:
Believes his letter of 17 Apr bears also on vol. 1 ofDescent.

Ability to move ears is common in his family.

Similarity of foot of man to that of gorilla continues beyond foetal stage.

Invites CD to stay overnight if visiting the area.

letters.title: To Alexander Agassiz   1 June [1871]
letters.summary:
Discusses homologies in various animal groups.

Comments on Mivart [Genesis of species].

letters.title: From Thomas Bradfield   1 June 1871
letters.summary: Instance of a dog able to discriminate a note played out of tune. [SeeDescent, 2d ed., p. 569.]

letters.title: To C. V. Riley   1 June [1871]
letters.summary:
Comments on CVR’s book [Third annual report on the noxious, beneficial, and other insects of the State of Missouri(1871)].

Discusses mimetic insects.

letters.title: To Edward Suess   1 June [1871]
letters.summary:
Thanks for his election to the Austrian Imperial Academy.

Is sorry ES has suffered in health.

letters.title: To Thomas Bradfield   2 June [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks for the fact about the dog.

letters.title: From A. G. Butler   2 June 1871
letters.summary: Facts contradicting Wallace’s views on coloration of Lepidoptera.

letters.title: To V. O. Kovalevsky   2 June [1871]
letters.summary:
Thanks VOK for sending F. Körte’s book [Die Streich-, Zug- oder Wander-Heuschrecke(1828)]. The passage CD wrote about [see7735] must occur in the second edition. If VOK ever comes upon the 1829 edition, it would be of use to him.

Agrees that the Versailles army has been savagely brutal [in siege of Paris], but thinks the "Communists [Communards] have made themselves everlastingly infamous".

letters.title: To John Murray   3 June [1871]
letters.summary:
Is disappointed at high price, 7s 6d, being considered for the cheap edition of theOrigin[6th ed.]. Has been told that, in Lancashire, workmen club together to buy theOrigin.

Little chance thatExpressionwill be done this autumn.

letters.title: From Henry Reeks   3 June 1871
letters.summary:
Observations on habits of caribou and deer in Newfoundland.

Suggests nightingale egg coloration evolved from white to olive for protection.
