letters.title: From Michael Foster   4 June [1871]
letters.summary: Sends answers to CD’s queries on expression.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   5 June 1871
letters.summary: Follows up CD’s observation of 13 May 1871, of a New Forest pony shedding its winter coat.

letters.title: From J. B. Innes   5 June 1871
letters.summary: On Down parish matters.

letters.title: To F. E. Abbot   6 June [1871]
letters.summary:
Sends subscription for theIndex.

FEA’s article ["The intuitional and scientific schools of free religion",Index15 Apr 1871] is one of the most striking CD has read.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   6 June [1871]
letters.summary:
Thanks for FD’s help. CD cannot conceive what Mivart means by "the identity between eyes of Cephalopods and Vertebrata".

Has invited Michael Foster to Down.

letters.title: To Michael Foster   6 June [1871]
letters.summary:
Comments on MF’s "little essay" [see7800].

Invites him to visit.

letters.title: From Gerhard Rohlfs   6 June 1871
letters.summary:
Various observations from his experience in Africa relevant toDescent.

Fertility of hybrids of blacks and whites.

Protective coloration of Sahara animals.

Natives’ ideas of female beauty.

letters.title: From Raphael Meldola   7 June 1871
letters.summary:
Discusses the origin and advantages of sexual differentiation in terms of division of labour.

Discusses the origin of the giraffe’s neck and the unsoundness of St G. J. Mivart’s view with respect to it.

Points out an error inDescent.

letters.title: To L. H. Morgan   7 June 1871
letters.summary: Directions to Down.

letters.title: To T. C. Eyton   8 June [1871]
letters.summary: Comments on dubious story involving natural history of Formosa. Suggests that Robert Swinhoe could give an answer.

letters.title: From L. H. Morgan   8 June 1871
letters.summary: Will call tomorrow.

letters.title: From Henry Reeks   8 June 1871
letters.summary: Argues that coloration of eggs is a protective adaptation.

letters.title: To Gerhard Rohlfs   8 June 1871
letters.summary: Thanks GR, who made one of the most wonderful expeditions on record, for some notes which he will consider if he ever has to prepare a new edition [ofDescent].

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   9 June [1871]
letters.summary:
Mentions the difficulties in explaining the separation of sexes and Carl Nägeli’s view that the sexes of plants were primordially distinct.

Has been experimenting for five or six years to demonstrate that the benefits of crossing are the same as those derived from a slight change of conditions.

letters.title: From Paolo Mantegazza   10 June 1871
letters.summary:
Michele Lessona will translateDescentinto Italian [1871].

Sends his review fromNuova Antologia[17 (1871): 177–94].

In a letter toArchivio per l’Anthropologiahe raises some doubts about sexual selection and proposes "Neogenesis" as a complement to natural selection in cases of rapid change.

letters.title: From László Dapsy   12 June 1871
letters.summary: As a professor of natural history, LD has spread CD’s doctrines in Hungary. Now wishes permission to translateDescent.

letters.title: From Henry Reeks   12 June 1871
letters.summary:
A geologist friend leaving for Nevada offers to investigate any questions CD may have for this region.

Nesting plumage of common chaffinch resembles adult winter plumage of female brambling.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [13 June 1871]
letters.summary: Reports the passing of [Universities Tests] Bill and the consequent end to a bother.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [after 13 June 1871]
letters.summary: Discusses his position at Cambridge, which is apparently under threat.

letters.title: To L. H. Morgan   14 June [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks LHM for his introductions for CD’s sons and for his instructions about their route [for their U. S. visit].

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   14 June 1871
letters.summary: Discussion of mimicry and sexual selection among butterflies, occasioned by readingDescent.

letters.title: From F. C. Donders   16 June 1871
letters.summary: Replies to CD’s queries on movement of the eyes in meditation, and changes in the iris in rage and terror [seeExpression, pp. 229, 304].

letters.title: From Ignatius Jackowski   18 June 1871
letters.summary: Has read ofDescentin Polish newspapers. Writes against theBibleview, but believes in the Almighty.

letters.title: To F. C. Donders   19 June 1871
letters.summary:
Thanks FCD for information about eyes [forExpression].

Must interrupt work on the subject to prepare new edition ofOrigin[6th].

Comments on gift of a new work by FCD [possibly "Die Projection der Gesichtserscheinung nach der Richtungslinien",Arch. Opthalmol.17 (1871) Abt. 2: 1–68].

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   19 June 1871
letters.summary: Observations on orchids.Ophrys apifera; confirms CD’s observation on pollinia.  The nesting of ducks in trees is an example of change of instinct and habit.

letters.title: From Ernst Pfitzer   19 June 1871
letters.summary:
Sends publication [unspecified].

Notes adaptive mechanism in epiphytes.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   21 June [1871]
letters.summary: Confesses to intense hatred of the bee [orchid] for its anomalous perpetual self-fertilisation.

letters.title: From Ferdinand Stoliczka   21 June 1871
letters.summary: CD elected an honorary member of the Asiatic Society of Bengal.

letters.title: From Chauncey Wright   21 June 1871
letters.summary: Sends his review of St George Mivart’s book [Genesis of species] [North Am. Rev.113 (1871): 64–103] in which CW defends natural selection.

letters.title: From J. T. Moggridge   [before 22] June 1871
letters.summary:
At Wallace’s suggestion he offers CD his observations on the seed-gathering habits of ants. Suggests their role in seed dispersal.

At work on the last part of his book [Contributions to the flora of Mentone(1867–71)].

Has found thatOphrys insectiferacan reproduce asexually.

letters.title: To J. T. Moggridge   22 June [1871]
letters.summary:
Thanks JTM for information on ants.

Mentions letter "from a Texas gentleman"Gideon Lincecumdescribing ants that plant seeds [see3082].

Notes that fly orchid is unattractive to insects. Asks JTM to attempt fertilisation experiment with this plant.

letters.title: From Lionel Ashburner   25 June 1871
letters.summary: Gives examples of animal species in which adult males castrate or kill younger males.

letters.title: From Michael Foster   25 June 1871
letters.summary: Regrets he cannot get to Queen Anne Street, but intends to come to Down.

letters.title: To Michael Foster   26 June [1871]
letters.summary:
Invites MF to visit.

Asks where he can obtain curare for plant experiment.

letters.title: From Michael Foster   [26 June 1871]
letters.summary: Has arranged to send CD a bottle ofurari[curare]. Describes its effect with strychnine.

letters.title: To Briton Riviere   27 June [1871]
letters.summary: Discusses animal drawing showing expression.

letters.title: To J. J. Moulinié   28 June [1871]
letters.summary:
Fears a pirated edition ofDescent; hopes JJM’s translation will come out soon.

Preparing new [6th] edition ofOrigin. Can publication of French edition be delayed in order to incorporate corrections?

letters.title: To ?   28 June [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks for the photographs.

letters.title: From A. G. Butler   29 June 1871
letters.summary:
Resemblance of ocelli, in a moth and the argus pheasant.

Mimicry.

Pugnacity of stickleback.

letters.title: To Michael Foster   29 [June 1871]
letters.summary: Thanks him for curare.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   29 [June 1871]
letters.summary:
Delighted to hear from Lyell of JDH’s return from successful ascent of the Atlas Mts.

Fears JDH found no Madeira or Canary types, but CD is pleased at his moraine discovery.

Thinks Lyell’s health is serious.

letters.title: To [W. W. Baxter?]   [early July 1871]
letters.summary:
Orders nitrate of ammonia for experiment on plants.

Are measuring glasses accurate?

letters.title: To Edward Bartlett   1 July [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks for ducks’ skins, for which he encloses postal order.

letters.title: To A. G. Butler   1 July [1871]
letters.summary:
Thanks AGB for "various notes".

Would like to hear his views about theBrahmaea.

letters.title: ToNature   1 July [1871]
letters.summary: Refers H. H. Howorth, the writer of "A new view of Darwinism" [Nature4 (1871): 161–2], toVariationfor a discussion of fertility and sterility of organisms in relation to increased food and other factors.

letters.title: To C. V. Riley   1 July [1871]
letters.summary:
Would be delighted to see CVR at Down, but is in precarious health and cannot talk to anyone for more than an hour.

Wrote to CVR a few weeks ago to thank him for his book [see7794].

Will expect CVR on Thursday unless he hears otherwise.

letters.title: To ?   1 July 1871
letters.summary: Regrets ill health will prevent his attending the BAAS meeting at Edinburgh.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   3 July 1871
letters.summary:
Plans to write an account of his trip to Morocco and, with John Ball, the botanical geography, for Linnean Society.

Results mainly negative; the Atlas exhibits "the dying out of European flora".

Only two or three beetles above 8000ft.

Disappointed that Canary Island species are absent from Atlas mountains; but an ocean current along Moroccan coast should help migration of Spanish, Portuguese, and Moroccan seeds to Canaries and Madeira.

Describes Lyell’s poor physical condition. Asks CD for his observations of symptoms.

letters.title: To W. R. Grove   4 July [1871]
letters.summary: Has never before noticed with care the markings on finger-ends. Compares them to the complex whirl-pool patterns of human foetal lanugo.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   4 July [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks for gift of WBT’s book [Pheasants for coverts and aviaries(1873)].

letters.title: From W. R. Grove   [5–8 July 1871]
letters.summary:
Mammae in human males.

The role of natural selection in the development of beards and manes of animals.

Hereditary pointing in setters.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   5 July [1871]
letters.summary:
Lady Lyell’s anxiety over Lyell’s health.

Preparing new edition ofOrigin.

Asks whether anything was observed [in Morocco] on expressions.

Did JDH notice whether pollen-masses inOphrys apiferain N. Africa fall on the stigma, as in England?

letters.title: To C. F. Bergstedt?   6 July [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks author of an anonymous Swedish review of CD’s works [inSamtiden, Vecksckrift för politik och litteratur, ed. C. F. Bergstedt, nos. 23–5 (1871): 358–64, 374–81, 390–7]. CD is surprised to learn theOriginhas appeared in Swedish [1869].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   6 July 1871
letters.summary:
He did observe thatOphrys apiferafertilised itself as CD described andO. luteaas well.

Moroccans are too civilised, taciturn, and unfriendly to make anything of them for expressions of emotions.

Moraines and negative results on Atlas alpine flora are the only points of the journey worth much.

letters.title: From J. J. Moulinié   7 July 1871
letters.summary: JJM’sOrigintranslation is being held up so that it can conform to the 6th English edition.

letters.title: To C. V. Riley   8 July [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks for letter of introduction for his sons visiting America.

letters.title: To W. R. Grove   9 July [1871]
letters.summary:
Does not think WRG’s theory [about ridges of skin on palm and finger-ends?] will hold.

Does not believe the beard in monkeys and goats could be protective like the lion’s mane.

Thanks him for fact about setters.

Is perplexed about the reported milk secretion in pubescent boys.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   9 July [1871]
letters.summary: Requests advice about Chauncey Wright’s article on Mivart’sGenesis of species[North Am. Rev.113 (1871): 64–103]. CD thinks of publishing it as a pamphlet to counter impact of Mivart’s criticism of natural selection.

letters.title: From R. H. Blair   11 July 1871
letters.summary: Reports observations on expression in the blind; facial contortions and blushing.

letters.title: To Violetta Galton   12 July [1871]
letters.deprecated: Frances Anne Violetta (Violetta) DarwinFrances Anne Violetta (Violetta) Galton
letters.recipient: Frances Anne Violetta (Violetta) DarwinFrances Anne Violetta (Violetta) Galton
letters.summary: Thanks his aunt for a note about a picture bought by CD’s sons.

letters.title: From Otto Kratz   12 July 1871
letters.summary: Sends photographs of very hairy Burmese natives; suggests they may be the "missing link".

letters.title: To J. J. Moulinié   12 July [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks JJM for willingness to introduce corrections into French edition ofOrigin.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   12 July [1871]
letters.summary:
CD is allowing his family to decide whether Chauncey Wright’s paper on Mivart is dull.

Health and despondency.

Doubts his ability to answer Mivart successfully [in 6th ed. ofOrigin].

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   12 July 1871
letters.summary:
Chauncey Wright’s article is sound, but so obscure ARW doubts utility of printing it separately.

Gives his own detailed analysis of Mivart’s attack.

letters.title: To Chauncey Wright   13 and 14 July [1871]
letters.summary:
Comments on CW’s article on phyllotaxy;

discusses criticisms ofOriginby Mivart.

letters.title: From John Coghlan   13 July 1871
letters.summary:
JC offers to collect information under CD’s guidance.

Gives some notes on the colours of different horse breeds.

Mentions a wild duck that appears to be polygamous

and his observations on male ostriches with broods of young.

letters.title: To John Murray   13 July [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks JM forQuarterly Review. Its "cutting" article [onDescent, 131 (1871): 47–90] is worthy of Mivart’s skill.

letters.title: From George Grove   15 July 1871
letters.summary: The cat exhibition was a success. Asks whether the next one might be made to serve interests of science and of CD’s investigations by, for example, offering prizes for cats with special modifications or characters.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   16 July [1871]
letters.summary: CD’s sons, George and Francis, are to visit the U. S. Can AG supply any letters of introduction?

letters.title: From Kaiserliche Akademie der Wissenschaften   16 July 1871
letters.summary: CD named a corresponding member of the mathematical-scientific section of the Kaiserliche Akademie der Wissenschaften.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   16 July 1871
letters.summary: Sorry CD allows criticisms of Darwinism to worry him.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [c.17 July 1871]
letters.summary: Gives CD some information on wills.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [17 July 1871]
letters.summary: Discusses legal matters; CD’s will and setting up trusts for Henrietta Darwin’s forthcoming marriage.

letters.title: To George Grove   17 July [1871]
letters.summary:
The cat exhibition might provide information on unusual breeds of cats and their inheritance.

Expresses interest in deafness of white, blue-eyed cats.

letters.title: From W. B. Tegetmeier   17 [July] 1871
letters.summary:
SendsFieldwith an account of the cat show; examples of cats with three extra toes.

Sexual preference of a blue turbit.

CD did not return skull of the horned cock figured inVariation[1: 265].

letters.title: To Chauncey Wright   17 July [1871]
letters.summary:
Wishes to republish CW’s review as pamphlet [Darwinism(1871)].

Two sons will visit America. Hopes they may call on CW.

letters.title: From A. G. Butler   18 July 1871
letters.summary:
Observations on ocelli ofBrahmaea certhia.

Monstrosity born to a woman – half bear, half human.

letters.title: From Andrew Smith   18 July 1871
letters.summary: Thanks CD for a letter to Galton which enabled him to get information on the inhabitants of a part of South Africa. Is trying to work up the ethnology of South Africa, but fears he will become disheartened.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   18 July [1871]
letters.summary: One of WBT’s poultry skulls has been misplaced; CD cannot believe he neglected to return it.

letters.title: To James Croll   19 July [1871]
letters.summary: Introduces E. L. Youmans to correspondent. Youmans is seeking small monographs by the most competent English authors [for his International Scientific Series].

letters.title: To J. D. Caton   20 July 1871
letters.summary: Letter of introduction for his sons [G. H. and Francis Darwin].

letters.title: From G. C. Oxenden   21 July 1871
letters.summary: Will sendOphrys apiferavar.lutea.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   22 July 1871
letters.summary:
Has given CD’s name to a species ofAbutilonfound by Fritz Müller.

Pleased at Henrietta [Darwin]’s engagement.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   23 July [1871]
letters.summary:
Honoured byAbutilonname; describes observations on its fertilisation.

Henrietta’s marriage a great loss to him.

LatestQuarterly Reviewhas article, "evidently by Mivart", that cuts CD into mincemeat.

Asks for name of species of mouse J. S. Henslow used to keep [see598].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   23 July 1871
letters.summary:
Identifies Henslow’s mouse that used tail as prehensile climbing organ asMus messorius.

Has not seen theQuarterly Review.

Inquires after Lyell’s health.

letters.title: To Vernon Lushington   24 July [1871]
letters.summary:
Thanks for providing turtle soup.

Not quite so sure he thanks VL for introducing Richard Buckley Litchfield into the Darwin family to be CD’s son-in-law.

Asks about the lip position of a pouting child.

letters.title: From H. G. Cavendish Browne   26 July 1871
letters.summary: Reports that a humble-bee fertilised a tropical orchid in his hothouse.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   26 July [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks for information about Henslow’s mouse.

letters.title: From Roland Trimen   26 July 1871
letters.summary: Hopes to visit during CD’s stay at Haredene.

letters.title: To Roland Trimen   27 July 1871
letters.summary: Invites RT to call on him while he is staying at Haredene.

letters.title: From Theodor Piderit   28 July 1871
letters.summary:
Interested in forthcomingExpression.

Sends publications.

Describes physiological theory of mental activity. Asks for CD’s opinion of his theory.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   29 July [1871?]
letters.summary: Wants CD to sign an enclosure [missing] and get the signatures of other family members.

letters.title: To E. A. Darwin   [after 29 July 1871?]
letters.summary: Asks [EAD] to get signatures as opportunity offers.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   30 July 1871
letters.summary:
Shocked at Lyell’s appearance and speech.

Family news.

letters.title: From L. H. Morgan   1 August 1871
letters.summary: John Lubbock’s paper [? "Remarks on stone implements from western Africa",Rep. BAAS40 (1870): 154–5] opposes some of his best sustained conclusions.

letters.title: From L. H. Morgan   [1 August 1871]
letters.summary: Sends abstract of a paper on hybridity read by Edward Moore to a natural history club in Rochester, NY. Argues the necessity of hybridity on CD’s theory.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   1 August [1871]
letters.summary: On a "remarkable" letter from Fritz Müller [see7820] about mimicry, protection, and sexual selection.

letters.title: From Chauncey Wright   1 August 1871
letters.summary:
Discusses revising hisNorth American Reviewarticle [see7829] for publication as a pamphlet in England.

Plans to publish a further article on phyllotaxy.

letters.title: To Elliott & Fry   [2 August 1871]
letters.summary: Thanks for the photographs, which are "very good".

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   2 August [1871]
letters.summary:
Opinions onDescent.

Sexual selection and mimicry in Lepidoptera; sexual selection as an aid to protective imitation.

letters.title: To Theodor Piderit   2 August [1871]
letters.summary:
Comments on TP’s work on mimicry.

Thanks for book he is sending [Wissenschaftliches System der Mimik und Physiognomik(1867)].

letters.title: From Asa Gray   3 August 1871
letters.summary: AG hopes to meet CD’s sons, who are visiting America.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   4 August [1871]
letters.summary: Sends enclosure for ARW to read.

letters.title: From C. A. Canfield   5 August 1871
letters.summary: Sends a series of factual corrections toVariationandDescent: barking of coyotes and colour of wild American horses.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   5 August 1871
letters.summary: Lengthy discussion of William Thomson’s address [BAAS, Edinburgh 1871].

letters.title: From Michele Lessona   5 August 1871
letters.summary:
On the malar bone [seeDescent1: 124].

Has verified hermaphroditism ofSerranusand other fishes as normal [seeDescent1: 208].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   6 August [1871]
letters.summary:
Has read Thomson’s address with "greatest interest", but JDH has said exactly what he [CD] thinks of it.

Herschel’s was a good sneer. It made him add the RaphaelMadonnasimile inDescent[2: 142].

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   7 August 1871
letters.summary: Sends notes on Fritz Müller’s letter.

letters.title: To W. W. Baxter   8 August [1871]
letters.summary: Asks WWB to send 8 grains of acetate of strychnine by post.

letters.title: To Friedrich Hildebrand   10 August [1871]
letters.summary:
Mentions experiments onLythrum.

Thanks for list of seeds.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   11 August 1871
letters.summary:
Sorry he will be away when CD comes down.

Congratulations on Henrietta Darwin’s engagement.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   12 August [1871]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: CD’s comments on proofs of JL’s book [Monograph of the Collembola and Thysanura(1873)].

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   15 August 1871
letters.summary: Sends on letter from Hacon about Captain Litchfield’s will.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   15 August 1871
letters.summary:
Differences in violet and honeysuckle cases.

Huxley basted Thomson awfully in Section D [of BAAS].

letters.title: From Emile Alglave   17 August 1871
letters.summary: Has reached an understanding with CD’s French translator [J. Moulinié] and publisher [C. Reinwald] forDescent. Has printed first chapter in last number ofRevue Scientifiqueand sent CD copies; is sending proofs of translation of next chapter for CD to correct.

letters.title: From James Croll   17 August 1871
letters.summary:
Refused to write a treatise on geological time.

His paper on W. B. Carpenter’s theory of ocean currents is appearing soon.

letters.title: To John Murray   17 August [1871]
letters.summary:
Asks JM whether he will publish 750 copies of a pamphlet [Chauncey Wright’s review of Mivart’sGenesis of species,North Am. Rev.113 (1871): 63–103] at CD’s expense.

Has been ill so cannot say when he will finish new edition ofOrigin.

Asks about sales and printing ofDescent.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   18 August 1871
letters.summary:
RC is sure Murray would not object to printing the pamphlet [C. Wright’sDarwinism: being an examination of Mr. St. G. J. Mivart’s "Genesis of species"].

After a lull in sales ofDescent, a fresh demand warrants keeping type set up. Has CD seen the review ofDescentin theGuardian?

letters.title: From James Crichton-Browne   18 August 1871
letters.summary: Sends CD a volume ofWest Riding Lunatic Asylum Medical Reports[1 (1871)], which contains some observations on blushing.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   19 August [1871]
letters.summary:
A. J. Gaudry is one of few supporters of Darwinism in Paris.

The climate is so hostile that Kovalevsky must mitigate his views so as not to irritate the French.

Working onAnchitherium, which he believes is intermediate betweenPalaeotheriumand the horse.

His brother-in-law has been arrested.

letters.title: From F. E. Abbot   20 August 1871
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for interest in FEA’s work and for money forIndex. Sends 1870 volume ofIndex.

Praises CD’s services to free-thought.

Asks for CD’s view of the influence of his theory on religion, to use in lecture.

letters.title: From J. F. McLennan   21 August 1871
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for helping with arrangements for an American edition [ofPrimitive marriage(1865)].

He is an old friend of CD’s son-in-law, R. B. Litchfield, and of John Lubbock.

letters.title: From Roland Trimen   [21] August [1871]
letters.summary: Intends to visit CD at Haredene.

letters.title: From James Lamont   23 August 1871
letters.summary: JL’s views on the sexual peculiarities of the bladder-nosed seal,Cystophora cristata.

letters.title: From W. B. Dawkins   27 August 1871
letters.summary: Describes the successful excavation of caves containing interred remains of Neolithic man.

letters.title: To Alexander Agassiz   28 August [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks AA for a ‘splendid case of gradation of structure’.

letters.title: To W. M. Hacon?   29 August 1871
letters.summary: Sends details of trains for a clerk to travel to Down from London and back.

letters.title: From J. W. Clark   31 August 1871
letters.summary:
Thanks CD forBeaglespecimens donated to the Museum.

Asks for a liveHelix pomatiafor dissection.

letters.title: To George Busk   2 September [1871]
letters.summary: Is preparing a new edition ofOrigin[6th ed. (1872)] and asks GB for information on the gradations between the vibracula and avicularia of the Polyzoa and on what he bases his opinion concerning the homology of the avicularium with the zooid.

letters.title: To H. E. Litchfield   4 September [1871]
letters.summary: An affectionate letter to HL on her honeymoon. Urges her to keep her mother as an example.

letters.title: From F. A. Hanbury   4 September 1871
letters.summary: Thanks for £5 for the Voysey fund.

letters.title: To F. E. Abbot   6 September [1871]
letters.summary: CD’s views [on religion] are far from clear. He cannot make up his mind how far an inward conviction that there must be some Creator or First Cause is really trustworthy evidence. Does not feel he has thought deeply enough to express himself publicly on religion.

letters.title: To E. A. Darwin   7 September [1871]
letters.summary: Wants to sell some shares held in trust by EAD and Josiah Wedgwood [III].

letters.title: From Anton Dohrn   7 September 1871
letters.summary:
Reports on the international support he has obtained for the zoological station [see7038]. Asks CD whether he will serve on a board of naturalists who would receive an annual report on the station.

Huxley is now convinced by AD’s views on homologies of the nervous system of arthropods, annelids, and vertebrates. Kovalevsky takes the same line but does not go far enough.

letters.title: To Anton Dohrn   8 September 1871
letters.summary:
Agrees to have his name on the list of naturalists to whom annual report [on zoological station] should be sent.

His health has been very bad for last six weeks.

letters.title: To Otto Kratz   8 September [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks for sending the photographs of hairy people at the Burmese court.

letters.title: ToGardeners’ Chronicle   [before 9 September 1871]
letters.summary: In response to a query [from "F. W. B."], CD describes his experience with seedingLeschenaultia, which demonstrates that insect agency is required.

letters.title: From H. E. Litchfield   9 September [1871]
letters.summary:
CD’s letter [7922] was very sweet to her, and if her marriage [to Richard B. Litchfield] can be half as perfect as CD’s she will be very happy.

Richard’s German fails in communicating with washerwomen.

letters.title: From Wallis Nash   9 September 1871
letters.summary: In hunting dogs behavioural and physical traits are often inherited together and from either male or female parent.

letters.title: From H. Ramu   9 September 1871
letters.summary: Informs CD that there are goats at Nancy with maxillary appendages similar to those of the ancient Irish pig [seeVariation1: 75].

letters.title: To Alexander Agassiz   10 September [1871 or 1873]
letters.summary: Discusses exchange of books.

letters.title: From George Busk   10 September 1871
letters.summary: Replies to CD’s queries about the homologies of the avicularian and vibracular organs of Polyzoa and gives examples of gradations between the two.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   10 September [1871]
letters.summary: Writes to check on stock certificates received.

letters.title: To Osbert Salvin   10 September [1871]
letters.summary: CD is interested in the gradation of character in the lamellae of the beaks of ducks. He finds that they are less developed or prominent in the common duck and goose than in true ducks. Is OS able to provide him with any information on this subject?

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   12 [September 1871]
letters.summary: Sees mistake he made on certificates; will make list for future use.

letters.title: To Wallis Nash   12 September [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks for facts relating to inheritance.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   12 September 1871
letters.summary:
Prefers W. C. Wells’s explanation of the formation of the Nehro type to CD’s sexual selection.

Outlines his view of the origin of man by natural selection.

letters.title: To Chauncey Wright   12 September 1871
letters.summary:
CW’s pamphlet [Darwinism(1871)] nearly ready. Friends have been much struck by it but say several passages rather obscure.

Glad CW coming to England. Will be delighted to see him at Down.

letters.title: To George Busk   13 September [1871]
letters.summary: CD plans to use notes provided by GB. [SeeOrigin, 6th ed., p. 193.]

letters.title: From Giuseppe Carboni   13 September 1871
letters.summary:
Requests CD’s autograph.

Sends photograph of an emblem, which he uses as his personal symbol: "Moleshott, Büchner, Darwin: Scienza e Natura, Forza e Materia".

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   13 September [1871]
letters.summary: Location of stock certificates.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   13 September 1871
letters.summary: Is turning to experiments with rats, "Siamesed together" for cross-circulation.

letters.title: To John Murray   13 September 1871
letters.summary: Arrangements for distribution and review of pamphlet [Chauncey Wright’sDarwinism: being an examination of Mr St. G. J. Mivart’s "Genesis of species"(1871)], which CD had reprinted at his own expense.

letters.title: To H. Ramu   13 September 1871
letters.summary: Obliged for letter about appendages on faces of goats.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   [after 13 September 1871]
letters.summary: Georgina [Tollet?] is eager to see a copy of Chauncey Wright’s pamphlet [Darwinism(1871)].

letters.title: To A. D. Bartlett   15 September 1871
letters.summary: CD questions ADB on the mode of feeding of geese and on the existence of variations in the structure of the bill; is trying to trace gradations in structure and habits.

letters.title: To J. R. Martin   15 September 1871
letters.summary: Buys ten shares in the Artizans, Labourers, & General Dwellings Co.

letters.title: From H. Marval   15 September 1871
letters.summary: Observations on behaviour of spiders in Astrakhan and Turkestan.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   15 September 1871
letters.summary: Believes CD will not consider him a good Darwinian since he accepts natural selection only as a secondary law.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   16 September [1871]
letters.summary:
Is preparing new edition ofOrigin[6th] in which he will introduce new chapter to answer Mivart’s criticisms. Mivart is unfair: suppresses facts in CD’s later editions.

Sends article [by Chauncey Wright, see7940] reviewingGenesis of species.

Mivart writes to CD full of respect, but reviles him in print.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   18 September 1871
letters.summary:
There is a primary law of growth and innate improvement. Natural selection is a secondary law that operates to "arrange the details". This is not Lamarckian, because will is not involved.

Thanks for Chauncey Wright’s pamphlet [Darwinism(1871)].

Amused by critics who say CD is metaphysically unsophisticated.

letters.title: From A. D. Bartlett   19 September 1871
letters.summary: Geese do not commonly sift water through their bills for food, as they feed on land. A few have well-developed lamellae for sifting. Will have his son check at Zoological Garden.

letters.title: To A. D. Bartlett   20 September [1871]
letters.summary: Asks whether any goose sifts water with its beak.

letters.title: From Edward Bartlett   20 September 1871
letters.summary: Reports on variations in the development of lamellae and how the bills are used in several kinds of geese. Will send skins for examination.

letters.title: From Michael Foster   20 September 1871
letters.summary:
Offers his services for the future.

Working hard at establishing physiology at Cambridge.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley and H. A. Huxley   20 September 1871
letters.summary:
Has received Chauncey Wright’s pamphlet [see7940].

Has reviewedQuarterly Reviewarticle and 2d ed. ofGenesis of speciesfor theContemporary Review[18 (1871): 443–76].

Mivart has hopelessly misunderstood Suarez [Disputiones(1630)] on evolution.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   20 September 1871
letters.summary: Surprised at Mivart’s harsh review [Q. Rev.131 (1871): 47–90], considering courteous tone of his book. Assures CD he has not been converted by Mivart.

letters.title: From Roland Trimen   20 September 1871
letters.summary: On St G. J. Mivart’sGenesis of speciesand Chauncey Wright’s review of it [North Am. Rev.(July 1871)].

letters.title: From Edward Bartlett   21 September 1871
letters.summary: Lists [with prices] four birds that he has forwarded to CD.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   21 September [1871]
letters.summary:
On Mivart’sGenesis of species, and THH’s intention to reply to it.

Chauncey Wright’s pamphlet [see7940].

CD is revisingOriginand will answer Mivart on incipient organs. "Pendulum is swinging against us, but will swing back again".

letters.title: From Osbert Salvin   21 September 1871
letters.summary:
Promises to answer questions about ducks next week when he has a specimen.

Recently met Capt. Arthur Mellersh.

letters.title: From Louis Bouton   22 September 1871
letters.summary: Is enjoyingDescent. Sends corroborating facts on heredity, concerning race of people from the Seychelles known for their tall stature, courage, and vigour.

letters.title: To W. H. Flower   22 September [1871]
letters.summary:
Asks WHF to check over some enclosed MS pages [Origin, 6th ed.?]. CD quotes some of WHF’s remarks, but should WHF not wish to be mixed with CD’s theoretic notions, CD will omit the whole paragraph.

Many think CD’s notions are "rubbish, pleasantly flavoured", like the reviewer in theQuarterly Review, who CD cannot doubt is "Mr Mivart, with bigotry arrogance illiberality & many other nice qualities".

letters.title: To Paolo Mantegazza   22 September 1871
letters.summary: Explains that he cannot agree with Mantegazza’s views on sexual selection.

letters.title: From John Murray   22 September [1871]
letters.summary: The pamphlet [Chauncey Wright’s review of Mivart, see7940] has been distributed to friends and to the press.

letters.title: To John Murray   23 September [1871]
letters.summary:
Has been so unwell that he could do absolutely nothing onOrigin[6th ed.]. A new chapter seven has cost much labour.

Sorry to hear R. I. Murchison is ill.

letters.title: To Chauncey Wright   23 September [1871]
letters.summary:
Forwards a letter. Has distributed 220 copies of the pamphlet [Darwinism1871].

Thomas Henry Huxley has sent review of St George Jackson Mivart’sOn the genesis of speciesand his review ofDescentinQuarterly Review(Mivart 1871a and [Mivart] 1871c) to theContemporary Review[18 (1871): 443–76] .

letters.title: To Edward Bartlett   [24] September [1871]
letters.summary:
Thanks for goose specimens.

Asks whether Egyptian goose throws water out of side of beak. Can it tear herbage like the domestic goose?

[Mistakenly dated 16 Sept by CD.]

letters.title: From H. Ramu   24 September 1871
letters.summary: Sends CD a sketch of goat with maxillary appendages and notes the dimensions of the structures.

letters.title: To E. B. Tylor   24 September [1871]
letters.summary: CD most interested byPrimitive culture[1871]. Impressed by EBT’s account of development of religious beliefs and of the survival of old customs. Hopes EBT will treat morals.

letters.title: From Guiseppe Carboni   25 September 1871
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for autograph and photograph.

TheOrigindestroys philosophical foundations of religion.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   25 September 1871
letters.summary:
Sees his ideas on conscious and non-conscious intelligence are already in Murphy [J. J. Murphy,Habit and intelligence(1869)].

Encloses an extract from S. W. Baker’sThe Albert N’yanza[1866] on the behaviour of the giraffe [SeeOrigin, 6th ed., p. 178], and some references to Baker’sNile tributaries[1867].

letters.title: From St G. J. Mivart   26 September 1871
letters.summary: Has seen an article by Chauncey Wright ["Darwinism",North Am. Rev.113 (1871): 63–103] and has heard it has been enlarged and reprinted [1871]. As CD has been distributing copies StGM wonders whether he might have one.

letters.title: To H. Ramu   26 September 1871
letters.summary: Obliged for note and sketch [of goat appendages].

letters.title: To St. G. J. Mivart   27 September [1871]
letters.summary: Sends a reprint of Chauncey Wright’s article ["Darwinism",North Am. Rev.113 (1871): 63–103].

letters.title: To [?]   27 September [1871–81]
letters.summary: Thanks for a book. "I am so much overworked at present that I cannot read it now, & I am a very poor German scholar".

letters.title: To Albert Günther   28 September [1871]
letters.summary:
Sends some questions [missing].

Bad health has prevented him from working for six weeks.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   28 September 1871
letters.summary:
Sends proof of article forContemporary Review[18 (1871): 443–76].

Is grieved to hear that Mivart is author ofQuarterly Reviewarticle. THH thought better of him than that.

Compares theOriginto Plato’sRepublic: "it will remain fresh for two thousand years".

letters.title: From E. B. Tylor   29 September 1871
letters.summary: Thanks for CD’s praise of his book [Primitive culture(1871)], wonders if he should abridge part into a small popular volume.

letters.title: From Thomas Druitt   30 September 1871
letters.summary: Sends CD £100 as requested. Gives information on bonds purchased on CD’s behalf.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   30 September [1871]
letters.summary: Sends proofs of Huxley’s article on Mivart, to be published inContemporary Review["Mr Darwin’s critics", 18 (1871): 443–76].

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   30 September [1871]
letters.summary: On THH’s review [see7977] of Mivart’sGenesis of speciesand theQuarterly Reviewarticle onDescent.

letters.title: From Albert Günther   1 October 1871
letters.summary:
Sorry to hear of CD’s poor health.

Is hard at work examiningCeratodus.

Encloses discussion ofMusspecies with functionally prehensile tails.

Encloses argument against freshwater fish entering the sea.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [2 October 1871]
letters.summary:
On Huxley’s article forContemporary Review[see7977] confuting Mivart. It has cheered him,

for he is very low about his mother’s state.

Is also in detestable position with "my lord and master", A. S. Ayrton. JDH has denounced him to the [First] Lord of the Treasury [W. E. Gladstone] for his conduct.

letters.title: To E. B. Tylor   2 October [1871]
letters.summary:
CD advises publishing a short version ofPrimitive culture[1871] for the general reader.

Would like to see EBT, but his health has been bad and conversation is extremely tiring.

letters.title: To Albert Günther   3 October [1871]
letters.summary:
Thanks AG for answer aboutGalaxias.

Asks him to mention questions about the ears ofMusto other naturalists.

Will send another copy of Chauncey Wright’s pamphlet [Darwinism(1871)].

AG has provedCeratodusto be a "wonderfully interesting creature" ["Descripton ofCeratodus",Philos. Trans. R. Soc. Lond.161 (1871): 511–72].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   4 October [1871]
letters.summary:
Sorry to hear of JDH’s troubles;

pleased he thinks so highly of Huxley’s article [see7977].

Huxley makes CD feel infantile in intellect (as JDH once said of himself). CD is not so good a Christian as JDH thinks, for he did enjoy his revenge on Mivart.

letters.title: From J. L. A. Hope   4 October 1871
letters.summary: Anecdote about a gathering of kangaroos.

letters.title: From St G. J. Mivart   4 October 1871
letters.summary: Thanks for Chauncey Wright’s article. Admits it is clever, but hardly expected CD to think it a serious defence of his position.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   5 October [1871]
letters.summary:
Hooker admires THH’s review of Mivart [see7977]. Most impressed by THH’s handling of metaphysics.

Hooker’s problems: family health and A. S. Ayrton [Commissioner of Works].

letters.title: From H. B. Dobell   6 October 1871
letters.summary: Asks CD’s opinion of his suggestion that a distinctive mark of species may be the duration of pregnancy, incubation, or germination.

letters.title: From T. N. Gill   6 October 1871
letters.summary:
Sends some articles on mammals [possibly "On the relations of the orders of mammals",Proc. Am. Assoc. Adv. Sci.19 (1870): 267–70, and "On the characteristics of the primary groups of the class of mammals",ibid.20 (1871): 284–306].

He is a disciple, convinced of CD’s theory of evolution and of natural selection.

In the U. S. almost all refuse to recognize natural selection.

letters.title: To John Murray   6 October [1871]
letters.summary: Has finished seven chapters of revision ofOrigin[6th ed.] despite poor health. Asks JM’s opinion on a glossary of scientific terms. Encloses text for advertisement.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   7 October 1871
letters.summary:
Publisher would like to produce a translation ofExpression. JVC offers to translate it.

Sends passage from Albertus Magnus on colour of horses.

Offers explanation of white colour of sea-birds.

Schweizerbart is now reprintingDescent, nearly all the first 3000 copies having been sold;

new editions ofOrigin

and ofVariationare also planned.

Possibility of a new German translation ofJournal of researches.

letters.title: To H. B. Dobell   7 October [1871]
letters.summary: "I should expect that the period of gestation will differ very little in the individuals of the same species, as long as its conditions of life remained the same. But I doubt whether it is sure as an absolute criteria; for although little or nothing on this field can be known with respect to species in a state of nature, yet with races of the same species as with dogs and cattle, the period is known slightly to differ. In the generation of seeds from the same capsule there is often the most wonderful and inexplicable difference in the periods".

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   8 October [1871]
letters.summary:
Glad to hear of new German edition ofOrigin. He is revising the English edition, adding a new chapter of "Answers".

No new edition ofDescenthas appeared.

Would be glad to see a new translation of theJournal of researches, which he revised in 1845.

Comments on white colour of sea-birds.

letters.title: To Lawson Tait   8 October 1871
letters.summary: Does not know anything about a supra-condyloid process on the humerus, but would like to see RLT’s paper should he publish on the subject.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   9 October 1871
letters.summary: Will give printer orders to set up first six chapters ofOrigin[6th ed.]. Murray thinks a glossary [of scientific terms] might be advisable, if not longer than ten pages. Will offer W. S. Dallas £10 for it.

letters.title: From J. K. Fowler   9 October 1871
letters.summary: Is preparing paper on breeding ["Breeding facts and principles",J. Farmers’ Club(1871): 45–53]. Seeks CD’s advice and assistance. Believes male parent influences external appearance and female the internal organisation.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   9 October [1871]
letters.summary:
Asks whether THH has written on affinities of Eocene cetaceanZeuglodon. Wants to cite it in 6th ed. ofOriginas in someslightdegree an intermediate form, but does not know how far he may venture.

Has had more evidence of profound impression of Mivart’s book [Genesis of species].

letters.title: From Hermann Müller   9 October 1871
letters.summary: Is preparing a work on fertilisation of flowers, and wants to add a list of works containing observations on cross-fertilisation of plants. Asks CD for any references he may have.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   10 October 1871
letters.summary:
Answers CD on transitional forms. Has no doubtZeuglodonis transitional form between Carnivora and Cetacea.

Met Mivart in Manchester. Some doubt that he was the author ofQuarterly Reviewarticle.

letters.title: From Osbert Salvin   10 October 1871
letters.summary: Encloses notes [missing] that he has made for CD on looking through his dried skins of American Anatidae.

letters.title: To T. R. R. Stebbing   10 October [1871]
letters.summary: Doubts whether an experiment to test the durability of human bones would be worth while. Absence of such bones in post-glacial river-bed deposits does not weigh in the least on CD.

letters.title: From Chauncey Wright   11 October 1871
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for copies of the pamphlet [Darwinism(1871)].

His memoir on phyllotaxy [Mem. Am. Acad. Arts & Sci.n.s. 9 (1867–73): 379–415] will soon be printed.

Has met CD’s sons.

letters.title: To an editor   12 October [1871]
letters.summary: Sends photograph of himself for a proposed memoir in correspondent’sReview.

letters.title: From W. H. Flower   12 October 1871
letters.summary: On structure and function of the cetacean larynx.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   12 October 1871
letters.summary: Has seen CD’s sons.

letters.title: To Osbert Salvin   12 October [1871]
letters.summary:
CD appreciates the great trouble OS has taken in providing a bundle of observations. [See8001.] They are useful and will save CD from at least one blunder.

The structure of the beak of the shoveller "filled me with admiration".

letters.title: From R. F. Albrecht   13 October 1871
letters.summary: CD has omitted in all his works one of the most interesting causes of variation, domestic or wild – i.e., frightening of a pregnant animal; quotes case of eight-footed horse from a French translation of G. S. W. von Adler.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   13 October [1871]
letters.summary: First six chapters [ofOrigin, 6th ed.] sent to printer.

letters.title: To W. H. Flower   13 October [1871]
letters.summary: Will strike out passage on larynx in cetaceans from his MS [ofOrigin, 6th ed.].

letters.title: From Osbert Salvin   14 October 1871
letters.summary: Is glad his notes on ducks are useful; would like them back when CD has finished with them as they might help him to put the South American Anatidae in order.

letters.title: To Edward Bartlett   15 October [1871]
letters.summary: Asks for information on feeding habits of Egyptian goose.

letters.title: To R. F. Albrecht   16 October [1871]
letters.summary:
Thanks RFA for extracts.

Does not believe resemblances can be produced as RFA suggests, but would not deny that a strong mental shock may cause arrest of embryonic development and thus give rise to monstrosities.

letters.title: From Edward Bartlett   16 October 1871
letters.summary: Replies on how Egyptian geese feed in the water; they do not move heads laterally like ducks sifting water; they tear herbage like common geese.

letters.title: From George Busk   16 October 1871
letters.summary: Returns CD’s MS [forOrigin6th ed.] on the defensive organs of the Polyzoa, with his comments.

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   16 October 1871
letters.summary:
Cannot accept JJW’s invitation to a party. His health has been worse than usual for some months – can see no one nor can he go anywhere.

Is preparing a cheap edition of theOrigin[6th] and will answer Mivart’s objections.

CD is pleased JJW likes C. Wright’s "Darwinism" [see7940]. Huxley will publish a splendid review of it inContemporary Review[Nov 1871].

letters.title: From H. B. Brady   18 October 1871
letters.summary: On visit to Boston was told by N. S. Shaler how habits of rattlesnake are consistent with natural selection. Informs CD, as rattlesnake is considered by some a difficult case for his theory.

letters.title: From A. C. Ramsay   18 October 1871
letters.summary: Sends two papers ["On the physical relations of the new red marl",Q. J. Geol. Soc. Lond.27 (1871): 189–98 and "On the red rocks of England",Q. J. Geol. Soc. Lond.27 (1871): 241–54] bearing on the continuance of generic and specific terrestrial types, in areas of Europe and elsewhere, that lasted from the Upper Silurian to the Lias.

letters.title: From Osbert Salvin   18 October 1871
letters.summary: Comments on lamellae inPrion. Offers to send specimen for CD to examine.

letters.title: To A. C. Ramsay   19 October 1871
letters.summary:
Thanks ACR for papers.

Glad present situation of our continents has been confirmed.

Wishes ACR would prove his view of origin of Red Sandstones, which many dispute.

letters.title: To Osbert Salvin   19 October [1871]
letters.summary: CD would like to see thePrion[see8016]. May he immerse the head in warm water so as to open the beak? Directions for sending the parcel.

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   19 October 1871
letters.summary:
"Like you I have often wondered at the different food of the old and young, as with graminivorous birds feeding their young with insects."

Recommends forthcoming book by John Lubbock [Monograph of the Collembola and Thysanura(1873)].

letters.title: To Henry Holland   [20 October 1871]
letters.summary: Seeks HH’s support for Hooker in JDH’s difficulties with A. S. Ayrton and the Ministry of Works [seeNature6 (1872): 211–16].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   20 October 1871
letters.summary: JDH’s servant carries his letter to Henry Holland about problems with Ayrton. Suggests servant take CD’s letter to Holland to town and post them at same time. Holland is said to be very intimate friend of Gladstone.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [20 October 1871]
letters.summary: Has written to Henry Holland in strongest terms. Will be surprised and disappointed if he does not accede to JDH’s request.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   20 [October 1871]
letters.summary: CD agitated by JDH’s letter. Forgot to say that he heard Henry Holland was going to Turin. Beseeches JDH not to resign. No one could possibly replace him.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   20 October 1871
letters.summary:
JDH has no intention of resigning. Thinks W. E. Gladstone would rather see Ayrton turned out than himself. Gladstone knows JDH has friends who would be troublesome. Only moral and political cowardice of Cabinet keeps Ayrton in office.

Lyell is much altered since autumn.

Has CD read Charles Martins’ paper on the glacial origin of thetourbièresof the Jura [Arch. Sci. Phys. & Nat.42 (1871): 286–308]?

John Scott has an admirable series on horticulture in Bengal ["Notes on horticulture in Bengal",J. Agric. & Hortic. Soc. India2 (1871) pt 1: 241–96; 3 (1872) pt 1: 1–82].

letters.title: From A. C. Ramsay   20 October 1871
letters.summary: Glad CD agrees with his views as much as he does. Not surprised that his red rocks [Red Sandstones] ideas are disputed. The red marls of Auvergne support his inland water theory.

letters.title: To Hermann Settegast   20 October 1871
letters.summary:
Thanks HS for the preface to the 3d edition [ofDie Thierzucht(1872)].

Has purchased H. von Nathusius’ work [?Vorträge über Viehzucht und Rassenkenntniss, Th. 1 (1872)]; feels he has ignored all that CD has attempted to make out with respect to domesticated animals.

letters.title: From C. S. Bate   22 October 1871
letters.summary: Has read in papers about CD’s forthcoming work [Expression]; sends anecdote about a dog visiting a dentist for relief of a toothache – thus showing "moral courage".

letters.title: From H. B. Brady   22 October 1871
letters.summary: Explains further N. S. Shaler’s view [see8015] on rattlesnake habits as consistent with natural selection: the rattle attracts rather than alarms its prey.

letters.title: From Osbert Salvin   22 October 1871
letters.summary:
Sends specimen ofPrion.

Discusses beaks of flamingo and other birds.

Comments on function of lamellae.

letters.title: From John Fiske   23 October 1871
letters.summary: JF’s indebtedness to Herbert Spencer. [Published version complete.]

letters.title: From W. D. Crotch   24 October 1871
letters.summary:
Gives possible explanation for retention of horns throughout the winter by female reindeer.

Work on Atlantis.

letters.title: To Osbert Salvin   25 October [1871]
letters.summary:
Very gladto seePrion. [See8029.]

CD offers OS upper and lower beaks of various ducks and geese if they are of interest to him.

letters.title: From W. Baranoff and Heinrich Koch   27 October 1871
letters.summary: Correspondents are giving public lectures onDescent. Would like CD to supply a statement of his religious views for inclusion.

letters.title: To Chauncey Wright   28 October 1871
letters.summary:
Glad CW has written on phyllotaxy [Mem. Am. Acad. Arts & Sci.n.s. 9 (1867–73): 379–415].

Sure that CW’s pamphlet [Darwinism(1871)] will do cause good service.

Grateful for kindness to sons in America.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   30 October 1871
letters.summary:
Has completed corrections forOrigin[6th ed.], but has received no proofs. Hopes it will be published without delay.

Has been reflecting on Murray’s suggestion to stereotype theOrigin. Sees advantage in that it will make him stop additions and changes in style. Inquires whether each separate sheet is stereotyped and can be altered.

Asks whether any copies of C. Wright’s pamphlet have been sold.

letters.title: From Osbert Salvin   30 October 1871
letters.summary: Sends CD some more ducks’ skins so that he can examine the lamellae.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   31 [October 1871]
letters.summary:
Writes about proof-correcting by WED [ofOrigin, 6th ed.].

Goes to Leith Hill on Friday.

letters.title: From Henry Gillman   31 October 1871
letters.summary: Sends details of his discoveries of relics and bones of the "mound-builders", and Jeffries Wyman’s comments on them.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   31 October 1871
letters.summary: Details of the JDH–Ayrton–Gladstone imbroglio.

letters.title: From Heinrich Koch   31 October 1871
letters.summary: Is sending some lectures as a sign of his society’s respect for CD and his work.

letters.title: From W. Baranoff and Heinrich Koch   [after 31 October? 1871]
letters.summary:
Received his last letter.

Their third lecture will contain a history of creation from the Darwinian point of view.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [November 1871]
letters.summary: Explains some proof-correcting symbols to be used by WED [onOrigin, 6th ed. proofs?].

letters.title: To John Phillips   [November–December 1871?]
letters.summary: Thanks for note concerning JP’s new book [Geology of Oxford(1871)].

letters.title: From F. E. Abbot   1 November 1871
letters.summary:
For CD’s approval, cites passage from CD note he wants to quote in a lecture;

pleads for CD’s moral support for FEA’s work in free-thought movement.

Sends $50 [dollars or pounds!?] because he wants CD to become regular contributor toIndex.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   1 November 1871
letters.summary:
Suggests CD haveOrigin[6th ed.] stereotyped.

Will sell out remaining copies ofDescentat forthcoming trade sale, print off 500 or 1000 more, and then have the type distributed.

14 copies of C. Wright’s pamphlet have been sold.

letters.title: To Osbert Salvin   1 November [1871]
letters.summary: He appreciates the two specimens [skins ofMergenettaandAix sponsa], especially theMergenetta, which as far as sifting is concerned, is a capital link between the shoveller and the common duck. Arrangements for their return.

letters.title: To John Scott   1 November 1871
letters.summary:
JS should not consider repaying CD; the money was a gift, not a loan.

JS’s information on expression is the best he has received.

letters.title: To James Crichton-Browne   2 November [1871]
letters.summary:
Asks JC-B to observe whether platysma muscle contracts during rigor or shivering fit.

Is just recommencing his essay on expression.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   2 November 1871
letters.summary: Henry Holland is taking an active part in helping JDH in the Ayrton affair.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [after 11 November 1871]
letters.summary:
Sends enclosure for Captain Jones.

Comments on essay by E. D. Cope ["On the origin of genera",Proc. Acad. Nat. Sci. Philadelphia20 (1868): 242–300].

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   3 [November 1871]
letters.summary: Is sending some proofs for correction by WED [6th ed. ofOrigin].

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [3 November 1871]
letters.summary: Apologises for not working very quickly on proofs. Comments on Huxley’s theological critique of Mivart.

letters.title: From Hermanus Hartogh Heijs van Zouteveen   3 November 1871
letters.summary: Wishes to translateExpressioninto Dutch.

letters.title: From G. J. Allman   4 November 1871
letters.summary: Learned of CD’s interest in new facts bearing on origins of specific forms and sends proof sheets of hisMonograph on tubularian hydroids[1871–2] stating his views on the descent of existing hydroids from ancient graptolites.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   4 November 1871
letters.summary:
Agrees to stereotypingOrigin[6th ed.].

Asks that 500 or 1000 more copies ofDescentbe printed. Will make no corrections except the number of thousands on title page. Would like to revise [Descent] if it goes on selling.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [4 November 1871]
letters.summary: Thanks WED for a correction [to proofs ofOrigin, 6th ed.].

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   4 November 1871
letters.summary: Will write to de Chaumont to ask whether anyone at Netley is able to observe shivering fits. Has not got H. Spencer essays.

letters.title: From J. W. Spengel   4 November 1871
letters.summary:
Sends CD additions to his bibliographical list [missing].

Reports observations indicating that chimpanzees show compassion.

letters.title: From H. E. Litchfield to Charles and Emma Darwin   [5 November 1871]
letters.summary: Describes the wedding party given for herself and Richard Buckley Litchfield at the Working Men’s College in London.

letters.title: To H. E. Litchfield   [after 5] November 1871
letters.summary:
CD is "more than pleased" by what R. B. Litchfield said of him. Congratulates HEL on having "so noble a husband".

All were "profoundly" interested by HEL’s account [of their welcome at the Working Men’s College].

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [after 5 November 1871]
letters.summary: Writes about proof-correcting by WED [ofOrigin, 6th ed.].

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [6 November 1871]
letters.summary: Asks who Fiske is. The articles [Harvard lectures?] are "so fair and in some respects so complimentary" that CD thinks he should write to him. [See8058.]

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   6 November 1871
letters.summary: Will send back proofs ofOrigin6th ed.

letters.title: From S. S. Hennell   7 November 1871
letters.summary: Marriage is basis of all religious forms of thought, and this is the subjective equivalent of CD’s law that sex is the most important agency of universal development.

letters.title: To H. M. Westropp   7 November [1871]
letters.summary: "Please accept my thanks for your kind present of your two Papers."

letters.title: To Hermanus Hartogh Heijs van Zouteveen   8 November 1871
letters.summary:
CD glad to hear of success of translation ofDescent.

Will not go to press withExpressionfor six or nine months; hopes HHHvZ will think it worth translating.

letters.title: From A. A. Regnard   8 November 1871
letters.summary: A French refugee and populariser of CD’s work asks for an audience.

letters.title: To John Fiske   9 November 1871
letters.summary: Thanks JF for his lectures, the arguments of which he finds very forcible; is glad to see JF has detected the falseness of much of Mivart’s reasoning.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   11 November 1871
letters.summary: Forwards a letter from R. O. Jones on the effects of castration on horns of male lambs.

letters.title: From O. G. Rejlander   11 November 1871
letters.summary:
Can photograph the scene CD requested only in the spring.

Heliotype is cheap but Woodburytype allows alterations.

letters.title: From J. M. Rodwell   11 November 1871
letters.summary: Has readVariationand reports on markings on donkeys similar to those in vol. 1, p. 63.

letters.title: From W. W. Baxter   13 November 1871
letters.summary: Sends CD a measure with capacity of 20 oz or 34.65925 cubic inches.

letters.title: From H. E. Litchfield   [13 November 1871]
letters.summary: Does not want CD to put his name to any religious movement. Discourages giving money to Abbott or Voysey.

letters.title: To Roland Trimen   13 November [1871]
letters.summary: Regrets he is too unwell to see RT before his departure for the Cape; wishes him well.

letters.title: To W. W. Baxter   14 November [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks for loan of measure.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   14 November 1871
letters.summary:
News of progress of German editions ofOrigin

andDescent.

Asks CD for references on chabius – a Chilean hybrid of goat and sheep.

letters.title: To A. W. Bennett   [before 16 November 1871]
letters.summary: Discussed observations made in 1863 ofImpatienspollen and humble-bees.

letters.title: From Federico Delpino   15 November 1871
letters.summary:
Sends paper onArtemesia.

Praise forDescent.

Has talked to St George Mivart about CD’s health.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   15 November 1871
letters.summary: Is it now thought that the spongioles of rootlets secrete carbonic acid which acts on bones and rocks?

letters.title: To F. E. Abbot   16 November [1871]
letters.summary: Explains why he must decline to write for theIndex: his health is poor and he has never systematically thought much on religion. FEA may print his comments, "with qualifications", if he wishes.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   16 November 1871
letters.summary: Almost 600 copies ofDescentsold at trade sale, with 120 left in stock. Suggests printing another 1000 to give more time for correcting the work for 2d edition.

letters.title: From M. C. Stanley   [16 November 1871]
letters.deprecated: Mary Catherine Stanley, countess of Derby
letters.sender: Mary Catherine Stanley, countess of Derby
letters.summary: W. Crookes’s article ["Enquiry into phenomena called spiritual",Q. J. Sci.n.s. 4 (1874): 77–97] "staggers" her. Would like to know CD’s opinion.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   17 November 1871
letters.summary:
CD offers to mark corrected passages in sheets of 6th edition ofOrigin.

Discusses question of hybrids between goats and sheep, on which H. von Nathusius has cast doubt in his recentViehzucht[1872]. CD gives several references for a contrary view.

Asks JVC to inquire about HvN’s assertion that castrated rams have no horns.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   17 November 1871
letters.summary:
Has decided that 1000 copies ofDescentshould be printed. Will make no alterations. "If it goes on selling it will shew that it is worth a thorough revision."

The U. S. sale ofDescent(10000 copies) is larger than in England.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [17 November 1871]
letters.summary: Says has sent a copy of CD’s memorial to Captain Jones. Passes on Sir Geo. Grey’s comments on pasturage near Morpeth. Tells superstition about straight furrows and fairies.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   17 November 1871
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Praises and comments on JL’s essay on insects ["Origin of insects",J. Linn. Soc. Lond.11 (1873): 422–5].

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   17 November 1871
letters.summary: Thanks for the information about the action of roots on rocks.

letters.title: To David Forbes   18 November [1871]
letters.summary: Inquires about the effect of turf covering on the rate of disintegration of rock.

letters.title: To M. C. Stanley   [18 November 1871]
letters.deprecated: Mary Catherine Stanley, countess of Derby
letters.recipient: Mary Catherine Stanley, countess of Derby
letters.summary: Much perplexed by W. Crookes’s article. He can neither disbelieve nor believe. Article has removed some of his difficulty in that the supposed power is not an anomaly. Hopes men such as G. G. Stokes will be induced to witness Crookes’s experiments.

letters.title: To [?]   18 November [1871 or later]
letters.summary: "With Mr. Charles Darwin’s compliments enclosing one guinea."

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [19 November 1871]
letters.summary: Sends comments from himself and Erasmus Darwin on proofs of chapter 7 ofOrigin6th ed.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   20 November 1871
letters.summary: Horns of castrated merino rams remain almost undeveloped.

letters.title: From R. O. Jones   20 November 1871
letters.summary: The horns of castrated male lambs compared with horns of ewes. [SeeDescent, 2d ed., p. 506.]

letters.title: From S. R. S. Norton   20 November [1871]
letters.summary: Sends CD a German pamphlet, "War Goethe ein Darwinianer?"

letters.title: From L. C. Wedgwood   20 November [1871]
letters.summary: Displays in turkeys.

letters.title: To ?   20 November [1871]
letters.summary: Asks for some pamphlets, the titles of which have been sent to him by Dr Spengel [see8053].

letters.title: From Francis Galton   21 November 1871
letters.summary: Asks that the rabbits CD has kept be sent to him; will continue [transfusion] experiments on rats, but using larger [surgical] connection.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   22 November 1871
letters.summary: Sends back proofs. Praises CD for calm treatment of Mivart. Looks at duck’s mouth. Asks whether CD has seen Snow’s article in the Spectator.

letters.title: To Federico Delpino   22 November 1871
letters.summary:
Will send FD’s work [Studi sopra un lignaggio anemofilo delle composte(1871)] toNaturefor review.

CD’s health has been poor all summer – he doubts that he will ever "have the strength to publish on Variability under a state of Nature".

Hopes to publish on cross- and self-fertilisation next summer.

Encloses his photo and asks for FD’s.

letters.title: From David Forbes   22 November [1871]
letters.summary: Effect of turf covering on the disintegration of rocks. Weathering of rock; relative importance of different agents with different rocks.

letters.title: To S. R. S. Norton   23 November [1871]
letters.summary:
Reports how his sons enjoyed their trip to America.

Is glad SRSN is settled in Dresden.

letters.title: From George Busk   24 November 1871
letters.summary: Thanks for information on platycnemic tibiae found in America. Believes the condition is of two kinds as exemplified by Gibraltar and Cro-Magnon tibiae on one side and the Welsh form on the other. Would like to know which of the two forms the American bones are; their proportions suggest they are very like the Welsh tibiae.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   24 November 1871
letters.summary: Going to Down to see the "most curious" results.

letters.title: From E. S. Foster   25 November 1871
letters.summary: Offers to provide information on the habits of the animals of northern New York and Canada.

letters.title: To Henry Lee   26 November 1871
letters.summary:
Thanks HL for his kind note, the interesting notice, & the photograph.

He has made a mistake about theLepas. It is theL. australisthat is confined to the S. Hemisphere.L. hilliiis found all over the world. Refers HL toLiving Cirripedia[1851].

letters.title: From C. Shuttleworth   27 November [1871–80]
letters.summary: Reports peculiar behaviour in a fantail pigeon, which persistently courted a ginger-beer bottle.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   28 November [1871]
letters.summary:
CD is considering repeating experiments on melastomads in which different pollen sizes produced differing seedling sizes.

Responds to JDH’s query on differences in pollen within the same species.

letters.title: From K. T. E. von Siebold   29 November 1871
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for copies of theOriginandCirripedia;

sends his latest publication in return [Beiträge zur Parthenogenesis der Arthropoden(1871)]. Discusses his work on parthenogenesis which, he believes, is a case of atavism.

letters.title: From H. E. Litchfield   [before 2 December 1871]
letters.summary: Summarises her theory about expression in music.

letters.title: To H. E. Litchfield   [before 2 December 1871]
letters.summary: Sends MS of section on voice as a means of expression [Expression, pp. 86–93]. CD is dissatisfied with it – wishes he could avoid the subject.

letters.title: From R. B. Litchfield   [before 2 December 1871]
letters.summary: Discussion of H. Spencer’s views on the origin of music.

letters.title: To H. E. Litchfield   2 December [1871]
letters.summary:
Sends MS chapter on voice fromExpressionto HL for examination.

Agrees with R. B. Litchfield about Herbert Spencer’s views on speech and music.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   2 December 1871
letters.summary: The rabbits arrived safely.

letters.title: To G. A. Eisen   3 December 1871
letters.summary: Thanks GAE for memoir on earthworms [Bidrag till Skandinaviens Oligochaetfauna(1871)]. CD by chance is just now observing "one little point in their habits". Will be happy to learn something about the places frequented by the various species.

letters.title: To E. S. Morse   3 December 1871
letters.summary: Obliged for ESM’s article ["On adaptive coloration of the Mollusca",Proc. Boston Soc. Nat. Hist.14 (1870–1): 141–5]. Glad to have error corrected about protective colouring of shells.

letters.title: From Ulrich Kirchenpauer   4 December 1871
letters.summary: Wishes to have CD’s autograph.

letters.title: To K. T. E. von Siebold   4 December 1871
letters.summary:
Thanks for the letter, photograph, and kind words about CD’s scientific work. [See8088.]

CTEvS’s view of pseudova is new to CD;

he has not yet received the recent work on parthenogenesis

though he did receive the memoir onPolistes.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   5 December 1871
letters.summary:
Sends sheets [of the 6th ed. ofOrigin].

Thanks JVC for his letter about the sheep.

letters.title: From Federico Delpino   5 December 1871
letters.summary:
Praise of CD. Acknowledges his indebtedness to CD for defining the subject of plant fecundation.

Expecting CD’s work on the effects of cross-fertilisation.

CD has put him in touch with George Bentham.

letters.title: From George Henslow   5 December 1871
letters.summary:
Has frequently defended evolution and natural selection among his clergy brethren.

Now elicits CD’s views on chance.

letters.title: To J. J. Moulinié   5 December 1871
letters.summary: Sends corrections for new French edition ofOrigin.

letters.title: From Armand de Watteville   5 December [1871]
letters.summary: Gives publication date for J. C. Lavater,L’Art de connaître les hommes, 1806–9, edited by J. L. Moreau. The first four volumes appeared in 1806.

letters.title: To Nevil Story-Maskelyne   6 December 1871
letters.summary:
Sends a copy ofOrchidsfor his wife, T. M. Story-Maskelyne, and a few other items she may wish to have.

Climbing Plantsmay be purchased at Williams and Norgate; he has no clean copies.

letters.title: To George Henslow   7 December [1871]
letters.summary: Refers GH to vol. 2, p. 431 ofVariationfor the "perplexed conclusion" at which CD has arrived on variation and design. Has nothing to add to this statement.

letters.title: From Nevil Maskelyne   8 December 1871
letters.summary: Thanks CD for papers he sent his wife. They will help her pass her time as an invalid.

letters.title: From Hubert Airy   9 December 1871
letters.summary:
Reply to CD’s letter of 5 Apr 1871 [7659], in which he asked HA for further details on when and how platysma myoides contracts.

Replies to CD’s questions about sources on leaf arrangement.

Gives news of speech and paper about CD.

letters.title: From Paul Broca   9 December 1871
letters.deprecated: Pierre Paul (Paul) BrocaSecretary, Soc. Anthrop. Paris
letters.sender: Pierre Paul (Paul) BrocaSecretary, Soc. Anthrop. Paris
letters.summary: Announces that the Société d’Anthropologie de Paris has elected CD a Foreign Associate.

letters.title: To Paul Broca   [after 9 December 1871]
letters.summary: Requests that PB express his thanks to the Société d’Anthropologie de Paris for the honour conferred upon him [see8102].

letters.title: To Hubert Airy   10 [December] 1871
letters.summary:
Discusses movement of ears and contraction of the platysma.

Discusses phyllotaxy, citing work of Carl Nägeli and Chauncey Wright.

letters.title: From F. W. C. Simmons   10 December 1871
letters.summary: Maoris of New Zealand admire beards, contrary to statement inDescent[2: 349].

letters.title: From Hubert Airy   12 December 1871
letters.summary: Thanks for letter and reference to Nägeli’s observations on leaf arrangement in the bud.

letters.title: From Louis Bouton   15 December 1871
letters.summary: Pleased to hear from CD. Sends more facts about the life and habits of the inhabitants of the Seychelles.

letters.title: To Horace Darwin   [15 December 1871]
letters.summary: Congratulates Horace on passing his "Little Go".

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   15 [December 1871]
letters.summary: Will be in London until 21st. Would rejoice if JDH could come to lunch during their stay.

letters.title: From Henry Holland   [16 December 1871]
letters.summary: Sends CD a ptarmigan.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [17 December 1871]
letters.summary: Cannot come to lunch to meet Sir Henry Holland. Holland may have seen Robert Lowe [Lord Sherbrooke] already. Will CD let him know his views?

letters.title: To Henry Lee   17 December [1871]
letters.summary: Apologises for expressing himself stupidly [see8086a]. He did not mean to give an opinion on what the species was, but merely referred to the range ofL. australis. CD will look at specimens, but "the subject has gone much out of my mind; & my health is so weak, & I am so overwhelmed with proof-sheets & other work" that he hopes to be excused if he does not investigate the specimens closely.

letters.title: To Louis Bertillon   18 December 1871
letters.summary:
Thanks for his articleValeur philosophique de l'hypothèse du transformisme(Bertillon 1870), which is very clear.

Would not himself trust so much in Agassiz’s conclusions.

Glad the essay has been published, as he believes ‘there are but few in France who admit the doctrine of evolution’.

letters.title: To A. B. Buckley   18 December [1871]
letters.summary:
Thanks her for marked proof-sheets.

Discusses climate in earlier geological periods.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [18 December 1871]
letters.summary: H. Holland keeps strongly to the opinion that Kew be under the Treasury, and will recommend this to Lowe.

letters.title: To A. D. Bartlett   19 December [1871]
letters.summary:
Can ADB allow T. W. Wood to sketch one of his dogs in hostile and friendly positions?

Do elephants in the Zoological Gardens carry tails aloft when excited?

letters.title: To F. E. E. Wedgwood   19 December [1871]
letters.summary: Asks FW to thank F. P. Cobbe for her liberal offer, but the differences [betweenDescentand Cobbe’s review "Darwinism in morals",Theol. Rev.33 (1871): 167–92] are too fundamental to be reconciled.

letters.title: To Archibald Geikie   20 December [1871]
letters.summary: Asks to borrow AG’s paper on denudation of flat or nearly flat surfaces ["On modern denudation", Trans. Geol. Soc. of Glasgow 3: 153-90]. CD has recently been making some observations he thinks throw a little light on the subject.

letters.title: From Mary Treat   20 December 1871
letters.summary:
Describes fly-catching activity ofDrosera longifolia.

Experiments onPapilio asterias; sex of adult determined by length of larval feeding time.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   21 December 1871
letters.summary:
Comments onDie Kalkschwämme[1872].

A Franciscan prior, Padre Buona-Grazia, agrees with human descent.

His trip to Dalmatia.

German reception ofDescent.

Mentions current work.

letters.title: To William Ogle   21 December [1871]
letters.summary: Thanks WO for a paper and for information about platysma. Has asked several persons to observe the muscle during a shivering fit, but all have failed.

letters.title: To A. C. Ramsay   21 December [1871]
letters.summary: Requests further information on subsidence of flagstones because of action of worms.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   22 December 1871
letters.summary: Encloses "account of Dr H. M. Butler’s hereditary odd habit".

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   22 December 1871
letters.summary:
Philosophical Club dinner.

Lyell contradicts W. B. Carpenter on current in Straits of Gibraltar.

James Orton’s report on fossil shells found by L. Agassiz 2000 miles up the Amazon. Their identification disposes of the glacial hypothesis.

No news yet from Gladstone on Ayrton affair.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   [after 22 December 1871]
letters.summary: Gives his account of H. M. Butler’s apparently inherited habit.

letters.title: To Henry Johnson   23 December 1871
letters.summary:
Is unable to accept invitation to Shrewsbury. Is grateful for offer of assistance at Wroxeter.

The weight of dry earth cast up by worms is 161/10 tons per acre annually.

letters.title: To Henry Lee   23 December [1871]
letters.summary: "I have now looked at both lots of specimens, & I thinkbothare the variable L. anatifera.–– I have disarticulated the right-hand scutal valve in both & the umbonal teeth are plain in both … I have hardly any doubt that both are L. anatifera.––"

letters.title: From Archibald Geikie   24 December 1871
letters.summary: Sends a paper on denudation ["On modern denudation",Trans. Geol. Soc. Glasgow3 (1871): 153–90].

letters.title: To William Ogle   25 December 1871
letters.summary: Sends notes on left- and right-handedness from observations made on his eldest son as an infant.

letters.title: To Archibald Geikie   27 December [1871]
letters.summary:
His admiration for the papers of AG [see8119].

Relates his recent discovery that earthworms have brought to surface no less than 161 tons of dry earth over an area of 10 acres, thus creating the conditions for significant denudation. Would welcome information about the persistence of ridges and furrows in old pasture lands ploughed centuries ago. Do they run down the slopes or transversely? Refers to [A. C.] Ramsay, [James] Croll, Elie de Beaumont, and [Henry] Johnson.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   27 December 1871
letters.summary:
Refers to priest who believes in "our ape-like progenitors".

EH’s work on sponges.

Pangenesis.

Describes new edition ofOrigin[6th]

and his work on plant crossing.

letters.title: From A. C. Ramsay   27 December 1871
