letters.summary: Sends description and measurements of the 18th century courtyard pavement of his house, the stones of which have sunk as a result of earthworm action [seeEarthworms, pp. 192–3].

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   28 December [1871]
letters.summary: Sends three sheets but keeps one. Suggests looking at a curved field on the way to Orpington.

letters.title: From Archibald Geikie   29 December 1871
letters.summary: Action of earthworms and weather on surface soil of old earthworks and fortifications.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   30 December 1871
letters.summary: Varying depth of top-soil in a ridge-and-furrow field with a depression.

letters.title: From Erasmus Galton   30 December 1871
letters.summary: After readingDescentsends two instances of men and animals using the same muscles to express similar emotional states.

letters.title: To Archibald Geikie   30 December 1871
letters.summary:
Is obliged for valuable letter [see8123] and encloses queries about the manner of gradual obliteration of ridges or furrows in old pasture lands in various parts of England.

Gives details of his experiment to test his observations of the downward flow of worm-casts.

Refers to [Lyon] Playfair, [A. C.] Ramsay, and AG’s edition of [J. B.] Jukes, [A student’s manual of geology, 3d ed., 1872].

letters.title: From James Paget   [1872]
letters.summary: "I am at work on the nervous mimicry of organic disease: I have some hope that, during my work, I may fall on some facts which may be of interest to you, and you may be sure that I shall send them to you."

letters.title: From ?   [1872–4]
letters.summary: Notes some corrections for 2d ed. ofDescent.

letters.title: To [?]   [1872?]
letters.summary: Queries about the pitch of children’s crying.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [1 January 1872]
letters.summary: Worm action at Stonehenge.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   1 January 1872
letters.summary:
Gladstone’s private secretary [West] has written that the Government plans to alter JDH’s position with regard to the First Commissioner of Works [Ayrton].

Huxley is not better after his Brighton trip.

letters.title: From J. J. Moulinié   1 January 1872
letters.summary: The difficulties of incorporating the reorganised chapters of the 6th English edition ofOrigininto JJM’s translation, which was made from the 5th edition.

letters.title: From [?]   [1872 or later]
letters.summary: Extract from theHistory of the rise and progress of the Killerby, Studley and Warlaby herds of shorthornsby William Carr (1867).

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   2 January 1872
letters.summary:
Heartily glad about the news of the Ayrton affair development.

Huxley looks very unwell from too much miscellaneous work; CD wishes he could be made a Director General for transference of British Museum and for other scientific work, as JDH suggests.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   3 January [1872]
letters.summary: Thanks for letter [8137]. Finds observation at Stonehenge of depth of mould at different parts of slope "most valuable".

letters.title: From A. C. Ramsay   3 January 1872
letters.summary: Further details and measurements of the stones in the courtyard pavement for CD’s investigation of earthworm action.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [4 January 1872]
letters.summary: Sends comments on his diagram of Stonehenge. Will go to Beaulieu.

letters.title: From St G. J. Mivart   4 January 1872
letters.summary: Sends his reply to Huxley’s criticisms [Contemp. Rev.19 (1872): 168–97].

letters.title: To J. J. Moulinié   4 January 1872
letters.summary: Was unaware that chapter headings [ofOrigin] had been printed off [in French edition (1873)]. Suggests that new part of chapter 7 be printed as appendix.

letters.title: To St G. J. Mivart   5 January 1872
letters.summary: Feels that StGJM’s review ofDescent[Q. Rev.131 (1871): 47–90] greatly misrepresents CD’s opinions and conclusions. Feels their differences of opinion are so great that discussion of almost any subject would be a waste of both their time.

letters.title: To Mary Treat   5 January 1872
letters.summary:
Praises MT’s observations and asks her to repeat experiments on the the relation of sexes of butterflies to the nutrition of the larvae.

Is glad she will publish her observations onDrosera.

letters.title: To L. C. Wedgwood   5 January [1872]
letters.summary: Asks her to probe worm-holes on grassy slopes with a knitting needle to ascertain whether they come out at right angles to the slope or to the horizon.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   6 January 1872
letters.summary: Asks FD questions about his sketch [missing] of ridges and furrows. [FD’s answers are interlined.]

letters.title: From St G. J. Mivart   6 January 1872
letters.summary: As a man of science, StGM has no choice but to pursue what he sees as the truth. Will happily admit he has misrepresented CD if CD will disclaim the position that StGM attacks.

letters.title: To F. E. Abbot   8 January 1872
letters.summary: CD is grateful for the eulogy inIndex[no. 104]. Many would disagree. It is the fashion to say he is a good observer with "an utterly illogical mind".

letters.title: To St G. J. Mivart   8 January [1872]
letters.summary: Wishes their correspondence regarding their differences to be dropped, as CD feels that nothing he could say would have any influence on StGJM.

letters.title: To John Murray   8 January [1872]
letters.summary:
Requests printing of diagram for new [6th] edition ofOrigin. Thinks 6s may be too dear for a cheap edition.

Dallas has done an excellent glossary.

letters.title: To ?   8 January [1872]
letters.summary: Declines to join movement; has not sufficiently considered subject.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   9 January [1872]
letters.summary: Thanks WED for checking through the proofs of a new [6th] edition ofOrigin.

letters.title: From Eduard von Eichwald   10 January 1872
letters.summary:
Sends paper on the coasts of Alaska.

Wishes to sell his large Russian palaeontological collection.

Wants to get in touch with American (Mr Dall), who is going to study geology of Alaskan and Aleutian coast.

letters.title: From St G. J. Mivart   10 January 1872
letters.summary: Agrees to close their correspondence. Defends his position against criticisms of Huxley and Chauncey Wright; assures CD of his continuing friendly feelings.

letters.title: To St G. J. Mivart   11 January [1872]
letters.summary: CD believes that StGJM has been unfair in his criticisms and has misrepresented him; he begs him not to write again. "Agassiz has uttered splendid sarcasms on me, but I still feel quite friendly towards him. M. Flourens cd. not find words to express his contempt of me: Pictet & Hopkins argued with great force against me: Fleeming Jenkin covered me with first-rate ridicule; & his crticisms were true & most useful: but none of their writings have mortified me as yours have done …" [See8154.]

letters.title: From Henri Apatowsky   11 January 1872
letters.summary: Asks CD whether he will find a translator and publisher for a paper Dr A wrote in 1870, siding with Carl Vogt in defence of CD’s view of descent of man.

letters.title: From Henry Johnson   12 January [1872]
letters.summary: Sends a map of a field showing the effect of earthworms.

letters.title: From Armand de Quatrefages   12 January 1872
letters.deprecated: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.sender: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.summary: Battle for CD’s nomination to the French Academy continues.

letters.title: To J. E. Taylor   13 January [1872]
letters.summary:
Thanks for sending his article in theWestminster Review[n.s. 41 (1872): 28–49] and the notice of CD’s work.

Natural selection is under a cloud at present, but CD expects that it will be resuscitated.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   15 January 1872
letters.summary: Questions AG on earthworm activity in North America and would welcome information from northern Canada if AG has a correspondent there.

letters.title: To Arthur Hough   15 January [1872–4]
letters.summary: His thanks for the curious photograph. Since he has similar ones he will not "rob" AH of it.

letters.title: To Armand de Quatrefages   15 January [1872]
letters.deprecated: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.recipient: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.summary:
Obliged for QdeB’s efforts [to have CD elected member of Académie Française].

With regard to stress that QdeB lays on man’s walking on two legs, no one attributes much significance to difference in mode of locomotion between seals and terrestrial Carnivora or kangaroos and other marsupials.

letters.title: To John Scott   15 January 1872
letters.summary: Is resuming the study of worm-casts as he believes they will bear on the denudation of land. Requests specific information on the relative number, size, and manner of deterioration of worm-casts in India.

letters.title: From J. J. Aubertin   16 January 1872
letters.summary:
A friend of JJA’s wants CD’s opinion on whether the disease porigo decalvans (hair falling out in clumps) demonstrates the link between man and dogs and has continued to evolve with man after he passed out of his "hairy-animal state".

Capt. [Richard?] Burton disagrees with CD’s notion of beauty in the abstract, and would like to meet him.

letters.title: To C. H. Morris   16 January [1872]
letters.summary:
Is sending the requested photograph.

Mr Murray will send a copy of CD’sJournal of researchesto L. S. Bouton [see8107a].

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   16 January 1872
letters.summary:
Has no objection to CD’s alluding to FM’s idea that sexual selection has come into play in mimetic butterflies.

Reports observations on other butterflies and on termites.

letters.title: To W. W. Baxter?   17 January [1872–4]
letters.summary: Requests a prescribed physic [not specified].

letters.title: From A. E. Dobbs   17 January 1872
letters.summary: Sends a pamphlet [not identified] in which he applies the principle of natural selection to the working of legislative institutions.

letters.title: From Henry Huxley   17 and 20 January 1872
letters.summary:
His father has gone to Egypt.

Tells of visit to circus.

letters.title: From P. C. Sutherland   17 January 1872
letters.summary: Has some birds which are allegedly the result of a cross between a common fowl and a guinea-fowl; describes their appearance, and will provide CD with likenesses.

letters.title: To J. W. Dawson   19 January 1872
letters.summary: Thanks recipient for memoir on fossil plants of the Devonian and Upper Silurian.

letters.title: To L. H. Morgan   20 January 1872
letters.summary: Thanks LHM for his work on consanguinity. [See7299].

letters.title: From L. C. Wedgwood   20 January [1872]
letters.summary: Gives results of probing worm-holes with wire.

letters.title: From Raphael Meldola   21 January [1872]
letters.summary: Discusses his paper on mimicry and natural selection [Land and Water9 (1871): 321]. Believes natural selection tends to fix mimetic characters rigidly.

letters.title: To L. C. Wedgwood   21 January [1872]
letters.summary: Thanks for observations on angles of worm-holes on slopes. William Darwin is observing at Stonehenge. She is worth her weight in gold.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   23 January [1872]
letters.summary: Discusses earthworm activity observed in old ploughed fields.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   23 January [1872]
letters.summary:
His rabbits have lost their patches and are grey.

Has FG seen William Crookes [spiritualist]?

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   23 January [1872]
letters.summary:
Discusses the problems of mimicry as related to natural selection; the general variability of colour as a character; and the conditions necessary for natural selection to fix firmly a character.

Encloses a Fritz Müller letter speculating that organisms respond to certain colours because of the prevalence of those colours in their environment.

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   23 January 1872
letters.summary: Louis Agassiz is going on a voyage to the Falklands, and BJS wonders whether it is worth while telling him of the Gallegos fossil bed so that he can investigate.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   24 January 1872
letters.summary:
William [Hooker] is in first division of matriculation list of London University.

Other family news.

No news on Ayrton affair. Ayrton has taken staff appointments out of JDH’s hands.

Asks whether CD knows aboutZizania aquatica– can hardly believe it is an annual.

letters.title: From Thomas Stanley   24 January 1872
letters.summary: Wants references to the work of Julius von Haast and James Hector on New Zealand glaciers, which CD mentions in theOrigin[6th ed., p. 335].

letters.title: To B. J. Sulivan   24 January 1872
letters.summary: Suggests BJS write to Louis Agassiz about his [fossil mammal?] specimens but doubts that he will have time to do the work. Regrets they were ignored at the Royal College of Surgeons; thinks Owen neglected many things because he was overworked.

letters.title: From William Bowman   [before 25 January 1872]
letters.summary:
Gives lengthy details from his medical experience on how structural and other changes in the parts of the eye are related to lacrimation.

Mentions belief in CD’s views.

letters.title: To William Bowman   25 January 1872
letters.summary: Discusses role of orbicular muscle and distended veins in eye in secretion of tears. Asks WB’s opinion.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   25 January [1872]
letters.summary:
Heartily glad about Willy.

Has never hadZizania.

Still hasLeersia. He cannot make the beast produce.

What slow coaches the Ministers are about the Ayrton affair.

letters.title: From Raphael Meldola   25 January 1872
letters.summary: Discusses the roles of natural and sexual selection in producing mimicry, and the problem of explaining the cause of the first mimetic variation; considers the ideas of A. R. Wallace and Fritz Müller on this problem.

letters.title: From Arthur Mellersh   25 January 1872
letters.summary:
Reminisces on the evening he, B. J. Sulivan, and J. C. Wickham from theBeaglespent with CD, nearly ten years ago.

Hopes the mission at Tierra del Fuego will not "improve" the people to extinction.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   26 January [1872]
letters.summary: Gives information on recent editions of Lyell’s works.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   27 January [1872]
letters.summary: CD sends some sheets [of 6th ed. ofOrigin]. Informs JVC that he is having it stereotyped, so he can never again make any serious alterations. "The little strength left to me shall be employed on new works."

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   27 January [1872]
letters.summary:
Invites RM to keep some specimens as long as he wishes.

Recalls vaguely the mention of a butterfly species in which the male alone is mimetic.

letters.title: To John Murray   27 January [1872]
letters.summary: Has corrected last page of index ofOrigin[6th ed.]. Sends instructions.

letters.title: From William Green   30 January 1872
letters.summary:
Calls CD’s attention to Andrew Jackson Davis’ work on the origin of man,

philosophy of evil,

the mode of producing rain at pleasure,

and who and what is God.

letters.title: To John Murray   30 January 1872
letters.summary: Requests that JM make stereotype plates of 6th edition ofOriginavailable to D. Appleton. This will be last edition and CD is "extremelyanxious" to spread his views.

letters.title: From John Ball   31 January [1872]
letters.summary: Expands on a letter toNatureconcerning the probability of the survival of a new variety in a given species. Differs with [F. Jenkin’s] argument, to which CD had agreed to a greater extent than JB feels it deserved.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   1 February 1872
letters.summary: Asks to have one pair of rabbits sent to him; is abandoning experiments with the rats.

letters.title: To J. J. Moulinié   1 February 1872
letters.summary:
Encloses a letter to be prefixed to JJM’s translation of theOrigin.

Expresses his satisfaction that JJM has undertaken the translation [of a fourth French edition] of Origin. Urges the use of the sixth English edition so as to include corrections and additions.

His interest in influencing the eminent men of science in France.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   2 February 1872
letters.summary: Notes the occurrence in U. S. of "vermiform piles" produced by earthworms.

letters.title: From Arthur Mellersh   2 February 1872
letters.summary: Exchange of photographs among CD, AM, and Philip G. King.

letters.title: From John Murray   2 February [1872]
letters.summary: Accedes to CD’s request to let Appleton have a set of stereotypes of the 6th English edition ofOriginat a little above cost.

letters.title: To Anton Dohrn   3 February 1872
letters.summary:
Thanks AD for his article inDas Ausland["Englische Kritiker und Anti-Kritiker über den Darwinismus", 49 (1871): 1153–7].

Mivart’s book [Genesis of species], which misinterprets CD’s views, has produced a great effect in England.

He has answered the point about incipient structures being useless in new [6th] edition ofOrigin.

HisDescenthas had immense circulation, but has met with approval of hardly any naturalists. He supposes it was a mistake to publish it, but it will pave way for a better work.

letters.title: From C. F. Martins   3 February 1872
letters.summary:
CD’s views, on which he has lectured, will succeed with time.

Joachim Barrande’s refutation cannot be impartial because he is a devout Catholic.

Many young French naturalists support CD but are silent for fear of their jobs. Houget has been reprimanded for his Darwinism.

letters.title: From Friedrich Hildebrand   5 February 1872
letters.summary: Praise forDescent.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [5 February 1872?]
letters.summary: Sends a communication [missing] from Gov. J. H. Lefroy of Bermuda.

letters.title: From J. F. Mackenzie   8 February 1872
letters.summary: An engineer in India, who has readDescent, sends observations on native racial characters.

letters.title: From L. C. Wedgwood   [8 February 1872]
letters.summary: Describes earthworm experiments. She has measured depth of mould in various locales, e.g., on ridges and furrows of an old ploughed field.

letters.title: To Friedrich Hildebrand   9 February 1872
letters.summary:
Comments on FH’s paper ["Verbreitungsmittel der Compositenfrüchte",Bot. Ztg.30 (1872): 1–14].

Discusses function of mucus filaments on seeds of Compositae and other plants.

Comments on Eugen Askenasy’s publication [Beiträge zur Kritik der Darwin’schen Lehre(1872)].

Comments on evolutionary views of Carl Nägeli.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   12 February 1872
letters.summary: Sends first copy of new [6th] edition ofOrigin. Expenses have been much higher than estimated because of extensive revisions. 3000 copies retailing at 6s would yield only £100 profit. Suggests fixing price at 7s 6d.

letters.title: To ?   [13 February – 21 March 1872]
letters.summary: "Be so good as the send receipt to above address".

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   13 February 1872
letters.summary:
Sending sheets of his forthcoming work on Africa [Martyrdom of man (1872)] with views that differ from CD’s on music and sexual selection.

ThePall Mall Gazettewill review the new [6th] edition of theOrigin, together with Mivart’sGenesis of species[1871].

letters.title: To John Murray   14 February [1872]
letters.summary: Asks to have copy ofOrigin[6th ed.] sent to thePall Mall Gazettefor review with Mivart’sGenesis[of species(1871)].

letters.title: From George Sparkes   14 February 1872
letters.summary:
Describes some crosses he has carried out withPrimula;

mentions the infertility of cherimoyer [Annona cherimolia] in England.

letters.title: From Anton Dohrn   15 February 1872
letters.summary:
AD is sorry CD thinks publication ofDescenta mistake. The excitement shows it was necessary for someone to speak plainly.

His great difficulties (Italian indolence, dishonesty, hatred) in establishing zoological station. Can at last start construction.

letters.title: To ?   15 February [1872–4]
letters.summary: Seeks permission for his son to look for a paper for him.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [16 or 23 February or 1 or 8 or 15 March 1872]
letters.summary: Suggests a visit to Kew to see the hot houses the following Sunday.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   16 February 1872
letters.summary: DefendsDescentagainst CD’s self-disparagement. The parts on the moral sense seem to him the finest in the book.

letters.title: From D. Appleton & Co.   17 February 1872
letters.summary:
Accepts CD’s proposal for new revised edition ofOrigin; will pay $50 [dollars or pounds!?] for casts of the plates and pay CD on sales.

Appleton edition of CD’sJournal of researches[1871] still selling well.

Also wants plates sent with CD’s new work onExpression. CD should arrange this with Murray’s.

letters.title: From W. H. Flower   18 February 1872
letters.summary: Thanks for new [6th] edition ofOrigin, which he read with great interest. Would welcome an edition with references to works cited.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   18 February 1872
letters.summary:
ComparesOriginto Newton’sPrincipiaand Adam Smith’sWealth of nations.

His view of CD’s response to Mivart.

On mammae;

gradualism of evolution;

suicide among savages.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [19 February 1872]
letters.summary: Received copy of Origin 6th ed. Has had trouble with worm measurements at Winchester.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   [19 February 1872]
letters.summary:
Sends 6th ed. ofOrigin;

draws attention to his criticism of ARW’s estimate of Kovalevsky;

mentions his disagreement with much of Spencer’s doctrine

and in a postscript points out an inaccuracy in an article inOnce a Month.

letters.title: To J. D. Hague   20 February 1872
letters.summary: Thanks for a quarto work on the mining industry. CD’s sons much obliged for kindness in California.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   20 February 1872
letters.summary: Saw editor of thePall Mall Gazetteabout review ofOriginandGenesis of species.

letters.title: From D. Appleton & Co.   23 February 1872
letters.summary: Enclosed account has had charged against it difference in costs between type composition in the U. S. and securing stereotype plates from Murray. CD should insist on securing plates from the London publisher of all future books, otherwise Appleton unable to pay 10% of gross price.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   23 [February 1872 – October 1874]
letters.summary: Asks for investment advice.

letters.title: To Amy Ruck   24 February [1872]
letters.summary: Wants AR to make any observations she can on the occurrence of little ledges on the side of steep, turf-covered slopes. Feels they may result from the washing down of worm-castings.

letters.title: To G. C. Wallich   24 February [1872]
letters.summary: Asks for the negative and permission to publish photo of smiling girl. [Expression, p. 202, plate III, fig. 2.]

letters.title: From Charles Nordhoff   27 February 1872
letters.summary:
Reports the case of a cockerel raised in isolation from other cocks which repeatedly attempted, but failed, to crow properly.

Also discusses behaviour in horses; one male will "look after" 20–25 females.

letters.title: To Anatole Roujou?   28 February [1872]
letters.summary:
Has read correspondent’s work. Glad he is not shocked at belief that man is descendant of lower form. An unusual attitude for a Frenchman.

Fears they differ greatly on origins of moral sense.

letters.title: To A. W. Bennett   29 February [1872]
letters.summary:
Asks AWB for a reference to a paper;

thanks him for his generous review of the last edition [6th] of theOrigin.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [29 February 1872]
letters.summary: Amount of clay present in certain chalk samples.

letters.title: From T. C. Eyton   29 February [1872]
letters.summary: Disagrees with the "Darwinian theory"; does not see evidence enough to support it. Will send CD any notes he makes for or against.

letters.title: From Charles Lyell   29 February 1872
letters.summary: Has been looking for something about crop rotation inOriginandVariation.

letters.title: To August Weismann   29 February 1872
letters.summary:
Glad AW’s eyesight is better.

Has received AW’s essay [Einfluss der Isolierung(1872)].

Glad he is turning attention to sexual selection. Hardly any naturalists agree with CD on subject.

letters.title: From Alfred Espinas   March 1872
letters.summary: AE, philosophy professor, is disposed to accept natural selection, but argues that it lacks direction. Suggests that direction would be given if one assumed the appearance of multiple advantageous traits in a single individual. Cites Herbert Spencer, Rudolf Virchow, Claude Bernard, and Carl Vogt.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [1 March 1872]
letters.summary: David Forbes thinks WED’s chalk samples have been penetrated by surface mud.

letters.title: From David Forbes   1 March 1872
letters.summary: Sends information on composition of chalk at Shoreham and Folkestone.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   1 March 1872
letters.summary:
Thanks CD forOrigin, 6th ed.

Has declined chair at Strasbourg.

Describes research on calcareous sponges.

Criticises Pangenesis.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [3 March 1872]
letters.summary: Sends dirt residue of chalk samples for David Forbes to examine.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   3 March 1872
letters.summary: Response to 6th ed. ofOrigin. CD’s answer to Mivart on initial stages of modifications is complete; the "eye and ear objection" is not handled so satisfactorily.

letters.title: From Alexander Agassiz   4 March 1872
letters.summary:
Thanks for new [6th] edition ofOrigin.

Is working on Echini.

The more material he gets the less easy it is to diagnose a genus or species. Has little doubt that "classification is nothing but the most arbitrary convenient tool, depending upon the material at our command at a special time".

letters.title: To T. C. Eyton   4 March [1872]
letters.summary:
Thanks for facts about ducks.

Thinks TCE will be converted to principle of evolution if he continues testing facts for and against it. Natural selection is another question.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   7 March 1872
letters.summary: A. S. Packard would like to visit CD to pay his respects.

letters.title: From John Murray   9 March 1872
letters.summary: JM arranges to pay CD for the latest issue ofDescent.

letters.title: To John Murray   [9 March 1872 or later]
letters.summary: CD is vexed to hear that some of his friends and some booksellers complain of the type of the new [6th] edition ofOrigin. CD, whose eyesight is not good, had no trouble reading proofs.

letters.title: To Bartholomaus von Carneri   12 March 1872
letters.summary: Offers to send German editions of his works when he return home.

letters.title: From Raphael Meldola   12 March 1872
letters.summary:
Wishes to use some of Fritz Müller’s observations in his paper on mimicry.

CD’s reply and Huxley’s article ["Mr Darwin’s critics",Contemp. Rev.18 (1871): 443–76] have answered all of Mivart’s objections to natural selection as applied to man.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   12 March 1872
letters.summary: Has just finished his work [?The martyrdom of man(1872)]. The new points are: (1) Negroes have whiskers; (2) their music is sometimes agreeable; (3) the Kaffirs are Negroes.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   14 March 1872
letters.summary: Plans for visit to CD.

letters.title: From Amy Ruck   15 March [1872]
letters.summary: Has failed to discover the signs of earthworm activity that CD described.

letters.title: To D. Appleton & Co.   16 March 1872
letters.summary: Acknowledges payment from sale of his books.

letters.title: From A. F. Boardman   18 March 1872
letters.summary:
On how various human emigrations have supported the work of natural selection.

Defends the view that soil and air account for taller stature of westerners in U. S.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   18 March [1872]
letters.summary: Will see CD tomorrow.

letters.title: From Gaston de Saporta   18 March 1872
letters.deprecated: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.sender: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.summary: CD insists too strongly, inDescent, on man’s origin from a simian ancestor, rather than some other primate.

letters.title: To G. C. Wallich   [20 March 1872]
letters.summary: Has received GCW’s negative from the Heliotype Co. Thanks him for the beautiful work of art which, however, will make others on the same plate look ugly. [SeeExpression, pl. III, fig. 2.]

letters.title: To John Lubbock   [after 21 March 1872]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Discusses problems of obtaining money for the alteration of Down church.

letters.title: From John Scott   22 March 1872
letters.summary:
Describes habits of worms.

DiscussesLeersiaexperiments.

letters.title: To ?   23 March [1872–4]
letters.summary: CD has lost his reference to cross between gold and silver pheasants.

letters.title: From Raphael Meldola   26 March 1872
letters.summary:
A. G. Butler has named the specimens sent by CD with Fritz Müller’s letter.

Sends several facts relating to sexual selection, mimicry, and hybrids.

Discusses the possibility that mimicked and mimicking forms have descended from originally allied forms and have diverged in structure but not in appearance.

letters.title: From J. R. Martin   27 March 1872
letters.summary: CD is urged to increase to 20 his shares in the Artizans, Labourers & General Dwellings Co. Ltd. Many prominent people have done so.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   [before 28 March 1872]
letters.summary: On colours and breeding of rabbits.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   28 March 1872
letters.summary:
Endorses revised statement about Butler’s odd hereditary habit;

describes a séance at William Crookes’s.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   28 March 1872
letters.summary: Feels it would be worth while but difficult to investigate mimicked and mimicking forms for structural similarities that would indicate a closer alliance in the past.

letters.title: From Leonard Darwin   [29 March 1872]
letters.summary: Data relating to experiments; shrinkage of earth on drying.

letters.title: To F. C. Donders   29 March 1872
letters.summary: Comments on action of eyes in a person lost in meditation. Asks about Charles Bell’s explanation [inAnatomy of expression(1806, 1844)].

letters.title: To Francis Galton   29 March [1872]
letters.summary:
Comments on FG’s description of a séance at the house of William Crookes.

Will use FG’s words about [H. M. Butler’s] hereditary habit [inExpression, p. 33 n. 8].

letters.title: From Thomas Rivers   29 March 1872
letters.summary:
Sends two vines for CD’s experiments, with instructions for grafting.

Mentions a hybrid plum–peach.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   30 March 1872
letters.summary:
Would like to do Russian translation ofExpression.

May come to England.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   31 March 1872
letters.summary: Has forwarded CD’s letter to Crookes.

letters.title: From James Murie   31 March 1872
letters.summary: Requests letter recommending him for the Chair of General and Comparative Physiology at the Royal Veterinary College.

letters.title: From F. C. Donders   1 April 1872
letters.summary: His analysis and explanation of the fact, observed by Charles Bell, that the eyeballs are turned upwards and inwards when consciousness begins to fail.

letters.title: To Briton Riviere   1 April 1872
letters.summary: Asks BR to make two drawings of dogs to show expressions. Discusses expressions of hostile dog and caressing dog.

letters.title: To Georg von Seidlitz   1 April 1872
letters.summary: Thanks for "Literatur & Tables zur Descendenz Theorie" [check title!?] taken from hisDie Darwin’sche Theorie[1871], which CD had read with gratification some time before.

letters.title: To James Murie   2 April 1872
letters.summary: Testimonial letter. JM would be well fitted for the Chair of General and Comparative Physiology of the Royal Veterinary College.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   3 April [1872]
letters.summary: Encloses a letter from Mr Moran, conveyed by Mr Lawrence.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   3 April 1872
letters.summary: Sends preface of his book [see8241]; he acknowledges debt to CD, but does not claim to have given a correct exposition of Darwinism.

letters.title: To Thomas Rivers   3 April 1872
letters.summary: Thanks for vines and for all the information given him. Fears experiment will be more difficult than he had expected.

letters.title: From Briton Riviere   3 April 1872
letters.summary: Will attempt to draw the two expressions CD wants.

letters.title: From Chauncey Wright   3 April 1872
letters.summary:
Discusses Mivart’s reply ["Genesis of species",North Am. Rev.114 (1872): 451–68] to CW’s review and to Huxley.

Asks whether CD knows anyone to whom he could usefully send a copy of his phyllotaxy paper [Mem. Am. Acad. Arts & Sci.n.s. 9 (1867–73): 379–415].

letters.title: To Briton Riviere   4 April 1872
letters.summary: Thanks for kindness. BR must not think of trying until he feels inclination and strength for task.

letters.title: From Adam Elliot   5 April 1872
letters.summary: Reports and asks questions about the offspring from the purported pairing of a woman with an ape.

letters.title: To August Weismann   5 April 1872
letters.summary:
Comments on AW’s work [Einfluss der Isolierung(1872)].

Discusses formation of local races.

Conchologist should investigate whether species of same genus vary during successive geological periods.

Comments on Franz Hilgendorf ["ÜberPlanorbis multiformis",Monatsber. K. Preuss. Akad. Wiss. Berlin(1866): 474–504].

Believes sexual selection will be judged a powerful agency.

letters.title: To Chauncey Wright   6 April 1872
letters.summary:
Delighted to have cloud of darkness removed by CW’s paper on phyllotaxy [Mem. Am. Acad. Arts & Sci.n.s. 9 (1867–73): 379–415].

Has heard that Mivart will answer CW’s pamphlet [Darwinism(1871)].

letters.title: To William Bowman   8 April [1872]
letters.summary: Asks to borrow "Sölberg Wells, Treatise on the Diseases of the Eye 1869" referred to by F. C. Donders.

letters.title: To Joseph Kaines?   8 April 1872
letters.summary:
Thanks correspondent for an interesting paper [unspecified] and his kind remarks about CD’s work.

CD had forgotten Auguste Comte’s "striking observations" on relations of man to lower animals.

letters.title: To F. C. Donders   8 April 1872
letters.summary:
Thanks FCD for information, which will make him "strike out a good deal".

Has received German pamphlet.

Will read work by John Soelberg Wells [?A treatise on the diseases of the eye(1869, 1870)].

Discusses his work on expression.

letters.title: From G. C. Oxenden   8 April 1872
letters.summary: Wild plants that live at the edges of civilisation, e.g., forest flowers growing on grazed land, are always reduced in size.

letters.title: To Gaston de Saporta   8 April 1872
letters.deprecated: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.recipient: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.summary: Responds to GdeS’s comments onDescent[see8246]. Cannot give up belief in close relationship of man to higher Simiae.

letters.title: From the Anthropological Society, Vienna   9 April 1872
letters.summary: Cancel: Diploma, not a letter.

letters.title: To Georg von Seidlitz   10 April 1872
letters.summary: Has received two copies of GvS’sDie Darwin’sche Theorie. As he already has a copy, CD will send one to the Royal Society [of London], and the other to the Linnean Society.

letters.title: To Chauncey Wright   [11 or 21] April [1872]
letters.summary: Sends details of Alexander Dickson’s paper ‘On some abnormal cones ofPinus Pinaster’ (Dickson 1871).

letters.title: To Williams & Norgate   12 April [1872]
letters.summary:
Orders books: J. R. Leifchild,The higher ministry of nature(1872);

Hermann Müller,The application of the Darwinian theory to flowers[(1872?), reprint fromAm. Nat.5 (1871): 271–97];

and a review by J. B. Hunter.

letters.title: From G. J. Allman   13 April 1872
letters.summary:
Thanks for sending translation of A. W. Malm’s paper ["On flatfishes",K. Svensk. Vetensk. Akad. Handl.N. F. 7 (1867–8) no. 4]; thinks it establishes that eye migrates across surface of head rather than through the skull.

Considers the relationship between direction of locomotion and the presence of stalked eyes in Crustacea.

letters.title: From Roland Trimen   13 April 1872
letters.summary:
On new [6th] edition of theOrigin; comments on additions.

Owen’s attitude toward evolution.

letters.title: From Arthur Russell   15 April 1872
letters.deprecated: Arthur John Edward (Arthur) Russell, Lord Arthur Russell
letters.sender: Arthur John Edward (Arthur) Russell, Lord Arthur Russell
letters.summary:
Has acquired some French frogs,Rana esculenta, which have mated withR. temporaria, but the spawn has not developed.

Asks whether anyone has successfully crossed frogs and toads.

letters.title: To John Scott   15 April [1872]
letters.summary: JS’s valuable observations on worms in India along with Asa Gray’s in the United States confirm CD’s opinion that worms work in the same way all over the world. Requests further information on the subject.

letters.title: To A. G. Carlier   16 April [1872]
letters.summary: Thanks AGC for some notes and his book [Darwinism refuted by researches in psychology(1872)].

letters.title: To Friend Lewin   16 April [1872]
letters.summary: Suggests FL and Dr Maudsley come to Down via Chislehurst.

letters.title: From F. C. Donders   17 April 1872
letters.summary: Protests against CD’s statement that FCD’s letter will make him "strike out a good deal". He would never pardon himself for being the cause of any suppression by CD. It is for specialists to put their knowledge at CD’s service. He is mistaken if he thinks a knowledge of physiology is sufficient for writing a book on expression. It is CD’s conception and spirit that all await. Offers to read those parts of the proofs ofExpressiondealing with physiology.

letters.title: To G. G. Leveson-Gower, Earl Granville   [before 19 April 1872]
letters.deprecated: George Granville Sutherland-Leveson-Gower, 2d Duke of Sutherland
letters.recipient: George Granville Sutherland-Leveson-Gower, 2d Duke of Sutherland
letters.summary: Writes on behalf of British authors requesting improved copyright rights with respect to United States.

letters.title: From Charles Crawley   [18 April 1872]
letters.summary:
His father sends a list (to be returned) of boarders at Shrewsbury School. Implies CD stayed at Mother Bromfield’s.

Sends Plautus quotation on expression.

letters.title: To William Bowman   19 April [1872]
letters.summary: Returns borrowed book. Is surprised that any of us have eyes "seeing what a frightful number of horrid diseases the eye is liable to".

letters.title: To Charles Crawley   19 April [1872]
letters.summary:
Thanks CC’s father for relic. Remembers almost every boy above him but few below him in the school.

CC’s translation seems capital.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   19 April 1872
letters.summary: Has attended one more séance, which he describes; tells of the freedom investigators have to check, although they cannot prearrange, experiments.

letters.title: To F. C. Donders   20 April 1872
letters.summary: Thanks FCD for suggested deletions in MS ofExpression. Declines offer from FCD to examine proofs also.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   21 April [1872]
letters.summary: Encourages FG to carry out investigation [of spiritualism]. However, his own health is too uncertain to accept Daniel Dunglas Home’s offer. Discusses possibility of reproducing Crookes’s apparatus for sale.

letters.title: To ?   21 April 1872
letters.summary: [An autograph.] "With Mr Darwin’s compliments."

letters.title: From Georg von Seidlitz   22 April 1872
letters.summary: Discusses his book [Die Darwin’sche Theorie(1871)], in which he emphasises natural selection acts on inborn variation and is the exclusive cause of transmutation, in opposition to the theories of Haeckel and Moritz Wagner.

letters.title: To W. H. Edwards   23 April [1872]
letters.summary:
Thanks for part nine of WHE’s [Butterflies of North America(1868–72)].

Comments on trimorphism inPapilio ajax.

letters.title: To Rifle Volunteer Corps   23 April 1872
letters.summary: Regrets that his health will prevent his attending concerts in aid of the Rifle Corps Fund.

letters.title: From A. B. Meyer   25 April 1872
letters.summary: Sends information on expression: head and hand movements of the Tagals of the Philippines, and of Malaysians.

letters.title: From F. C. Donders   26 April 1872
letters.summary: Royal Netherlands Academy of Science has elected CD.

letters.title: To F. C. Donders   29 April [1872]
letters.summary: Expresses gratitude on election to Royal Netherlands Academy.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   30 April [1872]
letters.summary:
Does not know Dr Mahoney.

Thanks CD for offer of photographs.

His mother’s health is no worse.

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   30 April [1872]
letters.summary:
Not surprised incipient disease in female would make her unattractive to male.

Sorry JJW’s official duties are so heavy.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   2 May 1872
letters.summary: Sends sentences from Hermann von Helmholtz about difference between minor and major chords.

letters.title: To Henry Johnson   2 May [1872]
letters.summary: Thanks for notes on worm-castings. Amount of ammonia surprises CD. David Forbes asserts that published analysis of carbon in vegetable matter valueless. Suspects that worms search for food and do not blindly swallow earth.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   3 May [1872]
letters.summary:
Thanks GHD for extracts, but says the subject of music is beyond him.

Suggests that GHD deliberate over one or two sentences of his paper on dress ["Developments in dress",Macmillan’s Mag.22 (1872): 410–16].

Refers to prospective marriage of Amy [Ruck and CD’s son Francis].

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   3 May 1872
letters.summary: Glad Mrs Darwin likes his preface, but fears she will not like his tone on religion.

letters.title: From J. H. Schmick   3 May 1872
letters.summary: Having sent CD his two essays outlining his theory on "A secular transposition of oceans" [see7368], JHS now forwards to CD a book he believes establishes his theory as an "eternal law of nature" [Die neue Theorie periodische säkularer Schwankungen des Seespiegels[periodischer!?] (1872)].

letters.title: From Paolo Mantegazza   4 May 1872
letters.summary:
CD has been elected Honorary Member of Società Italiana di Antropologia e di Etnologia.

Cranial measurements connect man and apes.

He has shown differences between male and female skulls that bear on sexual selection.

letters.title: To Hermann Müller   [before 5 May 1872]
letters.summary:
Comments on HM’s paper ["Anwendung der Darwin’schen Lehre auf Bienen",Verh. Naturhist. Ver. preuss. Rheinland29 (1872): 1–96];

sexual selection in bees.

Encloses account on habits ofBombus.

letters.title: From Hermann Müller   5 May 1872
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for MS on the routes of male bees.

His "Fertilisation of flowers" is complete [Die Befruchtung der Blumen(1873)].

letters.title: To Williams & Norgate   6 May [1872]
letters.summary: "Be so good as to send meUnsere Zeitwith Julius Frauenstädt’s article ["Darwin’s Auffassung des geistigen und sittlichen Lebens des Menschen" n.s. 8 (May 1872), 597–605]. I am much obliged for the information."

letters.title: From Albert Günther   10 May 1872
letters.summary:
Wants CD’s support for his application for post of Assistant Keeper in Zoological Department of British Museum.

Death of G. R. Gray.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   10 May [1872]
letters.summary:
Comments on CL’sPrinciples of geology, 11th ed.

Discusses natural selection in man.

letters.title: From Samuel Butler   11 May 1872
letters.summary: His chapter on machines inErewhonhas been misunderstood as laughing at theOrigin. He was only trying to show how an absurd proposition can be defended with a little ingenuity, distortion, and departure from strict scientific method. Will explain in a second edition, if one is called for.

letters.title: To Albert Günther   11 May [1872]
letters.summary:
Encloses a testimonial for AG [in support of his application for a promotion at British Museum].

Does he agree with Carl Gegenbaur’s paper on the limbs of fish [Jenaische Z. Naturwiss.5 (1870): 397–447]?

Asks what caused G. R. Gray’s sudden death.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   11 May 1872
letters.summary:
The die is cast on Ayrton affair. Lord Derby has called for all of the correspondence, as a result of pressure by men of science on JDH’s behalf.

Has just had a Greenland collection, which supports his views altogether; "I am ready to do fight for these with you."

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   13 May [1872]
letters.summary: Will FD try to persuade A. D. Bartlett to show a live snake to a porcupine and observe whether the porcupine rattles the quills on its tail? [See8333.]

letters.title: To H. E. Litchfield   13 May 1872
letters.summary: Wishes to insert R. B. Litchfield’s remarks [intoExpression] but will not give them as his own.

letters.title: From Albert Günther   13 May 1872
letters.summary: Thanks for CD’s testimonial.

letters.title: To Albert Günther   13 May [1872]
letters.summary:
Is the horned toad of Oregon a batrachian or a lizard?

Hopes AG will be promoted in the British Museum.

letters.title: From W. B. Tegetmeier   13 May 1872
letters.summary:
Has found the skull of the horned cock.

With regard to CD’s suggestion about the possibility of producing a pigeon breed with differently coloured sexes, WBT reports the results of crossing blue and silver dragons; the silver offspring are almost always hens.

Would like the latest edition of theOrigin.

Encloses notes on volume one [ofDescent].

Encloses a photograph showing the bleaching effect of the sun’s rays on dun feathers in pigeons.

letters.title: From Albert Günther   14 May 1872
letters.summary: AG’s application for an appointment to Assistant Keeper at the British Museum.

letters.title: To James Hector   14 May 1872
letters.summary: Acknowledges election as Honorary Member of the New Zealand Institute [now Royal Society N. Z.].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   14 May 1872
letters.summary: More on Ayrton affair. Conduct of Gladstone and the Ministry despicable. They have owned him to be in right but will not raise a finger until exposure in Parliament is imminent.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   14 May [1872]
letters.summary:
Is sorry JDH cannot come to Down.

Hopes the House of Lords "pitch into the accursed fellow" [Ayrton].

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   14 May [1872]
letters.summary:
Thanks for information on sexual colours in pigeons.

Will send latest edition ofOrigin.

letters.title: From Gerard Krefft   15 May 1872
letters.summary: Sends his article ["Review of Owen’s Cuvierian principle of palaeontology"].

letters.title: From A. D. Bartlett   16 May 1872
letters.summary: Reports aggressive reactions of three kinds of porcupines to a snake, concluding that in the wild they would probably kill and eat it [seeExpression, pp. 93–4]

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   16 May 1872
letters.summary: WWR is beginning to appreciate CD’s warnings against his polemical writing.

letters.title: From Briton Riviere   16 May 1872
letters.summary: Sends sketches of expressions in two dogs.

letters.title: From E. D. Smith   16 May 1872
letters.summary: Reports and describes massive hailstones which fell in Petoraghur [Nepal].

letters.title: From Hugh Browne   17 May 1872
letters.summary:
Sends quotation from Thomas Moore’sMemoirs[ed. Lord John Russell, (1853–6)] about hereditary peculiarity in handwriting.

On colour-blindness in his family.

letters.title: From Albert Günther   17 May 1872
letters.summary: O. Salvin will not be applying for the same post as AG.

letters.title: From Athénaïs Michelet   17 May 1872
letters.summary: AM [wife of Jules Michelet] offers information on crosses in cats.

letters.title: From William Green   18 May 1872
letters.summary: Sends duplicate of his previous letter [8189]; he addressed it simply to C. Darwin, England, and had no reply.

letters.title: To Briton Riviere   19 May [1872]
letters.summary:
Comments on drawings of hostile dog and affectionate dog.

Sends small gift of money.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   20 May 1872
letters.summary: His book has received bad reviews; therefore CD’s letter cheers him up.

letters.title: From Briton Riviere   20 May 1872
letters.summary: Will himself correct the details on the woodblock CD finds acceptable. The second one followed CD’s instructions, contrary to his own experience.

letters.title: To G. S. Ffinden   21 May [1872]
letters.summary: Sends £35 as his subscription towards the building of a vicarage.

letters.title: From Albert Günther   21 May 1872
letters.summary:
Believes many of the species and even genera of the fish family Labyrinthici are products of domestication.

Events at the British Museum.

letters.title: From Fulvio Martinelli   21 May 1872
letters.summary: [MS of a short paper on pigeon breeding by an Italian doctor.]

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   22 May [1872]
letters.summary: Comments on migration as a factor in evolution. Suggests pamphlet by August Weismann on the subject [Über den Einfluss der Isolierung(1872)].

letters.title: From Briton Riviere   22 May 1872
letters.summary: Will try again to draw the expression of a pleased dog.

letters.title: To ?   22 May 1872
letters.summary: Agrees to contribute £10 towards a new road in the area of Beckenham, although he doubts whether the road will be of much use to him.

letters.title: From J. D. Dana   23 May 1872
letters.summary: JDD is sending a copy of his book,Corals and coral islands[1872], with his compliments.

letters.title: To Athénaïs Michelet   23 May 1872
letters.summary: Discusses books about cats and crosses in cats. Thanks her for her book on cats.

letters.title: From Henry Montague   24 May 1872
letters.summary: Sends MS of a book on progressive development on this planet and in the universe. Asks CD to underwrite its publication.

letters.title: From Chauncey Wright   24 May 1872
letters.summary:
Has replied [inNorth Am. Rev.115 (1872): 1–30] to Mivart’s communication to theNorth American Review[114 (1872): 451–68].

Discusses the degree of fixedness of different characters in organisms.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   26 May 1872
letters.summary: Again seeks help with his rabbits; hopes one of CD’s men can take them.

letters.title: From Briton Riviere   26 May 1872
letters.summary: Thanks for CD’s books [unspecified].

letters.title: To Francis Galton   27 May [1872]
letters.summary:
Agrees to care for FG’s rabbits and will breed from them.

Plans to go to Southampton for ten days.

letters.title: To ?   27 May 1872
letters.summary: Invites correspondent to dinner and overnight the next Friday, and gives directions at length from London to Down. "I have heard from Mr Litchfield that you are in London … will you give us the pleasure of seeing you here".

letters.title: From Francis Galton   28 May 1872
letters.summary:
Delighted CD’s groom will take the rabbits;

has just done proof of a paper to the Royal Society on "blood-relationship", defining kinship between parents and offspring.

letters.title: From Briton Riviere   28 May 1872
letters.summary: Sends a drawing of dog’s expression for CD to approve and return.

letters.title: To Briton Riviere   29 May 1872
letters.summary:
Comments on drawing of dog. Will get it engraved [seeExpression, pp. 52, 53].

Will send MS ofExpressionto printers next week.

letters.title: From Samuel Butler   30 May 1872
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for his note and cheque for young May.

Will send copy of second edition ofErewhon, in which he has set himself straight about "having intended no villainy by the machines". [See8318.]

letters.title: To Nicholas Trübner   30 May [1872?]
letters.summary: Send parcel to Orpington station.

letters.title: From Hubert Airy   31 May 1872
letters.summary: A review and criticism of Chauncey Wright’s paper on phyllotaxy [Mem. Am. Acad. Arts & Sci.n.s. 9 (1867–73): 379–415]. Does not believe that the "distributive" and "cyclical" properties, which CW claims characterise the existing spiral orders of leaf arrangement, can be shown to be advantageous to plants. CW’s speculations on the origins of the spiral arrangement of leaves are purely hypothetical.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   31 May 1872
letters.summary: Sends, via C. L. Brace, his book [Botany for young people, pt 2How plants behave(1872)], "your own science adapted to juvenile minds".

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   1 June 1872
letters.summary: Thanks him for interesting letter from a Mr Wood on heredity in fruit-trees.

letters.title: To Chauncey Wright   3 June [1872]
letters.summary:
CW’s article responding to Mivart [see8351] on the fixity of species is very clear.

On evolution of language, CD doubts W. D. Whitney’s claim that changes are effected by the will of man. Asks CW when a thing may properly be said to be so effected.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   4 June 1872
letters.summary: Thanks CD for criticisms of his paper; explains why there is greater diversity among succeeding generations than in the first.

letters.title: From M. C. Stanley   4 June 1872
letters.deprecated: Mary Catherine Stanley, countess of Derby
letters.sender: Mary Catherine Stanley, countess of Derby
letters.summary: Sackville Cecil would like to be present with Francis Galton at one of William Crookes’s séances. Can CD arrange it?

letters.title: To M. C. Lloyd   5 June [1872]
letters.summary: Thanks her for drawing of dog.

letters.title: To William Marshall   6 June [1872]
letters.summary:
Thanks WALM for having sent interesting publications, especially the one on relation of structure of man to lower animals,

and just a few days since, on protuberances on bird skulls. WALM’s facts on the latter subject have an important bearing on the acquisition of sexual characters. CD is pleased that the influence of sexual selection is admitted.

letters.title: From Briton Riviere   6 June 1872
letters.summary:
Will need to see proofs of his drawings.

Flattered to be mentioned in introduction toExpression[p. 26].

letters.title: From Hubert Airy   7 June 1872
letters.summary: On leaf arrangement. [Badly damaged and almost illegible.]

letters.title: From Francis Galton   7 June 1872
letters.summary: Will do what he can for Lord Sackville Cecil, but he, himself, cannot get to séances when he likes. Introduction of a stranger always disturbs séances. Person most likely to help would be Lord Lindsey.

letters.title: From John Murray   7 June [1872]
letters.summary: Messrs Clowes have received MS ofExpression. JM submits specimen pages for CD’s approval.

letters.title: From Alfred Tylor   8 June 1872
letters.summary: AT is trying to publish his paper with important evidence on "the pluvial period".

letters.title: From John Tyndall   8 June [1872]
letters.summary: Sends CD a copy of the memorial supporting Hooker’s case against A. S. Ayrton’s interference in the administration of Kew Gardens.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   [after 8 June 1872]
letters.summary: In England to write a monograph onAnthracotherium.

letters.title: From C. L. Sutherland   [9–19 June 1872]
letters.summary: Proposes calling on CD with Prof. Wrightson of Royal Agricultural College, Cirencester.

letters.title: To Hubert Airy?   9 June [1872?]
letters.summary: Agrees to read paper; warns he lacks mathematical knowledge.

letters.title: To Herbert Spencer   10 June [1872]
letters.summary:
Expresses his "unbounded admiration" for HS’s article on Martineau ["Mr Martineau on evolution",Contemp. Rev.20 (1872): 141–54]

and his article on sociology [Contemp. Rev.19 (1872): 701–18]. CD never believed in the reigning influence of great men on the world’s progress but could not have given his reasons. "Now every one with eyes to see and ears to hear . . . ought to bow their knee to you, as I for one do."

letters.title: From Asa Gray   11 June 1872
letters.summary: O. N. Rood sends two copies of an amusing picture by T. F. Beard, "The young Darwinian" to AG, who forwards one to CD.

letters.title: From Menyhért Lónyay   11 June 1872
letters.summary: CD has been elected a Foreign Member of the Magyar Tudományos Akademia [Hungarian Academy of Sciences].

letters.title: To Menyhért Lónyay   [after 11 June 1872]
letters.summary: Thanks for his election to the Hungarian Academy of Sciences.

letters.title: From Herbert Spencer   12 June 1872
letters.summary: HS hopes in the future to show more fully "absolute emptiness" of James Martineau’s propositions; is glad CD approved of his article dealing with JM’s arguments. [J. Martineau, "The place of mind in nature",Contemp. Rev.19 (1872): 606–23; H. Spencer, "Mr Martineau on evolution",Contemp. Rev.20 (1872): 141–54.]

letters.title: To ? [a bookseller?]   13 June [1872–4]
letters.summary: Asks recipient to send parcels to his brother, Erasmus Alvey Darwin, at 6 Queen Anne Street, London, and not by post.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   14 June [1872]
letters.summary: Has signed the memorial by men of science with real pleasure. Fears it may be too severe. He told Lady Derby about JDH’s troubles. She said she would tell Lord Derby what he had said.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   15 June 1872
letters.summary: Expects the memorial to make Gladstone frantic. Government regrets granting Lord Derby the correspondence and Lubbock has been advised to postpone calling for it in Lower House. This looks fishy. Is exhausted by the affair.

letters.title: From B. A. Renshaw   15 June 1872
letters.summary: Reports a monkey-like child in Teneriffe.

letters.title: From L. C. Wedgwood   [15 June 1872?]
letters.summary: Worm-casts on a ridged hill.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   16 June 1872
letters.summary: Asks CD for seeds of some plants.

letters.title: From Friedrich Tiemann   16 June 1872
letters.summary: A goat in Breslau recently gave birth to three kids, two normal but one almost entirely lacking in hair.

letters.title: To F. C. Donders   17 June 1872
letters.summary:
Would be impractical to have FCD check references to physiology in proofs [ofExpression]. William Bowman has checked chapter on weeping.

Invites FCD to visit Down when he comes to England in July.

letters.title: From Albert Günther   19 June 1872
letters.summary: Has been appointed Assistant Keeper at the British Museum.

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   20 June 1872
letters.summary:
Privately advises CD against having anything to do with W. P. Snow, whose personality and past conduct on a mission vessel were very bad.

Reports on the successes of the missionaries on the Beagle Channel [Tierra del Fuego].

letters.title: From Rudolf Sundström   20 June 1872
letters.summary: Sends CD the first part of his Swedish translation ofDescent[1872].

letters.title: To Albert Günther   21 June [1872]
letters.summary: Rejoices at AG’s appointment [as Assistant Keeper at the British Museum].

letters.title: From Athénaïs Michelet   26 June 1872
letters.summary:
Her husband is very ill;

her book on cats does not go well.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [before 30 June 1872]
letters.summary: Quickening of heart-beat in fear. A. H. Garrod does not think that this means that the heart is working harder.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [before 30 June 1872]
letters.summary: A. H. Garrod on relationship of heart-beat to amount of work done by heart.

letters.title: From Dr von Gloeden   1 July 1872
letters.summary:
Comments onDescent.

Attempts to explain differing sex ratios in births from illegitimate unions, Jewish marriages, and Christian marriages.

Speculates on role of male and female elements in conception.

Thinks survival of individual conflicts in some degree with survival of species; for example, hybrids often live longer than fertile individuals.

letters.title: To F. E. Abbot   2 July 1872
letters.summary:
Renews subscription toIndex.

Was interested in FEA’s lecture on "The God of science" [Index24 Feb 1872].

letters.title: To Asa Gray   8 July [1872]
letters.summary:
Thanks for AG’s book,How plants behave[see8363].

Is correcting proofs ofExpression.

letters.title: To John Denny   9 July 1872
letters.summary:
Has read JD’s articles in theGardeners’ Chronicle[(1872): 872, 904–5].

Questions him on the fertility of certain varieties ofPelargoniumwhich are fertile with some varieties but infertile with others.

letters.title: To Leonard Darwin   11 July [1872]
letters.summary: CD wants no more alterations than are necessary [to proofs ofExpression]. Warns LD that "any alteration seems at first an improvement".

letters.title: From John Denny   12 July 1872
letters.summary:
Replies to CD’s queries. Duke of CornwallPelargoniumis fertile with its own pollen. Has failed to produce hybrids from other varieties besidesP. peltatumandP. elegans. Sends numbers of theFloristwhich contain an account of his mode of procedure ["On cross-breeding pelargoniums"Florist & Pomologist(1872): 10, 34, 50].

Reports a confirmation of his theory of the prepotence of the male parent.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   12 July [1872]
letters.summary: Overjoyed at the way the newspapers have taken up JDH’s case. The memorial has done great good this way, whatever the wretched Government does. It is enough to make one a Tory. JDH has done a service to all men of science by showing governments that they cannot be trampled on.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   12 July [1872]
letters.summary: Comments on enclosed discussion of S. American geology by Agassiz. Mentions elevation of Patagonia and glaciation.

letters.title: From W. D. Fox   13 July [1872]
letters.summary: Will not pass through London, so will not be able to call at Down.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   14 July 1872
letters.summary:
Asks whether he can start soon on translatingExpression.

Thinks CD has gone a little too far on St G. J. Mivart’s objection, which he thinks did very little harm in Germany.

JVC’s history of zoology is finished [Geschichte der Zoologie bis auf Joh. Müller und Charl. Darwin(1872)].

letters.title: To John Denny   14 July [1872]
letters.summary: Discusses JD’s crossing experiments withPelargonium; notes that his conclusions on male prepotence oppose those of Gärtner. Suggests that his observations on differences in fertility of certain varieties ofPelargoniumcrossed with certain other varieties be communicated to the Linnean Society.

letters.title: From F. C. Donders   14 July 1872
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for invitation but declines because of his need for a rest instead of coming to England in July.

Repeats his offer to help CD at any time. "I am always learning by trying to answer your questions."

letters.title: From Hubert Airy   [before 15] July 1872
letters.summary: Outlines his theory on the origin of existing orders of leaf arrangement. Believes spiral and whorled orders have evolved from a primitive distichous arrangement. These arrangements permit a compact bud form of small surface area that can withstand external changes in temperature, and in particular can tolerate frost.

letters.title: From Hubert Airy   16 July 1872
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for reading his MS [8412] and for his suggestions.

Clarifies his statement on the contraction of the bud-axis: did not mean to imply that this contraction occurred in an individual’s life-time, rather that it was the effect, after the course of ages, of successive favourable modifications.

Believes the true theory of phyllotaxy will give a convincing illustration and proof of the theory of evolution.

letters.title: To W. W. Baxter   16 July [1872?]
letters.summary: Orders a very small pot of "purest & best Extract of Hyosciamus for experimental purposes".

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   16 July 1872
letters.summary:
Will send second proofs ofExpression.

Glad JVC has finished translatingOrigin.

Assures him that Mivart’s book [On the genesis of species(1871)] has produced a great effect in England and America. CD has discussed incipient structures at some length because it enabled him to give many cases of gradation.

Asks JVC to note that he does not vouch forExpression’s being worth translating.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   16 July [1872]
letters.summary:
Is correcting proofs forExpression.

Family news.

letters.title: To Gerard Krefft   17 July 1872
letters.summary:
Thanks for JLGK’s article [see8331].

CD thinks it a pity that Owen shows so little consideration for the judgment of other naturalists.

letters.title: From F. E. Abbot   18 July 1872
letters.summary: Thanks CD for five dollars and two-year subscription toIndex, and for permission to quote CD’s compliments onTruths for the times.

letters.title: To Richard Litchfield   19 July [1872]
letters.summary: Thanks for explanation. Will follow RBL’s instructions.

letters.title: From Hubert Airy   20 July 1872
letters.summary: Discusses the significance of the node. Believes, with CD, that it has no independent importance but is merely the consequence of the presence of a leaf. Does not believe a distinction can be made between whorled and alternate leaf arrangements on the basis of the number of leaves springing from a node. The node, as the starting point of a leaf, is subject to any disarrangement which takes place among the leaves.

letters.title: To C. L. Brace   20 July [1872]
letters.summary: Comments on Brace’s work [The dangerous classes of New York(1872)].

letters.title: From John Denny   20 July 1872
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his offer to communicate the results of his experiments withPelargoniumto the Linnean Society. Prefers to continue experimenting for at least another season before doing so.

letters.title: From Hubert Airy   21 July 1872
letters.summary:
Corrects a factual error in his previous letter [8418].

Sends specimens illustrative of the "nodal" question.

letters.title: To John Denny   22 July 1872
letters.summary: Discusses the mutual sterility of some varieties ofPelargonium.

letters.title: From Armand de Quatrefages   23 July 1872
letters.deprecated: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.sender: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.summary: CD not nominated by French Academy.

letters.title: From Hubert Airy   24 July 1872
letters.summary:
Responds to CD’s comments on his MS on phyllotaxy.

The initial variation required by his theory would be a slight twist of the bud-axis; believes the frequent twisting of stems and branches renders such a variation possible.

Admits he placed too much emphasis on the importance of frost. He should have spoken more generally of "vicissitudes of climate".

letters.title: From William Bowman   24 July 1872
letters.summary: F. C. Donders coming to congress. Wants to arrange visit.

letters.title: To H. E. Litchfield   25 July 1872
letters.summary: Thanks for her pains over corrections [forExpression].

letters.title: To Leonard Darwin   26 July [1872]
letters.summary: CD cannot improve style [ofExpression] without great changes. "I am sick of the subject, and myself, and the world".

letters.title: To Heinrich Fick   26 July [1872]
letters.summary: Thanks HF for his essay ["Über den Einfluss der Naturwissenschaft auf das Recht",Jahrbücher für Nationalökonomie und Statistik18 (1872): 248–77]. CD gives views favouring competition among trades unions and the working classes.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   27 July 1872
letters.summary: Foreign translations, illustrations, and other arrangements forExpression. Foreign publishers must be bound not to publish before the English edition is out.

letters.title: From J. T. Gulick   27 July 1872
letters.summary: Mentions work he did in the Sandwich Islands. Asks to visit and bring shells.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   27 July [1872]
letters.summary:
On ARW’s "crushing" review [Nature6 (1872): 237–9] of C. R. Bree’sAn exposition of fallacies in the hypothesis of Mr Darwin.

Comments on other reviews and exchanges.

letters.title: To J. T. Gulick   28 July [1872]
letters.summary:
Invites JTG to visit.

Mentions visit from F. C. Donders.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   29 July 1872
letters.summary:
Queries and suggestions for arrangements about foreign editions ofExpression.

CD must see proofs for lettering on the plates [for Expression] to ensure that it matches the text.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   29 July 1872
letters.summary: May FG have lunch with CD Thursday [1 Aug] and arrange about rabbits?

letters.title: To Eduard Strasburger   29 July 1872
letters.summary: Comments on EAS’s work [?Die Coniferen und die Gnetaceen: eine morphologische Studie(1872)].

letters.title: To Edwards & Kidd   30 July [1872]
letters.summary: Discussion of the charge made for the plates [forExpression].

letters.title: From H. H. Howorth   30 July 1872
letters.summary:
Sends paper read before Anthropological Institute ["Strictures on Darwinism, pt 1",J. Anthropol. Inst.2 (1873): 21–40]. CD is his master, though they disagree.

Criticises Wallace’s "contemptuous phrases".

Is studying elevation and subsidence.

letters.title: To ?   30 July [1872–4]
letters.summary: Thanks recipient for information about eye colour of his shepherd dogs.

letters.title: From William Bowman   31 July 1872
letters.summary: Arranges to bring F. C. Donders to visit Down.

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   31 July 1872
letters.summary: On variegated leaves; a feature not inherited consistently.

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   31 July [1872]
letters.summary:
Thanks for new case.

Not very well.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   1 August 1872
letters.summary: Answers CD’s questions on arrangements for forthcoming publication ofExpression– including cost of stereotypes, woodcuts, and photo reproductions for foreign translations.

letters.title: From D. Appleton & Co.   1 August 1872
letters.summary: Statement of sales of U. S. editions ofOriginandDescent.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   1 August [1872]
letters.summary: George Snow, the carrier, now leaves Nag’s Head on Thursday mornings.

letters.title: From A. S. Packard Jr   1 August 1872
letters.summary: CD’s letter inviting him to visit did not reach him till he returned home.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [after August 1872?]
letters.summary: Sends quotation from Armand Trousseau,Lectures on clinical medicine[1868–72] 5: 213, on interruption of menstruation in young girls upon changing schools, as an example of the effect of changed conditions of life.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   3 August [1872]
letters.summary: Has sent sheets ofExpression.

letters.title: ToNature   3 August [1872]
letters.summary:
Replies to C. R. Bree’s letter of 27 July [Nature6 (1872): 260] contending that CD was wrong about early pedigree of man.

Defends the statement of CD’s view in Wallace’s review [Nature6 (1872): 237–9] of Bree’s book [Exposition of fallacies … of Darwin(1872)].

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   3 August [1872]
letters.summary: Encloses a letter toNature[see8448] correcting Dr Bree, who has accused ARW of "blundering". ARW should tear up CD’s letter if he does not like it or plans to reply himself.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   4 August 1872
letters.summary: Asks whether he can tell Appleton that Murray will supply clichés and stereotypes [forExpression] at only a small profit. Will make same offer to other foreign editors. Prefers that W. S. Dallas prepare the index.

letters.title: To Oswald Heer   4 August [1872–4]
letters.summary: Thanks OH for two memoirs on the fossil flora of Bear Island and Spitzbergen [K. Svensk. Vetensk. Akad. Handl.8 (1869) no. 7; 9 (1870) no. 5].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   4 August [1872]
letters.summary:
CD hopes theTimesabstract of minutes of Lords of the Treasury will make JDH’s position more comfortable.

The "wretched Lords" make CD indignant, but "nothing equals Owen’s conduct. – I used to be ashamed of hating him so much, but now I will carefully cherish my hatred & contempt to the last day of my life."

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   4 August 1872
letters.summary:
Has sent CD’s letter toNature[see8448].

Expresses admiration for H. C. Bastian’sThe beginnings of life[1872] and comments on its bearing uponOrigin.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   6 August 1872
letters.summary:
Sends Murray’s cheque for £315 for the last issue ofDescent.

Details regarding foreign editions ofExpression.

letters.title: From J. T. Gulick   6 August 1872
letters.summary: Sends synopsis of his paper "On diversity of evolution" [J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Zool.)11 (1873): 496–505] in which he attempts to show some of the means, other than natural selection, of modification of species.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   7 August 1872
letters.summary: On arrangements for paying for stereotyped plates forExpression. D. Appleton will be told not to publish "an hour before" Murray.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   [c. 7 August 1872]
letters.summary: Requests proofs ofExpression.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   [before 8 August 1872]
letters.summary:
So far VOK has lost money on his translation ofDescentbecause of pirate editions.

Agrees to share profits onExpression.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   8 August [1872]
letters.summary: Cannot understand the estimate of the Heliotype Company [for plates forExpression]. Discusses the original agreement as he understood it.

letters.title: To J. T. Gulick   8 August [1872]
letters.summary: Discusses a paper JTG wanted to read at a BAAS meeting.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   8 August [1872]
letters.summary: Wishes to come to Down to make arrangements for Russian translation ofExpression.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   9 August 1872
letters.summary: Agrees on price for supplying Appleton withExpressionelectrotypes and stereotypes. Difficulties with heliotypes [for illustrations ofExpression].

letters.title: To Francis Galton   9 August [1872]
letters.summary: "I telegraphed you this morning about the Rabbit. Our confounded carrier suddenly changed his mind & goes up to night, perhaps he will bring the rabbit tomorrow evening. If it does not then come I do not know how it had better be sent; if by Railway, I may not perhaps hear when it arrives at Orpington."

letters.title: To ?   9 August [1872 –4]
letters.summary: Will see that the error is corrected in the next reprint.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   10 August [1872]
letters.summary: CD suggests fair way for the Heliotype Company to charge for new negatives and copies of plates.

letters.title: To V. O. Kovalevsky   10 August [1872]
letters.summary: Sends proofs and details [concerning VOK’s Russian translation ofExpression(1872)].

letters.title: From Francis Galton   11 August 1872
letters.summary: The buck is well; Dr Carter has returned, and things will go better.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   [12–17 August 1872]
letters.summary:
CD cannot omit mention of Wilhelm Wundt’sThierseele[Vorlesungen über die Menschen und Thierseele(1863)] in his book.

Murray could control the number of copies of translation ofExpressionsold in Russia by the number of heliotypes he will supply.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   12 August [1872]
letters.summary: The carrier will call at University College on Thursday 15 August.

letters.title: To John Scott   12 August 1872
letters.summary:
Acknowledges a box of worm-casts from India and a bottle of worms in spirits. There is no memorandum.

His book on expression is finished and includes valuable information from JS.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   [after 12 August 1872]
letters.summary: VOK is marking the passages [in Wundt,Menschen und Thierseele(1863)] that may interest CD.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke to G. H. Darwin   13 August 1872
letters.summary: Explains the cost of heliotype plates [forExpression] and the consequent need to raise the price of the book.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [13 August 1872]
letters.summary: Discusses the price of some heliotype prints [forExpression?].

letters.title: From Charles Layton   13 August 1872
letters.summary: Is satisfied with CD’s arrangement with Murray for Appleton’s to pay $50 [pounds or dollars!?] for stereo plates and clichés of 21 woodblocks for CD’s new book [Expression, see8217]. Has ordered 5000 sets of plate impressions from Robert Cooke at Murray’s.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   [14 August 1872]
letters.summary: Is greatly relieved to hear that the estimate [of the Heliotype Company] was a mistake. Sends lettered copies of seven plates forExpression, and discusses payment to be made by foreign editors for copies of the plates.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   14 August 1872
letters.summary: Sends a set of plates [forExpression]. Price of the book must be 12s instead of 10s 6d, or 14s instead of 12s.

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   14 August 1872
letters.summary:
Hostility of birds toward others with same colour;

nuptial plumage.

Spiza cyaneaandSpiza ciris.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   15 August 1872
letters.summary: Arrangements for the plates forExpressionand charges to be made for them to foreign editors.

letters.title: From D. F. Tyler   15 August 1872
letters.summary:
Parallel quotations from Benjamin Franklin andDescentabout absorption of heat by different colours; applies to winter and summer plumage of birds.

Reasoning power in dogs.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   16 August 1872
letters.summary: Cost of plates [forExpression] is very high and will make "a terrible hole in the profits".

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   17 August 1872
letters.summary: Will inform all foreign publishers that John Murray will supply 1000 copies of heliotype plates [forExpression] for £75. CD would not have used so many photos had he foreseen the cost, but woodcuts would not have done.

letters.title: To V. O. Kovalevsky   17 August 1872
letters.summary: Cost of plates [forExpression] is greater than expected: £75 per 1000 copies.

letters.title: From K. M. Giuntsburg   20 August 1872
letters.summary: Sends a paper in which he has applied CD’s theory of natural selection to the explanation of the mortality rate of new-born infants ["Die Kindersterblickeit",J. Kinderkrankheiten(1872)].

letters.title: From Arthur Nicols   20 August 1872
letters.summary: Offers observations on expression in Australian dogs, since he knows CD plans to publish on the subject.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   21 August 1872
letters.summary: Has ordered printing of 2000 sets of illustrations [forExpression] for Murray’s and informed D. Appleton of price per thousand. Has answered letter from Eduard Koch [of Schweizerbart]. Has also arranged for index.

letters.title: From Anton Dohrn   21 August 1872
letters.summary:
