Has reported on the Naples Zoological Station to BAAS meeting at Brighton. Hopes to open it in January. Is at work building up the library by contributions from publishers and naturalists.

Deplores Wallace’s "drifting away" and his association with such men as H. C. Bastian.

Disbelieves in ascidians as our ancestors. Has a substitute he is sure will please CD.

letters.title: From Johan IJkema   21 August 1872
letters.summary: Wishes to have Dutch publication rights for a translation ofExpression.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [before 22 August 1872]
letters.summary: Sutton says monkeys often vomit, but cannot say whether they do it voluntarily.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   23 August 1872
letters.summary: CD has given translation right [forExpression] to Dutch publisher Joh. Ijkema.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   23 August 1872
letters.summary: Cost of impression of the heliotype plates [forExpression] is so high that he asks CD to consider having a set photographed onto wood and then engraved. Index [forExpression] is in hand.

letters.title: From Arthur Nicols   23 August 1872
letters.summary: Doubts reported cases of homing instinct in dogs.

letters.title: To Edward Vivian   23 August [1872]
letters.summary: Thanks for valuable information [about worms?]. "The more I investigate the extreme amount of work effected, the more perplexed as yet I become."

letters.title: From W. W. Baxter   [after 23 August 1872?]
letters.summary: Informs CD that he has forwarded some oils and opium.

letters.title: To Hubert Airy   24 August 1872
letters.summary: CD’s son Leonard of the Royal Engineers has applied to Sir George Biddell Airy to be an observer on the Venus Expedition. Leonard failed to mention his qualifications, which CD now relates with the request that HA draw them to his father’s attention.

letters.title: To Anton Dohrn   24 August [1872]
letters.summary:
Rejoices at success [of Naples Zoological Station]. Will send complete set of his books to the library.

If AD is interested, he will send a copy ofExpressionwhen it comes out.

Invites AD to visit Down.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   26 August 1872
letters.summary: Defers to CD and has ordered 2000 sets of impressions from heliotype plates [forExpression] for Murray’s and 3000 sets for Appleton. Also has directed printer to send Appleton a set of stereotype plates of the work and the woodcuts.

letters.title: From Anton Dohrn   28 August 1872
letters.summary: Will call on CD next year, when he will have worked out the embryology ofAmphioxus; he believes it is not primitive but a degenerate form of fish. He believes the true ancestors of vertebrates are annelids.

letters.title: From F. W. Harmer   28 August 1872
letters.summary: Has entered a newspaper controversy with W. P. Lyon [Homo versus Darwin(1872)] who ascribes to CD the saying "natural selection is a kind of god that never slumbers nor sleeps". FWH does not believe CD made this statement.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   28 August [1872]
letters.summary: Detailed response to reading of Bastian’sBeginnings of life[1872]. On the whole, it seems probable to CD that spontaneous generation is true.

letters.title: To F. W. Harmer   29 August 1872
letters.summary: Explains that William Penman Lyon has misquoted CD in Lyon [1871].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   29 August [1872]
letters.summary: Is now at work onDroseraand asks to borrowD. capensisand other species.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   29 August 1872
letters.summary:
Encloses letter and cheque [from John Scott].

Again in thick of Ayrton matter. Tyndall and Huxley have shown themselves equal to the occasion in grasp of subject, tenacity of purpose, independence, and good-will.

letters.title: From Chauncey Wright   29 August 1872
letters.summary: Discusses ideas on the development of language; agrees with CD that it is a process governed by unconscious selection; he considers it analogous to unconscious selection of domestic animals by savages. Remarks on the differing views of Max Müller and W. D. Whitney regarding the origin of language and its development. Comments on the extent to which unintentional effects can be ascribed directly to the agency of free intelligent wills.

letters.title: From Richard Harte   30 August 1872
letters.summary: Report about six-toed cats; trait persistent for three generations.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   30 August [1872]
letters.summary: Acknowledges receipt of cheque.

letters.title: To John Murray   30 August [1872]
letters.summary:
Asks JM to send copies of all his books to Anton Dohrn.

Koch [of Schweizerbart] requires 3000 sets of copies of the heliotype plates [for German edition ofExpression].

letters.title: To Williams and Norgate   30 August [1872]
letters.summary: Asks them to procure the two volumes ofLiving Cirripediafor Anton Dohrn’s zoological station in Naples.

letters.title: From F. W. Harmer   31 August 1872
letters.summary:
He became entrapped in the W. Lyon controversy by defending CD against Frederic Bateman of Norwich.

As a religious man, FWH wants to apologise for the attacks CD has suffered in the name of religion.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   31 August 1872
letters.summary:
Further reflections upon Bastian’s book [The beginnings of life(1872)].

ARW’s prospects for Directorship at Bethnal Green Museum.

letters.title: To Chauncey Wright   31 August [1872]
letters.summary:
CD thanks CW for long, interesting letter; hopes the ideas will be worked into an essay some day.

Suggests dates for a proposed visit and gives instructions for reaching Down.

letters.title: From ?   September 1872
letters.summary: On cats’ habit of leaving the room or house in which a corpse is lying.

letters.title: From A. G. Nathorst   [after August 1872]
letters.summary: Discusses the research for his paper on Arctic plant beds in the freshwater aquifers of Scania (Nathorst 1872).

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   2 September 1872
letters.summary:
Comments on EH’s criticism of authors in third edition ofNatürliche Schöpfungsgeschichte[1872].

Discusses book by H. C. Bastian [The beginnings of life(1872)].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   2 September 1872
letters.summary: Kew’sDrosera capensisis at CD’s service.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   [2 September 1872]
letters.summary: Huxley’s report of Bastian’s having watched the development of the scale ofSphagnum. The importance of studies of possible causes of heterogenesis.

letters.title: From Chauncey Wright   2 September 1872
letters.summary: Arranges to visit CD at Down.

letters.title: From John Murray   3 September [1872]
letters.summary: R. Cooke has increased the order for heliotypes [forExpression] to 8000. Reimburses CD for cost of artists.

letters.title: From N. Sobko   3 September 1872
letters.summary: Asks whether he may have the sheets ofExpressionto produce a Russian edition.

letters.title: To W. W. Baxter   4 September [1872?]
letters.summary: Orders some salts for plant experiments.

letters.title: To Ernest Edwards    4 September 1872
letters.summary: Testimonial letter stating how valuable CD found their advice and information.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   6 September [1872]
letters.summary: Studying palaeontology, as the British Museum is closed.

letters.title: To Chauncey Wright   6 September [1872]
letters.summary:
Recommends J. C. Houzeau’sÉtudes sur les facultés mentales des animaux[1872].

Was glad to make CW’s acquaintance.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   7 September 1872
letters.summary: Sends extract [from Carl Johan Andersson,Lake Ngami(1856)] on expression.

letters.title: From Chauncey Wright   9 September 1872
letters.summary: Discusses the mental powers and habits of animals and considers that those of man are not separated from those of animals by any sort of fundamental barrier; the gulf seems formidable only from a self-conscious, human point of view. Man’s important distinction is his greater ability to act and respond independently of external stimuli, in consequence of his internal accumulation of personal experience.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   10 September 1872
letters.summary:
Alexander [Kovalevsky] is intent on assisting Russian publication ofExpression. Sends estimates of costs and profits. At 7s 6d per copy a net profit of £150–200 is expected.

Wilhelm Wundt [Menschen und Thierseele(1863)] probably of no use.

letters.title: To the Linnean Society   12 September 1872
letters.summary: Instructions for forwarding a parcel and outstanding issues ofTransactionsdue him.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   12 September [1872]
letters.summary: Beginning work on his African travels [The African sketch-book(1873)].

letters.title: From C. L. Sutherland   12 September 1872
letters.summary: Sends CD a book on mule breeding in Poitou [Eugène Ayrault,De l’industrie mulassière en Poitou(1867)].

letters.title: To the Linnean Society   [after 12] September 1872
letters.summary: Note authorising James West to collectTransactionson CD’s behalf.

letters.title: From C.-F. Reinwald   13 September 1872
letters.summary:
J. J. Moulinié is ill in Geneva, but translations ofOriginandDescentprogress.

Will undertake to publish translation ofExpression.

letters.title: To W. W. Baxter   17 September [1872?]
letters.summary: Orders sulphuric ether, nitric ether, chloroform, and prussic acid [forDroseraexperiments? SeeInsectivorous plants, pp. 209, 219].

letters.title: From C.-F. Reinwald   17 September 1872
letters.summary:
J. J. Moulinié’s mental faculties are much weakened.

FortunatelyDescentandOriginare completely translated except the indexes.

A new translator will be needed forExpression.

letters.title: From H. A. Head   18 September 1872
letters.summary: Impressions of Duluth and the natural history of its environs.

letters.title: To V. O. Kovalevsky   18 September [1872]
letters.summary: CD sends schedule for VOK’s visit to Down.

letters.title: From Hubert Airy   20 September 1872
letters.summary: Disputes Thomas Meehan’s observations on the hardiness of exposed buds, and believes bud-scales are for the protection of the bud-leaves. Reiterates his opinion that the phyllotaxy of a plant is determined by causes acting when the leaves are crowded into close contact. Attempts to explain how a different phyllotaxy on the upper and lower parts of the same shoot could have arisen.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   20 September [1872]
letters.summary: His visit to Down.

letters.title: From William Cooper   21 September 1872
letters.summary: Requests financial support for horticultural researches, which, he promises, will enormously increase yields.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   23 September 1872
letters.summary:
Thanks JVC for hisHistory of zoology[Geschichte der Zoologie bis auf Joh. Müller und Charl. Darwin(1872)]. Considers the title one of the greatest honours ever paid him.

Reports on foreign orders for the heliotype plates ofExpression.

letters.title: To J. J. Moulinié   23 September 1872
letters.summary: States his reasons for authorising JJM to translate theOrigin.

letters.title: From Hubert Airy   24 September 1872
letters.summary:
Thanks for letter, in which CD cited [Anton] Kerner’s alpine observations.

Describes with diagrams the curious disposition of leaves on someAcaciatwigs, and points out that his theory should account for these anomalies as well as normal cases.

letters.title: To V. O. Kovalevsky   24 September [1872]
letters.summary:
Sends proof-sheets [ofExpression].

Is unwell and must stop work and leave home for a time.

letters.title: From John Scott   25 September 1872
letters.summary:
Acting as Superintendent of Royal Botanic Garden, Calcutta.

Observations on worm-castings in India.

letters.title: From C.-F. Reinwald   26 September 1872
letters.summary: Printing and translation ofExpression.

letters.title: To Henri de Lacaze-Duthiers   28 September 1872
letters.summary:
Thanks HdeL-D for two papers on Ascidians [by A. Giard inArch. Zool.1 (1872): 233–88; 397–428].

Some of the expressions in HdeL-D’s paper ["Direction des études zoologiques",Arch. Zool.1 (1872): 1–64] made CD think he accepted the principle of evolution.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   2 October 1872
letters.summary: Has learned that German edition [ofExpression] will be on larger pages than English one. No copies of heliotype plates [forExpression] have been delivered. Hopes Heliotype Company is not going to throw them over. Suggests CD write a strong letter.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   3 October 1872
letters.summary: Arrangements for foreign editions [ofExpression]. Delay by Heliotype Company is provoking.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   4 October 1872
letters.summary: Heliotype Company assures RC all 8000 sets of the plates [forExpression] will be ready next week.

letters.title: To George Harris   4 October [1872]
letters.summary: Thanks GH for hisTheory of the ants[1869] and offers to supply any zoological information that he can.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   4 October [1872]
letters.summary:
Is sendingDroseraback

and "the curious Kerguelen book".

"Drosera has almost been the death of me."

Hopes the accursed man [Ayrton] does not give JDH any more trouble.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   6 October 1872
letters.summary:
Discusses the coiling of tendrils of climbing plants.

AG’s recent tour of the U. S.

letters.title: From J. T. Moggridge   6 October 1872
letters.summary: He will send his book [Harvesting ants and trap-door spiders(1873)]. Describes two new types of trap-door spider nests.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   7 October 1872
letters.summary:
Has translated half ofExpression; is delighted with it. Comments on some points that he questions.

Is at work on concluding part of his handbook of zoology [Handbuch der Zoologie, 2 vols. (1863–75), with A. Gerstaecker].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   7 October 1872
letters.summary:
Miscellaneous personal matters.

What does CD think of Robert Mallet’s earthquake theory? Would it not account for strata dipping at base of range of mountains?

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   9 October 1872
letters.summary: Expressionis now almost ready. The plates will require great care in the binding.

letters.title: To J. T. Moggridge   9 October [1872]
letters.summary: Discusses JTM’s research on habits of insects. "How incomparably more valuable are such researches than the mere description of a thousand species."

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   10 October [1872]
letters.summary: Will consider JVC’s comments onExpressionwhen he prepares a new edition.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   10 October [1872]
letters.summary:
Is much vexed aboutDrosera.

Land-level changes and volcanic activity.

letters.title: To Alpheus Hyatt   10 October [1872]
letters.summary:
Thanks for "Embryology of the fossil cephalopods", [Bull. Mus. Comp. Zool. Harvard3 (1872–4): 59–112].

Regrets error in attributing acceleration concept to E. D. Cope instead of to AH in last edition ofOrigin, and misrepresentation of their joint view.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   11 October 1872
letters.summary: Corrects CD’s spelling of the name of a statue: the Arrotino (spelled "Arretino" by CD) [seeExpression, p. 184, on grief-muscles].

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   11 October 1872
letters.summary: D. Appleton has been sent 3000 sets of plates [forExpression]. Hopes to publish [Expression] on 12 Nov.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   [after 11 October 1872]
letters.summary: Discusses printing ofExpression.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   12 October 1872
letters.summary:
Much experiment and observation needed before spontaneous generation will be empirically advanced, but philosophically the matter is clear.

Thinks Ludwig Rütimeyer has attacked EH to satisfy pious opinion in Basel.

Will soon be finished with his monographDie Kalkschwämme[1872].

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   13 October [1872]
letters.summary:
THF’s article inNature["The fertilisation of a few papilionaceous flowers", 6 (1872): 478–80, 498–501] is extremely good.

Suspects he now has answer to why common peas and sweetpeas hardly ever intercross, a point which half drove CD mad for years.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   14 October [1872]
letters.summary: Huxley will be asked to reviewExpressioninPall Mall Gazette.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   15 October [1872]
letters.summary: Thanks JVC for correcting his blunder on spelling of "Arrotino" [seeExpression, p. 184]. "No Frenchman has a greater tendency to spell all proper names wrongly than I have."

letters.title: From William Marshall   15 October 1872
letters.summary:
WM converted to belief in evolution by experience of museum work.

Describes protective coloration of coots’ eggs.

letters.title: To H. A. Huxley   16 October [1872]
letters.summary: Wants to make a present to her on the move to a new house.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   17 October 1872
letters.summary:
Suggests possible experiments withPisumandLathyrus.

Has read the article CD spoke of; the doctrine of inherited mental and corporeal qualities is most fertile.

letters.title: From H. A. Huxley and T. H. Huxley   17 October 1872
letters.summary: Appreciation of the "marriage gift"; their affection for CD.

letters.title: To Emil Lehmann   18 October [1872]
letters.summary: CD would have been honoured to have EL translate forthcoming work [Expression], but J. V. Carus is already half way through this task.

letters.title: From C. I. F. Major   18 October 1872
letters.summary:
Asks permission to translateExpressioninto German. Will superintend an Italian translation.

Informs CD of hornless fossilBos etruscusand Miocene fossils of genusSus[seeDescent, 2d ed., pp. 505, 521].

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   20 October [1872]
letters.summary:
Remarks about an enclosed specimen,

and extract of letter from W. A. L. Marshall [8560].

ARW’s good review of J. C. Houzeau de Lehaie [Études sur les facultés mentales des animaux, inNature6 (1872): 469–71].

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   22 October 1872
letters.summary: Presentation copies [ofExpression] will be ready in a week. Has ordered only 250 copies to have cut edges because trade prefers uncut pages.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   22 October 1872
letters.summary:
Spiralling of tendrils.

Has worked hard onDrosera.

Is interested in tracing the "nerves" ofDionaeawhich follow the vascular bundles. Finds he can paralyse half of the leaf by pricking it at a certain point.

Wishes AG to carry out two experiments onD. filiformis.

Has received AG’s Dubuque address [Am. J. Sci.3d ser. 4 (1872): 282–98].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   22 October [1872]
letters.summary: Condolences on death of JDH’s mother.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   22 October [1872]
letters.summary: Supports the abolition of prize fellowships at the universities.

letters.title: From C.-F. Reinwald   22 October 1872
letters.summary:
Samuel Pozzi has been proposed by C. Martin and Paul Broca as translator ofExpression.

First volume ofDescenthas sold 1200 copies.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   23 October [1872]
letters.summary: Discusses presentation copies ofExpression.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   24 October 1872
letters.summary:
Doubts accuracy of Bible translations quoted by CD as evidence that Semitic races blush.

Questions his note on derivation of words like "ugly", "huge", etc.

Lists some mistakes and misprints.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   24 October [1872]
letters.summary:
Asks for London address of George King [Superintendent of Royal Botanic Garden, Calcutta], so he can ask about worm-castings sent by King from S. India. Has just received a splendid letter from John Scott on worms.

Asks where he can buyDionaea.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   [25 October 1872]
letters.summary: Comments on discussions with C. Reinwald concerning French edition ofExpression.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   25 October 1872
letters.summary:
Murray’s will allow CD 18 copies [ofExpression].

All foreign publishers, except Dutch, have paid for the plates.

letters.title: From W. D. Fox   25 October [1872]
letters.summary: Has not seen CD for about 25 years. Has heard an absurd story that CD and Emma are exploring an unknown part of America.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   26 October 1872
letters.summary: Does not understand Reinwald [French publisher ofExpression], who apparently intends an edition of only 500 copies. Sends first copy to CD.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   26 October 1872
letters.summary:
Has initiated inquiries aboutDionaea.

Sends George King’s address.

letters.title: To John Scott   26 October 1872
letters.summary:
Acknowledges JS’s excellent letter of 25 September. May CD assume that the gigantic worm-casts were nearly circular when measured before the rain?

That a medical man should always have the place of superintendent seems a piece of jobbery.

Mentions [George] King.

JS’s thin paper renders some words on other side almost illegible.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   27 October [1872]
letters.summary: Thanks JVC for his criticisms and corrections ofExpression. Asks him to alter his translation accordingly.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   27 October [1872]
letters.summary: Discusses distribution of presentation copies ofExpression. Sends instructions for mailing his copies. Discusses negotiations with C. Reinwald concerning French edition. Suggests journals to receive review copies.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   27 October [1872]
letters.summary:
Asks for address of a Mrs Barber somewhere in South Africa.

JDH’s letter inNature[6 (1872): 516–17] is excellent, and wonderfully quiet.

Severely criticises Owen’s conduct.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   27 October [1872]
letters.summary: Requests the address of F. F. Geach so that he may send him his book [Expression].

letters.title: To George King   28 October 1872
letters.summary: Asks to see notes on Indian worm-castings.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   29 October [1872]
letters.summary:
Has finishedExpression.

His strength fails more and more; needs to rest every six weeks or so.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   29 October 1872
letters.summary:
Sends Mrs Barber’s address.

Gratified that CD hates Owen. Hopes Owen will not answerNatureletter and draw JDH into controversy. Owen’s letter was not intended for Ayrton to use. Its appearance must have horrified him.

State of Huxley’s health makes JDH uneasy.

Willy is in a stockbroker’s office in London and likes it.

letters.title: To G. H. Kinahan and M. H. Close   29 October 1872
letters.summary: Much obliged for GHK and MHC’sGeneral glaciation[of Iar-Connaught(1872)].

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   31 October 1872
letters.summary: JVC questions accuracy of Hensleigh Wedgwood’s statement that the word for a toad in all European languages expresses the habit of swelling [seeExpression, p. 104]. Has changed "all" to "some".

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   31 October [1872]
letters.summary:
Dionaeaplants have arrived. Just ready to observe some points in their structure.

Has Murray sentExpressionbook?

JDH’s particulars about Owen, Ayrton and Co. ("a nice firm") amused CD much.

letters.title: From Alpheus Hyatt   [late] November 1872
letters.summary:
No need to apologise for not quoting AH’s paper on acceleration and retardation.

Agassiz introduced AH to ammonites and entrusted collection to him. Has followed developmental history of each species and placed them within geological formations. Found evolutionary history of species recapitulated only to a degree in individual development. Stages frequently skipped. Explains why young of later animals are like adults that preceded them. Retardation entirely idea of Edward Drinker Cope. Sends paper to explain it. Acceleration can explain degraded forms. Often like youthful stage with which series began. Often resemble old age of earlier series. Regularity of these series incompatible with natural selection. How can selection account for degraded final stages or for predictability of development? Franz Hilgendorf’s Paludinae from Steinheim lake show same parallelism in development. May be possible to reconcile this with selection. But Trochiformis begins to show degradation in beds where it is most numerous and has largest individuals, i.e., where selection seems to be favouring it. Will work on Steinheim shells this winter.

letters.title: To George King   November 1872
letters.summary: Obliged for letter on worm-castings. Asks GK to observe them in southern Europe.

letters.title: To S. H. Haliburton   1 November [1872]
letters.deprecated: Sarah Harriet (Sarah Harriet Williams) (Sarah Harriet Mostyn Owen) Haliburton
letters.recipient: Sarah Harriet (Sarah Harriet Williams) (Sarah Harriet Mostyn Owen) Haliburton
letters.summary:
Sends a copy ofExpression

and speaks fondly of his memories of Woodhouse and the Owen family.

letters.title: To Amy Ruck   [1 November 1872]
letters.summary: Sends a copy ofExpressionand his autograph.

letters.title: To Alphonse de Candolle   2 November [1872]
letters.summary:
Thanks for AdeC’sHistoire des sciences[1873].

Sends a copy ofExpression.

His health keeps him weak; he dreads grappling with the fearful subject of variation [in nature]

so he is working up some observations in botanical physiology to publish with his old papers on climbing plants.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [3 November 1872]
letters.summary: Is delighted to receive expression. Some comments on swallowing and scratching. Asks to be sent reviews.

letters.title: From S. H. Haliburton   3 November [1872]
letters.deprecated: Sarah Harriet (Sarah Harriet Williams) (Sarah Harriet Mostyn Owen) Haliburton
letters.sender: Sarah Harriet (Sarah Harriet Williams) (Sarah Harriet Mostyn Owen) Haliburton
letters.summary:
Thanks for copy ofExpression.

Reminiscences of their youth.

letters.title: From L. H. Jeitteles   3 November 1872
letters.summary: Sends CD a copy of the second part of his paper on the remains and antiquities of Olmütz in Moravia.

letters.title: From J. S. Craig   4 November 1872
letters.summary: A number of students wish to nominate CD as Lord Rector of the University of Aberdeen and JSC inquires whether CD’s state of health would prevent his standing as a candidate.

letters.title: From Auguste Houzeau de Lehaie   4 November 1872
letters.deprecated: Charles Auguste Benjamin Hippolyte (Auguste) Houzeau de Lehaie
letters.sender: Charles Auguste Benjamin Hippolyte (Auguste) Houzeau de Lehaie
letters.summary: Has receivedExpressionand will forward it to his brother [Jean-Charles Houzeau de Lehaie].

letters.title: From M. T. Masters   4 November 1872
letters.summary: Asks CD’s opinion of John Denny’s idea that males have prepotent transmission power in plants. A. J. F. Wegmann says the females are prepotent.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   5 November 1872
letters.summary: Observations on expression: women gnash teeth when sexually excited. W. Africans do not kiss.

letters.title: To S. H. Haliburton   6 November [1872]
letters.deprecated: Sarah Harriet (Sarah Harriet Williams) (Sarah Harriet Mostyn Owen) Haliburton
letters.recipient: Sarah Harriet (Sarah Harriet Williams) (Sarah Harriet Mostyn Owen) Haliburton
letters.summary: Thanks SH for news of her family. Would like her to visit Down in the spring.

letters.title: From Henry Holland   6 November [1872]
letters.summary: Has finished readingDescentand sends some comments [missing].

letters.title: From Henry Maudsley   6 November 1872
letters.summary: Thanks forExpression.

letters.title: From John Murray   6 November [1872]
letters.summary: Is convinced that 2000 more copies [ofExpression] must be printed without delay in order to meet demand. He therefore asks CD to send his corrections to the printer at once.

letters.title: To J. S. Craig   7 November 1872
letters.summary: Cannot accept honour of nomination as Lord Rector [of Aberdeen University].

letters.title: From Francis Galton   7 November 1872
letters.summary: Sends thanks forExpression; offers some additions, and will send printed queries abroad if CD wishes.

letters.title: To L. H. Jeitteles   7 November 1872
letters.summary: Thanks LHJ for a memoir [about remains and antiquities of Olmütz in Moravia].

letters.title: To John Murray   7 November [1872]
letters.summary:
Has sent off a few trifling errata [ofExpression] to Mr Clowes. Asks about the heliotypes.

Would like to hear about the sale of his books. [See8616.]

letters.title: To W. W. Baxter?   8 November [1872–4]
letters.summary: Orders enema.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   8 November [1872]
letters.summary:
Rabbits’ coats true in character. If the next ones are true, it is superfluous to keep trying.

Does not know why crying children rub eyes with knuckles.

Mentions FG’s article on prayer ["Statistical inquiries into the efficacy of prayer",Fortn. Rev.n.s. 12 (1872): 125–35].

letters.title: From S. H. Haliburton   8 November [1872]
letters.deprecated: Sarah Harriet (Sarah Harriet Williams) (Sarah Harriet Mostyn Owen) Haliburton
letters.sender: Sarah Harriet (Sarah Harriet Williams) (Sarah Harriet Mostyn Owen) Haliburton
letters.summary: Thanks for CD’s photograph, which recalls the Charles Darwin of olden days.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   8 November 1872
letters.summary:
Has been asked to take shares in the Artizans’ Dwellings Co., in which CD is a shareholder. If it is really a project for public good, he would be glad to be associated.

Owen has answered his letter inNature[7 (1872): 5–7].

A letter from Tyndall [from America] was read at the X Club.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   8 November 1872
letters.summary: Writes, as a P.S. to his previous letter, stating his friends have advised him not to answer Owen’s attack.

letters.title: From R. H. Blair   9 November 1872
letters.summary:
Thanks for copy [ofExpression].

Has now read Charles Bell’s book [Anatomy and philosophy of expression, 3d ed. (1844)].

Reports instance of person, blind from birth, frowning, when supposedly the blind cannot control the muscle required.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   9 November [1872]
letters.summary:
Pros and cons of answering Owen’s letter.

On Artizans’ Dwellings, he approves the object but it is lost money as an investment.

letters.title: From John Murray   9 November 1872
letters.summary: The reception ofExpressionhas exceeded even JM’s expectations; 5267 copies were sold at the annual sale. CD’s modesty about the work had misled him about its probable sale.

letters.title: To A. C. Ramsay   9 November [1872]
letters.summary: Thanks for 3rd edition of ACR’sPhysical geology and geography of Great Britain(A. C. Ramsay 1872).

letters.title: To W. W. Baxter?   10 November [1872–4]
letters.summary: Would greatly prefer an enema with a shorter nozzle but with a somewhat larger diameter.

letters.title: From Federico Delpino   10 November 1872
letters.summary: Going on circumnavigation voyage aboard theGaribaldi.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   11 November [1872]
letters.summary:
Reports on very successful sale ofExpressionin England. Suggests German publisher keep the type set up in case more than the expected 3000 copies are needed.

Has begun work on some old botanical observations [ofDroseraforInsectivorous plants].

letters.title: From George Cupples   11 November 1872
letters.summary: Praise forExpression.

letters.title: To John Murray   11 November 1872
letters.summary:
CD is delighted and astonished at sale ofExpression,

and pleased with sale of others, exceptDescent. He fears a new edition of that work may never be required. Would have liked to bring out a thoroughly revised one.

letters.title: From John Murray   12 November [1872]
letters.summary:
Price ofExpressionis 12s.

Sends cheque to pay CD his share of profits onOrigin[6th ed.].

letters.title: From Anton Dohrn   13 November 1872
letters.summary:
Is amazed atExpression. Like CD’s former works, it contains the material and principles of a new science.

The Zoological Station is making good progress – now has a fine building. Hopes for a stable income from contributions of various governments.

letters.title: To John Murray   13 November 1872
letters.summary:
Thanks JM for £210 on last reprint ofOrigin[6th ed.]. Pleased by its sale

and by the success ofExpression.

letters.title: From Albert Günther   14 November 1872
letters.summary: Many thanks forExpression. AG relates some relevant observations, the significance of which had previously escaped him.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   15 November 1872
letters.summary: Agrees the rabbit experiment has gone on long enough, but would like one more litter.

letters.title: From Jules Michelet   15 November 1872
letters.summary: Darwin and his followers have connected France and England like the projected tunnel and have demonstrated that the French and English are more free than Germany from scholasticism.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   15 November 1872
letters.summary: Appreciation [ofExpression]. ARW will review it inQuarterly Journal of Science[n.s. 3 (1873): 113–18].

letters.title: From William Bowman   16 November 1872
letters.summary:
Thanks CD forExpression, comments on it.

Describes celebration of F. C. Donders’ 25th year as professor at Utrecht.

letters.title: From Henry MacKay   16 November 1872
letters.summary: Has just readOriginandDescentand wants to know: 1. Has man a soul? 2. Is man morally responsible "to his creative cause or force"? 3. Is there any form of after-life?

letters.title: From Athénaïs Michelet   16 November 1872
letters.summary: The Michelets are ill and dispirited.

letters.title: From Herbert Spencer   16 November 1872
letters.summary: Thanks CD forExpression. Disagrees with his views on the genesis of melody; HS gives some reasons for believing it to originate in the natural cadences of emotional speech.

letters.title: From W. D. Crotch   17 November 1872
letters.summary:
Horns of female reindeer disappear after their calves are dropped [seeDescent, 2d ed., p. 503].

Lemmings in Norway.

letters.title: From C. I. F. Major   17 November 1872
letters.summary: Agrees to translateExpressioninto Italian.

letters.title: From D. T. Smith   19 November 1872
letters.summary:
Has sent printed reports on his lectures relating to the descent of man [missing].

Discusses his theories on heredity and on the "soul" as the governor of mental and physical development.

letters.title: To D. T. Smith   [after 19 November 1872]
letters.summary: Thanks forLouisville Courier Journal.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   20 November 1872
letters.summary: Quandary caused by Heliotype Company’s failure to deliver enough plates forExpressionbecause of a strike. Murray’s now has 7000 books and only 3000 sets of plates.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   20 November [1872]
letters.summary: Discusses production of plates [forExpression].

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   20 November [1872]
letters.summary:
Encloses a letter from Lady Bell, which should be burnt when read.

Discusses finances.

letters.title: To J. M. Herbert   21 November 1872
letters.summary:
SendsExpression.

Remarks on student days and old friends.

letters.title: From A. W. Bennett   22 November 1872
letters.summary: Proposes establishing a quarterly journal for longer, illustrated articles of some popular appeal. Seeks CD’s support.

letters.title: From Briton Riviere   22 November 1872
letters.summary: Thanks forExpression.

letters.title: To Albert Günther   23 November 1872
letters.summary: Thanks AG forPopular Science Reviewcontaining his article [onCeratodus, 11 (1872): 257–66]. CD had already read it with great interest.

letters.title: From J. M. Herbert   23 November 1872
letters.summary: Thanks for copy ofExpression.

letters.title: From C.-F. Reinwald   23 November 1872
letters.summary: J. J. Moulinié’s translations ofDescentandOriginrequired much reworking, which accounts for delays.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   25 November 1872
letters.summary: Murray’s must publish [Expression] tomorrow with only 4000 copies, because plates for 3000 additional copies have not yet been delivered. The trade and public will be dissatisfied. It may be advisable to get police to defend the house.

letters.title: From J. T. Rothrock   25 November 1872
letters.summary:
Thanks forExpression, which he received through Asa Gray.

Relates some personal experiences of unconscious sympathy.

letters.title: From F. P. Cobbe   [26 November 1872]
letters.summary:
Acknowledges presentation copy [ofExpression], which is not to be found in the market.

Interested in CD’s opinion of her article ["The consciousness of dogs",Q. Rev.133 (1872): 419–51].

Hopes she may see CD at Queen Anne St [home of E. A. Darwin].

letters.title: From William Main   26 November 1872
letters.summary: Has read a review ofExpressionand finds CD’s explanation of "antithesis" [seeExpression, p. 50] unsatisfactory. Proposes a theory of upward lines expressing energy and downward lines expressing the reverse.

letters.title: From R. Lydekker  [after 26 November 1872–1882]
letters.summary: Lydekker describes an inherited characteristic of drooping eyelids.

letters.title: From Isaac Markens   27 November 1872
letters.summary: Asks for an autographed copy ofExpression.

letters.title: To Wilhelm Spengel   27 November [1872 or 1873]
letters.summary: Thanks for WS’s updatings to his Darwinian bibliography and regrets he is a poor German scholar.

letters.title: To F. P. Cobbe   28 November 1872
letters.summary:
FPC’s article on consciousness of dogs is best analysis of an animal’s mind CD has read.

Regrets she quotes [Edward?] Jesse.

Since writingDescent, CD has come to believe dogs have a conscience.

letters.title: From F. P. Cobbe   28 November [1872]
letters.summary: More stories about dog behaviour.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   28 November 1872
letters.summary:
Is reading W. R. Greg’sEnigmas of life[1872]: "One of the most eloquent books I ever read".

Owen’s communications are doing incalculable mischief to science in the eyes of Government officials. "This ignorant, careless, unobservant government."

TheNatureeditors, J. N. Lockyer and Bennett, blame each other for printing Owen’s letter.

Huxley looks wretched.

letters.title: To William Main   29 November [1872]
letters.summary: Thanks WM for his letter. CD does not think WM’s principle of [up-tending and down-tending] lines explains the cases of expression of emotions referred to, and, even if it did, the problem would remain as to why the lines should express what WM believes they do.

letters.title: From M. I. Snow   29 [November 1872 or later]
letters.summary: Describes her experiences of blushing on her hands.

letters.title: To W. W. Baxter   2 [December 1872]
letters.summary: Asks about possible animal substances in samples ofBelladonnaandDigitalis.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   2 December 1872
letters.summary:
CD’s finding the nervous system ofDionaeais wonderful.

Coiling of tendrils of climbing plants.

Thanks CD for the new book [Expression].

letters.title: From Hubert Airy   3 December 1872
letters.summary:
Discusses works lent him by CD: Candolle, Kerner, Braun, Sachs, and CD’s own notes on relative positions of leaves. Plans paper on subject for Royal Society.

Just appointed medical inspector under local government board.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   3 [December 1872]
letters.summary: JDH Should do as he sees fit about proposing him [John Scott] [for fellowship of the Linnean Society].

letters.title: From Frédéric Baudry   4 December 1872
letters.summary:
Sends anecdotes relating toExpression;

criticises CD’s use of Hensleigh Wedgwood’s views on language.

Complains about J. J. Moulinié’s translation ofDescent.

letters.title: From W. W. Baxter   4 December 1872
letters.summary: Sends CD description of preparation of extract of belladonna.

letters.title: To Alpheus Hyatt   4 December [1872]
letters.summary:
If decapod does not pass through zoea stage, is this acceleration? If hypothetical adult retained zoea characters, would this be retardation? Believes obliteration of growth stages frequently due to natural selection. Most interesting points in AH’s letter deal with senile characters. CD attributes them to laws of growth not selection. Explains degraded characters as result of readaptation to simpler conditions. Believes no innate tendency to progressive development exists.

Hopes AH visits F. Hilgendorf’s famous deposit [at Steinheim]. A. Weismann [Einfluss der Isolierung(1872)] makes good use of Hilgendorf’s observations.

letters.title: From F. A. Nussbaumer and Rudolf Hoernes   4 December 1872
letters.summary: Thanks for copies of CD’s works.

letters.title: To W. W. Baxter   [after 4 December 1872]
letters.summary: Thanks for information about the Atropia.

letters.title: From Mr Topham   5 December 1872
letters.summary: Suggests that Shakespeare meant the blush was unseen, not absent.

letters.title: To ?   5 December 1872
letters.summary: Obliged for the note of reference, but does not know what to think of the statement about the watering mouth.

letters.title: To ? 5 December 1872
letters.summary: Thanks for gift of a book, and offers to send copy ofExpression.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   6 December 1872
letters.summary: First edition ofExpressionnearly exhausted. Asks CD to send corrections to the printer for another issue, Murray thinks, of 2000.

letters.title: To F. J. Furnivall   6 December [1872–3]
letters.summary: Formally declines the vice-presidency of a proposed society.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   7 December [1872]
letters.summary: Comments on additional printing ofExpression. Complains about poor quality of plates.

letters.title: To C. J. Maynard   7 December [1872–3]
letters.summary: CD sends a better photo for CJM.

letters.title: From Alpheus Hyatt   8 December 1872
letters.summary: Discusses his theory of acceleration and retardation of development.

letters.title: From Alexander Agassiz   9 December 1872
letters.summary:
Thanks forExpression.

Has lost a year’s work in the fire that has devastated Boston.

letters.title: From A. J. Munby   9 December 1872
letters.summary: Gives a graphic description of a woman being terrified by mistaking him for a ghost in an old house.

letters.title: To ?   9 December 1872
letters.summary: Thanks an unidentifiable natural history society for electing him an honorary member.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   10 December 1872
letters.summary: Asks whether CD has any changes to make in a new German edition ofVariation, which is to be published next year.

letters.title: To C. L. Dodgson   10 December 1872
letters.summary: Thanks for offer of photograph.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   10 December 1872
letters.summary:
Thanks CD forExpression.

Describes work onDie Kalkschwämmeand its principal conclusions.

The application of biogenetic law.

Notes variability among calcareous sponges.

Gastrula-like "Gastraea" as ancestor of multicellular animals.

Posits homology betweenHydra,Olynthusof calcareous sponges, and initial germ layers of higher animals.

Comments on Lubbock’sPrehistoric times[1865]

and on David Strauss’sDer alte und der neue Glaube[1872].

letters.title: To John Topham 10 December 1872
letters.summary: Thanks JT for his information and hopes to attend to it in any future edition.

letters.title: To Alphonse de Candolle   11 December 1872
letters.summary:
Thanks AdeC for great pleasure his new book [Histoire des sciences(1873)] has given him. Comments on several of the essays.

When AdeC backs up Asa Gray in saying all instincts are congenital habits, CD must protest.

Asks several questions about butterflies of the Alps discussed on p. 322 [ofHistoire].

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   11 December [1872]
letters.summary: Thinks Mr Salt has not understood about their wills and wants to clarify the matter when he has heard from CD.

letters.title: To Henri de Lacaze-Duthiers   11 December 1872
letters.summary: Thanks HdeL-D for his photograph and encloses one of himself.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   12 December [1872]
letters.summary:
Has not strength nor time to alter and improveVariation.

First English edition ofExpressionnow at 9000 copies.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   13 December [1872]
letters.summary: Hopes to have a visit to discuss proportions to be left to the children under their wills; thinks 5/6 to the boys, 1/6 to the girls who "will have as much as is good for them".

letters.title: From Mary Treat   13 December 1872
letters.summary:
Drosera filiformiscaptures only small insects [but see8989].

Writes of her experiments with butterflies.

CD’s theory steadily gains ground in the U. S., despite Agassiz.

letters.title: From James Dickson   14 December 1872
letters.summary: Sends CD the case of a man he knew who could reject food voluntarily, in substantiation of the passage inExpression[p. 259] in which CD says "the suspicion arises that our progenitors must formerly have had [this] power".

letters.title: To C. L. Dodgson   14 December [1872]
letters.summary:
His thanks for the excellent photograph. [See8668.]

He is no longer working on expression but appreciates the obliging offer.

letters.title: To Alpheus Hyatt   14 December [1872]
letters.summary:
Sends copy of last edition ofOrigin.

Respecting AH’s theory that acceleration of growth produces new characters, urges AH to examine decapods that do and do not pass through zoea stage. Believes there are no marked differences between them.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   14 December [1872?]
letters.summary: Will be in London for a week. Invites ARW to lunch.

letters.title: From Julius Althaus   16 December 1872
letters.summary: In his admirable work on expression CD has left out influence of fifth pair of cerebral nerves on the portiodura and on physiognomy; sends reference to his paper on this subject ["On certain points in the physiology and pathology of the fifth pair of cerebral nerves",Med.-Chir. Trans.52 (1869): 27–42].

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   [17] December [1872]
letters.summary: Plans to see THH in London.

letters.title: From Julius Herschel   17 December 1872
letters.summary:
Report of yellow fever among Brazilian monkeys probably untrue; his correspondent is only a journalist.

Encloses letter about monkeys allegedly dying from yellow fever.

letters.title: From Dora Roberts   17 December [1872 or later]
letters.summary: Describes a case of maternal instinct, in which a hen protected kittens.

letters.title: From A. Smither   19 December 1872
letters.summary: Considers that the erection of hair and feathers in fear may serve a real defensive purpose, which he details.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   20 December 1872
letters.summary:
Comments on EH’s forthcoming [Die Kalkschwämme(1872)].

Thinks EH is working much too hard.

letters.title: From S. J. Housley   20 December 1872
letters.summary: Describes the pointed right ear of his son.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   20 December 1872
letters.summary: Personal affairs – the move to Marlborough Place.

letters.title: To F. C. Donders   21 December 1872
letters.summary:
Mentions publication ofExpression.

Asks whether children born blind ever frown, shed tears, or contract orbicular muscles.

Congratulates FCD on his anniversary [as Professor at Utrecht].

letters.title: To William Bowman   [after 21 December 1872]
letters.summary: Exceptional cases of frowning by children born blind have been reported to CD by R. H. Blair [see8615]; CD asks WB for information and observations on the use of the muscles around the eye by those blind from birth.

letters.title: To D. H. Tuke   22 December 1872
letters.summary: Comments on DHT’sInfluence of the mind upon the body[1872].

letters.title: From H. Henry   23 December 1872
letters.summary: Comments onExpression.

letters.title: From Paolo Mantegazza   23 December 1872
letters.summary:
Ecstatic praise of CD andExpression, which has transformed physiognomy.

Sends his papers on sadness ["Dell’azione del dolore",Gaz. Med. Ital. Lombarda(1866, 1867)]. Sends some observations on physiognomy.

letters.title: From M. D. Conway   24 December 1872
letters.summary: Introduces himself as an acquaintance of E. A. Darwin. Offers miscellaneous observations on human expression.

letters.title: From F. C. Donders   24 December 1872
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for copy ofExpression.

Agrees to observe expression in children born blind.

letters.title: From F. P. Cobbe   25 December [1872]
letters.summary: Sends story of a dog’s suicide.

letters.title: To Paolo Mantegazza   28 December 1872
letters.summary:
Thanks for the letter commendingExpression[see8692]. CD "was not at all sure the work was worth publishing".

Acknowledges receipt of some pamphlets from PM, which his wife will translate.

Regretfully must refuse PM’s offer to translateExpressionsince it has been promised to another.

Has now received PM’sPhysiology of pleasure[Fisiologia del piacere(1870)].

letters.title: To Francis Galton   30 December [1872]
letters.summary: F. M. Balfour wants to experiment on Pangenesis. Asks FG to recommend coloured rabbits that breed true.

letters.title: From Gerard Krefft   30 December 1872
letters.summary:
Has read CD’s latest book and will make observations for CD.

Reports on a monkey that throws things when "angry".

Explains how natives count to more than four; CD incorrect on this point.

Sends photographs of blacks.

Cicadas out in force.

letters.title: From Felix Choice   [1873?]
letters.summary: Has readExpression, and assures CD some people cry when happy.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   [1873–81]
letters.summary: Notes on the shoveller, taken from John Gould’sBirds of Great Britain[1862–73].

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [1873]
letters.summary: Klein says water ought to be changed daily. Asks to tell G Revalenta shop shut. Klein reports discovery about toads’ ova does not bear on pangenesis.

letters.title: From Hermanus Hartogh Heijs van Zouteveen   [1873?]
letters.summary: Translation of some of his annotations in Dutch edition ofExpression.

letters.title: From Stanley Haynes   [1873?]
letters.summary: Notes headed "Observations on the expression of the emotions".

letters.title: From E. F. Lubbock   [1873?]
letters.summary: Observations on her pet cat.

letters.title: From Henry Jackson   [1873?]
letters.summary: Notes referring to passages inExpression[annotated in places by Francis Darwin, presumably when preparing 2d ed.].

letters.title: From James Paget   [1873]
letters.summary:
"Sir William Gull has just brought me the enclosed quotations from Chaucer, as illustrations of the closure of the eyes in effort. [In "The Nun’s priest’s tale" inCanterbury talesthe fox tricks Chanticleer into crowing, whereupon Chanticleer closes his eyes to make the effort (and gets seized by the fox).] He begs me to send them to you.

I have lately seen a terrier who very distinctly frowns during mental excitement – not always with anger, but often, I think, with anxiety, as in expecting food."

letters.title: From Cecil Smith   [1873?]
letters.summary: Describes some behaviour in herring gulls similar to that of sheldrakes as described by CD inExpression[pp. 47–8].

letters.title: From J. P. M. Weale to J. N. Lockyer   [January 1873]
letters.summary: On expression among Kaffirs and Hottentots.

letters.title: From ?   [1873?]
letters.summary: Notes on CD’sExpression.

letters.title: To Mary Treat   1 January 1873
letters.summary: Asks for certain observations to be made onDroseraandDionaea.

letters.title: To ?    2 January [1873 or 1874]
letters.summary: CD appreciates the correspondent’s suggestion.

letters.title: From Hubert Airy   3 January 1873
letters.summary: HA’s paper on leaf arrangement is almost ready; asks CD to communicate it to the Royal Society. Seeks permission to quote from CD’s notes.

letters.title: From Lajos Felméri   3 January 1873
letters.summary:
Thanks for copy ofExpression. Notes on expression among the Széklers.

Sends a copy of his book of travels in Scotland.

letters.title: From J. D. Baldwin   4 January 1873
letters.summary:
Has studied CD’s books and accepts evolution without giving up belief in creation of first forms.

On theory inDescent, suggests offspring of the original [human] progenitor dispersed before a human stage arrived at; this would account for races and languages with no discernible common origin.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   4 January [1873]
letters.summary:
Comments on FG’s article ["Hereditary improvement",Fraser’s Mag.87 (1873): 116–30]. Finds it "the sole feasible, yet I fear utopian, plan of procedure in improving the human race".

Thanks for rabbits for Balfour.

Mentions reading W. R. Greg’sEnigmas[of life(1872)].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   5 January [1873]
letters.summary:
Asks whether his observations on absorptive powers of glandular hairs of plants are new facts.

Asks for aDrosophyllum.

Comments on Francis Galton’s article inFraser’s Magazine,

Greg’sEnigmas,

and Alphonse de Candolle’sHistoire des sciences.

letters.title: To ?   6 January [1873 or 1874]
letters.summary: "If you will apply to any bookseller whatever you will procure a copy.–– Publisher Murray."

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   7 January 1873
letters.summary:
Fascinated by Greg’sEnigmas, though its matter is weak.

Is vexed at being drawn into hostility toward British Museum through William Carruthers’ insolence and presumption.

Recounts visit with Edward Cardwell [Secretary for War].

Has sent Candolle’s book to Gladstone.

JDH indignant at Gladstone’s speech putting English science below French and German.

Thinks it is an accepted dogma that glandular hairs are excreting only. Will ask others to confirm.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   8 January 1873
letters.summary:
Has received, through AG, a letter onDionaea[from W. M. Canby] which has greatly interested him. CD asks AG to question his correspondent on whether it catches large or small insects.

Mary Treat will observeDrosera filiformis.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   9 January 1873
letters.summary:
Explains why he wantsDrosophyllum.

Hopes JDH will be elected President of Royal Society.

Agrees with JDH on Greg’sEnigmas.

Would like Greg to visit Down if JDH comes as CD’s "protector".

letters.title: To ?   9 January 1873
letters.summary: Has pleasure in signing the [missing] enclosure, with every word of which he fully agrees.

letters.title: To M. D. Conway   11 January [1873]
letters.summary:
Thanks MDC for letter on expression [see8694].

Invites him to Down on 24th. CD warns that his health does not permit him to talk long with anyone.

letters.title: To theSpectator   11 January 1873
letters.summary: Discusses two factors possibly causing modification of body or mind of an organism; habit and direct action of external conditions on the one hand, and selection, natural or artificial, on the other; considers their relative importance.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   12 January 1873
letters.summary:
Drosophyllumis coming from Dublin. Will ship it to Down when it arrives.

The awful honour of Presidency of Royal Society; his aversion to dignities and honours.

R. Strachey [Proc. R. Geogr. Soc.(1873): 450] has paid him and CD a compliment.

Letter from Gladstone.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   12 January [1873]
letters.summary:
Had thrown Geographical Society’sProceedingsin waste-basket, but as Strachey shows such admirable powers of discrimination he will fish it out and read the whole article.

Comments on 3d ed. of Sachs’s work [Lehrbuch der Botanik(1873)]. Wishes he were more controversial.

Has become wonderfully interested inDroseraandDionaea.

9000 copies ofExpressionhave been printed and most are sold.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [13 or 20 January 1873]
letters.summary: TheDrosophyllumgoes to Orpington by train this evening.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   13 January [1873]
letters.summary: Response to ARW’s criticisms in his review [ofExpression,Q. J. Sci.n.s. 3 (1873): 113–18].

letters.title: From Alphonse de Candolle   14 January 1873
letters.summary:
Thanks forExpression, which has made him wonder whether his shyness in public until the age of 55 resulted from fear of subjecting his face to ridicule.

Criticises F. Galton’sHereditary genius[1869] for neglecting environmental influence.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   14 January 1873
letters.summary: Is not surprised CD dissents from his criticisms [ofExpression?]. Holds to his own interpretation of the expression of astonishment.

letters.title: To W. E. Gladstone   [before 16 January 1873]
letters.summary: Encourages the government to keep the herbarium and library of the Royal Botanic Gardens at Kew.

letters.title: From H. P. Lee   17 January 1873
letters.summary: Describes shaken index finger in Japan and blushing among Chinese servants.

letters.title: From Ernst Meitzen   17 January 1873
letters.summary: Sends his book [Bhawani(1872)], which is a poem in praise of evolutionary theory and showing its roots in ancient India.

letters.title: From James Paget   17 January 1873
letters.summary: Describes a patient’s ears with peculiar tufts of hair in places where he has never seen them before. Encloses sketch.

letters.title: From Alois Humbert   [before 18] January 1873
letters.summary: On a humming-birdSphinxmoth which tried to extract nectar from flowers on wallpaper. [SeeDescent, 2d ed., p. 317.]

letters.title: To Alphonse de Candolle   18 January [1873]
letters.summary:
The evidence of tameness of Alpine butterflies [see8672] seems good and the fact is surprising to CD for they can hardly have acquired this in their short life-time.

The question whether butterflies are attracted to bright colours independently of the supposed presence of nectar is still unanswered.

CD has great difficulty in believing that any temporary condition of parents can affect the offspring.

Pangenesis is much reviled, but CD must still look at generation from this point of view, which makes him averse to believing that an emotion has any effect on the offspring.

letters.title: To James Paget   18 January [1873]
letters.summary: JP’s note [8739] suggests reversion, but that is an easy trap. Will look to the ears of "our brethren at the Zool. Gardens".

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   20 January 1873
letters.summary: On EH’sDie Kalkschwämme[1872].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   20 January 1873
letters.summary:
HopesDrosophyllumwas all right.

Opinion of Council of Royal Society [on Presidency] is twelve for JDH, five for Duke of Devonshire, and G. B. Airy for William Spottiswoode.

letters.title: To Hubert Airy   [before 21 January 1873]
letters.summary: Sends HA’s paper ["On leaf arrangement"] with a supporting note [from CD] to Royal Society.

letters.title: From Hubert Airy   21 January 1873
letters.summary:
Has sent phyllotaxy paper to G. G. Stokes with the letter from CD to show credentials.

Will not have time to read new Sachs edition CD offered.

Thanks for CD’s sponsorship of paper [Proc. R. Soc. Lond.21 (1873): 176–9].

letters.title: To J. D. Baldwin   21 January [1873]
letters.summary: Discusses JDB’s views on the spread of human-like creatures across the world, and the development of language.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   21 January 1873
letters.summary: On a correction JVC thinks should be made inVariationon vertebrae of ducks.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   22 January 1873
letters.summary: Concerned about GHD’s health. Sends a prescription for a cough mixture.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   23 January 1873
letters.summary: Acknowledges correction in text of Variation. "You are a most conscientious editor & are as careful as I am apt to be careless."

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   24 January 1873
letters.summary: Popular Edition [6th] ofOriginhas sold out 3000 copies. Asks CD whether he has found any errors that should be corrected.

letters.title: To O. C. Marsh   25 January [1873]
letters.summary: Thanks OCM for the papers he has sent.

letters.title: From Anton Dohrn   27 January 1873
letters.summary: The Naples Zoological Station and its library are growing fast. His life is a constant battle with the municipality, but has managed to make a little progress on vertebrate ancestry and morphology. His views get further away from what is generally accepted.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   27 January [1873]
letters.summary:
Drosophyllumarrived; none of his observations turned out as he expected, but nevertheless he understands its habits better than he did. The secreting hairs that he observed may be explained as a mere chemical reaction.

Comments on various articles he has read.

Asks for Thiselton-Dyer’s notes.

letters.title: To Hermanus Hartogh Heijs van Zouteveen   28 January 1873
letters.summary: Is pleased that HHHvZ has appended his notes to his translation [ofExpressionand is obliged for the abstract of these notes [see 8712].

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   29 January 1873
letters.summary:
A new [German] edition ofExpressionis to be done. Has CD anything to add or alter?

JVC cites an article on cessation of breathing during mental concentration that supports Gratiolet as quoted inExpression, p. 179.

letters.title: To James Paget   29 January [1873?]
letters.summary: Has heard from Ashwin Conway Newman of Guy’s Hospital of a case of a child without any prepuce whose father was a renegade, uncircumcised Jew, but whose ancestors had all been Jews. Newman thinks this a good case of inheritance with reversion. JP’s letter [missing] now shows how rash such a conclusion would be.

letters.title: From F. S. B. F. de Chaumont   31 January 1873
letters.deprecated: Francis Stephen Bennet François de Chaumont
letters.sender: Francis Stephen Bennet François de Chaumont
letters.summary: Sends a paper on evolution by his friend J. D. MacDonald ["Distribution of Invertebrata",Proc. R. Soc. Lond.21 (1872–3): 218–23] for CD’s perusal before dispatching it to the Royal Society.

letters.title: From W. M. Canby   1 February 1873
letters.summary: At Asa Gray’s request, responds to CD’s questions about WMC’s observations onDionaeaand particularly about the size of the insects captured and the excitability of the leaves after an insect is captured.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   1 February 1873
letters.summary:
Has no corrections for second German edition [ofExpression]. Plans to bring out an improved edition in a year or two.

Thanks for reference JVC sent.

letters.title: To John Chapman   1 February 1873
letters.summary: Thanks for Chapman 1873 (Chapman, John. 1873.Neuralgia and kindred diseases of the nervous system).

letters.title: From J. T. Moggridge   1 February 1873
letters.summary:
He does not accept Wallace’s definition of instinct because it excludes "inherited experience", i.e., "knowledge acquired by and transmitted through ancestors".

House-flies do not seem to have an instinctive fear of trap-door spiders.

Miss Forster gives him news of CD.

letters.title: To W. B. Dawkins   3 February 1873
letters.summary: A letter of recommendation for W. B. Dawkins in his application for the Woodwardian professorship of geology in the university of Cambridge.

letters.title: To F. S. B. F. de Chaumont   3 February [1873]
letters.deprecated: Francis Stephen Bennet François de Chaumont
letters.recipient: Francis Stephen Bennet François de Chaumont
letters.summary:
Thanks for J. D. MacDonald’s paper ["Distribution of invertebrata",Proc. R. Soc. Lond.21 (1872–3): 218–23].

CD feels lines of genetic connection between animals offer a most difficult problem; Ernst Haeckel may have done mischief by facing the difficulty.

letters.title: To J. E. Gray   4 February [1873]
letters.summary: Is glad JEG has made out what theguemulis ["On the Guémul",Ann. & Mag. Nat. Hist.4th ser. 10 (1872): 445–6; 11 (1873): 214–20, 308–10].

letters.title: To E. H. Giglioli   6 February [1873]
letters.summary: Thanks his Italian colleague for articles on the skull of a chimpanzee.

letters.title: From C. I. F. Major   6 February 1873
letters.summary: Cannot find a publisher for Italian translation ofExpression. Gives up the project.

letters.title: From F. B. Goodacre   7 February 1873
letters.summary: Would like a museum set up illustrating origins, varieties, and uses of domestic animals; seeks CD’s approval of the idea.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   [8 February 1873]
letters.summary:
Forwards Matthew Arnold’sLiterature and dogma[1873].

Hopes they can secure Hooker for President of Royal Society.

letters.title: To Matthew Arnold   9 February [1873]
letters.summary: Thanks MA for hisLiterature and dogma[1873].

letters.title: From John Murray   10 February [1873]
letters.summary: Encloses cheque for 1000 guineas, CD’s share of profits on first 7000 copies ofExpression.

letters.title: To F. B. Goodacre   11 February [1873]
letters.summary: Thinks FBG’s idea of a room at the British Museum of domestic birds and animals an excellent one, but a collection of plants would be much more difficult.

letters.title: To C. I. F. Major   11 February 1873
letters.summary: Is sorry that CIFM has had to give up translatingExpressioninto Italian.

letters.title: ToNature   [before 13 February 1873]
letters.summary: Sends a letter from William Huggins about a case of inherited fright in three generations of mastiffs. Discusses the different origins of instincts and their inheritance.

letters.title: From E. M. Swanwick   [after 13 February 1873]
letters.summary: Gives a case of peculiar behaviour in cats that apparently is inherited.

letters.title: From Mariabella Fry   15 February 1873
letters.summary: Remarks on the "grief-muscles" shown in a Dürer picture.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   17 February 1873
letters.summary:
Is drawing up the account of his crossing experiments. Requests JDH to add the families after nine genera, the names of which he encloses. Whenever there is no objection he would like to arrange the families in some sort of natural order.

Recommends Spalding’s article on instinct inMacmillan’s Magazine[27 (1873): 265–81].

letters.title: To Gerard Krefft   17 February 1873
letters.summary:
Is glad JLGK has been interested inDescent.

Thanks him for his observations on monkey behaviour [see8698]

and drawings of skulls, which CD has sent to George Busk.

letters.title: From C. H. Schaible   17 February 1873
letters.summary:
Sends copy of Vinzenz Czerny [Beziehungen der Chirurgie(1872)], which applies Darwinian principles to pathology.

Recommends illustrations dealing with expression in the Atlas of K. H. Baumgärtner’sKranken-Physiognomik[1839].

letters.title: To George King   18 February 1873
letters.summary: Thanks for information on worm-castings. Comments on disintegration of castings.

letters.title: To W. M. Canby   19 February 1873
letters.summary: CD would like to know what were the sizes of insects caught by the older leaves ofDionaea.

letters.title: From T. R. Clephan   19 February 1873
letters.summary: Reports that he has the power of moving his left ear towards the top of his head [seeDescent1: 21].

letters.title: To Albert Gaudry   19 February 1873
letters.summary: Thanks for gift of first part of AG’s magnificent work [Animaux fossiles du mont Léberon(1873)].

letters.title: From F. X. Neumann von Spallart   19 February 1873
letters.summary: The editor of a supplement to theNew Free Pressto be published during the next Vienna Exhibition, asks CD to contribute a few columns on any topic.

letters.title: To ?   19 February 1873
letters.summary: Thanks recipient for a photograph.

letters.title: To a bookseller?   19 February [1873]
letters.summary: Orders a copy of theSt Paul’s Magazinefor February.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   20 February 1873
letters.summary:
Delighted with John Traherne Moggridge’s book [Harvesting ants(1873)].

Has suggested he plant seeds in various receptacles. Only two explanations for failure of seeds to germinate [in ants’ nests]: lack of circulating air or formic acid.

Has undertaken a botany primer for Macmillan.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   21 February [1873]
letters.summary:
Will see whether formic acid delays germination of fresh seeds.

Thinks primer not at all a folly. Refers JDH to Asa Gray’s "child’s book" [see8363].

letters.title: From Arthur Nicols   21 February 1873
letters.summary:
Comments on CD’s and William Huggins’ letter inNatureon "Inherited instinct" [Collected papers2: 170–1]

and on A. R. Wallace’s letter on the homing faculty of animals. Believes many instances of homing are less remarkable than they appear.

letters.title: From W. F. Collier   22 February 1873
letters.summary: Sends pamphlet on punishment in education [Punishments in education, read at Social Science Congress, 1872] in response toExpression. Proposes that character can be diagnosed from expression.

letters.title: From J. R. Martin   22 February 1873
letters.deprecated: John Royle Martin(Artizans, Labourers, & General Dwellings Co. Ltd.)
letters.sender: John Royle Martin(Artizans, Labourers, & General Dwellings Co. Ltd.)
letters.summary: CD is asked to increase his shares in the Artizans, Labourers, & General Dwellings Co. Ltd., which has trebled its capital in the last year and is paying a 6% dividend.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   23 February 1873
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for comments onDie Kalkschwämme.

Plans trip to Greece, Asia Minor, and Egypt.

Discusses work of a Polish translator, Ludwik Masłowski.

letters.title: From J. C. Houzeau   24 February 1873
letters.summary:
Thanks CD forExpression.

Suggests saving some anthropoid Quadrumana from extinction by taming and studying them in their own environments to learn about their development.

letters.title: From Robert Smith   24 February 1873
letters.summary: Asks for references to works on CD’s views for a paper he is preparing.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   25 February 1873
letters.summary: Sends "squib" he has written exposing the folly of some of Louis Agassiz’s ideas. AG cannot "fire off [his] cracker" in U. S. so sends it to amuse CD. If it is sent toNature, CD must not give AG’s name. [See "Survival of the fittest",Nature7 (1873): 404].

letters.title: From J. D. Hague   26 February 1873
letters.summary: Sends a paper on behaviour he has observed in ants.

letters.title: From R. B. Litchfield   26 February 1873
letters.summary: Additional errata inDescent.

letters.title: From H. A. Head   27 February 1873
letters.summary:
Winter in Duluth.

HAH is leaning toward spiritualism.

Limit of natural and sexual selection.

Has been around the world three times.

letters.title: To T. W. Higginson   27 February [1873]
letters.summary: Praises TWH’sArmy life in a black regiment[1870]. CD always thought well of Negroes, and is delighted to have his impressions confirmed.

letters.title: To Robert Smith   27 February [1873]
letters.summary: CD answers a question about the attitude of foreign naturalists towards Darwinism by distinguishing between the belief in evolution and belief in natural selection. Gives the views of [Louis] Agassiz, [R. A.] Kölliker, [C. W.] Nägeli, [Ernst] Häckel, [C. F. W.] Claus, [F. J.] Cohn, Alphonse de Candolle, [J. L.] Claparède, Asa Gray, Gaston de Saporta, [E. D.] Cope, and [Carl] Gegenbaur.

letters.title: To James Crichton-Browne   28 February [1873]
letters.summary: Hopes JC-B thinks that CD has properly acknowledged his debt inExpression.

letters.title: From Hermann Müller   28 February 1873
letters.summary: Sends his book [Die Befruchtung der Blumen(1873)]. Hopes CD will publish an opinion of it.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [1–15 March 1873]
letters.summary: Has sent Vichy water, discusses prescription. Tell Arthur Parslow not to continue on colchicum for gout if doesn’t suit him. May go to Pryor’s on Sunday.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [after March 1873]
letters.summary: Fears [CD’s] albumen theory will not work because albumen is coagulated and filtered out in making extracts of belladonna, hyoscyamine, and colchicine [alkaloid poisons].

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [after March 1873]
letters.summary: Has investigated whether it makes a difference if extracts [of alkaloid poisons] are made from leaves, seeds, or roots.

letters.title: From James Crichton-Browne   2 March 1873
letters.summary:
Thanks forExpression. Will write paper on it in next [July]West Riding Asylum Medical Report.

Sends photos of lunatics;

will send notes corroborative of CD’s views, including some on "hereditarily transmitted movements".

letters.title: From Thomas Meehan   3 March 1873
letters.summary:
Although he believes in evolution, TM feels that natural selection is an inadequate cause;

nor is he satisfied with E. D. Cope’s law of acceleration and retardation.

Discusses some of his work relating to nutrition and sex and colour and sex.

letters.title: From Henry Reeks   3 March 1873
letters.summary:
Praise for and detailed comments onExpression.

Two cases of coloration in animals – one from sexual selection, the other helping to procure prey [seeDescent, 2d ed., pp. 542–3].

letters.title: To James Crichton-Browne   4 March [1873]
letters.summary:
Pleased that JC-B will reviewExpression.

Fears he will not be able to improve the book with JC-B’s "wonderfully curious" photographs because Murray printed such a large edition.

Would be glad to have JC-B’s notes on inheritance – "a most important subject".

letters.title: From C.-F. Reinwald   4 March 1873
letters.summary:
Recounts the difficulties in preparing the French translation ofOrigin: the 1870 war, the illness and death of J. J. Moulinié, the alterations and additions from the 6th English edition. Despite competition from Royer’s three editions, Reinwald is contemplating a new edition.

Descent, vol. 1, has almost sold out. Offers CD £40 for rights to reprint a corrected version ofDescent.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   5 March [1873]
letters.summary: Distressed by the poor health of GHD and Horace. Asks them to come home.

letters.title: From W. H. Hall   5 March 1873
letters.summary: Asks CD about the origin of certain expressions in man.

letters.title: To Henry Reeks   5 March [1873]
letters.summary:
Thanks for HR’s valuable remarks aboutExpression, and returns HRs copy, signed.

Discusses some of HR’s anecdotes about children sucking their tongues.

Admits that the youth who trembled so that he could not reload his gun after killing his first snipe was himself, when a school-boy.

letters.title: From W. F. Collier   7 March 1873
letters.summary: Opposes all corporal punishment. Pleased CD agrees with his pamphlet.

letters.title: From Henry Reeks   8 March 1873
letters.summary: Insists that suckling babies pound and scratch mothers’ breasts. Perhaps CD’s evidence to the contrary comes from ladies, who only expose small portion of bosom, as opposed to working-class women.

letters.title: From F. B. Johnston   9 March 1873
letters.summary: Various observations on sexual selection portion ofDescent– ostriches, rosy-billed duck, egrets, rails, etc.

letters.title: From Athénaïs Michelet   9 March 1873
letters.summary: Thanks CD for one of his books.

letters.title: To J. T. Moggridge   10 March 1873
letters.summary:
Much obliged for seeds. Will expose seeds to chemical vapours.

Comments on JTM’s spider experiments.

letters.title: From H. F. H. Elliot to G. H. Darwin   [before 11 March 1873?]
letters.summary: Instinctive responses in animals.

letters.title: To A. W. Bennett   11 March [1873]
letters.summary: Asks about woodblocks of illustrations forClimbing plants[1875].

letters.title: To Asa Gray   11 March [1873]
letters.summary:
Astonished by Agassiz’s argument; has sent AG’s memorandum toNature[see8786].

Is working on cross- and self-fertilising plants and has temporarily stopped work onDrosera.

letters.title: From Otto Caspari   12 March 1873
letters.summary:
Sends CD a copy of his book [Die Urgeschichte der Menschheit, 2 vols. (1873)].

In Germany CD’s views have achieved great recognition among naturalists, but in other disciplines there is great controversy. OC’s book seeks to resolve the controversy by showing how state, morals, religion, and church have developed from natural beginnings.

letters.title: ToNature   [before 13 March 1873]
letters.summary: Recounts instances suggesting that animals have a sense of direction.

letters.title: To T. M. Hughes   13 March [1873]
letters.summary: Is glad and proud to honour the memory of Adam Sedgwick [d. 1873].

letters.title: To G. M. Humphry   14 March 1873
letters.summary: Sorry that his health prevents him attending a meeting to honour Adam Sedgwick.

letters.title: From A. W. Bennett   16 March 1873
letters.summary:
Thanks for CD’s regrets at AWB’s leavingNature.

Plans English editions of Asa Gray’s books [How plants grow;How plants behave].

Other publication plans.

letters.title: From Hubert Airy   17 March 1873
letters.summary:
Thanks for congratulations on appearance of abstract of HA’s paper [Nature7 (1873): 343–4].

Explains again his theory of "contraction with twist" by which compact buds and a spiral phyllotaxy have evolved. Explains how the peculiar phyllotaxy of the teasel is explicable by this process of "condensation".

letters.title: From William Pengelly   17 March 1873
letters.summary: CD’s notice inNature[Collected papers2: 171–2] induces WP to send letters from correspondents recounting stories of a dog that learned to open a door and of another that found his way home from London to Cowes.

letters.title: To F. P. Cobbe?   18 March [1873?]
letters.summary: CD has discovered correspondent intends to present a petition to the House of Commons on which CD’s is the sole signature. Asks that his name be erased unless other signatures are added.

letters.title: From J. C. Costerus and N. D. Doedes   18 March 1873
letters.summary: Two students express their gratitude and admiration.

letters.title: From Arthur Nicols   [before 20 March 1873]
letters.summary: Compares sense of smell in dogs and cats.

letters.title: To Thomas Meehan   19 March [1873]
letters.summary:
Does not understand TM’s views on sex and vitality.

Agrees no real "essences" in genera, only broken groups of species.

letters.title: To William Pengelly   19 March [1873]
letters.summary: Thanks WP for his accounts of sagacity of dogs. "I can believe almost anything about them."

letters.title: To Arthur Nicols   [20 March 1873]
letters.summary: Responds to Nichols’ observations on sense of smell in cats and dogs.

letters.title: From G. H. Eggers   21 March 1873
letters.summary: An admirer sends clipping from Bremen newspaper on hybrid between orange and lemon.

letters.title: To William Turner   21 March [1873]
letters.summary: Sends £10 subscription for James Murie.

letters.title: To J. C. Costerus and N. D. Doedes    [22?] March 1873
letters.summary: Thanks them for their kind letter and interest in his work. Sends photograph.

letters.title: From Johannes Huber   22 March 1873
letters.summary: Describes his critique of natural selection [Die Lehre Darwins kritisch betrachtet(1871)].

letters.title: From Raphael Meldola   24 March 1873
letters.summary:
Gives some information on variation of ocelli between sexes in butterfly species.

Proposes publishing a series of papers on mimicry.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   25 March [1873]
letters.summary: H. W. Bates says CD is in town. WWR would like to call.

letters.title: To T. L. Brunton   26 March 1873
