letters.summary: Thanks forIndian[Medical]Gazette. Comments on article.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   26 March [1873]
letters.summary: Thanks RM for note on ocelli.

letters.title: From Robert Swinhoe   26 March 1873
letters.summary: Discusses expression among the Chinese. Reports certain physical characters and the practice of certain unusual customs.

letters.title: To Henry Willett   26 March [1873]
letters.summary: CD subscribes an additional £10.

letters.title: From G. B. Thornbery   27 March 1873
letters.summary: Has read several of CD’s books; is curious about his remarks on "movements which are no longer useful but still inherited". Asks CD’s opinion on why people still swing arms with opposite leg in walking.

letters.title: From A. G. Butler   27 March 1873
letters.summary:
On ocelli and relation to sexual selection;

instance of rejection of male by female butterfly.

letters.title: From N. D. Doedes   27 March 1873
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for photograph – sends one in return,

questions CD on his religious views.

letters.title: To J. S. Burdon Sanderson   29 March 1873
letters.summary:
Reports that he has not received JSBS’s book on histology and physiology [Sanderson ed.,Handbook for the physiological laboratory(1873)], which Edward Emmanuel Klein told CD’s son was to be sent. He asks for information so that he may thank Dr Klein. [Klein and Michael Foster were co-authors with JSBS.]

He has returned the Gazette to Dr T. L. Brunton. [See8825.]

letters.title: To Marian Evans   30 March [1873]
letters.summary: Asks whether the Litchfields may call on her. "My wife complains that she has been very badly treated and that I ought to have asked permission for her to call on you with me when we next come to London: but I tell her that I still have some shreds of modesty."

letters.title: From T. W. Higginson   30 March 1873
letters.summary:
Pleased CD enjoyed his book [Outdoor papers(1871)].

Rejoices at CD’s kindly feelings toward the coloured race.

TheIndexis in financial trouble due to F. E. Abbot’s unworldliness.

Agassiz is setting up a summer school for natural history off the Massachusetts coast. His pupils develop more liberal scientific opinions than Agassiz’s.

Encloses some notes on expression.

letters.title: From Marian Evans   31 March 1873
letters.summary: The Leweses will be happy to see the Litchfields, and hope CD will come again, with Emma.

letters.title: To Samuel Butler   1 April [1873]
letters.summary: Comments on SB’s book [The fair haven(1873)]. CD is struck by SB’s dramatic power – thinks he could write "a really good novel". Surprised at strength of case SB makes that Jesus did not die on the cross. SB’s identity will soon be universally known: Leslie Stephen knows he is the author.

letters.title: To N. D. Doedes   2 April 1873
letters.summary: The impossibility of conceiving that the universe arose through chance is the chief argument for the existence of God, but CD has never been able to decide whether this is an argument of real value. Safest to believe that the subject is beyond man’s intellect, "but man can do his duty".

letters.title: From William Main   2 April 1873
letters.summary: Having now readExpression, WM repeats his criticism of "antithesis". Explains his theory of up-and-down-tending lines.

letters.title: ToNature   [before 3 April 1873]
letters.summary:
Comments on article ["Perception and instinct in lower animals",Nature7 (1871): 377–8].

Explains his contention that "many of the most wonderful instincts have been acquired, independently of habit, through the preservation of useful variations of pre-existing instincts". Cites examples: sterile workers of several species of social insects have acquired different instincts; movements of tumbler pigeons. Speculates that "many instincts have originated from modification or variations in the brain".

letters.title: ToNature   [before 3 April 1873]
letters.summary: "The following fact with respect to the habits of ants, which I believe to be quite new, has been sent to me by a distinguished geologist, Mr J. D. Hague [see8788]; and it appears well worth publishing."

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   [3 April 1873]
letters.summary: Anxious to have GHD come home because of his poor health. Recommends Huxley’s physician (Andrew Clark) – an advocate of milk diet.

letters.title: To J. D. Hague   3 April [1873]
letters.summary:
Has sent JDH’s letter toNature["Perception in ants",Nature7 (1873): 443–4].

Sons recall kindness received from JDH and others in America.

letters.title: From N. D. Doedes   4 April 1873
letters.summary: Debates the existence of God.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [6 April 1873]
letters.summary: Wants to discuss raising a testimonial fund for Huxley and whether Huxley would stand this.

letters.title: From Adolph Reuter   6 April 1873
letters.summary: Sends photograph of a diseased roebuck shot by Prince Frederick Charles of Prussia.

letters.title: From E. F. Lubbock   [before 7 April 1873]
letters.summary: Is trying to persuade "our friend" [T. H. Huxley?] to accept a gift.

letters.title: To Thomas Davidson   7 April 1873
letters.summary:
Thanks TWStCD for catalogue of his Cretacean fossils.

Regrets he cannot visit Brighton.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [7 April 1873]
letters.summary: Thinks the Huxley fund should be done. Difficulty will be getting him to accept it.

letters.title: From Charles Voysey   7 April 1873
letters.summary: Sends his 6th volume.

letters.title: From E. F. Lubbock   [after 7 April 1873?]
letters.summary: Observations on her pet pug.

letters.title: To William Spottiswoode   [8 April 1873]
letters.summary: Discusses the arrangements being made to present a gift to Huxley [see8872].

letters.title: From John Tyndall   8 April [1873]
letters.summary: William Spottiswoode was not at home, but JT sought out Herbert Spencer. Spencer will come with JT to see CD [about the Huxley fund].

letters.title: To John Tyndall   8 April [1873]
letters.summary: CD will write to William Spottiswoode about the fund for Huxley. CD is raising his subscription to £300. "We have done a good day’s work … [it] gives me a higher opinion of human nature than I had before, though I am not one of those who think lowly of mankind."

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [9 April 1873]
letters.summary: Hopes that Charles Lyell has enjoyed his excursion.

letters.title: From John Tyndall   9 April [1873]
letters.summary: Is convinced that the "brotherly spirit of the transaction" will cause Huxley not to raise objections.

letters.title: From John Tyndall   10 April 1873
letters.summary: W. G. Armstrong and T. H. Farrer have both contributed [to the Huxley fund].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   11 April 1873
letters.summary: George Henslow is worse. All plans to go abroad have been given up. James Paget’s diagnoses enclosed.

letters.title: To John Tyndall   11 April 1873
letters.summary: Sends JT the list and amounts subscribed for Huxley. It will probably amount to £1800. He will write to Huxley and use every argument he can to make him accept.

letters.title: To Albert Günther   12 April [1873]
letters.summary:
CD did not bring any tortoises back from the Galapagos. There may be specimens at the Military Institution in Whitehall.

Sorry AG was unable to lunch with the Darwins during their stay in London.

letters.title: To A. W. Merriam   13 April 1873
letters.summary: Thanks AWM for "Comus" and an abusive New Orleans Mardi Gras newspaper editorial; he cannot tell from the "wonderful mistakes" whether the writer is "witty, ignorant, or blunders for the sake of fun".

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [before 15 April 1873]
letters.summary: Sends to Pantlludw [North Wales] bottle of formic acid. FD and Amy [Darwin] can search for spawn. If found, keep in two basins and add 6 drops of acid to one and look for differences.

letters.title: From Samuel Butler   15 April 1873
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his kind letter aboutThe fair haven[1873]. Encouraged by its reception. All he wants is to compel "an attitude of fixed attention in the place of cowardly shrinking from examination". Says he will try "a novel pure and simple with little ""purpose"" next".

letters.title: To E. R. Lankester   15 April [1873]
letters.summary:
Discusses error in CD’s calculation of natural increase of elephants.

Includes extract fromOrigin.

letters.title: From James Crichton-Browne   16 April 1873
letters.summary:
Sends 15 studies in expression, acted by his wife.

Describes David Ferrier’s experiments on electrical brain stimulation of animals; these show direct relation between convolutions of the brain and groups of muscles [West Riding Asylum Med. Rep.(July 1873)].

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   16 April [1873]
letters.summary: "Try only 1 or 2 drops of Formic A[cid]."

letters.title: From John Tyndall   16 April 1873
letters.summary: It is Huxley’s "duty to do what we wish him to do – his duty to his wife and children, his duty to us and to the world". Shares CD’s wish that Mrs [Henry] L[yell?] had not subscribed – it suggests the idea of an effort.

letters.title: To James Crichton-Browne   17 April [1873]
letters.summary:
Photographs sent by JC-B show great power of acting.

David Ferrier’s researches sound wonderful. Does he believe that he excites an idea and this leads to the movement, or that he acts directly on the motor nerves?

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [17 April 1873]
letters.summary: Fears all the seeds are dead. Will try with less vapour of formic acid.

letters.title: To Leonard Blomefield   17 April [1873]
letters.summary:
Thanks LB for his essay on local biology.

CD with much care and discomfort is now able to work a few hours almost every day.

letters.title: To Adolph Reuter   17 April 1873
letters.summary: Thanks for letter and curious photographs. Urges AR not to send anything valuable unless he publishes it elsewhere because CD is growing old and may not have strength and time to continue his former researches.

letters.title: To John Tyndall   18 April [1873]
letters.summary: The Huxley fund amounts to £1955. CD trembles about THH’s answer.

letters.title: From Federico Delpino   20 April 1873
letters.summary:
Left theGaribaldiat Rio de Janeiro.

Phylogeny of aphids.

letters.title: To W. B. Carpenter   21 April [1873]
letters.summary: Writes of his extreme interest in WBC’s article ["On the hereditary transmission of acquired psychical habits",Contemp. Rev.21 (1873): 779–95].

letters.title: From John Tyndall   21 April 1873
letters.summary: [Sir Joseph?] Whitworth’s contribution brings total to over £2000. Wishes CD could be persuaded to come to lunch with Huxley and Emerson.

letters.title: From W. M. Canby   22 April 1873
letters.summary: Sends leaves ofDionaeawith insect prey in them. Size of insects captured may be affected by leaves not being fully grown.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   23 April 1873
letters.summary: Informs THH that 18 friends have given him a fund of £2100 to enable him to take a holiday.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   24 April 1873
letters.summary: Is overwhelmed by generosity of his friends. Admits he felt morally beaten and without energy for first time in his life. Someday wants the names of the friends.

letters.title: To J. D. Hague   25 April [1873]
letters.summary: Encloses note from J. T. Moggridge commenting on JDH’s letter ["Perception in ants",Nature7 (1873): 443–4].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   25 April 1873
letters.summary:
Charmed by Huxley’s letter of appreciation [8873].

Lady Lyell’s sudden death.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   25 April 1873
letters.summary: Affected by THH’s letter – will send a copy to the other 17 friends. Hopes for his and public’s sake his health will improve.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [25 April 1873]
letters.summary: Offers condolences on the death of CL’s wife.

letters.title: To subscribers to T. H. Huxley’s gift   [25 April 1873]
letters.deprecated: Subscribers to T. H. Huxley gift
letters.recipient: Subscribers to T. H. Huxley gift
letters.summary: A circular letter forwarding to subscribers a copy of Huxley’s letter of thanks [8873].

letters.title: To John Tyndall   25 April [1873]
letters.summary: Sends Huxley’s "charming letter". Asks whether it should be sent to Lady Millicent Jones. CD is "so happy about the whole affair".

letters.title: To John Tyndall   25 April [1873]
letters.summary: Sends another copy [of Huxley’s letter of thanks for holiday fund].

letters.title: To John Tyndall   25 April 1873
letters.summary: It has just occurred to CD that he ought not to leave a copy of Huxley’s confidential letter in the hands of anyone. Asks JT to write to ask recipients to return the copies to CD at Down.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   26 April 1873
letters.summary:
Concern for Lady Lyell;

will clear away work and set off for holiday in June.

SendsCritiques and addresses.

A life of J. D. Forbes [by J. C. Shairp, P. J. Tait, and A. A. Reilly (1873)] suggests that THH and Tyndall conspired to keep JDF from getting the Copley Medal. THH feels obliged to correct this.

letters.title: From Herbert Spencer   26 April 1873
letters.summary: Wants to use CD’s support to put pressure on Michael Foster to enable Huxley to take an immediate holiday.

letters.title: From Emil Buck   28 April 1873
letters.summary: Announces that CD has been elected Corresponding Member of the Senckenbergische Naturforschende Gesellschaft.

letters.title: To George Cupples   28 April [1873]
letters.summary: Asks whether GC knows who gave CD a scolding in lastEdinburgh Review[Apr 1873].

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   28 April 1873
letters.summary: Recommends Hermann Müller’sDie Befruchtung der Blumen[1873].

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   28 April 1873
letters.summary:
Lady Lyell’s death.

Sends names of donors of gift to THH.

TheEdinburgh Reviewhas a critical article against CD, THH, Tyndall, and H. Spencer [see8935]. Thinks Forbes reference not worth answering.

letters.title: To ?   28 April 1873
letters.summary: "I was born in the town of Shrewsbury Feb. 12, 1809."

letters.title: To H. C. F. Jenkin   30 April [1873]
letters.summary:
HCFJ’s review of theOriginwas the wittiest and in some respects the best written.

Thanks him for hisElectricity and magnetism[1873].

letters.title: From George Cupples   1 May 1873
letters.summary: Missed hostile review ofExpressioninEdinburgh Review. Agrees it might be by J. H. Stirling [see8935], who has written in a deplorably polemical style on Huxley and Sir William Hamilton.

letters.title: To Federico Delpino   1 May 1873
letters.summary: Asks whether, in Italy, varieties ofLathyrus odoratus,Pisum sativum, andPhaseolus multiflorusmust be grown separately to come true.

letters.title: To Isidoro Dell’Oro   2 May 1873
letters.summary: Thanks correspondent for sending him an account of silkworms.

letters.title: To John Tyndall   2 [May] 1873
letters.summary: Hopes JT does not think him over-cautious in requesting the return of the copies [of Huxley’s letter]. Has sent Huxley a list of the subscribers.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   3 May 1873
letters.summary:
Hopes affairs will enable him to get back to flowers.

Huxley’s letter [about the fund raised for him] was noble. Would like to have seen CD’s to him.

letters.title: From Gerard Krefft   3 May 1873
letters.summary: Suggests hopping lizards may show the connection between reptiles and birds as proposed by Huxley.

letters.title: To John Murray   4 May [1873]
letters.summary: Asks Murray not to announceCross and self-fertilisation.

letters.title: To ?   4 May [1873]
letters.summary: Explains that his publisher has erred in announcing his book [Cross and self-fertilisation] prematurely. [See8890and8897.]

letters.title: From William Ogle   [after 5 May 1873]
letters.summary: Thanks for reference to Hermann Müller’s book on fertilisation [Befruchtung der Blumen(1873)].

letters.title: From K. E. von Baer   5 May 1873
letters.summary: Has been told CD wants photo of him; sends one. Requests a portrait photo of CD for his album. KEvB apologises for his English and his shaky hand; he is 88 years old.

letters.title: To A. W. Bennett   5 May [1873]
letters.summary: Recommends H. Müller’sDie Befruchtung der Blumen(1873).

letters.title: To Felix von Luschan   5 May 1873
letters.summary: Thanks FL for sending his essays and some photographs.

letters.title: To Hermann Müller   5 May 1873
letters.summary: Comments on HM’s book [Die Befruchtung der Blumen(1873)]. Particularly glad to read historical sketch and discussion of work of C. K. Sprengel.

letters.title: To William Ogle   5 May [1873]
letters.summary: Recommends H. Müller’sDie Befruchtung den Blumen durch Insekten(1873).

letters.title: From W. F. Barrett   6 May 1873
letters.summary: Because of current interest in hereditary instinct, relates incident about a baby alligator, just emerged from its shell, attempting to bite a human.

letters.title: From George Hookham   6 May [1873]
letters.summary: A fact on expression: sheep do use hoofs in fighting.

letters.title: To W. M. Canby   7 May 1873
letters.summary: Thanks for theDionaealeaves. They support CD’s anticipation that they are adapted to let the smaller fry escape [seeInsectivorous plants, p. 312].

letters.title: To T. B. Leffen   7 May 1873
letters.summary:
Thanks for note and information.

Mentions venomous caterpillars in Africa and Australia.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   [before 8 May 1873]
letters.summary: Publisher [Schweizerbart] has seen CD’s new book advertised [Cross and self-fertilisation] and wishes to publish a German translation of it.

letters.title: From A. W. Bennett   8 May 1873
letters.summary:
Thanks for reference to Hermann Müller on fertilisation [Die Befruchtung der Blumen(1873)].

Publication plans.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   8 May [1873]
letters.summary:
John Murray has announced his next book [Cross and self-fertilisation] without CD’s knowledge. It is only half-written. JVC will hear when it is published and will decide whether it is worth translating. It will be dry, but, CD believes, of value.

Has read an account of JVC’s Scottish lectures.

Invites JVC to Down.

letters.title: To [W. W. Baxter?]   11 May [1873]
letters.summary: Requests litmus paper and gum.

letters.title: From S. J. Pozzi   11 May 1873
letters.summary: French translation ofExpression[1874].

letters.title: From Hermann Müller   12 May 1873
letters.summary: Thanks for CD’s praise of his book [see8901].

letters.title: From Ludwik Masłowski   14 May 1873
letters.summary: Requests permission to translateDescentinto Polish.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   14 May 1873
letters.summary: Has completed his book [The African sketch-book(1873)].

letters.title: From C.-F. Reinwald   14 May 1873
letters.summary:
Samuel Pozzi’s translation ofExpressionprogressing slowly.

J. J. Moulinié’s translation ofDescentis stylistically poor, which may account for low sales.

Difficult to find European naturalists to translate CD’s works. They would rather write books on "Darwinisme" under their own names.

letters.title: To Friedrich Hildebrand   15 May 1873
letters.summary:
Asks for results of FH’s experiments fertilizing some flowers with pollen from the same flower, & other flowers with pollen from distinct flowers borne by the same plant.

Has read FH’s paper on the distribution of the seeds of the Graminæ (Hildebrand 1872, pp. 740–1) with great interest.

letters.title: To S. J. Pozzi   15 May 1873
letters.summary: Answers questions about the translations of some species names.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   16 May [1873]
letters.summary: Thanks CL for copy ofAntiquity of man[4th ed. (1873)]; will read the modified or new parts.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   17 May 1873
letters.summary: Wishes to dedicate his memoir ["Monographie der GattungAnthracotherium",Paleontographica22 (1876): 131–347] to CD as founder of evolutionary theory.

letters.title: From Hermann Müller   19 May 1873
letters.summary:
PraisesExpression.

Reports on Fritz Müller’s observations of cross- and self-fertilisation. HM will cultivate the two forms [i.e., mainly self-fertilised and mainly cross-fertilised] in the way CD has described.

He continues his observation of wild flowers. Encloses drawing ofViola tricolorwith notes on its self-fertility.

letters.title: From Arthur Russell   19 May 1873
letters.deprecated: Arthur John Edward (Arthur) Russell, Lord Arthur Russell
letters.sender: Arthur John Edward (Arthur) Russell, Lord Arthur Russell
letters.summary: InVariationCD claims there are no distinct races of carp, but AR says that in Germany a peculiar and constant variety of carp has been bred.

letters.title: To V. O. Kovalevsky   21 May 1873
letters.summary:
VOK’s paper ["Osteology of Hyopotamidae",Proc. R. Soc. Lond.21 (1872–3): 147–65] appears a very valuable one.

Discusses work of VOK’s brother [Alexander] onSagittaand the ascidians.

letters.title: From Arthur Mostyn-Owen   21 May 1873
letters.summary:
Offers to exchange a water-colour portrait of CD, done, he believes, by Fanny Biddulph, for a copy ofDescent.

There has been a decrease of game-birds in the area.

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   22 May 1873
letters.summary:
Has no doubt he will find JJW’s address interesting.

Thinks same spot for nesting might prove attractive to birds, though they had had no intercommunication.

letters.title: From Friedrich Hildebrand   23 May 1873
letters.summary: Sends results of his observations of cross- and self-fertilisation ofHypecoum grandiflorumandEschscholzia californica[seeCross and self-fertilisation, pp. 331–2].

letters.title: From A. F. Baker   25 May 1873
letters.summary: Calls CD’s attention to the fact that Huxley’s view [inLessons in elementary physiology(1866)] of lymphatic fluid as overflow from blood supports CD’s view of secretion of tears inExpression.

letters.title: From Arthur Nicols   25 May 1873
letters.summary:
Thanks to CD his candidature for the Zoological Society has been entertained.

Observed a flamingo, at the Zoological Gardens, that vomited on a bustard in answer to the latter’s harsh cries.

letters.title: From Hermann Müller   27 May 1873
letters.summary: Poa annuashows putative evidence of nectar secretion in grasses. He will continue observations as CD requests.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   [before 28 May 1873]
letters.summary: Collecting information about antecedents of eminent men of science. Sends questionnaire.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   28 May 1873
letters.summary:
Comments about questionnaire CD completed for FG [for Galton’sEnglish men of science(1874)].

Describes his early interest in collecting and his education.

Asks about determining the mean heights of two groups of men.

letters.title: From Rudolf Hennig   28 May 1873
letters.summary: Wants a picture of CD for a book he is writing on the history of natural sciences.

letters.title: From Arthur Mostyn-Owen   28 May 1873
letters.summary: He will keep the portrait of CD.

letters.title: From William Harte   29 May 1873
letters.summary: Light sense in dogs.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   30 May 1873
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for completed questionnaire;

answers his query about determining mean heights of men.

letters.title: To Hermann Müller   30 May 1873
letters.summary: Further comments on HM’s [Befruchtung der Blumen(1873)].

letters.title: From László Dapsy   1 June 1873
letters.summary:
The Natural Philosophical Society [Academy of Sciences] will publish his translation ofOriginin August, beforeDescent.

A distinguished member of the Hungarian Parliament attacked CD’s theory. LD answered, and a controversy ensued.

LD has noted many signs of public support for CD.

letters.title: To Anton Dohrn   2 June [1873]
letters.summary: Thanks AD for kind review ofExpression. AD’s remarks on necessity of tracing development of functions are novel and valuable.

letters.title: To B. T. Lowne   3 June 1873
letters.summary:
Comments on BTL’s book [The philosophy of evolution(1873)].

"You are a bold man to speak in favour of pangenesis."

letters.title: From George Cupples   4 June 1873
letters.summary:
J. V. Carus’ lecture.

Edinburgh intellectual climate.

Ralph Waldo Emerson’s visit to Edinburgh.

J. H. Stirling did not write anonymous review ofExpressioninEdinburgh Review. Suggests T. Spencer Baynes of St Andrews. [? T. S. Baynes, "Darwin on expression", 137 (1873): 492–528.]

letters.title: From A. A. L. P. Cochrane   7 June 1873
letters.summary: Invites CD on a voyage to the western coast of North and South America.

letters.title: To George Cupples   7 June [1873]
letters.summary:
Thanks for report on J. V. Carus’ lecture.

Glad to hear suspicion about J. H. Stirling groundless.

CD has not seen R. W. Emerson. In last two or three years has seen several Yankees. Saw a good deal of the Nortons [Charles Eliot and Susan Ridley Sedgwick].

letters.title: From Anton Dohrn   7 June 1873
letters.summary:
News of Naples Zoological Station developments.

His remarks on physiology in theAcademywere aimed at Prof. Ludwig and his school.

The usual "exact" methods in experimental physiology want only a little pushing to put an end to superstition.

Recounts how he had worked out the explanation ofRhizocephalamorphology via theAnelasma– an example of both the power of inheritance and the power of genealogical investigation. R. Kossman’s work has now confirmed AD’s explanation.

letters.title: To A. A. L. P. Cochrane   [after 7 June 1873]
letters.summary: Is obliged because of health to decline the invitation [see8938] to make a voyage on the Admiral’s ship. "… I must rest contented with past memories …"

letters.title: From W. P. Ayres   8 June 1873
letters.summary: Has been discussing spontaneous generation with William Robinson of theGarden. Reports having found grubs that developed in an undamaged, hard-boiled egg. Has similarly treated eggs if CD wants to investigate.

letters.title: To László Dapsy   9 June 1873
letters.summary:
Is glad to hear LD’s translation [ofOrigin(1873–4)] progresses well.

Offers to send a photograph of himself.

letters.title: From Hermann Müller   10 June 1873
letters.summary: Reports on insects fertilisingViola tricolorand on the fertilisation of the two wild forms [seeCross and self-fertilisation, p. 124 n., 125].

letters.title: From Albert Günther   11 June 1873
letters.summary: Apologises for having given CD some unreliable information.

letters.title: To C. H. Blackley   14 June [1873]
letters.summary: Thanks for sendingExperimental researches. He will read it as soon as he finishes a book in hand. [See8965.]

letters.title: To Albert Günther   14 June [1873]
letters.summary: Thanks AG for information [unspecified]; so trifling an error will not alter his opinion that AG is "the most accurate of men".

letters.title: From Charles Hinton   15 June 1873
letters.summary: Observations on expression.

letters.title: From Federico Delpino   18 June 1873
letters.summary: Sends information onLathyrus odoratus,Phaseolus multiflorusandPisum sativum.

letters.title: To E. W. Lane   23 June 1873
letters.summary: Thanks EWL for his book about hydropathy [Old medicine and new(1873)].

letters.title: From C. F. Martins   23 June 1873
letters.summary:
CM and Henri Sicard have given what CM thinks is the first zoology course in France based on descent of species.

In Rome he was struck by ancient Greek statues of mythical figures which use the idea of environmental influence. Ascribes these ideas to both CD and Lamarck.

letters.title: To J. S. Burdon Sanderson   24 June 1873
letters.summary: Wishes JSBS to look over an abstract of hisDroseraexperiments and to answer some questions on it.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [before 26 June 1873]
letters.summary: Has discussed with E. E. Klein about the purchase of a Hartnack microscope from Paris.

letters.title: From J. S. Burdon Sanderson   25 June 1873
letters.summary:
Informs CD of the effects of certain salts and other chemicals on animals.

Comments on CD’s results withDrosera. Suggests some experiments.

letters.title: To Federico Delpino   25 June [1873]
letters.summary:
Discusses role of insects in crossing varieties ofLathyrus odoratusand other species.

Comments on Hermann Müller [Die Befruchtung der Blumen(1873)],

and Anton Kerner ["Die Schutzmittel des Pollens",Ber. Naturwiss. Med. Ver. Innsbruck, 3 (1873): 100–68].

Admires FD’s work on anemophilous plants.

letters.title: From A. C. Smith   25 June 1873
letters.summary: Wonders whether CD has any idea how the cuckoo manages to match its eggs to those of its host; believes it possible that the diet of the nestling cuckoo, which varies with its host, may affect its behaviour and the colour of its eggs.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [before 26 June 1873]
letters.summary: Sends FD £5 for the loan of his microscope.

letters.title: To J. S. Burdon Sanderson   26 June [1873]
letters.summary:
Would welcome JSBS visit to discussDrosera. Nitrogenous fluids can act as ferments only if they act merely by exciting molecular movement in adjoining molecules.

Glass and cotton excite movement and cause cell contents to change visibly. Huxley coming to see this phenomenon.

Studied effect of poisons 12 or 15 years ago to see whether the action was similar to that on nervous tissue.

letters.title: From J. D. Hague   26 June 1873
letters.summary: Confirms previous observations on ants [see8788].

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   26 June 1873
letters.summary: Is tired of inaction and so is leaving for Egypt and the East.

letters.title: From T. F. Cheeseman   27 June 1873
letters.summary: Sends his paper on fertilisation of the New Zealand species of the orchidPterostylis[Trans. & Proc. New Zealand Inst.4 (1871): 270–84].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   28 June 1873
letters.summary:
Thanks forDionaea.

George Bentham’s last Linnean Society [Presidential] Address [Proc. Linn. Soc. Lond.(1873): viii–xxix]. Admires it greatly.

CD’s recent work leads him to a different theory [from GB’s] on the separation of the sexes of plants.

Huxley has been at Down working with CD onDrosera– very helpful.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   28 June [1873]
letters.summary: Thanks for the extract from the American paper.

letters.title: From Friedrich Max Müller   29 June 1873
letters.summary:
Sends three lectures on the origin of human language [see8962].

Although a "sincere admirer", he differs with CD on the relation of human to so-called animal language.

letters.title: To W. H. Flower   30 June 1873
letters.summary: Thanks for sending WHF’s lecture, ‘On palaeontological evidence of the modifications of animal forms’ (Flower 1873).

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   30 June 1873
letters.summary:
Leaves Wednesday with Huxley for holiday.

Family news.

He too thinks well of Bentham’s address.

Asa Gray elected Foreign F.R.S.

G. J. Allman is being proposed for Royal Medal by JDH and Huxley.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   1 July [1873]
letters.summary:
Agrees with JDH on G. J. Allman’s work. Approves of JDH’s text proposing GJA for Royal Medal.

Will be proud to see General Richard Strachey at Down – a truly great man.

Specimens ofDroseraare waiting to be examined.

letters.title: From Hermann Müller   1 July 1873
letters.summary:
Sends a note on R. Caspary’s observations ofCorydalisself-fertilisation [seeCross and self-fertilisation, p. 331].

Has begun his experiments on the self- and cross-fertilised flowers.

letters.title: To Friedrich Max Müller   3 July 1873
letters.summary:
Thanks FMM for his "Lectures [on Mr Darwin’s philosophy of language",Fraser’s Mag.n.s. 7 (1873): 525–41, 659–78].

CD is not worthy to be FMM’s adversary as he knows very little about language and, being fully convinced man is descended from some lower animal, he is forced to believea priorithat language has developed from inarticulate cries.

letters.title: From J. E. Boehm   4 July 1873
letters.summary: Reports cases from his family of inheritance of turning in sleep, sleep-walking at full moon, and eyes giving out red light at early age.

letters.title: To C. H. Blackley   5 July [1873]
letters.summary:
Comments on CHB’s book [Experimental researches on catarrhus aestivus – hay-fever or hay-asthma(1873)].

Explains that some pollens are wind-blown while others depend on insects for dispersal. Effect of pollen on skin and mucous membrane astonishing. Sends a book [M. Wyman,Autumnal catarrh(1872)].

letters.title: To George King   6 July 1873
letters.summary: Thanks for specimens and information about worm-castings.

letters.title: From C. H. Blackley   7 July 1873
letters.summary:
Thanks for copy of Wyman’s book.

His own recent researches [on pollen] at high altitudes were inspired by CD’s account inJournal of researchesof distances dust may travel.

letters.title: From John Farr   7 July 1873
letters.summary: Would like a photograph of CD.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   8 July 1873
letters.summary: Corrects chemical concentrations CD has been using [in insectivorous plant experimentation].

letters.title: From Armand de Quatrefages   8 July 1873
letters.deprecated: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.sender: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.summary: CD’s nomination to French Academy fails again.

letters.title: From J. B. Dunbar-Brander   [before 9 July 1873]
letters.summary:
Offers different explanations [from CD’s inExpression] for movements of dogs after voiding, and for their turning around before lying down.

CD is also wrong in saying hares do not cry except when they suffer.

letters.title: From Bushell Anningson   9 July 1873
letters.summary:
Comments on the form and function of a muscle in the rectal region of animals.

Discusses the scratching action of dogs.

letters.title: To Armand de Quatrefages   9 July [1873]
letters.deprecated: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.recipient: Jean Louis Armand (Armand de Quatrefages) Quatrefages de Bréau
letters.summary: Thanks correspondent for his kind and generous exertions [to get CD elected to French Academy?].

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   9 July [1873]
letters.summary: Forwards photograph, sent by [J. L. G.] Krefft, of a chrysalis attached to its food-plant; the chrysalis has adjusted its colour remarkably.

letters.title: From John Farr   10 July 1873
letters.summary: Thanks for photograph.

letters.title: From C. H. Blackley   11 July 1873
letters.summary: Thanks for suggestion to try effect of dry heat on pollen and for other new information on pollen. Will begin new experiments soon, hoping to cure hay-fever.

letters.title: From A. W. Bennett   12 July 1873
letters.summary: Believes some flowers fail to produce seed because of the access of too great a quantity of pollen. Asks for CD’s opinion and references.

letters.title: To Edward Frankland   12 July 1873
letters.summary: Seeks the assistance of a professional chemist in securing a qualitative analysis of the fluid secreted by the glands ofDroserawhich have the power of dissolving animal matter out of the bodies of insects. [See8979.]

letters.title: To Gerard Krefft   12 July [1873]
letters.summary:
Thanks JLGK for photos of natives of Queensland.

Asks if he can observe whether worms throw up castings in wet weather.

letters.title: From J. T. Moggridge   12 July 1873
letters.summary: Sends his paper onOphrys insectifera, translated into German by H. G. Reichenbach [Abh. Kais. Leopold.-Carol. Dtsch. Akad. Naturforsch.33 (1870) no. 3], which shows the intermediates betweenO. araniferaandO. apifera. He has since gathered information on variation inOphrys.

letters.title: From Gerard Krefft   [after 12 July 1873]
letters.summary: JLGK’s public advocacy of Darwinism brings him into numerous arguments.

letters.title: To Henry Edwards   15 July [1873]
letters.summary: HE’s facts about the Mexican ant [Myrmecocystus mexicanus] are "most wonderful & interesting".

letters.title: From Edward Frankland   15 July 1873
letters.summary: Sends sodium carbonate forDroseraexperiments. Will try to determine what the solvent is.

letters.title: To the Royal Institution of Great Britain 15 July 1873
letters.summary: Thanks for the three essays: although they are beyond his scope, they seem to him very interesting.

letters.title: To Edward Frankland   16 July [1873]
letters.summary: Thanks EF for his offer of assistance. Could the viscid secretions [in glands ofDrosera] contain pepsin? Will the sodium carbonate render the testing of organic matter difficult? [See8979.] Will send the fluid in a fortnight.

letters.title: From M. C. Stanley   16 July 1873
letters.deprecated: Mary Catherine Stanley, countess of Derby
letters.sender: Mary Catherine Stanley, countess of Derby
letters.summary: Sends a bottle containing fish which Lord Arthur Russell had promised to send.

letters.title: From Edward Frankland   17 July 1873
letters.summary: Is going to Switzerland, so analysis ofDroserawashings will be delayed. Agrees with CD that solvent is probably pepsin.

letters.title: To Edward Frankland   18 July [1873]
letters.summary: Agrees to delay sending the fluid [from the glands ofDrosera] until early October. Will try suggestion about pepsin. [See8981.]

letters.title: To ?   18 July [1873?]
letters.summary: Comments on ability of recipient to move his scalp.

letters.title: From John Chapman   19 July 1873
letters.summary:
Asks CD to meet with Dr Wild to discuss theWestminster Review, which CD has supported.

Quotes from Alexander Kennedy on Maori observations on competition between native New Zealand birds and introduced bees for nectar of tree blossoms.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   21 July [1873]
letters.summary: JVC’s travel plans in England. Hopes to visit CD.

letters.title: From J. T. Moggridge   22 July 1873
letters.summary:
He will repeat the experiments in which CD found that formic acid vapour killed seeds [see8866]. John Lindley describes effects of other acids on germination.

He has tabulated the large amount of variation in EnglishOphrys apifera.

letters.title: ToNature   [before 24 July 1873]
letters.summary: Sends a letter from J. D. Hague confirming his earlier observation [see8788] of frightened behaviour of ants when they come upon dead ants. CD had asked for confirmation because J. T. Moggridge had suggested that the ants’ behaviour was alarm at the scent of the observer’s fingers.

letters.title: From J. T. Moggridge   24 July 1873
letters.summary: CD has clarified the way to conduct the formic acid experiment.

letters.title: To Armand Sabatier   24 July 1873
letters.summary: Thanks forÉtudes sur la coeur et la circulation centrale dans la série des vertébrés(Studies on the heart and the central circulation in the vertebrate series) (Sabatier 1873).

letters.title: To J. S. Burdon Sanderson   25 July 1873
letters.summary: Describes his recent work onDroseradigestion of organic materials, e.g., albumen and gelatin. Edward Frankland has given CD a rough test for pepsin. Some plant extracts cause as much inflection as meat. Has found some reversible inflection with heat and perhaps some heat rigor. Has measured the extreme sensitivity ofDroserawith very dilute solution of ammonium phosphate.

letters.title: From J. S. Burdon Sanderson   28 July [1873]
letters.summary: A hasty answer to CD’s letter [8987] of 25 July. Mentions Dr Osler’s observations on behaviour of colourless blood corpuscles in solutions of sodium and potassium salts of same strength.

letters.title: From Mary Treat   28 July 1873
letters.summary: Reports in detail on her experiments withDrosera. Finds she was mistaken in thinkingD. filiformiscaptured only small insects.

letters.title: From J. T. Moggridge   30 July 1873
letters.summary: His preliminary results with formic acid show that it inhibits germination of several kinds of seed. It also inhibits growing of mildew, which he speculates may facilitate germination.

letters.title: From Frank Chance   31 July – 7 August 1873
letters.summary:
Gives some observations on ponies’ becoming white in winter;

on skin pigmentation and the effects of heat;

on the bristling of the hair in man.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   31 July [1873]
letters.summary: Has three common garden plants of which he needs to know correct names; will send specimens as soon as he hears JDH is back.

letters.title: From C. L. Brace   [August? 1873]
letters.summary: Reports that the ability to move ears is common among the Sioux.

letters.title: From F. J. Wedgwood   [August–September? 1873]
letters.summary: Notes criticising Max Müller’s views on language and Darwinism.

letters.title: From Thomas Belt   2 August 1873
letters.summary: Sends extracts, from his forthcoming book [The naturalist in Nicaragua(1874)], about the secretion by plants of honey to attract the protection of ants. Invites CD’s comments.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   2 August [1873]
letters.summary:
Regrets he cannot receive JVC at Down on Monday as he would then be too unwell to travel on Tuesday, when he must leave for a visit [to Abinger Hall, according to theJournal].

Has been working hard onDroseraandDionaea. His next book will be on these plants and not, as he had intended, "On evil effects of Inter breeding".

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   2 August [1873]
letters.summary: Thinks highly of GHD’s article [probably "On beneficial restrictions to liberty of marriage",Contemp. Rev.22 (1873): 412–26]. A good omen for the future.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   3 August 1873
letters.summary:
Returned last night. Huxley, left at Baden Baden, remarkably well.

Would like to come to Down with Strachey.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   4 August [1873]
letters.summary:
Starts tomorrow for visit to Farrer and Effie [Euphemia Farrer, daughter of Hensleigh Wedgwood]. Has not done such a feat [i.e., staying as a guest of someone outside the immediate family?] for 25 years.

Has been half killing himself withDrosera.

letters.title: To Thomas Belt   [7 August 1873]
letters.summary:
Discusses utility of plant secretions to ants.

Will read TB’s book when published [The naturalist in Nicaragua(1874)].

letters.title: From J. O. W. Haweis   8 August [1873]
letters.summary: On inheritance of gesture.

letters.title: From Gerard Krefft   8 August 1873
letters.summary:
Sends paper to be published inSydney Mailon primitive man.

Sends lists of earth [castings] made by worms [seeEarthworms, p. 127],

and a catalogue of Australian Lepidoptera.

letters.title: To Frank Chance   10 August [1873]
letters.summary:
Thanks [FC] for his letter concerning a pony changing colour during the winter,

and remarks on the erection of human body hair, goose-skin, and the influence of colour and temperature on skin.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   10 August [1873]
letters.summary:
Asks THF to examine old flowers ofCoronillafor holes bored by bees.

Is investigating whether drops of water injure leaves.

letters.title: From Raphael Meldola   11 August 1873
letters.summary:
Encloses a copy of his paper on mimicry [Proc. Zool. Soc. Lond.(1873): 153–61].

Asks whether large variations are more often limited to one sex than slight ones.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   12 August 1873
letters.summary:
Observations on effect of water on leaves.

Coronilla.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   12 August [1873]
letters.summary:
Further observations concerning the fertilisation ofCoronillaby bees.

Reflections concerning the influence of cultivation (i.e., ploughing) upon variation.

letters.title: To Mary Treat   12 August 1873
letters.summary:
Thanks MT for information onDrosera filiformis[see8989].

Warns her against publishing statement aboutDroserabending towards flies or meat that they have not touched.

Will send his book [Insectivorous plants] when published.

letters.title: From J. S. Burdon Sanderson   13 August [1873]
letters.summary:
Answers CD’s questions of 25 July [8987] about temperatures at which cold-blooded animals are killed.

Doubts heat rigor was induced inDrosera. Gives his view of the relation of excitability to increase in temperature.

Suggests experiment to show that electrical changes in plant are the same as in animal muscle and nerve [seeInsectivorous plants, p. 318].

letters.title: From E. T. Gardner   13 August 1873
letters.summary: Sends CD an excerpt fromN. Y. Tribune[missing] about an account by W. D. Whitney, of Yale, of scientific work in Colorado.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   13 August 1873
letters.summary:
Asks JDH why so many plants are protected by a thin layer of waxy matter or with fine hairs.

Wrote to John Smith for a plant ofOxalis sensitiva, but it has not acted well.

Rejoices over Ayrton’s retirement. Hopes W. P. Adam, his successor, is a good sort of man.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   13 August [1873]
letters.summary:
Thanks RM for his paper on mimicry.

Cannot answer RM’s query because he believes it impossible to define large variations.

Believes monstrosities are generally injurious and are not often, if ever, taken advantage of in nature.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   14 August [1873]
letters.summary: Has foundLathyrus maritimaon the cliffs near Barmouth.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   14 August 1873
letters.summary: Thinks THF has solved the mystery ofCoronilla.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   14 August 1873
letters.summary:
Has observed CD’s points. Except for leaves ofNelumbium, would have supposed both wax and hairs were connected with absorption or respiratory functions. May subserve some function connected with rays of sun. Watering most prejudicial in the hot sun: a splendid subject for experiments.

Adam is a good man.

letters.title: To J. S. Burdon Sanderson   15 August 1873
letters.summary: Thinks it would be worth while testing for electrical changes in the leaves of insectivorous plants.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   15 August [1873]
letters.summary:
Observations on bees’ biting holes inLathyrus.

Suggests an experiment FD could carry out withDrosera.

CD is working onMimosa, and "everything has turned out as perversely as possible".

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [16 or 17 August 1873]
letters.summary: Gives his opinion on why tubes of peas split to the right of the loose stamens [inLathyrus sylvestris].

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   18 [August 1873]
letters.summary: Pollination and floral structure ofLathyrus. Asks where bees bite through the flowers.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   19 August 1873
letters.summary: Asks JDH to inquire of gardeners at Kew what they think about injury to plants from watering during sunshine. Wishes to experiment. He is already convinced that drops of water donotact as burning lenses.

letters.title: To C. J. Plumptre   19 August [1873?]
letters.summary: Agrees François Delsarte’s view [that the eyes do not show emotion, only indicate the object of it], is probably wrong.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   21 August 1873
letters.summary:
He and Strachey will arrive on Saturday.

Is aghast at thought of being questioned on injury to plants by watering. Fears he will be considered an ignorant Director of Kew.

letters.title: To Herbert Spencer   21 August [1873]
letters.summary: Thanks for copy of HS’sDescriptive sociology[1873].

letters.title: From W. G. Walker   21 August 1873
letters.summary: African elephants cry when distressed.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [22 August 1873]
letters.summary: Experiments withMimosa.

letters.title: From W. D. Fox   22 August [1873]
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for a copy ofExpression. Is always interested in CD’s work, but finds himself diverging from some of his leading ideas.

P.S. Has found shedding of toenails in a nephew as well.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [22 August 1873]
letters.summary: Will arrive at Orpington by usual train.

letters.title: From J. T. Moggridge   22 August 1873
letters.summary:
He has added carbolic acid to the seed germination experiments and sends more results on the effect of formic acid. Formic acid inhibits mildew on dough but not on seeds.

Mildew never grows in ants’ nests.

Sends an account, from theMishnah, of grain stored by ants.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin  [25 August 1873]
letters.summary: Regrets that "our brush theory" is wrong.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [25 August 1873]
letters.summary: Experiments onMimosa; effects of immersion.

letters.title: From Theodor Gomperz   25 August 1873
letters.summary: Comments onExpression. Suggests solutions to some of CD’s unresolved problems. Widens the "Principle of Association", whereby gestures associated with one emotion can also come to accompany a second emotion. Confirms the occurrence of blushing in the dark. Considers CD’s use of the "principle of Conservation of Force"; outlines its larger applications.

letters.title: From Hermann Müller   25 August 1873
letters.summary:
Fritz Müller is now working on the Brazilian honey-bees (MeliponaandTrigona).

HM thanks CD for fertilisation references.

letters.title: From Richard Strachey   25 August 1873
letters.summary: Reports that grapes are spoiled by rain at vintage time and that damaged grapes, whose "bloom" is not intact, are particularly susceptible.

letters.title: To J. S. Burdon Sanderson   27 August 1873
letters.summary:
CD can provide leaves ofDionaeaif JSBS wishes to investigate electric currents in them.

His experiments show that the digestive action ofDroseraseems like that of true digestion.

letters.title: To J. T. Moggridge   27 August 1873
letters.summary: Comments on experiments of touching seeds with acid.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   29 August 1873
letters.summary:
Has returned from Egypt because of trouble with his eyes.

Has read George Darwin’s article on consanguineous marriage.

letters.title: From E. C. Rye   29 August 1873
letters.summary: Reports a paper by H. von Kiesenwetter [Berliner Entomol. Z.16 (1872): 370] on theMalthodes, some species of which appear to have a sex ratio with females greatly outnumbering males, suggesting the occurrence of parthenogenesis.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   30 August – 14 September [1873]
letters.summary: Experiments onMimosa.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   30 August 1873
letters.summary: Identifies three plants sent by CD.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   30 August 1873
letters.summary: Talks of his attempts to describe the course of descent for a part of the animal kingdom, and thanks CD for his help and support.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   31 August [1873]
letters.summary: Going to the Ashanti war asTimescorrespondent.

letters.title: To Gerard Krefft   [September 1873]
letters.summary:
Thanks for observations on worm-castings and for JLGK’s amusing letter.

Wants to know whether species ofEucalyptusare dichogamous. [The P.S. onEucalyptusmay be part of another letter to another correspondent.]

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   1 September [1873]
letters.summary: Has been in bed for some days with ugly head symptoms. "We are a poor lot."

letters.title: To Theodor Gomperz   1 September [1873]
letters.summary: Will reread and consider TG’s letter when his health improves.

letters.title: From Andrew Clark   3 September 1873
letters.summary: Diagnosis of CD’s illness; prescribed diet.

letters.title: To W. W. Baxter   4 September 1873
letters.summary: Orders list of chemical salts. Ashamed to order from Hopkins and Williams because they charge him such an extremely low rate.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [4 September 1873]
letters.summary: Asks FD to bring any book that gives the affinities of the various earths, alkalis and metals.

letters.title: To W. W. Baxter   5 September [1873]
letters.summary: Orders salts of various metals; thinks chlorides (where soluble) would be better than nitrates.

letters.title: From Gerard Krefft   6 September 1873
letters.summary: Proud of CD’s good opinion of him. He worked in a merchant’s office in Germany for many years. Emigrated to Australia as a gold-digger and took up natural history after he was 30.

letters.title: To James Crichton-Browne   7 September [1873]
letters.summary: Thanks JC-B for volume ofAsylumreports and paper on epilepsy. Seems clear from reports that physiology of brain will soon be largely understood.

letters.title: To W. W. Baxter   8 September [1873]
letters.summary: Requests chemicals forDroseraexperiments. Lists 12 acids tried so far.

letters.title: To J. S. Burdon Sanderson   9 September [1873]
letters.summary:
Pleased JSBS has decided to work onDrosera; sends plants. Does not know whether thermo-electric pile could detect temperature change when leaves close.

CD’s experiment with very weak hydrochloric acid repeated with success: the plants digest albumen more quickly.

letters.title: To T. F. Cheeseman   9 September [1873]
letters.summary: Thanks TFC for his extremely interesting paper ["On the fertilisation of the New Zealand species ofPterostyles",Trans. & Proc. N. Z. Inst.5 (1872): 352–7]. Has no doubt his explanation [of the fertilisation mechanism] is correct. The case is analogous to that of theCypripediumthough TFC’s case is much more curious.

letters.title: From M. D. Conway   10 September [1873]
letters.summary: Comparative study of "ethnical scriptures" shows that natural selection has operated in the evolution of religion.

letters.title: From W. S. Wade   11 September 1873
letters.summary: Reports case of a man with an eyelid abnormality that apparently was acquired in infancy but was inherited by his children.

letters.title: To M. D. Conway   12 September [1873]
letters.summary: Thanks for strange debate, which CD returns. Principle of evolution has first-rate supporters in [Edward Sylvester?] Morse and Theodore Nicholas Gill.

letters.title: From James Crichton-Browne   12 September 1873
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for his praise ofWest Riding Asylum Medical Reports.

Hopes CD will come to Asylum if he attends BAAS meeting at Bradford.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   12 September [1873]
letters.summary:
Thanks JDH and Thiselton-Dyer for useful information.

Is surprisedMimosa albidaisnotsensitive to water. Asks that they try again, or lend it to him.

Remembers a walk in Brazil in great bed ofMimosa.

After JDH left, CD was very bad, with much loss of memory and severe shocks continually passing through his brain.

letters.title: To J. S. Burdon Sanderson   13 September [1873]
letters.summary: Thanks JSBS for telegraphing his results, which seem very remarkable; feels he should now tryDrosera.

letters.title: To J. S. Burdon Sanderson   14 September [1873]
letters.summary:
Very pleased at JSBS’s discovery ["On the electrical phenomena which accompany the contractions of the leaf ofDionaea muscipula",Rep. BAAS43 (1873): 133].

Asks for pure animal substances [proteins] forDroseraexperiments. His other sources have been T. L. Brunton, Edward Frankland, W. A. Miller (now dead), and Hoffmann of Berlin [A. W. von Hofmann?].

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [15–18 September 1873]
letters.summary: FD has asked J. B. Sanderson about Mucin.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   16 September 1873
letters.summary:
Mimosatoo far gone to send now.

CD’s marjoram is the common [Origanum]vulgare, not the pot herb.

On the water injury, Thiselton-Dyer and he may have used too fine a spray, but plant is insensitive.

Horribly angry at P. G. Tait’s letter inNature[8 (1873): 381–2].

Tyndall writes that he is strong – the next number ofNaturewill prove it.

G. Henslow is much better.

JDH leaves for Bradford [BAAS meeting] tomorrow.

Rejoices at CD’s success withDrosera; longs to be atNepenthes.

letters.title: To E. S. Morse   16 September 1873
letters.summary: Thanks for ESM’s paper ["On the systematic position of the Brachiopoda",Proc. Boston Soc. Nat. Hist.15 (1873): 315–72]. "What a wonderful change … to look at these ""shells"" as ""worms""."

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   18 September [1873]
letters.summary: JJW is quite at liberty to use CD’s name as patron of cat show.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [19 September 1873]
letters.summary: Reports that S. W. Moore may be able to provide various substances for CD’s research on the digestive power ofDrosera(sundew).

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   19 September [1873]
letters.summary:
Obliged for information onMimosa albida; if a vigorous plant behaves as JDH says, CD’s notions are all knocked on the head.

Anxious to read Tyndall’s answer to Tait [Nature8 (1873): 399].

Droserastory too long for his strength. Essentially the leaves act just like stomach of an animal.

Burdon Sanderson will give some grand facts at BAAS aboutDionaea.

Offers to help JDH withNepenthesexperiments. Finds experimental work always takes twice as much time as anticipated.

letters.title: From S. V. Wood Jr to Charles Lyell   19 September 1873
letters.summary: Thanks for proofs of the Supplement to Crag Mollusca. Sends crab apples.

letters.title: To E. A. Darwin   20 September 1873
letters.summary:
Consults about the wisdom of Frank’s becoming CD’s assistant rather than practising medicine.

Outlines his finances.

[Copy in EAD’s hand.]

letters.title: ToNature   20 September [1873]
letters.summary: CD, in commenting on Wyville Thomson’s "Notes from theChallenger" [Nature8 (1873): 347–9], recapitulates his work on rudimentary male cirripedes [Living Cirripedia], especially the complementary males attached to hermaphrodites. Offers an explanation, on evolutionary grounds, of their function and size.

letters.title: To W. W. Baxter   21 September [1873]
letters.summary: Requests 6 2oz bottles with corks. Folic acid produces remarkable effect. Orders hydriodic acid.

letters.title: To Edward Frankland   21 September [1873]
letters.summary: Although CD’s experiments with pepsin were unsuccessful, he observed that the glands [ofDrosera] as far as acid is concerned act just as the stomach of a mammal. Further experiments detailed. The secretion must contain something analogous to pepsin. [See9062.]

letters.title: From Edward Frankland   22 September 1873
letters.summary: CD’s discovery of acidity ofDroserasecretion is interesting. EF explains how hydrochloric acid can be detected and identified. [SeeInsectivorous plants, p. 88.]

letters.title: To Edward Frankland   23 September 1873
letters.summary: Will follow EF’s suggestions as to securing purity of fibrin.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [23 September 1873]
letters.summary:
Thanks for C. E. Norton’s address.

Tyndall’s answer [Nature8 (1873): 399] has surprised and disappointed him;

great trouble in announcing Tyndall’s election as President Elect [of BAAS] yesterday. Tyndall may throw up the Presidency. Spottiswoode and JDH have concocted a letter telling him the facts.

A very poor dull meeting. Comments on papers by W. C. Williamson, Clerk Maxwell, David Ferrier, Burdon Sanderson [Rep. BAAS43: lxx–xci, 23–32,126–7, 131–3].

Has heard Huxley is back quite well.

letters.title: From John Murray   23 September [1873]
letters.summary: Sends CD an account that has the novelty of having a balance against CD.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   24 September 1873
letters.summary:
Discusses apple specimens received from CL; reversion to crab state. Cites passage on subject inVariation.

Comments on letter from Mr Wood on inheritance in fruit-trees.

Would like to cross flowers of "Hawthornden" with many distinct varieties.

letters.title: To John Murray   24 September [1873]
letters.summary:
CD will have to make heavy corrections inExpressionandDescentif there ever is a new edition of either.

Will soon begin another book [Insectivorous plants].

It and a second one [Cross and self-fertilisation] will sell only "very specially".

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [25 September – 3 October 1873]
letters.summary:
Criticises CD’s letter toNature["Complemental males in certain cirripedes",Collected papers2: 177–82].

On the elimination of useless parts.

GHD fails to see the point of CD’s use of the law of distribution about a mean.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   25 September [1873]
letters.summary: EAD sees advantages to Frank’s becoming CD’s assistant.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   25 September 1873
letters.summary:
Comments on EH’sNatürliche Schöpfungsgeschichte[4th ed.].

Has written paper on rudimentary structures ["Complemental males of certain cirripedes", (1873)Collected papers2: 177–82].

Edward Morse thinks brachiopods should be classed with annelids ["The systematic position of the Brachiopoda",Proc. Boston Soc. Nat. Hist.15 (1873): 315–73].

letters.title: From John Murray   25 September [1873]
letters.summary:
Acknowledges CD’s cheque.

Sends CD cheque for profits onOrchidsand a statement of stock on hand of CD’s works [missing].

OriginandExpressionsales are stagnant.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   25 September 1873
letters.summary:
Seedling vigour resulting from crossing of parents.

CD to publish work on insectivorous plants.

letters.title: From Hubert Airy   26 [September–November 1873]
letters.summary: The Royal Society referees have rejected HA’s phyllotaxy paper, and it will not be printed inPhilosophical Transactions. HA is not sorry for he has found new facts which limit the applicability of his views. Now believes that the original leaf arrangement was not necessarily always two-ranked but rather that existing arrangements have developed from a variety of forms with differing numbers of leaf-ranks.

letters.title: From W. W. Keen   26 September 1873
letters.summary: Sends corrections ofDescentandExpression.

letters.title: From Edward Frankland   27 September 1873
letters.summary: Has sent CD some pure distilled water for hisDroseraexperiments.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   27 September 1873
letters.summary:
Had read Tyndall’s letter [Nature8 (1873): 399] – awfully savage, but certainly a great mistake to print it.

Thinks JDH will think better of Clerk Maxwell’s paper after he reads it.

Asks whether JDH could find out for him the temperature of rain in very hot countries.

letters.title: From M. T. Masters   27 September 1873
letters.summary: Seeks an interview with CD to discuss reorganisation ofGardeners’ Chronicle.

letters.title: To Edward Frankland   29 September 1873
letters.summary: Is sending washings of 445 leaves in EF’s distilled water with 20 grains of carbonate of soda. Details of the difficulties and complications involved.

letters.title: To M. T. Masters   29 September [1873]
letters.summary: CD refuses an interview because of a severe headache, but wishes all success to theGardeners’ Chronicle.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [30 September 1873]
letters.summary: He is travelling overnight by train from London to Pantlludw and will wake A. R. Ruck with a morningade on his flute.

letters.title: To Frederick Allen’s agent   [October 1873]
letters.summary: Has heard that Mr Allen wishes to let his house and thinks it probable that it would suit his son [Francis]. Asks whether he may have refusal of it.

letters.title: To J. S. Burdon Sanderson   1 October [1873]
letters.summary: Hears from Frank [Darwin] thatDroserabehaves perversely. Suggests that motor influence may move longitudinally away from the excited glands.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [1 October 1873]
letters.summary: Discusses his health following a visit to Dr C[lark?]. Has made an appointment for CD.

letters.title: To Karl Marx   1 October 1873
letters.summary: Thanks KM for gift of his "great work on Capital" [2d German ed. ofDas Kapital]. Wishes he understood more of "the deep & important subject of political Economy".

letters.title: From S. W. Moore   [1 October 1873]
letters.summary: Information for CD’s use in investigating digestion byDrosera.

letters.title: From Emma Wuttke   1 October 1873
letters.summary: Sends tracing of ancient Egyptian illustration of dogs and cattle.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [before 3 October 1873]
letters.summary: Sends CD a draft of a letter toNature[see9087], which he thinks expresses CD’s meaning.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   3 October [1873]
letters.summary: CD thinks GHD’s letter is an excellent clarification [of CD’s conjectural view on the elimination of useless parts in species], but does not want to publish it as his [CD’s] own. Asks GHD to think carefully before he publishes it.

letters.title: From S. W. Moore   3 October 1873
letters.summary: Sends formula for pure pepsin for experiments on digestion ofDrosera, and information on legumin. Will send chlorophyll soon.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   5 October 1873
letters.summary:
Has decided to send the letter ["Variation of organs",Nature8 (1873): 505].

Writes of his poor health and problems of settling in at Trinity.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   6 October 1873
letters.summary:
Mimosa prostrata, described by John Lindley asM. marginata, native of Brazil.

Who supplies CD with distilled water and chemicals?

letters.title: To Edward Frankland   7 October [1873]
letters.summary: Requests a piece of the most sensitive litmus paper in order to test the secretions of minute hairs of plants which catch minute flies. [See9098.]

letters.title: From S. W. Moore   7 October 1873
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for copies of his books.

Sends chlorophyll extract [for CD’s work onDroseradigestion].

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   8 October 1873
letters.summary:
On CD’s paper ["Complemental males of certain cirripedes",Collected papers2: 177–82].

Comments on paper by W. H. Dallinger and J. J. Drysdale ["Life history of a Cercomonad",Mon. Microsc. J.10 (1873): 53–8].

Discusses origin of life, the Gastraea theory and concept that primary germ layers are homologous in all animals. Notes similar views of E. Ray Lankester ["On the primitive cell-layers of the embryo",Ann. & Mag. Nat. Hist.4th ser. 11 (1873): 321–38].

Reception of Darwinism in Germany.

letters.title: To Alexander Bain   9 October 1873
letters.summary:
Thanks AB for his review ofExpression[May 1873, inThe senses and the intellect, 3d ed. (1874), pp. 697–714]. Admits vagueness of some points. Has never grasped AB’s principle of spontaneity. But, as they look at everything so differently, it is not likely that they should agree closely.

A recent review by T. S. Baynes, [Edinburgh Rev.137 (1873): 492–528] is "magnificently contemptuous" toward CD and many others.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   10 October 1873
letters.summary:
Asks for details about microscope parts.

Wants FD to ask Hooker for species ofDesmodium; CD believes he has found new movements.

Also ask whether Hooker hasDrosophyllum.

letters.title: From Edward Frankland   10 October 1873
letters.summary: The results of EF’s tests for acids in the secretion ofDroseraare largely negative [seeInsectivorous plants, p. 88].

letters.title: To W. H. Leggett   10 October [1873]
letters.summary: Has not seen number ofBotanical Bulletinwith account ofApocynum.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [11 October 1873]
letters.summary: Has got a cold, so will not go to Kew. Wrote to Hartnack about price of microscopes and describes own model. Told Hooker about Tisley Spiller’s microscope in Paris.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   12 October [1873]
letters.summary: Asks GHD whether he can tell him what inclination a polished or waxy leaf ought to hold to the horizon in order to let vertical rain rebound off as much as possible.

letters.title: To Edward Frankland   13 October 1873
letters.summary:
Finds the negative information sent by EF of great interest [see9094].

More on his own experiments and the perplexing results when using the sensitive litmus paper.

letters.title: To Horace Darwin [15 October 1873]
letters.summary: Sends notes on waxy secretion on leaves for F. M. Balfour; cannot procure any moreDionaea.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [c.16 October 1873?]
letters.summary: Sends table showing relative force of impact of weight dropped on a plane inclined at different angles.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   16 October 1873
letters.summary: On bodies of varying elasticity bouncing off inclined planes [see9096].

letters.title: From Edward Frankland   16 October 1873
letters.summary: Sends some litmus paper for CD.

letters.title: To J. S. Burdon Sanderson   18 October [1873]
letters.summary: Suggests experiments on artificial digestion.

letters.title: From Virginius Dabney   18 October 1873
letters.summary: Feeding habits of the tobacco worm; it eats only five plants, all very different, but of same botanical family.

letters.title: To Edward Frankland   18 October [1873]
letters.summary: Apologises for his ignorance in interpreting the results secured in his testing with blue litmus paper.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   18 October [1873]
letters.summary: Hopes to get another species ofDesmodiumfrom Mr Rollisson.

letters.title: To A. G. Dew-Smith   19 October [1873]
letters.summary: SendsDionaeaplant for experiment involving temperature.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [before 20 October 1873?]
letters.summary:
Lists plants in which he is interested, includingNeptuniaandMimosaspecies.

Do any strictly tropical plants have glaucous leaves?

Asks for observations on irritable plants.

letters.title: To John Downing   20 October [1873]
letters.summary:
Gratified that a man of JD’s experience agrees with him.

Would enjoy seeing him at Down but it could only be for a half-hour’s talk at most, because of his health.

letters.title: From C. G. Ehrenberg   20 October 1873
letters.summary:
Sends an essay ["Mikrogeologische Studien über das kleinste Leben der Meeres-Tiefgründe aller Zonen und dessen geologischen Einfluss", Abhandlungen der Preussischen Akademie der Wissenschaften zu Berlin (1873): 131-98.]

with expressions of admiration. CGE is confident their differences will not estrange them.

Remembers with gratitude the [Atlantic] dust that CD made available to him in 1844 [see747].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   20 October 1873
letters.summary:
Describes work onNepenthes– more difficult thanDrosera.

Has written to Dublin for aDrosophyllum.

letters.title: From W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   [after 20 October 1873?]
letters.summary: Composition of the residue left on evaporation of the fluid inNepenthes.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   21 October [1873]
letters.summary: CD gives his criticisms of GHD’s essay on religion and the moral sense. Urges him to delay publishing for some months and then to consider whether it is new and important enough to counterbalance the effects of its publication. J. S. Mill would never have influenced the age as he has done had he not refrained from expressing his religious convictions. Cites John Morley’sLife of Voltaire[1872]: direct attacks produce little effect; real good comes from slow and silent side attacks. "My advice is to pause, pause, pause."

letters.title: To Theodor Eimer   21 October [1873]
letters.summary: Thanks for TE’s work on [Beroe?] with illustrations of its parts [Zoologische Studien auf Capri1 (1873)].

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   22 October 1873
letters.summary: Lists observations he would like FD to make on the dried species ofDesmodiumat Kew.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   23 October [1873]
letters.summary: Wants FD to look at the little lateral leaflets ofDesmodium. CD has "awildhypothesis that the little leaflets may be tendrils reconverted into leaflets".

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   23 October [1873]
letters.summary:
Neptuniais evidently a hopeless case.

Good news that fluid ofNepenthesis acid.

No discovery ever gave him more pleasure than proving a true act of digestion inDrosera.

Has become profoundly interested inDesmodium. Asks whether Frank [Darwin] can look over the whole dried collection of the genus.

Has JDH any seed ofLathyrus nissolia?

letters.title: From W. S. Wade   23 October 1873
letters.summary: Further details on inheritance of an eyelid abnormality.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   24 [October 1873]
letters.summary:
"It is a fearfully difficult moral problem about speaking out on religion, & I have never been able to make up my mind."

An Irishman, a "grand breeder" of short-horns, declared at lunch that CD’s books had been "a great help to [him] in breeding!"

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [before 25 October 1873]
letters.summary:
Suggests experiments to try [withNepenthes].

Asks JDH to test whether cabbage seeds and peas exposed to the ferment germinate.

Cancel: same as 9523.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   25 October 1873
letters.summary: Describes his experiments onNepenthes; finds action analogous to that inDrosera.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [26? October 1873]
letters.summary: Observations on the leaves ofDesmodium. Most are trifoliate; none has tendrils. Gives some comments from Hooker.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   26 October [1873]
letters.summary:
Extremely glad to hear of the aggregation inNepenthesglands. Advises on experimenting with cubes of albumen – gives sizes, also suggests cubes of roast meat. Thanks for analyses of secretion ofNepenthes.

Asks for cutting ofAcacia farnesiana.

Longs to examine a species ofDesmodiumwith three leaflets. Has asked Frank [Darwin] to look for species ofDesmodiumwith tendrils.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   29 October 1873
letters.summary:
Sends plant specimens.

He and Thiselton-Dyer, working on withNepenthes, have independently found the spiral vessels going to the gland. CD’s view that the glands are secretory organs is suggestive. WhenNepenthesis as much done as CD wants,

he will turn toCephalotusandSarracenia.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   30 October 1873
letters.summary: Has visited Alford and Beesby.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   30 October [1873]
letters.summary:
Thanks for leaves. His notes on them will be of greatest service.

He cannot distinguish someEucalyptifromAcacia. Sends specimens, with numbers, for JDH to name.

Acacia farnesianabranches arrived withered, but saw enough to make him wish to examine the plant.

Has thought of some troublesome experiments forDrosophyllum.

Encloses remarks [missing] by Searles Wood, with which CD disagrees, about a new and strongly marked variety transmitting its characters.

The competition of better adapted forms seems to CD a sufficient explanation [for extinction].

letters.title: From John Fiske   31 October 1873
letters.summary:
Would like much to visit CD before returning to America;

is completing his work on evolution [Outlines of cosmic philosophy(1874)] for publication. Hopes to do away with the anthropomorphic distinction made between "divine action" and the "action of natural forces".

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   31 October 1873
letters.summary:
OnNepenthes.

Asks JDH, if he publishes, to mention CD’s work on digestive powers ofDroseraso that charges of plagiarism will not be made against CD later when he publishes.

Describes at length his observations on the movements ofDesmodium.

letters.title: To Herbert Spencer   31 October [1873]
letters.summary:
Discusses adaptations in flowers and their heritability.

Mentions advertisements for HS’s book [?Study of sociology(1873)].

Thought HS would have profited by principle that a character appearing late in life is inherited at same age.

letters.title: From Godfrey Wedgwood   [November 1873]
letters.summary: Captive and tame birds inheriting the migratory instinct.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [1 November 1873]
letters.summary:
Sends leaves and names by post.

Is writing everywhere forDrosophyllum.

Is deeply interested inDesmodium.

Had no intention of publishing onNepenthes, the experiments were solely for CD’s "eating". Will continue with egg and raw meat experiments. Asks for advice on how to prove fluid is secreted by the glands.

Searles Wood’s letter is confused and would deny atavism if his principles were accepted.

letters.title: From Gerard Krefft   [c.1 November 1873?]
letters.summary: Describes the behaviour of a pet donkey and pig.

letters.title: From Gerard Krefft   1 November 1873
letters.summary:
Many insects visitEucalyptusflowers as long as there is pollen to be seen. Asking his colleague, George Masters, to gather insects and flowers at Long Bay for CD.

Observations on wild New Guinea pig in captivity.

Will take CD’s advice to write a book.

letters.title: To Down School Board   [after 29 November 1873]
letters.summary: CD, Sir John Lubbock, Ellen Frances Lubbock, and S. E. Wedgwood, petition the Board to grant permission for the school hall to be used as a reading room in the evening during winter.

letters.title: To Virginius Dabney   3 November 1873
letters.summary:
Thanks VD for information on caterpillars selecting food plants from within one family,

and on similar behaviour in hogs, which will not eat any plants from a family containing some poisonous members.

letters.title: To John Fiske   3 November [1873]
letters.summary:
CD is glad to hear of nature of JF’s work;

proposes that JF call when CD comes to London.

Has read JF’s attack on Agassiz ["Agassiz and Darwinism"] inPopular Science Monthly[3 (1873): 692–705].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   3 November [1873]
letters.summary:
Discusses experiments and observations on pitchers [ofNepenthes]. Suggests procedures for JDH to follow.

Any plant of any family with a terminal or with any lateral leaflets greatly reduced would be interesting to CD for studying spontaneous movements.

Has not receivedEucalyptusorAcaciaplants from Rollisson.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   3 November 1873
letters.summary: W. H. Flower is ill and obliged to go off for six months. Wants to return the money Flower contributed to fund for his holiday, asks the amount.

letters.title: From Gerard Krefft   3 November 1873
letters.summary: Letter of introduction for Mr Bradley, an expert on spiders.

letters.title: To John Pennington Thomasson?   3 November 1873
letters.summary: Thanks for the paragraph, which he had not seen and now returns.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   4 November 1873
letters.summary:
Has time only to thank CD for the invaluable hints.

EnclosesLathyrus nissoliaseeds.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   4 November 1873
letters.summary: Answers THH’s query about W. H. Flower; gives the amount he contributed to the gift. Advises against returning it, even anonymously. Hopes WHF’s health improves.

letters.title: From J. T. Moggridge   4 November 1873
letters.summary: Formic acid kills seeds but only rarely makes them dormant – as he presumes ants do. He finds great variation in the vigour of individual seeds. Harvester ants, used in place of formic acid, do not affect germination.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   6 November [1873]
letters.summary: Suggests experiment and observations to carry out on pitcher [ofNepenthes].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   6 November 1873
letters.summary: Is coming to stay in London and wants to arrange a visit to Kew to talk with JDH, see theEucalypti, and observeMimosa albida.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [8 November 1873]
letters.summary:
Has had a week’s cessation ofNepentheswork.

Had to get out a paper for the Linnean Society on Thursday.

Has triedMimosa albidain hothouse and found it wonderfully sensitive.

A military report from India praises his travel book.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [9 November 1873]
letters.summary:
Returned from visit.

Thinks several species ofEucalyptuswould be worth experimenting on. Sends list.Mimosa albidawould be worth its weight in diamonds.Neptuniaworth more than diamonds.
