letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [9 November 1873 or 26 April or 6 December 1874]
letters.summary: Arranges a visit to CL.

letters.title: To Edward Frankland   [10 November 1873]
letters.summary: Requests permission to call upon EF either Friday or Saturday morning [14 or 15 November].

letters.title: From Alfred Moschkau   10 November 1873
letters.summary: Has been studyingOriginand other works. Has lectured on the subject and would like to send some of his conclusions if CD is willing.

letters.title: From F. M. Balfour   11 November 1873
letters.summary: Suggests raising money to help Anton Dohrn complete the Naples Zoological Station, which is in danger of remaining unfinished.

letters.title: From John Downing   13 November 1873
letters.summary:
Is pleased that CD found the letters fromBell’s Weekly Messengerto the point.

Encloses extracts relating to benefits derived by animals from altered conditions of life.

Encloses notes on deterioration of short-horns from inbreeding. Breeders agree with him on benefits of introducing fresh blood into inbred stocks.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   [13 November 1873]
letters.summary:
Arrangements for meeting in London.

Glad CD has heard about Dohrn’s affairs.

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   13 November 1873
letters.summary:
HybridMotacilla.

Case of female duck leaving mate to pair with male of another species.

letters.title: From W. D. Crotch   14 November 1873
letters.summary:
Sends information on shedding of reindeer horns in males and females.

Lemmings.

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   15 November 1873
letters.summary: Encloses A. R. Wallace’s reply [in which he says he will undertake revision ofDescentif CD wishes]. HWB says this shows that Wallace is unaware of the scope of revision; suggests need for well-defined terms.

letters.title: To J. S. Burdon Sanderson   15 November [1873]
letters.summary: Frankland is sending JSBS organic acids for him to try artificial digestion. CD will send globulin and haemoglobin.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   15 November [1873]
letters.summary: CD writes about organising a subscription for Dohrn’s Zoological Station at Naples. Has drawn up a draft circular for naturalists to sign to show their support for the Station.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley to Anton Dohrn   15 November 1873
letters.summary: THH sends to AD a draft, prepared by himself and CD, of a statement for a subscription fund to assist AD’s Naples Zoological Station.

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   16 November [1873]
letters.summary: Thanks for assistance. He will write fully to Wallace tomorrow.

letters.title: To Friedrich Hildebrand   16 November [1873]
letters.summary: Thanks for FH’s work on the means of the distribution of plants (Hildebrand 1873).

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   17 November [1873]
letters.summary: Informs JVC that he is beginning a second, corrected edition ofDescent, in case a new edition is wanted in Germany.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   [17 November 1873]
letters.summary:
Sorry to hear of GHD’s poor health – he could have pleasant society at Cambridge if he were stronger.

Contributes £75 [to a fund for Naples Zoological Station] "if the affair goes on after we hear from Dohrn".

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   17 [November 1873]
letters.summary:
Is sending specimens ofEucalyptus;

goes tomorrow to receive LL.D. [Glasgow].

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   17 November 1873
letters.summary: Would be happy if ARW would undertake to help with correcting the proof-sheets of his revised edition ofDescent. Outlines the job that would be required.

letters.title: From Valentin Salzmann   18 November 1873
letters.summary: Discusses human reactions to pleasant and unpleasant tastes; considers that modifications of these reactions produce several identifiable expressions of general like and dislike.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   18 November 1873
letters.summary: Discussion of his possible assistance on editorial work for revised edition ofDescent.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   [18 November 1873]
letters.summary: CD’s son [George] could do the work [of proof-correction forDescent, 2d ed.] if ARW finds he does not care for it.

letters.title: To J. S. Burdon Sanderson   19 November [1873]
letters.summary: Sends the very little globulin and haemoglobin he has to be tested with artificial gastric juice. He could get more from Samuel William Moore. Perhaps T. L. Brunton knows about the digestion of chlorophyll by animals.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   19 November [1873]
letters.summary: Further discussion of ARW’s help on new [2d] edition ofDescent.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   [19 November 1873]
letters.summary: Thinks CD’s son George would be more satisfactory than ARW for the work onDescent.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   20 November 1873
letters.summary: CD is looking for editorial assistance in preparing a new edition ofDescent, and inquires whether GHD might be interested in taking on such a tedious job.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   24 November 1873
letters.summary: Pleased that GHD will help with second edition ofDescent. Cautions him not to alter strength of CD’s expression or improve the style too much.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   24 November 1873
letters.summary:
Has been working hard onMimosa albida. Could JDH ever make its opposite leaflets shut up close, as in sleep, when he irritated them? CD doubts they do, except in sleep. Thinks movement a protection against water.

Has examined only one specimen ofEucalyptus.

Cannot believe JDH’s results from cutting a hole in pitcher in hisNepenthesexperiment.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   25 November 1873
letters.summary: He has noticed thatMimosa albidaleaves closed only partially. It can be objected to CD’s theory that, if true, all, or at least more, species would close their leaves on application of water, unless he can show special injury done toM. albidaby water.

letters.title: From William Bowman   26 November 1873
letters.summary: Discusses hereditary character of hypermetropia. Notes views of F. C. Donders on the subject.

letters.title: To William Bowman   27 November [1873]
letters.summary: "As the diseasehypermetropiais not very rare, & as it is known to be hereditary, I will not give the case (about which I was very doubtful) & am glad to decide in the negative".

letters.title: From G. G. Bianconi   28 November 1873
letters.summary: Thanks CD for promised observations on his book against evolution [La théorie Darwinienne et la création dite indépendante(1874)].

letters.title: To ?   28 November [1873]
letters.summary: Will not require assistance of correspondent’s cousin in correcting his MS [2d ed. ofDescent]. His son [George] will undertake it.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   1 December [1873]
letters.summary: Suggests a reference toAnnals and Magazine of Natural History, 1 Dec 1873, p. 497, when THF takes upCoronilla.

letters.title: From T. L. Brunton   2 December 1873
letters.summary:
Offers to experiment on the digestibility of chondrin and chlorophyll byDionaeafor CD.

Has noticed that painters depicting complex expressions give different expressions to the two sides of the face.

letters.title: From Alfred Moschkau   2 [December] 1873
letters.summary: Discusses variation and selection in Harz canaries.

letters.title: To T. L. Brunton   3 December 1873
letters.summary: Is interested in comparative nutritive values of chondrin and gelatin. The former seems to exciteDroseramore, though albumen does so to a higher degree than either. Also asks if chlorophyll is digested by animals;Droseradigests it hardly at all.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   3 December 1873
letters.summary:
A letter from Anton Dohrn declines the proposed fund [that THH and others suggested be raised in England for marine biological station at Naples].

Hooker’s inaugural as President of Royal Society a success.

R. Owen distinguished himself in his way.

letters.title: To Richard Fordman   4 December [1873]
letters.summary: Thanks RF for his kind note; cannot quite believe or disbelieve stories of children raised by wolves.

letters.title: From Jonathan Peel   4 December 1873
letters.summary:
On the vermiform appendix,

snipes breeding in England,

and the horns of crossbred sheep.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   4 December 1873
letters.summary: Wishes to identify a species ofCassiawhose movements interest him.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   5 December [1873]
letters.summary:
Sorry to hear of Dohrn’s troubles. Has written to prospective donors saying that nothing can be done because of attitude of Dohrn’s father.

New [2d] edition ofDescentis an awful job.

Diet no longer doing much for his health.

letters.title: From W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   6 December 1873
letters.summary:
Movement in plants.

Information on species ofCassia.

letters.title: From Hubert Airy   7 December 1873
letters.summary: Illustrates, with reference to different species ofGasteria, the role of twisting in the development of leaf arrangement.

letters.title: From Richard Strachey   9 December 1873
letters.summary:
Sends observations from a friend in India confirming CD’s view that bees cut the tubes of flowers to extract [nectar] in order to save time.

Also observations on snails descending from trees on threads suspended from their tails.

letters.title: To Jonathan Peel   10 December [1873]
letters.summary:
Obliged for letter about horns of sheep.

Mentions case of death from objects impacted in appendix.

Is aware of his error about snipe breeding.

letters.title: To Richard Strachey   10 December [1873]
letters.summary:
The case of the bees interests CD. He does not doubt that because of the size of their jaws humble-bees will be found all over the world to be the biters and hive-bees to profit from their work.

Thinks he has heard of land shells descending in the manner described by RS.

letters.title: To F. S. B. F. de Chaumont   17 December [1873]
letters.deprecated: Francis Stephen Bennet François de Chaumont
letters.recipient: Francis Stephen Bennet François de Chaumont
letters.summary: Thanks FdeC for his note and invites criticisms.

letters.title: To J. E. Lee   17 December 1873
letters.summary: Formal note enclosing five guineas for William Pengelly testimonial fund.

letters.title: From Alfred Moschkau   17 December 1873
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for book.

Mentions controversy involving Haeckel.

Describes his lectures on Darwinism.

letters.title: To Smith, Elder & Co   17 December [1873]
letters.summary: Suggests that hisCoral reefsbe republished.

letters.title: From J. L. H. Down   18 December 1873
letters.summary: Describes features of an ear of a microcephalous idiot, one of which contradicts Carl Vogt’s views [Mémoire sur les microcéphales(1867)].

letters.title: To Down School Board   19 December 1873
letters.summary: Expresses his opinion that the Board should allow the school hall to be used as a reading room in the evenings by the villagers of Down.

letters.title: To Alfred Moschkau   19 December 1873
letters.summary: Discusses speech of parrots and starling. [SeeDescent, 2d ed., p. 85 n.]

letters.title: From J. L. H. Down   20 December 1873
letters.summary:
Describes an ear from a microcephalous idiot, which does not lend support to Ludwig Mayer’s view [that points on ears are mere variations; seeDescent, 2d ed., pp. 15–16].

Is working on involution rather than evolution, with results confirming CD’s teaching.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   20 December [1873]
letters.summary:
His indignation at the malignant, odious, hypocrite Owen’s attack on JDH. History of Secretaryship [of Royal Society inNature9 (1873): 129–30] was best answer to Owen.

Is hard at work on new edition ofDescent– a truly awful job.

No use going on with experiments on effects of water on bloom-divested leaves. May have erred. Or it may be that water is only injurious when there is a good supply of actinic rays. Will wait until spring.

letters.title: To Eduard Koch   20 December [1873]
letters.summary:
Thanks for copy of translation ofVariation

and the "admirable work on the microscopical structure of rock" [C. G. Ehrenberg,Mikrogeologische Studien(1873)].

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   22 December 1873
letters.summary:
Concerning secretion of "bloom";

movements ofRobinia.

letters.title: From James Crichton-Browne   27 December 1873
letters.summary: Is about to undertake an intensive investigation with other scientists of general paralysis in its various aspects. Would appreciate CD’s comments on photographs he would submit.

letters.title: To James Crichton-Browne   30 December 1873
letters.summary: Will do what he can to help JC-B with his work on expression of patients suffering from general paralysis.

letters.title: To C. G. Ehrenberg   30 December 1873
letters.summary: Thanks CGE for gift of his latest work [Mikrogeologische Studien(1873)].

letters.title: From H. H. Howorth   31 December 1873
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for subsidence references in response to HHH’sNaturepaper ["The distribution of volcanoes", 9 (1874): 141–2].

Hopes to refer to CD’s having previously suggested the corresponding elevation of continents and sinking of the larger oceans in his next letter toNature[9 (1874): 201–2]. Occurrence of volcanoes at boundary between rising and sinking lands reconciles his views with CD’s.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   [c.January 1874]
letters.summary:
Agrees with Bates that neuter termites are not modified imagos (sterile females), but modified larvae (of both sexes).

Systematic relations of stingless honey-bees (MeliponaandTrigona) are not yet well established.

letters.title: To B. W. Richardson   [1874–82]
letters.summary: Convinced from the experience of his father and grandfather that no cause has led to so much suffering and inherited ill-health as the consumption of alcohol.

letters.title: To ?   [1874–5?]
letters.summary: Although he formed a high opinion of one of the correspondent’s papers, regrets that he could not presume to give an opinion of the merits of a candidate in chemistry.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   1 January 1874
letters.summary:
Thanks for two pamphlets.

Sends Thomas Belt’s [The naturalist in Nicaragua(1874)], "the best Nat. Hist. book of travels ever published".

letters.title: To ?   1 January 1874
letters.summary: CD sends thanks for the honour conferred by his election as an honorary member, though ill health may prevent his taking advantage of the privileges granted.

letters.title: From E. P. T. Houk   3 January 1874
letters.summary: Sends paper she read before AAAS, but which was not accepted forProceedings.

letters.title: From H. H. Howorth   3 January [1874]
letters.summary: On the extinction of populations. [SeeDescent, 2d ed., p. 183.]

letters.title: To ?   3 January 1874
letters.summary: Has no objection to having his name appear as honorary member of [unidentified] club.

letters.title: To James Crichton-Browne   5 January 1874
letters.summary: Requests help for George Darwin’s investigation of marriages of first cousins. Seeks to determine proportion of first-cousin offspring among the insane, deaf and dumb, blind, etc.

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   5 January 1874
letters.summary:
Mentions family news;

sends a little magazine [missing] dealing with South American mission and showing "what teaching and the gospel of Christ is doing for those poor Natives".

letters.title: To B. J. Sulivan   6 January [1874]
letters.summary:
Thanks BJS for the missionary pamphlet and his good account of the Fuegians.

Is under the care of Andrew Clark, and feels "very old & helpless".

letters.title: To William Waring   6 January 1874
letters.summary: CD has previously received information on colours of greyhounds. Now asks whether breeders rear all puppies, and, if not, do they selectively rear more males or females?

letters.title: From Hubert Airy   8 January 1874
letters.summary: W. J. Beal’s paper ["Phyllotaxis of cones",Am. Nat.7 (1873): 449–53] shows incompleteness of HA’s theory, but does not invalidate his basic principles on origin of leaf arrangement or the broad applicability of the theory.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   8 January 1874
letters.summary:
Thanks JDH for Asa Gray’s interesting letter.

Would like JDH’s copy ofCoral reefs. Needs it for corrections for a new edition. Cannot buy one.

letters.title: To Smith, Elder & Co.   8 January 1874
letters.summary:
Pleased they will publish a new edition ofCoral reefs, and he will soon consider any addenda and write a short preface.

Will return the wood-blocks ofJournal of Researchesthe following week.

Could his copy ofCoral Reefsplease be returned.

letters.title: To Horace Darwin   9 January [1874]
letters.summary:
CD is glad Horace has done "pretty well" in his examination.

Smith and Elder will publish new edition ofCoral reefs[1874]; thanks HD for aid.

letters.title: From William Waring   9 January 1874
letters.summary: Breeders normally destroy weak and puny puppies in large litters, but would keep females if only one or two.

letters.title: To Andrew Clark   10 January [1874]
letters.summary: Invites AC to visit.

letters.title: To William Waring   12 January [1874]
letters.summary:
CD requests WW to ask a large breeder of greyhounds whether the increase in litters requires that some puppies be destroyed. If so, is it sufficient to destroy merely the small and weak? Would this result in more males or females being destroyed?

CD once used theFieldto tabulate ratios of female to male births in greyhounds (110: 100).

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   [13 January 1874]
letters.summary:
The coral-reef book has been invaluable [J. D. Dana,Corals and coral islands(1872); used by CD inCoral reefs, 2d ed. (1874)].

Thanks forSaturday Review.

letters.title: To T. N. Staley   13 January [1874]
letters.summary:
Has read TNS’s article ["On the geography and recent volcanic eruption of the Sandwich Islands",J. R. Geogr. Soc.38 (1868): 361–9].

Asks for information on decline in population and infanticide in the Sandwich Islands. Seeks corroboration of A. Bishop’s reports.

letters.title: To C. L. Denison   14 January 1874
letters.summary: Seeks information on the number of Pitcairn islanders and the effect on their fertility of the transfer to Norfolk Island.

letters.title: From Robert Swinhoe   14 January 1874
letters.summary: Wants CD to propose him for the Royal Society.

letters.title: From ?   [after 14 January 1874]
letters.summary: Extract from theHonolulu Gazetteon the decreasing population of the Sandwich Islands.

letters.title: From H. T. Stainton   15 January 1874
letters.summary: Encloses R. McLachlan’s certificate of nomination for Royal Society. Hopes CD will sign it, as McLachlan is the most philosophic member of the Entomological Society in years.

letters.title: From William Dealtry   16 January 1874
letters.summary: On the increases in crossbred English and Tahitian population of Pitcairn islanders. [SeeDescent, 2d ed., p. 190.] Includes copy of letter from George Hunn Nobbs about the population of Norfolk Island.

letters.title: From C. L. Denison   17 January [1874]
letters.summary: Sends CD the number of Pitcairn islanders transferred to Norfolk Island cited in her deceased husband’s book [Sir William Thomas Denison,Varieties of a vice-regal life(1870)] but is unable to furnish additional information.

letters.title: From C.-F. Reinwald   17 January 1874
letters.summary: French translation ofExpressionsent for CD’s approval.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   18 January [1874]
letters.summary: Thanks THF for information from Colonial Office on population statistics showing the inhabitants of some areas are far from becoming sterile.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   18 January [1874]
letters.summary:
Reports on a séance. "The Lord have mercy on us all if we have to believe in such rubbish."

Asks JDH to vote for his nephew, Henry Parker, for Athenaeum membership.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   19 January 1874
letters.summary: A new German edition ofDescentis planned. Would like to work on proofs before leaving for lectures at Edinburgh.

letters.title: To C. L. Denison   19 January [1874]
letters.summary: Finds from the Colonial Office that a census [of the Pitcairn Islands?] is expected soon, from which he will get the information he desires. [See9241and9246.]

letters.title: From J. H. Martin   19 January 1874
letters.summary: JHM, who has not read CD’s works, must conduct a discussion on Darwinism and theology at a local literary society. He asks CD to define briefly his position on the origin of man and on descent.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   20 January 1874
letters.summary:
An awful row at the Linnean Society. William Carruthers and Co. packed a meeting to throw out a decision of the Council. He was beaten by one vote (more than two-thirds majority needed).

Spent two hours with Lyell talking about Thomas Belt’s book [The naturalist in Nicaragua(1874)]: "the tropical old Glaciers beat the seance I do think".

Lyell agrees that the glacial epoch is the great geological crux of the day. Lowering of the ocean level must also be investigated.

Curious about A. C. Ramsay’s paper coming at Royal Society on 29th ["On the comparative value of certain geological ages",Proc. R. Soc. Lond.22 (1874): 145–8].

Huxley’s new book [?Critiques and addresses(1873)].

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   20 January 1874
letters.summary:
RussianExpressionhas sold nearly 2000 copies.

Plans to come to England to study collections of vertebrate fossils from the Chalk. This will complement his work in the south of France.

letters.title: To superintendent of a lunatic asylum   20 January 1874
letters.summary: Would like recipient to ask inmates whether they are offspring of cousin marriages.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   21 January 1874
letters.summary:
Is glad to hear of new German edition ofDescent, but owing to his extensive revisions, corrected sheets will not be ready for about three months.

Is working on a new edition ofCoral reefs, which he thinks would sell in Germany.

Would like to hear "out of curiosity & vanity" how many copies of his books have been sold in Germany.

letters.title: To C. G. Semper   21 January [1874]
letters.summary: Asks for information about the title and date of Semper’s essay disputing CD’s theory of coral reefs.

letters.title: To V. O. Kovalevsky   24 January [1874]
letters.summary: Has ordered James Clerk Maxwell’s book [On the stability of the motion of Saturn’s rings(1859)] as a present for Sofya Kovalevsky.

letters.title: From I. L. Roberti   24 January 1874
letters.summary:
Has grown haricots in England following CD’s suggestion in theOriginthat this had never been done.

Wishes to see CD.

letters.title: From C. G. Semper   25 January 1874
letters.summary:
Discusses coral reefs

and encloses a copy of his "Reisebericht" [Z. Wiss. Zool.13 (1863): 538–70], as requested by CD.

letters.title: From H. H. Howorth   [27 January 1874]
letters.summary:
Sends paper ["Strictures on Darwinism, pt 2",J. Anthropol. Inst.3 (1874): 208–28].

Refers to articles in theArt Journalon changes in English countenance since the Tudor period.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   27 January 1874
letters.summary: Reports to CD on a spiritualist séance attended by himself (incognito) and G. H. Darwin.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   27 January 1874
letters.summary: On obtaining Clerk Maxwell’s memoir on Saturn for his wife, Sofya.

letters.title: From American Academy of Arts and Sciences   28 January 1874
letters.deprecated: American Academy of Arts and Sciences
letters.sender: American Academy of Arts and Sciences
letters.summary: CD elected Foreign Honorary Member of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences. [See9305.]

letters.title: From John Downing   29 January 1874
letters.summary:
On proportion of sexes in births of cattle; variations in families. Encloses a letter from J. G. Grove on proportions of sexes in animals.

The limitation of inbreeding.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   29 January [1874]
letters.summary: Discusses THH’s account of the séance. CD convinced all are fraudulent.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   31 January 1874
letters.summary: Has finished the index [forDescent, 2d ed.].

letters.title: From D. Appleton & Co.   1 February 1874
letters.summary: Statement of U. S. sales ofOrigin,Expression, andDescent.

letters.title: From K. S. Sievert   1 February 1874
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for copy ofExaminer.

Fear of communism is making CD’s theory popular among possessing classes.

Describes reception of Lyell’sAntiquity of manamong German country people.

letters.title: From George Cupples   3 February 1874
letters.summary: Responds to CD’s queries about breeders’ practices in destroying and saving males or females in litters of deerhounds.

letters.title: From J. F. McLennan   3 February 1874
letters.summary: Discusses the evolution of marriage systems; considers the scheme of development CD proposes: 1. Polygyny and monogamy; 2. Polyandry; 3. Promiscuity; 4. Polygyny and monogamy in recurrence. Explains what he understands by promiscuity. JFM believes that polygyny, monogamy, and polyandry must have occurred in "every district from the first, and grown up together into systems sanctioned by usage first and then law". Considers polygyny necessarily the privilege of the few and, as a system, believes it had less to do than any other with the history of marriage. He sees polyandry as an advance from promiscuity and the stage at which contractual obligations between men and their wives begin.

letters.title: From C.-F. Reinwald   4 February 1874
letters.summary:
Sends £40 for copyright to Édmond Barbier’s revision of Moulinié’sDescenttranslation.

Journal of researchestranslation is in press.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   5 February 1874
letters.summary: Do breeders rear more male than female greyhound puppies?

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   6 February 1874
letters.summary: Orders five works on the Sandwich Islands from the Royal Geographical Society Library for his investigation of infanticide and population trends there.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   6 February 1874
letters.summary: Finds statistical evidence that cousin marriages are at least three times as frequent in "our rank" as in the lower.

letters.title: From J. C. Symmes   6 February 1874
letters.summary: Believes that he has an important physical theory: all atoms revolve.

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   7 February 1874
letters.summary:
Books CD requested have been packed and sent.

He will present CD with the classified catalogue [of Royal Geographical Society].

He has not learned whereabouts of Thomas Staley.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   7 February 1874
letters.summary: Asks CD’s help in finding original woodcuts for "Voyage of a naturalist" [Journal of researches] for Reinwald.

letters.title: From George Cupples   7 February 1874
letters.summary: Will send CD’s query to eight or ten people.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   7 February [1874?]
letters.summary: George brought a plant from Cambridge, which he is keeping for CD.

letters.title: From O. G. Rejlander   7 February 1874
letters.summary: Thanks CD for £10 to help with his law case.

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   7 February 1874
letters.summary:
The Bishop of Falkland [Waite Hockin Stirling] is coming to visit BJS, who will question him for CD.

Discusses politics; regrets they have been badly beaten by the Tory candidate.

letters.title: From C. G. Semper   8 February 1874
letters.summary: Comments on G. H. Lewes’s book [The life and works of Goethe(1855)].

letters.title: From Robert Swinhoe   9 February 1874
letters.summary: Matters of etiquette concerning his certificate for the Royal Society.

letters.title: From George Harris   10 February 1874
letters.summary: Sends about 15 sheets on instinct from his book [A philosophical treatise on the nature and constitution of man(1876)] for CD’s comments.

letters.title: From W. T. Goodale   11 February 1874
letters.summary: Asks CD if he can reconcile a passage in Mark Hopkins’Outline study of man[1873] with the theory of development.

letters.title: ToNature   11 February [1874]
letters.summary: Prefaces Fritz Müller’s observations on termites and stingless bees [see9281].

letters.title: From Anton Dohrn  12 February 1874
letters.summary: Birthday greetings.

letters.title: To Albert Günther   12 February 1874
letters.summary: Asks AG to sign an enclosure [see9291].

letters.title: To George Harris   12 February 1874
letters.summary: Has read GH’s proofs and, although not entirely in agreement, has no criticisms worth sending.

letters.title: From T. N. Staley   12 February 1874
letters.summary: On the decline of population of the Hawaiian Islands, before advent of Europeans; infanticide, polyandry.

letters.title: To Anton Dohrn   13 February 1874
letters.summary:
Thanks for birthday greetings.

Comments on work at Naples Zoological Station. F. M. Balfour to visit Naples. Would like to send third son [Francis Darwin] to learn art of observing marine animals.

Health indifferent.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   13 February 1874
letters.summary:
Has sent FM’s letter on termites toNature["Habits of various insects",Nature10 (1874): 102–3].

Would be interested in observations on the stingless bees of Brazil.

letters.title: From T. M. Coan   14 February 1874
letters.summary: On the declining population of the Hawaiian Islands [seeDescent(1875), pp. 186–7, 187–8 n. 43].

letters.title: From Albert Günther   14 February 1874
letters.summary: Signs Robert Swinhoe’s certificate [for the Royal Society] with pleasure.

letters.title: From Leonard Darwin   [after 14 February 1874]
letters.summary: Statistics showing rate of decline of population in Sandwich Islands, 1832–72.

letters.title: From Hermann Müller   15 February 1874
letters.summary:
Feels CD’s and Fritz Müller’s judgments on his "Anwendung" essay [see8313] are of highest value. Mentions some of FM’s comments.

Looks forward to second English edition ofDescent.

letters.title: From C. S. Tomes   [before 16 February 1874]
letters.summary: Inherited dental abnormalities in man. [Enclosed are proofs of pp. 113–16 from J. Tomes,A system of dental surgery, 2d ed. (1873).]

letters.title: From A. S. G. Canning   16 February 1874
letters.summary: Offers information on pea-fowl for new edition ofVariation.

letters.title: To H. E. Litchfield   16 February [1874?]
letters.summary: On the "doubtful & obscure" subject of marriage of cousins, CD believes, that judging from the analogy of animals, no direct evil would follow from their marriage. He would, however, expect the offspring of unrelated parents to be somewhat superior in size and vigour. The injury from the increase of any bad tendency common to the family seems to CD more to be feared than mere consanguinity; "the good effects of crossing distinct families I look at as great & undoubted".

letters.title: From J. A. Gammie   16 February 1874
letters.summary: Sends his observations on the fertilisation ofHedychium gardnerianumby sphinx moths. Did not look for pollen on the wing tips.

letters.title: To George Harris   16 February [1874]
letters.summary: Returns proofs; has no criticisms or remarks worth sending.

letters.title: To C. S. Tomes   16 February [1874]
letters.summary:
Thanks for facts on inheritance

Thinks CST’s paper (C. S. Tomes 1874) about the enamel on the teeth of the armadillo is most remarkable.

letters.title: To H. B. Tristram   16 February 1874
letters.summary: Asks HBT to sign certificate [for Royal Society] for Robert Swinhoe.

letters.title: From Octavius Pickard-Cambridge   17 February 1874
letters.summary:
Criticises sexual selection theory. Supports natural selection.

Gives CD references on proportion of sexes in spiders.

letters.title: To G. E. Shuttleworth   17 February [1874]
letters.summary: At the suggestion of Crichton-Browne CD writes on behalf of his son George, who is making a study of marriages between first cousins and of their offspring to determine the proportion of the latter who may be among the insane, deaf and dumb, idiotic, blind etc. Is GES willing to ask his patients [at the Royal Albert Asylum] for the information relevant to this study?

letters.title: From W. B. Tegetmeier   17 February 1874
letters.summary: Gives the answers of two of the best dog breeders to CD’s queries.

letters.title: From A. S. G. Canning   18 February 1874
letters.summary: Reports on a female black-winged pea-fowl at his home in Ireland.

letters.title: To Hermanus Hartogh Heijs van Zouteveen   18 February 1874
letters.summary: Thanks for HHHvZ’s translation ofExpression. CD will have HHHvZ’s notes translated by one of his sons.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   18 February 1874
letters.summary: Thanks for answering his query on greyhound puppies.

letters.title: To Hugo de Vries   19 February 1874
letters.summary: Thanks for copies of HdV’s two articles on climbing plants (Vries 1873a and 1873b).

letters.title: To Octavius Pickard-Cambridge   [before 20 February 1874]
letters.summary:
Discusses meaning of term "sexual selection".

Comments on variability in males.

letters.title: To J. P. Cooke   20 February 1874
letters.summary: Thanks for his election as Foreign Honorary Member.

letters.title: To Ludwig Rütimeyer   20 February 1874
letters.summary: Thanks for LR’s essay on living and fossil turtles [Bull. Soc. Sci. Nat. Neuchâtel9 (1873): 439–41].

letters.title: From T. N. Staley   20 February 1874
letters.summary: General observations on the native Hawaiian population.

letters.title: From George Cupples   21 February 1874
letters.summary:
Answers to queries are being sent.

Enclosure 1: statistics on puppies bred by Rayner in 1873.

Enclosure 2 from W. N. Massey: number of males or females raised depends entirely on preference of greyhound breeders.

Enclosure 3 from E. L. Williams: breeders prefer to destroy bitch pups.

Enclosure 4: Thomas Morse answers CD’s three queries, transmitted by GC: (1) in deerhounds, females predominate, three to one; (2) in all but cattle, females are less worth preserving; (3) TM rearsallthe young.

Enclosure 5: John Wright responds to CD’s queries about proportion of sexes in births of horses, cattle, and dogs.

Enclosure 6: G. W. Hickman cannot give reliable answers to CD’s queries on proportion of sexes born [in greyhounds?].

letters.title: From P. F. Perfil’eva   22 February 1874
letters.summary: Asks for CD’s photograph.

letters.title: From A. S. G. Canning   23 February 1874
letters.summary: More details on pea-fowl.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   23 February 1874
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: CD wishes to acquire a piece of JL’s land.

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   23 February 1874
letters.summary: The Bishop of Falkland says the Fuegian natives’ health does not suffer through increased civilisation. Relates the Bishop’s observations on the state of Tierra del Fuego and its populace.

letters.title: From William Withers   23 February 1874
letters.summary: Thanks CD for presenting books to a gardeners’ society.

letters.title: To Albert Günther   25 February 1874
letters.summary: Has given inDescent2: 12, an account from AG of the brushes on the sides ofMonacanthus; has now learned of brush-like scales on the males ofMallotus. Asks whether the two genera are related.

letters.title: From T. N. Staley   25 February [1874]
letters.summary: Introduction of tropical fruits in Hawaiian Islands.

letters.title: To W. T. Goodale 26 February [1874]
letters.summary:
Has not the strength to discuss WTG’s letter, and points out that every organism develops from a single cell.

Does not wish to see the Book WTG offered.

letters.title: From Albert Günther   26 February 1874
letters.summary:
Comments on several points inDescent,

doubts facts aboutMonacanthusbrushes

and the two Cyprinidae males attending the female when spawning.

letters.title: To H. B. Tristram   26 February [1874]
letters.summary: Asks HBT whether he received the certificate nominating Robert Swinhoe for the Royal Society.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   27 February 1874
letters.summary: Asks CD to allow his name to be put on a committee to establish a Scientific Societies Club for the fellows of the six societies that will have rooms in Burlington House.

letters.title: From Eugène Desmarest   27 February 1874
letters.summary: CD has been elected an Honorary Member of the Society.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   27 February 1874
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: The land CD wants to buy probably belongs to his marriage-settlement and would thus be difficult to sell.

letters.title: From T. L. Brunton   28 February 1874
letters.summary:
Reports negative results of his experiments on digestion of chlorophyll byDroseraand by animals. [SeeInsectivorous plants, p. 126.]

Sends references for chondrin.

letters.title: From Hermanus Hartogh Heijs van Zouteveen   28 February 1874
letters.summary: CD’s son is considering translating into English HHHvZ’s notes in Dutch edition ofExpression; HHHvZ feels his notes toDescentwould be of more interest.

letters.title: To T. W. Denby   1 March 1874
letters.summary: Writes concerning the land he wishes to purchase from Sir John Lubbock.

letters.title: To Edmund Hartnack   1 March 1874
letters.summary: Has been waiting several months for a microscope objective and would like it without delay.

letters.title: To Albert Günther   [c.2 March 1874]
letters.summary:
Encloses a circular [9384?] to explain the predicament he is in. Asks whether AG can get anyone at the British Museum, other than Owen, to join J. E. Gray in signing.

Believes the account of theMallotusinAmerican Naturalist[5 (1871): 119] is trustworthy.

letters.title: To the Royal Society of London   2 March [1874]
letters.summary: A certificate for admission [of Robert Swinhoe] to Royal Society with many signatures has been lost by the Post Office. Asks for another so he can get the signatures anew.

letters.title: From F. E. Abbot   3 March 1874
letters.summary: Asks CD to read and comment, for publication, on his forthcoming essay inIndexon the evolution of conscience and morals through action and reaction between man and the moral environment.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   3 March 1874
letters.summary:
The row at the Linnean Society and other troubles.

The Agricultural Society has sent Anton De Bary £100 to investigate the potato disease – an insult to M. J. Berkeley, who had worked on it for 30 years.

letters.title: To H. B. Tristram   3 March [1874]
letters.summary: Thanks HBT for all the trouble he has taken for Robert Swinhoe and himself. Will try to get six signatures on a new certificate and deliver it to the Royal Society in time.

letters.title: To T. L. Brunton   4 March 1874
letters.summary:
On digestive powers ofDroseraand those of higher animals.

Comments on expression on two halves of human face.

Responds to TLB’s views of serpent- and fire-worship.

Poison of venomous snakes.

letters.title: To Eugène Desmarest   4 March 1874
letters.summary: Thanks for letter announcing election to honorary member of the Entomological Society of France. Has always felt entomology admirable for throwing light on general problems in biology.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   4 March [1874]
letters.summary:
CD guessed Carruthers was stirred up by Owen. Disgraceful treatment of Bentham.

Work onDescentandCoral reefsstops his doing anything of real interest.

Asa Gray’s letter. CD has acknowledged the honour [honorary membership in the Boston Soc. Nat. Hist.].

"What a demon on earth Owen is. I do hate him."

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   6 March 1874
letters.summary:
Has heard from Dohrn about his financial problems. Asks CD’s advice on what to do.

THH’s article inContemporary Review["Universities: actual and ideal" (1874),Collected essays, vol. 3 (1894)].

letters.title: To Anton Dohrn   7 March 1874
letters.summary: CD is grieved to hear that AD is overworked and troubled about the Zoological Station. Glad he is now writing to seek assistance from English naturalists. Sends a subscription of £100 and £10 each from George and Francis Darwin.

letters.title: From J. T. Moggridge   7 March 1874
letters.summary:
Sends abstract of Martin Ziegler’s paper on sensitive movements inDrosera["Sur un fait physiologique observé sur des feuilles deDrosera",C. R. Hebd. Acad. Sci.74 (1872): 1227–9].

JTM’s experiments with formic acid and ants have failed to reveal the secret of the ants, but have taught him a great deal about germination.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   8 March [1874]
letters.summary:
Looks forward to a visit from JVC and family in August.

Sheets of vol. 1 ofDescent[2d ed.] are going to printer;

new edition ofCoral reefsis half printed.

letters.title: To George Bentham   9 March [1874]
letters.summary: Asks GB to support the election of CD’s nephew, Henry Parker, to the Athenaeum Club.

letters.title: To William Bowman   9 March [1874]
letters.summary: Urges WB to give his vote "and exert any influence which you properly can" in favour of CD’s nephew, Henry Parker, a fellow of Oriel, at the next balloting at the Athenaeum.

letters.title: From T. L. Brunton   9 March 1874
letters.summary:
Writes on the possible origin of serpent-worship.

Is glad CD does not think his view regarding the two sides of the face is erroneous.

letters.title: To Edward Frankland   9 March [1874]
letters.summary: Requests EF’s vote and support in favour of Henry Parker for membership in the Athenaeum.

letters.title: To a member of the Athenaeum Club   9 March [1874]
letters.summary: Seeks correspondent’s support for his nephew, Henry Parker, for membership in the Athenaeum.

letters.title: To Alfred Newton   9 March [1874]
letters.summary: Asks AN to vote for CD’s nephew, Henry Parker, at the Athenaeum.

letters.title: To John Tyndall   9 March [1874]
letters.summary: Asks JT to support his nephew, Henry Parker, for election to the Athenaeum.

letters.title: To Thomas Woolner   9 March 1874
letters.summary: Seeks support for election of his nephew, Henry Parker, to the Athenaeum.

letters.title: To J. T. Moggridge   10 March 1874
letters.summary:
Criticises paper by Ziegler [see9339].

Acid experiments on seeds have failed.

letters.title: From Alfred Newton   10 March 1874
letters.summary:
Questions correctness of two statements inOrigin: 1. That fulmar petrels are the most numerous birds in the world;

2. That the increase of one form of thrush in Scotland has been concomitant with the decline of another form.

letters.title: To P. F. Perfil’eva   11 March 1874
letters.summary:
Sends photograph.

Comments on Mme P’s bulldogs.

letters.title: From Albert Wigand   11 March 1874
letters.summary: Sends copy of his book [Der Darwinismus und die Naturforschung Newtons und Cuviers, vol. 1 (1874)]. Expresses respect for CD in spite of the book’s criticism of him.

letters.title: To ?   11 March 1874
letters.summary: Thanks correspondent for offer of [unidentified] rare book but does not accept it.

letters.title: From George Cupples   12 March 1874
letters.summary:
Promises answers to CD queries on dogs.

Enclosure 1: G. A. Graham responds to CD’s questions (transmitted by GC) on greyhound breeding and proportion of sexes reared.

Enclosure 2: J. W. Robertson’s general rule has been to preserve male deerhound puppies in preference to females.

Enclosure 3: Proportion of sexes in dog litters [forDescent, 2d ed.] from W. Forbes.

letters.title: To Alfred Newton   12 March [1874]
letters.summary:
Cannot answer AN’s questions aboutOrigin; it would take weeks to find the references. Assures AN he stated nothing without an authority he thought good.

Feels sure missel thrushes have increased in number since his youth. Starlings have also increased astonishingly in Kent. "How inexplicable most of these cases are".

In a P.S. remembers his source for statement about increase of missel thrushes inOrigin.

letters.title: From Prior Purvis   12 March 1874
letters.summary: Sends report on an infant with congenital heart disease who died at ten months. Post-mortem showed it had the "heart of a fish": two cavities, one auricle and one ventricle.

letters.title: From Hubert Airy   13 March 1874
letters.summary: Has rewritten paper on leaf arrangement after criticism by Royal Society referees. Has found new factor influencing leaf arrangement, i.e., spontaneous variability in the number of vertical leaf-ranks.

letters.title: From Alfred Newton   13 March 1874
letters.summary:
Wishes CD could publishOriginwith footnotes.

Increases in bird populations: starlings are increasing, but AN cannot give reason; mistletoe-thrush increasing but not ousting song-thrush. Doubts trustworthiness of [George?] Edwards, CD’s authority inOriginon this matter [seeOrigin, 6th ed., p. 59].

AN opposed to bird protection legislation to prohibit egging. Argues egging does not decrease number of birds.

letters.title: From A. P. Fletcher   14 March 1874
letters.summary: Asks for a reference for Charles Pearson, who has applied to be appointed an agent for the Company.

letters.title: To Alfred Newton   14 March 1874
letters.summary: Can give no definite information. Believes severe winters are by far the most important check on numbers of birds; the destruction of eggs is of subordinate importance.

letters.title: From John Phillips   14 March 1874
letters.summary:
Will be out of town, so he cannot vote for Henry Parker.

CD ought to come to see hisCetiosaurus, of which he draws a likeness.

letters.title: To A. P. Fletcher   [after 14 March 1874]
letters.summary: Testifies to the trustworthiness of Charles Pearson.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   15 March 1874
letters.summary:
Proposal to collect all of CD’s works in a German edition. Asks CD’s opinion and suggests an outline of volumes.

Lists German sales of various volumes.

letters.title: From Alfred Newton   15 March 1874
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his opinion on egging. Despite the intensity of the practice sufficient eggs always remain to carry on the breed.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   17 [March 1874]
letters.summary: Reports the balloting [for Henry Parker at the Athenaeum?] went off just right.

letters.title: To Albert Wigand   17 March 1874
letters.summary: Thanks AJWW for his frank and generous criticism. [See9352.] Having viewed all natural objects under the light of natural selection for more than thirty years, CD thinks it unlikely that any arguments short of demonstration can convince him of error.

letters.title: From Henryk Stecki   18 March 1874
letters.summary: Relates the case of a woman from the Caucasus whose hair would frequently stand on end and who later went insane.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   19 March [1874]
letters.summary:
Would be glad to hear of a collected edition of his works [in Germany], but has no opinion on how it would sell. Has been surprised to learn that in England some think uniform collected works sell best. Tells JVC his publication plans and other details to guide him on extent of a "collected works".

Descentcorrections have been laborious and troublesome.

letters.title: To J. S. Burdon Sanderson   21 March 1874
letters.summary: Sends his MS onDionaeaand hopes it may be useful for JSBS’s lecture ["On the mechanism of the leaf ofDionaea muscipula",Not. Proc. R. Inst. G. B.7 (1874): 332–5].

letters.title: To H. E. Litchfield   21 [March 1874]
letters.summary: Proof-correcting [of 2d ed. ofCoral reefs?].

letters.title: To John Struthers   21 March 1874
letters.summary: Comments on JS’s lecture on evolution ["Address on evolution",Aberdeen Daily Free Press24 Feb 1874].

letters.title: From J. S. Burdon Sanderson   23 March [1874]
letters.summary:
Thanks for MS which he intends to read while on a week’s holiday.

Sends thanks for Francis Darwin’s offer of help and says that Francis’s experiments on digestion are complete.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   24 March 1874
letters.summary:
"Half an answer" to CD’s query on visit ofSphinxtoHedychium gardnerianum.

Business affairs and family ill health keep him busy.

G. J. Allman will succeed Bentham as President of Linnean Society. Busk has refused.

Huxley is well.

JDH has indoctrinated Sir Stafford Northcote with his merits.

Lyell frail.

Old J. E. Gray goes on publishing.

"Is not [Thomas] Belt splendid!"

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   25 March [1874]
letters.summary:
Thanks for information aboutHedychium. Hopes wings ofSphinxwill be found covered with pollen for that will be a fine bit of prophecy from the structure of a flower to special and new means of fertilisation.

Has been atDescentso hard he has done nothing, not even H. Spencer’s answer.

Has not yet read Croll ["Ocean currents",London Edinburgh & Dublin Philos. Mag.47 (1874): 94–122, 168–90].

Has heard nothing about Carter andEozoon.Eozoon, he infers, is done for.

Has read Belt [The naturalist in Nicaragua(1874)]: best of all natural history travel books.

Has written to Fritz Müller about leaf-carrying ants.

Hopes to resume work onDrosera.

letters.title: From Emile Alglave   27 March 1874
letters.summary:
On EA’s persecution by new government for liberal–republican position of hisRevues; threat to remove him from Faculté de Droit, unless he renounces relations withRevuesor changes their politics.

Has reviewed CD’sOrchids.

letters.title: To H. E. Litchfield   27 [March 1874]
letters.summary: Thanks her for her excellent criticisms and corrections [for 2d ed. ofCoral reefs?].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   27 [March 1874]
letters.summary: Etty [Henrietta Litchfield] is helping withCoral reefs[2d ed.]; will JDH lend her his copy?

letters.title: To Smith, Elder & Co.   27 March [1874]
letters.summary: Heavily correcting sheets forCoral reefs, 2d ed. [1874]. Offers to pay extra printer’s charges.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   28 March [1874]
letters.summary:
Asks for THH’s description of brain and skull [of man and apes] for 2d ed. ofDescent[supplement to ch. 7].

Asks about Dohrn affair and contributions for Naples station. Doubts subscriptions will be successful.

letters.title: To F. E. Abbot   30 March 1874
letters.summary:
FEA has expressed CD’s views on the moral sense with remarkable clearness and correctness; his eulogy is magnificent ["Darwin’s theory of conscience and its relation to scientific ethics",Index12 Mar 1874]. Cannot give a judgment on the essay because he has had "no practice in following abstract and abstruse reasoning".

CD does not see how morality can be "objective and universal". No one would call the maternal bond in lower animals a "moral obligation". When a social animal "becomes in some slight incipient degree" a moral creature "capable of approving or disapproving of its own conduct" do not such obligations remain of a so-called instinctive nature rather than becoming at once moral obligations?

letters.title: From J. S. Burdon Sanderson   30 March [1874]
letters.summary: Sends results of experiments on digestion. Encloses two sets of notes: "Experiments on the digestibility of certain preparations sent by Mr Darwin" and "Note for Mr Darwin" [marked by CD for insertion in ch. 6 ofInsectivorous plants].

letters.title: To J. S. Burdon Sanderson   31 March [1874]
letters.summary: Thanks for the careful experiments, particularly on organic acids.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   31 March 1874
letters.summary:
His note on brain [in man and apes for 2d ed. ofDescent] nearly finished.

Has heard nothing about Dohrn.

THH has been invited to lecture in America.

letters.title: To John Phillips   31 March [1874]
letters.summary:
Regrets he cannot visit Oxford.

Comments on sketches in letter from JP [9360].

letters.title: To Albert Wigand   31 March 1874
letters.summary: Confirms receipt of a book that had been lost by the Post Office (Vol. 1Der Darwinismus und die Naturforschung Newtons und Cuviers(Darwinism and the natural researches of Newton and Cuvier; Wigand 1874–7).

letters.title: To A. C. H. Gordon   April 1874
letters.deprecated: Arthur Charles Hamilton Gordon, 1st Baron Stanmore
letters.recipient: Arthur Charles Hamilton Gordon, 1st Baron Stanmore
letters.summary: Petition to protect gigantic tortoises on the Mascarene.

letters.title: From T. G. Appleton   2 April 1874
letters.summary:
Sends old Japanese picture suggesting evolution, found by Charles Longfellow.

Is pleased to hear CD attended a séance [18 Jan 1874]; asks for his views about communication among spirits.

letters.title: From John Lubbock    2 April 1874
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Is willing to sell the land CD wants for £300.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   3 April 1874
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Thanks for JL’s willingness to sell land.

letters.title: To G. H. Ford    [before 4 April 1874]
letters.summary: Regrets that a cut [forDescent] does not do justice to TWW’s original drawing and if it cannot be improved then CD will have to omit it. [Refers to fig. 60 inDescent(1874).]

letters.title: To John Murray   4 April 1874
letters.summary: Has finished corrections for 2d edition ofDescent– "as hard work as I have ever had in my life". Estimates it is 40 pages longer than 1st edition.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   4 April 1874
letters.summary:
Wants some plants for observation and for experimentation on their powers of movement.

Asks WTT-D to make observations on plants with sensitive stamens or pistil.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   [before 5 April 1874]
letters.summary: Subscribes to a reprint of Pieter Boddaert’sTable des planches enluminéez d’histoire naturelle[check ‘éez’!?] [1874].

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   5 April 1874
letters.summary: Hopes to visit CD during a stay in London.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   5 April 1874
letters.summary: Many thanks for Boddaert [see9389].

letters.title: From Anton Dohrn   6 April 1874
letters.summary:
His gratitude for CD’s gift. An account of his difficulties with the Zoological Station and his health.

F. M. Balfour has told him that CD would like to see the question of complemental males in cirripedes studied again. AD would like to enter the field and to study the whole morphological development of cirripedes.

Describes the interest in embryological work in Russia and Germany.

letters.title: ToNature   6 April [1874]
letters.summary: Comments on J. T. Moggridge’s article on the fertilisation ofFumaria capreolata[Nature9 (1874): 423].

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   6 April [1874]
letters.summary:
Just back from Gold Coast.

Would like to become a member of the Royal Institution.

letters.title: From Michael Foster   7 April [1874]
letters.summary: Is organising an appeal for the Naples Zoological Station.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   7 [April 1874]
letters.summary: C. V. Riley’s case ofPronubamoth and the fertilisation ofYucca, is the most wonderful case of fertilisation ever published [Am. Nat.7 (1873): 619–23].

letters.title: To John Lubbock, P. L. Sclater, Charles Lyell, W. B. Carpenter, and Michael Foster   [7 April 1874]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron AveburyPhilip Lutley SclaterCharles Lyell, 1st baronetWilliam Benjamin CarpenterMichael Foster
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron AveburyPhilip Lutley SclaterCharles Lyell, 1st baronetWilliam Benjamin CarpenterMichael Foster
letters.summary: Circular requesting recipients to sign an enclosed [missing] statement [relating to appeal for Naples Zoological Station] if they approve of it.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   8 April 1874
letters.summary:
Discusses illustrations for 2d edition ofDescent.

"My nephew [Henry Parker] got into the Athenaeumwith splendid success."

letters.title: To John Lubbock   8 April [1874]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Encloses a statement and circular he has been asked to send to JL.

letters.title: From Henry Cecil   9 April 1874
letters.summary: Has just readJournal of researchesand has been charmed out of his anti-Darwinian prejudice.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   [before 10 April 1874]
letters.summary: Observations onCoronilla.

letters.title: From Berry Benson   10 April 1874
letters.summary:
Supplies evidence to the contrary of CD’s assertion inExpressionthat dogs do not eat carrion.

Offers to send mud-wasps.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   10 April [1874]
letters.summary: Is glad to haveDescentcheaper and sold more largely, but would be sorry to see it printed like theOrigin. "The closeness of the lines is the great fault." Fears book might be very thick. "I hear scores of people complaining of the heavy and thick books which you publish."

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   10 April 1874
letters.summary: Delighted to hear aboutCoronilla. Urges publication ["Fertilisation of papilionaceous flowers–Coronilla",Nature10 (1874): 169–70].

letters.title: To Enrico Morselli   10 April 1874
letters.summary: Thanks EM for essay ["Sopra un rara anomalia dell’osso malare",Annu. Soc. Nat. Modena7 (1873): 1–50]. CD agrees as far as he understands. Cannot see how new modifications could arise by atavism. "The more I study nature, the more I feel convinced that species generally change by extremely slight modifications."

letters.title: To Edward Frankland   12 April 1874
letters.summary: Finding that the leaves ofDroseradigestallthe phosphate of lime out of bones and then remain clasped over the bones for a long time, CD wants to determine whether it is the phosphate of lime or the animal matter in the bones that keeps them clasped. He asks EF to send 2 or 3 grams of pure phosphate of lime for his testing. [See9411.] Will experiment in the summer using EF’s suggestion that leaves might serve to test weak sewage. Results of Sanderson’s experiments with acids of great use.

letters.title: To John Murray   12 April 1874
letters.summary: Discusses 2d edition ofDescent. CD is inclined to a cheap edition and asks JM to consider a one-volume edition in double-column format.

letters.title: From Leonard Rudd   12 April 1874
letters.summary: On supernumerary mammae in a male patient.

letters.title: To ? 12 April 1874
letters.summary: Thanks an unknown correspondent for the 4th edition of his 'remarkable work'.

letters.title: From William Waring   13 April 1874
letters.summary: On proportion of sexes in litters of greyhounds.

letters.title: To William Waring   13 April 1874
letters.summary: WW’s information accords with other accounts lately received. CD had formed an erroneous opinion on the subject.

letters.title: To Williams & Norgate   13 April [1874]
letters.summary: Asks correspondent to obtain odd numbers ofFlora.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   14 April 1874
letters.summary:
Sends his screed about the brain [forDescent], which he thinks pounds the enemy into a jelly.

Is in good health.

letters.title: From Edward Frankland   15 April 1874
letters.summary: Sends some phosphates of lime free of animal matter [seeInsectivorous plants, p. 109].

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   15 April 1874
letters.summary: Thanks for the seeds and plants that he requested.

letters.title: To Anton Dohrn   16 April and 9 August 1874
letters.summary:
Has written to J. Murray to have account of the Zoological Station inserted in the Murray guidebook.

The circular about the Station has been printed; some have already signed.

Received R. Kossman’s paper onAnelasma["Untersuchungen über die durch Parasitismus hervorgerufenen Umbildungen in der Familie der Pedunculata",Verh. Phys.-med. Ges. Würz.N. F. 5 (1874): 129–57]. The case is the most interesting ever recorded of gradation, i.e., from an animal with a stomach to one with roots like a plant.

Delighted he will examine the complemental males ofScalpellum.

letters.title: To W. M. Hacon   16 April [1874]
letters.summary: CD’s son Francis is to be married, so CD is seeking advice as to how much he should arrange as a marriage-settlement.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   16 April 1874
letters.summary:
His note on the brain should be in small type.

Glad CD agrees with him on hand, foot, and skull question.

Has heard from Dohrn.

letters.title: To Edward Frankland   17 April 1874
letters.summary: Thanks for the pure phosphate of lime.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   18 April 1874
letters.summary:
Sends queries [on proofs ofDescent, 2d ed.]. Will be finished, except for the index, in two days.

Is now less satisfied than formerly with his statistics on cousin marriage.

[Enclosure is a copy by GHD of J. S. Mill’s statement aboutOrigin(Logic2: 18 n.).]

letters.title: ToNature   18 April [1874]
letters.summary: CD has observed hundreds of primrose flowers cut off their stalks, and conjectures that this was done by birds to obtain the nectar. Asks readers ofNaturein England and abroad whether primroses are subject to such destruction in their localities.

letters.title: To Leonard Rudd   18 April [1874]
letters.summary: Discusses LR’s communication concerning supernumerary mammae.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   19 April [1874]
letters.summary:
Is sorry to hear the news about the cousin question – a real misfortune.

Congratulates GHD on being nearly finished with work onDescent.

letters.title: To Henry Willett   19 April [1874]
letters.summary: F. M. Balfour is in Naples. Comments on rate at which sea eats back the land, as given in early editions ofOrigin.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   20 April 1874
letters.summary:
SendsDescentmaterial. Is staggered by CD’s power of marshalling facts and his conciseness and clearness of thought. The only fault he finds is some slight want of conciseness of diction.

He feels CD’s power more now "that I quail before the thought of arranging the few paltry facts I’ve got about those d––d cousins".

letters.title: From Eliza Meteyard   20 April 1874
letters.summary:
The memorial failed last autumn. She asks for CD’s signature again so that it may be presented now that there is a new Government.

Her [Wedgwood]Handbookis now in press.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   20 April [1874]
letters.summary:
FM gives his own observations of leaf-cutting ants, which support those of Thomas Belt in his book [The naturalist in Nicaragua(1873)]. [See9223.] These ants feed only upon the fungus that grows upon the leaves that they carry to their nests.

He has caught a moth of the Glaucopidæ that when touched emitted a cloud of snow-white wool.

Observations on the stingless bees of Brazil.

letters.title: From Henry Cecil   21 April 1874
letters.summary: Affirms his belief in an impassable spiritual gulf between man and the lower creatures.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   [21 April 1874]
letters.summary:
GHD’s corrections seem very good. Murray hopes there will be few corrections inDescent. CD assured him no changes have been made merely for improving style.

Wants very much to hear about "the terrible cousin affair".

letters.title: To Edward Frankland   22 April [1874]
letters.summary: Requests permission to call briefly to discussDrosera.

letters.title: To Michael Foster   23 April [1874]
letters.summary: Approves of proof [of subscription appeal for Dohrn’s Naples station]. Suggests names.

letters.title: From Charles Lyell   24 April 1874
letters.summary: Will subscribe £25 towards F. A. Dohrn’s Zoological Station at Naples.

letters.title: From J. S. Burdon Sanderson   25 April 1874
letters.summary: Purpose of experiments was to determine digestive activity of liquids containing pepsin. Gives required amounts of hydrochloric, propionic, butyric and valerianic acids. Describes experiment and gives results. Also experimented on digestive activity of butyric acid at greater temperatures than the termperature of the body.

letters.title: To Michael Foster   25 April [1874]
letters.summary: Has received circulars, and contributions from Lyell and George Busk [for Naples biological station].

letters.title: From W. B. Dawkins   26 April 1874
letters.summary: Asks CD’s support for his application for the Chair of Geology at Oxford.

letters.title: From Edward Frankland   26 April 1874
letters.summary: Bullfinches’ instinctive capacity for removing nectaries from cowslips.

letters.title: From C. J. Monro   26 April 1874
letters.summary: Sends cherry blossoms damaged by birds in response to CD’s letter inNature["Flowers of the primrose",Collected papers2: 183–4].

letters.title: From A. S. G. Canning   27 April 1874
letters.summary: Further particulars on pea-fowl.

letters.title: To Edward Frankland   28 April [1874]
letters.summary: Thanks for letter relating to domesticated bullfinches’ instinctively cutting off cowslips [see9430]. Suggests observing whether the birds swallow any part of flower or particular parts.

letters.title: From Albert Günther   28 April 1874
letters.summary: Thanks for recent edition of CD’sJournal of researches.

letters.title: From F. S. B. François de Chaumont   29 April 1874
letters.deprecated: Francis Stephen Bennet François de Chaumont
letters.sender: Francis Stephen Bennet François de Chaumont
letters.summary: Observations on early shedding of tears and shrugging of shoulders.

letters.title: To C. H. Merriam   29 April 1874
letters.summary: Asks CHM to send his paper.

letters.title: From Edward Frankland   30 April 1874
letters.summary: Variation in bullfinches’ instinctive ability to remove nectaries and ovaries from cowslips.

letters.title: To F. S. B. François de Chaumont   30 April 1874
letters.deprecated: Francis Stephen Bennet François de Chaumont
letters.recipient: Francis Stephen Bennet François de Chaumont
letters.summary: Agrees to sign FDeC’s certificate for admission to the Royal Society.

letters.title: From J. M. Grandclément   [May 1874]
letters.summary: He was chagrined to read inDescentCD’s statement that smallpox vaccine has saved thousands of lives. He has found no scientific reason to believe in the prophylactic effect of the vaccine. In epidemic of 1870–1, smallpox killed more vaccinated persons than were killed by cholera, against which there is no vaccine, in 1853–4. Cites the difficulties in arriving at a conclusive proof of vaccine’s effectiveness.

letters.title: To Easton and Anderson   4 May [1874]
letters.summary: CD’s son Horace wishes to continue at Easton and Anderson’s Works. CD trusts they will not bind him to long hours of work as this would be against medical advice.

letters.title: To F. S. B. François de Chaumont   4 May 1874
letters.deprecated: Francis Stephen Bennet François de Chaumont
letters.recipient: Francis Stephen Bennet François de Chaumont
letters.summary: Returns FDeC’s certificate for the Royal Society signed.

letters.title: From T. M. Story-Maskelyne   4 May 1874
letters.summary: Reply to CD’s letter inNature["Flowers of the primrose",Collected papers2: 183–4]. She has a canary that eats primroses.

letters.title: To J. S. Burdon Sanderson   5 May [1874]
letters.summary: Thanks for the acid digestion experiments, which can be printed as they are. CD tryingDroseraon dentine and enamel.

letters.title: From J. F. McLennan   5 May 1874
letters.summary:
Would like to see C. S. Wake’s paper ["Marriage among primitive peoples",Anthropologia1 (1873–5): 197–207].

Will return L. H. Morgan’s work [?Systems of consanguinity(1871)].

Murray suggests Macmillan’s are more likely to reprint JFMcL’sPrimitive marriage.

letters.title: ToNature   7 and 11 May [1874]
letters.summary: ThanksNaturecorrespondents for their observations on destruction of primroses [Nature9 (1874): 509; 10 (1874): 6–7]. Reports an error in his observations: ovules, as well as nectar, are taken by the birds. As the habit of cutting off primrose flowers is widespread, CD concludes it is instinctive in bullfinches.

letters.title: From T. M. Reade   7 May 1874
letters.summary: Studying glacial drift in NW. England, he finds evidence of intense glacial activity, but the molluscan fauna does not appear to indicate a low sea temperature. Requests information on Tierra del Fuego molluscs for comparison.

letters.title: From W. D. Fox   8 May [1874]
letters.summary: Has left Delamere and settled on the Isle of Wight.

letters.title: From J. F. McLennan   8 May 1874
letters.summary: Thanks for issue ofAnthropologia. Would be pleased if CD would write to Murray on his behalf.

letters.title: To Béla Weisz   8 May 1874
letters.summary: Would be interesting to discuss political economy in light of evolution. Recommends Walter BagehotPhysics and politics[1872] andDescentin which source of moral sense is discussed.

letters.title: From Michael Foster   [before 9 May 1874]
letters.summary: Encloses a report on state of appeal for Naples Zoological Station.

letters.title: To William Crookes   9 May [1874]
letters.summary:
Regrets he cannot comply with request because of his work and poor health.

Delighted to have seen correspondent’s "wonderful experiment" at Royal Society.

letters.title: To Michael Foster   9 May [1874]
letters.summary: CD is rather disappointed by the money raised for Dohrn. Had hoped for £700–800.

letters.title: To John Murray   9 May [1874]
letters.summary: Recommends that JM consider publishing a new edition of J. F. McLennan’sPrimitive marriage[1865]. CD considers it very valuable and not too indelicate.

letters.title: To T. M. Reade   9 May 1874
letters.summary: Interested in TMR’s investigation of drift.Narrative1: 545–6 contains catalogue of shells collected. Much struck by marine productions of Tierra del Fuego.

letters.title: To T. L. Brunton   11 May 1874
letters.summary: Encloses, for examination, residue from skim-milk which has been on the glands ofDrosera. Asks TLB to confirm his views on action ofDroserasecretion on milk. Asks about effects of pepsin and hydrochloric acid in digestive juice.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   11 May [1874]
letters.summary:
Has just finished new editions ofDescent

andCoral reefs.

Is working on a book almost wholly onDrosera; thinks he has made some discoveries.

Will never have strength and life to complete more of the series of books related toOrigin.

letters.title: From J. S. Burdon Sanderson   12 May [1874]
letters.summary: Reports results of experiments comparing digestibility of gluten and fibrin for CD’s work onDrosera.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   12 May 1874
letters.summary:
Encloses letter and sketch from O. N. Rood on pointed ears.

Reports observations onSarracenia variolaris. A correspondent finds that the fluid in the pitchers is anaesthetic and that a sweet trail runs down the plant, nearly to the ground, to lure up ants.

Encloses two articles on insectivorous plants [Nation18 (1874): 216–17, 232–4].

letters.title: To J. N. Lockyer   13 May [1874]
letters.summary:
Encloses notes concerning his life and list of publications.

Returns the letters about primroses: they contain little that is new. Dr Bree’s is the best.

letters.title: From J. F. McLennan   13 May 1874
letters.summary: Bernard Quaritch interested in reprintingPrimitive marriage.

letters.title: To J. S. Burdon Sanderson   14 May 1874
letters.summary: Discusses digestion by insectivorous plants, asks JSBS to try same experiments using pepsin as the digestive agent to see how the results compare with CD’s observations on digestive power ofDrosera.

letters.title: To Edward Frankland   14 May [1874]
letters.summary: Requests sewage water (and oleic acid) for experiments to determine sensitivity of leaves [ofDrosera].

letters.title: From E. E. Klein   14 May 1874
letters.summary: Reports on his examination of the effects ofDroserasecretion on tooth enamel and dentine, and of artificial gastric juice on fibrous basis of bone.

letters.title: To Carl du Prel   19 May 1874
letters.deprecated: Carl Ludwig August Friedrich Maximilian Alfred (Carl) Du Prel, baron
letters.recipient: Carl Ludwig August Friedrich Maximilian Alfred (Carl) Du Prel, baron
letters.summary: Thanks him for copy of book [Der Kampf um’s Dasein am Himmel(1874)].

letters.title: From C. H. Merriam   19 May 1874
letters.summary:
Sends the 1872Reportof the U. S. Geological Survey of the Territories, for which he was zoologist.

Most American naturalists support CD. His study of ornithology convinced him.

Lepus bairdiihas a distribution limited to Yellowstone Lake.

No doubt CD knows of O. C. Marsh’s horse fossils.

letters.title: To Edward Frankland   20 May [1874]
letters.summary: Thanks for the sewage water and the oleic acid. The former does not seem to act.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   22 May 1874
letters.summary:
Sends Edinburgh address so he may be sent sheets ofDescent[2d English, for 3d German ed.].

Has a large class for his lectures.

letters.title: From T. L. Brunton   23 May 1874
letters.summary:
Comments on his examination of slides [of milk casein?] sent by CD.

Surprised by CD’s finding that a drop of one per cent hydrochloric acid stops digestion of albumen byDrosera.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   23 May [1874]
letters.summary:
Descent[2d English ed.] will not be published until November. Will send JVC first sheet of revised proofs soon.

Pleased to hear of success of JVC’s lectures.

Summer plans have changed. Does not yet know when he will take a month’s holiday.

letters.title: From G. E. Dobson   23 May 1874
letters.summary:
Sends his paper ["On secondary sexual characters in the Cheiroptera",Proc. Zool. Soc. Lond.(1873): 241–52]

and some of his observations of the gecko, which appear to contradict CD’s opinion.

letters.title: To Japetus Steenstrup   23 May [1874 or 1875?]
letters.summary: "With kind regards, & many thanks for Prof. Steenstrup’s Photograph, which is most highly valued by C. Darwin"

letters.title: From G. S. Anderson   24 May 1874
letters.summary: Sends CD photograph of a "natural curiosity", a bear apparently "painted" with red iron on the face of a soft rock; has also sent copies to a few U. S. scientists.

letters.title: To T. L. Brunton   25 May [1874]
letters.summary: CD responds to information about residue of milk digested byDrosera. Is obliged for information on strength of acids and albumen and now has little doubt acid had impaired the leaves. Awaits word on pepsin and papaw juice.

letters.title: To G. E. Dobson   25 May [1874]
letters.summary:
Thanks for note and paper ["Secondary sexual characters in Cheiroptera",Proc. Zool. Soc. Lond.(1873): 241–52].

Has corrected error in new edition ofDescent[1874].

Sees nothing strange in geckos inhabiting frost-clad land and having no claws.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   25 May 1874
letters.summary: Regret at reading of Huxley’s death [a false report].

letters.title: From J. S. Burdon Sanderson   26 May [1874]
letters.summary: Sends CD provisional information that artificial gastric juice dissolves bone entirely and that gluten and fibrin are completely dissolved in hydrochloric, propionic, and butyric acids. [SeeInsectivorous plants, pp. 118–19.]

letters.title: To J. C. Kemp   [26 May 1874]
letters.summary: There is no uniform edition of CD’s work.

letters.title: To J. S. Burdon Sanderson   27 May [1874]
letters.summary: Thanks JSBS for his work. CD concludes the ferment ofDroseramust differ from pepsin.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   27 May [1874]
letters.summary: D. A. Spalding has asked for information to help with his experiments on sense of direction in animals. Has arrived at same results as GHD with blindfolded children. Will GHD let him have his results?

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   [29 May 1874]
letters.summary:
CD has forwarded proofs ofDescent[2d edition]. Urges GHD not to work on them if his poor health makes them too tiring.

Thanks GHD about Spalding [i.e., for responding to Spalding’s request, see9472].

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   30 May 1874
letters.summary: Intends to keep working on [Descent, 2d ed.] proofs despite his illness.

letters.title: To Gaston de Saporta   30 May 1874
letters.deprecated: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.recipient: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.summary:
Thanks GdeS for his "Études sur la végétation" [Ann. Sci. Nat. (Bot.)5th ser. 15 (1872): 277–315]. "Nothing can be more important … than your evidence of the extremely slow and gradual manner in which specific forms change."

Hopes GdeS will shed light on whether polymorphic forms likeRubusandHieraciumare generating new species at present; CD doubts this.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   31 May [1874]
letters.summary: Comments on CL’s planned bequest to science. CD would do the same if he had fewer sons.

letters.title: From W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   31 May 1874
letters.summary: Movement in plants; effect of syringing onOpuntiaplants that capture insects with their flowers.

letters.title: To C. H. Merriam   1 June 1874
letters.summary: Thanks CHM for a report about birds of the United States [see9461].

letters.title: To Asa Gray   3 June [1874]
letters.summary:
CD is deeply pleased by AG’s article on him inNature[10 (1874): 79–81].

Is preparing book on "Droseraand Co." for the printers. Reports observations on digestion inDroseraandPinguicula.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   4 June 1874
letters.summary:
Discusses effects of water on movement of insectivorous plants.

Has just found thatPinguiculacan digest albumen.

Asa Gray writes thatSarraceniasecretes trail of fluid to attract insects [see9455].

letters.title: To I. L. Donnelly   5 June [1874]
letters.summary:
Thanks ID for interesting and curious facts but doubts that he will have time to enter more closely into the subject of the intellect of animals.

Nothing would give CD more "pleasure & interest" than to see ID’s country, "now so great & destined to be so much greater", but he is quite incapable of "so great an exertion as crossing the Atlantic".

letters.title: To Asa Gray   5 June [1874]
letters.summary: Profoundly grateful for AG’s article inNature; he is especially pleased by what AG says about teleology.

letters.title: From W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   5 June 1874
letters.summary: Sends information on nitrogen and albuminoid content of seeds ofBrassica.

letters.title: To W. C. Marshall   8 June [1874]
letters.summary: Asks what proportion of leaves of Pinguicula have insects adhering to them. Also, whether seeds of any plants ever adhere to the leaves, and in what situations does P. vulgaris grow.

letters.title: From Mary Treat   8 June 1874
letters.summary: Sends her observations onDionaeacapturing insects. [SeeInsectivorous plants, pp. 311–12.]

letters.title: To ?   8 June 1874
letters.summary: Asks about insects and seeds on leaves ofPinguicula.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   9 June 1874
letters.summary:
Did not know cabbage contained so much nitrogen.

Pinguiculamore excited by seeds thanDrosera. Asks for information aboutPinguicula.

Asks name of weed.

Asks to borrowUtriculariaplant.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   10 June 1874
