letters.summary: Comments on GHD’s paper ["Marriages between first cousins in England and their effects",Fortn. Rev.n.s. 18 (1875): 22–41]. Hopes it will be published and read at the Statistical Society.

letters.title: From J. T. Moggridge   11 June 1874
letters.summary:
Charles Martins has given the first Darwinian lectures on zoology at Montpellier.

Joseph Duval-Jouve is also a Darwinian. The latter has lost his position as Inspector of the Academy because of his liberal views.

Wallace suggests that a trap-door spider with an exposed nest preys on nocturnal insects.

letters.title: To J. S. Burdon Sanderson   12 June 1874
letters.summary:
JSBS’s article inNature["Venus’s fly-trap", 10 (1874): 105–7, 127–8] could not have been better done.

Has found another plant,Pinguicula, which can catch and digest flies.

letters.title: To J. T. Moggridge   12 June [1874]
letters.summary:
Did not know Duval-Jouve was an evolutionist.

Delighted at JTM’s success with spiders.

On JTM’s experiments with acids on seeds.

letters.title: From J. M. Grandclément   [after 15 June 1874]
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for his answer to his letter. It has not convinced him – he still sees no reason to believe in the prophylactic effect of the vaccine.

Sends an article he has written answering Émile Blanchard of the Academy. Naturalists in France who occupy official positions are not independent.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   16 June 1874
letters.summary: In doubt about size of printing of the 2d edition ofDescent. Profit on 2000 at 12s would be only £250.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   16 June 1874
letters.summary:
AG’s article inNaturewas "just and moderate".

Sends his review of C. Hodge’sWhat is Darwinism?(1874) [Nation18 (1874): 348–51].

It is uphill work making a theist out of CD.

Gives further observations onSarracenia variolaris.

letters.title: From Ferdinand von Mueller   16 June 1874
letters.summary:
Wants information from CD for a revision of the supplement of his work on timber trees and other industrial plants [Proc. Zool. & Acclim. Soc. Victoria3 (1874): 47–95].

Reports the ruin of his department thanks to two papers by Edward Wilson, McKinnon, and Sparrow.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   17 June [1874]
letters.summary:
Asks JVC if he can provide introductions in Leipzig and Dresden for his son George.

Has not yet received any revised sheets ofDescent[2d English ed.].

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   17 June [1874]
letters.summary: Hopes a printing of 2000 copies [ofDescent, 2d ed.] will be safe. Regrets price must be 12s. He is sure it is much improved.

letters.title: From Joseph Fayrer   17 June 1874
letters.summary: Sends CD some cobra poison for his experiments.

letters.title: From Michael Foster   17 June [1874]
letters.summary:
Encloses a report on current status of the appeal for Naples Zoological Station.

Shark embryology.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [before 18 June 1874]
letters.summary: Sends references onUtriculariaandPinguicula.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   18 June 1874
letters.summary: Asks for living plant ofUtriculariaand information onPinguicula lusitanica. Gives notes on habitats.

letters.title: From W. W. Keen   18 June 1874
letters.summary: The lack of a hereditary effect of circumcision among Jews argues against CD’s views.

letters.title: From J. S. Burdon Sanderson   19 June 1874
letters.summary: Sends cartilage from cat’s ear, the elastic fibres of which will probably resist digestion [byDrosera]. Is preparing fibro-cartilage, which he expects will be digested easily. [SeeInsectivorous plants, p. 104.]

letters.title: From Asa Gray   19 June 1874
letters.summary: Writes of his article inNature. Corrects some errors that have appeared in the published version.

letters.title: From H. W. Jackson   20 June 1874
letters.summary: Cites instances of invariable correlations of colour he has observed in cats, dogs, and sheep. [SeeVariation, 2d ed., 2: 316.]

letters.title: To J. S. Burdon Sanderson   21 June [1874]
letters.summary: Thanks for fibrin.DroseraandPinguiculadissolve it thoroughly.

letters.title: From T. M. Coan   22 June 1874
letters.summary: Passes on his father’s answer to CD’s query about Hawaiian infanticide.

letters.title: From W. D. Fox   22 June [1874]
letters.summary: Will try to get certain insectivorous plants for CD, especiallyUtricularia. Is glad to hear he has taken upDrosera.

letters.title: To Mary Treat   22 June 1874
letters.summary: Will soon publish on insectivorous plants; asks for a particular observation onDionaea.

letters.title: To ?   22 June [1874–81]
letters.summary:
Sends signed photo of himself.

Has published only one paper inPhilosophical Transactions of Royal Society, "Parallel roads of Glen Roy" [Collected papers1: 87–137]. His conclusions have proved erroneous.

letters.title: From T. C. Copland   23 June 1874
letters.summary: Sends a description ofDrosera dichotomaand its manner of fly-catching [seeInsectivorous plants, p. 282].

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   23 June 1874
letters.summary: Has foundPinguiculaexcited by bits of leaves; appears to digest leaves and seeds. Plant not only insectivorous but graminivorous. Asks WTT-D to identify seeds.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   24 [June 1874]
letters.summary: Describes howPinguiculacaptures insects.

letters.title: To Joseph Fayrer   [before 25 June 1874]
letters.summary: Sends observations of poison acting on glands of Drosera. Poison acts as a stimulant to protoplasm. Very remarkable that poison acts so differently on the cilia and protoplasm ofDrosera.

letters.title: From Thomas Aitken   [c. 25 June 1874]
letters.summary: Reports thatPinguiculais found in north of Scotland. Gives local names and uses. None of his patients, who are from all parts of Scotland, has heard of the use ofPinguiculato curdle milk.

letters.title: From John Ball   25 June [1874]
letters.summary:
Received CD’s note late and so could not comply, but promises to vote in future for anyone CD recommends for Athenaeum.

Will have new evidence on dog’s intelligence sent to CD.

letters.title: From Joseph Fayrer   25 June 1874
letters.summary: Action of cobra poison.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   25 June 1874
letters.summary: Remarks on his work onPinguicula. Notes its digestive power; it absorbs nutritious matter from leaves and seeds as well as insects.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   25 June 1874
letters.summary: Returns proof of his note on brain for 2d ed. ofDescent. Has added a reference to Abbé Lecomte’s "terrible pamphlet" [Le Darwinisme et l’origine de l’homme(1873)] "lest it be thought I meant our cher Owen".

letters.title: From W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   25 June 1874
letters.summary: Reports on his examination of the dried specimens ofPinguiculaat Kew to answer CD’s query whether all species secrete.

letters.title: To John Ralfs   [after 25 June 1874]
letters.summary: Wants particularly to know whether seeds or leaves of other plants are ever found adhering to the leaves of Pinguicula. Observations would perhaps best be made in a month or two.

letters.title: To John Ball   26 June 1874
letters.summary: Thanks for letter. CD’s nephew got into the club. The book about the beaver is probably that by Mr Morgan. Does not intend to publish further on the intelligence of the dog.

letters.title: From J. S. Burdon Sanderson   26 June [1874]
letters.summary: Is delighted to hear thatPinguiculaandDroseradigest fibrin. Suggests diluting gluten in weak hydrochloric acid to remove starch. Enamel was nearly digested [byDrosera] overnight. Would like to try separating the digestive ferment ofPinguicula.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   26 June 1874
letters.summary:
Thanks for letter and seeds.

Asks that Hooker return references about plants eating insects.

DiscussesPinguicula.

letters.title: From W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   26 June 1874
letters.summary: Identifies seeds adhering to leaves ofPinguicula[seeInsectivorous plants, p. 369].

letters.title: From Leonard Darwin   [before 27 June 1874]
letters.summary: LD has misplaced some figures on which he was to work.

letters.title: From Eliza Meteyard   27 June 1874
letters.summary:
Her memorial has passed and her civil list pension has been increased to £100 per annum for life.

Dr Johnson of Shrewsbury has R. W. Darwin letters.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   27 [June 1874]
letters.summary:
Thanks for letter onErica tetralix.

Identification of leaves digested byPinguicula.

letters.title: To David Moore   28 June 1874
letters.summary: Requests liveUtriculariaandDrosophyllumat suggestion of W. T. Thiselton-Dyer.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   28 [June 1874]
letters.summary:
Must stop work on "bloom" and leaf movements if he is ever to get anything published onDrosera, etc.

Sends thanks for seeds. Encloses memorandum in case WTT-D wishes to communicate information to Royal Horticultural Society. Has not time to prepare article.

Discusses condition of plants borrowed from Kew.

letters.title: From Joseph Fayrer   30 June 1874
letters.summary: Reports on results of experiments on effect of cobra poison on animal cilia and muscle.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   30 June [1874]
letters.summary:
Thanks forSarracenia, which is as wonderful as any orchid.

Asks AG to observePinguicula.

Has read AG’s semi-theological review [Nation18 (1874): 348–51] with interest

and has obtained the book [C. Hodge,What is Darwinism?(1874)].

letters.title: To ?   30 June [1874–81]
letters.summary: Asks for copy of [unspecified] essay, but will not answer it.

letters.title: To Joseph Fayrer   [1–3 July 1874]
letters.summary: Cobra poison is a stimulant to protoplasm. Poison acts very differently on cilia and protoplasm ofDrosera.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   1 July [1874]
letters.summary: Asks WED to visit Winchester soon and collect Utricularia for him

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   1 July 1874
letters.summary:
Has "given the slip" toNepenthes, but is setting a plant up in an enclosure for special observation.

Has some splendidSarraceniaand will perform any miracle regarding them CD puts him up to.

Charmed with CD’s account ofPinguicula. Would like to try whetherLychnishas the same use of viscid fluid.

Has written for EnglishUtriculariafor CD.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   1 July 1874
letters.summary: Describes leaf movements ofPinguiculaandDroserain capturing prey. Notes effects of ammonium carbonate on leaves.

letters.title: From L. C. Harrison   [1 July 1874]
letters.summary: Sends further details onPinguiculareference.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   2 July 1874
letters.summary: Thinks Frank and he have worked outPinguiculawell and they long to attackUtricularia. Tried several plants with sticky glandular hairs; some few absorb ammonia, but the greater number do not. If JDH sends plant or seed ofLychnisCD will examine it to see whether it catches many flies. Asa Gray has written him much aboutSarracenia, with a specimen showing the splendid dodge by which ground insects are enticed up and then drowned. Describes how it may be investigated, to see whether it absorbs decayed matter from flies, or ammonia thus generated.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   3 July 1874
letters.summary: Sends results of his observations onNepenthes. Would be grateful for any hints for further observations.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   4 July [1874]
letters.summary: Has read THF’s article onCoronilla[see9400] – "a very curious case"; is troubled byC. emerus.

letters.title: To Joseph Fayrer   4 July [1874]
letters.summary: Suggests experiment involving cobra poison on white corpuscles. Thanks for offer ofCrotaluspoison.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   4 July 1874
letters.summary: It would be interesting to prove that some plants feed on decayed animal matter whilst others likeDroseracan digest fresh animal matter. Suggests the method for observing this.

letters.title: From Joseph Fayrer   6 July 1874
letters.summary:
Will do experiments CD suggests.

Is sending his book on the poisonous snakes of India [The Thanatophidia of India(1872)].

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   7 July 1874
letters.summary:
Thanks for proofs [ofDescent, 2d English ed.].

Publisher would like better photographs forExpression[2d German ed.].

letters.title: To F. C. Donders   7 July 1874
letters.summary: Asks about the effect of atropine on the eye. Is interested in parallel case: influence of phosphate of ammonia on glands ofDrosera.

letters.title: From E. B. Baxter   8 July 1874
letters.summary: Sends quotation from R. C. Virchow which contravenes CD’s statement inExpressionthat there is no voluntary control of the iris.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   8 July 1874
letters.summary: The appetite ofNepenthesfor hard-boiled egg is prodigious.

letters.title: To John Ralfs   8 July 1874
letters.summary: Thanks for the Pinguicula plants, which have recovered, and asks if he could also send Utricularia, since his other supplies have failed.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   9 July [1874]
letters.summary:
Advises JVC on how his publisher might deal with problem of getting satisfactory heliotype copies for 2d [German] edition ofExpression.

Regrets that he will again be away in August, when JVC might have come for a visit.

letters.title: From David Moore   9 July 1874
letters.summary:
Sends anUtriculariaand aDrosophyllum.

Observations onPinguicula grandiflora. [SeeInsectivorous plants, p. 390.]

letters.title: From John Ralfs   9 July 1874
letters.summary: Sends specimens ofPinguiculaand observations made on them. [SeeInsectivorous plants, pp. 390–1.]

letters.title: From E. E. Klein   10 July 1874
letters.summary: Reports results [partly excised] of examination of fibro-cartilage subjected to artificial gastric juice and toDroserasecretion. [SeeInsectivorous plants, pp. 104–5.]

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   10 July 1874
letters.summary: Sets out some of his ideas on the effects of disuse on an organ. Disuse as a cause of reduction.

letters.title: From F. C. Donders   12 July 1874
letters.summary: On hearing of CD’s work withDrosera, tells of his experiment showing extreme sensitivity of the iris of a dog’s eye to atropine. [SeeInsectivorous plants, p. 173.]

letters.title: To David Moore   12 July 1874
letters.summary: Thanks forDrosophyllum. No longer needsUtricularia.

letters.title: To John Ralfs   13 July [1874]
letters.summary:
Discusses specimens ofUtricularia.

Mentions JR’s work on desmids [The British Desmidieae[Desmidiae!?] (1848)].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [before 15 July 1874]
letters.summary: Suggests experiments to try [with Nepenthes]. Asks JDH to test whether cabbage seeds and peas exposed to the ferment germinate.

letters.title: To F. C. Donders   15 July 1874
letters.summary:
Discusses effect of atropine solution on eye,

and effect of phosphate of ammonia solution on gland ofDrosera.

Would like to see work by T. W. Engelmann and possibly one by Dr De Ruyter.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   15 July 1874
letters.summary:
Asks what can be the meaning of appendages to tips of leaflets of enclosedAcaciaorMimosa.

Is at fibrin today.

Michael Foster suggests coagulation of protoplasm may be diseased, not digestive, symptom.

F. M. Balfour is at Kew today.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   16 July 1874
letters.summary:
TheAcaciamust be Belt’s "Bulls’ horns".

The complexity ofUtriculariahas driven Frank and CD almost mad. Suspects it is necrophagous, i.e., it cannot digest, but absorbs decaying animal matter.

Foster is certainly in error. Every insect thatDroseracatches causes aggregation.

letters.title: From T. L. Marshall   16 July [1874]
letters.summary: She and her father have been counting insect remains onPinguiculahairs.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   16 July 1874
letters.summary: Thanks GJR for his letter, regrets pressure of other work prevents his giving GJR’s remarks the attention they deserve. GJR makes clearer how an organ that has started to decrease will go on decreasing.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   18 July 1874
letters.summary:
TwoNepentheshave devoured two pieces of fibrin [sketch shows size] in three days.

Has CD any objection to JDH’s giving an account of CD’sDroseraobservations at Belfast [BAAS meeting] in a résumé of pitcher-plant results ["Address to the department of botany and zoology",Rep. BAAS44 (1874): 102–16]?

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin [19? July 1874]
letters.summary:
WED encloses a letter from H. M. Wilkinson about Utricularia and sundew.

H. M. Wilkinson has examined bladders ofUtricularia; doubts that they absorb or digest insects.

H. M. Wilkinson describes dragonfly trapped by sundew [Drosera].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   20 July [1874]
letters.summary:
"It is grand about Nepenthes."

JDH is welcome to notice in any way any of CD’s published or unpublished results with insectivorous plants. Gives an abstract of his observations onDrosera.

letters.title: From J. D. Dana   21 July 1874
letters.summary:
Thanks CD forCoral reefs[2d ed. (1874)].

JDD will correct his misunderstanding of CD on one point in the next edition of his book [Corals and coral islands].

Suggests CD consult Charles Wilkes’sNarrative[1844] for more accurate observations on Pacific islands.

letters.title: From D. A. Spalding   21 July 1874
letters.summary:
Thanks for CD’s son’s observations

and for allowing DAS to visit Down.

letters.title: From Joseph Fayrer   22 July 1874
letters.summary:
Is glad CD approves of his book;

has not yet done any more experiments on snake poison.

letters.title: To Edward Frankland   22 July 1874
letters.summary: Asks for the specific gravity of common phosphate of ammonia.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   22 July 1874
letters.summary:
Stupefied by CD’s trouble and kindness. All he wanted for Belfast meeting was assurance that mention of published work onDrosera, etc., inNature, etc., would not interfere with CD’s book.

Would like hisNepenthesresults to go to CD or to Royal Society, but prefers CD take them.

Cephalotusvery puzzling.

Peas and cabbage grow twice as fast after two days’ immersion inNepenthesas when placed in distilled water, but four days’ immersion seems to kill them.

Has a splendid AustralianDroseratwice as big asD. rotundifolia.

letters.title: From T. L. Brunton   23 July [1874]
letters.summary: Encloses a tracing of a portrait of John Bunyan showing the differences of the two sides of the face.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   23 July [1874]
letters.summary:
JDH should do as he likes with insectivorous plant materials.

He has always thought telling JDH what he has been doing was as good as publishing.

Cephalotusseems as horrid a puzzle asUtricularia.

Nepentheswill turn out a great job if the pitchers of different species act differently. JDH’s paper onNepenthes[Rep. BAAS44 (1874): 102–16] is too long for CD’s book. Well deserves a place inPhilosophical Transactions.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [after 23 July 1874]
letters.summary: Asks for a specimen ofPinguicula.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   24 [July 1874]
letters.summary: Arrangements for the visit to Southampton.

letters.title: From E. E. Klein   24 July 1874
letters.summary: Gives details of the smallest micrococci distinctly discernible under a microscope.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   24 July 1874
letters.summary: Encloses a copy of a letter from H. Spencer giving his opinion on GJR’s views on disuse and a draft of GJR’s reply to Spencer.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [c.27 July 1874]
letters.summary: Has been examiningUtricularia minor. Same essential structure but catches smaller Entomostraca. One bladder had 24, another 20, and another 15 Entomostraca. "What slaughter! We must make out the functions of the beast––".

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   [27 July 1874]
letters.summary: Advises GHD to get an eminent counsel. If counsel’s opinion is that the reviewer [Mivart, in "Primitive man",Q. Rev.137 (1874): 40–77] has falsified GHD’s statements, GHD should send the opinion to theQuarterly Reviewand demand publication, and if refused publish elsewhere. Then CD must decide whether to cut John Murray [publisher ofQ. Rev.] which will put CD in a nice perplexity [over his rights to the stereotyped editions of past works].

letters.title: From John Price   [27 July 1874]
letters.summary:
Has someUtricularia minorfor CD. Has found the bladders onU. vulgarisare not floats.

Thanks CD for book [Descent, 2d ed.].

letters.title: To John Price   27 [July 1874]
letters.summary: DiscussesUtriculariasent by JP.

letters.title: From Thomas Belt   28 July 1874
letters.summary: Has observed in his garden hive-bees using the holes bored at the base of flowers by humble-bees.

letters.title: To John Price   28 July [1874]
letters.summary:
Thanks JP for note.

Sends instructions for mailingUtriculariaplants to Down in his absence.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   28 July [1874]
letters.summary: Comments on Spencer’s terms.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   29 July 1874
letters.summary: After taking advice he has decided to write an explicit denial and short account of his essay and send it to theQuarterly Review.

letters.title: From John Murray   29 July [1874]
letters.summary:
Orchidsis at last sold out. Settles account.

TheOrigin[6th ed.] is making good [sales] progress.

Expressionis not selling.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   [30 July 1874]
letters.summary: Hasty note to express his most decided opinion that letter [toQ. Rev.] should not give a sketch of GHD’s essay – only an explicit denial "& do not allude to me".

letters.title: To Thomas Belt   31 July 1874
letters.summary:
Comments on bees.

Praises TB’sThe naturalist in Nicaragua.

letters.title: To J. T. Knowles   31 July 1874
letters.deprecated: James Thomas Knowleseditor of Contemporary Review
letters.recipient: James Thomas Knowleseditor of Contemporary Review
letters.summary:
Asks whether it would be possible forContemporary Reviewto republish an article on language fromNorth American Review[119 (1874): 61–88] by William Dwight Whitney which answers F. Max Müller; would pay expense of printing if necessary.

CD has been abused in theQuarterly Reviewfor "amazing ignorance".

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   1 August [1874]
letters.summary: GHD’s article will not do. It is too long and the denial seems weak and confused; also, it ought to be in the form of a letter to the editor. Encloses draft of the sort of letter of denial he thinks GHD should write.

letters.title: From H. H. Bancroft   3 August 1874
letters.summary: Sends a volume and will send next volumes of a work intended to contribute to the study of mankind.

letters.title: From J. T. Knowles   4 August 1874
letters.summary: Regrets he is unable to republish Whitney’s article in theContemporary Review. Would much appreciate an article from CD on the subject and suggests that CD might quote from Whitney to any extent he likes.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   5 August 1874
letters.summary: Regrets he cannot follow the line of denial CD suggests. Explains why he must defend himself against charge that he approves of oppressive laws.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   [5 or 6 August 1874]
letters.summary:
Has no objection to sending GHD’s letter as it is. The only accusation it seems necessary to rebut is about licentiousness. Regrets this is not made more prominent.

Gives some suggestions for GHD’s reply to Mivart’s attack.

letters.title: To J. T. Knowles   5 August 1874
letters.deprecated: James Thomas Knowleseditor of Contemporary Review
letters.recipient: James Thomas Knowleseditor of Contemporary Review
letters.summary: CD understands JTK’s reasons [for not republishing W. D. Whitney’s article]. Cannot undertake to write anything himself; he needs rest and is unwilling to enter into controversy.

letters.title: From John Tyndall   5 August 1874
letters.summary: Asks CD to look over those parts of the proofs of his Belfast address [Rep. BAAS44 (1874): lxvi–xcvii] that mention CD.

letters.title: To W. D. Whitney   5 August 1874
letters.summary: Praises WDW’s essay on language [North Am. Rev.119 (1874): 61–88] which argues against Max Müller’s views and is a good defence against an attack made inQuarterly Reviewon CD’s short discussion of language.

letters.title: From H. M. Wilkinson   5 August 1874
letters.summary: Reports his observations ofUtricularia[in their natural state] as CD requested.

letters.title: From Leyson Lewis   [before 6 August 1874]
letters.summary: Encloses specimen of a male hop with female flowers. It is the only peculiarity in the ground.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   6 [August] 1874
letters.summary: Sends a draft of his letter to the editor of theQuarterly Review[137 (1874): 587–9], answering Mivart’s charges. Encloses draft of CD’s letter to John Murray, urging publication of GHD’s defence, with George’s amendments.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [6 or 7 August 1874]
letters.summary: Urges CD not to break with Murray even if he does not force the editor [ofQ. Rev.] to insert GHD’s letter [in response to Mivart’s attack]. Murray may have a rule not to meddle with editor.

letters.title: From M. T. Masters   6 August 1874
letters.summary:
Thanks for the monoecious hop. It was the first monstrosity he ever observed.

Contemplates an article inGardeners’ Chronicleon the horticultural bearing of CD’s fertilisation work.

Will publish note forwarded by CD on a male hop with apparently female flowers (Gardeners’ Chronicle, 8 August 1874, p. 174).

letters.title: To M. T. Masters   7 August [1874]
letters.summary: Discusses flower structures of the hop.

letters.title: From Francis and Amy Darwin   8 August [1874]
letters.deprecated: Francis DarwinAmy Richenda (Amy) RuckAmy Richenda (Amy) Darwin
letters.sender: Francis DarwinAmy Richenda (Amy) RuckAmy Richenda (Amy) Darwin
letters.summary: Describe thePinguiculaspecies found at Mürren. Have found seeds on some. Their large roots seem to indicate that they do not get much animal food.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   [8 August 1874]
letters.summary: Approves of GHD’s letter [toQ. Rev.137 (1874): 587–9] and his present plan, which removes all CD’s objections. Will make his own letter to Murray less imperious. "It will be a dreadful evil to me, if … we come to a quarrel."

letters.title: To John Murray   11 August 1874
letters.summary: Asks JM, as a favour, to use his influence with the Editor ofQuarterly Reviewto print George Darwin’s answer to the charge made by the author of "Primitive man" [St George Mivart] that GD approved "of the encouragement of vice to check population".

letters.title: To John Tyndall   11 August [1874]
letters.summary:
CD has not received the proofs [of JT’s Belfast address to BAAS].

Wishes JT were through with Belfast [meeting of BAAS, 1874]. CD cannot imagine surviving such a week of excitement.

letters.title: From John Murray   12 August 1874
letters.summary: Acknowledges CD’s complaint against a paper [by St George Mivart] in the lastQuarterly Review[see9568]. Agrees to print George Darwin’s answer [see9596].

letters.title: To John Tyndall   12 August [1874]
letters.summary: Returns proofs [of JT’s Belfast address,Rep. BAAS44 (1874): lxvi–xcvii]. Gratified by what it says about his work and is anxious to read the whole address; it is a grand subject.

letters.title: From D. T. Gardner   13 August 1874
letters.summary: The Club is proposing to celebrate Humboldt’s 105th birthday and would welcome a message from CD.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   17 August 1874
letters.summary:
Describes his work onNepenthes.

Cephalotusis a beast.

His address is a history ofDionaea,Sarracenia, andDrosera.

Thiselton-Dyer has helped enormously except with the observations; but his health is so poor that JDH thinks he is "evidently cut out for a Literate not a working botanist".

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   [20? August 1874]
letters.summary: Likes GHD’s article ["Professor Whitney on the origin of language",Contemp. Rev.(1874): 894]. "You have defended me nobly."

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   20 August 1874
letters.summary:
It is splendid howNepenthesis behaving.DroseraandDionaeaare insignificant by comparison.

Takes rather a malicious pleasure in JDH’s failure withCephalotusas a match to his withUtricularia.

letters.title: To J. S. Burdon Sanderson   21 August [1874]
letters.summary:
Reports difficulties in experiments on digestion of fibro-cartilage. Asks about JSBS’s experiments with artificial digestive fluids.

JSBS must read Hooker’s address at Belfast [Rep. BAAS44 (1874): 103–16] to see what a magnificent digesterNepenthesis.

letters.title: From L. C. Harrison   [22 August 1874]
letters.summary: Sends specimens ofPinguiculawith insects adhering. [SeeInsectivorous plants, p. 369.]

letters.title: To Edward Nicholson   26 August [1874]
letters.summary: Thanks EN for his book [Indian snakes, 2d ed. (1874)]. CD is pleased that it calls attention to gradation in the character of snake poison.

letters.title: From A. V. W. Bikkers   27 August 1874
letters.summary: Reports on a crossbreed between a duck and a fowl, having duck’s beak, partly webbed feet, and fowl’s feathers.

letters.title: To D. T. Gardner   [c.27 August 1874]
letters.summary: States his indebtedness to and admiration for Humboldt and his work.

letters.title: From J. A. Gammie   28 August 1874
letters.summary: Sends his observations on the method of fertilisation ofHedychium coronariumbySphinxand other hawk-moths.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [29 August 1874]
letters.summary:
Lady Dorothy Nevill is CD’s best chance forDionaea.

Reports on Belfast meeting of BAAS. Lubbock’s lecture went off admirably. Huxley’s was the magnum opus.

Encloses letter from Mrs Barber on protective coloration of animals.

letters.title: From Henryk Stecki   29 August 1874
letters.summary: Reports observations on a chicken with a human face.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   30 August [1874]
letters.summary:
Thanks JDH for his "quite admirable" address [Rep. BAAS44 (1874) pt 2: 102–16]. Suggests revisions.

CD thinks he is "now on right track aboutUtricularia" after wasting several weeks "in fruitless trials and observations".

Mrs Barber’s paper is very curious and ought to be published.

letters.title: From W. C. Marshall   30 August [1874]
letters.summary: Sends CD a box ofPinguiculaleaves.

letters.title: To W. C. Marshall   [after 30 August 1874]
letters.summary: Glad to hear about sticky fluid on leaves. WCM need not bother to count leaves.

letters.title: To Edward Frankland   31 August 1874
letters.summary: Utriculariacatch freshwater Crustaceans, which cannot be digested and rot in the bladders. CD is interested to identify any substance produced in the putrefaction before it is resolved into gases and salts of ammonia. He has reason to believe that the plant absorbs such products.

letters.title: To A. W. Howitt    [September 1874]
letters.summary: Thanks Howitt for his offer of information from Australia and suggests that Howitt keep detailed notes for a future publication.

letters.title: From James Ross   September 1874
letters.summary:
Sends his book [On protoplasm(1874)], which defends CD’s theory.

Suggests why the lips are closed and the teeth clenched in the expression of determination: it originated as a means of protecting jaw-bone and teeth against a strong blow.

letters.title: From Charles Lyell   1 September 1874
letters.summary:
Comments on Tyndall’s [Presidential] Address at Belfast meeting [of BAAS] and praise of CD’s work there. Mentions criticism of Belfast clergy.

CL saw some crustacean footprints while in Ireland.

letters.title: From D F. Nevill   2 September [1874]
letters.summary: Hooker has told her of CD’s work on insectivorous plants. Offers plants, but herDionaeaplants are too small now.

letters.title: From J. S. Burdon Sanderson   3 September [1874]
letters.summary: Will prepare experiments with the fatty acids on digestion of gluten. Has found it is digested slowly, but entirely, with pepsin and hydrochloric acid.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   3 September [1874]
letters.summary:
Discusses belief in immortality and a personal God.

Describes his holiday in Southampton.

Comments on papers of John Wesley Judd.

letters.title: To D. F. Nevill   3 September 1874
letters.summary:
Thanks DFN for her letter [see9620].

Has nearly finished work onDionaea.

Asks her to send a specimen ofDrosera dichotoma.

letters.title: From Chauncey Wright   3 September 1874
letters.summary:
Writes at length on the origins and meanings of particular head movements as used to express assent or disagreement, especially the sideways movements of the head as an expression of consideration or contemplation.

Also discusses space and colour perception.

letters.title: From T. L. Brunton   4 September 1874
letters.summary: Observations of effect of pepsin and hydrochloric acid on urea indicate that it is not digested [byDrosera].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [after 4 September 1874]
letters.summary: Forwards a letter reporting on a blow-fly trapped by a leaf ofDionaea; decomposition of fly has also decomposed the leaf. JDH has written asking for a strong plant, and explaining the case [of surfeit].

letters.title: From W. C. Marshall   5 September [1874]
letters.summary: SendsPinguicula vulgarisleaves with seeds on them, together with his observations on proportion of leaves with insects on them.

letters.title: To W. C. Marshall   7 September [1874]
letters.summary: Thanks for the Pinguicula leaves, from which he has picked off sixteen seeds.

letters.title: To D. F. Nevill   7 September 1874
letters.summary: Thanks her for specimen ofDrosera. Asks for an epiphyticUtricularia.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   8 September [1874]
letters.summary:
Lady Dorothy Nevill has noDionaea.

CD anxious to talk with JDH aboutUtricularia.

letters.title: From D. F. Nevill   8 [September 1874]
letters.summary:
OffersUtricularia montanaand gives instructions for growingDrosera.

Wishes to visit CD at Down when she comes to London.

letters.title: From John Price   10 September 1874
letters.summary: Observations on flotation ofUtricularia vulgaris.

letters.title: To D. F. Nevill   11 September [1874]
letters.summary:
Returns aDrosera, from which he cut a piece for microscopic examination.

Utricularia montanajust arrived.

letters.title: From D. F. Nevill   [11 September 1874]
letters.summary:
Has sent theUtriculariawith the bladders that CD described.

InVariationCD does not mention a rare breed of Siamese cat, which she owns.

Asks for another photograph.

letters.title: To D. F. Nevill   12 September [1874]
letters.summary:
CD has never before seen theUtriculariaDN has sent. Hooker had told him about it. Asks that her gardener observe youngUtricularia: CD is interested in internal structure of little balls on bladders.

Sends photograph.

letters.title: To James Verrell?   13 September [1874]
letters.summary: Should like to borrow again a volume which he returned in error. RequestsThe Quarterly Magazine of the High Wycombe Natural History Societyfor 1867 and 1868 to locate paper onUtricularia.

letters.title: From ?   13 September 1874
letters.summary: An anonymous letter praising theOrigin.

letters.title: From S. W. Pennypacker   14 September 1874
letters.summary: He has physical peculiarities that support CD’s theories: e.g., ability to dilate nostrils like a rabbit and to spread out the toes of both feet.

letters.title: From Joseph Simms   14 September 1874
letters.summary:
Sends copy of one of his books.

Asks for drawing of CD’s right foot.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   15 September 1874
letters.summary: Thiselton-Dyer’s announcement of his inability to continue as JDH’s private secretary is a blow. He will now be doing original work. JDH is glad of that but the loss of his help is great.

letters.title: From John Murray Jr   15 September 1874
letters.summary: Sends CD a statement of number of thousands of copies printed thus far [by Murray’s] of:Journal of researches(12),Origin(13),Descent(10), andExpression(9).

letters.title: From W. J. L. Wharton   [15 September 1874]
letters.summary: Describes the coral formations of Zanzibar and east coast of Africa.

letters.title: From H. M. Wilkinson   15 September 1874
letters.summary: Utriculariahas broken into pieces and appears to be decaying.

letters.title: From W. J. L. Wharton   [15 September 1874 or later]
letters.summary: Describes the coral formations of the island of Rodriguez [Indian Ocean].

letters.title: From D. F. Nevill   16 [September 1874]
letters.summary:
CD should remove packing moss, and he will find bladders in foot-stalks ofUtriculariaDN sent.

Experimenting on insectivorous plants.

Implores CD to visit.

Thanks for photograph.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   [before 17 September 1874]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Sends MS intended some day for theViola tricolorsection ofCross and self-fertilisation[pp. 123–8] to be used by JL in hisBritish wild flowers(1875).

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [17 September 1874]
letters.summary:
Asks FD to come early to write from dictation.

Thanks Amy for her drawing ofUtricularia montana.

letters.title: From Milan Radovanović   17 September 1874
letters.summary: Has translatedOrigininto Serbian and wants CD’s authorisation to publish.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   18 September [1874]
letters.summary: Describes his observations onUtricularia montana.

letters.title: To D. F. Nevill   18 September [1874]
letters.summary: Stupidly missedUtriculariabladders, which he assumed were with the leaves. Has now found true bladders on roots and has evidence of captive prey. Thinks bladders capture subterranean insects. Thinks the large bladder-like structures are water reservoirs. DN’s plant has given him a most enjoyable day of work.

letters.title: From A. Haines   19 September 1874
letters.summary: States his admiration for CD’s views and their progress in the U. S.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   20 September 1874
letters.summary:
Thanks for 5th edition of his book [Natürliche]Schöpfungsgeschichte.

CD continues with his experiments on the digestive power of plants, which is much like that of mammals.

Is also preparing a revised edition ofDescent.

Would welcome hearing more of his ideas about Pangenesis.

Postscript aboutAnthropogenie, which has just arrived. EH’s astonishing productivity.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [20 September 1874]
letters.summary: Asks JDH to cut a bit of root from oldUtriculariaand bring it with him to Down.

letters.title: From A. W. Bennett   21 September 1874
letters.summary:
Sends papers and references.

Reports his microscopic observations onDroseraand other plants.

letters.title: To James Verrell   21 September 1874
letters.summary: "Naturepublished last Thursday has notyetarrived."

letters.title: To Chauncey Wright   21 September 1874 and 29 January 1875
letters.summary: Head movements and their expressive significance. [P.S. explains letter was returned to CD because of a mistake in the address.]

letters.title: To A. W. Bennett   22 September [1874]
letters.summary:
Thanks for sending papers by Hermann Hoffmann.

Discusses spiral cells inDroseraandPinguicula.

letters.title: From Thomas Meehan   22 September 1874
letters.summary:
Sends CD his photo

and a copy of his address at Hartford ["Change by gradual modification not the universal law",Proc. Am. Assoc. Adv. Sci.(1874) pt 2: 7–12]. Does not believe his observations are unfavourable to natural selection but feels there are other factors involved in the origin of form.

Discusses further his work on colour and sex in plants; the linking of high colour and maleness.

letters.title: From D. F. Nevill   22 [September 1874]
letters.summary: Will send a differentUtriculariaspecies when the seedlings are better established.

letters.title: From Auguste Forel   23 September 1874
letters.summary: Sends a copy of his book on Swiss ants [Les fourmis de la Suisse(1874)]. Notes points and passages that he thinks will interest CD.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   23 September 1874
letters.summary: CD’sUtriculariafindings – bladders, subterranean roots, and insects decomposing in them – a grand discovery.

letters.title: To Charles Lyell   23 September 1874
letters.summary:
Discusses paper on volcanoes by J. W. Judd.

Comments on volcanoes of the S. American Cordillera.

Mentions paper by T. F. Jamieson ["Glacial period in N. Britain",Q. J. Geol. Soc. Lond.30 (1874): 317–18].

letters.title: To T. L. Brunton   25 September 1874
letters.summary:
Comments on digestive action of pepsin and hydrochloric acid.

Photograph of Rubens’ picture has not arrived.

letters.title: From Charles Lyell   25 September 1874
letters.summary:
Notes recent confirmation of CD’s views on subsidence in [island of] St Jago.

Describes Carboniferous strata discovered on Island of Mull by J. W. Judd. Contained evidence of Miocene sinking of volcanoes.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   26 September [1874]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary:
JL’s two articles inNature["Common wild flowers", 10 (1874): 402–6, 422–6].

Cautions against C. K. Sprengel’s notion of bees’ being deceived by nectarless nectary.

Colour of calyces.

letters.title: To A. W. Bennett   27 September [1874]
letters.summary:
Returns copy ofBotanische Zeitung.

Responds to comments onDrosera.

letters.title: To Auguste Forel   28 September [1874]
letters.summary:
Thanks AHF for his book on ants of Switzerland;

recommends reading Thomas Belt’sNaturalist in Nicaragua[1874].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   28 [September 1874]
letters.summary: Queries about species ofUtricularia.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   29 September 1874
letters.summary: Information about various species ofUtricularia.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   30 [September 1874]
letters.summary: TheAldrovandahas arrived. Has examined the leaves. It is an aquaticDionaeawhich has acquired some structures identical to those ofUtricularia!

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   1 October 1874
letters.summary:
Notes that Mr[s] Barber’s communication [forwarded by CD] will be published because of more striking than usual facts ["Notes on … larva and pupa ofPapilio nireus",Trans. R. Entomol. Soc. Lond.(1874): 519–21].

Encloses Thomas Belt’s address.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   1 October [1874]
letters.summary: Thanks JDH for extract onHedychiumpollination; it shows CD’s prior interpretation was incorrect.

letters.title: From F. J. Cohn   4 October 1874
letters.summary:
An account of his observations onAldrovandaandUtricularia.

Sends CD his memoir onAldrovanda[Beitr. Biol. Pflanz.1 (1875) Heft 3: 71–92] in advance of publication [seeInsectivorous plants, pp. 321et seq., 395–6].

letters.title: To James Crichton-Browne   8 October 1874
letters.summary: Thanks JC-B for copy ofMedical Reports of the West Riding Lunatic Asylum.

letters.title: To J. S. Burdon Sanderson   9 October 1874
letters.summary: Has been testing the digestive powers ofDrosera; wants to know whether a group of substances that elicit similar responses are related.

letters.title: From Edward Frankland   9 October 1874
letters.summary: Sends information CD requested on phosphate of ammonia and on nitrogenous substances produced during putrefaction of animal matter.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   9 October 1874
letters.summary: Asks JDH for leaves ofByblisandRoridulato examine, and D. Oliver for an anomalous species ofUtricularia.

letters.title: To Thomas Meehan   9 October 1874
letters.summary:
Doubts whether sudden and great variations often occur.

Comments on colours of flowers.

letters.title: To Edward Frankland   11 October 1874
letters.summary: Acknowledges the information about the phosphate and about putrefaction. Regrets that there is no knowledge of the conjectured substance. [See9671.]

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   11 October 1874
letters.summary:
Oliver will attend to his letter.

Tells of discovery and rediscovery ofAldrovanda.

Asks what CD thinks of "old Pritchard’s discourse" [C. Pritchard,Natural science and natural religion(1874)]. Does not affect evolution at all. It does affect the rather unprofitable doctrine of materialism.

His plans for the Royal Society Presidential Address.

letters.title: From J. S. Burdon Sanderson   12 October 1874
letters.summary: Suggests an explanation for difference in excitability ofDroseraleaves to meat and albumen on the one hand and, on the other, fibrin, areolar tissue, gelatin, and fibrous basis of bone.

letters.title: From W. H. M. Christie   12 October 1874
letters.summary: Announces arrival of theMerope[Leonard Darwin’s ship] at Canterbury, New Zealand.

letters.title: To F. J. Cohn   12 October 1874
letters.summary:
CD responds [to9667] with description of his own effort to studyAldrovandaand his observations on the structure ofDionaea.

His admiration for FJC’s earlier studies of the Venus’s fly-trap.

He urges FJC to proceed promptly with publication of his memoir onAldrovanda[Beiträge zur Biologie der Pflanzen1, Heft 3 (1875): 71–92].

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   12 October 1874
letters.summary: Sends specimens ofByblis,Roridula, andUtriculariafor CD’s examination.

letters.title: To J. S. Burdon Sanderson   13 October 1874
letters.summary: Discusses the powers of digestion ofDroseraand why certain substances produce less excitement in the plant than others.

letters.title: To W. H. M. Christie   13 October [1874]
letters.summary: Thanks WHMC and the Astronomer Royal for informing him of the safe arrival of theMerope[Leonard Darwin’s ship] at New Zealand. [See9677.]

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   14 October 1874
letters.summary: Thanks him for specimens.

letters.title: To Auguste Forel   15 October 1874
letters.summary:
Writes about AHF’s book on Swiss ants.

Recounts his own observations on ants carrying cocoons.

letters.title: From J. S. Burdon Sanderson   16 October [1874]
letters.summary: Responds to CD’s questions about relation to gelatin of areolar tissue, fibrous basis of bone, and other substances CD is using in his work on digestion ofDrosera.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   18 October 1874
letters.summary:
Has been invited to lecture at the Royal Institution by Spottiswoode. Discusses subjects he might deal with and his reasons for attempting it.

Tells of a complicated case of a double sale of a living.

Huxley says F. M. Balfour passed brilliantly.

letters.title: To W. B. Dawkins   18 October [1874]
letters.summary: Thanks WBD for his book,Cave hunting(1874).

letters.title: To John Murray   18 October 1874
letters.summary: Thanks forQuarterly Review[Oct 1874, containing G. H. Darwin’s letter and a rejoinder]. Is convinced the author is Mivart. Is therefore not surprised at malice in the article attacking his son [George Darwin] and grossly misrepresenting CD.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   19 October [1874]
letters.summary:
Advice to GHD on whether to accept invitation to lecture at the Royal Institution.

Murray has sent theQuarterly Reviewissue. CD has told Murray that he is convinced Mivart is the author and what he thinks of him.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   19 October [1874]
letters.summary:
Returns insectivorous plants to Kew, with questions about their range. Most species seem to have remarkably confined ranges.

Asks for a BengalAldrovandaleaf so that he can see whether it differs from the German species.

Roridulainterested him extremely.

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   20 October 1874
letters.summary: Sends information about Indian and Australian species ofAldrovanda,Roridula, andByblis.

letters.title: From W. J. Beal   22 October 1874
letters.summary: Sends his observation of honey-bees gleaning after orioles had made holes in calyx of Missouri currant, while humble-bees were getting honey through the tube in the usual way.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   22 October [1874]
letters.summary:
Sends index [ofDescent, 2d ed.] with instructions for proof-reading.

Asks GHD questions about heat transmission; he wants to use it as an analogy to illustrate transmission of motor impulses through leaves ofDionaea.

letters.title: From Gerard Krefft   22 October 1874
letters.summary: After a conflict with the Museum’s trustees, he has been brutally evicted from his home and office. Plans to leave Australia and asks CD’s help.

letters.title: From Mary Treat   22 October 1874
letters.summary: Observation on the limitations on the power of digestion inDionaea.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   24 October 1874
letters.summary:
GHD explains conduction, radiation, and convection.

His paper on political economy for Royal Institution lecture has reached 60 pages. Plans to send it toContemporary Review.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   [24 October 1874]
letters.summary: Writes about instructions to compositor and return of proofs [ofDescent]. Requests return of 2d volume ofDescent, to which he may want to refer.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   25 [October 1874]
letters.summary:
Thanks GHD for clear lecture on heat.

Will keep paper on proportion of sexes, in case GHD wants it again.

Wants him to translate some pages of Swedish or Norwegian sent by A. W. Malm, "a good man".

Glad to see the statistical paper ["Theory of exchange value",Fortn. Rev.n.s. 17 (1875): 243–53].

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   26 October 1874
letters.summary:
Thanks CD forDescent, 2d ed.

Comments on German edition of CD’s collected works.

Sales of hisAnthropogenie[1874] in various countries.

Anticlericalism and progress of Darwinism in Germany.

letters.title: To W. W. Baxter   27 October [1874]
letters.summary: Orders two bottles of chlorodyne and bottles and corks of various sizes.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   27 October 1874
letters.summary: On German translation ofDescent[3d German, 2d English ed.]. Lists some misprints in proofs.

letters.title: From T. L. Brunton   [29] October [1874]
letters.summary: Forwards a photograph he thought had been lost. Has noticed that the two sides of the face are often asymmetric in portrait busts and statues.

letters.title: To T. L. Brunton   30 October 1874
letters.summary: Discusses expression on two halves of the face. Mentions photograph [of picture by Rubens].

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   30 October 1874
letters.summary:
Will soon send remaining sheets [ofDescent, 2d English ed.]. Fears JVC’s errata have come too late for printing.

His new work [Insectivorous plants] will make a rather big book.

letters.title: From Auguste Forel   31 October 1874
letters.summary: Thanks for CD’s favourable opinion of his book [Les fourmis de la Suisse(1874)]. Habits of ants; observations on their carrying empty eggs.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   [November 1874 – April 1882]
letters.summary: Invites FG to visit.

letters.title: From T. L. Brunton   2 November [1874]
letters.summary:
CD may keep the photograph of "the holy Mary of Egypt". TLB may have been led away by his imagination in thinking that one side of the face expressed repentance and the other devout joy.

Comments on David Ferrier’s observations on electrical stimulation of the brain. Extent of response relates to intensity of stimulus.

Crichton-Browne’s observations on the asymmetry of convolutions on the two sides of the brains of maniacs.

letters.title: To John Fiske   3 November [1874]
letters.summary: Thanks JF for copy ofCosmic philosophy[1874].

letters.title: From John Murray   3 November 1874
letters.summary:
Statement of stock on hand of CD’s works.

Expression, curiously, at a dead stand-still.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [4 November 1874]
letters.summary: GHD has been using E. Norman [CD’s copyist], and he apologises if this has caused delays to CD’s work.

letters.title: To D. Appleton & Co.   5 November 1874
letters.summary: Has just had printed a new edition ofDescent[1874] and is anxious that this improved version be circulated in America.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   5 November [1874]
letters.summary:
Mainly family news.

Eager to read GHD’s political economy MS "though Heaven knows whether I shall understand it".

letters.title: To John Murray   5 November [1874]
letters.summary:
Thanks JM for granting his request. Will write to D. Appleton.

CD is sorry about heavy loss fromExpression; still thinks the book will sell in the course of years.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [8 November 1874]
letters.summary: Spottiswoode is pressing for an answer to invitation to GHD to lecture at the Royal Institution. GHD is having MS of the paper he has written sent to CD, so that CD can advise whether he should accept the invitation.

letters.title: To W. J. Beal   9 November 1874
letters.summary: Thanks WJB for his reference [see9691]. Is curious fact that the humble bees did not use the pollen, but the hive bees did.

letters.title: To J. F. McLennan   10 November [1874]
letters.summary: Will send Alexis Giraud-Teulon’s book [Origines de la famille(1874)], which he has received but not read, if JFM cares to read it.

letters.title: From F. E. Nipher   10 November 1874
letters.summary: Cites examples of the inheritance of maternal impressions.

letters.title: From Herbert Spencer   11 November 1874
letters.summary:
Wishes to know where, in his works, CD refers to some particular behaviour in dogs.

Mentions the sensitivity of cirripedes to passing shadows.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   12 November 1874
letters.summary: New edition ofDescentjust off the press. Murray feels price must be 9s instead of 12s, if it is to sell. This will reduce profit to almost nil.

letters.title: From Auguste Forel   12 November 1874
letters.summary: Thanks for the present of the book [Thomas Belt,The naturalist in Nicaragua(1874)].

letters.title: To ?   12 November 1874
letters.summary: Is obliged for addressee’s courteous note and is indifferent to how his name is used.

letters.title: From F. T. Köppen   13 November 1874
letters.summary: Calls CD’s attention to a book that deals with subjects related to bothDescentandExpression: Ferdinand Jahn,Die abnormen Zustände des menschlichen Lebens als Nachbildungen und Wiederholungen normaler Zustände des Thierlebens[1842].

letters.title: To Down School Board   16 November 1874
letters.summary: Must resign because of his health.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   17 November 1874
letters.summary: Booksellers approve of [9s] price for 2d edition ofDescent. 1350 copies were sold at annual sale.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [17 November 1874]
letters.summary: Extremely glad to have JDH come to Down. It is wise of JDH to exert himself and face the inevitable as well as he can. [Death of JDH’s wife, 13 Nov.]

letters.title: To [?]   [18 November 1874–8]
letters.summary: Invites correspondent to luncheon on Friday or Saturday.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   18 November 1874
letters.summary: An omission in a bibliographical note inDescent[2d English ed.].

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   18 November [1874]
letters.summary: Sends Murray’s report of November sales of CD’s books. "I am well content."

letters.title: To F. T. Köppen   18 November 1874
letters.summary: Thanks FTK for telling him of Jahn’s work [see9719], of which CD had not heard. It would have been of greatest use in writingDescent.

letters.title: From D. Appleton & Co   [c.19] November 1874
letters.summary:
Accepts CD’s suggestion of new edition ofDescent, and asks that Murray supply the stereotype plates and woodcuts for $50 [dollars or pounds!?], as soon as possible; supply of copies ofDescentis exhausted.

Will publish CD’s proposed book [Insectivorous plants(1875)] on same terms as other works.

letters.title: To Ludwig Noiré   19 November [1874?]
letters.summary: CD thanks LN for his book [Die Welt als Entwicklung des Geistes], which he hopes to read soon, but his poor German hampers him.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   20 November [1874]
letters.summary: Thanks JVC for a correction to 2d English edition ofDescent, which is now finished. 1350 copies were sold at Murray’s sale.

letters.title: To George King   20 November 1874
letters.summary: Asks for specimen ofAldrovandafor book on insect-eating plants.

letters.title: From T. M. Reade   21 November 1874
letters.summary:
Sends his paper ["Tidal action as a geological cause",Proc. Liverpool Geol. Soc.2 (1874): 50–72].

Has not yet studied CD’s list of South American molluscs.

letters.title: From Martin Ziegler   21 November 1874
letters.summary: OnDrosera, with which MZ has worked for four years.

letters.title: From E. M. Courtenay   22 November 1874
letters.summary: Sends photograph of epileptic idiot and encloses case history.

letters.title: From R. B. Sharpe   23 November [1874]
letters.summary: RBS seeks a testimonial from CD; he is applying for the British Museum vacancy left by J. E. Gray’s resignation and A. Günther’s promotion.

letters.title: To R. B. Sharpe   24 November [1874]
letters.summary: Testimonial stating CD’s opinion of RBS’s fitness for a higher post at the British Museum.

letters.title: To Leonard Darwin   25 November 1874
letters.summary:
LD’s letter recalled old scenes on board theBeagle.

CD’s "bothering correspondents" seem to increase in number and in folly; has just answered "two precious fools".

Has been working very hard on Droseraceae and can "now see daylight".

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   25 November 1874
letters.summary:
Encloses a letter [from Huxley about his invitation to lecture at Edinburgh]. Has done his best to dissuade Huxley from accepting the burden.

JDH’s depression in bereavement.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   26 November [1874]
letters.summary:
Quite agrees with JDH on inadvisability of Huxley’s taking on the Edinburgh lectures.

Is awaiting JDH’s memorial to the Board [of Works?] on his burdensome duties.

Glad to hear JDH finds ease in his work.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   27 November [1874]
letters.summary:
CD thinks better of "cousin paper" than GHD does.

With respect to GHD’s "viscous work", remembers endless discussions of movement of viscous matter 20 years back, apropos of movement of glaciers.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   28 November 1874
letters.summary:
Huxley feels he can accept the Edinburgh lecture invitation.

Also tells JDH he is preparing a paper for Linnean Society on classification which will uphold evolution ["On the classification of the animal kingdom",J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Zool.)12 (1876): 199–226]. He has thrown overboard all his old ideas of definite demarcation. He will make a clean breast of it, and will bear hard on necessity of all such ideas as Haeckel’s in dealing with systematic zoology.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   29 November [1874]
letters.summary: Hooker is greatly overworked at Kew and is trying to get the Government to provide some help. CD hopes THF will take an interest in the matter and forwards a copy of JDH’s application for an assistant.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   30 November [1874]
letters.summary: Has forwarded JDH’s memorial to T. H. Farrer to take up with Sir Stafford Northcote and to ask him to consider the case of Kew personally. Has told Farrer that JDH was thinking of resigning if Government would not give him an assistant secretary.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   2 December [1874]
letters.summary: Appleton will bring out the new edition ofDescentin the U. S., so GHD’s work will now be in three editions.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   2 December [1874]
letters.summary: Farrer has taken the case to Northcote. JDH’s letter will show how overworked he is.

letters.title: From Mary Treat   2 December 1874
letters.summary: Observations on the insects captured byUtricularia.

letters.title: To Thomas Belt   3 December [1874]
letters.summary: Invites TB to visit. Wants to make his acquaintance.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [3 December 1874?]
letters.summary: Probably a discussiion of J. D. Hooker’s feelings after death of his wife, Frances Harriet, on 13 November 1874: the letter is badly damaged.

letters.title: To William Ogle   [4 December 1874 – 22 November 1878]
letters.summary: Invites WO to lunch.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   5 December 1874
letters.summary:
Has finished the "cousin paper" and will offer it to W. Farr for the Statistical Society.

Describes other work in progress.

Has CD heard of A. M. Mayer’s curious work on audition of insects [Am. J. Sci.3d ser. 8 (1874): 89–103?]

letters.title: To H. A. Huxley   [5 December 1874]
letters.summary: Wants to see Huxley tomorrow, but knows he is going down to High Elms to see Colenso.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   [6 December 1874]
letters.summary: Returns historical sketch [of GHD’s "cousin paper"?] with comments. "For Heavens sake put a sentence in some conspicuous place that your results seem to indicate that consanguineous marriage, as far as insanity is concerned, cannot be injurious in any very high degree."

letters.title: From W. G. Walker   6 December 1874
letters.summary: On voluntary vomiting. Dogs re-swallow vomited food.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   6 December 1874
letters.summary:
Thanks for new edition ofDescent.

His work on geographical distribution; drudgery and the often unsatisfactory nature of the result.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   [7 December 1874]
letters.summary: Speaks of visiting GJR at the Brown Institution.

letters.title: To John Fiske   8 December [1874]
letters.summary:
Praises JF’s book [Cosmic philosophy(1874)].

Has long wished to understand H. Spencer but is not convinced by him and some others. CD cannot trust deduction from a starting principle, as his mind is so fixed by the inductive method.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   8 December 1874
letters.summary:
Delighted with Farrer’s assistance. A. Helps has also spoken to Sir S. Northcote.

JDH is getting on well but has periods of great depression.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   8 December 1874
letters.summary:
K. G. Semper’s article ["On the relationship of the Vertebrata and Annelida",Ann. & Mag. Nat. Hist.15 (1875): 94–5] is ill-natured. Misinterprets facts already discovered by F. M. Balfour.

Has been working onAmphioxus. Puts his theory of vertebrate skulls on firm footing at last.

letters.title: To [F. C. Noll?]   8 December [1874]
letters.summary: Thanks for the essay on a curious new cirripede. He will not accept the offer of microscopical preparations.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   [9 December 1874]
letters.summary: Invites GJR to visit.

letters.title: From C.-F. Reinwald   10 December 1874
letters.summary: Sends French translation ofJournal of researchesand will send the £20 due to CD when 750 copies have been sold.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   11 December 1874
letters.summary:
Cannot help withPinguiculaorUtricularia. Mrs Mary Treat is studyingUtricularia.

Forwards his short piece on duration of varieties [New York Tribune8 Dec 1874;Am. J. Sci.3d ser. 9 (1875): 109–14].

letters.title: From F. E. Nipher   11 December 1874
letters.summary: Cites more examples of inheritance of maternal impressions.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   12 [December 1874 or January 1875?]
letters.summary: Regrets the trouble GHD has had.

letters.title: To Theodor Eimer   12 December 1874
letters.summary: Thanks for work onLacerta muralis coerulea[Zoologische Studien auf Capri2 (1874)].

letters.title: To C.-F. Reinwald   [12 December 1874]
letters.summary:
Thanks for translation of hisJournal of researches. Is pleased by its appearance.

Also thank Edmond Barbier for his kind words. [See9752.]

letters.title: From Arnold Dodel   13 December 1874
letters.summary: Describes his university lectures on evolution and their publication in a book [Die neuere Schöpfungsgeschichte(1875)].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   14 December 1874
letters.summary: Thanks JDH for his and Huxley’s countering of the false attack on George [Darwin] by Mivart. Encloses a note to Mivart on which he asks JDH’s opinion.

letters.title: To John Murray   14 December 1874
letters.summary: Sends a suggested title [forInsectivorous plants?].

letters.title: To John Lubbock   15 December [1874]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary:
Asks JL to send ten shillings for the Down Friendly Club.

Has just read JL’s paper on bees and wasps [J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Zool.)12 (1876): 110–39]. Is astonished by their stupidity. The experiments on colour are especially good. Suggests JL examine their retinas; sends enclosure [missing] on eyes of reptiles and birds.

letters.title: From O. G. Rejlander   15 December 1874
letters.summary:
Awakened by a mouse scratching at night, he mewed like a cat and the mouse disappeared.

Sending a group of stuffed sparrows.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   16 December 1874
letters.summary:
Thanks GJR for copy of his book [Christian prayer and general laws(1874)].

Discusses breeding and sterility.

Discusses experiments to test Pangenesis. Cites useful references.

Suggests GJR visit Kew gardens.

letters.title: From George King   18 December 1874
letters.summary: Sends three specimens ofAldrovanda verticulata.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   18 December 1874
letters.summary: Asks four favours: sort out confusion about the nameByblis giganteaorgrandiflora; can he see dried specimens ofGenlisea ornata; is there a more recent list ofDroseraspp. than Steudel 1841; are there at Kew any dried specimens ofUtricularia montanacollected from the plant’s native haunts.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   18 December [1874]
letters.summary:
Bishop J. W. Colenso supports his old contention that the Kaffirs (including Zulus of South Africa) are Negroes.

[Horace Waller’s]The last journals of David Livingstone[in central Africa(1874)] cites CD’s plant research and has many facts "for Darwin".

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   19 December 1874
letters.summary:
SendsUtricularia montanaandByblisspecies.

Droseracensus numbers 100 species.

Genliseadistinguished fromUtricularia.

letters.title: To Henry Sidgwick   19 December 1874
letters.summary: Thanks for hisMethods of ethics[1874].

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   20 December 1874
letters.summary:
Discusses hisAnthropogenie[1874]. Remarks on the tables.

Has CD received Friedrich von Hellwald’sCulturgeschichte[1875]?

Plans research trip to the Mediterranean.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   20 December 1874
letters.summary: Asks JDH to help G. J. Romanes, who wishes to try Pangenesis experiment.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   21 December 1874
letters.summary:
His view of Huxley’s cutting Mivart without explanation. States his own intentions. Mivart’s apology in OctoberQuarterly Reviewis abominable.

Has heard of aDrosophyllumin Edinburgh. Is it too late?

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   22 December 1874
letters.summary:
Expresses his gratitude to JDH and Huxley in the Mivart affair. Thinks he should write directly to Mivart, if Mivart does not retract.

Would be glad to have anotherDrosophyllum.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   22 December 1874
letters.summary: Will help Romanes. Offers Kew’s facilities for experiments. Is writing to the Board [of Works?] about a physiological laboratory, which Sir Philip Joddrell has offered to build. Thinks Government should support original research like Romanes’.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   22 December [1874]
letters.summary: Thanks THH and Hooker for defending George Darwin against Mivart’s libel.

letters.title: To Arnold Dodel   23 December 1874
letters.summary: Thanks AD-P for sending his work, not yet received, on evolution [Die neuere Schöpfungsgeschichte(1875)].

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   23 December 1874
letters.summary: Entirely sympathises with CD about Mivart’s attack on George. THH has had a letter from Mivart in which he pleads guilty, but THH has decided there is no patching the matter up. Advises against doing anything unless Mivart takes initiative.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   23 December 1874
letters.summary: Urges GJR to visit Hooker at Kew.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   24 December [1874]
letters.summary: Encloses note from Huxley and copy of Huxley’s answer to Mivart – a tremendous reproof. On Huxley’s advice, CD will not write to Mivart. Thinks Mivart’s private apology to Huxley makes the case even worse.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   24 December [1874]
letters.summary:
THH’s letter to Mivart is "tremendous". CD’s feelings and intentions about the matter.

If THH has made out homology of the skull, it is grandest discovery in years.

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   24 December 1874
letters.summary: Sends capsules with results fromGenliseaspecimens and fragments ofPolypompholyx.

letters.title: To [Joseph Prestwich] 24 December [1874–81]
letters.summary: Sends compliments and thanks.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   25 December 1874
letters.summary:
Read AG’s article [see9753] on longevity and duration of varieties with great interest.

Death of Mrs Hooker.

HopesInsectivorous plantswill be out in the spring.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   26 December 1874
letters.summary:
Comments on review of EH’sAnthropogenie[1874].

Mentions recent work of Huxley and other scientists.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [26 December 1874]
letters.summary: Has gone over Huxley’s letter, thinks it a model. All must now await developments. If Mivart does not apologise, JDH will write to him.

letters.title: From D. F. Nevill   26 [December 1874]
letters.summary:
Would like to know the results of CD’sUtriculariaexperiments.

A Brazilian love-bird, escaped from captivity, has been found in a robin’s nest, apparently starved to death along with three young robins.

letters.title: To Arnold Dodel   27 December 1874
letters.summary: Thanks AD-P for the copy of his work [see9756].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   27 December [1874]
letters.summary: Has not heard from Mivart. He is not so good a Christian as JDH and cannot forgive a man for malicious lying merely because he says he is sorry. Does not think Mivart will apologise. Still thinks the simple, most manly thing, is to write to Mivart directly and tell him what he thinks of him.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   27 December 1874
letters.summary: Discourages grafting ears of rabbits. Suggests comb of fowl.

letters.title: To John Tyndall   27 December 1874
letters.summary: Asks JT to persuade Lady Lubbock to change physicians and put herself in the care of Andrew Clark. Thinks this alone will save her.

letters.title: From John Tyndall   28 December 1874
letters.summary:
JT had not known Lady Lubbock was ill. Will try to persuade her [to change physicians]. Agrees Andrew Clark is best.

Hooker has survived his crisis [death of his wife].

St G. J. Mivart’s act is a natural outflow of his character.

letters.title: To James Crichton-Browne   29 December [1874?]
letters.summary: States his very high opinion of [JC-B’s?] abilities as judged from his writings and many excellent letters, and his suitability for some post in histology and pathology.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   29 December 1874
letters.summary:
Explains that his letter had to do with how he should act publicly to Mivart if he retracted. He would not forgive him. If he does not retract, it would no longer be possible to keep him Secretary of the Linnean Society.

Drosophyllumwill be sent when weather permits.

letters.title: To D. F. Nevill   29 December 1874
letters.summary:
CD thought he had already reported to DN onUtricularia. The large swellings in roots store water. The minute bladders are adapted to catch live animals and feed on decayed remains.

Will visit DN when in London this winter.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [1875?]
letters.summary: Had two mornings working on Drosera but it was sluggish. Frog preparations are pretty good.

letters.title: From W. D. Fox   [1875–80]
letters.summary:
Sends date of his mother’s death – 7 Apr 1859.

Was completely mystified by conjuring performance of [John Nevil] Maskelyne.

letters.title: To F. J. Cohn   1 January 1875
letters.summary: Asks whether he might copy two of FJC’s drawings ofAldrovanda. He would like to have a proof of the plate for two woodcuts to be used in his forthcoming book [Insectivorous plants].

letters.title: To Linnean Society   1 January [1875]
letters.summary: Asks permission to republish his climbing plants paper [J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)9 (1867): 1–118] in a corrected form [Climbing plants].

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   1 January [1875]
letters.summary: Returning the plants DO had sent him from Kew

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   2 January 1875
letters.summary: The generic nameGenliseamust be preserved for Utriculariaceae with five-part calyces.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   3 January [1875]
letters.summary: Disapproves of Huxley’s article [review of Ernst Haeckel’sAnthropogenie] inAcademy[7 (1875): 16–18].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   3 January [1875]
letters.summary: Has not heard from Mivart; CD is convinced he is a hypocrite.

letters.title: To H. E. Litchfield   4 January [1875]
letters.summary: Describes his views on vivisection. Cannot sign petition of F. P. Cobbe, with its attack on Rudolf Virchow.

letters.title: To F. B. Goodacre   5 January 1875
letters.summary: CD would be pleased to have FBG’s essay dedicated to him but fears that he will be unable to give any assistance towards FBG’s ‘excellent scheme’.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   5 January 1875
letters.summary: Huxley strongly dissuades JDH from writing to Mivart because of his Presidency of Royal Society. JDH will hold his letter until he hears what Bentham says.

letters.title: To Friedrich Max Müller   5 January 1875
letters.summary:
Has read FMM’s article inContemporary Review[25 (1875): 305–26].

Never suspected FMM was responsible for theQuarterly Reviewarticle ["Primitive man",Q. Rev.137 (1874): 40–77]; knows it was written by Mivart.

letters.title: From Joseph Fayrer   6 January 1875
letters.summary: Encloses results of experiments on influence of snake poison on ciliary action and vegetable protoplasm.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   6 January [1875]
letters.summary: Is not inclined to restrain himself from expressing his opinion of Mivart. Huxley’s article inAcademy.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   6 January 1875
letters.summary: Thanks THH for his article in theAcademyand his defence of CD and G. H. Darwin against Mivart. Still thinks he should write plainly to Mivart.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   6 January [1875]
letters.summary: CD’s observations [forInsectivorous plants] seem to indicate that the same species ofGenliseamay bear two kinds of bladders, so he asks for rhizomes and leaves of three species to test this possibility.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   7 January 1875
letters.summary: Tyndall, T. A. Hirst and Spencer dissuade him from writing to Mivart, but he will let him feel his disapproval.

letters.title: From Friedrich Max Müller   7 January 1875
letters.summary:
FMM discusses his reply to George Darwin’s article [see9711].

Intends within a year to place his whole argument before CD when, he hopes, his difficulties connected with the origin of language will be carefully considered by CD.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   8 January [1875]
letters.summary: JDH would be rash not to follow advice of his friends. [CD’s] wife and George oppose his writing to Mivart.

letters.title: From Alpheus Hyatt   8 January [1875]
letters.summary:
Encloses report on his paper "Old age characteristics among ammonites", [Proc. Boston Soc. Nat. Hist.17 (1875): 236–41].

Stability of long inherited characters. Dependence of some recently acquired characters on the environment.

letters.title: From F. J. Cohn   9 January 1875
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for his letter of 1 Jan 1875. Will send a paper on the genusVolvox["Die Entwicklungsgeschichte der Gattung Volvox",Cohn Beitr. Biol. Pflanz.1 (1875) Heft 3: 99–115].

Informs CD of his discoveries of the "house"-building capacity ofDifflugia, one of the lowest forms of organism.

Sends CD his writing onAldrovandaandUtricularia, which he is welcome to use in his forthcoming book [Insectivorous plants].

Has observed aDionaeafertilised without insect aid.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   11 January [1875]
letters.summary: Thanks for F. v. Hellwald [Culturgeschichte(1875)].

letters.title: To St G. J. Mivart   12 January 1875
letters.summary: StGJM’s article in theQuarterly Review[137 (1874): 40–77] contains wholly false and malicious accusations against CD’s son George. Since StGJM has refused to make any sort of retraction, CD will not hold any future communication with him.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   [after 12 January 1875]
letters.summary: CD has written to Mivart to say that he will never hold any communication with him in future.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   13 January [1875]
letters.summary: Describes accounts of potato grafting in a German journal.

letters.title: To F. P. Cobbe [14 January 1875]
letters.summary: Explains why he cannot sign Miss Cobbe’s anti-vivisection petition.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   14 January 1875
letters.summary: Is on the eve of another row with the Office of Works about his application for assistance.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   14 January 1875
letters.summary: Is alarmed by the petitions against vivisection that are being circulated. Believes there is scope for reasonable legislation and would like to see eminent physiologists prepare a petition so that the science could be protected and animals saved from needless suffering.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   14 January 1875
letters.summary:
Would like to see papers [on potato grafting] mentioned by CD.

CD has doubtless seen case inGardeners’ Chronicleof vine in which scion has affected the stock [P. Grieve, "Singular sport upon a grape vine",Gard. Chron.(1875): 21].

letters.title: From W. B. Dawkins   15 January 1875
letters.summary: Wants references to facts quoted inVariationfor an essay he is writing on origin of British cattle.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   15 January [1875]
letters.summary:
Hopes JDH will beat Sir Douglas Galton.

Continues to work on insectivorous plants.

letters.title: To W. B. Dawkins   16 January [1875]
letters.summary: Can give no more information about white and dark cattle than William Youatt gave in his book on cattle (Youatt 1834).

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   16 January 1875
letters.summary:
JDH wins over Douglas Galton and Lord Henry Lennox on assistant secretary for himself.

Has called on Murray and told himQuarterly Reviewhad disgraced itself by attacking George and CD.

letters.title: From A. G. Dew-Smith   17 January 1875
letters.summary: Sends a letter from Anton Dohrn, which, if CD approves, will be printed with a list of all donors to the Naples Zoological Station. AGD-S has just returned from a visit to the Station and gives an account of its status. German government has made a grant.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   17 January [1875]
letters.summary:
Astonished at JDH’s success versus Galton

and his attack on Murray is superb. Has written a formal letter to Mivart enumerating his offences.

letters.title: To George Bentham   18 January [1875]
