letters.summary: Thanks GB for his "Report on [the recent progress and present state of] systematic botany" [Rep. BAAS(1874): 27–54] and for the way in which he refers to CD’s book.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   18 January 1875
letters.summary:
Agrees with CD on vivisection. Will communicate with Burdon Sanderson and see what can be done.

Mivart’s wriggle.

letters.title: To A. G. Dew-Smith   19 January [1875]
letters.summary: Discusses subscriptions for the Naples Zoological Station.

letters.title: To Alpheus Hyatt   21 January [1875]
letters.summary:
Thanks for note and extract.

Will be glad to read AH’s memoir when published [? "The Jurassic and Cretaceous Ammonites collected in South America by Prof. James Orton"Boston Soc. Nat. Hist.[Proc Mem Jnl!?] 17 (1875): 365–72].

Recalls AH’s visit to Down.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   22 January 1875
letters.summary: Writes on behalf of Royal Society Polar Committee for suggestions concerning instructions to naturalists on new expedition.

letters.title: To Linnean Society   23 January [1875]
letters.summary: Thanks Council for their kindness; even if he had known that the right to reprint papers was a recognised one he would have asked the Council’s consent [before reprintingClimbing plants?].

letters.title: To John Murray   23 January [1875–82]
letters.summary: Thanks for two German letters about translations, which he has answered. The enclosed one contains a proposal for CD’s correspondent to bring out a translation of a very successful German book, and must be answered by the correspondent.

letters.title: To ?   23 January [1875–82]
letters.summary: Turns down an offer to undertake a German translation of one of his works.

letters.title: To B. G. Wilder   26 January [1875]
letters.summary: CD expresses his high opinion of BGW’s papers. Thinks one on brains of dogs particularly valuable ["Anatomical papers on brain of dogs",Rep. Am. Assoc. Adv. Sci.(1874)].

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   27 January [1875]
letters.summary: Sends suggestions for observations on glacial phenomena that might be made on the [Polar] expedition [of H. M. S.AlertandDiscovery, 1875–6].

letters.title: To E. B. Tylor   [28 January 1875]
letters.summary: The review of EBT’s book ["Primitive Man: Tylor and Lubbock"] in theQuarterly Review[137: 40–77] last year contained a false and malicious attack on CD’s son George. CD knows it was written by St George Mivart. CD wishes to take every opportunity to say how false a man he considers him to be.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   29 January [1875]
letters.summary: Asks AG to forward [unspecified] enclosure to Chauncey Wright.

letters.title: From E. B. Tylor   29 January [1875]
letters.summary: Does CD think it desirable for EBT’s wife to produce a new English translation of A. E. Brehm’s work [Illustrirtes Thierleben(1864–7)]?

letters.title: From George Brownen   30 January 1875
letters.summary: Suspects a plant he has found,Hyoscyamus niger, is insectivorous. Its hairs in water caused dissolution of egg-white.

letters.title: To B. A. E. Cookson   30 January 1875
letters.summary: Is happy to send his autograph.

letters.title: From Michael Foster   30 January 1875
letters.summary: Account of the fund to help Anton Dohrn’s zoological station at Naples.

letters.title: From A. W. Malm   31 January 1875
letters.summary: Sends his paper.

letters.title: To [?]   31 [January 1875–82]
letters.summary: [Provides directions for travel to Down by train.]

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [c.February 1875?]
letters.summary: Begs FD’s pardon: his notes onUtricularia amethystinaare on same page with those onU. nelumbifolia.

letters.title: From G. G. Bianconi   1 February 1875
letters.summary: At work on new editions of his books against CD’s theory [La teoria dell’uomo-scimmia(1864);La théorie darwinienne(1874)]. Had hoped to receive CD’s comments, as earlier promised; they would still be useful.

letters.title: From D. Appleton & Co   1 February 1875
letters.summary: Statement of U. S. sales ofOrigin,Expression, andDescent.

letters.title: To Gustav Jäger   3 February 1875
letters.summary: Comments on GJ’s book [In Sachen Darwins ins-besondere contra Wigand(1874)]. Not convinced that there are species which are fixed or variable independently of the conditions to which they are subjected.

letters.title: To ?   3 February [1875–82]
letters.summary: Asks that enclosed letter be posted for him.

letters.title: From Anton Bachmaier   4 February 1875
letters.summary: Asks for information about alleged regeneration of amputated human fingers and toes. Mentions observations on regeneration of salamander extremities.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   5 February 1875
letters.summary:
New [3d] German edition ofDescentwill soon be out.

Will begin translatingJournal of researches, which will be first volume of CD’s collected works.

JVC has proposed bringing out all CD’s botanical papers in one or two volumes.

Errata inDescentenclosed.

letters.title: From Albert Günther   6 February 1875
letters.summary: Has been appointed to a Keepership at British Museum.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   7 February 1875
letters.summary:
Thanks JVC for errata [inDescent, 2d ed.].

Discusses work in progress and publication plans.

Will be pleased to receive concluding volume of JVC’sZoologie[see8531].

letters.title: From Anton Dohrn   7 February 1875
letters.summary:
Thanks to CD’s help Zoological Station has passed a crisis and is now flourishing.

Is writing pamphlet on "the origin of vertebrates and the principle of succession of functions" [see9991and10003]. It is likely CD will not be pleased with it, but he thinks he must now, after seven years, bring it out. Seeks to open the way for a new series of theoretical questions.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [7 February 1875]
letters.summary:
Has met Capt. George Strong Nares of theChallengerexpedition at Huxley’s.

Huxley much at a loss to explain red clay at deep sea-bottom.

letters.title: To Anton Dohrn   [after 7 February 1875]
letters.summary:
The Zoological Station has already resulted in "capital work" by F. M. Balfour and Ray Lankester. G. J. Romanes is coming next year.

CD will be interested in AD’s ancestry of vertebrates. "I shall be very sorry to give up the ascidians."

letters.title: To J. W. Clark  9 February 1875
letters.summary: Thanks for information about effect of fear on the iris.

letters.title: To Albert Günther   9 February [1875]
letters.summary: Rejoices at AG’s "honourable & important" position [Keeper of the Zoological Department, British Museum].

letters.title: From J. T. Knowles 9 February 1875
letters.summary: Assures CD that space will be reserved in the AprilContemporary Reviewfor W. D. Whitney’s article and solicits an introductory section from C.D.

letters.title: To J. S. Burdon Sanderson   10 February 1875
letters.summary:
Has been experimenting with phosphates onDroseraand wonders whether animals digest a particular one.

Asks whether Huxley has approached him regarding the introduction of a vivisection act.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   10 [February 1875]
letters.summary:
J. T. Knowles [editor ofContemp. Rev.] hopes W. D. Whitney’s article will be a long one.

CD is sorry about GHD’s account of his low spirits. "I know well the feeling of life being objectless & all being vanity of vanities."

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   10 February [1875]
letters.summary:
Is provoked by trouble he is having writingInsectivorous plants.

Curious case of an unknown form ofGlauciumin earth covered with slag for 1400 years.

letters.title: From Mary Treat   11 February 1875
letters.summary: Structure ofUtricularia; its resemblance to an animal vascular system.

letters.title: From J. S. Burdon Sanderson   12 February 1875
letters.summary:
Discusses the experiments with phosphates onDroseraand animals.

Considers the question of preparing a petition on the question of animal experiments, with the aim of promoting rather than hindering science. [Response to9849.]

letters.title: To Gustaf Retzius   12 February 1875
letters.summary: His thanks for MGR’s valuableAnatomische Untersuchungen(1872).

letters.title: To Gustavus Fritsche   13 February 1875
letters.summary: Suggests that Fritsche comes to lunch on Tuesday 16 February.

letters.title: From J. C. Douglas   14 February 1875
letters.summary:
Sends observations inspired by reading CD’s works.

Animal showing teeth an indication of pleasure, connected with sexual instinct.

Infant feet will curl around an object placed on the sole, indicating a primitive prehensile function.

Effects of climate on man’s physical countenance evidenced in similarity of N. American Indians and Yankees.

letters.title: From D. F. Nevill   14 [February 1875]
letters.summary: Understands from Lady Hawkshaw that CD generally visits London [in February]. Requests meeting with CD.

letters.title: From J. W. Draper   15 February 1875
letters.summary: Asks to introduce Mr. N. Jovanovich of Belgrade, Serbia.

letters.title: To D. F. Nevill   15 February 1875
letters.summary: Cannot visit now because of work onInsectivorous plants.

letters.title: To John Murray   16 February [1875]
letters.summary: Asks whether JM thinks another edition ofVariationworth while. Asks because a Polish translation is planned and he would undertake corrections for a 2d edition, but not just for a Polish edition.

letters.title: From ?   [16 February 1875]
letters.summary: "The learned Darwin states that Moses taught confusion. | For Man, he boldly says, descends from Ape or Monkey – | I, having read his book, am come to this conclusion | Darwin (at least himself) descends from Ass or Donkey."

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   17 February 1875
letters.summary:
Lyell very ill.

No two specimens ofGlauciumare alike.

Lord Henry [Lennox] still burkes JDH’s application.

letters.title: From John Murray   17 February [1875]
letters.summary:
JM expresses his willingness to publish a new edition ofVariationwhenever CD revises it.

Descent[2d ed.] has not sold much since the annual sale – 1300 copies altogether.

letters.title: From G. C. Robertson   17 February 1875
letters.summary: Sends a prospectus for the new journal,Mind, and invites CD’s co-operation.

letters.title: To ?   17 February [1875–8]
letters.summary: Tells correspondent how to locate Michael Faraday’s widow [Sarah Barnard].

letters.title: To ?   [after 17 February 1875]
letters.summary: CD is obliged for a note he will use for a new [2d] edition ofVariation[1875].

letters.title: To G. C. Robertson   19 February [1875]
letters.summary: The plan of the new journal [Mind] seems excellent. CD regrets that he has so much work to do in natural history that it is improbable he can be a contributor.

letters.title: To F. B. Goodacre   20 February 1875
letters.summary: Thanks FBG for his essay. Thinks FBG’s planned collection would be very useful but is ‘not sanguine of success’. Most naturalists do not care about domesticated productions. ‘A strong remnant of the feeling yet survives that there is a marked distinction between varieties & species, & naturalists regard only the latter.’

letters.title: From G. G. Bianconi   22 February 1875
letters.summary: Thanks for CD’s reception of his book. The evidence GGB has assembled has convinced him of independent creation. The future will say whether he or CD is correct.

letters.title: To A. B. Buckley   23 February 1875
letters.summary: Expresses his feelings following the death of Charles Lyell.

letters.title: From James Gibb   23 February 1875
letters.summary: Thinks he has observed the origin of the shake of the head as signifying "no" in his seven-month-old son.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   23 February 1875
letters.summary: Mourns death of Lyell. Wonders whether enough men of science were attached to him to raise a fitting testimonial.

letters.title: To Thomas Belt   24 February 1875
letters.summary: Will not come to London for some weeks. Hopes to make TB’s acquaintance.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [24 February 1875]
letters.summary:
On Lyell’s death; JDH has arranged for burial in Westminster Abbey. His thoughts on a testimonial.

More trouble with Lord Henry Lennox.

letters.title: To Thomas Woolner   24 February 1875
letters.summary: Is much obliged to TW and his friend for having told him about the azalea, but CD had already seen the account.

letters.title: From Chauncey Wright   24 February 1875
letters.summary: Speculates on the function of eyebrows and of hair and the furrows of the forehead. Considers many features and faculties to serve, or to have served, more than one function, either simultaneously or successively. Determining the one function through which natural selection has acted in developing it is unrealistic and not worth while.

letters.title: To George Cupples   25 February 1875
letters.summary: "Last night it suddenly occurred to me that I had not sent you the last Edition of the Descent of Man published in November."

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   25 February [1875]
letters.summary: CD on his memory of Lyell. Deeply rejoices that he is to be buried in Westminster Abbey.

letters.title: To ?   [February 1875 or earlier?]
letters.summary: Reports thatVariationis out of print. Suggests means of obtaining a copy.

letters.title: From George Cupples   1 March 1875
letters.summary: Thanks for presentation copy ofDescent, 2d ed.

letters.title: From Oswald Heer   1 March 1875
letters.summary:
Comments on hisFlora fossilis Arctica[vol. 3 (1875)]. Discusses successive appearance of plant families in geological periods. Relates plant development to rise of herbivorous mammals.

Comments on death of Charles Lyell.

letters.title: From Moritz Traube   2 March 1875
letters.summary: Sends two treatises which explain cell-wall formation and some aspects of cell growth in physico-chemical terms ["Experimente zur Theorie d. Zellenbildung und Endosmose",Arch. Anat. Physiol.(1867): 87–128, 126–65].

letters.title: To Moritz Traube   5 March 1875
letters.summary: Thanks correspondent for two essays.

letters.title: To [M. T. Masters?]   7 March 1875
letters.summary: Thanks correspondent for article on CD inGardeners’ Chronicle.

letters.title: To Oswald Heer   8 March [1875]
letters.summary: Thanks OH for his book [see9876]; agrees that the sudden appearance of many dicotyledons in the Upper Chalk is a perplexing phenomenon for the evolutionist.

letters.title: From G. A. Wolfe   9 March 1875
letters.summary:
CD’sDescent.

Fighting among beetles.

Similarity between dogs and men; intelligence of dogs.

letters.title: To ?   10 March 1875
letters.summary: No uniform edition of CD’s works has appeared in England.

letters.title: To P. P. C. Hoek   11 March 1875
letters.summary: Thanks for publication [Berste bijdrage tot een nauwkeuriger kennis der sessile cirripedien(1875)]. Cannot read Dutch. Mentions PPCH’s research on cirripedes.

letters.title: From A. W. Bennett   12 March 1875
letters.summary: Has found the relation of pollen-grain size to style size inPrimulato be the opposite of CD’s view; asks whether there is an error or just remarkable variation.

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   12 March [1875]
letters.summary: Purpose of bushy tails; their usefulness to their owners as a means of keeping warm.

letters.title: To Lawson Tait   [13–15 March 1875]
letters.summary: Thinks CD is right about the retention of a tail.

letters.title: To Chauncey Wright   13 March 1875
letters.summary:
Discusses function of the eyebrows in protecting the eyes from sweat.

Mentions notices in theNation.

letters.title: From W. B. Dawkins   14 March 1875
letters.summary:
Is glad CD is pleased with his book [Cave hunting(1874)].

Relationship between language and race. The Basques.

letters.title: From John Fiske   15 March 1875
letters.summary:
Thanks CD forDescent

and for his praise ofCosmic philosophy[1874].

letters.title: From E. J. Johnston   16 March 1875
letters.summary: Reports anAraujiain Portugal that captures various insects on the horns of its stigma. Relates this to another asclepiad,Apocynum, which also captures insects. Is this "insectivory" or insect fertilisation?

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   16 March [1875]
letters.summary: Uses of tails of mice. Functions of tails generally.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   17 March 1875
letters.summary: No action on assistance yet, but has had a private note from Disraeli asking whether Thiselton-Dyer is his recommendation.

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   17 March [1875]
letters.summary: Sends a short essay [The pathology and treatment of diseases of the ovaries(1874)] on which he would welcome CD’s opinion. Believes problems of pathology can be attacked by regarding them from "Darwinian" point of view.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   19 March 1875
letters.summary: A curious alteration in the reprint ofVariation.

letters.title: From F. M. Balfour   [20 March – 14 April 1875]
letters.summary: Gives Carl Claus’s identifications of the organisms sent by CD.

letters.title: From Horatio Piggot   20 March 1875
letters.summary: Suggests advantage to students of adding coloured drawings of the coral-producing zoophytes in next edition ofCoral reefs.

letters.title: To Horatio Piggot   20 March [1875]
letters.summary: Thanks for his suggestion about drawings for future edition [ofCoral reefs].

letters.title: To Lawson Tait   20 March [1875]
letters.summary: Has read RLT’s essay [The pathology and treatment of diseases of the ovaries(1874)] with interest. His facts about tumours seem to CD "highly favourable to some such notion as Pangenesis".

letters.title: From Anton Bachmaier   21 March 1875
letters.summary:
Thanks for reference concerning regeneration of human fingers and toes.

Sends lecture on language.

Asks for information about animal communication by vocal sounds.

letters.title: From E. J. Johnston   22 March 1875
letters.summary: He will write to Portugal for the insect-capturingAraujia.

letters.title: From Oswald Heer   23 March 1875
letters.summary:
Discusses his work [Flora fossilis Arctica, vol. 4, pt 1 (1876)].

Sends copy of [Fossile Pflanzen von Sumatra(1874)]. Comments on climate in Tertiary period, especially on Sumatra.

Comments on theory of Thomas Belt concerning climatic change in ice age.

letters.title: From John Murray   23 March [1875]
letters.summary: Sends CD a cheque for 68 guineas – his two-thirds share of profit on sale of 2000 copies of 2d edition ofDescent.

letters.title: From J. P. Thomasson   23 March 1875
letters.summary:
On nesting habits of pied and spotted flycatchers.

JPT disagrees with CD’s comment inDescent.

Marriages of first cousins produce congenital deaf-mutism.

letters.title: From A. E. J. Modderman to Charles Darwin and 20 others   24 March 1875
letters.summary: Informing CD (and 20 others) of the award of an honorary degree by Leiden University.

letters.title: To Lawson Tait   25 March 1875
letters.summary: Would be glad to make RLT’s acquaintance, but CD’s health would make RLT’s visit to Down unprofitable. Suggests a meeting in London at end of month.

letters.title: From Thomas Burgess   26 March 1875
letters.summary: TB, who sailed with CD [as a Royal Marine] in theBeagle, asks for CD’s portrait. Recalls some events they shared.

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   27 March [1875]
letters.summary: Is preparing a paper on the umbilical cord ["On the anatomy of the umbilical cord",Proc. R. Soc. Lond.23 (1875): 498–501; 24 (1876): 417–40] of which he sends a preliminary note [missing]. Believes spiral growth of the umbilical cord is important evidence of the descent of man; speculates on spiral growth in general.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   30 March [1875]
letters.summary:
Has at last finishedInsectivorous plants

and is rewritingClimbing plants.

W. W. Ouless has finished his picture of CD for Academy.

letters.title: To J. P. Thomasson   30 March 1875
letters.summary: Seems to be in error about the nests of the two flycatchers.

letters.title: To Thomas Belt   31 March [1875]
letters.summary: Has just come to London. Invites TB to luncheon.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   2 [April 1875]
letters.summary: CD recounts events of the April-fool’s day séance at Hensleigh [Wedgwood]’s. Asks GHD to find out whether Sidgwick’s account of it agrees with what he has heard. "What rubbish the whole does seem to be!"

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [2 April 1875]
letters.summary: About elections to [an unspecified] club.

letters.title: From Thomas Belt   3 April 1875
letters.summary: Sends reference to Codrington paper on gravels ["The superficial deposits of the south of Hampshire and the Isle of Wight",Q. J. Geol. Soc. Lond.26 (1870): 3–28]. Comments on local gravels in railway cutting and the violent agency of their removal from hills.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   3 April 1875
letters.summary:
Payne will send vine cuttings.

Thomas Belt has been visiting; they are to meet Huxley.

He is moved by denudation of the Weald.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [4 April 1875]
letters.summary: Will write to Strickland. Asks whether name has already been put down for Athenaeum.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   [4 April 1875]
letters.summary: Sends his thoughts on [vivisection] petition. Thinks they might make petition more talked about. Leaves it to J. Paget, Burdon Sanderson, and CD to deal with.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [5 April 1875]
letters.summary: Another message about club elections.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   5 April [1875]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Expresses concern about the "coolness" between CD and [G. S.] Ffinden in regard to the Infant School.

letters.title: From J. S. Burdon Sanderson   7 April [1875]
letters.summary: Sends the Memorial [concerning animal experimentation].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   7 April 1875
letters.summary: Likes draft of petition on vivisection. Asks whether phrase "and the lower animals" might not be added at end.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   7 April [1875]
letters.summary:
Is sending plants from cut-leaved vine.

Invites GJR to visit.

"When in presence of my ladies do not talk about experiments on animals."

letters.title: From Federico Delpino   8 April 1875
letters.summary: Sends last part of his book [Ulteriori observazioni sulla dicogamia(1868–74)] [osservazioni!?] and describes contents.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   8 April 1875
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Writes regarding local difficulties concerning Down School and the setting up of a reading-room; his strained relationship with G. S. ffinden following some misunderstanding.

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   8 April [1875]
letters.summary: Arrangements for a visit to Down.

letters.title: To ?   8 April [1875–82]
letters.summary: Explains that there is no need for the addressee to apologise.

letters.title: From John Murray   9 April [1875]
letters.summary: JM expresses willingness to publish CD’sClimbing plants[2d ed.].

letters.title: From J. S. Burdon Sanderson   10 April 1875
letters.summary: Discusses the handling of the Memorial concerning animal experimentation.

letters.title: To John Murray   10 April [1875]
letters.summary: Is glad JM will publish [Climbing plants] as a separate little book. Some people have been much interested in it, though it has been read by very few.

letters.title: To J. S. Burdon Sanderson   [11 April 1875]
letters.summary: "We have not a day to lose if our [Vivisection] Bill or our petition is to do any good". Reports on the activities of the opposition and the attitude of politicians on the subject. Believes a meeting with a minister should be arranged and thinks Lord Derby would be a good man. "All will depend on some half-dozen or 9 or 12 men agreeing on the bill."

letters.title: From J. S. Burdon Sanderson   [12 April 1875]
letters.summary: Considers the question of recognised lecturers being allowed a licence to perform animal experiments without having to obtain a certificate of fitness.

letters.title: From J. S. Burdon Sanderson   12 April [1875]
letters.summary: Discusses the best means of presenting the draft bill about animal experimentation. Suggests that CD inform Lord Derby that scientific men concurred with the bill that had been prepared. [See9923.]

letters.title: From Thomas Burgess   13 April 1875
letters.summary: Sends CD an account of his career since leaving theBeagle.

letters.title: From Thomas Allen   14 April 1875
letters.summary: Encloses draft bill about vivisection; CD and friends may have influence enough to get it introduced in Commons or Lords; TA and the Cruelty Society do not. The Society, however, can pay for preparation of bill.

letters.title: From J. S. Burdon Sanderson   14 April [1875]
letters.summary: Agrees that CD should write to Lord Derby to say that a bill on animal experimentation was being prepared and that the government should not comment at this stage. [See9933.] Ridicules the idea of using inspectors. Distinguishes between dissection and vivisection.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   14 April 1875
letters.summary: Is sending some seeds of sweetpeas, which George [Darwin] said CD would plant for him.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   14 April [1875]
letters.summary:
CD and others now think it advisable to go further than a petition on vivisection, and a bill has been drafted.

F. Delpino’s pamphlet on pitchers ["Sulle pianti a bicchieri",Nuovo G. Bot. Ital.3 (1871): 174–6].

letters.title: From E. F. W. Pflüger   14 April 1875
letters.summary: Sends CD his latest treatise, in which he discusses the origin of life ["Über die Physiologische Verbrennung in den lebendigen Organismen",Arch. Gesammte Physiol.10 (1875): 251–367].

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   14 April [1875]
letters.summary: Thanks WTT-D for his present of Sachs’s book [Textbook of botany(1875)].

letters.title: To E. F. W. Pflüger   [after 14 April 1875]
letters.summary: Thanks EFWP for sending him his treatise.

letters.title: To J. S. Burdon Sanderson   15 and 19 April [1875]
letters.summary: Has written to Lord Derby about the vivisection issue and urged him to speak to the proper members of the Cabinet to prevent "hasty legislation versus science". CD offered to send the sketch of the bill that has been drafted or a small deputation to wait on any member of the Cabinet. Lubbock does not think the petition should be presented as he feels sure that nothing will be done this session.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   15 April 1875
letters.summary:
Approves vivisection memorial.

Lyon Playfair supports his request for Kew assistant.

Asks whether CD has botanical suggestions for Arctic expedition.

letters.title: To E. H. Stanley   15 April 1875
letters.deprecated: Edward Henry Stanley, 15th earl of Derby
letters.recipient: Edward Henry Stanley, 15th earl of Derby
letters.summary: CD has helped leading physiologists to prepare a draft bill for legislation with regard to vivisection, and he hopes Lord Derby will support the bill and mention it to ministers of the Cabinet. Has heard that other groups are preparing bills for the same purpose, and feels it important that the science of physiology be protected as well as animals.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   16 April 1875
letters.summary:
Approves draft of vivisection bill. Huxley strongly in favour of a bill.

Knows of the pitchers of one species ofDischidia.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   17 April 1875
letters.summary:
Sends concluding part of hisZoologie[see8531].

Enjoys translatingJournal of researches. Questions several passages.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   17 April 1875
letters.summary: On pitchers ofDischidiaand insects found in them.

letters.title: From D. F. Nevill   17 [April 1875]
letters.summary: Hooker has told her CD is in London. She requests a meeting.

letters.title: From E. H. Stanley   17 April 1875
letters.deprecated: Edward Henry Stanley, 15th earl of Derby
letters.sender: Edward Henry Stanley, 15th earl of Derby
letters.summary: He is honoured by CD’s selection of him as the medium of communication with Government. The matter [Vivisection Bill] now lies with the Home Secretary.

letters.title: From Federico Delpino   18 April 1875
letters.summary:
Looking forward to publication ofInsectivorous plants, which he will review.

Paul Mantegazza has criticised FD on insectivorous plants

and CD on sexual selection; FD maintains dichogamy in plants supports sexual selection.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   19 April [1875]
letters.summary:
Pleased JVC likesJournal of researches. Responds to his queries and thanks him for conscientiousness as a translator.

Insectivorous plantsis so large that Murray will publishClimbing plantsas a separate little book. HopesInsectivorous plantsis worth translating.

letters.title: From W. W. Reade   20 April 1875
letters.summary: Staying with the [Ore H.] Sandwiths during his convalescence.

letters.title: From Thomas Burgess   21 April [1875]
letters.summary: Thanks for letter of 15th and book. Recollects many sights of Tierra del Fuego described by CD.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   21 April 1875
letters.summary:
V. O. Kovalevsky has paid for theExpressionplates.

Still has 400 copies of Chauncey Wright’s pamphlet

and 450 of Müller’sFacts and arguments for Darwin.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   21 April 1875
letters.summary:
Lord Cardwell thinks it unlikely that Parliament will take any action on a vivisection bill this session. Playfair should be consulted.

E. F. W. Pflüger’s important memoir on how carbonic acid is produced by living matter and his speculation about origin of living matter [see9931].

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   21 April 1875
letters.summary:
Returns papers [unidentified].

One on inheritance destitute of meaning. How can "force" act without any material on which to act? Discussion must assume truth of some such theory as Pangenesis.

letters.title: From J. S. Burdon Sanderson   23 April [1875]
letters.summary: Further discussion about the act regulating animal experimentation; believes the licensing of places to be impracticable.

letters.title: To J. S. Burdon Sanderson   24 [April 1875]
letters.summary: CD has seen Sir John [Lubbock] who suggests that L. Playfair would be the best man to present the [vivisection] petition, but thinks the proposed bill much more important and useful. JL also suggests that the bill be given a more humanitarian aspect and that it be presented to both Houses of Parliament.

letters.title: From T. M. Coan   24 April 1875
letters.summary: Transcribes extracts from Sir James Mackintosh and J. S. Polack on infanticide.

letters.title: To R. B. Litchfield   [24 April 1875]
letters.summary: On the petition by scientists regarding vivisection and plans for presenting it in Parliament.

letters.title: To R. B. Litchfield   24 April [1875]
letters.summary: Sir John Lubbock’s advice on draft of petition on vivisection. Agrees with Lubbock’s opinion that a bill would be more effective – but the more the subject is stirred up, the better.

letters.title: To W. R. S. Ralston   24 April [1875]
letters.summary: Asks WRSR to explain a diploma and letter he has received from Russia, so he can return his thanks. [Probably a reference to CD’s being made an honorary fellow of the Society of Naturalists of the Imperial Kazan University in 1875.]

letters.title: From Humphrey Sandwith   25 April 1875
letters.summary: Announces death of W. W. Reade.

letters.title: From W. R. S. Ralston   26 April 1875
letters.summary: Translates letter [of 30 Mar 1875, missing] to CD from the Society of Naturalists in the Imperial University of Kazan, awarding an honorary membership.

letters.title: To Humphrey Sandwith   26 April 1875
letters.summary: Comments on death of W. W. Reade. "… it is best that he should have been relieved from all future suffering, as he was evidently a doomed man".

letters.title: To George Harris   27 April 1875
letters.summary: Briefly answers GH’s query whether animals can perceive any qualities unperceived by man.

letters.title: To Edward Cardwell   [before 29 April 1875]
letters.summary: Believes correspondent is interested in how physiologists regard the question of legislating on vivisection. He forwards the sketch of a bill drawn up by physiologists for that purpose.

letters.title: To Lyon Playfair   [before 29 April 1875]
letters.deprecated: Lyon Playfair, 1st Baron Playfair of St Andrews
letters.recipient: Lyon Playfair, 1st Baron Playfair of St Andrews
letters.summary: Sends a sketch of a bill on vivisection that he understands LP wishes to see.

letters.title: From J. S. Burdon Sanderson   28 April [1875]
letters.summary: Informs CD that he has taken no further action about the petition concerning animal experimentation on the understanding that it would be presented only if the government introduced an objectionable bill. [See9948.]

letters.title: From Thomas Allen   29 April 1875
letters.summary: Encloses extract which suggests that CD and friends oppose any restriction on vivisection; asks CD to state his principles. Another bill is being sketched for Cruelty Society.

letters.title: From Edward Cardwell   29 April 1875
letters.summary: Acknowledges CD’s letter and enclosure on vivisection.

letters.title: To John Murray   29 April [1875]
letters.summary: Insectivorous plantswill soon be ready to print. Does not know what to advise on size of printing. May sell poorly.

letters.title: From Lyon Playfair   29 April 1875
letters.deprecated: Lyon Playfair, 1st Baron Playfair of St Andrews
letters.sender: Lyon Playfair, 1st Baron Playfair of St Andrews
letters.summary: Supports the Vivisection Bill, with a more humanitarian preamble. Working to get it through the House of Lords.

letters.title: From J. S. Burdon Sanderson   30 April [1875]
letters.summary: Lyon Playfair approves the bill concerning animal experimentation and would be prepared to introduce it should it be necessary. Believes a bill could be passed by Parliament by September.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   30 April [1875]
letters.summary: Sends a chapter [ofInsectivorous plants]. Never was there anything so dull, but later chapters will be better. Please correct an error on p. 86.

letters.title: From the Royal Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals   30 April 1875
letters.deprecated: Royal Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals
letters.sender: Royal Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals
letters.summary: The Society wishes to introduce a bill to limit vivisection and is arranging a meeting with medical men to discuss the bill.

letters.title: To R. A. Cross   May 1875
letters.deprecated: Richard Assheton Cross, Viscount Cross of Broughton in Furness
letters.recipient: Richard Assheton Cross, Viscount Cross of Broughton in Furness
letters.summary: Sends a copy of the draft vivisection bill [see9933] and hopes that it may be approved of and supported by the Government.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   1 and 2 May [1875]
letters.summary: Proofs arrived and Francis is correcting them. Tells Emma Darwin that Amy is delighted about the azaleas. The Ruck family very much like Isabella Bird’sSix months in the Sandwich Islands.

letters.title: To J. S. Burdon Sanderson   1 May [1875]
letters.summary: CD is delighted to hear that JSBS’s exertions and labour will probably be rewarded by success. He has had a note from Playfair who, like Lubbock, thinks the title and preamble [of the proposed bill] "had better wear a more humanitarian aspect".

letters.title: From John Murray   1 May [1875]
letters.summary: JM proposes to print 1000 copies [ofInsectivorous plants].

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   1 May 1875
letters.summary: August Weismann is interested in JJW’s experiments on birds and the caterpillars they eat.

letters.title: To August Weismann   1 and 4 May 1875
letters.summary:
Comments on AW’s work [Studien zur Descendenz-Theorie, vol. 1 (1875)].

On seasonal dimorphism in Lepidoptera in relation to sexual selection.

Discusses evolutionary reversion.

Comments on birds’ avoiding brightly coloured caterpillars. Offers references on subject.

Alpheus Hyatt says Franz Hilgendorf mistaken [aboutPlanorbis multiformis].

Quotes from letter from J. J. Weir on birds’ rejection of brightly-coloured caterpillars.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   3 May [1875]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Arrangements to meet a Duke [unidentified] at High Elms [Lubbock residence].

letters.title: To John Murray   3 May 1875
letters.summary: CD proposes setting price [ofInsectivorous plants] on a printing of 1000 copies, but to have 250 additional copies printed – with CD paying for paper and press work. JM would not repay CD until 1000 are sold; and profits on the 250 to be divided as usual. CD proposes this because he does not think a second edition will ever be needed.

letters.title: To James Paget   3 May 1875
letters.summary:
Thanks JP for volume of his lectures [Clinical lectures and essays, ed. H. Marsh (1875)].

Mentions "vivisection question".

letters.title: To the Royal Society for Prevention of Cruelty to Animals   3 May 1875
letters.deprecated: Royal Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals
letters.recipient: Royal Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals
letters.summary: Regrets he cannot attend proposed meeting [on vivisection]. Hopes legislation may be passed limiting vivisection while not interfering with the progress of physiology.

letters.title: To ?   4 May [1875]
letters.summary: Sends photograph.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [4 May 1875]
letters.summary: Will send corrected proofs [ofInsectivorous plants].

letters.title: From John Murray   4 May [1875]
letters.summary: JM agrees to raise number of first printing [ofInsectivorous plants] to 1250 if CD will wait for his share of profits until sales reach 750 or 800.

letters.title: From E. B. Tylor   4 May 1875
letters.summary:
EBT’s brother, Alfred Tylor, wishes to visit CD with George Young.

AT’s "pluvial period" theory.

letters.title: To John Murray   5 May 1875
letters.summary: Agrees not to receive his share of sales onInsectivorous plantsuntil 750 or 800 copies are sold. 1250 to be printed.

letters.title: From J. S. Burdon Sanderson   6 May [1875]
letters.summary: Informs CD that Lyon Playfair would introduce the bill in the House of Commons, and that Lord Cardwell and Lord Shaftesbury had agreed to support it, the former introducing the bill in the House of Lords.

letters.title: From J. B. Innes   7 May 1875
letters.summary:
Writes about a white rabbit which is turning fawn-coloured,

and about Scottish education.

letters.title: From J. S. Burdon Sanderson   [8 May 1875]
letters.summary: Further discussion of the introduction of a bill by Lyon Playfair on animal experimentation.

letters.title: To W. D. Whitney   8 May 1875
letters.summary: Hopes WDW will come to Down.

letters.title: To J. B. Innes   10 May [1875]
letters.summary:
On colour changes in rabbits. Suspects JBI’s is of impure origin.

Is correcting proof ofInsectivorous plants.

letters.title: From T. C. Brown   12 May 1875
letters.summary: Notes absence of material on fossil coral reefs in CD’s 2d edition [Coral reefs(1874)]. Has been collecting specimens from a fossil reef near his home for four years; gave many to Oxford.

letters.title: From James Paget   12 May 1875
letters.summary: A letter introducing T. F. Burgers, President of the Transvaal Republic.

letters.title: From T. F. Burgers   13 May 1875
letters.summary: Would like to call on CD if convenient.

letters.title: To T. F. Burgers   [after 13 May 1875]
letters.summary: Proposes that TFB visit in about a week; at present CD is unwell.

letters.title: To Lyon Playfair   15 May [1875]
letters.deprecated: Lyon Playfair, 1st Baron Playfair of St Andrews
letters.recipient: Lyon Playfair, 1st Baron Playfair of St Andrews
letters.summary: Discusses Vivisection Bill.

letters.title: From F. F. Hallett   18 May 1875
letters.summary: Sends his paper to show his priority over John Le Couteur. Claims discovery of the "law of development" of cereals.

letters.title: To F. F. Hallett   [19 or 20 May 1875]
letters.summary: Thanks FFH for his note and enclosure [see9982]. Quotes from Le Couteur [On … wheat(1836)?] to justify statements made inVariation[1868].

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   19 May 1875
letters.summary: Lyon Playfair’s bill [on vivisection] is unacceptable to all teachers of physiology. It prohibits dissections for demonstrations to students. He will have to repudiate it. Asks CD’s advice.

letters.title: From F. F. Hallett   21 May 1875
letters.summary: Insists that he, not Le Couteur, was the first to recognise and exploit variationwithinwheat varieties. Disturbed he was not acknowledged inVariation.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   21 May 1875
letters.summary: CD believes Playfair’s bill would not restrict demonstrations under anaesthetic.

letters.title: From Lyon Playfair   21 May 1875
letters.deprecated: Lyon Playfair, 1st Baron Playfair of St Andrews
letters.sender: Lyon Playfair, 1st Baron Playfair of St Andrews
letters.summary: The Government has decided to hold a Royal Commission on vivisection with Lord Cardwell as chairman.

letters.title: From J. S. Burdon Sanderson   23 May [1875]
letters.summary: Believes Lyon Playfair has been led to compromise too far on bill about animal experimentation as a result of pressure from men wishing to suppress science. A full enquiry is to take place. [See9987.] Suggests that CD send Playfair Huxley’s letter on the subject.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   23 May [1875]
letters.summary: Discusses the price to be charged to Appleton’s for the plates ofInsectivorous plants.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   24 May 1875
letters.summary: Replies to CD’s various questions and suggestions concerning publication plans forInsectivorous plants.

letters.title: To Anton Dohrn   24 May 1875
letters.summary: Thanks AD for hisUrsprung[der Wirbelthiere(1875)], which astonished CD. AD’s views, if accepted by competent authorities, will show how much we have to learn about the history of every animal. Suggests caution on "degradation principle". Comments on other views in the work. Has long seen importance of the principle of "Functionswechsel" [transfer [change!?] of function], but never enunciated it as a distinct principle.

letters.title: To T. M. Hughes   24 May 1875
letters.summary: Reports some details of the geological tour he took with Sedgwick in North Wales in 1831. Recalls how neither he nor Sedgwick saw the obvious signs of past glaciation.

letters.title: From E. J. Johnston   24 May 1875
letters.summary:
The insect-capturingAraujiahas been forwarded from Portugal.

He discoversApocynumis not in the same family, and he has misquoted [John Leonard Knapp’sJournal of a naturalist(1829)];Apocynumcaptures by stamens, not stigma.

Sends seeds of PortugueseDrosera.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   26 May 1875
letters.summary: A set of electros of the woodcuts toVariationwas sent to an Italian publisher in 1869, but no reply or payment has been made since then.

letters.title: To Lyon Playfair   26 May 1875
letters.deprecated: Lyon Playfair, 1st Baron Playfair of St Andrews
letters.recipient: Lyon Playfair, 1st Baron Playfair of St Andrews
letters.summary: Writes about the Vivisection Bill; there is great fear that it may prevent demonstration dissections on insensible animals.

letters.title: From Lyon Playfair   27 May 1875
letters.deprecated: Lyon Playfair, 1st Baron Playfair of St Andrews
letters.sender: Lyon Playfair, 1st Baron Playfair of St Andrews
letters.summary: The Vivisection Bill was defeated because it was repudiated by one of its own fathers: J. S. Burdon Sanderson.

letters.title: To Lyon Playfair   28 May [1875]
letters.deprecated: Lyon Playfair, 1st Baron Playfair of St Andrews
letters.recipient: Lyon Playfair, 1st Baron Playfair of St Andrews
letters.summary: Writes again on the Vivisection Bill, expresses his desire not to ruin the progress of physiology whilst avoiding useless vivisection.

letters.title: From W. F. Segrave   28 May 1875
letters.summary: Has heard from Italian minister that the inhabitants of the Japanese island of Saghalien [Sakhalin], lately ceded to Russia, have their bodies covered with hair, like the gorilla, and are supposedly the remnant of the aboriginal population of the Japanese islands.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   29 May 1875
letters.summary: Asks whether enclosure [missing] has the correct title ofInsectivorous plants.

letters.title: To Edward Frankland   29 May [1875–81]
letters.summary: Hearty thanks for the two bottles of pure water.

letters.title: To William Marshall   29 May 1875
letters.summary: Comments on WM’s paper about ostrich feathers.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   30 May [1875]
letters.summary: Wants seeds ofNesaea verticillatafor crossing experiments to see whether seedlings from "illegitimate unions" are sterile like true hybrids.

letters.title: To C. V. Riley   30 May 1875
letters.summary: Thanks for the seventh of CVR’sAnnual reports on the noxious, beneficial and other insects in the state of Missouri(Riley 1869–77).

letters.title: From Anton Dohrn   31 May 1875
letters.summary: AD is aware of revolutionary character of his pamphlet [Ursprung der Wirbelthiere]. Authorities will not agree with him. Carl Gegenbaur and Ernst Haeckel are opposed. Younger biologists are disposed to accept his views. All he can expect is to put a stop to "the Amphioxus–Ascidian affair, and to open a road for speculation and for investigation on the side of the Annelid-homology".

letters.title: To ?   31 [May 1875]
letters.summary:
Agrees that time alone can do nothing to modify species.

Is aware that the Papaveraceae are self-fertile but feels this does not preclude an occasional cross.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   2 June 1875
letters.summary: Interested to hear about the peas.

letters.title: From William Marshall   2 June 1875
letters.summary:
Discusses feather as case of evolutionary atavism.

Will soon publish on siliceous sponges

and the skin of caterpillars.

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   2 June [1875]
letters.summary: Paralysis of the nervous system ofDionaea. Uses of tails of mice.

letters.title: To A. E. J. Modderman 3 June 1875
letters.summary: Thanks for the diploma conferring on him an honorary doctorate of medicine from Leiden University.

letters.title: From Otto Zacharias   3 June 1875
letters.summary: Intends to set up a biological periodical called “Darwinia” to spread and popularise Darwin’s theories; hopes CD may contribute a few words to the opening issue.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [after 3 June 1875]
letters.summary: Returns corrected proofs [ofInsectivorous plants].

letters.title: To Lawson Tait   4 June [1875]
letters.summary: CD’s observations on the power of movement and transmission of motor impulses in plants. If RLT succeeds with the tails of mice, it will be "a beautiful little discovery"; CD will enjoy it the more "because some German sneered at natural selection and instanced the tail of the mouse" [see10013].

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   5 June 1875
letters.summary: Playfair "disgusted at our pronunciamentos against the Bill". Burdon Sanderson and William Sharpey agreed to it. THH feels he must serve on Vivisection Commission.

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   5 June [1875]
letters.summary:
May publish a lecture on insectivorous plants and would like to dedicate it to CD.

Wishes to become an F.R.S.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   6 June 1875
letters.summary:
Comments on Fritz Schultze,Kant und Darwin[1875].

Describes recent activities.

letters.title: To Lydia Wendland   7 June [1875]
letters.summary: Is very grateful for the gift of a fender-stool. Will send her a copy ofInsectivorous plants.

letters.title: To W. C. Marshall   9 June [1875–80]
letters.summary: Asks questions about earthworms.

letters.title: To Lawson Tait   11 June [1875]
letters.summary: Has found that H. G. Bronn in the chapter appended to his translation ofOrigincited ears and tail of mice as facts opposed to natural selection. Suggests RLT examine hairs of tails of mice for possible nerves.

letters.title: To Otto Zacharias   [11 June 1875]
letters.summary: CD is convinced by the conclusions of Malthus.

letters.title: From Fritz Schultze   12 June 1875
letters.summary: Comments on his book [Kant und Darwin: ein Beitrag zur Geschichte der Entwicklungslehre(1875)].

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   12 June [1875]
letters.summary: Has separated out a pepsin-like substance from the secretion ofDrosera, which he proposes to call "Droserin".

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   12 June [1875]
letters.summary: Intends sending a paper containing some of his histological work [see "Freezing process for section-cutting; … staining and mounting sections",J. Anat. & Physiol.9 (1875): 249–58].

letters.title: To Lawson Tait   13 June [1875]
letters.summary:
RLT’s observations come too late, as CD’s book on Droseraceae has been printed.

Reports on his observations of ferment in secretions inDrosera rotundifoliaandDrosophyllum.

letters.title: To Fritz Schultze   14 June [1875]
letters.summary:
Thanks FS for his book [Kant und Darwin].

Sends regards to Haeckel.

letters.title: From G. Chiantore   16 June 1875
letters.summary: Agrees to wait for the new edition ofVariationand accepts Mr Murray’s offer of the clichés at £10. [See9981.]

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   16 June [1875]
letters.summary: Is waiting impatiently for the appearance of CD’s book [Insectivorous plants].

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   17 June [1875]
letters.summary: Sends clean sheets ofInsectivorous plants. JVC will now be able to judge whether it is worth translating. The book has wearied him and cost much labour.

letters.title: DCP-LETT-10022
letters.summary: Insectivorous plants: the means and site of absorption of digested animal matter. [Newspaper clipping enclosed.]

letters.title: To Lawson Tait   [after 17 June 1875]
letters.summary: RLT will find abundant evidence of absorption byAldrovandain CD’s forthcoming book [Insectivorous plants]. Congratulates him on his discovery of ferments.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   19 June [1875]
letters.summary: Has come to Abinger Hall for a rest afterInsectivorous plants, soon to appear. Is sick of the accursed subject.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   20 June 1875
letters.summary:
Thiselton-Dyer’s appointment has come.

Wants to discuss insectivorous plants and get some experiments going.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   22 June 1875
letters.summary: Rejoices at [Thiselton-Dyer’s] appointment.

letters.title: To Linnean Society   23 June 1875
letters.summary: Gives a report on a paper by Thomas Powell on coral islands ["Notes on the nature and productions of several atolls of the Tokelan, Ellice, and Gilbert Groups, South Pacific", read 15 Apr 1875, not published].

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   24 June [1875]
letters.summary: Insectivorous plantsready for publication. Asks price. Suggests advertisements inNatureandGardeners’ Chronicle.

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   24 June [1875]
letters.summary: An article on RLT’s lecture on insectivorous plants has appeared; the author adopts an anti-Darwinian attitude [see "Flower traps",Spectator19 June 1875, pp. 784–5; RLT’s reply inSpectator26 June 1875, pp. 816–17.]

letters.title: From J. W. Clark   25 June 1875
letters.summary: Observations of fear in animals marked by dilation of pupils.

letters.title: To C. V. Riley   25 June [1875]
letters.summary:
Is staying at a friend’s [T. H. Farrer’s] house for rest until after 6 July, so cannot see CVR at Down.

Hopes he thanked CVR for the last Report [one of CVR’sAnnual reports on the noxious, beneficial and other insects of the State of Missouri(1868–76)].

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   26 June 1875
letters.summary: Sends first copy ofInsectivorous plantsto CD. Price must be 15s.

letters.title: To Mr Russell   26 June [1875]
letters.summary: Is sorry his correspondent has had so much trouble about his address. Suggests he send the book from R. D. Fitzgerald [Australian orchids, vol. 1 (1875–82)] either by post or by rail.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   27 June [1875]
letters.summary: Sorry to hear price of 15s [forInsectivorous plants]. Asks that JM consider 14s. Fears small sale at 15s. It is his fault – he never can help making his books too big.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   28 June 1875
letters.summary:
ThinksInsectivorous plantsmust be translated and published in Germany.

Journal of researchesnearly finished.

A new [German] edition ofOriginis wanted.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   28 June 1875
letters.summary:
Agrees to priceInsectivorous plantsat 14s.

Has CD quoted a price for stereotype plates to D. Appleton?

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   29 June [1875]
letters.summary: Mentioned to Appleton only that stereotypes [forInsectivorous plants] would be provided for "a little above cost price". Glad the price of the book will be 14s. He likes making money, but cares more for wider distribution of his books. Is uneasy about sale ofInsectivorous plants.

letters.title: To F. J. Cohn   [30 June 1875]
letters.summary: CD’s publisher is sending FJC an early copy ofInsectivorous plants, in which he hopes that FJC’s admirable papers are acknowledged with the respect that they deserve.

letters.title: From J. G. F. Riedel   30 June 1875
letters.summary: Pigmentation of Celebesians’ skin changes from birth onward. Passes through some of Paul Broca’s types.

letters.title: To W. C. Williamson   30 June [1875]
letters.summary: Thanks WCW for sending his lecture ‘The dawn of animal life’, which seems "a wonderfully clear & interesting sketch of the lower organisms".

letters.title: To M. T. Masters   [July 1875]
letters.summary: Has told publisher to send a copy ofInsectivorous plants.

letters.title: From W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   [July 1875–8?]
letters.summary: Comments onInsectivorous plants, p. 353 mentioning J. J. T. Schloesing’s experiments with carbonate of ammonia [see J. J. T. Schloesing, "Sur l’absorption de l’ammoniaque de l’air par les végétaux",C. R. Hebd. Acad. Sci.78 (1874): 1700–3].

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   1 July [1875]
letters.summary:
Insectivorous plantsto be published in two or three days.

Climbing plantsand 2d ed. ofVariationwill be published early in November.

Has no strength for corrections for the new printing ofOrigin, though many are desired.

Pleased that JVC will translateInsectivorous plants.

letters.title: From D. F. Nevill   2 July [1875]
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for his book [Insectivorous plants].

Would like to visit again before August.

letters.title: From E. F. Lubbock   [after 2 July] 1875
letters.summary: A poem onInsectivorous Plants.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   3 July 1875
letters.summary: CD’s pessimistic view [of prospective sale ofInsectivorous plants] is to blame for the small printing. Murray’s printed only 1250 copies and sold 1700. A thousand more have been ordered.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   4 July [1875]
letters.summary: Very glad about sales [ofInsectivorous plants]. CD had hard work to persuade Murray to increase printing to 1250 copies, but owns he thought that number would last for eternity. U. S. publication and French, German, and Russian translations in the offing.

letters.title: From Julius Sachs   4 July 1875
letters.summary:
Thanks forInsectivorous plants.

Has just finished hisGeschichte der Botanik[1875].

Compares action ofDroseraglands to action of sprouting embryo and to action of roots in absorbing minerals.

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   5 July 1875
letters.summary: Discusses case ofCytisusgraft described by JJW.

letters.title: From Arnold Dodel   6 July 1875
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for a copy ofInsectivorous plants.

Describes experiment onDroseracarried out with his pupils.

Describes reception of the book at the University of Zurich.

Comments on Nägeli’s concept of a "morphological species".

Expresses belief in importance of natural selection.

Mentions his forthcoming publication ["Ulothrix zonata",Jahrb. f. wiss. Bot.10 (1876): 417–550].

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   6 July 1875
letters.summary: Yellow flowers occurring on a purpleCytisusgrafted onto a yellow stock.

letters.title: From John Lubbock   7 July [1875]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Arrangements to invite the Duke [unidentified].

letters.title: From James Paget   7 July 1875
letters.summary:
Thanks forInsectivorous plants.

Intrigued by the analogy between fairy-rings and annular skin diseases, e.g., herpes and psoriasis.

letters.title: From Herbert Spencer   7 July 1875
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his new volume [Insectivorous plants].

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   7 July 1875
letters.summary:
Discusses corrections toVariation.

Extends invitation to E. Ray Lankester to visit Down.

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   7 July 1875
letters.summary: Yellow and purple flowers occur on plant grafted withCytisus purpureus, but only on separate racemes. Only yellow blooms seed.

letters.title: From T. S. Baynes   8 July 1875
letters.summary: Asks CD to write short article on breeds and breeding for new edition ofEncyclopaedia Britannica. Huxley has suggested natural history topics to be covered, and recommended CD.

letters.title: From Joseph Fayrer   8 July 1875
letters.summary: Thanks for copy of CD’s latest work [Insectivorous plants].

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   8 July [1875]
letters.summary: Is very interested in JJW’s report on a purple laburnum grafted onto yellow stock which then produces yellow flowers. CD requests racemes to examine.

letters.title: From Rudolph Riemann   9 July 1875
letters.summary: Professional sheep-breeder interested in laws of inheritance reports his crosses betweenSerinus hortulanusandDryospiza canaria. Seeks to make a new species. Crosses carried out with animals varying in their proportion ofSerinusandDryospizaparentage. Confirms Prosper Lucas’ law as given inOrigin, ch. 9, with exception that strong individuals exhibit prepotency.

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   9 July 1875
letters.summary: Sends CD some of theCytisus, which has produced yellow flowers on a purple graft.

letters.title: To M. J. Berkeley   10 July 1875
letters.summary: Enquires about fairy rings.

letters.title: To M. T. Masters   10 July [1875]
letters.summary:
Thanks MTM for his excellent review [ofInsectivorous plants]

and for his trouble about the gooseberry.

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   10 July 1875
letters.summary: RegardingCytisusgraft with yellow flowers, CD thinks nurseryman has soldCytisus adamito JJW’s brother in place ofC. purpureus. This explains apparent "sport". [P.S. on envelope:]C. purpureusseeds freely.C. adaminever does.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   11 July 1875
letters.summary: Asks CD’s opinion of an experiment onDrosera.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   12 July 1875
letters.summary: Describes difficulty of conditions for the experiment withDroserasuggested by THF.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   12 July [1875]
letters.summary:
Discusses revisions forVariation, 2d ed.

Discusses experiments involving graft-hybrids.

Alludes to Pangenesis.

letters.title: To Mr Russell   12 July 1875
letters.summary: Acknowledges with thanks "Mr Fitzgerald’s magnificent work" [R. D. Fitzgerald’sAustralian orchids, part 1 (1875)]. [See10069.]

letters.title: From W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   12 July 1875
letters.summary:
WTT-D and E. R. Lankester wish to visit CD.

Has corrected some references for new edition ofVariation.

letters.title: From M. J. Berkeley   13 July 1875
letters.summary: Fairy-rings grow because the fungal spawn radiates outwards then dies off at the centre as it becomes exhausted. The verdure of the grass depends upon the decay of the fungus supplying nitrogenous manure. Rings are formed mainly in upland pastures poor in nitrogenous matter. Gives examples of woodland fungi that form rings.

letters.title: From D. F. Nevill   13 [July 1875]
letters.summary:
Thanks CD again for his book [Insectivorous plants];

would like an autograph to put in it.

Would be delighted if ever she could visit Down again.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   14 July 1875
letters.summary: Describes experiments designed to produce graft-hybrid. Has achieved adhesion in great majority of experiments. Too early to tell what ultimate success will be.

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   14 July 1875
letters.summary: JJW is to think no more about mistake [regardingCytisusgraft].

letters.title: From Alphonse de Candolle   15 July 1875
letters.summary: Thanks forInsectivorous plants.

letters.title: To D. F. Nevill   15 July [1875]
letters.summary:
Sends his autograph

and is delighted DN was interested by part of his book [Insectivorous plants].

Would be pleased to see DN at Down.

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   15 July [1875]
letters.summary: Has readInsectivorous plantsand is to review it for theSpectator.

letters.title: From William Clowes & Sons   15 July 1875
letters.summary: First proof of errata slip for inclusion inInsectivorous plants2d thousand.

letters.title: To J. S. Burdon Sanderson   16 July 1875
letters.summary:
Thanks for JSBS’s essays; wishes he had said something on Lister’s observations. Speculates on the fungoid nature of smallpox and why there is seldom re-infection.

Discusses digestion byDrosera, the action of its secretion being the same as that of gastric juice.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   16 July 1875
letters.summary: The second printing of 1000 copies [ofInsectivorous plants] has sold out. Will print 750 more [3000 in all]. Mudie’s Library and Simpkin & Co. have ordered more copies.

letters.title: To R. D. Fitzgerald   16 July 1875
letters.summary: Thanks RDF for a part of his book [Australian orchids, vol. 1 (1875–82)]; suggests further observations RDF could make and defends some of his own conclusions.

letters.title: From W. D. Fox   16 July [1875]
letters.summary:
Thanks CD forInsectivorous plants.

Is coming to London and hopes to visit Down.

letters.title: From Charlotte Papé   16 July 1875
letters.summary: Wants to study hereditary mental characters to see whether they are limited by sex – an idea CD holds provisionally and which she doubts. She sends a questionnaire form that she asks CD to criticise. Has read Francis Galton [Hereditary genius(1869)].

letters.title: From a lady [before 17 July 1875]
letters.summary: Reports the possible extinction of the Macartney Rose.

letters.title: To A. W. Bennett   17 July [1875]
letters.summary: Thanks AWB for review inNature[probably review ofInsectivorous plants, 12 (1875): 206–9, 228–31].

letters.title: To Friedrich Hildebrand   17 July 1875
letters.summary: Asks about FH’s research on maize. Suggests experiments.

letters.title: To Ludwig Rütimeyer 17 July 1875
letters.summary: Thanks for KLR’s latest work (Rütimeyer 1875).

letters.title: To Georg von Seidlitz   17 July 1875
letters.summary: Is obliged to be given a second and improved edition of GKMvS’s excellent lectures.

letters.title: To Lawson Tait   17 [July 1875]
letters.summary:
Informs RLT of J. D. Hooker’s work onNepenthes["Nepenthaceae, Cytinaceae", inProdromus systematis naturalis regni vegetabilisby A. P. de Candolle (1873), 17: 90–116].

Has asked JDH to try secretions of pitchers that had caught no insects.

letters.title: To Pieter Harting   18 July [1875–6?]
letters.summary: Sends photographs.

letters.title: To J. N. Hoare   18 July [1875]
letters.summary: Compliments JNH on the instructive tone of his sermon [‘Hospital Sunday’ preached in Chapel Royal, Dublin, 15 Nov 1874].

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   18 July 1875
letters.summary: Comments on GJR’s experiments.

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   19 July [1875]
letters.summary: Sends a note on the ferment of theNepenthessecretion, which he asks CD to forward toNatureif he thinks it worth while [see "Insectivorous plants",Nature12 (1875): 251–2].

letters.title: From William Clowes & Sons   19 July 1875
letters.summary: Errata slip forInsectivorous plants

letters.title: From the Kaiserliche Akademie der Wissenschaften   20 July 1875
letters.summary: CD has been elected an Honorary Member of the Akademie.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   20 July 1875
letters.summary:
Looks forward to reading CD’s statements about reflex action inInsectivorous plants.

Has prepared paper ["Physiology of the nervous system of Medusae",Rep. BAAS(1876): 158–63] in which he insists on occurrence of reflex action in absence of nerves. Would like to cite CD’s authority for occurrence of reflex action in plants.

letters.title: To Lawson Tait   20 July [1875]
letters.summary: CD returns MS of a paper by RLT. "If you have succeeded in separating the ferment, the fact is manifestly important." Asks whether RLT tested the digestive ability of fluid from pitchers without animal matter. This would be necessary to prove that there was ferment in the fluid. CD is glad to hear about the [passage?] for guiding insects; he had guessed this to be the case.

letters.title: To the Kaiserliche Akademie der Wissenschaften   [after 20 July 1875]
letters.summary: Acknowledges his election to the Akademie.

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   21 July [1875]
letters.summary:
Insectivorous plants: observations on the digestive fluid ofNepenthes.

Reproduction of plant by "parthenogenesis".

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   21 July 1875
letters.summary: Would be obliged for correction of references inVariation[1st ed.].

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   21 July 1875
letters.summary: Response toInsectivorous plants. Surprised that CD did not discuss origin of the contrivances. Critics will interpret them as inexplicable by theory of natural selection.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   22 July [1875]
letters.summary:
Glad to hear that ARW is so busy.

CD believes that he has thrown some light on the acquirement of the power of digestion in Droseraceae [inInsectivorous plants].

letters.title: From W. T. Thiselton Dyer   23 July 1875
letters.summary: Encloses corrections and notes onVariation[1st ed.].

letters.title: From J. H. Gilbert   24 July 1875
letters.summary: Thiselton-Dyer has asked on CD’s behalf for results of experiments at Rothamsted on herbage of permanent meadow land. Sends report and tables of botanical analysis.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   25 July 1875
letters.summary: Solicits JDH and others at Kew for signatures to nomination of Francis Darwin for membership of Linnean Society.

letters.title: From Friedrich Hildebrand   26 July 1875
letters.summary: No new experiments on mutually sterile maize varieties since his paper inBotanische Zeitungin 1868.

letters.title: To Annie Dowie   27 July 1875
letters.summary: Has previously quoted details concerning the regrowth of her amputated extra digit inVariation[2: 14–15]. The case has since been disputed, so CD, who is revising his work, asks for some fuller details.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   27 July 1875
letters.summary: His appreciation ofInsectivorous plants, especiallyUtriculariasection.

letters.title: From Annie Dowie   [after 27 July 1875]
letters.summary: Gives extracts from her father’s diary concerning the amputation and regrowth of her sister’s extra finger.

letters.title: To Friedrich Hildebrand   28 July [1875]
letters.summary: Apologises that he cannot supply any maize seed.

letters.title: To H. A. Huxley   28 July 1875
letters.summary: Asks HAH to keep Francis Darwin’s nomination paper [for Linnean Society] for Huxley to sign on return. FD appends personal note.

letters.title: From Giovanni Canestrini   29 July 1875
letters.summary:
Italian translation ofVariationwill at last be published; will await second [English] edition to incorporate corrections.

Asks permission to translateExpression.

The second [Italian] edition ofOriginis now in press.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   29 July 1875
letters.summary: Sends CD specimen pages, with two different type spacings, forClimbing plants.

letters.title: From Anton Dohrn   29 July 1875
letters.summary: Regrets he is too busy to accept CD’s invitation to visit Down, but could only thank him again for saving the Zoological Station from shipwreck.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   29 July 1875
letters.summary: Has received but not yet readInsectivorous plants.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [29 July 1875]
letters.summary: JDH will arrive by train on Saturday.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [30 July 1875]
letters.summary: Will be delayed on Saturday because of unveiling of a monument to Sir J. Franklin at Westminster Abbey.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   31 July 1875
letters.summary:
RC will confer with printer about type, etc., for reprint ofVariation.

Only 250 copies remain of [2d ed. of]Descent– will print 1000 more for annual sale.

Expressiondoes not move.

letters.title: To Annie Dowie   1 August [1875]
letters.summary: Thanks AD for her account [of the regrowth of her sister’s amputated supernumerary finger]. Is much perplexed what to conclude. Feels he should either retract his account [inVariation, 1st ed., 2: 14–15] or substantiate it by judgment of a physiologist like James Paget. Asks for tracings of her sister’s hand. [SeeVariation, 2d ed., 1: 459].

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   3 August 1875
letters.summary:
Murray is willing to make same arrangement with D. Appleton forClimbing plantsas forInsectivorous plants.

There will be no difficulty about corrections for reprint ofDescent, providing new matter fills same space as old.

letters.title: From A. M. Lane Fox   3 August 1875
letters.summary: Hexadactyly. Regrowth of removed supernumerary digits.

letters.title: To Annie Dowie   4 August [1875]
letters.summary:
CD sends his thanks for her intercession with her sister [Alice Chambers]. The extract from her father’s [Robert Chambers] diary will be sufficient.

He forwards the requested autograph.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   6 August 1875
letters.summary: Giovanni Canestrini should be reminded that before any plates for another of CD’s books can be sent, payment must be made for those already sent.

letters.title: From Hermann Müller   7 August 1875
letters.summary:
Thanks forInsectivorous plants.

Believes Lepidoptera are of greater importance as fertilisers in alpine regions than in lowlands.

The famous stone pits of Ohningen are for sale.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   [8 August 1875 or earlier]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Discusses the time of the Duke’s arrival on Tuesday. [See9968.]

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   8 August [1875]
letters.summary: Is preparing new edition ofVariationand has a query on speed of racehorses.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   9 August 1875
letters.summary: Sends papers concerned with [copyright?] registration for French and German editions [ofInsectivorous plants].

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   10 August 1875
letters.summary:
Encloses specimens of type forVariation[2d ed.].

ThinksClimbing plants[2d ed.] had better be kept in type; 1500 copies to be printed, with stereotypes to be made for Appleton.

letters.title: From Annie Dowie   10 August [1875]
letters.summary: Has re-examined her sister’s extra finger. Reports her sister’s recollections regarding its regrowth.

letters.title: To J. H. Gilbert   11 August 1875
letters.summary:
Apologises for keeping the tables so long [see10090]. The results seem extremely curious.

Comments on paper by JHG and J. B. Lawes.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   12 August 1875
letters.summary: It would be an advantage to start printing vol. 1 ofVariation[2d ed.] at once, if CD can release it. Knotty problem: the number of copies to be printed.

letters.title: From James Paget   14 August 1875
letters.summary: Encloses copy of description of an outgrown stump. Refers to letter [missing] in which CD reports on a case of amputation. Would like to check J. Simpson’s cases before thinking everything is settled.

letters.title: To Lawson Tait   15 August [1875]
letters.summary: Thanks him for his kind review ofInsectivorous plantsin theSpectator. Disputes Tait’s report of aNepenthesthat trapped a fly but did not digest it.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   15 August [1875]
letters.summary:
Thanks for answer to racehorse query;

would be grateful for correction of any errors inVariation.

letters.title: From D. Appleton & Co.   16 August 1875
letters.summary:
Accepts offer of stereotype plates from Murray forClimbing plants, and will give same terms.

Has only just madeInsectivorous plantsready. Long and favourable review just appeared inTimes.

Wants to publishVariationand so will approach Judd & Co. [publishers of first U. S. edition (1868)].

letters.title: To Annie Dowie   16 August [1875]
letters.summary: The question is whether additional digits possess power of regrowth beyond the ordinary. James Paget has convinced CD that they do not. CD must alter what he has published. [SeeVariation, 2d. ed., 2: 459.]

letters.title: From Ernst von Hesse-Wartegg   16 August 1875
letters.summary: Sends his review ofInsectivorous plantsin thePall Mall Gazetteof Vienna.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   16 August 1875
letters.summary: JDH reports his battle with Lord Henry Lennox over whether to locate new Herbarium on the Queen’s or public part of Garden.

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   16 August 1875
letters.summary: Digestive fluid in insectivorous plants. RLT’s work on tails.

letters.title: From Édouard van Beneden   18 August 1875
letters.deprecated: Édouard Joseph Louis Marie (Édouard) van Beneden
letters.sender: Édouard Joseph Louis Marie (Édouard) van Beneden
letters.summary: The unreliability of the work of J.-B. Legrain on consanguineous marriages [Recherches critiques et experimentales relatives aux marriages consanguins, extrait duBull. Acad. R. Med. Belg.2d ser. 9, no. 3].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   18 August [1875]
letters.summary:
Shares Hooker’s feelings about Douglas Galton and Lord Henry Lennox.

Bored with preparing new editions.

letters.title: To ? 18 August 1875
letters.summary: Thanks for the photographs of disks of stone, but not to trouble to send casts, as he will not work on expression again.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   19 August 1875
letters.summary:
Sends errata inInsectivorous plants.

Is correcting proofs of [2d ed. of]Climbing plants, to be published in November. It is, he thinks, worth translating.

A second, much corrected, edition ofVariationalso will be published.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   [19 August 1875]
letters.summary: Suggests GHD write a supplement to his review [of A. H. Huth’sThe marriage of near kin(1875)]. Feels sorry Huth was taken in by the Legrain fraud. [SeeAutobiography(1958), pp. 143–4.]

letters.title: From Otto Zacharias   19 August 1875
letters.summary:
Thanks forInsectivorous plants.

Describes difficulties in launching Darwinian journal.

Mentions recent criticism of evolution in Germany.

Would like to translate essay on marriage between relatives [by G. H. Darwin, see9487].

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   20 August 1875
letters.summary:
CD’s suspicions that Legrain falsified experiments on interbred rabbits are like second sight. Has sent a copy of the letter to A. H. Huth.

Henry Sidgwick and A. J. Balfour are "spiritualising" again.

letters.title: From F. J. Cohn   21 August 1875
letters.summary:
Acknowledges presentation copy ofInsectivorous plants.

StudyingDroseraon vacation in Bohemia. Thinks CD has erred in considering "aggregation" to have occurred in the protoplasm. Suggests it is result of exosmosis of vacuole.

letters.title: From William Marshall   21 August 1875
letters.summary: Doubts ostrich descended from reptiles. Its ancestors true birds. Of course, all birds descended from reptiles. Compares foetus of birds to that of reptiles.

letters.title: To Osbert Salvin   22 August [1875]
letters.summary: Obliged for his memoir ["On the avifauna of the Galapagos",Trans. Zool. Soc.(April 1875)]. His surprise that the birds from the different islands prove so similar. Comparison of the habits, nests, eggs of the commonest species of each island would throw a flood of light upon variation.

letters.title: From Hensleigh Wedgwood   [22 August 1875]
letters.summary: Errata in first edition ofInsectivorous plants.

letters.title: To A. G. Butler   23 August 1875
letters.summary: Sends a moth from Queensland, Australia. The sender says a large number have been caught with proboscises embedded in oranges. CD interested as having a bearing on hisOrchiswork. Can AGB name the family and any closely allied English genus? The proboscis seems an extraordinary structure [see F. Darwin, "On the structure of the proboscis ofOphideres fullonica",Q. J. Microsc. Sci.n.s. 15 (1875): 384–9].

letters.title: From A. G. Butler   24 August 1875
letters.summary: "The moth is rightly namedOphideres Fullonica." Gives its range, family, allied European and British species, etc.

letters.title: To F. J. Cohn   24 August 1875
letters.summary: Responds to FJC’s criticism regarding "aggregation" as it occurs in protoplasm [see10131].

letters.title: From E. A. Clowes   27 August 1875
letters.summary: R. Cooke has complained about the size of paper on which proofs are printed. He does not know that CD requested a larger size. Asks CD what should be done.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   27 August 1875
letters.summary:
The two volumes ofVariation[2d ed.] are unequal in size. Can CD reduce vol. 2 and increase vol. 1?

Does CD wish to publishClimbing plants[2d ed.] at once?

letters.title: To T. M. Story-Maskelyne   27 August [1875–81]
letters.summary: Explains that the plant is not consuming the flies, but that they die becasue they get stuck in the flowers when fertilising them.

letters.title: From F. J. Cohn   28 August 1875
letters.summary: Clarifies his thoughts on "aggregation" inDrosera.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   29 August [1875]
letters.summary:
On publishing details ofVariation[2d ed.].

CD mortified and annoyed to hear that RC has complained to Messrs Clowes of the extra expense because proofs forClimbing plantswere put on wider paper at CD’s request.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   30 August 1875
letters.summary: Apologises for the annoyance caused about the size of proof paper. Clears up misunderstanding. As forClimbing plants, RC thinks no less than 1500 copies of a book by CD should be printed.

letters.title: From Samuel Newington   30 August 1875
letters.summary: Reports a competition between the air roots of two varieties of grapevines. The victor changed the flavour and shape of the loser’s fruit.

letters.title: From George Rolleston   30 August 1875
letters.summary:
Sends copy of his "Address [to the department of anthropology",Rep. BAAS45 (1875): 142–56].

Notes criticism of remark by Walter Bagehot dealing with extinction of barbarians [cited inDescent1: 239].
