letters.title: From Joseph Fayrer   31 August 1875
letters.summary: Sends a copy of his book [The royal tiger of Bengal(1875)].

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [31 August 1875 or later]
letters.summary: Sends proofs ofVariation[2d ed.] for FD to look over.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   1 September [1875]
letters.summary: Thanks RC for his kind note. It was onlyClimbing plantsfor which he wanted the proofs to have wide margins. Wishes he understood more about printing. It would be a great convenience to authors if exterior margins of proofs were broad.

letters.title: To Joseph Fayrer   1 September 1875
letters.summary:
Thanks JF for his book.

At present has no observations he wishes made in India.

letters.title: To Samuel Newington   1 September [1875]
letters.summary:
Cannot believe in possibility that the duck is a hybrid, but correlation accords with some other facts.

Requests specimens of berries and more information about the Madresfield Court vine.

letters.title: To W. D. Whitney   1 September 1875
letters.summary: Regrets he will not return home in time to see WDW.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [1 September 1875 or later]
letters.summary: Proofs have come. It will be jolly coming down to Southampton.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [September 1875 or later?]
letters.summary: Asks FD to make out [Hermann] Hoffmann’s conclusions about the fertilisation ofPhaseolus multiflorus[inUntersuchungen zur Bestimmung des Werthes von Species und Varietät(1869)].

letters.title: To F. J. Cohn   2 September 1875
letters.summary: Further discussion of the process of aggregation in response to [10137].

letters.title: From Samuel Newington   2 September 1875
letters.summary:
Tells CD of his many experiments on interarching vines, potato tubers, exudation of carbon dioxide from roots,

and the synchrony of the pulse and the step while walking.

Would like to meet CD.

letters.title: To George Rolleston   2 September [1875]
letters.summary:
Thanks for GR’s "Address" [see10141].

Wishes he had not quoted Bagehot’s remark [inDescent1: 239] about decrease in savage populations. Interest in subject.

letters.title: From A. J. Stuart   2 September 1875
letters.summary:
Has observed a dun pony with black stripes.

Intends breeding native fowls and will happily furnish CD with any information he can.

Discusses the domestication of animals.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   3 September 1875
letters.summary:
Since the new edition ofVariationwill be stereotyped, Murray’s will always have means to provide plates if they are wanted in America.

Explains their way of sending proofs for authors who want wide margins for corrections.

Thinks it better to keepClimbing plantsfor the annual trade sale.

letters.title: From F. J. Morphy   6 September 1875
letters.summary: Reports a hybrid ram and sow, thecuinoof Mexico, which is very common and fertile.

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   7 September [1875]
letters.summary: RLT speculates on the "moral nature" of parental protection shown by humans and traces it back to its first occurrence in the animal world.

letters.title: To H. E. Dresser   [10 September 1875]
letters.summary: Hopes to meet Dresser and his guest, N. A. Severtsov, on returning to Down.

letters.title: To Lawson Tait   10 September [1875]
letters.summary: CD gives a few instances of various animals (starfish, earwigs, spiders) that take charge of their young.

letters.title: From Federico Delpino   11 September 1875
letters.summary:
Thanks for Thomas Belt’sNaturalist in Nicaragua[1874], which confirms some of his observations,

and forInsectivorous plants, which he praises.

Suggests that a book integrating knowledge of plant–animal interactions be written by a Darwinist.

Defines biology as the science of external interactions.

German reception is far more positive than Italian.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller  12 September 1875
letters.summary:
Has read CD’s book onDrosera[Insectivorous plants] and found that it presents new material and is very interesting.

Has discovered that the parasites he thought he had found inMeliponanests are in fact true females. It is remarkable that they differ so greatly from the sterile females and males of their species.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   13 September [1875]
letters.summary: Sends comments and suggestions for Huth’s experiment on crossbreeding rabbits.

letters.title: From M. C. Stanley   14 September 1875
letters.deprecated: Mary Catherine Stanley, countess of Derby
letters.sender: Mary Catherine Stanley, countess of Derby
letters.summary: Thanks CD for telling her "such exact truth". She saw Thomas Carlyle at Keston – the country air has done him good – "he is half sorry to have been so unsociable on his first arrival".

letters.title: From J. W. Clark   16 September 1875
letters.summary: Examples of pupillary dilation.

letters.title: From Woodward Emery   17 September 1875
letters.summary: Informs CD of Chauncey Wright’s death.

letters.title: To Samuel Newington   17 September 1875
letters.summary:
Thanks SN for his explanation of vines.

Discusses SN’s observation on roots secreting carbonic acid.

letters.title: To John Price   18 September [1875–9]
letters.summary: Working on plant physiology; has not strength to discuss difficult subject with anyone.

letters.title: From R. D. Fitzgerald   20 September 1875
letters.summary: On fertilisation in certain orchids.

letters.title: From Ernst von Hesse-Wartegg   20 September 1875
letters.summary: Writing article for a German newspaper on CD’s life. Requests autobiographical information.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   22 September 1875
letters.summary: Thinks CD’s case of twins with crooked fingers may be one from his twin study.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   22 September 1875
letters.summary:
Agrees to write to William Ogle [about twins with crooked fingers].

Describes growth of sweetpeas for experiment.

letters.title: From C. E. Norton   22 September 1875
letters.summary: Reports the death of Chauncey Wright: "a great blow … to the interests of sound thought and scientific inquiry throughout the country".

letters.title: To William Ogle   22 September 1875
letters.summary: Asks whether the twins WO reported to CD [see5470] were named Macrae. F. Galton has told him of a similar case with twins so named who inherited crooked little fingers from the maternal side [seeVariation, 2d ed., 2: 240]. [The twins referred to by WO were actually his sisters, see10170.]

letters.title: From William Ogle   [23–4 September 1875]
letters.summary: Asks whether CD has observed that bees limit their visits to a single kind of flower on each journey from the hive, as Aristotle has said they do. What advantage would such a limitation be to the insects?

letters.title: To ?   23 September [1875–6?]
letters.summary: Encloses a photograph and [?].

letters.title: From Francis Galton   24 September 1875
letters.summary:
Sends a lecture CD wished to see

and corrects himself about the twins.

letters.title: To J. G. F. Riedel 24 September 1875
letters.summary: Thinks JGFR should send report of coloured spots on infants’ buttocks to some ethnological society.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   24 September [1875]
letters.summary:
Will propose GJR for membership in Linnean Society.

Discusses GJR’s grafting experiments.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   25 September 1875
letters.summary:
Thanks FG for issues ofRevue[Scientifiquevol. 7, containing lectures by Claude Bernard].

Ogle says twins [with crooked fingers] are his sisters.

Recommends book by M. A. Puvis [De la dégénération des variétés de végétaux(1837)].

letters.title: To William Ogle   25 September 1875
letters.summary:
From Galton’s "twin study" he suspects that some progenitor of WO’s had the peculiarities in question.

Has collected cases of signs of assent for a revised edition ofExpression.

Suggests bees visit same species because they know how far to insert proboscis and thus save time.

letters.title: From N. A. Severtsov   25 September [1875]
letters.summary:
Sends CD the 2d part of his travels into the Tien-shan mountains [Erforschung des Thian-Schan Gebirgs-Systems(1875)].

Has written a paper on the ranges and systematics of wild sheep and on modifications probably resulting from competition with domestic sheep, which he wishes to translate into English and would like to see appended toVariation.

Discusses sexual selection in thrushes; it apparently modifies one species into another.

letters.title: From Oswald Heer   28 September 1875
letters.summary:
Comments onInsectivorous plants.

Describes his own work on fossil flora of Eastern Siberia.

Discusses genusGinkgo.

letters.title: From W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   28 September 1875
letters.summary: Reports onSchrankia aculeatain which pinna and pinnule are sensitive, but, unlikeMimosa pudica, rachis does not move.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   29 September 1875
letters.summary: Sends specimens of grafted potatoes. Describes grafting experiments designed to prove possibility of graft-hybrids, and thus, Pangenesis.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   30 September 1875
letters.summary:
CD obliged about theSchrankia

and thanks WTT-D for details of last number ofGardeners’ Chronicle.

letters.title: From W. M. Canby   1 October 1875
letters.summary: Acknowledges copy ofInsectivorous plants; has observedDrosera filiformisleaves closing around prey.

letters.title: From Mr Turner   2 October 1875
letters.summary: When the tails of horned cattle are rubbed ‘just below the root,’ they invariably twist their bodies, stretch their necks, and begin to lick their lips.

letters.title: To Thomas Meehan   3 October 1875
letters.summary:
Comments on review [ofInsectivorous plants] inNew York Independent.

Working onCross and self-fertilisation.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   3 October [1875]
letters.summary:
Suggests WTT-D read account ofBignonia capreolatain forthcomingClimbing plants.

Plans experiments [on Melastomataceae]. Describes similar experiment performed onMonochaetum. Interested in meaning of differently coloured stamens.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   5 October 1875
letters.summary:
Hopes printing ofVariation[2d ed.] is going satisfactorily.

Climbing plants[2d ed.] is finished.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   6 October 1875
letters.summary: FearsVariation[2d ed.] will not be ready for Murray’s annual sale unless printer sends proof more quickly. Arrangements with Italian publishers.

letters.title: To C. E. Norton   7 October 1875
letters.summary: Comments on the sudden death of Chauncey Wright.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   8 October 1875
letters.summary:
Canestrini still owes £10 from 1869 for electros of 1st edition [ofVariation].

RC has urged Clowes on with printing ofVariation[2d ed.],

but withClimbing plants[2d ed.] ready, it need not be done before the annual sale.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   8 October 1875
letters.summary:
CD is circulating certificate proposing GJR for membership in Linnean Society.

Discusses hybrid potatoes from Germany.

letters.title: From Edouard Bergson   10 October 1875
letters.summary: Asks CD’s opinion on whether there is a fundamental difference between the "primitive forms" of animals and plants. Mentions and rejects various views of major distinguishing characteristics.

letters.title: From D. Appleton & Co.   11 October 1875
letters.summary: Has secured rights toVariationfrom Judd & Co.; had to pay $350 [dollars or pounds!?] for old plates and promise 50% discount on 150 copies of the new edition. Hopes Murray’s charge for plates of new edition will not exceed cost of doing the work in the U. S. Judd lost out considerably from small sale of his edition.

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   11 October 1875
letters.summary: Wishes CD to present RLT’s paper on insectivorous plants to the Royal Society.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   12 October 1875
letters.summary: Charge for 500 sets of the heliotype illustrations ofExpressionis £37 10s 6d.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   12 October 1875
letters.summary:
Sends an article for CD’s opinion.

Has finished an account of the globes for thePhilosophical Magazine["On maps of the world", 50 (1875): 431–44].

His poor health has interfered with his pitch experiments.

letters.title: To Edouard Bergson   13 October 1875
letters.summary: Comments on difficulty of distinguishing between lower animal and vegetable organisms.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   13 October [1875]
letters.summary:
Pleased by W. Stanley Jevons’ letter.

Has ordered Dr Cohn’s book.

Is sure that GHD’s energy will lead to success with work on viscous fluids.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   13 October [1875]
letters.summary:
R. L. Tait has requested CD send his [Tait’s] paper onNepenthesto Royal Society. CD considers this a nuisance.

Certificate for G. J. Romanes.

Francis’ experiments on mechanism of twisted seeds.

letters.title: From Friedrich Max Müller   13 October [1875]
letters.summary: Sends CD his answers to W. D. Whitney’s articles. Sees man as separated from other animals by the possession of language. There is no scientific evidence for even the slightest attempt at language in the higher animals, which cannot, therefore, be reasonably regarded as "stunted man". [See "In self-defence",Chips from a German workshop4 (1875): 473–549.]

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   14 October [1875]
letters.summary:
Sends sheets ofClimbing plants[2d ed.], which will be published in November. Suggests JVC have someone translate it under his supervision,

since he has not yet finishedInsectivorous plants.

Admires the appearance of [German ed. of]Journal of researches.

Discusses other publication prospects.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   14 October 1875
letters.summary:
JDH shares CD’s annoyance with R. L. Tait.

Has identified awned carpels for CD.

Sports ofParitium.

Suggests extending Francis’ experiments with glycerine on twisted seeds, toMimosa.

letters.title: To Lawson Tait   14 October [1875]
letters.summary: Will be happy to present RLT’s paper onNepenthesto Royal Society.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   15 October [1875]
letters.summary:
Has decided to send R. L. Tait’s paper to the Royal Society.

Will try glycerine onMimosabut doubts it will have an effect.

letters.title: To Friedrich Max Müller    15 October [1875]
letters.summary: Thanks FMM for his essay [see10194]. Though some of FMM’s remarks are "stinging", they have all been made "gracefully".

letters.title: From W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   [16–22 October 1875]
letters.summary: PS concerningImantophyllum.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   16 October 1875
letters.summary: Sent a copy of Orchis book to Gentry. Mentions Morley’s article on Diderot. Asks for another copy of the new edition of Descent.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   16 October [1875]
letters.summary: Thanks for information. Absorption of ammonium carbonate by glandular hairs.

letters.title: From Thomas Belt   17 October 1875
letters.summary: Reports observations of T. C. Renshaw on how some flowers of theTritomacatch bees and other insects. Thinks it may be a contrivance against unbidden visitors, as insects caught are not consumed.

letters.title: From Charles Voysey   18 October 1875
letters.summary: Wants CD to contribute to a new magazine to promote theism.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   19 October 1875
letters.summary: Gives directions for growing plants he has sent and corrects CD’s taxonomy.

letters.title: From W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   20 October 1875
letters.summary: It has been empirically established at Kew that insular plants tend to be heteromorphic, plants with entire leaves tending to produce divided leaves.

letters.title: To John Tyndall   20 October [1875]
letters.summary: JT’s tube [of boiled infusion] dated 16 Oct was clear on 19th; on the 20th it was muddy and contained many bacteria in living movement.

letters.title: To John Fiske   21 October [1875]
letters.summary:
Thanks for excellent notice of Chauncey Wright.

Would like a copy of Wright’s "Darwinism in Germany" [Nation21 (1875): 168–70].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   21 October [1875]
letters.summary: Describes observations by his son Horace on the extreme sensitivity of twisted seeds to moisture.

letters.title: From Giovanni Canestrini  22 October 1875
letters.summary:
Has heard that 2d ed. ofVariationis out. If CD will send it to him, he will complete the Italian translation in a short time.

His translation ofExpressionis nearly finished [published in 1878],

and the 2d ed. ofOriginis almost entirely published.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   22 October 1875
letters.summary:
Sends a copy ofClimbing plants[2d ed.]. Price cannot be higher than 6s.

Variation[2d ed.] price will be 18s, if CD approves. Future reprints will not be costly, since both have been stereotyped.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   22 October 1875
letters.summary:
Encloses manuscript [missing] by George King ["Sport inParitium",J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)15 (1877): 101–3].

Sends thanks to Hooker for correction of name. Mentions other errors.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   23 October [1875]
letters.summary:
Sends list for complimentary copies and suggests various arrangements related to publication ofClimbing plants.

Thinks a revised edition ofOrchidsis needed.

letters.title: From Gustavus Fritsche   23 October 1875
letters.summary: About a Polish edition ofVariation.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   23 October 1875
letters.summary: Comments on Hermann Müller’s article on the structure ofGunneraflowers.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   23 October [1875]
letters.summary:
Thanks for THH’s essay on species [article for an American encyclopedia].

Will probably never again write on large and general subjects; will keep to easier specific ones such as insectivorous and climbing plants.

letters.title: From Hermann Müller   23 October 1875
letters.summary: Is glad CD is working on cross- and self-fertilisation; reports recent works of botanists, notably Thomas Meehan’s ["Are insects any material aid to plants in fertilisation?",Philadelphia Press13 Aug 1875], in which the importance of cross-fertilisation is denied.

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   23 October [1875]
letters.summary: Thanks CD for consenting to present his paper.

letters.title: From John Tyndall   23 October [1875]
letters.summary: Asks whether he may send two or three other tubes [of boiled infusions] to be placed in the open and observed for him.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   25 October 1875
letters.summary:
Stereotype plates ofClimbing plantssent to D. Appleton’s agent.

A revised edition ofOrchidswould be desirable.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   [25 October 1875]
letters.summary: Asks that a copy of GHD’s paper on cousin marriage be sent to Hermann Müller. J. F. McLennan admires it "as a model".

letters.title: From G. W. Morehouse   25 October 1875
letters.summary: Has found a spiral fibre inDrosera rotundifolialeaves which resembles animal muscle but is probably a modified ordinary plant fibre.

letters.title: To John Tyndall   25 October [1875]
letters.summary: Asks JT to send the tubes [of boiled infusions]. Frank Darwin will do his best. Asks for full instructions.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [26 October 1875]
letters.summary:
Has sent a copy [of his article on cousin marriage] to Hermann Müller.

Problem he is now working on is a tough nut: "It does not do what [James Clerk] Maxwell said it wd or ought to do".

letters.title: From James Jameson   26 October 1875
letters.summary: Report, from a reader ofExpression, of a Negro boy’s monkey-like screams while having fractured femur adjusted without chloroform.

letters.title: To Hermann Müller   26 October 1875
letters.summary: On HM’sBefruchtung der Blumen[1873].

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   26 October [1875]
letters.summary:
WantsImantophyllumfor crossing experiments.

Is glad WTT-D thinks George King’s notes worth sending to the Linnean Society.

letters.title: To Gustavus Fritsche   27 October 1875
letters.summary: Will send vol. 1 [ofVariation, 2d ed.] as soon as complete so that correspondent can decide about the translation.

letters.title: From Edward Cardwell   28 October 1875
letters.summary: CD is asked to testify before a Royal Commission on experiments on living animals.

letters.title: To Edward Cardwell   29 October 1875
letters.summary: CD would feel bound to give evidence to the Royal Commission on vivisection should they ask him, but he has no personal experience of the matter. Expresses his opinions on the importance to physiology of experiments on live animals.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   30 October 1875
letters.summary: Encloses an invitation to give evidence to Vivisection Commission. Satisfied with way things were going, but E. E. Klein’s evidence that he is utterly indifferent to pain of animals has done great mischief.

letters.title: To Smith, Elder & Co   30 October 1875
letters.summary: Acknowledges receipt of £2 8s 10d for 2d edition ofCoral reefs.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   1 November [1875]
letters.summary: Astonished and disgusted at Klein’s evidence. No doubt there will be severe and vicious legislation against physiology. Will give evidence before Commission.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   2 November [1875]
letters.summary: Has heard that FG will write on inheritance. Huxley does not believe in E. G. Balbiani’s views on subject.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   2 November 1875
letters.summary: Arrangements for CD’s appearance before Vivisection Commission.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   3 November 1875
letters.summary: Outlines a memoir he will give at the Anthropological Society [see10238] [error for 10242!?] in which he differs theoretically with Pangenesis.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   [before 4 November 1875]
letters.summary:
Sends successful graft-hybrid of red and white carrot.

CD should correct passage inVariationexplaining deformation of sternum in fowls [Variation, 2d ed., 1: 287–8].

Chapter inVariationon Pangenesis is admirable.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   4 November [1875]
letters.summary:
In London yesterday for Vivisection Commission.

Is revising his chapter on Pangenesis [inVariation, 2d ed.] to allow that gemmules probably multiply in the reproductive organs.

Notes examples of inheritance of acquired characteristics cited by Brown-Séquard.

Doubts that double parentage is necessary for complex organisations.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   [4 November 1875]
letters.summary:
Mentions his appearance before Vivisection Commission.

Discusses his plans for planting and observing the carrots sent by GJR.

Mentions views of J. S. Burdon Sanderson on graft-hybrids.

Comments on GJR’s paper ["Instinct and acquisition",Nature12 (1875): 553–4].

[Letter incorrectly dated "Thursday 8th" by CD.] [!? shd be note not synopsis]

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   4 November 1875
letters.summary: Carrots have arrived; CD has potted them.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   5 November 1875
letters.summary: Sends a proof of his "Theory of heredity" from theContemporary Review[27 (1875): 80–95; revised inJ. Anthropol. Inst.5 (1876): 329–48]. Welcomes CD’s help and criticism.

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   6 November [1875]
letters.summary: Composition of "Droserin" [see10015].

letters.title: To Francis Galton   7 November [1875]
letters.summary:
Comments on FG’s paper ["A theory of heredity"]. Finds essay difficult to understand. Objects that FG’s theory conflicts with phenomenon of use and disuse. Conflicts also with rarity of bud-variations in nature.

Says he has ordered FG’s article ["The history of twins",Fraser’s Mag.92 (1875): 566–76; revised inJ. Anthropol. Inst.5 (1876): 391–406].

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   7 November 1875
letters.summary:
Thanks CD forClimbing plantsandInsectivorous plants.

Discusses his research on phylogeny. Results described in "Die Gastrula und die Eifurchung der Tiere" [Jena. Z. Naturw.9 (1875): 402–508].

Describes newly discovered coral.

letters.title: From Hugo de Vries   7 November 1875
letters.summary: Thanks for 2d edition ofClimbing plantsand for CD’s recognition of HdeV’s two essays on the subject [Climbing plants, pp. v–vi, 9 n., 22, 160]. Cause of spiral growth of tendrils.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   7 November 1875
letters.summary:
Thanks forClimbing plants[2d ed.].

Is reading proofs [ofGeographical distribution(1876)].

letters.title: From Francis Galton   8 November 1875
letters.summary: Responds to suggestions and criticisms CD made to "theory of heredity" [see10245].

letters.title: To the secretary of the Royal Commission on vivisection   8 November 1875
letters.deprecated: Secretary of the Royal Commission on vivisection
letters.recipient: Secretary of the Royal Commission on vivisection
letters.summary: CD sends a draft bill which he helped to prepare relating to experiments on live animals; the Commissioners may wish to see it.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   9 November [1875]
letters.summary:
Climbing plantshas sold better than he expected.

Thinks another 1000 ofOriginmay have to be printed; he has no corrections to make.

letters.title: From Arthur Nicols   [before 10 November 1875]
letters.summary:
Discusses his ambitions.

Writes of rats that gnaw through lead pipes to find water.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   10 November [1875]
letters.summary:
Comments on FG’s paper ["The history of twins"].

CD is "in a passion with theSpectatorwho always muddles".

letters.title: From Arthur Nicols   10 November 1875
letters.summary: Apologises for troubling CD to look for his lost MS.

letters.title: To Hugo de Vries   10 November 1875
letters.summary: Suggests that, if HdV make further observations on tendrils, he attend to Echinocystis, as described on p. 132 ofClimbing plants.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   12 November [1875]
letters.summary: Thanks forElementary biology[1875]. Wishes he had had a course like it.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   13 November 1875
letters.summary:
Mentions receipt of EH’sHistory of creation[1876].

Describes his own work on cross- and self-fertilised flowers. Subject bears on the very principle of life.

letters.title: From W. H. Scott   13 November 1875
letters.summary: Gives an example of the power of reasoning shown by dogs.

letters.title: To Herbert Spencer   13 November 1875
letters.summary:
CD cannot remember whether he was on the committee of the Jamaica affair [for prosecution of Governor Eyre in 1866] but he subscribed £10.

It is curious and amusing how positivists hate all men of science, possibly because their prophet [Comte] made laughable and gigantic blunders in predicting the course of science.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   16 November 1875
letters.summary:
Electrotypes of woodcuts inClimbing plants[2d ed.]

andVariation[2d ed.] for Appleton.

Asks CD whether he has any corrections forInsectivorous plantsbefore stereotypes are made.

letters.title: To W. H. Scott?   16 November? [1875?]
letters.summary: Thanks for a ‘very remarkable & trustworthy case of reason in the dog’.

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   16 November [1875]
letters.summary: Has CD ever come acrossDischidia rafflesiana?

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   16 November [1875]
letters.summary: Has extracted a highly deliquescent substance from digestive secretion of insectivorous plants.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   17 November 1875
letters.summary:
Reminds RC that he will lose £200 unlessVariation[2d ed.] sells pretty well in the U. S. [and therefore Murray’s price for stereotypes should be kept low].

Is unwilling thatInsectivorous plantsbe stereotyped until he has profited by criticisms and new facts. It would be better to wait a few years and correct the book thoroughly before stereotyping.

letters.title: From Hugo de Vries   17 November 1875
letters.summary: Hopes to continue study of climbing plants next summer and to observe facts mentioned in CD’s letter.

letters.title: From John Murray   19 November [1875]
letters.summary: Report on sales ofOrigin,Insectivorous plants, andClimbing plants.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   20 November 1875
letters.summary: Queries concerned with his translation ofInsectivorous plants, which has been delayed by illness but is now two-thirds done.

letters.title: To John Murray   20 November 1875
letters.summary:
Greatly pleased at sale [ofClimbing plants].

Points out a discrepancy in their records of copies ofOriginprinted.

500 more copies ofInsectivorous plantsshould last forever.

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   20 November [1875]
letters.summary: His paper [for Royal Society] is completed; would CD like to read it?

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   [c. 22 November 1875]
letters.summary: Calculates ounce and gram equivalents of pints (old and imperial).

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   22 November [1875]
letters.summary:
Thanks JVC for corrections inInsectivorous plants. Explains confusion of fluid and dry measures. The work has sold well in England.

Repeats suggestion that JVC employ someone to translateClimbing plantsunder his supervision.

letters.title: From John Murray   22 November [1875]
letters.summary:
Sends cheques in payment on three of CD’s books.

Proposes to print 500 copies ofInsectivorous plantsbefore distributing the type.

letters.title: From D. Appleton & Co   23 November 1875
letters.summary:
Can cut the electros from the plates of the illustrations for the new edition ofVariationif they are the same as in the first edition.

Has received plates forClimbing plantsand will print immediately.

letters.title: To John Murray   23 November 1875
letters.summary:
Asks to be informed whenever more copies of his books are printed, as there may be errors to correct.

Asks how many copies ofOriginhave been printed "from the first". The number will be "a good puff" when listed in the new edition ofVariation.

letters.title: From John Murray   23 November [1875]
letters.summary: JM has printed 16250 copies ofOriginsince 1859.

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   23 November [1875]
letters.summary: RLT’s paper will be sent to CD. Will CD notify him of any serious defects?

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   24 November 1875
letters.summary: JDH concerned about preparations for [his address at] Royal Society [anniversary] meeting [Proc. R. Soc. Lond.(1876): 72–94].

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   25 November 1875
letters.summary: Has read EH’sHistory of creation[trans. E. R. Lankester (1875)]. Was much struck with many "brilliant & original remarks". Is gratified by the way EH speaks of CD’s books.

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   25 November [1875]
letters.summary: RLT’s paper on insectivorous plants is being copied.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   26 November 1875
letters.summary: Thanks for the peas which arrived in "beautiful order".

letters.title: To the secretary of the Royal Society of London  27 November 1875
letters.summary: Communicates a paper by Lawson Tait to the Royal Society [not published by Royal Society, see10452].

letters.title: To Lawson Tait   27 November [1875]
letters.summary: Because CD has been unwell, he has not read RLT’s paper carefully, but it seems an important contribution to science. Hopes RLT’s chemical observations will be confirmed. It seems a great anomaly that two substances with an acid should be requisite for digestion.

letters.title: From Quintino Sella   28 November 1875
letters.summary: Letter enclosing decree from the Accademia dei Lincei, with signatures dated 2 and 16 July 1875.

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   29 November [1875]
letters.summary:
RLT’s insectivorous plants paper.

The success of a recent lecture.

letters.title: From W. B. Dawkins   1 December 1875
letters.summary: Asks CD to sign papers for Royal Society candidacy of W. B. Clarke.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   1 December [1875]
letters.summary: Comments on R. L. Tait’s claimed isolation of digestive ferments fromNepenthes.

letters.title: To Lawson Tait   1 December [1875]
letters.summary: Abstract sent to the Royal Society. It seems to CD "uncommonly clear and well-done".

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   2 December 1875
letters.summary: E. R. Lankester is in danger of being black-balled for admission to the Linnean Society; Thiselton-Dyer is in the midst of the fight.

letters.title: From W. R. S. Ralston   2 December 1875
letters.summary: CD’s letter from Tiflis is not in Russian but Georgian.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [after 2 December 1875]
letters.summary: Sends thanks for CD’s help in making him a Fellow of the Linnean Society. Dyer has sent some Erinem.

letters.title: From W. R. S. Ralston   3 December 1875
letters.summary: S. C. Malan, Rector of Broadwindsor, could translate Georgian letter from Tiflis.

letters.title: To Thomas Carlyle   4 December 1875
letters.summary: A letter of congratulation to Thomas Carlyle on his 80th birthday signed by CD and 118 others; to accompany the gift of a commemorative medal.

letters.title: To Quintino Sella   4 December 1875
letters.summary: Acknowledges QS’s letter [10280f] and the diploma of the Accademia dei Lincei.

letters.title: To August Weismann   6 December 1875
letters.summary: Comments on AW’s essay [on "Axolotl",Z. Wiss. Zool.25 (suppl.) (1875): 297–342] with respect to evolutionary reversion. Peloric flowers must also be considered reversion.

letters.title: From Archibald Geikie   7 December 1875
letters.summary: Asks for CD to add his name to James Croll’s application to the Royal Society of London.

letters.title: To W. R. S. Ralston   7 December [1875]
letters.summary: Snow has caused postponement of trip to London. Will inform WR when he arrives.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [before 8 December 1875]
letters.summary: Sends Linnean papers.

letters.title: From Arthur Nicols   8 December 1875
letters.summary:
He will repeat his experiments on the cat’s sense of smell.

The intelligence of rats is shown by their gnawing through lead pipes to find water.

letters.title: To? Archibald Geikie?   9 December 1875
letters.summary: CD has signed James Croll’s certificate [of nomination to Royal Society] with real pleasure.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   10 December [1875]
letters.summary: Asks JDH to try to come to luncheon if he is in London.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   10 December [1875]
letters.summary: Is coming to London. Will call on THH.

letters.title: From Samuel Newington   10 December 1875
letters.summary:
Reports on various observations and experiments: a duck–fowl hybrid with queer habits,

three cases of man–dog hybrids,

his interarching vine experiments,

and orange scale.

letters.title: To ?   [after 11 December 1875]
letters.summary: Strongly disapproves of the blackballing of Edwin Ray Lankester by the Linnean Society. States the reasons for his disapproval and hopes they will be considered.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [12 December 1875]
letters.summary: CD is furious at the prospect of Lankester’s being black-balled by the Linnean Society. He plans to solicit support from various members and to come up with Frank for the voting.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [13 December 1875]
letters.summary: [The black-balling of Edwin Ray Lankester by the Linnean Society] is a most scandalous shame. Will arrange for his own admission to fellowship of the Society.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   14 December 1875
letters.summary:
Copies remaining in stock ofClimbing plants[2d ed.], 105,

andOrigin[6th ed.], 100.

CD should send the printer any corrections he wants made before reprinting.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [15? December 1875]
letters.summary: Asks CD whether it is worth sending money to prop up the Index.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   [15 December 1875]
letters.summary: Ferdinand Cohn has already sent a copy of his article, [possibly: "Über die Function der Blasen vonAldrovandaundUtricularia",Beitr. Biol. Pflanz.1 (1870–5) pt 3: 71–89].

letters.title: To A. W. Bennett   16 December [1875]
letters.summary: Arranges to visit AWB.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   16 December [1875]
letters.summary: Discusses blackballing of E. R. Lankester [at Linnean Society]. Reports on his attempts to persuade other Fellows to support Lankester’s election.

letters.title: From A. W. Bennett   17 December 1875
letters.summary:
Is delighted CD plans to call on him.

Wants to discuss botanical work.

letters.title: To A. W. Bennett   [17 December 1875]
letters.summary: Declines invitation to breakfast.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   17 December [1875]
letters.summary:
Discusses payment of £10 owed by Italians.

"No corrections for Voyage of Beagle [Journal of researches]."

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   17 [December 1875]
letters.summary:
Suggests skin-grafting experiment on birds.

Discusses case of Edwin Ray Lankester; it has aroused his indignation.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   18 December [1875]
letters.summary:
Mentions revisions [inVariation, 2d ed.].

Argues with FG’s theory of heredity, defending Pangenesis: "I cannot doubt that every unit of the hybrid is hybridised and sends forth hybridised gemmules."

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   18 December [1875]
letters.summary: E. Ray Lankester blackballed by Linnean Society. Another election planned. Would JJW use his influence in Lankester’s favour?

letters.title: From Francis Galton   19 December 1875
letters.summary: Outlines in simple form the statistical distribution of inherited characteristics in a theory of "organic units".

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   [19 December 1875]
letters.summary: CD’s attempts to get support for Lankester among Fellows of the Linnean Society. He has encountered opposition to the Council.

letters.title: To W. R. S. Ralston   20 December 1875
letters.summary: Encloses S. C. Malan’s letter which WRSR need not return. The letter in Georgian is so foolish he will not reply.

letters.title: From G. G. Stokes   20 December 1875
letters.summary: Notifies CD that information he [GGS] gave before on colours of peacock’s feathers was wrong [see5891et seq.] and refers CD to H. C. Sorby, who has worked on the subject.

letters.title: From J. P. Thompson   20 December 1875
letters.summary: Sends CD an address [missing] on Lucretius and St Paul.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   21 December [1875]
letters.summary: Encloses a correction [forClimbing plants, 2d ed.]. Asa Gray made a mistake in name of species ofPassiflora.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   21 December 1875
letters.summary: Sends list of misprints in first edition ofInsectivorous plantsfor the German collected works.

letters.title: To James Crichton-Browne   22 December 1875
letters.summary: Thanks for 5th volume of theWest Riding Asylum Medical Reports.

letters.title: From Louis Grenier   22 December 1875
letters.summary: Asks permission to make a résumé ofInsectivorous plantsfor Société Botanique de Lyon.

letters.title: From M. C. Stanley   22 December 1875
letters.deprecated: Mary Catherine Stanley, countess of Derby
letters.sender: Mary Catherine Stanley, countess of Derby
letters.summary: Lord Derby was pleased by CD’s warm and genuine expression of approval [of his support of Vivisection Bill? see9933].

letters.title: To G. G. Stokes   22 December 1875
letters.summary: CD is curious about the feathers but will wait to see whether H. C. Sorby’s paper appears.

letters.title: To F. S. B. François de Chaumont   23 December 1875
letters.deprecated: Francis Stephen Bennet François de Chaumont
letters.recipient: Francis Stephen Bennet François de Chaumont
letters.summary: Thanks for FdeC’s work [Lectures on state medicine(1875)].

letters.title: To James Sully   23 December 1875
letters.summary: Thanks JS forSensation and intuition[1874]. Regrets that it was not published earlier, so he could have profited by some of the discussions.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   23 December 1875
letters.summary: E. R. Lankester has been unfairly blackballed at the Linnean Society. He is to be proposed for a second time, with CD seconding the proposal. Urges ARW to attend the ballot.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   25 December 1875
letters.summary:
Thanks for errata inInsectivorous plants.

Sends spare copies of his papers, but thinks several are not worth publishing.

Has only one copy, which he will lend JVC, of the best one, on "Erratic boulders of South America" [Collected papers1: 145–63].

Has not sent "Parallel roads of Glen Roy" [Collected papers1: 87–137], as he is sure he was wrong.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   25 December 1875
letters.summary:
"Sambaquis", or shell mounds accumulated by former inhabitants of the coast, contain shells of some animals that FM has never seen living.

Ants that live onimbaubatrees (Cecropia) are attracted by small bodies at base of each petiole.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   [before 26 December 1875]
letters.summary:
Asks to borrow Ernst Haeckel’sBeiträge zur Naturgeschichte der Hydromedusen(1865) [andZur Entwicklungsgeschichte der Siphonophoren(1869)].

Has not been neglecting Pangenesis for Medusae.

letters.title: From Henry Edwards   26 December 1875
letters.summary: Sends his paper on an American pitcher-plant [Darlingtonia californica].

letters.title: To K. M. Lyell   26 December [1875]
letters.summary: Sends Charles Lyell’s letters. Those from 1862–9 are so heavy that they have to be put in two parcels.

letters.title: From D. F. Nevill   26 [December 1875?]
letters.summary: Regrets having missed seeing CD when he was in London.

letters.title: To C.-F. Reinwald   26 December 1875
letters.summary: Encloses list of errata inInsectivorous plants[1875] for the French translator.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   26 December 1875
letters.summary:
Sends books.

Discusses GJR’s Pangenesis experiments; views of Galton on the theory.

letters.title: From Nevil Story-Maskelyne   26 December 1875
letters.summary: He is proposing [John Wesley?] Judd for F.R.S. and asks for CD’s support.

letters.title: To Henry Edwards   [after 26 December 1875]
letters.summary:
Thanks for sending "wonderful speciment of Darlingtonia".

"I will not forget your obliging offer of giving me information with respect to California about which I may be curious."

letters.title: From Asa Gray   28 December 1875
letters.summary:
AG’s notices ofInsectivorous plants[Nation22 (1876): 12–14, 30–2]

andClimbing plants[2d ed.,Am. J. Sci.3d ser. 11 (1876): 69–74].

Use of flower peduncles for support inMaurandia. Transition from branches to tendrils.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   28 December 1875
letters.summary: Is glad ARW will attend to vote for Lankester [at the Linnean Society].

letters.title: To Nevil Story-Maskelyne   29 December 1875
letters.summary:
Has signed John Wesley Judd’s certificate.

Hopes his wife, Thereza Mary Story-Maskelyne, will not forget about the meeting at the Linnean Society on 3 February; feels E. R. Lankester’s case is very cruel.

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   29 December 1875
letters.summary:
BJS has just moved.

Gives the information he has of their old shipmates.

Tells of his brother’s misfortunes.

letters.title: From J. H. Gilbert   31 December 1875
letters.summary: Discusses fairy rings.

letters.title: From Nemo   [1876?]
letters.summary: A believer in evolution seeks to convince CD that a spiritual creative force, rather than natural selection, explains its operation.

letters.title: To [?]   [1876 or later?]
letters.summary: Complies with correspondent’s request; encloses photographs of himself.

letters.title: To William Robinson   4 January 1876
letters.summary: Thanks for the copies of theGarden, which contain a drawing of CD and notice of his work.

letters.title: From J. H. Gilbert   6 January 1876
letters.summary: Thanks for a copy ofInsectivorous Plants.

letters.title: From John Murray   6 January [1876]
letters.summary:
At last,Expressionis beginning to sell again.

Cooke has not yet decided on number ofVariation[2d ed.] to print.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   8 January [1876]
letters.summary: Asks GHD to calculate average or mean heights of crossed and self-fertilised plant species.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [after 8 January 1876]
letters.summary: Provides CD with a method of obtaining a numerical ratio that expresses the superiority in heights of crossed plants to self-fertilised plants.

letters.title: From W. H. Dallinger   10 January 1876
letters.summary:
Has confirmed CD’s observations onDrosera.

Asks whether CD agrees that it is "no longer a fact" that the bladders ofUtricularia vulgarisenable the plant to become lighter for fecundation and heavier when that act is accomplished. Plans to undertake further observations, under very high-powered microscopes, of mechanism of digestion.

letters.title: From Hermann Hoffmann   10 January 1876
letters.summary: Bug onTilia, cited inVariation, wasCimex apterus.

letters.title: From Charles O’Shaughnessy   10 January 1876
letters.summary:
He has confutedDescent.

Enclosures announce his cures of potato blight, epilepsy, etc.

letters.title: To William Robinson   10 January [1876?]
letters.summary: Accepts WR’s offer of copies of theGardenfor the next half-year.

letters.title: To W. H. Dallinger   [after 10 January 1876]
letters.summary:
CD has read all of WHD’s and J. J. Drysdale’s papers [on spontaneous generation, monads, and the origin of life] and finds them the best work on the subject.

The function of bladders inUtriculariais not to float the plant.

letters.title: From T. W. Clarke   12 January 1876
letters.summary: Two photographs of T. W. Clarke, Jr, aged three, offered as examples of expression.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   13 January [1876]
letters.summary: Thanks FG for his report [on the statistical validity of CD’s experiments; seeCross and self-fertilisation, pp. 16–18]. Discusses FG’s comments, his own experiments, and the means by which the results may be analysed.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   13 January 1876
letters.summary:
Sends copy ofArabische Korallen[1876].

Comments on reception of his paper on "Gastrula" [see10012].

letters.title: From S. L. Lovén   [14 January 1876]
letters.summary: Has sent his paper onEchinoidea[see10373] as a token of his veneration. He tried to address the confusion in knowledge about the different parts of the exoskeleton of the Echinodermata by tracing certain relations of homology not previously noticed. Much more work is required.

letters.title: From T. B. Blow   15 January 1876
letters.summary: Reports on the tendency of the normally fruitlessConvolvulus arvensis, to form fruit when roots are cut and plant is in danger of dying.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   15 January [1876]
letters.summary: Thanks EH forArabische Korallen[1876].

letters.title: From H. B. Smyth   15 January 1876
letters.summary:
Reports an observation on his child’s behaviour;

claims to have captured two moths of different species in the act of copulating with each other.

letters.title: From A. S. von Mansfelde   17 January 1876
letters.summary: Proposes an unorthodox theory of generation that explains sex determination and atavism.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   21 January [1876]
letters.summary: EH’sArabische Korallenis spirited, clear, and poetical. With respect to formation of islands, thinks EH lays too much stress on views of Ehrenberg. Admires drawings.

letters.title: From M. T. Masters   24 January 1876
letters.summary: He is surveying the literature on the struggle for existence among pasture plants. Asks CD for the "many cases on record" of changed relations among plants under slightly changed conditions alluded to in theOrigin. [See M. T. Masters, J. B. Lawes and J. M. Gilbert "Agricultural, botanical, and chemical results of experiments on the mixed herbage of permanent meadow, conducted for more than twenty years in succession on the same land (pt 2, The botanical results)",Philos. Trans. R. Soc. Lond.173 (1883): 1181–413.]

letters.title: To Karl von Scherzer   24 January [1876]
letters.summary:
Thanks for KHvS’s book [La province de Smyrne(1873)].

Discusses possible meeting.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   24 January 1876
letters.summary: Are plants that arise from vegetative propagation individuals or merely parts of the original parent plant?

letters.title: From M. T. Masters   26 January 1876
letters.summary: In response to CD’s query, answers that he has frequently heard discussions at the Horticultural Society of a saccharine secretion from leaves of the lime and has no doubt it really does occur. [SeeCross and self-fertilisation, p. 402.]

letters.title: To James Torbitt   26 January 1876
letters.summary:
Obliged forBelfast Journal.

Almost impossible to determine what constitutes an individual. Definition for sexually reproducing organisms does not apply to lower ones.

letters.title: To Hubert Airy   27 January [1876?]
letters.summary: Agrees to aid HA in applying for membership in a society.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   28 January 1876
letters.summary:
Thanks for reviews ofInsectivorous plantsand ofClimbing plantsinNationandAmerican Journal Science[see10329].

AG’s essay on seed dispersal ["Burs in the borage family",Am. Nat.10 (1876): 1–4].

Preparing book on advantages of crossing [Cross and self-fertilisation].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   28 January 1876
letters.summary:
Asks CD to come up to vote for Lankester.

Severely critical of R. L. Tait’s paper onNepenthescommunicated to the Royal Society.

letters.title: To S. L. Lovén   28 January 1876
letters.summary: Thanks for SL’s [Études sur les echinoïdées(1875)]. Nothing could be more difficult than the homologies of this group.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin [before 29 January 1876?]
letters.summary: Purchases cigarettes for CD.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   29 January 1876
letters.summary:
Promises to vote for Lankester.

Acknowledges faults of R. L. Tait’s paper.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   31 January and 1 February 1876
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for comments onArabische Korallen[1876].

Comments onMonoenia darwinii[?] as a primitive sponge.

Discusses criticisms of CD’s theory by K. E. von Baer ["Über Darwin’s Lehre", inReden2 (1876): 235–480].

letters.title: From John Tyndall   2 February 1876
letters.summary:
Tells CD of his engagement to Louisa, eldest daughter of Lord Claud Hamilton.

His investigations [into spontaneous generation] continue. He will deal with Bastian’s work [The modes of origin of lowest organisms(1871)].

The medical journals see that the end of the nonsense they have so long countenanced is nigh.

letters.title: To ?   3 February 1876
letters.summary: Sends autograph.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   [4 February 1876]
letters.summary:
Congratulates WTT-D on [election of E. Ray Lankester to] Linnean Society.

Mentions visit to Royal Society.

Pleased to see George Bentham looking well.

letters.title: To John Tyndall   4 February 1876
letters.summary:
Sends congratulations and a teapot on the occasion of JT’s engagement.

Is pleased JT is not giving up on the spontaneous generation question. Feels strongly that subject will not be clear until it is understood how J. S. Burdon Sanderson and others succeeded in getting bacteria in infusions they had boiled for a long time.

letters.title: From John Tyndall   5 February 1876
letters.summary: JT will not quit the subject [of spontaneous generation] until light is let in on every cranny of the question.

letters.title: From John Tyndall   5 February 1876
letters.summary: The teapot is exquisite. Louisa says to say "the gift is worthy of the giver. Nothing higher can be said."

letters.title: To Eduard Koch?   6 February 1876
letters.summary: Discusses use by correspondent of clichés from one of his books.

letters.title: To J. B. Innes   7 February [1876]
letters.summary: Sends forms to be signed so that the trustees of the Down Friendly Society may be properly registered.

letters.title: To Società dei Naturalisti di Modena   8 February 1876
letters.summary: Thanks for his election as an Honorary Member

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   [9 February 1876]
letters.summary:
Has sent FM’s letter ontoNature["Brazil kitchen middens, habits of ants, etc.",Nature13 (1876): 304–5].

Would be grateful forCeropegiaseeds.

letters.title: To A. B. Buckley   11 February [1876]
letters.summary: Comments on her new book [A short history of natural science(1876)].

letters.title: To J. M. F. Ludlow   11 February 1876
letters.summary: Writes as a trustee of the Down Friendly Society regarding difficulties over the recording of the names of the trustees.

letters.title: To H. T. Stainton   11 February [1876]
letters.summary: Has signed enclosure [Royal Society nomination for McLachlan] with pleasure.

letters.title: To A. C. Thomson   11 February 1876
letters.summary: Writes regarding affairs of the Down Friendly Society.

letters.title: From A. B. Buckley   12 February 1876
letters.summary: Thanks CD for letter complimenting her book. Responds to his comments on botany and geology in book.

letters.title: From S. B. Herrick   12 February 1876
letters.summary: Inquires whether insectivorous habit in plants supplements or replaces the normal method of plant nutrition.

letters.title: From Charles and Francis Darwin to W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   14 February [1876]
letters.summary:
Asks for identification of aCinerariawhich is self-sterile.

Fritz Müller’s letter onCecropia[see10384].

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   14 February [1876]
letters.summary: Declines invitation to accompany JJW to Crystal Palace.

letters.title: To ?   15 February 1876
letters.summary: Thanks correspondent for present of book [unspecified].

letters.title: From B. J. Edwards & Co.   16 February 1876
letters.summary: Sends set of illustrations forExpressionmarked to show those that could be improved for a future edition.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   16 February 1876
letters.summary: Sends packets of seeds of peas of different sizes [i.e., weights] for CD’s experiments; identifies size of the seeds that produced them. FG is experimenting "in the same direction" and is curious how his results will compare with CD’s.

letters.title: To J. H. Gilbert   16 February 1876
letters.summary:
Describes self- and cross-fertilisation experiments.

Asks JHG’s advice on setting up an experiment designed to test whether the cause of variation in cultivated plants lies in different substances absorbed from the soil when absorption is not interfered with by other plants in a state of nature. Can JHG suggest how he can get soil free of all the substances which plants naturally absorb?

letters.title: From Hermann Müller   16 February 1876
letters.summary: Observations on hive- and humble-bees. Perforating habits differ in different individuals of the same species.

letters.title: From D. Appleton & Co.   18 February 1876
letters.summary:
Encloses statement of sales ofOrigin,Expression,Descent, andInsectivorous plantsto 1 Feb 1876.

Has charged against CD’s account half the cost of old plates from Judd forVariation. When will plates for new edition be sent?

Insectivorous plantsnot selling well because of general depression in business.

letters.title: To J. N. Lockyer   18 February [1876]
letters.summary: Asks that the copy ofNaturecontaining letter from Fritz Müller be forwarded to FM [see10324].

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   [18 February 1876]
letters.summary:
Has received seeds ofCecropia pellatafrom Kew.

Has asked Hermann Müller to send copy of FM’s paper as soon as published.

letters.title: From Charles and Francis Darwin to W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   18 February 1876
letters.summary:
Thanks for plants supplied from Kew.

On structure and function of leaf glands of certain plants.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   21 February 1876
letters.summary: Murray wishes to settle payments forDescent[2d ed., 11th thousand]. Over 500 copies of the 1000 printed have been sold.

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   21 February 1876
letters.summary:
RLT to review 2d ed. ofVariationand write an article on Pangenesis.

Discussion of "Survival of the Fittest".

letters.title: To Lawson Tait   22 February [1876]
letters.summary:
Herbert Spencer invented the term "survival of the fittest". CD used it but found "natural selection" more convenient.

He has often spoken of natural selection’s destruction of individuals which do not come up to "proper standards of structure", which comes to nearly the same thing as RLT’s suggested distinction.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   23 February 1876
letters.summary:
Sends cheque forDescent[2d ed., 1875 issue].

Has sent corrections to printer forClimbing plants

andOrigin. Has ordered to print: 1250 copies ofOrigin,

500 ofClimbing plants,

and 1000 ofNaturalist’s voyage[Journal of researches].

letters.title: From Arthur Nicols   24 February 1876
letters.summary: Is putting together a natural history book for intelligent children [The puzzle of life(1877)]; would like CD’s opinion on the project in general and on the completed first chapter in particular.

letters.title: To Arthur Nicols   [after 24 February 1876]
letters.summary: Supports AN’s idea [of a natural history book for children].

letters.title: To ?   25 February 1876
letters.summary: Sends his autograph.

letters.title: To Henry Edwards   1 March [1876]
letters.summary: Comments on paper by HE [see10328].

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   1 March 1876
letters.summary: Regrowth of an amputated extra thumb.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   2 March [1876]
letters.summary:
Sends signed enclosure.

FG will hear of germination of peas in a few days.

letters.title: To Lawson Tait   2 March 1876
letters.summary: Thanks RLT for his letter. CD took much trouble over his two cases [regrowth of amputated supernumerary digits, inVariation] but the evidence was shaky.

letters.title: From J. H. Gilbert   4 March 1876
letters.summary: Discusses in detail how to prepare for experimental purposes a soil that lacks nutrients.

letters.title: To S. B. Herrick   6 March 1876
letters.summary:
CD came to believeDroseradrew its nourishment from insects because it grows where no other plants survive. Doubts glands are modified stomata.

Suggests works by Grönland and Trécul.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   8 March [1876]
letters.summary: Sends some cash to help WED with moving expenses.

letters.title: To J. H. Gilbert   [before 9 March 1876]
letters.summary:
Thanks for advice concerning preparation of soil for experiments. Will order the salts. Asks about burning soil or washing it with acid.

Thanks for invitation. His son [Francis] would like to inspect JHG’s plots.

letters.title: From J. H. Gilbert   9 March 1876
letters.summary: Sends advice on preparing and washing soil in preparation for CD’s experiments.

letters.title: To E. A. Strasburger   9 March 1876
letters.summary: Thanks for EAS’s paper, translated from its original German,Sur la formation et la division des cellules(Strasburger 1876a).

letters.title: From Charles Layton   10 March 1876
letters.summary:
Encloses cheque for balance listed on accompanying statement of sales [see10401].

Stereo plates for new edition ofVariationhave been sent to New York.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   [c. 19 March 1876]
letters.summary: Thanks for copy of 2d ed. ofVariation.

letters.title: From J. G. Fenwick   17 March 1876
letters.summary:
Recounts family trait of excessive orderliness

and the behaviour of his dog.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   19 March 1876
letters.summary:
Insectivorous plantsis out

andClimbing plantsis at the printer’s.

He is now at work on the geological writings.

Thinks all of CD’s papers extremely interesting "for the spirit and the method".

Cites some misprints inClimbing plants.

letters.title: To J. G. Fenwick   19 March 1876
letters.summary: "The longer I live the more I come to believe in inheritance. I have some ""orderlings"" in my own composition, and I wish I had transmitted more of it to my own offspring."

letters.title: From J. C. E. Kollmann   19 March 1876
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for copy ofVariationin name of Anthropologische Gesellschaft, Munich.

Dr Born has demonstrated that all Batrachia and their relatives the Anura have six toes.

Sends short paper on intelligence of cephalopods ["Die Cephalopoden in der zoologischen Station des Dr Dohrn",Z. Wiss. Zool.26 (1876): 1–23].

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   21 March 1876
letters.summary:
Glad to hear that [German edition of]Insectivorous plantsis published.

Thanks for errata inClimbing plants[2d ed.].

Sends list [missing] of his papers, with those certainly not worth translating marked with a red line.

Reports on work in progress.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   21 March 1876
letters.summary: A difficulty with a passage inCoral reefsabout "vertical thickness", which JVC thinks should read "horizontal extent".

letters.title: To ? 21 March 1876
letters.summary: Thanks for sending the impressions of the gems, but, because CD is ignorant of archaeology, the recipient should not send one for inspection.

letters.title: To Ernst von Hesse-Wartegg   22 March 1876
letters.summary:
All who battle in the cause of evolution do good service.

Has no questions about the natural history of Bermuda.

letters.title: From H. C. Sorby   22 March 1876
letters.summary: Discusses chemical tests for the detection of glucose and cane-sugar in solution.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   23 March 1876
letters.summary: Clarifies a passage [inCoral reefs, 2d ed. (1874)], which JVC had questioned.

letters.title: To Lawson Tait   25 March [1876]
letters.summary:
RLT’s two articles inSpectator[4 Mar and 25 Mar 1876] greatly honour CD.

Tait has made a good point about "Survival of the Fittest".

Dr Rudinger’s extensive inquiries show that all eminent German surgeons are unanimous about non-growth of extra digit after amputation.

J. Kollmann has written regretting CD has given up atavism and extra digits [in 2d ed. ofVariation]; gives new evidence of a rudimentary sixth digit in batrachians.

letters.title: From Naphtali Lewy   [26 March – 24 April 1876]
letters.summary: NL has written an essayToldot adam(Lewy 1874, privately printed in book form as Lewy [1875]) to convince his people of the truth of CD’s theory.

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   26 March [1876]
letters.summary: Cat born tailless as a consequence of a spina bifida.

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   27 March [1876]
letters.summary: Regrowth of amputated digits is a capacity possessed by the new-born but rapidly lost.

letters.title: From Robert Bell   28 March 1876
letters.summary: Encloses letter printed in theToronto Globeabout the discovery on Prince Edward Island of a skeleton of a tailed man.

letters.title: To Axel Blytt   28 March 1876
letters.summary: Thanks AB for his paper on the Norwegian flora ["Forsög til en Theori om Invandringen af Norges Flora",Nyt Mag. Naturvidensk.21 (1876): 279–362]. Appears to CD to be the most important contribution towards understanding the present distribution of plants since Edward Forbes’s essay on the effects of the glacial period ["On the connexion between the distribution of existing fauna and flora of the British Isles and the geological changes which have affected their area",Mem. Geol. Surv. Engl. & Wales1 (1846): 336–432].

letters.title: From F. J. Cohn   28 March 1876
letters.summary: Has had doctoral student [Alexander Fraustadt] working on the physiology and chemistry (i.e., chlorophyll and starch distribution) and comparative anatomy ofDionaea.

letters.title: To Lawson Tait   28 March 1876
letters.summary: James Paget’s scepticism about regrowth of digits. Suggests RLT experiment with amputation of digits, both extra and normal, of kittens and fowls. Fears they will fail to regrow, but, if regrowth is proved, it will be an important discovery.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [after 28 March 1876]
letters.summary:
Personal news – is unwell.

Mentions "Twin-papers" ["Short notes on heredity, etc., in twins",J. Anthropol. Inst.5 (1876): 324–9] sent by Galton.

letters.title: To F. J. Cohn   31 March [1876]
letters.summary:
Thanks FJC for paper by Alexander Fraustadt ["Vegetative Organe vonDionaea",Ell. Beitr. Biol. Pfl.2 (1877): 27–64].

Mentions paper by A. W. Bennett ["Glands of carnivorous plants",Mon. Microsc. J.15 (1876): 1–5].

letters.title: From James Torbitt   1 April 1876
letters.summary:
Thanks for response to query on what is an individual.

Sends paper on potatoes [see10440].

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   3 April 1876
letters.summary:
A Dr Sarazin offers services as translator.

Will read CD’s letter about Robert Swinhoe to Royal Society Council and see what can be done for him.

letters.title: From Mary Treat   3 April 1876
letters.summary:
EnclosesPinguiculaspecimens.

Believes she has found a new species of water-lily.

letters.title: To James Torbitt   4 April 1876
letters.summary:
Thanks for essay [Cras credemus: a treatise on the cultivation of the potato from the seed, having for proposed results the extinction of the disease(1876)] and seeds. Thinks principle on which JT is acting is right.

Cannot allow publication of his earlier letter [10368], as he cannot recall what he wrote.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   6 April 1876
letters.summary: Requests permission to publish CD’s previous letter [10440].

letters.title: To James Torbitt   6 April 1876
letters.summary: JT may publish CD’s letter.

letters.title: To D. F. Nevill   6 April [1876 or later]
letters.summary:
ReceivedDarlingtonia; cannot explain its fructification.

Declines invitation.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   7 April 1876
letters.summary:
Believes publishing CD’s letter will enable JT to suppress the potato disease several years sooner.

Returns CD’s answer to JT’s question "What is an individual?", and repeats his request for permission to publish it.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   8 April 1876
letters.summary: Requests CD’s evaluation of the work of the entomologist Robert McLachlan, who is up for F.R.S. in competition with the physiologist A. H. Garrod.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   9 April [1876]
letters.summary: McLachlan has as strong a claim to be F.R.S. as any entomologist, but Garrod’s work is of higher quality.

letters.title: To James Torbitt   10 April [1876]
letters.summary: JT may publish enclosed [letter by CD?], but it is not worth publication.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   11 April 1876
letters.summary: Lists the 14 men elected to be F.R.S. Garrod defeated McLachlan.

letters.title: To Henry Bradshaw   12 April [1876]
letters.summary: Thanks HB for obtaining a translation by a learned rabbi of [the Naphtali Lewy] letter – "a real curiosity". [See10430.]

letters.title: From James Torbitt   12 April 1876
letters.summary:
JT still thinks CD’s opinions on "what is an individual?" should be published.

Seeking financial backing for his research.

letters.title: To Robert Bell   14 April [1876]
letters.summary:
Suspects that the reported skeleton of a tailed man is that of some distinct animal [see10432].

Amused by brief visit of strange man about whom RB had written.

Hopes that geology continues to flourish in Canada.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   14 April 1876
letters.summary:
Mentions receiving GJR’s paper on Medusae [J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Zool.)12 (1876): 524–31].

Will call on GJR in London.

letters.title: From G. G. Stokes   14 April 1876
letters.deprecated: George Gabriel Stokes, 1st baronetSecretary, Royal Society
letters.sender: George Gabriel Stokes, 1st baronetSecretary, Royal Society
letters.summary: The Royal Society have not accepted R. L. Tait’s paper on insectivorous plants; it will be returned to CD, who submitted it.

letters.title: To James Torbitt   14 April 1876
letters.summary: Gives advice on breeding of blight-resistant potatoes.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   16 April 1876
letters.summary: Queries about some references inCoral reefsand a list of misprints.

letters.title: From Hermann Brehmer   17 April 1876
letters.summary:
Discusses geographic distribution of tuberculosis and possible explanations for disease-free areas and populations.

Does not think a local population with some distinct physiological character can properly be designated as a race. Thinks local conditions, not natural selection, responsible for such characters. Ernst Haeckel agrees. Asks CD’s opinion.

letters.title: From P. M. G. Egerton   17 April 1876
letters.deprecated: Philip de Malpas Grey- Egerton, 10th baronet Egerton
letters.sender: Philip de Malpas Grey- Egerton, 10th baronet Egerton
letters.summary: F. S. Holmes is welcome to examine his fish vertebrae.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [18 April 1876]
letters.summary: JDH has heard from Asa Gray, who approves of the botany primer [Botany(1876)].

letters.title: From James Torbitt   18 April 1876
letters.summary: Sends some potato plants and tubers.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   19 April [1876]
letters.summary: Daughter Henrietta’s illness prevents a trip to London.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   19 April 1876
letters.summary: JT’s crossing experiments on potatoes. Attempts to develop resistance toPeronospora.

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   20 April [1876]
letters.summary: Asks for information he needs for the German translation [ofCoral reefs], including correct titles of reference books and the name of a voyager.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   20 April [1876]
letters.summary: Sends a pamphlet for FD and Ruck, who did not turn up for breakfast.

letters.title: To Smith, Elder & Co.   20 April [1876]
letters.summary: J. V. Carus wishes to translateVolcanic islandsandSouth Americainto German. Can Smith and Elder provide copies?

letters.title: To C. S. Wedgwood   20 April 1876
letters.summary: Grieves over poor account of her health. Emma and Henrietta are also ill.

letters.title: To G. G. Stokes   21 April [1876]
letters.summary: The Society’s rejection of R. L. Tait’s paper onNepenthesis a lesson which will last CD for his life. It is clear that he should not have sent it.

letters.title: To James Torbitt   21 April 1876
letters.summary:
Does not think that publishing his letters as advertisement [for potato experiments] would help JT’s cause, so CD cannot give permission.

Regrets that he has neither the time nor health to undertake crossing experiments with JT’s specimens. Discusses crossing varieties.

letters.title: To Mary Treat   21 April [1876]
letters.summary:
Congratulations on finding water-lily.

Thanks forPinguiculaspecimens.

Asks for reference to her article onUtricularia[see10508].

letters.title: To Bartholomäus von Carneri   22 April 1876
letters.summary: Is obliged for Carneri’s new work,Eine psychologische Studie.

letters.title: To T. C. Eyton   22 April 1876
letters.summary:
Fondly remembers the days he spent with TCE.

Doubts the Canadian skeleton will have anything to do with man.

Returns extracts.

Samuel Haughton is a bitter opponent.

CD now working on plants;

doubts he will ever return to working on man.

letters.title: To Smith, Elder & Co.   22 April 1876
letters.summary: Discussing a reprint ofSouth America.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   22 April 1876
letters.summary: Thanks for CD’s assistance and his advice on crossing.

letters.title: From Heinrich Goldschmidt and E. v. Portheim   23 April 1876
letters.deprecated: Heinrich Jacob (Heinrich) GoldschmidtEduard Porges von Portheim
letters.sender: Heinrich Jacob (Heinrich) GoldschmidtEduard Porges von Portheim
letters.summary: Two student adherents of his theory correct an error inInsectivorous plants.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   24 April 1876
letters.summary:
Answers queries concerning errata inCoral reefs.

All copies ofVolcanic islandsare sold. Smith, Elder & Co. want to bring out a new edition, but CD is resolved not to look at a single proof.

letters.title: From W. H. Patterson   24 April 1876
letters.summary: Observations on expression and variation in cats.

letters.title: To Lawson Tait   24 April 1876
letters.summary: The Royal Society have returned RLT’sNepenthespaper and will not have it read because of unfavourable reports from referees.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   25 April 1876
letters.summary: Is elated by his work on the alteration in the earth’s axis and the displacement of the poles. [See10689.]

letters.title: To Federico Delpino   25 April 1876
letters.summary: Thanks FD for the volumes ofRevista Botanica[1874–5].

letters.title: To G. C. Druce   25 April 1876
letters.summary: Thanks Naturalist Society and Club of Northampton for his election.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   25 April [1876]
letters.summary: CD preparing new English and German editions of his early geology [of the voyage of theBeagle] books. Asks for Hooker’s copies as he no longer has his own.

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   25 April [1876]
letters.summary: Apologises for placing CD in the objectionable position of sponsor for a rejected paper. RLT has gone over old ground in ignorance.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   [before 26 April 1876]
letters.summary: Asks to show GJR’s letter to George Darwin and other sons. A secret cannot be well kept.

letters.title: To J. E. Harting   26 April 1876
letters.summary: Thanks for the offer of JEH’s manuscript notes, but he is not planning to work on the subject again.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   26 April 1876
letters.summary: Forwards copies of CD’s geology books.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   26 April [1876]
letters.summary: Trip to London delayed.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   26 April [1876]
letters.summary: Asks for titles of papers on structure ofNepenthesfor use by R. L. Tait. Mentions paper by RLT.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   27 April [1876]
letters.summary: SendsMind. Henry Sidgwick’s article ["The theory of evolution in its application to practice",Mind1 (1876): 52–67] is so clear it makes CD feel "a muddle-headed man". But he disagrees with Sidgwick on the origin of morality within tribes.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   27 April [1876]
letters.summary: Is sure mathematical discussion of elevation of continents will be valued by geologists.

letters.title: To Edward Frankland   27 April [1876]
letters.summary: Requests permission to call upon EF any morning from Saturday through Tuesday.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   27 April [1876]
letters.summary: Will call tomorrow morning.

letters.title: To Enrique Godínez   28 April 1876
letters.summary: Gives permission for a Spanish translation of theOriginand wishes it success.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   29 April [1876]
letters.summary: Congratulates GJR on lecture ["The physiology of the nervous system ofMedusa",Not. Proc. R. Inst. G. B.8 (1875–8): 166–77].

letters.title: To Lawson Tait   29 April [1876]
letters.summary:
Sends Thiselton-Dyer’s suggestions for references toNepenthes,

and gives his opinion on what will influence the Royal Society’s Council in considering RLT’s candidacy.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   29 April [1876]
letters.summary: Thanks for references for R. L. Tait.

letters.title: To J. S. Burdon Sanderson   30 April [1876]
letters.summary: Suggests JSBS’s new machine for observing arterial action be used to test CD’s hypothesis that blushing is caused by thinking intensely about a part of the body and thus releasing the arteries.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [30 April 1876]
letters.summary: CD has just had an interview with Edward Frankland, who "almost laughs" at FD’s idea of getting potash and soda out of the soil by treating it with sulphuric acid. Asks FD to send him a soil sample to give to Frankland. Sends enclosures giving address and labels for soil samples.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [1 May 1876]
letters.summary: Good news about Frankland. Expecting burnt earth. Almost finished the Foodbodies Paper on Acacia. He and Amy are learning to use the new printing machine.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [1 May 1876]
letters.summary:
Expresses his pride in FD, whose article ["On the structure of the snail’s heart",J. Anat. Physiol.10 (1876): 506–10] was highly praised by G. H. Lewes.

Lewes has also been quoting FD’s letter inNature[13 (1876): 384–5] on pycrotoxine in relation to the vivisection controversy.

Was introduced to James Sully, author of the article inMindon Wilhelm Wundt ["Physiological psychology in Germany", 1 (1876): 20–43]

andSensation and intuition(1874) [see10320], by "Mrs Lewes" (George Eliot).

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   1 May 1876
letters.summary: Writes of his "geo-mathematical" work.

letters.title: From Smith, Elder & Co.   1 May 1876
letters.summary: Informs CD which woodblocks of illustrations to theGeology of "Beagle"are in their possession and which are missing.

letters.title: From Hubert Airy   2 May 1876
letters.summary:
On his new paper for Royal Society on a point of leaf arrangement. Asks CD to communicate it and "gives some details of its contents", e.g., recorded observations of changing leaf-order on individual specimens.

Comments on a paper by George Henslow ["Helianthus tuberosus",Trans. Linn. Soc. Lond.26 (1876): 647].

letters.title: To C. F. Claus   2 May 1876
letters.summary: Thanks CC for dedication [of hisGrundlage des Crustaceen-Systems(1876)]. Congratulates CC on completion of work.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   2 May 1876
letters.summary: Has read letter from Jemmy. Amy has been practicing on the printing machine. Fritz has come back from the Vicar of Orpington.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   2 May [1876]
letters.summary: Comments on the reaction of geologists to GHD’s work on elevation of continents.

letters.title: From Thomas Laxton   2 May 1876
letters.summary: Responds to CD’s query as to the duration of crossed varieties of peas. [SeeCross and self-fertilisation, p. 305.]

letters.title: To Edward Frankland 3 May 1876
letters.summary: His samples of earth have been sent for analysis. EF has saved CD and his son from wasted experimenting.

letters.title: To A. W. von Hofmann   3 May 1876
letters.summary: Thanks AWvH for his work on Justus Liebig [The life-work of Liebig(1876)].

letters.title: From Hermann Brehmer   4 May 1876
letters.summary: Encloses article on local immunity to tuberculosis. Has he interpreted CD’s views correctly? Believes the immunity notable in areas like Iceland or mountain areas is due to local conditions, not natural selection. Describes his sanatorium in mountains of Silesia and medical criticism of his work.

letters.title: To the Geological Society of London   5 May 1876
letters.summary: Asking to borrow three wood blocks.

letters.title: To Lawson Tait   5 May 1876
letters.summary: CD sends the gist of an extremely negative report from the [Royal Society’s] physiological referee on the value of RLT’s modifications of Brücke’s process for isolating pepsin [see10470].

letters.title: From Giovanni Canestrini   6 May 1876
letters.summary:
Two parts of the second edition of the Italian translation ofVariationare already out.

Expressionwill soon follow [published in 1878].

The publisher [Unione] asks CD to give him the right of Italian translations of his works.

letters.title: ToNature   6 May [1876]
letters.summary: Reports seeing flowers of wild cherry bitten off in same manner as primroses [see9418and9444]. In this case it was done by a squirrel, though birds also bite the flowers of the cherry-tree.
