letters.title: From Moritz Schiff   8 May 1876
letters.summary:
Has repeated his observations and experiments used inInsectivorous plants; finds them sound.

Revises his reference to production of pepsin.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   9 May 1876
letters.summary:
SendsDie Perigenesis der Plastidule[1876]. Comments on CD’s theory of Pangenesis. Explains his own theory of Perigenesis.

Returns Webb and Berthelot,Îles Canaries; Géographie botanique[1840].

Describes work on 3d ed. ofAnthropogenie.

letters.title: To Auguste Daubrée   10 May 1876
letters.summary: Thanks AD for sending a memoir on foliation of rocks ["Expériences sur la schistosité des roches",C. R. Hebd. Acad. Sci.82 (1876): 710–16, 798–804]. Regrets to say that it never reached him.

letters.title: From James Murphy   10 May 1876
letters.summary:
A reader ofDescentoffers two items: 1. Masters observed a pericardial fold in humans and other mammals which is a vestigial left superior vena cava;

2. JM suggests the frenum of the human penis became necessary forvis-à-viscopulation when man became bipedal.

letters.title: To Otto Zacharias   10 May 1876
letters.summary: Promises to send sheets of his new book [Cross and self-fertilisation].

letters.title: To Auguste Daubrée?   13 May [1876]
letters.summary: AD’s memoir [see10504] has arrived at last.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   14 May 1876
letters.summary:
Book [Webb and Berthelot] has reached CD.

Sorry EH dissents from Pangenesis.

letters.title: To Smith, Elder & Co.   15 May 1876
letters.summary: Discusses corrections and illustrations [forVolcanic islands and parts of South America, 2d ed. (1876)].

letters.title: From Mary Treat   15 May 1876
letters.summary:
Sends her article onUtricularia["Is the valve ofUtriculariasensitive?",Harper’s New Mon. Mag.52 (1875): 382–7].

Proposes to write onSarracenia["Carnivorous plants of Florida",Harper’s New Mon. Mag.53 (1876): 546–8, 710–14].

letters.title: From Ebenezer Norman   18 May 1876
letters.summary: Sends his copies of CD’s MS ofCross and self-fertilisationand calls attention to errors in addition.

letters.title: From Federico Delpino   19 May 1876
letters.summary:
Has become Professor of Botany at Genoa.

Offers to send his paper on the necessity of out-crossing.

letters.title: To ?   19 May 1876
letters.summary: Sends his autograph.

letters.title: From Louis Grenier   20 May 1876
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for his authorisation for the résumé which LG will read to the Société Botanique de Lyon.

Insectivorous plantshas made a sensation in France. Some are for, some against. Some doubt that a plant could absorb and assimilate the matter dissolved by the secretions. Asks CD if N. B. Ward’s method of culture might be used to answer the question definitively.

letters.title: From F. B. Zincke   23 [May 1876]
letters.summary: On communication noises used by domestic poultry.

letters.title: From William Jackson   [24–8?] May [1876?]
letters.summary: CD’s servant submits estimate for work to be done on pantry.

letters.title: To D. J. Wetterhan   25 May [1876]
letters.summary:
Thanks for letter of 21st.

When the curiousSalviaarrives, CD will have it carefully planted. Interested in seeing its flowers.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   26 May [1876]
letters.summary:
Caroline [Wedgwood] has been ill for the last 20 months.

James Paget to be consulted about William Darwin’s brain concussion.

letters.title: To F. B. Zincke   26 May [1876]
letters.summary: Thanks for a letter describing variation in chickens.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   27 May 1876
letters.summary: Has had a cold. Salvia hasn't come yet. Will look for orchids tomorrow. Will send off bull's-horn acacia on Monday or Tuesday.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [28 May 1876]
letters.summary: Reports his discovery of the behaviour of protoplasm in teasel cells.

letters.title: To H. E. Wedgwood   [28 May 1876]
letters.summary:
Asks her to send seeds from a flower in the garden at Hopedene, and the name of a dwarf crimsonOxalis.

Expresses appreciation of the house, which the Darwins have borrowed.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [29 May 1876]
letters.summary:
The Salvia has arrived.

Has found several fly orchids coming in flower, but no Cephalanthera or Musk.

Cannot do any teazel work.

Anthelme Thozet has sent him a lot of Ophideres.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   29 May [1876]
letters.summary:
Encloses essay by Haeckel criticising Pangenesis [Die Perigenesis der Plastidule(1876)]. Discusses Haeckel’s theory of inheritance.

Asks about the Physiological Society.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   30 [May 1876]
letters.summary: Discusses FD’s observations on the protrusion of protoplasmic masses by cells of the teasel. Suggests analogy with amoeba. "I would work at this subject if I were you, to the point of death."

letters.title: From James Paget   30 May 1876
letters.summary: Instructs CD that his son [William] should take a holiday following his concussion.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [31 May 1876]
letters.summary: Has sent off Bulls Horn to Kew; has sent hamper to CD; is preparing drawings for his presentation at the Linnean Society; asks after William, and hopes to be able to come to visit.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   31 May 1876
letters.summary:
His paper on the alterations of the poles and changes in level of continents is in shape.

Sends Cambridge news.

letters.title: To P. P. C. Hoek   [after May 1876]
letters.summary: Thanks for PPCH’s ["Entwicklungsgeschichte der Entomostraken, pt 1: Embryologie von Balanus",Niederl. Arch. Zool.3 (1876–7): 47–82].

letters.title: To William Bowman   1 June [1876]
letters.summary:
Regrets he cannot hear lecture by F. C. Donders.

Hopes to see WB before he returns home.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [1 June 1876]
letters.summary: Has examined sections of teasel in putrid meat infusion and ammonia.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [1 June 1876]
letters.summary: Comments on FD’s discovery – "if it so proves". It will be important to see whether the protoplasm oozes through the cell-walls [ofDipsacus] or whether it can be withdrawn.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   1 June 1876
letters.summary: Greatly excited by the astronomical implications of his work.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   1 June 1876
letters.summary:
Anticipates reading Haeckel’sPerigenesis der Plastidule[1876].

Physiologists will think vivisection bill stringent.

Honorary memberships of Physiological Society created expressly to honour CD.

Working hard at jellyfish just now. Needs snake poison.

letters.title: To Mary Treat   1 June 1876
letters.summary: Thanks MT for her article ["Is the valve ofUtriculariasensitive?",Harper’s New Mon. Mag.52 (1875): 382–7]. Does not understand why he failed to detect movement [inUtricularia], but it appears from her observations that the valve is sensitive.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [2 June 1876]
letters.summary: Looks to FD’s "grand discovery" as almost certain. Suggests observations.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [2 June 1876]
letters.summary: Has got a dodge to see protoplasm inDroserain dead state. Comes to Hopedene with Amy tomorrow. his paper went off well.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   2 June [1876]
letters.summary:
Further comments on GHD’s work on the influence of geological changes on the earth’s axis.

Frank [Francis Darwin] has made a fine zoological discovery.

letters.title: To Georg von Giźycki   2 June [1876]
letters.summary: Thanks for essay [Philosophische Consequenzen der Lamarck–Darwin’schen Entwicklungstheorie(1876)].

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   [4 June 1876]
letters.summary: Is determined not to believe in GHD’s astronomical work until J. C. Adams accepts it, for he would be so disappointed if it breaks down.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   4 June [1876]
letters.summary:
Joseph Fayrer can supply cobra poison.

Discusses vivisection.

Mentions visit to the John Hawkshaws.

letters.title: From J. H. Kidder   5 June 1876
letters.summary: Sends his papers ["Contributions to the natural history of Kerguelen Island",U. S. Nat. Mus. Bull.1, nos. 2, 3 (1876)], which are inspired byJournal of researches.

letters.title: To John Tyndall   5 June [1876]
letters.summary: CD has quite given up the marine theory [of Glen Roy] and has accepted glacier lakes. "Nothing makes me gnash my teeth so much as that confounded paper of mine." It is a lesson "never in science to infer one explanation is right because no other one seems possible".

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   5 June 1876
letters.summary: Response to ARW’s "grand and memorable work" [Geographical distribution(1876)]. Most interesting part to CD is ARW’s "protest against sinking imaginary continents".

letters.title: To Edward Frankland   [before 6 June 1876]
letters.summary: Requests chemical analysis of sample of both natural and burnt soil.

letters.title: From Edward Frankland   [before 6 June 1876]
letters.summary: Sends analysis of burnt and unburnt samples.

letters.title: To Edward Frankland   6 June [1876]
letters.summary: Gratitude for the invaluable assistance. Is disappointed that natural soil is richer than burnt. Problem of securing sufficient chemically pure soil to test growth of plants.

letters.title: From W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   6 June 1876
letters.summary: References to figures ofCoryanthes.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   7 June 1876
letters.summary:
Comments on CD’s criticism ofGeographical distribution.

Plans to sell his house.

letters.title: To S. A. Cecil   8 June 1876
letters.deprecated: Sackville Arthur Cecil, Lord Sackville Arthur Cecil
letters.recipient: Sackville Arthur Cecil, Lord Sackville Arthur Cecil
letters.summary: Thanks for kindness in organising special train for Caroline Sarah Wedgwood when she was taken ill.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   11 June [1876]
letters.summary:
Delighted to hear of Frank Darwin’s discovery.

Seems hopeless to reason with people about vivisection.

letters.title: To ?   13 June 1876
letters.summary: CD thanks the editor of a picture book "for … the photographs of your striking pictures, & for the honour which you have done me by the introduction of my name and likeness into one of them".

letters.title: To ?   13 June 1876
letters.summary: Thanks for his interesting essay on insectivorous plants.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   [15 June 1876 or later]
letters.summary: Describes discovery by his son [Francis Darwin] of protoplasmic filaments extending from small glands in the leaves ofDipsacus[seeProc. R. Soc. Lond.26 (1877): 4–8].

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   17 June 1876
letters.summary:
Further detailed comments onGeographical distribution.

Base treatment [of George Darwin] by Mivart inQuarterly Review[137 (1874): 40–77].

letters.title: To August Weismann   [17 June 1876 or later]
letters.summary:
Comments on Weismann’s remarks on the possibility of sexual selection in the genusDaphnia.

A. R. Wallace has published paper giving up sexual selection [Review of St George Jackson Mivart’sLessons from nature, as manifested in mind and matter.] inAcademy, 10 and 17 June 1876, pp. 587–8.]

letters.title: To Auguste Forel   19 June 1876
letters.summary: Asks how the Coleoptera that inhabit the nests of ants colonise a new nest. Wallace has suggested their ova become attached to winged female ants.

letters.title: To James Orton   19 June 1876
letters.summary: Obliged for the new edition ofThe Andes.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   20 June 1876
letters.summary: Comments on an address by William Thomson (‘On the rigidity of the earth’?), which is about the same problem that GHD is working on. Is confident Thomson has overlooked some points.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   20 June 1876
letters.summary:
JDH’s suggested text for Lyell’s tablet in Westminster Abbey.

Vigner[?] separates digestive principle fromNepenthes, disproving R. L. Tait.

letters.title: To Andrew Clark   [late June 1876]
letters.summary: Wishes to arrange for William Darwin to see AC. William has suffered a concussion.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   21 June [1876]
letters.summary:
CD and family suggest inscriptions for Lyell memorial at Westminster Abbey.

CD communicating H. Airy’s paper on phyllotaxis to the Royal Society.

Frank observes pod-like emanations from glands of insectivorous plant ingesting solid insect particles [see10520].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   22 June [1876]
letters.summary: Returns Mrs Lyell’s versions of Lyell memorial inscription. Disapproves of religious tone.

letters.title: From Auguste Forel   23 June 1876
letters.summary: Coleoptera inhabiting ants’ nests. Means of colonisation of new nests.

letters.title: To the editor ofThe Times   23 June 1876
letters.summary: Forwards for publication an article by Dr Richardson [apparently not published] showing the necessity of experiments on living animals. Hopes it will make women, "who from the tenderness of their hearts and from their profound ignorance are the most vehement opponents of all such experiments", pause.

letters.title: From Bruno Schreiber   24 June 1876
letters.summary: Describes cosmological ideas of Christian Radenhausen.

letters.title: To Bruno Schreiber   [after 24 June 1876]
letters.summary: Doubts Christian Radenhausen’s cosmological views are based on fact.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   25 June 1876
letters.summary: Has finishedGeographical distribution; sends his comments.

letters.title: To John Scott   1 July 1876
letters.summary:
CD has read the two reports on culture of poppies with interest and has planted seeds.

Suggests an experiment for evidence on whether plants, thought merely varieties, are like species and fail to intercross, despite insect pollination.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   4 July 1876
letters.summary:
JDH hopes Thiselton-Dyer does not discourage Frank’s investigation of insectivorous plants.

Preparing new editions of botany text-books.

His marriage is set for August.

letters.title: From C. F. Martins   5 July 1876
letters.summary:
Richard Gordon’s French translation ofClimbing plants[1877] is half printed.

In Martins’ Introduction to [Éd. Barbier’s translation of]Insectivorous plants[1877] he wants to include a complete bibliography of CD’s works: their extent is not generally known in France.

letters.title: To Edmund Gurney   8 July 1876
letters.summary: Read EG’s article ["Some disputed points in music",Fortn. Rev.n.s. 20 (1876): 106–30]. Diversity of musical taste in man indicates that it is acquired during individuals’ lives. The origin of the "sense of sublimity".

letters.title: To C. F. Claus   9 July 1876
letters.summary: Thanks for copy of Claus’s book,Untersuchungen zur Erforschung der genealogischen Grundlage des Crustaceen-Systems: ein Beitrag zur Descendenzlehre(Studies on the investigation of the genealogical foundation of the Crustacea: a contribution to the theory of descent; Claus 1876).

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   13 July [1876]
letters.summary:
All rejoice that J. C. Adams thinks well of GHD’s work and will present his paper to the Royal Society.

Gives news of his other sons.

letters.title: To Jean-Baptiste Liagre   18 July 1876
letters.summary: Acknowledges receipt of publications of the Académie Royale de Belgique.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin  [before 22 July 1876]
letters.summary: Asks FD to write on his behalf and say that he is unwilling to join a deputation [on vivisection] and that he believes in the need to protect physiology as well as lower animals.

letters.title: To William Ogle   22 July [1876]
letters.summary: Would like to cite WO’s case of bees perforating white but not blue monkshood (Aconitum napellus) in his next book [Cross and self-fertilisation, pp. 427–8]. Believes it is probably sterile if insects are excluded.

letters.title: From William Ogle   23 July 1876
letters.summary: Recounts his observations on the different ways bees perforate flowers of white and blue varieties of monkshood. [SeeCross and self-fertilisation, p 428.]

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   23 July 1876
letters.summary: Responds to CD’s comments and criticism ofGeographical distribution.

letters.title: From Wilhelm Breitenbach   26 July 1876
letters.summary:
Observations on pollinia ofOrchis maculata

and onPrimula elatior. [On latter, seeForms of flowers, p. 34.]

letters.title: From Casimir de Candolle   30 July 1876
letters.summary:
Experimenting on climbing plants.

Has no further information onDionaea.

letters.title: To August Müller Beeck   31 July [1876]
letters.summary: CD refuses to send AMB a copy of one of his works. "I did think your request unreasonable, as I have to give from 50 to 100 copies of all my books to those who aid me.––"

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   3 August 1876
letters.summary: Requests orchid specimens for experiment.

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   4 August [1876]
letters.summary:
Wishes to make CD an Honorary Member of the Birmingham Natural History Society.

RLT has attempted [in a paper] to apply evolution to moral life.

letters.title: To Lawson Tait   6 August 1876
letters.summary:
CD accepts membership in the Birmingham Natural History Society.

Thanks RLT for article. CD cannot quite agree that "under a theological point of view, the origin of evil is explained by survival".

Is glad RLT has not given up polydactylism.

letters.title: To Hermann Müller   7 August 1876
letters.summary: Comments on Fritz Müller’s article onHedychium.

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   8 August 1876
letters.summary: Proposes to work on the origin of diseases; is going to study syphilis.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   8 August [1876]
letters.summary: Thanks for WTT-D’s kindness about the orchids.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   9 August 1876
letters.summary:
AG’sDarwiniana[1876].

Cross and self-fertilisationhas now gone to press.

Is preparing new edition ofOrchids.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   10 August 1876
letters.summary:
Asa Gray’s directed variation would make natural selection superfluous.

CD has read new theological reconciliations of Darwinism and religion.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   12 August 1876
letters.summary:
Glad EH is coming to England.

Will be visiting eldest son in Southampton in September [but visit apparently delayed until 7 Oct, see "Journal"].

letters.title: To Gaston de Saporta   12 August 1876
letters.deprecated: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.recipient: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.summary: Thanks GdeS for hisRecherches sur les végétaux fossiles[1876].

letters.title: To John Lubbock   16 August [1876]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Glad to have heard JL’s admirable speech read aloud.

letters.title: To R. D. Fitzgerald   18 August [1876]
letters.summary: Thanks for RDF’sAustralian orchids[1874]. It comes just as CD’sOrchids[2d ed.] is going to press.

letters.title: From Milan Radovanović   18 August 1876
letters.summary:
Sends Serbian edition of Ernst Haeckel’sNatürliche Schöpfungsgeschichtetranslated by his late brother.

Serbian edition ofOrigin, translated by MMR, not yet published because of war with Turks.

letters.title: From George Rolleston   18 August 1876
letters.summary:
Sends three of his anthropological papers.

CD understates his case when he says the mandibular wattle of the "Irish greyhound pig" has no analogue or homologue.

letters.title: To Smith, Elder & Co.   21 August [1876]
letters.summary: Asks for tougher paper to be used for maps inCoral reefs, 2d ed.

letters.title: To George Rolleston   24 August [1876]
letters.summary:
Thanks GR for his notes and essays [see10581].

Similar appendages to those GR mentions [see10581] appear on the necks of goats, but the idea of reversion to a common progenitor of goats and pigs "stumps" CD.

letters.title: To Milan Radovanović   25 August [1876]
letters.summary:
His thanks for the present of Haeckel’s work.

He will be much gratified to have MMR translateOriginif the state of his country permits. [See10580.]

letters.title: To Bibliographisches Institut   28 August 1876
letters.summary: Thanks for A. E. Brehm’sThierleben[2d ed. (1876)].

letters.title: From J. A. Ransome-Marriott  1 September 1876
letters.summary: Reports on rats that gnawed holes in lead pipes.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   1 September 1876
letters.summary: Thanks forCatasetumand other specimens.

letters.title: From Gaston de Saporta   2 September 1876
letters.deprecated: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.sender: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.summary: Claims to have proved the great antiquity of several plant races. But this does not contradict the tendency to vary. Insists that heredity can make permanent varieties of sufficient duration to occur as fossils.

letters.title: From P. A. Hanaford   3 September 1876
letters.summary:
PAH’s friend, a florist, is repeating CD’s experiments withDionaea muscipula.

CD’s works stir interest in America.

letters.title: From Hermann Müller   4 September 1876
letters.summary:
Bombus mastrucatus, an alpine bee, conforms to his observations thatB. terrestrisbreaks open the flowers ofTrifolium pratense. However, in the Alps,B. terrestrisdoes not behave this way.

Gentianaspecies are adapted to lepidopteran cross-fertilisation.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   [after 4 September 1876]
letters.summary:
Has received a baffling article on God, immortality, and socialism under a Darwinian point of view.

Clerk Maxwell has disagreed with CD on molecular calculations in relation to Pangenesis inEncyclopaedia Britannicaarticle ["Atom",Encyclopaedia Britannica, 9th ed. (1875) 3: 36–49].

letters.title: To G. S. Ffinden   5 September 1876
letters.summary: Sends £25 subscription, though he is not a churchman.

letters.title: To John Price   8 September [1876–80?]
letters.summary:
Kind of JP to send notes on horses, but will not write on subject again.

Erasmus Darwin has not left his house for three years.

letters.title: To Gaston de Saporta   10 September 1876
letters.deprecated: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.recipient: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.summary:
Hopes GdeS will publish on subjects discussed in his letter [10587]. CD had noted similar persistence of variation in fossil shells.

Calls his attention to Nägeli’s work onHieracium.

Expresses skepticism about O. Heer’s view that dicotyledonous plants developed suddenly. Believes they must have developed slowly in some part of the globe completely isolated from other regions.

letters.title: From Wilhelm Breitenbach   11 September 1876
letters.summary:
His research onOrchis maculata.

Discusses effect of disuse of anthers inSalvia officinalis.

Pleased CD can use his observations onPrimula elatior.

letters.title: To Leonard Darwin   11 September [1876]
letters.summary: Informs LD of the death of Francis Darwin’s wife, Amy.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   11 September [1876]
letters.summary: Reports the death of Francis’ wife, Amy.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   11 September [1876]
letters.summary: CD grieves over death of Frank’s wife Amy; worries that it will weaken Frank’s determination to pursue his scientific work.

letters.title: To Japetus Steenstrup   11 September 1876
letters.summary:
Thanks JS for three essays. Has read with great interest the essay on the basking shark ["Sur les appareils tamiseurs ou fanons branchiaux du Pélerin",Kjo|benhaven Oversigt(1873): 47–66]. The explanation that the comb-like structures are of the nature of teeth is a "most wonderful case".

Sends his photograph.

letters.title: From Japetus Steenstrup   [after 11 September 1876]
letters.summary: Thanks CD for sending a photograph.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   13 September 1876
letters.summary: JDH’s condolences at Amy Darwin’s death.

letters.title: From Johann von Fischer   [before 15 September 1876]
letters.summary: Describes behaviour of apes and monkeys in presenting coloured hindquarters.

letters.title: From Johann von Fischer   15 September 1876
letters.summary: Mentions observations on apes and other mammals. Describes habits of apes and monkeys in presenting hindquarters. Thinks species that present always have colourful hindquarters. Discusses possible exceptions to rule.

letters.title: To G. W. Norman   15 September [1876]
letters.summary: Thanks GWN for condolences on death of Amy, his daughter-in-law.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   16 September 1876
letters.summary:
ConvincedCross and self fertilisationis of permanent value, though an extremely dry, special subject. Thinks it will sell for many years and suggests a printing of 1500 copies. Asks that a good indexer be found and put to work. Appleton has agreed to publish it

andOrchids, [2d ed.], if Murray’s will supply stereotype plates.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   16 September [1876]
letters.summary:
Forwards chapter [ofOrchids(1877)] for correction.

Sadness at the death of Amy.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   16 September 1876
letters.summary:
Discusses death of his daughter-in-law

and possible visit by EH.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   16 September 1876
letters.summary:
Discusses the death of his daughter-in-law.

Plans to visit Southampton.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   17 September [1876]
letters.summary: CD thanks JDH for his condolences. Amy’s baby will live with the Darwins.

letters.title: From Thomas Seare   18 September 1876
letters.summary:
Describes example of instinctive behaviour in new-born leveret.

Cites experiment in which rabbit breathed vapour of nitrite of amyl.

Suggests that change in terrestrial atmosphere is responsible for evolution from scales to fur or feathers.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   19 September [1876]
letters.summary: Discusses page length [ofCross and self-fertilisation]. Doubts 1500 copies will be sold until lapse of some years.

letters.title: To P. M. Duncan   19 September 1876
letters.summary: Encloses coral specimen and manuscript account of it by William Lonsdale.

letters.title: To P. A. Hanaford   19 September 1876
letters.summary: Pleased to hear of Peter Henderson’s intended experiment [onDrosera, see10588]. Asks that she tell Mr Henderson that he believes good derived from animal diet will be shown only by production of larger number of seeds and more luxuriant growth in the ensuing year. Wishes to hear the results.

letters.title: To George King   19 September 1876
letters.summary:
Would like to see the pigeons, though he is not likely to work on the subject again. When he hears from Dr Scully, he will present them to the British Museum.

Has not had time to use the information about earthworms yet, but hopes to use it in about a year’s time.

letters.title: To W. C. Marshall   19 September 1876
letters.summary: Asks WCM to design additional rooms for Down House.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   20 September [1876]
letters.summary:
Suggests German works worth translating.

Is glad FD is keeping busy; he has worked excellently on proof-sheets [ofOrchids(1877)].

letters.title: To Karl von Scherzer   22 September 1876
letters.summary:
Thanks for sending Moritz Wagner’s letter and his essays [on "Der Naturprocess der Artbildung" inDas Ausland(1875)]. Will read them and write to Wagner when his health is better.

Declines to receive Scherzer at Down.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   22 September [1876]
letters.summary: Would likeCatasetumandAcroperaplants.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   [after 23 September 1876]
letters.summary:
No results yet with graft-hybrids.

Has been writing a paper.

"Lankester seems to have doubled up [H.] Slade [the medium] in fine style".

letters.title: To W. H. Flower   24 September [1876]
letters.summary:
Sends photographs received from Mr Van der Weyde who is working with associates in Montevideo collecting fossil bones. Asks WHF’s opinion of a specimen about which they are curious.

CD intends urging them to search the Tertiary bed beneath the Pampean formation.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [24 September 1876]
letters.summary:
JDH again expresses his condolences.

The Glasgow BAAS meeting was good, except for Tait’s shameful attack on Tyndall.

Immensely impressed on Scottish geological and glacial features. Is CD aware that the earth beneath Glen Roy roads was found to containfreshwaterdiatoms?

Recounts the itinerary of his honeymoon in Scotland.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   25 September [1876]
letters.summary: FD’s corrections forOrchids[1877] are all very good and useful.

letters.title: To Rudolf Schmid   25 September 1876
letters.summary: Thanks for RS’s work [Die Darwin’schen Theorien und ihre Stellung zur Philosophie, Religion und Moral(1876)].

letters.title: To F. J. Cohn   26 September [1876]
letters.summary: Invites him to visit Down.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   27 September 1876
letters.summary:
Sends first sheets ofCross and self fertilisation. The book is a very dull record of experiments, but nevertheless CD believes it is valuable for its remarkable and well-established results.

Orchids[2d ed.] will soon go to the printer.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   27 [September 1876]
letters.summary:
Sends last chapter ofOrchids[1877] for revision.

Has some articles that might interest FD.

Has invited Ferdinand Cohn and his wife to Down but hopes they will not come.

letters.title: From W. H. Flower   27 September 1876
letters.summary: Identifies South American fossils in photographs sent by John Van der Weyde.

letters.title: From M. L. Baxter   28 September 1876
letters.summary: Sends J. H. Baxter,Statistics, medical and anthropological[2 vols. (1875)]; asks CD’s opinion on correlation of stature with certain types of diseases.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [28 September 1876]
letters.summary:
Sends [unidentified] volume for FD.

Ferdinand Cohn is coming to Down.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin 28 September [1876]
letters.summary: Recommends that CD buy a plot of land.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   29 September [1876]
letters.summary:
Discusses the purchase of some land;

plans to visit Southampton.

letters.title: To W. C. Marshall   29 September [1876]
letters.summary: Mr Laslett, a builder, will meet WCM on Tuesday.

letters.title: To John van der Weyde   29 September 1876
letters.summary:
Thanks JVdW for photographs of fossils; [W. H.] Flower has identified them asToxodonandMylodon.

Sends suggestions for collecting fossil mammals in Argentina and Uruguay.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   [early October 1876]
letters.summary:
Tells JVC that to the title on the first page [ofCross and self-fertilisation] is to be added "in the vegetable kingdom".

Guesses thatOrchids[2d ed.] will be 20 or 30 pages longer than the old edition.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   2 October [1876]
letters.summary:
Thanks FD for corrections [toOrchids(1877)].

Thinks Johann von Fischer’s paper on monkeys’ rumps [Der Zoologische Garten17 (1876): 116–27, 174–9] worth translating, and he intends to write a letter on it toNature[Collected papers2: 207–11].

letters.title: From Otto Zacharias   2 October 1876
letters.summary:
Can CD send sheets ofCross and self-fertilisationas previously promised? OZ writing article on subject ["Darwin über Kreuzung und Selbstbefruchtung im Pflanzenreiche",Das Ausland(1877)].

German Darwinists preparing a Darwin album with photographs of themselves as gift.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [after 2 October 1876]
letters.summary: Sorry the corrections were so tedious, and offers to do revises.

letters.title: From George Cross   4 October 1876
letters.summary: Droseraplants grown with insects excluded have developed normally.

letters.title: From Hermann Müller   4 October 1876
letters.summary:
He has never observed the straight line flight routes in male humble-bees that CD reports.

His last letter was in error: alpineBombus terrestrisdoes break into some flowers.

letters.title: To Otto Zacharias   5 October [1876]
letters.summary: The sheets ofCross and self-fertilisationwill be sent to OZ as they become ready.

letters.title: To George Cross   6 October [1876]
letters.summary: CD is much interested in a change inDroserareported by GC, but "rather doubts" exclusion of insects can have caused it; would like to see the plant and suggests sending it to Down.

letters.title: To William Clowes & Sons   7 October [1876]
letters.summary: Approves the type forOrchids[2d ed.]. The printer should advise Murray that it will be 300 pages.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   8 October [1876]
letters.summary:
Sends an article for FD.

Is glad he is able to work on his teasel paper [Proc. R. Soc. Lond.26 (1878): 4–8]; suggests some observations FD could make.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [after 8 October 1876]
letters.summary: Thanks for papers and letter; has been working in the mornings on teasel.

letters.title: From George Cross   9 October 1876
letters.summary: Sending specimens ofDroseragrown without insects.

letters.title: To M. T. Masters   10 October [1876]
letters.summary:
Discusses views of [Alexander James] Maule on potatoes.

Discusses graft-hybrids.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [11 October 1876]
letters.summary: Asks for reference to an article on a mandrill.

letters.title: From M. D. Conway   12 October [1876 ]
letters.summary: Forwards a flower from a Mrs Crawshay, who sees its "evident struggle to become double as another instance of gradual evolution".

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [12 October 1876]
letters.summary: Has seen notice onEmpetrumbut cannot understand how leaves in bud could act as fly-catchers.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   12 October 1876
letters.summary: Would like sheets ofCross and self-fertilisationif it is not already out.

letters.title: From J. I. Rogers   12 October 1876
letters.summary: His brother, George, reports from Calcutta a case of a man whose hands are divided like a cow’s foot.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   13 October 1876
letters.summary:
JDH back from his honeymoon.

Finds he has gout, as his father and grandfather had.

letters.title: To Georg von Seidlitz   13 October 1876
letters.summary: CD is much obliged to receiveBeiträge zur Descendenz-Theorie[1876].

letters.title: To Moritz Wagner   13 October 1876
letters.summary: Comments on essays by MW [Das Ausland, May 1875]. Criticises his theory of isolation as source of species change: "But my strongest objection to your theory is that it does not explain the manifold adaptations in structure in every organic being". Believes MW has misunderstood his views: "I believe that all the individuals of a species can be slowly modified within the same district … I do not believe that one species will give birth to two or more new species, as long as they are mingled together within the same district."

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   17 October [1876]
letters.summary: Frank, who has been reclusive and very hardworking, is returning from Wales after a period of mourning for Amy.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   18 October [1876]
letters.summary: Proof sheets [ofCross and self-fertilisation] have been lost.

letters.title: From George Henslow   20 October 1876
letters.summary: Asks whether CD’s conclusions on cross- and self-fertilising plants agree with his own as set out in a notice inNature[14 (1876): 543–4].

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   21 October [1876]
letters.summary: Refers him toNature[14 (1876): 553] in which a Russian doctor [Prof. Poplavsky] contradicts GHD on deaf mutes not being closely interrelated.

letters.title: From George Cross   23 October 1876
letters.summary: SendsDroseraplants and details of treatment that led them to form normal leaves when grown without insects.

letters.title: From George Cross   23 October 1876
letters.summary: SendingDroseraplants by post instead of rail because they are rotting.

letters.title: To George Henslow   23 October [1876]
letters.summary: Floral structure. The order of the development of the whorls and its relationship to a protandrous or protogynous condition in flowers.

letters.title: To Gustav Jäger   23 October 1876
letters.summary: Thanks for a copy of GJ’sZoologische Briefe(Jäger 1876).

letters.title: To R. B. Smyth   23 October 1876
letters.summary: Thanks for the third number of theGeological survey of Victoria.

letters.title: From George Henslow   24 October 1876
letters.summary:
Thanks for CD’s book [Cross and self-fertilisation] and information on protandry and protogyny.

Health better, but paralysis lingers.

letters.title: To ?   24 October [1876]
letters.summary: Asks his correspondent to thank Prof. Reichenbach for his kindness. A plant was discovered in flower at Kew, and he was able to examine the doubtful point.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   25 October 1876
letters.summary:
Sends sheets [ofCross and self-fertilisation].

Heliotypes forExpressiondelayed because new negatives must be made.

Thanks Herr Koch [of Schweizerbart] for copies ofCoral reefsandClimbing plants.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   25 October [1876]
letters.summary: Asks JDH to find young imperfect flowers ofHoya. CD has observed seed set although there was no trace of anthers.

letters.title: To James Geikie   26 October 1876
letters.summary: Comments on JG’s book [The great ice age and its relation to the antiquity of man, 2d ed. (1877)]. Recalls erratic boulder he knew in Shropshire as a boy.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin 27 October [1876]
letters.summary: Discussing a purchase of land.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   28 October [1876]
letters.summary: Discusses legal arrangements [unspecified].

letters.title: To Asa Gray   28 October 1876
letters.summary: Is sending sheets ofCross and self-fertilisation. He will be curious to see what AG thinks of it, as AG speaks the truth whether or not he approves. Is sick of trying to correct his "horrid bad style".

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   29 October 1876
letters.summary:
JDH looking forHoyafor CD.

Hookers tried to visit Down on foot, but weather was too inclement.

letters.title: To W. C. Marshall   30 October [1876?]
letters.summary: Sends an enclosure [missing] concerned with a very provoking delay.

letters.title: From H. N. Moseley   3 November 1876
letters.summary: Sends a Japanese book illustrating the expression of emotions.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   4 [November 1876]
letters.summary: Sends some sheets [ofCross and self-fertilisation].

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   4 November 1876
letters.summary:
Promises to propose JJW for membership in Zoological Society.

Sympathises with JJW’s enthusiasm about theDanaisand hopes it may become naturalised in this country.

letters.title: To H. N. Moseley   5 November 1876
letters.summary:
Thanks for Japanese book and for HNM’s papers on observations made duringChallengervoyage.

Would be pleased if HNM visited him.

letters.title: From J. F. McLennan   7 November 1876
letters.summary:
L. H. Morgan has plagiarised his and Henry Maine’s works for years.

Encourages George Darwin to continue his work on consanguineous marriages.

letters.title: From H. N. Moseley   7 November 1876
letters.summary: Accepts invitation to Down for 17 or 18 November.

letters.title: From Frigyes Medveczky   11 November 1876
letters.summary: Writing under the name of Friedrich von Bärenbach, FM sends his paper on J. G. Herder as a precursor of Darwin’s theory [Herder als Vorgänger Darwins(1877)]; hopes CD will acknowledge him as such.

letters.title: From E. B. Tylor   11 November 1876
letters.summary: Is attempting to write a book on elementary lessons in anthropology [Anthropology(1881)] and wonders whether CD’s son [Francis] would care to collaborate and aid him with the biological parts.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   12 November 1876
letters.summary:
Thanks for sheets of new book. Intends to talk about it at a scientific social club meeting.

Is amused to read CD’s criticisms of his own style, as in the U. S. it is spoken of as being as faultless as his temper. Corrects a reference.

letters.title: To E. B. Tylor   12 November 1876
letters.summary: Responds to request that his son [Francis] aid EBT with book. Comments on EBT’s excellence as anthropologist.

letters.title: To August Weismann   13 November 1876
letters.summary: Thanks for present ofStudien[zur Descendenz-Theorie, vol. 2 (1876)].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   14 November 1876
letters.summary:
JDH prepares Anniversary Address to the Royal Society [Proc. R. Soc. Lond.(1876): 339–62].

Return ofChallenger.

letters.title: From Peter Henderson   15 November 1876
letters.summary: Reports graft-hybrids inCytisus.

letters.title: From J. W. Judd   15 November 1876
letters.summary:
Thanks for new edition ofCoral reefs[1874]

andVolcanic islands[1876].

His travels and studies confirm CD’s explanation of the banded structure of lavas.

letters.title: To John Murray   15 November 1876
letters.summary:
Is satisfied with sales of his books.

Did not expectOrchidsto sell more than 600 or 700 copies.

Only bad item isExpression, which astonishes him, since it sells well in Germany.

Asks size of printing ofCross and self-fertilisation; thinks 1500 would be ample.

letters.title: To James Geikie   16 November 1876
letters.summary:
On JG’sGreat ice age.

Discusses formation of drift deposits near Southampton.

Comments on Axel Blytt [Immigration of Norwegian flora(1876)].

Has had fearful misgivings that the step-like plains of Patagonia may have been caused by changes in level of sea, not land.

Comments on book [Archibald Geikie,Life of Sir Roderick I. Murchison(1875)].

letters.title: From Horace Pearce   16 November 1876
letters.summary: Asks advice on transplanting insectivorous plants.

letters.title: From Charles Voysey   17 November 1876
letters.summary: Asks CD’s opinion of a proposed protest [unspecified] and asks whether he will sign it.

letters.title: From H. N. Moseley   [after 17 November 1876]
letters.summary:
Finds he does not have a duplicate of the Japanese natural history book. Sends other volumes of grotesque pictures.

He can show F. W. Hutton erred in callingPeripatus novae zelandiaeself-fertilising; suspects J. F. Bullar has made a similar error on parasitic Isopoda. They both mistook spermatophores for testes.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   19 November 1876
letters.summary:
Agrees with CD that Charles Voysey’s "Protest" would not do any good.

Has less sympathy with half-hearted sentimental school than with thorough-going orthodoxy. On theological dogmas, benevolence of the Creator.

[Encloses copy of his letter to Voysey.]

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   20 November 1876
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for [2d English edition of]Volcanic islands and South America[1876].

Is at work onCross and self-fertilisation. Asks about some doubtful points.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   20 November [1876]
letters.summary: Writes about the purchase of a horse.

letters.title: From James Geikie  20 November 1876
letters.summary:
Glaciation in the British Isles.

S. B. J. Skertchley’s researches on Palaeolithic man in England [Nature14 (1876): 448–9].

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [after 20 November 1876]
letters.summary: Has written of his idea [on the formation of the gravels near Southampton] to James Geikie, who thought it very feasible.

letters.title: To Charles Voysey   21 November [1876]
letters.summary: Agrees with much of CV’s proposed protest but cannot sign it. Feels it is likely to do more harm than good.

letters.title: From Charles Voysey   21 November 1876
letters.summary: Thanks CD for considering his protest, which he has now decided not to carry out.

letters.title: To W. C. Marshall   22 November [1876]
letters.summary: Mr Laslett’s estimate is too high. Mr Deards is quicker and better. Discusses building details for house improvement.

letters.title: To H. N. Moseley   22 November [1876]
letters.summary:
Thanks for Japanese books, and papers by HNM.

Comments onPeripatus.

Not disappointed at what William Thomson says about evolution.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   23 November 1876
letters.summary:
Tells JVC what changes have been made in the new edition of his geological book [Volcanic islands and South America].

Does not know why he doubted about the Atlantic dust paper – now thinks it worth translating.

Glad JVC has not foundCross and self-fertilisationas intolerably dull as CD feared. Answers his queries aboutCross and self-fertilisation.

letters.title: From Fritz Hoddick   23 November 1876
letters.summary:
Met CD at a bath the previous summer.

Proposes he work on human illness.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [27? November 1876]
letters.summary: Sends W. Thomson’s complimentary opinion of his paper "On the influence of geological changes on the earth’s axis" [Philos. Trans. R. Soc. Lond.167 (1877): 271–312].

letters.title: To Asa Gray   27 November 1876
letters.summary: Thanks for a correction. Hopes AG now has all the sheets ofCross and self-fertilisation.

letters.title: From Robert Shaw   28 November 1876
letters.summary: Encloses printed letter fromLand and Waterin which he proposes a hypothesis that explains how soaring birds can stay aloft by expelling air from their lungs.

letters.title: From Henry Wilson   28 November 1876
letters.summary: Sends photograph of man with peculiar facial features, whom HW treated at St Mark’s Ophthalmic Hospital.

letters.title: From F. B. Zincke   29 November 1876
letters.summary: Considers different animal instincts, some of which have reversed, others of which have proved persistent.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [before 30 November 1876]
letters.summary:
Is working at dimorphic plants;

is astonished at WED’s labour.

letters.title: From Thomas Brittain   30 November 1876
letters.summary: Informs CD aboutApocynum androsaemifolium, an insectivorous plant not mentioned in CD’s book. Offers to send specimen.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   30 November [1876]
letters.summary: Pleased to hear about GHD’s paper at the Royal Society.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [c.December 1876]
letters.summary: Asks for details of dimorphism inSethiafrom Thwaites,Enumeratio plantarum Zeylaniae[1864]. [SeeForms of flowers, p. 122.]

letters.title: To Thomas Brittain   1 December 1876
letters.summary: Thanks TB for calling his attention to the case of theApocynum; is unable to understand the trap-like arrangement [of the flowers].

letters.title: From Francis Galton   1 December 1876
letters.summary: Gives another instance of curious habit in the Butler family.

letters.title: From Albert Gaudry   2 December 1876
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for translation ofClimbing plants.

AG is at work onLes enchaînements du monde animal[1878]. Will send CD a copy as soon as it is ready.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   4 December 1876
letters.summary: Plans to republish his paper on dimorphism with additions [Forms of flowers]. Is convinced it is necessary to compare pollen-grains and the state of the stigma to recognise dimorphic plants. Requests specific plants to test for dimorphism and would welcome examples from any family in which he has not encountered dimorphic species.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   5 December 1876
letters.summary:
Dimorphism and cleistogamy inHottonia.

AG wants new, unambiguous term for what is now referred to as "dimorphism", "dioecio-dimorphism", or "heterostyly"; proposes "heterogone".

Sends an excerpt fromBulletin of Torrey Botanical Club2 (June 1871) onHottonia inflata.

letters.title: From Friedrich Hildebrand   6 December 1876
letters.summary: Repeated maize crosses without success: i.e., in most cases yellow and red varieties did not produce fertile offspring.

letters.title: To Gerard Krefft   6 December 1876
letters.summary: Sorry to hear of JLGK’s troubles. Cannot organise a subscription but sends £5.

letters.title: From Hermann Müller   6 December 1876
letters.summary:
Thanks forCross and self-fertilisation.

Fritz Müller has been appointed "Naturalista Viajante" of the Rio de Janeiro Museum, which will help his income greatly.

letters.title: From A. W. Bennett   7 December 1876
letters.summary:
Thanks for copy ofCross and self-fertilisation.

Reports instances of cross-fertilisation in maize,

and succession of forms of flowers on Isle of Wight.

Asks CD’s suggestions for his second edition of Julius von Sachs’sText-book of botany.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   7 December 1876
letters.summary: Questions CD on sale of his books in America by Appleton and other publishers; copyright and translation rights.

letters.title: From George Henslow   [c. 7 December 1876]
letters.summary: Considers some flowers especially adapted for self-fertilisation, and believes all flowers are self-fertilising under some conditions. Gives examples of plants in which he believes all flowers are cleistogamous. Believes self-fertilisation is the primordial condition of flowering plants.

letters.title: To George Bentham   8 December 1876
letters.summary:
Asks GB to send him flowers of the two forms ofBoronia pinnata, as he is republishing his papers on dimorphic plants [Forms of flowers].

Sends copy ofCross and self-fertilisation.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   8 December 1876
letters.summary:
He has examinedHoyaflowers with Bentham and Oliver, but they are not satisfied about the five processes alternating with the sepals. [SeeForms of flowers, pp. 331–2.] Sends specimens of plants.

Babington’s surprise at JDH’s advocacy of Darwinian views at Norwich [BAAS meeting].

Criticism of the behaviour of the trustees of the British Museum [in theChallengeraffair].

letters.title: To G. S. Ffinden   9 December 1876
letters.summary: Sends £9 for Down Coal and Clothing Club, consisting of £5 for self, £1 for his son George, and £3 for his son Francis.

letters.title: To Eduard Strasburger   9 December [1876]
letters.summary: Thanks for a copy of the second edition of Strasburger’sÜber Zellbildung und Zelltheilung(On cell formation and cell division; Strasburger 1876b).

letters.title: From George Bentham   10 December 1876
letters.summary:
Sends specimens ofBoronia.

Discusses the section on diclinous trees and herbs in CD’s new book [Cross and self-fertilisation, pp. 411–13]. CD’s theory that diclinism preceded hermaphroditism seems confirmed.

letters.title: From Robert Shaw   10 December [1876]
letters.summary: Adds a point to his previous letter regarding the buoyancy of birds and their soaring capacity.

letters.title: From F. M. Balfour   11 December 1876
letters.summary: Asks CD to renew his former offer to propose him for the Royal Society, as Michael Foster, now on the Council, is unable to do so.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   11 December 1876
letters.summary:
Plants received from JDH.

Requests he verify an identification by Fritz Müller.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   11 December 1876
letters.summary:
FM’s new position in Rio.

CD interested in nature of surface deposits at Rio.

Sends a copy ofCross and self-fertilisation.

letters.title: To George Bentham   12 December 1876
letters.summary:
Has examined the specimens ofBoronia pinnata. No evidence of two distinct bodies of individuals.

Asks whether extra-American species ofAegiphilaare heterostyled.

letters.title: To F. M. Balfour   13 December 1876
letters.summary: CD is glad to propose FMB for Royal Society. Explains information and certificates needed.

letters.title: From George Bentham   13 December 1876
letters.summary:
BelievesAegiphilato be exclusively American.

Contrasts fertilisation of AustralianAcaciawith BrazilianMimosa.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   13 December 1876
letters.summary: Complains at Albert Günther’s imputations against Charles Wyville Thomson [as a result of the dispute between Thomson and the British Museum, regarding the disposal of the specimens from theChallenger].

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   13 December 1876
letters.summary: Responds to CD’s new work [Cross and self-fertilisation]. Suggests results might have been more convincing if CD had measured weights instead of heights. The fact that infertile hybrids have not been produced means that the "one great objection" has not been got rid of: the physiological characteristic of species. Suggests an experiment to produce "sterile mongrels" which would remove objection.

letters.title: From F. M. Balfour   [14 December 1876]
letters.summary: Michael Foster approves of names FMB suggested CD apply to [in proposing FMB to the Royal Society] and adds George Allman, Foster, W. H. Flower, and P. M. Duncan, the only biologists on the Council.

letters.title: From F. M. Balfour   [14] December [1876]
letters.summary: Lists his chief publications and suggests names of biologists in the Royal Society whom CD might ask to sign his nomination certificate.

letters.title: From William Renton   14 December 1876
letters.summary: CorrectsDescent[1: 294] on inheritance of tortoise-shell colour in cats. It does not violate rule that characters appearing late in one sex are transmitted exclusively to the same sex.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   15 December 1876
letters.summary: JDH has sent a short-styledForsythiafrom Kew. CD surmises that allForsythiaat Kew may be short-styled, hence he is curious to know whether they set seed.

letters.title: To John Scott   15 December 1876
letters.summary: CD is eager for further information aboutLagerstroemia, which is sterile with its own pollen. Does the collection of dried plants reveal more than one form? Plans to republish papers on dimorphism.

letters.title: To Samuel Smiles   15 December 1876
letters.summary: Thanks SS for present ofLife of a Scotch naturalist[1876]. Has read every one of his biographies with "extreme pleasure".

letters.title: From Alphonse de Candolle   16 December 1876
letters.summary:
Thanks forCross and self-fertilisation.

Discusses geographical implications of inbreeding. Can the length of time an insular flora has been isolated be estimated by its weakness due to inbreeding?

letters.title: From Julius von Haast   16 December 1876
letters.summary:
Sends a passage relevant to Pangenesis [on regional accents distinguishable in the speech of those born deaf] fromLife, letters, and journals of George Ticknor[ed. G. S. Hillard, vol. 1 (1876)], p. 196.

Tells of the controversy about evolution raging in Dunedin, with clergy playing a prominent part.

letters.title: From Peter Henderson   16 December 1876
letters.summary: His long experience with propagation ofCytisusand other "sports".

letters.title: From Robert Shaw   16 December 1876
letters.summary:
Discusses further his theory relating to the soaring capacity of birds.

Mentions hybrids produced by various crossings of game-birds.

letters.title: To Samuel Smiles    16 December 1876
letters.summary:
Has written via John Murray to thank for SS’s biography of Thomas Edward (Smiles 1876).

Is happy to sign a memorial concerning a Civil List pension for Thomas Edward.

letters.title: From Robert Caspary   17 December 1876
letters.summary:
Thanks for copy ofCross and self-fertilisation.

Francis Darwin’s observation of nectaries inPterisis most curious.

Doubts cross-fertilisation in the rare cases of two flowers on the same stalk inVictoriaandEuryale.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   18 December 1876
letters.summary: Notes variation in style and stamen length inForsythia.

letters.title: From G. E. S. Boulger   20 December [1876]
letters.summary:
Is engaged in translating Hermann Müller’sBefruchtung der Blumen[1873].

Has observedSphinxmoths onPetunia.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   20 December 1876
letters.summary: Sends an omitted reference to an article by Dr Ascherson [Bot. Ztg.(1871): 444et seq.] forCross and self-fertilisation.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   20 December 1876
letters.summary:
Thanks for information aboutHottonia.

Has found dimorphism inForsythia.

Considers AG’s arguments on different terms for dimorphism, but cannot change to using the proposed new term [see10699].

letters.title: To ?   21 December 1876
letters.summary: Sends his signature

letters.title: From Asa Gray   22 December 1876
letters.summary:
Discusses some dimorphic plants.

Sends specimens ofRhamnusbut his few specimens ofLeucosmiaare very poor.

letters.title: To Karl von Scherzer   24 December 1876
letters.summary:
Thanks for volume on craniology

and for suggestion to Austrian Government that CD receive volumes onNovaravoyage.

letters.title: From George Rolleston   26 December 1876
letters.summary:
Sending certificates for Balfour and Moseley for CD to sign.

Calls attention to a paper by Emil Bessels on Eskimos, which he extracts [see10737].

CD has cited GR for material that is not his inVariation, 2d ed., 1: 469, on transmission of mutilation.

letters.title: From E. M. Heckel     27 December 1876
letters.summary: Has read and greatly admires CD’s latest book,Cross and self-fertilisation; seeks permission to translate it into French and to add some annotations. [EMH’s translation was published in 1877.]

letters.title: From Hermann Müller   28 December 1876
letters.summary: No papers on heterostyly have appeared since 1873.

letters.title: From George Rolleston   29 December 1876
letters.summary:
Studying anatomy of the Irish pig.

Emil Bessels’ paper is inArchiv für Anthropologie8 (1875): 107. He connects a band of poor Eskimos encountered at Smith’s Sound with glacial man.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   30 December 1876
letters.summary:
Describes new journal,Kosmos, to be edited by Ernst Krause. Asks CD to lend his name to journal.

Has sentAnthropogenie, 3d ed.

Will send his study [Biologische Studien, pt 2:Studien zur Gastraea-theorie(1877)] in January.

Thanks CD for hospitality at Down.

letters.title: From F. J. Cohn   31 December 1876
letters.summary:
Acknowledges presentation copy ofCross and self-fertilisation.

Thanks for visit to Down.

Praise for CD’s theories.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   31 December 1876
letters.summary: Much pleased with CD’s book [Cross and self-fertilisation]. Is struck by width and caution of his generalisations and by the application of experiment to processes of life hitherto merely observed.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   31 December 1876
letters.summary:
Thanks for EH’sAnthropogenie, 3d ed.

SendsCross and self-fertilisation.

letters.title: From Allen Thomson   31 December 1876
letters.summary:
Is happy to sign F. M. Balfour’s application for admission to the Royal Society.

Remembers CD from Edinburgh days.

letters.title: From Marcellin de Bonnal   [1877]
letters.summary: Asks CD why some living forms have evolved and others have not.

letters.title: From Alphonse de Candolle   January 1877
letters.summary: Introduces his son Casimir, who is visiting England.

letters.title: To [E. M. Dicey?]   [1877]
letters.summary: Gives his opinion on the education of girls in physiology. Would regret that any girl who wished to learn physiology should be checked.

letters.title: From Sigmund Fuchs   [1877–8?]
letters.summary: Asks if CD agrees with Carl Claus’sGrundzüge der Zoologie[3d ed. (1876)], in separating tunicates from molluscs.

letters.title: To Sigmund Fuchs   [1877–8?]
letters.summary: [Draft of letter for Francis Darwin to write to SF.] CD declines to express an opinion on SF’s query.

letters.title: From Alpheus Hyatt   January 1877
letters.summary: Reports on his work. Relationships of shells found at Steinheim; attempts to elucidate the genesis of different forms.

letters.title: From Adolphe de Stillfried   [1877?]
letters.summary: Writes of his admiration for CD and requests an autograph or photo.

letters.title: To ?   [1877–81]
letters.summary: Letter of reference giving his opinion of the character of a man who has been his footman for a year.

letters.title: To Octavian Blewitt   1 January 1877
letters.summary: A letter in support of [Ann Jane] Cupples’ request to the Royal Literary Fund for assistance. Her talent, industry, and need.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   [1 January 1877]
letters.summary: Would like Price’s address.

letters.title: From Arthur Mellersh   1 January 1877
letters.summary:
Has "the missing link" been found in New Guinea, as he read in the newspaper?

Offers CD the nest of a foreign bird pressed on him by a neighbour.

letters.title: To Alfred Newton   2 January 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks AN for telling him of the complex cross among wagtails. CD is surprised that so much close interbreeding does not check their propagation.

CD does not suppose he will ever have strength to work up his data on hybridism, so he will not write to Mr Monk.

letters.title: From Charles and Francis Darwin to G. J. Romanes   2 January [1877]
letters.summary:
Agrees to propose GJR for membership in Royal Society.

Remarks on GJR’s paper on Medusae [Philos. Trans. R. Soc. Lond.167 (1877): 659–752].

letters.title: From T. A. B. Spratt   2 January 1877
letters.summary: TABS is pleased that CD found something of interest in his researches in Crete [Travels and researches in Crete(1869)].

letters.title: ToGardeners’ Chronicle   3 January [1877]
letters.summary: Suggests that the scarcity of holly berries is owing to the scarcity of bees during the spring, rather than to frost. He does not know what caused the scarcity of bees.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   3 January 1877
letters.summary:
Asks AG not to send his rare specimens [ofLeucosmia].

Is glad of the notice about black pigs.

Has great faith in Jeffries Wyman;

thinks A. R. Wallace founds his speculation on a feeble basis.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   4 January 1877
letters.summary: Discusses certificate proposing GJR as Fellow of Royal Society.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   5 January 1877
letters.summary:
Orchids[2d ed.] will soon be published.

1000 more copies ofDescent[2d ed.] will soon have to be printed, so CD could send any alterations to be made in the plates.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   [6–12 January 1877]
letters.summary: Has received French essay on effects of conscription on [decreasing] height of men, due to unfit left at home to propagate race. Would FG care to see it?

letters.title: From George Hodgskin   6 January 1877
letters.summary: Sends nest of a Uruguayan bird.

letters.title: From Julius Sachs   6 January 1877
letters.summary:
Sends photographs of himself.

Thanks CD for book [Cross and self-fertilisation]

and Francis Darwin for publications.

letters.title: From Otto Zacharias   7 January 1877
letters.summary:
Discusses publication of CD’s essays in three German popular periodicals.

Haeckel is ill.

German translation of George Darwin, "Marriage between first cousins" [1875] has sold 250 copies.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   [after 8 January 1877]
letters.summary: Returns E. Haeckel’sPerigenesis[der Plastidule(1876)]. EH’s "plastidules" do not differ from Spencer’s "physiological units". Does not see that biology gains anything from EH’s theory.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   9 January [1877]
letters.summary: Can FG come to lunch on Sunday? George Darwin wants to meet him.

letters.title: To Howard Miller   10 January 1877
letters.summary: Declines offer involving embryological studies.

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   11 January 1877
letters.summary:
Encloses extract [missing] on a caterpillar.

Mentions William Buckler’s magnificent drawings of caterpillars [The larvae of the British butterflies and moths, Ray Soc. (1886–91)], but doubts Buckler will lend them for any Darwinian purpose. John Hellins has a portion of drawings and is more liberal.

letters.title: From Allen Stoneham   11 January 1877
letters.summary: Has read CD’s note on the scarcity of holly berries ["Holly berries" (1877),Collected papers2: 189–90] resulting from the scarcity of bees. Believes the shortage of bees resulted from the wet year 1875, which led to a very poor honey harvest.

letters.title: From G. M. Tracy   11 January 1877
letters.summary: Observations on and explanations of the scarcity of fruit and berries (especially holly berries) evident that year.

letters.title: To G. M. Tracy   [after 11 January 1877]
letters.summary: GMT’s observations [on scarcity of holly berries] throw doubt on CD’s conclusions [seeCollected papers2: 189–90].

letters.title: From Francis Galton   12 January 1877
letters.summary: Would like to see essay [on effects of conscription in France, see10774]. Knows of Swiss memoir to the same effect. Author says Swiss yeomen apt to leave homestead to sickly son. Landed populations deteriorate.

letters.title: From T. M. Reade   12 January 1877
letters.summary: TMR’s address ["Geological time" (Presidential Address, 1876),Proc. Liverpool Geol. Soc.3 (1878): 211–35] not yet published. Will send copy.

letters.title: To August Weismann   12 January 1877
letters.summary:
Comments on AW’s book [Studien zur Descendenz-Theorie(1875–6)], especially on mimicry in caterpillars.

Mentions sets of drawings of British Lepidoptera in all stages. Would AW like to see them?

letters.title: From Emile Alglave   13 January 1877
letters.summary: Asks whether CD has any observations to make on J. R. L. Delboeuf’s article ["Les mathématiques et la transformisme"] inRevue Scientifique[2d ser. 29 (1877): 669–79]. He would be pleased to receive a letter or article for publication.

letters.title: To T. L. Brunton   13 January 1877
letters.summary: CD asks if he may call next day for talk.

letters.title: To Emile Alglave   [after 13 January 1877]
letters.summary: Has not seen Delboeuf’s article [see10786] and would be obliged for a copy. He is not likely to have any comments as he is engaged in other work.

letters.title: From Alfred Grugeon   14 January [1877]
letters.summary: Believes CD is in error in his notice on the scarcity of holly berries [Collected papers2: 189–90] in asserting that holly is not a hermaphrodite.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [15 January 1877]
letters.summary: Thanks for the copy ofOrchids.

letters.title: From W. H. Leggett   15 January 1877
letters.summary: At Asa Gray’s request, writes what he knows aboutPontederia cordata.

letters.title: To D. F. Nevill   15 January 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks DN for references.

The Apocyanaceae that catch Lepidoptera represent the most gratuitous case of cruelty in nature known to CD, since the captured butterfly is of no use to the plant.

letters.title: From F. W. Pim   15 January 1877
letters.summary: Reply to CD’s note ["Holly berries",Collected papers2: 189–90] from a beekeeper: attributes the scarcity of bees to the harshness of weather in preceding spring.

letters.title: From L. E. Becker   16 January 1877
letters.summary: Sends letter clipped fromManchester Courieron CD’s accounting for scarcity of holly berries by scarcity of bees, and writer’s explanation of latter.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   16 January [1877]
letters.summary: [Samuel] Laurence, having painted the Prince of Wales, now wants to paint another great man; will use a photograph but would like a ten minute interview with CD to mix his tints.

letters.title: To Wilhelm Rimpau   16 January 1877
letters.summary: Thanks for essays ["Das Aufschiessen der Runkelrüben",Landwirtsch. Jahrb. Berlin5 (1876): 31–45; "Die Züchtung neuer Getreide Varietäten",ibid6 (1877): 193–233]. Surprised aboutBeta vulgaris.

letters.title: To R. B. Sharpe?   16 January 1877
letters.summary: Has received from the region of the River Uruguay in S. America "a wonderful nest" of a bird called "El boyero", said to perch on the back of cattle and horses.

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   16 January 1877
letters.summary: Is writingDiseases of women[1877]; sends some proof-sheets for criticism.

letters.title: From W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   [before 17 January 1877]
letters.summary: Remarks on the difference between the sexes inRestionaceaeand other subjects – occasioned by reading the introduction [toForms of flowers].

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   17 [1875–1881]
letters.summary: Wants Francis [Rhodes] Darwin’s address; also asks if CD has heard "the great news".

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   17 January 1877
letters.summary:
JVC’s publisher [Schweizerbart] must decide soon how many copies of two maps inVolcanic islands and South Americaare needed.

Has sent new edition ofOrchids– greatly altered, but he hopes improved.

letters.title: ToGardeners’ Chronicle   17 January [1877]
letters.summary: CD confesses his error with respect to the cause of the scarcity of holly berries. It appears that several causes in combination have led to it. CD still believes rarity of bees played a part, though a subordinate one.

letters.title: To Lawson Tait   17 January [1877]
letters.summary: CD has only a trifling point to make in criticism [of RLT’s excerpt fromDiseases of women]: he believes "the high value of well-bred males is due to their transmitting their good qualities to a far greater number of offspring than can the female".

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   17 January 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks WTT-D for praise ofCross and self-fertilisation

and for information aboutMussaenda.

Has some algae from Queensland if WTT-D is interested.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   17 January 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks for new edition ofOrchids.

The remarkable papers of Mott on Ernst Haeckel ["On Haeckel’s history of creation",Proc. Lit. & Philos. Soc. Liverpool31 (1876–7): 41–89].

The part played by carbon in geological changes.

letters.title: From Thomas Belt   [before 18] January 1877
letters.summary: TB is seeking a Government grant through the Royal Society so that he can give up his business and pursue his work on the glacial period; wants CD to support him with a note to Hooker.

letters.title: To Thomas Belt   18 January 1877
letters.summary: Thinks it would be a serious mistake for TB to give up his profession. How the Royal Society will distribute funds is as yet very uncertain, and CD feels that TB may well receive no support as his proposal is too theoretical.

letters.title: From Friedrich Hildebrand   18 January 1877
letters.summary: Praise forCross and self-fertilisation: most important point proved is benefit of crossing between related individuals grown under different conditions. This explains adaptive value of dispersal mechanisms.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   18 January 1877
letters.summary: JDH discusses his and others’ experiments on survival of seeds. Impressed with resistance of some seeds and rapid decomposition of others. He wonders about "vitality" in the abstract.

letters.title: From Arthur Rawson   19 January 1877
letters.summary: Has observed the scarcity of humble-bees and subsequently of holly berries this year. But does not think humble-bees ever visit holly flowers, however plentiful they may be.

letters.title: From Thomas Belt   20 January 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks for CD’s frank criticism of his views.

Hooker advises him to apply for aid to work out glaciation between Pyrenees and Alps.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   20 January 1877
letters.summary:
Lists misprints inCross and self-fertilisation.

Sends observations and references relevant to a new edition ofExpression.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   22 January 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks JVC for errata [inCross and self-fertilisation]

and especially for interesting and amusing notes on expression. Will use them if a new edition [ofExpression] is needed, but Murray has printed too many copies of first edition.

letters.title: To W. H. Leggett   22 January 1877
letters.summary: Comments on WHL’s paper ["Pontederia cordata",Bull. Torrey Bot. Club6 (1875–9): 62–3]. Cites Fritz Müller’s conclusion that plant is trimorphic. Has WHL made further observations?

letters.title: From George Paul   22 January 1877
letters.summary: Suggests CD write to Mr Fisher, a nurseryman, on his experiments with crossing varieties of holly.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   23 January 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks AG for card aboutPontederia.

Asks for specimens ofPhlox subulataandGilia aggregatato check for dimorphism.

letters.title: From J. J. Murphy   23 January 1877
letters.summary: Requests permission to use illustrations from F. Müller’sFacts and arguments for Darwinin the new edition [of hisHabit and intelligence, 2d ed. (1879)].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   25 January [1877]
letters.summary:
CD notes growth of Royal Society may force it to hire officers.

Speculates on cold resistance of bacterial germs.

Will communicate to Royal Society Frank’s paper on the ingestion of solid particles by the protoplasmic protrusions ofDipsacusglands.

CD working on plant dimorphism.

letters.title: From Hermann Müller   25 January 1877
letters.summary: Thanks CD for calling attention to a "considerable error" in his observations onHottoniafertility [inDie Befruchtung der Blumen(1873)]. [SeeForms of flowers, p. 52.]

letters.title: From A. W. Malm   26 January 1877
letters.summary:
Sends his papers [unspecified].

Linnaeus was a "Darwinist" because he placed the simians in the genusHomo.

letters.title: From G. J. Allman   27 January 1877
letters.summary: On Royal Society Council’s deliberations on awards. GJA argues that older men should be given first claim lest they die neglected; CD had stressed importance of encouraging younger men.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   27 January [1877]
letters.summary: Carlyle hoped CD had not been annoyed by that forged letter, which was the reverse of his opinion. [Enclosed is a published extract, said to be taken from a Thomas Carlyle letter, which denies CD’s intellect and regrets his influence.]

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   27 January 1877
letters.summary:
JDH recounts discussion at Royal Society over Günther’s paper on distribution and affinities of gigantic tortoises ["Description of the living and extinct races of gigantic land-tortoises, Parts III and IV",Proc. R. Soc. Lond.25 (1876–7): 506–7]. Huxley suggests they are Miocene relics.

Royal Society will publish Frank’sDipsacuspaper [but see10971and11073].

Thiselton-Dyer will reviewCross and self-fertilisation.

letters.title: To Albert Günther   28 January [1877]
letters.summary: Has signed certificates.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   28 January 1877
letters.summary: CD thinks A. Günther’s tortoises are relics of closely allied forms, once widely distributed. Expressed this view to AG a few months ago. Cannot explain their restriction to volcanic islands.

letters.title: To Pietro Siciliani   28 January 1877
letters.summary: Thanks for a copy of PS’sCritica nella filosofia zoologica del XIX secolo: dialoghi di Pietro Siciliani …(Naples: Cav. Antonio Morano Editore, 1876).

letters.title: From C. C. Graham   30 January 1877
letters.summary: He has defended Tyndall, CD, and others against attacks of a clergyman.

letters.title: From J. B. Saint-Lager   30 January 1877
letters.summary:
Sends CD parts of theAnnales[Soc. Bot. Lyon] in response to his request for a particular article.

States that, despite CD’s work, he does not believe that any plants, including insectivorous ones, can utilise organic material, and that they live solely on mineral elements in the soil and air.

letters.title: To G. S. Ffinden   31 January 1877
letters.summary: Encloses £25 contribution.

letters.title: From Thomas Palmer   February 1877
letters.summary: Reports on expression in his Pomeranian dog.

letters.title: To J. W. Judd   [after 1 February 1877]
letters.summary: Tells of his pleasure and surprise at reading JWJ’s article ["Darwin’s ""Geological observations"" ",Nature15 (1877): 289–90].

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   6 February [1877]
letters.summary:
Requests return of August Weismann’s letter which refers to eggs.

Curious about the drawing [of the caterpillar? See10780].

letters.title: From A. A. van Bemmelen and H. J. Veth   6 February 1877
letters.deprecated: Adriaan Anthoni van BemmelenHuibert Johannes Veth
letters.sender: Adriaan Anthoni van BemmelenHuibert Johannes Veth
letters.summary:
A letter from CD’s admirers in the Netherlands, sent with an album of their photographs, in celebration of his sixty-eighth birthday.

Presents an account of early efforts in the Netherlands in the direction of developmental theories, and evidence of the support and enthusiastic reception given CD’s theory.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   6 February 1877
letters.summary: Sends specimen ofGilia aggregataand will try to getPhlox subulata.

letters.title: From D. T. Fish   7 February 1877
letters.summary: Sends holly specimens. Differences in flowering times of various hollies.

letters.title: To H. N. Moseley   7 February 1877
letters.summary:
Would like to see the photographs.

Was glad to read HNM’s paper on the New Zealand Peripatus.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   9 February 1877
letters.summary:
Sends birthday wishes. Album of photographs from German admirers has been sent.

Plans trip to Mediterranean.

letters.title: To T. M. Reade   9 February 1877
letters.summary:
Comments on TMR’s essay ["Geological time"].

It is monstrous that P. G. Tait should say that earth is less than ten million years old.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   10 February 1877
letters.summary: Sends specimens of two forms ofRhamnus lanceolata.

letters.title: From Hugo Schneider   10 February 1877
letters.summary: Sends birthday greetings. Asks for autographed photograph.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   11 February [1877]
letters.summary: Sends enclosure regarding inherited handwriting fromLife, letters, and journals of George Ticknor[ed. G. S. Hillard (1876)].

letters.title: To Julius von Haast   [c.11 February 1877]
letters.summary: The extract from Ticknor [see10722] is one of the most curious cases of inheritance CD has met with. He has sent it to Francis Galton as CD is not likely to write on inheritance again.

letters.title: From Karl Beger   [12 February 1877]
letters.summary: Intends to name his son after CD.

letters.title: To A. A. van Bemmelen   12 February 1877
letters.summary: Expresses his gratitude for the gift [a birthday album from a number of Dutch scientists]; he cannot imagine a more honourable testimonial.

letters.title: From Berliner Gesellschaft für Anthropologie, Ethnologie und Urgeschichte   12 February 1877
letters.deprecated: Berliner Gesellschaft für Anthropologie, Ethnologie und Urgeschichte
letters.sender: Berliner Gesellschaft für Anthropologie, Ethnologie und Urgeschichte
letters.summary: CD made a corresponding member of the Berliner Gesellschaft für Anthropologie, Ethnologie und Urgeschichte.

letters.title: To Alpheus Hyatt   13 February 1877
letters.summary:
Regrets that F. Hilgendorf proved so greatly in error ["Planorbis Multiformis",Monatsber. K. Akad. Wiss. Berlin(1866): 474–504; "Noch einmalPlanorbis Multiformis",Z. Dtsch. Geol. Ges.29 (1877): 50–62].

Discusses polymorphic species.

Surprised that shell form developed from various different progenitors.

Reminds CD of C. Nägeli’s conclusions onHieracium.

But still retains belief expressed in first edition ofOriginthat variation in protean species is neither advantageous nor disadvantageous.

letters.title: To Karl von Scherzer   13 February 1877
