letters.summary: Has read a large part of theNovaravoyage [Narrative of the circumnavigation of the globe by the Austrian frigate "Novara"(1861–3)] with pleasure. CD was particularly interested in the scandalous French behaviour at Tahiti.

letters.title: To Ferdinand von Hochstetter   14 February 1877
letters.summary: Sends thanks to Anthropological Society for sending birthday greetings.

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   14 February 1877
letters.summary:
Sends another extract [fromDiseases of women(1877)].

Has reviewedCross and self-fertilisationin theSpectator.

letters.title: To Richard Kippist   15 February 1877
letters.summary: Asks RK [Linnean Society Librarian] to send several journal volumes and articles.

letters.title: From C.-F. Reinwald   15 February 1877
letters.summary: Reports on French translations ofCross and self-fertilisation,Climbing plants, andInsectivorous plants.

letters.title: From Emil Rade   [before 16] February 1877
letters.summary: Sends album of photographs of German scientists as birthday honour.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   16 February 1877
letters.summary: Thanks EH for album of photographs of German scientists.

letters.title: To Emil Rade   16 February 1877
letters.summary: Thanks for the honour conferred upon him [see10826]; it is quite beyond his deserts.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   16 February 1877
letters.summary: Pleased and honoured by WTT-D’s review ["Darwin on fertilisation",Nature15 (1876–77): 329–32]. Comments on review.

letters.title: To August Weismann   17 February 1877
letters.summary: Negotiations for loan of drawings [of Lepidoptera] have failed.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   18 February [1877]
letters.summary:
Praises AG’s abstract ofCross and self-fertilisation[Am. J. Sci.3d ser. 13 (1877): 125–41].

Hopes soon to finish with dimorphic plants.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   19 February 1877
letters.summary: Corrects an important misprint in English edition ofCross and self-fertilisation, p. 275, line six from top [but see10877].

letters.title: To Down Friendly Society   19 February 1877
letters.summary: CD, who has acted as treasurer of the Down Friendly Club for the last 27 years, urges the members not to dissolve the Club, but to continue it and retain about £1000 of the funds on hand to ensure its safety and ability to give assistance to members when they are ill or invalided, or to provide for their burial when dead.

letters.title: ToGardeners’ Chronicle   19 February [1877]
letters.summary: Replies to some of George Henslow’s criticisms [ofCross and self-fertilisation] made in his article ["Fertilisation of plants",Gard. Chron.n.s. 7 (1877): 203–4].

letters.title: To Arnold Dodel-Port   20 February 1877
letters.summary: Thanks AD-P for his articles [Wesen und Begründung der Abstammungs- und Zuchtwahltheorie(1877)] and the eulogistic manner in which he mentions CD’s name.

letters.title: From John Gibbs   20 February 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks CD forOrchids. Has written a notice forChelmsford Chronicle.

Finds some botanical observations on inflorescences.

letters.title: From Franz von Rekowsky   20 February 1877
letters.deprecated: Franz Friedrich Hugo Wilhelm Michael (Franz) von Wotoch-Rekowsky (Franz von Rekowsky)
letters.sender: Franz Friedrich Hugo Wilhelm Michael (Franz) von Wotoch-Rekowsky (Franz von Rekowsky)
letters.summary: Requests CD’s autograph. [Translation of letter made by O. Dill, see10871.]

letters.title: From C.-F. Reinwald   21 February 1877
letters.summary:
Édouard Heckel of Grenoble is translatingCross and self-fertilisation.

Expressionhas sold out; wants a new edition.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   22 February 1877
letters.summary: Attributes the Castilian accent of speech of deaf and dumb men to imitation of their teachers’ lip movements.

letters.title: From John Gibbs   22 February 1877
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his advice. No doubt one may be misled by a few experiments in matters on which many forces come into play. Describes his plans to observe the flowering of 23 plants ofLychnis gilhagoraised from a single capsule.

letters.title: From Hunter Nicholson   23 February 1877
letters.summary: Gives an example of atavism in American cattle.

letters.title: From Otto Zacharias   23 February 1877
letters.summary:
Was CD already convinced of evolution when he publishedJournal of researches?

Photograph album will be late coming.

Evolutionary magazine to appear in March under title ofKosmos.

letters.title: ToNature   24 February [1877]
letters.summary: Darwin consents to his correspondence withPieter Hartingbeing published inNature.

letters.title: From John Scott   24 February 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks forCross and self-fertilisation.

His work on poppy varieties confirms increased vigour with crossing.

JS is carrying out opium poppy experiments CD suggested. He is busy with opium duties. Observing many fields of poppies, day and night, JS finds them remarkably free of insects. Believes they are wind-pollinated and that varieties have prepotent pollen since he has shown they do not cross naturally.

Plans to send a paper onCyclosisto Linnean Society.

letters.title: To Otto Zacharias   [24 February 1877]
letters.summary:
Thanks OZ for a "magnificent Album".

OnBeaglevoyage CD believed in permanence of species. Had occasional vague doubts. In autumn of 1836 saw how many facts indicated common descent of species. In 1837 opened notebook to record facts.

letters.title: From Alfred Grugeon   25 February [1877]
letters.summary: Comments on CD’sCross and self-fertilisation: its usefulness to florists, and his solution of a long standing puzzle in showing the increase of monstrosities in self-fertilised plants.

letters.title: To Albert Günther   25 February [1877]
letters.summary: His specimen catalogue has not been returned from Cambridge museum. If not lost, will answer query.

letters.title: To J. B. Innes   25 February [1877]
letters.summary: CD has harangued the Down Friendly Club. Does not think it will dissolve.

letters.title: To Miss Jacobson   25 February 1877
letters.summary: Accedes to her [unspecified] request.

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   25 February 1877
letters.summary: Wants to know how to obtainThe thoughts of Marcus Aurelius, mentioned inDescent[1: 106].

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   26 February 1877
letters.summary: Is unconvinced that correction inCross and self-fertilisationrequested by CD [see10852] should be made. Asks CD to reconsider.

letters.title: From O. Dill   26 February 1877
letters.summary: Encloses his translation of a draft letter from his friend Franz von Rekowsky [see10855], who is German Consular Secretary at Messina.

letters.title: To ?   26 February 1877
letters.summary: Acknowledges receipt of a publication from a German author. Hopes that the German will not be too difficult to understand in an "important & abstruse" subject.

letters.title: From John Colby   27 February 1877
letters.summary:
Reports a bluebell monster.

Response toCross and self-fertilisation, reviewed inSpectator.

letters.title: To Oswald Heer   28 February 1877
letters.summary: Thanks for work on Fossil arctic flora.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [2 March 1877]
letters.summary: JDH reports on Frank’s reading of hisDipsacuspaper at the Royal Society. Huxley slept through much of it, but JDH is well pleased with it.

letters.title: To G. B. Ercolani   3 March 1877
letters.summary: Thanks GBE for his essay on the placenta [Sull’unità del tipo anatomico della placenta nei mammiferi e nell’umana specie(1877)].

letters.title: To Albert Günther   3 March 1877
letters.summary: Discusses spider specimens.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   3 March [1877]
letters.summary:
CD counters Thiselton-Dyer’s objection to protoplasmic filaments ofDipsacusprotruding beyond cell-wall, as Frank’s paper claims, by citing white "blood cells passing through vessels".

Has received Moseley’s collection of photographs.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   4 March 1877
letters.summary: Apologises for sending wrongCross and self-fertilisationerratum. The error is on p. 191 (where "cross-seeds" appears, it should read "self-fertilised"). There is no error on p. 275.

letters.title: To Édouard Heckel   4 March 1877
letters.summary: Asks EH to make a small correction in his translation [ofCross and self-fertilisation].

letters.title: From C. F. Claus   5 March 1877
letters.summary: Has read in the newspapers about the album of photographs of German scientists sent in tribute to CD. His name and photograph are missing only because he was not asked to participate. CC assures CD he is one of his ardent supporters.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   6 March 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks forOrchids[2d ed.].

Does not feel his abstract ofCross and self-fertilisation[Am. J. Sci.3d ser. 13 (1877): 125–41] was thorough enough.

Has heard of their sad bereavement last autumn [death of Amy, wife of Francis Darwin].

letters.title: To Smith, Elder & Co.   7 March 1877
letters.summary: Baillière wishes to bring out a French translation ofCoral reefs; CD requests their co-operation.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   8 March 1877
letters.summary: Leucosmia burnettianais in all probability dimorphic. ThinksGiliais truly heterostyled andPhlox subulatawas, perhaps, once heterostyled. Has good evidence of heterostyly in 39 genera from 14 families.

letters.title: To C. H. Blackley   9 March 1877
letters.summary: Thanks for CHB’s essay [New observations on hay-fever(1877?)]. The calculation of the weight of pollen-grains is wonderful. Suggests he consultCross and self-fertilisation, pp. 376, 405 for information on this subject.

letters.title: To C. F. Claus   9 March 1877
letters.summary: Warm thanks for CC’s letter. CD needed no word from CC to be convinced of his high opinion.

letters.title: To Melchior Neumayr   9 March 1877
letters.summary: Thanks MN for essay ["Die Congerien",Abh. Geol. Bundesanst. Wien7 (1875)]. It is the best case CD has met, showing "direct influence of conditions of life on the organization". A. Hyatt has come to same conclusion: that closely similar forms may be derived from distinct lines of descent. CD did not emphasise inOriginthe direct action of environment on modification of species; most of the best evidence has been observed since its publication.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   10 March [1877]
letters.summary: Enquiring about cleistogamic flowers ofOxalis.

letters.title: From J. G. F. Riedel   10 March 1877
letters.summary: Asks CD to publish inNatureJGFR’s observation that natives of Hainan have movable tail bones up to 4 cm long.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   11 March 1877
letters.summary:
As editor of the new journal,Kosmos, thanks CD for the permission he has granted Ernst Haeckel to publish with CD’s approval.

Cites his long support for evolution as exemplified by his book [Die botanische Systematik in ihrem Verhältniss zur Morphologie(1866)].

CD has many German supporters.

letters.title: To John Andrews   [before 12 March 1877]
letters.summary: Asks when his waggonette will be finished.

letters.title: From Leonard Blomefield   12 March 1877
letters.summary:
Congratulates CD on testimonials from the savants of Germany and the Netherlands [Nature15 (1877): 356, 410–12] and generally on his contributions to biology.

Asks if and when CD’s "Variability of organic beings in a state of nature", as projected in 1868 [seeVariation1: 4] is to appear.

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   12 March 1877
letters.summary: Discusses the cleistogamous flowers ofOxalis. Thinks they may not be truly cleistogamous but merely arrested or imperfectly developed normal flowers.

letters.title: To Leonard Blomefield   13 March 1877
letters.summary: CD doubts that he will be able to do much more that is new, but cannot bear idleness. Has great amount of material on variation under nature, but so much has been published since the appearance of theOriginthat he doubts he has the power of mind to render the mass into a digested whole.

letters.title: To Daniel Oliver   13 March 1877
letters.summary: Discusses possible cleistogamic flowers inOxalis.

letters.title: From Karl von Estorff   15 March 1877
letters.summary:
Sends belated birthday greetings

and an archaeological pamphlet.

Asks for CD’s autograph.

letters.title: From R. D. Fitzgerald   15 March 1877
letters.summary: Fertilisation of orchids. Believes some plants so constituted as to dispense with cross-fertilisation.

letters.title: From C. C. Babington   16 March 1877
letters.summary:
Thinks flowers ofHottoniaproject from the stem nearly horizontally, perhaps slightly upwards.

Sorry that he cannot help withPulmonaria angustifolia.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   16 March 1877
letters.summary:
Sends cheques in payment of CD’s share of profits onCross and self-fertilisation, now nearly exhausted,

and the latest printing ofOrigin.

letters.title: To C. E. Norton   16 March 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks for Chauncey Wright’s work [Philosophical discussions(1877)].

Gladstone visited recently, and they discussed the future role of the United States as a world power.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   19 March 1877
letters.summary: Murray’s will not announce CD’s new work [Forms of flowers] until informed to do so.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   19 March [1877]
letters.summary:
Sends an informal title-page [forOrchids, 2d ed.].

Appreciates the condolences for Frank [on death of his wife, Amy].

letters.title: To Pieter Harting   19 March 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks for account of his work. Cannot read Dutch, but son has translated it.

Thanks for album sent by PH’s countrymen.

letters.title: From Friedrich Hildebrand   19 March 1877
letters.summary: Regrets he cannot help onOxalisquestion. He did not note the names of species with cleistogamic flowers as he thought they were sufficiently known.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   19 March 1877
letters.summary: Oliver cannot, as CD has requested, hunt for trimorphic flowers in the Herbarium’s collection ofOxalisspecimens. He would help Frank if he comes.

letters.title: To Richard Kippist   19 March 1877
letters.summary: Wishes to reprint his four Linnean Society papers on di- and trimorphic plants [Forms of flowers]. Requests permission and woodblocks of figures.

letters.title: From J. C. Morton   19 March 1877
letters.summary: The editor of theAgricultural Gazetteasks CD to settle a point being debated in his journal. Can a desirable breed of cattle, which is so inbred as to have scrofula, be maintained by crossing with a breed of healthy constitution?

letters.title: From G. J. Wilson   19 March 1877
letters.summary: Pangenesis supports the existence of gemmules; does not accept Galton’s experiments as disproving their existence or importance.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [c.20 March 1877]
letters.summary: Asks FD to mollify Daniel Oliver and assure him that CD asks "onlyfor what I wd. give my life’s blood for".

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   20 March [1877]
letters.summary:
CD apologises for his burdensome request of Oliver.

Criticises JDH’s notice onForsythia, which JDH said was dioecious.Forsythiasent to CD from Kew was heterostylous.

letters.title: From Charles Layton   20 March 1877
letters.summary: Encloses statement of sales forOrigin,Expression,DescentandInsectivorous plantsand sends a cheque for the balance due to CD.

letters.title: To Enrique Godínez   21 March 1877
letters.summary: Has received the sheets of EG’s Spanish translation ofOrigin. Regrets that he cannot undertake to read them because of his health, over-work, and having forgotten much of the language. What he has read seems clearly expressed.

letters.title: ToAgricultural Gazette   22 March 1877
letters.summary:
Evidence for inheritance of constitutional diseases like scrofula so good that it seems rash to breed tainted animal.

Experiments given inCross and self-fertilisationshow that evil of inbreeding follows from near relations possessing closely similar constitution.

Size and vigour increased by breeding plants and animals from ancestors that lived some generations under different conditions of life.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   22 March 1877
letters.summary: A curious error – too late to change: inCross and self-fertilisationCD has "cleistogenous" for "cleistogamous" flowers throughout.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [25 March? 1877]
letters.summary: Staying with W. D. Fox on the Isle of Wight. Offers to findPulmonariaplants.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   25 March 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks for EK’s book [Werden und Vergehen(1876)].

Regrets he cannot write for EK’s journal, but his son, Francis, may do so.

Suggests EK as editor urge on readers [ofKosmos] the investigation of the causes of variability; why, for instance, do wild Pampas cattle change colour when domesticated? Thinks experiments and observations on recently domesticated animals and cultivated plants would throw light on the subject.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   25 March 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for new [2d] edition ofOrchids.

Mentions some observations on dimorphic plants.

Reports on a third species ofPontederia[seeForms of flowers, p. 185].

Describes some unusual grasses.

Reports rumours from southern Brazil concerning the existence of a gigantic subterranean animal.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   26 March 1877
letters.summary:
Had found out his error [use of "cleistogenous" for "cleistogamous" inCross and self-fertilisation] some timeago.

Is now writing on cleistogamic flowers [forForms of flowers(1877)], and, with it, will have worked up all his old materials on plants. JVC will then have a rest from his labours of translation.

letters.title: From William Saville-Kent   26 March 1877
letters.summary: Proposes to construct an aquarium on Jersey and wants to use CD’s name in support of the project.

letters.title: To G. H. K. Thwaites   26 March 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks for specimens [of insects].

Wonders whether difference between male and female plays part in fertilisation of fig.

Flowers ofOxalis sensitiva, sent long ago, are trimorphic and cleistogamic.

letters.title: To W. R. S. Ralston   27 March 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks for the reviews, particularly the one in theTimes.

CD will be pleased to receive Mr Wallace.

letters.title: To William Saville-Kent   28 March [1877]
letters.summary: Regrets he cannot permit his name to be used to support WSK’s aquarium project. If WSK decides to set up an aquarium solely for scientific purposes he would consider subscribing.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   30 March 1877
letters.summary: Lithospermum longiflorumhas cleistogamous flowers and, unlike other species of genus, it is not dimorphic.

letters.title: To ?   30 March 1877
letters.summary: Sends autograph as requested.

letters.title: To Leonard Darwin   31 March 1877
letters.summary:
Is "awfully glad" at LD’s appointment [as an instructor at Chatham].

Thinks LD should start reading chemistry "though reading does not do much".

Reports scientific work of George and Frank Darwin.

letters.title: From Edward Harris   April 1877
letters.summary: Wishes to bring CD his trained cockatoo.

letters.title: To Josef Kořenský   2 April 1877
letters.summary: "Charles Darwin Down, Kent April 2d. 1877; With Mr Darwin’s compliments. – "

letters.title: From Hermann Müller   2 April 1877
letters.summary: Is pleased that CD agrees with HM’s suggestions and criticisms of CD’s work. Will undertake experiments withViola tricolorseeds to see if they produce both large- and small-flowered plants.

letters.title: From W. D. Fox   3 April [1877]
letters.summary: Reports on upward projection ofPulmonariaflowers.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   4 April 1877
letters.summary: Arrangements about a purchase of land.

letters.title: From John Colby   9 April 1877
letters.summary: Notes on competition among tree species in South Wales.

letters.title: From Johannes Schön   10 April 1877
letters.summary: In the name of a student science club, asks whether CD’s theory of evolution applies to mental as well as physical characteristics of men and animals. Asks whether animals have free-will like humans. Do animals have a sense that humans lack?

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   11 April 1877
letters.summary: Sends MS [ofForms of flowers]. Since sale is likely to be small, Murray may not want to publish it on usual terms. CD thinks it may be his last book and asks Murray to publish it on most favourable terms he can afford.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   12 April 1877
letters.summary: JM will be pleased to publish the new work [Forms of flowers] on the usual terms. MS has been sent to the printer.

letters.title: From John Scott   12 April 1877
letters.summary:
Comments on various species ofLagerstroemia.

In the series of opium poppy intercrosses made at CD’s suggestion, JS has learned that the reason they failed to intercross was the absence of insects at the period of their flowering.

letters.title: From G. N. de Stoppelaar   14 April 1877
letters.summary: CD made a Foreign Member of the Zeeland Scientific Society at Middelburg.

letters.title: From H. N. Ridley   15 April 1877
letters.summary: Sends specimens ofSaxifraga tridactyliteswith insects caught by it. Asks if colour of leaves attracts insects.

letters.title: To H. N. Ridley   16 April [1877]
letters.summary: Thanks forSaxifraga. CD had shown inInsectivorous plants[pp. 345–7] that this genus had some powers of absorption.

letters.title: To G. N. de Stoppelaar   17 April 1877
letters.summary: Thanks for membership of Zeeland Scientific Society at Middelburg.

letters.title: To G. H. Lewes   18 April 1877
letters.summary: Thanks GHL for a copy of hisPhysical basis of mind[1877].

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   19 April 1877
letters.summary: Has heard CD is about to be proposed again for the Académie Française, but Huxley is proposed at the same time and may succeed against CD "as being more orthodox!"

letters.title: From Thomas Howie   20 April 1877
letters.summary:
Offers key to CD’s theory: fern roots are like little grubs.

Claims to have crossed the Australian Alps where Dr Müller [Ferdinand von Mueller?] failed.

letters.title: To W. C. Marshall   20 [April 1877]
letters.summary: Discusses locks and window-fastenings, which CD has discovered are not included in the contract for alterations to the house at Down, and a cornice in a passage-way..

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   21 April [1877]
letters.summary: CD regrets not being able to see JDH.

letters.title: From Otto Zacharias   21 April 1877
letters.summary: Sends abnormal pig’s foot. Does abnormality occur often?

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   [23 April 1877]
letters.summary: "Frank has sent the cards here."

letters.title: From Robert McLachlan   23 April 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for helping his successful candidacy for F.R.S.

He is working up Arctic insects.Bombusis found at 83° N., as far north as has been reached.

letters.title: To E. S. Morse   23 April 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks for ESM’s address ["What American zoologists have done for evolution",Proc. Am. Assoc. Adv. Sci.25 (1876)].

J. A. Allen’s work is important as apparently showing change through direct action of [external] conditions.

CD has given up trying to understand E. D. Cope and Alpheus Hyatt on acceleration and retardation.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [24 April 1877?]
letters.summary: Sends notes made in June 1867, onRhamnus catharticusandR. lanceolatus. Encloses diagrams and measurements relating to pollen size inR. lanceolatus.

letters.title: From J. W. Judd   24 April 1877
letters.summary: Grateful for CD’s support for his election as F.R.S.

letters.title: From C. G. Semper   26 April 1877
letters.summary: Explains why he did not add his photograph to the album presented by German naturalists to CD. Instead he wishes to dedicate to CD his work on the vertebrate-type eyes on the back of some Mollusca. [Enclosed is a MS introduction to this work,Über Sehorgane von Typus der Wirbelthieraugen auf dem Rücken von Schnecken.].

letters.title: To Otto Zacharias   26 April 1877
letters.summary: CD has sent the pig’s foot to William Henry Flower to examine.

letters.title: To G. C. Robertson   27 April 1877
letters.summary: CD submits his paper ["A biographical sketch of an infant",Collected papers2: 191–200] for possible publication.

letters.title: To G. O. Sars   29 April 1877
letters.summary: Thanks for GOS’s memoir onBrisinga[1875].

letters.title: To C. G. Semper   30 April 1877
letters.summary:
Is honoured by CGS’s dedication [see10942].

His observation of the dorsal eyes of Onchidium is interesting and surprising.

letters.title: From J. E. Harting   1 May [1877–81]
letters.summary: Wild cat gestation is twelve days longer than domestic cat, a fact not mentioned inVariation.

letters.title: To [Francis Lloyd]   1 May [1877]
letters.summary: CD does not feel a subscription could be got up to aid correspondent. Sends a cheque for £10.

letters.title: From C. W. Thomson   1 May 1877
letters.summary: Is sorting material collected by theChallengerand wonders whether CD would care to examine the cirripedes.

letters.title: To W. H. Flower   2 May [1877]
letters.summary: "The pigs-foot has been dispatched to day per Rail."

letters.title: From W. H. Flower   3 May 1877
letters.summary: Discusses abnormal pig’s foot sent to him by CD.

letters.title: To Albert Günther   4 May [1877]
letters.summary: Pigeons’ skins dispatched today.

letters.title: To Albert Günther   7 May 1877
letters.summary: Sends MS about pigeons.

letters.title: To George King  7 May 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks GK for the seeds of the Melastomaceae

and skins of the pigeons,

and forwards a note to Dr Scully.

letters.title: From A. G. Butler   8 May 1877
letters.summary: Can CD explain why house sparrows persist in trying to build a nest in a spot from which it is daily removed?

letters.title: To A. G. Butler   9 May 1877
letters.summary: "I have always been inclined to think that sparrows were acute & crafty birds, but you certainly show that they are Fools, & if they go on behaving in so idiotic a manner, you will do quite right to expose their conduct in some public Journal!--"

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   9 May 1877
letters.summary: Is printing a book on dimorphic plants [Forms of flowers] in which he will make considerable use of FM’s work.

letters.title: From C.-F. Reinwald   9 May 1877
letters.summary:
French translation ofInsectivorous plantspublished.

Climbing plantshas not sold well.

letters.title: From George Rolleston   9 May 1877
letters.summary: Discusses the structure of the human cranium, in particular a find by Cocchi and observations by Canestrini.

letters.title: From D. B. Miller   12 May 1877
letters.summary: Offers a supplementary component to sexual selection which CD ignored inDescent: the direct effect of differences in ardour between males and females.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   14 May 1877
letters.summary:
Requests observations on sensitiveMimosaand movements of plants in rain.

Worm-castings.

letters.title: To Karl von Scherzer   14 May [1877]
letters.summary:
Received Moritz Wagner’s essays [Das Ausland(May 1875)] and sent him a long letter [10643] disagreeing with his views because they do not explain adaptation.

Thanks for Büchner’s essay [Die Darwin’sche Theorie, 4th ed. (1876)].

letters.title: From W. B. Bowles   17 May 1877
letters.summary:
Has read a German author’s exposition of CD’s theory.

Believes "missing link" between higher mammals and man consists of a race of "speaking monkeys" – akin to Africans – who pollute blood of better race and impede civilisation.

letters.title: To John Price   17 May 1877
letters.summary:
Stripes on animals curious subject for investigation. Not likely to take it up again.

Recommends cutting plant stems under water.

letters.title: From W. B. Bowles   18 May 1877
letters.summary: Is less certain of views in letter of 17 May [10963]. Asserts interest in explaining the presence of "speaking monkeys", which occur in higher as well as lower classes.

letters.title: From E. S. Morse   18 May 1877
letters.summary:
Lectured on Darwinism in Cincinnati, Minneapolis, Buffalo, and to 3500 people in New York City.

Despite close friendship with Cope and Hyatt and many explanations by the latter, he cannot understand their views.

Thanks CD for appreciation of his papers.

letters.title: From E. H. von Baumhauer   19 May 1877
letters.summary: CD elected unanimously as a foreign member of the Dutch Society of Sciences. [See10970.]

letters.title: To W. H. Flower   19 May [1877]
letters.summary: Will be delighted to see WHF on 26th.

letters.title: To C. V. Riley   19 May 1877
letters.summary: Thanks him for the 9th Report [on the noxious, beneficial, and other insects of the State of Missouri]. "What a pretty illustration of a sub-rudimentary organ is that of the saw-fly!"

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [before 21 May 1877]
letters.summary: Edwin Ray Lankester wants to reprint FD’s paper ‘Food bodies’ in theQuarterly Journal of Microscopical Science.

letters.title: To ?   [before 22 May 1877?]
letters.summary: Writes as Treasurer of the Down Friendly Society; discusses financial matters related to the Society.

letters.title: To E. H. von Baumhauer    22 May 1877
letters.summary: Acknowledges election to the Society.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   22 May 1877
letters.summary: Asked C. E. Bessey whetherLithospermum longiflorumwas dimorphic like its relatives. Encloses CEB’s reply.

letters.title: To G. C. Robertson   22 May 1877
letters.summary: CD is gratified that GCR thinks "Sketch of an infant" [Collected papers2: 191–200] worth publishing. Returns corrected proofs. Assures GCR he took pains to observe carefully.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   23 May 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks him for book by Grant Allen [Physiological aesthetics(1877)].

Comments on dispute over spontaneous generation.

The Council [of the Royal Society] will not print Frank Darwin’s paper onDipsacus[inPhilos. Trans. R. Soc. Lond.].

Mentions GJR’s grafting experiments

and his investigation of spiritualism.

letters.title: To C. H. Drinkwater   24 May 1877
letters.summary: Sends a contribution [£10] to CHD’s fundraising.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   25 May [1877]
letters.summary: CD has again become interested in "bloom" on plants; requests JDH’s help with seeds and plants.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   27 May [1877]
letters.summary:
Discusses Francis Darwin’s paper on teasel [Dipsacus].

Comments on GJR’s investigation of spiritualism.

Comments on book by Grant Allen [Physiological aesthetics(1877)].

Invites him to visit

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [before 28 May 1877]
letters.summary: Cambridge University will offer CD an honorary degree.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   28 May 1877
letters.summary: Writes in detail about Cambridge offer of the honorary LL.D.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   29 May 1877
letters.summary:
JDH’s view of Thiselton-Dyer’s engagement to his daughter, Harriet.

JDH is pleased to help with "bloom" questions.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   30 May [1877]
letters.summary: Has not yet received letter [about Cambridge honorary LL.D.].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   31 May 1877
letters.summary: Responding to CD’s request for assistance with his study of "bloom", JDH sends seeds, a list of available plants, and a list of English wild plants with "bloom".

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   31 May 1877
letters.summary: CD thanks JDH for assistance with "bloom" study.

letters.title: From J. M. Rodwell   1 June 1877
letters.summary: Sends extract abusing CD, from a sermon by a Greek priest.

letters.title: From W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   [June 1877 or later]
letters.summary: Notes and extracts relating to "bloom".

letters.title: From P. L. Sclater   2 June 1877
letters.summary: Encloses a memorandum [missing] drawn up by W. H. Flower, Huxley, and himself, defending Charles Wyville Thomson against an attack made upon him.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   [3 June 1877]
letters.summary: Has not yet heard from Cambridge. Thinks perhaps they do not intend to give him the degree.

letters.title: To J. M. Rodwell   3 June 1877
letters.summary: Thanks for an extract from a sermon, in which CD is abused by an archimandrite: he considers it a great honour.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   4 June [1877]
letters.summary:
C. E. Bessey’s case [see10969] came too late, as the sheets had been printed, but CD thinks it should be carefully investigated as a possible case of incipient heterostyly.

Is trying to make out the function of "bloom", the waxy secretion on leaves and fruits.

letters.title: From Charles Bradlaugh   5 June 1877
letters.summary: Wants to subpoena CD in a case pending against himself and Annie Besant, to be tried 18 June. [Bradlaugh and Besant were indicted for issuing an "obscene libel".]

letters.title: To [Henry Huntsman?]   5 June [1877]
letters.summary: Urgently requests a pair of braces. "Please remember that I am 6. ft high & require rather long bracers."

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   5 June 1877
letters.summary: Sends quotation from Lamarck’sPhilosophie zoologique[(1809), 2: 318] on effects of habit.

letters.title: To Charles Bradlaugh   6 June 1877
letters.summary: CD would prefer not to be a witness in court. In any case CD’s opinion is strongly opposed to that of CB and Annie Besant. Has read only notices of their book [Charles Knowlton,Fruits of philosophy, with preface by the publishers A. Besant and C. Bradlaugh (1877)] but believes artificial checks to the natural rate of human increase are very undesirable and that the use of artificial means to prevent conception would soon destroy chastity and, ultimately, the family.

letters.title: From D. T. Fish   6 June 1877
letters.summary: Sends holly specimens.

letters.title: To [Charles Roberts?]   6 June 1877
letters.summary: Sends six photographs of himself as a contribution to correspondent’s charity.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   6 June 1877
letters.summary:
Sends MS notes on intercrossing.

Describes different reactions of rabbits and guinea-pigs to stinging nettles.

Has made a number of grafts at Kew.

Encloses notes on natural selection; discussion of factors mitigating the swamping influence of intercrossing on incipient variations.

letters.title: From C. F. Martins   7 June 1877
letters.summary:
All young intelligent French naturalists support CD. But the professors are afraid of being called materialists, atheists, or communists.

A paper of his ["Sur l’origine paléontologique",C. R. Hebd. Acad. Sci.84 (1877): 534–7] met with silence, except from Bureau. If only France had become Protestant!

letters.title: To ?   7 June 1877
letters.summary: Thanks correspondent for his essay and kind allusions [toCross and self-fertilisation].

letters.title: To Edward Atkinson   9 June 1877
letters.summary: Pleased that a Grace has been submitted to confer on CD an honorary LL.D.; hopes his health will permit him to attend the ceremony.

letters.title: To L. H. Morgan   9 June 1877
letters.summary: Thanks LHM for hisAncient society[1877].

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [10 June 1877]
letters.summary:
Asks FD to forward some eczema mixture to Southampton for him

and to hunt out notes on earthworm activity at Beaulieu Abbey.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   10 June 1877
letters.summary: Has two young friends who wish to call on CD.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   11 June 1877
letters.summary: Lists the tasks he has completed; sends on letter from Romanes; news of Bernard.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   11 June [1877]
letters.summary:
Discusses effects of natural selection. Discusses absence of blending between geographical races as a problem. Discusses effect of natural selection on productivity of an organism.

Comments on GJR’s review of Grant Allen’s book [Physiological aesthetics(1877)].

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   13 June 1877
letters.summary:
Cites a misprint inOrchids.

Asks how longForms of flowerswill be, and publication date.

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   13 June [1877]
letters.summary: Forwards a copy of his bookDiseases of women[1877].

letters.title: From ?   13 June 1877
letters.summary: Objects to the passage about the Irish quoted by CD inDescent[1: 174].

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [14 June? 1877]
letters.summary: Forwards letters.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   14 June 1877
letters.summary: JDH has to entertain the Emperor of Brazil [Pedro II], who wants to meet CD.

letters.title: To Lawson Tait   15 June [1877]
letters.summary:
Thanks RLT for his work,Diseases of women.

CD is also interested by RLT’s letter reporting a cat rearing chickens. "What a wonderful instinct is the maternal one."

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   16 June [1877]
letters.summary: CD cannot see the Emperor of Brazil because he is in Southampton, but he sends sincere respects for the Emperor’s role in assisting science.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   16 June 1877
letters.summary: JDH finds the Emperor, once an energetic man, all used up.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   16 June [1877]
letters.summary:
Galton agrees with GJR about rudimentary organs.

GJR’s note referred to possibility of selection acting on organic types as distinguished from individuals.

Thinks Grant Allen has not made out his point [inPhysiological aesthetics(1877)], but his fundamental principle probably has much truth.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   17 June [1877]
letters.summary:
Forms of flowerswill soon be published and is not a long book.

Does not suppose he will publish any more books, "though perhaps a few more papers". He "cannot endure being idle, but Heaven knows whether I am capable of any more good work".

Erratum JVC sent was due to a printer’s error after he had seen last proofs.

letters.title: From C. H. Blackley   18 June 1877
letters.summary: Asks if phosphoric acid could have killedDroserahe received in a matchbox.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   18 June 1877
letters.summary: JDH recounts circumstances of his receiving Star of India (K.C.S.I.).

letters.title: From Emile Alglave   21 June 1877
letters.summary: Concerning the publication of a French edition ofCoral Reefs.

letters.title: To G. C. Robertson   22 June [1877]
letters.summary: Has no objection to the flattering wish of theCologne Gazette[to publish a translation of "Sketch of an infant",Collected papers2: 191–200], but wishes the editor had first read the article. Still doubts it was worthy of admission toMind.

letters.title: From Clipson Wray   22 June 1877
letters.summary:
States that the sheep of the Cape will produce twins only when herbage is plentiful before rutting-time.

Makes some observations on bustards and baboons.

letters.title: To G. C. Robertson   24 June [1877]
letters.summary: Asks permission for French translation [of "Biographical sketch of an infant"].

letters.title: To ?   24 June [1877]
letters.summary:
Advises correspondent on adopting a career; "each person shd. follow his natural bent & improve his special abilities".

Strongly recommends study of J. S. Mill’sLogic.

His own zeal for science was most stimulated by Herschel’sIntroduction to the study of natural philosophy.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   25 June 1877
letters.summary:
Emperor of Brazil continues to press JDH for a meeting with CD.

JDH’s daughter, Harriet, marries W. T. Thiselton-Dyer.

letters.title: From G. G. Bianconi   26 June 1877
letters.summary: Having just readClimbing plants, wishes CD to have enclosed pamphlets, one on cucumbers from 20 years ago, and another on movement in vegetables, also very old.

letters.title: To Otto Busch   26 June 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks OB for his work on Schopenhauer [Arthur Schopenhauer. Beitrag zu einer Dogmatik der Religionslosen(1877)]

and for his remarks on bees and clover. When CD spoke, last spring, of the few seeds produced by red clover, he supposed it was due to rarity of humble-bees.

letters.title: From Alfred Martinelli   26 June 1877
letters.summary: Reports an annual bean plant that formed a tuber and is now growing in the second year.

letters.title: From L. H. Morgan   26 June 1877
letters.summary: Criticises Herbert Spencer’sPrinciples of sociology, particularly for its treatment of the family, for its superficiality, and for its dependence on J. F. McLennan’s views on exogamy. Americans are coming to see Spencer’s ideas as too broad.

letters.title: To ?   26 June [1877]
letters.summary: Asks for a copy [of an unknown item] to be sent to Down.

letters.title: From C. E. Bessey   28 June 1877
letters.summary: Has heard through Asa Gray of CD’s interest in his work onLithospermumandOxalis. Thinks dimorphism inOxalisis but early stage toward complete separation of sexes.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   29 June 1877
letters.summary: Explains the delay in publishing [Forms of flowers].

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   30 June [1877]
letters.summary: Has not heard from Appleton about an American edition [ofForms of flowers]. Asks how many copies Murray is printing.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   30 June 1877
letters.summary:
CD interested in EK’s argument against belief that sense of colour has been recently acquired by man. Describes his observations of the difficulty his own children had in distinguishing, or naming, colours.

Adds that it appeared to him the gustatory sense of his children, when young, differed from that of grown-up persons.

letters.title: From William Roberts   30 June 1877
letters.summary: He is delivering address at the British Medical Association’s Manchester meeting ["Address in medicine",Br. Med. J.(1877) pt 2: 168–73]. Will develop theme that parasites are variations of common types, e.g.,Bacillus anthracesis a variant ofB. subtilis. Asks for more examples.

letters.title: From C. W. Thomson   30 June 1877
letters.summary: Wants CD’s advice on who would undertake describing the Crustacea from theChallengerexpedition [1872–6].

letters.title: To Alfred Espinas   [before 1 July 1877]
letters.summary: As AE hardly admits evolution, they view all subjects differently.

letters.title: From Oscar Comettant   1 July 1877
letters.summary: Circular letter advertising Ernest Lavigne’s scheme to educate wealthy foreign children in Paris.

letters.title: From Alfred Espinas   1 July 1877
letters.summary: On painful state of CD’s reception in France.

letters.title: From Thomas Meehan   1 July 1877
letters.summary: Credits himself with stimulating most of the American work on plant cross-fertilisation. Sends his review ofCross and self-fertilisation[inPenn Monthly(June 1877)]. Suggests CD, A. Gray, and TM now agree on the extent of self-fertilisation in nature.

letters.title: From R. I. Lynch   [July 1877 or later]
letters.summary: Cotyledon sleep movement inHaematoxylon.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   2 July 1877
letters.summary: "Young Mr Appleton", when in London, told Murray’s to send a set of stereotype plates [ofForms of flowers]. A printing of 1000 copies has been ordered for the English edition.

letters.title: From Arnold Dodel-Port   3 July 1877
letters.summary: Sends CD lithograph plates as examples of a book he hopes to publish.

letters.title: From Hermann Hoffmann   4 July 1877
letters.summary: Reports monstrousPapaver hybridumnot mentioned in M. T. Masters’Teratology[1869].

letters.title: From Max Schlesinger   4 July 1877
letters.summary: Thanks CD for allowing him to translate his paper ["Biographical sketch of an infant"] for theCologne Gazette. Sends copies.

letters.title: To ?   4 July [1877]
letters.summary: Passes judgment on photo of embryological interest.

letters.title: To Constantin James   5 July 1877
letters.summary: Thanks him for his book [Du Darwinisme ou l’homme singe(1877)] and letter.

letters.title: To Thomas Meehan   5 July [1877]
letters.summary:
Thanks for review. Fears "we must agree to differ".

Health weak. Not worth TM’s time to visit.

letters.title: From John Brigg   6 July 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for account of F. A. Pouchet’s experiments. Cannot yet dispute his conclusions.

Continues experiments on the colour of goldfish as affected by light and presence of plants.

letters.title: To Arnold Dodel-Port   6 July 1877
letters.summary: Thanks AD-P for plates [from Arnold and Carolina Dodel-Port,Atlas der Botanik(1878–83)]. Will be useful to all who teach botany.

letters.title: From William Preyer   6 July 1877
letters.summary: Asks for CD’s "Sketch of an infant" [Collected papers2: 191–200]. He has made observations on new-born children and mammals to determine what behaviour is inherited and what acquired.

letters.title: From C. L. Bernays   7 July 1877
letters.summary:
Has enjoyed CD’s last publications, especially on self-fertilisation of plants.

Believes a visit by CD to the U. S. would do much to promote his theories.

Reports on American campaign against locusts [by C. V. Riley].

letters.title: To [a bookseller?]   [7 July?] 1877
letters.summary: Asks for Tom. 23 of theBulletin de la Soc. Bot. de Franceto be purchased for him.

letters.title: To William Preyer   8 July 1877
letters.summary:
Discusses inheritance.

Has WP heard of Douglas Spalding’s experiments of blindfolding chickens ["Instinct – with original observations on young animals",Rep. BAAS42 (1872): 141–3]?

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   9 July 1877
letters.summary:
Asks permission to print translation of "A biographical sketch of an infant" [Collected papers2: 191–200] inKosmos.

Notes divisions among German Darwinists.

letters.title: To L. H. Morgan   9 July [1877]
letters.summary: CD admires Herbert Spencer’s genius but not his "deductive style" of expression.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   9 July [1877]
letters.summary:
Asks for advice on how to care for previously sent species.

Occurrence of "bloom".

letters.title: From George Bentham   10 July 1877
letters.summary: Thanks CD forForms of flowers. Comments on the chapter on cleistogamic flowers; offers some corrections.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   11 July [1877]
letters.summary:
EK may publish a translation [of "Sketch of an infant"] if he wishes, but CD hardly thinks it deserves the honour.

Glad to hear thatKosmossucceeds fairly well; has found several articles interesting.

letters.title: To George Bentham   12 July 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks GB for corrections to chapter on cleistogamic flowers [Forms of flowers].

Asks for his opinion on "bloom"-producing plants in different climates.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [12 or 19 July 1877]
letters.summary:
Discusses an experiment.

His dogs appear to have rabies.

letters.title: From Daniel Oliver   12 July 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks forForms of flowers.

Alexander Dickson would like to know whether anyone has described the epidermal cells lining the pitcher ofCephalotus.

letters.title: From George Bentham   [after 12 July 1877]
letters.summary: Answers CD’s query on "bloom".

letters.title: To G. C. Robertson   13 July [1877]
letters.summary: Thanks for offprints [of "Sketch of an infant",Collected papers2: 191–200]. Several Germans have asked permission to translate it.

letters.title: From C. G. Semper   13 July 1877
letters.summary: Sends work on dorsal eyes ofOnchidium["Über Schneckenaugen",Arch. Mikrosk. Anat.14 (1877): 118–24]. Comments on work.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   14 July 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for permission to print ["Sketch of an infant"] inKosmos.

Discusses children’s ability to distinguish colours.

Describes disagreements among German supporters of CD. Discusses reaction of German protestants to Darwinism.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   14 July [1877]
letters.summary: "Frank and I are working very hard on ""bloom"" and sleep" [movements]. Asks for succulent species for experiment.

letters.title: To Rudolph Ludwig   [16 July 1877]
letters.summary: Thanks RABL for his book on crocodiles [Fossile Crocodiliden(1877)].

letters.title: From W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   16 July 1877
letters.summary: Is forwarding several plants requested by CD.

letters.title: To C. G. Semper   18 July 1877
letters.summary: Thanks for CGS’s work [“Über Schneckenaugen” (1877)].

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   18 July [1877]
letters.summary:
Thanks him for various plants sent for experiments.

Frank [Darwin] has been feedingDroserameat to study differences between fed and unfed plants.

letters.title: From W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   18 July 1877
letters.summary: Has sentMimosa. The horticultural and physiologicalMimosaisM. albida, which has a western distribution, rather thanM. sensitivaas it is commonly called in error.

letters.title: From Adam Fitch   20 July 1877
letters.summary: Queries about cauliflowers.

letters.title: To H. H. M. Herbert   20 July 1877
letters.deprecated: Henry Howard Molyneux Herbert, 4th earl of Carnarvon
letters.recipient: Henry Howard Molyneux Herbert, 4th earl of Carnarvon
letters.summary: With 88 others signs a letter supporting the representation of natives in the legislative assembly of the Union of South Africa.

letters.title: To J. M. F. Ludlow   20 July [1877]
letters.summary: Writes as a trustee of the Down Friendly Society. Hopes the Society will soon be permitted to distribute its surplus funds, as there is agitation to dissolve the club and divide its assets.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   22 July [1877]
letters.summary:
Describes experiments on sensitivity of plant leaves to water.

Frank [Darwin] has found thatDroseraleaves fed with meat contain more starch.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   23 July 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks CD forForms of flowers.

Further objections to "voluntary" sexual selection. Believes that he can explainallthe phenomena of sexual ornaments and colours by laws of development aided by simple natural selection.

Excited by Thomas Belt’s "oceanic glacier river-damming" hypothesis. The last paper, "Glacial period in the Southern Hemisphere" in theQuarterly Journal of Scienceis particularly fine.

letters.title: From J. F. McLennan   24 July 1877
letters.summary:
Asks for details on CD’sDescentreferences to female infanticide.

JFM’s work on the laws of incest finds strong evidence for man’s relation to animals.

letters.title: From W. G. Smith   24 July 1877
letters.summary: Reports a fossil fungus, complete with fossil zoospores, within the vascular bundles of aLepidodendronfrom the Coal Measures. The genus isPythiumand it appears no different from living species.

letters.title: From R. I. Lynch   25 July 1877
letters.summary: List of plants sent.

letters.title: From W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   25 July 1877
letters.summary: Is acquiring some "maritime and glaucous" plants for CD.

letters.title: To F. J. Cohn   26 July 1877
letters.summary: Comments on paper by Francis Darwin ["Glandular hairs of the common teasel",Q. J. Microsc. Sci.17 (1877): 169–74, 245–72].

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   26 [July 1877]
letters.summary:
Thanks for the plants.

Is doubtful whether he will make out anything about "bloom".

letters.title: From A. H. Sayce   27 July 1877
letters.summary: Having read CD’s article inMind["Biographical sketch of an infant",Collected papers2: 191–200], AHS questions CD about the child’s first attempts at speech, hoping to throw light on the origin of language.

letters.title: From W. G. Smith   27 July 1877
letters.summary: Has examined some sea-kale and iris leaves sent by CD and does not think the scars are caused by fungus but rather through the action of insects. Feels "bloom" may protect leaves from such insect attack.

letters.title: From R. I. Lynch   [before 28 July 1877]
letters.summary: Sleep movements ofAverrhoa bilimbileaves.

letters.title: From R. I. Lynch   [before 28 July 1877]
letters.summary: Sleep movements ofAverrhoa bilimbi.

letters.title: To Bartholomaeus von Carneri   28 July 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks BvC for his letter and will read the references concerning instinct.

"I can see that the discussion of the Philosophy of Evolution is at present very important."

letters.title: To A. H. Sayce   28 July 1877
letters.summary: Thinks "mum" comes from shutting the mouth repeatedly as a sign of wanting to eat.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   28 July [1877]
letters.summary: Thanks R. I. Lynch for his MS onAverrhoa.

letters.title: To Thomas Druitt   29 July [1877]
letters.summary: Writes as a trustee of the Down Friendly Society to ask whether the Bank will act as their agent in withdrawing funds from the National Debt Office.

letters.title: From Oswald Heer   29 July 1877
letters.summary:
Comments onForms of flowers.

Describes his work on fossil plants collected in the Arctic.

Notes work onGinkgo.

letters.title: To the National Debt Office   [after 29 July 1877]
letters.summary: Writes as a trustee of Down Friendly Society about withdrawing some funds.

letters.title: From H. N. Ellacombe   30 July [1877]
letters.summary: Sends a specimen ofSchrankia.

letters.title: From J. F. McLennan   30 July 1877
letters.summary: Sees abortion as a refinement of infanticide; all such practices originate in female infanticide. Herbert Spencer’s over-speculation.

letters.title: From A. H. Sayce   30 July 1877
letters.summary: Thanks CD for statement about children’s speech. Asks permission to quote him in his forthcoming book.

letters.title: To James Torbitt   30 July 1877
letters.summary: Makes suggestions regarding statement on potato experiments to be published inDaily News.

letters.title: From Alphonse de Candolle   31 July 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks forForms of flowers.

In hisMonographiae phanerogamarum[vol. 1 (1878)] he discusses transitional forms of dioecism in three genera ofSmilax.

Criticises CD’s use of the words "purpose" and "end", but acknowledges that in English they can mean both cause and effect.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   31 July [1877]
letters.summary: THF is seeking advice regarding the selection of an entomologist to carry out some duties [apparently pest destruction].

letters.title: From D. Appleton & Co.   [1 August – 15 September 1877]
letters.summary: Statement of U. S. sales of CD’s works.

letters.title: To Friedrich Ludwig   1 August 1877
letters.summary: Much obliged for account of cleistogamic flowers.

letters.title: To W. D. Whitney   1 August [1877]
letters.summary:
Sends thanks for a newspaper abstract; will be pleased to see the paper [probably "Economy as a phonetic force",Trans. Am. Philological Assoc.8 (1877): 123–34] when printed.

Sends his own ["Biographical sketch of an infant"], saying it is of little value, the observations having been made before recent advances in philology.

letters.title: From Theodor von Heldreich   2 August 1877
letters.summary: Sends paper on Greek plants.

letters.title: From A. H. Sayce   2 August 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for permission to quote his comments; mentions some of his conclusions with regard to the early speech of children.

Thanks for [newspaper] account of American Philological Association meeting.

letters.title: To Alphonse de Candolle   3 August 1877
letters.summary:
Will be interested in reading AdeC’s paper onSmilax. The transition from hermaphroditic to unisexual condition is a perplexing problem.

CD agrees that there is much justice in AdeC’s criticism of his use of the terms "object", "end", and "purpose" but thinks "those who believe that organs have been gradually modified by natural selection for a special purpose, may I think use the above terms correctly though no conscious being has intervened".

CD and Francis are hard at work on the function of "bloom" but CD doubts that the experiments will tell them much.

Does AdeC have a decided opinion on whether plants with glaucous leaves are more frequent in hot or dry than in cold or wet countries?

Francis has been getting "striking" results from feeding meat toDrosera.

letters.title: From F. J. Cohn   5 August 1877
letters.summary:
Praises unbroken series of CD’s and Francis [Darwin]’s botanical works.

Confirms FD’sDipsacusobservations. Problem of interpreting microscopic filaments as protoplasm or as inorganic and osmotic artifacts.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   7 August 1877
letters.summary: Requests plants that show movement, and any with "bloom" living near the sea.

letters.title: To F. J. Cohn   8 August 1877
letters.summary: Asks permission to publish comments by FJC regarding paper by Francis Darwin [see11073].

letters.title: To Ludwig Noiré   8 August 1877
letters.summary: CD sends his thanks for LN’s book [Der Ursprung der Sprache] and for the obliging words on the title page.

letters.title: To James Croll   9 August 1877
letters.summary: Comments on JC’s paper ["On the tidal retardation argument for the age of the earth",Rep. BAAS(1876): 88–9].

letters.title: To Theodor von Heldreich   9 August 1877
letters.summary: Obliged for essay on plants of Greece.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   9 August [1877]
letters.summary:
Comments on GJR’s papers inNature[see11103].

Mentions manuscript by Miss Lawless on fertilisation in plants.

Discusses work of Francis Darwin onDipsacus

and his own experiments onDrosera.

letters.title: From F. J. Cohn   [10?] August 1877
letters.summary:
Accepts CD’s offer to publish his letter, confirming Francis Darwin’s observations [seeCollected papers2: 205–7].

H. Hoffmann’s observations onAmanitacontractile filaments must be repeated.

Microscopic examination of secretory gland filaments inDipsacusleafcups. FD’s pseudopod theory ofDipsacus.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   10 August [1877]
letters.summary: Comments on GJR’s paper inNature.

letters.title: From W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   10 August 1877
letters.summary: Information on plants requested by CD.

letters.title: To Veitch & Sons   [before 11 August 1877]
letters.summary: Asks specific questions on looking after plants ofDionaea. [The correspondent’s replies to the questions are written beneath them.]

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   11 August 1877
letters.summary: Believes in differentiated nerve-tracts [in Medusa] because of experiment in which contractile waves blocked. [See GJR’s "Evolution of nerves",Nature16 (1877): 231–3, 269–71, 289–93.] Did not know author of MS wasMissLawless. Describes experiment on contractile waves inAurelia. Also studying starfish.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   11 August 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks for plants.

Thanks R. I. Lynch for information about "bloom" on leaves.

WTT-D should not write to Mr Smith about plants near seashore.

letters.title: From E. W. Black   13 August 1877
letters.summary: Encloses specimens of milk-weed with trapped insects. Indian hemp catches insects in the same way but with less success.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   13 August 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks for CD’s comments on ["Evolution of nerves"]. Admits that he may have "been too keen in my scent after nerves".

Notes effect of reversing direction of current in muscular tissue.

letters.title: From Alphonse de Candolle   14 August 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks for Francis Darwin’sDipsacuspaper.

Dislikes the word "protoplasm", because improved microscopes will uncover more fundamental substances. Also "plasma" merely hides the ignorance of modern chemists.

Expects waxy, glaucous-leaved plants to be most frequent in dry temperate climates.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   15 August 1877
letters.summary: Electrotypes of woodcuts [ofForms of flowers] are ready for Koch [of Schweizerbart]. Murray has printed 1250 copies, instead of 1000 as planned.

letters.title: ToNature   15 August [1877]
letters.summary: CD forwards letter from F. J. Cohn [11093] that provides confirmation of observations by Francis Darwin on the contractile filaments protruded from the glands ofDipsacus.

letters.title: To W. H. Leggett   19 August 1877
letters.summary: Thanks for letter aboutPontederia.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   [20–4 August 1877]
letters.summary:
Discusses plants sent for experiments and "bloom" on leaves ofTrifolium.

Sends enclosure for R. I. Lynch.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   20 [August 1877]
letters.summary: Asks WED to make some observations onAcaciaorRobinia.

letters.title: From William Ogle   21 August 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks forForms of flowers.

Suggests plant hairs protect them from insects either mechanically or by stinging.

letters.title: To R. I. Lynch   23 August [1877]
letters.summary: Asks about sleep movements ofErythrina crista-galli. Comments on movements ofAverrhoa.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   [before 24 August 1877]
letters.summary:
Would like specimen ofCassia mimosoides.

Offers books to R. I. Lynch in return for services rendered.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [24 August 1877]
letters.summary: Action of heavy rain on the leaves ofRobinia.

letters.title: From W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   25 August 1877
letters.summary:
CD’s curious observations onTrifolium resupinatum.

Describes aMarantaremarkable for its leaf asymmetry: its leaves are elliptical on one side and oblong on the other.

letters.title: To Giovanni Canestrini   26 August [1877]
letters.summary: Thanks GC for his new work [La teoria dell’evoluzione esposta(1877)]. CD regrets he cannot read Italian.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   26 August 1877
letters.summary: Counted 40 worm-holes after rain; four or five in the wall.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   27 August [1877]
letters.summary: CD is delighted with report from THF about activity of worms in Roman-British ruins at Abinger.

letters.title: From Herman Semmig   27 August 1877
letters.summary: Sends a published diary [Das Kind, 2d ed. (1876)] in which he recorded the early growth of his first child. Hopes it may find an English translator.

letters.title: From R. I. Lynch   [28 August 1877]
letters.summary: Observations on movements of leaves ofErythrina crista-galliin green-house and out of doors.

letters.title: From G. H. K. Thwaites   28 August 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks forForms of flowers.

Insects that infest and are parasitic upon the fig fruit.

letters.title: From Frederick Schwerzfeger   29 August 1877
letters.summary: Asks for a loan.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   31 August [1877]
letters.summary:
Sends a dividend.

Recommends a novel but is sure Emma will not like it.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   31 August [1877]
letters.summary:
Discusses plants to be sent to Kew.

Thanks for letter aboutTrifolium

and for R. I. Lynch’s observations on sleep ofErythrina.

Mentions letter from F. J. Cohn, dealing with discovery by Francis Darwin, that CD has had printed inNature["The contractile filaments of the teasel",Nature16 (1877): 339;Collected papers2: 205–7].

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   31 August 1877
letters.summary: Response to Wallace’s article ["The colours of animals and plants",Macmillan’s Mag.(Sept 1877)] on sexual colours and "voluntary" sexual selection.

letters.title: From Roland Trimen   2 September 1877
letters.summary: Thanks forForms of flowers.

letters.title: From Thomas Churton   3 September 1877
letters.summary: Report of child with tail and man with four nipples.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   3 September 1877
letters.summary: Sexual selection, he thinks, must be left to others to settle. "Conscious" will be substituted for "voluntary" selection. Sound- and scent-producing organs attributed to "natural", not "conscious", selection.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   5 September 1877
letters.summary:
Sends two papers on Roman ruins at Cirencester, which he asks CD to return.

Worm observations.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   5 September [1877]
letters.summary: Has made out some of the functions of "bloom", which he outlines.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   5 September [1877]
letters.summary: Further discussion of evidence for sexual selection. Prefers "conscious" to "voluntary" action. Distinguishes features that serve as charms and those that serve as challenges.

letters.title: To R. D. Fitzgerald   6 September 1877
letters.summary: Thanks for another part ofAustralian orchids.

letters.title: From J. W. Clark   8 September 1877
letters.summary: An example of inheritance confined to one sex.

letters.title: From W. M. Moorsom   10 September 1877
letters.summary: InDescent[1: 12] CD discusses intoxication among animals. South African elephants reportedly eat a plant that makes them wild.

letters.title: From F. E. Nipher   10 September 1877
letters.summary: Cites another example of inheritance of maternal impressions.

letters.title: To W. M. Moorsom   11 September [1877]
letters.summary: Thinks most monkeys would become habituated to alcohol if they could get it.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   13 September 1877
letters.summary: Sends a list of errata inForms of flowers.

letters.title: From Raphael Meldola   13 September 1877
letters.summary: Has reread copy of Fritz Müller’s letter that CD sent some time ago and would like to publish the entomological observations in it.

letters.title: From W. M. Moorsom   13 September [1877]
letters.summary: Pleased with CD’s interest in temperance. Can he quote CD? Sorry the elephant story is a myth. It fits his argument for temperance: a passion for alcohol is natural [primitive]. Only the morally developed can resist. Moral development will take a long time. Thus education cannot cure alcoholism now. Thus public sale of alcohol must be outlawed. Although he is a follower of J. S. Mill and Herbert Spencer he has been forced to this conclusion.

letters.title: From Horatio Piggot   13 September 1877
letters.summary: Criticises passages ofInsectivorous plants. Suggests plants be weighed before and after feeding to prove they have gained nourishment.

letters.title: From R. I. Lynch   [before 14 September 1877]
letters.summary: Notes the movements of leaves ofEuphorbia jacquiniaeflorain response to light intensity.

letters.title: To R. I. Lynch   14 September 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks RIL for notes.

Asks about movement ofEuphorbia.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   14 September 1877
letters.summary: Is doubtful about the publication of Fritz Müller’s letter after so long an interval.

letters.title: From L. A. Errera   15 September 1877
letters.summary: Young Belgian students [L. A. Errera and Gustave Gevaert] ask CD to read their paper, which summarisesCross and self-fertilisation. They criticise CD’s views on the comparative effects of crossing flowers on the same stem and fertilisation of a flower by its own pollen ["Sur la structure et les modes de fécondation des fleurs",Bull. Soc. Bot. Belg.17 (1878): 38–181, 182–248].

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   15 September [1877]
letters.summary: Wants aEuphorbiato test for leaf movements.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   16 September [1877]
letters.summary:
Thanks JVC for correcting a bad blunder inForms of flowers.

His health fairly good; has been able to work "pretty hard".

letters.title: To L. A. Errera   18 September 1877
letters.summary: Agrees to look over MS.

letters.title: From Wilhelm Breitenbach   19 September 1877
letters.summary: Describes data relating to variability ofPrimula elatior.

letters.title: From M. C. Stanley   19 September 1877
letters.deprecated: Mary Catherine Stanley, countess of Derby
letters.sender: Mary Catherine Stanley, countess of Derby
letters.summary: Count Schouvaloff asserts that CD’s works are prohibited in Russia. Is he not mistaken?

letters.title: From Raphael Meldola   21 September 1877
letters.summary:
Encloses Fritz Müller’s letter.

Is exhibiting butterflies in which variations in the female show a finely graded series. Believes dimorphism can be explained by the selection of the extremes of such a series and the consequent extinction of the intermediates.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   22 September [1877]
letters.summary:
Thinks the facts in Fritz Müller’s letter could be published.

Recommends August Weismann’s essay on dimorphism ["Über den Saison-Dimorphismus der Schmetterlinge",Studien zur Descendenz-Theorie1 (1875)]

and has no doubt that intermediate forms could be eliminated as RM suggests.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   22 September 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks forEuphorbia.

Asks for plants for "bloom" experiments.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   23 September 1877
letters.summary: Sends "worm journal" – observations of earthworm activity at Abinger.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   24 September [1877]
letters.summary: Thanks THF for the diary of worm activity at Abinger site.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   27 September 1877
letters.summary: Has received CD’s book [Forms of flowers]; thanks him for the compliment of the dedication.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   27 September [1877]
letters.summary:
Does not think Fritz Müller can object to anything RM has said in his essay.

Has alluded to colour preference among butterflies inDescent[1: 400–1].

letters.title: To C. W. von Nägeli   27 September 1877
letters.summary: Thanks forDie niederen Pilze(Nägeli 1877).

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   27 September [1877]
letters.summary: Thanks for Australian leaves for "bloom" experiments.

letters.title: From W. W. Bailey   28 September 1877
letters.summary: Has noticed citation of his observations in CD’s latest books; writes to add some notes on fertilisation and forms of flowers.

letters.title: To Sara Sedgwick   29 September [1877]
letters.summary: Rejoices that SS has accepted his son [William]. Judging from his own experience "life would be a most dreary blank without a dear wife to love with all one’s soul".

letters.title: From L. A. Errera   30 September 1877
letters.summary:
Sending MS.

Used Anton Kerner’s nomenclature for designating crosses.

Thanks CD forForms of flowers.

letters.title: From Sara Sedgwick   [30 September 1877]
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his kind letter on her engagement to his son William.

letters.title: From Sociedade de Geographia de Lisboa   30 September 1877
letters.summary: CD named corresponding member of the Geographical Society of Lisbon.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   2 October 1877
letters.summary: Hive-bees captured in tubes of nectary ofTritoma. Seems a maladaptation of the bees.

letters.title: To W. E. Gladstone   2 October 1877
letters.summary:
Has read WEG’s article ["The colour sense",Nineteenth Century2 (1877): 366–88] on H. Magnus’ view. Informs him of a criticism of this view and reply by Magnus inKosmos. Offers to send the article.

CD has contributed some facts on the difficulty children have in distinguishing colours (or naming them correctly).

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   3 October [1877]
letters.summary: Encloses his marriage present, which he fears Sara [Darwin née Sedgwick] will think "atrociously unsentimental", but he hopes useful.

letters.title: To H. E. Litchfield   4 October [1877]
letters.summary:
Is glad to hear R. B. Litchfield is better.

Discusses William Darwin’s engagement to Sara Sedgwick.

letters.title: To L. A. Errera   4 October 1877
letters.summary:
Approves terms used in LAE’s manuscript. Discusses relative advantages of self-fertilisation and cross-fertilisation.

Thanks LAE for pointing out erratum [inCross and self-fertilisation].

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   5 October 1877
letters.summary: About 150 copies remain ofForms of flowers.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   5 October [1877]
letters.summary: Thanks CD for present of £300.

letters.title: To J. B. Innes   5 October 1877
letters.summary: CD’s opinion of a specimen sent by JBI from an unknown tree, and the Ross-shire tale about it.

letters.title: To Hjalmar Linnström   7 October 1877
letters.summary: Gives permission to translateExpression.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   7 October 1877
letters.summary: Wants seed with large cotyledons to test for sensitivity and movement.

letters.title: From Alphonse de Candolle   8 October 1877
letters.summary:
Speculates that the function of "bloom" is to prevent evaporation.

Raised CD’s question about the geographical distribution of glaucous plants at recent botanical meeting.

letters.title: From J. D. Caton   8 October 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for acknowledging receipt of JDC’s bookThe antelope and deer of America[1877].

Castration suppresses deer antlers.

letters.title: To W. W. Bailey?   10 October 1877
letters.summary: Thanks for information, which will be useful if CD ever brings out a corrected edition of his book [Forms of flowers].

letters.title: To Alphonse de Candolle   10 October 1877
letters.summary: AdeC’s two letters on bloom will be very useful; his remarks on evaporation and absorption seem very just. CD has made few experiments as yet. The investigation has been tedious and difficult.

letters.title: From L. A. Errera   10 October 1877
letters.summary: CD has made clear that inCross and self-fertilisationhe had not intended to suggest thatautogamie(fertilisation of a flower by its own pollen) is superior togitonogamie(fertilisation of a flower by one on the same plant).

letters.title: From C. T. E. von Siebold   10 October 1877
letters.summary:
Sends article and photograph of abnormally hairy family.

Mentions death of his student, Rudolf von Willemoes-Suhm.

letters.title: To Gaston de Saporta   11 October 1877
letters.deprecated: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.recipient: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.summary: Thanks GdeS for communicating his discovery. It is especially important at a time when several naturalists have declared that development occurs quite suddenly at intervals. Joseph Le Conte in N. America urges that even new families and orders are developed within an extremely short period.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   11 October [1877]
letters.summary: Movements in cotyledons; outlines tracing technique. [A tracing of movements of red cabbage cotyledon enclosed.]

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   12 October 1877
letters.summary: Another issue ofOriginwill be needed for Murray’s annual sale. Has CD any corrections?

letters.title: From Robert Damon   12 October 1877
letters.summary: Asks whether CD considers it possible that a mollusc could poison anyone on contact, as RD has heard from missionaries about a certain South Sea variety.

letters.title: To T. M. Reade   12 October [1877]
letters.summary:
CD is occupied with vegetable physiology.

Prefers to read MS when published.

letters.title: From C.-F. Reinwald   13 October 1877
letters.summary:
Pleased CD is satisfied with translation ofCross and self-fertilisation.

Sends £20 royalties forInsectivorous plants(700 sold).

letters.title: To Robert Damon   15 October 1877
letters.summary: Cannot give information requested. Seems incredible that mere contact should be poisonous.

letters.title: To C. T. E. von Siebold   15 October 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks CTEvS for photographs of human abnormality;

regrets death of Rudolf von Willemoes-Suhm.

letters.title: From A. R. Smith  16 October 1877
letters.summary: Gives a possible explanation of exceptions to CD’s observation [Descent, ch. 7] that characters correlated with one sex tend to appear late in life.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   17 October 1877
letters.summary: Electrotypes and heliotypes can now be sent to Hjalmar Linnström, since payment is guaranteed by the Swedish Consul.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   18 [October 1877]
letters.summary:
Sends a query he would like GHD to put to Clerk Maxwell: why does a sponged leaf dry more rapidly, although sponging cannot remove the waxy bloom from the minute pores through which it is secreted?

Is very glad to hear about tides in the earth.

letters.title: From G. O. Wight   18 October 1877
letters.summary: Sends notes on expression [missing].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   19 October 1877
letters.summary: JDH has just returned from U. S., where he worked on N. American geographical distribution with Asa Gray.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   19 October [1877]
letters.summary: Interesting article by Fritz Müller on sexual selection in butterflies,Kosmos[1 (1877): 388–95].

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   19 October 1877
letters.summary:
Doubts that glands of calyx of cleistogamic Malpighiaceae serve as protection.

Some species ofSolanumbear long- and short-styled flowers on same plant.

Changing colours of some flowers may show insects the proper moment for fertilisation.

Doubts that the style ofPontederia cordatachanges length.

Sexual difference in wings of some butterflies due to development in male of scales that emit odours to excite female.

letters.title: From J. B. Innes   20 October 1877
letters.summary: JBI reports that the editor ofJournal of Horticulturehas identified the tree at Loch Carron asSambucus racemosa, red-berried elder.

letters.title: From Raphael Meldola   20 October 1877
letters.summary:
Would like to see theKosmosarticle.

Is considering producing a translation of August Weismann’s essays.

Comments on Wallace’s paper on the colours of animals and plants [Macmillan’s Magazine36 (1877): 384–408, 464–71].

letters.title: To John Tyndall   20 October 1877
letters.summary: Has read JT’s address ["Science and man",The Times, 2 October 1877, p. 8]. What JT says about CD honours and pleases him. JT’s short character of Faraday is beautiful.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   21 October [1877]
letters.summary: Welcomes JDH home from American expedition.

letters.title: From W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   [21 October 1877]
letters.summary: Hooker, just returned from U. S., saysPinus nordmannianaleaves are spread horizontally in the morning and rise during the day.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   22 October [1877]
letters.summary:
Thinks Weismann would welcome a translation.

Was dissatisfied with Wallace’s article.

letters.title: To [Agnes Taylor?]   22 October [1877]
letters.summary: CD sends £5.5.0 with a formal note "as some aid to Mrs Beke", but does not wish to subscribe for Dr Beke’s work on Mt Sinai.

letters.title: To W. C. Williamson   22 October [1877]
letters.summary:
Specimen ruined in transit.

Drosera spathulatamodified form ofD. rotundifolia.

Sends reference regardingBolbophyllum.

letters.title: From T. F. Cheeseman   23 October 1877
letters.summary:
Sends his paper onSellierafertilisation [Trans. & Proc. N. Z. Inst.9 (1876): 542–5]; contrasts it to CD’s description ofLeschenaultia[Collected papers2: 162–5].

Describes the irritability ofGlossostigma elationoideswhich he concludes is a mechanism to ensure cross-fertilisation.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   23 October 1877
letters.summary:
Loss of water from leaf surfaces; action of a still air layer.

Proposal for CD’s LL.D.

letters.title: From W. E. Gladstone   23 October 1877
letters.summary:
Accepts CD’s offer to send numbers ofKosmos.

WEG thinks the evidence from Homer’s text is conclusive that his "discrimination of colour was as defective as his sense of form and of motion was exact and lively".

letters.title: From E. M. Holmes   23 October 1877
letters.summary: Sends seeds of plants for CD to elucidate floral anatomy.

letters.title: To R. I. Lynch   23 October [1877]
letters.summary: Asks for some seeds of coniferous plants. Wants to examine their first leaves.

letters.title: From W. C. Williamson   23 October 1877
