letters.summary: Sends plant specimens for CD’s examination for genetic affinity withDrosera rotundifolia

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   24 October 1877
letters.summary: Asks for key and letter to be sent to him at the New University Club in London.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   24 October [1877]
letters.summary: Returns [unspecified] enclosure.

letters.title: To W. C. Williamson   24 October [1877]
letters.summary: Thanks WCW for sending specimens.Drosera spathulatamust be descended from some form likeD. rotundifolia.

letters.title: From Edward Atkinson   25 October 1877
letters.summary: CD awarded honorary LL.D. degree by Cambridge University. [See11212.]

letters.title: To W. E. Gladstone   25 October [1877]
letters.summary:
Sends WEG the two articles [see11163] with references.

CD thinks savages do not have names for shades of colours, which is curious since those he has known have names for every slight promontory or hill.

letters.title: To C. E. Norton   25 October 1877
letters.summary: CD and Emma are delighted with forthcoming marriage of W. E. Darwin to Sara [Sedgwick].

letters.title: From William Saville-Kent   25 October 1877
letters.summary: Enlists CD’s support for a marine biological research institution to be built soon on Jersey.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [26 October 1877]
letters.summary: Requests seeds for experiments he and Frank are doing on automatic movements of cotyledons.

letters.title: To Edward Atkinson   27 October 1877
letters.summary: Pleased the Senate has passed Grace conferring his LL.D.

letters.title: From J. P. Chesney   28 October 1877
letters.summary: Gives a detailed description of the "Colorado Giant" found near Pueblo, alleged to be a fossil man with a tail. [See also11272.]

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [28 October 1877?]
letters.summary: FD has sent proofs; nutating of Ricinus; Horace Darwin and the wormograph.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [28 October 1877]
letters.summary:
Writes again about arrangements for the honorary degree ceremony.

Has been working on tides, which he is almost certain have altered the obliquity of the ecliptic.

letters.title: From W. M. Moorsom   28 October 1877
letters.summary: Sends extract reporting elephants that get drunk on a plant.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   [after 28 October 1877]
letters.summary: Has given dates [for the Cambridge University honorary degree] to the Vice-Chancellor.

letters.title: To Emil Ertl   [31 October 1877]
letters.summary: Sends autograph and wishes EE success in his scientific studies and career.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   31 October [1877]
letters.summary: Hopes RM finds a publisher [for his translation of Weismann’sStudien].

letters.title: From W. W. Bailey   [November 1877]
letters.summary: Encloses flowers. Long-styled form may be a sport.

letters.title: To James Cartmell   [November 1877]
letters.summary: Regrets he cannot accept JC’s invitation to the [Master’s] Lodge [of Christ’s College] when he comes to Cambridge to accept his LL.D., as his health demands he stay quite by himself.

letters.title: To Horace Darwin   1 November [1877]
letters.summary: Wants HD to observe earthworm activity at Roman antiquities of Chedworth and Cirencester.

letters.title: To ?   1 November [1877–9]
letters.summary: Asks to be sent Dr. Frank’sDie Natur: wagerechte Richtung von Pflanzentheilen.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   2 November [1877?]
letters.summary: A friend of EAD’s has removed a CD letter pasted into a book given by CD to a library, and kept it lest the author think CD did not like his book.

letters.title: From ‘Bronsomerulay’ Frazier   [2 November 1877]
letters.summary: A student meeting at Edinburgh University has unanimously voted to nominate CD as candidate for lord rector, if he will agree to stand.

letters.title: To ‘Bronsomerulay’ Frazier   [2 November 1877]
letters.summary: Although honoured by being asked, regrets the state of his health prevents his standing as a candidate for Lord Rector of Edinburgh.

letters.title: From A. D. Austin   6 November 1877
letters.summary: His discovery that in the binocular vision of the stereoscope faces can be blended with decided improvement in beauty. Suggests the possibility of experiments in thus photographing the faces of animals, different races and orders of men.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   6 November [1877]
letters.summary:
Requests seeds for study of movement in cotyledons. Would love to studyWelwitschiacotyledons.

Son William is to be married 28 November.

letters.title: From G. M. Asher   7 November 1877
letters.summary: On receiving CD’s letter GMA wrote for wheat seeds to send CD. Gives information on the wheat and on grasses to suggest that variability of the soil accounts for replacement ofkubankabysaxonka.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   7 November 1877
letters.summary:
Sent rare cycad seeds for CD’s cotyledon study.

Welwitschiaseed germinated at Kew had ordinary cotyledons. JDH thinks matureWelwitschialeaves are original cotyledons.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   8 November [1877]
letters.summary:
CD and Frank working hard on cotyledonary movement.

CD suggests technique for growingWelwitschia.

Approves of J. D. Dana and of O. Heer.

letters.title: From G. M. Asher   11 November 1877
letters.summary:
Regarding CD’s inability to find a young botanist to investigate Russian wheat; comments on utter lack of organisation in scientific research in Britain as compared with Germany.

Gives arguments against CD’s suggestion that thesaxonkaseeds could have long dormancy period which would account for their gradual overtaking ofkubanka.

letters.title: To J. W. Clark   12 November 1877
letters.summary: Thanks his correspondent for his letter; hopes he will convey to the president how obliged he is for the invitation, which he cannot accept as it would tire him too much.

letters.title: From J. T. Riches   12 November 1877
letters.summary: Has studied theComparettia falcata, not mentioned inOrchids, and found it is often self-fertilising.

letters.title: From R. A. Vance   12 November 1877
letters.summary: Writes of his observations on the "valves of Houston" in the rectum, which he believes to be rudimentary organs.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   13 November 1877
letters.summary:
JDH cannot attend at the bestowal of CD’s honorary doctorate at Cambridge.

O. C. Marsh is rash to suggest all vertebrate types originated in America.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   13 November 1877
letters.summary: Asks forCassiaseed for experiments.

letters.title: To Lawson Tait   13 November [1877]
letters.summary: CD declines to write for RLT’s new journal. He is not fitted for the work and dislikes it particularly. It costs loss of time as he "cannot change with ease from one job to another".

letters.title: From J. G. Joyce   15 November 1877
letters.summary: Memorandum on Silchester. Report by IGJ of investigations carried out at Silchester with Frank and Horace [Darwin] on earthworm activity at the site of a Roman villa. Sections of vertical cuttings at Silchester, traced from the journal of the excavations of the Roman house, and notes on the same.

letters.title: To Hyacinth Hooker   [18 November 1877]
letters.summary:
Having a splendid time at awarding of LL.D.

Thanks for bananas.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   19 November [1877]
letters.summary: Deeply grateful for THH’s tribute to him at conferring of LL.D. at Cambridge.

letters.title: From E. W. Black   20 November 1877
letters.summary:
Gives exceptions to maize being monoecious, as CD claims inCross and self-fertilisation; reversion may be cause of hermaphrodite flowers observed.

Sends paper on potatoes and asks CD to republish.

letters.title: To Édouard Heckel   20 November 1877
letters.summary:
Thinks EH’s translation ofCross and self-fertilisation[1877] is excellent.

Would like him to doForms of flowers, but Reinwald is afraid to have it translated in the present political state of France.

letters.title: From Charles Hoare   20 November 1877
letters.summary: A poem in tribute to CD following the award of his Cambridge LL.D.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   21 November [1877]
letters.summary:
Asks GHD to determine whether there are worm-castings in cloisters of [Neville?] Court.

Enjoyed his visit to Cambridge. Asks for newspaper account of the LL.D.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   21 November 1877
letters.summary: He said nothing in his tribute to CD that was not strictly accurate. Has written out a version as well as he can recollect it and will send CD a copy.

letters.title: ToNature   21 November [1877]
letters.summary: Sends letter from Fritz Müller [11191] containing observations on plants and insects of South Brazil, with prefatory comments.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   22 November 1877
letters.summary:
Will look for worm-castings in the cloisters,

and will send CD items from the Cambridge papers on the honorary degree.

Has hit on a possible fallacy in W. Thomson’s theory of secular cooling of the earth.

letters.title: From William Saunders   22 November 1877
letters.summary: Sends plant specimens of a hybrid he has raised by crossing two species ofRubus. Describes procedure by which he obtained them. Cites his paper on hybridisation.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   23 November 1877
letters.summary:
Two thousand more copies ofOriginto be printed. Has CD any corrections to make?

Type forCross and self-fertilisation,Orchids, andForms of flowersmust now be broken up. If CD does not object, Murray will have stereotypes made of the three works. Asks for any corrections CD may want embodied.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [23 November 1877]
letters.summary: Asks CD if he would like to sign GHD’s Royal Society proposal for membership.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   24 November 1877
letters.summary:
Asks exact number of copies of recent printing ofOrigin.

Approves stereotypingOrchids,

but fears he cannot approve of stereotypingCross and self-fertilisationandForms of flowers. It is too soon for the latter, and he is too busy to correct the former.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   24 November [1877]
letters.summary:
Thinks he had better not sign GHD’s paper [as a candidate for F.R.S.], since he obviously is no judge of the quality of his work.

Asks if Thomson did not overlook heat generated by the crushing and folding of strata during the refrigeration of the globe.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   25 November [1877]
letters.summary:
Neptuniaseeds germinated by applying great heat. CD wants advice of Kew gardener, R. I. Lynch, on how to proceed.

Printed public oration for CD’s Cambridge doctorate enclosed.

letters.title: From John Murray   27 November [1877]
letters.summary:
Sends CD his share of profits onDescentandForms of flowers.

Wants to reprintCross and self-fertilisationbecause supply of copies is entirely exhausted.

Congratulates CD on his Cambridge honour [LL.D.].

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   [27 November 1877]
letters.summary:
Sends proboscis of a Sphinx-moth that is 22 cms long.

Discusses eleven species of butterfly which visitLantana, a plant which blooms only for three days and whose flowers are yellow on the first day, orange on the second, and purple on the third. Most species only visit the flowers when they are yellow.

Describes and draws the odiferous organs of a Sphinx-moth.

Describes a secondary sexual character of several species ofCallidryasand otherPierinæ: the costal margin of the anterior wing is sharply serrated in the males, while it is smooth in the females.

letters.title: From Leonard Darwin   28 November 1877
letters.summary: LD is supplying coloured-glass light filters for CD’s experiments.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   28 November [1877]
letters.summary: Suggests revisions in JDH’s 1877 Presidential Address to the Royal Society [Proc. R. Soc. Lond.(1877): 427–46].

letters.title: To John Murray   28 November 1877
letters.summary:
On publishing details for various CD books.

Has no corrections for new issue ofDescent[2d ed.].

Questions amount of cheque for profits.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   29 November 1877
letters.summary:
Answers CD’s query about number of copies ofOriginrecently printed. Order to print 2000, rather than 1000, was given after JM’s annual sales showed demand was keeping up.

Cross and self-fertilisationwill be stereotyped after CD’s corrections have been made.

Printer will be asked to keep type ofForms of flowersstanding, for the present.

letters.title: From W. D. Fox   29 November [1877]
letters.summary:
Congratulates W. E. Darwin, who is about to be married,

and CD for the LL.D. conferred upon him by Cambridge.

letters.title: From John Murray   29 November [1877]
letters.summary: Answers CD’s query about payment made to him [forDescentandForms of flowers] and explains the basis on which it was made. Because of CD’s wish to be paid before editions are sold off, profits must be estimated. If he were willing to accept annual statements of sales, payments based on them, and final accounting when all were sold, there would be no uncertainty. This is JM’s usual practice.

letters.title: To John Murray   30 November 1877
letters.summary: Thanks for accounts which make everything intelligible to him. Since he was glad to haveOrchidspublished at one-half of profits for himself, he believes it would be very shabby to accept JM’s new offer of two-thirds profits. Thinks it would be fairer to both to change to JM’s usual practice with authors [i.e., annual statements of sales, payments based on them, and final accounting when all copies have been sold].

letters.title: From R. W. Griffiths   December 1877
letters.summary: A sheep-breeder friend has found that he can produce twins and triplets in his flock by "a sudden supply of improved feeding stuff" at time of conception. This would appear to remove the objection CD refers to inDescentthat animals supplied with an excess of food become sterile.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   [1 and 2 December 1877]
letters.summary:
Comments on GJR’s lecture on evolution.

Regrets failure of graft experiments.

Hopes GJR will not give up on Pangenesis. Mentions article by Gustav Jäger on Pangenesis.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   1 December 1877
letters.summary: Reprint ofOriginwill bring number to 19500 – so title-page may safely read "Twentieth Thousand".

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   2 December 1877
letters.summary:
Working hard on physiology of plants.

His son George sees no reason to change his view on marriage of cousins.

George’s astronomical work is too deep for CD.

letters.title: To Jacob Moleschott   [2 December 1877]
letters.summary: Is obliged to JAWM for the honour done in sending CD hisDer Kreislauf des Lebens(1877).

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   2 December 1877
letters.summary:
Thanks for letter. Values CD’s opinion more than that of anybody else.

Perfectly astonished at reception CD got among popular audiences at GJR’s lectures.

letters.title: To R. A. Vance   4 December 1877
letters.summary: Thanks RAV for valuable letter [11232]. CD too ignorant of anatomy to form a decided opinion, but is inclined to attribute spiral folds to reversion and the valves to partial abortion of the fold. Asks RAV to verify by examining lower intestine of an opossum for the structure. If missing he would hesitate to allude to reversion. If RAV can prove the nature of these remnants it would be a conclusion of much interest.

letters.title: From Charles and Francis Darwin to G. J. Romanes   5 December 1877
letters.summary: Discusses planting onions for experiment.

letters.title: To M. T. Masters   [6–12 December 1877]
letters.summary: Reports on the flowering and growth of a branch ofEcheveria stolonifera.

letters.title: From T. A. Edison   7 December 1877
letters.summary: Offers to send green insects that give off a powerful odour of napthalene.

letters.title: From John Michels   9 December 1877
letters.summary: Sends a drawing [missing] of alleged fossil man found in Colorado. JM is certain it is a hoax perpetrated by P. T. Barnum. It was designed to conform to CD’s well-known views of man’s ancestor.

letters.title: To W. W. Bailey   10 December [1877]
letters.summary: "Many thanks for the specimens which will be very useful whenever a new Edition is required."

letters.title: From A. W. Rimpau   10 December 1877
letters.summary:
Sends his paper ["Die selbst-sterilität des Roggens",Landwirtsch. Jahrb.6 (1877): 1073–6] on self-sterility inSecale cereale. AWR was wrong in claimingBeta vulgariswas perfectly self-sterile.

Reports results of crossing wheat varieties. In the first generation offspring are always uniform; some are intermediate, some resemble one parent. In the second generation, on the contrary, he got a diversity of parental and intermediate forms.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   11 December [1877]
letters.summary:
Sends corrected sheets ofCross and self-fertilisation. How many copies will be printed? Asks whether he is correct in thinking that he has not been paid for the July printing.

Plans to correctForms of flowerswhen new edition is needed.

letters.title: To C. H. Merriam   [11 December 1877]
letters.summary: Thanks him for sending hisBirds of Connecticut.

letters.title: To E. H. Sieveking   11 December 1877
letters.summary: Would like the letters from grandfather [Erasmus Darwin] to J. A. H. Reimarus to be published.

letters.title: From M. T. Masters   [before 13 December 1877]
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his specimen of "self-containedness". Some of the bromeliads will flower under similar treatment, but MTM does not know whether they seed.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   13 December 1877
letters.summary:
Messrs Clowes will make CD’s corrections and adjust index ofCross and self-fertilisation. Of this work only 1500 copies have been printed. Edition is sold out and account is enclosed.

Of 500 copies ofClimbing plants[2d ed.] printed in June 1876, 450 were still unsold as of June 1877.

letters.title: From M. T. Masters   [13 December 1877]
letters.summary: Sends the name of a plant:Cotyledon stolonifera.

letters.title: To A. W. Rimpau   13 December [1877]
letters.summary: Thanks for letter about beet. Will strike out statement about it in MS of new edition ofForms of flowers.

letters.title: From E. A. Greaves   14 December 1877
letters.summary: Offers to sell CD a portrait of Dr Erasmus Darwin by Joseph Wright of Derby.

letters.title: From Gaston de Saporta   16 December 1877
letters.deprecated: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.sender: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.summary:
He has heard CD is about to be elected to the Académie des Sciences.

Cross and self-fertilisation, with its emphasis on insect pollination, helps explain the problem he has worked on for so long: i.e., the rapid diversification of angiosperms in the fossil record occurs in conjunction with the diversification of insects.

letters.title: From J. C. Conybeare   17 December 1877
letters.summary: JCC and his young daughter have observed that blossoms ofDrosera rotundifoliaopen in afternoon, which contradictsForms of flowers.

letters.title: To Axel Key   20 December 1877
letters.summary: Expresses his gratitude and admiration for AK’s and M. G. Retzius’sStudien in der Anatomie des Nervensystems und des Bindegewebes(2 vols. 1875–6).

letters.title: From A. W. Malm   21 December 1877
letters.summary: Thanks forOrigin, 6th ed.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   23 December 1877
letters.summary: A misprint inVariation.

letters.title: To Gaston de Saporta   24 December 1877
letters.deprecated: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.recipient: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.summary:
Such honours as proposal for election to Institut affect CD very little.

GdeS’s idea that dicotyledonous plants were not developed until sucking insects evolved is a splendid one. The suggestion that fertilisation of the surviving members of the most ancient dicotyledons should be studied is a good one. CD hopes GdeS will keep it in mind.

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   25 December 1877
letters.summary:
BJS was pleased to see CD’s son [William] and his wife at Charles Langton’s.

His own son is preparing for marriage.

Reports meeting a formerBeagleshipmate.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   26 December [1877]
letters.summary: Thanks JVC for a correction [for 3d German edition ofVariation]. He is the most accurate translator that ever lived.

letters.title: To R. A. Blair   27 December 1877
letters.summary: Asks for the wing of a goose said to have transmitted effects of an injury by hereditary descent.

letters.title: From Hyde Clarke   27 December 1877
letters.summary: Informs CD of his work on the "unity of language in its development".

letters.title: To W. C. Marshall   27 December 1877
letters.summary: Cannot allow WCM to pay extra charge for glass. Rooms all very comfortable.

letters.title: To Albert Gaudry   28 December 1877
letters.summary: Thanks AG for his kindness in sending his valuable work [Les enchaînements du monde animalvol. 1 (1878)].

letters.title: To Hyde Clarke   [29 December 1877]
letters.summary: "If you finally succeed in proving that all languages have been developed from a common root, you will indeed have effected a most valuable piece of work."

letters.title: From F. J. Cohn   31 December 1877
letters.summary:
Sends details of H. H. R. Koch’s work on bacteria, including first photographs.

J. S. Burdon Sanderson’s and Koch’s collaboration on systemic fever.

Thinks movement of Francis Darwin’sDipsacusfilaments is an artifact.

letters.title: To the Down Friendly Society   31 December [1877?]
letters.summary: Reports, as treasurer, on the financial position of the Club.

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   31 December [1877]
letters.summary: Speculation on the process by which tails have been lost; believes he has evidence from man that it is related to spina bifida.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [1878?]
letters.summary: Forwards an unspecified work for FD to read.

letters.title: To H. D. Garrison   [1 January – 31 December 1878]
letters.summary:
Regrets he was not at home when HDG called.

HDG’s observations on the evolution of the human ear are well worth consideration.

letters.title: To Édouard Heckel   1 January 1878
letters.summary: Pleased EH is translatingForms of flowers. Agrees "cowslip" and "oxlip" ought to be translated by their scientific names.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   1 January [1878]
letters.summary: Good article by Fritz Müller inKosmossupporting August Weismann’s views on caterpillars.

letters.title: To Hermann Müller   1 January [1878]
letters.summary:
Thanks HM for his review [ofForms of flowers,Kosmos2 (1877–8): 286].

Thinks HM’s previous article was very important [Kosmos2 (1877–8): 128–40]. CD will "heartily rejoice" if HM has explained the steps by whichRhamnusandValerianahave been rendered dioecious.

letters.title: From Raphael Meldola   2 January [1878]
letters.summary:
Wishes to borrow third part of Fritz Müller’s article on sexual selection in butterflies [Kosmos2 (1877–8): 218–24].

Is forwarding material on stridulation, including Prof. Wood-Mason’s paper ["Note onMygale stridulans",Trans. R. Entomol. Soc. Lond.(1877): 281–2], which should interest CD.

letters.title: To ?   2 January 1878
letters.summary: Thanks correspondent for note and specimen; they will be of use in new edition ofForms of flowers.

letters.title: To F. J. Cohn   3 January 1878
letters.summary:
Comments on discovery of micro-organisms in disease.

Describes experiments carried out by Francis Darwin on filaments ofDipsacus.

letters.title: From E. A. Greaves   3 January 1878
letters.summary: The portrait of Erasmus Darwin by Wright of Derby has been dispatched.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   3 January 1878
letters.summary:
Is dispatching December number ofKosmos.

Will read the discussion on stridulation that RM mentioned.

letters.title: From William Farrer   4 January 1878
letters.summary:
Sends cutting on origin of variety of merino sheep.

Would like references to works on breeding.

letters.title: To Karl von Scherzer?   4 January 1878
letters.summary: Discusses dates when he might meet the prince (Crown Prince Rudolf of Austria) in London, or perhaps the Prince might visit Down.

letters.title: From Hyde Clarke   5 January 1878
letters.summary: Cites language books; a comparison of them shows unity of language.

letters.title: To W. W. Baxter   6 January [1878]
letters.summary: Asks about the composition of a spermaceti ointment which he has been buying for some years "because I blackened some young shoots of plants with this ointment mixed with Lamp-black & it produced an extraordinary effect on the shoots, which I think cannot be accounted for merely by the exclusion of light".

letters.title: From W. W. Baxter   7 January 1878
letters.summary: Constituents of spermaceti ointment supplied to CD. Perhaps effect was caused by substance used to bleach the bees-wax.

letters.title: From Leonard Darwin   7 January 1878
letters.summary: LD’s chemical analysis of lamp-black.

letters.title: From Leonard Darwin   8 January 1878
letters.summary: Has been testing lamp-black for ammonia.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   11 January [1878]
letters.summary: Thinks there can be no objection to RM’s using a Fritz Müller letter [see11319].

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   12 January 1878
letters.summary:
CD and son [Francis] working on spontaneous movements of plants and heliotropism.

Has given [Raphael Meldola] permission to read extracts of FM’s last letter [not found], on odours emitted by moths, before Entomological Society [Trans. R. Entomol. Soc. Lond.(1878): ii–iii].

letters.title: From E. L. Sturtevant   12 January 1878
letters.summary: Encloses some notes on maize that may be useful.

letters.title: To Adolf Ernst   16 January 1878
letters.summary:
Thanks AE for his book [Estudios sobre la flora y fauna de Venezuela(1877)].

Asks whether glaucous plants in Venezuela are more common in drier areas.

letters.title: From Eugenio Montero Ríos and Jacinto Mesía   16 January 1878
letters.summary: CD elected an honorary professor of the Institucion Libre de Enseñanza.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   17 [January 1878]
letters.summary: In London and wishes to meet JDH.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   18 January 1878
letters.summary: Invites CD to Kew.

letters.title: From Arthur Nicols   18 January 1878
letters.summary: He has obtained further evidence that rats gnaw through lead pipes for water. CD’s opinion that they hear trickling confirms his view that they possess reason.

letters.title: From W. K. Parker   18 January 1878
letters.summary: Sorry he was out when CD called.

letters.title: From Hugh Dalziel   19 January 1878
letters.summary: A "dog fancier" and newspaper critic of dog shows, HD seeks CD’s opinion on the origin, cause, and use of "dew claws".

letters.title: From W. C. Williamson   19 January 1878
letters.summary: Insectivorous plants.

letters.title: To W. K. Parker   20 January [1878]
letters.summary: Thanks for kind note, would like to meet him.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   [20 January 1878?]
letters.summary: CD will call on Tuesday morning.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   21 [and 22] January 1878
letters.summary:
Thanks for AG’s review ofForms of flowers[Am. J. Sci.3d ser. 15 (1878): 67–73].

Thomas Carlyle’s letter about CD was a forgery.

Gives Hermann Müller’s observations onValeriana dioica.

Is unsure about function of "bloom"; are glaucous plants more or less common in arid parts of U. S.?

Observations on heliotropism.

Thomas Meehan reports that Linum perenne is self-fertile; CD thinks that he has mistaken the species.

letters.title: To William Preyer   25 January 1878
letters.summary: Thanks WP for election [as honorary member of the Medicinisch-Naturwissenschaftliche Gessellschaft zu Jena].

letters.title: From Raphael Meldola   26 January 1878
letters.summary:
ReturnsKosmos.

Thanks CD for permission to use Fritz Müller’s last letter, which contains new observations.

letters.title: From W. E. Hart   27 January 1878
letters.summary: Offers observations on pollination.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   28 January 1878
letters.summary: Has been reading Samuel Haughton on geological time ["Notes on physical geology, no. III",Proc. R. Soc. Lond.26 (1877): 534–46]. It is utter rubbish. Asks whether CD thinks GHD should write a critical note on the subject [seeNature17 (1878): 509–10].

letters.title: From John Evans   28 January 1878
letters.summary:
Asks for subscription for A. H. Everett’s cave explorations in Borneo.

Is sure CD is pleased with Albert Gaudry’s new book [Les enchaînements du monde animal dans les temps géologiques(1878)].

letters.title: To John Evans   29 January 1878
letters.summary: Happy to subscribe to A. H. Everett’s expedition to the caves of Borneo.

letters.title: From J. B. Thayer   29 January 1878
letters.summary: Is using CD’s correspondence with Chauncey Wright in his book on CW [Letters of Chauncey Wright(1878)].

letters.title: From W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   29 January 1878
letters.summary:
Information onCyclamenand other plants.

Identification of some plants.

"Bloom".

letters.title: From F. M. Balfour   [c.31 January 1878?]
letters.summary: His brother Cecil is readingCoral reefs, and, as his business involves the Keeling Islands and Torres Straits, he offers to make any observations CD might want.

letters.title: From Carl Kraus   [31?] January 1878
letters.summary: Sends birthday greetings and respects.

letters.title: To Gaston de Saporta   31 January 1878
letters.deprecated: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.recipient: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.summary:
Has sent GdeS’s drawing to Hooker. He, Oliver, and Thiselton-Dyer have been perplexed by it.

L. Lesquereux’s discoveries in the Cincinnati Lower Silurian beds.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   31 January [1878]
letters.summary:
Thanks for WTT-D’s help.

Burying action of seeds.

"Bloom" on ferns.

letters.title: From W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   [before 3 February 1878]
letters.summary: The amphicarpic habit.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   3 February [1878]
letters.summary: CD at first thought GHD should not answer Haughton [see10689], but Hooker thinks if no correction is made Haughton’s error will be quoted for 20 years. CD is now inclined to agree.

letters.title: From Asa Gray 3 February 1878
letters.summary:
AG’s review of Joseph Cook ["Lectures on biology",New Englander37: 100–13].

Encourages CD to work at heliotropism.

Thinks Thomas Meehan is as "rattle-brained" as Joseph Cook.

[A damaged fragment cut from this letter is pinned to11051.]

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   3 February [1878]
letters.summary:
Thanks for letter. CD now has all the seeds and information he requires.

Value and origin of amphicarpic habit.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   4 February 1878
letters.summary: Sends CD’s and George’s tithes.

letters.title: To Gaston de Saporta   4 February [1878]
letters.deprecated: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.recipient: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.summary: The Permian fossil sent by GdeS has stirred up the Kew botanists. Hooker suggests it was aCeratopteris.

letters.title: From R. T. Clarke   6 February [1878]
letters.summary: Sends curious, coloured pea seeds.

letters.title: From Theodor von Heldreich   8 February 1878
letters.summary:
Thanks forForms of flowers.

Sends Greek translation of CD’s "Sketch of an infant".

Is working for Greek acceptance of Darwinism.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   9 February 1878
letters.summary:
Sends birthday wishes.

Discusses his work on theChallenger[expedition] Radiolaria.

letters.title: To Martin Beckhard   10 February [1878]
letters.summary:
Thanks him for works by Lazarus Geiger [probablyZur Entwickelungsgeschichte der Menschheit(1871)

andDer Ursprung der Sprache, 2d ed. (1878)].

letters.title: From Carl Kraus   10 February 1878
letters.summary:
Thanks for photograph.

Sends birthday greetings.

Regrets CD has not lately published inKosmos.

Requests photograph of CD’s family.

letters.title: To John Price   10 February [1878]
letters.summary:
Thanks JP for congratulations on LL.D. [awarded by Cambridge University].

Comments on Rudolf Virchow’s book [Die Freiheit der Wissenschaft im modernen Staat(1877)].

letters.title: To Milan Radovanović   [before 12 February 1878]
letters.summary: Thanks for congratulations on his coming birthday. Has nothing special to say as a preface to S[erbian] edition [ofOrigin(1878)], except to hope it is in every way successful.

letters.title: From W. D. Fox   12 February [1878]
letters.summary:
Congratulates CD on his birthday.

WDF has been suffering from bronchitis.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   12 February [1878]
letters.summary:
Thanks EH for birthday greetings.

Mentions his work on movement of plants.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   12 February [1878]
letters.summary: Thanks RM for his interesting paper ["Entomological notes bearing on evolution",Ann. & Mag. Nat. Hist.5th ser. 1 (1878): 155].

letters.title: From G. M. Asher   14 February 1878
letters.summary: Has forwarded CD’s request for wheat specimens to Mr Galkine-Wrasky, Governor of Saratoff in Russia. Asks CD to send his thanks to the Governor and to allow GMA to visit Down to explain the specimens when they arrive.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   14 February 1878
letters.summary: CD and Frank Darwin hard at work on physiology of plants.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   14 February 1878
letters.summary: Asks opinion of his proposal to Bartholomew Price to translate and publish C. K. Sprengel [Das entdeckte Geheimniss(1793)] and Hermann Müller [Die Befruchtung der Blumen(1873)] in one volume.

letters.title: From James Houston   14 February 1878
letters.summary: Praise forDescentwith slight criticism of CD’s opinion that racial divergence occurred after the continents were settled.

letters.title: To J. B. Thayer   14 February 1878
letters.summary: Acknowledges safe return of Chauncey Wright’s letters. Has no objection to JBT’s publishing extracts from CD’s letters to Wright. [See11338.]

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   15 February 1878
letters.summary:
Supports idea to translate C. K. Sprengel, but opposes publishing it together with H. Müller because this would raise price of Müller’s useful book.

Confirms JDH’s observation that only tip of cabbage radicle shows geotropism.

letters.title: From G. M. Asher   16 February 1878
letters.summary:
Apologises for taking liberty of request made in previous letter.

Tells CD ways in which large box of wheat specimens might be shipped from St Petersburg.

letters.title: To M. N. Galkin-Vraskoi   16 February 1878
letters.summary: CD has been informed by G. M. [Asher] that G-W has undertaken the shipment of "Froment des Steppes" for examination. He is most grateful. [See11361.]

letters.title: From Gaston de Saporta   16 February 1878
letters.deprecated: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.sender: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.summary:
Discusses the difficulty of reconstructing angiosperm phylogeny.

Discovery of polar fossil plants helps explain migrations.

Hooker has identification of GdeS’s Permian fossil.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   16 February [1878]
letters.summary: WantsTrifolium resupinatumfor "bloom" experiment.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   17 February [1878]
letters.summary: Heterostyly inLinum perenne. Believes the American form may be a distinct species.

letters.title: From T. M. Reade   18 February 1878
letters.summary:
TMR believes rate of limestone formation is same now as in past.

He expects his address [of 10 Oct 1876] on geological time [Proc. Liverpool Geol. Soc.3 (1878): 211–35], which contradicts William Thomson’s view of the earth’s age, to appear soon.

letters.title: To D. F. Nevill   19 and 21 February [1878]
letters.summary: Will call on addressee when he is next in London.

letters.title: From Richard Randolph   19 and 20 February 1878
letters.summary: A Quaker essayist and poet who seeks to reconcile science and religion sends some samples of his work.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   19 and 21 February [1878]
letters.summary:
Letter from Gaston de Saporta.

Germination of onion.

letters.title: From George Henslow   [c.20 February 1878]
letters.summary: Discusses various authors’ interpretations of the structure of the embryo of grasses.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [c.20 February 1878]
letters.summary: Discusses the structure of grass embryos; states differing theories regarding which part of the seed corresponds to the cotyledon.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   20 February 1878
letters.summary:
Reports butterfly species that apparently mimic each other and gives details of some odoriferous species.

[Letter copied in Raphael Meldola’s hand from original sent to Meldola with11449.]

letters.title: To T. M. Reade   20 February [1878]
letters.summary: Doubtful that great heat would favour development of lower organisms.

letters.title: From A. S. Wilson   21 February 1878
letters.summary: On crossingAegilops.

letters.title: To William Bowman   22 February 1878
letters.summary: Thinks WB’s proposal a very good one. CD could suggest two or three subjects for essays with respect to the vegetable kingdom, but they would require a long course of experiments "& unfortunately there is hardly any one in this country who seems inclined to devote himself to experiments".

letters.title: To George Francis   22 February 1878
letters.summary:
Thanks for the specimens: the bulbs have been planted.

He has not attended to the colouring matter of plants, but he will ask H. C. Sorby if he would like the specimens.

letters.title: To A. S. Wilson   23 February 1878
letters.summary:
Thanks for specimen ofAegilopsflour.

Comments on ASW’s papers.

Cites paper by Wilhelm Rimpau on self- and cross-fertilisation in wheat ["Die Züchtung neuer Getreide-Varietäten",Landwirtsch. Jahrb.6

letters.title: From James Torbitt   24 February 1878
letters.summary: Wants CD to forward to Chancellor of Exchequer a letter which explains the progress he has made in his potato crossing. Wants to print a CD letter to arouse public interest in the work.

letters.title: To W. H. Flower   25 February 1878
letters.summary: Encloses letter from R. A. Blair concerning goose with abnormal wing. Hopes WHF will look at bones.

letters.title: From John Simon   25 February 1878
letters.summary: Has sent CD a paper partly relating to Dr Creighton’s curious observations ["Some points of science and practice concerning cancer",Br. Med. J.(1878) pt 1: 219–24].

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   26 February 1878
letters.summary:
Asks CD’s opinion on number of copies to be printed ofCross and self-fertilisation[2d ed.]. Now that it is revised, they will stereotype.

Type ofForms of flowersstands, awaiting CD’s corrections, before stereotyping and printing of more copies.

RC regrets delay in supply ofOrigin.

letters.title: To W. H. Flower   26 February [1878]
letters.summary: Will bring photograph of goose with abnormal wing to London.

letters.title: To James Torbitt   26 February 1878
letters.summary: Comments on letter on potato experiments JT intends to publish. Will talk with T. H. Farrer concerning JT’s work. Could he undertake work if aided by moderate grant or subscription?

letters.title: From S. B. J. Skertchly   27 February 1878
letters.summary:
Sends CD a copy of his memoir on the fenland [Geology of the fenland(1877)].

Outlines the results of his recent researches into the geological history of man, the development of Palaeolithic culture, the occurrence of Palaeolithic remains in the boulder-clays of eastern England, and their relation to glacial and inter-glacial periods.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   28 February 1878
letters.summary: CD’s quest for Government support for potato experiments by James Torbitt.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   [28 February 1878]
letters.summary: THF would do a good deal if he gets Agricultural Society to rear cross-fertilised seeds. Society excellent channel for distribution of fungus-proof variety [of potato]. If James Torbitt will carry on work another year, CD will offer him £100.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   28 [February 1878]
letters.summary: CD solicits JDH’s aid in obtaining Government funds for James Torbitt’s efforts to breed disease resistance in potatoes.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   28 February 1878
letters.summary: Thanks for letter. Prepared to continue experiments if aided. Thinks of distributing new [potato] varieties. Believes seeds should be planted this spring.

letters.title: To James Torbitt   [28 February 1878]
letters.summary: T. H. Farrer will consider which department of Government to apply to [for funds for potato experiments]. Government will probably ask Hooker for advice, so CD has written to him. How much money does JT need?

letters.title: From A. S. Wilson   28 February 1878
letters.summary:
Fertilisation of wheat.

Would like to borrow Wilhelm Rimpau’s papers.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [after 28 February 1878]
letters.summary: He is getting some of the Heracleum seed sowed and the Cycas planted. Does CD want anything done with the potatoes sent by James Torbitt?

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [1 March 1878]
letters.summary: CD again asks JDH to support Torbitt’s project to breed disease-resistant potatoes. He has also sought support of Farrer, Duke of Richmond, and James Caird.

letters.title: To Sara Darwin   [1 March 1878]
letters.summary: Hopes to visit [Sara and William] later in the year.

letters.title: To James Torbitt   1 March 1878
letters.summary: T. H. Farrer has talked to James Caird. He believes Royal Agricultural Society will cultivate JT’s seeds. CD pledges £100 for JT’s own experiments.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   2 March 1878
letters.summary: Describes James Torbitt’s plan for producing disease-resistant potato varieties. [Letter is an earlier version of11406.]

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   2 March 1878
letters.summary: Supports Torbitt. Keenly aware of danger of growing crops from a single variety. Torbitt’s paper to Belfast BAAS meeting ["On the potato-disease",Rep. BAAS44 (1874): 134] was sat upon.

letters.title: From John Michels   2 March 1878
letters.summary: Describes a post-mortem dissection of a chimpanzee’s brain. The several doctors who observed it were struck by its resemblance to the human brain.

letters.title: To S. B. J. Skertchly   2 March 1878
letters.summary: Thanks for letter. Comments on SBJS’s research on Palaeolithic flint tools.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   [after 2 March 1878]
letters.summary: Forwards letter from James Caird concerning funds for potato experiments. CD will correct his letter to THF [11389] and then forward it to Hooker for his opinion.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [3 or 4 March 1878]
letters.summary:
His attempts to obtain a Government grant for Torbitt seem hopeless.

CD is suffering from constant swimming of the head.

letters.title: To John Tyndall   3 March [1878]
letters.summary:
Sends W. K. Clifford subscription.

Has been unwell and hardly able to do anything. Has seen Andrew Clark.

letters.title: From James Caird   4 March 1878
letters.summary: Returns CD’s letter [11389] of which he has kept a copy.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   [4 March 1878]
letters.summary: Agricultural Society will not do potato experiments. Torbitt telegraphs that seeds to be sown tomorrow. Memorial with a few signatures might get grant from Government. Hooker believes plan the right one.

letters.title: To W. H. Flower   [4 March 1878]
letters.summary:
Has been poorly.

Comments on goose with abnormal wing.

letters.title: From S. B. J. Skertchly   4 March 1878
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his expression of interest in SBJS’s work. His researches on the age and divisions of the Palaeolithic period will be published soon by the Geological Survey [On the manufacture of gun-flints, the methods of excavating for flint, the age of Palaeolithic man, etc.(1879)].

letters.title: To James Torbitt   4 March 1878
letters.summary: No use in thinking about Royal Agricultural Society. William Carruthers, botanist of Society, thinks attempt hopeless. T. H. Farrer and James Caird are thinking of application to Government. Makes suggestions about experiments [on potatoes].

letters.title: From James Grant   6 March 1878
letters.summary: As a believer in the existence of God from the evidence of nature, he is somewhat staggered by CD’s and Tyndall’s books. Asks CD to tell him whether the doctrine of descent of man destroys the evidence of the existence of a God looked at through natural phenomena.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   6 March 1878
letters.summary: Problems of continuing with his crossing experiments; financial help from CD.

letters.title: To A. S. Wilson   6 March 1878
letters.summary: Thanks for essays by ASW ["Experiments with turnip seeds",Trans. Bot. Soc. Edinburgh13 (1876–9): 25–39, and a short notice, "Experiments in singling turnips"] andAegilopsseed.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   7 March 1878
letters.summary: If THF and James Caird [Enclosure Commissioner] approve of enclosed letter, CD will send it to Hooker.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   7 March 1878
letters.summary: CD’s gardener says not to sow onion seeds until middle of March. Should he risk sowing them at once?

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   9 March 1878
letters.summary: Believes letter from CD endorsed by JDH will virtually guarantee Government or private support for Torbitt’s experiments. Queries experimental procedure.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   9 March 1878
letters.summary: Caird agrees that there will be no difficulty in getting finances.

letters.title: From Anton Schobloch   9 March 1878
letters.summary: Asks CD to explain why there are hermaphrodites.

letters.title: From Anton Stecker   9 March 1878
letters.summary: Intends to translateOriginandDescentinto Bohemian to be published at Prague; asks CD’s permission to do so.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   11 March 1878
letters.summary: Has returned letter to Caird and dispatched corrected letter to Hooker [11406] [concerning potato experiments].

letters.title: To James Grant   11 March 1878
letters.summary: The strongest argument for the existence of God is the intuitive feeling that there must have been an intelligent beginner of the universe; "but then comes the doubt and difficulty whether such intuitions are trustworthy". CD is forced to leave the problem insoluble. "No man who does his duty has anything to fear, and may hope for whatever he earnestly desires."

letters.title: To James Torbitt   11 March [1878]
letters.summary: T. H. Farrer and James Caird think it would be less trouble to get subscription from rich agriculturists than from Government. CD thinks it utopian to hope to raise variety of potatoes from seed; must be propagated from tubers.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   12 March 1878
letters.summary:
Has written to Farrer in support of Torbitt’s grant.

Resistance of Liberian coffee to "fly" and susceptibility to fungus.

letters.title: To Frederick Smith   12 March 1878
letters.summary: Sends FS some specimens of harvesting ants along with the observations of their habits made by Mary Treat. If the facts are new, he believes that Mrs Treat would be gratified by their being mentioned before the Entomological Society. [See11422.]

letters.title: From Grant Allen   13 March [1878]
letters.summary:
Sends MS of his paper, "On the coloration of flowers and fruits", filling a gap in CD’s theory relating to these structures, and asks for CD’s comments.

Plans a book on colour sense.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   13 March 1878
letters.summary: Hooker approves of Torbitt’s plan [concerning potato experiments]. Torbitt, wine and spirit merchant in Belfast, highly respectable.

letters.title: To Anton Stecker   13 March 1878
letters.summary: Authorises publication of a Bohemian edition ofOrigin.

letters.title: From Frederick Smith   14 March 1878
letters.summary: Thanks CD for specimens of, and curious facts on, the "harvesting ant".

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   14 March 1878
letters.summary: CD gives his opinion on how the physiological laboratory at Kew should be equipped. It would be a pity if the laboratory were not supplied with as many good instruments as their funds could provide.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   14 March 1878
letters.summary: Talk of a subscription to help JT’s experiments. Progress of experiment; loss of fungus-resistance in varieties as they age.

letters.title: From A. S. Wilson   14 March 1878
letters.summary:
On germination of wheat.

Can supplyDroseraif CD wants some.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   15 March 1878
letters.summary: Potato crossing experiments. Encloses printed copies of letters from people who have grown his potato seed.

letters.title: From James Grant   16 March 1878
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his kind reply. JG does not feel he can rely on instinct or "intuition" in relation to existence of God. Is there no analogy between natural organisations and mechanical constructions to justify an intelligent first cause?

letters.title: To A. S. Wilson   16 March [1878]
letters.summary: Thanks for second lot ofAegilopsseed.

letters.title: From S. B. J. Skertchly   17 March 1878
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his gift of theOrigin.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   17 March 1878
letters.summary: Life history of potato varieties. Changes in fruit, flower, and seed production with increasing age of a variety.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   18 March 1878
letters.summary: Has been consulting with Mrs Lyell about the possibility of publishing Lyell’s letters. Asks CD’s opinion on the matter.

letters.title: From Grant Allen   19 March [1878]
letters.summary: Thanks for comments on paper and references to related works. Clarifies points on colour distinction between energy-absorbing (green) and energy-expending (bright-hued) portions of plants and on the influence of flower colour in modifying the insect organism.

letters.title: From W. M. Hacon   19 March 1878
letters.summary: Further codicil to CD’s will to settle £14000 instead of £12000 on each child.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   20 March 1878
letters.summary: What does Torbitt propose to do with CD’s £100; does he want another £100 now or soon?

letters.title: To James Torbitt   20 March 1878
letters.summary: Discusses sterility of potato flowers.

letters.title: From James Caird   21 March 1878
letters.summary: Success of James Torbitt’s potato experiments so far does not warrant an application for Government aid.

letters.title: To James Torbitt   21 March [1878]
letters.summary: Asks how much aid JT requires [for potato experiments].

letters.title: From Raphael Meldola   22 March 1878
letters.summary: Encloses proof of the Entomological Society’sProceedingsfor February to show the use he has made of Fritz Müller’s letter [see11319].

letters.title: From Franklin Society, Union Christian College   23 March 1878
letters.summary: CD elected an honorary member of the Franklin Literary Society, who would like to commission a life-size portrait of him.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   24 March [1878]
letters.summary: Asks RM to send a copy of the Entomological Society’sProceedingsto Fritz Müller.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   24 March 1878
letters.summary: Sales of [potato] varieties have reduced amount of money needed [for experiments].

letters.title: From James Torbitt   24 March 1878
letters.summary: Thanks for CD’s criticism and advice. The difficult question of whether varieties "wear out".

letters.title: To Sophy Wedgwood   24 March [1878–80]
letters.summary: Asks her to observe seedlings ofNeottiabreaking the surface to see whether the flower stems grow straight up or form arches, and whether they secrete water that softens the surrounding ground.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   25 March [1878]
letters.summary: CD and Frank think they have proved that function of plant sleep is to protect leaves from injury by chilling radiation. Requests plants for experiment to determine whether underside of leaf is hardier than upper.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer  26 March [1878]
letters.summary: James Caird does not think Torbitt’s success justifies application to Government. Torbitt has four acres planted with seedlings. Has sent back CD’s £100. Shall CD insist that he keep it?

letters.title: From Alfred Moschkau    26 March 1878
letters.summary:
Describes hereditary defect in ear muscle.

Discusses influence of wet nurse on infant.

Describes talking starlings.

letters.title: From W. M. Hacon   27 March 1878
letters.summary: Sending the further codicil to CD’s will.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   27 March [1878]
letters.summary: Thinks RM may like to see the enclosed [Fritz Müller letter].

letters.title: To Fritz Müller 27 March 1878
letters.summary:
Thanks FM for letter of 22 Feb [not found] on Lepidoptera. Will send it to Entomological Society to be read. FM’s earlier letters produced best discussions of the season.

Thanks for seeds ofViola.

He and Francis [Darwin] are at work on biology of seedling plants and wish to observe how the flowers penetrate the earth.

ThePontederiadid not germinate, probably pressed too much [in post].

letters.title: To Wallis Nash   27 March 1878
letters.summary:
Pleased that WN wishes to dedicate his book [Oregon: there and back(1878)] to him.

WN’s move from Down irreparable loss to the village.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   28 March [1878]
letters.summary:
Studying geotropism.

Experiments using exposure to frost to study nyctitropism are difficult to perform because species vary in frost tolerance.

letters.title: To Alfred Moschkau   28 March 1878
letters.summary:
Does not believe that nature of milk can affect character of child.

Facts about starling very curious, but CD now absorbed by vegetable physiology. Not likely to attend to animal minds again.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   29 March 1878
letters.summary: Suggests Torbitt proceed with his work for this year; if he wishes to continue next year THF will try to arrange Government support.

letters.title: To G. F. Yeo   29 March [1878]
letters.summary: Wishes to contribute to the memorial for Claude Bernard, but first wants to be assured that, in his experiments, Bernard was not reckless with respect to the suffering of animals.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   31 March 1878
letters.summary: Thanks THF and James Caird for their assistance. Will send back the £100 to Torbitt.

letters.title: From J. W. Howell   31 March 1878
letters.summary: Asks why pigeons fly in a circle.

letters.title: To James Torbitt   31 March 1878
letters.summary: Sends £100 to JT. T. H. Farrer and James Caird think they can get another £100 next year [for potato experiments].

letters.title: To Karl von Scherzer   1 April 1878
letters.summary:
Glad to hear of Ernst Haeckel’s reception in Vienna.

R. Virchow’s address ["Liberty of science",Nature17 (1877–8): 72–4, 92–4, 111–13] very arrogant.

Sorry to hear of death of Arthur Lane.

letters.title: To John Price   2 April [1878]
letters.summary:
On his discovery of ova ofFlustra.

"Pray do not call me Dr Darwin."

letters.title: From James Torbitt   3 April 1878
letters.summary: Thanks for £100; will pay for planting this year’s varieties.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   5 April 1878
letters.summary:
Observations on a sensitiveMimosa.

Comments on structure and positioning of "odoriferous organs" of moths and butterflies,

and feeding habits of butterfly larvae.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   5 April 1878
letters.summary: Review ofForms of flowers[Nature17 (1878): 445–7].

letters.title: To T. M. Reade   8 April 1878
letters.summary: It is important that notion of "small antiquity" of the earth be upset.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   9 April [1878]
letters.summary:
Sympathises with GJR on dreadful loss [of his sister, Georgina].

Can GJR visit Down?

Onions not yet up.

letters.title: From T. T. Sherlock   9 April 1878
letters.summary: Encloses some notes onDescent[2d ed.]. Discusses CD’s contention [p. 130] that natural selection could not act to increase altruistic behaviour in man; considers that the benefits conferred upon a person exhibiting such virtues would outweigh the threat to survival that such behaviour would pose.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   10 April 1878
letters.summary:
Thanks for letter of sympathy.

Would like to visit in May.

letters.title: To W. H. Flower   11 April 1878
letters.summary: Asks whether WHF has had time to look at goose’s wing.

letters.title: From G. E. Dobson   12 April 1878
letters.summary:
Sends CD two specimens ofFuchsiamonstrosities.

He is writing on the geographical distribution of Cheiroptera and can find no information on presence or absence of bats in the Galapagos. Did CD see any there?

letters.title: To G. E. Dobson   12 April 1878
letters.summary:
Monstrosity of fuchsia sent by GD not uncommon.

Does not recall bats at Galapagos.

letters.title: From W. H. Flower   12 April 1878
letters.summary: Bones in goose’s wing perfectly normal. Malformation probably due to want of balance in muscles; analogous to club-foot. Injury of the parent not reproduced in offspring, but may have led to disturbance in functions of nerves which control muscles. Would like further study.

letters.title: To W. H. Flower   13 April [1878]
letters.summary: Will ask Blair for more [goose] wing specimens.

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan  [14–20] April [1878]
letters.summary: Asks whether CD wishes to join other old "Beagles" in supporting an orphan grandson of Jemmy Button.

letters.title: To R. A. Blair   14 April 1878
letters.summary:
Encloses report by W. H. Flower on goose’s wing.

Asks RAB to obtain wings from young birds and broken wing from old one. Asks about details of injury.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   15 April [1878]
letters.summary: Regrets that GJR was passed over for membership in Royal Society. Discusses criteria applied by Council.

letters.title: From Henry Potonié   16 April 1878
letters.summary: Points out evolutionary comments by Alexander Braun in hisBetrachtungen über die Erscheinung der Verjüngung in der Natur 1849–50.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   17 April 1878
letters.summary: Would like to have some insect photographs identified; they seem to show pretty and new case of protective resemblance.

letters.title: To Henry Potonié   20 April 1878
letters.summary: Thanks for information [about early evolutionary views of Alexander Braun].

letters.title: To B. J. Sulivan   22 April 1878
letters.summary: Will be happy to subscribe to support Jemmy FitzRoy Button. Supposes BJS has considered whether it would be a real kindness to educate the boy.

letters.title: From Federico Delpino   23 April 1878
letters.summary:
Has reviewedForms of flowersinRevista Botanica[(1877): 84–106].

CD’s treatment by the French Academy.

Hypothesises that the mollusc-like mantle ofBalanusoriginates from a form of grafting.

letters.title: To A. S. Wilson   24 April 1878
letters.summary: Sends specimens of Russian wheat varietykubanka, which after sowing for two years degenerates into a different variety,saxonka. Suggests that ASW conduct experiments.

letters.title: From Leonard Darwin   25 April 1878
letters.summary: Encloses two photos [missing].

letters.title: To Karl von Scherzer   26 April 1878
letters.summary:
Congratulates correspondent on appointment to important post.

Leaving tomorrow for visit [with William Darwin].

letters.title: From Thomas Meehan   28 April [1878]
letters.summary:
Sends CD Dr Wood’s lecture on insectivorous plants.

Had no intention of antagonising CD with his observations onLinum; was anxious to account for its apparently different behaviour.

letters.title: From Edmund Mojsisovics von Mojsvár   28 April 1878
letters.deprecated: Johann August Georg Edmund (Edmund) Mojsisovics von Mojsvár
letters.sender: Johann August Georg Edmund (Edmund) Mojsisovics von Mojsvár
letters.summary: Sends the first part [ofDie Dolomit-Riffe von Südtirol und Venetien(1878–9)], which explains the coral reefs of the Triassic in terms of CD’s theory and discusses the imperfection of the geological record.

letters.title: To G. G. Stokes   28 April 1878
letters.summary: Gives a referee’s report on Samuel Haughton’s paper ["Notes on physical geology, no. IV", read 4 Apr 1878; published as "Physical geology",Nature18 (1878): 266–8]. Believes his estimate of geological time is extremely wild. The conclusion that the interval of time separating the Miocene from the present is greater than that between the commencement of the Secondary period and the Miocene "seems almost monstrous". Recommends the paper not be published in theProceedings.

letters.title: To Thomas Whitelegge   28 April 1878
letters.summary: Has not studiedGeum, but suppression of one sex is not rare in plants.

letters.title: From Édouard van Beneden   29 April 1878
letters.deprecated: Édouard Joseph Louis Marie (Édouard) van Beneden
letters.sender: Édouard Joseph Louis Marie (Édouard) van Beneden
letters.summary: Asks for CD’s autograph and photograph.

letters.title: To A. S. Wilson   29 April [1878]
letters.summary:
Thanks for specimen.

Always was sceptical of James Buckman’s experiment; heard afterwards that cruel trick was played on him.

Glad ASW is willing to look into Russian wheat case.

letters.title: From Robert Thomson   1 May 1878
letters.summary: On earthquakes, and the generation of massive sea-waves that accompany them.

letters.title: From Raphael Meldola   3 May 1878
letters.summary:
Will exhibit the photos at the Entomological Society and have them identified.

Fritz Müller’s observations on relative abundance of mimicking and mimicked species.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   4 May 1878
letters.summary:
SendsLedum, the nectar of which catches many insects.

Describes hisPrimulavarieties.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   7 May [1878]
letters.summary:
Has receivedLedumwith its captured flies.

"At present I care for nothing in this wide world except the biology of seedling plants."

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   8 May [1878]
letters.summary: DoubtsLedumwarrants investigation. Glands probably serve only to protect the flowers against crawling insects, which would not cross-fertilise them.

letters.title: From A. F. Gray   8 May [1878]
letters.summary: Found a live mussel attached to a blue-winged teal’s foot. Had the bird not been shot, the mussel might have been transported miles.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [before 9 May 1878]
letters.summary:
Recounts some figures relating deaf-mutism and consanguineous marriages.

GHD has failed to be elected to the Royal Society.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   9 May [1878]
letters.summary: CD believes few or none have attributed deaf-mutism to consanguineous marriages.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   9 May [1878]
letters.summary: CD wants some plants; asks Lynch to raise some Cactaceae for him. Observations on sensitivity and movements of radicle.

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   10 May 1878
letters.summary: Scheme for Jemmy Button’s grandson has fallen through, as he has already been "adopted".

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [11 May 1878]
letters.summary: Julius von Sachs will "swear & curse" when he finds out he has missed sensitiveness of root apex. Has been putting his notes together and the case is conclusive. [Dated "Saturday 10th" by CD.]

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   11 [May 1878]
letters.summary: Invites GJR to visit on the 18th.

letters.title: From W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   11 May 1878
letters.summary:
WTT-D’s statement perverted byTimes[4 May 1878, p. 6, on WTT-D’s Royal Institution lectures on vegetable morphology].

S. H. Vines’s work on light inhibition ofPhycomyceshyphae ["The influence of light upon the growth of unicellular organs" (1878),Arb. Bot. Inst. Würzburg2 (1882): 133–47] suggests heliotropism in green plants is independent of, and more primitive than, photosynthesis.

Heliotropism in aerial roots.

Frank Darwin’s work.

letters.title: From C. B. Clarke   12 May 1878
letters.summary: Reports curious case of dimorphism in Rubiaceae. Encloses envelope containing bud samples.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [12 May 1878]
letters.summary: Thanks for sendingNature; plans to leave on 22 May; anecdote about Bernard.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [13–26 May 1878]
letters.summary: Has had conflicting information on the movement of radicles; wants FD to experiment with them.

letters.title: To Thomas Meehan   13 May 1878
letters.summary: Criticises article by TM. "Such a manner of treating the work of other observers did not appear to me the way to encourage truth."

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   13 May [1878]
letters.summary:
Blood-red onions enclosed.

GJR to come whenever convenient.

letters.title: From Naphtali Lewy   14 May 1878
letters.summary: Believes that weakness of hybrids explains Biblical injunctions against improper unions.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   14 May 1878
letters.summary: Heliotropism. Requires some plants for experiments.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   15 May [1878]
letters.summary: Encloses Fritz Müller letter, which may be of interest [see11463].

letters.title: From Charles Layton  16 May 1878
letters.summary: Encloses statement of U. S. sales of CD’s work to 29 April 1878 and sends a cheque for balance due to CD.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   16 May 1878
letters.summary:
Has forwarded FM’s letter to Raphael Meldola.

Thanks for information onMimosa.

Would like to know howCassiabehaves in the rain.

letters.title: From Thomas Whitelegge   16 May 1878
letters.summary: Gynodioecism inRanunculus acris.

letters.title: To Thomas Whitelegge   17 May 1878
letters.summary: Will use TW’s case of gynodioeciousRanunculusif he prints a new edition ofForms of flowers.

letters.title: To R. A. T. Gascoyne-Cecil   [18 May 1878]
letters.deprecated: Robert Arthur Talbot Gascoyne-Cecil, 3d marquess of Salisbury
letters.recipient: Robert Arthur Talbot Gascoyne-Cecil, 3d marquess of Salisbury
letters.summary: Requesting permission to present a declaration against war to the Foreign secretary.

letters.title: To T. W. Higginson   [18 May 1878]
letters.summary: Glad to see TWH for Sunday dinner.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   19 [May 1878]
letters.summary: Germination of Cactaceae; CD wants seeds. Site of action of growth-stimuli.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   20 May [1878]
letters.summary: RM should take no more trouble over the subject [Otto Zacharias’ photos; see 11510].

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   20 [May 1878]
letters.summary: Will dispatch plants for Kew tomorrow.

letters.title: To W. J. Beal   21 May 1878
letters.summary: Thanks for his notice ofCross and self-fertilisation.

letters.title: To A. F. Gray   21 May [1878]
letters.summary: Thanks AFG for his interesting communication. Has sent it toNaturefor publication [see11497].

letters.title: To J. N. Lockyer   21 May [1878]
letters.summary: Hopes that the enclosure [11497] is worth printing inNature[seeNature(30 May 1878)]. A wood-cut would add interest.

letters.title: ToNature   [21? May 1878]
letters.summary: CD’s letter on wide distribution of freshwater plants and animals introduces a letter to him from Arthur H. Gray [see11497].

letters.title: From Thomas Whitelegge   21 May 1878
letters.summary: Gynodioecism.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   22 May [1878]
letters.summary: Extract fromAthenæum11 May [1878], p. 606, of R. I. Lynch on germination of the provision tree.

letters.title: From Raphael Meldola   23 May 1878
letters.summary:
Prof. Wood-Mason has examined Otto Zacharias’ insect photographs and confirmed the genera.

RM is going to work up Fritz Müller’s observations into a paper.

letters.title: To Robert Thomson   23 May 1878
letters.summary: Cannot express opinion on RT’s views on earthquakes. To do good work on that subject a man must be deeply versed in wave motions.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   24 May 1878
letters.summary: Sends some "composite portraits", including three of their family ancestors, as described inNature[18 (1878): 97–100].

letters.title: From M. C. Stanley   24 May 1878
letters.deprecated: Mary Catherine Stanley, countess of Derby
letters.sender: Mary Catherine Stanley, countess of Derby
letters.summary: Sends fragment of bone from the head of a fish called "Corbin", brought from River Plate by her brother.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   25 May 1878
letters.summary: Is glad RM will draw up a paper from Fritz Müller’s letter.

letters.title: From Blanche and Alice   27 May 1878
letters.summary: Request an autograph.

letters.title: From George Cupples   27 May 1878
letters.summary: Applies sexual selection to origin of dog race [deerhound]. Proposes descent from a large extinct dog.

letters.title: From Thomas Whitelegge   27 May 1878
letters.summary: Has found a few examples ofRanunculus repenswith stamens reduced as inR. acris.

letters.title: To Friedrich Ludwig   29 May 1878
letters.summary: Thanks FL for thePlantagospecimens. FL’s view of the stages by which the plant has become gynodioecious seems very probable.

letters.title: To Wallis Nash   29 May 1878
letters.summary: Comments on WN’sOregon: there and back(1878).

letters.title: From E. W. Fithian   30 May 1878
letters.summary: Requests, as Treasurer of the Knockholt & Chevening Footpath Fund, part of the amount guaranteed by CD and family to defray expenses incurred in resisting closure of the footpath.

letters.title: From Alice and Blanche   31 May 1878
letters.summary: Thank CD for autograph.

letters.title: To E. W. Fithian   [31 May 1878]
letters.summary: Remits subscription as requested by EWF as the Knockholt & Chevening Footpath Fund [see11535].

letters.title: To Edmund Mojsisovics von Mojsvár   1 June 1878
letters.deprecated: Johann August Georg Edmund (Edmund) Mojsisovics von Mojsvár
letters.recipient: Johann August Georg Edmund (Edmund) Mojsisovics von Mojsvár
letters.summary: Discusses EM’s book [Die Dolomit-Riffe von Südtirol und Venetien(1878–9)]. Pleased by EM’s views of geological chronology based on evolution. Thinks distribution of land and sea formerly very different. New genera and families may have been developed on isolated tracks and migrated.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   2 June 1878
letters.summary:
CactusandCycasseedlings: observations and queries.

Working hard on plant movements.

letters.title: To F. J. Cohn   5 June 1878
letters.summary: Comments on achenia ofPumilio argyrolepis.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   5 [June 1878]
letters.summary:
Sends letter and seeds from [F. J. Cohn].

Is working too hard.

letters.title: To W. H. Kesteven   5 June 1878
letters.summary: Feels WHK’s views on the origin of tumbling in pigeons are very likely correct.

letters.title: From Edmund Mojsisovics von Mojsvár   6 June 1878
letters.deprecated: Johann August Georg Edmund (Edmund) Mojsisovics von Mojsvár
letters.sender: Johann August Georg Edmund (Edmund) Mojsisovics von Mojsvár
letters.summary: Pleased with CD’s praise of his work. He agrees with CD that intermediate marine fossils are rare in the same bed. The difficulty is overcome by extensive search of "isotopic" fauna in different beds of the same "isotopic" region.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   8 June 1878
letters.summary:
Sends article on "Evolution" [Encyclopaedia Britannica, 9th ed.]. CD will be interested in Lamarck’s opinions in 1794.

Is working on crayfish and their distribution.

letters.title: From John Coghlan   9 June 1878
letters.summary: Report of an "eight legged horse" considered to be an example of reversion.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   9 June 1878
letters.summary: JDH’s scheme for lowering F.R.S. fees by creating a fund through membership subscription.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   11 June [1878]
letters.summary: Thanks for evolution article; would like to know what made Lamarck "change his front" so completely.

letters.title: From Arnold Dodel-Port   12 June 1878
letters.summary: Comments on publication of hisAtlas der Botanik[1878]. Discusses possible English edition. Draws CD’s attention to plates ofDroserainAtlas. Mentions contribution offered by Hermann Müller, and support by German professors of botany.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   12 June [1878]
letters.summary: Has received interesting essay from August Weismann on sexual selection in daphnoids [“Schmuckfarben der Daphnoiden”,Z. Wiss. Zool.(1878)].

letters.title: From Raphael Meldola   13 June 1878
letters.summary:
Would like to read Weismann’s essay on Daphnidae.

Fritz Müller’s paper on odours emitted by butterflies was read at last Entomological Society meeting.

letters.title: To Arnold Dodel-Port   15 June 1878
letters.summary: Thanks AD-P for his magnificentAtlas; hopes it will find an English publisher. Suggests Longman & Co.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   16 June [1878]
letters.summary:
Sends two pages from MS chapter on instinct. Presumes it is too late for chapter to be of use to GJR.

After train ride Baby [Bernard Richard Meirion Darwin] calls every vehicle "boo boo".

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   18 June [1878]
letters.summary: Has been observing the movements of leaves and cotyledons; sleep movements are exaggerated circumnutation. Reports some odd observations on movement inOxalisspecies.

letters.title: From Arnold Dodel-Port   18 June 1878
letters.summary: Comments on positive response to publication [ofAtlas]. CD’s approval will help make an English edition possible. Rejects suggestion that CD should subscribe.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   18 June 1878
letters.summary: Thanks for permission to use CD’s observations on instinct. Would like to use CD’s MS chapter in preparing forthcoming book [Mental evolution in animals(1883)].

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   18 June [1878]
letters.summary:
Movements of cotyledons ofOxalis.

Francis Darwin at Würzburg with Julius Sachs.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   19 June [1878]
letters.summary: GJR may have CD’s MS chapter on instinct. It was abstracted forOrigin, but CD probably will not prepare it for publication.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   21 June 1878
letters.summary: Thanks for permission to use CD’s MS chapter on instinct for forthcoming book.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [22 June 1878]
letters.summary: Describes his talk with Julius von Sachs about canary-grass.

letters.title: From C. W. Thomson   22 June 1878
letters.summary: Seeks CD’s support for W. C. M’Intosh, candidate for Chair in Natural History at Aberdeen.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [c.23 June 1878]
letters.summary: Can send FD twisted branches of some climbing plants if he wishes.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   23 June [1878]
letters.summary:
Thanks for seeds and plants.

News of Francis and Horace Darwin.

letters.title: From J. E. Taylor   25 June 1878
letters.summary: Sends CD a copy of his book [Flowers; their origin, shapes, perfumes and colours(1878)].

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   25 June [1878]
letters.summary: Asks WTT-D to identify a leaf.

letters.title: To J. E. Taylor   [after 25 June 1878]
letters.summary: Thanks JET for his book.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   26 June [1878]
letters.summary:
Asks questions related to movement in plants. The cotyledons ofOxalisoffer a promising field for study.

Wonders why Julius von Sachs thinks bloom is a protection against insects.

Encloses notes on the cotyledons ofOxalisspecies.

letters.title: From J. W. Judd   26 June 1878
letters.summary:
Sends a paper by Melchior Neumayr [‘Über unvermittelt auftretende Cephalopodentypen’,Jahrb. K.-K. Geol. Reichsanst.28 (1878): 37–80].

Plans to marry soon.

Next year he will begin a practical course in geology to supplement his lectures.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   26 June 1878
letters.summary: Progress of experiments. Wants CD’s advice on best way to cross-fertilise his plants.

letters.title: To J. W. Judd   27 June 1878
letters.summary:
Congratulates JWJ on marriage.

Thanks for essay by Neumayr [see11569].

Comments on paper by Edmund Mojsisovics ["Kleine Beiträge zur Kenntniss der Anneliden",Sitzungsber. K. Akad. Wiss. Wien Math.-naturwiss. Cl.76 (1877) Abt. 1: 7–20].

CD’s health better than a few years ago.

letters.title: From W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   [27 June 1878]
letters.summary: Name of plant:Colocasia antiquorum, Schott. =Caladium esculentum, Hort. Vent.

letters.title: To James Torbitt   28 June 1878
letters.summary: Discusses methods of fertilising potatoes.

letters.title: From W. H. Dallinger   29 June 1878
letters.summary: The results of WHD’s long series of investigations of effects of steadily and slowly altered environment on putrefactive organisms "palpably demonstrate [CD’s] great doctrine".

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [29 June] 1878
letters.summary:
Sleep ofPorlieria hygrometricaseems independent of light.

Will have lots of time for oats. W. F. P. Pfeffer’s point is that there is no growth in sleepers with joints. A. F. Batalin says there is a slight growth.

[Dated Saturday 28th by FD.]

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   29 [June 1878]
letters.summary:
Will dispatch the best twisted stems he can find.

Considers the role of the pulvinus in leaf movement.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [30 June 1878]
letters.summary:
Is frustrated to see, from a paragraph inNature[18 (1878): 242], that Charles Lagrange has got hold of the same sort of ideas as he has.

Erasmus is unwell.

letters.title: From H. S. Sanguinetti   July 1878
letters.summary: Change of address.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   1 July 1878
letters.summary:
JDH may put CD’s name down for £200 for the proposed fund.

Does JDH have a plant ofPorlieria hygrometricahe could lend to CD?

letters.title: To M. H. Truelove   1 July 1878
letters.summary:
Regrets he cannot sign a memorial for correspondent’s father [Edward Truelove], which states an opinion on a life that is totally unknown to him. Feels that Edward Truelove’s sentence was very harsh [ET was imprisoned and fined for selling "obscene" publications advocating artificial control of conception] even though CD is strongly opposed to all the views expressed.

Comments on R. D. Owen’sMoral physiology[1831].

letters.title: To W. H. Dallinger   2 July 1878
letters.summary: Has no doubt WHD’s experiments on mutation of lower organisms under changed conditions of life will be curious and valuable. The fact of their becoming accustomed to much higher temperatures than those to which they are adapted is very remarkable. It explains the existence of algae in hot springs.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   2 July [1878]
letters.summary:
Suggests FD call on Carl Semper.

Inquires aboutPorlieria: Do the leaves shut to check evaporation? Does it appear silver under water?

Explains how he thinks the pulvinus acts; wishes FD would investigate the point.
