letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   2 July 1878
letters.summary:
JDH details the subscription fund’s finances.

Has finished lecture for Royal Society on N. American plant distribution.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   2 July 1878
letters.summary: Othniel Marsh of Yale would like to visit CD.

letters.title: To O. C. Marsh   2 July 1878
letters.summary: Will be glad to see OCM at Down. If he comes Friday, he will meet J. F. McLennan, author ofPrimitive marriage, a "remarkable man".

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   3 July [1878]
letters.summary: CD contributes £200 to JDH’s Royal Society fund.

letters.title: To [G.-G. Baillière?]   5 July 1878
letters.summary: Hopes Baillière will inform Cosserat how pleased he is with the new translation ofCoral Reefs.

letters.title: To O. C. Marsh   5 July [1878]
letters.summary: Delighted to see him on Tuesday.

letters.title: From Hermann Müller   5 July 1878
letters.summary: Reports results of crosses between the two forms ofViola tricolor: 1. Female small flower crossed with male large flower yields all small flowers (cleistogamous self-fertilisation suspected); 2. Male small flower crossed with female large yields intermediate flowers; 3. Large flower crossed with large flower yields self-sterility symptoms.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   6 [July 1878]
letters.summary: Has a magnificent bush ofPorlieria. There is no vestige of bloom; CD will test for sleep movements. Reports successful experiments on temperature-induced sensitivity of radicles.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [before 7 July 1878]
letters.summary: He has been talking to Julius von Sachs about sleeping plants that move with and without growth.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   7 [July 1878]
letters.summary:
Describes sleep movements inPorlieriaand his experiments on movements of radicles.

Thaliaflowers have interesting mechanism to ensure cross-fertilisation.

letters.title: To William Spottiswoode   7 July [1878]
letters.summary: Has been approached by [H. R. Hope-]Pinker who wishes to sculpt him for the Royal Institution; asks whether WS has any knowledge of the matter.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [after 7 July 1878]
letters.summary:
Sleep inPorlieriastudied.

Oats begin germinating.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   10 [July 1878]
letters.summary: Asks for sketches of [Thalia] pistil, in which he is much interested.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   10 July [1878]
letters.summary: Has taken OCM to the photographer’s, and is sending photographs to be signed.

letters.title: To W. D. Fox   10 July 1878
letters.summary: Letter of condolence on readingTimesreport of death of WDF’s daughter.

letters.title: From William Spottiswoode   10 July 1878
letters.summary: Writes about [H. R. Hope-]Pinker, who tried to approach CD via the Royal Institution in order to sculpt a bust of him. WS advises against agreeing to sit for him.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [before 11 July 1878]
letters.summary: Refers to Charles Lagrange, who is working on the same subject as GHD, but in a fundamentally different way.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   11 [July 1878]
letters.summary:
Rejoices that "Lagrange’s case does not seem very bad".

CD is working hard at dissectingThalia. Has recovered some handiness with microscope.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [12 July 1878]
letters.summary:
Chlorophyll development in oat seedling.

Lists the sleeping plants he has seen.

Julius Sachs thinks Hugo de Vries has not cleared up everything [about climbing plants]. But Sachs has not worked on the mechanical problem.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   12 July 1878
letters.summary: Sends drawings of specimens [ofThalia] CD requested.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   13 [July 1878]
letters.summary: Thanks GHD for his drawings [ofThalia]. Some parts need attention.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   14 July [1878]
letters.summary:
Asks for list of families of sleeping plants. Believes sleep is merely modified circumnutation at a particular time of day.

Porlieriahas had no water for some time but shows no sign of flagging.

Describes the response ofThaliaflowers to touch.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   14 [July 1878]
letters.summary: Writes to say that the point on which he thought GHD’s drawings were mistaken proves to be an error in his own observation.

letters.title: To O. C. Marsh   14 July [1878]
letters.summary:
Enjoyed OCM’s visit.

Sends photographs.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   14 July [1878]
letters.summary: Movement and sensitivity of flower parts; relationship to cross-fertilisation.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [after 14 July 1878]
letters.summary: Thinks it would be a good idea to give the typing machine to Karl Semper.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   15 [July 1878]
letters.summary: A report has arrived for FD which CD will forward.

letters.title: From Thomas Whitelegge   15 July 1878
letters.summary: Has found examples of small female flowers inStachys germanicaandRanunculus bulbosus.

letters.title: To F. G. Stokes   16 July [1878]
letters.summary: Discusses "highly expressive" speech of young children.

letters.title: From W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   16 July 1878
letters.summary:
Sends specimens.

Sensitive plants.

letters.title: To Thomas Whitelegge   16 July 1878
letters.summary:
Asks TW not to send more information as CD does not expect a new edition ofForms of flowers.

TW’sStachyscase is what he calls gynodioeciousness.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [before 17 July 1878]
letters.summary:
More sleepers from green-house.

Julius Sachs’s view of climbing plants: he distinguishes between nutation to find a support and growth after support is found.

letters.title: From R. A. Blair   17 July 1878
letters.summary: Explains difficulties in supplying wings of geese. Describes injury of old gander that sired the abnormal geese.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   17 July [1878]
letters.summary:
Discusses sleep movements ofPorlieria.

Has read an abstract of Julius Wiesner on heliotropism and geotropism ["Die heliotropischen Erscheinungen im Pflanzenreiche",Anz. Kais. Akad. Wiss. Wien15 (1878): 137–40] which seems important but is puzzling.

Gives details of his observations on climbing plants with reference to comments by Julius Sachs.

letters.title: To E. F. Lubbock   18 July [1878]
letters.summary: EFL’s account of what CD has done in natural history is full and accurate and could not have been done better. He has added the titles of his later books and the name of his maternal grandfather [Josiah Wedgwood] of whom he is proud.

letters.title: To C. G. Semper   19 July 1878
letters.summary: Offers to give CGS a writing machine.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   19 July [1878]
letters.summary: Federico Delpino on mechanical movements of flower parts ofMaranta. CD’s observations onMaranta, and his eagerness to compare cases of movement and irritability in plants.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   20 [July 1878]
letters.summary:
Has offered Carl Semper the writing machine.

Speculates on the mechanism of movement in plants and their reception of and response to stimuli.

letters.title: From Thomas Druitt   20 July 1878
letters.summary: Informs CD that certain cash from U. S. investments does not have income tax deducted.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [21 July 1878]
letters.summary:
Has been investigating nutational movements of climbing plants; comments on the opinions of Julius von Wiesner and Julius Sachs. Remarks on the sleep movements of certain plants and the mechanism of tendril curvature. Is experimenting withPorlieria.

Has visited K. G. Semper’s laboratory.

letters.title: To Eugène Dupuy   21 July 1878
letters.summary: Considers Brown-Séquard’s discovery of inheritance of injury to nerves most important hereditary observation ever. Extremely interested in correspondent’s confirmation. Impressed that in reported cases of inherited injury suppuration tends to follow the injury.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   21 July 1878
letters.summary: Is sending CD the seeds of a beautifulCassiagiven to him by a friend. He sketched the unripe fruit a few months ago. This plant is rare in the area around Sta Catharina. He has found their largest and most beautiful butterflyCallidryas manippenear this tree and its caterpillars living on its leaves. Comments on how remarkable it is to find a species limited to living on a single tree in so large an area.

letters.title: From W. D. Fox   22 July [1878]
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for his condolences. Reminisces about their youth.

On the death of his naturalist friend, W. C. Hewitson.

letters.title: From C. G. Semper   22 July 1878
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his kind letter and accepts his offer of a writing machine.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   24 and 25 July 1878
letters.summary:
Notes Julius Sachs’s opinion on the heliotropism of moulds: he can see no use in the response.

C. E. Stahl is working on swarm spores which can be made both helio- and apheliotropic.

Sachs has told him that some ferns sleep, and he suspects that some grasses may move.

Sachs also feels they may be working at bloom from a wrong point of view and suggests leaves may need to keep dry in order to keep their stomata open.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   24 July [1878]
letters.summary: Does not think thePetuniais anything remarkable.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   24 July 1878
letters.summary:
Thanks for seeds

and information about earthworms.

Is working hard at movement in plants.

letters.title: To C. G. Semper   24 July [1878]
letters.summary: Pleased CGS will accept machine.

letters.title: From A. D. Austin   25 July 1878
letters.summary: Idea has struck him that might be of use to CD: that rapid changes during growth as in some plants and in insect metamorphosis may bear analogy to the slower changes resulting in the formation of new varieties.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   25 July [1878]
letters.summary:
Is forwarding the writing machine to Carl Semper.

Is glad FD has taken up his old friends, the twiners.

Hopes to get heliotropic aerial roots from J. D. Hooker. Asks FD to find out whether any moulds or roots are apheliotropic. Is puzzled by heliotropism in subterranean roots.

letters.title: From Franz Ritter von Kobell    25 July 1878
letters.summary: CD named corresponding member of the Royal Bavarian Academy of Science. [See11634.]

letters.title: From J. A. Allen   29 July 1878
letters.summary:
Explains that it was his son, Grant, who sent JAA’s article defending Darwinian origins of morality.

Comments on CD’s Canadian admirers

and asks whether Grant may visit CD at Down.

letters.title: To Franz Ritter von Kobell   29 July 1878
letters.summary: Thanks for election as a Foreign Member.

letters.title: From M. E. Johnson   [after 29 July 1878]
letters.summary: She and her father will not be idle working on worms for CD.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   30 July [1878]
letters.summary:
Comments on function of bloom.

Describes the effect of water shortage on sleep movements inPorlieria.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [30 July 1878]
letters.summary: Describes observations and experiments on the response to light ofBignonia capreolatatendrils.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   31 July 1878
letters.summary:
Burdened with Anniversary Address to the Royal Society.

Quips that even Huxley is running out of speeches.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   2 August [1878]
letters.summary: Thanks for plants and seeds; requests for more to test Sachs’s notion on "bloom".

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [before 3 August 1878]
letters.summary:
Sachs jumps to the conclusion twiners and tendrils are similar from theMenispermumthat twined without a stick.Akebiagrows down a stick; not only the free end is involved.

Sleeping plants.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   3 August [1878]
letters.summary:
Is pleased FD’s climbing work goes well.

Thanks him for information on heliotropism.

Discusses sleep movements

and his observations on the sensitivity of radicle tips.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [4–7 August 1878]
letters.summary: Experiments on effects of removing "bloom" from leaves and fruit.

letters.title: To R. A. Blair   4 [August] 1878
letters.summary: Thanks RAB for kindness. Says W. H. Flower will examine wings [of geese].

letters.title: To W. H. Flower   4 [August] 1878
letters.summary:
Encloses letters from Blair on inheritance of injured wing in geese. Says specimens have been sent.

Mentions case of pigeon born without eyes.

letters.title: From Paul Broca   5 August 1878
letters.summary: Invites CD and Mrs Darwin to stay at his home if they plan to attend the International Congress of Anthropological Sciences, 16–21 August, and the seventh session of the French Association for the Advancement of Science, 22–9 August.

letters.title: From J.-B. Dumas and Joseph Bertrand   5 August 1878
letters.summary: CD elected corresponding member in the botanical section of the Académie des Sciences, Paris. [See11653.]

letters.title: From A. S. Wilson   6 August 1878
letters.summary:
Observations on dimorphic and trimorphic plants of Scotland.

On fertilisation ofScrophularia nodosa.

letters.title: To Thomas Woolner   6 August [1878]
letters.summary: TW’s account of the Ourang is very curious. CD hopes to see the primate whenever he goes to London, but he is leaving home for three weeks.

letters.title: From George Bentham   7 August 1878
letters.summary: CD’s election to the French Academy delights GB. Nationalistic prejudices have at last been overcome; congratulates him on what is now universal adoption of his views.

letters.title: To L. A. Errera   8 August [1878]
letters.summary: Regrets that LAE went to Down for nothing.

letters.title: To J. F. Fisher   8 August [1878]
letters.summary: Agrees to read manuscript if short.

letters.title: To Hugo de Vries   8 August [1878]
letters.summary: Regrets he cannot receive HdeV at Down, because he has just left home.

letters.title: From Gaston de Saporta   9 August 1878
letters.deprecated: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.sender: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.summary: Congratulations on election to the French Academy of Sciences, Botany Section.

letters.title: To A. S. Wilson   9 August [1878]
letters.summary:
Responds to ASW’s information aboutErythraea

and about wasps onScrophularia.

letters.title: To Hugo de Vries   [10 or 11 August 1878]
letters.summary: Arranges for HdeV to call.

letters.title: To George Bentham   10 August [1878]
letters.summary: GB’s note has given him more pleasure than his election to the French Academy.

letters.title: From Alphonse de Candolle   10 August 1878
letters.summary: Congratulations on CD’s long-overdue election to the French Academy of Sciences.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   11 August [1878]
letters.summary: CD’s election to Botany Section of French Academy amuses him, because he "doesn’t know the characters of a single natural order!".

letters.title: To J.-B. Dumas and Joseph Bertrand   12 August [1878]
letters.summary: Acknowledges his election as a Corresponding Member of the Academy.

letters.title: From L. A. Errera   12 August 1878
letters.summary:
Regrets not seeing CD.

Congratulates CD on election to French Academy.

letters.title: From Hermenegildo Giner de los Ríos   12 August 1878
letters.summary: The secretary of the Comision de Propaganda of the Institución Libre de Enseñanza, Madrid, asks CD to send list of his publications to the Society.

letters.title: From J. F. Fisher   13 August 1878
letters.summary: Discourses on the rights of animals.

letters.title: To Édouard Heckel   13 August 1878
letters.summary: CD grateful to EH for making his works known in France.

letters.title: To ?   13 August 1878
letters.summary: Cannot help with correspondent’s study. CD has a poor ear for music. Recommends Helmholtz’s work.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   14 [August 1878]
letters.summary:
Instructs FD to plant someOxalisseeds.

Wishes to trace the movement of an old cotyledon. Asks him to examine and compare the pulvinus of a species which moves its cotyledon greatly with one of a species that moves it only moderately.

Are the tendrils ready for heliotropic experiment yet?

letters.title: From W. J. L. Wharton   14 August 1878
letters.summary: Gives results of recently completed survey of islands in the Seychelle group mentioned inCoral reefs, 2d ed., pp. 243–4.

letters.title: To Alphonse de Candolle   15 August 1878
letters.summary:
CD cannot say he cares greatly about his election to the Institut but he does care for the sympathy of his friends.

Will look toSmilaxwhen he returns to Down.

Regrets the insecurity of the identification of fossil leaves.

He has heard that De Bary has cultivatedUtriculariawith and without aquatic animals and that the plants that have been fed flourished "in a stupendous manner".

letters.title: To Asa Gray   15 August 1878
letters.summary:
Climbing plants.

Requests seeds ofEchinocystis lobatafor Hugo de Vries.

letters.title: From Kasimir Ledeganck and Jean Crocq   15 August 1878
letters.summary: CD made an honorary member of the Royal Society for Medical and Natural Sciences of Brussels.

letters.title: To Gaston de Saporta   15 August 1878
letters.deprecated: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.recipient: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.summary:
It would be false to pretend he cares very much about his election to the Institut.

Glad to hear GdeS plans to publish a work on the more ancient fossil plants. Hopes he will report also on the more recent Tertiary forms because the close gradation of such forms is "a fact ofparamountimportance for the principle of evolution".

letters.title: To Hugo de Vries   [15] August [1878]
letters.summary:
Enjoyed seeing HdeV yesterday.

Following the point mentioned by HdeV, CD has observed the difference in corrugation of primary roots in plants exposed to dry and damp soil.

letters.title: From George Rolleston   16 August 1878
letters.summary:
Sends a copy of a letter from Herbert Blakeway of Illinois, which accompanied a pig’s head with wattles.

Discusses the Castle Martin breed ofBos, the history of which shows parallels with the Himalayan rabbits.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [17 August 1878]
letters.summary:
Instructions to sow some seeds

and suggestions for experiment on effects of removal of bloom.

Likes Hugo de Vries very much; has hardly ever seen so modest a man.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   17 [August 1878]
letters.summary: He and Emma rejoice that GHD’s mathematical troubles are at an end. It is miraculous that he unconsciously followed the right course – like composing a sonata by a fluke.

letters.title: From F. B. Goodacre   17 August 1878
letters.summary: Crossing experiments with common and Chinese geese. Offers CD geese if he wishes to repeat experiments.

letters.title: To William Ogle   17 August 1878
letters.summary: Is glad WO is undertaking the editing of Anton Kerner’s book [Schutzmittel der Blüthen gegen unberufene Gäste(1876)], which appears to open out "highly original & curious fields of research". [Used as prefatory letter to Kerner,Flowers and their unbidden guests, The translation revised and edited by W. Ogle (1878).]

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   17 August 1878
letters.summary: GJR’s speech at Dublin [BAAS meeting] was an enormous success, with tremendous applause at mention of CD’s name at the finale.

letters.title: From Hugo de Vries   17 August 1878
letters.summary: Contraction of plant roots.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [19 August 1878]
letters.summary: Asks FD to reply to a letter [11653a] requesting a list of CD’s books.

letters.title: To F. B. Goodacre   20 August [1878]
letters.summary: Thanks FBG for his offer [of geese for breeding experiments] but cannot undertake anything. Suggests FBG or any friend cross half-bred birds for a few generations; it would be a valuable contribution to science.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   20 August 1878
letters.summary:
Comments on GJR’s lecture on animal intelligence [Rep. BAAS].

Comments on J. R. L. Delboeuf,La psychologie[1876].

Suggests that GJR keep a young monkey to observe.

letters.title: To F. B. Goodacre   23 August [1878]
letters.summary: Has changed his mind and would like some of FBG’s hybrids to breed from. Feels he should not lose the chance of perhaps recording the fertility of hybrids of two distinct species.

letters.title: From Richard Randolph   23 August 1878
letters.summary:
Sends pamphlet.

Thanks CD for his reply.

letters.title: To E. Vignes   23 August 1878
letters.summary: Is gratified by EV’s "spirited and able defence" in the article printed inLa France[26 April 1878].

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   24 August [1878]
letters.summary:
Heliotropic responses in aerial roots and tendrils.

Sends seeds received from Fritz Müller.

Has been reading WTT-D’s lecture ["Plant-distribution as a field for geographical research",Proc. R. Geogr. Soc.22: 412–45].

letters.title: To Octavius Pickard-Cambridge   26 August [1878]
letters.summary: Sends address of Fritz Müller.

letters.title: From A. L. Adams   29 August [1878]
letters.summary:
Thanks for letter on ALA’s qualifications for vacant chair of natural history.

Reports observations on deer which have larger left antlers than right, possibly for protection of heart.

letters.title: To Wilhelm Behrens   29 August [1878]
letters.summary: Thanks him for ["Beiträge zur Geschichte der Bestäubungstheorie", inProgram der Königlichen Gewerbeschule zu Elberfeld, 1877/78(1879)]. Agrees with appreciation of Carl Sprengel’s work. Rejoices how highly GWJB appreciates Hermann Müller.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   29 August 1878
letters.summary:
Thanks for comments on his lecture ["Nervous system of Medusa"]

and for information [about J. R. L. Delboeuf,La psychologie(1876)].

letters.title: From Marinko Radovanović    30 August 1878
letters.summary: His son, the Serbian translator of theOrigin, has died.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   30 August [1878]
letters.summary:
Heliotropism in roots.

Francis Darwin’s work on "bloom" and its relation to stomata.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   31 August [1878]
letters.summary: Movements of flower-stalks ofOxalis.

letters.title: From F. B. Goodacre   2 September 1878
letters.summary:
Sends geese to CD.

Crossbreeding of Chinese and common geese; believes they may be same species.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   2 September [1878]
letters.summary:
Discusses animal intelligence.

Advises GJR on acquiring monkey.

Sends book by Delboeuf [La psychologie(1876)].

letters.title: To F. B. Goodacre   3 September [1878]
letters.summary: The geese have arrived. Does not think FBG’s view that the two forms are domestic varieties will hold good. Many ornithologists put them in different genera, and the wild type of each is known.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   10 September 1878
letters.summary: Thanks for letter and book [J. R. L. Delboeuf,La psychologie(1876)].

letters.title: From Édouard van Beneden   11 September 1878
letters.deprecated: Édouard Joseph Louis Marie (Édouard) van Beneden
letters.sender: Édouard Joseph Louis Marie (Édouard) van Beneden
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his subscription to the bust in honour of Theodor Schwann.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [12 September 1878]
letters.summary: He has been working hard at Kew for two days.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   12 September [1878]
letters.summary:
Julius von Sachs’s views on stomata seem largely correct, but CD cannot understand how leaves can survive submerged for such long periods.

Has been observingDroseraand concludes that none of the movement of the tentacles is caused by growth.

Suggests observations to show role of pulvinus in leaf movement.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   12 September 1878
letters.summary: Has forwarded what he believes to be a new species ofSolanum.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   13 [September 1878]
letters.summary:
Asks what position the sub-peduncles assume when the main flower peduncle ofOxalisis tied so as to be horizontal.

Asks whether FD can find some plants at Kew for CD to trace epinastic and hyponastic movements.

letters.title: From C. E. Fry   13 September 1878
letters.summary: Sends photographs showing expressions in a young boy.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   14 September [1878]
letters.summary: Thinks most of the experimental onions have died. Suspects the red and white were distinct species. If GJR is not "sick of the whole job" he might try with radishes or carrots.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   14 September 1878
letters.summary:
Requests support for his appointment as Superintendent of Epping Forest.

Working on a book [Australasia. Stanford’s compendium of geography and travel, edited and extended by A. R. Wallace (1879)].

letters.title: To B. J. Placzek   15 September 1878
letters.summary:
Will be interested to read BP’s work on history [of evolution?].

A learned Jew in Poland [Napthali Lewy?] has published a volume showing that evolution is an ancient belief.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   16 September 1878
letters.summary:
Apologises for his error over theSolanum.

Thanks CD for his good wishes; JT believes he will increase yield and disease-resistance by his crossing and selection.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   16 September 1878
letters.summary:
Supports Epping Forest appointment.

Continues work on vegetable physiology.

letters.title: To Hermann Müller   20 September 1878
letters.summary:
Writing on vegetable physiology.

Nothing in CD’s life has ever interested him more than the fertilisation of such plants asPrimulaandLythrum.

letters.title: From W. C. Williamson   20 September 1878
letters.summary: Droseraspecies vary in form depending upon conditions. Send specimens

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   21 September 1878
letters.summary:
Inquires about a rumour that CD or Francis Darwin is preparing a new book on the "Power of inheritance".

Tells CD of his new periodical:Zoologische Anzeiger.

letters.title: To Frederick Howlett   21 September [1878]
letters.summary: Cannot explain the peculiarities of the blood corpuscles of the Camelidae; maybe similarity between camels and ostriches arises from adaptation rather than common ancestry.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   21 September [1878]
letters.summary: Discusses spiritualism. Says Williams, the medium, is exposed as fraud.

letters.title: To W. C. Williamson   21 September [1878]
letters.summary:
Thanks him for plant specimens.

Asks about sowingDroseraseeds.

letters.title: From E. A. Floyer   22 September 1878
letters.summary:
Sends fruit of date-palm which has not been impregnated by pollen from a male.

Has readOrigin, which "puts everything straight".

letters.title: From E. A. Floyer   [after 22 September 1878?]
letters.summary: Sends an example of natural selection: survival of water-buffalo eating Indian corn submerged by flooding might depend on how long animal could keep nose under water. Encloses measurements of this behaviour.

letters.title: From E. B. Aveling   23 September 1878
letters.summary: Forwards a copy of theStudent’s Magazine, which contains the first of a series of articles on CD and his work.

letters.title: To G. D. Campbell   23 September 1878
letters.deprecated: George Douglas Campbell, 8th duke of Argyll
letters.recipient: George Douglas Campbell, 8th duke of Argyll
letters.summary: Doubts that "the same well-characterized species should be produced in two distinct countries, or at two distinct times".

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   23 September 1878
letters.summary:
Neither he nor [Francis Darwin] intends publishing on inheritance.

They are working on physiology of plants [Movement in plants], but will not print for a year.

Thinks JVC’s new journal [Zoologische Anzeiger] will be of great use to students of zoology.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   23 September 1878
letters.summary: Thanks for CD’s support for [Epping Forest] appointment. Doubts about the proposed management.

letters.title: To F. B. White   23 September [1878]
letters.summary: Comments on FBW’s paper ["Hemipterous fauna of St Helena",Proc. Zool. Soc. Lond.(1878): 444–77].

letters.title: To E. B. Aveling   [after 23 September 1878]
letters.summary: Thanks EBA for the copy of theStudent’s Magazine.

letters.title: From W. C. Marshall   25 September [1878]
letters.summary: Observations on insectivorous plants.

letters.title: From Hermann Müller   25 September 1878
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for his efforts to get HM’s book,Die Befruchtung der Blumen[1873], translated into English. [SeeFertilisation of flowers, translated by D’Arcy W. Thompson, preface by C. Darwin (1883).]

Will soon return to his observations on insects in general and bees in particular.

letters.title: To W. C. Marshall   27 September [1878]
letters.summary:
Thanks WCM for plant.

Mentions "your new room" at Down.

letters.title: To ?   28 September 1878
letters.summary: Urges publication of an exposure of Williams the spiritualist medium.

letters.title: To John Murray   1 October [1878]
letters.summary: Encloses a cheque for £11.19.9. Will transmit £7.9.4 to Fritz Müller. Thanks for account of the sale of his books, which appears to be in a "lamentable state".

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   1 October [1878]
letters.summary:
Comments on GJR’s article inFortnightly Review["The beginning of nerves", n.s. 24 (1878): 509–26].

Comments on "poor old"Edinburgh Review.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   3 October [1878]
letters.summary: WantsOxalisspecimen named; is fascinated by cotyledonary movements of the genus.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   4 October 1878
letters.summary:
Frank asked to summarise work with CD for use in JDH’s Royal Society address.

Work with A. Gray shows Colorado plants closer to Altai than to E. or W. America.

Work with J. Ball shows Moroccan plants very distinct from nearby Canaries.

JDH on Royal Commission to Paris Exhibition.

letters.title: To Eduard Strasburger   4 October 1878
letters.summary: Thanks for a copy of Strasburger’s essay on ‘swarmspores’.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   5 October [1878]
letters.summary: Before JDH discusses flora of Canary Islands CD suggests he read F. B. White’s paper [see11707], which explains stocking of Atlantic island fauna as due to changed currents during [last, or Miocene] northern glacial period.

letters.title: From C. G. Semper   5 October 1878
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for writing machine.

Recalls visit by CD’s son [Francis].

letters.title: To R. D. Fitzgerald   7 October 1878
letters.summary: Thanks for pt 4 ofAustralian orchids[1874–].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   7 October 1878
letters.summary: Botanical evidence is against F. B. White’s origin of St Helena fauna. JDH holds flora is S. African. Since plants must arrive before insects, if fauna is Palearctic then flora survived glacial period. Flora not Miocene since old and relic orders are absent. Suggests S. African west coastal mountains as insects’ origin.

letters.title: To Joseph Lister   7 October 1878
letters.summary:
Suggests that benzoic acid would be a deadly poison to bacteria and their allies.

Is puzzled about the use of borax as a disinfectant because in his experimentsDroserawere not in the least injured by boracic acid.

letters.title: From C.-F. Reinwald   8 October 1878
letters.summary:
Forms of flowers, translated by Édouard Heckel, is published.

Cross and self-fertilisationhas only sold 450–500 copies.

Originsells regularly; he looks forward to a cheaper edition.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   8 October 1878
letters.summary: Forwards letter from Victor Kennedy reporting on the growth of JT’s potatoes in W. Ireland.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   10 October 1878
letters.summary: Recounts the experiments on Fechner’s law he has found in Helmholz; they are on the smallest perceptible differences of illumination. Describes how to test whether plants’ responses to lights are in accordance with it.

letters.title: From Wilhelm Behrens   11 October 1878
letters.summary:
Thanks for CD’s remarks on and agreement with his paper on history of pollination theories [see11678].

Will shortly send his essay on the anatomy of nectaries in flowers [see12300].

letters.title: From James Torbitt   [after 18 October 1878]
letters.summary: Forwards letter from George Callwell reporting what a large and disease-free potato crop JT’s seed yields.

letters.title: To Virginius Dabney   20 October 1878
letters.summary: CD is puzzled by VD’s supposed hybrid tomato. If a hybrid, it would have to result from the "direct action of the pollen of a distinct species in the mother plant". CD believes this sort of inheritance occurs in varieties (though some botanists disagree), but not for species. Suggests "bud-variation".

letters.title: From R. M. Middleton   22 October 1878
letters.summary: Did cats and dogs become pets because they are scrupulous in the discharge of their faeces? He has a pet parakeet whose behaviour supports this view.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   24 October [1878]
letters.summary: Wants some plants for sleep-movement observations. Has almost finished experimental work and must start sorting his notes.

letters.title: From Eduard Strasburger   26 October 1878
letters.summary:
EAS eagerly awaits the publication of CD’s work on heliotropism.

Sends him a paper on "Polyembryonie" [Jenaische Z. Med. & Naturwiss.12 (1878): 647–70].

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   29 October [1878]
letters.summary: Rejoices that he should have "staggered" William Thomson so quickly and that the latter should speak of GHD’s "discovery". The internal heat [of the earth] will please geologists and evolutionists.

letters.title: From Raphael Meldola   30 October 1878
letters.summary: Plans to produce a translation of Weismann’sStudien zur Descendenz-Theorie[1875–6] and would welcome a preface from CD.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   30 October [1878]
letters.summary: WantsImpatiensseeds, in order to observe movements of cotyledons.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   31 October [1878]
letters.summary: Will do his best to provide preface for Weismann’sStudien[seeCollected papers2: 280–1].

letters.title: From Raphael Meldola   1 November 1878
letters.summary:
Thanks for agreeing to write the preface for RM’s translation of Weismann.

Will arrange to meet CD when he comes to London.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   2 November [1878]
letters.summary: Forwards pamphlet (Jules Carret 1878) to GHD.

letters.title: To A. C. Ramsay   3 November 1878
letters.summary: Thanks for ACR’sPhysical geology[5th ed. (1878)]; delighted with its success, proving there is a large body of men in England capable of appreciating sound geological science.

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   3 November 1878
letters.summary:
Encloses a letter [missing] on the progress of the Fuegians.

His eldest son has married.

letters.title: To B. J. Sulivan   5 November [1878]
letters.summary:
Thanks for account of Fuegians

and news about old "Beaglers".

Has been reading A. A. Brassey [Around the world in the yacht "Sunbeam"(1878)].

letters.title: From Albert Gaudry   6 November 1878
letters.summary: Acknowledges receipt of French translation ofForms of flowers. "No one more than you has made us feel the beauties of Creation and made us enter more profoundly into the secrets of nature."

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   7 November 1878
letters.summary: Encloses William Thomson’s report on GHD’s paper. Some of it was written in Rayleigh’s hand.

letters.title: From Emil du Bois-Reymond   7 November 1878
letters.summary:
CD elected foreign associate of the Royal Academy of Sciences [K. Preussische Akademie der Wissenschaften].

EdB-R’s paper will be available in English in the New York periodical,Popular Science Monthly, and he hopes CD will read it. [See11742and11842.]

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   7 November 1878
letters.summary:
Explains the occurrence of cattle on the Fuegian islands.

Discusses intentions with regard to missionary stations and steamers in the area.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   8 November [1878]
letters.summary: Delighted with [William Thomson’s] report. "There can be no doubt now about the value of your work." CD has "not been so much pleased for a long time".

letters.title: From J. A. Harker   11 November 1878
letters.summary: Has observed rare instances ofOphrys apiferawith "cut labellum". Suggests it was done by large dragonfly mistaking the flower for a fly visiting a flower. Stimulated to studyOphrysbyOrchids.

letters.title: From Edouard Bergson   12 November 1878
letters.summary: Describes the change in shape of a worm over a candle-flame.

letters.title: To Emil du Bois-Reymond   12 November 1878
letters.summary:
Sends thanks [for election to Prussian Academy of Sciences].

Appreciates the copy of address [Darwin versus Galiani(1876)].

letters.title: From G. A. Gaskell   13 November 1878
letters.summary: Discusses three "laws of race preservation" which are evolving: (1) natural selection; (2) the sociological law of sympathetic selection, or indiscriminate survival; (3) moral law – social selection or the "Birth of the Fittest".

letters.title: To Benjamin Disraeli   [15–18 November 1878]
letters.summary: A memorial signed by CD and many others, calling upon the Prime Minister, Benjamin Disraeli, to convene Parliament to discuss the ultimatum addressed to the Amir of Afghanistan, Sher Ali Khan, by the Viceroy of India, E. R. Bulwer-Lytton.

letters.title: To G. A. Gaskell   15 November 1878
letters.summary: CD hopes GAG is right [see11744]. His second law seems largely acted on in civilised societies. Evil that would follow from checking benevolence to weak and diseased would be greater than by allowing them to survive and procreate. CD doubts that artificial checks would be advantageous to the world at large. If birth could be prevented, and control were not thought immoral, "would there not be a danger of profligacy amongst unmarried women?"

letters.title: From M. D. Conway   18 November 1878
letters.summary: Invites CD to join the Association of Liberal Thinkers and encloses information on its constitution. Huxley and Tyndall are co-operating.

letters.title: From A. B. Farn    18 November 1878
letters.summary: Discusses colour variations in the geometer moth,Gnophos obscurata. Concludes that the increasing proportion of the darker form is related to the effect of smoke that is blackening the chalk slopes on which they live.

letters.title: To M. D. Conway   19 November 1878
letters.summary: Glad to join Association of Liberal Thinkers and to pay usual subscription. Refuses any office nor allows his name to promote the association because neither his health nor his mental habits will allow him to take an active part.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   19 November [1878]
letters.summary: Invites RM to luncheon.

letters.title: From T. H. Noyes   19 November 1878
letters.summary: THN, a medium with a gift to cure occult diseases, outlines a course of treatment to remedy CD’s ailments.

letters.title: From G. A. Gaskell   20 November 1878
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his encouraging letter. Replies to CD’s points. Thinks more attention should be given to the origin and growth of sexual shame.

letters.title: To W. K. Parker?   20 November [1878]
letters.summary: Invites [WKP] to lunch.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   20 [November 1878]
letters.summary: CD will visit tomorrow.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [21 November 1878]
letters.summary: Instructs FD to make some observations on movement inTrifoliumandImpatiens. Sends some seeds to be sown.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   21 November [1878]
letters.summary: CD hopes his book [Movement in plants] will be worth the effort WTT-D has put into getting plants for him; fears he has achieved little.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [before 22 November 1878]
letters.summary: Horse chestnut roots have not acted at all well.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [22 November 1878]
letters.summary:
Suggests experiment to detect salts deposited on surface of leaves.

Wants FD to have another go at horse-chestnut radicles.

letters.title: To Edward Frankland   22 November [1878]
letters.summary: Asks whether he may call to discuss a chemico-physiological point.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [23 November 1878]
letters.summary: Many thnks for the pelargonium letter.

letters.title: From H. N. Moseley   24 November 1878
letters.summary: Sends revises [of hisNotes by a naturalist on the "Challenger", 1872–6(1879)] and asks permission to dedicate it to CD.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [25–7 November 1878]
letters.summary: He has had no success with horse or Spanish chestnuts.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   25 November [1878]
letters.summary: CD sends his preface [to RM’s translation of August Weismann,Studies in the theory of descent(1882);Collected papers2: 280–1].

letters.title: From Raphael Meldola   25 November 1878
letters.summary: Thanks for preface. When RM’s translation is complete, would like CD to expand it slightly to refer to overlap between Weismann’s observations and CD’s theories.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   26 November [1878]
letters.summary: Regrets he cannot compare his work with Weismann’s in his preface as he feels “an author is never a fit judge of his own work”. [Appended note explains that RM wished CD’s work to be fully acknowledged, which was frequently not the case in continental writings.]

letters.title: To H. N. Moseley   26 November [1878]
letters.summary: Thanks for HNM’s offer to dedicate book [Notes by a naturalist on the "Challenger"(1879)].

letters.title: To C. G. Semper   26 November [1878]
letters.summary: Discusses views of Moritz Wagner on modification of species. Two different cases: one in which a species is modified in the same country and cases in which a species splits. Glad CGS is taking up subject.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   27 November 1878
letters.summary: Sends report on annual trade sale [missing]. New printings ofJournal of researchesandDescentare needed.

letters.title: To J. B. Innes   27 November [1878]
letters.summary: CD disappointed in Pusey’s sermon against evolution [Un-science, not science, adverse to faith(1878), sermon read by H. P. Liddon at St Mary’s, Oxford, on 3 Nov 1878]. Does not agree that religion and science can be kept as distant as Pusey desires. Geology and biology must deal with history of earth and of man. But that is no reason for bitter hostility.

letters.title: To William Ogle   [after 27 November 1878]
letters.summary: Thanks for his translation of [Anton] Kerner [Flowers and their unbidden guests: the translation revised and edited by W. Ogle (1878)].

letters.title: From H. N. Ridley   [before 28 November 1878]
letters.summary: Wishes to defend CD from the attacks E. B. Pusey made in his sermon [see11763]. Raises specific questions on CD’s theological views in order to refute Pusey’s accusations.

letters.title: From Laureano Figuerola Ballester   28 November 1878
letters.summary: As an honorary professor of the Free Institution of Enseñanza [see11321a] CD is sent the discourse pronounced by the Rector at their opening session with a number of theIlustracion Española y Americanawith portraits of the members of the executive committee of the Institucion.

letters.title: To H. N. Ridley   28 November 1878
letters.summary: Does not think sermon by E. B. Pusey [see11763] is worth a reply. HNR may quote CD as saying that Pusey is "mistaken in imagining that I wrote the Origin with any relation whatever to Theology". Pusey’s attack will be powerless to retard belief in evolution.

letters.title: To C. G. Semper   30 November 1878
letters.summary: Discusses effect of isolation on species modification and the views of Moritz Wagner on the subject.

letters.title: From J. B. Innes   1 December 1878
letters.summary: JBI on CD’s integrity and the separateness of science and religion.

letters.title: To Edward Frankland   2 December [1878]
letters.summary:
Thanks for the Blue Book [Report to the Local Government Board on the water supplied to London].

Gives instructions for sending the pure water.

Has sent for the Wenham ice.

Enjoyed his talk with EF.

letters.title: To John Power   3 December 1878
letters.summary: Petition Cambridge University that candidates for an Honour degree may be relieved from the obligation of passing an examination in Greek.

letters.title: To R. I. Lynch   4 December [1878]
letters.summary: Encloses letter of recommendation for RIL [for position as Curator, Botanic Garden, Cambridge?]. [See11770.]

letters.title: To the syndics of Cambridge Botanic Garden   4 December 1878
letters.summary: Letter recommending R. I. Lynch [for position as Curator, Botanic Garden, Cambridge].

letters.title: To John Tyndall   4 December [1878]
letters.summary: Has observed, perhaps erroneously, that certain plants were excited to movement by a prolonged high note on the bassoon. Would now like to try a siren and asks JT to bring one from the Royal Institution.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   5 December [1878]
letters.summary: Comments on GJR’s anonymous book [A candid examination of theism(1878)]. Notes possible theological objections.

letters.title: From John Tyndall   5 December 1878
letters.summary: Will provide the siren.

letters.title: From W. H. Flower   6 [December] 1878
letters.summary: Describes findings of examination of geese with abnormal wings. Says old gander that sired geese is without injury or abnormality. Encloses his assistant’s report.

letters.title: From C. G. Semper   6 December 1878
letters.summary:
Asks whether he may use CD’s letters in his work [Die natürlichen Existenzbedingungen der Thiere(1880)] in order to show that Moritz Wagner has misrepresented CD’s views.

Discusses the influence of isolation and external conditions on animals, and the relative importance of the direct effect of external conditions and of selection in bringing about change.

letters.title: To C. G. Semper   [after 6 December 1878]
letters.summary:
Gives CGS permission to use his letters in any way he thinks fit.

Discusses the direct effect of external conditions as an agent of change in organisms; has encountered many cases since the publication ofOrigin.

letters.title: From Anthony Rich   7 December 1878
letters.summary: Informs CD of his intention to bequeath his property to him.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   [8] December 1878
letters.summary: Thinks conservation of energy not evidence for Deity. Agrees with CD that there is little hope to illuminate subject with light of intellect. Intends to drop it.

letters.title: To R. A. Blair   9 December 1878
letters.summary: Says deformity of wings of geese is not related to injury to gander. Forwards a report on the birds [11717].

letters.title: To G.S. Ffinden   9 December 1878
letters.summary: Encloses a cheque for £5.5.0 for the Down Coal and Clothing Club.

letters.title: To W. H. Flower   9 December 1878
letters.summary:
Much obliged to WHF and Dr Garron for their trouble [over deformed goose wings]. Has no doubt that WHF’s view of the deformity is the right one. Will send WHF’s report to Blair.

CD and Emma enjoyed extremely meeting the Dean at WHF’s house.

letters.title: To Anthony Rich   9 December 1878
letters.summary: Is deeply gratified by AR’s proposed generosity.

letters.title: From Anthony Rich   10 December 1878
letters.summary: Gives CD details of the property he proposes to bequeath to him.

letters.title: From Raphael Meldola   11 December 1878
letters.summary:
Is making progress with the Weismann translation.

Wonders whether Francis Darwin would give a botanical lecture at a Bayswater school.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   11 December [1878]
letters.summary: Sends copy of H. D. Lindemuth, "Vegetative Bastarderzeugung" [Landwirtsch. Jahrb.7 (1878): 887–939].

letters.title: To E. A. Darwin   12 December 1878
letters.summary: Informs EAD of Anthony Rich’s proposal to bequeath his property to CD.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   12 December [1878]
letters.summary: Writes of Anthony Rich’s bequest.

letters.title: To Anthony Rich   12 December 1878
letters.summary: Thanks AR for the details of his bequest and invites him to Down.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   12 December 1878
letters.summary: Has examined this year’s crop, which looks good; will prepare a report.

letters.title: From J. D. Cooper   13 December 1878
letters.summary: Sends CD a proof of an illustration reduced on to the block by photography. The method is expensive but scientifically accurate.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   13 December [1878]
letters.summary: Very glad to hear Anthony Rich is leaving CD money "encouraging science in such a very practical manner".

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   13 [December 1878]
letters.summary: Surprised and delighted by Mr Rich’s bequest as it will greatly increase his income. Intends to leave money to the Royal Society to contribute to science. Houses in London are a good investment even in times that are nervous for bankers.

letters.title: To J. D. Cooper   [after 13 December 1878]
letters.summary: Approves of the proof. However, his book [Movement in plants] will have a large number of diagrams so he feels only the complicated diagrams and drawings should be copied by photography.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   14 December 1878
letters.summary: Asks CD if he would screw himself up to inviting A. Newton to Down.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   14 December [1878]
letters.summary:
Thanks for JDH’s description of CD’s work inNature.

Anthony Rich to bequeath his property (over £1100 a year) to CD.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   14 December 1878
letters.summary:
Congratulates CD on the Anthony Rich bequest.

Sad but relieved to retire as President of the Royal Society.

Describes battle with Treasury over use of an empty house at Kew.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   14 December [1878]
letters.summary:
Is glad book progresses; answers translation query.

Francis Darwin does not have time to lecture.

letters.title: To James Torbitt   [1]4 December 1878
letters.summary: Congratulates JT on success in breeding potato varieties.

letters.title: To William Ogle   16 December [1878]
letters.summary:
Thanks WO for advice and assistance for his son, Horace.

Has read Kerner’s book [see11666]; finds the translation "as clear as daylight" but fears it is too good for the English public who like "very washy food".

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   17 December [1878]
letters.summary: Waiting for frost to go so experiments can start again.

letters.title: From W. M. Hacon   20 December 1878
letters.summary: Revision of CD’s will to reflect Anthony Rich’s gift and to increase daughters’ inheritance.

letters.title: From Gabriel Max   21 December 1878
letters.summary: Relates dream suggesting CD’s belief in spiritualism. Asks if Wallace is clairvoyant.

letters.title: To Gaston de Saporta   22 December 1878
letters.deprecated: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.recipient: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.summary:
Thanks for GdeS’sLe monde des plantes[1879].

CD has just read "Végétation polaire" [C. R. Congr. Int. Sci. Geogr.1 (1878): 197–242] with interest. Hooker gave it conspicuous place in his Royal Society Address (1878).

letters.title: To John Tyndall   22 December [1878]
letters.summary: Returns the siren; the plants "ill luck to them, are not sensitive to aerial vibrations". Is ashamed of his blunder.

letters.title: From W. M. Hacon   24 December 1878
letters.summary: Writes regarding CD’s will in the light of Anthony Rich’s proposed bequest.

letters.title: From Anthony Rich   25 December 1878
letters.summary: Regrets that illness prevents his travelling to visit CD but would be pleased to see CD or his sons at Worthing.

letters.title: From F. S. Arnold   [2]6 December 1878
letters.summary: Would like CD to explain how he reconciles two passages in 6th ed. ofOrigin.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   27 December [1878]
letters.summary: Recommends article on "Brute and human intellect" by William James [J. Speculative Philos.12 (1878): 236–78].

letters.title: From W. M. Hacon   28 December 1878
letters.summary: Sending second codicil for CD to sign.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   28 December 1878
letters.summary: Describes Anthony Rich, whom he has visited.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   29 December 1878
letters.summary: About Anthony Rich, who has decided to leave his fortune to CD [and later also to make a bequest to THH]. CD’s account of what he wrote to Rich.

letters.title: From Anthony Rich   29 December 1878
letters.summary: He would be happy to receive a visit from one of CD’s sons at any time.

letters.title: From W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   30 December 1878
letters.summary: Sends specimens ofCommelyna.

letters.title: To F. S. Arnold   31 December [1878]
letters.summary: Responds to criticism concerning varieties, species, and genera.

letters.title: To W. R. Greg   31 December 1878
letters.summary: Discusses a chapter on design, written by WRG’s son [Percy Greg,The devil’s advocate(1878)]. Comments on the younger Greg’s criticisms of natural selection and evolution.

letters.title: From C. V. Smith   [1879]
letters.summary: Notes on reefs in the SW Pacific and the Indian Ocean.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   [1879?]
letters.summary: Has found no [potato] variety whose foliage can resist the parasite, except when grown under glass.

letters.title: To Albert Günther   1 January 1879
letters.summary: Thanks AG for his kind note and returns his good wishes.

letters.title: From Marius Koch   3 January 1879
letters.summary: A young disciple wishes to know if reports of people with tails in New Guinea could be true.

letters.title: To Edward Frankland   4 January [1879]
letters.summary: Fears that the promised bottle of pure water may have been despatched or stolen in passage. [See11768a.]

letters.title: From Mary Jung   7 January 1879
letters.summary: Young Austrian woman asks for CD’s autograph.

letters.title: From Carl Kraus   8 January 1879
letters.summary: A supporter of "the presumptive connection between socialism and evolution through natural selection" sends essays of Carl Vogt and requests CD to comment on them publicly.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   9 January 1879
letters.summary: Sends figures on increase in value of North Western Railway stocks. Says consol stock considered much more secure for bankers. Does not think his own bank is in danger of a run. Is glad to see the Emperor of Prussia has confirmed CD’s appointment to Academy. Is snowing at Bassett.

letters.title: To ?   9 January 1879
letters.summary: Thanks correspondent for the copies of his engraving. "The work seems to be, though I cannot pretend to be a judge, a vy fine production".

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   10 January [1879]
letters.summary: G[eorge] has visited A[nthony] R[ich] at Worthing.

letters.title: From Leopold Würtenberger   10 January 1879
letters.summary: Asks about possibility of securing grant in England in order to complete work on ammonites. Describes progress. Could CD recommend him to a foundation? Describes personal background.

letters.title: To Mary Jung   11 January 1879
letters.summary: Suggests MJ does not worry about the differences in opinion between ecclesiastics and scientists.

letters.title: From C. H. Blackley   13 January 1879
letters.summary: Relates anecdote about a provincial girl’s reaction to being told men descended from monkeys.

letters.title: To Karl Höchberg   13 January 1879
letters.summary: Thanks for essay on origin of taste for music. Will send to Edmund Gurney.

letters.title: To C. H. Blackley   14 January 1879
letters.summary: Thanks CHB for his anecdote about a provincial girl’s reaction to being told men descended from monkeys.

letters.title: To Melchior Neumayr   15 January 1879
letters.summary: Asks MN about trustworthiness of Leopold Würtenberger. Would like to aid LW financially in his work.

letters.title: To Leopold Würtenberger   15 January 1879
letters.summary: Is sorry that LW’s circumstances interfere with his scientific work. Does not think any English scientific society can help.

letters.title: From Gaston de Saporta   16 January 1879
letters.deprecated: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.sender: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.summary: Sends his photograph; asks for CD’s.

letters.title: From Karl Höchberg   17 January 1879
letters.summary: Points out comment by Grant Allen supporting his theory of the origin of colour sense. Is English translation of his essay possible?

letters.title: From W. K. Parker   17 January 1879
letters.summary: Sends CD a book on science and scriptures written by a clergyman friend [unidentified].

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   18 January 1879
letters.summary:
Has readHumewith great pleasure, but found parts very stiff reading.

George Darwin has visited Anthony Rich.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   [18 January 1879]
letters.summary: Notes advertisement of Tito Vignoli,Fundamentalgesetz der Intelligenz im Thierreiche[1879].

letters.title: To Gaston de Saporta   19 January 1879
letters.deprecated: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.recipient: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.summary: Thanks GdeS for his photograph; sends his own. Glad to hear GdeS’s work [Le monde des plantes(1879)] is popular in France.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   20 January 1879
letters.summary: Sends the Fritz Müller article fromKosmos.

letters.title: To H. N. Moseley   20 January 1879
letters.summary: Thanks for HNM’s [Notes by a naturalist on the "Challenger"(1879)].

letters.title: From W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   [20 January 1879]
letters.summary:
H. N. Moseley says [in "Notes on plants collected and observed at the Admiralty Islands",J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)15 (1877): 77] pigeons eject seeds in fit state for germination. He regards pigeons as providing most efficient means of transport in Malayan Archipelago.

CD’s collected notes on geographical distribution would make a good book.

letters.title: From H. N. Moseley   21 January 1879
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for accepting dedication.

Asks CD to support his candidacy for position as Registrar of the University of London by talking to Sir John Lubbock, one of the most influential members of the Senate.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   21 January 1879
letters.summary:
Has lately found frog that has eggs on its back.

Pupae of caddis-flies living on rocks have lost fringe of hairs on their feet. In species that live in the water these are used for swimming.

letters.title: From Melchior Neumayr   21 January 1879
letters.summary:
Respects Leopold Würtenberger’s work. Will initiate inquiry if CD wishes. LW’s work suffers from his limited circumstances. Will assist him if he asks.

Mentions his own forthcoming work ["Zur Kenntniss der Fauna des untersten Lias in den Nordalpen",Abh. K.-K. Geol. Reichsanst.7 (1874–82), vol. 5].

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   23 January 1879
letters.summary: Suggests references that might answer CD’s [unidentified] request for information about coral islands.

letters.title: To Emil du Bois-Reymond   23 January 1879
letters.summary: Acknowledges receipt of diploma.

letters.title: To H. N. Moseley   23 and 30 January 1879
letters.summary: Has told John Lubbock how highly he thinks of HNM’s work, and has heard that HMN’s claims will be fully considered.

letters.title: To ?   23 January [1879?]
letters.summary: Orders a sheet of gold-beater’s skin for plant experiments.

letters.title: To Melchior Neumayr   24 January 1879
letters.summary: Has offered Leopold Würtenberger money to aid in his work.

letters.title: From H. W. Bates   25 January 1879
letters.summary: F. Galton and others suggest that he go in for Fellowship [of Royal Society]. Asks that CD propose him. If he is unable to do so HWB will not be hurt to wait another year.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   25 January [1879]
letters.summary: Movements inOxalis.

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   26 January 1879
letters.summary: It will give CD real pleasure to propose HWB for F.R.S. Asks that he send him the necessary information for the certificate as well as a list of men he would like to sign it. He should not be disappointed if not elected first time. [Bates elected F.R.S. 2 June 1881.]

letters.title: From W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   27 January 1879
letters.summary: Oxalisseeds incorrectly named. H. N. Moseley says pigeons in Malaya eject seeds fit for germination.

letters.title: From A. F. Batalin   29 January 1879
letters.summary:
Thanks for CD’s interest in his paper on plant movements ["Über die Ursachen der periodischer Bewegungen der Blumen und Laubblätter",Flora56 (1873): 433–41, 449–55]. AFB concentrated on clear cases, though he knows there are others.

Experiments on function of movement:Mimosaleaves, held so they cannot move, die.

letters.title: To Edmund Mojsisovics von Mojsvár   29 January 1879
letters.deprecated: Johann August Georg Edmund (Edmund) Mojsisovics von Mojsvár
letters.recipient: Johann August Georg Edmund (Edmund) Mojsisovics von Mojsvár
letters.summary:
Comments on EM’s work in Dolomites [Die Dolomit-Riffe von Südtirol(1879)]. Had wondered whether ancient corals formed reefs.

Obliged for EM’s photograph. Sends his own.

letters.title: From Leopold Würtenberger   29 January 1879
letters.summary: Thanks CD for gift to support his research.

letters.title: To W. B. Cheadle   31 January 1879
letters.summary: Declines to sign petition concerning Professorship of Pathology at Cambridge.

letters.title: From C. F. Austin   February 1879
letters.summary:
EnclosesBulletin of the Torrey Botanical Club, with account of a fungus that exhales chlorine;

relates his discovery in 1852 of a flowering plant that had "perfectly formed beetles" in the place of anthers.

letters.title: From D. Appleton & Co.   1 February 1879
letters.summary: Statement of U.S. sales of CD’s works.

letters.title: From Henry Potonié    1 February 1879
letters.summary: Cites evolutionary passages by Alexander Braun in English edition of Braun’sVerjüngung[1853].

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   3 February 1879
letters.summary: Heliotropic movements. Is giving up experiments until the spring.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [4 February – 8 March 1879]
letters.summary:
Requests some seeds.

Believes the leaves ofPhyllanthussleep like those ofCassia.

letters.title: To H. N. Moseley   4 February 1879
letters.summary: Comments on HNM’s book [Notes by a naturalist on the "Challenger"(1879)].

letters.title: From Thomas Maston   5 February 1879
letters.summary: A stonemason who has readOriginandDescentand defends CD’s theory against theological prejudice, would like to read CD’s other books but is too poor to afford them.

letters.title: From H. N. Moseley   5 February 1879
letters.summary:
Sends regards from Capt. Charles Owen, who had collected beetles for CD.

Owen’s son is going to Oregon with Wallis Nash.

letters.title: From Raphael Meldola   6 February 1879
letters.summary:
Has arranged for publication of his translation of Weismann.

S. H. Scudder article on sexual dimorphism in butterflies [Proc. Am. Acad. Arts & Sci.12 (1877): 150–8].

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   7 February 1879
letters.summary:
Wishes to subscribe to RM’s translation of Weismann.

Has seen Scudder’s article.

A. R. Wallace’s article ["Animals and their native countries",Nineteenth Century5 (1879): 247–59] is excellent.

letters.title: From Leopold Würtenberger   7 February 1879
letters.summary: £100 has arrived and LW will set to work.

letters.title: To Edward Frankland   8 February 1879
letters.summary: Gives results of the experiments: the leaves in most cases make the water alkaline. It cannot be ammonia. He and his son, Francis, suspect potash, which is valued as a manure. Will be grateful for the analysis EF has offered.

letters.title: From George Henslow   8 February 1879
letters.summary: GH no longer believes in the value of cross-fertilisation in plants.

letters.title: From Karl Alberts   9 February 1879
letters.summary: Birthday congratulations from the editors ofKosmos. They will mark the occasion with a special number ofKosmos.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   9 February 1879
letters.summary:
Sends birthday wishes.

Comments on progress of CD’s theory in Germany. Mentions opposition of Rudolf Virchow and his replyFreie Wissenschaft und freie Lehre[1878].

Describes research trip to Brittany and Normandy.

Research onChallengerRadiolaria.

letters.title: To Karl Alberts   [after 9 February 1879]
letters.summary: Thanks KA and the other editors ofKosmosfor the issue published in honour of his birthday. Sees there is much in it that will interest him greatly.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   10 February 1879
letters.summary: Birthday greetings.

letters.title: To Anton de Bary   11 February 1879
letters.summary: Thanks ADeB for sending himBotanische Zeitung, but asks him to send it no more, as CD takes it regularly and has procured the volumes from the beginning.

letters.title: To George Henslow   11 February 1879
letters.summary: Disagrees with GH over the value of cross-fertilisation.

letters.title: From Grant Allen   12 February 1879
letters.summary: Has sent copy of his new book,Colour-sense[1879]; in anticipation of criticism, he justifies his reliance on recorded observations rather than experiments, by the heavy demands of his career as a journalist.

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   12 February 1879
letters.summary: Encloses HWB’s Royal Society certificate with seven signatures, which CD thinks is ample.

letters.title: From Karl Beger   [c.12 February 1879]
letters.summary: Birthday wishes.

letters.title: To N. N. Christophe   12 February 1879
letters.summary: Thanks for birthday greetings.

letters.title: To J. A. Crawley   12 February 1879
letters.summary: Can give no information. Has never read works of Aristotle, but has unbounded respect for him as observer.

letters.title: To Arnold Dodel-Port   12 February 1879
letters.summary: Thanks AD-P for the gift of part of hisAtlas[see11039].

letters.title: From the masters of Greiz College   12 February 1879
letters.summary: Send 70th birthday congratulations.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   12 February 1879
letters.summary:
Thanks for kind letter.

Has not yet read EH’s article inKosmos["Einstämmiger und vielstämmiger Ursprung", 4 (1878–9): 360–76].

Rudolf Virchow affair lamentable. Virchow’s conduct inexplicable.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   12 February 1879
letters.summary: Thanks for honour of latest number ofKosmos.

letters.title: To Hermann Müller   12 February [1879]
letters.summary: Has just heard that HM has been treated shamefully by his Government. What has happened?

letters.title: From Hermann Müller   12 February 1879
letters.summary: Seventieth birthday greetings.

letters.title: From the Naples Zoological Station   12 February 1879
letters.summary: Seventieth birthday greetings.

letters.title: From Arthur Mellersh   13 February 1879
letters.summary: Birthday wishes.

letters.title: To Hugo de Vries   13 February 1879
letters.summary: Discusses heliotropism in plant cotyledons. Asks for information.

letters.title: To Henry Woodward   13 February [1879]
letters.summary:
Has signed a paper [unspecified];

thanks HW for his interesting letter and kind expressions about himself and his son.

letters.title: From Hermann Müller   14 February 1879
letters.summary: HM’s teaching methods and his ideas are under attack in Germany along with the works of Ernst Krause.

letters.title: To John Tyndall   14 February 1879
letters.summary: Has been asked to contribute to W. K. Clifford memorial fund. Asks JT’s advice on how much the committee hopes to raise. Would like to give handsomely but feels bound "with such a lot of children, not to be extravagant".

letters.title: From C. A. Lindvall   16 February 1879
letters.summary: Outlines his theory to explain the form of certain Swedish sandhills and puts forward his ideas regarding the geological history of the earth.

letters.title: To Friedrich Ludwig   16 February 1879
letters.summary: Sends thanks to the Masters for congratulations on his birthday, saying "the approbation & sympathy of one’s fellow-workers in the acquisition of knowledge is the highest possible reward which any man ought to desire".

letters.title: From W. B. Cheadle   17 February 1879
letters.summary: Second request that CD sign a Cambridge memorial [i.e., petition]. The heading has been amended to include graduates who have formerly studied medicine.

letters.title: To Carlos Ribeiro   17 February 1879
letters.summary: Thanks for having sent prehistoric remains.

letters.title: To John Tyndall   17 February [1879]
letters.summary: Thanks JT for his information. Sends £50 to the W. K. Clifford memorial fund.

letters.title: From A. G. Butler   19 February 1879
letters.summary: Requests testimonial from CD for position of Assistant Keeper, Zoological Dept, British Museum.

letters.title: From Anton de Bary   20 February 1879
letters.summary: Since he was innocent of sending theBotanische Zeitungto CD, he inquired of the editor, who informs him that it is sent every week by post by order of Williams and Norgate.

letters.title: To A. G. Butler   20 February [1879]
letters.summary:
"I do not know whether the enclosed will be of any use to you.– I can say nothing of your fitness for the desired office, as I know nothing whatever of its duties.

I am sincerely sorry to hear of Mr F. Smith’s death."

letters.title: To Grant Allen   [before 21 February 1879]
letters.summary:
Read GA’s book [The colour-sense] with "great interest". Makes criticisms and suggestions.

Cannot believe in GA’s theory of the origin of pleasure and pain.

Is glad he defends sexual selection;

CD finds A. R. Wallace’s explanations "mere empty words" and for many years he has "quite doubted [ARW’s] scientific judgment".

Considers the possible effect of environmental colour on the colour tastes of animals.

letters.title: From Grant Allen   21 February [1879]
letters.summary:
Thanks for criticisms ofColour-sense.

Clarifies his views that actions desirable for species result in development of nervous organs capable of pleasurable stimulation.

Believes that all "tastes" occurring in nature are explicable with reference to ancestral habits and that none is purely arbitrary.

letters.title: To the British Museum   21 February 1879
letters.summary: Letter of recommendation for Richard Bowdler Sharpe, ornithologist.

letters.title: To the Darwin children   21 February 1879
letters.deprecated: Elizabeth (Bessy) (Lizzy) DarwinFrancis DarwinGeorge Howard DarwinHorace DarwinLeonard DarwinWilliam Erasmus DarwinHenrietta Emma DarwinHenrietta Emma Litchfield
letters.recipient: Elizabeth (Bessy) (Lizzy) DarwinFrancis DarwinGeorge Howard DarwinHorace DarwinLeonard DarwinWilliam Erasmus DarwinHenrietta Emma DarwinHenrietta Emma Litchfield
letters.summary: Circular about the distribution of the overplus of his income and advice on investment.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   21 February [1879]
letters.summary:
Is increasing FD’s allowance.

Has begun his chapter on sleep of plants [forMovement in plants].

letters.title: From C. W. Hamilton   21 February 1879
letters.summary: Encloses a press clipping [missing] of his observations [on stem structure?].

letters.title: From Karl Höchberg   21 February 1879
letters.summary: Describes health-related arguments for vegetarianism. Notes arguments that anthropoid apes are vegetarians. Asks whether man is sufficiently adapted to mixed diet so that meat is not harmful?

letters.title: To R. B. Sharpe   21 February [1879]
letters.summary: Sends short testimonial [missing] for RBS, but doubts its value as he has has already given one for the same office [to A. G. Butler, see11888].

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   21 February [1879]
letters.summary: Wants to borrow Duchartre’sÉléments de botanique[1867].

letters.title: From Anton Stecker   24 February 1879
letters.summary:
Has not been able to complete Bohemian edition ofOriginbecause of trip to Africa.

Is collecting zoological evidence for CD’s theory.

letters.title: From Hugo de Vries   24 February 1879
letters.summary: Did not wish to imply that some leaves are insensitive to light, only that he could not measure their sensitivity. Contraction of roots seems common.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin  [before 25 February 1879]
letters.summary:
CD cannot find his pincers and other tools for microscopical dissection. Does FD know where he should look?

Hopes FD will feel better after "so complete a change" [trip to North Africa].

Sends his love to George.

Bernard gets more charming every day.

CD has been put on a committee for a memorial fund for W. K. Clifford.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [c.25 February 1879]
letters.summary: Directs CD where to find tools in his room. Has been looking at agave and aloe flowers. Thanks family for their letters.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   25 February [1879]
letters.summary: Thanks CD profusely for the circular which detailed his and Emma Darwin’s plans to increase their children’s income. Thinks a few hundred really makes the difference for feeling really rich, especially as he now knows how important it is for bankers to have available personal savings.

letters.title: To Karl Höchberg   25 February 1879
letters.summary: Discusses the value of a vegetable diet.

letters.title: To C. A. Lindvall   25 February 1879
letters.summary:
CAL’s letter [see11885] would not be printed by the Geological Society as it is too speculative and has no new information.

Encloses his photograph.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   25 [February 1879]
letters.summary: Thanks for book [Duchartre,Éléments de botanique].

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   [after 25 February 1879]
letters.summary: Frank [Darwin] has found aTrifoliumremarkable for "bloom", but it was not in flower. If GHD knows where it grows, could he dig up the whole plant?

letters.title: To E. K. Blyth   26 February [1879]
letters.summary: Details of publications by G. H. Darwin.

letters.title: To S. J. Pozzi   26 February 1879
letters.summary: Thanks for sending him work on the skull.

letters.title: From E. P. Wright   26 February 1879
letters.summary: Is applying for the Chair of Botany at Edinburgh and asks CD for a testimonial.

letters.title: From Frederick King   27 February 1879
letters.summary: A founding member of the Royal Agricultural Society sends information on the specificity of sheep varieties to soil types.

letters.title: From A. S. Wilson   27 February 1879
letters.summary: Sends results of the first year’s experiments with the Russian wheat varieties sent by CD [see11483].

letters.title: From A. F. Batalin   28 February 1879
letters.summary: Sleep movements inOxalis acetosella.

letters.title: To the curators of patronage, Edinburgh University   28 February 1879
letters.summary: CD has read several papers by E. Perceval Wright and has a high opinion of his abilities and great zeal for natural science.

letters.title: To E. P. Wright   28 February [1879]
letters.summary: Has already written a testimonial for [?William Ramsay] McNab as Professor of Botany. Hence what he can write for EPW will not be of much use.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   [1 March 1879?]
letters.summary:
Can FG come to lunch on Monday?

Sorry FG has not been well and is soon going abroad.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   3 March [1879]
letters.summary: Astonished at circular and will risk revolutions to invest. Describes Blidah, Algeria.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   3 March 1879
letters.summary:
Thanks CD [for his increased allowance?].

Writes of his tour [in Algeria].

letters.title: From W. D. Fox   3 March [1879]
letters.summary:
Sends family news;

describes what remains of his "menagerie" and tells of his interest in the framework of his son’s German badger-hound.

letters.title: To J. N. Lockyer   4 and 6 March [1879]
letters.summary: Encloses a letter [from Fritz Müller, see11839] which "eminentlydeserves to be published inNature". Discusses the form and illustration needed. Spelling problems to be referred to Robert McLachlan.

letters.title: From A. R. Leeds   4 March 1879
letters.summary: CD elected an honorary member of the New York Academy of Sciences.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   4 March 1879
letters.summary: Has sent FM’s letter on caddis-fly toNature["On a frog and caddis-flies",Nature19 (1879): 462–4].

letters.title: To L. A. Errera   5 March 1879
letters.summary: Thanks LAE for publication [Errera and G. Gevaert,Sur la structure et les modes de fécondation des fleurs, 1ère partie (1878)].

letters.title: To A. S. Wilson   5 March 1879
letters.summary: Discusses ASW’s discovery of error in Russian belief about wheat varieties. Suggests that he publish paper inJournal of Royal Agricultural Society. [Results actually published inGard. Chron.n.s. 11 (1879): 622–4.]

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   8 March [1879]
letters.summary: Has read Krause’s "Life of Erasmus Darwin" [Kosmos4 (1879): 397–424]; thinks it very interesting to anyone interested in "Darwinismus" – everybody.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   9 March 1879
letters.summary: CD and his brother Erasmus have read EK’s article on Erasmus Darwin. Asks whether EK would object to a translation by W. Dallas, to be offered toFortnightly Reviewor to be published at CD’s expense as a book.

letters.title: From C. H. Browning   10 March 1879
letters.summary: Is readingOriginon inheritance. Reports case of a man who went bald through illness, whose three sons, all born later, also became bald.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   10 March [1879]
letters.summary: Thanks for second edition of Duchartre.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   11 March [1879]
letters.summary: Suggests CD sendKosmosto W. S. Dallas as Krause will surely give his permission for translation.

letters.title: To W. S. Dallas   12 March [1879]
letters.summary: Asks whether WSD would be interested in translating Ernst Krause’s article on Erasmus Darwin [Kosmos4 (1879): 397–424] into English.

letters.title: From Alexander Dick-Cunyngham   12 March 1879
letters.summary: Report of wild ass crossed with tame one in India.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   12 March 1879
letters.summary: Glad CD is pleased by his "Erasmus Darwin". Was not able to obtain book by Anna Seward [Memoirs of the life of Dr Darwin(1804)]. Could CD check relevant passages for errors? Would be great honour if CD could arrange English translation. Wants to enlarge essay into book.

letters.title: To Robert McLachlan   12 March [1879]
letters.summary: Asks RMcL to correct the proper names in enclosed proof of a letter from Fritz Müller to be published inNature. CD has no book with names of Trichoptera. [See11930.]

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   13 March [1879]
letters.summary: Sends suggestions for CD’s preface toErasmus Darwin.
