letters.title: To L. A. Errera   13 March 1879
letters.summary: Comments on book by LAE and Gustave Gevaert [see11916].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   13 March 1879
letters.summary: Urges Frank to reconsider his refusal of Cambridge Examinership.

letters.title: From Robert McLachlan   13 March 1879
letters.summary:
Returns to CD a corrected proof [of "Fritz Müller on a frog having eggs on its back",Nature19 (1878–9): 462–4].

Discusses adaptations of the pupae of, and Fritz Müller’s work on, Trichoptera.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   13 March 1879
letters.summary: Thanks for seeds and for kindness to Frank Darwin.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   14 March 1879
letters.summary:
Offers to translate [E. Krause’s] "Erasmus Darwin" for £10.

Thanks CD for signing his certificate for the Royal Society.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   14 March 1879
letters.summary:
Pleased to hear that EK agrees to CD’s request to have article on Erasmus Darwin translated. Will wait for EK’s enlargement. Has decided submission toFortnightly Reviewwould be useless.

Warns against Anna Seward’s biography of Dr Darwin.

letters.title: To B. W. Richardson   14 March 1879
letters.summary: Remembers that BWR had planned to write a life of Erasmus Darwin. Ernst Krause now intends to enlarge hisErasmus Darwin; would welcome any information or material.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   15 March 1879
letters.summary: Repeats his willingness to translate E. Krause’s "Erasmus Darwin".

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   16 March [1879]
letters.summary: Frank’s reasons for not accepting the Cambridge Examinership.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   17 March 1879
letters.summary:
Had doubts about excerpt from Anna Seward’s book [Life of Dr Darwin]. Sends slightly enlarged version of his "Erasmus Darwin". Includes footnote denouncing Seward’s book.

Finds that part 2 of ED’sBotanic garden, 2d ed. (1790), appeared before part 1 (1791).

letters.title: From W. B. Tegetmeier   17 March 1879
letters.summary: Asks if CD would like to subscribe to a reprint of Edward Blyth’sFieldarticles on cranes.

letters.title: To Hendrik Weyenbergh   18 March 1879
letters.summary:
Acknowledges the diploma [of the Academia Nacional de Ciencias, Argentina].

Sends his photograph and a copy ofOrigin.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   19 March 1879
letters.summary:
Sends copy of a lecture [by John Dowson, see11949] published in 1861.

Has not yet found a copy of Anna Seward’s biography for EK. It is a wretched, inaccurate book. To contradict Anna Seward’s version, CD intends to write a short preface to the translation of EK’s essay. Doubts that it will be worth translating into German.

letters.title: ToNature   [before 20 March 1879]
letters.summary: Comments on a letter from Fritz Müller [11839] and particularly on the subject of the disappearance of certain structures in organisms. FM’s explanation deserves serious consideration.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   20 March 1879
letters.summary: CD agrees to subscribe to reprint of Blyth’sFieldarticles on cranes.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   22 March 1879
letters.summary:
Describes plans to publish English edition of Krause’s work on Erasmus Darwin.

Will correct Anna Seward’s calumnies [inMemoirs of the life of Dr Darwin(1804)].

Asks about family letters.

Doubts some stories about Erasmus Darwin [in Christiana C. Hankin, ed.,Life of Mary Anne Schimmelpenninck(1858)].

letters.title: To Wilhelm Pfeffer   23 March 1879
letters.summary: Seeks clarification of statements on sleep movements on p. 29 of WFPP’s work [Die periodischen Bewegungen der Blattorgane(1875)].

letters.title: To C. M. C. Darwin   24 March 1879
letters.summary: Can CMCD provide a photograph of Elston, the birthplace of Erasmus Darwin, with permission to have it reproduced inErasmus Darwin.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   24 March 1879
letters.summary: Thanks for sketch of Erasmus Darwin by John Dowson [seeErasmus Darwin, p. iv]; would like to incorporate this information into MS. Previous biographers of Erasmus Darwin had insufficient knowledge of what appeared in his works.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   24 March 1879
letters.summary:
Wants aCassiaidentified

and several plants and seeds for experimental purposes.

letters.title: From L. A. Errera   25 March 1879
letters.summary: Sends his photograph as requested.

letters.title: From E. A. Wheler   25 March 1879
letters.summary: Regrets she has none of Dr Erasmus Darwin’s letters. Relates some anecdotes concerning her grandfather.

letters.title: From E. S. Galton   25 March 1879
letters.summary: Notes and a copy of a letter written by ESG to John Dowson of Whitby. Expresses her opinion of the biographies of Erasmus Darwin written by Mrs Schimmelpenninck and Anna Seward.

letters.title: From Frederick King   25 March 1879
letters.summary: Cattle and sheep varieties removed from their native soils degenerate rapidly.

letters.title: To E. A. Wheler   26 March 1879
letters.summary: Thanks for information and stories about Erasmus Darwin.

letters.title: To C. S. Wedgwood   26 March 1879
letters.summary: Discusses information about Dr Erasmus Darwin.

letters.title: ToNature   [before 27 March 1879]
letters.summary: In reply to a query [inNature19 (1879): 433] CD reports that vessels full of water were kept on the deck of a ship to discourage rats from gnawing holes in the ship’s water casks.

letters.title: From C. M. C. Darwin   27 March 1879
letters.summary:
They have never had any Erasmus Darwin letters.

Sends photographs [of Elston Hall].

letters.title: To Reginald Darwin   27 March 1879
letters.summary: Announces his intention to translate and preface [E. Krause’s] sketch of Dr Erasmus Darwin’s life. Asks whether RD has any documents concerning Dr Darwin or letters by him.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   27 March 1879
letters.summary:
CD has written to members of the family for Dr Erasmus Darwin materials and letters. Is apprehensive lest his preface and EK’s essay interfere with one another. Will confine himself to ED’s character and letters;

has begun investigating the influence he had on medical practice.

letters.title: From E. A. Wheler   28 March 1879
letters.summary: Sends a book by her uncle, Charles Darwin [1758–78], and recounts some details of the life of her grandfather, Dr Erasmus Darwin.

letters.title: From Reginald Darwin   29 March 1879
letters.summary:
Sends Dr Erasmus Darwin’s commonplace book, some letters, and poems.

Family news.

letters.title: To Friedrich Hildebrand   29 March 1879
letters.summary: Thanks for FHGH’s new book; also for the list of seeds, but he does not want any at present.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   30 March 1879
letters.summary: Wants to finish revision of MS on Erasmus Darwin before Dallas begins translation. Has discussed possible German edition with Carl Alberts.

letters.title: From A. G. Butler   31 March 1879
letters.summary:
Has succeeded in obtaining Assistant Keeper’s post.

Believes it would be interesting and valuable to study the variation in organs such as scent-fans and "strigillating" [stridulating?] organs among related species of Lepidoptera.

letters.title: To E. A. Wheler   31 March [1879]
letters.summary:
Requests information about a travel route used by their grandfather, Erasmus Darwin. Thanks FG for his help.

CD is "now trying to find out how far theZoonomiainfluenced medical practice in England".

letters.title: From E. S. Galton   31 March 1879
letters.summary: Sends drawings of several of Dr Erasmus Darwin’s residences, together with suggestions of sources of other material.

letters.title: To Reginald Darwin   1 April 1879
letters.summary:
The "great book" [presumably Dr Erasmus Darwin’s commonplace book, seeErasmus Darwin, p. iii] arrived safely.

Can RD supply a photograph of [Breadsall] Priory?

letters.title: From Alfred Newton   1 April 1879
letters.summary: Asks CD to join W. H. Flower and Huxley in signing a memorial in support of Dr Cone. He is a U. S. Army surgeon who has been working on an ornithological bibliography and needs support to complete his work in England.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   1 April [1879]
letters.summary: Thanks for the plants for heliotropic experiments.

letters.title: From Reginald Darwin   2 April 1879
letters.summary:
Will try to find an engraving of [Breadsall] Priory.

Offers a photograph of Dr Erasmus Darwin’s house in Derby.

letters.title: To E. S. Galton   2 April [1879]
letters.summary: Parcel of drawings and MS arrived safely.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   2 April 1879
letters.summary: CD agrees entirely with EK’s proposal. Has collected a good deal of material. Useless to hunt for correspondence between Dr Darwin and Samuel Johnson. They met only once and hated one another. Dr Darwin is said to have taken Henry Brooke, who published a poem entitled "Universal beauty", as a model.

letters.title: From Nicolai Mengden   2 April 1879
letters.summary: NvM is 17 years old. Confused by reading CD’s works and Ernst Haeckel’sNatürliche Schöpfungsgeschichte[1868]. Can a believer in CD’s theory believe in God?

letters.title: To Alfred Newton   2 April [1879]
letters.summary:
"I have signed the enclosed with pleasure."

Thanks AN for his kind expression about Frank [Darwin].

letters.title: From Henry Reeks   3 April 1879
letters.summary: Sends a sample of seeds ofOnobrychis sativaandPoterium muricatum, plants that show mimicry.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   3 April [1879]
letters.summary: Thanks for WTT-D’s trouble.

letters.title: To Reginald Darwin   4 April 1879
letters.summary:
Has been "deeply interested by the great book" [see11966]. Asks permission to publish extracts.

Did Dr Darwin go to Edinburgh when his son, Charles, died? Asks whether RD has ever heard a story about Dr Darwin that had been told to CD by the Galtons.

letters.title: From V. H. Darwin   4 April 1879
letters.summary: Is interested to hear of CD’s life of Dr Erasmus Darwin. There is no photo of Breadsall Priory, but she would be happy to make a drawing of it.

letters.title: From Raphael Meldola   4 April 1879
letters.summary:
Sends specimens from F. Müller.

Criticises A. R. Wallace’s review of Grant Allen’sThe colour-sense[Nature19 (1879): 501–5].

letters.title: From H. G. Zeuthen   5 April 1879
letters.summary: CD made an ordinary member of the Royal Danish Academy. [See11984.]

letters.title: To C. M. C. Darwin   6 April 1879
letters.summary:
Sends details of the progress of his researches forErasmus Darwin.

His son Leonard will photograph Elston and Cleatham. He has found an early drawing of Elston.

Asks for a letter of introduction for Leonard Darwin to CMCD’s tenant at Elston.

letters.title: From Reginald Darwin   7 April 1879
letters.summary:
Is glad CD has found interest in "the old book" [Dr Erasmus Darwin’s commonplace book].

Discusses Erasmus Darwin and his belongings, which RD has inherited.

Owns a portrait of Erasmus Darwin by Joseph Wright of Derby.

letters.title: From Henry Reeks   7 April 1879
letters.summary: Suggests that mimicry of sainfoin by burnet plants is an adaptation against farmers’ weeding.

letters.title: To Reginald Darwin   8 April 1879
letters.summary:
Details of family history. Has discovered Dr Darwin did get to Edinburgh before his son, Charles, died.

The more CD reads of Dr Darwin the higher he rises in his estimation.

Is tired of writing letters, "half the fools throughout Europe write to ask me the stupidest questions".

letters.title: From Reginald Darwin   9 April 1879
letters.summary:
Has found a pamphlet of 1780 about Charles Darwin [1758–78].

RD’s sister, Violetta, has found some early verses and a MS by Dr Erasmus Darwin.

letters.title: From V. H. Darwin   9 April 1879
letters.summary: Gives some examples of Dr Erasmus Darwin’s benevolence; will forward some books that may interest CD.

letters.title: To H. G. Zeuthen   9 April 1879
letters.summary: Thanks Royal Danish Academy for electing him as a Member, and for the kind expressions toward him from so many illustrious naturalists.

letters.title: To Reginald Darwin   10 April [1879]
letters.summary: Research forErasmus Darwin. CD has always thought there is one "golden rule" for biographers: "not to insert anything which … would interest only the members of the Family".

letters.title: From V. H. Darwin   12 April [1879]
letters.summary: Discusses material forErasmus Darwinincluding an engraved portrait by Joseph Wright.

letters.title: To E. A. Wheler   12 April 1879
letters.summary: Thanks EAW for assistance. Describes plans for writing preliminary sketch [for Ernst Krause’sErasmus Darwin].

letters.title: From B. W. Richardson   12 April 1879
letters.summary: He has nothing at all to send in answer to CD’s questions respecting the book on Erasmus Darwin.

letters.title: From V. H. Darwin   13 April [1879]
letters.summary: Sends her sketch of [Breadsall] Priory, as renovated by present owner.

letters.title: To Fanny Kellogg   13 April 1879
letters.summary: Sends thanks for "communicating the curious case of a habitual gesture, like that which I have treated as inherited. I may add that since I write, the action has been transmitted to another generation. Your case shall be sent to Mr Galton, who gave me the information".

letters.title: From C. M. C. Darwin   14 April 1879
letters.summary:
Answers CD’s query about Robert Darwin of Lincoln’s Inn.

Sends an introduction for Leonard Darwin to their tenants at Elston Hall.

letters.title: To C. M. C. Darwin   15 April 1879
letters.summary:
Thanks for letter of introduction for Leonard Darwin to CMCD’s tenant at Elston.

Sends some information about R. W. Darwin’s residence at Elston; does not plan to include a portrait of him.

Asks the acreage of land at Cleatham.

Offers to send a print of the portrait of himself by W. W. Ouless.

letters.title: From C. M. C. Darwin   16 April [1879]
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for offer of his portrait.

Suggests a solicitor who has Darwin papers and who may have information about Cleatham.

Describes her portrait of Erasmus Darwin.

letters.title: To Reginald Darwin   16 April 1879
letters.summary: Sends letters from RD’s father to R. W. Darwin.

letters.title: From Wilhelm Breitenbach   17 April 1879
letters.summary: Observations on unusual mating behaviour of canaries.

letters.title: From E. A. Wheler   17 April 1879
letters.summary: Relates more family history and anecdotes concerning Dr Erasmus Darwin.

letters.title: From C.-F. Reinwald   17 April 1879
letters.summary:
Second edition of Edmond Barbier’s revised translation ofOriginselling out; third one to be published.

A new edition ofVariation, virtually retranslated by Barbier, is in press.

Second edition ofDescentselling out.

CD’s botanical books are losing money.

letters.title: From Reginald Darwin   18 April 1879
letters.summary: Thanks CD for sending some old family letters of RD’s father’s [Francis Sacheverel Darwin (1786–1859)].

letters.title: From E. A. Wheler   18 April 1879
letters.summary: Forwards a letter [missing] from her cousin relating to Dr Erasmus Darwin.

letters.title: From Raphael Meldola   18 April 1879
letters.summary: Comments on the branchiate trichopteran specimen from Fritz Müller sent previously.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   19 April [1879]
letters.summary: Thanks him for his efforts. CD cared most about the letter to Thomas Okes [seeErasmus Darwin, pp. 14–15]. "Cannot think who the calumnious article cd have been about [in?] 1802."

letters.title: To E. A. Wheler   19 April 1879
letters.summary: Thanks his cousin for lending two letters [to be used in Ernst Krause’s biography of Erasmus Darwin, their grandfather].

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   19 April 1879
letters.summary:
Thanks for Haeckel’sFreedom in science and teaching[1879], with preface by THH.

Enjoyed rap on knuckles THH gives Rudolf Virchow.

letters.title: From C. M. C. Darwin   21 April [1879]
letters.summary: Thanks CD for the engraving, which has arrived.

letters.title: To ?   21 April 1879
letters.summary:
Thanks for letter and articles: gratifying to hear that agriculturalists attend to his works.

Cannot decipher German writing so has stuck the address from the letter on the envelope.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   22 April [1879]
letters.summary: Discusses his work on Dr Erasmus Darwin’s life.

letters.title: From Wilhelm Pfeffer   22 April 1879
letters.summary: In response to CD’s query, discusses sleep movements of plants. Recommends papers on subject.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   22 April [1879]
letters.summary: Asks for identification of anOxalisflower.

letters.title: From W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   22 April 1879
letters.summary: Oliver saysOxalis colorataisO. floribunda.

letters.title: To T. L. Brunton   25 April 1879
letters.summary: Asks for information about his grandfather’s influence on medical practice, to be used in his preface toErasmus Darwin[1879, p. 107].

letters.title: From T. L. Brunton   26 April [1879]
letters.summary: Regrets he has not givenZoonomiathe attention it deserves. Informs CD that Erasmus Darwin may have anticipated a discovery about paralysis of vessels by exposure to heat [seeErasmus Darwin, p. 109].

letters.title: To T. L. Brunton   28 April 1879
letters.summary: Thanks for information about Erasmus Darwin and for lending journal.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   29 April [1879]
letters.summary: There is a hyacinth growing upside down in Hankinson’s garden. Sends picture of it. Leslie Stephen knows of no worthwhile sources of information on Dr Erasmus Darwin.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   29 April 1879
letters.summary:
Admires EH’sFreie Wissenschaft und freie Lehre[1878].

Virchow’s conduct is shameful.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   30 April [1879]
letters.summary: Thanks FG for an extract [about Dr Erasmus Darwin?].

letters.title: From Anthony Rich   30 April [1879]
letters.summary: Will see CD in Worthing next week.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   30 April 1879
letters.summary: Has had an account of his experiments published. Sends CD some specimens of seedlings and tubers.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin?   [May 1879?]
letters.summary: Reginald Darwin’s pleasure at receiving some old family information.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   1 May 1879
letters.summary: Describes one of his varieties of potato in its third and fourth years. [CD notes his observations on this variety grown at Down, July 1879.]

letters.title: To Grant Allen   2 [May] 1879
letters.summary: Has just read GA’s article inFortnightly Review["A problem of human evolution", 31 (1879): 778–86]. GA’s views very probable. Something wonderful to hear anyone defending sexual selection.

letters.title: To Reginald Darwin   2 May 1879
letters.summary:
Leaves home on 6th for a rest.

Will commence writingErasmus Darwin.

Apologises for keeping RD’s various books for so long a time.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   2 May 1879
letters.summary: CD is leaving home for three weeks’ rest. If EK finishes his life of Dr Darwin while CD is away, asks him to send the MS to W. S. Dallas for translation. CD will begin his preface, but needs rest and will not do much until he returns.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [before 3 May 1879]
letters.summary: Encloses some references [missing] to information on Dr Erasmus Darwin.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   3 May [1879]
letters.summary: Asks GHD to look in Cambridge University Library forMonthly Magazinearticles containing a malicious calumny concerning Dr [Erasmus] D[arwin] [seeErasmus Darwin, pp. 65–70].

letters.title: To E. A. Wheler   3 May 1879
letters.summary: Returns documents pertaining to Dr Erasmus Darwin.

letters.title: To James Torbitt   3 May 1879
letters.summary: Encourages JT’s experiments. His case of flowering of black potatoes is curious. CD surprised that they are odoriferous and visited by bees. This letter was thought to be to David Moore, because it was in the private collection of a descendant, but is extremely close to a draft to JT on the letter from JT, 30 April 1879 (DCP-LETT-12020). It is not known how it passed from JT to David Moore.

letters.title: To C. S. Wedgwood   [3 May 1879]
letters.summary:
Was it Lady Charlemont or Charleville who remarked how agreeable their grandfather was?

Asks her to confirm story about Robert Darwin (father of Dr Erasmus).

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   4 May 1879
letters.summary: Is struck by the amazing variations of the hardyPrimulavarieties.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   5 May [1879]
letters.summary: Asks GHD to look for a life of Sir Henry Rayburn [Raeburn] "who is spoken of as famous and who painted Charles Darwin [1758–1778] when dead". Asks why he painted the corpse.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   5 May 1879
letters.summary:
Sends CD an article on Dr Erasmus Darwin [fromMonthly Magazine, see12028].

Tells of a "discovery" he has made about taking observations of the sun. Does not know yet whether it is new.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   5 [May] 1879
letters.summary:
Thinks it better to send proofs of his preface [toErasmus Darwin] rather than MS – he always corrects proofs heavily. Doubts that it is worth translating into German – it is written for the English public. Supposes EK will not object to a French translation and an American edition of the little book. Has written a dozen pages during a break

in his experimental work [on movement of plants].

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   5 May 1879
letters.summary:
Sends first part of MS ofErasmus Darwin.

Has found useful criticism of Anna Seward in J. G. Lockhart’sLife of Sir Walter Scott.

CD should regard MS as a draft and correct anything that seems incorrect or questionable. Asks biographical questions about Dr Darwin. Can CD give information about origin of family name?

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   7 May 1879
letters.summary: Has received the enlarged MS forErasmus Darwinfrom E. Krause.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   7 May [1879]
letters.summary:
A big book arrived for GHD before CD left Down. Hopes it is Thomson and Tait [Treatise on natural philosophy, 2 vols., 2d ed. (1869)]. It shows what they think of GHD.

Thinks it grand if GHD has made a correction about "such an old sinner as the Sun" and hopes his arithmetic on his old subject will turn out right.

letters.title: From Leonard Darwin   7 May 1879
letters.summary: Has been trying unsuccessfully to weigh something for CD.

letters.title: To John Fordyce   7 May 1879
letters.summary: Believes it absurd to doubt that a man may be an ardent theist and evolutionist; gives the examples of Kingsley and Asa Gray. As regards CD’s own views, his judgement often fluctuates but "I have never been an Atheist in the sense of denying the existence of God". Thinks that "generally (and more and more as I grow older) … an Agnostic would be the most correct description of my state of mind".

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   8 May 1879
letters.summary:
Has difficulty with E. Krause’s orthography and quotations.

Asks CD to lend him Anna Seward’s biography [Memoirs of the life of Dr Darwin(1804)].

letters.title: From John Fordyce   8 May 1879
letters.summary: Compatibility of evolution and theism.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   8 May 1879
letters.summary: Will wait for CD’s preliminary essay before proceeding with German edition [ofErasmus Darwin]. Regards CD’s essay as the principal attraction. Would like to finish German edition by end of July.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   9 May 1879
letters.summary: Has CD seen Samuel Butler’sEvolution, old and new[1879], which contains a biography of Erasmus Darwin and exposition of his philosophy? "Does not this rather take the wind out of our sails?"

letters.title: From K. P. von Kaufman   9 May 1879
letters.deprecated: Konstantin Petrovich (Константин Петрович фон Кауфман) von Kaufman
letters.sender: Konstantin Petrovich (Константин Петрович фон Кауфман) von Kaufman
letters.summary: Sends a collection of wheat varieties from Turkestan in response to a newspaper notice of CD’s interest.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   9 May [1879]
letters.summary: Answers EK’s queries about Erasmus Darwin’s friends and relations. Will rectify Anna Seward’s false account of Dr Darwin’s conduct. Advises EK to leave to him the account of the Darwin family. Declines EK’s offer to allow CD to alter his MS. Fears repetition in the two essays. They can judge how best to present the material when they have seen each other’s manuscripts.

letters.title: From H. A. Pitman   9 May 1879
letters.summary: CD awarded the Baly Medal of the Royal College of Physicians.

letters.title: From Robert Tachau   9 May 1879
letters.summary: Are modifications in human form and intellect due solely to natural selection or do altered external conditions also play a role?

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   10 May 1879
letters.summary: Sends abstracts of more articles [on Dr Erasmus Darwin] fromMonthly Magazine.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   [11 May 1879]
letters.summary: CD is particularly obliged for the copy of Maria Edgeworth’s letter.

letters.title: To J. S. Burdon Sanderson   13 May 1879
letters.summary: CD astonished at receiving the Baly Medal of the Royal College of Physicians.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   13 May 1879
letters.summary:
Assures EK he will lose no time in writing his essay [on Erasmus Darwin].

A book by Samuel Butler on Erasmus Darwin and Lamarck has been announced [Evolution, old and new(1879)]. Will have a copy sent to EK.

letters.title: To H. A. Pitman   [13 May 1879]
letters.summary: Appreciates award of the Baly Medal and hopes to attend ceremony on 26 June.

letters.title: From J. S. Burdon Sanderson   14 May 1879
letters.summary: Has received CD’s letter [see12050]. Gives CD the history of the Baly Medal and names previous recipients. It is not necessary for CD to be present for the award, but if he chooses to attend, arrangements could be made for him to arrive just before the presentation. CD will not be required to make an acceptance speech.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   14 May 1879
letters.summary:
Assures EK that he will not change his mind about publishing a translation of EK’s article on Erasmus Darwin. It is unfortunate that Samuel Butler should have published [Evolution, old and new] just then, but that does not change CD’s determination.

Butler is clever, but knows no science. His views that cells have memory and the power of wishing – even if correct – cannot explain how they could change themselves chemically or structurally.

EK can do anything he likes with CD’s preface [toErasmus Darwin].

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   15 May [1879]
letters.summary: Sends some queries connected with his writing of the biographical preface toErasmus Darwin.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   15 May 1879
letters.summary:
Thanks for answers to questions [in12032].

Has ordered the new book by Butler [Evolution, old and new(1879)]. It may make EK’s own essay superfluous.

letters.title: From Charles Moore   15 May 1879
letters.summary: Sends an ammonite from the Upper Lias, which hasBalanus-like bodies on surface. He wants CD’s interpretation. Discusses possible function of aptychi, siphuncular tube, and operculum in ammonites.

letters.title: From W. T. Winn   16 May 1879
letters.summary: Sends newspaper cutting referring to CD.

letters.title: From C. Harris   20 May 1879
letters.summary: Wants some Sunday tickets for the Zoological Garden.

letters.title: From E. J. Collings   21 May 1879
letters.summary: Wants information on the use of reason by animals.

letters.title: From W. M. Hacon   22 May 1879
letters.summary: Has searched to no avail for 17th- and 18th-century wills to learn how Elston Hall was acquired by Robert Darwin rather than by William Darwin, even though Robert was the younger son.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   23 May 1879
letters.summary:
Samuel Butler seems not even to have read works of Erasmus Darwin. Quotes only passages quoted by other authors. Thorough account now more necessary than ever.

CD’s preliminary notice should be incorporated in German edition completely unchanged, though some annotation is needed to explain matters unfamiliar to German readers.

Would like to have article by CD forKosmos.

letters.title: To E. J. Collings   25 May [1879]
letters.summary: Refers EJC to papers by G. J. Romanes ["Animal intelligence",Nineteenth Century4 (1878): 653–72] and William James ["Brute and human intellect",J. Speculative Philos.12 (1878): 236–76] on the mind of animals.

letters.title: To Grant Allen   26 May [1879]
letters.summary: Has GA seen an article on GA’sColour-senseby a great man, J. R. L. Delboeuf, inRevue Scientifique24 May 1879? It has pleased CD greatly.

letters.title: From Albin Gaertner   27 May 1879
letters.summary:
CD’s works have opened a new world for him.

Sends a case of inheritance: a fingernail biting habit has persisted for four generations in a Viennese lawyer’s family.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   27 May 1879
letters.summary:
CD’s preface [forErasmus Darwin] is delayed by his sitting for a portrait.

Explains to EK why he feels unable to contribute articles toKosmos.

letters.title: From V. H. Darwin   28 May [1879]
letters.summary: Will attempt to copy the drawing of Elston Hall [Erasmus Darwin, p. 3]. Does not remember the highway robber story [ibid., pp. 64–5].

letters.title: To G. G. Stokes   28 May 1879
letters.summary: Reports on Joseph Prestwich’s paper, "On the origin of the parallel roads of Lochaber" [read 1 May 1879]. Strongly recommends that the paper be published inPhilosophical Transactions[Philos. Trans. R. Soc. Lond.170 (1880): 663–726].

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [before 29 May 1879]
letters.summary: Try to find and read [a German] account of the fir-trees affected by some fungus which produces upright shoots. CD wants to know whether the case is same as what he has observed in the silver fir. Includes diagram.

letters.title: From Grant Allen   29 May 1879
letters.summary: Thanks for postcard informing him of Delboeuf’s review of his book; he had already seen review.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   29 May 1879
letters.summary: Fungus is an Aecidium. Porliera, Anthuriums and Aroids will hopefully sprout if weather gets hot. Sachs has changed his ideas about the cause of heliotropism. Describes men he is sharing a lab with.

letters.title: To Reginald Darwin   29 May [1879]
letters.summary:
Encloses a family document [another letter from F. S. Darwin to R. W. Darwin?].

Asks whether RD has ever heard a story about their grandfather and a highway robber.

letters.title: From V. H. Darwin   30 [May 1879]
letters.summary:
Will be glad to draw Elston Hall for CD.

Gives some details of Sir Brook Boothby.

letters.title: From Anthony Rich   30 May 1879
letters.summary:
Speaks of the delight of having met CD.

Hopes William Darwin may be able to visit Worthing.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   31 May [1879]
letters.summary:
Sends a letter [missing] on the chance that GHD might give the writer information about tides.

Rejoices at GHD’s friendship with Sir W. Thomson and grand vein of research he has struck on.

First draft of life of Dr [Erasmus] D[arwin] is nearly finished.

letters.title: From Reginald Darwin   31 May 1879
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for another letter [of his father’s].

Cannot call to mind the story about the robber [seeErasmus Darwin, pp. 64–5].

letters.title: To G. S. Ffinden   31 May 1879
letters.summary: CD’s sister-in-law, S. E. Wedgwood, is willing to refund £10 of the money paid for her land if the Ecclesiastical Commissioners will write saying she ought to do so, or if a qualified surveyor proves that the first measurement was wrong.

letters.title: From G. S. Ffinden   31 May 1879
letters.summary: The official parish tithe map shows that a greater error than at first thought was made in measuring Miss Wedgwood’s land. She was overpaid £15 10s.

letters.title: To Albin Gaertner   31 May 1879
letters.summary: Thanks FAG for "the curious case of inheritance" [see12064].

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [2 June 1879 or earlier]
letters.summary: Wants FD to find out what sort of man Ernst Krause is.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   2 June [1879]
letters.summary:
Thanks for FD’s letter describing microscopic work under experienced supervision.

Is glad to hear of C. E. Stahl’s objection to treating plants as mere machines.

Pleased that J. von Sachs has yielded on growth.

Perhaps Stahl will recognise whether the case of the silver fir is the same as that referred to in the German account [see12074b].

CD has finished the first draft of his essay on Erasmus Darwin’s life and is "heartily sick of the job".

letters.title: To John Murray   2 June 1879
letters.summary: Intends to publish a translation of Ernst Krause’s essay on Dr Erasmus Darwin, with a prefatory notice by himself. Asks JM to decide whether to publish it on commission or on usual two-thirds profit terms. CD incapable of judging chance of its selling.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [after 2 June 1879]
letters.summary:
Geotropism.

Experimenting onPorlieriain damp and dry earth.

Hermann Müller has been ridiculed for teaching children "in the beginning was Carbon".

Will ask about Ernst Krause.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   3 June [1879]
letters.summary:
Asks whether canary grass and oats have chlorophyll in their cotyledons.

Has been working hard at circumnutation of leaves to see whether sleep movements are exaggerated circumnutation.

letters.title: From Nicolai Mengden   3 June 1879
letters.summary: Thanks for reply to query. Asked E. Haeckel same question and his answer agreed with CD’s. Haeckel disbelieves in the supernatural. What does CD think?

letters.title: From John Murray   3 June [1879]
letters.summary: Is well disposed toward publishing Krause’s essay on Dr Erasmus Darwin, particularly if CD undertakes to fill up its gaps. He thinks ED’s reputation is increasing.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   4 June 1879
letters.summary: Has finished the first part of Krause’s MS [ofErasmus Darwin]. Expects to receive the concluding portion soon.

letters.title: To G. S. Ffinden   4 June 1879
letters.summary: Does not feel competent to judge on matters of measurement. R. B. Litchfield to look into case.

letters.title: From Raphael Meldola   4 June 1879
letters.summary: Wants to republish Fritz Müller’s paper ["ItunaandThyridia",Kosmos5 (1879): 100–8] inProceedings of the Entomological Society. [Thyridita!?]

letters.title: To A. S. Wilson   4 [June] 1879
letters.summary: Mentions wheat varieties sent by Governor General of Turkestan.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [before 5 June 1879]
letters.summary: Believes that he will prove that the tip of radicle is the brain as far as geotropism is concerned.

letters.title: From V. H. Darwin   5 June [1879]
letters.summary: Sends her drawing of Elston Hall as it was in 1754.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   5 June 1879
letters.summary: Has read Dallas’ translation of first part of EK’s essay [on Erasmus Darwin]. Has sent his MS to printer. Is perplexed by duplication. Thinks EK’s essay is better than his. Wishes he had sent all his material to him for a single biography. Best plan may be for EK to incorporate whatever he thinks useful in CD’s material.

letters.title: To Nicolai Mengden   5 June 1879
letters.summary: NvM’s questions cannot be answered fully. "Science has nothing to do with Christ, except in so far as the habit of scientific research makes a man cautious in admitting evidence. For myself, I do not believe that there has ever been any Revelation."

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   5 June 1879
letters.summary:
Has been writing life of Erasmus Darwin.

Wants plants with heliotropic aerial roots. Has proved root apex governs nature of flexure in upper part of root.

letters.title: To ?   5 June 1879
letters.summary:
Unable to accept invitation.

Looked at leaves and saw no sign that animal matter was absorbed. Believes insects were caught only accidentally.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   6 and 7 June [1879]
letters.summary: Describes his experiments investigating the geotropic responses of radicles.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   6 June [1879]
letters.summary: Suggests he write to Ernst Krause about publication of translation of Fritz Müller’s paper. FM’s view of mutual protection is quite new to CD.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   7 June 1879
letters.summary: Conveys some information about Dr Erasmus Darwin’s second wife and discusses photos of him and his wife.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   7 June 1879
letters.summary: Hopes to send last part of his work soon. CD may lay it aside or print only parts of it. Wants to add account of evolutionists before Erasmus Darwin. Superficial account by Samuel Butler makes this necessary.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   8 June [1879]
letters.summary: Caroline Darwin says mysterious visitor’s name was Brand. It was in time of Colonel Pole. Never visited Mrs Pole or Mrs Darwin [Elizabeth Collier], but sent respectful messages.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   9 June 1879
letters.summary: Memorandum about Dr Erasmus Darwin’s bequests.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   9 June [1879]
letters.summary:
CD is glad to hear that EK plans a short historical discussion on evolution [inErasmus Darwin],

but hopes he will not spend much powder and shot on Butler – his ephemeral work is not worth it. Sends a review [ofEvolution, old and new].

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   9 June 1879
letters.summary: Reports on his family’s illnesses and other domestic matters.

letters.title: To John Fiske   10 June 1879
letters.summary: Invitation to Down for the 18th. W. B. Richmond, who is painting CD’s portrait, will also be there.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   10 June [1879]
letters.summary: CD’s father thought he had not been treated fairly about his share of his mother’s [Mary Howard Darwin’s] fortune. Will not allude to this [inErasmus Darwin]. Surprising that grandfather did not make more money. Has found memorandum of his having lost £1500 in ironworks.

letters.title: To B. J. Sulivan   10 June 1879
letters.summary:
The progress of the Fuegians is wonderful.

Sympathises with the "lamentable state" BJS and his family have been in.

letters.title: From W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   10 June 1879
letters.summary:
Sleep inCrotalaria.

Report of John Ball’s lecture to Geographical Society: Alpine flora is direct descendant of Palaeozoic flora ["On the origin of the flora of the European Alps",Proceedings of the Royal Geographical Society and Monthly Record of Geography1: 564–88].

letters.title: From F. B. White   11 June 1879
letters.summary: Is applying for the Chair in Zoology at Owens College and asks CD for a testimonial.

letters.title: To F. B. White   [after 11 June 1879]
letters.summary: Does not feel he knows enough of FBW to offer his opinion as a testimonial.

letters.title: From Paul Aussant-Carà   13 June 1879
letters.summary: Expresses great admiration for CD and requests a picture of him with his signature.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   13 June 1879
letters.summary:
Has completed his MS and sent it to Dallas.

Has ignored Butler’s criticism of natural selection and corrected only his views of Buffon and Goethe.

It would be best to drop EK’s text from book and quote only certain portions of it.

letters.title: To John Fiske   14 June [1879]
letters.summary: Will send carriage to station on 18th.

letters.title: From Thomas Comber   15 June 1879
letters.summary: Sends specimens showing gynodioecism inPlantago lanceolata.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   15 [June 1879]
letters.summary:
CD’s little biography [Erasmus Darwin] has turned out very dull.

May FG’s tour turn out pleasant.

letters.title: From Hermann Otto   15 June 1879
letters.summary: Thanks for copy ofDescent.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   16 June 1879
letters.summary: Has just received concluding portion of Krause’s MS.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   16 June [1879]
letters.summary:
Has given his reasons for believing that twisting of stem is related to circumnutation inClimbing plants.

Tells results of experiments on movement of cotyledons and radicles.

Is getting aerial heliotropic roots from Kew.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   16 June [1879]
letters.summary: CD will attend to ELK’s suggestions, but there is plenty of time, because Dallas translates slowly and Murray will not publish the book before November.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [after 16 June 1879]
letters.summary: Reports on roots and climbing plants experiments he is performing in Sachs’ laboratory. Orchids with air roots have come. Goebel says proshelic better than helic.

letters.title: To H. A. Pitman   17 June 1879
letters.deprecated: Henry Alfred PitmanRoyal College of Physicians
letters.recipient: Henry Alfred PitmanRoyal College of Physicians
letters.summary: Asks for directions on how to behave at ceremony conferring the Baly Medal.

letters.title: From Raphael Meldola   18 June 1879
letters.summary: Discusses Fritz Müller’s paper on the mutual protection of certain mimics ["ItunaandThyridita",Trans. R. Entomol. Soc. Lond.(1879): xx–xxviii]. [Thyridia!?]

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   18 June 1879
letters.summary:
Thanks for plants

and case of sleepingCrotalaria.

"Bloom" for the present has "gone to the dogs".

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   19 [June 1879]
letters.summary: Shares RM’s misgivings about Fritz Müller’s mutually protecting mimics. Would expect bird’s response to distasteful caterpillars to be instinctive. Believes J. J. Weir or Thomas Belt may have investigated the point.

letters.title: To C. W. von Nägeli   21 June 1879
letters.summary: Thanks for a copy ofTheorie der Gärung.

letters.title: To W. D. Crick   24 June [1879]
letters.summary:
Thinks there is no particular interest in the abnormality in question.

Also CD has looked at several flowers and believes WDC may be mistaken in believing there is a rudimentary anther cell.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   24 June [1879]
letters.summary:
Movement in plants:PhilodendronandDendrobium.

Will go to London on Thursday to receive Baly Medal. Laura Forster has offered them her house in London.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   24 June 1879
letters.summary: Sends results of his researches on the Darwin family at the Record Office.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [after 24 June 1879]
letters.summary: Movement of radicles.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   25 June [1879]
letters.summary:
Suggests experiments to test the response of radicles to light. Considers an alternative term for heliotropism.

Will be curious to have FD’s spiral theory about circumnutation explained to him.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   25 June [1879]
letters.summary:
Comments in jocular vein on GHD’s "Darwin discoveries" about their ancestors.

Emma says CD needs a change and rest.

letters.title: To L. M. Forster   25 June 1879
letters.summary: Thanks her for loan of her house [Abinger Hammer].

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [before 26 June 1879]
letters.summary: Discusses results of geotropism experiment. Has started some heliotropic caustic experiments on mustard roots. Has trouble making marks.

letters.title: From T. L. Brunton   26 June [1879]
letters.summary: Has tried in vain to find out about the influence of Erasmus Darwin on the administration of stimulants in fever.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [26 June 1879]
letters.summary: Believes that the response of root tips to being "blinded" with foil is much more interesting than response to cauterisation.

letters.title: To T. L. Brunton   27 June 1879
letters.summary: Sir Robert Christison says Dr Darwin not the first to recommend alcohol for fever.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   27 June [1879]
letters.summary: Wishes to call on THF to discuss the situation with regard to Horace Darwin [who wishes to marry THF’s daughter, Emma Cecilia (Ida)].

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   28 June [1879]
letters.summary: Discusses the movements of radicles. His observations show that sensitivity to touch resides in the root tip and he believes that sensitivity to gravity governing geotropic responses is also in the root tip. Would much like to convert Julius von Sachs to his ideas on radicle movement.

letters.title: To Horace Darwin   [28 June 1879]
letters.summary: Sends an enclosure [a statement of CD’s finances and estimate of the inheritance his children may expect] for HD and Ida to read; CD very pleased to be able to leave his children comfortably provided for.

letters.title: To James Paget   28 June [1879]
letters.summary: Thanks JP for his kindness, but unfortunately the [unspecified] case is of no use to him.

letters.title: To G. B. Hill   1 July [1879]
letters.summary: Thanks GBNH for a fact about CD’s grandfather [Erasmus Darwin], but he will not be able to use it in his brief notice.

letters.title: To H. W. Reichardt   1 July 1879
letters.summary: Sends his autograph to HR for theGalerie internationale[1880].

letters.title: From Anthony Rich   1 July 1879
letters.summary:
Starlings seem to share their food. Are they communists as they struggle for their existence?

Describes movement of a caterpillar.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   2 July [1879]
letters.summary: FD’s experiment shows that caustic does not interfere with the bending of radicles. Believes that the apex is a kind of brain for certain movements, being specialised to receive certain irritations.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   2 July [1879]
letters.summary: Stresses importance of ensuring that cauterisation of radicles does not, through injury, prevent movement. Plans an experiment to test for "apheliotropism" in certain radicles.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   4 July 1879
letters.summary:
Heliotropism nomenclature. Apheliotropic mustard roots grow more quickly in dark. Measures growth with microscope as S. H. Vines did in mould. Studying air roots.

FD’s and Stahl’s negative opinion of Sachs.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   4 July [1879]
letters.summary:
CD gives suggestions concerning FD’s experiments on the radicles of roots. Asks him to find out whether J. von Sachs tried beans. Should also try other gramineous plants.

Bernard looking forward to his father’s return.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   4 July [1879?]
letters.summary: Thanks WTT-D forDrosophyllumseeds.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [6 July 1879]
letters.summary: Describes bean experiments. Will tell Emma Darwin to tell Elizabeth Darwin that he has written to the Riffel.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   7 [July 1879]
letters.summary: Francis wants a copy of a book on "Shakespeare’s merry tales" to present to a friend in Würzburg.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   7 July 1879
letters.summary: Sends proofs of his preface [to EK’sErasmus Darwin], with which he is disappointed. Suggests additions and improvements he would like to make.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   8 July 1879
letters.summary: F. P. Cobbe called on EAD to present a letter from the Secretary of the Anti-Vivisection Society; she hoped CD might support limiting repetitions of experiments.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   8 [July 1879]
letters.summary: Inquires concerning a possibility of searching old deeds about the Darwin family history.

letters.title: To Reginald Darwin   8 July 1879
letters.summary: CD has corrected the first proofs [ofErasmus Darwin] and so returns RD’s books. CD is disappointed with his work and fears RD will be also.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   9 July 1879
letters.summary: Pressure paralyses the streaming of protoplasm in the hairs ofTradescantia.

letters.title: To E. R. Lankester   9 July 1879
letters.summary:
Asks that authoress be thanked for poem. Enjoyed poetry in old days; now cannot read a line.

Delighted that ERL will find time for original investigations.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   9 July [1879]
letters.summary: Structure of some "very curious" tendrils.

letters.title: From C. C. Blake   10 July 1879
letters.summary:
Points to CD’s favourable notice of his anthropological work;

details current financial difficulties and work efforts. Asks to borrow £5.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   10 July 1879
letters.summary: Has written to Col. J. L. Chester [genealogist] to ask whether he would like to see the deeds [for Darwin genealogy, seeEmma Darwin2: 237].

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   10 July 1879
letters.summary:
Has received printed sheets from CD. Hopes CD does not intend to delete anything. EK comments on value of his own sketch forErasmus Darwin.

Hopes CD can excuse article he wrote in response to a review of Grant Allen’s book [The colour-sense(1879)].

letters.title: From J. L. Chester   11 July 1879
letters.summary: Does not believe that deeds will throw light on the first William Darwin and his ancestors, but they will have much of interest for CD’s researches [forErasmus Darwin].

letters.title: From Reginald Darwin   11 July 1879
letters.summary:
Is gratified if he has helped [withErasmus Darwin].

Thanks for another consignment of family records.

letters.title: From Leonard Darwin   [before 12 July] 1879
letters.summary:
Suggests revisions in proofs ofErasmus Darwin.

[Letter wrongly dated Nov by LD.]

letters.title: To J. L. Chester   12 July 1879
letters.summary: Thanks for assistance. Nothing more should be done at present about the deeds. JLC’s letter sent to CD’s son [George].

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   12 July [1879]
letters.summary:
Notes observations on sensitivity and movement of radicles.

Has finished chapter [ofMovement in plants] on sleeping plants and is now looking over heliotropism notes.

Is perplexed byErasmus Darwin; Erasmus [A. Darwin] likes it, but Henrietta thinks it much too long.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   12 July 1879
letters.summary:
CD thinks nothing had better be done about the deeds at present.

Henrietta thinksErasmus Darwinalmost too dull to publish.

letters.title: To Leonard Darwin   12 July [1879]
letters.summary: Will shorten or leave out many parts [ofErasmus Darwin] but cannot agree that it is not worth while to say something about the family.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   12 July 1879
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for comments onFreie Wissenschaft und freie Lehre[1878].

Describes work on Medusae.

Describes work onChallengerRadiolaria and publication plans.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   12 July [1879]
letters.summary:
Relieved to hear that EK approves of his notice [preface forErasmus Darwin]. Is reflecting on idea that it might appear after EK’s article as "an additional or supplementary notice".

Grieved to hear that Grant Allen has been accused of plagiarism.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   13 July 1879
letters.summary: Sorry to hear Henrietta’s opinion of the [Erasmus Darwin] proofs. GHD did not think it dull. He makes some suggestions.

letters.title: To Anton Dohrn   13 July 1879
letters.summary: Thanks AD for the handsome Annual Report of the Zoological Station (1878). Rejoices at its success and its great service to science.

letters.title: From J. B. Innes   14 July 1879
letters.summary: Reports finding a wood pigeon’s nest on the ground, though woods are nearby.

letters.title: To E. H. O’Callaghan   14 July 1879
letters.summary: "… hardly any event seems to me of such great importance as the settling of Australia, New Zealand, &c &c by the so called Anglo Saxons". CD thinks this due to population pressure.

letters.title: To James Paget   14 July 1879
letters.summary:
Returns an "old book" [? Baeta,Comparative view of the theories and practice of Drs Cullen, Brown and Darwin(1800); seeErasmus Darwin, p. 107]. Glad to see that Dr Erasmus Darwin’s views on fever were attended to.

Fears his life of Dr Darwin will be a poor affair. "Never again will I be tempted out of my proper work."

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   15 July 1879
letters.summary: Thanks CD for sending volumes of Dr Erasmus Darwin’s works. Hopes to finish Krause’s MS in a fortnight.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   15 July 1879
letters.summary:
Suggests possible visit by EH.

Comments on EH’s research.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   16 July 1879
letters.summary: Rejects proposal that CD’s sketch appear as a supplement or appendix to his own. Offers alternative suggestions. Proposes title-page for German edition ofErasmus Darwin.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   17 July 1879
letters.summary:
Gives an account of his publication plans for his and Ernst Krause’sErasmus Darwin.

CD has never even dreamed of publishing his own autobiography.

Is now working, with Francis, on plant movements.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   18 July [1879]
letters.summary: Is inclined to publish his "notice" after EK’s text inErasmus Darwin. May condense and alter it, so EK should not translate yet. As soon as Dallas finishes translating EK’s text, CD will set to work. Thinks EK’s article more interesting than what he has written.

letters.title: From Felix Marchand   20 July 1879
letters.summary: CD has been elected to the Naturforschende Gesellschaft, Halle. Asks for a photograph. Encloses diploma.

letters.title: To Ann Marston   20 July [1879]
letters.summary: Will not sign a petition, for he feels vivisection is essential to the progress of physiology.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   22 July [1879]
letters.summary:
At work onMovement in plants.

Discusses John Ball’s, G. de Saporta’s, and his own theories of higher plant origin. Their rapid development remains an "abominable mystery".

Frank is working in Würzburg.

letters.title: From Carl Hensgen   23 July 1879
letters.summary: CH, a chemist interested in zoology, asks CD’s opinion of research programme described on enclosed memorandum. Programme involves investigation of ability of molluscs to build shells out of other carbon compounds in absence of calcium carbonate.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   23 July 1879
letters.summary:
Contributes to subscription for Grant Allen.

Regrets GJR and wife could not visit.

Encloses paper [not identified] by Thomas Meehan, a very inaccurate observer.

letters.title: From W. E. Gladstone   24 July 1879
letters.summary: Sends CD his collection of Homeric epithets on motion, which "indicate ideas of motion more precise and scientifically adjusted than … any other author".

letters.title: From T. M. Coan   25 July 1879
letters.summary: Sends CD his article on causes of decline of Hawaiian population.

letters.title: From James Paget   25 July 1879
letters.summary: Regrets that he cannot send the promised volume [Biographie médicale, 7 vols, 1820–5, biographical appendix toDictionaire des sciences medicales]. Offers to have his son make an abstract of the biography [of Erasmus Darwin].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   26 July 1879
letters.summary: JDH criticises John Ball’s theory of origin of higher plants in Carboniferous highlands, where low carbon dioxide levels permitted survival.

letters.title: From Samuel Wilks   26 July 1879
letters.summary: Sends an oration he delivered at the Royal College of Physicians in CD’s presence.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   [after 26] July [1879]
letters.summary: Has failed with his experiments on aerial roots.

letters.title: From Anthony Rich   27 July 1879
letters.summary: Best wishes for CD’s trip to Cumberland.

letters.title: To Samuel Wilks   27 July 1879
letters.summary:
Thanks SW for text of his oration

and an [unspecified] article on parrots.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   29 July 1879
letters.summary: Difficulties with Krause’s handwriting and the time required to correct his sources have delayed the translation [ofErasmus Darwin].

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [before 31 July 1879]
letters.summary: Discusses Müller-Thurgau’s work on heliotropism. Will start on Thursday for Heidelberg and Strassburg.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   [31 July 1879]
letters.summary: Asks GHD to send name and address of tailor from whom he got the [LL.D.] gown to W. B. Richmond.

letters.title: To Felix Marchand   [c.1 August 1879]
letters.summary: Thanks for his election to the Naturforschende Gesellschaft, Halle. Will send photograph as requested.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [2 August 1879]
letters.summary: Tells arrangements for their journey to Coniston.

letters.title: From R. T. Wright   2 August 1879
letters.summary: Lack of success in breeding horses in Bengal is related to damp climate. Encloses letter from F. G. Ravenhill concerning an unpublished report by the Stud Commission on animal breeds in Bengal.

letters.title: From Reginald Darwin   4 August 1879
letters.summary: Sends an address by Dr Erasmus Darwin [to the Derby Philosophical Society].

letters.title: To W. E. Gladstone   4 August [1879]
letters.summary: Thanks WEG for his essay showing how Homer distinguished between different kinds of movement.

letters.title: To Anton de Bary   5 August 1879
letters.summary: Thanks ADeB for sending specimens ofUtriculariato Francis [Darwin]. Urges him to publish his observations, becauseUtriculariadiffers widely fromDrosera. CD has been unable to detect any evidence of true digestion inUtricularia.

letters.title: To John Fiske   5 August [1879]
letters.summary: Thanks for JF’s book [Darwinism and other essays(1879)].

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   6 August 1879
letters.summary: Last minute checking of some quotations has delayed his translation [ofErasmus Darwin].

letters.title: From J. R. Atkin   7 August [1879]
letters.summary:
Thanks for present and letter.

Wishes a good trip to the lakes and sends love to family members.

letters.title: From Archibald Liversidge   7 August 1879
letters.summary: CD elected honorary member of the Royal Society of New South Wales.

letters.title: From Hugo de Vries   7 August 1879
letters.summary: Experiments to determine mechanism of tendril curvature; importance of variations in cell turgidity. Contraction in roots caused by increased turgor.

letters.title: From John Ball   8 August 1879
letters.summary: Hopes CD will read and comment on his lecture ["Origin of flora of the Alps",Proc. R. Geogr. Soc.(1879)]. Disgrees with CD; JB maintains that the high antiquity of existing plant genera and families explains wide differences in their distribution.

letters.title: From Anton de Bary   9 August 1879
letters.summary: His experiments on nutrition ofUtriculariaare not sufficiently exact or complete to allow them to be published. He will resume experimentation and report to CD.

letters.title: From F. B. Goodacre   11 August 1879
letters.summary: Crossbreeding experiments with geese.

letters.title: To Leonard Darwin   12 August 1879
letters.summary: Coniston is most beautiful, but CD finds "there are too many human beings for my taste".

letters.title: To Hugo de Vries   12 August 1879
letters.summary:
Thanks for letter.

Comments on growth and movement of plants.

letters.title: To F. B. Goodacre   13 August [1879]
letters.summary: Reports the results of breeding from FBG’s hybrid geese. The hybrids are fertileinter se. Would FBG like the geese back? If CD publishes his observations may he use FBG’s results?

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   13 August 1879
letters.summary: CD regrets that he feels large parts of Krause’s essay [on Erasmus Darwin] must be omitted. Gives his criticisms and his plan for condensed publication of his own article, with only parts of EK’s. If EK is unwilling to change, CD will publish his article privately. It is manifest that EK can publish his essay in its extended form in Germany if he wishes to do so.

letters.title: From John Denny   16 August 1879
letters.summary: JD communicates, after seven years, news of a new "sport" ofPelargonium, sterile both with other varieties and with the mother plant, thus indicating that it is possibly a new species.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause  16 August 1879
letters.summary:
Regards his part only as material from which CD can select for English edition ofErasmus Darwin.

Regrets dropping comment on Erasmus Darwin’s evolutionary theory.

Asks for translation of British plant names.

Asks CD not to mention in introduction that EK’s part has been reduced.

letters.title: To John Fiske   17 August [1879]
letters.summary: Thanks JF again for hisEssays, which he has now read.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   18 August 1879
letters.summary: WSD sent MS of his translation ofErasmus Darwinon 6 August. Hopes CD received all of it.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   19 August [1879]
letters.summary: CD is relieved by EK’s response to his criticisms. Will attend to all his instructions and will not print his preface until EK has seen it.

letters.title: To A. A. W. Hubrecht   25 August 1879
letters.summary: Thanks for essay. Doubts AAWH’s theory concerning modifications in first- and last-born offspring.

letters.title: To Victor Marshall   25 August 1879
letters.summary: CD expresses the pleasure the Darwins had in the courtesies extended them by the Marshalls at Coniston.

letters.title: From E. S. Morse   26 August 1879
letters.summary: Sends proofs [of "The shell mounds of Omori, Japan",Tokyo Univ. Mem.1 (1879)], which may interest CD for the changes between ancient and modern forms.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   28 August 1879
letters.summary: He has no cause to complain at CD’s suppression of parts of his translation. Will do his best to correct and improve the proofs.

letters.title: From W. M. Hacon   28 August 1879
letters.summary: Requests a letter of introduction to Prof. Jowett for his son, who is entering Balliol College.

letters.title: To Gustaf Retzius   28 August 1879
letters.summary: CD is honoured to receive the magnificent workFinska Kranier(1878).

letters.title: To F. B. Goodacre   29 August 1879
letters.summary: What should CD do with the geese? One gander chases and frightens his grandchild. Does FBG intend to publish his results?

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   30 August 1879
letters.summary:
Accepts invitation to visit Down.

Describes travel plans in Scotland.

letters.title: From F. B. Goodacre   1 September 1879
letters.summary: Would like CD to write a paper on the results of geese experiments; hopes CD will not object to his doing the same despite the variance of their conclusions [see F. B. Goodacre, "Question of identity of Chinese and domestic goose",Proc. Zool. Soc. Lond.(1879): 710–12 and CD’s "Fertility of hybrids from the Chinese and common goose",Collected papers2: 219–20].

letters.title: From Otto Hahn   1 September 1879
letters.summary:
Sends copy ofDie Urzelle[1879].

Clerical party in Germany rejoicing because science cannot explain all facts at once.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   1 September 1879
letters.summary:
Acquaintances say principal contents of Seward book should be recounted in German edition ofErasmus Darwin.

Will CD check MS for errors?

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   1 September [1879]
letters.summary: Wants a plant that shows interesting sleep movements identified.

letters.title: To F. B. Goodacre   2 September 1879
letters.summary: Will do nothing with the geese until he hears from FBG. Is glad FBG intends to publish his results.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   2 September 1879
letters.summary: Invites EH to spend night at Down.

letters.title: To C.-F. Reinwald   2 September [1879]
letters.summary: Until C-FR sees the whole ofErasmus Darwin, he cannot decide if it is worth translating into French.

letters.title: From Hugo de Vries   2 September 1879
letters.summary: Force of turgor is true cause of movement in plants. HdeV hopes to identify the substance which increases the cell’s water-absorbing power.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel    3 September 1879
letters.summary: Arranges to visit Down.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   3 September [1879]
letters.summary: Urges EK to do as he thinks best about German edition ofErasmus Darwin. CD sends original of EK’s essay and translation of parts he has not used.

letters.title: From John Murray   3 September [1879]
letters.summary: Likes CD’s memoir of his grandfather and offers to publish 1000 copies at his own risk, giving half the profits to CD.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   [4 September 1879]
letters.summary: Confirms details of EH’s visit to Down.

letters.title: To John Murray   4 September 1879
letters.summary: Though not sanguine about sale [ofErasmus Darwin] it seems fair that if over 1500 copies are sold he should receive two-thirds profit. If JM does not agree, he would prefer publishing on commission or asking Macmillan if they will give him larger profits.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   6 September 1879
letters.summary: Murray’s offer to publishErasmus Darwin. RC states terms and preliminary arrangements.

letters.title: To Hugo de Vries   6 September 1879
letters.summary:
Perhaps movement from side to side in plants is caused by the contraction of one side, rather than the expansion of the other.

Sends seeds ofLychnis Githago: he observed the hypocotyledenous stem, not the root, contracting.

letters.title: From Victor Marshall   7 September 1879
letters.summary:
VAEGM pleased CD enjoyed his stay at Coniston.

Reports some rude remarks about CD made by John Ruskin.

letters.title: From F. B. Goodacre   8 September 1879
letters.summary: Can dispose of CD’s geese if he wishes.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   9 September 1879
letters.summary:
Pleased that JM will allow two-thirds profits [onErasmus Darwin] for he wants Krause to receive some profit.

He and his son [Francis] are preparing a large botanical work [Movement in plants], dry as dust, which he must publish on commission. He will be lucky to lose only £100.

letters.title: To F. B. Goodacre   10 September [1879]
letters.summary: Has sent some geese.

letters.title: From Hugo de Vries   10 September 1879
letters.summary: Movement of tentacles ofDrosera.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   11 September 1879
letters.summary: On cost of the portrait of Dr Darwin, forErasmus Darwin.

letters.title: To C.-F. Reinwald   11 September 1879
letters.summary: Has sent remaining sheets for proposed French translation ofErasmus Darwin. Edmond Barbier should consider the pages from Seward’sLifethat have been cut from the English edition.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause  12 September 1879
letters.summary:
Thanks for printed sheets and MS. Intends that German version should follow the English, but will add notes to clarify unfamiliar material for German readers.

Thanks for list of plant names.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   13 September 1879
letters.summary: Acknowledges proofs ofErasmus Darwin.

letters.title: To Victor Marshall   14 September 1879
letters.summary:
CD responds to VM’s desire to plant a tree in his honour by offering three choices.

Again expresses his pleasure in Coniston.

Acknowledges that Ruskin was right about his feeling "a deep and tender interest about the brightly coloured hinder half of certain monkeys".

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   14 September [1879]
letters.summary:
Thanks GJR for gift of game.

Contributes to [Naples] Zoological Station.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   15 and 16 September 1879
letters.summary: Sends his corrected proofs [ofErasmus Darwin] for CD’s approval, with questions and final arrangements.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   15 September 1879
letters.summary: Agrees to EK’s proposals [for publishingErasmus Darwin]. Will send sheets to Paris, but is not sure there will be a French translation.

letters.title: To Karl Alberts   16 September 1879
letters.summary: Explains his arrangements with Messrs Reinwald in France and Appleton in America, if they were to publish his work on Erasmus Darwin.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   18 September 1879
letters.summary:
Illness of his wife.

Potato crossing experiments; believes he has increased yield considerably.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   19 September 1879
letters.summary: Final decisions about the printing ofErasmus Darwin.

letters.title: From Melchior Neumayr   19 September 1879
letters.summary:
Sends new publication [see11838].

Plans major study of evolutionary palaeontology.

Comments on form series discovered by Joachim Barrande.

Has not heard from Leopold Würtenberger.

letters.title: From Henry Johnson   22 September [1879]
letters.summary:
Requests autograph for a friend.

Has retired to Ludlow because of angina pectoris.

He and his daughter, Mary, were present in the cave near Tenby when George Rolleston found so many antediluvial bones.

letters.title: To Henry Johnson   24 September 1879
letters.summary:
Sends the requested signature,

with sympathy for HHJ’s state of health [see12236].

Reports that HJ’s experiments on tension of parts are often quoted in German works and periodicals.

letters.title: To George Sleigh   [before 26 September 1879]
letters.summary: Asks correspondent to consider taking a position as his gardener.

letters.title: To Thomas de Grey   26 September 1879
letters.summary: Asks for a character reference for a former servant of correspondent.

letters.title: From Henry Johnson   26 September [1879]
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his autograph.

letters.title: From E. Desrousseaux   30 September 1879
letters.summary:
ED is at work on a book to be called "Les grands phénomènes de la nature", which will furnish additional proof of CD’s doctrine.

Expounds his theory that all phenomena originate in movement.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   1 October [1879]
letters.summary: Searching for the right gardener.

letters.title: To Harvard University Library?   2 October [1879]
letters.summary: Sends postal order for Samuel Scudder’sCatalogue[of scientific serials(1879)].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   2 October 1879
letters.summary: JDH looking for a gardener for CD’s unusual needs.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   2 October 1879
letters.summary: Has returned corrected sheets [ofErasmus Darwin] to Dallas. [CD’s note forwards this letter to a third person, presumably W. S. Dallas.]

letters.title: To Gustaf Retzius   2 October 1879
letters.summary: CD invites MGR and his wife to lunch. Travel directions. Regrets that he will be unable to converse for more than an hour and a half. [See12246.]

letters.title: To C. G. Semper   2 October 1879
letters.summary: Discusses CGS’s account of Pellew Islands. Still believes atolls and barrier reefs in Pacific indicate subsidence. But cases like Pellew Islands, if frequent, would make his conclusions of little value.

letters.title: From Gustaf Retzius   3 October 1879
letters.summary:
Declines invitation to Down, having heard from Haeckel of CD’s poor health.

Working on vertebrate organ of hearing from fishes to man.

Unsuccessful at getting exotic batrachians and reptiles in London.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   4 October [1879]
letters.summary: Final arrangements for publishingErasmus Darwin. If he were publishing on commission he would have printed only 1000 copies.

letters.title: From W. P. Garrison   4 October 1879
letters.summary:
Sends CD his version for children ofJournal of researches[What Mr Darwin saw].

During the last illness of his father, William Lloyd Garrison, WPG showed him CD’s passages on slavery.

"In combating the enemies of freedom in this country he [W. L. Garrison] emancipated himself from the theology the destruction of which is perhaps your highest title to the honor of your own time and the blessings of posterity."

letters.title: To W. P. Garrison   [after 4 October 1879]
letters.summary: Gratified to know that WPG’s father, William Lloyd Garrison, approved of CD’s words on slavery inJournal of researches.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   5 October 1879
letters.summary: E. Krause has sent his corrected proofs with suggestions and questions.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   5 October [1879]
letters.summary: Will get in touch with young gardener about terms of employment. It is good of Hooker to remember about heliotropism of insectivorous plants.

letters.title: To Arnold Dodel-Port   6 October 1879
letters.summary: Thanks AD-P for part three of hisAtlas[see11039].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   7 October 1879
letters.summary: JDH requests specimens from Miss [Sophy] Wedgwood.

letters.title: To Karl Alberts   8 October 1879
letters.summary: John Murray could supply clichés of two woodcuts at a trifling cost.

letters.title: To Daniel Mackintosh   9 October 1879
letters.summary: Comments on DM’s ["Drift deposits of west of England",Q. J. Geol. Soc. Lond.35 (1879): 425–55].

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   12 October 1879
letters.summary: Gives up his wish to keep secret the engagement of his daughter to Horace Darwin.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   13 October 1879
letters.summary: Rejoices at THF’s consenting to the marriage of his daughter Ida and Horace Darwin, although the match is a poor one for Ida "in a worldly point of view". [See12253.]

letters.title: From W. M. Hacon   13 October 1879
letters.summary: How to bargain on Horace Darwin’s marriage-settlement: Francis received £5000; Horace could receive more as an inducement for the Farrers to increase Ida’s dowry.

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   13 October 1879
letters.summary: The "Beagles" are, after all, to provide for Jemmy Button’s grandson [see11501].

letters.title: From Daniel Mackintosh   14 October 1879
letters.summary: DM is highly gratified by CD’s opinion of his labours on boulders [see12252]. He owes his start on this subject to CD. Since 1843 he has supported CD’s views on transportation of boulders by ice.

letters.title: To B. J. Sulivan   15 October 1879
letters.summary: Sends £2 for the "Buttonian subscription" [see9229].

letters.title: From Emily Beke   16 October 1879
letters.summary: Thanks for CD’s reply to her letter and his kindness. She is getting over her difficulties.

letters.title: To W. P. Garrison   16 October 1879
letters.summary:
Sends his thanks for the beautifully illustrated book for children [What Mr Darwin saw]

and for the memorials of William Lloyd Garrison. [See12248.]

letters.title: To Daniel Mackintosh   16 October 1879
letters.summary:
DM may show CD’s letter [to the Royal Society].

Pleased that his old paper should have stimulated DM to such excellent work.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   17 October [1879]
letters.summary: Wants some seeds to see how certain seedlings break through ground.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   18 October 1879
letters.summary: Suggests £20 as a fair payment for his work onErasmus Darwin.

letters.title: From George Sim   18 October 1879
letters.summary:
Describes cow with three toes

and a woman with two functional nipples on left breast.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   20 October 1879
letters.summary:
Sends corrections. Printing of German edition has not yet begun.

Charles Reinwald wishes to print only CD’s sketch. French hostility to Germans the reason.

Gustav Jäger and Robert Caspary no longer on title-page ofKosmos.

letters.title: To Casimir de Candolle   21 October 1879
letters.summary: Thanks CdeC for his work [Anatomie comparée des feuilles(1879)]. The plates are wonderfully good.

letters.title: To E. S. Morse   21 October 1879
letters.summary:
Thanks for ESM’s paper [see12201].

Remarks on progress of Japan.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   22 October 1879
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Condolences on the death of JL’s wife.

letters.title: To George Sim   22 October 1879
letters.summary: Polydactylism is very common, and so are supernumerary mammae in men and women.

letters.title: To Horace Darwin   23 October [1879]
letters.summary: Thanks for all Horace has done for him and for his ship-shape account. Hopes Horace has charged him enough. There will be less to divide amongst them, which seems to please Frank.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   23 October 1879
letters.summary: Forwards newspaper reports by growers of Torbitt’s potatoes. Torbitt is in much distress and CD fears all his work will be thrown away unless he is aided.

letters.title: From Eduard Schulte   23 October 1879
letters.summary: Sends drawing and description of butterfly discovered in Celebes. It is noteworthy for its colour, which plays a role in mating.

letters.title: To ?   23 October 1879
letters.summary: Is obliged for the note about Wallis Nash’s death, but he has since heard that the report was false.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   24 October 1879
letters.summary:
Requests seeds ofIpomoeaandMegarrhizafor observations on seedling growth.

Is rereading MS ofMovement in plants.

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   25 October 1879
letters.summary: Asks CD what title to put on spine ofErasmus Darwin. Suggests 7s 6d as the price.

letters.title: From G. M. Asher   26 October 1879
letters.summary: Asks CD to examine his idea that human and animal sociology are related, as each is based on the principle of mutual concession (derived from Schopenhauer’s law of compassion). If CD approves, he should write a note and forward it and GMA’s letter toMacmillan’s Magazine.

letters.title: To G. M. Asher   28 October 1879
letters.summary: Cannot answer questions on origin of instinct, sociology, etc. Suggests references inOriginandDescent.

letters.title: To Eduard Schulte   28 October 1879
letters.summary: Discusses case of colour display in butterfly.

letters.title: To C.-F. Reinwald   29 October 1879
letters.summary: Discusses arrangements for a French translation ofErasmus Darwin(1879).

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   29 October 1879
letters.summary: Wants cryptogam identified; has been observing its movements.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   30 October 1879
letters.summary: Has Torbitt any further results? THF has forgotten what he had proposed to do.

letters.title: From A. S. Packard   30 October 1879
letters.summary: This autumn several observers have notedPlusiamoths caught in the flowers ofPhysianthus albens. Also bees attack and devour the trapped moths.

letters.title: From Eduard Schulte   30 October 1879
letters.summary: Asks for reference to article on butterfly [see CD’s "Sexual colours of certain butterflies",Collected papers2: 220–2].

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   31 October 1879
letters.summary: Discusses financial and other arrangements for marriage of Horace Darwin and Ida Farrer. Mentions anticipated inheritance of children.

letters.title: From W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   31 October 1879
letters.summary: Terminology for asexual gemmae ofLunularia vulgarisand comparison withMarchantia.

letters.title: To Julius von Haast   1 November 1879
letters.summary:
Thanks JvH for admirably illustratedGeology of New Zealand. Will be particularly glad to read about the old glaciers.

Admires extent of cultivation of science in New Zealand.

letters.title: To James Torbitt   1 November 1879
letters.summary: Has seen newspaper accounts of JT’s potato experiments. T. H. Farrer wants to know whether JT has published any account of them, and how much assistance he needs.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   2 November 1879
letters.summary:
Concerning the settlement for Horace Darwin and Ida.

Will give CD’s potato papers to Lord Sandon.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   3 November 1879
letters.summary: Has written to Torbitt.

letters.title: From W. B. Cooper   4 November 1879
