letters.summary: Response toDescent. Suggests some human races may have been produced by natural rather than sexual selection.

letters.title: From W. M. Hacon   4 November 1879
letters.summary: WMH will negotiate with William Farrer on Horace’s marriage-settlement. Will attempt to make the settlement £5000, the same as Francis received.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   4 November [1879]
letters.summary: Wants seedling ofQuercus rubraorQ. coccinea.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   4 November 1879
letters.summary: CD complains of unfair treatment by EK’s publisher [ofErasmus Darwin, Karl Alberts], who has written that he now does not want the copies of the photographs CD has ordered for him. Is sure that EK will agree that the costs should be deducted from any profits from the sales.

letters.title: To Victor Marshall   4 November [1879]
letters.summary: Promises to send an oak.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   4 November 1879
letters.summary: Success of his experiments; report on recent work.

letters.title: From Victor Marshall   [after 4 November 1879]
letters.summary: Hopes CD will be able to plant a tree in VAEGM’s garden as a memorial of his visit.

letters.title: From Victor Marshall   [after 4 November 1879]
letters.summary: Sends some doggerel verse about a literary dandy who is critical of Darwin and Spencer and approves of Ruskin.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   6 November 1879
letters.summary: Will try to getIpomoeaandMegarrhizaseeds for CD.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   6 November 1879
letters.summary: Shocked by Karl Alberts’ behaviour in dealing with Murray. Will write to ask him what it means. Thanks for arranging matters with Reinwald.

letters.title: From W. M. Hacon   7 November 1879
letters.summary: Reports bargaining with William Farrer on Horace’s marriage-settlement.

letters.title: From Anthony Rich   7 November 1879
letters.summary:
Thanks for CD’s amusing letter from Coniston.

Commiserates on CD’s proof-reading chore.

George Darwin has visited him.

letters.title: To James Torbitt   7 November 1879
letters.summary: Wrote to T. H. Farrer about JT’s potato experiments. Would be calamity if JT were prevented from trying successful fungus-proof variety for a few more years.

letters.title: From Wilhelm Behrens   8 November [1879]
letters.summary:
Sends copy of his article ["Die Nectarien der Blüthen",Flora62 (1879): 2–11, 17–27, 49–54, 81–90, 113–23, 145–53, 233–40, 241–7, 305–14, 369–75, 433–8, 449–57].

GWJB’s experiments inspired by reading CD’s botanical works.

letters.title: To W. M. Hacon   8 November [1879]
letters.summary: Discusses the marriage-settlement for Horace and Ida.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [9 November 1879]
letters.summary: Sends CD petition from Olmstead and asks him to forward it around to get good signatures.

letters.title: From W. P. Garrison   9 November 1879
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for his good opinion of his book,What Mr Darwin saw,

and his expressions [concerning W. L. Garrison] "which will be treasured by his children".

letters.title: To Wilhelm Behrens   10 November 1879
letters.summary: Thanks GWJB for work on nectaries ["Anatomisch-physiologische Untersuchungen der Blüthen-Nectarien",Flora(1878): 454–60].

letters.title: From W. M. Hacon   10 November 1879
letters.summary: Negotiations on Horace’s marriage-settlement.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   10 November 1879
letters.summary: Only a few copies of the photographs [for German edition ofErasmus Darwin] had been printed, so loss will not be great. CD was rather angry when he wrote [12291] "but it is all over now".

letters.title: From R. A. Vance   10 November 1879
letters.summary: Sends his article ["Diseases of the rectum",Cincinnati Lancet & Obs.21 (1878): 224–41] through his friend, Dr Letcher.

letters.title: To August Weismann   10 November 1879
letters.summary:
Thanks for AW’s work ["Zur Naturgeschichte der Daphniden",Z. Wiss. Zool.27: 51–112; 28: 93–254; 30 (suppl.): 123–65; 33: 55–270]. CD always interested in adaptations which appear to owe their structure to other causes.

Has not heard from Raphael Meldola for a long time about translation of AW’sStudien.

letters.title: From J. S. Burdon Sanderson   [11 November 1879]
letters.summary: Thanks CD for a copy ofErasmus Darwin.

letters.title: To G. S. Ffinden   11 November 1879
letters.summary: Encloses a cheque to the Down Coal and Clothing Club.

letters.title: From A. E. Darwin   12 November [1879]
letters.summary: On behalf of her sister Violetta, who is ill, thanks CD for copy ofErasmus Darwin.

letters.title: From Reginald Darwin   12 November 1879
letters.summary: Thanks for copy ofErasmus Darwin. The refutation of Miss Seward is admirable and conclusive.

letters.title: From Douglas Fox   12 November 1879
letters.summary: Thanks for book [Erasmus Darwin].

letters.title: From E. S. Galton   12 November 1879
letters.summary: Thanks CD on behalf of herself and sister [E. A. Wheler] for the gift ofErasmus Darwin. Comments to amplify parts of it.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   12 November 1879
letters.summary:
Praises CD’s biography of Erasmus Darwin;

asks CD to answer some queries he is circulating. Is particularly interested in "visualizing faculty" in CD and Dr Darwin.

letters.title: From Henry Maudsley   12 November 1879
letters.summary: Thanks for copy ofErasmus Darwin. Has wished that justice be done to Dr Darwin’s originality and his anticipation of some modern scientific theories.

letters.title: From Jan van Bolhuis   [13 November 1879]
letters.summary: Does CD believe in the "Word of the Lord", i.e., Genesis?

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   14 November 1879
letters.summary: Thanks CD for a copy ofErasmus Darwin.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   14 November [1879]
letters.summary:
Returns completed questionnaire concerning visualising faculty [seeLL3: 177–9]. Thinks age important. Recalls faces of school friends but cannot remember those of people recently met.

Comments on his part [ofErasmus Darwin].

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   14 November 1879
letters.summary: Thanks for English edition [ofErasmus Darwin]. John Murray has not answered letters of German publisher. Questions CD about persons mentioned in book, in order to annotate German edition.

letters.title: To Newman Marks   14 November [1879]
letters.summary: Returns the memorial, signed, expressing concern about proposed renovations at St Mark’s in Venice.

letters.title: From Anthony Rich   14 November 1879
letters.summary: Thanks forErasmus Darwin.

letters.title: From Newman Marks   15 November 1879.
letters.summary: Thanks CD for signing a memorial.

letters.title: From G. W. Norman   15 November 1879
letters.summary: Thanks forErasmus Darwin.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   15 November 1879
letters.summary: Encloses latest report on his new potatoes. Believes the plants should be grown from seed every fourth year to preserve yield and disease-resistance.

letters.title: From Reginald Darwin   17 November 1879
letters.summary:
Sends a book on shorthand

and a paper, probably by Erasmus Darwin, entitled "Moral and physical hermeneutics", on the subject of temperance.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   17 November 1879
letters.summary: Received enclosed report from Torbitt on potato experiments.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   17 November 1879
letters.summary: Answers EK’s questions. Sorry to reportErasmus Darwinsold only 600 copies at advance sale.

letters.title: To C. H. Tindal   17 November 1879
letters.summary: Thanks for the offer of lending a manuscript relating to his grandfather. It will be of use if a second edition of the Life of Dr. Darwin should appear. Will take the greatest care of them and return them as soon as he has read them.

letters.title: To James Torbitt   17 November 1879
letters.summary: Describes problems of raising money [for potato experiments]. "A Government official in another office remarked to me that it was very difficult for Ministers to decide what to do in such cases as they must be prepared for mere cavillers in the H[ouse] of Commons."

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   18 November [1879]
letters.summary:
Thinks W. P. Garrison’s book [extracts fromJournal of researchesfor juvenile readers] would serve as an advertisement for theJournal.

Disappointed at sale ofErasmus Darwin.

letters.title: From James Paget   18 November 1879
letters.summary: Thanks forErasmus Darwin. It is a rare life and an unmatched illustration of the transmission of intellectual strength.

letters.title: From Eduard Schulte   18 November 1879
letters.summary:
Supports CD’s theory but doubts that butterfly life-cycle is consistent with it. Metamorphosis of butterflies is not comparable to that of other insects.

Comments on butterfly fertilisation of flowers.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   [after 19 November 1879]
letters.summary: Encloses a report on JT’s potato varieties by William Meredith, one of the many individuals in the country who are growing them.

letters.title: To E. S. Galton   20 November 1879
letters.summary:
Thanks ESG for list of errata in his part [ofErasmus Darwin].

Extends sympathy on death of Edward Wheler, E. S. G’s brother-in-law.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   20 November 1879
letters.summary:
Wants a plant identified;

would like some cotton seeds.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   20 November 1879
letters.summary:
Intends to get his ideas on the "wearing out" of varieties printed.

This year’s crosses were failures.

letters.title: To A. S. Packard   23 November 1879
letters.summary: Has never heard of bees that are carnivorous; hopes someone will investigate ASP’s observations.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   24 November 1879
letters.summary: German edition ofErasmus Darwinwill not appear until next year.

letters.title: From John Ball   28 November 1879
letters.summary: Thanks CD for noticing some difficulties in his hypothesis. Concedes that there is no proof that higher plants are more intolerant of carbon dioxide than lower plants. Argues that the main difference between the lowlands and the high mountains in Palaeozoic times would be the much greater climatic fluctuations that would occur on the mountains. Discusses carbon dioxide diffusion in the Palaeozoic atmosphere. Thinks that the large number of species and genera peculiar to high mountains favours the assumption that "their diffusion must date from a geologically remote period" [seeML2: 20–2].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   29 November 1879
letters.summary:
Congratulations onErasmus Darwin; likes CD’s part better than Ernst Krause’s.

Received false notice of Asa Gray’s death.

Gray and JDH engaged in comparing widely separated but floristically similar regions.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [30 November 1879]
letters.summary: Erasmus thinks CD should give a copy ofErasmus Darwinto Henry Parker.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   1 December [1879]
letters.summary:
Movement of cotton plant cotyledons.

Thanks JDH for his praise ofErasmus Darwin.

Delighted that JDH is thinking about geographical distribution, wishes he would go over the New Zealand flora again.

letters.title: From A. A. W. Hubrecht   2 December 1879
letters.summary: Expresses his gratitude for CD’s criticism and advice relating to his unripe hypothesis [see12200]. His new results regarding the anatomy of different genera of Nemerteans, especially the discovery of a central nervous system.

letters.title: From E. R. Shaw   2 December 1879
letters.summary: Describes bearded horses seen on island of Sark.

letters.title: From Robert Christison   4 December 1879
letters.summary: Acknowledges receipt ofErasmus Darwin.

letters.title: To E. R. Shaw   4 December 1879
letters.summary: Thanks ERS for information about variation in horses.

letters.title: From E. L. Sturtevant   4 December 1879
letters.summary: Observations on maize.

letters.title: From T. L. Brunton   5 December 1879
letters.summary: Thanks for copy ofErasmus Darwin.

letters.title: To F. B. Goodacre   5 December 1879
letters.summary: Were the hybrid geese FBG sent to CD brother and sister from the same hatch? CD intends to send a letter on their breeding toNature[Collected papers2: 219–20].

letters.title: From A. H. Payne   5 December 1879
letters.summary: Asks CD to express his opinion on vivisection to help the anti-vivisection cause in Germany.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [8 December 1879]
letters.summary: Returns Guthrie. Comments at length on Guthrie’s critique of Spencer.

letters.title: From F. B. Goodacre   8 December 1879
letters.summary: The hybrid geese FBG sent to CD were brother and sister from the same hatch. Would greatly value a copy ofNaturecontaining CD’s letter.

letters.title: From J. W. Judd   9 December 1879
letters.summary: Sorry he was out when CD came to visit.

letters.title: From Emma Nixon   10 December 1879
letters.summary:
Thanks forErasmus Darwin.

Violetta Darwin is near death.

letters.title: From J. F. Moulton   10 December 1879
letters.summary: At CD’s request he has read Malcolm Guthrie’s book [On Mr Spencer’s formula of evolution(1879)], which is a critique ofFirst principles. He finds it a helpful clarification of Spencer’s views; however, it is as pseudo-scientific as the book it criticises.

letters.title: To A. H. Payne   10 December 1879
letters.summary: Gives his opinion on vivisection. CD detests cruelty but believes that physiology "is one of the most important sciences" and that it cannot progress without experiments on living animals.

letters.title: To H. E. Litchfield   11 [December 1879]
letters.summary: Sends M. Guthrie’s book [On Mr Spencer’s formula of evolution(1879)], although HEL may not care to read it having seen Moulton’s letter [12350].

letters.title: From Raphael Meldola   11 December 1879
letters.summary: Sends subscription form for English edition of Weismann’sStudien.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   11 December [1879]
letters.summary: Wants some apheliotropic plants for experiments.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   12 December [1879]
letters.summary: Would like to subscribe to English edition of Weismann.

letters.title: From A. G. Butler   13 December 1879
letters.summary: Supplies facts on the colours of each sex in butterflies from the generaOrnithopteraandHeterochroa.

letters.title: From J. F. Moulton   13 December 1879
letters.summary: Herbert Spencer, though not the scientific thinker he sees himself to be, was extremely important in conditioning the generation’s acceptance of evolution. Compares Spencer and Robert Chambers as teachers, rather than discoverers, of new ideas.

letters.title: ToNature   15 December [1879]
letters.summary: CD has repeated a test of whether hybrids of the common and Chinese goose are fertileinter se. Reports his success, and comments on its significance for the theory of descent.

letters.title: From A. B. Buckley   16 December 1879
letters.summary: On Wallace’s need for a regular income. He has been rejected as Superintendent of Epping Forest. Thinks men such as Lubbock, Hooker, and CD might help.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   16 December 1879
letters.summary:
Thanks for AG’s trouble about the seeds. Is curious to see their germination and the early seedling growth.

Asks for cotton seeds, as he observes odd movements of the cotyledon.

letters.title: ToNature   16 December 1879
letters.summary:
Reports information sent by E. Schulte [12254] on the colours of the maleDiadema bolina.

Discusses extent to which consciousness came into play in the origin of certain instincts, including sexual display.

letters.title: To A. B. Buckley   17 December 1879
letters.summary: Discusses possibility of Government pension for Wallace.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   17 December 1879
letters.summary: Miss Arabella Buckley’s letter on Wallace’s poor health and finances leads CD to seek JDH’s aid in getting a Government pension.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   18 December 1879
letters.summary: Argues against pension for Wallace because of his spiritualism; the underhanded way he brought about discussion of spiritualism at BAAS; his pocketing money from a bet on the sphericity of the earth; his lack of absolute poverty.

letters.title: From A. B. Buckley   19 December 1879
letters.summary: Thanks CD for acting on her suggestion about getting Wallace an income; acknowledges the difficulty. Is not sure Wallace would accept government money for doing nothing in return.

letters.title: To A. B. Buckley   19 December 1879
letters.summary: Has discussed with Hooker possibility of Government pension for Wallace. Hooker is pessimistic.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   19 December [1879]
letters.summary: JDH convinces CD not to press for pension for Wallace.

letters.title: From A. B. Buckley   20 December 1879
letters.summary: Thanks CD for trouble over Wallace, even though success not assured.

letters.title: From R. W. Dixon   20 December 1879
letters.summary: RWD has read "with deep interest"Erasmus Darwin. He has copies of four letters from Erasmus Darwin to his great-grandfather, Richard Dixon, and he encloses a copy of the most interesting one.

letters.title: From Adam Fitch   20 December 1879
letters.summary: Questions CD on the possibility of selecting disease-resisting potatoes to produce ultimately a disease-resistant variety.

letters.title: From R. W. Dixon   [after 20 December 1879]
letters.summary: Three letters from Erasmus Darwin to Dixon’s great-grandfather, transcribed by Dixon. Enclosure to a missing letter.

letters.title: From Lewis Wright   22 December 1879
letters.summary:
Is sending CD hisIllustrated book of poultryin which the chapter on the "Origin of the domestic fowl" may be of interest.

He ventures to mention several errors inVariation.

Mentions the late Mr Lane of Bristol, a celebrated Spanish breeder (of poultry).

letters.title: From R. A. Job   23 December 1879
letters.summary: RAJ is the son of cousins and wishes to marry his cousin. Is anxious for information on consanguineous marriages and on the advisability of his proposed marriage.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   25 December 1879
letters.summary: Reports thatPhylloxera-resistant vines have been found in an infected region of Portugal.

letters.title: To Karl von Scherzer   26 December 1879
letters.summary: What a foolish idea seems to prevail in Germany on the connection between Socialism and Evolution through Natural Selection.

letters.title: From C. E. Ferguson   27 December 1879
letters.summary: Asks for a list of books on evolution relating to man.

letters.title: To James Torbitt   27 December 1879
letters.summary:
Glad to hear about vines.

Hopes JT will be able to continue work without Government aid. "It is enough to sicken one to see how politicians waste their time squabbling and neglect doing any good."

letters.title: From Michele Lessona   28 December 1879
letters.summary: The Academy of Sciences of Turin has awarded CD a 12000 franc prize for his work during the past four years.

letters.title: From Anthony Rich   28 December 1879
letters.summary: New Year greetings.

letters.title: From Antonio Mendola   29 December 1879
letters.summary: Reports from an Italian baron that a calf’s horn that was buried in a field set roots; mule’s hairs incubated in water come alive.

letters.title: From Ercole Ricotti   29 December 1879
letters.summary: CD awarded a prize of 12,000 lire in recognition of his recent research on plant physiology.

letters.title: To C. H. Tindal   29 December 1879
letters.summary: Thanks for MS as it shows many of Erasmus Darwin’s ideas were formed 20 years before he publishedZoonomia.Would like to publish last letter if there is a second edition of his little book. MS will be returned registered post.

letters.title: From Emil Witte   29 December 1879
letters.summary: Relates case of selective immunity to rinderpest.

letters.title: To A. S. Wilson   30 December [1879]
letters.summary: Package of wheat varieties from Russia lost in transit.

letters.title: From W. M. Hacon   31 December 1879
letters.summary: WMH’s agent is coming to Down for CD to sign transfer of £5000 North Eastern Railway stocks. Horace is coming to his office to execute the marriage-settlement.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [1880–1?]
letters.summary: Wants some more rubber bands for his wrist.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   [1880–1]
letters.summary: Asks him to visit.

letters.title: From ‘Maria’   [1880–2]
letters.summary: On the Christian God; questioning of CD’s religious beliefs.

letters.title: To ‘Maria’   [1880–2]
letters.summary: Regrets he has not time to develop points touched on in her letter and that he does not understand what information she wants.

letters.title: From ‘Maria’ [1880–2]
letters.summary: Writes at length on importance of God and Catholicism, and the need to seek salvation.

letters.title: To Horace Darwin   1 January 1880
letters.summary: Arrangements regarding HD’s allowances.

letters.title: From C. H. Tindal   1 January 1880
letters.summary: Encloses extracts from the correspondence of [the Ven. Robert] Clive concerning Erasmus Darwin.

letters.title: From Samuel Butler   2 January 1880
letters.summary: Asks CD for reference to the edition ofKosmosthat contains the original of Ernst Krause’s article on Dr Erasmus Darwin. There are serious differences between the translation by W. S. Dallas and the Feb [1879] article by Krause on which CD, in the preface toErasmus Darwin, says it was based. SB notes in particular that the concluding sentence of the translation, which is clearly aimed at [SB’s]Evolution, old and new, is not in the original. Since readers will assume the text ofErasmus Darwinwas written before his book appeared, SB asks for an explanation.

letters.title: From Joseph Prestwich   2 January 1880
letters.summary: Having reviewed the history of the Glen Roy debate ["On the origin of the parallel roads of Lochaber, and their bearing on other phenomena of the glacial period",Philos. Trans. R. Soc. Lond.170 (1880): 663–776], JP wishes to know whether it is accurate to say CD has abandoned the marine theory.

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   2 January [1880]
letters.summary: Repeats extracts of a letter received from Bishop Stirling’s daughter containing anecdotes and observations of the Fuegian natives.

letters.title: To Samuel Butler   3 January 1880
letters.summary: Krause altered the MS [of his essay on Erasmus Darwin] considerably before sending it to be translated. This is a common practice, but CD now regrets he did not state in his preface that the article had been modified. The translation had been arranged before SB’s book [Evolution, old and new] was announced.

letters.title: From J. H. C. Fabre   3 January 1880
letters.summary: Sends a copy of hisSouvenirs entomologiques[1879].

letters.title: To Joseph Prestwich   3 January 1880
letters.summary: JP is right; CD gave up [Glen Roy theory] when he read T. F. Jamieson ["On the parallel roads of Glen Roy",Q. J. Geol. Soc. Lond.19 (1863): 235–58].

letters.title: To B. J. Sulivan   3 January 1880
letters.summary:
Returns BJS’s Christmas good wishes.

The progress of Tierra del Fuego is almost as wonderful as that of Japan.

Is sorry to hear about Mellersh.

letters.title: From Wallis Nash   4 January 1880
letters.summary: Reports on the comfortable life of an immigrant in Oregon.

letters.title: To Ercole Ricotti   4 January 1880
letters.summary: Thanks for awarding him the Bressa prize. Has sent an order to receive the 12,000 lira.

letters.title: To Adolf Ernst   5 January 1880
letters.summary: Has read AE’s paper inNature[21 (1880): 217] onMelochia, a new family of heterostyled plants, and suggests some crosses to be carried out to determine the fertility of illegitimate seedlings.

letters.title: To [Italian Bank]   5 January 1880
letters.summary: Requests that they receive, on his behalf, an award of 12000 lira [lire!?] from the Royal Academy of Sciences of Turin, and transmit it to the Union Bank, London.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   5 January 1880
letters.summary: The reviews ofErasmus Darwinare mainly favourable.

letters.title: To C. H. Tindal   5 January 1880
letters.summary: Thanks for the information about Dr Erasmus Darwin and his parents.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   5 January 1880
letters.summary:
Admiration of ARW’s ["The origin of species and genera",Nineteenth Century(Jan 1880)]. Good use of Allen’s "admirable researches".

Disappointment about the Epping Forest appointment.

Farrer’s article inFortnightly Review.

letters.title: From A. S. Wilson   5 January 1880
letters.summary:
Results of his second year of experiments with Russian wheat varieties will be published inGardeners’ Chronicle[n.s. 13 (1880): 108, 172–3].

Observations on germination of wheat.

letters.title: To William Cole   6 January 1880
letters.summary: Regrets he is unwilling to join [Epping Forest Field Club], but encloses a guinea to aid with their preliminary expenses.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   6 January [1880]
letters.summary: Delighted by honour CD has received from Turin. Agrees with Horace that the money ought to be given to the Zoological Station at Naples.

letters.title: To J. H. C. Fabre   6 January 1880
letters.summary: Thanks JHF for copy of hisSouvenirs entomologiques[1879].

letters.title: To John Thomas Murray  6 January 1880
letters.summary: Thanks JM for sendingDroseraspecimens.

letters.title: From F. B. Goodacre   7 January 1880
letters.summary: FBG greatly interested in CD’s article ["Fertility of hybrids from the Chinese and common goose"] but has not altered his opinion on the matter.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   7 January 1880
letters.summary: Pleased by favourable English newspaper reviews ofErasmus Darwin. Charles Reinwald has not yet said whether he wants to use annotations intended for German readers.

letters.title: To Antonio Mendola   8 January [1880]
letters.summary: Thanks for the offer of specimens, but cannot use them due to other work.

letters.title: To A. S. Wilson   8 January 1880
letters.summary:
Glad ASW has solved puzzle of outer seeds.

Quite agrees about great improbability of sudden transformations.

Asks for copy of report fromGardeners’ Chronicle[see12404].

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   9 January 1880
letters.summary:
Gratified by CD’s praise.

Describes plan of his new book [Island life(1880)].

Efforts to secure a post.

letters.title: To CD’s Children   10 January 1880
letters.deprecated: Elizabeth (Bessy) (Lizzy) DarwinFrancis DarwinGeorge Howard DarwinHorace DarwinLeonard DarwinWilliam Erasmus DarwinHenrietta Emma DarwinHenrietta Emma Litchfield
letters.recipient: Elizabeth (Bessy) (Lizzy) DarwinFrancis DarwinGeorge Howard DarwinHorace DarwinLeonard DarwinWilliam Erasmus DarwinHenrietta Emma DarwinHenrietta Emma Litchfield
letters.summary: Circular letter regarding the distribution of CD’s excess income, with a note addressed to W. E. Darwin concerning his handling of Elizabeth Darwin’s share.

letters.title: From E. A. Wheler   10 January 1880
letters.summary:
Thanks CD forErasmus Darwin. Comments on it.

News of Violetta Darwin’s death.

letters.title: To Horace Darwin   11 January [1880]
letters.summary: Sends enclosure [missing], which HD is to forward to W. E. Darwin, as everyone else has seen it.

letters.title: To C. E. Ferguson   12 January 1880
letters.summary: Suggests CEF read Ernst Haeckel’sEvolution of man[1879] andDescent.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   12 January 1880
letters.summary: Sends some cotton seeds for CD.

letters.title: To Alfred Krakauer   12 January 1880
letters.summary: "I am much obliged for your note. I have heard of the other analogous cases, but there remains a doubt whether they may not be accidental coincidences, for such cases certainly occur in non-Jewish families.––"

letters.title: From R. L. Tait   12 January 1880
letters.summary: Plans a "Darwin Festival" to celebrate CD’s birthday.

letters.title: From J. I. Rogers   13 January 1880
letters.summary: Responds to article inNatureon the sexual colours of butterflies [Collected papers2: 220–2].

letters.title: To R. L. Tait   13 January 1880
letters.summary: The honour RLT proposes [Darwin Festival] is a great one, "but would it not be better to wait until I am in my grave?"

letters.title: From W. C. Williamson   13 January 1880
letters.summary: Sends a seedlingDrosera capensis.

letters.title: To Jabez Hogg   14 January 1880
letters.summary: CD’s grandfather, Erasmus Darwin, must have published on arsenic, as his father never published on medical subjects.

letters.title: From Daniel Mackintosh   15 January 1880
letters.summary: The violent stranding of floating ice as first mentioned in CD’s article ["Ancient glaciers of Caernarvonshire",Collected papers1: 163–71] is the most remarkable of the Moel Tryfan phenomena.

letters.title: To R. L. Tait   15 January [1880]
letters.summary:
Sends copy ofKosmos[containing Krause’s article on Erasmus Darwin].

Believes he can spare an Erasmus Darwin letter.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   15 January 1880
letters.summary:
Thanks for cotton seeds.

Germination ofMegarrhiza.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   16 January 1880
letters.summary: What are functions of "yeomen of the armoury" on p. 1? Who is "old Hooker" on p. 34? Needs to explain them in annotations [toErasmus Darwin].

letters.title: From C. D.’s children   17 January 1880
letters.deprecated: Elizabeth (Bessy) (Lizzy) DarwinFrancis DarwinGeorge Howard DarwinHorace DarwinLeonard DarwinWilliam Erasmus DarwinHenrietta Emma DarwinHenrietta Emma Litchfield
letters.sender: Elizabeth (Bessy) (Lizzy) DarwinFrancis DarwinGeorge Howard DarwinHorace DarwinLeonard DarwinWilliam Erasmus DarwinHenrietta Emma DarwinHenrietta Emma Litchfield
letters.summary: Send CD a present of a fur coat.

letters.title: To CD’s Children   17 [January 1880]
letters.deprecated: Elizabeth (Bessy) (Lizzy) DarwinFrancis DarwinGeorge Howard DarwinHorace DarwinLeonard DarwinWilliam Erasmus DarwinHenrietta Emma DarwinHenrietta Emma Litchfield
letters.recipient: Elizabeth (Bessy) (Lizzy) DarwinFrancis DarwinGeorge Howard DarwinHorace DarwinLeonard DarwinWilliam Erasmus DarwinHenrietta Emma DarwinHenrietta Emma Litchfield
letters.summary: Thanks his children for their present of a fur coat.

letters.title: From R. L. Tait   18 January [1880]
letters.summary: The Birmingham Philosophical Society proposes to celebrate CD’s birthday and make him their first Honorary Member. RLT will draft the address.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   18 January [1880]
letters.summary: Suspects WTT-D is the author of a good review ofErasmus DarwininNature[21 (1880): 245–7].

letters.title: From Hermann Welcker   18 January 1880
letters.summary:
Sends publications.

Discusses comparative anatomy and evolutionary implications of several ligaments.

Thinks effects of Chinese foot-binding are inherited.

Criticises article on Darwinism inBrockhaus’ Lexikon.

Mentions forthcoming book on mammalian vertebrae.

letters.title: From Charles Dixon   19 January 1880
letters.summary: Sends seed attached to breast feathers of a heron that had been shot.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   19 January 1880
letters.summary:
Describes the germination and early growth ofMegarrhizaabout which AG has been misinformed. The tubular petioles act functionally like a root.

Ipomoeadid not germinate.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   19 January 1880
letters.summary: Replies to EK’s queries about German translation of CD’s preface toErasmus Darwin.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   20 January [1880]
letters.summary: Germination ofDelphiniumandMegarrhiza.

letters.title: From Samuel Butler   21 January 1880
letters.summary: SB has decided to lay the matter [the subject of12393and12396] before the public and has written to theAthenæumstating the facts. [Athenæum31 Jan 1880.]

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   21 January 1880
letters.summary: Thanks EH for copy of book [Das System der Medusen(1879)].

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   27 January 1880
letters.summary: Asa Gray wants seeds of a variety of cotton known as vine cotton.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [28 January 1880]
letters.summary: Thanks CD for giving money to the children. Is going to give money to Bessy, but not invest it until she is really rich. Returns Butler’s letter. Thinks Butler is looking for a grievance to write an article about.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   29 January [1880]
letters.summary:
Sorry to hear of his illness.

On his visit to J. F. McLennan, GHD might tell him that CD thinks A. R. Wallace would work up McLennan’s materials conscientiously.

letters.title: From Oskar von Giesl   29 January 1880
letters.summary: Asks CD to write his opinion of the views expressed in "Die Darwin’sche Theorie und die Landwirtschaft" in his journal,Reunion.

letters.title: To Hermann Welcker   30 January 1880
letters.summary:
Thanks for letter of 18th January 1880 and for present of Essays. Interested in Welcker’s investigation of the 'ligamentum teres', and his comment on the feet of the Chinese.

Will esteem it an honour if Welcker dedicates his next book to him.

letters.title: To J. H. C. Fabre   31 January 1880
letters.summary:
Comments on JHF’s book [Souvenirs entomologiques(1879)].

Discusses story told by Erasmus Darwin about a wasp cutting off wings of fly.

Sorry JHF is opposed to descent theory.

Suggests experiment concerning insects’ sense of direction.

letters.title: To W. H. Flower   [after 16 February 1880]
letters.summary: Thanks correspondent for a gift of books.

letters.title: To H. E. Litchfield   1 February 1880
letters.summary: Sends the Litchfields two drafts of a letter in reply to Samuel Butler’s letter to theAthenæum; hopes for their approval.

letters.title: From H. E. Litchfield   [1 February 1880]
letters.summary: Criticises CD’s draft of a letter to theAthenæumanswering S. Butler’s charges. Suggests changes.

letters.title: From R. B. Litchfield   1 February 1880
letters.summary: Advises against making any reply to Samuel Butler’s charges.

letters.title: From R. B. Litchfield   1 February 1880
letters.summary: Has shown S. Butler’sAthenæumletter to Frederick Pollock, who confirms RBL’s advice that it needs no answer. Sends an imaginary response by Butler.

letters.title: To Wallis Nash   1 February 1880
letters.summary: Can well understand WN’s new life. WN’s departure a heavy loss.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   2 February 1880
letters.summary: Asks THH to advise him about a response to Samuel Butler’s attack accusing CD of dishonesty. Quotes the advice of others but will do what THH advises.

letters.title: To R. B. Litchfield   2 February 1880
letters.summary: Thanks RBL for advice [concerning dispute with Samuel Butler]. Notes reaction of family.

letters.title: From W. Z. Seddon   2 February 1880
letters.summary: WZS, 12-year-old pupil, asks where he can find answer to question of what causes different shades of colour in inhabitants of earth.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   3 February 1880
letters.summary: Germination ofMegarrhiza. AG’s observations at variance with CD’s.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   3 February 1880
letters.summary: Has read Butler’s letter and CD’s draft reply and Litchfield’s letter. Has no hesitation in saying CD should take no notice. Litchfield’s advice is judicious.

letters.title: From R. B. Litchfield   3 February 1880
letters.summary: Thinks Huxley’s judgment on answering S. Butler’s charges would be trustworthy, though THH is horribly pugnacious and would naturally be for fighting.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   3 February 1880
letters.summary:
Says it is not likely he will be able to criticise GJR’s work.

Recommends Jean-Henri Fabre,Souvenirs entomologiques[1879].

Encloses letters from J. F. Moulton [12350and12356].

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   4 February [1880]
letters.summary: Greatly relieved by THH’s letter [advising against a reply to Samuel Butler].

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   4 February 1880
letters.summary: Samuel Butler’s fierce attack on CD and EK inAthenæum. CD’s sentence saying that EK had altered hisKosmosarticle was accidentally omitted from second proofs. Butler insinuates that EK’s attack on his book was suggested by CD or interpolated by him in EK’s text.

letters.title: To W. Z. Seddon   4 February 1880
letters.summary: Comments on colours of races of man. Wishes WZS "or anybody else" could account for them.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   5 February 1880
letters.summary:
Since CD has decided not to answer S. Butler’s charge, WSD will not reply either.

Will look over Francis Darwin’s lecture ["Climbing plants"] with a view to publishing it inPopular Science Review[19 (1880): 213–29].

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   5 February 1880
letters.summary:
On GJR’s work on mental evolution in animals. Emphasises "love" among animals.

Comments on stimulation of plants.

On pleasure and pain.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   6 February 1880
letters.summary: Thinks CD has no need to reply to Samuel Butler’s hostile article [in theAthenæum]. Offers to reply himself.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   6 February 1880
letters.summary:
Thinks Herbert Spencer has done little service to science but a great service to thinking.

Thinks importance of mathematics overestimated [by J. F. Moulton] in criticising Spencer.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   7 February 1880
letters.summary: Returns [Butler’s] attack, which he forgot to send yesterday.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   9 February 1880
letters.summary:
Sends birthday wishes.

Discusses work on Medusae.

Recalls visit to Down.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   9 February 1880
letters.summary:
CD advises EK on his proposed letter answering Butler.

Considering the favourable reviews, sale ofErasmus Darwinhas been poor.

letters.title: From Wilhelm Breitenbach   10 February 1880
letters.summary: Describes formation of student nature study club at the University of Jena. Sends birthday greetings from the club.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   10 February [1880]
letters.summary:
"Dia" [as a prefix] means "through, across".

WED’s wife would like to meet the Huxleys.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   10 February 1880
letters.summary:
Birthday greetings.

Regrets Butler’s malicious attack.

letters.title: From Anton Dohrn   11 February 1880
letters.summary:
Sends birthday greetings

and the good news of a subvention for the Zoological Station received from the German government. There are now 20 naturalists working at the Station.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   12 February 1880
letters.summary: Thanks for his very kind letter.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   12 February 1880
letters.summary: It might be possible to borrow £500 [for potato experiments]. Variety of "The Champion" spreading over the Kingdom. Champion lately less able to produce.

letters.title: To Wilhelm Breitenbach   13 February 1880
letters.summary: Thanks society of students at Jena for birthday congratulations.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause 13 February 1880
letters.summary:
Thanks EK for kind letter.

CD’s date on epitaph is a dreadful mistake. CD often overlooks errata.

letters.title: From Lawson Tait   [13 February 1880]
letters.summary: Encloses cuttings fromBirmingham Daily Post, 12 February 1880, p. 4, and 13 February 1880, p.5, reporting the presentation to CD of the first honorary membership of the Birmingham Philosophical Society.

letters.title: To Lawson Tait 13 February 1880
letters.summary: CD thanks RLT for his two notes, a newspaper article, and a copy of RLT’s address honouring him.

letters.title: To A. S. Wilson   13 February 1880
letters.summary:
Thanks for articles by ASW inGardeners’ Chronicle[see12404]. Agrees with him.

Asks about growth of rootlets from knobs caused by fungus on roots of Cruciferae.

letters.title: From William Cole   14 February 1880
letters.summary: At the inaugural meeting of the Epping Forest & Essex Naturalists’ Field Club, CD was elected an Honorary Member.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   14 February 1880
letters.summary: Torbitt too poor to go on with [potato] experiments. If anything is to be done it must be by Government.

letters.title: To Lawson Tait   14 February 1880
letters.summary: Would be glad to see RLT at Down if he thinks it fit to come there to deliver the address honouring CD.

letters.title: From George Bentham   15 February 1880
letters.summary: Has been at work on Orchideae forGenera plantarumand has found CD’sOrchidswonderfully useful. Comments on some problems of botanical terminology.

letters.title: To Anton Dohrn   15 February 1880
letters.summary:
Thanks AD and the naturalists at the Station for their birthday congratulations.

CD has been awarded the Bressa prize of the Accademia delle Scienze in Turin, and it occurs to him that if the Station wanted some apparatus costing about £100, he would like to pay for it.

letters.title: To George Bentham   16 February 1880
letters.summary: CD pleased to be of use to GB. He remembers his own work on orchids with pleasure. Thinks GB will be able to improve CD’s terminology for orchids.

letters.title: From Henry Faulds   16 February 1880
letters.summary: Asks CD’s help in obtaining data on finger-prints – both of ancient impressions in pottery and of living men of all races. Suggests a comparative study with similar markings of lemuroid monkeys might yield results of value about man’s origin. Gives the practical utility of prints in identification in criminal and legal studies and investigations. Encloses a form.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   16 February 1880
letters.summary: Agrees not to reply to Butler.

letters.title: From S. B. J. Skertchly   16 February [1880]
letters.summary: Asks CD to telegraph a testimonial for him.

letters.title: To William Cole   17 February 1880
letters.summary: Thanks for the honour conferred upon him by the Epping Forest Field Club.

letters.title: To Edinburgh University   [17? February 1880]
letters.summary: Testimonial for S. B. J. Skertchly, stating CD’s high opinion of his work.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   17 February 1880
letters.summary:
Seed germination.

Strange that his plants [ofMegarrhiza] behaved differently from AG’s [see12455].

letters.title: From A. S. Wilson   17 February 1880
letters.summary:
On clubroot fungus of cultivated Cruciferae.

Will give Russian wheat varieties another trial.

letters.title: From J.-H. Fabre   18 February 1880
letters.summary: On instinct in insects. Intends to experiment as CD proposes.

letters.title: To J.-H. Fabre   20 February 1880
letters.summary: Discusses sense of direction of cats and other animals.

letters.title: To A. S. Wilson   20 February 1880
letters.summary: Speculates on origin of habit [of insects?] of laying eggs on plants of certain families.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   21 [February 1880]
letters.summary: Nature[21 (1880): 382] has an item about tremors and earth movements in Japan.

letters.title: From Anton Dohrn   21 February 1880
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his offer. Suggests it be used to start a fund to pay travel expenses of English naturalists who want to come to the Station.

letters.title: To A. Gapitche   24 February 1880
letters.summary: No one can prove death is inevitable, but the evidence in favour of this belief is overwhelming. It is in the highest degree improbable that man should cease to follow the general law of evolution, and evolution implies successive generations, which implies death.

letters.title: To Anton Dohrn   27 February 1880
letters.summary: Leaves decision as to use of his gift to AD.

letters.title: From H. W. Crosskey   28 February 1880
letters.summary: Forwards, on behalf of the Birmingham Philosophical Society, an address offering CD the first honorary membership of the Society. Encloses formal record of this meeting.

letters.title: From Adolf Ernst   29 February 1880
letters.summary:
Plants in Venezuelan plains.

Observations onTurnera: heterostyly, leaf-base glands’ secretion eaten by ants.

Observations on role of leaf secretions in fertilisation ofMarcgraviaandPassiflora.

letters.title: To J. L. Chester   2 March 1880
letters.summary: Thanks JLC for his letter, pedigree, and MS of the history of the Darwin family.

letters.title: From J. L. Chester   3 March 1880
letters.summary: Thanks for CD’s appreciation of his work on family history. Sends one of his books [unidentified].

letters.title: From Robert Cooke   3 March 1880
letters.summary:
Three hundred copies ofErasmus Darwinremain from the 1000 printed. Demand is small.

Should 250 copies ofForms of flowersbe printed before type is distributed?

letters.title: From Anton Dohrn   3 March 1880
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his cheque for £100. Has told Secretary of BAAS Committee [for the Station], so that he may report it. [See O. J. R. Howarth,The British Association(1931), pp. 196–7.]

letters.title: From James Torbitt   3 March 1880
letters.summary: Potatoes will be lost unless JT has immediate authority to proceed.

letters.title: To H. W. Crosskey   [4 March 1880]
letters.summary: Thanks HWC and the Birmingham Philosophical Society for their address in his honour.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   4 March 1880
letters.summary:
Writes on family matters and researches.

Mentions construction of a pendulum

and completion of a paper he will send to the Royal Society.

letters.title: To James Torbitt   4 March 1880
letters.summary: Will go to London tomorrow to speak to T. H. Farrer about funds for potato breeding experiments. "I have told Farrer I would subscribe £50."

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   5 March [1880]
letters.summary:
The Colonel [J. L. Chester] is pleased [see12509].

Jos[iah Wedgwood III] is dying.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   5 March 1880
letters.summary: [Letter written as a postscript to11406.] CD has reread his letter of 7 Mar 1878 about the value of James Torbitt’s work on the potato disease and has nothing to withdraw. Emphasises Torbitt’s need for immediate financial help.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   [5 March 1880]
letters.summary: Is in town and will call on Sunday morning.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   5 March 1880
letters.summary: Wonders whether Lord Derby would advance him the money to continue his work.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   5 March 1880
letters.summary: Is prepared to continue his work, if financial help is forthcoming.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   6 March 1880
letters.summary:
Has sent off paper to the Royal Society

and begun work on a new problem which he feels contains the meaning of Bode’s Law, concerning the mean distances of the planets from the sun. There are mathematical difficulties, however, which he may be unable to surmount.

Will get to work on the pendulum next week.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   6 March 1880
letters.summary: Suggests Torbitt make a report on his progress so far.

letters.title: To James Torbitt   6 March 1880
letters.summary: Encloses check [cheque!?] for £50. James Caird will guarantee £75 and T. H. Farrer £25. Above gentlemen think JT should get report on his experiments from independent agriculturists.

letters.title: To James Torbitt   6 March [1880]
letters.summary: P.S. to letter posted that morning. James Caird cannot pledge £75. Erasmus Darwin and Hensleigh Wedgwood will subscribe. May write letter to theTimes. Asks for report on experiments.

letters.title: To Leopold Würtenberger   6 March 1880
letters.summary: Thanks for LW’s work [Studien über die Stammesgeschichte der Ammoniten(1880)].

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   7 [March 1880]
letters.summary: Describes subscription for Torbitt [to continue potato experiments]. Would dislike writing to any paper, but Hensleigh [Wedgwood] and Erasmus [Darwin] advise CD to write to theTimes.

letters.title: From Anthony Rich   7 March 1880
letters.summary:
Writes of the weather,

his reading of Huxley’sCrayfish[1880],

and domestic matters.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   8 March 1880
letters.summary: Encloses note and cheque from James Caird [for Torbitt].

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   8 March 1880
letters.summary: Agrees that CD should write to theTimes[about Torbitt’s potato experiments].

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   9 March 1880
letters.summary: Thanks THF for his contribution; now has £170 to permit Torbitt to carry on his experiments. Describes the scale of the experiments and his belief in their value.

letters.title: To T. L. Brunton   10 March 1880
letters.summary: Thanks for copy of TLB’sPharmacology[1880].

letters.title: To James Torbitt   10 March 1880
letters.summary: Sends funds for potato experiments. Asks for information on progress.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   11 March 1880
letters.summary: Sends seeds ofMegarrhizaand gives details of species.

letters.title: From D. Appleton & Co   11 March 1880
letters.summary: Encloses statement of U. S. sales of CD’s works to 1 Feb 1880 and sends a cheque for balance due to CD.

letters.title: To James Torbitt   11 March [1880]
letters.summary: Queries how much land has been used to cultivate potato varieties, and how many seedlings have been raised in any one year.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   12 March 1880
letters.summary: Encloses letter from James Caird, who has entire confidence in CD’s appropriation of the money [collected for Torbitt’s experiments].

letters.title: From James Torbitt   12 March 1880
letters.summary: Hopes to finish his report tomorrow; last year’s crosses were failures.

letters.title: To James Torbitt 12 March 1880
letters.summary: Asks about possible erratum in JT’s account of experiments.

letters.title: From Arthur Nicols 15 March 1880
letters.summary: Sends pheasant tail coverts, which he believes are unusual in pattern, resembling those of a peacock.

letters.title: To William Whitaker?   16 March 1880
letters.summary: Thanks for sending article on inheritance.

letters.title: From Williams & Norgate   16 March 1880
letters.summary: Sends details of Netter 1879 (Abraham Netter. 1879.De l’intuition dans les découvertes et inventions.Strasbourg: Treuttel & Wurtz.)

letters.title: To James Torbitt   17 March [1880]
letters.summary: Asks for additional information about JT’s potato experiments.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   [18 March 1880]
letters.summary: On the disease-resisting qualities and yield of certain potatoes.

letters.title: From G. S. Ffinden   19 March 1880
letters.summary: A letter of resignation from the Down Schools Committee. He will send a cheque for balance in hand when he is informed as to whom it is to be sent.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   20 March [1880]
letters.summary:
Asks AG to confirm whetherIpomoea leptophylla"makes a great tuber as big as a mangel-wurzel".

Petioles ofCotyledonsbehave partly like those ofMegarrhiza.

letters.title: To James Torbitt   20 March 1880
letters.summary: Thanks for letter and documents [about potato experiments]. Will send testimonial letter to James Caird to be circulated among possible financial supporters of JT’s work.

letters.title: From Alfred Tylor   20 March 1880
letters.summary: Wishes to see some small appointment found for A. R. Wallace, whose present labours are trying.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   22 March 1880
letters.summary:
German edition ofErasmus Darwindelayed because Murray has not sent phototypes and galvanographs.

Two of CD’s articles fromNatureto appear in AprilKosmos["Sexual colours in butterflies",Collected papers2: 220–2,Kosmos7 (1880): 72–4;

"Fertility of hybrids from the Chinese goose",Collected papers2: 219–20,Kosmos7 (1880): 77–8].

Moritz Wagner will begin a series criticising natural selection.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   23 March 1880
letters.summary: Regrets delay of photographs [for German edition ofErasmus Darwin].

letters.title: From E. S. Morse   23 March 1880
letters.summary: Offended by F. V. Dickins’ review [Nature21 (1880): 350] of his Omori mound paper. Asks CD to have it reviewed elsewhere and encloses a letter toNaturehe wants CD to forward. [See12571.]

letters.title: To James Caird   [24 March 1880]
letters.summary: Encloses a statement regarding the progress of Torbitt’s potato experiments, and discusses the handling of the fund CD holds for Torbitt.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   24 March [1880]
letters.summary:
Thanks forMegarrhizaseeds and information. Has been greatly interested byMegarrhizagermination.

Samuel Butler has attacked CD overErasmus Darwin.

letters.title: From James Caird   25 March 1880
letters.summary: Is impressed by the scale of Torbitt’s experiments. Discusses financial assistance. If Torbitt’s work succeeds, they will be amply repaid.

letters.title: From C. G. Gordon   27 March 1880
letters.summary: Encloses a statement [missing] and asks CD, if he uses it, to omit CGG’s name and to attribute it to "an officer, who has been long among Asiatics".

letters.title: From C. C. Graham   28 March 1880
letters.summary: Informs CD that the letter CCG received from him has been framed to be hung in the Kentucky State House.

letters.title: To James Torbitt   28 March 1880
letters.summary: "[James] Caird seems satisfied with what I have said of your method and the results hitherto attained." Can now promise to send £90 in the autumn.

letters.title: To C. W. Fox   29 March 1880
letters.summary: Grieves with CWF at the approaching death of his father, W. D. Fox. Remembers how they breakfasted together every day at Cambridge.

letters.title: To James Torbitt   30 March 1880
letters.summary: Encloses letter about JT’s potato experiments sent to T. H. Farrer.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   [1 April 1880]
letters.summary: Germination and root ofIpomoea.

letters.title: From James Torbitt, Wine Merchant   1 April 1880
letters.summary: Is keeping down his expenditure; has some landowners growing potatoes for him.

letters.title: From S. M. Herzfeld   2 April 1880
letters.summary: Impoverished German doctor asks for money.

letters.title: From Jules Rouquette    2 April 1880
letters.summary: Sends a poem he has composed in honour of CD.

letters.title: From G. H. Schneider   2 April 1880
letters.summary:
Describes studies with Ernst Haeckel

and research on psychology of lower animals.

Sends book [Der thierische Wille(1880)] and describes his views on the subject.

letters.title: To G. H. Schneider   3 April 1880
letters.summary: CD thanks the author for the copy ofDer thierische Wille.

letters.title: To Adolf Ernst   4 April 1880
letters.summary:
Thanks for interesting letter; is sure it would be worth while to test fertility of illegitimate offspring of heterostyled plants.

Would welcome any information on occurrence of bloom-covered leaves on dry plains.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   4 April 1880
letters.summary: Encloses a letter from Volney Rattan of California.

letters.title: From S. M. Herzfeld   4 April 1880
letters.summary:
Thanks for cheque.

Wants to see CD.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   5 [April 1880]
letters.summary:
Discusses a book

and the "splendid news about the elections".

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   6 April [1880]
letters.summary: Is beginning Geikie’sIce age. Describes flints found on the common. Comments on exciting election.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   7 April 1880
letters.summary: Encloses letter [see12488] and circular from Henry Faulds [regarding thumb impressions]. Anthropology Institute may care about it.

letters.title: From Valentine Ball   8 April 1880
letters.summary:
Has received CD’s acknowledgment, through Ernest De La Rue, for the copy he sent ofJungle life[in India(1880)].

Offers to collect material for CD on his return to India.

letters.title: From C. W. Fox   8 April 1880
letters.summary: W. D. Fox’s sufferings have ended; he died that morning.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   8 April 1880
letters.summary: Will see what can be done about getting thumb impressions, to see if the markings are persistent.

letters.title: From Henry Woodward   8 April 1880
letters.summary: Seeks testimonial, as he is applying for the Keepership of Geology at the British Museum.

letters.title: To E. S. Morse   9 [April] 1880
letters.summary:
[Copy erroneously dated March.]

Has forwarded ESM’s letter toNature["Omori shell mounds",Collected papers2: 222–3].

letters.title: ToNature   9 April [1880]
letters.summary: Forwards a letter from E. S. Morse on Omori shell mounds refuting F. V. Dickins’ review [Nature21 (1880): 350] of Morse’s memoir ["The shell mounds of Omori",Mem. Sci. Dep. Univ. Tokyo1 (1879) pt 1].

letters.title: To C. W. Fox   10 [April] 1880
letters.summary:
Condolences upon the death of CWF’s father, William Darwin Fox.

[Wrongly dated March by CD.]

letters.title: From Henry Woodward   10 April 1880
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his testimonial and congratulates him on "The coming of age of the ""Origin of Species""". [T. H. Huxley,Not. Proc. R. Inst. G. B.9 (1879–81): 361–8;Collected essays, vol. 2.]

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   11 [April] 1880
letters.summary: Sorry he missed THH’s lecture ["The coming of age ofThe origin of species", Royal Institution, 9 Apr 1880]. Has read press notices and heard from his children of its great success.

letters.title: To G. B. Ercolani   14 April 1880
letters.summary: Thanks GBE for his great work on the placenta [Nuove ricerche sulla placenta nei pesci cartilaginosi e ne mammiferi(1880)]. The relationship between placental structure and mammalian classification has always seemed interesting to CD.

letters.title: To F. E. Abbot   15 April 1880
letters.summary:
Thanks FEA for copy of a review of a book on evolution by "an ignorant lawyer".

Sends £5 forIndexsubscription.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   15 April 1880
letters.summary: WantsIpomoeaseeds for observing germination.

letters.title: From William Tearle   [before 16] April 1880
letters.summary: Attempts to reconcile accounts of man’s creation inOriginand in Genesis, to both of which he is devoted.

letters.title: To W. Tearle   16 April 1880
letters.summary: Comments on concept of revelation.

letters.title: From C. C. Graham   17 April 1880
letters.summary: CD’s framed letter may be hung in a fireproof gallery in the State House, now being finished.

letters.title: To William Newton?   17 April 1880
letters.summary:
Unable to comment on F. Lloyd’s criticism of Francis Galton’sHereditary genius[?A scientific view of Mr Galton’s theories of heredity(1876)].

Sorry about Lloyd’s health.

Does not care much about abuse or fame, an advantage of age.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   19 April 1880
letters.summary:
Thanks for the letter from Volney Rattan [see12553].

Discusses protective adaptation of seedlings from frost.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   19 April 1880
letters.summary:
Sends German edition ofErasmus Darwin.

[CD’s notes form part of a draft for12586.]

letters.title: To Horace Darwin   20 April [1880]
letters.summary: Gives advice regarding a house.

letters.title: From John Fiske   20 April 1880
letters.summary: Is coming to England to lecture and would like to meet CD again.

letters.title: To Edward Frankland   20 April 1880
letters.summary: May CD’s son send some bottles of water, in whichPelargoniumleaves have been immersed, for more precise analysis of the potassium or other soluble ash? Can EF recommend a professional analyst to take on further experiments?

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   21 April 1880
letters.summary: Glad to receive the German edition ofErasmus Darwin. Hopes sales will be good. Favourable review has appeared in the United States, in theNation.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes| 22 April 1880
letters.summary:
Preparing his book,Animal intelligence[1882].

Spent an afternoon with a spiritualist but did not learn anything.

letters.title: To R. F. Cooke   23 April [1880]
letters.summary: His family shake heads in dismal manner at his proposed title for his MS: "The Circumnutating Movements of Plants". Makes several other suggestions [none of which was adopted].

letters.title: From Henry Pitman   24 April 1880
letters.summary: Would like more information about Erasmus Darwin’s shorthand writing for his series on "Shorthand writers of renown".

letters.title: From R. F. Cooke   27 April 1880
letters.summary: His publishers are as puzzled as CD about what the title of his new book [Movement in plants] should be. Sends a tentative one in proof [missing].

letters.title: From Hermann Müller   27 April 1880
letters.summary: Fritz Müller’s daughter has committed suicide.

letters.title: To ?   27 April 1880
letters.summary: Thanks correspondent for writing, "but such malconformations, as you mention, are not very rare & therefore do not possess much novelty".

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   28 April 1880
letters.summary: MS ofMovement in plantsin final stage. Fears it will displease many German physiologists. It is an attempt to bring all the diversified movements of plants under one general law or system.

letters.title: From Thomas Meehan   28 April 1880
letters.summary: There has been talk in American papers of CD’s admitting he was wrong about hybrid sterility. TM has presented CD’s views in theNew York Independent.

letters.title: To H. D. Garrison   29 April 1880
letters.summary: Thanks for the interesting case of inheritance.

letters.title: From H. N. Moseley   30 April 1880
letters.summary: F. V. Dickins feels hurt at CD’s censure of him over the Omori shell mound controversy [seeCollected papers2: 222–3]. Dickins is well educated in science and long familiar with Japan, having been editor of theJapan Mail. In Japan, E. S. Morse is considered a charlatan, and American scientists, e.g., A. Agassiz, have a low opinion of him.

letters.title: To H. N. Moseley   2 May 1880
letters.summary: Invites HNM to Down on 9 May.

letters.title: To Williams & Norgate   3 May [1880]
letters.summary: Requests a copy of Ray Lankester’s lecture or essay on degeneration (Lankester, E. Ray. 1880.Degeneration: A chapter in Darwinism. London: Macmillan.).

letters.title: To F. J. Hughes   5 May 1880
letters.summary:
Still remembers FJH. Thinks no scientific journal would publish her essay on Genesis and science.

Regrets death of her brother [W. D. Fox].

letters.title: To E. R. Lankester   6 May [1880]
letters.summary: Hopes that Lankester will come stay next Sunday. Clark, Galton and Moseley will also be there.

letters.title: From James Dixon   7 May 1880
letters.summary: Corrects CD’s statement [Descent1: 19] that the platysma myoides muscle cannot be brought into voluntary action. He can move every one of his facial muscles.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   [7 May]1880
letters.summary: Expresses his delight with and admiration for THH’s "Coming of age [ofThe origin of species]" inNature[22 (1880): 1–4].

letters.title: To James Dixon   8 May 1880
letters.summary: Thanks for information.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [9 May 1880]
letters.summary: Forwards John Lubbock’s letter and hopes WED might influence the men "for the sake of science".

letters.title: From John Lubbock   9 May 1880
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.sender: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Writes regarding an [unspecified] election at a university. JL wonders whether William Darwin would speak to two Southampton men about it.

letters.title: To James Torbitt   9 May 1880
letters.summary: Cannot offer any assistance in urging Government to aid JT’s experiments. Thinks best chance through [William Edward?] Forster. William Carruthers reported to Royal Agricultural Society that JT’s attempt was hopeless.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   10 May 1880
letters.summary:
Hopes CD does not think his faith in natural selection is weak because he omitted mention of it in his lecture.

Is working on dogs. They will make a case for "Darwinismus".

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   11 May 1880
letters.summary: Comments on natural selection. Sometimes he can persuade himself that it is of quite subordinate importance, but so many structures have been explained by it that he can also persuade himself that every structure developed through it. Cites H. G. Bronn’s list [of structures not explicable by natural selection].

letters.title: From James Torbitt   13 May 1880
letters.summary: Has planted six, as opposed to eleven acres last year, to keep within expenditure. Must pollen be used immediately? Fourteen landowners are growing potatoes for JT.

letters.title: To John Fiske   14 May [1880]
letters.summary: Invites JF to Down.

letters.title: From F. E. Abbot   15 May 1880
letters.summary:
Thanks for money for further subscription toIndex; FEA soon to step down as editor.

On CD’s solid reputation in America among rising men of science.

letters.title: To B. J. Sulivan   16 May [1880]
letters.summary:
Lends BJS Titus Coan’sAdventures in Patagonia[1880].

Thanks him for copies of the missionary journal.

letters.title: To Giovanni Canestrini   17 May 1880
letters.summary: Thanks GC for having sent his book [La teoria di Darwin criticamente esposta(1880)].

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   20 May [1880?]
letters.summary:
Thanks for two pamphlets;

Otto Zöckler’s [Darwin’s Grossvater(1880)] he thinks worthless.

letters.title: From S. T. Preston   20 May 1880
letters.summary:
Thanks for CD’s comments on his paper ["On a point relating to brain dynamics",Nature22 (1880): 29–30].

Contends that self-interest as a motive for conduct is more salutary than is generally thought, and should be considered in the evolution of morality.

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   20 May 1880
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for the loan of a book;

discusses his family’s health and other domestic affairs.

letters.title: To J. Harris   21 May 1880
letters.summary: Cannot precisely explain conditions of existence of any organism.

letters.title: From William Spottiswoode   21 May 1880
letters.summary: S. M. Hersfeld [Herzfeld] has applied to WS for financial assistance in order to retrieve some books and apparatus from a carrier. He has previously been aided by CD, so WS seeks his advice.

letters.title: To S. T. Preston   22 May 1880
letters.summary: Discusses ethics of risking one’s life to save another.

letters.title: From William Spottiswoode   24 May 1880
letters.summary: Since CD supplied Herzfeld with money to retrieve his goods from the carrier, but he did not use it for that purpose, WS sees no way of helping him except to send him home as "a distressed Austrian subject".

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [25–7 May 1880]
letters.summary: Hopes CD got telegram about Convolvulus. Is measuring plants every four hours. Will go to Brittany by boat from Southampton on Monday night.

letters.title: To Alphonse de Candolle   28 May 1880
letters.summary:
Thanks for AdeC’sPhytographie[1880]. CD finds in it a number of "philosophical" remarks new to him. The work would have been invaluable to him in dealing with puzzles when writing his cirripede monographs.

Describes his system of keeping notes on separate pieces of paper filed in several scores of large portfolios.

Has just sent MS ofMovement in plantsto the printer. Thinks he has suceeded in showing "that all the more important great classes of movements are due to the modification of a kind of movement common to all plants from their earliest youth".

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   28 May 1880
letters.summary: Writes of a Mrs Noel, who is annoyed with CD’s neglect of Erasmus Darwin’s brother, W[illiam] A[lvey] D[arwin I], [inErasmus Darwin].

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   30 May [1880]
letters.summary:
Discusses GHD’s genealogical researches

and his health.

letters.title: To Williams & Norgate   [June 1880]
letters.summary: Requests a list of books.

letters.title: To a bookseller?   June [1880]
letters.summary: Ordering a copy of a book for his research on vegetable mould [presumably Werner Hofmeister 1845 (Die bis jetzt bekannten Arten aus der Familie der Regenwürmer: als Grundlage zu einer Monographie dieser Familie.].

letters.title: From Henry Comstock   4 June 1880
letters.summary: Summarises points of interest in hisReport upon cotton insects[U. S. Dept. of Agriculture, Bureau of Entomology (1879)].

letters.title: From Anthony Rich   4 June 1880
letters.summary: CD’s portrait at exhibition is praised by critics. CD and the Prime Minister may boast of having been in their day "the best abused men in England".

letters.title: From James Torbitt   7 June 1880
letters.summary: Sets out specific propositions concerning his potato varieties, which he will make to the Government, if he is given CD’s and T. H. Farrer’s support.

letters.title: From R. F. Charles   9 June 1880
letters.summary: Requests permission to quoteJournal of researchespassages in a school text-book [Relfe Brothers model reading-books … in prose and verse(1880–3)]. John Murray has previously refused.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   9 [June 1880]
letters.summary:
Sends Asa Gray’s lectures onNatural science and religion[1880].

Greatly enjoyed their stay at Bassett.

letters.title: To Robert Hunt   9 June 1880
letters.summary: Thanks for gift of [Panthea,]the spirit of nature[1849].

letters.title: To Henry Johnson   9 June 1880
letters.summary:
Thanks for enclosures.

Remembers Edward Vivian.

Glad to hear of flint tools.

letters.title: To John Murray   9 June 1880
letters.summary: Asks JM to provideQuarterly Journal of Sciencewith five woodcuts fromClimbing plantsto illustrate an article, based on that work, by Francis Darwin [see12462].

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   11 June [1880]
letters.summary: Some essays have arrived for GHD.

letters.title: To John Murray   11 June 1880
letters.summary: Asks John Murray to allow R. F. Charles to quoteJournal of researchespassages in a school text-book [Relfe Brothers model reading-books … in prose and verse(1880–3)].

letters.title: To Edward Vivian   11 June 1880
letters.summary: "The enclosed, evidently intended for you, has by a mistake been addressed to me."

letters.title: From R. F. Charles   12 June [1880]
letters.summary: Thanks CD for writing to Murray concerningJournal of researchesextracts for his reading-book.

letters.title: From Robert Cooke| 12 June 1880
letters.summary:
Matters related toClimbing plants

and reprint [1880] ofForms of flowers.

letters.title: To John Murray   13 June [1880]
letters.summary: Letter of introduction for R. B. Litchfield.

letters.title: From Thomas Meehan   14 June 1880
letters.summary: Suggests plants whose stamens show movement.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   14 June 1880
letters.summary: JT attempting to get Government backing for his experiments; wishes to quote from CD’s letter in support of his work.

letters.title: From C.-F. Reinwald   16 June 1880
letters.summary: Annual report on sale of Reinwald editions of CD’s works.

letters.title: To James Torbitt   16 June 1880
letters.summary: Offers advice concerning letter to [William Edward?] Forster requesting Government aid [for potato experiments].

letters.title: To A. C. Ramsay   17 June 1880
letters.summary: Notes on worm action, and CD’s questions concerning source of nutriment for worms in ACR’s courtyard [seeEarthworms, pp. 192–3].

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   18 June 1880
letters.summary: Wants WED to collect some worm-castings from Beaulieu Abbey.

letters.title: To W. C. McIntosh   18 June 1880
letters.summary: Asks for information about worms.

letters.title: To E. B. Tylor   [19 June 1880]
letters.summary: Discusses animals’ ability to learn to recognise danger, especially poisonous herbs.

letters.title: From E. B. Tylor   21 June 1880
letters.summary: Learning by experience of others: birds being killed by telegraph wires when first set up; sheep in Australia eating poisonous plants.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   24 June [1880]
letters.summary: Asks whether CD will forward enclosed to Lord Derby, and offers to send him a copy of the New York state survey. Will go to Beaulieu in the early autumn. Tells story about gallenes raised by hens being attacked.

letters.title: To Edward Henry Stanley   25 June 1880
letters.deprecated: Edward Henry Stanley, 15th earl of Derby
letters.recipient: Edward Henry Stanley, 15th earl of Derby
letters.summary: Sending EHS (Lord Derby) information about the Niagara affair.

letters.title: From Spallanzani Monument Committee   30 June 1880
letters.summary: Printed circular from the committee to set up a monument to Lazzaro Spallanzani in Scandiano.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [July 1880?]
letters.summary: Are there old furrowed fields on hillsides in N. Wales, if so can FD look for earthworm activity?

letters.title: To Theodor von Heldreich   1 July 1880
letters.summary: Thanks for essay.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   3 July 1880
letters.summary: Confirmation of CD’s idea: AG planted seedsIpomœa pandurata. One seed has come up and its germination is same as ofI. leptophylla.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   5 July 1880
letters.summary:
Thanks for mentioning CarlVogt, to whom he will write.

Comments on Dr Erasmus Darwin’s interest in mental imagery.

letters.title: To W. E. Gladstone   7 July 1880
letters.sender: Charles Robert DarwinHenry Thompson, 1st baronetGeorge JesselJames Risdon BennettThomas Henry HuxleyWilliam MorrisAlfred Russel WallaceWilliam Benjamin CarpenterAlfred John CarpenterDr Abbott
letters.summary: Supporting the abolition of clerical headships and fellowships at Oxford and Cambridge.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   8 July 1880
letters.summary:
The article [Francis Darwin, "Climbing plants"] has appeared inPopular Science Review[n.s. 4 (1880): 213–29].

Asks CD to allow John [Richard de Capel] Wise to dedicate a poem to him.

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   8 July [1880]
letters.summary: Details about tithes.

letters.title: To E. H. Stanley   8 July 1880
letters.deprecated: Edward Henry Stanley, 15th earl of Derby
letters.recipient: Edward Henry Stanley, 15th earl of Derby
letters.summary: Thanks EHS (Lord Stanley) for his trouble in providing information about the Niagara affair.

letters.title: To H. W. Jackson   9 [July 1880]
letters.deprecated: H. W JacksonLewisham and Blackheath Sci. Assoc.
letters.recipient: H. W JacksonLewisham and Blackheath Sci. Assoc.
letters.summary: CD would be happy to receive the members of the Lewisham and Blackheath Scientific Association at Down.

letters.title: To John Murray   10 July 1880
letters.summary: Asks advice on size of printing forMovement in plants. Expects it to sell a few copies for some years. Asks price of paper and of printing of 250 copies. Sends instructions for the index.

letters.title: From Robert Cooke   15 July 1880
letters.summary: Movement in plantswill be 600 pages. Does CD wish to publish at own expense or on the usual terms with Murray? Estimates expense of printing and possible profit.

letters.title: From James Geikie   15 July 1880
letters.summary: Wishes to publish CD’s explanation of positions of stones in certain gravelly drifts in a forthcoming book [Prehistoric Europe(1881)].

letters.title: To H. W. Jackson   15 July 1880
letters.summary: Thanks HWJ for his kind note. If the weather had been better CD could have made the visit [of the Lewisham & Blackheath Scientific Association] more agreeable.

letters.title: From Koninklijke Natuurkundige Vereeniging in Nederlandsch-Indië   15 July 1880
letters.deprecated: president of K. Natuurk. Ver. Ned.-Indie?
letters.sender: president of K. Natuurk. Ver. Ned.-Indie?
letters.summary: Announces CD’s election as a Corresponding Member.

letters.title: From R. L. Tait   15 July [1880]
letters.summary: The Birmingham Philosophical Society wishes to establish a Darwin prize medal for original scientific work. A fund is being raised to support research. Asks CD to contribute.

letters.title: To Unidentified   [after 15 July 1880]
letters.deprecated: president of K. Natuurk. Ver. Ned.-Indie?
letters.recipient: president of K. Natuurk. Ver. Ned.-Indie?
letters.summary: Thanks for the honour of election.

letters.title: To Robert Cooke   16 July 1880
letters.summary: CD had intended to pay costs of publishingMovement in plantsbecause he did not think it fair that Murray should risk publishing a purely scientific work. He would certainly prefer publishing on the usual terms if JM decided to do so. The book contains much new and curious matter, but there are very few persons in England interested in physiological botany.

letters.title: To R. L. Tait   16 July 1880
letters.summary: Is honoured by RLT’s announcement, and offers a contribution to the Birmingham scientific fund.

letters.title: From Edward W. Badger   17 July 1880
letters.deprecated: Edward William Badgerhonorary secretary of Midland Union Nat. Hist. Socs
letters.sender: Edward William Badgerhonorary secretary of Midland Union Nat. Hist. Socs
letters.summary: Gives history of the Union; explains plan to encourage original work by offering an annual "Darwin Prize". Asks CD’s permission to use his name.

letters.title: To E. W. Badger   [after 17 July 1880]
letters.summary: CD is honoured to have a medal named after him by an organisation [Midland Union of Natural History Societies] dedicated to the advancement of science. [See12660.]

letters.title: To Hermann Müller   18 July 1880
letters.summary: Enjoyed HM’s castigation of Gaston Bonnier ["Gaston Bonniers angebliche Widerlegung der modernen Blumentheorie",Kosmos7 (1880): 219–36].

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [19 July 1880]
letters.summary: Writes about gravel deposits [at Southampton] and sends a James Geikie letter [12655?] on the subject.

letters.title: To James Geikie   19 July 1880
letters.summary: Gives permission to use letter [10676].

letters.title: To R. L. Tait   19 July 1880
letters.summary: Sends £25 for the Birmingham Philosophical Society scientific fund.

letters.title: To the secretary of the Midland Union of Natural History Societies   [before 20 July 1880]
letters.summary: Asks the Honorary Secretary to convey to the committee his acceptance of the honour of naming a medal after him.

letters.title: From Robert Cooke   20 July 1880
letters.summary: RC estimates that 1000 copies ofMovement in plantsif sold at 14s would produce a profit of £6. Might more be printed, or the price raised?

letters.title: To Robert Cooke   21 July 1880
letters.summary: CD will take the risk and the loss ofMovement in plantson his own shoulders. He will have 1000 copies printed and, on RC’s advice, will charge 15s.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin to C. R. and Emma Darwin   22 July 1880
letters.summary: Returns Geikie’s letter; is glad he has accepted settlement of gravel through melting of snow. Is trudging around with hammer and bag with help of Ramsay’s book. Describes visits to Kenilworth and Stratford. Sara consulted a physician. Called on Reginald D. and enjoyed meeting relations and seeing picture of Erasmus. Reginald very taken with George.

letters.title: From James Geikie   22 July 1880
letters.summary: Thanks for permission to use CD’s letter.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   27 July 1880
letters.summary: Asks CD’s advice on how to answer a letter requesting his endorsement of Wrigley, his former teacher at Clapham School.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   27 July 1880
letters.summary:
No significant reviews ofErasmus Darwinhave appeared yet in Germany.

Sends response from a theological opponent.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas   28 July 1880
