letters.summary: John Wise is much pleased by CD’s permitting the dedication of Wise’s poem to him; it will be anouvrage de luxe, with drawings by Walter Crane [The first of May, a fairy masque; presented in a series of 52 designs by Walter Crane(1881)].

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   28 July [1880]
letters.summary: Thanks FD for criticisms [ofMovement in plants]. J. D. Hooker was interested in the observations of movement inDesmodium.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   28 July [1880]
letters.summary:
Advises GHD on what to write if he is asked for a reference for Alfred Wrigley.

Thanks GHD for information about trypsin.

letters.title: From O. C. Marsh   28 July 1880
letters.summary: Sends a copy of his memoir on theOdontornithes[1880].

letters.title: From Asa Gray   29 July [1880]
letters.summary: Information aboutIpomœa jalapa.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   29 July 1880
letters.summary:
Thanks EK for two articles aboutErasmus Darwin.

Does not think it right that he should receiveKosmosfree. Asks for a bill for subscription.

Has not heard from J. Murray if there is any profit onErasmus Darwin, but "vehementer dubito".

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   30 July 1880
letters.summary: Profit onErasmus Darwinis £9 15s 5d. Sends cheque. 218 copies remain unsold.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [1 August 1880]
letters.summary: Thanks for letter and journals. Sends information on earthworms and also information from Mr Ruck. Describes his fishing and his success finding sea shore plants that are new to him.

letters.title: To ?   3 August 1880
letters.summary: CD sends thanks for further instructions for making a solution, which will be followed as soon as Francis [Darwin] returns.

letters.title: To Registrar Friendly Societies   4 August 1880
letters.summary: Sends a statement of the assets of the Down Friendly Society. Asks for advice on consulting an actuary.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   5 August [1880]
letters.summary: Discusses corrections [toMovement in plants]. Has dispatched chapter nine.

letters.title: From S. T. Preston   5 August 1880
letters.summary:
Sends his paper on "Natural science and morality", notwithstanding CD’s disinclination for the subject. This work parallels H. Spencer’s in theData of ethics[1879].

Clerk Maxwell and William Thomson have encouraged his work in physics; STP looks for CD’s support on evolution.

letters.title: To R. P. Hardy   6 August [1880]
letters.summary: Asks RPH [an actuary] to act on behalf of the Down Friendly Society whose members wish the rates of benefits to be raised.

letters.title: To R. P. Hardy,   [after 6 August 1880]
letters.summary: Forwards some tables on behalf of the Down Friendly Society and discusses the changes in benefits requested by the members.

letters.title: From Adolf Ernst   7 August 1880
letters.summary:
Cobaeafertilisation.

Describes moth-pollination of gentian growing on Venezuelan mountains.

letters.title: From S. T. Preston   8 August 1880
letters.summary: Appreciates what CD says about his writing on two diverse subjects. Argues for value of "interdisciplinary approach". Has CD seen the pamphlet, "Physics and ethics" which he co-authored with an anonymous friend?

letters.title: To E. A. Strasburger   8 August 1880
letters.summary: Thanks for his book on the formation and division of cells.

letters.title: From W. C. Williamson   10 August 1880
letters.summary: On growth and development ofDrosera.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   11 August [1880]
letters.summary: Dispatches a chapter [ofMovement in plants] for FD to look over.

letters.title: To R. P. Hardy   11 August [1880]
letters.summary: Discusses matters relating to the Down Friendly Society.

letters.title: From Hermann Mùller   14 August 1880
letters.summary:
HM’s son will visit CD when he comes to London.

Is glad CD approves of his judgment of G. Bonnier’s paper on nectaries [Gaston Bonnier, "Les nectaires",Ann. Sci. Nat. (Bot.)8 (1879): 5–212].

letters.title: To J. W. Judd   [15 August 1880]
letters.summary: Invites him to lunch.

letters.title: To Arabella Buckley   16 August [1880]
letters.summary: Believes A. S. Packard is in error on some points. Refers to his own observations on slave-making ants inOrigin.

letters.title: From W. E. A. Axon   17 August 1880
letters.summary: Inquires whether a printed letter of CD’s [see11902] correctly represents his views on vegetarianism.

letters.title: To H. H. Higgins   18 August [1880]
letters.summary:
Thanks HHH for essay.

Describes disposition of cirripede specimens.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   18 August 1880
letters.summary:
Responds to CD’s offer to pay for subscription toKosmos.

Comments on his own honorarium for English edition ofErasmus Darwin. Success of German edition.

letters.title: To W. C. Williamson   18 August [1880]
letters.summary: WCW’s specimens are interesting, but CD thinks the slowness of the change might have been expected.

letters.title: From J. B. Innes   19 August 1880
letters.summary: Sends specimens of what he takes to be barnacles found on rocks in the mountains.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   20 August 1880
letters.summary: Asks CD to invite William James to stay before he returns to America.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   23 [August 1880]
letters.summary:
Asks GHD to decipher a letter [in German] he has received with a book:The Bible in science.

Enjoyed his stay in Cambridge extremely.

letters.title: To T. M. Hughes   23 August 1880
letters.summary: Honoured by offer of medal from Chester Natural History Society, but if he is expected to attend in person to receive it he regrets he must decline. Asks TMH to decide for him.

letters.title: To J. B. Innes   23 August [1880]
letters.summary:
JBI’s "barnacles" would have been extraordinary, but they are hard lichens.

Has revisited Cambridge.

letters.title: From J. B. Innes   24 August 1880
letters.summary:
"Barnacles" [from rocks in Scottish mountains, identified as lichens],

burglar alarms,

and family news.

letters.title: From J. W. Judd   24 August 1880
letters.summary: Plans to visit Down.

letters.title: To J. W. Judd   25 August [1880]
letters.summary: Explains how to reach Down.

letters.title: To T. M. Hughes   26 August 1880
letters.summary: CD is sorry for the trouble TMH has had. Fully approves of the rule [that the medal be awarded to a local worker?]. The knowledge that the Chester Natural History Society wished to honour him is the real gratification, which he will never forget.

letters.title: From H. W. Monk   27 August 1880
letters.summary: Believes he knows some "great truth" and wishes to meet with CD to discuss it.

letters.title: From J. W. Judd   28 August 1880
letters.summary:
Overjoyed at having met CD.

Sends a paper by William Whitaker [? "On subaerial denudation",Q. J. Geol. Soc. Lond.23 (1867): 265–6].

letters.title: To O. C. Marsh   31 August 1880
letters.summary: Has received OCM’sOdontornithesmemoir. Believes his work affords the best support to evolution that has appeared in the last 20 years.

letters.title: From Robert Cooke   2 September 1880
letters.summary: Has CD made arrangements with D. Appleton forMovement in plants? CD’s instructions about the index have been forwarded.

letters.title: To F. M. Balfour   4 September 1880
letters.summary:
Praises FMB’s BAAS address [on embryology,Rep. BAAS50 (1880): 636–44]. Recent progress of embryology splendid.

In work on plants, astonished at sensitivity of radicle and its power to transmit stimuli to adjoining part; such general sensitivity should be considered in genesis of nervous system.

Feels "malicious" pleasure at FMB’s criticism of Herbert Spencer.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   4 September 1880
letters.summary: Observations on earthworms.

letters.title: To R. P. Hardy   7 September 1880
letters.summary: Thanks RPH for the trouble he has taken on behalf of the Down Friendly Society.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   9–12 September 1880
letters.summary: Reports evidence of earthworm activity.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   10 September [1880]
letters.summary: Writes about worm-castings; tells WED not to bother with samples from Beaulieu Abbey.

letters.title: To Adolf Ernst   11 September 1880
letters.summary:
Thanks for seeds ofCobaea;

was much interested in AE’s article ["On the fertilisation ofCobaea penduliflora",Nature22 (1880): 148–9] opposing G. E. M. Bonnier’s view ["Les nectaires",Ann. Sci. Nat. (Bot.)6th ser. 8 (1879): 6–212].

Case ofLisianthusis an excellent one of structure and movement of parts adapted to cross-fertilisation.

Asks whether worm-castings are found in the area.

letters.title: From F. M. Balfour   13 September 1880
letters.summary:
Thanks for letter, which made up for difficulty of his speech [at BAAS meeting, Swansea].

Has met Horace Darwin and wife;

climbed Matterhorn.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   14 September 1880
letters.summary: Sends sheets ofMovement in plantsfor translation, if JVC sees fit. It has some value and novelty, CD believes, but is very dull.

letters.title: From B. D. Wrangham   [before 16 September 1880]
letters.summary: An extract from a life of Kepler about the motions of Mars.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   16 September 1880
letters.summary: Sends four wrist bands, and advice on putting them on. George is well. Can easily get worm castings. Lilly and Mlle Wild arrived in a storm to stay the night. Is much amused by Sedgwick’s ferocious letter aboutVestiges.

letters.title: To Wilhelm? Vietor   16 September 1880
letters.summary: Improvement in orthography would be national benefit, but cannot contribute to WV’s paper.

letters.title: To B. D. Wrangham   16 September 1880
letters.summary: Thanks for sending him a copy of the striking passage from Kepler.

letters.title: From D. Appleton   17 September 1880
letters.summary: Would be glad to have a set of plates forMovement in plants.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   18 September 1880
letters.summary: Will be happy to translate CD’s new book [Movement in plants]. Asks how large the book will be.

letters.title: To Wilhelm Breitenbach   21 September 1880
letters.summary: Comments on WB’s paper ["Über Variabilitäts-Erscheinungen an den Blüthen vonPrimula elatiorund eine Anwendung des biogenetischen Grundgesetzes",Bot. Ztg.38 (1880): 577–80].

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   21 September 1880
letters.summary:
CD is ashamed of length ofMovement in plants– with index, nearly 600 pages. JVC will be awfully sick of ch. 1.

In intervals of correcting proofs, he is writing on the formation of vegetable mould through the action of worms. It will be a curious little book [Earthworms].

letters.title: From T. M. Reade   21 September 1880
letters.summary:
Sends his paper ["Oceans and continents",Geol. Mag.7 (1880): 385–91].

Thinks John Murray of Edinburgh goes out of his way to deny an elevation/subsidence view of coral reefs ["On the origin and structure of coral reefs and islands",Proc. R. Soc. Edinburgh10 (1878–80): 505–18].

letters.title: To Josiah Mason   22 September 1880
letters.summary: Sends formal regrets that he cannot accept luncheon invitation or attend Huxley’s address [at opening of Mason College, Birmingham].

letters.title: To T. M. Reade   22 September 1880
letters.summary:
Obliged for paper ["Oceans and continents" (1880)].

Agrees that John Murray’s view [of coral reefs] is far-fetched.

letters.title: From E. M. Heckel   23 September 1880
letters.summary: Supervising French translation ofMovement in plants. Why does not CD consider spontaneous movements of flower parts, which EMH sees also as circumnutation?

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   24 September 1880
letters.summary:
Can Alphonse de Candolle see CD?

Asa Gray at Kew; will meet JDH in Italy in December.

letters.title: From J. S. Keltie   24 September 1880
letters.summary: Asks whether CD would care to preface the letter of Burt G. Wilder which he forwarded for publication ["Two kinds of vivisection",Nature22 (1880): 517–18].

letters.title: From Charles Layton (D. Appleton & Co)   24 September 1880
letters.summary: Encloses statement of U. S. sales of CD’s works to 1 Aug 1880 and a cheque for the balance due to CD.

letters.title: To J. S. Keltie, Editor Nature   [after 24 September 1880]
letters.summary: Writes a sentence with which to preface B. G. Wilder’s letter [see12726]. [Not used by and, perhaps, not sent toNature.]

letters.title: From James Torbitt   26 September 1880
letters.summary: Has raised about 500 varieties out of the crop of the second generation comprising about 1500 varieties. Growers report immense yield and no disease. Doubts if variety free of disease will live for ever. New varieties must be continually coming into existence.

letters.title: From George King   28 September 1880
letters.summary:
Sends two preserved pigs (showing some hereditary phenomenon) that the late John Scott intended for CD.

King has all of Scott’s papers.

letters.title: To George King   29 September 1880
letters.summary:
Grieved to hear of John Scott’s death.

Could GK visit Down?

letters.title: To James Torbitt   29 September 1880
letters.summary: Rejoices at good news. Will let T. H. Farrer hear the result. Cannot see why some of new varieties should not endure fungus-proof for years.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   30 September 18[80]
letters.summary: Leaves Kew the next day for three or four months of travel.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   1 October 1880
letters.summary: Sends some questions raised by THF’s notes on earthworms at Abinger; he plans to use them in his book.

letters.title: From George King   1 October 1880
letters.summary: Very pleased to receive CD’s dinner invitation.

letters.title: From the Council of the Otago Institute   1 October 1880
letters.summary: Congratulations to CD on twenty-first anniversary ofOrigin.

letters.title: To George King   2 October 1880
letters.summary: Glad GK will come. But cannot talk long to anyone.

letters.title: From Frederick Parsons   3 October 1880
letters.summary: Reports case of a girl’s sudden death when a large abscess, formed by a cherry-stone in the vermiform appendix, burst into the peritoneum. Perhaps relevant toDescent[2d ed., pp. 20–1].

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   4 October 1880
letters.summary: Has sent 2d ed. of his book,Werden und Vergehen[1880]. Notes that book was attacked in Prussian House of Deputies by ultramontane critics of Hermann Müller who had recommended it to his pupils.

letters.title: From W. S. Dallas:| 6 October 1880
letters.summary: Asks CD to join in a testimonial supporting James Murie’s candidacy for Librarian of Linnean Society.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   6 October 1880
letters.summary:
Replies to CD’s questions [in12732] regarding the Abinger Hall excavations.

Torbitt.

Family news.

letters.title: From Horace Darwin   7 October 1880
letters.summary: Worm-castings. Encloses notes about worm activities at Gravetye Manor.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   7 October 1880
letters.summary: Insists that EK take the profits from the English edition ofErasmus Darwin. EK’s essay is the valuable part of the book; CD’s is mainly gossip.

letters.title: From Charles Reinwald   7 October 1880
letters.summary: Edmond Barbier is dead and his widow needs support.

letters.title: To H. E. Litchfield   8 [October 1880]
letters.summary: Reports on Sarah Elizabeth Wedgwood’s illness.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   8 October 1880
letters.summary: Questions the exact location of rooms and trenches at Abinger excavation [forEarthworms].

letters.title: To Sophy Wedgwood   8 October [1880]
letters.summary: Asks her to look for worm-castings in heath. Thinks heath conditions may be unfavourable. CD is sure Lucy would look with her, from her well-known affection for worms. Asks what sort of lantern Lucy used.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   [before 9 October 1880]
letters.summary: Discusses how fruits of lime-trees arranged themselves in a ripple-like way on a flooded walk.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   9 October 1880
letters.summary: Is having a trough made to try experiments [on ripple-marks].

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   9 October 1880
letters.summary: Sends the marked plans of the Abinger Hall excavation site.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   10 October [1880]
letters.summary: Thanks THF for notes on Abinger excavation. Asks for more castings.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer| 10 October 1880
letters.summary: Replies to CD’s questions about worms at Abinger ruins.

letters.title: To R.-L. Moniez   10 October 1880
letters.summary: Acknowledges receipt of R-LM’s book on parasitic worms. [PerhapsEssai monographique sur les cysticerques(1880) in vol. 3 of theTravauxof the Institut Zoologique de Lille.]

letters.title: To Hyacinth Hooker   10 October 1880
letters.summary: Thanks for the bananas.

letters.title: From James Caird   11 October 1880
letters.summary: Comments on the progress of Torbitt’s experiments.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace| 11 October 1880
letters.summary:
Indicates portions ofIsland lifethat will interest CD. Explanation of the geological climate is the foundation stone of the book.

Hooker’s approval of the theory of Australian and New Zealand floras.

letters.title: From E. B. Aveling   12 October 1880
letters.summary: Mentions CD’s approval of earlier articles on CD’s works, and requests approval and permission to dedicate to CD a second work on CD’s thought for theInternational Library of Science and Free-thought.

letters.title: To E. B. Aveling   13 October 1880
letters.summary: Publication of EA’s remarks on CD’s writings requires no consent on CD’s part. CD would prefer that no part or volume be dedicated to him as it would imply his general approval of the publication, of which he knows nothing. Though he is a strong advocate of free-thought CD feels that direct attacks on Christianity and theism produce hardly any effect. Freedom of thought is best promoted by gradual illumination of men’s minds produced by advance of science. Has therefore avoided writing on religion though "I may have been unduly biassed by the pain which it would give members of my family, if I aided in any way direct attacks on religion".

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   13 October 1880
letters.summary: THF’s copybook has cleared up all points. The castings are invaluable. Encloses further queries [missing].

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   13 October [1880]
letters.summary: Is worried about brick particles in worm-castings. Asks THF for castings from a site where possible error would be avoided.

letters.title: To MBaxter, Payne & Co   14 October 1880
letters.summary: Questions BP & Co. on notices requesting the payment of rent charges.

letters.title: From Charles Reinwald   14 October 1880
letters.summary: Édouard Heckel will translateMovement in plants.

letters.title: From Sophy Wedgwood   15 October [1880]
letters.summary: On worms and worm-castings.

letters.title: To Robert Cooke   16 October 1880
letters.summary: C. Reinwald wishes to publish a French translation [ofMovement in plants] but is doubtful on account of cost. CD wants to supply him with stereotypes of the 195 cuts at prime cost.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   16 October 1880
letters.summary: Notes and replies to queries on worm-castings and worm activity on a rubble-covered road.

letters.title: From Adolf Ernst   17 October 1880
letters.summary: Observations on earthworms in Venezuela.

letters.title: From G. E. Mengozzi   17 October 1880
letters.summary: Asks CD to clarify his religious position.

letters.title: From Robert Cooke   19 October 1880
letters.summary: Cost of electrotypes from the woodcuts [inMovement in plants] for French and German editions. Suggests CD charge more than actual cost in order to repay his expenses.

letters.title: To Robert Cooke   20 October 1880
letters.summary: CD promised Reinwald the clichés [forMovement in plants] at cost, so he is to be charged £10. Eduard Koch should be charged £25, since CD’s books sell well in Germany – but Koch must not know the French have them for £10.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   20 October 1880
letters.summary: Has started experiment to see whether particles of stone become rounded in the gizzards of worms.

letters.title: To Charles Reinwald?   20 October 1880
letters.summary:
CD has arranged with Murray for CR to have woodcuts at cost for proposed French translation [ofMovement in plants].

Has sent £10 to Mme Barbier.

letters.title: From A. de Souza Corréa, Sec. Brazilian Legation   20 October 1880
letters.deprecated: A. de Souza CorreaSecretary, Brazilian Legation
letters.sender: A. de Souza CorreaSecretary, Brazilian Legation
letters.summary: The Baron de Villa Franca would like CD’s evaluation of an enclosed memoir on the culture and propagation of sugar-cane [see13600].

letters.title: To ?   22 October 1880
letters.summary: Thanks correspondent and H. J. Schaaffhausen for interesting photographs of fine footprints.

letters.title: From A. de Souza Correa, Sec. Brazilian Legation   23 October 1880
letters.deprecated: A. de Souza CorreaSecretary, Brazilian Legation
letters.sender: A. de Souza CorreaSecretary, Brazilian Legation
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his gracious and instructive reply to the Baron de Villa Franca; his letter will be forwarded to Brazil.

letters.title: To ?   23 October 1880
letters.summary: Answers correspondent’s questions on his birth date and when he began work on origin of species.

letters.title: From S. T. Preston   24 October 1880
letters.summary: Regrets the pretentious tone of his 5 Aug letter [12678].

letters.title: To S. T. Preston| 25 October 1880
letters.summary: Comments on STP’s article on women ["Evolution and female education",Nature22 (1880): 485–6].

letters.title: From S. T. Preston   26 October 1880
letters.summary: His intent in quotingDescenton the law of equal hereditary transmission to both sexes in his article "Evolution and female education" was to support female education.

letters.title: From Anthony Rich   26 October 1880
letters.summary:
ThePhiladelphusCD sent is flourishing and appears to attract a particular kind of fly.

Science and the law as professions. Lawyers in politics.

letters.title: To G. E. Mengozzi   [before 28] October 1880
letters.summary:
Does not believe any organic being is evidence of design; refers GEM to the last pages ofVariationfor his reasons. Even if no organism shows evidence of design, this does not preclude faith in the existence of a loving creator; evidence of such a creator must be looked for outside the limits of physical science.

Thanks him for the volume on the philosophy of medicine,

and asks him to convey to the Scuola Italica thanks for the great honour they have done him.

letters.title: From G. E. Mengozzi   28 October 1880
letters.summary: Extremely grateful for CD’s reply. He continues in his faith in God and his devotion to CD.

letters.title: From Lady Florence Dixie   29 October [1880]
letters.summary: With reference to CD’s account of the subterranean habits of the tucutuco [Journal of researches, p. 58], sends her personal experience of having seen them come out of their burrows. One which she caught was not blind.

letters.title: To James Torbitt   29 October 1880
letters.summary:
"Your secret shall be inviolable, and to make sure in case of my illness or death I have now burnt your letter."

Wishes JT success in commercial venture.

letters.title: From Bartholomaeus Carneri   30 October 1880
letters.summary: Is dedicating hisFoundations of ethicsto CD.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   30 [October 1880]
letters.summary: Invites FG to lunch.

letters.title: To James Murie, Linnean Society   30 October 1880
letters.summary: Requests a volume ofZoologistwith an article dated Oct 1849.

letters.title: To A. B. Buckley   31 October [1880]
letters.summary: Has talked to Lubbock and Huxley about pension for Wallace. Asks for help in getting information about Wallace’s circumstances.

letters.title: From F. M. Balfour   [November 1880]
letters.summary: Thanks for copy ofMovement in plants; CD’s discovery of a "nervous system without nerves" will have important bearing on origins of animal nervous system.

letters.title: To J. Crier   November 1880
letters.summary: Discusses matters relating to Great Western Railway Company stock.

letters.title: From W. D. Roebuck   1 November 1880
letters.summary: Sends the Yorkshire Naturalists’ Union’s publications prior to the visit to Down of its deputation.

letters.title: From W. R. Browne   [2?] November [1880]
letters.summary: Announces intention to hold a private conference with the Archbishop of Canterbury with the aim of encouraging men of science to reaffirm their religious beliefs and also to publish a series of articles in theContemporary Reviewon the state of the various sciences.

letters.title: To W. D. Roebuck   [after 2 November 1880]
letters.summary: Expresses his gratitude for the Address he has been given.

letters.title: To Volney Rattan   3 November 1880
letters.summary:
Thanks for seeds ofMegarrhizaand for information in letter to Asa Gray.

Will send copy ofMovement in plantsin whichMegarrhizais discussed [see pp. 81–2].

letters.title: To W. D. Roebuck   3 November 1880
letters.summary: Thanks for address honouring him.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   3 November 1880
letters.summary: High praise forIsland life; ARW’s "best book". Encloses notes of comments and criticism. Hooker pleased by dedication.

letters.title: From Robert Cooke   4 November 1880
letters.summary: If every copy [ofMovement in plants] is sold at 15s, CD will lose about £50.

letters.title: From F. C. Dixie 4 November [1880]
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for his reply to her letter.

Offers to send him a copy of her book on her expedition to Patagonia [Across Patagonia(1880)].

letters.title: From Robert Cooke   5 November 1880
letters.summary: Six hundred copies ofMovement in plantswere wanted [at Murray’s annual sale] – a good start.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   5 November 1880
letters.summary:
Has read THH’s review of Sir Wyville Thomson’s [Introduction to the]Voyage of the "Challenger".

Sends a draft of a letter forNature[Collected papers2: 223–4]. He particularly asks THH to decide whether he should include a certain paragraph [seeML1: 389].

letters.title: ToNature   5 November [1880]
letters.summary: Sir Wyville Thomson misunderstands natural selection when he says the theory "refers the evolution of species to extreme variation guided only by natural selection". CD demurs at the "extreme variation" and the "only". No one has said evolution depends only on natural selection. CD has adduced many facts on the effects of use and disuse and on the direct action of the environment.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   5 November 1880
letters.summary:
Lectured on mental evolution in Newcastle.

Has conducted interesting research on locomotor systems of echinoderms.

letters.title: To ?   5 November 1880
letters.summary: Refers correspondent toDescentfor some information on marriage arrangements, and on the mental and moral nature of monkeys.

letters.title: From George Maw   6 November 1880
letters.summary: He has observed several instances of animals’ tails lying to the left in rigor mortis. Is this a general rule?

letters.title: From A. B. Buckley   7 November 1880
letters.summary: Has spoken to Wallace to see if reluctant to accept a Government pension. He would accept if CD and Huxley believe it justified. Encloses details of Wallace’s efforts to obtain a position as naturalist and his claims for a pension.

letters.title: From William Clowes & Sons   [before 8 November 1880]
letters.summary: Explains delay in printing proofs [ofMovement in plants?].

letters.title: To Robert Cooke   8 November [1880]
letters.summary:
Thanks RC for telling him about sale of 600 copies [ofMovement in plants]. He had expected less, so loss will not be as heavy as he feared. Asks whether he should not have 250 more copies printed and what it would cost to have the type kept up.

Instructions for presentation copies.

The index is the worst ever published.

letters.title: To George Maw   8 November 1880
letters.summary: Believes the flexure in GM’s dead animals must result from the greater strength of the muscles on the left side. Thinks his son George once tested the strength of each leg of a group of boys, and CD could get his notes if wanted.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   8 November 1880
letters.summary:
Response to CD’s notes [onIsland life]:

1. On relation of paucity of fossils to coldness of water;

2. Cessation of the glacial period;

3. Rate of deposit and geological time;

4. The importance of preoccupation (by plants) in relation to plants arriving later.

Charge of speculative explanations is just.

Defends plausibility of migration of plants from mountain to mountain.

letters.title: To A. B. Buckley   9 November 1880
letters.summary: Thanks for information about Wallace. Is preparing memorial to be submitted to Government [seeking pension for Wallace].

letters.title: From Robert Cooke   10 November 1880
letters.summary:
Movement in plantsneeds only the index. Distressed by CD’s dissatisfaction with the indexer.

Eight hundred copies have now been sold. Type will be kept up.

Decision on printing additional copies should await reviews.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [11 November 1880]
letters.summary: Sorry he forgot the gardener’s address. Having a very nice time in Cambridge, and is almost finished the bramble paper. Drawing room is upside down, so living in Horace’s working room and dining room. Greek question was lost in the Senate House. George dined there last night. Too muddy to bicycle. Has some stuff for spectacles.

letters.title: From Daniel Mackintosh   11 November 1880
letters.summary: Has found three zones of stones in the Welsh and Pennine mountains which he accounts for by elevation and subsidence. Does CD think that these movements in historical times have been caused by earthquakes or by slow and gradual movements?

letters.title: From J. J. Eyre   12 November 1880
letters.summary:
Reports inability to control depressor anguli oris muscle in grief.

Has readExpression.

letters.title: From James Paget   12 November 1880
letters.summary: Sends a copy of his lectureElemental pathology: an address on elemental pathology delivered in the pathological section of the British Medical Association(Paget 1880).

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   12 November 1880
letters.summary:
Is collecting annual subscriptions for the support of J[emmy] FitzRoy Button. Has only just been told of the death of Miss [Sarah Elizabeth] Wedgwood.

Gives news of some formerBeaglecrew members.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   13 November 1880
letters.summary: Sends draft of memorial for a pension for Wallace with suggested names of signers. Asks THH’s help.

letters.title: To Daniel Mackintosh   13 November 1880
letters.summary:
Comments on DM’s ["The Moel-Tryfan shelly deposits",Q. J. Geol. Soc. Lond.37 (1881): 351–69].

Comments on cause of earthquakes.

Believes formation of ice lowered level of sea.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes| 13 November 1880
letters.summary: Sends proofs ofEncyclopaedia Britannicaarticle on hybridism [9th ed., 12: 422–6]. Can CD mention authorities who should be cited?

letters.title: To A. B. Buckley   14 November 1880
letters.summary: Comments on her new book [Life and her children(1880)]. "… you have treated evolution with much dexterity and truthfulness".

letters.title: From E. A. Darwin   14 November [1880]
letters.summary:
Asks CD to sign his guarantee.

Reports events at Cambridge involving Horace.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   14 November 1880
letters.summary:
Will support the petition for a pension for Wallace.

CD’s paragraph [about Wyville Thomson, see12796] was so good that if he had written it he would have sent it to the printer, but [for CD] it is best to refrain.

letters.title: To H. H. Johnson   14 November 1880
letters.summary:
Thanks for information on the slope of ground at Worcester.

CD’s passion now is worms.

SendsMovement in plants. While correcting proof, CD remembered an old article by HHJ, which he regrets not including.

letters.title: To James Paget   14 November 1880
letters.summary:
Surprising thought that diseases of plants should illustrate human pathology.

Will recommend A. B. Frank’s article in a German encyclopedia, on diseases of plants, to Francis Darwin.

Gives JP a good case of regeneration in plants – the radicle of the common bean. That plants have little power of regeneration is not difficult to understand by anyone who believes in Pangenesis, "if such a man exists … There is reason to think that my imaginary gemmules have small power of passing from cell to cell."

Refers to early experiments in which he tried to produce galls in plants by injecting poisons.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   14 November [1880]
letters.summary: Comments on hybridisation; cites authorities. Sends book by Wilhelm Olbers Focke [Die Pflanzen-Mischlinge(1881)].

letters.title: From A. R. Carrington   15 November 1880
letters.summary: ARC found a frog in New Zealand; contradicts CD [inOrigin, 6th ed. (1872), p. 350.]

letters.title: From Robert Cooke   15 November 1880
letters.summary: Murray’s must reprintDescent. Does CD want to make any corrections in the plates?

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   15 November 1880
letters.summary:
Comments on GJR’s article on hybridisation.

Recommends his article ["Fertility and hybrids from the Chinese and common goose",Collected papers2: 219–20].

Discusses crosses ofLythrum.

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   16 November 1880
letters.summary: Wonders whether CD can explain why white muscat grapes growing between two black grapevines have started turning black on ripening but retain the muscat flavour.

letters.title: To Williams and Norgate 16 November 1880
letters.summary: Although he cannot use the Neapolitan work, his respect for the service to science rendered by the Zoological Station at Naples leads him to subscribe.

letters.title: To B. J. Sulivan   17 November 1880
letters.summary: BJS’s case is one of the direct action of the pollen of one variety on the mother plant of another variety. Gives references to analogous cases.

letters.title: From W. C. Williamson   17 November 1880
letters.summary: Thanks CD for receiving the Yorkshire Naturalists’ Union’s deputation.

letters.title: To Henry Johnson   18 November 1880
letters.summary:
Is obliged for the clear answers to his queries.

Regrets that his health will not permit a visit to Wroxeter.

Will sign his name on next page, but "what geese people are about autographs".

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   18 November 1880
letters.summary:
Thanks for copy of W. O. Focke [Die Pflanzen-Mischlinge(1881)].

Has nearly finished paper on locomotor system in echinoderms.

letters.title: To W. C. Williamson   18 November 1880
letters.summary: Receiving deputation gave CD pleasure.

letters.title: To B. J. Plačzek   [after 19 November 1880]
letters.summary: Expresses doubts that pigeons could rest one wing during flight.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   19 November 1880
letters.summary:
Comments on CD’s book [Movement in plants].

Continues with his experiments with ripple-marks.

Is in despair about his astronomy.

letters.title: From B. J. Plačzek   19 November 1880
letters.summary: Behaviour of pigeons is now different from that described inBeresbith Raba, a 3d century gloss on Genesis.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   20 November 1880
letters.summary: Some sheets [ofMovement in plants] are missing. Is delighted with its "lesson of methods of observation patience and thought".

letters.title: To Robert Cooke   20 November 1880
letters.summary:
Likes appearance [ofMovement in plants].

TheTimesreview should sell a few more copies.

Thanks Murray for present of volumes by Charles St John [A tour in Sutherlandshire, 2 vols. (1849?)].

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   20 November [1880]
letters.summary:
Glad GHD goes on with ripple-marks; if he makes out a theory of ripples, they might give important information about the most ancient deposits.

CD has been wonderfully glorified in theTimes[review ofMovement in plants, 20 Nov 1880].

letters.title: From Anthony Rich   20 November [1880]
letters.summary:
Thanks forMovement in plants.

Condolences on S. E. Wedgwood’s death.

letters.title: From Sarah Haliburton   21 November [1880]
letters.deprecated: Sarah Harriet (Sarah Harriet Williams) (Sarah Harriet Mostyn Owen) Haliburton
letters.sender: Sarah Harriet (Sarah Harriet Williams) (Sarah Harriet Mostyn Owen) Haliburton
letters.summary: A laudatory reference in theTimes[19 Nov 1880, p. 4] impels her to write after many years. Hopes to see him.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   [21 November 1880]
letters.summary:
Wishes to see CD.

He has been proposed as Professor of Geology at the University of Moscow.

letters.title: From Daniel Mackintosh   21 November 1880
letters.summary:
The use of earthquakes as a geological cause in his previous letter was careless.

Shelly beach deposits over considerable distance from Ireland to Scotland seem better explained by high sea-level than low land.

Only CD seems to have reported shattered rocks under the Moel Tryfan drift.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   21 November 1880
letters.summary: Thanks for book [Movement in plants].

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   22 November 1880
letters.summary: Very pleased by JVC’s note aboutMovement in plants. Feared he would find it intolerably dull. Some missing sheets are being replaced. Also sends a perfect copy.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   22 November [1880]
letters.summary: Thanks CD for copy of Worms and says he is enjoying it. Is pleased that a full article appeared in the Times. Will go to Beaulieu soon for worm casts. His gardener calls worms “our civil engineers”. Promised to tell Frank how to make plants bend.

letters.title: To Sarah Haliburton   22 November 1880
letters.deprecated: Sarah Harriet (Sarah Harriet Williams) (Sarah Harriet Mostyn Owen) Haliburton
letters.recipient: Sarah Harriet (Sarah Harriet Williams) (Sarah Harriet Mostyn Owen) Haliburton
letters.summary: Thanks SH for her kind letter; would like to see her again.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   22 November 1880
letters.summary:
Praise forMovement in plants, lately arrived.

Praise for Wallace’sIsland life

and astonishment that he could be a spiritualist.

Differs with Wallace on age of SW. Australian flora. JDH ascribes its peculiarities to isolation by an inland sea.

letters.title: From W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   [23 November–31 December 1880]
letters.summary:
CD may not mean same thing as WTT-D by absorbent pegs inAbronia.

F. O. Bower’s paper onWelwitschia[germination] [Q. J. Microsc. Sci.21 (1881): 15–30] will appear in January.

Has observed earthworms for CD: they do not drawRobinialeaves into burrows by the petioles.

letters.title: From O. A. Ainslie   23 November 1880
letters.summary: Has learned of death of Sarah Elizabeth Wedgwood, former proprietor of Tromer Lodge, and writes about his deceased father’s earlier attempts to purchase this property. Requests information on any future transfer of it.

letters.title: From Alphonse de Candolle   23 November 1880
letters.summary:
Finds CD was correct inVariation: hybrid bees tend to sting more often than pure-bred bees.

Preparing a second edition of the chapter on the origin of cultivated plants in hisGéographie botanique. The work done since 1855 confirms his opinions.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   23 November [1880]
letters.summary:
Discusses GHD’s ripple theory. Asks him how they are formed.

Delighted to hear that light is dawning in GHD’s eyes on the planetary system.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   23 [November 1880]
letters.summary:
Asks WED to observe whether worms consistently draw acacia leaves into their burrows with a particular end first.

Will soon know whether he will need worm-castings from Beaulieu.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   23 November 1880
letters.summary:
Admires Wallace’sIsland life.

Criticises: 1. His view of similar plants on distant mountains – CD prefers previous low-land connections to Wallace’s summit–summit dispersal;

2. Source of warmth for ancient Arctic climate;

3. Origin of S. Australian flora.

CD’s favourite cases inMovement in plants.

letters.title: From Frederick McDermott   23 November 1880
letters.summary: Wishes to read CD’s books; will not do so without an assurance of CD’s faith in the New Testament.

letters.title: From Samuel Newington   23 November 1880
letters.summary: He has proved that heat is generated by the exudation of oxygen from roots, and that there is continuous electrical action from leaves to roots.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   23 November [1880]
letters.summary:
WTT-D’s suggestion about absorbent function of pegs inAbroniasuggests origin of pegs inWelwitschia, which deeply interests CD. Previously could not see how pegs became large enough to be of mechanical use. Now thinks tissue between hypocotyl and radicle absorbs fluid, which would favour rise of peg to expose larger surface.

Rejects German contempt for investigating use of organs.

Asks WTT-D to observe how worms drawRobinialeaves into burrows.

letters.title: To Frederick McDermott   24 November 1880
letters.summary: CD does "not believe in the Bible as a divine revelation".

letters.title: From Raphael Meldola   24 November 1880
letters.summary: Wants information on Fritz Müller’s papers bearing on Weismann’s work.

letters.title: From G. E. Mengozzi   24 November 1880
letters.summary: Announces proposal to make CD an Honorary Member of La Scuola Italica.

letters.title: To G. E. Mengozzi   [after 24 November 1880]
letters.summary: Asks GEM to thank La Scuola Italica for the honour conferred upon him.

letters.title: From O. A. Ainslie   25 [November 1880?]
letters.summary: [Too damaged to be read.]

letters.title: To V. O. Kovalevsky   25 November [1880]
letters.summary: Will be pleased to have VOK come to Down any day.

letters.title: From M. T. Masters   25 November 1880
letters.summary:
Praise forMovement in plants.

He thinks G. A. Chatin, whom CD quotes [p. 389], is mistaken about movement of conifer leaves. Cites his own paper ["Relations between morphology and physiology in the leaves of certain conifers",J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)17 (1880): 517–52].

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   25 November 1880
letters.summary: References to Fritz Müller’s papers relevant to Weismann’sStudien[inKosmos(Aug, Sept, and Oct 1877)].

letters.title: From W. F. P. Pfeffer   25 November 1880
letters.summary:
Thanks forMovement in plants.

Describes work [onPflanzenphysiologie, 2 vols. (1881)].

letters.title: From William Preyer   25 November 1880
letters.summary:
Sends his book [Naturwissenschaftliche Thatsachen und Probleme. Populäre Vorträge(1880)].

Anxious to receiveMovement in plantsbecause CD’s methods may be applicable to his experiments on the earliest movements of animal embryos.

letters.title: To Carlos Ribeiro   25 November 1880
letters.summary: Thanks for his great work on prehistoric remains in Portugal and his paper on Tertiary formations.

letters.title: To M. T. Masters   [after 25 November 1880]
letters.summary: Thanks for note. CD had had misgivings about Chatin but had assumed he was trustworthy [seeMovement in plants, p. 389].

letters.title: From Robert Cooke   26 November 1880
letters.summary: Five hundred more copies ofMovement in plantsmust be printed immediately. Asks CD to send any corrections to printer.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   26 November [1880]
letters.summary: Observations on worms’ pulling leaves into their burrows.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   26 November 1880
letters.summary: Huxley has persuaded JDH that the Wallace memorial may not be hopeless; JDH still has misgivings about Wallace’s spiritualism but will follow CD’s and Huxley’s decision.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   26 November 1880
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for copy ofMovement in plants. It will be reviewed inKosmos[8 (1880–1): 258–71] by Hermann Müller.

Kosmoswill probably cease publication. Publisher has decided to sell.

Fritz Müller has suffered from flood.

Müller’s latest letter contains a polemic against Wagner’s migration theory,

and some interesting observations on Crustacea.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   [after 26 November 1880]
letters.summary: Is glad that Hooker will sign memorial for Wallace’s pension. Had thought it hopeless because Hooker objected to ARW’s spiritualism and his bet on the sphericity of the globe.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   [27 November 1880]
letters.summary: Thanks toTimesreview, Murray needs 500 more copies [ofMovement in plants].

letters.title: To James Geikie   27 November 1880
letters.summary: Thanks JG for his magnificent book [Prehistoric Europe].

letters.title: To Hermann Mùller   27 November 1880
letters.summary: Has heard of flood from which Fritz Müller escaped. Has he lost books, microscope, apparatus? Offers £50 or £100.

letters.title: From Hermann Müller   27 November 1880
letters.summary: Movement in plantshas shown him CD’s research method: 1. Find a fundamental idea of great generality (circumnutation); 2. Pursue it everywhere with observations and experiment; 3. Conduct special observations which undo any doubt of generality.

letters.title: To William Preyer   27 November 1880
letters.summary:
Will send copy ofMovement in plants.

Encloses copies of articles [unspecified].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   28 November [1880]
letters.summary:
Wants to see Frank become F.R.S. before he dies.

Pities Wallace and wants a pension for him very much.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   28 November 1880
letters.summary:
Bad news aboutKosmos[ceasing publication].

Fritz Müller’s losses [in a flood]; "I have long looked on him as the best observer in the world."

EK’s astonishing account of crustacean that repairs its legs in an ancestral form seems to support Pangenesis, which has hardly any friends.

letters.title: To Walter White, Royal Society   28 November [1880]
letters.summary: Asks for list of Royal Society Council members, which CD needs because council members never back up certificates.

letters.title: From F. C. Dixie   29 November [1880]
letters.summary:
Sends CD a copy of her book [Across Patagonia(1880)],

together with a privately printed "tragedy" written at the age of 14.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   29 November 1880
letters.summary: Quality of Frank’s work merits F.R.S., but quantity could defer speedy election. Will advise best strategy.

letters.title: From J. B. Innes 29 November 1880
letters.summary: Has heard that land may be available for parsonage at Down.

letters.title: To A. W. Howitt [before 30 November 1880]
letters.summary: Thanks AWH for copy of Fison and Howitt 1880, which he will read when it is returned by J. F. McLennan.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   30 November [1880]
letters.summary: Asks whether WED can collect some worm-castings from Beaulieu Abbey.

letters.title: From J. F. McLennan   30 November 1880.
letters.summary:
Thanks for reference [to Lorimer Fison and A. W. Howitt,Kamilaroi and Kurnai(1880)].

Irate against L. H. Morgan.

letters.title: From Hermann Mùller   30 November 1880
letters.summary:
Fritz Müller suffered moderate damage in Brazilian flood.

Continued praise for the universal importance for botany ofMovement in plants.

letters.title: To J. W. C. Fegan   [December 1880–February 1881]
letters.summary: Gladly turns reading room over to JWCF for his mission work. Through his gospel services there is not a drunkard left in the village.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   1 December [1880]
letters.summary: Will soon manage to go to Beaulieu. Is glad the book is going off well. Is thinking of going to the Roman Villa at Brading on the Isle of Wight.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   1 December 1880
letters.summary: Responds, with some embarrassment, to JDH’s caution on Frank’s F.R.S. prospects.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   2 December [1880]
letters.summary:
Gives instructions to WED about looking for earthworm activity at Brading.

Mentions James Geikie’s excellent book [Prehistoric Europe(1881)].

letters.title: To J. B. Innes   2 December 1880
letters.summary: Hensleigh Wedgwood has told CD that land JBI had inquired about will be sold at auction with the house [Trowmer [Tromer!?] Lodge].

letters.title: From William Preyer   2 December 1880
letters.summary: CD’s comment that certain instincts originate as variations of the brain, rather than as habits, is supported by Brown-Séquard’s and C. F. O. Westphal’s work on epileptiform movements.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   3 December [1880]
letters.summary: Description of remains of a Roman villa and the worm activity at the site.

letters.title: From James Paget   3 December 1880
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for his note and his new book [Movement in plants].

Makes him feel "we must go beyond plants for a really elemental pathology".

Wishes he knew enough about crystals to work at them.

letters.title: From Friedrich Hildebrand   4 December 1880
letters.summary:
Preoccupied by reorganisation of Botanic Garden.

Regards to Francis Darwin.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   4 December 1880
letters.summary: Wants to propose Frank for F.R.S. now, with election in 1882.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   4 December 1880
letters.summary:
Comments on Pangenesis. Quotes long passage from article by Fritz Müller concerning regeneration of lost members among crustaceans.

Kosmoshas been sold to Eduard Koch in Stuttgart; will be converted into a weekly. Science will be de-emphasised. Krause seeking new publisher to continue on old basis.

Gustav Jäger injured in train accident.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   5 December 1880
letters.summary:
Thanks for agreeing to propose Frank as F.R.S.

Would have enjoyed discussingIsland life.

letters.title: From Edouard Strasburger   5 December 1880
letters.summary: Thanks CD for a copy of his book [Movement in plants].

letters.title: From Federico Delpino   6 December 1880
letters.summary: Thanks forMovement in plants; particularly supports indirect rather than direct action of light and gravity on plants.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   [7 December 1880]
letters.summary: Asks to see THH on Thursday or Friday to hear about the Wallace affair.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   7 December 1880
letters.summary:
THH will be at Kensington.

He has been so busy that he has let the Wallace business stand over.

letters.title: From T. M. Reade   7 December 1880
letters.summary: Recommends letters by William Topley inGeological Magazine. WT discusses past distribution of oceans and continents.

letters.title: From Arnold & Carolina Dodel-Port   8 December 1880
letters.summary:
Have receivedMovement in plants. It will interest not only botanists but zoologists and biologists.

Ten years ago AD-P encountered great opposition when he started teaching Darwinism at Zurich. Now all except old Oswald Heer call themselves Darwinists.

letters.title: From Hugo de Vries| 8 December 1880
letters.summary: Many thanks forMovement in plants; is especially interested in sensitivity of young seedlings.

letters.title: From Hermann Vöchting   8 December 1880
letters.summary:
Thanks forMovement in plants, which confirms HV’s unpublished conclusions concerning gravity and the horizontal bending of radicles.

[CD note forwards letter to Francis Darwin.]

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   9 December [1880]
letters.summary:
The Kovalevskys have been to lunch.

Madame Kovalevsky is greatly interested in GHD’s papers.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   9 December 1880
letters.summary: Thinks Wallace memorial should not be presented to Lord Aberdare, nor to Owen, for signature, but will follow THH’s wishes.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   9 December 1880
letters.summary: Would like to reply to Samuel Butler’sUnconscious memory[1880] inKosmos.

letters.title: To T. M. Reade   9 December 1880
letters.summary: Comments on TMR’s "Oceanic islands" [Geol. Mag.8 (1881): 75–7]. Fact that oceanic islands are all volcanic argues for view that no continent ever occupied the oceans. Chalk seemed best evidence of ocean having existed where continent now stands. CD leans to view that continents have occupied present positions since Cambrian.

letters.title: From T. M. Reade   10 December 1880
letters.summary: Argues against volcanic origin of coral islands and for the submergence of continents. Cites Judd’s argument on the volcanoes of the moon.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   10 December 1880
letters.summary:
Returns book [W. O. Focke,Pflanzen-Mischlinge]. It was of great use.

Suggests experiment involving light stimulation of plants.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   11 December 1880
letters.summary: Sends draft of the Wallace memorial.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   11 December 1880
letters.summary: Thinks his private notes failed to convey his ideas. JT wanted CD "to look at the product and express an opinion as to its value".

letters.title: From Sarah Haliburton   12 December [1880]
letters.deprecated: Sarah Harriet (Sarah Harriet Williams) (Sarah Harriet Mostyn Owen) Haliburton
letters.sender: Sarah Harriet (Sarah Harriet Williams) (Sarah Harriet Mostyn Owen) Haliburton
letters.summary: Writes of the pleasure of seeing him again.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   [12 December 1880]
letters.summary: CD is pleased that EK will answer Butler. Thinks Butler is half insane.

letters.title: To James Geikie   13 December 1880
letters.summary:
Comments onPrehistoric Europe.

Asks JG’s opinion of Daniel MacKintosh’s paper ["Results of a systematic survey of erratic blocks",Q. J. Geol. Soc. Lond.35 (1879): 425–53].

Comments on loess.

Feels uneasy about streams of stone of Falkland Islands.

letters.title: To Sarah Haliburton   13 December 1880
letters.deprecated: Sarah Harriet (Sarah Harriet Williams) (Sarah Harriet Mostyn Owen) Haliburton
letters.recipient: Sarah Harriet (Sarah Harriet Williams) (Sarah Harriet Mostyn Owen) Haliburton
letters.summary: CD and Emma enjoyed SH’s visit to Queen Anne Street and would like her to come to Down. When he next comes to London, he hopes to call on Fanny Biddulph.

letters.title: To James Paget   13 December 1880
letters.summary: "Perhaps you would like to see a very small ""tumour"" on a lateral branch of the Silver Fur, caused by an Oestrum, as stated (with references) in my Power of Movement in Plants. These tumours are sometimes almost as big as a child’s head. At what age they emit theuprightshoot, I do not know."

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   13 December 1880
letters.summary:
Discusses GJR’s idea of subjecting plants to brief flashes of light.

Hoped to see GJR in London, but was too tired.

Delighted his book [Movement in plants] has interested GJR.

Asks if GJR has example of dogs calling on each other to go hunting; there is a case half a mile away.

Has heard that Samuel Butler has abused him in his latest book, but he does not intend to look at it.

letters.title: To James Torbitt   13 December 1880
letters.summary:
Thanks for report [on potato experiments].

Still has subscription money for JT’s experiments. How much does he need?

letters.title: To James Murie   14 December 1880
letters.summary: Requests G. J. Allman’s address.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   14 December 1880
letters.summary:
Glad CD thinks experiment worth trying [see12904]. Has written to John Tyndall for permission to do it at Royal Institution.

Paper on echinoderms written [with J. C. Ewart, "Locomotor system of Echinodermata",Philos. Trans. R. Soc. Lond.172 (1881): 829–85].

letters.title: From G. E. Mengozzi   15 December 1880
letters.summary:
Pleased CD has accepted honorary membership in his academy, La Scuola Italica.

Encloses three "tableaux synoptiques" from a work he intends to dedicate to CD.

[CD’s notes are for his reply.]

letters.title: From James Torbitt   15 December 1880
letters.summary: Forster cannot help at present. Is sending copies of an enclosure [missing] to Downing Street.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [before 15 December 1880]
letters.summary: Will stay until London until after the Linnean Society meeting unless CD wants anything. Asks to send abstracts of papers. Has made short abstracts of papers for Nature.

letters.title: From W. R. Browne   16 December 1880
letters.summary: Writes on behalf of the Archbishop of Canterbury to invite CD to a private conference organised in an attempt to reconcile science and religion. [Enclosed is a printed two-page memorial calling for such a conference.]

letters.title: From Otto Hahn   16 December 1880
letters.summary: Sends his book [Die Meteorite und ihre Organismen(1880)]. Claims to have discovered the beginning of life on earth, which confirms CD’s theory.

letters.title: To Hermann Vöchting| 16 December 1880
letters.summary:
Comments on HV’sÜber Organbildung im Pflanzenreich: über Wachstumsursachen und Lebenseinheiten[pt 1, 1878].

Mentions paper by his son [Francis Darwin, "The theory of the growth of cuttings, illustrated by observations on the bramble,Rubus fruticosus",J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)18 (1881): 406–19].

letters.title: To G. J. Allman   17 December 1880
letters.summary: Asks GJA to sign memorial [petitioning Government for pension for Wallace].

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   17 December [1880]
letters.summary:
Worm-castings from [Roman] ruins at Brading contained bits of tiles or bricks. Obliged for WED’s trouble about Brading castings.

Movement in plantswell received in Germany.

letters.title: To W. H. Flower   17 December 1880
letters.summary: Asks Flower to sign document [application for pension for Wallace].

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   17 December 1880
letters.summary:
John Tyndall has provided apparatus for experiment with light.

Frank [Darwin]’s paper a brilliant success [J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)18: 406–19, 420–55. Read 16 Dec].

Has got a monkey for observation.

letters.title: To W. R. Browne   18 December 1880
letters.summary: Will not be able to attend the proposed conference and feels no benefit will arise from it.

letters.title: To James Torbitt   19 December 1880
letters.summary: Does JT require part or all of £90 that CD holds from subscribers for his experiments?

letters.title: To Patrick Geddes   20 December 1880
letters.summary: Gives permission to copy figures fromInsectivorous plantsfor article inEncyclopaedia Britannica[by PG, 9th ed., vol. 13, pp. 134–40].

letters.title: From James Geikie   20 December 1880
letters.summary: DiscussesPrehistoric Europe; establishing the existence of interglacial periods; iceberg vs glacier transport of erratic boulders.

letters.title: To Otto Hahn   20 December 1880
letters.summary: Thanks for his letter and magnificently illustrated book.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   20 December 1880
letters.summary: On Wallace’s pension and Frank’s F.R.S.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   20 December 1880
letters.summary:
Comments on papers by Francis Darwin.

Suggests methods for growing seedlings for experiments involving light.

Comments on GJR’s observations on monkey.

letters.title: From W. R. Browne| 21 December 1880
letters.summary: Regrets CD is unable to attend proposed conference [see12918]. Would like his opinion on why it is not desirable.

letters.title: To ?   21 December 1880
letters.summary:
The recipient is thanked for his "interesting letter".

CD sends an article received from [James Geikie?]. "You will see that it is important to know whether the laminae of slate have ever been bent up-hill."

letters.title: To W. R. Browne   22 December 1880
letters.summary: Believes the conference will be of no value because individuals can only decide for themselves on the truths of science and religion.

letters.title: To A. C. L. G. Günther   22 December [1880]
letters.summary: Anxious that AG should consider a memorial [for A. R. Wallace]. Makes arrangements to avoid delay.

letters.title: To J. L. Hawkins   23 December 1880
letters.summary: Thanks for information about cats avoiding certain species of mice.

letters.title: To Dorothy Nevill   23 December 1880
letters.summary: CD is familiar with cases of prepotency that are so strong that a cross has no effect.

letters.title: From James Torbitt| 23 December 1880
letters.summary: Will CD hold the £90 for JT? Asks him to read enclosed printed letter to W. E. Gladstone which he hopes will attract attention.

letters.title: From Daniel Mackintosh   24 December 1880
letters.summary: Thanks for the American pamphlet, which has caused him to write the enclosed extract on "bent and shattered edges of slaty laminae".

letters.title: To J. M. Herbert   25 December [1880]
letters.summary:
Recalls student days at Cambridge and microscope JMH gave him.

Discusses his children, health, and work.

letters.title: To James Torbitt   25 December [1880]
letters.summary: Suggests JT make public his letter to W. E. Gladstone [on results of potato experiments]; thinks post office would object to JT’s plan of distribution.

letters.title: From F. J. Cohn| 26 December 1880
letters.summary: Response toMovement in plants. Setting out to confirm CD’s experiments. Believes plant cell motion, like that of animals, depends on protoplasm more than water.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   26 December 1880
letters.summary:
CD’s sons tell him that Samuel Butler inUnconscious memorystates that some passages inErasmus Darwinwere taken from hisEvolution, old and new. Their unprejudiced view is that the passages do come from Butler. CD hopes EK will give a clear explanation if he writes on the matter inKosmos.

CD is taking no public notice of Butler’s attack on himself.

letters.title: To George Bentham   27 December 1880
letters.summary: Asks GB to sign certificate for Francis Darwin [candidate for Royal Society].

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   27 December [1880]
letters.summary: FD’s abstract ["Physiology of plants",Nature23 (1880): 178–81] is excellent, and as clear as daylight.

letters.title: To A. C. L. G. Günther   27 December 1880
letters.summary: Sends memorial [for A. R. Wallace] for AG to sign. Asks whether AG will forward it to Owen; CD cannot send it as he has not spoken to him for 20 years.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   27 December 1880
letters.summary: Has obtained signatures for the memorial. Wonders whether Gladstone would see a deputation and offers to write to Gladstone instead. Asks THH’s advice.

letters.title: From Henry Johnson   27 December [1880]
letters.summary: Article in Shrewsbury newspaper makes him worry about CD’s health.

letters.title: To Duke of Argyll   [before 28 December 1880]
letters.deprecated: George Douglas Campbell, 8th duke of Argyll
letters.recipient: George Douglas Campbell, 8th duke of Argyll
letters.summary: Encloses a memorial for Wallace which he hopes the Duke will sign. Asks, if he does sign, that he inform Gladstone of the fact.

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   [28? December 1880]
letters.summary: Informs HWB of arrangements for signing the memorial to W. E. Gladstone [for a civil pension for Wallace]. CD has got Duke of Argyll to write to Gladstone in favour of it.

letters.title: From George Bentham   28 December 1880
letters.summary:
Pleased to sign certificate for Francis Darwin.

Has never underrated importance of [plant] physiological studies, especially when carried out as FD has been doing.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [28? December 1880]
letters.summary: The Duke of Argyll has written to Gladstone in support of a pension for A. R. Wallace.

letters.title: From A. C. L. G. Günther| [28 December 1880]
letters.summary: Has signed and returned memorial [for Wallace]; does not know where to find Owen.

letters.title: From J. M. Herbert   28 December 1880
letters.summary:
News of JMH’s second marriage.

Death of Charles Whitley’s wife.

Thinks CD’s fame in Europe is greater than that of Cuvier.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   28 December 1880
letters.summary:
Sees no use in a deputation. Suggests CD send the memorial with a letter.

Family news.

letters.title: To Henry Johnson   28 December [1880]
letters.summary: The report that CD is seriously ill is false, but the kind letters that it produced have done a good turn. [See12943.]

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   [after 28 December 1880]
letters.summary: Asks HWB to sign the memorial, possibly with official title, and then to pass it quickly to Hooker.

letters.title: To J. S. B. Sanderson   29 December 1880
letters.summary: Requests JSBS sign certificate for [Francis Darwin’s] candidacy [for Royal Society].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   [29 Dec 1880]
letters.summary: Asks JDH to read the enclosed Memorial, sign it, and send it to T. H. Huxley.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   [29 December 1880]
letters.summary:
Has asked Hooker to sign the Wallace memorial and send it on to THH.

Read splendid lecture by THH on evolution in theTimes["On the application of the laws of evolution to the arrangement of the Vertebrata and more particularly of the Mammalia",Proc. Zool. Soc. Lond.(1880): 649–62].

letters.title: To P. L. Sclater   29 December 1880
letters.summary: Asks PLS to sign the memorial for a pension for Wallace.

letters.title: ToNature   [before 30 December 1880]
letters.summary: Quotes an extract from a letter from Mr Sanderson of Chislehurst on the disappearance of black or spotted sheep from Australian flocks when the coloured sheep ceased to be of use to man.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   30 December 1880
letters.summary: Statement of money transactions with James Torbitt and record of year’s success enclosed. Torbitt desires him to return £90. He is doubtful of being able to continue this spring.

letters.title: From J. S. B. Sanderson   31 December 1880
letters.summary:
Signs a certificate sent to him by CD [see12954].

Sends CD a ticket to his lecture on 25 February, in which he will propose that the mode by which the excitable parts of plants influence other parts at a distance is essentially the same as in the excitable structure of animals, contrary to the views of Hermann Munk and Julius Sachs.

Interested in chapters 6 and 7 ofMovement in plants.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   31 December [1880]
letters.summary: Sends diagrams [missing] showing worm action at two sites.

letters.title: From Alexander Kielland 31 December 1880
letters.summary: Discusses Chinese lions at Fontainebleau; considers their appearance may indicate an ancient knowledge of some sort of evolutionary connection between lions and toads.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   [1881–2?]
letters.summary: Will GHD ask Lord R[ayleigh] whether "gas-men in testing light, exclude the diffused light".

letters.title: To Julius Lippert   [1881]
letters.summary: Thanks JL for copy ofDie Religionen[1881].

letters.title: To Alexander Agassiz   1 January 1881
letters.summary:
Thanks AA for letter on coral reefs. "I used to think … that areas of elevation and of subsidence must – as a general rule be separated by a single great line of fissure, or rather of several".

Suggests that AA urge again his views on reappearance of old characters.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin 1 January [1881]
letters.summary: Discusses possible investments.

letters.title: To V. O. Kovalevsky   1 and 6 January 1881
letters.summary:
Thanks VOK for the Russian tea.

Rejoices at his prosperity and appointment at Moscow [Associate Professor, Moscow University, 1880–3].

letters.title: To Post Office Savings Bank   1 January [1881]
letters.summary: Asks to have some funds of the Down Friendly Society transferred.

letters.title: To James Torbitt   1 January 1881
letters.summary: T. H. Farrer and James Caird express great interest in JT’s report. Have instructed CD to hold £90 for use by JT in spring. Caird asks that potatoes be sent to his gardener for trials.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   1 January 1881
letters.summary: ARW’s view of migration of plants from mountain to mountain gains support from case described inNature[23 (1880): 125–6] by J. G. Baker. Identical species of alpine plants found in African mountains and Madagascar.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   2 January [1881]
letters.summary:
Concerning subscriptions raised for Torbitt’s experiments on potato disease.

Comments on CD’s latest book [Insectivorous plants].

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   2 January 1881
letters.summary:
Encloses reply to Butler [Kosmos8 (1881): 321–2]. Has also written a reply intended for English reader. Will have it translated forPopular Science Reviewif CD thinks suitable.

Report of Jäger accident was an error.

Kosmoshas been purchased by Eduard Koch in Stuttgart and will continue as in the past.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   2 January 1881
letters.summary: On land migration of plants. The case inNatureis striking but CD doubts that seeds of plants could be blown from mountains of Abyssinia to mountains of Madagascar.

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   3 January 1881
letters.summary: Alarm over Wallace’s memorial; asks HWB if he has received it and forwarded it to Hooker. Wanted to get it to Gladstone before Parliament met.

letters.title: From James Caird   3 January 1881
letters.summary: JC and Farrer are impressed with Torbitt’s papers. Will continue financial support.

letters.title: To CD’s Children   3 January 1881
letters.deprecated: Elizabeth (Bessy) (Lizzy) DarwinFrancis DarwinGeorge Howard DarwinHorace DarwinLeonard DarwinWilliam Erasmus DarwinHenrietta Emma DarwinHenrietta Emma Litchfield
letters.recipient: Elizabeth (Bessy) (Lizzy) DarwinFrancis DarwinGeorge Howard DarwinHorace DarwinLeonard DarwinWilliam Erasmus DarwinHenrietta Emma DarwinHenrietta Emma Litchfield
letters.summary: About the distribution of [surplus income] funds among the children.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   3 January [1881]
letters.summary:
Thanks WED for some earthworm observations.

Discusses investments.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   3 January 1881
letters.summary:
Returns [Wallace] memorial.

Hopes to be able to send classification paper soon. [See12935.]

letters.title: To W. E. Gladstone   [before 4 January 1881]
letters.summary: Covering letter to enclose a memorial [petitioning for a civil list pension for Wallace].

letters.title: To A. B. Buckley   4 January 1881
letters.summary: Memorial for Wallace pension dispatched to W. E. Gladstone.

letters.title: To Henrietta Litchfield   4 January 1881
letters.summary: Seeks R. B. Litchfield’s advice about publishing a translation of a letter and article by E. Krause [answering Samuel Butler’sUnconscious memory].

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   4 January [1881]
letters.summary: CD is pleased with EK’s account inKosmos[8 (1880–1): 321–2] of the Buffon and Coleridge passage [cited by Samuel Butler, see12939,12969]. Would like a translation published in England, but Butler seeks notoriety and would make unscrupulous use of it. Will ask advice. Thinks EK’s letter toPopular Science Monthly, just received, an excellent reply to Butler.

letters.title: From Gottlieb Haberlandt   5 January 1881
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for a second copy ofMovement in plants. His letter acknowledging the first must have gone astray. Marvels at the number of interesting observations and is honoured by CD’s mention of his work.

In recent years GH has been applying CD’s principles to the histologico-anatomical structure of plant organs. He will send CD the papers.

letters.title: From R. B. & H. E. Litchfield   5 January [1881]
letters.deprecated: Richard Buckley LitchfieldHenrietta Emma DarwinHenrietta Emma Litchfield
letters.sender: Richard Buckley LitchfieldHenrietta Emma DarwinHenrietta Emma Litchfield
letters.summary: The Litchfields and George Darwin think care should be taken that E. Krause’s reply to S. Butler’sUnconscious memorydoes not appear to be instigated by CD. Suggest it be sent toPopular Science Review, notAthenæum.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin 6 January 1881
letters.summary: Passes on legal advice.

letters.title: From W. E. Gladstone   6 January 1881
letters.summary: He will recommend a pension of £200 a year for Wallace.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   6 January 1881
letters.summary: Letter of introduction for V. O. Kovalevsky.

letters.title: To H. W. Bates   7 January 1881
letters.summary: Gladstone has recommended yearly pension of £200 for Wallace.

letters.title: To A. B. Buckley   7 January [1881]
letters.summary: Good news from Gladstone [concerning pension for Wallace]. Duke of Argyll’s private note greatly influenced Gladstone.

letters.title: To G. D. Campbell, eighth duke of Argyll [7 January 1881?]
letters.deprecated: George Douglas Campbell, 8th duke of Argyll
letters.recipient: George Douglas Campbell, 8th duke of Argyll
letters.summary: Has heard that Gladstone will recommend A. R. [Wallace] for a pension. Thanks the Duke for having written to Gladstone on the matter.

letters.title: To W. E. Gladstone   7 January 1881
letters.summary: CD expresses his great pleasure at WEG’s letter informing him that Wallace has been granted a pension.

letters.title: To É. M. Heckel   7 January [1881]
letters.summary: Sends photograph.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   7 January 1881
letters.summary:
Success of the memorial for Wallace. Sends letter from Gladstone.

Congratulates THH on appointment as Inspector of Fisheries.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   7 January 1881
letters.summary: Informs ARW of favourable reception by Gladstone of memorial respecting ARW’s services to science, and the establishment of a pension for him.

letters.title: To ?   7 January 1881
letters.summary: CD thanks correspondent for her "very elegant work" – a book on nature.

letters.title: From Walter Raleigh Browne   [after 7] January 1881
letters.summary: Announces the resolution passed by the Archbishop of Canterbury’s conference of 7 Jan 1881.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   8 January 1881
letters.summary:
Congratulates CD on success of Wallace memorial.

Butler has attacked again.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause 8 January 1881
letters.summary: CD may choose where to publish EK’s reply to Butler. Would preferAthenæum. Thinks it better that CD not reply himself.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   8 January 1881
letters.summary: Report on the progress of his experiments with potatoes; some varieties spoilt by an apparently hereditary disease.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   8 January 1881
letters.summary: Appreciation of CD’s efforts in recommending him for pension. Asks about proprieties of thanking Gladstone and the signers of the memorial.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   9 January 1881
letters.summary:
Thanks for CD’s offer of assistance after flood damage.

Comments onMovement in plants. Discusses sleep movements and paraheliotropism ofMarantaand other plants.

Describes the fertilisation of figs by Hymenoptera.

letters.title: From T. L. Brunton   10 January 1881
letters.summary: Sends proofs of lectures he intends to reprint as a book [The Bible and science(1881)]; asks CD if he would check one for errors.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   10 January 1881
letters.summary:
All his advisers agree that CD ought not to take notice of Butler’s attack.

F. M. Balfour has offered to translate EK’s reply to Butler and to send it toNature. [The letter was published inNature23 (1881): 288.]

letters.title: From Montague Lubbock   10 January 1881
letters.summary: Wants a letter of introduction to Joseph Fayrer.

letters.title: To Lawrence Ruck   10 January 1881
letters.summary: Asks whether sheep and cattle grazing on a steep slope move across the slope horizontally or ascend it.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   10 January 1881
letters.summary: On the proprieties of thanking Gladstone and the signers of the memorial.

letters.title: To Joseph Fayrer   [after 10 January 1881]
letters.summary: Letter of introduction for Montagu Lubbock.

letters.title: From A. B. Buckley   11 January 1881
letters.summary:
Thanks for news about Wallace memorial; excellent names on it give hope of success.

Mentions Alfred Haddon, an acquaintance of hers who might call on CD.

letters.title: To Leslie Stephen   11 January 1881
letters.summary: Discusses allegation [aboutErasmus Darwin] made by Samuel Butler. Will value LS’s verdict highly.

letters.title: To F. M. Balfour   12 January 1881
letters.summary: Asks FMB to translate letter from Ernst Krause [answering criticisms by Samuel Butler] and to send it toNature[ "Unconscious memory – Mr Samuel Butler" 23 (1881): 288].

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   12 January 1881
letters.summary: Has written to Balfour concerning the Butler affair.

letters.title: From Lawrence Ruck   12 January [1881]
letters.summary: Discusses the grazing habits of sheep and cattle on steep hillsides.

letters.title: From Leslie Stephen   12 January [1881]
letters.summary: Advises CD to "take no notice of Butler whatever" and gives his reasons.

letters.title: From F. M. Balfour   13 January [1881]
letters.summary: Will gladly translate Krause’s letter forNature; denounces Butler’s book attacking CD.

letters.title: From A. B. Buckley   13 January 1881
letters.summary: Congratulates CD on success of memorial; agrees he should be the one to tell Wallace.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin 13 January [1881]
letters.summary: He is buying a portable fire engine, and suggests one is purchased for Down. Wishes to join the Geological Society of London. Is eager to hear Leslie Stephen’s opinion.

letters.title: To Leslie Stephen   13 January 1881
letters.summary: Thanks LS for his advice and his kind note. When CD thinks how he has been treated he will say to himself "so good a judge as Leslie Stephen thinks nothing of the accusation".

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   14 January [1881]
letters.summary:
Discusses earthworm activity

and animal grazing on slopes.

letters.title: From Leslie Stephen   14 January 1881
letters.summary: Thanks CD for the offer of one of his books [Erasmus Darwin] which he gratefully accepts.

letters.title: To William Ogle   17 January 1881
letters.summary: Thanks WO for copying and translating [unspecified] passages. CD knew nothing about them, but doubts they are of real use. Passage about summer solstice may indicate something new.

letters.title: From Alphonse de Candolle   18 January [1881]
letters.summary:
Thanks forMovement in plants. Praises the terms CD introduces, but criticises CD’s use of the teleological word "purpose".

Outlines his efforts to study the inheritance of characters in his family. F. Galton overemphasises the inheritance of good qualities.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   18 January 1881
letters.summary: Asks THF to obtain sample of chalk immediately below vegetable mould at Abinger.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   20 January [1881]
letters.summary:
[Ernst Krause’s] letter toNature["Unconscious memory – Mr Samuel Butler", 23 (1881): 288] has been dispatched.

Gladstone has dated Wallace’s pension from last July, "which is splendid".

letters.title: From F. J. Myers   20 January 1881
letters.summary: Gives an account of the Syracuse Botanical Club and its activities.

letters.title: To [Mr Seymours]   20 January 1881
letters.summary: Sends address of A. R. Wallace. Comments on Wallace’s pension.

letters.title: To J. H. C. Fabre   21 January 1881
