letters.summary: Discusses JHF’s investigations of animals’ sense of direction. Suggests experiment involving magnetism.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   22 January 1881
letters.summary: Asks THH to sign a certificate of nomination to Geological Society for his son William, if an interest in geology is still enough to qualify for election.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [23? January 1881]
letters.summary: Thanks CD for writing for papers to enter Geological Society. Will return Leslie Stephen’s letter. Has had a severe frost. Emma’s puppy died.

letters.title: To Alphonse de Candolle   24 January 1881
letters.summary:
Thanks AdeC for interesting letter. CD has been annoyed by the multitude of new terms lately invented in all branches of biology in Germany. What AdeC says about the word "purpose" made CD vow not to use it again, but it is difficult to cure oneself of a vicious habit and difficult to avoid for anyone who tries to make out the use of a structure.

Francis will write about the diagram [see13642].

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   24 January 1881
letters.summary:
Has signed William Darwin’s certificate of nomination to Geological Society.

Gives details of his Fisheries appointment.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   24 January [1881]
letters.summary: Discusses possible case of inherited memory involvingPompilus. Cites similar example of electric eel.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   24 January 1881
letters.summary: Describes difficulty of obtaining pigs for experiment.

letters.title: To W. S. Dallas   25 January 1881
letters.summary: Asks WSD to suspend the enclosed certificate.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   25 January 1881
letters.summary:
Writes of WED’s certificate for the Geological Society

and discusses various instances of earthworm activity.

letters.title: From Asa Gray   27 January 1881
letters.summary:
Apologises for his silence when Francis Darwin’s paper was read at the Linnean Society.

AG’s review ofMovement in plants[Nation32 (1881): 17–18].

letters.title: To F. M. Balfour   28 January 1881
letters.summary: Thanks FMB for translation of Ernst Krause’s letter forNature.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   28 January 1881
letters.summary:
Has read with interest GJR’s review [of Samuel Butler,Unconscious memory(1880)] inNature[23 (1880–1): 285–7]. Heroic of GJR to call down [Butler’s] revenge on his own head. Ernst Krause’s letter [Nature23 (1880–1): 288] very good.

As magistrate, CD must enforce rules regarding infection in pigs.

letters.title: To Asa Gray   29 January 1881
letters.summary: Thanks for AG’s reviews [ofMovement in plants] in theJournalandNation[Am. J. Sci.3d ser. 21 (1881): 245–9 andNation32 (1881): 17–18], especially for AG’s comment about Frank Darwin.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   29 January 1881
letters.summary:
Sends copy ofNaturein which EK’s letter, translated by Balfour, is printed. Thanks him. Now feels easy.

G. J. Romanes’ language in his review of Butler’s book [Unconscious memory] is perhaps too strong. Butler’s vanity is a "real psychological curiosity".

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   29 January 1881
letters.summary: Further information about the pension with particular thanks to CD for his role.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin 30 January [1881]
letters.summary: Discusses his election to the Geological Society, worm researches, GHD’s travels, investments,G J Romanes on Samuel Butler, the snow, politics.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   31 January [1881]
letters.summary:
Discusses investments,

earthworms,

and an article by Romanes [see13029].

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [February–March 1881?]
letters.summary:
Discusses some business matters

and E. A. Darwin’s health.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin 3 February [1881]
letters.summary: Worm observations.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin 4 February 1881
letters.summary: Discusses possible investments.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   4 February [1881]
letters.summary: Discusses earthworms and their ability to perceive narrowest points of leaves to draw them into their burrows.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   5 February [1881]
letters.summary:
Discusses investments.

The action of worms when drawing leaves into their burrows.

letters.title: To J. H. Gilbert   5 February 1881
letters.summary: Asks whether vegetable mould has an acid reaction. The contents of intestines of earthworms and castings are acid, which leads him to inquire about mould.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   6 February 1881
letters.summary: Reports his observations on numbers ofRhododendronleaves found buried [by earthworms].

letters.title: To C. G. Semper   6 February 1881
letters.summary:
Comments on CGS’sThe natural conditions of existence[1881] and on views of Moritz Wagner on geographical distribution.

Discusses cause of variability.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   7 February 1881
letters.summary: Butler’s reply to EK is a renewed attack on CD. Urges EK not to answer it. His last letter contains everything necessary. Asks EK for dates of CD’s letter asking EK’s permission to publish a translation of his article [on Erasmus Darwin] and of the letter in which he told EK that Butler’s book had been advertised.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   7 February 1881
letters.summary:
Describes polymorphism in the pistil ofLagerstroemia, which CD spoke of as doubtful inForms of flowers.

Also reports on dimorphism in Pontederiacea (Heteranthera reniformis).

Has received from Paul Mayer an interesting paper on metamorphosis inPalaemonetes varians, which is also being studied by J. E. V. Boas in Denmark. Shows differences between larval development in Danish forms and those found in southern Italy.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   8 February [1881]
letters.summary:
Thanks WED for sending leaves and making observations on how earthworms drag them into their burrows.

Doubts justice of fierce review against J. Geikie’s book [Prehistoric Europe(1881)] inNature[by W. B. Dawkins, 23 (1881): 309–10], but if reindeer and hippopotamus have really been found in close contact in same bed – "it tells horribly against interglacial periods".

letters.title: To [W. W. Baxter]   9 February 1881
letters.summary: Orders vaseline and pomatum – the latter to put on his beard, which in dry weather feels uncomfortably harsh.

letters.title: To R. D. Fitzgerald   9 February 1881
letters.summary: Thanks for pt 6 of [Australian orchids].

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   9 February 1881
letters.summary:
Sends birthday wishes.

Comments onMovement in plants.

SendsSystem der Ascrapeden[1880].

Describes work onChallengerMedusae.

Comments on success of CD’s theory.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   9 February 1881
letters.summary: Asks EH to call on Zeiss and to help arrange for microscope for Francis Darwin.

letters.title: From Anthony Rich   9 February 1881.
letters.summary:
Contemptuous of Samuel Butler.

Has read that Huxley will be Inspector of Fisheries.

When CD visits in spring, he will acquaint him with legalities of Worthing house.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   10 February 1881
letters.summary:
Birthday greetings.

Thinks it best not to reply further to Butler. Has read G. J. Romanes’ article with great pleasure. Romanes is right to ridicule Butler. Quotes passages about Butler from CD letters. Has received letter from F. M. Balfour urging him not to reply to Butler.

letters.title: From Josef Popper   11 February 1881
letters.summary:
Interested in theory of flight machines. Thinks it may be possible to fly by hitching man to large birds. What does CD think?

Recalls gift of book sent to CD.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   11 February 1881
letters.summary: Thanks GJR for his second letter replying to Butler [Nature23 (1880–1): 335–6].

letters.title: To T. R. R. Stebbing   11 February 1881
letters.summary: Thanks him for his letter inNature[23 (1880–1): 336, concerning Samuel Butler’sUnconscious Memory]. Explains how revision in Krause’s part [ofErasmus Darwin] and the subsequent misunderstanding came about.

letters.title: To L. C. J. G. de Saporta   13 February 1881
letters.deprecated: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.recipient: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.summary: Thanks for work sent by GdeS and A. F. Marion [L’évolution du règne végétal1 (1881)]. CD greatly pleased at boldness with which GdeS expresses his belief in evolution. Some of GdeS’s countrymen have been "a little timid" on this head.

letters.title: From T. L. Brunton   14 February 1881
letters.summary: Forwards the preface to his book [see12999] and comments on the effect of the Bible on science.

letters.title: To Josef Popper   15 February 1881
letters.summary: Cannot help JP [with bird-powered flying machine].

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin 16 February 1881
letters.summary: Brokers have purchased Leeds Corporation Stock.

letters.title: To Grant Allen   17 February 1881
letters.summary: Thanks forEvolutionist at large[1881]. Envies GA’s power of writing. Some statements are too bold, but several of the views are new to CD and seem "extremely probable".

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin 18 February 1881
letters.summary: Discusses the possible rebuilding of a pair of cottages on CD’s farm at Beesby, Lincolnshire.

letters.title: From Anton Dohrn   18 February 1881
letters.summary:
Belated birthday greetings

and reminiscences of CD’s help to the Station, which continues to prosper. A recent innovation is the establishment of theZoologische Jahresberichtedited by J. V. Carus.

letters.title: From Grant Allen   19 February [1881]
letters.summary:
Thanks for compliments onEvolutionist at large.

Reports on his improving health.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   19 February [1881]
letters.summary:
Uncle Erasmus is very ill.

Thanks WED for his trouble about the cottages.

He has signed the note to Higgins.

CD has used WED’sRhododendroncase inEarthworms[p. 69].

Is using paper triangles in experiments on intelligence of worms.

letters.title: To ?   [20 February 1881]
letters.summary: Queries account for book "Fauna Neapol. II"

letters.title: To Henry Edwards, Jr   21 February 1881
letters.summary: Acknowledges with thanks the honour conferred by the Entomological Club of New York in electing CD an honorary member.

letters.title: To T. M. Hocken, President of the Otago Institute 21 February 1881
letters.summary: Thanks for honour conferred upon him by the Otago Institute.

letters.title: To Anton Dohrn   22 February 1881
letters.summary:
AD exaggerates what CD has done for science.

On theZoological Yearbook, CD thinks it would be an excellent plan to give an account of zoological publications from all countries in a single work.

letters.title: From J. H. Gilbert   22 February 1881
letters.summary: The laboratory has scarcely any experimental evidence on acidity of humus soil and earthworm excreta. Refers CD to some sources of information.

letters.title: ToNature   22 February [1881]
letters.summary: Summarises the "remarkable facts about the movements of plants" in Fritz Müller’s letter of January [12996]. CD comments that Müller’s observations support the conclusion that he and Francis Darwin arrived at – that leaves go to sleep to escape the full effects of radiation.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   23 February 1881
letters.summary: CD interested by FM’s facts on movement of plants; has sent some toNature["Movement of leaves",Collected papers2: 228–9]. Greatly admires FM’s work. Suggests an experiment to investigate movement inPhyllanthus.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   24 February 1881
letters.summary:
The debt of plant geography to voyages may be JDH’s topic at BAAS meeting [at Swansea].

Photographs from New Zealand forwarded.

letters.title: To J. H. Gilbert   25 February 1881
letters.summary:
Discusses acidity of earthworm castings. JHG’s reply will make him more cautious.

Would like to see W. A. Detmer’s paper [Landwirtsch. Versuchs-Stat.14 (1871): 248–300] and S. W. Johnson’s work [How crops feed].

Comments on food value of white and brown bread.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   26 [February 1881]
letters.summary: Island lifecontinues to stimulate: Wallace ignores effects of glaciers on alpine flora and generally exaggerates those of débâcles and wind dispersal. CD encourages JDH to prepare a geographical address including history of geographical distribution.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   27[–8] February [1881]
letters.summary:
Describes lecture at Royal Institution by J. S. Burdon Sanderson on movement of plants and animals; JSBS’s preliminary part was so long that he never got to the plants.

Comments on the triumph of the ladies in the voting at Cambridge.

Mentions F. Galton’s visit to Down, a call on the Huxleys, and a visit with the Duke of Argyll.

Tells a story about the absent-mindedness of Burdon Sanderson.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   28 February 1881
letters.summary: In his last letter FM told CD about four flowers ofLagerstroemiathat he had fertilised with the yellow pollen of another variety or species and which had subsequently fallen off. He has now repeated the experiment using the yellow pollen of a different variety and successfully produced good fruit as large as that fertilised with green pollen.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes| March 1881
letters.summary: Intends experiment to see if cats released in country can find their way back.

letters.title: From ?   [March 1881]
letters.summary: Notes on the thickness of mould on the slope of the inland side of Beachy Head.

letters.title: From Anthony Rich   1 March 1881
letters.summary: AR plans, when he dies, to leave sea-side house at Worthing to Huxley.

letters.title: From Anthony Rich   4 March 1881
letters.summary: Pleased that Huxley is likely to accept gift of AR’s house.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   5 March 1881
letters.summary: CD tells how it came about that Anthony Rich bequeathed his house and land to THH.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   6 March 1881
letters.summary: Astonished by Rich’s act. Has written to him.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   7 March 1881
letters.summary: Reports observations of worms for CD’s use.

letters.title: From J. H. Gilbert   7 March 1881
letters.summary: Sends some books.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   7 March [1881]
letters.summary: Comments on the meaning of his definition of the term, "animal intelligence". Encloses further discussion from his forthcoming book [Earthworms].

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   7 March 1881
letters.summary: Responds to MS ofEarthworms. An objective but arbitrary test of intelligence in animals is the ability to learn from experience. Earthworms fall on the border of intelligence. They could justly be called intelligent if they could learn by experience to manipulate some unknown, exotic leaf. CD should make clear that intelligence does not imply self-consciousness.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   8 March [1881]
letters.summary:
Discusses dead earthworms on surface of ground after rainfall.

Describes experiments involving sensitivity of earthworms to light and how it reflects on their intelligence.

letters.title: From J. W. Jeudwine   8 March [1881]
letters.summary: Requests a subscription for Shrewsbury School.

letters.title: From Frank Norgate   [8 March 1881]
letters.summary: Sends a number of facts for CD’s attention, including cases of water-beetles and newts in his aquarium having a foot caught by small bivalves. This might explain migration of bivalves.

letters.title: From Anthony Rich   8 March 1881
letters.summary:
Huxley has written to accept gift of Rich’s house.

Approves of Lord Derby’s politics.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   9 March [1881]
letters.summary: Comments on GJR’s view of animal consciousness. Mentions experiment on learning among worms.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   10 March 1881
letters.summary: Sends CD some samples of recent produce. Is "pretty well disgusted by the apathy and stupidity" he has encountered whilst trying to arouse interest and support for his work.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   12 March 1881
letters.summary: Will proof-read his preface to Weismann’sStudien.

letters.title: From H. L. F. de Saussure   14 March 1881
letters.summary: Sends boxes of Lake Geneva pebbles that CD requested.

letters.title: From H. M. Wallis   14 March 1881
letters.summary: Reports some observations on the growth of hair on his baby son’s ears.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   [before 15 March 1881]
letters.summary: Cannot write so is using Lily as secretary. Proud to be member of Geological Society. Sends observations of rhododendron leaves. Could not find piece of ploughed land. Has proves Josiah Wedgwood III’s death in North Eastern Railway Company. Taking care because head hurts.

letters.title: To J. H. Gilbert   15 March 1881
letters.summary: Returns the two books JHG had lent him. "I can plainly see I had better say nothing about the acidity of common mould."

letters.title: To James Torbitt   15 March 1881
letters.summary: Obliged for potatoes. Has instructed that they be planted and labelled.

letters.title: From Charles Layton   17 March 1881
letters.summary: Encloses statement of U. S. sales of CD’s works to 1 Feb 1881 and sends cheque for balance due to CD.

letters.title: To [Henri de Saussure]   17 March 1881
letters.summary:
Thanks HdS for pebbles of Roman bricks. When he goes over MS [Earthworms] again, he will compare smoother ones with those having undergone attrition in gizzards of worms.

Has received book [QQQQ] sent by HdS.

Also sends photograph taken by Leonard Darwin of CD.

Requests photograph of HdS to add to his collection.

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   18 March 1881
letters.summary: Reports the observations of Thomas Bridges on the Fuegian natives. Discusses especially the languages of the area.

letters.title: From E. J. Loomis   [19 March 1881]
letters.summary: Describes light-stimulated movement in fronds of the fernAsplenium.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   20 March 1881
letters.summary: FM’s view on meaning of two-coloured stamens in many flowers; CD has been looking through his old notes on dimorphism for supporting evidence. Intends to send extract of FM’s letter toNatureor to Linnean Society.

letters.title: To B. J. Sulivan   20 March 1881
letters.summary: Thanks for BJS’s account of the Fuegians. CD would have predicted that "not all the missionaries in the world could have done what has been done".

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   21 March [1881]
letters.summary: Wants plants with two sets of anthers of different colours. Fritz Müller letter [13041a] has made him wish to renew experiments and observations carried out 20 years ago.

letters.title: To H. M. Wallis   22 March 1881
letters.summary: Comments on HMW’s discovery concerning growth of hair on human ears. Asks permission to publish fact.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   23 March 1881
letters.summary:
Thanks JVC for corrections ofMovement in plants. Sends a clarifying sentence.

Earthwormsnearly done – "a small book of little moment".

Reports his health is better than it was, "but I have little strength & feel very old".

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   24 March 1881
letters.summary:
Suggests transplanting plant ovaries to test Pangenesis.

None of the cats released in experiment found its way back.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   26 March 1881
letters.summary: Discusses difficulties involved in plant experiment designed to test Pangenesis.

letters.title: From H. M. Wallis   27 March 1881
letters.summary:
Is glad CD finds his observations on hair growth on ears new and interesting.

Mentions instances in which young birds possess abilities lacking in the adult.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   29 March 1881
letters.summary: Has received WBT’s fine work [Edward Blyth,The natural history of the cranes, enlarged and reprinted by WBT (1881)].

letters.title: To E. B. Tylor   29 March 1881
letters.summary: Thanks EBT for gift ofAnthropology[1881].

letters.title: To H. M. Wallis   31 March 1881
letters.summary:
Encourages HMW’s study of growth of hair on ears. Recommends he publish findings inNature.

Comments on facts about goatsucker and dorkings.

letters.title: To the New York Entomological Club   [after March 1881]
letters.summary: Wishes the society and its publications every success.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin [April 1881]
letters.summary: Reports splendid cases of "paraheliotropism" which he now believes is one of the commonest movements of plants.

letters.title: From Jules Rouquette de St Geniez   April 1881
letters.summary: Dedication of his essay in the form of a letter to CD.

letters.title: From Marie McElroy   1 April 1881
letters.summary: Asks whether blue eyes are peculiar to the human species.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   1 April 1881
letters.summary: WantsMonochaetumflowers for examination as he has forgotten the structure and cannot publish until he has repeated his observations and experiments.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   3 April [1881]
letters.summary: Thanks forMonochaetumflowers; his old notes have now become intelligible.

letters.title: To E. J. Loomis   4 April 1881
letters.summary: CD is familiar with EJL’s work [onAspleniummovements]; findsAspleniuman unusual case.

letters.title: From Frithiof Holmgren   7 April 1881
letters.summary: Swedish anti-vivisectionists are claiming CD is opposed to animal experiments; Holmgren wishes CD to state his position.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   9 April 1881
letters.summary: About Francis Darwin’s application for election to [Royal] Society.

letters.title: To Robert Cooke   10 April 1881
letters.summary: Asks for quick decision on publication [ofEarthworms]. Does not care whether it is published on commission or on usual terms, but wants it published in a hurry. Cannot guess at sales.

letters.title: From Gaston de Saporta   10 April 1881
letters.deprecated: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.sender: Louis Charles Joseph Gaston (Gaston) de Saporta, comte de
letters.summary: Sends GdeS and A. F. Marion,L’évolution du règne végétal. Les cryptogames[1881].

letters.title: From Robert Cooke   11 April 1881
letters.summary: Murray’s will be happy to publish [Earthworms] on usual terms of two-thirds profits.

letters.title: To Robert Cooke   12 April 1881
letters.summary:
Agrees that new book [Earthworms] be published on old terms. Hopes it will not fail.

CD is curious to read an essay on evolution by a Hindu, which is being sent to Murray from India.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   12 April 1881
letters.summary:
Earthworm book with printer.

Has sent FM’s observations on paraheliotropism toNature["Movement of leaves",Collected papers2: 228–9].

Plants with differently coloured anthers.

Intends gathering together his notes on "bloom".

letters.title: To Frithiof Holmgren   [14] April 1881
letters.summary: CD gives his opinion on vivisection with the understanding that the whole letter will be published. Worked for Act of Parliament, but disapproves of the one passed. CD convinced English physiologists do not perform cruel experiments.

letters.title: ToNature   14 April [1881]
letters.summary: Summarises a letter from Fritz Müller [missing] giving details of leaf movement inMucuna,Desmodium, andBauhinia. CD is especially interested in the paraheliotropic movements, which appear to be as common as sleep movements.

letters.title: From A. S. Wilson   14 April 1881
letters.summary:
Sends his last report on Russian wheat varieties [Gard. Chron.n.s. 15 (1881): 430–2].

Considers which part of grass embryo is the cotyledon.

letters.title: From Alphonse Engelhardt   15 April [1881]
letters.summary: A student and an admirer of CD wishes to have a few lines from him.

letters.title: From Alexander Agassiz   16 April 1881
letters.summary: Is mapping coral distribution on the Tortugas reef. His observations on the Florida peninsula suggest that it was built up from the debris of animal remains and was not elevated.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   16 April [1881?]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Suggests that the pappus of Compositae, when lying on ground, may absorb water which may function in seed germination.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   16 April 1881
letters.summary:
Discusses concept of intelligence in hisEarthwormsmanuscript.

Remarks on GJR’s work on echinoderms.

Comments on Wilhelm Roux [Der Kampf der Theile im Organismus(1881)].

Discusses animal instincts, citing Fabre’s description of sand-wasps.

letters.title: To A. S. Wilson   16 April 1881
letters.summary:
Obliged for extract fromGardeners’ Chronicleabout Russian wheat. "It is a capital instance of one var. gradually beating out another."

Cannot remember where he put G. Henslow’s note [on the cotyledon of grass embryos].

letters.title: From E. L. Zeuschner   16 April 1881
letters.summary: Sends pamphlet showing that magnetism is the fundamental element by which all is created and maintained.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   17 April 1881
letters.summary:
Looks forward to reading CD’sEarthworms.

Agrees that habits of sand-wasp are determined by natural selection.

Experiment of exposing plants to flashing light gives uncertain result.

letters.title: From K. S. Barnes   18 April 1881
letters.deprecated: K. S BarnesSecretary, Syracuse Bot. Club
letters.sender: K. S BarnesSecretary, Syracuse Bot. Club
letters.summary: Announces CD’s election as an Honorary Corresponding Member of the Club.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   18 April 1881
letters.summary:
Discusses GJR’s experiments on heliotropism in plants; views of Philippe van Tieghem and Julius von Wiesner. Describes his own experiments.

Mentions his letter on vivisection [to Frithiof Holmgren, see13115] in theTimes[18 Apr 1881].

letters.title: From H. B. Taylor   18 April 1881
letters.summary: Sends "Ginger Beer Plant", a seed that assists the fermentation of ginger beer. [Also enclosed are instructions for making ginger beer dated, presumably erroneously, 18 Oct 1881.]

letters.title: From W. von Voigts-Rhetz   [after 18 April 1881]
letters.summary: On vivisection. Has read CD’s letter to Frithiof Holmgren and answers the points raised in it.

letters.title: From G. R. Jesse   19 April 1881
letters.deprecated: George Richard Jessehonorary secretary of Soc. Abolition Vivisection
letters.sender: George Richard Jessehonorary secretary of Soc. Abolition Vivisection
letters.summary: Discusses vivisection and contradicts CD’s defence of English physiologists.

letters.title: From J. D. Spain   19 April 1881
letters.summary: Requests that CD lecture on evolution in Lichfield.

letters.title: To G. R. Jesse   21 April 1881
letters.summary: Vivisection; CD’s exchange with Holmgren.

letters.title: To The Editor ofThe Times   21 April 1881
letters.summary: Replies to F. P. Cobbe’s letter [Times19 Apr 1881] accusing CD of having misinformed his Swedish correspondent about the findings of the Royal Commission on vivisection.

letters.title: To W. R. Thiselton-Dyer   21 April 1881
letters.summary:
WantsTrifoliumseed.

Has been rereading WTT-D’s letters on "bloom".

letters.title: From G. R. Jesse   22 April 1881
letters.deprecated: George Richard Jessehonorary secretary of Soc. Abolition Vivisection
letters.sender: George Richard Jessehonorary secretary of Soc. Abolition Vivisection
letters.summary: Asks if he may publish CD’s reply to his previous letter.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   22 April [1881]
letters.summary:
Only more sensitive seedlings respond to flashing light.

CD’s letter toTimes["On vivisection", 22 Apr 1881] in every way admirable.

GJR to be Zoological Secretary of Linnean Society.

Has decided on arrangement of material for his booksAnimal intelligence[1882]

andMental evolution in animals[1883].

letters.title: To G. R. Jesse   23 April 1881
letters.summary: CD will not permit publication of his previous letter on vivisection.

letters.title: To J. D. Spain   23 April 1881
letters.summary: Cannot give lecture.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [24 April or 1 May 1881]
letters.summary: Sends observations of wormcasts at Malvern. Describes stay at Abinger.

letters.title: From I. P. Bishop   24 April 1881
letters.summary:
Gives case of the inheritance of a tendency to turn grey at a particular age,

and, from his own family, details of the inheritance of a thumb deformity that apparently originated with his grandfather.

letters.title: From G. R. Jesse   25 April 1881
letters.deprecated: George Richard Jessehonorary secretary of Soc. Abolition Vivisection
letters.sender: George Richard Jessehonorary secretary of Soc. Abolition Vivisection
letters.summary: Regrets CD will not allow publication of his letter.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   25 April 1881
letters.summary: Comments on GJR’s letter in theTimes[25 Apr 1881] concerning vivisection. Mentions activity of anti-vivisectionists, G. R. Jesse and F. P. Cobbe.

letters.title: From W. E. Gladstone   30 April 1881
letters.summary: CD is invited to allow his name to be suggested for the vacancy in the Trust of the British Museum caused by the death of Lord Beaconsfield. [See13142.]

letters.title: To Eduard Koch   30 April 1881
letters.summary:
Thanks for German translation ofMovement in plants.

GladKosmosis to be continued [by Schweizerbart].

letters.title: To C. E. Norton   30 April 1881
letters.summary: Sends some anecdotal material about Benjamin Franklin, whom his father knew while studying medicine in Paris.

letters.title: To W. E. Gladstone   2 May 1881
letters.summary: CD declines an invitation to be a trustee [of British Museum] because his strength is insufficient to permit regular attendance at meetings.

letters.title: From the Société royale de Botanique de Belgique 2 May 1881
letters.deprecated: Société royale de Botanique de Belgique
letters.sender: Société royale de Botanique de Belgique
letters.summary: CD made an associate member of the Royal Belgian Botanical Society.

letters.title: From Spencer Fullerton Baird   3 May 1881
letters.summary: Introduces Capt. George Montague Wheeler of the U. S. Engineers, who has charge of the government expedition west of the 100th meridian.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   4 May [1881]
letters.summary:
Discusses his investments.

P.S. on earthworms.

letters.title: To Alexander Agassiz   5 May 1881
letters.summary:
Responds to comments on geology of Florida.

Discusses coral reefs and paper by John Murray ["On the structure and origin of coral reefs and islands",Proc. R. Soc. Edinburgh10 (1880): 505–18].

Comments on AA’s paper ["Paleontological and embryological development",Proc. Am. Assoc. Adv. Sci.29 (1880): 389–414].

letters.title: To R. G. Whiteman   5 May 1881
letters.summary: Passage in first edition ofOrigin, [p. 184] on bears rendered larger and more aquatic by selection was omitted from subsequent editions on advice of Richard Owen. Has always regretted following that advice.

letters.title: From Francis Ewbank   6 May 1881
letters.summary: Mr Coleman has retired. FE can see CD and can arrange for administering the gas.

letters.title: From F. A. Tscherning   6 May 1881
letters.summary: Sends a copy of his dissertation on the germination of the Cucurbitaceae.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin 7 May 1881
letters.summary: Discusses possible investments.

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   7 May [1881]
letters.summary: Wants aClematisidentified. Has been observing how earthworms drag down its petiole.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   8 May [1881]
letters.summary: Asks for return of letter from J. P. Bishop [13137] about hair turning grey at an early age in three generations.

letters.title: From Frithiof Holmgren   8 May 1881
letters.summary: Thanks for letter expressing CD’s position with regard to experiments on living animals and for getting the letter printed in theTimes[18 Apr 1881,Collected papers2: 226–7].

letters.title: To Alpheus Hyatt   8 May 1881
letters.summary:
Aware that AH thinks CD has done nothing to advance the good cause of the descent theory.

Obliged for gift of AH’s [Tertiary species of Planorbis at Steinheim(1880)].

letters.title: To Edward W. Bok   10 May 1881
letters.summary: Sends autograph. Hopes collecting will lead Bok to science, as it did him.

letters.title: To Daniel McAlpine   10 May 1881
letters.summary: Thanks for DM’s [Zoological atlas(1881)].

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   10 May 1881
letters.summary: Thanks for WTT-D’s attempts to get theTrifoliumseeds.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   12 May [1881]
letters.summary: Copies of FD’s paper have arrived ["The theory of growth",J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Bot.)18 (1881): 406–19]. Does he want them dispatched?

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   14 May 1881
letters.summary: News from the laboratory at Strasbourg; is working onEquisetumroots. Wortmann has found circumnutation in the mycelium of a fast-growing fungus. Please send papers (see 13155).

letters.title: From C. E. Södling   14 May 1881
letters.summary: Sends a likeness [missing] of a monstrous woman who may be considered as "Darwin’s lost link".

letters.title: To W. von Voigts-Rhetz   14 May 1881
letters.summary: CD defends English physiologists on vivisection.

letters.title: From Ernst Krause   15 May 1881
letters.summary:
Sends his review ofMovement in plantsfromDie Gartenlaube.

Comments on the future prospects ofKosmos.

Comments on review of Samuel Butler’sUnconscious memoryby Romanes inNature[23 (1880–1): 285–7] and Romanes’ reply to Butler [pp. 335–6].

Asks whether he might have a chapter ofEarthwormsto print inKosmos.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   16 & 17 May 1881
letters.summary:
Some papers have arrived for FD.

Comments on the work of Phillipe van Tieghem who evidently knows nothing of insectivorous plants.

Leslie Stephen’s visit to Down went off well.

letters.title: From C. E. Norton   17 May 1881
letters.summary: Thanks CD for R. W. Darwin’s memoranda respecting Franklin. Would be grateful for copies of any Franklin letters that exist among Dr Darwin’s papers.

letters.title: To Alphonse Engelhardt [after 17 May? 1881]
letters.summary: Wishes AE every success in his scientific studies.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   18 May 1881
letters.summary: Ernst Krause wishes to publish a section ofEarthwormsinKosmos. CD has consented. Hopes JVC will not object. He feels under obligation to Krause.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   18 May 1881
letters.summary:
Thanks EK for his article [on CD’sMovement in plants?].

Admires EK’s wide interest in science. Would like to send him something to publish inKosmos.

Fears his new book [Earthworms] will hardly do, but will send sheets when printed so that EK can decide whether any chapter or a part of one will serve. Victor Carus’ consent would be needed for publication inKosmos, and CD will ask for it.

letters.title: To James Torbitt   18 May 1881
letters.summary: Sends £90 [for experiments on potatoes]. Sorry JT cannot get his varieties well enough known to ensure large sale.

letters.title: From Alexander Agassiz   19 May 1881
letters.summary: Discusses the structure and formation of the Florida peninsula. Part played by marine animals in building banks on which coral can thrive.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   19 [May 1881]
letters.summary: Is sorry to have involved himself in a priority dispute between Wortmann and Elfring. Intends to publish on circumnutation; will CD send him his notes? Apologises for taking CD’s protractor, will send it back. Has met Oscar Schmidt.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   20 May 1881
letters.summary: Thanks FD for his excellent corrections [to MS ofEarthworms].

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   20 May [1881]
letters.summary: Discusses his investments.

letters.title: From James Torbitt   20 May 1881
letters.summary: Receipt, in CD’s hand, signed by JT, acknowledging subscriptions.

letters.title: From J. Victor Carus    21 May 1881
letters.summary: [text missing!?]

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   22–3 May 1881
letters.summary:
Is sending chapter [ofEarthworms] for FD to look over.

Comments on FD’s work on movements of mould.

Is glad to hear about Julius von Sachs and the circumnutation theory.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   23 [May 1881]
letters.summary: Would like some of his notes. Has been looking at roots ofLinum, cucurbits, larch, and orchids. Is content that mother should teach Bernard whatever religion she likes.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin 23 May 1881
letters.summary: Discusses possible investments.

letters.title: From Alpheus Hyatt   23 May 1881
letters.summary:
Wishes to correct impression of his attitude towards CD’s contribution: CD has successfully explained how differences arise.

Pleased CD will read his book [Tertiary species of Planorbis at Steinheim(1880)].

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   25 May [1881]
letters.summary: Sends further chapters ofEarthwormsfor correction.

letters.title: From Victor Hensen   25 May 1881
letters.summary: Mentions article by P. E. Müller on worms: "Structur over skovjord [forest soil]" [Tidsk. Skovbrug3 (1878)].

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   25 May [1881]
letters.summary: Suggests CD delay arrangements for his Linnean Society portrait. GJR thinks John Collier would be willing to paint it.

letters.title: From Frithiof Holmgren   26 May 1881
letters.summary: Thanks CD for photograph. They are battling for same cause.

letters.title: To H. M. Westropp   26 May 1881
letters.summary: Cannot discuss HMW’s essay [unidentified]. Does not believe there has been progress in all organisms. There has been much degradation, as in parasites.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   27 May 1881
letters.summary:
Dispatches chapters six and seven [ofEarthworms].

Asks for any opinions on V. Hensen and his book,Physiologie der Zeugung[1881], which seems interesting.

letters.title: From W. H. Goodwin   27 May 1881
letters.summary:
Requests CD’s autograph.

WHG grew up within 200 yards of "The Mount" [Darwin residence] in Shrewsbury.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   27 May 1881
letters.summary: Agrees to sit for portrait. Thinks John Collier is a good artist, an opinion based on his portrait of Hooker.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [28–9 May 1881]
letters.summary:
Thanks FD for corrections [forEarthworms].

Discusses experiments on absorption inDrosera.

letters.title: From J. B. Hannay   28 May 1881
letters.summary: In complex molecules such as proteins, liquid and gaseous states merge.

letters.title: To Yves Delage   29 May 1881
letters.summary: Thanks YD [forContribution à l’étude de l’appareil circulatoire des crustacés édriopthalmes marins(1881)].

letters.title: From C. M. Owen   29 May 1881
letters.summary: Would like to visit CD. Has not seen him for 40 years.

letters.title: From C. M. Owen   [after 29 May 1881]
letters.summary: Sorry to hear CD is unwell. Hopes outing [to Patterdale] will benefit him.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   30 May [1881]
letters.summary:
CD looks forward with dread to future as he does not have the strength to begin any new subject requiring much work.

Plans to look again at the absorption by roots and root-hairs.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   31 May 1881
letters.summary:
Has just received CD’s letter of 12 April [13113]. To answer CD’s query,Heteranthera reniformisis an amphibious plant that grows as well on moist ground as it does in ditches filled with water.

For the past few weeks has been observingPhyllanthusplants that had shown the irregular movement in leaves returning from the positions assumed at night, but none has repeated the irregularity. Perhaps the progeny from the seeds he has collected will inherit the tendency for irregular movement.

Describes his observations of the power of movement inCassia,Desmodium, and a few other plants.

Paul Mayer has identified seven new species of insects FM found in nine different species of figs.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [June–July? 1881]
letters.summary: Some stock certificates have arrived for FD.

letters.title: To C. E. Norton   1 June 1881
letters.summary:
No Benjamin Franklin letters to Erasmus Darwin preserved.

Was inaccurate about Franklin’s nephews [inErasmus Darwin].

Recounts story about Franklin at court of France.

letters.title: From James Paget   1 June 1881
letters.summary: Asks CD to lunch to meet the Prince of Wales.

letters.title: To James Dawson   [3 June 1881?]
letters.summary: Thanks JD for his book [Australian aborigines(1881)].

letters.title: To James Paget   3 June [1881]
letters.summary: Is honoured by, and accepts JP’s invitation for 3 August.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [before 4 June 1881]
letters.summary: Encloses letter from Elfving (not found). Should he publish on false circumnutation?

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [4–28 June 1881]
letters.summary:
Has accepted FD’s correction to chapter seven [ofEarthworms].

Weather is bad; sky like lead and the lake as black as ink.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   4 [June 1881]
letters.summary: Has taken almost all FD’s corrections for chapter six [ofEarthworms]. Is glad FD approves of the book.

letters.title: From J. H. Gilbert   5 June 1881
letters.summary: Invites CD to visit Rothamsted. The experimental plots are at their best "as illustrating the vast influence of external conditions on the character and results of the struggle between the numerous components of an established mixed herbage".

letters.title: From Leopold Sirk   5 June 1881
letters.summary: [Text extremely confused and unreadable.] [shd poss be note not synopsis!?]

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   8 June [1881]
letters.summary:
Discusses a letter [not found] from R. S. Ball that has quite delighted him.

Describes events at Patterdale.

letters.title: To J. H. Gilbert   8 June 1881
letters.summary: Regrets that he has not strength enough to visit [Rothamsted].

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [after 8 June 1881]
letters.summary:
Has nearly finished his mathematical paper.

Is not sure when he will go to Patterdale.

letters.title: From R. A. Blair   9 June 1881
letters.summary:
MentionsMastodonremains that he has seen.

Praises CD and his work.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   12 June 1881
letters.summary: Has struggled for months with complexity of structure and distribution of palms forGenera plantarum.

letters.title: From Francisco d’Arruda Furtado   13 June 1881
letters.summary: Offers his services to CD as an observer in the Azores. Has studied the local natural history and is a great disciple of CD’s.

letters.title: From Anthony Rich   13 June 1881
letters.summary: The Huxleys have visited; CD may come soon.

letters.title: To Mr and Mrs C. W. Siemens   13 June 1881
letters.summary: Regrets that CD’s health does not allow him to accept any invitations.

letters.title: From R. M. Lloyd   14 June 1881
letters.summary: Although CD says inExpressionthat foxes are not known to lick hands of their masters, RML can report a case of such an occurrence.

letters.title: From George Payne   14 June 1881
letters.summary: Sends seeds ofAnemone pulsatillathat bury themselves like feather grass.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [after 14 June 1881]
letters.summary: Describes seeds sent by Leo Payne [see13205]. Is surprised that they bury themselves.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   15 June 1881
letters.summary: CD complains of discomfort, but has not the strength for a project that would let him forget it.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   17 June 1881
letters.summary: Glad CD approves of Diaheliotropic paper. Reports on experiments with Carex and Yucca. Discusses translation of ‘Vâxtbook’ from Swedish. Heard some escellent music the previous night.

letters.title: To R. M. Lloyd   17 June 1881
letters.summary: Is obliged to RML for pointing out an error inExpression.

letters.title: To ?   17 June 1881
letters.summary: Thanks correspondent for sending paper on molluscs.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [after 17 June 1881]
letters.summary: Passes on an account from Cohen of preparations by Hahn of fossil coral-like structures.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   18 June 1881
letters.summary: At 63 JDH still works hard to support his family. Many friends have died. Memories of times past spent with CD lift his pessimism.

letters.title: From A. C. Ramsay   18 June 1881
letters.summary: Further details of pavement that sank from action of earthworms. There were plenty of castings, which first led him to think worms were involved.

letters.title: From Wilhelm Breitenbach[before 20 June 1881]
letters.summary:
Arrived in Brazil three months ago. Studying insects and plants, but work suffers from lack of scientific literature.

Fritz Müller has written to him to observe relations between ants and plants.

Writing popular articles about evolution for German newspaper in Brazil.

Sends paper fromKosmos.

Expects to spend several years in Brazil.

letters.title: To Wilhelm Breitenbach 20 [June] 1881
letters.summary: Glad WB has arrived in Brazil. Suggests study of insects and study of fertilisation in Melastomataceae. Want of books is not a serious evil.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   20 June [1881]
letters.summary:
Cheered by JDH’s friendly words.

Wishes he could help JDH with geographical distribution, but the subject has "gone mud" in his mind.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   21 June 1881
letters.summary:
Plans visit to Ceylon.

Describes rejection of his application for funds by Berlin Academy. Asks about possibility of obtaining support in England. Is writing to Lubbock and Huxley about it.

Hopes that new microscope from Zeiss is satisfactory. Ernst Abbe selected lenses.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller 21 June 1881
letters.summary:
Wants seeds of heterostyled plants to test fertility of illegitimate seedlings.

Offers £100 to FM to replace books lost in flooding.

letters.title: From Archibald Geikie   22 June 1881
letters.summary: Thanks for CD’s sympathy for James Croll; George Howard Darwin’s signature would have been welcome.

letters.title: To J. B. Hannay   22 June 1881
letters.summary:
Suggests modification in JBH’s experiment on formation of diamonds.

Speculates about chemical products of constituents of living organisms when subjected to heat and pressure.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   22 June 1881
letters.summary: Has had letter from Rothenburg asking him to help obtain a grant for Haeckel’s expedition to Ceylon.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   24 June 1881
letters.summary: Koch [of Schweizerbart, publisher of CD’s works in Germany and also publisher ofKosmos] has asked JVC to translateEarthwormsand send one chapter of it toKosmosfor advance separate publication. He thinks a chapter on the practical work of the earthworms would be most interesting to the general reader.

letters.title: To R. A. Blair   25 June 1881
letters.summary: Congratulates him onMastodondiscovery.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   25 June 1881
letters.summary: EH’s scheme to visit Ceylon an excellent one. Has written to Huxley about getting money from Royal Society. If funds are unavailable, would like to subscribe £100.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   26 June [1881]
letters.summary:
Ernst Haeckel wants to go to Ceylon to examine Medusae and Radiolariae, CD has offered him £100.

Is working on revises ofEarthworms.

Has seen a pied flycatcher for the first time.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [26 June 1881]
letters.summary: Discusses observations on circumnutation by FD, Kraus, Wortmann.

letters.title: To Ernst Haeckel   26 June [1881]
letters.summary: Thanks EH and Ernst Abbe in connection with microscope for his son [Francis].

letters.title: From J. B. Hannay   27 June 1881
letters.summary: Experiments on change of state in albumen under high temperature and pressure.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   27 June [1881]
letters.summary:
CD is glad the portrait [of CD by John Collier] has been arranged; suggests dates, but feels he should have no say in the subscriptions or remuneration.

Thinks the Lakes are beautiful.

Is reading W. Graham’sThe creed of science.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   28 June [1881]
letters.summary:
Comments on FD’s notions about movement of multicellular and unicellular organisms.

Comments on an interesting letter received from J. B. Hannay [see13222] which leads CD to speculate on the possibility of organisms inhabiting a red hot earth under great pressure.

letters.title: From E. J. J. G. Edwards   28 June 1881
letters.summary:
Remembers, as a Shrewsbury schoolmate, being taken by CD on a botanical collecting trip.

Sends a portrait [of CD?] from an old portfolio.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   28 June 1881
letters.summary: Has heard from Haeckel the story of refusal [by Humboldt fund] of Berlin Academy to support him because he was supporter of Darwin. R. Virchow has been so unfair to Haeckel that THH is inclined to think it is a true account. But obtaining the funds in England is extremely difficult.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   28 June 1881
letters.summary: CD has offered Ernst Haeckel £100 but does not know where to get further aid. Sorry to hear about Du Bois-Reymond, but is not in the least surprised about R. Virchow.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   29 June 1881
letters.summary: CD will soon finish corrections [ofEarthworms] for printer, and then clean sheets will be sent to JVC for translation of the book and to Ernst Krause. The subject has been a "hobby-horse" with CD, and he has perhaps treated it in foolish detail. Has told Krause he does not think any part of the MS suitable forKosmos, but Krause must decide.

letters.title: From Ernst Haeckel   1 July 1881
letters.summary: Thanks CD for offer of financial support. Discusses application for funds for Ceylon trip.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   1 July [1881]
letters.summary:
Has told John Collier to write to CD to arrange for portrait.

Will read [W. Graham’s]Creed of science.

Has got into row with W. B. Carpenter over thought-reading.

letters.title: To Francisco d’Arruda Furtado   3 and 6 July 1881
letters.summary:
Thanks Fd’AF for his interesting letter. CD suggests observations it would be worth making [in the Azores] although he is too old to make any direct use of them. Fauna and flora of different islands should be compared and the plants and animals from all high mountain summits collected. Suggests Fd’AF investigate the presence of glacial deposits and fossils on the islands. Survival of eggs in salt-water should be tested, as the wide distribution of lizards, land molluscs, and earthworms is a perplexing problem.

Will be very glad to read the essays Fd’AF sent.

letters.title: To William Graham   3 July 1881
letters.summary:
Praises WG’sCreed of science.

He disagrees that the existence of natural laws implies purpose, but his "inmost conviction" is that "the Universe is not the result of chance". But then has horrid doubt whether convictions of man’s mind, which has been developed from lower animals, are at all trustworthy.

Believes natural selection is doing more for progress of civilisation than WG admits.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   4 July 1881
letters.summary:
Movement of plants to shake off water: FM’s invaluable observations.

Inquires about "bloom" on leaves.

Fertilisation of Melastomataceae, roles of the two sets of anthers.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   4 July [1881]
letters.summary:
Is returning to Down.

Rejoices that GJR writes so much inNature.

letters.title: To F. M. Balfour   6 July 1881
letters.summary: Comments on FMB’s book [Treatise on comparative embryology, 2 vols. (1880–1)]. Had already purchased copy. Could second copy be sent to someone else? Fritz Müller?

letters.title: To A. B. Buckley 6 July [1881]
letters.summary: Will be glad to read over her article.

letters.title: To Alphonse de Candolle   6 July [1881]
letters.summary: Thanks for a "grand volume" [vol. 3 ofMonographiae phanerogamarum(1878–96)].

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   8 July 1881
letters.summary:
Comments on the response toMovement in plants, which seems to have been successful.

Is going over revises ofEarthworms.

Is investigating further his notion that leaves align themselves in the rain so as to shoot off drops of water.

letters.title: From Alphonse de Candolle   9 July 1881
letters.summary: AdeC thinksMonographiae phanerogamarummay be of some use to CD for the most nearly correct names to adopt.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   9 July 1881
letters.summary: Enthusiasm for Henry George’sProgress and poverty. Considers it to rank with Adam Smith’s work. His own work on the land question [Land nationalisation(1882)].

letters.title: From F. M. Balfour   10 July 1881
letters.summary: Thanks for suggesting that a spare copy of his book [Treatise on comparative embryology(1880–1)] be sent to Fritz Müller.

letters.title: From W. W. Gull   10 July 1881
letters.summary: Would be honoured if CD would come to dine with him, distinguished foreign guests, and H.R.H. Prince of Wales, on 3 Aug, the opening of the [7th International Medical] Congress.

letters.title: To A. B. Buckley   11 July 1881
letters.summary: Comments on her life of Lyell.

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   12 July 1881
letters.summary:
Will orderProgress and poverty. Comments on ARW’s political interests

and his own absorption in W. Graham’sThe creed of science.

His sojourn at Ullswater: "life has become very wearisome to me".

letters.title: To A. G. Blytt   13 July 1881
letters.summary:
Thanks AB for his letter,

his essay on climates ["Theorie der wechselnden kontinentalen und insularen Klimate",Bot. Jahrb.2 (1882): 1–50, 177–84],

and for his photograph. Sends his own.

letters.title: ToNature   13 July [1881]
letters.summary: Communicates two cases of inheritance reported by J. P. Bishop [in13137]. The work of E. Brown-Séquard has demonstrated that effects of injuries can be inherited ["Hereditary transmission of an epileptiform affection accidentally produced",Proc. R. Soc. Lond.10 (1860): 297–8]. E. Dupuy has sent CD a still more remarkable case.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   16 July 1881
letters.summary: Reports de Bary’s opinion of Max Cornu. Accounts of various botanical experiments and observations.

letters.title: From C. G. Semper   16 July 1881
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for his kind judgment on his book [The natural conditions of existence(1881)].

E. Ray Lankester has written an unfriendly review of it [Nature23 (1880–1): 405–9].

letters.title: To W. & J. Burrow Ltd.   18 July 1881
letters.summary: Orders a case of soda water.

letters.title: To ?   18 July 1881
letters.summary: Asks what to do with [unspecified] receipt.

letters.title: To C. G. Semper   19 July 1881
letters.summary:
Thinks CGS right not to reply to critical article by Lankester.

Discusses direct action of environment as cause of variability; the finding of Hermann Hoffmann that direct action of environment affects plants very little.

letters.title: To Joseph Sinel   19 July 1881
letters.summary: Thinks hairs on moles’ skin are secondary effect like hairs on ulcerated surfaces. Suggests he not publish until he has independent evidence of reversion.

letters.title: To Emily Talbot   19 July 1881
letters.summary: Interested in investigation of child development. Suggests questions. Does education of parents influence mental power of children? Desirable to test statement that coloured children at first learn as fast as white but afterwards fall behind. Does pitch of chidren’s voices vary with mood? Children’s tastes often related to occupation of progenitor. Do these last?

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   23 July 1881
letters.summary:
GHD’s abstract fromNature[24 (1881): 231] has been published inKosmos.

John Collier has finished his portrait of CD.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [25 July 1881]
letters.summary: Reports on a visit to Hermann Vöchting and discussion of Julius Sachs.

letters.title: From Leopold Würtenberger   26 July 1881
letters.summary: Has not been able to win a position that would allow him to conduct research. Seeks technical job instead. Asks for loan to tide himself over probationary period.

letters.title: To Watson C. Holbrook   27 July 1881
letters.summary: Appreciates WCH’s letter with references to the anatomy of ancient human beings. Rejoices in the progress of anthropology.

letters.title: From Robert Cooke   28 July 1881
letters.summary: Surprised by CD’s intention to publish [Earthworms] so soon. Remonstrates against doing so. Asks deferment until October to co-ordinate with American publication and ensure best profit.

letters.title: To Johannes Steenstrup   28 July 1881
letters.summary:
Thanks JS for essays. CD read the French abstract [? of "Sepiadarium og Idiosepius",K. Dan. Vidensk. Selsk. Skr. (Naturvidensk. Math. Afd.)1 (1880–5): 211–42]. Hectocotylisation has always astonished him.

Wishes JS believed in evolution.

letters.title: From Francisco d’Arruda Furtado   29 July 1881
letters.summary: Many thanks for CD’s advice and suggestions. His letter is a great source of encouragement.

letters.title: To Robert Cooke   29 July 1881
letters.summary: CD thought it was understood that he wanted to publish [Earthworms] at once, but as Murray "has the risk" CD must yield, though it destroys all his satisfaction in the book to have the publication hanging over him.

letters.title: From R. L. Tait   29 July 1881
letters.summary: Points out what he believes to be two errors in CD’s paper on inheritance [Nature24 (1881): 257;Collected papers2: 230–1].

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   30 July 1881
letters.summary: Delay in publication [ofEarthworms] vexes CD, as he likes to throw a subject off his mind.

letters.title: From Robert Cooke   30 July 1881
letters.summary: Hastens to assure CD that his book [Earthworms] will be published as soon as possible, since CD wishes it.

letters.title: From James Dawson   30 July 1881
letters.summary:
The material for hisAustralian aborigineswas collected by his daughter, who had lived among them from age three to fifteen.

Will try to verify a story he heard that there are pouched or marsupial rabbits in Australia.

letters.title: From E. L. Jellinek   30 July 1881
letters.summary: Asks whether CD believes in the immortality of the soul.

letters.title: To Ernst Krause   30 July 1881
letters.summary:
Publication ofEarthwormsdelayed, but will send sheets to EK when he receives them [so that he can decide about publishing extracts inKosmos].

Thanks for "Die Gegenwart".

"’Instinct’ of plants" is a most puzzling problem.

Does not see how mind can be defined "if we subtract consciousness".

letters.title: To E. L. Jellinek   [after 30 July 1881]
letters.summary: Regrets he cannot answer ELJ’s question in a note.

letters.title: To Robert Cooke   31 July 1881
letters.summary: CD obliged to Murray for yielding to his wish for prompt publication [ofEarthworms] but now uneasy about the risk. If Murray feels it will sell badly at this season he is unwilling to bear the responsibility. Murray should decide as he sees fit. CD is no longer so sulky as when he last wrote.

letters.title: From G. E. Mengozzi (La Scuola Italica)   31 July 1881.
letters.summary: Forwards to CD the diploma of "Presidente Onorario degli Anziana Pitagorica".

letters.title: To?   31 July [1881]
letters.summary: Thanks for note and plant specimen. Will take care of it for his own sake and Kew’s.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   2 August 1881
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Comments on MS of JL’s [1881] BAAS Presidential Address. Suggests that more attention be given to parthenogenesis.

letters.title: To Marianne North   2 August 1881
letters.summary: Obliged for the shrub "Australian Sheep" [Raoulia eximia] and pleased to have seen MN’s Australian pictures. Can still recall scenes from various countries with vividness.

letters.title: From Leopold Würtenberger   3 August 1881
letters.summary: Repeats request for loan in order to spend probationary training period in chemical factory.

letters.title: To T. L. Brunton   [4 August 1881]
letters.summary: CD wants to see TLB before he leaves London. Much obliged for his aid.

letters.title: To ?   4 August 1881
letters.summary: Acknowledges receipt of parcel of colours and chemical reagents.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   4 August [1881]
letters.summary: Reports on a luncheon of scientific savants at which the Crown Prince of Germany [and Prince of Wales?] were present.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   4 August 1881
letters.summary: Outlines address to York BAAS meeting on history of geographical distribution. Organising theme: advancement in this science based on ideas enunciated by scientific voyagers. Asks CD’s advice.

letters.title: From William Graham   [before 5 August 1881]
letters.summary: Quotes CD’s "horrid doubt" [see13230]. WG fails to see force of the argument. Evolution throws no suspicion on man’s reasoning faculties. The case is no different with the faculty that gives data.

letters.title: To William Graham   5 August 1881
letters.summary:
Thanks him for his letter. "I am not a quick thinker or a good talker and you would learn nothing from me on the many important subjects you have discussed."

Suggests meeting in London in lieu of a visit to Down.

letters.title: To Leopold Würtenberger   5 August 1881
letters.summary: CD does not lend money, but he encloses a cheque as a present.

letters.title: From August Dupré   6 August 1881
letters.summary: AD’s son has inherited the same head malformation as one AD had received as a result of the pressure of his nurse’s arm while carrying him when a baby.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   6 August 1881
letters.summary:
Responds to JDH’s outline history of plant geography.

Considers Humboldt the "greatest scientific traveller who ever lived".

Discusses the origin and rapid radiation of angiosperms in Cretaceous period.

Comments on importance of work of Alphonse de Candolle, Saporta, Axel Blytt.

letters.title: To William Clowes and Sons   6 August [1881]
letters.summary: Asks the printers that the table of contents [forEarthworms] be done in the same fashion used in his other books. Requests another proof.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   7 August [1881]
letters.summary:
Encloses notice about Wilhelm Roux’s book [see13118].

Comments on John Collier’s portrait.

letters.title: To August Dupré   8 August 1881
letters.summary:
AD’s case is a "curious one"; it seems impossible to explain as accidental coincidence.

[Letter sent in error to Raphael Meldola and apparently never forwarded to AD.]

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   8 August 1881
letters.summary: Requests name of the publishers of RM’s translation of Weismann’sStudien.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   8 August 1881
letters.summary:
Delighted that portrait of CD has "pleased those who are the best judges".

Arranging for vote on vivisection by International Medical Congress.

letters.title: From E. B. Aveling   9 August 1881
letters.summary: Sends a copy of his book [The student’s Darwin(1881)]. Hopes he may be forgiven for carrying his reasoning further than CD may allow.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   9 August 1881
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for his letter of 21 June [13212].

Is sending seeds ofOxalis sepium, which came from a cross between a plant with long pistils and another with pistils intermediate in length. Perhaps some of the plants that come from them will have short pistils.

FM does not know who told Dr B [Wilhelm Breitenbach] that he had lost a whole library in the flood. In fact, he lost only a few books that he had left behind thinking they were safe where they were.

Has taken the opportunity of a recent cold spell to test CD’s views on nyctitropism [night movements] in plants. DescribesPandanusandOxalis sepium.

Has just received CD’s letter of 4 July and he is glad that his observations on the effects of rain on plants interested CD.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   10 August [1881]
letters.summary: Apologises for the trouble he has caused RM. Encloses letter [13280?] which has been returned to CD [by August Dupré, to whom CD had sent it in error?]

letters.title: From William Thompson   10 August 1881
letters.summary:
Many thanks forMovement in plants.

Sends some seeds wanted by CD.

letters.title: To E. B. Aveling   11 August [1881]
letters.summary: Thanks EBA for his book [see13283]. Has no objection to people differing from him or carrying his arguments further than he would consider safe.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   11 August 1881
letters.summary: Working on York BAAS address; finds CD’s comments helpful. JDH writes detailed response and expansion.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   12 August 1881
letters.summary:
Responds to JDH on history of plant geography.

Opinion of Humboldt.

Origin of higher phanerogams.

Importance of the occurrence of south temperate forms in the Northern Hemisphere.

letters.title: From Francisco d’Arruda Furtado   17 August 1881
letters.summary: Has been collecting on the mountain summits and wants someone with whom to communicate about plants.

letters.title: To?   18 August [1881]
letters.summary: Thanks correspondent for information on a plant. It is too late for his present work.

letters.title: From Charles Naudin   19 August 1881
letters.summary: Trifolium resupinatumis not in season.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   20 August 1881
letters.summary: Is making final preparations for his address [at York BAAS meeting] and questions CD on specific points.

letters.title: To ?   20 August 1881
letters.summary: Fly adheres to ceiling by viscid matter on feet. Refers correspondent to B. T. Lowne,Anatomy and physiology of the blow-fly(1870).

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   21 August 1881
letters.summary: Sends CD information he had requested on W. Graham.

letters.title: To ?   21 August 1881
letters.summary: Declines an invitation to write for an unidentified periodical. "I am unable to write short articles in an interesting manner, & they would consume much of my time."

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   21 August 1881
letters.summary:
No one could have thought about evolution and not about representative species; yet no one discussed it fully untilOrigin, including von Baer.

Did not know of Leopold von Buch’sDescription physique des îles Canaries[1836] whenOriginwas published.

"As far as I know no one ever discussed the meaning of the relation between representative species before I did & as I suppose Wallace did in his paper before the Linn. Soc. [1858]."

letters.title: To ? 21 August 1881
letters.summary: Encloses a letter from his son G. H. Darwin and another from his son Francis Darwin.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   24 August [1881]
letters.summary: The General Post Office sent one penny in response to GHD’s complaint, and demanded a receipt, which CD has sent. CD will keep the penny.

letters.title: From Anthony Rich   25 August 1881
letters.summary:
Looks forward to CD’s visit on 8 Sept.

E. J. Trelawney, the friend of Shelley and Byron, has just died in a nearby village.

letters.title: To A. B. Buckley   26 August [1881]
letters.summary:
Comments on large orange.

Glad she is going to York [BAAS meeting].

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   27 August 1881
letters.summary:
On William Graham’s book [The creed of science(1881)].

Darwinism, chance, and the existence of evil.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   [28 August 1881]
letters.summary: Suggests that GHD employ W. M. Hacon as solicitor for selling E. A. Darwin’s house, rather than Mr Salt’s agents; he remembers that firm as full of odious people.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   28 August 1881
letters.summary: Discusses funeral arrangements for E. A. Darwin, and his will.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   28 August 1881
letters.summary:
More on W. Graham’s book,The creed of science. Chance and design. Happiness.

E. A. Darwin’s death [26 Aug 1881].

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [29 August 1881]
letters.summary: E. A. Darwin’s funeral arrangements.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   29 August 1881
letters.summary: Condolences on death of CD’s brother Erasmus. Recalls first meeting CD in Erasmus’ rooms over 40 years ago.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   30 August [1881]
letters.summary: CD is sorry he bothered GHD about the solicitor, but he boils with indignation to this day when he remembers how rudely he was treated by Mr Salt’s firm in London [40 years earlier].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   30 August 1881
letters.summary: Erasmus’ death and CD’s sentiments on death.

letters.title: From Stephen Price   30 August [1881]
letters.summary: Asks CD whether he thinks it probable that the gnat may develop into the mosquito in hot weather.

letters.title: To A. A. W. Hubrecht   31 August 1881
letters.summary: Thanks for copy of essay. Erasmus Alvey Darwin to be buried at Down the next day.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes 31 August 1881
letters.summary: Asks CD to contribute to symposium on vivisection to be published inNineteenth Century[10: 920–48].

letters.title: To John Lubbock   [30 August 1881]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: JL’s address [Presidential Address, 31 Aug 1881,Rep. BAAS(1881): 1–51] has made him think about important steps in advancing geology. Lists major advances in his lifetime.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [10 September 1881]
letters.summary: The merchants suggest that CD keep the wine and return it if more is corked.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [9? September 1881]
letters.summary: Asks for two property valuations. Is afraid he has made a mistake in CD’s property settlements.

letters.title: From J. B. B. Dykes   1 September [1881]
letters.summary: Sends condolences on the death of E. A. Darwin. LBBD was a schoolfellow at Shrewsbury.

letters.title: To S. A. Price   1 September [1881]
letters.summary: Regrets he cannot answer SAP’s question on gnats.

letters.title: To Francisco d’Arrudo Furtado   2 September 1881
letters.summary:
Sends a copy of A. R. Wallace’s work [The geographical distribution of animals(1876)].

Advises Fd’AF on how to carry out his work, "Keep notes & go on accumulating facts". CD will write to J. D. Hooker about the plants Fd’AF has collected.

letters.title: From Anthony Rich   2 September [1881]
letters.summary: Condolences on the death of E. A. Darwin.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   2 September 1881
letters.summary:
Unable to contribute an essay to a symposium on the subject of vivisection. Objects to use of term "symposium".

Mentions articles of Hermann Müller.

Death of his brother Erasmus [26 Aug 1881].

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   3 & 4 September [1881]
letters.summary:
Praises JDH’s York address.

S. B. J. Skertchly has paralleled Axel Blytt’s work in Cambridgeshire fens.

JDH too cautious on southern glacial period.

Is Kew interested in Azores plants collected by Arruda Furtado, a local inhabitant and an evolutionist?

letters.title: To John Lubbock   3 September [1881]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Discusses insect attraction to artificial flowers. CD’s experiments of 40 years ago failed, but Nägeli reported success by scenting them.

letters.title: To John Price   3 September [1881]
letters.summary:
Thanks for letter about death of Erasmus Darwin.

Cannot answer question about dotterels.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   4 September [1881]
letters.summary:
Not intended to call vivisection article a symposium [Nineteenth Century10 (1881): 920–48].

Sympathy on death of Erasmus Darwin.

Trying some experiments with bees to test their direction-finding methods.

letters.title: To ?   5 September 1881
letters.summary: Asks him to deliver two or three feet of linoleum.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   6 [September 1881]
letters.summary:
Is obliged to GHD for arranging everything.

Sorry about the proof-sheets.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   6 September 1881
letters.summary: Discusses some of his observations on the sleep movement in plants. Has been studying the leaflets ofCrotalaria; has discovered they move to face the setting sun.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [7 September 1881]
letters.summary: Gives an account of the reception of his paper at York [BAAS meeting].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   7 September 1881
letters.summary:
Comte de Paris requests an orchid from CD for his huge collection.

JDH responds to CD’s criticism of York address.

Arruda Furtado could work on mystery of buried cypress trunks in the Azores.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   8 September [1881]
letters.summary: Has been visiting Anthony Rich, who persists in his intention to leave his property to CD despite the large fortune left by Erasmus. It is now all the more necessary for CD to arrange his own will.

letters.title: From S. H. Haliburton   8 September [1881]
letters.deprecated: Sarah Harriet (Sarah Harriet Williams) (Sarah Harriet Mostyn Owen) Haliburton
letters.sender: Sarah Harriet (Sarah Harriet Williams) (Sarah Harriet Mostyn Owen) Haliburton
letters.summary: Condolences on death of Erasmus.

letters.title: From Wilhelm Breitenbach   9 September 1881
letters.summary:
Thanks for gift ofMovement in plants.

Plans botanical research in Brazil.

Hermann von Jhering is conducting experiments on snakes.

WB obliged to work as newspaper correspondent.

Plans breeding experiments on dimorphic plants.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   9 September 1881
letters.summary: Erasmus has left half his fortune to CD. Anthony Rich nevertheless insists on keeping to his testamentary arrangements. He also referred to leaving some additional property to THH.

letters.title: From Robert Cooke   10 September 1881
letters.summary:
Only 270 copies ofMovement in plantsremain. Suggests printing another 250 and then breaking up type. If CD agrees, has he any corrections?

Sends a copy ofEarthworms.

letters.title: From W. F. Hurndall   10 September 1881
letters.summary: Reports that a living frog was found in a lump of coal.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   10 September 1881
letters.summary:
Has sent FM’s account ofPandanusandOxalistoNature["Leaves injured at night by free radiation",Nature24 (1881): 459].

Is crossing heterostyled plants.

Hopes to get his notes on bloom together.

letters.title: To Hyacinth Hooker   10 September [1881]
letters.summary: Thanks HH for a newspaper containing an article of interest.

letters.title: To W. M. Hacon   11 September 1881
letters.summary: Wishes to draw up a new will; outlines the changes to be made in the provisions.

letters.title: To Francisco d’Arruda Furtado   12 September 1881
letters.summary:
Hooker would be very glad to see the mountain plants Fd’AF has collected.

Hooker says huge cypress trunks have been found buried in the ground [in the Azores]; the site needs to be described and investigated. CD suggests collecting earth from same bed to see whether any seeds have remained viable.

letters.title: From John Harmer   12 September 1881
letters.summary: Observed a bird carrying a long worm.

letters.title: From G. H. Haydon   12 September 1881
letters.summary: Sending some Hudson’s Bay mosquitoes because of a letter of CD’s quoted inEvening Standard, 5 Sept 1881.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   12 September 1881
letters.summary:
Hopes Anthony Rich will keep to his intention of leaving his fortune to CD, despite CD’s increased wealth.

His BAAS address at York inNature["The rise and progress of palaeontology" 24 (1881): 452–5].

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   13 September [1881]
letters.summary: Discusses financial affairs.

letters.title: From W. M. Hacon   13 September 1881
letters.summary: Drafting new will as CD requested.

letters.title: From George King   13 September 1881
letters.summary: Sends preserved pitchers and figure ofDischidia rafflesiana, a rare plant from East Bengal, which GK and the late John Scott had tried in vain to cultivate.

letters.title: From J. B. Innes   14 September 1881
letters.summary: JBI’s observations on bees and wasps. The hexagonal cells made by solitary queen wasps do not fit explanation inOrigin.

letters.title: To Nature   [before 15 September 1881]
letters.summary: Quotes from a Fritz Müller letter of 9 Aug [missing] supporting CD’s views that leaves position themselves at night so as to minimise heat loss by radiation. It is a new fact to CD that leaves take different positions at different seasons.

letters.title: To J. B. Innes   15 September 1881
letters.summary:
CD interested in JBI’s observations of behaviour of bees. Finds his criticism about hexagonal cells made by queen wasps a good one. Cannot remember how he got out of the difficulty.

His book on worms to be published soon.

E. A. Darwin has died after short illness.

letters.title: To CD’s Children   16 September 1881
letters.deprecated: Elizabeth (Bessy) (Lizzy) DarwinFrancis DarwinGeorge Howard DarwinHorace DarwinLeonard DarwinWilliam Erasmus DarwinHenrietta Emma DarwinHenrietta Emma Litchfield
letters.recipient: Elizabeth (Bessy) (Lizzy) DarwinFrancis DarwinGeorge Howard DarwinHorace DarwinLeonard DarwinWilliam Erasmus DarwinHenrietta Emma DarwinHenrietta Emma Litchfield
letters.summary: A circular letter on the distribution of his money at death and the division ofErasmus’ estate.

letters.title: From John Price   17 September 1881
letters.summary: Nathan Hubbersty [of Cambridge days] is very ill.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin   [after 16 September 1881]
letters.summary: Discusses division of Trust. Is concerned Bessy’s portion will be smaller than Henrietta's. Had a pleasant visit in Cambridge. There is a clerical error in the division of CD’s property.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   18 September [1881]
letters.summary:
Comte [de Paris] will have plants next summer.

Arruda Furtado will send his mountain plants from Azores.

letters.title: From W. M. Hacon 20 September 1881
letters.summary: Details of new will. 12/74ths to each son and 7/74ths to each daughter.

letters.title: To Frank Hurndall   20 September 1881
letters.summary: No frogs or toads are able to live in completely closed holes. Cites experiment by William Buckland.

letters.title: From J. B. Innes   20 September 1881
letters.summary:
Did not intend his last letter as criticism. Is sure CD would not "wriggle out" of a difficulty if he had observed it.

Sends CD a wasps’ nest.

letters.title: From S. B. J. Skertchly   20 September 1881
letters.summary: Asks for a testimonial from CD to enable him to get an adequate Treasury pension. An accident at work has killed his son and injured him to such an extent that he must resign his appointment.

letters.title: To Caroline Wedgwood   20 September [1881]
letters.summary:
Division of CW’s share [of E. A. Darwin’s estate]. Investment advice.

Recounts his memories of their mother and of her death. Remembers "her black velvet gown and her work table and the death scene", but cannot remember her face. Remembers that Caroline "always acted like a mother" to him and Catherine.

letters.title: To J. B. Innes   22 September [1881]
