letters.summary:
Wasps’ nest has arrived.

Gives his view of how queen wasp builds a hexagonal cell by straightening walls between several cells, which she builds at the same time.

letters.title: From William Nation   22 September 1881
letters.summary: Reports on the behaviour of the Peruvian cow bird,Molothrus, which lays its eggs in other birds’ nests.

letters.title: From Herbert Spencer   22 September 1881
letters.summary: Sends CD a circular [missing] and asks whether he will add his name to group [Anti-Aggression League].

letters.title: To Herbert Spencer   [after 22 September 1881]
letters.summary: Although he agrees with the object of HS’s league he will not join until he has seen how it works.

letters.title: From W. M. Hacon   23 September 1881
letters.summary: Clarifies some details of CD’s new will.

letters.title: From H. N. Moseley   24 September 1881
letters.summary: Asks CD for a testimonial as he is a candidate for Chair in Zoology at Oxford.

letters.title: To H. N. Moseley   25 September 1881
letters.summary: Gives his high opinion of HNM’s abilities.

letters.title: From W. M. Hacon   26 September 1881
letters.summary: WMH’s agent taking will to Down for CD to sign.

letters.title: From E. B. Aveling   27 September [1881]
letters.summary: Ludwig Büchner is in London. Requests interview for him with CD on Wednesday or Thursday; he leaves Friday.

letters.title: From B. W. Savile   27 September 1881
letters.summary:
Finds it difficult to reconcile evolution with Mosaic record, but thinks it does not necessarily involve "infidel" principles.

Asks "How life born of an egg, can evolve life born of a mammal?"

letters.title: From A. G. More   28 September 1881
letters.summary: Writes, as a former correspondent, asking CD for a testimonial.

letters.title: To C. V. Riley   28 September 1881
letters.summary: Comments on CVR’s paper ["Further notes on the pollination ofYuccaand onPronubaandProdoxus",Proc. Am. Assoc. Adv. Sci.(1880): 617–39]. "What an inaccurate man Mr Thomas Meehan is." Interested in further observations onPronuba.

letters.title: To H. T. Stainton   28 September 1881
letters.summary: Thanks HTS for aDahliaflower, but analogous cases of such "bud-variation" have been observed before.

letters.title: To A. G. More   [after 28 September 1881]
letters.summary: Knows nothing of AGM’s work and is not personally acquainted with him so he cannot provide a testimonial.

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   29 September 1881
letters.summary:
Gives further details on his grapes.

Tells of his recent movements and state of health.

letters.title: From B. W. Savile   30 September 1881
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his reply and, in attempting to clarify his question [see13358], asks: "how could the first mammal species be nourished, if its immediate progenitor was non-mammal?"

letters.title: To B. J. Sulivan   30 September [1881]
letters.summary:
BJS’s grape case is a mystery.

CD is still able to work a little but does not expect to do much more of any interest to naturalists.

The death of his brother [E. A. Darwin] was a heavy loss.

letters.title: To B. W. Savile   [after 30 September 1881]
letters.summary: There is "some gradation in perfection with mammals in the mammery glands". Discusses milk secretion inEchidna. Instances a fish in which the ova hatch in a sack on the male and the young feed on mucus secreted by the sack lining; "here … we see what might be the commencement of a simple mammery gland".

letters.title: From Julius Wiesner   1 October 1881
letters.summary: Sends copy of hisDas Bewegungsvermögen der Pflanzen[1881]. Disagrees with CD about plant movement.

letters.title: From Peter Beveridge   3 October 1881
letters.summary:
Regarding CD’s paper ["Black sheep",Nature23 (1880): 193;Collected papers2: 224] he comments on absence of black sheep at his father’s sheep station.

Notes that the repeated brandings of sheep produce no inherited effect, and a woman’s withered leg was not inherited by her children.

letters.title: From Robert Cooke   3 October 1881
letters.summary: Will send copies [ofEarthworms] shortly. Troubled by rumour of a mysterious copy in hands of a reviewer.

letters.title: To Julius Wiesner   4 October 1881
letters.summary: Thanks JW for book [Das Bewegungsvermögen der Pflanzen(1881)]. Discusses movement in plants.

letters.title: To Robert Cooke   5 October 1881
letters.summary:
Glad book [Earthworms] will soon be published.

G. J. Romanes has copy and often writes reviews forNature. Probably did not know it was incorrect to publish it prematurely.

letters.title: From William Graham   5 October 1881
letters.summary: WG is a candidate for a new chair at University College, Liverpool. Asks CD’s permission to use extracts from his letter [13230] for a testimonial.

letters.title: To ?   5 October 1881
letters.summary: Has resolved never to write for periodicals.

letters.title: From J. S. Billings   7 October 1881
letters.summary: Asks whether he and W. M. Ord may call on CD.

letters.title: From Robert Cooke   7 October 1881
letters.summary: Murray has sold 1200 copies [ofEarthworms], so another printing of 500 is proposed. Has CD any corrections to send?

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [7? October? 1881]
letters.summary: Has found the missing packet of forks, which he will send or take to Down.

letters.title: From H. N. Moseley   7 October 1881
letters.summary:
Thanks for presentation copy ofEarthworms.

Describes a worm from Ceylon.

letters.title: To J. S. Billings   8 [October 1881]
letters.summary: Invites JSB and W. M. Ord to Down, and gives instructions for getting there.

letters.title: From Robert Cooke   8 October 1881
letters.summary: Will perhaps have to print off 1000 extra copies [ofEarthworms]. Electros of the woodcuts are ready for the German edition.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin   8 October 1881
letters.summary: [Empty cover.]

letters.title: To ?   8 October 1881
letters.summary: Encloses a check [cheque!?] for £11.5.0 for subscriptions from CD and members of his family.

letters.title: From A. W. Buckland   9 October 1881
letters.summary: On the effects of a mother’s imagination on a new-born child. Reports that a hen, startled by an alarm clock, laid eggs with clock faces on them.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   9 October 1881
letters.summary: Thanks CD forEarthwormsand comments on it.

letters.title: From J. M. Herbert   9 October 1881
letters.summary:
Thanks forEarthworms.

Condolences on death of Erasmus.

letters.title: From W. C. McIntosh   9 October 1881
letters.summary: Thanks forEarthworms.

letters.title: From H. N. Moseley   9 October 1881
letters.summary: Sends a paper by A. C. Lasaulx ["Über Untersuchungen sogennanter kosmischer Staube",Sitzungsber. Niederrheinischen Ges. Bonn(1881): 114–15, 173–6]. HNM does not believe in meteoric dust, which CD takes for granted inEarthworms.

letters.title: To Miss Buckland   10 October [1881]
letters.summary: Does not believe imagination of mother can affect new-born infant.

letters.title: From Archibald Geikie   10 October 1881
letters.summary:
Thanks forEarthworms.

Importance of wind in soil formation and transport.

letters.title: From James Geikie   10 October 1881
letters.summary:
Thanks forEarthworms.

Terraces on the Cheviot Hills.

letters.title: From Victor Hensen   10 October 1881
letters.summary: Thanks CD forEarthworms. Not convinced that worms derive nutrition from eating soil.

letters.title: From J. W. Judd   10 October 1881
letters.summary: Thanks and praises CD forEarthworms.

letters.title: From B. W. Savile   10 October 1881
letters.summary: Thanks CD for answering his query about evolution.

letters.title: To Peter Price    [after 10 October 1881?]
letters.summary: Giving his opinion on the possible role of earthworms in the dilapidation of a pier in Llandaff Cathedral.

letters.title: To T. L. Brunton 11 October 1881
letters.summary: Thanks TLB for the collection of his writings.

letters.title: From Julius Wiesner   11 October 1881
letters.summary:
Thanks for copy ofEarthworms.

Responds to CD’s comments on his book [Das Bewegungsvermögen der Pflanzen(1881)].

letters.title: From Leonard Darwin   12 October [1881]
letters.summary: Will be home on Saturday.

letters.title: To R. L. Tait   12 October 1881
letters.summary: Owes much to Birmingham and great honour conferred on him, but cannot write what RLT wishes.

letters.title: To E. R. Lankester   13 October [1881]
letters.summary:
Says that salt water kills earthworms.

Interested in ERL’s study of worm anatomy.

letters.title: From Anthony Rich   13 October 1881
letters.summary: Thanks forEarthworms.

letters.title: From Robert Cooke   14 October 1881
letters.summary: Has sent copies [ofEarthworms] toAnnals & Magazine of Natural Historyand toPopular Science Review. If W. S. Dallas edits both, he will have two copies.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   14 October [1881]
letters.summary: Thanks GJR for his review ofEarthworms[Nature24 (1881): 553–6].

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   15 October 1881
letters.summary: Sends text of the gravestone inscription [for E. A. Darwin] and details of arrangements for removal of furniture from Queen Anne St.

letters.title: From Henry Johnson   15 October [1881]
letters.summary: Thanks forEarthworms.

letters.title: From Hugo de Vries   15 October 1881
letters.summary:
Thanks forEarthworms.

HdeV is studying the causes of variation in plants and is very interested in Pangenesis.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [after 15 October 1881]
letters.summary: Has sent the inscription [for E. A. Darwin’s gravestone]. If CD approves, will he forward it to G. S. ffinden [Vicar of Downe Parish] and William [Darwin].

letters.title: From Francisco d’Arruda Furtado   16 October 1881
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for sending Wallace’s book [see13313]

and for writing to Hooker about Fd’AF’s plants. Has written to Hooker to tell him of the plants he is sending and discuss the subject of the cypress trunks.

Thanks CD for his detailed instructions for suggested experiments.

letters.title: From G. J. Romanes   16 October 1881
letters.summary:
Thinks CD guilty of mock modesty regarding GJR’s review ofEarthworms.

Has been working on echinoderms again with J. C. Ewart.

letters.title: From Lady Derby   16 October 1881
letters.deprecated: Mary Catherine Stanley, countess of Derby
letters.sender: Mary Catherine Stanley, countess of Derby
letters.summary: Has readEarthwormswith great interest. Remembers CD once said, laughing, that he was finding that "worms could revolutionise the world". CD has succeeded in proving greatness of their power.

letters.title: From T. L. Brunton   17 October 1881
letters.summary: Thanks CD for a copy ofEarthworms.

letters.title: From R. B. Carter   17 October 1881
letters.summary: Requests interview to get CD’s views on stages in evolution of the eye for a talk he is to give at a health congress [see lecture on colour-blindness inNot. Proc. R. Inst. G. B.13 (1890): 116–33].

letters.title: From J. H. Chamberlain   17 October 1881
letters.summary: Has readEarthwormsand suggests, as an architect, that leaf linings protect worm burrow from the worm’s rapid movements.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   17 October 1881
letters.summary:
Has been reading Julius von Wiesner’s book [Das Bewegungsvermögen der Pflanzen(1881)]. Comments that it is "an excellent book, but he vivisects me in the most grievous terms, but most effectively".

Has been experimenting on aggregation of chlorophyll but with little success.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [18 October 1881]
letters.summary: Occupied with details of E. A. Darwin’s house and furniture. He has ordered a gravestone.

letters.title: From W. R. S. Ralston   18 October 1881
letters.summary: CD will be figured tomorrow inPunch. The artist, Linley Sambourne, expresses his deep respect.

letters.title: To Hugo de Vries   [18 October 1881]
letters.summary: Delighted to hear that HdeV intends working on the causes of variation.

letters.title: From A. R. Wallace   18 October 1881
letters.summary: Thanks for book [Earthworms]. Asks whether leaf-mould is not formed by decay as well as by the agency of worms.

letters.title: To L. C. Harrison   18 October [1881]
letters.summary: Can think of no suggestion to send to Mrs Forsyth. "The best plan is to read, think and speculate and then some suggestion or doubt will occur which can be determined or verified out of observation."

letters.title: From R. S. Pattrick 19 October 1881
letters.summary: Thanks forEarthworms.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin 20 October [1881]
letters.summary: Thanks forWorms.

letters.title: From J. F. Galbraith 20 October 1881
letters.summary: Recounts a remarkable incident of development of worms in a barrel of wheat. Sends his account, having pondered CD’s view that plants and animals may have had a common ancestor.

letters.title: From R. B. Carter   21 October 1881
letters.summary: Thanks for F. M. Balfour reference, which will serve purpose of his lecture on evolution of the eye.

letters.title: From Francisco d’Arruda Furtado   22 October 1881
letters.summary: Reports having found orthopteran egg-cases, affixed to a chalk statuette, that had themselves been coated with chalk, without doubt by the insect that deposited them.

letters.title: From James Croll   22 October 1881
letters.summary: Thanks for presentation copy ofEarthworms.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   22 [October 1881]
letters.summary: Thinks FD should review Julius von Wiesner’s book [Das Bewegungsvermögen der Pflanzen(1881)]. CD comforted that Wiesner’s experiments support their findings but finds it laughable how differently he has interpreted them.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   22 October 1881
letters.summary:
Visiting his son Horace.

Studying action of carbonate of ammonia. Finds similar lookingEuphorbiaroot cells react differently.

Intrigued byDischidia rafflesiana, whose pitchers manufacture manure-water that nourishes adventitious roots. Does JDH know histologist for detailed study?

Julius von Wiesner’s criticism ofMovement in plants"vivisects" CD in "a most courteous but awful manner" [Das Bewegungsvermögen der Pflanzen(1881)].

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   22 October 1881
letters.summary:
Is in Cambridge with his son, resting

and reading F. M. Balfour’sComparative embryology[1880–1].

Sent FM a copy ofEarthworms.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   [23 or 30 October 1881]
letters.summary:
Pleasure in readingEarthworms.

Buying land to build a cottage.

Finishing palms forGenera plantarumafter three years’ work.

letters.title: From Edward Fry   24 October 1881
letters.summary: Describes worms blocking their burrows with mulberries.

letters.title: From Félix Hément   24 October 1881
letters.summary: Sends notes of reports by E. A. Axon, George Eickner, and Joseph Alley to Académie des Sciences on deaf mutes.

letters.title: To George King   24 October 1881
letters.summary: Thanks for specimen ofDischidia. Will ask Hooker who might dissect it.

letters.title: From W. F. P. Pfeffer   24 October 1881
letters.summary:
Will send 2d vol. [of hisPflanzenphysiologie(1881)].

CD has occasionally misinterpreted him inMovement in plants; by "after-working" (Nachwirkung) he means "after-working of preceding movements", not of the irritating cause [light].

letters.title: From Robert Cooke   25 October 1881
letters.summary: Second thousand [ofEarthworms] has been exhausted and 3d is being printed. Asks CD to send corrections to the printer.

letters.title: To J. B. Dancer   25 October [1881]
letters.summary: Informs JBD that his book [Earthworms] profited from JBD’s interesting notice ["On the transfer of subsoil to the surface",Proc. Manchester Lit. & Philos. Soc.16: 247–8].

letters.title: From Carl Möbius   25 October 1881
letters.summary: Thanks for presentation copy ofEarthworms.

letters.title: To Julius Wiesner   25 October 1881
letters.summary: Further comments on JW’sDas Bewegungsvermögen der Pflanzen[1881]. Discusses heliotropism and sensitivity of root tips. Bewildered by their differences concerning circumnutation.

letters.title: To Robert Cooke   [after 25 October 1881?]
letters.summary: Has no corrections. Pleased at sale of book [Earthworms].

letters.title: From Joseph Plimsoll   26 October 1881
letters.summary: Urges CD to find God.

letters.title: To P. R. Head   27 October 1881
letters.summary: Thanks for errata [inEarthworms].

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   27 October 1881
letters.summary:
On plants CD requested.

Frank should work onDischidia.

Work on palms.

Overloaded with reading.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   28 [October 1881]
letters.summary:
Earthwormsis selling well.

Discussed how to repeat some of their plant experiments while in Cambridge.

Comments on Julius Wiesner’s views on plant movement.

S. H. Vines was very much surprised at the action of carbonate of ammonia on the roots ofEuphorbia.

letters.title: From E. L. Henn   28 October 1881
letters.summary: Note on habits of earthworms.

letters.title: To William Preyer   28 October 1881
letters.summary: Thanks WP for copy of hisDie Seele des Kindes[1882].

letters.title: To B. J. Sulivan   28 October [1881]
letters.summary: Has looked at BJS’s grapes. Can give no explanation of the case.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   29 October 1881
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for letter of 10 September [13326]

and for copy ofNature.

Reports onLagerstroemiaexperiments.

Has been making observations on what happens to plants following heavy rain. Sends CD three specimens to show how dirt attaches to the undersides of leaves.

letters.title: From Alfred Newton   29 October 1881
letters.summary: Thanks CD for the reference to Audubon’s story. T. M. Brewer is to be trusted, but his account does not suggest why the bird always moved northward.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   30 October 1881
letters.summary:
Profuse thanks for plants.

Specifies which euphorbs he wants. Euphorbs’ alternate rows of ammonium carbonate reactive/non-reactive cells are worth more study.

letters.title: From W. C. McIntosh   30 October 1881
letters.summary: Marine annelids are ingenious builders.

letters.title: To Francisco d’Arrudo Furtado   31 October 1881
letters.summary:
Is glad Fd’AF will find Wallace’s work useful [see13313].

Has examined the egg-cases ofBlattaand suspects the white matter may be cement or plaster. If Fd’AF observes similar cases the fact would be worth publishing as a good instance of skill in protection.

letters.title: To E. R. Lankester 31 October 1881
letters.summary: Testimonial for ERL, who is a candidate for the Chair of Natural History in Edinburgh.

letters.title: From Edward Parfitt   31 October 1881
letters.summary: Corrects Wilhelm Hoffmeister, cited inEarthworms, p. 63: earthworms do not block their holes to keep outScolopendrasbut to prevent evaporation.

letters.title: To Hugo de Vries   [November–December 1881]
letters.summary: Can HdV supply a reference to a paper describing a stem or a root divided longitudinally and the separate parts acted on by geotropism.

letters.title: To Camilla Pattrick   [November 1881]
letters.summary: Discusses criticism of his studies on heliotropism by Julius von Wiesner. Mentions views of W. F. P. Pfeffer.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin 1 November 1881
letters.summary: Requests a list of CD’s trust securities; he and Sara have finishedWorms; asks what he should do with dividdend warrant.

letters.title: From L. J. Jones   1 November [1881]
letters.summary: Points out an error inEarthworms.

letters.title: To S. H. Vines   1 November 1881
letters.summary: Asks SHV about nature of granular matter formed in root cells ofEuphorbia pepluswhich have been placed in solution of ammonium carbonate.

letters.title: From F. B. Zincke   1 November 1881
letters.summary: Has found prehistoric tools in his orchard that he believes have been buried by the action of earthworms.

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   2 November 1881
letters.summary: Sends corrections ("two bad errata & a blunder") inEarthworms, which is selling well in England.

letters.title: To L. J. Jones   2 November 1881
letters.summary: Thanks LJJ for informing him of error [inEarthworms].

letters.title: To C.-F. Reinwald   2 November 1881
letters.summary: Errata discovered inEarthwormsare listed. Large sales in England, but this is no indication for France. [See13510.]

letters.title: From W. B. Tegetmeier   2 November 1881
letters.summary: Encloses his review ofEarthworms.

letters.title: From S. H. Vines   2 November [1881]
letters.summary: On the action of ammonium carbonate on plant cells. "Aggregation" of protoplasm.

letters.title: From D. Appleton & Co   3 November 1881
letters.summary: Encloses statement of U. S. sales of CD’s works and sends a cheque for the balance due to CD.

letters.title: To W. B. Tegetmeier   3 November 1881.
letters.summary: Thanks for the review [ofEarthworms].

letters.title: To F. B. Zincke   3 November 1881
letters.summary:
CD thinks the celts [prehistoric tools] on the pan could not have been buried wholly by worms.

As for large size of Arctic mammals, CD suggests it is an advantage in retaining warmth.

letters.title: From J. F. Simpson   4 November 1881
letters.summary: Relates some of his observations on the behaviour and activity of earthworms.

letters.title: To S. H. Vines   4 November 1881
letters.summary:
Thanks SHV for his letter [13455] in answer to his questions about the action of ammonium carbonate on the root cells ofEuphorbia peplus. Suggests further observations.

Has read J. von Sachs [Textbook of botany, English translation (1875)] and H. A. De Bary [Vergleichende Anatomie(1877)] on milk-tubes. He believes that tubes he has observed in germinating roots ofEuphorbia myrsinitesare modified milk tubes. Will send a paper on the subject to the Linnean Society.

letters.title: From Robert Cooke   5 November 1881
letters.summary: Memorandum: "3500 Worms!!!" sold at annual sale; 117Movement in plants; 180 "Naturalist" [Journal of researches]; 600Origin; 320Descent.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   5 November 1881
letters.summary: Has receivedEarthworms.

letters.title: To Robert Cooke   6 November 1881
letters.summary: Discusses additional printing ofEarthworms.

letters.title: From A. E. Graves   6 November 1881
letters.summary: Sends his observations on the behaviour of a worm. They seem to indicate some sensory apparatus enabling it to "see".

letters.title: To L. J. Jones   6 November 1881
letters.summary: Explains source of error [inEarthworms].

letters.title: To John Lubbock   6 November 1881
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary:
Supports the statements on Henry Hicks in JL’s address.

Bonney is an "objector general".

CD has always supported A. C. Ramsay.

letters.title: From [W. F. P. Pfeffer]   6 November 1881
letters.summary: It is impossible to trace the direct connections between stimuli and responses in plant movements. Disagrees with much of Julius von Wiesner [Die Bewegungsvermögen der Pflanzen(1881)]. Disagrees with CD on induced movements and circumnutation.

letters.title: From T. M. Reade   6 November 1881
letters.summary: Praise forEarthworms.

letters.title: From C. J. Breese   7 November 1881
letters.summary: Sends CD an 1871 abstract of his paper on the earthworm, and requests information on the phenomenon of luminosity.

letters.title: From Sarah Marshall   7 November 1881
letters.summary: Can CD explain why in a mollusc (Bulimus decollatus) immature forms are always broken at the apex.

letters.title: ToNature   7 November [1881]
letters.summary: Summarises letter of William Nation [13350]. The facts given strongly support the conclusion that there is some close connection between the parasitic habits of birds that lay their eggs in others’ nests and the fact of their laying eggs at "considerable intervals of time".

letters.title: To F. B. Zincke   7 November 1881
letters.summary: Would like to cite the case of the celt in a new printing ofEarthworms. Asks for details.

letters.title: To T. M. Reade   8 November 1881
letters.summary: "Roots often run down worm burrows, but can penetrate the ground without such aid."

letters.title: From J. F. Simpson   8 November 1881
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his letter and gives permission to use his observations, although not considering himself a worthy authority. Enlarges upon some of his previous observations.

letters.title: From F. B. Zincke   8 November 1881
letters.summary: Describes the soil in which he found prehistoric tools.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [before 9 November 1881]
letters.summary: Commiserates on news of Wiesner and experiment on transmission of heliotropism. Asks whether he should review book forNature.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [9 November 1881]
letters.summary: Tells some of his observations on root cells. Has thought of three good experiments to oppose Julius von Wiesner.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   9 November [1881]
letters.summary:
Comments on two letters received from W. F. P. Pfeffer [13425,13464] who thinks Julius Wiesner’s view that light, etc. acts directly on plants is wrong.

Is frantic over the number of letters received about worms; feels the enthusiasm of the reception ofEarthwormsis laughable.

Is confounded byEuphorbiarootlets and has re-examined the effect of carbonate of ammonia.

letters.title: To A. E. Graves   9 November 1881
letters.summary: Cannot explain worm behaviour observed by AEG. Cannot believe in power of vision. Inclined to speculate on capacity for distinguishing damp air.

letters.title: From Johann August Georg Edmund (Edmund) Mojsisovics von Mojsvár   10 November 1881
letters.deprecated: Johann August Georg Edmund (Edmund) Mojsisovics von Mojsvár
letters.sender: Johann August Georg Edmund (Edmund) Mojsisovics von Mojsvár
letters.summary: Thanks forEarthworms.

letters.title: To J. F. Galbraith 11 November 1881
letters.summary: Explains that the animals in the cask cannot have developed from the wheat.

letters.title: To Archibald Geikie   11 November 1881
letters.summary: Interested in the fossil scorpions found by AG in the Lower Carboniferous strata of Scotland. Hopes further searches will yield more land animals and offers to subscribe funds to such a search if it falls outside the Geological Survey’s work.

letters.title: From Julius Wiesner   11 November 1881
letters.summary: CD has misunderstood his views on heliotropism. Agrees that his experiments on the movement of root tips are weak. Will conduct further research. Thinks that since mechanical conception of botany is not so widespread, those who agree with CD probably are in majority.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   12 November [1881]
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: JL’s sentence about glaciation will do excellently. Is glad JL thought about dimorphism of butterflies.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   12 November 1881
letters.summary: Discusses GJR’s controversy with the Duke [of Argyll] concerning Roux’s book [Der Kampf der Theile im Organismus(1881)].

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   12 November [1881]
letters.summary: Progress of his and Frank Darwin’s work; "all natural science seems now to depend on section-cutting".

letters.title: From J. C. Clutterbuck   13 November 1881
letters.summary: Describes earthworms moving to the surface to escape moles.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   13 November 1881
letters.summary:
Is experimenting with effect of ammonium carbonate on chlorophyll and roots, but finds the results confusing.

Julius von Wiesner has published a book reinterpreting CD’s observations inMovement in plants[see13422].

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   14 November [1881]
letters.summary: Forwards a letter from W. F. P. Pfeffer, who opposes some of Julius Wiesner’s notions on plant movements.

letters.title: From Archibald Geikie   14 November 1881
letters.summary: Thanks CD for offer of assistance in exploration of Eskdale beds. Describes finds of scorpions and unusual amphibians.

letters.title: From J. P. Taylor   14 November 1881
letters.summary: Thinks CD overestimates earthworms’ role in creating mould. Gives some observations on worms and questions about their breeding habits.

letters.title: From R. S. Bartleet   15 November 1881
letters.summary:
Has readEarthworms.

Wonders if CD has studied gnats; inquires about their apparently useless hovering over one spot for hours.

letters.title: To S. H. Vines   15 November 1881
letters.summary:
More observations of the radicles of germinating seeds ofEuphorbia peplusfor appearance of milk-tubes.

Comments on J. v. Wiesner’s and W. F. P. Pfeffer’s views and criticism of his experiments.

letters.title: From Francis Darwin   [after 14 November 1881]
letters.summary: Thanks for two letters from Pfeffer. Will return translation of Pfeffer and send a letter from Elfring. Looking forward to working on "antiWiesner" experiments. Will return on 26th or 27th.

letters.title: To J. P. Taylor   16 November 1881
letters.summary: Elaborates on the theories propounded in his recently published work [Earthworms], describing the reproductive system of worms and the absorption of organic matter in the soil. [See13483.]

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   16 November 1881
letters.summary: Would be grateful for someEuphorbiaspecies for examination of the roots. "The subject is by no means worth all the labour I am bestowing on it, but I cannot bear to be beaten."

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   17 November 1881
letters.summary:
Sends an agreement for his signature and forwarding to Patterson & Bloxham.

Hears that James Challis [Plumian Professor of Astronomy, Cambridge] is on the point of death. Believes he has a good chance to succeed him; sends a list of the electors.

letters.title: To L. T. Brunton   19 November 1881
letters.summary:
Wishes to contribute to subscription to pay legal expenses of David Ferrier [in vivisection prosecution].

Comments on physiological papers.

letters.title: From Adolphe Damseaux   19 November 1881
letters.summary: AD asks CD’s advice on possible causes of a decline in the Belgian hop crop.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   19 November [1881]
letters.summary: Tremendously interested by GHD’s news [about the Plumian Professorship at Cambridge]. Suggests he get William Thomson to write to the electors.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [20 November 1881]
letters.summary:
Writes of Challis’ health

and of other matters of family interest.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   20 November [1881]
letters.summary: Cannot read signature on letter sent via JDH from Lima.

letters.title: To K. M. Lyell   20 November 1881
letters.summary:
Thanks forLife, letters and journals of Sir Charles Lyell, Bart.(K. M. Lyell ed. 1881), but he has already ordered a copy. Can he send the ordered copy to her to give to another, or can he send it on her behalf?

...

letters.title: To W. T. Thiselton-Dyer   20 November [1881?]
letters.summary: Magnificent supply ofEuphorbiaearrived safely.

letters.title: From Francisco d’Arruda Furtado   21 November 1881
letters.summary:
The statues on which the egg-cases were found were perfectly clean and had never been painted.

Reports on fossilised leaf-prints he has found on the island. Found no seeds or land shells at the site.

letters.title: From T. L. Brunton   21 November 1881
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for his offer of assistance to David Ferrier.

Discusses CD’s earthworm book.

Tonsils in man as rudimentary organs.

letters.title: From Frederick Capes   21 November 1881
letters.summary: Reports extract of spurge [Euphorbia] killing earthworms.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin 21 November 1881
letters.summary: Financial matters; executing EAD’s will; pleased to hear news about Prof. Challis.

letters.title: From George King   21 November 1881
letters.summary:
Thanks forEarthworms.

Glad CD liked theDischidiadrawing. GK wishes he could see it in the wild to study its habits and those of the insects that visit it.

letters.title: From W. C. MIntosh   21 November 1881
letters.summary: Asks for a testimonial for the Chair of Natural History at Edinburgh.

letters.title: From W. P. Snow   21 November 1881
letters.summary:
Is planning a revised edition of hisCruise in Tierra del Fuego[1857], and finds his opinions on the natives the reverse of CD’s.

Hopes he may call some time.

letters.title: To W. C. MIntosh   [after 21 November 1881]
letters.summary: Must refuse WCM’s request for a testimonial as he has already recommended E. Ray Lankester for the post.

letters.title: From Thomas Birkett   22 November 1881
letters.summary: Has readEarthworms; would like to know if his friend’s belief is true that worms, if not destroyed, eat the tender rootlets of grass.

letters.title: To T. L. Brunton   22 November 1881
letters.summary: Writes to ask how much he should subscribe to fund for David Ferrier.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [22 November 1881]
letters.summary: Thinks William Thomson will support him [for Plumian Professorship at Cambridge].

letters.title: To W. P. Snow   22 November 1881
letters.summary:
Hopes WPS may succeed with a new edition of his book [see13495]. WPS saw so much more of the natives of Tierra del Fuego than did CD and his opinion of them is probably right.

Discourages him from visiting.

letters.title: To S. H. Vines   22 November 1881
letters.summary: Rows of cells with granular matter following treatment with carbonate of ammonia also found in white and young rootlets of common zonalPelargonium. Differs slightly fromEuphorbiain that 2, 3, 4, or 5 rows often adjoin. CD wrong in supposing that these rows of cells were connected with lacticiferous ducts ("milk-tubes"). Root hairs arise exclusively from rows of cells without brownish granular matter. It appears that certain rows of cells with hairs are absorbant [absorbent!?] and store matter of some kind. This is a new view of the structure and function of rootlets. Francis Darwin will soon set up the salt solution to make the experiment SHV recommends.

letters.title: To W. R. Browne   23 November 1881
letters.summary: Regrets that he cannot write the requested journal article on comparative anatomy.

letters.title: To Frederick Capes   23 November 1881
letters.summary: Discusses milk ducts inEuphorbia[spurge].

letters.title: To P. P. C. Hoek   23 November 1881
letters.summary:
Thanks him for magnificent work on Pycnogonida [The zoology of the voyage of H. M. S. Challenger, vol. 3, part 10 (1881)].

Is delighted that he is undertaking the Cirripedia [1883–4].

letters.title: To A. R. Wallace   23 November 1881
letters.summary: At Mrs Lyell’s request, passes on a spare copy of K. M. Lyell ed. 1881.

letters.title: To ?   23 November 1881
letters.summary: Sends copies ofVariation,Descent, andJournal of researchesfrom "the library of my late brother".

letters.title: From Charles Reinwald   24 November 1881
letters.summary:
Concerning French translation ofEarthworms

andMovement in plants.

letters.title: From S. H. Vines   24 November [1881]
letters.summary: Will observe the granular cells in roots, to investigate CD’s observation that root-hairs spring from cells that are not granular. Hopes they may be soluble in [carbonate of ammonia] solution.

letters.title: From G. Wegner   24 November 1881
letters.summary: Reports observing two wheat flowers that bent towards each other and pressed together in a "quick throbbing motion".

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   25 November [1881]
letters.summary: Last issue ofNaturehas made him "awfully proud". [See R. S. Ball, "A glimpse through the corridors of time",Nature25 (1881): 79–82.]

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   26 November 1881
letters.summary: Sends some additions and corrections he has made in the 5th thousand, [ofEarthworms] now being printed.

letters.title: From T. L. Brunton   27 November 1881
letters.summary: Writes regarding subscription to set up the Science Defence and Advancement Fund to protect investigators from anti-vivisectionists and to promote knowledge of the purpose and importance of vivisection.

letters.title: From E. T. Crabbe   27 November 1881
letters.summary: Offers for sale a MS of lost Erasmus Darwin poem on materialism [Francis Darwin note: "Swindle"].

letters.title: From H. N. Moseley   27 November 1881
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for support in his election as Linacre Professor at Oxford.

J. Y. Buchanan, of theChallenger, says deep-sea red mud is fine because, like CD’s vegetable mould, it has been digested by worms and echinoderms.

Visited by John MacNeile Price, the son of CD’s friend from Chile, Mr Price; the son is now Surveyor General of Hong Kong.

letters.title: To S. H. Vines   27 November 1881
letters.summary: Describes experiment in whichEuphorbiaandDrosophyllumroots were exposed to ammonium carbonate solution. Asks SHV’s opinion.

letters.title: To E. F. Gladwin   28 November 1881
letters.summary: Hopes EFG pursues more worthy object than collecting autographs.

letters.title: From J. C. Clutterbuck   29 November 1881
letters.summary: Sends specimen of soil and buried clay.

letters.title: To Messrs. Asher   29 November [1881]
letters.summary: Instructions to send parcel to Orpington Station, S. E. R.

letters.title: To Dorothy Nevill   29 November 1881
letters.summary: Has much pleasure in signing the little book; is glad his book on earthworms interested her.

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   29 November 1881
letters.summary: BJS is looking forward to reading the life of Lyell [K. M. Lyell,Life, letters and journals of Sir Charles Lyell, 2 vols. (1881)].

letters.title: To J. C. Clutterbuck   [after 29 November 1881]
letters.summary: Draft letter for Francis Darwin to write to JCC thanking him for the soil specimen.

letters.title: From Benjamin Atkinson Irving   30 November 1881
letters.summary: Reports on the greener grass and the worm-castings found on the lines, which contain lime, of tennis courts.

letters.title: To Hugo de Vries   December 1881
letters.summary: Thanks for HdeV’s letter, which is a great relief to him.

letters.title: To George Warde Norman   1 December 1881
letters.summary: "I should be a strange creature if I did not feel real pleasure in seeing you." Recalls GWN’s kindness and assistance over forty years.

letters.title: From James Paget 1 December 1881
letters.summary: Thanks forEarthworms. Is going to Nice for a few weeks to recuperate.

letters.title: From J. F. Simpson   1 December 1881
letters.summary: Thanks CD for offer of a copy ofEarthworms.

letters.title: To B. J. Sulivan   1 December 1881
letters.summary:
Sends his subscription for the adopted Fuegian [Jemmy FitzRoy Button].

Feels very old and wishes he could be idle but finds himself miserable without any daily work.

Is reading Lyell’s biography [K. M. Lyell (1881)].

letters.title: To James Paget   3 December 1881
letters.summary: Is delighted with JP’s article on vivisection ["Vivisection: its pains and its uses, No. 1",Nineteenth Century10 (1881): 920–30]. CD is "boiling over with indignation on the subject".

letters.title: From F. G. M. Powell   3 December 1881
letters.summary: Expresses his admiration for CD and his work.

letters.title: From B. J. Sulivan   3 December 1881
letters.summary: BJS’s son has seen six Fuegians being exhibited in Berlin; BJS hopes that they might be bought from their master and returned to Tierra del Fuego.

letters.title: To F. G. M. Powell   [after 3 December 1881]
letters.summary: Thanks FGMP for his sympathetic and very kind letter.

letters.title: From A. Hall   5 December 1881
letters.summary: Vegetable mould covering paving-stones in Oxfordshire lanes accumulated over 14 or 16 centuries.

letters.title: From E. B. Wilson   5 December 1881
letters.summary: Gives case of a mollusc,Scyllaea, which mimics theSargassumon which it lives.

letters.title: From J. V. Carus   6 December 1881
letters.summary: Lists errata inEarthworms, which he is translating.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [6 December 1881]
letters.summary: Asks whether he is to give a gratuity of "cinquanta lire sterling" to the cook at 6 Queen Anne St.

letters.title: To Arthur Hall   6 December 1881
letters.summary: Case of Roman roads would have been worth investigating forEarthworms. [See13531.]

letters.title: From J.D. Brander   7 December [1881]
letters.summary:
Comments on CD’sEarthworms.

Discusses breeding habits of salmon; will the reliance on autumn-breeding fish to produce young lead to the decline of the number of spring- and summer-breeders in the rivers?

letters.title: To J. V. Carus   8 December 1881
letters.summary: Thanks JVC for his corrections of "stupid errata" [inEarthworms]. Explains, in answer to JVC’s query, that he has used the word "humus" as the equivalent of vegetable mould.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   8 December 1881
letters.summary: Discusses subscription for Grant Allen. Suggests present of microscope.

letters.title: From F. B. Zincke   8 December 1881
letters.summary: Thanks CD for copy ofEarthworms.

letters.title: From D. J. Wintle   [before 9] December 1881
letters.summary: Earthworms leave their burrows on hearing rifle volleys.

letters.title: To Horace Darwin   9 December 1881
letters.summary: CD is glad birth [of Erasmus Darwin] is over and that Ida has borne it so well.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin 9 December 1881
letters.summary: Financial paperwork; pleased at news of Horace and Ida Darwin’s baby, Erasmus.

letters.title: To Patrick Geddes   9 December 1881
letters.summary:
PG’s article inEncyclopaedia Britannicawonderfully well done ["Insectivorous plants", 9th ed., 13: 134–40].

Admires PG’s researches on chlorophyll in animal kingdom ["Sur la chlorophylle animale",Arch. Zool. Exp. Gen.8 (1880): 51–8].

letters.title: From H. N. Moseley   9 December 1881
letters.summary: He would support a foreigner for Professorship of Botany as CD suggests. W. Thiselton Dyer is proposing [W. C.?] Williamson, whom HNM considers a disaster.

letters.title: From Edward Parfitt   9 December 1881
letters.summary:
Thanks forEarthworms[2d ed.].

Sends several of his papers.

letters.title: To D. J. Wintle   9 December 1881
letters.summary: DJW’s facts are new and curious. CD has other reasons to believe he was wrong in doubting the effect on earthworms of beating the ground.

letters.title: From Grant Allen   10 December [1881]
letters.summary:
Thanks for copy ofOriginwith its flattering inscription.

Hopes some day to have leisure to do original research.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   10 December [1881]
letters.summary: Declines to provide testimonial for J. C. Ewart, since he has already done so for Lankester. Was also asked by W. C. M’Intosh.

letters.title: From Heinrich Simon   10 December 1881
letters.summary: Remarks on the sinking of piles of cannonballs in old forts; presumably a consequence of earthworm activity.

letters.title: From M. W. Tanner   12 December 1881
letters.summary: Earthworms appear on surface after a heavy storm.

letters.title: To Francis Darwin   [13 or 20 December 1881]
letters.summary: Andrew Clark finds that CD’s heart is perfectly right.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin 14 December 1881
letters.summary: Paperwork relating to 6 Queen Anne Street, London.

letters.title: From W. W. Cheshire   15 December 1881
letters.summary: Sends photograph of a wild goose that survived being shot by a nine-inch arrowhead.

letters.title: From James Geikie   15 December 1881
letters.summary: Seeks a testimonial for the Chair of Geology at Edinburgh.

letters.title: From W. F. Stanley   15 December 1881
letters.summary:
Sends CD his book of experimental work on fluids [Experimental researches into the properties and motions of fluids(1881)].

Draws his attention to a particular passage on liquid behaviour which, he speculates, may relate to the form of some lower plants.

letters.title: From G. W. Turner   15 December 1881
letters.summary: Requests autograph.

letters.title: To James Geikie   [after 15 December 1881]
letters.summary: Testimonial letter stating his belief in JG’s suitability for the Chair of Geology at Edinburgh.

letters.title: From Nicholas Krohn   16 December 1881
letters.summary: Perchloride of mercury applied to his lawn destroyed thousands of earthworms, but ruined the grass.

letters.title: To A. P. Tilt   16 December 1881
letters.summary: Explains he was not a member of the congress [7th International Medical Conference, August 1881], and hence it would be inappropriate to introduce his likeness into the correspondent’s composition.

letters.title: To T. L. Brunton   17 December 1881
letters.summary: Feels he should decline nominal presidency of the proposed Science Defence Association.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   17 December 1881
letters.summary:
Benjamin D. Jackson will edit new Steudel’sNomenclator.

JDH’s impressions of Lyell’sLife and letters, edited by Mrs K. M. Lyell [1881].

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   17 [December 1881]
letters.summary: Asks him to visit.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   18 [December 1881]
letters.summary: Can FG call on Monday evening?

letters.title: To [Nicholas Krohn]   18 December 1881
letters.summary: "The number of worms in your garden is astonishing … it will be an interesting observation, how soon the land is again stocked with worms, & whether the grass grows better before this happens. – I neglected to observe whether worms distruct [disturb?] the roots of grasses. – You will probably be able to borrow … my bookOn the Formation of Vegetable Mould… in which … you will find a good deal about the natural history of worms."

letters.title: From C. V. Riley   18 December 1881
letters.summary: Concurs in CD’s criticism of Thomas Meehan [see13360].

letters.title: From Francis Warner   18 December 1881
letters.summary: Sends CD a pamphlet on muscular conditions expressive of states of the brain [Brain3 (1881): 478–95; 4 (1882): 190–206]. [CD’s notes are for his reply.]

letters.title: From James Geikie   19 December 1881
letters.summary: Thanks CD for his support.

letters.title: To Albert Günther   19 December 1881
letters.summary: Asks how he can obtain a Museum post for his late brother’s butler, F. W. Surman.

letters.title: From V. L. Seoane   19 December 1881
letters.summary: Asks CD for some references to aid his work. [Brief annotations for a reply by CD.]

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   19 December 1881
letters.summary:
Waxy secretion or "bloom" on leaves.

FM’s article onCrotalaria.

letters.title: From G. S. Owen   19 December 1881
letters.summary:
Observations on rattlesnakes

and on tunnels built by Brazilian ants.

letters.title: From P. H. Pye-Smith   19 December 1881
letters.summary: Urges CD to write on vivisection forNineteenth Centuryor suggest a competent scientific author. Forming an association to forward interests of vivisectionists.

letters.title: To F. W. Surman   19 December [1881]
letters.summary: Asks for personal information about FWS, former employee of E. A. Darwin. [FWS is applying for position at British Museum.]

letters.title: To CD’s executors & other children   20 December 1881
letters.deprecated: Elizabeth (Bessy) (Lizzy) DarwinFrancis DarwinGeorge Howard DarwinHorace DarwinLeonard DarwinWilliam Erasmus DarwinHenrietta Emma DarwinHenrietta Emma Litchfield
letters.recipient: Elizabeth (Bessy) (Lizzy) DarwinFrancis DarwinGeorge Howard DarwinHorace DarwinLeonard DarwinWilliam Erasmus DarwinHenrietta Emma DarwinHenrietta Emma Litchfield
letters.summary: Has promised to pay Hooker about £250 annually "for the formation of a perfect MS catalogue of all known plants [Index Kewensis]".

letters.title: From Albert Günther   21 December 1881
letters.summary: Explains how to go about getting an Attendantship at the British Museum.

letters.title: To [N. A. E. Nordenskiold]   21 December 1881
letters.summary: Acknowledges presentation copy of publication about theVegavoyage [The voyage of the Vega(1881)].

letters.title: From P. H. Pye-Smith   21 December 1881
letters.summary: Difficulty of using concrete instances of the benefit of vivisection in medical science.

letters.title: To M. G. Retzius   21 December 1881
letters.summary: CD again has the pleasure of accepting another grand present,Das Gehörorgan der Wirbelthiere(1881).

letters.title: To W. F. Stanley   21 December 1881
letters.summary: Comments on WFRS’s book [Properties and motions of fluids(1881)].

letters.title: To E. B. Wilson   21 December 1881
letters.summary: Thanks EBW for his curious case of mimicry inScyllaea, which parallels that observed by Albert Günther inHippocampus.

letters.title: To Albert Günther   22 December [1881]
letters.summary: Discusses position [at British Museum]. "My case is hopeless as my man [F. W. Surman] is 31 years old."

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   22 December 1881
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for his endowment of new Steudel’sNomenclator[later to becomeIndex Kewensis].

K. White’s gruesome ballad "Gondoline" frightened JDH as a child.

letters.title: To F. W. Surman   22 December 1881
letters.summary: Case is hopeless since applicant [for position at British Museum] must not be over thirty years old.

letters.title: From A. C. Horner   23 December 1881
letters.summary: Detailed criticism ofEarthworms.

letters.title: From Caroline Kennard   26 December 1881
letters.summary: The author of a paper on the inferiority of women has cited CD’sOriginas her authority. CK wishes to know if she has satisfactorily represented CD’s views.

letters.title: From W. P. Marshall   26 December 1881
letters.summary: The Birmingham Natural History Society found the soft coralVirgularia mirabiliswhile dredging near Oban, Scotland. They resembleBeaglespecimens from Bahia Blanca, which draw themselves into the mud when touched.

letters.title: To V. Lopez de Seoane   27 December 1881
letters.summary:
CD is unable to give the desired information relating to embryology of the Vertebrata. He advises the procuring of F. M. Balfour’sComparative embryology, in two volumes [1880–1], which he believes to be the most valuable biological work in many years.

Hopes to find time to read VLS’s essays.

Discussion of the problem of naming species. [See13568.]

letters.title: To John Price   27 December 1881
letters.summary:
Congratulates JP on marriage of daughter.

Consoles him on his poor health.

Death of Mrs Smith a severe loss.

letters.title: From J. J. Weir   27 December 1881
letters.summary: Discusses mule’s resemblance to parents.

letters.title: To Walter Baily   28 December 1881
letters.summary: Statement about a beetle-hunting worm is new to CD.

letters.title: From H. C. Sorby   28 December 1881
letters.summary:
Discusses colour changes of plant colouring material.

Is doing much marine work from his yacht; asks whether CD has any suggestions for profitable observations.

letters.title: From A. de Souza Correa, Brazilian Legation   28 December 1881
letters.deprecated: A. de Souza CorreaSecretary, Brazilian Legation
letters.sender: A. de Souza CorreaSecretary, Brazilian Legation
letters.summary: Forwards observations from the Baron de Villa Franca relating to sugar-cane culture.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin 29 December 1881
letters.summary: North East Railway Consols.

letters.title: From W. P. Marshall   29 December 1881
letters.summary: Thanks for reference to A. von Kölliker’s monograph on Alcyonaria [Anatomisch-systematische Beschreibung der Alcyonarien(1872)].

letters.title: To J. J. Weir   29 December 1881
letters.summary:
Comments on JJW’s observations on mule

and hermaphroditism in hybrid moths.

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   30 December 1881
letters.summary: New Year’s greetings.

letters.title: From Horatio Piggot   31 December 1881
letters.summary: Slugs do no damage to his flowering plants.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   [1882?]
letters.summary: Encloses a letter from a Mr Hill on some [unspecified] legal matter.

letters.title: From F. Müller   1 January 1882
letters.summary:
In answer to CD’s query, FM thinks the seeds he sent were those of the sensitiveMimosa.

Reports his observations of movement of leaves ofBauhinia grandifloraandB. brasiliensis. They do not "sleep" in hot weather.

Sends some seeds ofPontederiahe had fertilised.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   1 January [1882]
letters.summary: Describes grafting experiment of Baron de Villa Franca, which produced new varieties of sugar-cane. Encloses related documents.

letters.title: To Grant Allen   2 January 1882
letters.summary:
Thanks GA for his article ["The daisy’s pedigree",Cornhill Mag.44 (1881): 168–81].

The evolutionary argument that petals are transformed stamens is "striking and apparently valid". Doubts petals are naturally yellow.

Wallace’s "generalization about much modified parts being splendidly coloured" is also dubious except as both are caused by sexual selection.

letters.title: To V. O. Kovalevsky   2 January [1882]
letters.summary: Thanks VOK for a photograph and his New Year wishes.

letters.title: From A. de Souza Correa, Secretary to the Brazilian Legation   2 January 1882
letters.deprecated: A. de Souza CorreaSecretary, Brazilian Legation
letters.sender: A. de Souza CorreaSecretary, Brazilian Legation
letters.summary: Thanks CD for letter for Villa Franca. Would be happy if CD published the Baron’s observations in an English scientific journal.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   3 January [1882]
letters.summary: Asks GJR’s opinion about grafting experiments on sugar-cane carried out by the Baron [de Villa Franca].

letters.title: From H. C. Sorby   3 January 1882
letters.summary: Reports the inconclusive results of some experiments he has been doing for CD [related to plant colouring material?].

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin 4 January 1882
letters.summary: Has sold London & South Western Railway stock and has purchased Great Western stock.

letters.title: To Fritz Müller   4 January 1882
letters.summary:
On F. M. Balfour.

Effects of ammonium carbonate on roots.

FM’sPontederiacase is very curious.

letters.title: To Theodor Eimer   6 January [1882]
letters.summary: Is obliged for TE’s paper on the wall lizard and another paper.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   6 January 1882
letters.summary:
Accepts GJR’s offer to prepare sugar-cane paper for publication [Villa Franca and Glass, "New varieties of sugar-cane",Proc. Linn. Soc. Lond.(1880–2): 30–1]. Suggests introduction and outline.

Agrees with GJR on microscope for Grant Allen.

letters.title: From J. F. Simpson   7 January 1882
letters.summary: Has readEarthworms; discusses parts and encloses a list of errata. Writes of worm-castings, describing his observations; speculates on the variation in their distribution under different conditions.

letters.title: From Hyacinth Hooker   7 January 1882
letters.summary: Thanks CD for financial assistance for Mr Fitch and his wife.

letters.title: To Darwin Children   8 January 1882
letters.deprecated: Elizabeth (Bessy) (Lizzy) DarwinFrancis DarwinGeorge Howard DarwinHorace DarwinLeonard DarwinWilliam Erasmus DarwinHenrietta Emma DarwinHenrietta Emma Litchfield
letters.recipient: Elizabeth (Bessy) (Lizzy) DarwinFrancis DarwinGeorge Howard DarwinHorace DarwinLeonard DarwinWilliam Erasmus DarwinHenrietta Emma DarwinHenrietta Emma Litchfield
letters.summary: Advises his children as to how some money will be distributed among them.

letters.title: From J. W. Judd   8 January 1882
letters.summary: Praises G. H. Darwin’s letter ["On the geological importance of the tides",Nature25 (1882): 213–14] which criticises the use made of George Darwin’s views by Robert Ball ["A glimpse through the corridors of time",Nature25 (1881): 79–82, 103–7]. JWJ argues from the fineness of Cambrian sediments against Ball’s intensification of geological forces. Massive Carboniferous river deltas also contradict Ball’s excessively high tides.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin 9 January [1882]
letters.summary: CD’s division of his surplus income; fire engines; Sara Darwin’s relatives; GHD’s paper inNature.

letters.title: From J. H. Gilbert   9 January 1882
letters.summary:
Thanks CD forEarthworms.

Discusses the problem of accounting for difference between nitrogen in permanent grassland and ordinary arable soil. Finds castings of earthworms rich in nitrogen. Asks CD if his observations enable him to explain the source. If from below top-soil, it would be a considerable manuring.

letters.title: From Gottlieb Haberlandt   9 January 1882
letters.summary:
Sends his paper on the comparative anatomy of the assimilatory tissue systems of plants [Jahrb. Wiss. Bot.13 (1882): 74–188]. This work has made clear to him how CD’s principles produce rich results when applied to plant anatomy.

Also sends a paper on the difficult problem of the gulf between cryptogamic and phanerogamic plants in the evolutionary development, in order to present another proof of the continuity of the phylogenetic development of the plant kingdom.

letters.title: To C. A. Kennard   9 January 1882
letters.summary: Thinks that "women though generally superior to men [in] moral qualities are inferior intellectually". Believes that men and women may have been aboriginally equal in this respect but that to regain equality women would have to "become as regular ""bread-winners"" as are men". Suspects the education of children and "the happiness of our homes" would greatly suffer in that case.

letters.title: To T. H. Farrer   10 January 1882
letters.summary: Requests that THF forward an enclosure if he thinks it proper. James Torbitt’s blunder in using the pollen of a diseased variety accounts for the bad varieties raised last year.

letters.title: To James Torbitt   10 January 1882
letters.summary: CD’s gardener reports that potatoes were not attacked by disease, but yield was not good. Noble of JT to plan the return of subscriptions if trade continues to improve.

letters.title: To F. J. Cohn   11 January 1882
letters.summary: Thanks FJC for presentation copy [ofDie Pflanze(1882)].

letters.title: From Raphael Meldola   11 January 1882
letters.summary: Wishes to borrow Weismann’s pamphlet on the Daphnidae [? "Über einige neue oder unvollkommen gekannte Daphniden",Verh. Freiburger Naturforsch. Ges.7 (1877)]. Is preparing an essay on "alternation of generations".

letters.title: To J. H. Gilbert   12 January 1882
letters.summary:
Quantity of nitrogen in castings surprises CD.

Comments on papers: [J. B. Lawes and J. H. Gilbert, "Results of experiments on mixed herbage, pt 1",Philos. Trans. R. Soc. Lond.171 (1880): 289–416; Gilbert, Lawes and M. T. Masters, "pt 2: The botanical results",Philos. Trans. R. Soc. Lond.173 (1882): 1181–413].

Has never made sections to see how deep worms burrow – five or six feet is probable. Wishes the problem had arisen when he made his observations.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   12 January 1882
letters.summary: B. D. Jackson’s plan for new SteudelNomenclatorapproved. JDH asks for CD’s cheque.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   12 January 1882
letters.summary:
Thanks forScience and culture[1881].

Refers to "Automatism" ["On the hypothesis that animals are automata"], wishing THH could review himself and answer himself and thus go onad infinitumto the joy and instruction of the world.

letters.title: From F. B. Sanborn   12 January 1882
letters.summary:
Sends CD some of the [American Social Science] Association’s publications; asks if they may enrol him as a corresponding member. They have printed CD’s letter to Mrs Talbot

and also his paper fromMind(1877) ["Biographical sketch of an infant"].

letters.title: From Leslie Stephen   12 January 1882
letters.summary:
Discusses a lectureship at Aberdeen

and a recent visit to Down.

letters.title: From T. H. Farrer   13 January 1882
letters.summary: Potatoes [from Torbitt experiment] sent him for eating were very poor. Those for seed produced abundantly, but have not resisted disease better than other kinds that Payne [his gardener] has grown.

letters.title: From William Trelease   14 January 1882
letters.summary: Sends article on dimorphism inOxalis violacea[Am. Nat.16 (1882): 13–19].

letters.title: From J. F. Simpson   15 January 1882
letters.summary:
Encloses an extract (from theBayswater Chronicle[missing]), which is part of an ongoing disagreement in which JFS is involved.

Has read some references to CD’s hypothesis on music and offers a MS by himself which deals with the subject.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin 16 January [1882]
letters.summary: Has ordered a tin of Somerset Mixture snuff for CD.

letters.title: From A. B. Mitford   17 January 1882
letters.summary: The Secretary to the First Commissioner of Her Majesty’s Works thanks CD for providing the funds for a new edition ofSteudel’s Nomenclator[Index Kewensis].

letters.title: From William Ogle   17 January 1882
letters.summary: Sends a translation of Aristotle’sDe partibus animaliumand imagines that if the old teleologist were alive CD would convince him of his errors.

letters.title: To William Ogle   17 January 1882
letters.summary: Thanks WO for gift of his translation [Aristotle’sDe partibus animalium]. Suspects the introduction would interest him more than the text "notwithstanding that he [Aristotle] was such a wonderful old fellow".

letters.title: From Michael Foster   18 January 1882
letters.summary: Responds to CD’s query about the sensitivity of plants in light and darkness and Julius Wiesner’s assumptions [inDas Bewegungsvermögen der Pflanzen(1881)].

letters.title: From V. O. Kovalevsky   18 January [1882]
letters.summary: Trying to get some Darwinians into the Institut de France.

letters.title: From J. D. Hooker   19 January 1882
letters.summary: Politics at Kew lead [led!?] to a letter of thanks to CD from the First Commissioner for his gift.

letters.title: From Melchior Neumayr   19 January 1882
letters.summary:
Thanks forEarthworms.

Sends preferred address.

letters.title: From W. C. Brooks   20 January [1882]
letters.summary: Has just read CD’s book on worms and is finding tower-like worm-casts, as CD described, in Alpes-Maritimes. Relates case of garden worms and moles.

letters.title: To J. D. Hooker   20 January 1882
letters.summary: CD sends cheque for £250 [see13620].

letters.title: From J. D. Kendall   20 January 1882
letters.summary: Suggests that the tendency of the left arm to move with the right leg (and vice versa) during walking is a rudiment of quadrupedal locomotion and thus bears on the descent of man.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   20 January 1882
letters.summary: Prefers to make the present of microscope at once [to Grant Allen].

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   21 January 1882
letters.summary: Asks GHD to send a copy of his "paper on the moon" [probablyPhilos. Trans. R. Soc. Lond.171 (1880): 713–891] to V. O. Kovalevsky.

letters.title: To John Whittaker Ellis   21 January 1882
letters.sender: Charles Robert DarwinArchibald Campbell TaitHenry Edward ManningAnthony Ashley-Cooper, 7th earl of ShaftesburyJohn (Bishop of London) JacksonAlfred Nathaniel Holden Curzon, 4th Baron ScarsdaleCharles John Ellicott, Bishop of Gloucester and BristolWilliam Francis Cowper-Temple, Baron Mount-TempleJohn Fielder Mackarness, Bishop of OxfordJames FraserEdmond (Edmond George Petty-Fitzmaurice) FitzmauriceEdward Frederick (Frederick) Leveson-GowerFrancis Wemyss-Charteris-Douglas, Lord ElchoArthur OtwayDonald CurrieJames MartineauHenry RichardSamuel MorleyWilliam St John BrodrickMichael BiddulphJohn James Stewart PerowneBenjamin JowettFrederic William FarrarHenry Donald Maurice SpenceWilliam Page RobertsCharles MagniacJohn Gellibrand HubbardWilliam James Richmond CottonJohn Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron AveburyJames Clarke LawrenceWilliam LawrenceWilliam James Erasmus (Erasmus) WilsonJohn TyndallMatthew ArnoldAlexander McArthurFrederick Andrew InderwickCharles Benjamin Bright McLaren
letters.summary: Asking the lord mayor of London to call a public meeting concerning the persecution of the Jews in Russia.

letters.title: To John Murray   21 January 1882
letters.summary:
Thanks JM for copy ofQuarterly Review, with article on his worm book [Henry Wace, "Darwin on earthworms",Q. Rev.153 (1882): 179–202].

Writer will change his mind on evolution. CD cannot think of any young worker in biology who is not convinced of the truth of evolution, though many believe that natural selection has not done much.

letters.title: From James Sinclair   21 January 1882
letters.summary: JS is proposing to write a detailed history of the polled Aberdeen breed of cattle [James Macdonald and James Sinclair,History of polled Aberdeen or Angus cattle(1882)] and would be grateful for any instances of hornless breeds known to CD; in particular asks his opinion on the cause of the peculiarity.

letters.title: From H. Y. Thompson   21 January 1882
letters.summary: Sends a letter [missing] from a Mr Moorhouse on lapwing behaviour that makes earthworms rise to surface.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [22 January 1882]
letters.summary:
Writes of his work and a paper accepted for publication in thePhilosophical Transactions[? "Stresses caused in the interior of the earth",Philos. Trans. R. Soc. Lond.173 (1883): 187–230].

Gives news of friends.

letters.title: To F. B. Sanborn   22 January 1882
letters.summary: Accepts election as a corresponding member of the American Social Science Association [see13615].

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   [23 January 1882]
letters.summary: Has sent Kovalevsky his major paper on the moon’s motion, with references to others.

letters.title: From G. H. Darwin   23 January 1882
letters.summary:
Encloses letter from R. S. Ball [missing], who has placed reliance on Samuel Haughton’s wild speculations.

Has heard that J. Challis’ health is worse.

letters.title: To Emil Holub   23 January 1882
letters.summary: Thanks EH for gift of 2d ed. of his book of travels [Seven years in South Africa(1881)]. Expresses admiration for EH’s courage and zeal for Science.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   23 [January 1882]
letters.summary:
Discusses present of microscope to Grant Allen.

Mentions sugar-cane paper [by Baron de Villa Franca].

letters.title: From James Williams   24 January 1882
letters.summary: Are the animal and vegetable kingdoms so united as to be indistinguishable?

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin 25 January 1882
letters.summary: Requests CD to sent a cheque for the succession duty on Erasmus Alvey Darwin’s estate.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   25 [January 1882?]
letters.summary: Agrees about Grant Allen affair.

letters.title: From E. G. Evans   27 January [1882]
letters.summary: Reports observations on curious cats that appear to be cat–rabbit hybrids.

letters.title: To E. G. Evans   28 January 1882
letters.summary: Dismisses report of cat–rabbit hybrid.

letters.title: From Emil Holub   28 January 1882
letters.summary: Requests visit to Down before he goes on expedition to South and Central Africa.

letters.title: From C. A. Kennard  28 January 1882
letters.summary: Argues that women are as regular "bread-winners" as men, though generally unrecognised as such, and that they possess the same qualities as men but lack the educational opportunities. Before women can be judged intellectually inferior to men they must share the same environment and opportunities. With "enlightened intellect, united with her wholesome moral nature" woman could help with the "propagation of the best and the survival of the fittest in the human species".

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   28 January 1882
letters.summary:
Agrees to write a page or two on behalf of Donald McAlister.

Declines to write testimonial for J. C. Ewart.

Says if W. C. M’Intosh "were to apply again, I could not refuse to allow him to use again my former testimonial".

letters.title: From H. M. Baynes   30 January 1882
letters.summary: Reports remarkable case of inheritance of one of his habits by his infant son.

letters.title: To D. W. Thompson   [before February 1882]
letters.summary: Is glad to hear that Hermann Müller approves of D’AWT’s translation of his work [Die Befruchtung der Blumen(1873)]; he hopes a publisher may be found for a work of such high value.

letters.title: From Raphael Meldola   31 January 1882
letters.summary: Encloses proof of CD’s prefatory notice for RM’s translation of Weismann; hopes CD might enlarge upon it.

letters.title: From Anthony Rich   1 February 1882
letters.summary: Has observed earthworms drawing pine needles into their burrows.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin 2 February [1882]
letters.summary: Suggested T. G. Bonney contacted CD to confirm story was apocryphal.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   2 February 1882
letters.summary:
Regrets he can add no more to his preface for Weismann’sStudies. Offers donation to aid with publishing expenses.

Thinks RM’s preface is excellent.

letters.title: From Raphael Meldola   3 February 1882
letters.summary: Declines CD’s generous offer of assistance with publishing costs of Weismann’sStudies, but would welcome his help in getting elected to the Royal Society.

letters.title: From F. W. Surman   3 February [1882]
letters.summary: FWS is applying for a position and wants a character reference.

letters.title: To Miss Ashley   [after 3 February 1882]
letters.summary: Testifies to F. W. Surman’s good character and honesty.

letters.title: To ?   4 February 1882
letters.summary: Discusses plate for use in article ["Action of carbonate of ammonia on chlorophyll-bodies",Collected papers2: 256–76].

letters.title: To Emil Holub   4 February 1882
letters.summary:
Thanks EH for book on ornithology of South Africa and for his essays [Beiträge zur Ornithologie Südafrikas von Aug. von Holub und E. Pelzeln(1882)].

Will be pleased to see him when he comes to England.

letters.title: From C. A. T. Rice   4 February 1882
letters.summary: The editor ofNorth American Reviewasks CD to write an article in support of systematic observations of mental development in infants.

letters.title: To Anthony Rich   4 February 1882
letters.summary:
Exchanges news on health.

Thanks AR for his worm observations.

George Darwin’s work is attracting attention; he intends to try for Plumian Professorship at Cambridge. Adds other news of George and of CD’s sons Leonard and William.

CD has finished his microscopic work and has only to write up two papers for the Linnean Society.

letters.title: To S. H. Vines   4 February 1882
letters.summary: CD will put together his notes on the action of carbonate of ammonia on roots in a few days. Asks SHV to send any information he may have, but not to answer if he has none. [See13666.]

letters.title: From T. G. Bonney   5 February 1882
letters.summary: Thanks for writing. Had disbelieved the story. He has seen Dr Hahn’s slides and it is clear that Hahn cannot distinguish between mineral and organic structures.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   5 February 1882
letters.summary: Agrees to propose RM for the Royal Society.

letters.title: From Joseph Hewett   6 February 1882
letters.summary: Can he improve his oat crop by growing home-grown and purchased cereals together?

letters.title: From Henry Johnson 6 February 1882
letters.summary:
Offers CD gift of slab with fossil annelid tracks.

Does CD know geologist who might give lecture in Dudley?

letters.title: From Raphael Meldola   6 February 1882
letters.summary: Thanks for agreeing to propose him for the Royal Society.

letters.title: From S. H. Vines   6 February 1882
letters.summary:
On aggregation of protoplasm in root cells.

Is preparing new edition of Sachs [Text-book of botany, morphological and physical, ed. S. H. Vines, 2d ed. (1882)].

letters.title: From William Horsfall   7 February 1882
letters.summary:
Asks about significance of trilobites for evolution.

Asks if any organism can be designated as animal in one stage and vegetable in another.

letters.title: To H. H. Johnson   7 February 1882
letters.summary:
Thanks for offer of sandstone with annelid tracks.

Suggests J. W. Judd, "most able of living geologists", as lecturer.

letters.title: To Edward Frankland   8 February 1882
letters.summary: Asks EF to sign enclosed certificate if he thinks Raphael Meldola deserves being elected F.R.S. [See13674.] Requests that his note with certificate be passed on to Norman Lockyer.

letters.title: To William Horsfall   8 February 1882
letters.summary:
Does not feel that the occurrence of perfect trilobites in the oldest known fossil-bearing rocks is fatal to evolution, as he does not believe these rocks to be contemporaneous with the first appearance of life.

Locomotive spores of some algae are like animals.

letters.title: To W. E. Darwin 9 February 1882
letters.summary: Writes about WED’s purchasing a house.

letters.title: From Anton Dohrn   9 February 1882
letters.summary:
Birthday congratulations from the Naples Zoological Station. A new physiological department will be constructed. Describes work in progress at the Station.

Sends his paper on teleosteans.

Heard R. Owen read a paper at York [meeting of BAAS]. Owen had views similar to AD’s, but seemed not to be aware of work of others.

letters.title: From Edward Frankland   9 February 1882
letters.summary: Will not support Raphael Meldola’s application to the Royal Society.

letters.title: To A. A. Reade   9 or 13 February 1882
letters.summary: Describes his use of alcohol and tobacco.

letters.title: To Trübner & Co.   9 February [1882]
letters.summary: OrdersInternational scientific dictionary.

letters.title: To G. Church   10 February 1882
letters.summary: Discusses function of bud-scales.

letters.title: ? 10 February 1882
letters.summary: Asks correspondent to sign certificate for Raphael Meldola [as a candidate for Royal Society].

letters.title: From Henry Johnson 11 February 1882
letters.summary: Slab with annelid tracks being sent. Memorandum enclosed describing bed from which it came.

letters.title: From T. L. Brunton   12 February 1882
letters.summary: Writes regarding the form which the proposed Science Defence Association should take and encloses a draft of proposed resolutions.

letters.title: From Max Steffen & six other German students   12 February 1882
letters.deprecated: Steffen, Max , & six other German students
letters.sender: Steffen, Max , & six other German students
letters.summary: Seven German students drink to CD’s health on his 75th [sic] birthday.

letters.title: To W. B. Carpenter   13 February 1882
letters.summary:
Asks WBC for his vote and influence in favour of Albert Dicey at the Athenaeum balloting.

CD feels "as old as Methusalem".

letters.title: To Anton Dohrn   13 February 1882
letters.summary:
Thanks for AD’s letter.

Owen has published a paper on the brain in relation to the mouth ["On the homology of the conario-hypophysial tract",J. Linn. Soc. Lond. (Zool.)16 (1882): 131–49]. CD cannot avoid suspicion that the original idea was borrowed from AD.

F. M. Balfour very ill. His death would be a great loss.

letters.title: From Hugo Schneider   13 February 1882
letters.summary: Birthday congratulations.

letters.title: To Lawson Tait   13 February 1882
letters.summary:
Thanks for the birthday greetings.

"I feel a very old man and my course is nearly run."

letters.title: To John Tyndall   13 February 1882
letters.summary: Asks JT to support Albert Dicey for the Athenaeum.

letters.title: To Lauder Brunton   14 February 1882
letters.summary: Agrees with TLB’s views regarding the constitution of the proposed Science Defence Association.

letters.title: From J. L. Ambrose   15 February 1882
letters.summary: Asks for autographs.

letters.title: To John Collier   16 February 1882
letters.summary:
Thanks JC for the gift of his book [A primer on art(1882)]. Wishes JC could explain why certain lines and figures give pleasure.

Comments on Huxley’s essays on Priestley and [animal] automation [Science and culture and other essays(1881)].

JC’s portrait [of CD] is much admired.

letters.title: To K. M. Lyell   16 February 1882
letters.summary: Offering to send a copy ofKosmoscontaining a short review of herLife, letters and journals of Sir Charles Lyell, Bart.(K. M. Lyell ed. 1881).

letters.title: To Giuseppe Merighi   16 February [1882]
letters.summary: CD’s observations on the geology of S. Africa, which he considers of no value, were published inVolcanic islands.

letters.title: To W. H. Bates   17 February 1882
letters.summary: Asks HWB to sign and return F.R.S. certificate for Raphael Meldola; if he objects to signing, CD will not mention the fact. [Meldola elected F.R.S., June 1886.]

letters.title: To Max Steffen   17 February 1882
letters.summary: CD thanks MS and his fellow German students for their kind birthday wishes.

letters.title: From W. D. Crick   18 February 1882
letters.summary: Has found aDytiscus marginaliswith a small bivalve attached to its leg.

letters.title: From A. H. M. Kepley   20 February 1882
letters.summary: An experienced keeper of house plants assures CD that earthworms do not injure roots.

letters.title: To ? 20 February 1882
letters.summary: Has heard that correspondent is collecting subscriptions for Mrs George Cupples and so he encloses £40.

letters.title: To W. D. Crick   21 February 1882
letters.summary: HisDytiscusfact interesting. Indispensable to know name of shell. Case worth communicating toNature. [See "On dispersal of freshwater bivalves",Collected papers2: 276–8.]

letters.title: From A. G. Dew-Smith   21 February [1882]
letters.summary: F. M. Balfour slept well; doctors think he is improving.

letters.title: From Wilhelm Breitenbach   22 February 1882
letters.summary: Describes his collections and research on Brazilian insects, especially Orthoptera. Comments on insect phylogeny.

letters.title: From John Collier   22 February 1882
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for note on his book on the sense of beauty [A primer on art(1882)].

Views of Huxley and Spencer on consciousness.

letters.title: To ?   22 February 1882
letters.summary: Instructs engraver on illustrations for his paper ["The action of carbonate of ammonia on the roots of certain plants",Collected papers2: 236–56].

letters.title: To Henry Johnson   22 February 1882
letters.summary: Slab with fossil annelid tracks safely arrived.

letters.title: To William Ogle   22 February 1882
letters.summary: Has rarely read anything more interesting than WO’s introduction to his Aristotle translation. Had no notion what a wonderful man Aristotle was. Linnaeus and Cuvier were mere schoolboys compared to him. His ignorance on some points, as on muscles and the means of movement, is curious.

letters.title: To Raphael Meldola   23 February 1882
letters.summary: RM’s application to the Royal Society.

letters.title: To ?   23 February 1882
letters.summary: Asks correspondent to suspend an enclosed certificate [missing].

letters.title: From W. D. Crick   24 February 1882
letters.summary: Has identified the shell, now separated from the beetle. Sends both to CD.

letters.title: To G. H. Darwin   24 February [1882]
letters.summary:
Has sent last week’sNaturewth J. S. Newberry’s paper ["Hypothetical high tides",Nature25 (1882): 357–8]. CD thinks Newberry is right. This week’s issue has a letter against Newberry by Charles Callaway ["Letters to the editor: hypothetical high tides",Nature25 (1882): 385].
