The Archbishop of Canterbury has launched a series by scientists in theContemporary Reviewon what is known and what is theoretical in science. [The series appears to have begun with an article by Robert S. Ball, "The boundaries of astronomy", 41 (1882): 923–41]. CD was asked to participate, but refused.

letters.title: To W. D. Crick   25 February 1882
letters.summary: Asks further questions about shell attached to beetle’s leg.

letters.title: From A. G. Dew-Smith   25 February 1882
letters.summary: F. M. Balfour getting on better in hospital.

letters.title: From A. V. Dicey   25 February 1882
letters.summary: Thanks CD for helping to get him elected to the Athenaeum.

letters.title: From Daniel Mackintosh   25 February 1882
letters.summary: Asks for CD’s opinion on certain theistic ideas. If spontaneous generation from inorganic material is denied, then life must be derived from some eternal being.

letters.title: To ?   26 February 1882
letters.summary:
CD cannot answer his question concerning the death of earthworms. The usual cause is through parasitic larva of a fly. Worms are susceptible to certain poisons from plants.

Glad his book [Earthworms] has interested HHL.

letters.title: From W. T. Van Dyck   27 February 1882
letters.summary: Encloses MS on sexual selection acting on street dogs of Beirut [MS of "On the modification of a race of Syrian street dogs",Proc. Zool. Soc. Lond.25 (1882): 367–70, published with a prefatory notice by CD;Collected papers2: 278–80].

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin 28 February [1882]
letters.summary: Gives information about the Great Western Railway dividend.

letters.title: To Daniel Mackintosh   28 February 1882
letters.summary:
Comments on James Geikie’s ["Intercrossing of erratics",Scottish Naturalist6 (1882): 193–200, 241–54]. Believes JG underrates importance of floating ice in explaining drift deposits.

Comments on origin of life and natural theology.

Recommends William Graham’sThe creed of science[1881].

letters.title: To Ignatius Donnelly   2 March 1882
letters.summary: Thanks ID for a copy of his book,Atlantis[1882], which CD will read with interest but "in a very sceptical spirit".

letters.title: From Adolf Ernst   2 March 1882
letters.summary: Thanks forEarthworms.

letters.title: To John Lubbock   2 March 1882
letters.deprecated: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.recipient: John Lubbock, 4th baronet and 1st Baron Avebury
letters.summary: Letter of introduction for Romilly Allen.

letters.title: From W. D. Crick   3 March 1882
letters.summary: Sends further details about the beetle and mussel sent to CD.

letters.title: From C. B. Plowright   [before 6? March 1882]
letters.summary: Recounts court case brought for damages caused by destruction of earthworms by salt-water flooding of cultivated land. Plaintiff won the case.

letters.title: From J. H. Barrois   6 March [1882]
letters.summary: The French government plan to set up an international laboratory at Villefranche; JB wonders whether CD would express support for the scheme.

letters.title: From Mary A. Peek to C. B. Plowright   6 March 1882
letters.summary: Cannot find papers on 1862 and 1863 lawsuit involving harm to their farm after worms had been killed by a flood.

letters.title: To J. H. Barrois   [after 6 March 1882]
letters.summary: Strongly supports the proposed biological laboratory at Villefranche.

letters.title: From Charles Naudin   8 March 1882
letters.summary:
J. Decaisne has died.

Sends a few rare seeds ofTrifolium resupinatum.

letters.title: From W. D. Crick   9 March 1882
letters.summary: Has found a frog with bivalve attached to hind leg.

letters.title: To W. D. Crick   10 March [1882]
letters.summary: Will send shell by post to British Museum. Will prepare article forNature[see13696].

letters.title: To [W. W. Baxter]   11 March 1882
letters.summary: Orders morphia pills in case of severe pain, which he hopes may never occur.

letters.title: From G. F. Crawte   11 March 1882
letters.summary: Sends an account of a combat between a frog and a worm.

letters.title: To ?   12 March 1882
letters.summary: Thanks for letter and promise to send pamphlet.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin 13 March 1882
letters.summary: Sends a dividend cheque.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin 15 March 1882
letters.summary: News about his dividends.

letters.title: From Andrew Clark   17 March 1882
letters.summary: Twelve "Revised Directions" for CD’s treatment, mainly diet.

letters.title: To W. W. Baxter   18 March [1882]
letters.summary: Orders two bottles of "the simple Antispasmodic" and "the Glycerin Pepsin mixture". Andrew Clark wishes him to commence his physic at once.

letters.title: From P. H. Pye-Smith   18 March 1882
letters.summary: CD invited to [Science Defence Association] meeting at Royal College of Physicians.

letters.title: From J. F. Simpson   18 March 1882
letters.summary: Sends his measurement of an unusually large worm-casting.

letters.title: To The President of the Royal College of Physicians   20 March [1882]
letters.summary: Much regrets the state of his health will prevent his attending the [Science Defence] Association meeting.

letters.title: From Agnes Taylor   20 March [1882]
letters.summary: Seeking contributions to assist the widow of C. T. Beke.

letters.title: To Francis Galton   22 March [1882]
letters.summary: Sends enclosure [missing].

letters.title: To Symington Grieve   22 March 1882
letters.summary: Subject of SG’s essay would be well worth pursuing. CD has long known that stones were transported by floatingFuci, but not that they were dragged along the sea-bottom.

letters.title: To W. D. Crick   23 March 1882
letters.summary: Shell smashed by careless servant. May have beenCyclas cornea. Will send letter toNature.

letters.title: From W. E. Darwin 23 March 1882
letters.summary: News of Great Western Railway dividend; discussion of Leonard Darwin’s ‘exciting news’.

letters.title: From Francis Galton   23 March 1882
letters.summary: Thanks CD for an article [unspecified].

letters.title: From Grant Allen   24 March 1882
letters.summary: CD and other friends who got up fund for GA in 1879 have now bought him a microscope; thanks CD, especially as the idea came from him; plans to take up original observations with it.

letters.title: From W. D. Crick   24 March 1882
letters.summary: According to John Gwyn Jeffreys’ book [British conchology(1862–9)] shell isSphaerium corneum, a synonym ofCyclas cornea.

letters.title: To W. Newberry   24 March 1882
letters.summary: Mechanism of flowers ofMarantahas already been described by F. H. G. Hildebrand and Federico Delpino.

letters.title: From T. H. Huxley   25 March 1882
letters.summary: Concern over CD’s health. Advises him to get one of the cleverer young London doctors to communicate with Andrew Clark. Only way out of difficulties with Clark.

letters.title: From G. C. Wallich   25 March 1882
letters.summary: In a forthcoming lecture GCW will dispute Haeckel onProtistaand his statement that spontaneous generation is necessary to complete evolution as a doctrine. Wishes to confirm his understanding that CD has nowhere expressed himself on the "origin of life", and has considered only the manner of succession.

letters.title: To W. D. Crick   26 March 1882
letters.summary: Will send letter toNatureabout shell [attached to beetle]. Will use old name ofCyclas.

letters.title: From Agnes Taylor   26 March [1882]
letters.summary: Formal letter of thanks for contribution to Mrs C. T. Beke.

letters.title: From William Trelease   26 March 1882
letters.summary: Believes heterostyly could be produced by artificial selection.

letters.title: To Patrick Geddes   27 March 1882
letters.summary: Recommends PG for chair of natural history.

letters.title: To Henry Groves   27 March 1882
letters.summary: Thanks HG for kind offer. CD is not well enough to examine theUtricularia, but will try to look at theMitella.

letters.title: To T. H. Huxley   27 March 1882
letters.summary: Feels better. Grateful for THH’s kind letter. Wishes there were more automata like him.

letters.title: To G. C. Wallich   28 March 1882
letters.summary: GCW has correctly expressed CD’s views when he says he intentionally left the question of the origin of life uncanvassed as being altogetherultra viresin the present state of our knowledge. Thinks he may somewhere have said that principle of continuity renders it possible that the principle of life will be shown to be a part of, or consequence of, some general law.

letters.title: To Mr Loct?   29 March 1882
letters.summary: Thinks Mr Loct[?] ought to have sent an addressed envelope.

letters.title: To G. J. Romanes   29 March 1882
letters.summary: Sends manuscript by Baron de Villa Franca on the apparent grafting of sugar canes.

letters.title: To ?   29 March 1882
letters.summary: "Earthworms are hermaphrodite, but two must unite & both produce eggs.–– I have seen hundreds coupled, early in the morning & occasionally during the night.––"

letters.title: To Joseph Fayrer   30 March 1882
letters.summary: Requests snake poison for experiment.

letters.title: From Fritz Müller   31 March 1882
letters.summary:
Apologises for not having answered CD’s letters of 19 December [13564] and 4 January [13599] sooner.

Gives the results of his crossing experiments withPontederia (Eichhornia) crassipesandP. azurea. Has also begun experiments onHeteranthera reniformis.

Thanks CD for sending three parts of the first volume of Bentham and Hooker’sGenera plantarum.

letters.title: From Henry Groves   1 April 1882
letters.summary: Has forwarded some plants ofMitella opaca. Has observed their struggle for existence for several years in the gravel-pit pools at Mitcham.

letters.title: From Joseph Fayrer   2 April 1882
letters.summary: Is trying to get some cobra poison for CD.

letters.title: From J. L. Ambrose   3 April 1882
letters.summary: Reminds CD of three cards JLA sent in February for CD to sign and date and write his good wishes on.

letters.title: To Adolf Ernst   3 April 1882
letters.summary:
Edmond Perrier of Paris would be pleased to receive earthworms collected in Venezuela.

CD fears that he exaggerated the importance of worms in forming ledges on hillsides [seeEarthworms, p. 278 ff.].

letters.title: To Henry Groves   3 April 1882
letters.summary:
Thanks HG for specimen ofMitella.

CD has tried effects of carbonate of ammonia on chlorophyll grains, but his observations are hardly trustworthy. He finds stooping over the microscope affects his heart.

letters.title: To Rodulfo Amando Philippi   3 April 1882
letters.summary: Thanks for hisCatalogue of the Chilean plants.

letters.title: To P. L. Sclater   3 April 1882
letters.summary: Encloses paper [by W. Van Dyck] for publication by the Zoological Society ["On Syrian street dogs",Proc. Zool. Soc. Lond.(1882): 367–70].

letters.title: To W. T. Van Dyck   3 April 1882
letters.summary: Very anxious that WTVD’s essay [on Syrian street dogs, see13710] should be published. Has sent it to Zoological Society with a few introductory remarks [see13753].

letters.title: To Margaret Hadley   4 April 1882
letters.summary: Sends signature.

letters.title: From H. N. Moseley   5 April 1882
letters.summary: Solicits CD’s subscription to the Rolleston Memorial Fund, which will be used for a post-graduate prize at Oxford and Cambridge.

letters.title: ToNature   [before 6 April 1882]
letters.summary: Reports observations of W. D. Crick [see13705,13715, and13721] and Frank Norgate [see13079]. They leave no doubt that living bivalves are often carried from pond to pond.

letters.title: To Margaret Hadley   6 April [1882]
letters.summary: Sends his birth date.

letters.title: To W. E. A. Axon   7 April [1882?]
letters.summary: Cannot contribute article to new journal [The Field Naturalist and Scientific Student]. Writes only to communicate new facts.

letters.title: To H. N. Moseley   7 April 1882
letters.summary:
Adds to his previous subscription for the Rolleston Memorial Fund.

Hopes HNM’s position at Oxford is satisfactory.

letters.title: From H. N. Moseley   8 April 1882
letters.summary:
Thanks CD for contribution to Rolleston Fund

and for congratulations on his Professorship at Oxford.

letters.title: From A. N. Hopkins   9 April 1882
letters.summary: Sends fact about earthworms.

letters.title: To J. E. Todd   10 April 1882
letters.summary:
Requests seeds ofSolanum rostratum.

Fritz Müller believes that in plants with anthers of different colours, bees collect from one set alone.

Suggests JET send copy of paper ["Flowers ofSolanum rostratumandCassia chamaecrista",Am. Nat.16 (1882): 281–7] to Müller.

letters.title: From William Ogle   12 April 1882
letters.summary: A friend once "caught" an oyster while fishing, which confirms CD’s note ["On the dispersal of freshwater bivalves",Collected papers2: 276–8].

letters.title: To J. L. Ambrose   15 April 1882
letters.summary: Remembers signing cards but they must have been lost in the post. Sends signature.

letters.title: From Charles Naudin   15 April 1882
letters.summary:
Sends moreTrifolium resupinatum.

In France as in England there is indignation at the insults Decaisne suffered in the last years of his life.

Charles Martins has lost his Professorship at Montpellier.

letters.title: To William Watson   17 April 1882
letters.summary: Corrects WW’s misunderstanding of passage about habit of dogs in burying food [seeExpression: 44].
